patientidentificationsystems.name: patient identification systems
patientidentificationsystems.definition: Patient identification systems is organized procedures for establishing patient identity, including use of bracelets, etc.

bonediseases,developmental.name: bone diseases , developmental
bonediseases,developmental.definition: Developmental bone diseases is diseases resulting in abnormal growth or abnormal morphogenesis of bones.

polymorphism,singlenucleotide.name: polymorphism , single nucleotide
polymorphism,singlenucleotide.definition: Single nucleotide polymorphism is a single nucleotide variation in a genetic sequence that occurs at appreciable frequency in the population.

skinabsorption.name: skin absorption
skinabsorption.definition: Skin absorption is uptake of substances through the skin.

unitedstates.name: united states
unitedstates.definition: United states is a country in north america between canada and [MASK].

pregnancy,interstitial.name: pregnancy , interstitial
pregnancy,interstitial.definition: Interstitial pregnancy is a type of ectopic pregnancy in which the extrauterine embryo implantation occurs in the portion of the fallopian tube that traverses the muscular wall of the uterus.

intestine,large.name: intestine , large
intestine,large.definition: Large intestine is a segment of the lower gastrointestinal tract that includes the cecum; the colon; and the rectum.

graftocclusion,vascular.name: graft occlusion , vascular
graftocclusion,vascular.definition: Vascular [MASK] occlusion is obstruction of flow in biological or prosthetic vascular [MASK].

surgicaltape.name: surgical tape
surgicaltape.definition: Surgical tape is a flat, flexible strip of material used to cover or fasten together damaged tissue.

adaptorproteincomplexbetasubunits.name: adaptor protein complex beta subunits
adaptorproteincomplexbetasubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex beta subunits is a family of large adaptin protein complex subunits of approximately 90-130 kDa in size.

riskreductionbehavior.name: risk reduction behavior
riskreductionbehavior.definition: Risk reduction behavior is reduction of high-risk choices and adoption of low-risk quantity and frequency alternatives.

healthphysics.name: health physics
healthphysics.definition: Health physics is the science concerned with problems of radiation protection relevant to reducing or preventing radiation exposure, and the effects of ionizing radiation on humans and their environment.

esophagealperforation.name: esophageal perforation
esophagealperforation.definition: Esophageal perforation is an opening or hole in the esophagus that is caused by trauma, injury, or pathological process.

microsomes,liver.name: microsomes , liver
microsomes,liver.definition: Liver microsomes is closed vesicles of fragmented endoplasmic reticulum created when liver cells or tissue are disrupted by homogenization. They may be smooth or rough.

receptors,opioid,kappa.name: receptors , opioid , kappa
receptors,opioid,kappa.definition: Kappa opioid receptors is a class of opioid receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Kappa opioid receptors bind dynorphins with a higher affinity than endorphins which are themselves preferred to enkephalins.

argininekinase.name: arginine kinase
argininekinase.definition: [MASK] kinase is an enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of the guanidine nitrogen of [MASK] in the presence of atp and a divalent cation with formation of phosphorylarginine and adp. ec 2.7.3.3.

andersensyndrome.name: andersen syndrome
andersensyndrome.definition: Andersen syndrome is a form of inherited long qt syndrome (or lqt7) that is characterized by a triad of potassium-sensitive periodic paralysis, ventricular ectopic beats, and abnormal features such as short stature, low-[MASK] ears, and scoliosis. It results from mutations of kcnj2 gene which encodes a channel protein (inward rectifier potassium channels) that regulates resting membrane potential.

vaccines,attenuated.name: vaccines , attenuated
vaccines,attenuated.definition: Attenuated vaccines is live vaccines prepared from microorganisms which have undergone physical adaptation (e.g., by radiation or temperature conditioning) or serial passage in laboratory animal hosts or infected tissue/cell cultures, in order to produce avirulent mutant strains capable of inducing protective immunity.

rna,transfer,leu.name: rna , transfer , leu
rna,transfer,leu.definition: Leu transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying [MASK] to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

powderdiffraction.name: powder diffraction
powderdiffraction.definition: Powder diffraction is method of using a polycrystalline powder and Rietveld refinement (least squares analysis) of x-ray diffraction or [MASK]. It circumvents the difficulties of producing single large crystals.

neoplasmmetastasis.name: neoplasm metastasis
neoplasmmetastasis.definition: Neoplasm metastasis is the transfer of a neoplasm from one organ or part of the body to another remote from the primary site.

platinumcompounds.name: platinum compounds
platinumcompounds.definition: [MASK] compounds is inorganic compounds which contain [MASK] as the central atom.

drugresistance,multiple,fungal.name: drug resistance , multiple , fungal
drugresistance,multiple,fungal.definition: Fungal multiple drug resistance is the ability of fungi to resist or to become tolerant to several structurally and functionally distinct drugs simultaneously. This resistance phenotype may be attributed to multiple gene mutations.

rna,transfer,asp.name: rna , transfer , asp
rna,transfer,asp.definition: Asp transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying aspartic acid to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

chocells.name: cho cells
chocells.definition: Cho cells is cell line derived from the ovary of the Chinese hamster, Cricetulus griseus (cricetulus). The species is a favorite for cytogenetic studies because of its small chromosome number. The cell line has provided model systems for the study of genetic alterations in cultured mammalian cells.

chromosomes.name: chromosomes
chromosomes.definition: Chromosomes is in a prokaryotic cell or in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell, a structure consisting of or containing dna which carries the genetic information essential to the cell. (From Singleton & Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

collectionsastopic.name: collections as topic
collectionsastopic.definition: Collections as topic is works about items gathered and assembled in some order to facilitate access or use.

tertiarycarecenters.name: tertiary care centers
tertiarycarecenters.definition: Tertiary care centers is a medical facility which provides a high degree of subspecialty expertise for patients from centers where they received secondary care.

forcedexpiratoryflowrates.name: forced expiratory flow rates
forcedexpiratoryflowrates.definition: Forced expiratory flow rates is the rate of airflow measured during a forced vital capacity determination.

sleep.name: sleep
sleep.definition: Sleep is a readily reversible suspension of sensorimotor interaction with the environment, usually associated with recumbency and immobility.

cobaltisotopes.name: cobalt isotopes
cobaltisotopes.definition: Cobalt isotopes is stable cobalt atoms that have the same atomic number as the element cobalt, but differ in atomic weight. Co-59 is a stable cobalt isotope.

acidphosphatase.name: acid phosphatase
acidphosphatase.definition: Acid phosphatase is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of an orthophosphoric monoester and water to an alcohol and orthophosphate. ec 3.1.3.2.

pediatricdentistry.name: pediatric dentistry
pediatricdentistry.definition: Pediatric dentistry is the practice of dentistry concerned with the dental problems of children, proper maintenance, and treatment. The dental care may include the services provided by dental specialists.

bookreview.name: book review
bookreview.definition: Book review is work consisting of critical analyses of books or other monographic works.

injections,jet.name: injections , jet
injections,jet.definition: Jet injections is the injection of solutions into the skin by compressed air devices so that only the solution pierces the skin.

negativeresults.name: negative results
negativeresults.definition: Negative results is subject matter related to research studies in which the data do not demonstrate any clear evidence of effect, especially if an effect was expected.

emergencyservice,hospital.name: emergency service , hospital
emergencyservice,hospital.definition: Hospital emergency service is hospital department responsible for the administration and provision of immediate medical or surgical care to the emergency patient.

healthimpactassessment.name: health impact assessment
healthimpactassessment.definition: Health impact assessment is combination of procedures, methods, and tools by which a policy, program, or project may be judged as to its potential effects on the health of a population, and the distribution of those effects within the population.

receptors,laminin.name: receptors , laminin
receptors,laminin.definition: Laminin receptors is glycoprotein molecules on the surface of cells that react with or bind to laminin whose function allows the binding of epithelial cells to the basement membrane. The molecular weight of this high-affinity receptor is 67 kD.

carbonsequestration.name: carbon sequestration
carbonsequestration.definition: Carbon sequestration is any of several processes for the permanent or long-term artificial or natural capture or removal and storage of carbon dioxide and other forms of carbon, through biological, chemical or physical processes, in a manner that prevents it from being released into the atmosphere.

friendmurineleukemiavirus.name: friend murine leukemia virus
friendmurineleukemiavirus.definition: Friend murine leukemia virus is a strain of Murine leukemia virus (leukemia virus, murine) producing leukemia of the reticulum-cell type with massive infiltration of liver, spleen, and bone marrow. It infects dba/2 and Swiss mice.

carcinoma,hepatocellular.name: carcinoma , hepatocellular
carcinoma,hepatocellular.definition: Hepatocellular carcinoma is a primary malignant neoplasm of epithelial liver cells. It ranges from a well-differentiated tumor with epithelial cells indistinguishable from normal [MASK] to a poorly differentiated neoplasm. The cells may be uniform or markedly pleomorphic, or form giant cells. Several classification schemes have been suggested.

continuityofpatientcare.name: continuity of patient care
continuityofpatientcare.definition: Continuity of patient care is health care provided on a continuing basis from the initial contact, following the patient through all phases of medical care.

transportation.name: transportation
transportation.definition: Transportation is the means of moving persons, animals, goods, or materials from one place to another.

physicians'offices.name: physicians ' offices
physicians'offices.definition: Physicians' offices is establishments of licensed physicians primarily engaged in the private or group practice of general or specialized medicine or surgery.

rheumatoidnodule.name: rheumatoid nodule
rheumatoidnodule.definition: Rheumatoid nodule is subcutaneous nodules seen in 20-30% of rheumatoid arthritis patients. They may arise anywhere on the body, but are most frequently found over the bony prominences. The nodules are characterized histologically by dense areas of fibrinoid necrosis with basophilic streaks and granules, surrounded by a palisade of cells, mainly fibroblasts and histiocytes.

pyruvatedehydrogenasecomplex.name: pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
pyruvatedehydrogenasecomplex.definition: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is a multienzyme complex responsible for the formation of acetyl coenzyme a from pyruvate. The enzyme components are pyruvate dehydrogenase (lipoamide); dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase; and lipoamide dehydrogenase. Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is subject to three types of control: inhibited by acetyl-CoA and nadh; influenced by the energy state of the cell; and inhibited when a specific serine residue in the pyruvate decarboxylase is phosphorylated by atp. pyruvate dehydrogenase (lipoamide)-phosphatase catalyzes reactivation of the complex. (From Concise Encyclopedia Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 3rd ed)

geneticloci.name: genetic loci
geneticloci.definition: Genetic loci is specific regions that are mapped within a genome. Genetic loci are usually identified with a shorthand notation that indicates the chromosome number and the position of a specific band along the p or q [MASK] of the chromosome where they are found. For example the locus 6p21 is found within band 21 of the P-[MASK] of chromosome 6. Many well known genetic loci are also known by common names that are associated with a genetic function or hereditary disease.

agedeterminationbyteeth.name: age determination by teeth
agedeterminationbyteeth.definition: Age determination by teeth is a means of identifying the age of an animal or human through tooth examination.

collagentypexii.name: collagen type xii
collagentypexii.definition: Collagen type xii is a fibril-associated collagen found in many tissues bearing high tensile stress, such as tendons and ligaments. It is comprised of a trimer of three identical alpha1(XII) chains.

asthma,occupational.name: asthma , occupational
asthma,occupational.definition: Occupational asthma is asthma attacks caused, triggered, or exacerbated by occupational exposure.

aminoacids,aromatic.name: amino acids , aromatic
aminoacids,aromatic.definition: Aromatic amino acids is amino acids containing an aromatic side chain.

outcomeassessment,healthcare.name: outcome assessment , health care
outcomeassessment,healthcare.definition: Health care outcome assessment is research aimed at assessing the quality and effectiveness of health care as measured by the attainment of a specified end result or outcome. Measures include parameters such as improved health, lowered morbidity or mortality, and improvement of abnormal states (such as elevated blood pressure).

flavonoids.name: flavonoids
flavonoids.definition: Flavonoids is a group of phenyl benzopyrans named for having structures like flavones.

physicianincentiveplans.name: physician incentive plans
physicianincentiveplans.definition: Physician incentive plans is compensatory plans designed to motivate physicians in relation to patient referral, physician recruitment, and efficient use of the health facility.

aaaproteins.name: aaa proteins
aaaproteins.definition: Aaa proteins is a large, highly conserved and functionally diverse superfamily of NTPases and nucleotide-binding proteins that are characterized by a conserved 200 to 250 amino acid nucleotide-binding and [MASK], the aaa+ module. They assemble into hexameric ring complexes that function in the energy-dependent remodeling of macromolecules. Members include atpases associated with diverse cellular activities.

academicsuccess.name: academic success
academicsuccess.definition: Academic success is level of engagement in educationally purposeful activities, [MASK], acquisition of desired knowledge, skills, and competencies, persistence and attainment of educational outcomes.

basecomposition.name: base composition
basecomposition.definition: Base composition is the relative amounts of the purines and pyrimidines in a nucleic acid.

soyfoods.name: soy foods
soyfoods.definition: Soy foods is foods made from soybeans. Soy foods are high in dietary proteins and phytoestrogens such as isoflavones.

socialcontrol,formal.name: social control , formal
socialcontrol,formal.definition: Formal social control is control which is exerted by the more stable organizations of society, such as established institutions and the law. They are ordinarily embodied in definite codes, usually written.

waterpollutants,radioactive.name: water pollutants , radioactive
waterpollutants,radioactive.definition: Radioactive water pollutants is pollutants, present in water or bodies of water, which exhibit radioactivity.

cellseparation.name: cell separation
cellseparation.definition: Cell separation is techniques for separating distinct populations of cells.

ciliaryneurotrophicfactorreceptoralphasu.name: ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit
ciliaryneurotrophicfactorreceptoralphasu.definition: Ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit is a ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor subunit. It is anchored to the cell surface via glycosylphosphatidylinositol linkage and has specificity for binding to ciliary neurotrophic factor. It lacks signal transducing domains which are found on the other two subunits of the receptor.

infant,lowbirthweight.name: infant , low birth weight
infant,lowbirthweight.definition: Low birth weight infant is an infant having a birth weight of 2500 gm. (5.5 lb.) or less but infant, very low birth weight is available for infants having a birth weight of 1500 grams (3.3 lb.) or less.

genetransfer,horizontal.name: gene transfer , horizontal
genetransfer,horizontal.definition: Horizontal gene transfer is the naturally occurring transmission of genetic information between organisms, related or unrelated, circumventing parent-to-offspring transmission. Horizontal gene transfer may occur via a variety of naturally occurring processes such as [MASK]; genetic transduction; and transfection. It may result in a change of the recipient organism's genetic composition (transformation, genetic).

classicalswinefevervirus.name: classical swine fever virus
classicalswinefevervirus.definition: Classical swine fever virus is a species of the pestivirus genus causing exceedingly contagious and fatal hemorrhagic disease of swine.

child,preschool.name: child , preschool
child,preschool.definition: Preschool child is a child between the ages of 2 and 5.

virus.name: virus
virus.definition: Virus is minute infectious agents whose genomes are composed of DNA or RNA, but not both. They are characterized by a lack of independent metabolism and the inability to replicate outside living host cells.

disabledpersons.name: disabled persons
disabledpersons.definition: Disabled persons is persons with physical or mental disabilities that affect or limit their activities of daily living and that may require special accommodations.

mutantproteins.name: mutant proteins
mutantproteins.definition: Mutant proteins is proteins produced from genes that have acquired mutations.

proteintransport.name: protein transport
proteintransport.definition: Protein transport is the process of moving proteins from one cellular compartment (including extracellular) to another by various sorting and transport mechanisms such as gated transport, protein translocation, and vesicular transport.

operativebloodsalvage.name: operative blood salvage
operativebloodsalvage.definition: Operative blood salvage is recovery of blood lost from surgical procedures for reuse by the same patient in autologous blood transfusions. It is collected during (intraoperatively) or after completion of (postoperatively) the surgical procedures.

immunization,passive.name: immunization , passive
immunization,passive.definition: Passive immunization is transfer of immunity from immunized to non-immune host by administration of serum antibodies, or transplantation of lymphocytes (adoptive transfer).

placentalcirculation.name: placental circulation
placentalcirculation.definition: Placental circulation is the circulation of blood, of both the mother and the fetus, through the placenta.

lamintypeb.name: lamin type b
lamintypeb.definition: Lamin type b is a subclass of ubiquitously-expressed lamins having an acidic isoelectric point. They are found to remain bound to nuclear membranes during [MASK].

dentaldeposits.name: dental deposits
dentaldeposits.definition: Dental deposits is accumulations of microflora that lead to pathological plaque and calculus which cause periodontal diseases. It can be considered a type of biofilms. It is subtly distinguished from the protective dental pellicle.

racerelations.name: race relations
racerelations.definition: Race relations is cultural contacts between people of different races.

tibialnerve.name: tibial nerve
tibialnerve.definition: Tibial nerve is the medial terminal branch of the sciatic nerve. The tibial nerve fibers originate in lumbar and sacral spinal segments (l4 to s2). They supply motor and sensory innervation to parts of the calf and [MASK].

rna,smallinterfering.name: rna , small interfering
rna,smallinterfering.definition: Small interfering rna is small double-stranded, non-protein coding RNAs (21-31 nucleotides) involved in gene silencing functions, especially rna interference (RNAi). Endogenously, siRNAs are generated from dsRNAs (rna, double-stranded) by the same ribonuclease, Dicer, that generates miRNAs (micrornas). The perfect match of the siRNAs' antisense strand to their target RNAs mediates RNAi by siRNA-guided rna cleavage. siRNAs fall into different classes including trans-acting siRNA (tasiRNA), repeat-associated rna (rasiRNA), small-scan rna (scnRNA), and Piwi protein-interacting rna (piRNA) and have different specific gene silencing functions.

coaltar.name: coal tar
coaltar.definition: Coal tar is a by-product of the destructive distillation of coal used as a topical antieczematic. It is an antipruritic and keratoplastic agent used also in the treatment of psoriasis and other skin conditions. Occupational exposure to soots, tars, and certain mineral oils is known to be carcinogenic according to the Fourth Annual Report on Carcinogens (ntp 85-002, 1985) (Merck Index, 11th ed).

visualpathways.name: visual pathways
visualpathways.definition: Visual pathways is [MASK] of cell bodies and nerve fibers conducting impulses from the eyes to the cerebral cortex. It includes the retina; optic nerve; optic tract; and geniculocalcarine tract.

peergroup.name: peer group
peergroup.definition: Peer group is group composed of associates of same species, approximately the same age, and usually of similar rank or [MASK].

fructose.name: fructose
fructose.definition: Fructose is a monosaccharide in sweet fruits and honey that is soluble in water, alcohol, or ether. It is used as a preservative and an [MASK] in parenteral feeding.

telephone.name: telephone
telephone.definition: Telephone is an instrument for reproducing sounds especially articulate [MASK] at a distance. (Webster, 3rd ed)

practiceguideline.name: practice guideline
practiceguideline.definition: Practice guideline is work consisting of a [MASK] of directions or principles to assist the health care practitioner with patient care decisions about appropriate diagnostic, therapeutic, or other clinical procedures for specific clinical circumstances. Practice guidelines may be developed by government agencies at any level, institutions, organizations such as professional societies or governing boards, or by the convening of expert panels. They can provide a [MASK] for assessing and evaluating the quality and effectiveness of health care in terms of measuring improved health, reduction of variation in services or procedures performed, and reduction of variation in outcomes of health care delivered.

fattyacids,volatile.name: fatty acids , volatile
fattyacids,volatile.definition: Volatile fatty acids is short-chain fatty acids of up to six carbon atoms in length. They are the major end products of microbial fermentation in the ruminant digestive tract and have also been implicated in the causation of neurological diseases in humans.

universalhealthcare.name: universal health care
universalhealthcare.definition: Universal health care is access for all people to needed health services (including prevention, promotion, treatment, rehabilitation and palliation) of sufficient quality to be effective while also ensuring that the use of these services does not expose the user to financial hardship. (From https://www.who.int/healthsystems/universal_health_coverage/en/)

hivenhancer.name: hiv enhancer
hivenhancer.definition: Hiv enhancer is cis-acting regulatory sequences in the hiv long terminal repeat (ltr) which play a major role in induction or augmentation of hiv gene expression in response to environmental stimuli such as mitogens, phorbol esters, or other viruses. The hiv enhancer is the binding site for many cellular transcription factors including the nuclear factor NF-kappa b.

socialskills.name: social skills
socialskills.definition: Social skills is the personal [MASK] of abilities required to successfully interact and communicate with others, both verbally and non-verbally through gestures, body language and personal appearance.

combatdisorders.name: combat disorders
combatdisorders.definition: Combat disorders is neurotic reactions to unusual, severe, or overwhelming military stress.

lysosomalstoragediseases.name: lysosomal storage diseases
lysosomalstoragediseases.definition: Lysosomal storage diseases is inborn errors of metabolism characterized by defects in specific lysosomal hydrolases and resulting in intracellular accumulation of unmetabolized substrates.

nuclearmicroscopy.name: nuclear microscopy
nuclearmicroscopy.definition: Nuclear microscopy is a method of simultaneously imaging and measuring elements at the submicron level. Nuclear microscopy uses a focused high-energy ion beam of protons and [MASK] (a nuclear microprobe) to interact with the sample. The resulting emitted radiations are analyzed by a group of techniques simultaneously: particle induced x ray emission spectrometry for minor and trace element identification; Rutherford Backscattering Spectroscopy to assess sample thickness and bulk elements such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen; and Scanning Transmission Ion Microscopy to assess sample structure and density.

sinusthrombosis,intracranial.name: sinus thrombosis , intracranial
sinusthrombosis,intracranial.definition: Intracranial sinus thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in the cranial sinuses, large endothelium-lined venous channels situated within the skull. Intracranial sinuses, also called cranial venous sinuses, include the superior sagittal, cavernous, lateral, petrous sinuses, and many others. Cranial sinus thrombosis can lead to severe headache; seizure; and other neurological defects.

dictionary,dental.name: dictionary , dental
dictionary,dental.definition: Dental dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to dentistry-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

childofimpairedparents.name: child of impaired parents
childofimpairedparents.definition: Child of impaired parents is child with one or more parents afflicted by a physical or mental disorder.

pulmonaryvalve.name: pulmonary valve
pulmonaryvalve.definition: Pulmonary valve is a valve situated at the entrance to the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle.

maternalhealth.name: maternal health
maternalhealth.definition: Maternal health is the health of women during pregnancy; childbirth and the postpartum period.

acidosis,renaltubular.name: acidosis , renal tubular
acidosis,renaltubular.definition: Renal tubular acidosis is a group of genetic disorders of the kidney tubules characterized by the accumulation of metabolically produced acids with elevated plasma chloride, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. Defective renal acidification of urine (proximal tubules) or low renal acid excretion (distal tubules) can lead to complications such as hypokalemia, hypercalcinuria with nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis, and rickets.

healthpersonnel.name: health personnel
healthpersonnel.definition: Health personnel is men and women working in the provision of health services, whether as individual practitioners or employees of health institutions and programs, whether or not professionally trained, and whether or not subject to public regulation. (From a Discursive Dictionary of Health Care, 1976)

aceticacid.name: acetic acid
aceticacid.definition: Acetic acid is product of the oxidation of ethanol and of the destructive distillation of [MASK]. It is used locally, occasionally internally, as a counterirritant and also as a reagent. (Stedman, 26th ed)

lens,crystalline.name: lens , crystalline
lens,crystalline.definition: Crystalline lens is a transparent, biconvex structure of the eye, enclosed in a capsule and situated behind the iris and in front of the [MASK] ([MASK]). It is slightly overlapped at its margin by the ciliary processes. Adaptation by the [MASK] is crucial for ocular accommodation.

pacemaker,artificial.name: pacemaker , artificial
pacemaker,artificial.definition: Artificial pacemaker is a device designed to stimulate, by electric impulses, contraction of the heart muscles. It may be temporary (external) or permanent (internal or internal-external).

dna,circular.name: dna , circular
dna,circular.definition: Circular dna is any of the covalently closed dna molecules found in bacteria, many viruses, mitochondria, plastids, and plasmids. Small, polydisperse circular DNA's have also been observed in a number of eukaryotic organisms and are suggested to have homology with chromosomal dna and the capacity to be inserted into, and excised from, chromosomal dna. It is a fragment of dna formed by a process of looping out and deletion, containing a constant region of the mu heavy chain and the 3'-part of the mu switch region. Circular dna is a normal product of rearrangement among gene segments encoding the variable regions of immunoglobulin light and heavy chains, as well as the T-cell receptor. (Riger et al., Glossary of Genetics, 5th ed & Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

oralhygiene.name: oral hygiene
oralhygiene.definition: Oral hygiene is the practice of personal hygiene of the mouth. It includes the maintenance of oral cleanliness, tissue tone, and general preservation of [MASK].

spinalnerveroots.name: spinal nerve roots
spinalnerveroots.definition: Spinal nerve roots is paired bundles of nerve fibers entering and leaving the spinal cord at each segment. The dorsal and ventral nerve roots join to form the mixed segmental spinal nerves. The dorsal roots are generally afferent, formed by the central projections of the spinal (dorsal root) ganglia sensory cells, and the ventral roots are efferent, comprising the axons of spinal motor and preganglionic autonomic fibers.

hearing.name: hearing
hearing.definition: Hearing is the ability or act of sensing and transducing [MASK] to the central nervous system. It is also called audition.

cellshape.name: cell shape
cellshape.definition: Cell shape is the quality of surface form or [MASK] of cells.

skillednursingfacilities.name: skilled nursing facilities
skillednursingfacilities.definition: Skilled nursing facilities is extended care facilities which provide skilled nursing care or rehabilitation services for inpatients on a daily basis.

footinjuries.name: foot injuries
footinjuries.definition: [MASK] injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the [MASK].

thailand.name: thailand
thailand.definition: Thailand is formerly known as Siam, this is a Southeast Asian nation at the center of the Indochina peninsula. Bangkok is the capital city.

dentalcarefordisabled.name: dental care for disabled
dentalcarefordisabled.definition: Dental care for disabled is dental care for the emotionally, mentally, or physically disabled patient. It does not include dental care for the chronically ill ( = dental care for chronically ill).

patientcare.name: patient care
patientcare.definition: Patient care is the services rendered by members of the health profession and non-professionals under their supervision.

congress.name: congress
congress.definition: Congress is published record of the [MASK] delivered at or issued on the occasion of individual congresses, symposia, and meetings; [MASK] of [MASK] delivered at such congresses; reports of the officers and delegates of such congresses; combinations of the foregoing; or proceedings of the conference of a society if they are not limited to matters of internal organization.

recombinantfusionproteins.name: recombinant fusion proteins
recombinantfusionproteins.definition: Recombinant fusion proteins is recombinant proteins produced by the genetic translation of fused genes formed by the combination of nucleic acid regulatory sequences of one or more genes with the protein coding sequences of one or more genes.

serialpublications.name: serial publications
serialpublications.definition: Serial publications is publications in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to be continued indefinitely. (ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p203)

magneticresonancespectroscopy.name: magnetic resonance spectroscopy
magneticresonancespectroscopy.definition: Magnetic resonance spectroscopy is spectroscopic method of measuring the magnetic moment of elementary particles such as atomic nuclei, protons or [MASK]. It is employed in clinical applications such as nmr Tomography (magnetic resonance imaging).

ventricularfunction,right.name: ventricular function , right
ventricularfunction,right.definition: Right ventricular function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the right heart ventricle.

myelomaproteins.name: myeloma proteins
myelomaproteins.definition: Myeloma proteins is abnormal immunoglobulins characteristic of multiple myeloma.

dataaggregation.name: data aggregation
dataaggregation.definition: Data aggregation is process of searching, gathering, and presenting data in a summarized format.

models,organizational.name: models , organizational
models,organizational.definition: Organizational models is theoretical representations and constructs that describe or explain the structure and hierarchy of relationships and interactions within or between formal organizational entities or informal social groups.

adolescentpsychiatry.name: adolescent psychiatry
adolescentpsychiatry.definition: Adolescent psychiatry is the medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders in individuals 13-18 years.

cerebralhemorrhage.name: cerebral hemorrhage
cerebralhemorrhage.definition: Cerebral hemorrhage is bleeding into one or both cerebral hemispheres including the basal ganglia and the cerebral cortex. It is often associated with hypertension and craniocerebral trauma.

northwesternunitedstates.name: northwestern united states
northwesternunitedstates.definition: Northwestern united states is the geographic area of the northwestern region of the United States. The states usually included in this region are Idaho, Montana, Oregon, [MASK], and Wyoming.

antigens,bacterial.name: antigens , bacterial
antigens,bacterial.definition: Bacterial antigens is substances elaborated by bacteria that have antigenic activity.

synovialcyst.name: synovial cyst
synovialcyst.definition: Synovial cyst is non-neoplastic tumor-like lesions at joints, developed from the synovial membrane of a joint through the joint capsule into the periarticular tissues. They are filled with synovial fluid with a smooth and translucent appearance. a synovial cyst can develop from any joint, but most commonly at the back of the [MASK], where it is known as popliteal cyst.

respiratorydeadspace.name: respiratory dead space
respiratorydeadspace.definition: Respiratory dead space is that part of the respiratory tract or the air within the respiratory tract that does not exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with pulmonary capillary blood.

functionalconcept.name: functional concept
functionalconcept.definition: Functional concept is concepts that are functional.

microscopy.name: microscopy
microscopy.definition: Microscopy is the use of instrumentation and techniques for visualizing material and details that cannot be seen by the unaided eye. It is usually done by enlarging images, transmitted by light or [MASK] beams, with optical or magnetic lenses that magnify the entire image field. With scanning microscopy, images are generated by collecting output from the specimen in a point-by-point fashion, on a magnified scale, as it is scanned by a narrow beam of light or [MASK], a laser, a conductive probe, or a topographical probe.

nervetissue.name: nerve tissue
nervetissue.definition: Nerve tissue is differentiated tissue of the central nervous system composed of nerve cells, fibers, dendrites, and specialized supporting cells.

hepatitisbvaccines.name: hepatitis b vaccines
hepatitisbvaccines.definition: Hepatitis b vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines containing inactivated hepatitis b or some of its component antigens and designed to prevent hepatitis b. Some vaccines may be recombinantly produced.

nadphoxidase4.name: nadph oxidase 4
nadphoxidase4.definition: Nadph oxidase 4 is an nadph oxidase that is strongly expressed in the kidney. It forms a complex with cyba-p22phox and produces intracellular superoxides that may regulate cellular signaling in apoptosis; bone resorption; and nf-kappa b activation.

portionsize.name: portion size
portionsize.definition: Portion size is the amount of a particular food one chooses to eat at a single meal. It is different from [MASK], which is a reference amount of food as defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the united states department of agriculture.

contactlenses,hydrophilic.name: contact lenses , hydrophilic
contactlenses,hydrophilic.definition: Hydrophilic contact lenses is soft, supple contact lenses made of plastic polymers which interact readily with water molecules. Many types are available, including continuous and extended-wear versions, which are gas-permeable and easily sterilized.

tokeneconomy.name: token economy
tokeneconomy.definition: Token economy is a practice whereby tokens representing money, toys, candy, etc., are given as secondary reinforcers contingent upon certain desired behaviors or performances.

selection,genetic.name: selection , genetic
selection,genetic.definition: Genetic selection is differential and non-random reproduction of different genotypes, operating to alter the gene frequencies within a population.

alloys.name: alloys
alloys.definition: Alloys is a mixture of metallic elements or compounds with other metallic or metalloid elements in varying proportions.

retinalhemorrhage.name: retinal hemorrhage
retinalhemorrhage.definition: Retinal hemorrhage is bleeding from the vessels of the retina.

cyclicampreceptorprotein.name: cyclic amp receptor protein
cyclicampreceptorprotein.definition: Cyclic amp receptor protein is a transcriptional regulator in prokaryotes which, when activated by binding cyclic amp, acts at several promoters. Cyclic amp receptor protein was originally identified as a catabolite gene activator protein. It was subsequently shown to regulate several functions unrelated to catabolism, and to be both a negative and a positive regulator of transcription. Cell surface cyclic amp receptors are not included (cyclic amp receptors), nor are the eukaryotic cytoplasmic cyclic amp receptor proteins, which are the regulatory subunits of cyclic amp-dependent protein kinases.

sodiumfluoride.name: sodium fluoride
sodiumfluoride.definition: Sodium fluoride is a source of inorganic fluoride which is used topically to prevent dental caries.

fermdomains.name: ferm domains
fermdomains.definition: Ferm domains is widely occuring protein domains that function to link signaling and cytoskeletal proteins to the plasma membrane. They occur mostly at the N-terminal region of proteins that contain them.

musculoskeletalmanipulations.name: musculoskeletal manipulations
musculoskeletalmanipulations.definition: Musculoskeletal manipulations is various manipulations of body tissues, muscles and bones by hands or equipment to improve health and circulation, relieve fatigue, promote healing.

obstetricsurgicalprocedures.name: obstetric surgical procedures
obstetricsurgicalprocedures.definition: Obstetric surgical procedures is surgery performed on the pregnant woman for conditions associated with pregnancy, labor, or the puerperium. It does not include surgery of the newborn infant.

germination.name: germination
germination.definition: Germination is the initial stages of the growth of [MASK] into a seedlings. The embryonic shoot (plumule) and embryonic plant roots (radicle) emerge and grow upwards and downwards respectively. Food reserves for germination come from endosperm tissue within the [MASK] and/or from the [MASK] leaves (cotyledon). (Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)

informationmanagement.name: information management
informationmanagement.definition: Information management is management of the acquisition, organization, storage, retrieval, and dissemination of information. (From Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, 1994)

receptors,patternrecognition.name: receptors , pattern recognition
receptors,patternrecognition.definition: Pattern recognition receptors is a large family of cell surface receptors that bind conserved molecular structures (pamps) present in pathogens. They play important roles in host defense by mediating cellular responses to pathogens.

arousal.name: arousal
arousal.definition: Arousal is cortical vigilance or readiness of tone, presumed to be in response to sensory stimulation via the reticular activating system.

efficiency.name: efficiency
efficiency.definition: Efficiency is ratio of output to effort and or resources, or the ratio of effort and or resources produced to energy expended.

neuromuscularagents.name: neuromuscular agents
neuromuscularagents.definition: Neuromuscular agents is drugs used for their actions on skeletal muscle. Included are agents that act directly on skeletal muscle, those that alter neuromuscular transmission ([MASK]), and drugs that act centrally as skeletal muscle relaxants (muscle relaxants, central). Drugs used in the treatment of movement disorders are anti-dyskinesia agents.

deathdomainreceptorsignalingadaptorprote.name: death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins
deathdomainreceptorsignalingadaptorprote.definition: Death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins is intracellular signaling adaptor proteins that contain [MASK] and bind to the cytoplasmic death domain region found on death domain receptors. Many of the proteins in this class take part in intracellular signaling involving tumor necrosis factor receptors.

attachmentsites,microbiological.name: attachment sites , microbiological
attachmentsites,microbiological.definition: Microbiological attachment sites is specific loci on both the [MASK] (attB) and the phage dna (attP) which delineate the sites where recombination takes place between them, as the phage dna becomes integrated (inserted) into the [MASK] during lysogeny.

hospitaladministration.name: hospital administration
hospitaladministration.definition: Hospital administration is management of the internal organization of the hospital.

microvasculardecompressionsurgery.name: microvascular decompression surgery
microvasculardecompressionsurgery.definition: Microvascular decompression surgery is surgery performed to relieve pressure from microvessels that are located around nerves and are causing nerve compression syndromes.

amygdala.name: amygdala
amygdala.definition: Amygdala is almond-shaped group of basal nuclei anterior to the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle of the temporal lobe. The amygdala is part of the limbic system.

basalgangliadiseases.name: basal ganglia diseases
basalgangliadiseases.definition: Basal ganglia diseases is diseases of the basal ganglia including the putamen; globus pallidus; claustrum; amygdala; and caudate nucleus. dyskinesias (most notably involuntary movements and alterations of the rate of movement) represent the primary clinical manifestations of these disorders. Common etiologies include cerebrovascular disorders; neurodegenerative diseases; and craniocerebral trauma.

urethralobstruction.name: urethral obstruction
urethralobstruction.definition: Urethral obstruction is partial or complete blockage in any part of the urethra that can lead to difficulty or inability to empty the [MASK]. It is characterized by an enlarged, often damaged, [MASK] with frequent urges to void.

fetalmembranes,prematurerupture.name: fetal membranes , premature rupture
fetalmembranes,prematurerupture.definition: Premature rupture fetal membranes is spontaneous tearing of the membranes surrounding the fetus any time before the onset of obstetric labor. Preterm prom is membrane rupture before 37 weeks of gestation.

zincphosphatecement.name: zinc phosphate cement
zincphosphatecement.definition: Zinc phosphate cement is a material used for cementation of inlays, crowns, bridges, and orthodontic appliances and occasionally as a temporary restoration. It is prepared by mixing zinc oxide and magnesium oxide powders with a liquid consisting principally of phosphoric acid, water, and [MASK]. (From Bouchers' Clinical Dental Terminology, 3d ed)

suicide,attempted.name: suicide , attempted
suicide,attempted.definition: Attempted suicide is the unsuccessful attempt to kill oneself.

epiduralabscess.name: epidural abscess
epiduralabscess.definition: Epidural abscess is circumscribed collections of suppurative material occurring in the spinal or intracranial [MASK]. The majority of epidural abscesses occur in the spinal canal and are associated with osteomyelitis of a vertebral body; analgesia, epidural; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations include local and radicular pain, weakness, sensory loss, urinary incontinence, and [MASK]. Cranial epidural abscesses are usually associated with osteomyelitis of a cranial bone, sinusitis, or otitis media. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p710 and pp1240-1; j Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 1998 Aug;65(2):209-12)

manualcommunication.name: manual communication
manualcommunication.definition: Manual communication is method of nonverbal communication utilizing hand movements as [MASK] equivalents.

bloodcoagulation.name: blood coagulation
bloodcoagulation.definition: Blood coagulation is the process of the interaction of blood coagulation factors that results in an insoluble fibrin clot.

crackcocaine.name: crack cocaine
crackcocaine.definition: Crack cocaine is the purified, alkaloidal, extra-potent form of cocaine. It is smoked (free-based), injected intravenously, and orally ingested. Use of crack results in alterations in function of the cardiovascular system, the autonomic nervous system, the central nervous system, and the gastrointestinal system. The slang term "crack" was derived from the crackling sound made upon igniting of this form of cocaine for smoking.

secondarycarecenters.name: secondary care centers
secondarycarecenters.definition: Secondary care centers is a healthcare facility equipped to provide all but the most specialized forms of care, surgery, and diagnostic techniques.

edema,cardiac.name: edema , cardiac
edema,cardiac.definition: Cardiac edema is abnormal fluid retention by the body due to impaired cardiac function or heart failure. It is usually characterized by increase in venous and capillary pressure, and swollen legs when standing. It is different from the generalized edema caused by renal dysfunction (nephrotic syndrome).

gastricfundus.name: gastric fundus
gastricfundus.definition: Gastric fundus is the superior portion of the body of the stomach above the level of the cardiac notch.

epidemiologicalmonitoring.name: epidemiological monitoring
epidemiologicalmonitoring.definition: Epidemiological monitoring is collection, analysis, and interpretation of data about the frequency, distribution, and consequences of disease or health conditions, for use in the planning, implementing, and evaluating public health programs.

cyclint.name: cyclin t
cyclint.definition: Cyclin t is a cyclin subtype that is found associated with cyclin-dependent kinase 9. Unlike traditional cyclins, which regulate the cell cycle, type t cyclins appear to regulate transcription and are components of positive transcriptional elongation factor b.

hospitals,voluntary.name: hospitals , voluntary
hospitals,voluntary.definition: Voluntary hospitals is private, not-for-profit hospitals that are autonomous, self-established, and self-supported.

hemoglobinc.name: hemoglobin c
hemoglobinc.definition: Hemoglobin c is a commonly occurring abnormal hemoglobin in which lysine replaces a glutamic acid residue at the sixth position of the beta chains. It results in reduced plasticity of erythrocytes.

financialmanagement.name: financial management
financialmanagement.definition: Financial management is the obtaining and management of funds for institutional needs and responsibility for fiscal affairs.

urinaryincontinence.name: urinary incontinence
urinaryincontinence.definition: Urinary incontinence is involuntary loss of urine, such as leaking of urine. It is a symptom of various underlying pathological processes. Major types of incontinence include urinary urge incontinence and urinary stress incontinence.

reflexsympatheticdystrophy.name: reflex sympathetic dystrophy
reflexsympatheticdystrophy.definition: Reflex sympathetic dystrophy is a syndrome characterized by severe burning pain in an extremity accompanied by sudomotor, vasomotor, and trophic changes in bone without an associated specific nerve injury. This condition is most often precipitated by trauma to soft tissue or nerve complexes. The skin over the affected region is usually erythematous and demonstrates hypersensitivity to tactile stimuli and erythema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1360; Pain 1995 Oct;63(1):127-33)

earlydetectionofcancer.name: early detection of cancer
earlydetectionofcancer.definition: Early detection of cancer is methods to identify and characterize cancer in the early stages of disease and predict tumor behavior.

encephalitisviruses,japanese.name: encephalitis viruses , japanese
encephalitisviruses,japanese.definition: Japanese encephalitis viruses is a subgroup of the genus flavivirus which comprises a number of viral species that are the etiologic agents of human encephalitis in many different geographical regions. These include Japanese encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, japanese), St. Louis encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, st. louis), Murray Valley encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, murray valley), and west nile virus.

immunoglobulina.name: immunoglobulin a
immunoglobulina.definition: Immunoglobulin a is represents 15-20% of the human serum immunoglobulins, mostly as the 4-chain polymer in humans or dimer in other mammals. Secretory IgA (immunoglobulin a, secretory) is the main immunoglobulin in secretions.

neuralstemcells.name: neural stem cells
neuralstemcells.definition: Neural stem cells is self-renewing cells that generate the main phenotypes of the nervous system in both the embryo and adult. Neural stem cells are precursors to both neurons and neuroglia.

periodontalindex.name: periodontal index
periodontalindex.definition: Periodontal index is a numerical rating scale for classifying the periodontal status of a person or population with a single figure which takes into consideration [MASK] as well as severity of the condition. It is based upon probe measurement of [MASK] and on gingival tissue status.

solidphaseextraction.name: solid phase extraction
solidphaseextraction.definition: Solid phase extraction is an extraction method that separates analytes using a solid phase and a liquid phase. It is used for preparative sample cleanup before analysis by chromatography and other analytical methods.

employerhealthcosts.name: employer health costs
employerhealthcosts.definition: Employer health costs is that portion of total health care costs borne by an individual's or group's employing organization.

nasalseptalperforation.name: nasal septal perforation
nasalseptalperforation.definition: Nasal septal perforation is an opening or hole in the [MASK] that is caused by trauma, injury, drug use, or pathological process.

spinalcordventralhorn.name: spinal cord ventral horn
spinalcordventralhorn.definition: Spinal cord ventral horn is one of three central columns of the spinal cord. It is composed of gray matter spinal laminae viii and ix.

chromosomepairing.name: chromosome pairing
chromosomepairing.definition: Chromosome pairing is the alignment of chromosomes at homologous sequences.

fetaldeath.name: fetal death
fetaldeath.definition: Fetal death is death of the developing young in utero. birth of a dead fetus is stillbirth.

meningitis,viral.name: meningitis , viral
meningitis,viral.definition: Viral meningitis is viral infections of the leptomeninges and subarachnoid space. togaviridae infections; flaviviridae infections; rubella; bunyaviridae infections; orbivirus infections; picornaviridae infections; orthomyxoviridae infections; rhabdoviridae infections; arenaviridae infections; herpesviridae infections; adenoviridae infections; jc virus infections; and retroviridae infections may cause this form of meningitis. Clinical manifestations include fever, headache, [MASK] pain, vomiting, photophobia, and signs of meningeal irritation. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1996, Ch26, pp1-3)

militaryhealthservices.name: military health services
militaryhealthservices.definition: Military health services is services organized for the diagnosis and treatment of disease and the maintenance of health primarily of military personnel.

spectrometry,mass,secondaryion.name: spectrometry , mass , secondary ion
spectrometry,mass,secondaryion.definition: Secondary ion mass spectrometry is a mass-spectrometric technique that is used for microscopic chemical analysis. a beam of primary ions with an energy of 5-20 kiloelectronvolts (keV) bombards a small spot on the surface of the sample under ultra-high vacuum conditions. Positive and negative secondary ions sputtered from the surface are analyzed in a mass spectrometer in regards to their mass-to-charge ratio. Digital imaging can be generated from the secondary ion beams and their intensity can be measured. Ionic images can be correlated with images from light or other microscopy providing useful tools in the study of molecular and drug actions.

reactiveoxygenspecies.name: reactive oxygen species
reactiveoxygenspecies.definition: Reactive oxygen species is molecules or ions formed by the incomplete one-[MASK] reduction of oxygen. These reactive oxygen intermediates include [MASK]; superoxides; peroxides; hydroxyl radical; and hypochlorous acid. They contribute to the microbicidal activity of phagocytes, regulation of signal transduction and gene expression, and the oxidative damage to nucleic acids; proteins; and lipids.

planttumors.name: plant tumors
planttumors.definition: Plant tumors is a localized proliferation of plant tissue forming a swelling or outgrowth, commonly with a characteristic shape and unlike any organ of the normal plant. Plant tumors or galls usually form in response to the action of a pathogen or a pest. (Holliday, p., a Dictionary of Plant Pathology, 1989, p330)

sarcoma,myeloid.name: sarcoma , myeloid
sarcoma,myeloid.definition: Myeloid sarcoma is an extramedullary tumor of immature myeloid cells or myeloblasts. Granulocytic sarcoma usually occurs with or follows the onset of [MASK].

buildingcodes.name: building codes
buildingcodes.definition: Building codes is standards or regulations for construction which are designed to ensure safety against electrical hazards, fires, etc.

imageenhancement.name: image enhancement
imageenhancement.definition: Image enhancement is improvement of the quality of a picture by various techniques, including computer processing, digital filtering, echocardiographic techniques, light and ultrastructural microscopy, fluorescence spectrometry and microscopy, scintigraphy, and in vitro image processing at the molecular level.

voluntaryhealthagencies.name: voluntary health agencies
voluntaryhealthagencies.definition: Voluntary health agencies is non-profit organizations concerned with various aspects of health, e.g., education, promotion, treatment, services, etc.

intracellularsignalingpeptidesandprotein.name: intracellular signaling peptides and proteins
intracellularsignalingpeptidesandprotein.definition: Intracellular signaling peptides and proteins is proteins and peptides that are involved in signal transduction within the cell. Included here are peptides and proteins that regulate the activity of transcription factors and cellular processes in response to signals from cell surface receptors. Intracellular signaling peptide and proteins may be part of an enzymatic signaling cascade or act through binding to and modifying the action of other signaling factors.

psychologicalphenomena.name: psychological phenomena
psychologicalphenomena.definition: Psychological phenomena is mechanisms and underlying psychological principles of mental processes and their applications.

hepatitisbvirus.name: hepatitis b virus
hepatitisbvirus.definition: Hepatitis b virus is the type species of the genus orthohepadnavirus which causes human hepatitis b and is also apparently a causal agent in human hepatocellular carcinoma. The Dane particle is an intact hepatitis virion, named after its discoverer. Non-infectious spherical and tubular particles are also seen in the serum.

socialproblems.name: social problems
socialproblems.definition: Social problems is situations affecting a significant number of people, that are believed to be sources of difficulty or threaten the stability of the community, and that require programs of amelioration.

pulmonaryvalveinsufficiency.name: pulmonary valve insufficiency
pulmonaryvalveinsufficiency.definition: Pulmonary valve insufficiency is backflow of blood from the [MASK] into the right ventricle due to imperfect closure of the pulmonary valve.

religionandpsychology.name: religion and psychology
religionandpsychology.definition: Religion and psychology is the interrelationship of psychology and religion.

myosinheavychains.name: myosin heavy chains
myosinheavychains.definition: Myosin heavy chains is the larger subunits of myosins. The heavy chains have a molecular weight of about 230 kDa and each heavy chain is usually associated with a dissimilar pair of myosin light chains. The heavy chains possess actin-binding and ATPase activity.

speechtherapy.name: speech therapy
speechtherapy.definition: [MASK] therapy is treatment for individuals with [MASK] defects and disorders that involves counseling and use of various exercises and aids to help the development of new [MASK] habits.

healthequity.name: health equity
healthequity.definition: Health equity is opportunity to attain full health potential and no one is disadvantaged from achieving this potential because of their social position or other socially determined circumstance.

intrauterinedevicemigration.name: intrauterine device migration
intrauterinedevicemigration.definition: [MASK] migration is the shifting in position or location of an [MASK] from its original placement.

wordassociationtests.name: word association tests
wordassociationtests.definition: Word association tests is lists of words to which individuals are asked to respond ascertaining the conceptual meaning held by the individual.

necrosis.name: necrosis
necrosis.definition: Necrosis is the death of cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury or failure of the blood supply.

arizona.name: arizona
arizona.definition: Arizona is state of the united states of america bounded on the east by New [MASK], on the north by Utah, on the west by Nevada and California, and on the south by [MASK].

onlinesocialnetworking.name: online social networking
onlinesocialnetworking.definition: Online social networking is connectivity facilitated by computer-based communications among persons with family, work, or other common interests.

receptors,fsh.name: receptors , fsh
receptors,fsh.definition: Fsh receptors is cell surface proteins that bind follicle stimulating hormone with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

lipidmobilization.name: lipid mobilization
lipidmobilization.definition: Lipid mobilization is lipolysis of stored lipids in the adipose tissue to release free fatty acids. Mobilization of stored lipids is under the regulation of lipolytic signals (catecholamines) or anti-lipolytic signals (insulin) via their actions on the hormone-sensitive lipase. This concept does not include lipid transport.

humanactivities.name: human activities
humanactivities.definition: Human activities is activities performed by humans.

endocrinesystem.name: endocrine system
endocrinesystem.definition: Endocrine system is the system of glands that release their secretions (hormones) directly into the circulatory system. In addition to the endocrine glands, included are the chromaffin system and the neurosecretory systems.

tachycardia.name: tachycardia
tachycardia.definition: Tachycardia is abnormally rapid heartbeat, usually with a heart rate above 100 beats per minute for adults. Tachycardia accompanied by disturbance in the cardiac depolarization (cardiac arrhythmia) is called tachyarrhythmia.

chemistrytechniques,analytical.name: chemistry techniques , analytical
chemistrytechniques,analytical.definition: Analytical chemistry techniques is methodologies used for the isolation, identification, detection, and quantitation of chemical substances.

geneticprofile.name: genetic profile
geneticprofile.definition: Genetic profile is a [MASK] of characteristics unique to the dna of an individual organism or population obtained by analyzing small samples of biological material such as body tissues or fluids, used especially in the context of predicting susceptibility to a particular disease. For example, some populations have identifiable genetic profiles which put them at higher risk for cancer. Distinguish from genetic background and genetic variation.

alaska.name: alaska
alaska.definition: Alaska is state of the united states of america bounded on the east by Canada and on the north, west, and south by the Pacific Ocean and the Bering Sea.

casemanagement.name: case management
casemanagement.definition: Case management is a traditional term for all the activities which a physician or other health care professional normally performs to insure the coordination of the medical services required by a patient. It also, when used in connection with managed care, covers all the activities of evaluating the patient, planning treatment, referral, and follow-up so that care is continuous and comprehensive and payment for the care is obtained. (From Slee & Slee, Health Care Terms, 2nd ed)

food.name: food
food.definition: Food is substances taken in by the body to provide nourishment.

operatorregions,genetic.name: operator regions , genetic
operatorregions,genetic.definition: Genetic operator regions is the regulatory elements of an operon to which activators or repressors bind thereby effecting the transcription of genes in the operon.

smokingdevices.name: smoking devices
smokingdevices.definition: Smoking devices is gadgets, utensils, apparatuses or instruments used for smoking.

spores.name: spores
spores.definition: Spores is the reproductive elements of lower organisms, such as bacteria; fungi; and cryptogamic plants.

geriatricnursing.name: geriatric nursing
geriatricnursing.definition: Geriatric nursing is nursing care of the aged patient given in the home, the hospital, or special institutions such as nursing homes, psychiatric institutions, etc.

immunesera.name: immune sera
immunesera.definition: Immune sera is serum that contains antibodies. It is obtained from an animal that has been immunized either by antigen injection or infection with microorganisms containing the antigen.

cellaggregation.name: cell aggregation
cellaggregation.definition: Cell aggregation is the phenomenon by which dissociated cells intermixed in vitro tend to group themselves with cells of their own type.

plantdevelopment.name: plant development
plantdevelopment.definition: Plant development is processes orchestrated or driven by a plethora of genes, plant hormones, and inherent biological timing mechanisms facilitated by secondary molecules, which result in the systematic transformation of plants and plant parts, from one stage of maturity to another.

sentinelspecies.name: sentinel species
sentinelspecies.definition: Sentinel species is organisms used to determine measurable environmental risks or hazards to human health and or well-being, thereby serving as advance or early warning signs of impending danger to humans. Examples of sentinel species are monkeys, [MASK] pigs, and the fabled canary in the coal mine.

healthexpenditures.name: health expenditures
healthexpenditures.definition: Health expenditures is the amounts spent by individuals, groups, nations, or private or public organizations for total health care and/or its various components. These amounts may or may not be equivalent to the actual costs (health care costs) and may or may not be shared among the patient, insurers, and/or employers.

tissue.name: tissue
tissue.definition: Tissue is Collections of differentiated cells, such as epithelium, connective tissue, muscles, and nerve tissue. Tissues are cooperatively arranged to form organs with specialized functions such as respiration, [MASK], reproduction, movement, and others.

reducingagents.name: reducing agents
reducingagents.definition: Reducing agents is materials that add an [MASK] to an element or compound, that is, decrease the positiveness of its valence. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

perceptualdefense.name: perceptual defense
perceptualdefense.definition: Perceptual defense is selective perceiving such that the individual protects himself from becoming aware of something unpleasant or threatening, e.g., obscene words are not heard correctly, or violent acts are not seen accurately.

alberta.name: alberta
alberta.definition: Alberta is a province of western Canada, lying between the provinces of [MASK] and Saskatchewan. Its capital is Edmonton. It was named in honor of Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, the fourth daughter of Queen Victoria. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p26 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p12)

receptors,androgen.name: receptors , androgen
receptors,androgen.definition: Androgen receptors is proteins, generally found in the cytoplasm, that specifically bind androgens and mediate their cellular actions. The complex of the androgen and receptor migrates to the cell nucleus where it induces transcription of specific segments of dna.

maxillarynerve.name: maxillary nerve
maxillarynerve.definition: Maxillary nerve is the intermediate sensory division of the trigeminal (5th cranial) nerve. The maxillary nerve carries general afferents from the intermediate region of the face including the lower eyelid, nose and upper [MASK], the maxillary teeth, and parts of the dura.

axoninitialsegment.name: axon initial segment
axoninitialsegment.definition: Axon initial segment is first segment of axon that connects distal axon segments to the neuronal cell body at the axon hillock region. The axon initial segment is not protected by the myelin sheath and has properties critical for axonal growth. The axon initial segment and the axon hillock form an axonal trigger zone.

power,psychological.name: power , psychological
power,psychological.definition: Psychological power is the exertion of a strong influence or control over others in a variety of settings--administrative, social, academic, etc.

bloodgroupantigens.name: blood group antigens
bloodgroupantigens.definition: Blood group antigens is sets of cell surface antigens located on blood cells. They are usually membrane glycoproteins or glycolipids that are antigenically distinguished by their carbohydrate moieties.

sentinellymphnodebiopsy.name: sentinel lymph node biopsy
sentinellymphnodebiopsy.definition: Sentinel [MASK] node biopsy is a diagnostic procedure used to determine whether [MASK] has occurred. The sentinel [MASK] node is the first [MASK] node to receive drainage from a neoplasm.

asia,northern.name: asia , northern
asia,northern.definition: Northern asia is a subregion of Asia, consisting of the Asian portion of Russia.

clonecells.name: clone cells
clonecells.definition: Clone cells is a group of genetically identical cells all descended from a single common ancestral cell by [MASK] in eukaryotes or by binary fission in prokaryotes. Clone cells also include populations of [MASK] molecules all carrying the same inserted sequence. (From King & Stansfield, Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

pediatricobesity.name: pediatric obesity
pediatricobesity.definition: Pediatric obesity is body mass index in children (ages 2-12) and in adolescents (ages 13-18) that is grossly above the recommended cut-off for a specific age and [MASK]. For infants less than 2 years of age, obesity is determined based on standard weight-for-length percentile measures.

medicallyunexplainedsymptoms.name: medically unexplained symptoms
medicallyunexplainedsymptoms.definition: Medically unexplained symptoms is persistent health symptoms which remain unexplained after a complete medical evaluation. a cluster of symptoms that consistently appear together but without a known cause are referred to as a medically unexplained syndrome (mus).

pigments,biological.name: pigments , biological
pigments,biological.definition: Biological pigments is any normal or abnormal coloring matter in plants; animals or micro-organisms.

peptidemapping.name: peptide mapping
peptidemapping.definition: Peptide mapping is analysis of peptides that are generated from the [MASK] or fragmentation of a protein or mixture of proteins, by electrophoresis; chromatography; or mass spectrometry. The resulting peptide fingerprints are analyzed for a variety of purposes including the identification of the proteins in a sample, genetic polymorphisms, patterns of gene expression, and patterns diagnostic for diseases.

models,nursing.name: models , nursing
models,nursing.definition: Nursing models is theoretical models simulating behavior or activities in nursing, including nursing care, management and economics, theory, assessment, research, and education. Some examples of these models include Orem Self-Care Model, Roy Adaptation Model, and Rogers Life Process Model.

adaptorproteincomplexsubunits.name: adaptor protein complex subunits
adaptorproteincomplexsubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex subunits is the subunits that make up the large, medium and small chains of adaptor proteins.

hypertension,renal.name: hypertension , renal
hypertension,renal.definition: Renal hypertension is persistent high blood pressure due to kidney diseases, such as those involving the renal parenchyma, the renal vasculature, or tumors that secrete renin.

crosscirculation.name: cross circulation
crosscirculation.definition: Cross circulation is the circulation in a portion of the body of one individual of blood supplied from another individual.

kidneytransplantation.name: kidney transplantation
kidneytransplantation.definition: Kidney transplantation is the transference of a kidney from one human or animal to another.

cobalt.name: cobalt
cobalt.definition: Cobalt is a trace element that is a component of vitamin b12. It has the atomic symbol Co, atomic number 27, and atomic weight 58.93. It is used in nuclear weapons, alloys, and pigments. Deficiency in animals leads to anemia; its excess in humans can lead to erythrocytosis.

independentpracticeassociations.name: independent practice associations
independentpracticeassociations.definition: Independent practice associations is a partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity that enters into an arrangement for the provision of services with persons who are licensed to practice medicine, osteopathy, and dentistry, and with other care personnel. Under an ipa arrangement, licensed professional persons provide services through the entity in accordance with a mutually accepted compensation arrangement, while retaining their private practices. Services under the ipa are marketed through a prepaid health plan. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

leukocytecommonantigens.name: leukocyte common antigens
leukocytecommonantigens.definition: Leukocyte common antigens is high-molecular weight glycoproteins uniquely expressed on the surface of leukocytes and their hemopoietic progenitors. They contain two [MASK] and possess cytoplasmic protein tyrosine phosphatase activity, which plays a role in intracellular signaling from the cell surface receptors. Leukocyte common antigens occur as multiple isoforms that result from alternative mRNA splicing and differential usage of three exons.

urbanhealth.name: urban health
urbanhealth.definition: Urban health is the status of health in urban populations.

suggestion.name: suggestion
suggestion.definition: Suggestion is the uncritical acceptance of an idea or plan of action.

choicebehavior.name: choice behavior
choicebehavior.definition: Choice behavior is the act of making a selection among two or more alternatives, usually after a period of deliberation.

clonaldeletion.name: clonal deletion
clonaldeletion.definition: Clonal deletion is removal, via cell death, of immature lymphocytes that interact with antigens during maturation. For T-lymphocytes this occurs in the thymus and ensures that mature T-lymphocytes are self tolerant. B-lymphocytes may also undergo clonal deletion.

centralnervoussystemdiseases.name: central nervous system diseases
centralnervoussystemdiseases.definition: Central nervous system diseases is diseases of any component of the brain (including the cerebral hemispheres, diencephalon, brain stem, and cerebellum) or the spinal cord.

readingframes.name: reading frames
readingframes.definition: Reading frames is the three possible sequences of codons by which genetic translation may occur from one nucleotide sequence. a segment of mRNA 5'auccga3' could be translated as 5'auc.. or 5'ucc.. or 5'ccg.., depending on the location of the start codon.

personalprotectiveequipment.name: personal protective equipment
personalprotectiveequipment.definition: Personal protective equipment is specialized clothing or equipment worn for protection against health hazards. Personal Protective Equipment may include masks; respiratory [MASK] protective devices; eye protective devices; ear protective devices; protective clothing; and protective footwear.

circulatoryandrespiratoryphysiologicalph.name: circulatory and respiratory physiological phenomena
circulatoryandrespiratoryphysiologicalph.definition: Circulatory and respiratory physiological phenomena is functional processes and properties characteristic of the blood; cardiovascular system; and respiratory system.

periodontalatrophy.name: periodontal atrophy
periodontalatrophy.definition: Periodontal atrophy is degradation or wasting of the periodontium tissues that may involve the gum (gingiva), the alveolar bone (alveolar process), the dental cementum, or the periodontal ligament.

cellline.name: cell line
cellline.definition: Cell line is established cell cultures that have the potential to propagate indefinitely.

diabeticfoot.name: diabetic foot
diabeticfoot.definition: Diabetic [MASK] is common [MASK] problems in persons with diabetes mellitus, caused by any combination of factors such as diabetic neuropathies; peripheral vascular diseases; and infection. With the loss of sensation and poor circulation, injuries and infections often lead to severe [MASK] ulceration, gangrene and [MASK].

renalreplacementtherapy.name: renal replacement therapy
renalreplacementtherapy.definition: Renal replacement therapy is procedures which temporarily or permanently remedy insufficient cleansing of body fluids by the kidneys.

temporalmuscle.name: temporal muscle
temporalmuscle.definition: Temporal muscle is a masticatory muscle whose action is closing the jaws; its posterior portion retracts the mandible.

accountbook.name: account book
accountbook.definition: Account book is book in which personal or commercial accounts of financial transactions are recorded. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

virusrelease.name: virus release
virusrelease.definition: Virus release is release of a virus from the host cell following virus assembly and maturation. Egress can occur by host cell lysis, exocytosis, or budding through the plasma membrane.

dentalaudit.name: dental audit
dentalaudit.definition: Dental audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel for evaluating quality of dental care.

neuromusculardiseases.name: neuromuscular diseases
neuromusculardiseases.definition: Neuromuscular diseases is a general term encompassing lower motor neuron disease; peripheral nervous system diseases; and certain muscular diseases. Manifestations include muscle weakness; fasciculation; muscle atrophy; spasm; myokymia; muscle hypertonia, myalgias, and muscle hypotonia.

nasalabsorption.name: nasal absorption
nasalabsorption.definition: Nasal absorption is uptake of substances through the nasal mucosa.

ethnicgroups.name: ethnic groups
ethnicgroups.definition: Ethnic groups is a group of people with a common cultural heritage that sets them apart from others in a variety of social relationships.

dopplereffect.name: doppler effect
dopplereffect.definition: Doppler effect is changes in the observed frequency of waves (as sound, light, or radio waves) due to the relative motion of source and observer. The effect was named for the 19th century Austrian physicist Johann Christian Doppler.

percutaneouscoronaryintervention.name: percutaneous coronary intervention
percutaneouscoronaryintervention.definition: Percutaneous coronary intervention is a family of percutaneous techniques that are used to manage coronary occlusion, including standard balloon angioplasty ([MASK]), the placement of intracoronary stents, and atheroablative technologies (e.g., atherectomy; endarterectomy; thrombectomy; percutaneous transluminal laser angioplasty). ptca was the dominant form of pci, before the widespread use of stenting.

prionproteins.name: prion proteins
prionproteins.definition: Prion proteins is membrane glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored glycoproteins that may aggregate into rod-like structures. The prion protein (prnp) gene is characterized by five tandem repeat sequences that encode a highly unstable protein region of five octapeptide repeats. Mutations in the repeat region and elsewhere in this gene are associated with creutzfeldt-jakob disease; fatal familial insomnia; gerstmann-straussler disease; Huntington disease-like 1, and kuru.

continuousrenalreplacementtherapy.name: continuous renal replacement therapy
continuousrenalreplacementtherapy.definition: Continuous renal replacement therapy is procedures with continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration or perfusion) via vascular access designed to mimic kidney function in kidney diseases (e.g., acute renal failure and poisoning).

referencevalues.name: reference values
