referencevalues.definition: Reference values is the range or frequency distribution of a measurement in a population (of organisms, organs or things) that has not been selected for the presence of disease or abnormality.

hepatitisaviruscellularreceptor1.name: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 1
hepatitisaviruscellularreceptor1.definition: Hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 1 is an Ig domain-containing membrane receptor for hepatitis a virus; ebola virus; marburg virus; and dengue virus. It may also function to modulate asthma and hypersensitivity.

students,medical.name: students , medical
students,medical.definition: Medical students is individuals enrolled in a school of medicine or a formal educational program in medicine.

impdehydrogenase.name: imp dehydrogenase
impdehydrogenase.definition: Imp dehydrogenase is an enzyme that catalyzes the dehydrogenation of inosine 5'-phosphate to xanthosine 5'-phosphate in the presence of nad. ec 1.1.1.205.

receptor,parathyroidhormone,type2.name: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 2
receptor,parathyroidhormone,type2.definition: Type 2 parathyroid hormone receptor is a parathyroid hormone receptor subtype found in the brain and the pancreas. It is a G-protein-coupled receptor with a ligand specificity that varies between homologs from different species.

malaria,avian.name: malaria , avian
malaria,avian.definition: Avian malaria is any of a group of infections of fowl caused by protozoa of the genera plasmodium, Leucocytozoon, and Haemoproteus. The [MASK] of these parasites and the disease produced bears strong resemblance to those observed in human malaria.

cervicalribsyndrome.name: cervical rib syndrome
cervicalribsyndrome.definition: Cervical rib syndrome is a condition associated with compression of the brachial plexus; subclavian artery; and subclavian vein at the thoracic outlet and caused by a complete or incomplete anomalous cervical rib or fascial band connecting the tip of a cervical rib with the first thoracic rib. Clinical manifestations may include pain in the [MASK] and [MASK] which radiates into the upper extremity, paresis or paralysis of brachial plexus innervated muscles; sensory loss; paresthesias; ischemia; and edema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p214)

renalplasmaflow.name: renal plasma flow
renalplasmaflow.definition: Renal plasma flow is the amount of plasma that perfuses the kidneys per unit time, approximately 10% greater than effective renal plasma flow (renal plasma flow, effective). It should be differentiated from the renal blood flow; (rbf), which refers to the total volume of blood flowing through the renal vasculature, while the renal plasma flow refers to the rate of plasma flow (rpf).

atrialprematurecomplexes.name: atrial premature complexes
atrialprematurecomplexes.definition: Atrial premature complexes is a type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites. The ectopic signals may or may not conduct to the heart ventricles. Atrial premature complexes are characterized by premature p waves on ecg which are different in configuration from the p waves generated by the normal pacemaker complex in the sinoatrial node.

pancreaticducts.name: pancreatic ducts
pancreaticducts.definition: Pancreatic ducts is ducts that collect pancreatic juice from the pancreas and supply it to the duodenum.

rome.name: rome
rome.definition: Rome is the capital city of Italy.

mitochondria,heart.name: mitochondria , heart
mitochondria,heart.definition: Heart mitochondria is the mitochondria of the myocardium.

cranialirradiation.name: cranial irradiation
cranialirradiation.definition: Cranial irradiation is the exposure of the head to roentgen rays or other forms of radioactivity for therapeutic or preventive purposes.

muscle,smooth.name: muscle , smooth
muscle,smooth.definition: Smooth muscle is unstriated and unstriped muscle, one of the muscles of the internal organs, blood vessels, hair follicles, etc. Contractile elements are elongated, usually spindle-shaped cells with centrally located nuclei. Smooth muscle fibers are bound together into sheets or bundles by reticular fibers and frequently elastic nets are also abundant. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

maximalrespiratorypressures.name: maximal respiratory pressures
maximalrespiratorypressures.definition: Maximal respiratory pressures is a respiratory function test that includes the maximal inspiratory pressure and maximal expiratory pressure. It is determined by spirometry that measures the patient's residual volume and total lung capacity and assesses the strength of respiratory muscles.

bovinerespiratorydiseasecomplex.name: bovine respiratory disease complex
bovinerespiratorydiseasecomplex.definition: Bovine respiratory disease complex is a multifactorial disease of cattle resulting from complex interactions between environmental factors, host factors, and pathogens. The environmental factors act as stressors adversely affecting the immune system and other host defenses and enhancing transmission of infecting agents.

dentalrestorationrepair.name: dental restoration repair
dentalrestorationrepair.definition: Dental restoration repair is the process of repairing broken or worn parts of a permanent dental restoration.

adultsurvivorsofchildadverseevents.name: adult survivors of child adverse events
adultsurvivorsofchildadverseevents.definition: Adult survivors of child adverse events is persons who experienced traumatic events during childhood.

hospitals,special.name: hospitals , special
hospitals,special.definition: Special hospitals is hospitals which provide care for a single category of illness with facilities and staff directed toward a specific service.

integrins.name: integrins
integrins.definition: Integrins is a family of transmembrane glycoproteins (membrane glycoproteins) consisting of noncovalent heterodimers. They interact with a wide variety of ligands including extracellular matrix proteins; complement, and other cells, while their intracellular domains interact with the cytoskeleton. The integrins consist of at least three identified families: the cytoadhesin receptors(RECEPTORS, cytoadhesin), the leukocyte adhesion receptors (receptors, leukocyte adhesion), and the [MASK]. Each family contains a common beta-subunit (integrin beta chains) combined with one or more distinct alpha-subunits (integrin alpha chains). These receptors participate in cell-matrix and cell-cell adhesion in many physiologically important processes, including embryological development; hemostasis; thrombosis; wound healing; immune and nonimmune defense mechanisms; and oncogenic transformation.

hearingloss,unilateral.name: hearing loss , unilateral
hearingloss,unilateral.definition: Unilateral hearing loss is partial or complete hearing loss in one ear.

genes,erbb.name: genes , erbb
genes,erbb.definition: Erbb genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (erbB) originally isolated from, or related to, the avian erythroblastosis virus (aev). These genes code for the [MASK] (egfr) family of receptors which is important in the control of normal cell proliferation and in the pathogenesis of human cancer. The genes include erbB-1 (genes, erbb-1), erbB-2 (genes, erbb-2), and erbB-3, all of which show abnormalities of expression in various human neoplasms.

bookindustry.name: book industry
bookindustry.definition: Book industry is the aggregate enterprise of manufacturing and technically producing books. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

needlesharing.name: needle sharing
needlesharing.definition: Needle sharing is usage of a single needle among two or more people for injecting drugs. Needle sharing is a high-risk behavior for contracting infectious disease.

nutritionalsciences.name: nutritional sciences
nutritionalsciences.definition: Nutritional sciences is the study of nutrition processes as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease.

dna,antisense.name: dna , antisense
dna,antisense.definition: Antisense dna is dna that is complementary to the sense strand. (The sense strand has the same sequence as the mRNA transcript. The antisense strand is the template for mRNA synthesis.) Synthetic antisense DNAs are used to hybridize to complementary sequences in target RNAs or DNAs to effect the functioning of specific genes for investigative or therapeutic purposes.

ultraviolettherapy.name: ultraviolet therapy
ultraviolettherapy.definition: Ultraviolet therapy is the use of ultraviolet electromagnetic radiation in the treatment of disease, usually of the skin. This is the part of the sun's spectrum that causes sunburn and tanning. Ultraviolet a, used in puva, is closer to visible light and less damaging than Ultraviolet b, which is ionizing.

sheep,domestic.name: sheep , domestic
sheep,domestic.definition: Domestic sheep is a species of sheep, Ovis aries, descended from Near Eastern wild forms, especially mouflon.

toothresorption.name: tooth resorption
toothresorption.definition: Tooth resorption is resorption of calcified dental tissue, involving demineralization due to reversal of the cation exchange and lacunar resorption by osteoclasts. There are two types: external (as a result of tooth pathology) and internal (apparently initiated by a peculiar inflammatory hyperplasia of the pulp). (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p676)

hypothermia,induced.name: hypothermia , induced
hypothermia,induced.definition: Induced hypothermia is abnormally low body temperature that is intentionally induced in warm-blooded animals by artificial means. In humans, mild or moderate hypothermia has been used to reduce tissue damages, particularly after cardiac or spinal cord injuries and during subsequent surgeries.

coloringagents.name: coloring agents
coloringagents.definition: Coloring agents is chemicals and substances that impart [MASK] including soluble dyes and insoluble pigments. They are used in inks; paints; and as indicators and reagents.

physicians,primarycare.name: physicians , primary care
physicians,primarycare.definition: Primary care physicians is providers of initial care for patients. These physicians refer patients when appropriate for secondary or specialist care.

vasculardiseases.name: vascular diseases
vasculardiseases.definition: Vascular diseases is pathological processes involving any of the blood vessels in the cardiac or peripheral circulation. They include diseases of arteries; veins; and rest of the vasculature system in the body.

harmfulalgalbloom.name: harmful algal bloom
harmfulalgalbloom.definition: Harmful algal bloom is an algal bloom where the algae produce powerful toxins that can kill fish, birds, and mammals, and ultimately cause illness in humans. The harmful bloom can also cause oxygen depletion in the water due to the death and decomposition of non-toxic algae species.

drive.name: drive
drive.definition: Drive is a state of internal activity of an organism that is a necessary condition before a given stimulus will elicit a class of responses; e.g., a certain level of hunger (drive) must be present before food will elicit an eating response.

bloodtransfusion.name: blood transfusion
bloodtransfusion.definition: Blood transfusion is the introduction of whole blood or blood component directly into the blood [MASK]. (Dorland, 27th ed)

bookcollecting.name: book collecting
bookcollecting.definition: Book collecting is seeking, locating, acquiring, organizing, cataloging, displaying, storing, and maintaining whatever books are of interest to a given individual collector.

schoolmentalhealthservices.name: school mental health services
schoolmentalhealthservices.definition: School mental health services is services which focus on the mental well-being of pre-college and pre-university students that include counseling and therapy.

cellphone.name: cell phone
cellphone.definition: Cell phone is analog or digital communications device in which the user has a wireless connection from a telephone to a nearby transmitter. It is termed cellular because the service area is divided into multiple "cells." As the user moves from one cell area to another, the call is transferred to the local transmitter.

oxidativestress.name: oxidative stress
oxidativestress.definition: Oxidative stress is a disturbance in the prooxidant-antioxidant balance in favor of the former, leading to potential damage. Indicators of oxidative stress include damaged dna bases, protein oxidation products, and [MASK] products (Sies, Oxidative Stress, 1991, pxv-xvi).

capitalexpenditures.name: capital expenditures
capitalexpenditures.definition: Capital expenditures is those funds disbursed for facilities and equipment, particularly those related to the delivery of health care.

cardiacoutput.name: cardiac output
cardiacoutput.definition: Cardiac output is the volume of blood passing through the heart per unit of time. It is usually expressed as liters (volume) per minute so as not to be confused with [MASK] (volume per beat).

digitaldermatitis.name: digital dermatitis
digitaldermatitis.definition: Digital dermatitis is highly contagious infectious dermatitis with lesions near the interdigital spaces usually in cattle. It causes discomfort and often severe lameness (lameness, animal). Lesions can be either erosive or proliferative and wart-like with papillary growths and hypertrophied hairs. dichelobacter nodosus and treponema are the most commonly associated causative agents for this mixed bacterial infection disease.

quaternaryammoniumcompounds.name: quaternary ammonium compounds
quaternaryammoniumcompounds.definition: Quaternary ammonium compounds is derivatives of ammonium compounds, nh4+ y-, in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with hydrocarbyl groups. These are distinguished from imines which are rn=cr2.

tincompounds.name: tin compounds
tincompounds.definition: Tin compounds is inorganic compounds that contain tin as an integral part of the molecule.

diabetesmellitus,type2.name: diabetes mellitus , type 2
diabetesmellitus,type2.definition: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a subclass of diabetes mellitus that is not INSULIN-responsive or dependent (niddm). It is characterized initially by insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia; and eventually by glucose intolerance; hyperglycemia; and overt diabetes. Type ii diabetes mellitus is no longer considered a disease exclusively found in adults. Patients seldom develop ketosis but often exhibit obesity.

rehabilitation.name: rehabilitation
rehabilitation.definition: Rehabilitation is restoration of human functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from disease or injury.

proteinstructure,secondary.name: protein structure , secondary
proteinstructure,secondary.definition: Secondary protein structure is the level of protein structure in which regular hydrogen-bond interactions within contiguous stretches of polypeptide chain give rise to alpha-helices; beta-strands (which align to form beta-sheets), or other types of coils. This is the first folding level of protein conformation.

glucagon.name: glucagon
glucagon.definition: Glucagon is a 29-amino acid pancreatic peptide derived from proglucagon which is also the precursor of intestinal glucagon-like peptides. Glucagon is secreted by pancreatic alpha cells and plays an important role in regulation of blood glucose concentration, ketone metabolism, and several other biochemical and physiological processes. (From Gilman et al., Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 9th ed, p1511)

chromatography,gas.name: chromatography , gas
chromatography,gas.definition: Gas chromatography is fractionation of a vaporized sample as a consequence of partition between a mobile gaseous phase and a stationary phase held in a column. Two types are gas-solid chromatography, where the fixed phase is a solid, and gas-liquid, in which the stationary phase is a nonvolatile liquid supported on an inert solid matrix.

arterialswitchoperation.name: arterial switch operation
arterialswitchoperation.definition: Arterial switch operation is surgical procedure for anatomical correction of transposed great arteries (e.g., double outlet right ventricle).

lowtensionglaucoma.name: low tension glaucoma
lowtensionglaucoma.definition: Low tension glaucoma is a form of glaucoma in which chronic optic nerve damage and loss of vision normally attributable to buildup of intraocular pressure occurs despite prevailing conditions of normal intraocular pressure.

gastricfistula.name: gastric fistula
gastricfistula.definition: Gastric fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the stomach.

jawabnormalities.name: jaw abnormalities
jawabnormalities.definition: Jaw abnormalities is congenital absence of or defects in structures of the jaw.

dyedilutiontechnique.name: dye dilution technique
dyedilutiontechnique.definition: Dye dilution technique is method for assessing flow through a system by injection of a known quantity of dye into the system and monitoring its concentration over time at a specific point in the system. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

kidneyneoplasms.name: kidney neoplasms
kidneyneoplasms.definition: Kidney neoplasms is tumors or cancers of the kidney.

africa,western.name: africa , western
africa,western.definition: Western africa is the geographical area of Africa comprising benin; burkina faso; capo verde, cote d'ivoire; gambia; ghana; [MASK]; [MASK]-bissau; liberia; mali; mauritania; [MASK]; nigeria; senegal; sierra leone; and togo.

lignin.name: lignin
lignin.definition: Lignin is the most abundant natural aromatic organic polymer found in all vascular plants. Lignin together with cellulose and hemicellulose are the major cell wall components of the fibers of all [MASK] and grass species. Lignin is composed of coniferyl, p-coumaryl, and sinapyl alcohols in varying ratios in different plant species. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

uricacid.name: uric acid
uricacid.definition: Uric acid is an oxidation product, via xanthine oxidase, of oxypurines such as xanthine and hypoxanthine. It is the final oxidation product of purine catabolism in humans and primates, whereas in most other mammals urate oxidase further oxidizes it to allantoin.

bodysurfacepotentialmapping.name: body surface potential mapping
bodysurfacepotentialmapping.definition: Body surface potential mapping is recording of regional electrophysiological information by analysis of surface potentials to give a complete picture of the effects of the currents from the heart on the body surface. It has been applied to the diagnosis of old [MASK], localization of the bypass pathway in Wolff-Parkinson-[MASK] syndrome, recognition of ventricular hypertrophy, estimation of the size of a myocardial infarct, and the effects of different interventions designed to reduce infarct size. The limiting factor at present is the complexity of the recording and analysis, which requires 100 or more electrodes, sophisticated instrumentation, and dedicated personnel. (Braunwald, Heart Disease, 4th ed)

stressdisorders,traumatic.name: stress disorders , traumatic
stressdisorders,traumatic.definition: Traumatic stress disorders is anxiety disorders manifested by the development of characteristic symptoms following a psychologically traumatic event that is outside the normal range of usual human experience. Symptoms include re-experiencing the traumatic event, increased arousal, and numbing of responsiveness to or reduced involvement with the external world. Traumatic stress disorders can be further classified by the time of onset and the duration of these symptoms.

gbvirusa.name: gb virus a
gbvirusa.definition: Gb virus a is a species of virus in the family flaviviridae, that have been identified in at least six species of New World monkeys. They do not cause hepatitis in the host or other susceptible species.

monocytes.name: monocytes
monocytes.definition: Monocytes is large, phagocytic mononuclear leukocytes produced in the vertebrate bone marrow and released into the blood; contain a large, oval or somewhat indented nucleus surrounded by voluminous cytoplasm and numerous organelles.

anesthesia,general.name: anesthesia , general
anesthesia,general.definition: General anesthesia is procedure in which patients are induced into an [MASK] state through use of various medications so that they do not feel pain during surgery.

clinicalenzymetests.name: clinical enzyme tests
clinicalenzymetests.definition: Clinical enzyme tests is analyses for a specific enzyme activity, or of the level of a specific enzyme that is used to assess health and disease risk, for early detection of disease or disease prediction, diagnosis, and change in disease status.

righttodie.name: right to die
righttodie.definition: Right to die is the right of the patient or the patient's representative to make decisions with regard to the patient's dying.

socialmarketing.name: social marketing
socialmarketing.definition: Social marketing is use of marketing principles also used to sell products to consumers to promote ideas, attitudes and behaviors. Design and use of programs seeking to increase the acceptance of a social idea or practice by target groups, not for the benefit of the marketer, but to benefit the target audience and the general society.

bacterialvaccines.name: bacterial vaccines
bacterialvaccines.definition: Bacterial vaccines is suspensions of attenuated or killed bacteria administered for the prevention or treatment of infectious bacterial disease.

advancedirectiveadherence.name: advance directive adherence
advancedirectiveadherence.definition: Advance directive adherence is compliance by health personnel or proxies with the stipulations of advance directives (or similar directives such as resuscitation orders) when patients are unable to direct their own care.

tuberculosisvaccines.name: tuberculosis vaccines
tuberculosisvaccines.definition: Tuberculosis vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat tuberculosis.

ethicscommittees,clinical.name: ethics committees , clinical
ethicscommittees,clinical.definition: Clinical ethics committees is hospital or other [MASK] committees established to consider the ethical dimensions of patient care. Distinguish from ethics committees, research, which are established to monitor the welfare of patients or [MASK] participating in research studies.

spatialprocessing.name: spatial processing
spatialprocessing.definition: Spatial processing is integration of spatial information perceived by visual and/or auditory cues.

teatreeoil.name: tea tree oil
teatreeoil.definition: Tea tree oil is essential oil extracted from melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree). It is used as a topical antimicrobial due to the presence of terpineol.

nitrogen.name: nitrogen
nitrogen.definition: Nitrogen is an element with the atomic symbol n, atomic number 7, and atomic weight [14.00643; 14.00728]. Nitrogen exists as a diatomic gas and makes up about 78% of the earth's atmosphere by volume. It is a constituent of proteins and nucleic acids and found in all living cells.

transforminggrowthfactorbeta.name: transforming growth factor beta
transforminggrowthfactorbeta.definition: Transforming growth factor beta is a factor synthesized in a wide variety of tissues. It acts synergistically with TGF-alpha in inducing phenotypic transformation and can also act as a negative autocrine growth factor. TGF-beta has a potential role in embryonal development, cellular differentiation, hormone secretion, and immune function. TGF-beta is found mostly as homodimer forms of separate gene products TGF-beta1, TGF-beta2 or TGF-beta3. Heterodimers composed of TGF-beta1 and 2 (TGF-beta1.2) or of TGF-beta2 and 3 (TGF-beta2.3) have been isolated. The TGF-beta proteins are synthesized as precursor proteins.

kneedislocation.name: knee dislocation
kneedislocation.definition: [MASK] dislocation is slippage of the femur off the tibia.

healthrecords,personal.name: health records , personal
healthrecords,personal.definition: Personal health records is longitudinal patient-maintained records of individual health history and tools that allow individual control of access.

education,medical,continuing.name: education , medical , continuing
education,medical,continuing.definition: Continuing medical education is educational programs designed to inform physicians of recent advances in their field.

antibiotic.name: antibiotic
antibiotic.definition: Antibiotic is substances that inhibit the growth or reproduction of bacteria.

models,structural.name: models , structural
models,structural.definition: Structural models is a representation, generally small in scale, to show the structure, construction, or appearance of something. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

diet,food,andnutrition.name: diet , food , and nutrition
diet,food,andnutrition.definition: And nutrition food diet is concepts involved with nutritional physiology, including categories of substances eaten for sustenance, nutritional phenomena and processes, eating patterns and habits, and measurable nutritional parameters.

rna,algal.name: rna , algal
rna,algal.definition: Algal rna is ribonucleic acid in algae having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

receptors,peptide.name: receptors , peptide
receptors,peptide.definition: Peptide receptors is cell surface receptors that bind peptide messengers with high affinity and regulate intracellular signals which influence the behavior of cells.

pyruvatesynthase.name: pyruvate synthase
pyruvatesynthase.definition: Pyruvate synthase is a ferredoxin-containing enzyme that catalyzes the coenzyme A-dependent oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl-COENZYME a and carbon dioxide.

radiation.name: radiation
radiation.definition: Radiation is emission or propagation of acoustic waves (sound), electromagnetic energy waves (such as light; radio waves; gamma rays; or x-rays), or a [MASK] of subatomic particles (such as [MASK]; neutrons; protons; or [MASK]).

glycogenstoragediseasetypeii.name: glycogen storage disease type ii
glycogenstoragediseasetypeii.definition: Glycogen storage disease type ii is an autosomal recessively inherited glycogen storage disease caused by glucan 1,4-alpha-glucosidase deficiency. Large amounts of glycogen accumulate in the lysosomes of skeletal muscle (muscle, skeletal); heart; liver; spinal cord; and brain. Three forms have been described: infantile, childhood, and adult. The infantile form is fatal in infancy and presents with hypotonia and a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic). The childhood form usually presents in the second year of life with proximal weakness and respiratory symptoms. The adult form consists of a slowly progressive proximal myopathy. (From Muscle Nerve 1995;3:s61-9; Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp73-4)

adrenalglandneoplasms.name: adrenal gland neoplasms
adrenalglandneoplasms.definition: Adrenal gland neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the adrenal glands.

leukocyteadherenceinhibitiontest.name: leukocyte adherence inhibition test
leukocyteadherenceinhibitiontest.definition: Leukocyte adherence inhibition test is test for cell-mediated antitumor immunity and related serum blocking factors based on the finding that leukocytes from cancer patients, but not from controls, when mixed in vitro with antigenic extracts of tumors of the same histological type, undergo a diminution in their normal adherence to glass surfaces. Sera from tumor-bearing patients block the lai reaction of their own leukocytes or those of other patients with the same type of tumor.

parentalleave.name: parental leave
parentalleave.definition: Parental leave is the authorized absence from work of either parent prior to and after the birth of their child. It includes also absence because of the illness of a child or at the time of the adoption of a child. It does not include leave for care of siblings, parents, or other family members: for this family leave is available.

mothers.name: mothers
mothers.definition: Mothers is female parents, human or animal.

plantshoots.name: plant shoots
plantshoots.definition: Plant shoots is new immature growth of a plant including stem, leaves, tips of branches, and seedlings.

germany.name: germany
germany.definition: Germany is a country in central Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea and the [MASK], between the [MASK] and Poland, south of Denmark. The capital is Berlin.

deadboxprotein20.name: dead box protein 20
deadboxprotein20.definition: Dead box protein 20 is a multifunctional protein that is both a DEAD-box rna helicase and a component of the smn protein complex.

culturemedia.name: culture media
culturemedia.definition: Culture media is any liquid or solid preparation made specifically for the growth, storage, or transport of microorganisms or other types of cells. The variety of media that exist allow for the culturing of specific microorganisms and cell types, such as differential media, selective media, test media, and defined media. Solid media consist of liquid media that have been solidified with an agent such as agar or gelatin.

mesenchymalstemcells.name: mesenchymal stem cells
mesenchymalstemcells.definition: Mesenchymal stem cells is mesenchymal stem cells, also referred to as multipotent stromal cells or mesenchymal stromal cells are multipotent, non-hematopoietic adult stem cells that are present in multiple tissues, including bone marrow; adipose tissue; and wharton jelly. Mesenchymal stem cells can differentiate into mesodermal lineages, such as adipocytic, osteocytic and chondrocytic.

perinataldeath.name: perinatal death
perinataldeath.definition: Perinatal death is the death of a fetus of gestational age 28 weeks or more, or the death of a live-born infant less than 28 days of age.

infectiousdiseasetransmission,vertical.name: infectious disease transmission , vertical
infectiousdiseasetransmission,vertical.definition: Vertical infectious disease transmission is the transmission of infectious disease or pathogens from one generation to another. It includes transmission in utero or intrapartum by exposure to blood and secretions, and postpartum exposure via breastfeeding.

skindiseases,viral.name: skin diseases , viral
skindiseases,viral.definition: Viral skin diseases is skin diseases caused by viruses.

receptors,dopamine.name: receptors , dopamine
receptors,dopamine.definition: Dopamine receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind dopamine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

contractileproteins.name: contractile proteins
contractileproteins.definition: Contractile proteins is proteins which participate in contractile processes. They include muscle proteins as well as those found in other cells and tissues. In the latter, these proteins participate in localized contractile events in the cytoplasm, in motile activity, and in cell aggregation phenomena.

equipmentreuse.name: equipment reuse
equipmentreuse.definition: Equipment reuse is further or repeated use of equipment, instruments, devices, or materials. It includes additional use regardless of the original intent of the producer as to disposability or durability. It does not include the repeated use of fluids or solutions.

shapememoryalloys.name: shape memory alloys
shapememoryalloys.definition: Shape memory alloys is alloys designed to recover their original shape upon [MASK].

ionchannelgating.name: ion channel gating
ionchannelgating.definition: Ion channel gating is the opening and closing of ion channels due to a stimulus. The stimulus can be a change in membrane potential (voltage-gated), drugs or chemical transmitters (ligand-gated), or a mechanical deformation. Gating is thought to involve conformational changes of the ion channel which alters selective permeability.

accidentalfalls.name: accidental falls
accidentalfalls.definition: Accidental falls is falls due to slipping or tripping which may result in injury.

macrophages.name: macrophages
macrophages.definition: Macrophages is the relatively long-lived phagocytic cell of mammalian tissues that are derived from blood monocytes. Main types are [MASK]; alveolar macrophages; histiocytes; kupffer cells of the liver; and osteoclasts. They may further differentiate within chronic inflammatory lesions to epithelioid cells or may fuse to form foreign body giant cells or langhans giant cells. (from The Dictionary of Cell Biology, Lackie and Dow, 3rd ed.)

clinicalgovernance.name: clinical governance
clinicalgovernance.definition: Clinical governance is a framework through which the United Kingdom's National Health Service organizations are accountable for continually improving the quality of their services and safeguarding high standards of care by creating an environment in which excellence in clinical care will flourish. (Scally and Donaldson, bmj (4 July 1998): 61-65)

urea.name: urea
urea.definition: Urea is a compound formed in the liver from [MASK] produced by the deamination of amino acids. It is the principal end product of protein catabolism and constitutes about one half of the total urinary solids.

consumerorganizations.name: consumer organizations
consumerorganizations.definition: Consumer organizations is organized groups of users of goods and services.

checkpointkinase2.name: checkpoint kinase 2
checkpointkinase2.definition: Checkpoint kinase 2 is enzyme activated in response to dna damage involved in cell cycle arrest. The gene is located on the long (q) [MASK] of chromosome 22 at position 12.1. In humans it is encoded by the chek2 gene.

eyeinfections,fungal.name: eye infections , fungal
eyeinfections,fungal.definition: Fungal eye infections is infection by a variety of fungi, usually through four possible mechanisms: superficial infection producing conjunctivitis, keratitis, or lacrimal obstruction; extension of infection from neighboring structures - skin, paranasal sinuses, nasopharynx; direct introduction during surgery or accidental penetrating trauma; or via the blood or lymphatic routes in patients with underlying mycoses.

triplenegativebreastneoplasms.name: triple negative breast neoplasms
triplenegativebreastneoplasms.definition: Triple negative breast neoplasms is breast neoplasms that do not express estrogen receptors; progesterone receptors; and do not overexpress the neu receptor/her-2 proto-oncogene protein.

mercury,planet.name: mercury , planet
mercury,planet.definition: Planet mercury is the first planet in order from the sun. It has no known natural satellites. It is one of the four inner or terrestrial planets of the solar system.

vaccines,combined.name: vaccines , combined
vaccines,combined.definition: Combined vaccines is two or more vaccines in a single dosage form.

infantmortality.name: infant mortality
infantmortality.definition: Infant mortality is postnatal deaths from birth to 365 days after birth in a given population. Postneonatal mortality represents deaths between 28 days and 365 days after birth (as defined by National Center for Health Statistics). Neonatal mortality represents deaths from birth to 27 days after birth.

lymphoidprogenitorcells.name: lymphoid progenitor cells
lymphoidprogenitorcells.definition: Lymphoid progenitor cells is stem cells from which b-lymphocytes; t-lymphocytes; natural killer cells; and some [MASK] derive.

finding.name: finding
finding.definition: Finding is a conclusion reached as a result of an inquiry, investigation, or trial.

endothelium,vascular.name: endothelium , vascular
endothelium,vascular.definition: Vascular endothelium is single pavement layer of cells which line the luminal surface of the entire vascular system and regulate the transport of macromolecules and blood components.

hypothalamicneoplasms.name: hypothalamic neoplasms
hypothalamicneoplasms.definition: Hypothalamic neoplasms is benign and malignant tumors of the hypothalamus. Pilocytic astrocytomas and hamartomas are relatively frequent histologic types. Neoplasms of the hypothalamus frequently originate from adjacent structures, including the optic chiasm, optic nerve (see optic nerve neoplasms), and pituitary gland (see pituitary neoplasms). Relatively frequent clinical manifestations include visual loss, developmental delay, macrocephaly, and precocious puberty. (From Devita et al., Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology, 5th ed, p2051)

anatomy,comparative.name: anatomy , comparative
anatomy,comparative.definition: Comparative anatomy is the comparative study of animal structure with regard to homologous organs or parts. (Stedman, 25th ed)

magnesium.name: magnesium
magnesium.definition: Magnesium is a metallic element that has the atomic symbol Mg, atomic number 12, and atomic weight 24.31. It is important for the activity of many enzymes, especially those involved in oxidative phosphorylation.

salmonella.name: salmonella
salmonella.definition: Salmonella is a genus of gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that utilizes citrate as a sole carbon source. It is pathogenic for humans, causing enteric fevers, gastroenteritis, and bacteremia. Food poisoning is the most common clinical manifestation. Organisms within this genus are separated on the basis of antigenic characteristics, sugar fermentation patterns, and bacteriophage susceptibility.

securitymeasures.name: security measures
securitymeasures.definition: Security measures is regulations to assure protection of property and equipment.

injuryseverityscore.name: injury severity score
injuryseverityscore.definition: Injury severity score is an anatomic severity scale based on the Abbreviated Injury Scale (ais) and developed specifically to score multiple traumatic injuries. It has been used as a predictor of mortality.

genetics,microbial.name: genetics , microbial
genetics,microbial.definition: Microbial genetics is a subdiscipline of genetics which deals with the genetic mechanisms and processes of microorganisms.

electricity.name: electricity
electricity.definition: Electricity is the physical effects involving the presence of electric charges at rest and in motion.

factorxiideficiency.name: factor xii deficiency
factorxiideficiency.definition: Factor xii deficiency is an absence or reduced level of blood coagulation factor xii. It normally occurs in the absence of patient or family history of hemorrhagic disorders and is marked by prolonged clotting time.

elastictissue.name: elastic tissue
elastictissue.definition: Elastic tissue is connective tissue comprised chiefly of elastic fibers. Elastic fibers have two components: elastin and microfibrils.

synovialfluid.name: synovial fluid
synovialfluid.definition: Synovial fluid is the clear, viscous fluid secreted by the synovial membrane. It contains mucin, albumin, fat, and mineral [MASK] and serves to lubricate joints.

healthriskbehaviors.name: health risk behaviors
healthriskbehaviors.definition: Health risk behaviors is pattern of behavior which predisposes certain individuals to increased risk for contracting disease or sustaining personal injury. These behaviors may cluster into a risky lifestyle.

childabuse,sexual.name: child abuse , sexual
childabuse,sexual.definition: Sexual child abuse is sexual maltreatment of the child or minor.

socialsupport.name: social support
socialsupport.definition: Social support is support systems that provide assistance and encouragement to individuals with physical or emotional disabilities in order that they may better cope. Informal social support is usually provided by friends, relatives, or peers, while formal assistance is provided by churches, groups, etc.

encephalitis.name: encephalitis
encephalitis.definition: Encephalitis is inflammation of the brain due to infection, autoimmune processes, toxins, and other conditions. Viral infections (see encephalitis, viral) are a relatively frequent cause of this condition.

occupationalgroups.name: occupational groups
occupationalgroups.definition: Occupational groups is members of the various professions (e.g., physicians) or occupations (e.g., [MASK]).

chemicalactionsanduses.name: chemical actions and uses
chemicalactionsanduses.definition: Chemical actions and uses is a group of pharmacologic activities, effects on living systems and the environment, and modes of employment of drugs and chemicals. They are broken into actions, which describe their effects, and uses, which describe how they are employed.

acylcarrierprotein.name: acyl carrier protein
acylcarrierprotein.definition: Acyl carrier protein is consists of a polypeptide chain and 4'-phosphopantetheine linked to a serine residue by a phosphodiester bond. Acyl groups are bound as thiol esters to the pantothenyl group. Acyl carrier protein is involved in every step of fatty acid synthesis by the cytoplasmic system.

rnaprecursors.name: rna precursors
rnaprecursors.definition: Rna precursors is rna transcripts of the dna that are in some unfinished stage of post-transcriptional processing (rna processing, post-transcriptional) required for function. rna precursors may undergo several steps of rna splicing during which the phosphodiester bonds at exon-intron boundaries are cleaved and the introns are excised. Consequently a new bond is formed between the ends of the exons. Resulting mature RNAs can then be used; for example, mature mRNA (rna, messenger) is used as a template for protein production.

gingivalpocket.name: gingival pocket
gingivalpocket.definition: Gingival pocket is an abnormal extension of a gingival sulcus not accompanied by the apical migration of the epithelial attachment.

grainproteins.name: grain proteins
grainproteins.definition: Grain proteins is dietary protein from edible grains.

warfarin.name: warfarin
warfarin.definition: Warfarin is an anticoagulant that acts by inhibiting the synthesis of vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors. Warfarin is indicated for the prophylaxis and/or treatment of venous thrombosis and its extension, pulmonary embolism, and atrial fibrillation with embolization. It is also used as an adjunct in the prophylaxis of systemic embolism after myocardial infarction. Warfarin is also used as a rodenticide.

aging,premature.name: aging , premature
aging,premature.definition: Premature aging is changes in the organism associated with senescence, occurring at an accelerated rate.

centralnervoussystemagents.name: central nervous system agents
centralnervoussystemagents.definition: Central nervous system agents is a class of drugs producing both physiological and psychological effects through a variety of mechanisms. They can be divided into "specific" agents, e.g., affecting an identifiable molecular mechanism unique to target cells bearing receptors for that agent, and "nonspecific" agents, those producing effects on different target cells and acting by diverse molecular mechanisms. Those with nonspecific mechanisms are generally further classed according to whether they produce behavioral depression or stimulation. Those with specific mechanisms are classed by locus of action or specific therapeutic use. (From Gilman ag, et al., Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 8th ed, p252)

absorption,physicochemical.name: absorption , physicochemical
absorption,physicochemical.definition: Physicochemical absorption is the physical process of passing into, or being taken up or taken in by a substance.

centralvenouscatheters.name: central venous catheters
centralvenouscatheters.definition: Central venous catheters is catheters that are inserted into a large central vein such as a subclavian vein or femoral vein.

genome,microbial.name: genome , microbial
genome,microbial.definition: Microbial genome is the genetic complement of a microorganism as represented in its dna or in some microorganisms its rna.

respiratorycareunits.name: respiratory care units
respiratorycareunits.definition: Respiratory care units is the hospital unit in which patients with respiratory conditions requiring special attention receive intensive medical care and surveillance.

liverglycogen.name: liver glycogen
liverglycogen.definition: Liver glycogen is glycogen stored in the liver. (Dorland, 28th ed)

delirium.name: delirium
delirium.definition: Delirium is a disorder characterized by confusion; inattentiveness; disorientation; illusions; hallucinations; agitation; and in some instances autonomic nervous system overactivity. It may result from toxic/metabolic conditions or structural brain lesions. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp411-2)

corebindingfactorbetasubunit.name: core binding factor beta subunit
corebindingfactorbetasubunit.definition: Core binding factor beta subunit is a non-DNA binding transcription factor that is a subunit of core binding factor. It forms heterodimeric complexes with core binding factor alpha subunits, and regulates genetic transcription of a variety of genes involved primarily in cell differentiation and cell cycle progression.

burns.name: burns
burns.definition: Burns is injuries to tissues caused by contact with heat, steam, chemicals (burns, chemical), electricity (burns, electric), or the like.

disseminatedintravascularcoagulation.name: disseminated intravascular coagulation
disseminatedintravascularcoagulation.definition: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a disorder characterized by procoagulant substances entering the general circulation causing a systemic thrombotic process. The activation of the clotting mechanism may arise from any of a number of disorders. a majority of the patients manifest skin lesions, sometimes leading to purpura fulminans.

vitaminb6.name: vitamin b 6
vitaminb6.definition: Vitamin b 6 is vitamin b 6 refers to several picolines (especially pyridoxine; pyridoxal; & pyridoxamine) that are efficiently converted by the body to pyridoxal phosphate which is a coenzyme for synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters (serotonin, norepinephrine), sphingolipids, and aminolevulinic acid. During transamination of amino acids, pyridoxal phosphate is transiently converted into pyridoxamine phosphate. Although pyridoxine and Vitamin b 6 are still frequently used as synonyms, especially by medical researchers, this practice is erroneous and sometimes misleading (ee Snell; Ann ny Acad Sci, vol 585 pg 1, 1990). Most of vitamin b6 is eventually degraded to pyridoxic acid and excreted in the urine.

activitycycles.name: activity cycles
activitycycles.definition: Activity cycles is bouts of physical irritability or movement alternating with periods of quiescence. It includes biochemical activity and hormonal activity which may be cellular. These cycles are shorter than 24 hours and include sleep-wakefulness cycles and the periodic activation of the digestive system.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilya.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily a , member 4
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilya.definition: Member 4 subfamily a atp binding cassette transporter is an atp binding cassette sub-family a transporter that translocates 11-cis and all-trans isomers of N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (retinoids) from the extracellular surface to the cytoplasmic membrane surface of retinal rod cells and [MASK]. Mutations in the abca4 gene are associated with Stargardt Disease 1, a hereditary juvenile form of macular degeneration.

schoolhealthservices.name: school health services
schoolhealthservices.definition: School health services is preventive health services provided for students. It excludes college or university students.

oncogeneproteins.name: oncogene proteins
oncogeneproteins.definition: Oncogene proteins is proteins coded by oncogenes. They include proteins resulting from the fusion of an oncogene and another gene ([MASK]).

africanunion.name: african union
africanunion.definition: African union is a geopolitical organization of African nations with a mission to integrate vital interests, promote international relations, political stability, and economic development among member states.

radio.name: radio
radio.definition: Radio is the transmission and reception of electric impulses or signals by means of electric waves without a connecting wire, or the use of these waves for the wireless transmission of electric impulses into which sound is converted. (From Webster's 3d)

skintransplantation.name: skin transplantation
skintransplantation.definition: Skin transplantation is the grafting of skin in humans or animals from one site to another to replace a lost portion of the body surface skin.

neoplasms,squamouscell.name: neoplasms , squamous cell
neoplasms,squamouscell.definition: Squamous cell neoplasms is neoplasms of the squamous epithelial cells. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in tissue composed of squamous elements.

unitedkingdom.name: united kingdom
unitedkingdom.definition: United kingdom is country in northwestern Europe including Great Britain and the northern one-sixth of the island of Ireland, located between the [MASK] and north Atlantic Ocean. The capital is London.

catalog,drug.name: catalog , drug
catalog,drug.definition: Drug catalog is lists of drugs for sale.

balancedanesthesia.name: balanced anesthesia
balancedanesthesia.definition: Balanced anesthesia is the use of several anesthetics together in small amounts, as opposed to a larger amount of one drug, to induce loss of sensation and loss of consciousness.

liquidbiopsy.name: liquid biopsy
liquidbiopsy.definition: Liquid biopsy is obtaining material for pathological examination and analysis, from bodily fluids. Material retrieved includes cell-free nucleic acids; cell-derived microparticles; exosomes; circulating neoplasm cells; and other circulating cells and cellular structures.

biliarytractneoplasms.name: biliary tract neoplasms
biliarytractneoplasms.definition: Biliary tract neoplasms is tumors or cancer in the biliary tract including the [MASK] and the gallbladder.

retinalvein.name: retinal vein
retinalvein.definition: Retinal vein is central retinal vein and its tributaries. It runs a short course within the optic nerve and then leaves and empties into the superior ophthalmic vein or cavernous sinus.

patientrights.name: patient rights
patientrights.definition: Patient rights is fundamental claims of patients, as expressed in statutes, declarations, or generally accepted moral principles. (Bioethics Thesaurus) The term is used for discussions of patient rights as a group of many rights, as in a hospital's posting of a list of patient rights.

hydrocarbons.name: hydrocarbons
hydrocarbons.definition: Hydrocarbons is organic compounds that primarily contain carbon and hydrogen atoms with the carbon atoms forming a linear or circular structure.

hypoxia,brain.name: hypoxia , brain
hypoxia,brain.definition: Brain hypoxia is a reduction in brain oxygen supply due to anoxemia (a reduced amount of oxygen being carried in the blood by hemoglobin), or to a restriction of the blood supply to the brain, or both. Severe hypoxia is referred to as anoxia, and is a relatively common cause of injury to the central nervous system. Prolonged brain anoxia may lead to brain death or a [MASK]. Histologically, this condition is characterized by neuronal loss which is most prominent in the hippocampus; globus pallidus; cerebellum; and inferior olives.

mapkinasekinase2.name: map kinase kinase 2
mapkinasekinase2.definition: Map kinase kinase 2 is a 44 kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 and mitogen-activated protein kinase 3.

earneoplasms.name: ear neoplasms
earneoplasms.definition: Ear neoplasms is tumors or cancer of any part of the hearing and equilibrium system of the body (the external ear, the [MASK], and the [MASK]).

peroxidase.name: peroxidase
peroxidase.definition: Peroxidase is a hemeprotein from leukocytes. Deficiency of this enzyme leads to a hereditary disorder coupled with disseminated moniliasis. It catalyzes the conversion of a donor and peroxide to an oxidized donor and water. ec 1.11.1.7.

policymaking.name: policy making
policymaking.definition: Policy making is the decision process by which individuals, groups or institutions establish policies pertaining to plans, programs or procedures.

hormones,hormonesubstitutes,andhormonean.name: hormones , hormone substitutes , and hormone antagonists
hormones,hormonesubstitutes,andhormonean.definition: And hormone antagonists hormone substitutes hormones is a collective grouping for both naturally occurring and synthetic hormones, substitutes, and antagonists.

tendontransfer.name: tendon transfer
tendontransfer.definition: Tendon transfer is surgical procedure by which a tendon is incised at its insertion and placed at an anatomical site distant from the original insertion. The tendon remains attached at the point of origin and takes over the function of a muscle inactivated by trauma or disease.

feedercells.name: feeder cells
feedercells.definition: Feeder cells is cells used in coculture techniques which support the growth of the other cells in the culture. Feeder cells provide auxillary substances including attachment substrates, nutrients, or other factors that are needed for growth in culture.

bodyspaceorjunction.name: body space or junction
bodyspaceorjunction.definition: Body space or junction is body space or junction

chromosomes,artificial,human.name: chromosomes , artificial , human
chromosomes,artificial,human.definition: Human artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, all elements, such as a replication origin; telomere; and centromere, required for successful replication, propagation to and maintainance in progeny human cells. In addition, they are constructed to carry other sequences for analysis or gene transfer.

memoryconsolidation.name: memory consolidation
memoryconsolidation.definition: Memory consolidation is neurological process involving the conversion of learned information into long-term memory.

textbook.name: textbook
textbook.definition: Textbook is book intended for use in the study of specific subjects, containing systematic presentation of the principles and essential knowledge of the subjects.

elasticcartilage.name: elastic cartilage
elasticcartilage.definition: Elastic cartilage is a type of cartilage whose matrix contains elastic fibers and elastic lamellae, in addition to the normal components of hyaline cartilage matrix. Elastic cartilage is found in the external ear; eustachian tube; epiglottis; and larynx.

eyeinjuries.name: eye injuries
eyeinjuries.definition: Eye injuries is damage or trauma inflicted to the eye by external means. The concept includes both surface injuries and intraocular injuries.

sympatheticnervoussystem.name: sympathetic nervous system
sympatheticnervoussystem.definition: Sympathetic nervous system is the thoracolumbar division of the autonomic nervous system. Sympathetic preganglionic fibers originate in neurons of the intermediolateral column of the spinal cord and project to the paravertebral and prevertebral ganglia, which in turn project to target organs. The sympathetic nervous system mediates the body's response to stressful situations, i.e., the fight or flight reactions. It often acts reciprocally to the parasympathetic system.

directlyobservedtherapy.name: directly observed therapy
directlyobservedtherapy.definition: Directly observed therapy is a treatment method in which patients are under direct [MASK] when they take their medication or receive their treatment. This method is designed to reduce the risk of treatment interruption and to ensure patient compliance.

hospitalbedcapacity.name: hospital bed capacity
hospitalbedcapacity.definition: Hospital bed capacity is the number of beds which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds [MASK] up and staffed for use.

receptors,cxcr.name: receptors , cxcr
receptors,cxcr.definition: Cxcr receptors is chemokine receptors that are specific for cxc chemokines.

spindlepoles.name: spindle poles
spindlepoles.definition: Spindle poles is the sites in a dividing cell where the minus ends of the spindle [MASK] assemble and where the separated sister chromatids converge.

biologicalclocks.name: biological clocks
biologicalclocks.definition: Biological clocks is the physiological mechanisms that govern the rhythmic occurrence of certain biochemical, physiological, and behavioral phenomena.

biochemistry.name: biochemistry
biochemistry.definition: Biochemistry is the study of the composition, chemical structures, and chemical reactions of living things.

bodycomposition.name: body composition
bodycomposition.definition: Body composition is the relative amounts of various components in the body, such as percentage of body fat.

softtissueneoplasms.name: soft tissue neoplasms
softtissueneoplasms.definition: Soft tissue neoplasms is neoplasms of whatever cell type or origin, occurring in the extraskeletal connective tissue framework of the body including the organs of locomotion and their various component structures, such as nerves, blood vessels, lymphatics, etc.

humidity.name: humidity
humidity.definition: Humidity is a measure of the amount of water vapor in the air.

corticalspreadingdepression.name: cortical spreading depression
corticalspreadingdepression.definition: Cortical spreading depression is the decrease in neuronal activity (related to a decrease in metabolic demand) extending from the site of cortical stimulation. It is believed to be responsible for the decrease in [MASK] that accompanies the aura of [MASK] with aura. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

rootcauseanalysis.name: root cause analysis
rootcauseanalysis.definition: Root cause analysis is multi-step [MASK] process used for improving safety by investigation of incidents to find what happened, why it happened, and to determine what can be done to prevent it from happening again.

neoplasmsbyhistologictype.name: neoplasms by histologic type
neoplasmsbyhistologictype.definition: Neoplasms by histologic type is a collective term for the various histological types of neoplasms. It is more likely to be used by searchers than by indexers and catalogers.

myocardialreperfusion.name: myocardial reperfusion
myocardialreperfusion.definition: Myocardial reperfusion is generally, restoration of blood supply to heart tissue which is ischemic due to decrease in normal blood supply. The decrease may result from any source including atherosclerotic obstruction, narrowing of the artery, or surgical clamping. Reperfusion can be induced to treat ischemia. Methods include chemical dissolution of an occluding thrombus, administration of vasodilator drugs, angioplasty, catheterization, and artery bypass [MASK] surgery. However, it is thought that reperfusion can itself further damage the ischemic tissue, causing myocardial reperfusion injury.

primates.name: primates
primates.definition: Primates is an order of mammals consisting of more than 300 species that include lemurs; lorisidae; tarsiers; monkeys; and hominids. They are characterized by a relatively large brain when compared with other terrestrial mammals, forward-facing eyes, the presence of a calcarine sulcus, and specialized mechanoreceptors in the hands and [MASK] which allow the perception of light touch.

changemanagement.name: change management
changemanagement.definition: Change management is processes, tools, and techniques involved in the management of organizational innovation, the purpose of which is to help individuals and work groups make successful personal transitions which ensure overall successful outcomes.

rectalneoplasms.name: rectal neoplasms
rectalneoplasms.definition: Rectal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the rectum.

auditorybrainstemimplantation.name: auditory brain stem implantation
auditorybrainstemimplantation.definition: Auditory brain stem implantation is surgical insertion of an electronic hearing device (auditory brain stem implants) with electrodes to the cochlea nucleus in the brain stem rather than to the [MASK] as in cochlear implantation.

interview,psychological.name: interview , psychological
interview,psychological.definition: Psychological interview is a directed conversation aimed at eliciting information for psychiatric diagnosis, evaluation, treatment planning, etc. The interview may be conducted by a social worker or psychologist.

malaria.name: malaria
malaria.definition: Malaria is a protozoan disease caused in humans by four species of the plasmodium genus: plasmodium falciparum; plasmodium vivax; plasmodium ovale; and plasmodium malariae; and transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito of the genus anopheles. Malaria is endemic in parts of Asia, Africa, Central and South America, Oceania, and certain Caribbean islands. It is characterized by extreme exhaustion associated with paroxysms of high fever; sweating; shaking chills; and anemia. Malaria in animals is caused by other species of plasmodia.

education,veterinary.name: education , veterinary
education,veterinary.definition: Veterinary education is use for general articles concerning veterinary medical education.

lasers,dye.name: lasers , dye
lasers,dye.definition: Dye lasers is tunable liquid lasers with organic compounds (i.e., dye) which have a strong absorption band, used as the active medium. During emission, the dye has to be optically excited by another light source (e.g., another laser or flash lamp). The range of the emission wavelength may be anywhere from the ultraviolet to the near infrared (i.e., from 180 to 1100nm). These lasers are operated in continuous wave and pulsed modes. (umdns, 2005)

hematoma.name: hematoma
hematoma.definition: Hematoma is a collection of blood outside the blood vessels. Hematoma can be localized in an organ, space, or tissue.

bodytemperaturechanges.name: body temperature changes
bodytemperaturechanges.definition: Body temperature changes is significant alterations in temperature of the [MASK], above or below 98.6 degrees f. or 37 degrees c. when taken orally.

mice,inbrednod.name: mice , inbred nod
mice,inbrednod.definition: Inbred nod mice is a strain of non-obese diabetic mice developed in Japan that has been widely studied as a model for T-cell-dependent autoimmune insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in which insulitis is a major histopathologic feature, and in which genetic susceptibility is strongly MHC-linked.

electrophoresis,starchgel.name: electrophoresis , starch gel
electrophoresis,starchgel.definition: [MASK] gel electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which a [MASK] gel (a mixture of amylose and amylopectin) is used as the diffusion medium.

peritonealdialysis,continuousambulatory.name: peritoneal dialysis , continuous ambulatory
peritonealdialysis,continuousambulatory.definition: Continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis is portable peritoneal dialysis using the continuous (24 hours a day, 7 days a week) presence of peritoneal dialysis solution in the peritoneal cavity except for periods of drainage and instillation of fresh solution.

motorneurons,gamma.name: motor neurons , gamma
motorneurons,gamma.definition: Gamma motor neurons is motor neurons which activate the contractile regions of intrafusal skeletal muscle fibers, thus adjusting the sensitivity of the muscle spindles to stretch. Gamma motor neurons may be "static" or "dynamic" according to which aspect of responsiveness (or which fiber types) they regulate. The alpha and gamma motor neurons are often activated together (alpha gamma coactivation) which allows the spindles to contribute to the control of movement trajectories despite changes in muscle length.

fetaltissuetransplantation.name: fetal tissue transplantation
fetaltissuetransplantation.definition: Fetal tissue transplantation is transference of fetal tissue between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

circadianclocks.name: circadian clocks
circadianclocks.definition: Circadian clocks is biological mechanism that controls circadian rhythm. Circadian clocks exist in the simplest form in cyanobacteria and as more complex systems in fungi, plants, and animals. In humans the system includes photoresponsive [MASK] and the suprachiasmatic nucleus that acts as the central oscillator.

atlanticislands.name: atlantic islands
atlanticislands.definition: Atlantic islands is widely scattered islands in the Atlantic Ocean as far north as the azores and as far south as the South Sandwich Islands, with the greatest concentration found in the caribbean region. They include Annobon Island, Ascension, [MASK], Falkland Islands, Fernando Po (also called Isla de Bioko and Bioko), Gough Island, Madeira, Sao Tome and Principe, Saint Helena, and Tristan da Cunha.

workengagement.name: work engagement
workengagement.definition: Work engagement is extent to which members of a workplace perceive their emotional commitment to and involvement in the organization and its goals.

streptavidin.name: streptavidin
streptavidin.definition: Streptavidin is a 60-kDa extracellular protein of Streptomyces avidinii with four high-affinity biotin binding sites. Unlike avidin, streptavidin has a near neutral isoelectric point and is free of carbohydrate side chains.

brainstem.name: brain stem
brainstem.definition: Brain stem is the part of the brain that connects the cerebral hemispheres with the spinal cord. It consists of the mesencephalon; pons; and medulla oblongata.

bookillustrations.name: book illustrations
bookillustrations.definition: Book illustrations is works consisting of photographs, prints, drawings, portraits, plates, diagrams, facsimiles, maps, [MASK], or other representations or systematic arrangements of data designed to elucidate or decorate the contents of a publication. (From The ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p114)

germlayers.name: germ layers
germlayers.definition: Germ layers is the three primary germinal layers (ectoderm; endoderm; and mesoderm) developed during gastrulation that provide tissues and body plan of a mature organism. They derive from two early layers, hypoblast and epiblast.

chemistry,inorganic.name: chemistry , inorganic
chemistry,inorganic.definition: Inorganic chemistry is a field of chemistry which pertains to chemical compounds or ions that do not contain the element carbon (with the exception of carbon dioxide and compounds containing a carbonate radical, e.g., calcium carbonate).

neckpain.name: neck pain
neckpain.definition: [MASK] pain is discomfort or more intense forms of pain that are localized to the cervical region. This term generally refers to pain in the posterior or lateral regions of the [MASK].

bonycallus.name: bony callus
bonycallus.definition: Bony callus is the bony deposit formed between and around the broken ends of bone fractures during normal healing.

angiotensiniii.name: angiotensin iii
angiotensiniii.definition: Angiotensin iii is a heptapeptide formed from angiotensin ii after the removal of an amino acid at the N-terminal by aminopeptidase a. Angiotensin iii has the same efficacy as angiotensin ii in promoting aldosterone secretion and modifying renal blood flow, but less vasopressor activity (about 40%).

animals,laboratory.name: animals , laboratory
animals,laboratory.definition: Laboratory animals is animals used or intended for use in research, testing, or teaching.

electronicsupplementarymaterials.name: electronic supplementary materials
electronicsupplementarymaterials.definition: Electronic supplementary materials is supporting content or information, such as animation, datasets, multimedia files, video, movies, audio files, text files, or software, which is submitted for publication in an online journal or an online edition of a journal. This information may be referenced in the text of the article with a link to the supplementary data provided. catalog: do not use

warcrimes.name: war crimes
warcrimes.definition: War crimes is criminal acts committed during, or in connection with, war, e.g., maltreatment of prisoners, willful killing of civilians, etc.

hepatitisaviruscellularreceptor2.name: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 2
hepatitisaviruscellularreceptor2.definition: Hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 2 is an Ig domain-containing membrane receptor that is expressed by th1 cells. It regulates the activation of macrophages and inhibits TH1-mediated auto- and alloimmune responses to promote immune tolerance.

regulatoryelements,transcriptional.name: regulatory elements , transcriptional
regulatoryelements,transcriptional.definition: Transcriptional regulatory elements is nucleotide sequences of a gene that are involved in the regulation of genetic transcription.

adaptation,physiological.name: adaptation , physiological
adaptation,physiological.definition: Physiological adaptation is the non-genetic biological changes of an organism in response to challenges in its environment.

spinalcordinjuries.name: spinal cord injuries
spinalcordinjuries.definition: Spinal cord injuries is penetrating and non-penetrating injuries to the spinal cord resulting from traumatic external forces (e.g., wounds, gunshot; whiplash injuries; etc.).

anatomy,regional.name: anatomy , regional
anatomy,regional.definition: Regional anatomy is the anatomical study of specific regions or parts of organisms, emphasizing the relationship between the various structures (e.g. muscles, nerves, skeletal, cardiovascular, etc.).

sexcharacteristics.name: sex characteristics
sexcharacteristics.definition: [MASK] characteristics is those characteristics that distinguish one [MASK] from the other. The primary [MASK] characteristics are the ovaries and testes and their related hormones. Secondary [MASK] characteristics are those which are masculine or feminine but not directly related to reproduction.

rnaligase(atp).name: rna ligase ( atp )
rnaligase(atp).definition: Rna ligase (atp) is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of 3′ → 5′ phosphodiester bonds between 3′-OH and 5′-P groups of RNA molecules.

infantfood.name: infant food
infantfood.definition: Infant food is food processed and manufactured for the nutritional health of children in their first year of life.

siblings.name: siblings
siblings.definition: Siblings is persons or animals having at least one parent in common. (American College Dictionary, 3d ed)

germcells.name: germ cells
germcells.definition: Germ cells is the reproductive cells in multicellular organisms at various stages during gametogenesis.

neurogenesis.name: neurogenesis
neurogenesis.definition: Neurogenesis is formation of neurons which involves the differentiation and division of stem cells in which one or both of the daughter cells become neurons.

transplantation.name: transplantation
transplantation.definition: Transplantation is transference of a tissue or organ from either an alive or deceased donor, within an individual, between individuals of the same species, or between individuals of different species.

sigmoidneoplasms.name: sigmoid neoplasms
sigmoidneoplasms.definition: Sigmoid neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the sigmoid colon.

climaticprocesses.name: climatic processes
climaticprocesses.definition: Climatic processes is characteristic events occurring in the atmosphere during the interactions and transformation of various atmospheric components and conditions.

capacitybuilding.name: capacity building
capacitybuilding.definition: Capacity building is organizational development including enhancement of management structures, processes and procedures, within organizations and among different organizations and sectors to meet present and future needs.

edema.name: edema
edema.definition: Edema is abnormal fluid accumulation in tissues or body cavities. Most cases of edema are present under the skin in [MASK].

parasiteload.name: parasite load
parasiteload.definition: Parasite load is measure of the number of the parasites present in a host organism.

proteome.name: proteome
proteome.definition: Proteome is the protein complement of an organism coded for by its genome.

sustainablegrowth.name: sustainable growth
sustainablegrowth.definition: Sustainable growth is achievement of an economic system that can continue to grow for the foreseeable future.

sunlight.name: sunlight
sunlight.definition: Sunlight is irradiation directly from the sun.

neoadjuvanttherapy.name: neoadjuvant therapy
neoadjuvanttherapy.definition: Neoadjuvant therapy is preliminary cancer therapy (chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone/endocrine therapy, immunotherapy, hyperthermia, etc.) that precedes a necessary second modality of treatment.

liability,legal.name: liability , legal
liability,legal.definition: Legal liability is accountability and responsibility to another, enforceable by civil or criminal sanctions.

ubiquitinc.name: ubiquitin c
ubiquitinc.definition: Ubiquitin c is a single protein comprised of tandem repeats of the ubiquitin 78-amino acid sequence. It is a product of the polyubiquitin gene which contains multiple copies of the ubiquitin coding sequence. Proteolytic processing of ubiquitin c results in the formation of individual ubiquitin molecules. This protein is distinct from polyubiquitin, which is a protein formed through isopeptide linkage of multiple ubiquitin species.

mandible.name: mandible
mandible.definition: Mandible is the largest and strongest bone of the face constituting the lower jaw. It supports the lower teeth.

ruralhealthservices.name: rural health services
ruralhealthservices.definition: Rural health services is health services, public or private, in rural areas. The services include the promotion of health and the delivery of health care.

glutathionesynthase.name: glutathione synthase
glutathionesynthase.definition: Glutathione synthase is one of the enzymes active in the gamma-glutamyl cycle. It catalyzes the synthesis of glutathione from gamma-glutamylcysteine and glycine in the presence of atp with the formation of adp and orthophosphate. ec 6.3.2.3.

plantviralmovementproteins.name: plant viral movement proteins
plantviralmovementproteins.definition: Plant viral movement proteins is viral proteins that facilitate the movement of viruses between plant cells by means of plasmodesmata, channels that traverse the plant cell walls.

leukemiainhibitoryfactor.name: leukemia inhibitory factor
leukemiainhibitoryfactor.definition: Leukemia inhibitory factor is an interleukin-6 related cytokine that exhibits pleiotrophic effects on many physiological systems that involve cell proliferation, differentiation, and survival. Leukemia inhibitory factor binds to and acts through the lif receptor.

pituitaryhormonereleaseinhibitinghormone.name: pituitary hormone release inhibiting hormones
pituitaryhormonereleaseinhibitinghormone.definition: Pituitary hormone release inhibiting hormones is polypeptide hormones produced in the hypothalamus which inhibit the release of pituitary hormones. Used for phrih in general or for which there is no specific heading.

acutechestsyndrome.name: acute chest syndrome
acutechestsyndrome.definition: Acute chest syndrome is respiratory syndrome characterized by the appearance of a new pulmonary infiltrate on chest x-ray, accompanied by symptoms of fever, [MASK], [MASK], tachypnea, or dyspnea, often seen in patients with sickle cell anemia. Multiple factors (e.g., infection, and pulmonary fat embolism) may contribute to the development of the syndrome.

hospitals,public.name: hospitals , public
hospitals,public.definition: Public hospitals is hospitals controlled by various types of government, i.e., city, county, district, state or federal.

survivalofmotorneuron2protein.name: survival of motor neuron 2 protein
survivalofmotorneuron2protein.definition: Survival of motor neuron 2 protein is an smn complex protein that is closely-related to survival of motor neuron 1 protein. In humans, the protein is encoded by an often duplicated gene found near the inversion centeromere of a large inverted region of chromosome 5.

sexchromosomedisordersofsexdevelopment.name: sex chromosome disorders of sex development
sexchromosomedisordersofsexdevelopment.definition: [MASK] chromosome disorders of [MASK] development is congenital conditions of atypical sexual development associated with abnormal [MASK] chromosome constitutions including monosomy; trisomy; and mosaicism.

surveysandquestionnaires.name: surveys and questionnaires
surveysandquestionnaires.definition: Surveys and questionnaires is collections of data obtained from voluntary subjects. The information usually takes the form of answers to questions, or suggestions.

proteaseinhibitors.name: protease inhibitors
proteaseinhibitors.definition: Protease inhibitors is compounds which inhibit or antagonize biosynthesis or actions of proteases (endopeptidases).

glycogenstoragediseasetypevii.name: glycogen storage disease type vii
glycogenstoragediseasetypevii.definition: Glycogen storage disease type vii is an autosomal recessive glycogen storage disease in which there is deficient expression of 6-phosphofructose 1-kinase in muscle (phosphofructokinase-1, muscle type) resulting in abnormal deposition of glycogen in muscle tissue. These patients have severe congenital muscular dystrophy and are exercise intolerant.

clinicaldecisionrules.name: clinical decision rules
clinicaldecisionrules.definition: Clinical decision rules is scores or algorithms that correlate with clinically significant findings and that are used to predict an outcome, or suggest a diagnostic or therapeutic action.

consciousnessmonitors.name: consciousness monitors
consciousnessmonitors.definition: Consciousness monitors is devices used to assess the level of consciousness especially during anesthesia. They measure brain activity level based on the eeg.

erythrocytevolume.name: erythrocyte volume
erythrocytevolume.definition: Erythrocyte volume is volume of circulating erythrocytes . It is usually measured by radioisotope dilution technique.

proteinfolding.name: protein folding
proteinfolding.definition: Protein folding is processes involved in the formation of tertiary protein structure.

dentalalloys.name: dental alloys
dentalalloys.definition: Dental alloys is a mixture of metallic elements or compounds with other metallic or metalloid elements in varying proportions for use in restorative or prosthetic dentistry.

clinicaltrialprotocolsastopic.name: clinical trial protocols as topic
clinicaltrialprotocolsastopic.definition: Clinical trial protocols as topic is works about the written descriptions of a clinical study. It contains the study's objectives, design, and methods including subject target and/or enrollment criteria. It may also present relevant scientific background and statistical information.

disordersofsexdevelopment.name: disorders of sex development
disordersofsexdevelopment.definition: Disorders of [MASK] development is in gonochoristic organisms, congenital conditions in which development of chromosomal, gonadal, or anatomical [MASK] is atypical. Effects from exposure to abnormal levels of gonadal hormones in the maternal environment, or disruption of the function of those hormones by endocrine disruptors are included.

stents.name: stents
stents.definition: Stents is devices that provide support for tubular structures that are being anastomosed or for body cavities during skin grafting.

heatshocktranscriptionfactors.name: heat shock transcription factors
