heatshocktranscriptionfactors.definition: Heat shock transcription factors is heat and cold stress-inducible, transcription factors that bind to inverted 5'-ngaan-3' pentamer dna sequences and are regulated by poly-adp-ribosylation. They play essential roles as transcriptional activators of the heat-shock response by inducing expression of large classes of molecular chaperones and heat-shock proteins. They also function in dna repair; transcriptional reactivation of latent hiv-1; and pre-mRNA processing and nuclear export of hsp70 heat-shock proteins during heat stress.

internationalhealthregulations.name: international health regulations
internationalhealthregulations.definition: [MASK] regulations is regulations to prevent, protect against, control and provide a public health response to the international spread of disease in ways that are commensurate with and restricted to public health risks. (www.who.int/features/qa/39/en)

pyrolysis.name: pyrolysis
pyrolysis.definition: Pyrolysis is high temperature decomposition without addition of extra air or oxygen. It yields syngas, bio-oil and bio-char.

healthcaresurveys.name: health care surveys
healthcaresurveys.definition: Health care surveys is statistical measures of utilization and other aspects of the provision of health care services including hospitalization and ambulatory care.

sexualdysfunction,physiological.name: sexual dysfunction , physiological
sexualdysfunction,physiological.definition: Physiological sexual dysfunction is physiological disturbances in normal sexual performance in either the male or the female.

healthliteracy.name: health literacy
healthliteracy.definition: Health [MASK] is degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process, and understand basic health information and services needed to make appropriate health decisions.

epidermis.name: epidermis
epidermis.definition: Epidermis is the external, nonvascular layer of the skin. It is made up, from within outward, of five layers of epithelium: (1) basal layer (stratum basale epidermidis); (2) spinous layer (stratum spinosum epidermidis); (3) granular layer (stratum granulosum epidermidis); (4) clear layer (stratum lucidum epidermidis); and (5) horny layer (stratum corneum epidermidis).

domesticviolence.name: domestic violence
domesticviolence.definition: Domestic violence is deliberate, often repetitive physical, verbal, and/or other types of abuse by one or more members against others of a household.

statistics,nonparametric.name: statistics , nonparametric
statistics,nonparametric.definition: Nonparametric statistics is a class of statistical methods applicable to a large [MASK] of probability distributions used to test for correlation, location, independence, etc. In most nonparametric statistical tests, the original scores or observations are replaced by another variable containing less information. An important class of nonparametric tests employs the ordinal properties of the data. Another class of tests uses information about whether an [MASK] is above or below some fixed value such as the median, and a third class is based on the frequency of the occurrence of runs in the data. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed, p1284; Corsini, Concise Encyclopedia of Psychology, 1987, p764-5)

agegroups.name: age groups
agegroups.definition: Age groups is persons classified by age from birth (infant, newborn) to octogenarians and older (aged, 80 and over).

solitarynucleus.name: solitary nucleus
solitarynucleus.definition: Solitary nucleus is gray matter located in the dorsomedial part of the medulla oblongata associated with the solitary tract. The solitary nucleus receives inputs from most organ systems including the terminations of the facial, glossopharyngeal, and vagus nerves. It is a major coordinator of autonomic nervous system regulation of cardiovascular, respiratory, gustatory, gastrointestinal, and chemoreceptive aspects of homeostasis. The solitary nucleus is also notable for the large number of neurotransmitters which are found therein.

medicalinformaticsapplications.name: medical informatics applications
medicalinformaticsapplications.definition: Medical informatics applications is automated systems applied to the patient care process including diagnosis, therapy, and systems of communicating medical data within the health care setting.

transcriptionfactors,general.name: transcription factors , general
transcriptionfactors,general.definition: General transcription factors is transcription factors that form transcription initiation complexes on dna, bind to specific dna-directed rna polymerases and are required to initiate transcription. Although their binding may be localized to distinct sequence and structural motifs within the dna they are considered non-specific with regard to the specific gene being transcribed.

riskmanagement.name: risk management
riskmanagement.definition: Risk management is the process of minimizing risk to an organization by developing systems to identify and analyze potential hazards to prevent accidents, injuries, and other adverse occurrences, and by attempting to handle events and incidents which do occur in such a manner that their effect and cost are minimized. Effective risk management has its greatest benefits in application to insurance in order to avert or minimize [MASK]. (From Slee & Slee: Health care terms, 2d ed)

nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member3.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 4 , group a , member 3
nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member3.definition: Member 3 group a nuclear receptor subfamily 4 is an orphan nuclear receptor that is closely related to members of the thyroid-steroid receptor family. It was originally identified in nerve cells, however it may play regulatory roles in a variety of other tissues.

genes,neoplasm.name: genes , neoplasm
genes,neoplasm.definition: Neoplasm genes is genes whose abnormal expression, or mutation are associated with the development, growth, or progression of neoplasms.

parentaldeath.name: parental death
parentaldeath.definition: Parental death is the death of the [MASK] or mother or another person in this role.

directory.name: directory
directory.definition: Directory is work consisting of an alphabetical or classified list of names, organizations, subjects, etc., giving usually titles, addresses, affiliations, and other professional data.

obesity,morbid.name: obesity , morbid
obesity,morbid.definition: Morbid obesity is the condition of weighing two, three, or more times the ideal weight, so called because it is associated with many serious and life-threatening disorders. In the body mass index, morbid obesity is defined as having a bmi greater than 40.0 kg/m2.

complementfactorb.name: complement factor b
complementfactorb.definition: Complement factor b is a glycine-rich, heat-labile serum glycoprotein that contains a component of the c3 convertase alternate pathway (C3bBb). Bb, a serine protease, is generated when factor b is cleaved by complement factor d into Ba and Bb.

malaria,falciparum.name: malaria , falciparum
malaria,falciparum.definition: Falciparum malaria is malaria caused by plasmodium falciparum. This is the severest form of malaria and is associated with the highest levels of parasites in the blood. This disease is characterized by irregularly recurring febrile paroxysms that in extreme cases occur with acute cerebral, renal, or gastrointestinal manifestations.

physicalchromosomemapping.name: physical chromosome mapping
physicalchromosomemapping.definition: Physical chromosome mapping is mapping of the linear order of genes on a chromosome with units indicating their distances by using methods other than genetic recombination. These methods include nucleotide sequencing, overlapping deletions in polytene chromosomes, and [MASK] micrography of heteroduplex dna. (From King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 5th ed)

psychosocialsupportsystems.name: psychosocial support systems
psychosocialsupportsystems.definition: Psychosocial support systems is organized efforts to address ongoing psychological and social problems of individuals, their partners, families and caregivers.

diabetesmellitus,experimental.name: diabetes mellitus , experimental
diabetesmellitus,experimental.definition: Experimental diabetes mellitus is diabetes mellitus induced experimentally by administration of various diabetogenic agents or by pancreatectomy.

muscleweakness.name: muscle weakness
muscleweakness.definition: Muscle weakness is a vague complaint of debility, fatigue, or exhaustion attributable to weakness of various muscles. The weakness can be characterized as subacute or chronic, often progressive, and is a manifestation of many muscle and neuromuscular diseases. (From Wyngaarden et al., Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p2251)

education,pharmacy.name: education , pharmacy
education,pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy education is formal instruction, learning, or training in the preparation, dispensing, and proper utilization of drugs in the field of medicine.

peritonealabsorption.name: peritoneal absorption
peritonealabsorption.definition: Peritoneal absorption is uptake of substances from the peritoneal cavity.

enhancerelements,genetic.name: enhancer elements , genetic
enhancerelements,genetic.definition: Genetic enhancer elements is cis-acting dna sequences which can increase transcription of genes. Enhancers can usually function in either orientation and at various distances from a promoter.

tobaccouse.name: tobacco use
tobaccouse.definition: Tobacco use is use of tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum l) and [MASK].

sensorygating.name: sensory gating
sensorygating.definition: Sensory gating is the ability of the brain to suppress neuronal responses to external sensory inputs, such as auditory and visual stimuli. Sensory filtering (or gating) allows humans to block out irrelevant, meaningless, or redundant stimuli.

childnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: child nutritional physiological phenomena
childnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Child nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of children aged 2-12 years.

contraception,barrier.name: contraception , barrier
contraception,barrier.definition: Barrier contraception is methods of contraception in which physical, chemical, or biological means are used to prevent the sperm from reaching the fertilizable ovum.

prematurebirth.name: premature birth
prematurebirth.definition: Premature birth is childbirth before 37 weeks of pregnancy (259 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period, or 245 days after fertilization).

genes,insect.name: genes , insect
genes,insect.definition: Insect genes is the functional hereditary units of insects.

environmentalmicrobiology.name: environmental microbiology
environmentalmicrobiology.definition: Environmental microbiology is the study of microorganisms living in a variety of environments (air, soil, water, etc.) and their pathogenic relationship to other organisms including man.

examinationquestions.name: examination questions
examinationquestions.definition: Examination questions is work consisting of compilations of questions and answers pertaining to a particular subject, used for study and review.

lightcoagulation.name: light coagulation
lightcoagulation.definition: Light coagulation is the coagulation of tissue by an intense beam of light, including laser (laser coagulation). In the eye it is used in the treatment of retinal detachments, retinal holes, aneurysms, hemorrhages, and malignant and benign neoplasms. (Dictionary of Visual Science, 3d ed)

lowerextremity.name: lower extremity
lowerextremity.definition: Lower extremity is the region of the lower limb in animals, extending from the gluteal region to the [MASK], and including the buttocks; hip; and leg.

systemsintegration.name: systems integration
systemsintegration.definition: Systems integration is the procedures involved in combining separately developed modules, components, or subsystems so that they work together as a complete system. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

tissuetransplantation.name: tissue transplantation
tissuetransplantation.definition: Tissue transplantation is transference of tissue within an individual, between individuals of the same species, or between individuals of different species.

mice,inbredstrains.name: mice , inbred strains
mice,inbredstrains.definition: Inbred strains mice is genetically identical individuals developed from brother and sister matings which have been carried out for twenty or more generations, or by parent x offspring matings carried out with certain restrictions. All animals within an inbred strain trace back to a common ancestor in the twentieth generation.

evaluationstudy.name: evaluation study
evaluationstudy.definition: Evaluation study is works consisting of studies determining the effectiveness or utility of processes, personnel, and equipment.

housing.name: housing
housing.definition: Housing is living facilities for humans.

prostatichyperplasia.name: prostatic hyperplasia
prostatichyperplasia.definition: Prostatic hyperplasia is increase in constituent cells in the prostate, leading to enlargement of the organ (hypertrophy) and adverse impact on the lower urinary tract function. This can be caused by increased rate of cell proliferation, reduced rate of cell death, or both.

ppargamma.name: ppar gamma
ppargamma.definition: Ppar gamma is a nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with retinoid x receptor alpha is important in regulation of glucose metabolism and cell growth processes. It is a target of thiazolidinediones for control of diabetes mellitus.

quantumtheory.name: quantum theory
quantumtheory.definition: Quantum theory is the theory that the radiation and absorption of energy take place in definite quantities called quanta (e) which vary in size and are defined by the equation E=hv in which h is Planck's constant and v is the frequency of the radiation.

posteriorcerebralartery.name: posterior cerebral artery
posteriorcerebralartery.definition: Posterior cerebral artery is artery formed by the bifurcation of the basilar artery. Branches of the posterior cerebral artery supply portions of the occipital lobe; parietal lobe; inferior temporal gyrus, brainstem, and choroid plexus.

carbondioxide.name: carbon dioxide
carbondioxide.definition: Carbon dioxide is a colorless, odorless gas that can be formed by the body and is necessary for the respiration cycle of plants and animals.

practicepatterns,physicians'.name: practice patterns , physicians '
practicepatterns,physicians'.definition: Physicians' practice patterns is practice patterns , physicians '

validationstudiesastopic.name: validation studies as topic
validationstudiesastopic.definition: Validation studies as topic is works on research using processes by which the reliability and relevance of a procedure for a specific purpose are established.

ionpumps.name: ion pumps
ionpumps.definition: Ion pumps is a general class of integral membrane proteins that transport ions across a membrane against an electrochemical gradient.

spirallamina.name: spiral lamina
spirallamina.definition: Spiral lamina is the bony plate which extends outwards from the modiolus into the spiral canal of the cochlea, forming part of the structure that divides the upper scala vestibuli and the lower scala tympani.

gastricabsorption.name: gastric absorption
gastricabsorption.definition: Gastric absorption is uptake of substances via the stomach.

organicchemistryphenomena.name: organic chemistry phenomena
organicchemistryphenomena.definition: Organic chemistry phenomena is the conformation, properties, reaction processes, and the properties of the reactions of organic carbon compounds.

sulfurdioxide.name: sulfur dioxide
sulfurdioxide.definition: Sulfur dioxide is a highly toxic, colorless, nonflammable gas. It is used as a pharmaceutical aid and antioxidant. It is also an environmental air pollutant.

microscopy,fluorescence.name: microscopy , fluorescence
microscopy,fluorescence.definition: Fluorescence microscopy is microscopy of specimens stained with fluorescent dye (usually fluorescein isothiocyanate) or of naturally fluorescent materials, which emit light when exposed to ultraviolet or blue light. Immunofluorescence microscopy utilizes antibodies that are labeled with fluorescent dye.

sodiumchannels.name: sodium channels
sodiumchannels.definition: Sodium channels is ion channels that specifically allow the passage of sodium ions. a variety of specific sodium channel subtypes are involved in serving specialized functions such as neuronal signaling, cardiac muscle contraction, and kidney function.

artificialcells.name: artificial cells
artificialcells.definition: Artificial cells is chemically synthesized structures which functionally resemble natural cells.

models,molecular.name: models , molecular
models,molecular.definition: Molecular models is models used experimentally or theoretically to study molecular shape, electronic properties, or interactions; includes analogous molecules, computer-generated graphics, and mechanical structures.

manufacturedobject.name: manufactured object
manufacturedobject.definition: Manufactured object is a physical object created by hand or machine.

synapticpotentials.name: synaptic potentials
synapticpotentials.definition: Synaptic potentials is the voltages across pre- or post-SYNAPTIC membranes.

familycharacteristics.name: family characteristics
familycharacteristics.definition: Family characteristics is size and composition of the family.

federalgovernment.name: federal government
federalgovernment.definition: Federal government is the level of governmental organization and function at the national or country-wide level.

asthma.name: asthma
asthma.definition: Asthma is a form of bronchial disorder with three distinct components: airway hyper-responsiveness (respiratory hypersensitivity), airway inflammation, and intermittent airway obstruction. It is characterized by spasmodic contraction of airway smooth muscle, wheezing, and dyspnea (dyspnea, paroxysmal).

respiratoryparalysis.name: respiratory paralysis
respiratoryparalysis.definition: Respiratory paralysis is complete or severe weakness of the muscles of respiration. This condition may be associated with motor neuron diseases; peripheral nerve diseases; neuromuscular junction diseases; spinal cord diseases; injury to the phrenic nerve; and other disorders.

digestivesystemneoplasms.name: digestive system neoplasms
digestivesystemneoplasms.definition: Digestive system neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the digestive system.

dentalenamel.name: dental enamel
dentalenamel.definition: Dental enamel is a hard thin translucent layer of calcified substance which envelops and protects the dentin of the crown of the tooth. It is the hardest substance in the body and is almost entirely composed of calcium [MASK]. Under the microscope, it is composed of thin rods (enamel prisms) held together by cementing substance, and surrounded by an enamel sheath. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p286)

nitricoxidesynthase.name: nitric oxide synthase
nitricoxidesynthase.definition: [MASK] synthase is an NADPH-dependent enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of [MASK] and oxygen to produce citrulline and [MASK].

singlephotonemissioncomputedtomographyco.name: single photon emission computed tomography computed tomography
singlephotonemissioncomputedtomographyco.definition: Single photon emission computed tomography computed tomography is an imaging technique using a device which combines tomography, emission-computed, single-photon and tomography, x-ray computed in the same session.

physicalabuse.name: physical abuse
physicalabuse.definition: Physical abuse is violence inflicted on an individual through physical contact.

broadligament.name: broad ligament
broadligament.definition: Broad ligament is a broad fold of peritoneum that extends from the side of the uterus to the wall of the pelvis.

cities.name: cities
cities.definition: Cities is a large or important municipality of a country, usually a major metropolitan center.

drugusers.name: drug users
drugusers.definition: Drug users is people who take drugs for a non-therapeutic or non-medical effect. The drugs may be legal or illegal, but their use often results in adverse medical, legal, or social consequences for the users.

practice,psychological.name: practice , psychological
practice,psychological.definition: Psychological practice is performance of an act one or more times, with a view to its fixation or improvement; any performance of an act or behavior that leads to learning.

informationcenters.name: information centers
informationcenters.definition: Information centers is facilities for collecting and organizing information. They may be specialized by subject field, type of source material, persons served, location, or type of services.

texas.name: texas
texas.definition: Texas is state bounded on the north by Oklahoma, on the east by Arkansas and Louisiana, on the south by [MASK], and on the west by New [MASK].

catalog.name: catalog
catalog.definition: Catalog is work consisting of bibliographic records, created according to specific and uniform principles of construction and under the control of an authority file, which describe the materials contained in a collection, library, or group of libraries. Catalogs include also lists of materials prepared for a particular purpose, such as exhibition catalogs, sales catalogs, garden catalogs, medical supply catalogs. (From The ala Glossary of Library and Information Sciences, 1983)

tomography,opticalcoherence.name: tomography , optical coherence
tomography,opticalcoherence.definition: Optical coherence tomography is an imaging method using lasers that is used for mapping subsurface structure. When a reflective site in the sample is at the same optical path length (coherence) as the reference mirror, the detector observes interference fringes.

staticelectricity.name: static electricity
staticelectricity.definition: Static electricity is the accumulation of an electric charge on a object

skindiseases,bacterial.name: skin diseases , bacterial
skindiseases,bacterial.definition: Bacterial skin diseases is skin diseases caused by bacteria.

caffeine.name: caffeine
caffeine.definition: Caffeine is a methylxanthine naturally occurring in some beverages and also used as a pharmacological agent. Caffeine's most notable pharmacological effect is as a central nervous system stimulant, increasing alertness and producing agitation. It also relaxes smooth muscle, stimulates cardiac muscle, stimulates diuresis, and appears to be useful in the treatment of some types of headache. Several cellular actions of caffeine have been observed, but it is not entirely clear how each contributes to its pharmacological profile. Among the most important are inhibition of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases, antagonism of adenosine receptors, and modulation of intracellular calcium handling.

personnel,hospital.name: personnel , hospital
personnel,hospital.definition: Hospital personnel is the individuals employed by the hospital.

telomerehomeostasis.name: telomere homeostasis
telomerehomeostasis.definition: Telomere homeostasis is maintenance of telomere length. During dna replication, chromosome ends loose some of their telomere sequence ([MASK].) Various cellular mechanism are involved in repairing, extending, and recapping the telomere ends.

leadpoisoning,nervoussystem,adult.name: lead poisoning , nervous system , adult
leadpoisoning,nervoussystem,adult.definition: Adult nervous system lead poisoning is neurologic conditions in adults associated with acute or chronic exposure to lead or any of its [MASK]. The most common lead related neurologic syndrome in adults consists of a polyneuropathy involving motor fibers. This tends to affect distal nerves and may present as wrist drop due to radial neuropathy. Additional features of chronic lead exposure include anemia; constipation; colicky abdominal pain; a bluish lead line of the gums; interstitial nephritis (nephritis, interstitial); and saturnine gout. An encephalopathy may rarely occur. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1212)

metricsystem.name: metric system
metricsystem.definition: Metric system is a system of units used in scientific work throughout the world and employed in general commercial transactions and engineering applications. Its units of length, time, and mass are the meter, second, and kilogram respectively, or decimal multiples and submultiples thereof. ( McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

sportsandrecreationalfacilities.name: sports and recreational facilities
sportsandrecreationalfacilities.definition: Sports and recreational facilities is places designed, built, or installed for leisure activities outside of the home.

philosophy,nursing.name: philosophy , nursing
philosophy,nursing.definition: Nursing philosophy is the underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of nursing.

organelles.name: organelles
organelles.definition: Organelles is specific particles of membrane-bound organized living substances present in eukaryotic cells, such as the mitochondria; the golgi apparatus; endoplasmic reticulum; lysosomes; plastids; and vacuoles.

pediatricnursing.name: pediatric nursing
pediatricnursing.definition: Pediatric nursing is the nursing specialty concerning care of children from birth to adolescence. It includes the clinical and psychological aspects of nursing care.

fruit.name: fruit
fruit.definition: Fruit is the fleshy or dry ripened ovary of a plant, enclosing the [MASK] or [MASK].

splenicdiseases.name: splenic diseases
splenicdiseases.definition: Splenic diseases is diseases involving the spleen.

communicationbarriers.name: communication barriers
communicationbarriers.definition: Communication barriers is those factors, such as language or sociocultural relationships, which interfere in the meaningful interpretation and transmission of ideas between individuals or groups.

triggerpoints.name: trigger points
triggerpoints.definition: Trigger points is discrete spots in taut bands of muscle that produce local and [MASK] when muscle bands are compressed.

rnaisoforms.name: rna isoforms
rnaisoforms.definition: Rna isoforms is the different gene transcripts generated from a single gene by rna editing or [MASK] of rna precursors.

thyroidneoplasms.name: thyroid neoplasms
thyroidneoplasms.definition: Thyroid neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the thyroid gland.

dnacleavage.name: dna cleavage
dnacleavage.definition: Dna cleavage is a reaction that severs one of the covalent sugar-phosphate linkages between nucleotides that compose the sugar phosphate backbone of dna. It is catalyzed enzymatically, chemically or by radiation. Cleavage may be exonucleolytic - removing the end nucleotide, or endonucleolytic - splitting the strand in two.

concurrentreview.name: concurrent review
concurrentreview.definition: Concurrent review is review of the medical necessity of hospital or other health facility admissions, upon or within a short time following an admission, and periodic review of services provided during the course of treatment.

spinalcorddorsalhorn.name: spinal cord dorsal horn
spinalcorddorsalhorn.definition: Spinal cord dorsal horn is one of three central columns of the spinal cord. It is composed of gray matter spinal laminae i-vi.

serumalbumin.name: serum albumin
serumalbumin.definition: Serum albumin is a major protein in the blood. It is important in maintaining the colloidal osmotic pressure and transporting large organic molecules.

psychopathology.name: psychopathology
psychopathology.definition: Psychopathology is the study of significant causes and processes in the development of mental illness.

hypothalamicarea,lateral.name: hypothalamic area , lateral
hypothalamicarea,lateral.definition: Lateral hypothalamic area is area in the hypothalamus bounded medially by the mammillothalamic tract and the anterior column of the fornix (brain). The medial edge of the internal capsule and the subthalamic region form its lateral boundary. It contains the lateral hypothalamic nucleus, tuberomammillary nucleus, lateral tuberal nuclei, and fibers of the medial forebrain bundle.

touch.name: touch
touch.definition: Touch is sensation of making physical contact with objects, animate or inanimate. Tactile stimuli are detected by mechanoreceptors in the skin and mucous membranes.

excitatorypostsynapticpotentials.name: excitatory postsynaptic potentials
excitatorypostsynapticpotentials.definition: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials is depolarization of membrane potentials at the synaptic membranes of target neurons during neurotransmission. Excitatory postsynaptic potentials can singly or in summation reach the trigger threshold for action potentials.

perfusionimaging.name: perfusion imaging
perfusionimaging.definition: Perfusion imaging is the creation and display of functional images showing where the blood flow reaches by following the distribution of tracers injected into the blood [MASK].

infectiousdiseaseincubationperiod.name: infectious disease incubation period
infectiousdiseaseincubationperiod.definition: Infectious disease incubation period is the amount time between exposure to an infectious agent and becoming symptomatic.

researchactivity.name: research activity
researchactivity.definition: Research activity is a process of students study the scientific knowledge system by specially developed means and methods with the aim of cognitive skills developing, world perception, moral and other qualities of the person, as well as creative powers and abilities developing.

judicialrole.name: judicial role
judicialrole.definition: Judicial role is the kind of action or activity proper to the judiciary, particularly its responsibility for decision making.

molecularfarming.name: molecular farming
molecularfarming.definition: Molecular farming is the large scale production of pharmaceutically important and commercially valuable recombinant proteins.

chondrocytes.name: chondrocytes
chondrocytes.definition: Chondrocytes is polymorphic cells that form cartilage.

socialsecurity.name: social security
socialsecurity.definition: Social security is government sponsored social insurance programs.

ear,external.name: ear , external
ear,external.definition: External ear is the outer part of the hearing system of the body. It includes the shell-like ear auricle which collects sound, and the [MASK], the tympanic membrane, and the external ear cartilages.

standingorders.name: standing orders
standingorders.definition: Standing orders is medical procedures and prescriptions regarding treatment of a patient that can be exercised by other health care personnel when predetermined conditions have been met.

vesiculartransportproteins.name: vesicular transport proteins
vesiculartransportproteins.definition: Vesicular transport proteins is a broad category of proteins involved in the formation, transport and dissolution of transport vesicles. They play a role in the intracellular transport of molecules contained within membrane vesicles. Vesicular transport proteins are distinguished from membrane transport proteins, which move molecules across membranes, by the mode in which the molecules are transported.

telomere.name: telomere
telomere.definition: Telomere is a terminal section of a chromosome which has a specialized structure and which is involved in chromosomal replication and stability. Its length is believed to be a few hundred [MASK].

primaryprevention.name: primary prevention
primaryprevention.definition: Primary prevention is specific practices for the prevention of disease or mental disorders in susceptible individuals or populations. These include health promotion, including mental health; protective procedures, such as communicable disease control; and monitoring and regulation of environmental pollutants. Primary prevention is to be distinguished from secondary prevention and [MASK].

internationalclassificationofdiseases.name: international classification of diseases
internationalclassificationofdiseases.definition: International classification of diseases is a system of categories to which morbid entries are assigned according to established criteria. Included is the entire range of conditions in a manageable number of categories, grouped to facilitate mortality reporting. It is produced by the [MASK] Organization (From icd-10, p1). The Clinical Modifications, produced by the united states dept. of health and human services, are larger extensions used for morbidity and general epidemiological purposes, primarily in the u.s.

newjersey.name: new jersey
newjersey.definition: New jersey is state bounded on the north by New York and Pennsylvania, on the east by New York and the Atlantic Ocean, on the south by Delaware Bay, and on the west by Pennsylvania.

surgecapacity.name: surge capacity
surgecapacity.definition: Surge capacity is a health care system's ability to rapidly mobilize to meet an increased demand, to rapidly expand beyond normal services levels to meet the increased demand in the event of large-scale disasters or public health emergencies.

epidemiologicstudies.name: epidemiologic studies
epidemiologicstudies.definition: Epidemiologic studies is studies designed to examine associations, commonly, hypothesized causal relations. They are usually concerned with identifying or measuring the effects of risk factors or exposures. The common types of analytic study are case-control studies; cohort studies; and cross-sectional studies.

igadeficiency.name: iga deficiency
igadeficiency.definition: Iga deficiency is a dysgammaglobulinemia characterized by a deficiency of immunoglobulin a.

nitricoxidesynthasetypeii.name: nitric oxide synthase type ii
nitricoxidesynthasetypeii.definition: [MASK] synthase type ii is a CALCIUM-independent subtype of [MASK] synthase that may play a role in immune function. It is an inducible enzyme whose expression is transcriptionally regulated by a variety of cytokines.

infusions,subcutaneous.name: infusions , subcutaneous
infusions,subcutaneous.definition: Subcutaneous infusions is the administration of liquid medication or nutrients under the skin, usually over minutes or hours.

myocardialinfarction.name: myocardial infarction
myocardialinfarction.definition: Myocardial infarction is necrosis of the myocardium caused by an obstruction of the blood supply to the heart (coronary circulation).

headinjuries,penetrating.name: head injuries , penetrating
headinjuries,penetrating.definition: Penetrating head injuries is head injuries which feature compromise of the skull and dura mater. These may result from gunshot wounds (wounds, gunshot), stab wounds (wounds, stab), and other forms of trauma.

pathologydepartment,hospital.name: pathology department , hospital
pathologydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital pathology department is hospital department which administers and provides pathology services.

fattyalcohols.name: fatty alcohols
fattyalcohols.definition: Fatty alcohols is usually high-molecular-weight, straight-chain primary alcohols, but can also range from as few as 4 carbons, derived from natural fats and oils, including lauryl, stearyl, oleyl, and linoleyl alcohols. They are used in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, detergents, plastics, and lube oils and in textile manufacture. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

proteinstructuralelements.name: protein structural elements
proteinstructuralelements.definition: Protein structural elements is distinguishing three-dimensional structures characteristically formed by homologous protein sequences.

embryo,mammalian.name: embryo , mammalian
embryo,mammalian.definition: Mammalian embryo is the entity of a developing mammal (mammals), generally from the cleavage of a zygote to the end of embryonic differentiation of basic structures. For the human embryo, this represents the first two months of intrauterine development preceding the stages of the fetus.

education,medical,undergraduate.name: education , medical , undergraduate
education,medical,undergraduate.definition: Undergraduate medical education is the period of medical education in a medical school. In the United States it follows the baccalaureate degree and precedes the granting of the m.d.

hypothalamicdiseases.name: hypothalamic diseases
hypothalamicdiseases.definition: Hypothalamic diseases is neoplastic, inflammatory, infectious, and other diseases of the hypothalamus. Clinical manifestations include appetite disorders; autonomic nervous system diseases; sleep disorders; behavioral symptoms related to dysfunction of the limbic system; and neuroendocrine disorders.

appetite.name: appetite
appetite.definition: Appetite is natural recurring desire for food. Alterations may be induced by appetite depressants or appetite stimulants.

receptors,wnt.name: receptors , wnt
receptors,wnt.definition: Wnt receptors is cell-surface receptors that specifically bind to [MASK] and activate the wnt signaling pathway.

digestivesystem.name: digestive system
digestivesystem.definition: Digestive system is a group of organs stretching from the mouth to the anus, serving to breakdown foods, assimilate nutrients, and eliminate waste. In humans, the digestive system includes the gastrointestinal tract and the accessory glands (liver; biliary tract; pancreas).

dna.name: dna
dna.definition: Dna is a deoxyribonucleotide polymer that is the primary genetic material of all cells. Eukaryotic and prokaryotic organisms normally contain dna in a double-stranded state, yet several important biological processes transiently involve single-stranded regions. dna, which consists of a polysugar-phosphate backbone possessing projections of purines (adenine and guanine) and pyrimidines (thymine and cytosine), forms a double helix that is held together by hydrogen bonds between these purines and pyrimidines (adenine to thymine and guanine to cytosine).

antimicrobialcationicpeptides.name: antimicrobial cationic peptides
antimicrobialcationicpeptides.definition: Antimicrobial cationic peptides is small cationic peptides that are an important component, in most species, of early innate and induced defenses against invading microbes. In animals they are found on mucosal surfaces, within phagocytic granules, and on the surface of the body. They are also found in insects and plants. Among others, this group includes the defensins, protegrins, tachyplesins, and thionins. They displace divalent cations from phosphate groups of membrane lipids leading to disruption of the membrane.

meatproducts.name: meat products
meatproducts.definition: Meat products is articles of food which are derived by a process of manufacture from any portion of carcasses of any animal used for food (e.g., head cheese, sausage, scrapple).

eyeneoplasms.name: eye neoplasms
eyeneoplasms.definition: Eye neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the eye.

insulinreceptorsubstrateproteins.name: insulin receptor substrate proteins
insulinreceptorsubstrateproteins.definition: Insulin receptor substrate proteins is a structurally-related group of signaling proteins that are phosphorylated by the insulin receptor protein-tyrosine kinase. The proteins share an N-terminal pleckstrin homology domain, a phosphotyrosine-binding domain that interacts with the phosphorylated insulin receptor, and a C-terminal TYROSINE-rich domain. Upon tyrosine phosphorylation, insulin receptor substrate proteins interact with specific sh2 domain containing proteins that are involved in insulin receptor signaling.

pancreaticneoplasms.name: pancreatic neoplasms
pancreaticneoplasms.definition: Pancreatic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the pancreas. Depending on the types of islet cells present in the tumors, various hormones can be secreted: glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells; insulin from pancreatic beta cells; and somatostatin from the somatostatin-secreting cells. Most are malignant except the insulin-producing tumors (insulinoma).

endoscopy.name: endoscopy
endoscopy.definition: Endoscopy is procedures of applying endoscopes for disease diagnosis and treatment. Endoscopy involves passing an optical instrument through a small incision in the skin i.e., percutaneous; or through a natural orifice and along natural body pathways such as the digestive tract; and/or through an incision in the wall of a tubular structure or organ, i.e. transluminal, to examine or perform surgery on the interior parts of the body.

orthodonticappliances,fixed.name: orthodontic appliances , fixed
orthodonticappliances,fixed.definition: Fixed orthodontic appliances is orthodontic appliances attached to the teeth by adhesive material which cannot be removed from the mouth by the patient. These devices apply force to the teeth and supporting structures, thereby producing changes which control their growth and development.

nursingmethodologyresearch.name: nursing methodology research
nursingmethodologyresearch.definition: Nursing methodology research is research carried out by nurses concerning techniques and methods to implement projects and to document information, including methods of interviewing patients, collecting data, and forming inferences. The concept includes exploration of methodological issues such as human subjectivity and human experience.

fertilityagents,female.name: fertility agents , female
fertilityagents,female.definition: Female fertility agents is compounds which increase the capacity to conceive in females.

abdominalmuscles.name: abdominal muscles
abdominalmuscles.definition: Abdominal muscles is muscles forming the [MASK] including rectus abdominis; abdominal oblique muscles, transversus abdominis, pyramidalis muscles and quadratus abdominis.

carcinogenesis.name: carcinogenesis
carcinogenesis.definition: Carcinogenesis is the origin, production or development of cancer through genotypic and phenotypic changes which upset the normal balance between cell proliferation and cell death. Carcinogenesis generally requires a constellation of steps, which may occur quickly or over a period of many years.

geneticprivacy.name: genetic privacy
geneticprivacy.definition: Genetic privacy is the protection of genetic information about an individual, family, or population group, from unauthorized disclosure.

ringchromosomes.name: ring chromosomes
ringchromosomes.definition: Ring chromosomes is aberrant chromosomes with no ends, i.e., circular.

cytoplasmicvesicles.name: cytoplasmic vesicles
cytoplasmicvesicles.definition: Cytoplasmic vesicles is membrane-limited structures derived from the plasma membrane or various intracellular membranes which function in storage, transport or metabolism.

vitamins.name: vitamins
vitamins.definition: Vitamins is organic substances that are required in small amounts for maintenance and growth, but which cannot be manufactured by the [MASK].

endocrinecells.name: endocrine cells
endocrinecells.definition: Endocrine cells is secretory cells of the ductless glands. They secrete hormones directly into the blood circulation (internal secretion) to be carried to the target cells. The secreted chemicals can be peptides; steroids; neuropeptides; or biogenic amines.

retinaldysplasia.name: retinal dysplasia
retinaldysplasia.definition: Retinal dysplasia is congenital, often bilateral, retinal abnormality characterized by the arrangement of outer nuclear retinal cells in a palisading or radiating pattern surrounding a central ocular space. This disorder is sometimes hereditary.

australia.name: australia
australia.definition: Australia is the smallest continent and an independent country, comprising six states and two territories. Its capital is Canberra.

chiefcells,gastric.name: chief cells , gastric
chiefcells,gastric.definition: Gastric chief cells is epithelial cells that line the basal half of the gastric glands. Chief cells synthesize and export an inactive enzyme pepsinogen which is converted into the highly proteolytic enzyme pepsin in the acid environment of the stomach.

electricimpedance.name: electric impedance
electricimpedance.definition: Electric impedance is the resistance to the flow of either alternating or direct electrical current.

patientdischargesummaries.name: patient discharge summaries
patientdischargesummaries.definition: Patient discharge summaries is summaries that serve as the primary documents communicating a patient's care plan to the post-hospital care team.

environmentalpollutants.name: environmental pollutants
environmentalpollutants.definition: Environmental pollutants is substances or energies, for example heat or light, which when introduced into the air, water, or land threaten life or health of individuals or ecosystems.

endocytosis.name: endocytosis
endocytosis.definition: Endocytosis is cellular uptake of extracellular materials within membrane-limited vacuoles or microvesicles. endosomes play a central role in endocytosis.

catheters.name: catheters
catheters.definition: Catheters is a flexible, tubular device that is used to carry fluids into or from a blood vessel, hollow organ, or body cavity.

pitchdiscrimination.name: pitch discrimination
pitchdiscrimination.definition: Pitch discrimination is the ability to differentiate sound frequency or pitch.

feedingbehavior.name: feeding behavior
feedingbehavior.definition: Feeding behavior is behavioral responses or sequences associated with eating including modes of feeding, rhythmic patterns of eating, and time intervals.

arabidopsisproteins.name: arabidopsis proteins
arabidopsisproteins.definition: Arabidopsis proteins is proteins that originate from plants species belonging to the genus arabidopsis. The most intensely studied species of Arabidopsis, Arabidopsis thaliana, is commonly used in laboratory experiments.

bloodpreservation.name: blood preservation
bloodpreservation.definition: Blood preservation is the process by which blood or its components are kept viable outside of the organism from which they are derived (i.e., kept from decay by means of a chemical agent, cooling, or a fluid substitute that mimics the natural state within the organism).

receptors,polymericimmunoglobulin.name: receptors , polymeric immunoglobulin
receptors,polymericimmunoglobulin.definition: Polymeric immunoglobulin receptors is specialized Fc receptors (receptors, fc) for polymeric immunoglobulins, which mediate transcytosis of polymeric immunoglobulin a and immunoglobulin m into external secretions. They are found on the surfaces of epithelial cells and [MASK]. After binding to immunoglobulin a, the receptor-ligand complex undergoes endocytosis, transport by vesicle, and secretion into the lumen by exocytosis. Before release, the part of the receptor ([MASK]) that is bound to immunoglobulin a is proteolytically cleaved from its transmembrane tail. (From Rosen et al., The Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

toxins,biological.name: toxins , biological
toxins,biological.definition: Biological toxins is specific, characterizable, poisonous chemicals, often proteins, with specific biological properties, including immunogenicity, produced by microbes, higher plants (plants, toxic), or animals.

california.name: california
california.definition: California is state bounded on the east by Nevada and Arizona, on the south by [MASK] and the Pacific Ocean on the south and west, and on the north by Oregon.

shoulderdislocation.name: shoulder dislocation
shoulderdislocation.definition: [MASK] dislocation is displacement of the humerus from the scapula.

trachealstenosis.name: tracheal stenosis
trachealstenosis.definition: Tracheal stenosis is a pathological narrowing of the [MASK].

birthweight.name: birth weight
birthweight.definition: Birth weight is the mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual at birth. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

opticalstoragedevices.name: optical storage devices
opticalstoragedevices.definition: Optical storage devices is a computer disk read by a laser beam, containing data prerecorded by a vendor. The buyer cannot enter or modify data in any way but the advantages lie in the speed of accessibility, relative immunity to damage, and relatively low cost of purchase.

hydrocarbons,cyclic.name: hydrocarbons , cyclic
hydrocarbons,cyclic.definition: Cyclic hydrocarbons is organic compounds composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen forming a closed ring that may be either alicyclic or aromatic.

androgenantagonists.name: androgen antagonists
androgenantagonists.definition: Androgen antagonists is compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of androgens.

rasguaninenucleotideexchangefactors.name: ras guanine nucleotide exchange factors
rasguaninenucleotideexchangefactors.definition: Ras guanine nucleotide exchange factors is a family of guanine nucleotide exchange factors that are specific for ras proteins.

swinevesiculardisease.name: swine vesicular disease
swinevesiculardisease.definition: Swine vesicular disease is an enterovirus infection of swine clinically indistinguishable from [MASK]-and-mouth disease, vesicular stomatitis, and vesicular exanthema of swine. It is caused by a strain of human enterovirus b.

geneexpressionregulation,neoplastic.name: gene expression regulation , neoplastic
geneexpressionregulation,neoplastic.definition: Neoplastic gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in neoplastic tissue.

computerstoragedevices.name: computer storage devices
computerstoragedevices.definition: Computer storage devices is devices capable of receiving data, retaining data for an indefinite or finite period of time, and supplying data upon demand.

musculardiseases.name: muscular diseases
musculardiseases.definition: Muscular diseases is acquired, familial, and congenital disorders of skeletal muscle and smooth muscle.

atrialfunction,left.name: atrial function , left
atrialfunction,left.definition: Left atrial function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left atrium.

environmentalexposure.name: environmental exposure
environmentalexposure.definition: Environmental exposure is the exposure to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals.

ethics,nursing.name: ethics , nursing
ethics,nursing.definition: Nursing ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of nurses themselves, their patients, and their fellow practitioners, as well as their actions in the care of patients and in relations with their families.

noseneoplasms.name: nose neoplasms
noseneoplasms.definition: Nose neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the nose.

oxygeninhalationtherapy.name: oxygen inhalation therapy
oxygeninhalationtherapy.definition: Oxygen [MASK] therapy is [MASK] of oxygen aimed at restoring toward normal any pathophysiologic alterations of gas exchange in the cardiopulmonary system, as by the use of a respirator, nasal catheter, tent, chamber, or mask. (From Dorland, 27th ed & Stedman, 25th ed)

senseorgans.name: sense organs
senseorgans.definition: Sense organs is specialized organs adapted for the reception of stimuli by the nervous system.

toxicitytests.name: toxicity tests
toxicitytests.definition: Toxicity tests is an array of tests used to determine the toxicity of a substance to living systems. These include tests on clinical drugs, foods, and environmental pollutants.

organizationalobjectives.name: organizational objectives
organizationalobjectives.definition: Organizational objectives is the purposes, missions, and goals of an individual organization or its units, established through administrative processes. It includes an organization's long-range plans and administrative philosophy.

dentalstressanalysis.name: dental stress analysis
dentalstressanalysis.definition: Dental stress analysis is the description and measurement of the various factors that produce physical stress upon dental restorations, prostheses, or appliances, materials associated with them, or the natural oral structures.

adrenalcortexhormones.name: adrenal cortex hormones
adrenalcortexhormones.definition: Adrenal cortex hormones is hormones produced by adrenal cortex, such as cortisol and aldosterone.

proteinbiosynthesis.name: protein biosynthesis
proteinbiosynthesis.definition: Protein biosynthesis is the biosynthesis of peptides and proteins on ribosomes, directed by messenger rna, via transfer rna that is charged with standard proteinogenic amino acids.

atrialfunction.name: atrial function
atrialfunction.definition: Atrial function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the heart atria.

headandneckneoplasms.name: head and neck neoplasms
headandneckneoplasms.definition: Head and [MASK] neoplasms is soft tissue tumors or cancer arising from the mucosal surfaces of the [MASK]; oral cavity; pharynx; larynx; and cervical esophagus. Other sites included are the nose and paranasal sinuses; salivary glands; thyroid gland and [MASK]; and melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers of the head and [MASK]. (from [MASK] et al., Cancer Medicine, 4th ed, p1651)

colonoscopy.name: colonoscopy
colonoscopy.definition: Colonoscopy is endoscopic examination, therapy or surgery of the luminal surface of the colon.

alcoholicneuropathy.name: alcoholic neuropathy
alcoholicneuropathy.definition: Alcoholic neuropathy is a condition where damage to the peripheral nervous system (including the peripheral elements of the autonomic nervous system) is associated with chronic ingestion of alcoholic beverages. The disorder may be caused by a direct effect of alcohol, an associated nutritional deficiency, or a combination of factors. Clinical manifestations include variable degrees of weakness; atrophy; paresthesias; pain; loss of reflexes; sensory loss; diaphoresis; and postural hypotension. (From Arch Neurol 1995;52(1):45-51; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1146)

seleniumcompounds.name: selenium compounds
seleniumcompounds.definition: [MASK] compounds is inorganic compounds that contain [MASK] as an integral part of the molecule.

transportvesicles.name: transport vesicles
transportvesicles.definition: Transport vesicles is vesicles that are involved in shuttling cargo from the interior of the cell to the cell surface, from the cell surface to the interior, across the cell or around the cell to various locations.

acutepain.name: acute pain
acutepain.definition: Acute pain is intensely discomforting, distressful, or agonizing sensation associated with trauma or disease, with well-defined location, [MASK], and timing.

africa,northern.name: africa , northern
africa,northern.definition: Northern africa is the geographical area of Africa comprising algeria; [MASK]; libya; morocco and tunisia. It includes also the vast deserts and oases of the Sahara. It is often referred to as North Africa or the Maghreb.

eukaryoticcells.name: eukaryotic cells
eukaryoticcells.definition: Eukaryotic cells is cells of the higher organisms, containing a true nucleus bounded by a nuclear membrane.

prosthesisfitting.name: prosthesis fitting
prosthesisfitting.definition: Prosthesis fitting is the fitting and adjusting of artificial parts of the body. (From Stedman's, 26th ed)

carcinoma,pancreaticductal.name: carcinoma , pancreatic ductal
carcinoma,pancreaticductal.definition: Pancreatic ductal carcinoma is carcinoma that arises from the pancreatic ducts. It accounts for the majority of cancers derived from the pancreas.

injections,intravenous.name: injections , intravenous
injections,intravenous.definition: Intravenous injections is injections made into a vein for therapeutic or experimental purposes.

middleaged.name: middle aged
middleaged.definition: Middle aged is an adult aged 45 - 64 years.

biliarytractsurgicalprocedures.name: biliary tract surgical procedures
biliarytractsurgicalprocedures.definition: Biliary tract surgical procedures is any surgical procedure performed on the biliary tract.

insuranceselectionbias.name: insurance selection bias
insuranceselectionbias.definition: Insurance selection bias is adverse or favorable selection bias exhibited by insurers or enrollees resulting in disproportionate enrollment of certain groups of people.

germany,east.name: germany , east
germany,east.definition: East germany is the former German Democratic Republic which was reunified with the former Federal Republic of Germany in 1990.

nuclearreceptorsubfamily6,groupa,member1.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 6 , group a , member 1
nuclearreceptorsubfamily6,groupa,member1.definition: Member 1 group a nuclear receptor subfamily 6 is an orphan nuclear receptor expressed mainly in the germ cells of gonads. It functions as a transcription factor that binds to a direct repeat of the sequence aggtca and may play a role in the regulation of embryogenesis and germ cell differentiation.

programevaluation.name: program evaluation
programevaluation.definition: Program evaluation is studies designed to assess the efficacy of programs. They may include the evaluation of cost-effectiveness, the extent to which objectives are met, or impact.

sexualandgenderdisorders.name: sexual and gender disorders
sexualandgenderdisorders.definition: Sexual and gender disorders is mental disorders related to sexual dysfunction, paraphilias, and gender identity disorders.

hepatitisavirus,human.name: hepatitis a virus , human
hepatitisavirus,human.definition: Human hepatitis a virus is a strain of hepatitis a virus which causes hepatitis in humans. The virus replicates in [MASK] and is presumed to reach the intestine via the [MASK]. Transmission occurs by the fecal-oral route.

pelvicneoplasms.name: pelvic neoplasms
pelvicneoplasms.definition: Pelvic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the pelvic region.

racefactors.name: race factors
racefactors.definition: Race factors is a constituent element or influence that could be used in studies for racial disparities as variables such as those related to risk factors and disease and or differential access to services.

pollen.name: pollen
pollen.definition: Pollen is the fertilizing element of plants that contains the male gametophytes.

proteinconformation.name: protein conformation
proteinconformation.definition: Protein conformation is the characteristic 3-dimensional shape of a protein, including the secondary, supersecondary (motifs), tertiary (domains) and quaternary structure of the peptide chain. protein structure, quaternary describes the conformation assumed by multimeric proteins (aggregates of more than one polypeptide chain).

medullaryspongekidney.name: medullary sponge kidney
medullaryspongekidney.definition: Medullary sponge kidney is a non-hereditary kidney disorder characterized by the abnormally dilated (ectasia) medullary and inner papillary portions of the collecting ducts. These collecting ducts usually contain cysts or diverticula filled with jelly-like material or small calculi (kidney stones) leading to infections or obstruction. It should be distinguished from congenital or hereditary polycystic kidney diseases.

sepsis.name: sepsis
sepsis.definition: Sepsis is systemic inflammatory response syndrome with a proven or suspected infectious etiology. When sepsis is associated with organ dysfunction distant from the site of infection, it is called severe sepsis. When sepsis is accompanied by hypotension despite adequate fluid infusion, it is called septic shock.

feedingmethods.name: feeding methods
feedingmethods.definition: Feeding methods is methods of giving food to humans or animals.

ternarycomplexfactors.name: ternary complex factors
ternarycomplexfactors.definition: Ternary complex factors is a subclass of c-ets proto-oncogene proteins that were first described by their property of binding to dna when associated with other regulatory proteins such as serum response factor. They contain an amino-terminal ets domain that binds to dna along with centrally located serum response factor interacting domain, and carboxy-terminal map kinase activation domains. They play an important role in transcriptional regulation by intracellular signaling peptides and proteins.

machineactivity.name: machine activity
machineactivity.definition: Machine activity is the activity of machines.

breastimplantation.name: breast implantation
breastimplantation.definition: Breast implantation is surgical insertion of an inert sac filled with silicone or other material to augment the female form cosmetically.

manuscriptsastopic.name: manuscripts as topic
manuscriptsastopic.definition: Manuscripts as topic is works about compositions written by hand, as one written before the invention or adoption of printing.

patientsafety.name: patient safety
patientsafety.definition: Patient safety is efforts to reduce risk, to address and reduce incidents and accidents that may negatively impact healthcare consumers.

animals,inbredstrains.name: animals , inbred strains
animals,inbredstrains.definition: Inbred strains animals is animals produced by the mating of progeny over multiple generations. The resultant strain of animals is virtually identical genotypically. Highly inbred animal lines allow the study of certain traits in a relatively pure form. (Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

organicchemicals.name: organic chemicals
organicchemicals.definition: Organic chemicals is a broad class of substances containing carbon and its derivatives. Many of these chemicals will frequently contain hydrogen with or without oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, phosphorus, and other elements. They exist in either carbon chain or carbon ring form.

laboronset.name: labor onset
laboronset.definition: Labor onset is the beginning of true obstetric labor which is characterized by the cyclic [MASK] of increasing frequency, duration, and strength causing cervical dilatation to begin (labor stage, first ).

carcinoma,transitionalcell.name: carcinoma , transitional cell
carcinoma,transitionalcell.definition: Transitional cell carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm derived from transitional epithelial cells, occurring chiefly in the [MASK]; ureters; or [MASK].

onlychild.name: only child
onlychild.definition: Only child is child who has no siblings.

hospitalcosts.name: hospital costs
hospitalcosts.definition: Hospital costs is the expenses incurred by a hospital in providing care. The hospital costs attributed to a particular patient care episode include the direct costs plus an appropriate proportion of the overhead for administration, personnel, building maintenance, equipment, etc. Hospital costs are one of the factors which determine [MASK] (the price the hospital sets for its services).

disclosure.name: disclosure
disclosure.definition: Disclosure is revealing of information, by oral or written communication.

factorxii.name: factor xii
factorxii.definition: Factor xii is stable blood coagulation factor activated by contact with the subendothelial surface of an injured vessel. Along with prekallikrein, it serves as the contact factor that initiates the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. Kallikrein activates factor xii to XIIa. Deficiency of factor xii, also called the Hageman trait, leads to increased incidence of thromboembolic disease. Mutations in the gene for factor xii that appear to increase factor xii amidolytic activity are associated with hereditary angioedema type iii.

alveolarepithelialcells.name: alveolar epithelial cells
alveolarepithelialcells.definition: Alveolar epithelial cells is epithelial cells that line the pulmonary alveoli.

economics,nursing.name: economics , nursing
economics,nursing.definition: Nursing economics is economic aspects of the nursing profession.

mutation,missense.name: mutation , missense
mutation,missense.definition: Missense mutation is a mutation in which a codon is mutated to one directing the incorporation of a different amino acid. This substitution may result in an inactive or unstable product. (From a Dictionary of Genetics, King & Stansfield, 5th ed)

phospholipasecdelta.name: phospholipase c delta
phospholipasecdelta.definition: Phospholipase c delta is a phosphoinositide phospholipase c subtype that is structurally defined by the presence of an N-terminal pleckstrin-homology and EF-hand domains, a central [MASK], and a C-terminal calcium-dependent membrane-binding domain.

pancreatitis,graft.name: pancreatitis , graft
pancreatitis,graft.definition: [MASK] pancreatitis is an inflammatory disease and serious complication of pancreas transplantation. It is caused by a premature activation of pancreatic proenzymes leading to autodigestion of the gland and can be attributed to immunological or nonimmunological causes.

review.name: review
review.definition: Review is an article or book published after examination of published material on a subject. It may be comprehensive to various degrees and the time range of material scrutinized may be broad or narrow, but the reviews most often desired are reviews of the current literature. The textual material examined may be equally broad and can encompass, in medicine specifically, clinical material as well as experimental research or case reports. State-of-the-art reviews tend to address more current matters. a review of the literature must be differentiated from historical article on the same subject, but a review of historical literature is also within the scope of this publication type.

voicetraining.name: voice training
voicetraining.definition: Voice training is a variety of techniques used to help individuals utilize their voice for various purposes and with minimal use of muscle energy.

antigens,viral,tumor.name: antigens , viral , tumor
antigens,viral,tumor.definition: Tumor viral antigens is those proteins recognized by antibodies from serum of animals bearing tumors induced by viruses; these proteins are presumably coded for by the nucleic acids of the same viruses that caused the neoplastic transformation.

motionsickness.name: motion sickness
motionsickness.definition: Motion sickness is disorder caused by motion. It includes sea sickness, train sickness, roller coaster rides, rocking chair, hammock swing, car sickness, air sickness, or space motion sickness. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting and/or dizziness.

newsouthwales.name: new south wales
newsouthwales.definition: New south wales is a state in southeastern Australia. Its capital is Sydney. It was discovered by Captain Cook in 1770 and first settled at Botany Bay by marines and convicts in 1788. It was named by Captain Cook who thought its coastline resembled that of South Wales. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p840 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p377)

chromium.name: chromium
chromium.definition: Chromium is a trace element that plays a role in glucose metabolism. It has the atomic symbol Cr, atomic number 24, and atomic weight 52. According to the Fourth Annual Report on Carcinogens (ntp85-002,1985), chromium and some of its compounds have been listed as known carcinogens.

militaryhealth.name: military health
militaryhealth.definition: Military health is the physical and mental conditions of military personnel, active duty and retired u.s. Military personnel and their dependents.

nasallavage.name: nasal lavage
nasallavage.definition: Nasal lavage is irrigation of the nose with saline or irrigation solutions for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. It is used to remove irritants, allergens, or microorganisms from the nose.

familytherapy.name: family therapy
familytherapy.definition: Family therapy is a form of group psychotherapy. It involves treatment of more than one member of the family simultaneously in the same session.

surfaceplasmonresonance.name: surface plasmon resonance
surfaceplasmonresonance.definition: Surface plasmon resonance is a biosensing technique in which biomolecules capable of binding to specific analytes or ligands are first immobilized on one side of a metallic film. Light is then focused on the opposite side of the film to excite the surface plasmons, that is, the oscillations of free [MASK] propagating along the film's surface. The refractive index of light reflecting off this surface is measured. When the immobilized biomolecules are bound by their ligands, an alteration in surface plasmons on the opposite side of the film is created which is directly proportional to the change in bound, or adsorbed, mass. Binding is measured by changes in the refractive index. The technique is used to study biomolecular interactions, such as antigen-antibody binding.

receptors,tie.name: receptors , tie
receptors,tie.definition: Tie receptors is a family of structurally-related tyrosine kinase receptors that are expressed predominantly in endothelial cells and are essential for development of blood vessels (neovascularization, physiologic). The name derives from the fact that they are tyrosine kinases that contain Ig and egf domains.

openfracturereduction.name: open fracture reduction
openfracturereduction.definition: [MASK] reduction is restoration of normal alignment of a fractured bone via an operative surgical procedure.

feedingandeatingdisorders.name: feeding and eating disorders
feedingandeatingdisorders.definition: Feeding and eating disorders is a group of disorders characterized by physiological and psychological disturbances in appetite or food intake.

pulse.name: pulse
pulse.definition: Pulse is the rhythmical expansion and contraction of an artery produced by waves of pressure caused by the ejection of blood from the left ventricle of the heart as it contracts.

substratespecificity.name: substrate specificity
substratespecificity.definition: Substrate specificity is a characteristic feature of enzyme activity in relation to the kind of substrate on which the enzyme or catalytic molecule reacts.

pancreaticdiseases.name: pancreatic diseases
pancreaticdiseases.definition: Pancreatic diseases is pathological processes of the pancreas.

milksubstitutes.name: milk substitutes
milksubstitutes.definition: Milk substitutes is food beverages that are used as nutritional substitutes for milk.

childdevelopment.name: child development
childdevelopment.definition: Child development is the continuous sequential physiological and psychological maturing of an individual from birth up to but not including adolescence.

neurosurgery.name: neurosurgery
neurosurgery.definition: Neurosurgery is a surgical specialty concerned with the treatment of diseases and disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral and sympathetic nervous system.

anteriorhypothalamicnucleus.name: anterior hypothalamic nucleus
anteriorhypothalamicnucleus.definition: Anterior hypothalamic nucleus is loose heterogeneous collection of cells in the anterior hypothalamus, continuous rostrally with the medial and lateral preoptic areas and caudally with the tuber cinereum.

sickleave.name: sick leave
sickleave.definition: Sick leave is an absence from work permitted because of illness or the number of days per year for which an employer agrees to pay employees who are sick. (Webster's New Collegiate Dictionary, 1981)

solitarypulmonarynodule.name: solitary pulmonary nodule
solitarypulmonarynodule.definition: Solitary pulmonary nodule is a single lung lesion that is characterized by a small round mass of tissue, usually less than 1 cm in diameter, and can be detected by chest radiography. a solitary pulmonary nodule can be associated with neoplasm, tuberculosis, cyst, or other anomalies in the lung, the chest wall, or the pleura.

plant.name: plant
plant.definition: Plant is multicellular, eukaryotic life forms of kingdom Plantae. Plants acquired chloroplasts by direct endosymbiosis of cyanobacteria. They are characterized by a mainly photosynthetic mode of nutrition; essentially unlimited growth at localized regions of cell divisions (meristems); cellulose within cells providing rigidity; the absence of organs of locomotion; absence of nervous and sensory systems; and an alternation of haploid and diploid generations. It is a non-taxonomical term most often referring to land plants. In broad sense it includes rhodophyta and glaucophyta along with viridiplantae.

apoptosis.name: apoptosis
apoptosis.definition: Apoptosis is a regulated cell death mechanism characterized by distinctive morphologic changes in the nucleus and cytoplasm, including the endonucleolytic cleavage of genomic dna, at regularly spaced, internucleosomal sites, i.e., [MASK].  It is genetically-programmed and serves as a balance to [MASK] in regulating the size of animal tissues and in mediating pathologic processes associated with tumor growth.

visiontests.name: vision tests
visiontests.definition: Vision tests is a series of tests used to assess various functions of the eyes.

oxidativephosphorylationcouplingfactors.name: oxidative phosphorylation coupling factors
oxidativephosphorylationcouplingfactors.definition: Oxidative phosphorylation coupling factors is oxidative phosphorylation coupling factors

toothfractures.name: tooth fractures
toothfractures.definition: Tooth fractures is break or rupture of a tooth or tooth root.

ethanol.name: ethanol
ethanol.definition: Ethanol is a clear, colorless liquid rapidly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and distributed throughout the body. It has bactericidal activity and is used often as a topical disinfectant. It is widely used as a solvent and preservative in pharmaceutical preparations as well as serving as the primary ingredient in alcoholic beverages.

referralandconsultation.name: referral and consultation
referralandconsultation.definition: Referral and consultation is the practice of sending a patient to another program or practitioner for services or advice which the referring source is not prepared to provide.

gingivalneoplasms.name: gingival neoplasms
gingivalneoplasms.definition: Gingival neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the gingiva.

infectiousencephalitis.name: infectious encephalitis
infectiousencephalitis.definition: Infectious encephalitis is brain inflammation caused by an infectious agent.

diet,mediterranean.name: diet , mediterranean
diet,mediterranean.definition: Mediterranean diet is a diet typical of the Mediterranean region characterized by a pattern high in fruits and vegetables, edible grain and bread, potatoes, poultry, beans, nuts, [MASK] and fish while low in red meat and dairy and moderate in alcohol consumption.

perioperativemedicine.name: perioperative medicine
perioperativemedicine.definition: Perioperative medicine is a medical specialty concerned with the patient before and after surgical procedures.

chromosomes,human,pair14.name: chromosomes , human , pair 14
chromosomes,human,pair14.definition: Pair 14 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group d chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

cerebellum.name: cerebellum
cerebellum.definition: Cerebellum is the part of brain that lies behind the brain stem in the posterior base of skull (cranial fossa, posterior). It is also known as the "little brain" with convolutions similar to those of cerebral cortex, inner [MASK] matter, and deep cerebellar nuclei. Its function is to coordinate voluntary movements, maintain balance, and learn motor skills.

vitaminkdeficiencybleeding.name: vitamin k deficiency bleeding
vitaminkdeficiencybleeding.definition: Vitamin k deficiency bleeding is hemorrhage caused by vitamin k deficiency.

dentalpins.name: dental pins
dentalpins.definition: Dental pins is small cylindrical pieces of metal used to enhance retention.

neuroendocrinecells.name: neuroendocrine cells
neuroendocrinecells.definition: Neuroendocrine cells is specialized neurons that produce hormones, such as neuropeptides or biogenic amines. They generally are in the nervous system, such as hypothalamus, but can be found in other organs or systems. These neurons contain dense neurosecretory granules and proprotein convertases allowing the rapidly release of neurohormones into the blood circulation upon stimulation.

pakistan.name: pakistan
pakistan.definition: Pakistan is a country located in southern Asia, bordering the Arabian Sea, between India on the east and Iran and Afghanistan on the west and China in the north. The capital is Islamabad.

dentinsensitivity.name: dentin sensitivity
dentinsensitivity.definition: Dentin sensitivity is pain associated with exposed dentin surfaces of the teeth.

spindlepolebodies.name: spindle pole bodies
spindlepolebodies.definition: Spindle pole bodies is [MASK] organizing centers of fungi and diatoms. They are embedded in the nuclear envelope and evolve into the spindle apparatus during cell division.

masks.name: masks
masks.definition: Masks is devices that cover the nose and mouth to maintain aseptic conditions often for the prevention of the spread of infections (e.g. covid19) or to administer inhaled anesthetics or other gases.

survivalrate.name: survival rate
survivalrate.definition: Survival rate is the proportion of survivors in a group, e.g., of patients, studied and followed over a period, or the proportion of persons in a specified group alive at the beginning of a time interval who survive to the end of the interval. It is often studied using [MASK].

centralamerica.name: central america
centralamerica.definition: Central america is a region of southern north america extending from the southern border of [MASK] to the northern border of [MASK]. It separates the Caribbean Sea from the Pacific Ocean and is linked to south america by the Isthmus of Panama.

cyclinb.name: cyclin b
cyclinb.definition: Cyclin b is a cyclin subtype that is transported into the cell nucleus at the end of the g2 phase. It stimulates the g2/m phase transition by activating cdc2 protein kinase.

hepatitisviruses.name: hepatitis viruses
hepatitisviruses.definition: Hepatitis viruses is any of the viruses that cause inflammation of the liver. They include both dna and rna viruses as well viruses from humans and animals.

lysosomes.name: lysosomes
lysosomes.definition: Lysosomes is a class of morphologically heterogeneous cytoplasmic particles in animal and plant tissues characterized by their content of hydrolytic enzymes and the structure-linked latency of these enzymes. The intracellular functions of lysosomes depend on their lytic potential. The single unit membrane of the lysosome acts as a barrier between the enzymes enclosed in the lysosome and the external substrate. The activity of the enzymes contained in lysosomes is limited or nil unless the vesicle in which they are enclosed is ruptured or undergoes [MASK]. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

drugadministrationroutes.name: drug administration routes
drugadministrationroutes.definition: Drug administration routes is the various ways of administering a drug or other chemical to a site in a patient or animal from where the chemical is absorbed into the blood and delivered to the target tissue.

gels.name: gels
gels.definition: Gels is colloids with a solid continuous phase and liquid as the dispersed phase; gels may be unstable when, due to temperature or other cause, the solid phase liquefies; the resulting colloid is called a sol.

depthperception.name: depth perception
