depthperception.definition: Depth perception is perception of three-dimensionality.

sequencetaggedsites.name: sequence tagged sites
sequencetaggedsites.definition: Sequence tagged sites is short tracts of dna sequence that are used as landmarks in genome mapping. In most instances, 200 to 500 [MASK] of sequence define a Sequence Tagged Site (sts) that is operationally unique in the human genome (i.e., can be specifically detected by the polymerase chain reaction in the presence of all other genomic sequences). The overwhelming advantage of STSs over mapping landmarks defined in other ways is that the means of testing for the presence of a particular sts can be completely described as information in a [MASK].

prospectivestudies.name: prospective studies
prospectivestudies.definition: Prospective studies is [MASK] of a population for a sufficient number of persons over a sufficient number of years to generate incidence or mortality rates subsequent to the selection of the study group.

drosophila.name: drosophila
drosophila.definition: Drosophila is a genus of small, two-winged flies containing approximately 900 described species. These organisms are the most extensively studied of all genera from the standpoint of genetics and cytology.

coronaryarterybypass.name: coronary artery bypass
coronaryarterybypass.definition: Coronary artery bypass is surgical therapy of ischemic coronary artery disease achieved by grafting a section of saphenous vein, internal mammary artery, or other substitute between the aorta and the obstructed coronary artery distal to the obstructive lesion.

biologicaltherapy.name: biological therapy
biologicaltherapy.definition: Biological therapy is treatment of diseases with biological materials or biological response modifiers, such as the use of genes; cells; tissues; organs; serum; vaccines; and humoral agents.

heartseptum.name: heart septum
heartseptum.definition: Heart septum is this structure includes the thin muscular atrial septum between the two heart atria, and the thick muscular ventricular septum between the two heart ventricles.

receptors,ccr.name: receptors , ccr
receptors,ccr.definition: Ccr receptors is chemokine receptors that are specific for [MASK].

mesentericischemia.name: mesenteric ischemia
mesentericischemia.definition: Mesenteric ischemia is ischemic tissue injury produced by insufficient perfusion of intestinal tissue by the mesenteric circulation (i.e., celiac [MASK] artery; infererior mesenteric artery; and mesenteric veins). It can progress from ischemia; edema; and gangrene of the bowel wall to peritonitis and cardiovascular collapse.

rna,transfer,gln.name: rna , transfer , gln
rna,transfer,gln.definition: Gln transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying [MASK] to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

deliveryofhealthcare,integrated.name: delivery of health care , integrated
deliveryofhealthcare,integrated.definition: Integrated delivery of health care is a health care system which combines physicians, hospitals, and other medical services with a health plan to provide the complete spectrum of medical care for its customers. In a fully integrated system, the three key elements - physicians, hospital, and health plan membership - are in balance in terms of matching medical resources with the needs of purchasers and patients. (Coddington et al., Integrated Health Care: Reorganizing the Physician, Hospital and Health Plan Relationship, 1994, p7)

foodindustry.name: food industry
foodindustry.definition: Food industry is the industry concerned with processing, preparing, preserving, distributing, and serving of foods and beverages.

ecosystem.name: ecosystem
ecosystem.definition: Ecosystem is a functional system which includes the organisms of a natural community together with their environment. (McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

clinicalpharmacyinformationsystems.name: clinical pharmacy information systems
clinicalpharmacyinformationsystems.definition: Clinical pharmacy information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of [MASK].

pulmonarygasexchange.name: pulmonary gas exchange
pulmonarygasexchange.definition: Pulmonary gas exchange is the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between alveolar air and pulmonary capillary blood that occurs across the blood-air barrier.

lithiumchloride.name: lithium chloride
lithiumchloride.definition: [MASK] chloride is a [MASK] of [MASK] that has been used experimentally as an immunomodulator.

rna,transfer,ala.name: rna , transfer , ala
rna,transfer,ala.definition: Ala transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying [MASK] to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

arsenicpoisoning.name: arsenic poisoning
arsenicpoisoning.definition: Arsenic poisoning is disorders associated with acute or chronic exposure to compounds containing arsenic (arsenicals) which may be fatal. Acute oral ingestion is associated with gastrointestinal symptoms and an encephalopathy which may manifest as seizures, mental status changes, and coma. Chronic exposure is associated with mucosal irritation, desquamating rash, myalgias, peripheral neuropathy, and [MASK] transverse (Mees) lines in the fingernails. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1212)

carbohydratemetabolism.name: carbohydrate metabolism
carbohydratemetabolism.definition: Carbohydrate metabolism is cellular processes in biosynthesis (anabolism) and degradation (catabolism) of carbohydrates.

bellpalsy.name: bell palsy
bellpalsy.definition: Bell palsy is a syndrome characterized by the acute onset of unilateral [MASK] which progresses over a 2-5 day period. Weakness of the orbicularis oculi muscle and resulting incomplete eye closure may be associated with corneal injury. Pain behind the ear often precedes the onset of paralysis. This condition may be associated with herpesvirus 1, human infection of the facial nerve. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1376)

fingers.name: fingers
fingers.definition: Fingers is four or five slender jointed digits in humans and primates, attached to each hand.

groundwater.name: groundwater
groundwater.definition: Groundwater is liquid water present beneath the surface of the earth.

clinicaltrialprotocol.name: clinical trial protocol
clinicaltrialprotocol.definition: Clinical trial protocol is the written description of a clinical study. It contains the study's objectives, design, and methods including subject target and/or enrollment criteria. It may also present relevant scientific background and statistical information.

cellularsenescence.name: cellular senescence
cellularsenescence.definition: Cellular senescence is process by which cells irreversibly stop dividing and enter a state of permanent growth arrest without undergoing cell death. Senescence can be induced by dna damage or other cellular stresses, such as oxidative stress.

syphilis.name: syphilis
syphilis.definition: Syphilis is a contagious venereal disease caused by the spirochete treponema pallidum.

microarrayanalysis.name: microarray analysis
microarrayanalysis.definition: Microarray analysis is the simultaneous analysis, on a microchip, of multiple samples or targets arranged in an array format.

genes,viral.name: genes , viral
genes,viral.definition: Viral genes is the functional hereditary units of viruses.

smallcelllungcarcinoma.name: small cell lung carcinoma
smallcelllungcarcinoma.definition: Small cell lung carcinoma is a form of highly malignant lung cancer that is composed of small ovoid cells (small cell carcinoma).

transientsandmigrants.name: transients and migrants
transientsandmigrants.definition: Transients and migrants is people who frequently change their place of residence.

animaldistribution.name: animal distribution
animaldistribution.definition: Animal distribution is a process by which animals in various forms and stages of development are physically distributed through time and space.

factorv.name: factor v
factorv.definition: Factor v is heat- and storage-labile plasma glycoprotein which accelerates the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin in blood coagulation. Factor v accomplishes this by forming a complex with factor Xa, [MASK], and calcium (prothrombinase complex). Deficiency of factor v leads to Owren's disease.

hipinjuries.name: hip injuries
hipinjuries.definition: Hip injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the hip.

vacuum.name: vacuum
vacuum.definition: Vacuum is a space in which the pressure is far below atmospheric pressure so that the remaining gases do not affect processes being carried on in the space.

cellrespiration.name: cell respiration
cellrespiration.definition: Cell respiration is the metabolic process of all living cells (animal and plant) in which oxygen is used to provide a source of energy for the cell.

medicalinformatics.name: medical informatics
medicalinformatics.definition: Medical informatics is the field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of medical data through the application of computers to various aspects of health care and medicine.

pregnancyinadolescence.name: pregnancy in adolescence
pregnancyinadolescence.definition: Pregnancy in adolescence is pregnancy in human adolescent females under the age of 19.

tissueconditioning,dental.name: tissue conditioning , dental
tissueconditioning,dental.definition: Dental tissue conditioning is the use of a treatment material (tissue conditioner) to re-establish tone and health to irritated oral soft tissue, usually applied to the edentulous alveolar ridge.

nitrocompounds.name: nitro compounds
nitrocompounds.definition: Nitro compounds is compounds having the nitro group, -no2, attached to carbon. When attached to nitrogen they are nitramines and attached to oxygen they are nitrates.

siliconegels.name: silicone gels
siliconegels.definition: Silicone gels is synthetic organosiloxane gels that are formed from synthetic polymers of silicone oxide with organic sidechains (polydimethylsiloxane) by lengthening the polymer chains. Unlike silicone elastomers, they are not treated with amorphous silica. They are used as fillers in breast implants.

healthcareactivity.name: health care activity
healthcareactivity.definition: Health care activity is the concept concerned with all aspects of providing and distributing health services to a patient population.

clinicalprotocols.name: clinical protocols
clinicalprotocols.definition: Clinical protocols is precise and detailed plans for the study of a medical or biomedical problem and/or plans for a regimen of therapy.

attentionalbias.name: attentional bias
attentionalbias.definition: Attentional bias is an increased focus or awareness of certain stimuli over others, which influence behavior.

pharmaceuticalsolutions.name: pharmaceutical solutions
pharmaceuticalsolutions.definition: Pharmaceutical solutions is homogeneous liquid preparations that contain one or more chemical substances dissolved, i.e., molecularly dispersed, in a suitable solvent or mixture of mutually miscible solvents. For reasons of their ingredients, method of preparation, or use, they do not fall into another group of products.

cardiacoutput,high.name: cardiac output , high
cardiacoutput,high.definition: High cardiac output is a state of elevated cardiac output due to conditions of either increased hemodynamic demand or reduced cardiac oxygen output. These conditions may include anemia; arteriovenous fistula; thyrotoxicosis; pregnancy; exercise; fever; and hypoxia. In time, compensatory changes of the heart can lead to pathological form of high cardiac output and eventual heart failure.

designerdrugs.name: designer drugs
designerdrugs.definition: Designer drugs is drugs designed and synthesized, often for illegal street use, by modification of existing drug structures (e.g., amphetamines). Of special interest are mptp (a reverse ester of meperidine), mda (3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine), and mdma (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine). Many drugs act on the aminergic system, the physiologically active biogenic amines.

receptors,cytokine.name: receptors , cytokine
receptors,cytokine.definition: Cytokine receptors is cell surface proteins that bind cytokines and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

colonicpolyps.name: colonic polyps
colonicpolyps.definition: Colonic polyps is discrete tissue masses that protrude into the lumen of the colon. These polyps are connected to the wall of the colon either by a stalk, pedunculus, or by a broad base.

peptideelongationfactor2.name: peptide elongation factor 2
peptideelongationfactor2.definition: Peptide elongation factor 2 is peptide Elongation Factor 2 catalyzes the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA from the a site to the p site of eukaryotic ribosomes by a process linked to the hydrolysis of gtp to gdp.

element,ion,orisotope.name: element , ion , or isotope
element,ion,orisotope.definition: Or isotope ion element is element , ion , or isotope

molar,third.name: molar , third
molar,third.definition: Third molar is the aftermost permanent tooth on each side in the maxilla and mandible.

organism.name: organism
organism.definition: Organism is living thing that has an organized structure, can react to stimuli, reproduce, grow, adapt, and maintain homeostasis.

carcinoma,ductal,breast.name: carcinoma , ductal , breast
carcinoma,ductal,breast.definition: Breast ductal carcinoma is an invasive (infiltrating) carcinoma of the mammary ductal system (mammary glands) in the human breast.

identification,psychological.name: identification , psychological
identification,psychological.definition: Psychological identification is a process by which an individual unconsciously endeavors to pattern himself after another. This process is also important in the development of the personality, particularly the superego or conscience, which is modeled largely on the behavior of adult significant others.

crohndisease.name: crohn disease
crohndisease.definition: Crohn disease is a chronic transmural inflammation that may involve any part of the digestive tract from mouth to anus, mostly found in the ileum, the cecum, and the colon. In Crohn disease, the inflammation, extending through the intestinal wall from the mucosa to the serosa, is characteristically asymmetric and segmental. Epithelioid granulomas may be seen in some patients.

mobileapplications.name: mobile applications
mobileapplications.definition: Mobile applications is computer programs or software installed on mobile electronic devices which support a wide range of functions and uses which include television, telephone, video, music, word processing, and Internet service.

spiritpossession.name: spirit possession
spiritpossession.definition: Spirit possession is the idea that abnormal behavior or a medical condition is evidence that a person is under the control of a supernatural power or spirit. This belief was most commonly held in religion and medicine of the medieval period and is also held in many tribal cultures today.

animalusealternatives.name: animal use alternatives
animalusealternatives.definition: Animal use alternatives is alternatives to the use of animals in research, testing, and education. The alternatives may include reduction in the number of animals used, replacement of animals with a non-animal model or with animals of a species lower phylogenetically, or refinement of methods to minimize pain and distress of animals used.

bloodcoagulationdisorders.name: blood coagulation disorders
bloodcoagulationdisorders.definition: Blood coagulation disorders is hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders that occur as a consequence of abnormalities in blood coagulation due to a variety of factors such as coagulation protein disorders; blood platelet disorders; blood protein disorders or nutritional conditions.

histonecode.name: histone code
histonecode.definition: Histone code is the specific patterns of changes made to histones, that are involved in assembly, maintenance, and alteration of chromatin structural states (such as euchromatin and heterochromatin). The changes are made by various histone modification processes that include acetylation; methylation; phosphorylation; and ubiquitination.

proteinphosphatase1.name: protein phosphatase 1
proteinphosphatase1.definition: Protein phosphatase 1 is a eukayrotic protein serine-threonine phosphatase subtype that dephosphorylates a wide variety of cellular proteins. The enzyme is comprised of a [MASK] and regulatory subunit. Several isoforms of the protein phosphatase [MASK] exist due to the presence of multiple genes and the [MASK] of their mRNAs. a large number of proteins have been shown to act as regulatory subunits for this enzyme. Many of the regulatory subunits have additional cellular functions.

abnormalities,multiple.name: abnormalities , multiple
abnormalities,multiple.definition: Multiple abnormalities is congenital abnormalities that affect more than one organ or body structure.

sexdeterminationbyskeleton.name: sex determination by skeleton
sexdeterminationbyskeleton.definition: [MASK] determination by skeleton is validation of the [MASK] of an individual by means of the bones of the skeleton. It is most commonly based on the appearance of the pelvis; skull; sternum; and/or long bones.

seriallearning.name: serial learning
seriallearning.definition: Serial learning is learning to make a series of responses in exact order.

symptomassessment.name: symptom assessment
symptomassessment.definition: Symptom assessment is evaluation of manifestations of disease.

duodenaldiseases.name: duodenal diseases
duodenaldiseases.definition: Duodenal diseases is pathological conditions in the duodenum region of the small intestine (intestine, small).

epidemiologicfactors.name: epidemiologic factors
epidemiologicfactors.definition: Epidemiologic factors is events, characteristics, or other definable entities that have the potential to bring about a change in a health condition or other defined outcome.

speechdiscriminationtests.name: speech discrimination tests
speechdiscriminationtests.definition: [MASK] discrimination tests is tests of the ability to hear and understand [MASK] as determined by scoring the number of words in a word list repeated correctly.

psychology,positive.name: psychology , positive
psychology,positive.definition: Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths that enable individuals and communities to thrive. It is founded on the belief that people want to lead meaningful and fulfilling lives, to cultivate what is best within themselves, and to enhance their experiences of love, work, and play. (https://ppc.sas.upenn.edu/)

digestivesystemabnormalities.name: digestive system abnormalities
digestivesystemabnormalities.definition: Digestive system abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the digestive system.

brainhemorrhage,traumatic.name: brain hemorrhage , traumatic
brainhemorrhage,traumatic.definition: Traumatic brain hemorrhage is bleeding within the brain as a result of penetrating and nonpenetrating craniocerebral trauma. Traumatically induced hemorrhages may occur in any area of the brain, including the cerebrum; brain stem (see brain stem hemorrhage, traumatic); and cerebellum.

patternrecognition,visual.name: pattern recognition , visual
patternrecognition,visual.definition: Visual pattern recognition is mental process to visually perceive a critical number of facts (the pattern), such as [MASK], shapes, displays, or designs.

sleeplatency.name: sleep latency
sleeplatency.definition: Sleep latency is the time it takes to reach rem sleep. It is typically measured by polysomnography or eeg as a part of various sleep pattern tests (e.g., multiple sleep latency test).

proteins.name: proteins
proteins.definition: Proteins is linear polypeptides that are synthesized on ribosomes and may be further modified, crosslinked, cleaved, or assembled into complex proteins with several subunits. The specific sequence of amino acids determines the shape the polypeptide will take, during protein folding, and the function of the protein.

carotidarterydiseases.name: carotid artery diseases
carotidarterydiseases.definition: Carotid artery diseases is pathological conditions involving the carotid arteries, including the common, internal, and external carotid arteries. atherosclerosis and trauma are relatively frequent causes of carotid artery pathology.

mapkinasekinasekinase3.name: map kinase kinase kinase 3
mapkinasekinasekinase3.definition: Map kinase kinase kinase 3 is a 70-kDa mapk kinase kinase with specificity for map kinase kinase 5.

auditorycortex.name: auditory cortex
auditorycortex.definition: Auditory cortex is the region of the cerebral cortex that receives the auditory radiation from the medial geniculate body.

potassiumchannels,tandemporedomain.name: potassium channels , tandem pore domain
potassiumchannels,tandemporedomain.definition: Tandem pore domain potassium channels is potassium channels that contain two pores in tandem. They are responsible for baseline or leak currents and may be the most numerous of all k channels.

europe.name: europe
europe.definition: Europe is the continent north of africa, west of asia and east of the atlantic ocean.

aminoacidtransportsystema.name: amino acid transport system a
aminoacidtransportsystema.definition: Amino acid transport system a is a sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter that accounts for most of the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid uptake by mammalian cells. The preferred substrates for this transporter system include [MASK]; serine; and [MASK].

gridcells.name: grid cells
gridcells.definition: Grid cells is neurons in the entorhinal cortex that project to the hippocampus. Grid cells and place cells play a role in cognitive representation of [MASK] and navigation.

spinalfractures.name: spinal fractures
spinalfractures.definition: Spinal fractures is broken bones in the vertebral column.

hemoglobinh.name: hemoglobin h
hemoglobinh.definition: Hemoglobin h is an abnormal hemoglobin composed of four beta chains. It is caused by the reduced synthesis of the alpha chain. This abnormality results in alpha-thalassemia.

serotoninplasmamembranetransportproteins.name: serotonin plasma membrane transport proteins
serotoninplasmamembranetransportproteins.definition: Serotonin plasma membrane transport proteins is sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters located primarily on the plasma membrane of serotonergic neurons. They are different than serotonin receptors, which signal cellular responses to serotonin. They remove serotonin from the extracellular space by high affinity reuptake into presynaptic terminals. Regulates signal amplitude and duration at serotonergic synapses and is the site of action of the serotonin uptake inhibitors.

lymphnoderatio.name: lymph node ratio
lymphnoderatio.definition: [MASK] node ratio is the ratio of metastatic to total examined [MASK] nodes.

functionalneuroimaging.name: functional neuroimaging
functionalneuroimaging.definition: Functional neuroimaging is methods for visualizing regional blood flow, metabolic, electrical, or other physiological activities in the central nervous system using various imaging modalities.

weather.name: weather
weather.definition: Weather is the state of the atmosphere over minutes to months.

qualitycontrol.name: quality control
qualitycontrol.definition: Quality control is a system for verifying and maintaining a desired level of quality in a product or process by careful planning, use of proper equipment, continued inspection, and corrective action as required. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

uterineperforation.name: uterine perforation
uterineperforation.definition: Uterine perforation is a hole or break through the wall of the uterus, usually made by the placement of an instrument or [MASK].

bonesubstitutes.name: bone substitutes
bonesubstitutes.definition: Bone substitutes is synthetic or natural materials for the replacement of bones or bone tissue. They include hard tissue replacement polymers, natural coral, hydroxyapatite, beta-tricalcium phosphate, and various other biomaterials. The bone substitutes as inert materials can be incorporated into surrounding tissue or gradually replaced by original tissue.

internetofthings.name: internet of things
internetofthings.definition: Internet of things is networking capability which facilitates information flow to and from objects and devices using the internet.

receptors,deathdomain.name: receptors , death domain
receptors,deathdomain.definition: Death domain receptors is a family of cell surface receptors that signal via a conserved domain that extends into the cell cytoplasm. The conserved domain is referred to as a death domain due to the fact that many of these receptors are involved in apoptosis signaling pathways. Several death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins can bind to the death domains of the activated receptors and through a complex series of interactions activate apoptotic mediators such as caspases.

rats,inbredlec.name: rats , inbred lec
rats,inbredlec.definition: Inbred lec rats is a cinnamon-colored strain of Long-Evans rats which carries a mutation causing [MASK] and jaundice, with an associated gross accumulation of [MASK] in the liver. This strain is a model for Wilson's Disease (see hepatolenticular degeneration).

transientreceptorpotentialchannels.name: transient receptor potential channels
transientreceptorpotentialchannels.definition: Transient receptor potential channels is a broad group of eukaryotic six-transmembrane cation channels that are classified by sequence homology because their functional involvement with sensation is varied. They have only weak voltage sensitivity and ion selectivity. They are named after a drosophila mutant that displayed transient receptor potentials in response to light. a 25-amino-acid motif containing a trp box (ewkfar) just C-terminal to s6 is found in trpc, trpv and trpm subgroups. ankyrin repeats are found in trpc, trpv & trpn subgroups. Some are functionally associated with tyrosine kinase or type c phospholipases.

oocytedonation.name: oocyte donation
oocytedonation.definition: Oocyte donation is transfer of preovulatory oocytes from donor to a suitable host. Oocytes are collected, fertilized in vitro, and transferred to a host that can be human or animal.

vascularendothelialgrowthfactorb.name: vascular endothelial growth factor b
vascularendothelialgrowthfactorb.definition: Vascular endothelial growth factor b is a vascular endothelial growth factor expressed in a variety of tissues. It binds with high specificity to vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 and neuropilin-1.

typeiisecretionsystems.name: type ii secretion systems
typeiisecretionsystems.definition: Type ii secretion systems is gram-negative bacterial secretion systems which carry out the secretion of folded proteins.T2SSs secrete folded proteins from the periplasmic space that have been exported there by sec translocase or tat secretion systems, or they secrete folded proteins directly from the cytoplasm. The T2SSs have four substructures, an ATPase, an inner membrane platform, a pseudopilin, and secretin, an outer membrane complex which is a channel for secretion. (This bacterial secretin is not the same as the mammalian hormone also named secretin.)

timeandmotionstudies.name: time and motion studies
timeandmotionstudies.definition: Time and motion studies is the [MASK] and analysis of movements in a task with an emphasis on the amount of time required to perform the task.

tibia.name: tibia
tibia.definition: Tibia is the second longest bone of the skeleton. It is located on the medial side of the lower leg, articulating with the fibula laterally, the talus distally, and the femur proximally.

cognitivebehavioraltherapy.name: cognitive behavioral therapy
cognitivebehavioraltherapy.definition: Cognitive behavioral therapy is a directive form of psychotherapy based on the interpretation of situations (cognitive structure of experiences) that determine how an individual feels and behaves. It is based on the premise that cognition, the process of acquiring knowledge and forming beliefs, is a primary determinant of mood and behavior. The therapy uses behavioral and verbal techniques to identify and correct negative thinking that is at the root of the aberrant behavior.

peaproteins.name: pea proteins
peaproteins.definition: Pea proteins is dietary proteins that are present in or isolated from the [MASK] of pisum sativum.

tightjunctionproteins.name: tight junction proteins
tightjunctionproteins.definition: Tight junction proteins is proteins that take part in the formation or structure of tight junctions.

foodcoloringagents.name: food coloring agents
foodcoloringagents.definition: Food coloring agents is natural or synthetic dyes used as coloring agents in processed foods.

pituitarygland,intermediate.name: pituitary gland , intermediate
pituitarygland,intermediate.definition: Intermediate pituitary gland is the intermediate lobe of the pituitary gland. It shows considerable size variation among the species, small in humans, and large in amphibians and lower vertebrates. This lobe produces mainly melanocyte-stimulating hormones and other peptides from post-translational processing of pro-opiomelanocortin (pomc).

chromosomes,artificial,yeast.name: chromosomes , artificial , yeast
chromosomes,artificial,yeast.definition: Yeast artificial chromosomes is chromosomes in which fragments of exogenous dna ranging in length up to several hundred kilobase pairs have been cloned into yeast through [MASK] to vector sequences. These artificial chromosomes are used extensively in molecular biology for the construction of comprehensive genomic libraries of higher organisms.

datainterpretation,statistical.name: data interpretation , statistical
datainterpretation,statistical.definition: Statistical data interpretation is application of statistical procedures to analyze specific observed or assumed facts from a particular study.

biologicaltransport.name: biological transport
biologicaltransport.definition: Biological transport is the movement of materials (including biochemical substances and drugs) through a biological system at the cellular level. The transport can be across cell membranes and epithelial layers. It also can occur within intracellular compartments and extracellular compartments.

fructoseintolerance.name: fructose intolerance
fructoseintolerance.definition: Fructose intolerance is an autosomal recessive fructose metabolism disorder due to deficient fructose-1-phosphate aldolase (ec 2.1.2.13) activity, resulting in accumulation of fructose-1-phosphate. The accumulated fructose-1-phosphate inhibits glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, causing severe hypoglycemia following ingestion of fructose. Prolonged fructose ingestion in infants leads ultimately to hepatic failure and death. Patients develop a strong distaste for sweet food, and avoid a chronic course of the disease by remaining on a fructose- and sucrose-free diet.

twins.name: twins
twins.definition: Twins is two individuals derived from two fetuses that were fertilized at or about the same time, developed in the uterus simultaneously, and born to the same mother. Twins are either monozygotic (twins, monozygotic) or dizygotic (twins, dizygotic).

hemorrhagicdiseasevirus,rabbit.name: hemorrhagic disease virus , rabbit
hemorrhagicdiseasevirus,rabbit.definition: Rabbit hemorrhagic disease virus is a species in the genus lagovirus which causes hemorrhagic disease, including hemorrhagic septicemia, in rabbits.

culturallyappropriatetechnology.name: culturally appropriate technology
culturallyappropriatetechnology.definition: Culturally appropriate technology is a science or technology that promotes self-sufficiency and is suitable to the cultural, environmental, economic and social conditions of the geographic area in which it is applied.

mice,neurologicmutants.name: mice , neurologic mutants
mice,neurologicmutants.definition: Neurologic mutants mice is mice which carry mutant genes for neurologic defects or abnormalities.

bloodpressuremonitors.name: blood pressure monitors
bloodpressuremonitors.definition: Blood pressure monitors is devices for continuously measuring and displaying the arterial blood pressure.

bonetransplantation.name: bone transplantation
bonetransplantation.definition: Bone transplantation is the grafting of bone from a donor site to a recipient site.

receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type2.name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 2
receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type2.definition: Type 2 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor which contains three extracellular immunoglobulin i-[MASK] domains and is expressed as two isoforms. One receptor isoform is expressed in the mesenchyme and is activated by fibroblast growth factor 2. a second isoform is expressed mainly by epithelial cells and is activated by fibroblast growth [MASK] and [MASK]. Mutation of the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 can result in craniosynostotic syndromes (e.g., apert syndrome; and crouzon syndrome).

dnasequence,unstable.name: dna sequence , unstable
dnasequence,unstable.definition: Unstable dna sequence is a region of dna that is highly polymorphic and is prone to strand breaks, rearrangements or other mutations because of the nature of its sequence. These regions often harbor palindromic, or repetitive sequences (repetitive sequences, nucleic acid). Variability in stability of the dna sequence is seen at chromosome fragile sites.

tertiarylymphoidstructures.name: tertiary lymphoid structures
tertiarylymphoidstructures.definition: Tertiary lymphoid structures is aggregates of immune cells formed near the sites of chronically inflamed, infected, or tumorous tissues.

falsenegativereactions.name: false negative reactions
falsenegativereactions.definition: False negative reactions is negative test results in subjects who possess the attribute for which the test is conducted. The labeling of diseased persons as healthy when screening in the detection of disease. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

healthservicesresearch.name: health services research
healthservicesresearch.definition: Health services research is the integration of epidemiologic, sociological, economic, and other analytic sciences in the study of health services. Health services research is usually concerned with relationships between need, demand, supply, use, and outcome of health services. The aim of the research is evaluation, particularly in terms of structure, process, output, and outcome. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

sequenceanalysis.name: sequence analysis
sequenceanalysis.definition: Sequence analysis is a multistage process that includes the determination of a sequence (protein, carbohydrate, etc.), its fragmentation and analysis, and the interpretation of the resulting sequence information.

patientcareplanning.name: patient care planning
patientcareplanning.definition: Patient care planning is usually a written medical and nursing care program designed for a particular patient.

abbreviationsastopic.name: abbreviations as topic
abbreviationsastopic.definition: Abbreviations as topic is works about shortened forms of written words or phrases used for brevity.

certificateofneed.name: certificate of need
certificateofneed.definition: Certificate of need is a certificate issued by a governmental body to an individual or organization proposing to construct or modify a health facility, or to offer a new or different service. The process of issuing the certificate is also included.

coppersulfate.name: copper sulfate
coppersulfate.definition: [MASK] sulfate is a sulfate [MASK] of [MASK]. It is a potent emetic and is used as an antidote for poisoning by phosphorus. It also can be used to prevent the growth of algae.

reproductivetechniques,assisted.name: reproductive techniques , assisted
reproductivetechniques,assisted.definition: Assisted reproductive techniques is clinical and laboratory techniques used to enhance fertility in humans and animals.

webarchivesastopic.name: web archives as topic
webarchivesastopic.definition: [MASK] as topic is works about collections of preserved web pages.

fear.name: fear
fear.definition: Fear is the affective response to an actual current external danger which subsides with the elimination of the threatening condition.

psychology,educational.name: psychology , educational
psychology,educational.definition: Educational psychology is the branch of psychology concerned with psychological aspects of teaching and the formal learning process in school.

skincare.name: skin care
skincare.definition: Skin care is maintenance of the hygienic state of the skin under optimal conditions of cleanliness and comfort. Effective in skin care are proper washing, bathing, cleansing, and the use of soaps, detergents, oils, etc. In various disease states, therapeutic and protective solutions and ointments are useful. The care of the skin is particularly important in various occupations, in exposure to sunlight, in neonates, and in pressure [MASK].

acutekidneyinjury.name: acute kidney injury
acutekidneyinjury.definition: Acute kidney injury is abrupt reduction in kidney function. Acute kidney injury encompasses the entire spectrum of the syndrome including acute kidney failure; [MASK]; and other less severe conditions.

coagulationproteindisorders.name: coagulation protein disorders
coagulationproteindisorders.definition: Coagulation protein disorders is hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders resulting from abnormalities or deficiencies of coagulation proteins.

rankligand.name: rank ligand
rankligand.definition: Rank ligand is a transmembrane protein belonging to the tumor necrosis factor superfamily that specifically binds receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa b and osteoprotegerin. It plays an important role in regulating osteoclast differentiation and activation.

genelibrary.name: gene library
genelibrary.definition: Gene library is a large collection of dna fragments cloned (cloning, molecular) from a given organism, tissue, organ, or cell type. It may contain complete genomic sequences (genomic library) or complementary dna sequences, the latter being formed from messenger rna and lacking intron sequences.

mentalhealth.name: mental health
mentalhealth.definition: Mental health is emotional, psychological, and social well-being of an individual or group.

boston.name: boston
boston.definition: Boston is city located in Massachusetts.

collagentypeii.name: collagen type ii
collagentypeii.definition: Collagen type ii is a fibrillar collagen found predominantly in cartilage and [MASK]. It consists of three identical alpha1(II) chains.

tumorcells,cultured.name: tumor cells , cultured
tumorcells,cultured.definition: Cultured tumor cells is cells grown in vitro from neoplastic tissue. If they can be established as a tumor cell line, they can be propagated in cell culture indefinitely.

naildiseases.name: nail diseases
naildiseases.definition: Nail diseases is diseases of the nail plate and tissues surrounding it. The concept is limited to primates.

bodyremains.name: body remains
bodyremains.definition: Body remains is the physical entity of a deceased human or animal.

genotypingtechniques.name: genotyping techniques
genotypingtechniques.definition: Genotyping techniques is methods used to determine individuals' specific alleles or snps (single nucleotide polymorphisms).

inorganicchemicals.name: inorganic chemicals
inorganicchemicals.definition: Inorganic chemicals is a broad class of substances encompassing all those that do not include carbon and its derivatives as their principal elements. However, carbides, carbonates, cyanides, cyanates, and carbon disulfide are included in this class.

voice.name: voice
voice.definition: Voice is the sounds produced by humans by the passage of air through the larynx and over the vocal cords, and then modified by the resonance organs, the nasopharynx, and the mouth.

chiefexecutiveofficers,hospital.name: chief executive officers , hospital
chiefexecutiveofficers,hospital.definition: Hospital chief executive officers is individuals who have the formal authority to manage a hospital, including its programs and services, in accordance with the goals and objectives established by a governing body (governing board).

bacteria,anaerobic.name: bacteria , anaerobic
bacteria,anaerobic.definition: Anaerobic bacteria is bacteria that can survive and grow in the complete, or nearly complete absence of oxygen.

laryngealnerveinjuries.name: laryngeal nerve injuries
laryngealnerveinjuries.definition: Laryngeal nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the laryngeal nerve.

glutamateplasmamembranetransportproteins.name: glutamate plasma membrane transport proteins
glutamateplasmamembranetransportproteins.definition: Glutamate plasma membrane transport proteins is a family of plasma membrane neurotransmitter transporter proteins that couple the uptake of glutamate with the import of sodium ions and protons and the export of potassium ions. In the central nervous system they regulate neurotransmission through synaptic reuptake of the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate. Outside the central nervous system they function as signal mediators and regulators of glutamate metabolism.

schools,veterinary.name: schools , veterinary
schools,veterinary.definition: Veterinary schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of veterinary medicine.

footjoints.name: foot joints
footjoints.definition: [MASK] joints is the articulations extending from the ankle distally to the toes. These include the ankle joint; tarsal joints; metatarsophalangeal joint; and toe joint.

plantleaves.name: plant leaves
plantleaves.definition: Plant leaves is expanded structures, usually green, of vascular plants, characteristically consisting of a bladelike expansion attached to a stem, and functioning as the principal organ of [MASK] and transpiration. (American Heritage Dictionary, 2d ed)

diagnosticimaging.name: diagnostic imaging
diagnosticimaging.definition: Diagnostic imaging is any visual display of structural or functional patterns of organs or tissues for diagnostic evaluation. It includes measuring physiologic and metabolic responses to physical and chemical stimuli, as well as ultramicroscopy.

aerosols.name: aerosols
aerosols.definition: Aerosols is colloids with a gaseous dispersing phase and either liquid (fog) or solid (smoke) dispersed phase; used in fumigation or in [MASK] therapy; may contain propellant agents.

correspondenceastopic.name: correspondence as topic
correspondenceastopic.definition: Correspondence as topic is works on written communication between persons or between institutions or organizations.

lamintypea.name: lamin type a
lamintypea.definition: Lamin type a is a subclass of developmentally regulated lamins having a neutral isoelectric point. They are found to disassociate from nuclear membranes during [MASK].

knowledgemanagement.name: knowledge management
knowledgemanagement.definition: Knowledge management is the leveraging of collective wisdom within an organization as a catalyst to increase responsiveness and innovation.

vascularresistance.name: vascular resistance
vascularresistance.definition: Vascular resistance is the force that opposes the flow of blood through a vascular bed. It is equal to the difference in blood pressure across the vascular bed divided by the cardiac output.

mesentericcyst.name: mesenteric cyst
mesentericcyst.definition: Mesenteric cyst is a rare intra-abdominal tumor in the mesentery. Mesenteric cysts are usually benign and can be very large fluid-filled (2000 mL) lesions.

cellsurvival.name: cell survival
cellsurvival.definition: Cell survival is the span of viability of a cell characterized by the capacity to perform certain functions such as metabolism, growth, reproduction, some form of responsiveness, and adaptability.

rnarecognitionmotif.name: rna recognition motif
rnarecognitionmotif.definition: Rna recognition motif is an approximately 80 amino acid rna binding motif that consists of four anti-parallel surface beta sheets and two alpha helices arranged in a beta-alpha-beta-beta-alpha-beta configuration. One of the surface beta sheets interacts with two or three specific rna bases. Interactions between additional sequences and the rna, as well as within the rna recognition motif increase the affinity and specificity of the protein-RNA interaction.

glycogensynthasekinase3.name: glycogen synthase kinase 3
glycogensynthasekinase3.definition: Glycogen synthase kinase 3 is a glycogen synthase kinase that was originally described as a key enzyme involved in glycogen metabolism. It regulates a diverse array of functions such as cell division, [MASK] function and apoptosis.

anger.name: anger
anger.definition: Anger is a strong emotional feeling of displeasure aroused by being interfered with, injured or threatened.

anomalousleftcoronaryartery.name: anomalous left coronary artery
anomalousleftcoronaryartery.definition: Anomalous left coronary artery is malformations of left coronary artery where it is connected to the [MASK] instead of the aorta.

professionalpracticegaps.name: professional practice gaps
professionalpracticegaps.definition: Professional practice gaps is difference between observed and ideal delivery of health care and healthcare outcomes that reflect the current state of knowledge.

endoplasmicreticulum.name: endoplasmic reticulum
endoplasmicreticulum.definition: Endoplasmic reticulum is a system of cisternae in the cytoplasm of many cells. In places the endoplasmic reticulum is continuous with the plasma membrane (cell membrane) or outer membrane of the nuclear envelope. If the outer surfaces of the endoplasmic reticulum membranes are coated with ribosomes, the endoplasmic reticulum is said to be rough-surfaced (endoplasmic reticulum, rough); otherwise it is said to be smooth-surfaced (endoplasmic reticulum, smooth). (King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

rna3'endprocessing.name: rna 3 ' end processing
rna3'endprocessing.definition: Rna 3' end processing is The steps that generate the 3' ends of mature RNA molecules. For most mRNAs (rna, messenger), 3' end processing referred to as polyadenylation includes the addition of poly A.

intestinaldiseases.name: intestinal diseases
intestinaldiseases.definition: Intestinal diseases is pathological processes in any segment of the intestine from duodenum to rectum.

sodiumdodecylsulfate.name: sodium dodecyl sulfate
sodiumdodecylsulfate.definition: Sodium dodecyl sulfate is an anionic surfactant, usually a mixture of sodium alkyl sulfates, mainly the lauryl; lowers [MASK] of aqueous solutions; used as fat emulsifier, wetting agent, detergent in cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and toothpastes; also as research tool in protein biochemistry.

invasivefungalinfections.name: invasive fungal infections
invasivefungalinfections.definition: Invasive fungal infections is mycoses which manifest as infections of deep tissue or blood.

kinetics.name: kinetics
kinetics.definition: Kinetics is the rate dynamics in chemical or physical systems.

fiberoptictechnology.name: fiber optic technology
fiberoptictechnology.definition: Fiber optic technology is the technology of transmitting light over long distances through strands of glass or other transparent material.

flowcytometry.name: flow cytometry
flowcytometry.definition: Flow cytometry is technique using an instrument system for making, processing, and displaying one or more measurements on individual cells obtained from a cell suspension. Cells are usually stained with one or more fluorescent dyes specific to cell components of interest, e.g., dna, and fluorescence of each cell is measured as it rapidly transverses the excitation beam (laser or mercury arc lamp). Fluorescence provides a quantitative measure of various biochemical and biophysical properties of the cell, as well as a basis for cell sorting. Other measurable optical parameters include light absorption and light scattering, the latter being applicable to the measurement of cell size, shape, density, granularity, and stain uptake.

nuclearmedicine.name: nuclear medicine
nuclearmedicine.definition: Nuclear medicine is a specialty field of radiology concerned with diagnostic, therapeutic, and investigative use of radioactive compounds.

africanswinefevervirus.name: african swine fever virus
africanswinefevervirus.definition: African swine fever virus is the lone species of the genus Asfivirus. It infects domestic and wild pigs, warthogs, and bushpigs. Disease is endemic in domestic swine in many African countries and Sardinia. Soft ticks of the genus Ornithodoros are also infected and act as vectors.

narrativemedicine.name: narrative medicine
narrativemedicine.definition: Narrative medicine is narration as a tool to collect and interpret information on a patient's experience of illness

renin.name: renin
renin.definition: Renin is a highly specific (Leu-Leu) endopeptidase that generates angiotensin i from its precursor angiotensinogen, leading to a cascade of reactions which elevate blood pressure and increase sodium retention by the kidney in the renin-angiotensin system. The enzyme was formerly listed as ec 3.4.99.19.

neoplasms,fibroustissue.name: neoplasms , fibrous tissue
neoplasms,fibroustissue.definition: Fibrous tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of fibrous tissue, the ordinary connective tissue of the body, made up largely of yellow or [MASK] fibers. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in fibrous tissue.

spiritualtherapies.name: spiritual therapies
spiritualtherapies.definition: Spiritual therapies is mystical, religious, or spiritual practices performed for [MASK].

licensedpracticalnurses.name: licensed practical nurses
licensedpracticalnurses.definition: Licensed practical nurses is health personnel who do not hold professional degrees or credentials, but have completed training and are licensed to provide routine patient care under the direction of registered nurses and physicians.

mice,knockout.name: mice , knockout
mice,knockout.definition: Knockout mice is strains of mice in which certain genes of their genomes have been disrupted, or "knocked-out". To produce knockouts, using [MASK] technology, the normal dna sequence of the gene being studied is altered to prevent synthesis of a normal gene product. Cloned cells in which this dna alteration is successful are then injected into mouse embryos to produce chimeric mice. The chimeric mice are then bred to yield a strain in which all the cells of the mouse contain the disrupted gene. Knockout mice are used as experimental animal models for diseases (disease models, animal) and to clarify the functions of the genes.

polymorphism,restrictionfragmentlength.name: polymorphism , restriction fragment length
polymorphism,restrictionfragmentlength.definition: Restriction fragment length polymorphism is variation occurring within a species in the presence or length of dna fragment generated by a specific endonuclease at a specific site in the genome. Such variations are generated by mutations that create or abolish recognition sites for these enzymes or change the length of the fragment.

intimatepartnerviolence.name: intimate partner violence
intimatepartnerviolence.definition: Intimate partner violence is a pattern of assaultive and coercive behavior by an individual against their partner or spouse that may include physical injury, psychological abuse, sexual assault, progressive isolation, stalking, deprivation, intimidation, and reproductive coercion.

stakeholderparticipation.name: stakeholder participation
stakeholderparticipation.definition: Stakeholder participation is a process between an entity and those groups or individuals potentially or actually impacted by the actions of that entity over a range of activities and approaches.

gabaplasmamembranetransportproteins.name: gaba plasma membrane transport proteins
gabaplasmamembranetransportproteins.definition: Gaba plasma membrane transport proteins is a family of plasma membrane neurotransmitter transporter proteins that regulates extracellular levels of the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid. They differ from gaba receptors, which signal cellular responses to gamma-aminobutyric acid. They control gaba reuptake into presynaptic terminals in the central nervous system through high-affinity sodium-dependent transport.

warexposure.name: war exposure
warexposure.definition: War exposure is the health and other ramifications of military and civilian exposure to war.

childlanguage.name: child language
childlanguage.definition: Child language is the language and sounds expressed by a child at a particular maturational stage in development.

radiography.name: radiography
radiography.definition: Radiography is examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes by means of x-rays or gamma rays, recording the image on a sensitized surface (such as photographic film).

speechreceptionthresholdtest.name: speech reception threshold test
speechreceptionthresholdtest.definition: [MASK] reception threshold test is a test to determine the lowest sound intensity level at which fifty percent or more of the spondaic test words (words of two syllables having equal stress) are repeated correctly.

bonediseases.name: bone diseases
bonediseases.definition: Bone diseases is diseases of bones.

opticnervediseases.name: optic nerve diseases
opticnervediseases.definition: Optic nerve diseases is conditions which produce injury or dysfunction of the second cranial or optic nerve, which is generally considered a component of the central nervous system. Damage to optic nerve fibers may occur at or near their origin in the retina, at the [MASK], or in the nerve, optic chiasm, optic tract, or lateral geniculate nuclei. Clinical manifestations may include decreased visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, impaired [MASK] vision, and an afferent pupillary defect.

electronicnicotinedeliverysystems.name: electronic nicotine delivery systems
electronicnicotinedeliverysystems.definition: Electronic nicotine delivery systems is devices or objects designed to provide nicotine in the form of an inhaled aerosol.

plateletstoragepooldeficiency.name: platelet storage pool deficiency
plateletstoragepooldeficiency.definition: Platelet storage pool deficiency is disorder characterized by a decrease or lack of platelet dense bodies in which the releasable pool of adenine nucleotides and 5ht are normally stored.

stimulation,chemical.name: stimulation , chemical
stimulation,chemical.definition: Chemical stimulation is the increase in a measurable parameter of a physiological process, including cellular, microbial, and plant; immunological, cardiovascular, respiratory, reproductive, urinary, digestive, neural, musculoskeletal, ocular, and skin physiological processes; or metabolic process, including enzymatic and other pharmacological processes, by a drug or other chemical.

lforms.name: l forms
lforms.definition: L forms is bacterial variants, unable to form a complete cell wall, which are formed in cultures by various bacteria; granules (l bodies) appear, unite, and grow into amorphous bodies which multiply and give rise to bacterial cells morphologically indistinguishable from the parent strain.

pneumonia,aspiration.name: pneumonia , aspiration
pneumonia,aspiration.definition: Aspiration pneumonia is a type of lung inflammation resulting from the aspiration of food, liquid, or gastric contents into the upper respiratory tract.

autonomicpathways.name: autonomic pathways
autonomicpathways.definition: Autonomic pathways is nerves and plexuses of the autonomic nervous system. The central nervous system structures which regulate the autonomic nervous system are not included.

thoracicinjuries.name: thoracic injuries
thoracicinjuries.definition: Thoracic injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the chest area.

osteoarthritis,hip.name: osteoarthritis , hip
osteoarthritis,hip.definition: Hip osteoarthritis is noninflammatory degenerative disease of the hip joint which usually appears in late middle or old age. It is characterized by growth or maturational disturbances in the femoral [MASK] and head, as well as acetabular dysplasia. a dominant symptom is pain on weight-bearing or motion.

pregnancycomplications,infectious.name: pregnancy complications , infectious
pregnancycomplications,infectious.definition: Infectious pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and an infection. The infection may precede or follow fertilization.

selfpsychology.name: self psychology
selfpsychology.definition: Self psychology is psychoanalytic theory focusing on interpretation of behavior in reference to self. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Terms, 1994) This elaboration of the psychoanalytic concepts of narcissism and the self, was developed by Heinz Kohut, and stresses the importance of the self-awareness of excessive needs for approval and self-gratification.

heartfailure,systolic.name: heart failure , systolic
heartfailure,systolic.definition: Systolic heart failure is heart failure caused by abnormal [MASK] during systole leading to defective cardiac emptying.

visualacuity.name: visual acuity
visualacuity.definition: Visual acuity is clarity or sharpness of ocular vision or the ability of the eye to see fine details. Visual acuity depends on the functions of retina, neuronal transmission, and the interpretative ability of the brain. Normal visual acuity is expressed as 20/20 indicating that one can see at 20 [MASK] what should normally be seen at that distance. Visual acuity can also be influenced by brightness, [MASK], and contrast.

cathepsinh.name: cathepsin h
cathepsinh.definition: Cathepsin h is an ubiquitously-expressed lysosomal [MASK] protease that is involved in protein processing. The enzyme has both endopeptidase and aminopeptidase activities.

midlinethalamicnuclei.name: midline thalamic nuclei
midlinethalamicnuclei.definition: Midline thalamic nuclei is small, nonspecific nerve cells scattered in the periventricular gray matter, separating the medial part of the thalamus from the ependyma of the third ventricle. The group includes the paraventricular nucleus, paratenial nucleus, reuniens nucleus, rhomboidal nucleus, and subfascular nucleus.

periodcircadianproteins.name: period circadian proteins
periodcircadianproteins.definition: Period circadian proteins is circadian rhythm signaling proteins that influence circadian clock by interacting with other circadian regulatory proteins and transporting them into the cell nucleus.

goldcolloid.name: gold colloid
goldcolloid.definition: Gold colloid is a suspension of metallic gold particles.

earlydiagnosis.name: early diagnosis
earlydiagnosis.definition: Early diagnosis is methods to determine in patients the nature of a disease or disorder at its early stage of progression. Generally, early diagnosis improves prognosis and treatment outcome.

mucus.name: mucus
mucus.definition: Mucus is the viscous secretion of mucous membranes. It contains mucin, [MASK] blood cells, water, inorganic [MASK], and exfoliated cells.

patternrecognition,physiological.name: pattern recognition , physiological
patternrecognition,physiological.definition: Physiological pattern recognition is the analysis of a critical number of sensory stimuli or facts (the pattern) by physiological processes such as vision (pattern recognition, visual), touch, or hearing.

catalog,commercial.name: catalog , commercial
catalog,commercial.definition: Commercial catalog is lists of merchandise for sale.

ribosomesubunits,large,eukaryotic.name: ribosome subunits , large , eukaryotic
ribosomesubunits,large,eukaryotic.definition: Eukaryotic large ribosome subunits is the large subunit of the 80s ribosome of eukaryotes. It is composed of the 28s [MASK], the 5.8s [MASK], the 5s [MASK], and about 50 different ribosomal proteins.

anxietydisorders.name: anxiety disorders
anxietydisorders.definition: Anxiety disorders is persistent and disabling anxiety.

airconditioning.name: air conditioning
airconditioning.definition: Air conditioning is the maintenance of certain aspects of the environment within a defined space to facilitate the function of that space; aspects controlled include air temperature and motion, radiant heat level, moisture, and concentration of pollutants such as dust, microorganisms, and gases. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

geneticcode.name: genetic code
geneticcode.definition: Genetic code is the meaning ascribed to the base sequence with respect to how it is translated into amino acid sequence. The start, stop, and order of amino acids of a protein is specified by consecutive triplets of nucleotides called codons (codon).

electronicdataprocessing.name: electronic data processing
electronicdataprocessing.definition: Electronic data processing is applications that store and process large quantities of data.

receptors,oxytocin.name: receptors , oxytocin
receptors,oxytocin.definition: Oxytocin receptors is cell surface proteins that bind oxytocin with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Oxytocin receptors in the uterus and the mammary glands mediate the hormone's stimulation of contraction and milk ejection. The presence of oxytocin and oxytocin receptors in neurons of the brain probably reflects an additional role as a neurotransmitter.

kidneytubules.name: kidney tubules
kidneytubules.definition: Kidney tubules is long convoluted tubules in the nephrons. They collect filtrate from blood passing through the kidney glomerulus and process this filtrate into urine. Each renal tubule consists of a bowman capsule; proximal kidney tubule; loop of henle; distal kidney tubule; and kidney collecting duct leading to the central cavity of the kidney ([MASK]) that connects to the ureter.

plateletaggregationinhibitors.name: platelet aggregation inhibitors
plateletaggregationinhibitors.definition: [MASK] inhibitors is drugs or agents which antagonize or impair any mechanism leading to blood [MASK], whether during the phases of activation and shape change or following the dense-granule release reaction and stimulation of the prostaglandin-thromboxane system.

respiratorysystem.name: respiratory system
respiratorysystem.definition: Respiratory system is the tubular and cavernous organs and structures, by means of which pulmonary ventilation and gas exchange between ambient air and the blood are brought about.

suppressorofcytokinesignalingproteins.name: suppressor of cytokine signaling proteins
suppressorofcytokinesignalingproteins.definition: Suppressor of cytokine signaling proteins is a family of structurally related proteins that are induced by cytokines and negatively regulate cytokine-mediated signal transduction pathways. socs proteins contain a central sh2 domain and a C-terminal region of homology known as the socs box.

accesstoinformation.name: access to information
accesstoinformation.definition: Access to information is individual's rights to obtain and use information collected or generated by others.

urinarysphincter,artificial.name: urinary sphincter , artificial
urinarysphincter,artificial.definition: Artificial urinary sphincter is an artifical implanted device, usually in the form of an inflatable silicone cuff, inserted in or around the [MASK] [MASK] in the surgical treatment of urinary incontinence caused by sphincter weakness. Often it is placed around the bulbous urethra in adult males. The artificial urinary sphincter is considered an alternative to urinary diversion.

insulin.name: insulin
insulin.definition: Insulin is a 51-amino acid pancreatic hormone that plays a major role in the regulation of glucose metabolism, directly by suppressing endogenous glucose production (glycogenolysis; gluconeogenesis) and indirectly by suppressing glucagon secretion and lipolysis. Native insulin is a globular protein comprised of a zinc-coordinated hexamer. Each insulin monomer containing two chains, a (21 residues) and b (30 residues), linked by two disulfide bonds. Insulin is used as a drug to control insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (diabetes mellitus, type 1).

patientparticipation.name: patient participation
patientparticipation.definition: Patient participation is patient involvement in the decision-making process in matters pertaining to health.

languagearts.name: language arts
languagearts.definition: Language arts is skills in the use of language which lead to proficiency in written or spoken communication.

childcare.name: child care
childcare.definition: Child care is care of children in the home or in an institution.

cathepsink.name: cathepsin k
cathepsink.definition: Cathepsin k is a [MASK] protease that is highly expressed in osteoclasts and plays an essential role in bone resorption as a potent extracellular MATRIX-degrading enzyme.

academicfailure.name: academic failure
academicfailure.definition: Academic failure is student’s unsuccessful attempt at academic achievement or a marked inadequacy in the areas of scholarship or study. This is not underachievement which is performance, usually in school work, poorer than that predicted from aptitude and/or intelligence testing.

millerfishersyndrome.name: miller fisher syndrome
millerfishersyndrome.definition: Miller fisher syndrome is a variant of the guillain-barre syndrome characterized by the acute onset of oculomotor dysfunction, ataxia, and loss of deep tendon reflexes with relative sparing of strength in the extremities and trunk. The ataxia is produced by peripheral sensory nerve dysfunction and not by cerebellar injury. Facial weakness and sensory loss may also occur. The process is mediated by autoantibodies directed against a component of myelin found in peripheral nerves. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1313; Neurology 1987 Sep;37(9):1493-8)

nuclearreceptorsubfamily2,groupc,member1.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 2 , group c , member 1
nuclearreceptorsubfamily2,groupc,member1.definition: Member 1 group c nuclear receptor subfamily 2 is a DNA-binding orphan nuclear receptor that has specificity for directly repeated (dr) aggtca sequences. It binds dna as either as a homodimer or as a heterodimer with the closely-related orphan nuclear receptor nuclear receptor subfamily 2, group c, member 2. The protein was originally identified as a PROSTATE-specific protein and is involved in the regulation of variety of cellular processes, including cell differentiation; cell proliferation; and apoptosis.

exons.name: exons
exons.definition: Exons is the parts of a transcript of a split gene remaining after the introns are removed. They are spliced together to become a messenger rna or other functional rna.

acids.name: acids
acids.definition: Acids is chemical compounds which yield hydrogen ions or protons when dissolved in water, whose hydrogen can be replaced by metals or basic radicals, or which react with bases to form [MASK] and water (neutralization). An extension of the term includes substances dissolved in media other than water. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

microspheres.name: microspheres
microspheres.definition: Microspheres is small uniformly-sized spherical particles, of micrometer dimensions, frequently labeled with radioisotopes or various reagents acting as tags or markers.

socialfacilitation.name: social facilitation
socialfacilitation.definition: Social facilitation is any enhancement of a motivated behavior in which individuals do the same thing with some degree of mutual stimulation and consequent coordination.

carrierstate.name: carrier state
carrierstate.definition: Carrier state is the condition of harboring an infective organism without manifesting symptoms of infection. The organism must be readily transmissible to another susceptible host.

personalconstructtheory.name: personal construct theory
personalconstructtheory.definition: Personal construct theory is a psychological theory based on dimensions or categories used by a given person in describing or explaining the personality and behavior of others or of himself. The basic idea is that different people will use consistently different categories. The theory was formulated in the fifties by George Kelly. Two tests devised by him are the role construct repertory test and the repertory grid test. (From Stuart Sutherland, The International Dictionary of Psychology, 1989)

polysaccharides.name: polysaccharides
polysaccharides.definition: Polysaccharides is a large molecule made of many smaller monosaccharides. Monosaccharides are simple sugars, like glucose.

hospitals,chronicdisease.name: hospitals , chronic disease
hospitals,chronicdisease.definition: Chronic disease hospitals is hospitals which provide care to patients with long-term illnesses.

internationalcooperation.name: international cooperation
internationalcooperation.definition: International cooperation is the interaction of persons or groups of persons representing various nations in the pursuit of a common goal or interest.

nutritionassessment.name: nutrition assessment
nutritionassessment.definition: Nutrition assessment is evaluation and measurement of nutritional variables in order to assess the level of nutrition or the [MASK] of the individual. nutrition surveys may be used in making the assessment.

cardiovascularagents.name: cardiovascular agents
cardiovascularagents.definition: Cardiovascular agents is agents that affect the rate or intensity of cardiac contraction, blood vessel diameter, or blood volume.

publicationcomponents.name: publication components
publicationcomponents.definition: Publication components is specific parts of publications.

nitrogencompounds.name: nitrogen compounds
nitrogencompounds.definition: Nitrogen compounds is inorganic compounds that contain nitrogen as an integral part of the molecule.

saliva,artificial.name: saliva , artificial
saliva,artificial.definition: Artificial saliva is a solution used for irrigating the mouth in xerostomia and as a substitute for saliva.

incometax.name: income tax
incometax.definition: Income tax is tax on the net income of an individual, organization, or business.

seizures,febrile.name: seizures , febrile
seizures,febrile.definition: Febrile seizures is seizures that occur during a febrile episode. It is a common condition, affecting 2-5% of children aged 3 months to five years. An autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance has been identified in some families. The majority are simple febrile seizures (generally defined as generalized onset, single seizures with a duration of less than 30 minutes). Complex febrile seizures are characterized by focal onset, duration greater than 30 minutes, and/or more than one seizure in a 24 hour period. The likelihood of developing epilepsy (i.e., a nonfebrile seizure disorder) following simple febrile seizures is low. Complex febrile seizures are associated with a moderately increased incidence of epilepsy. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p784)

chromosomes,mammalian.name: chromosomes , mammalian
chromosomes,mammalian.definition: Mammalian chromosomes is complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic dna and are part of the cell nucleus of mammals.

relaxationtherapy.name: relaxation therapy
relaxationtherapy.definition: Relaxation therapy is treatment to improve one's health condition by using techniques that can reduce physiological stress; psychological stress; or both.

matingfactor.name: mating factor
matingfactor.definition: Mating factor is a protein also known as pheromone mating factor that occurs on the surfaces of organisms such as yeast and fungi.

toothloss.name: tooth loss
toothloss.definition: Tooth loss is the failure to retain teeth as a result of disease or injury.

environmentalpsychology.name: environmental psychology
environmentalpsychology.definition: Environmental psychology is the field that studies interactions between individuals and the built and natural environment. It includes investigating behaviors that inhibit or foster sustainable, climate-healthy, and nature-enhancing choices.

stemcellniche.name: stem cell niche
stemcellniche.definition: Stem cell niche is a particular zone of tissue composed of a specialized microenvironment where stem cells are retained in a undifferentiated, self-renewable state.

orbitalfractures.name: orbital fractures
orbitalfractures.definition: Orbital fractures is fractures of the bones in the [MASK], which include parts of the frontal, ethmoidal, lacrimal, and sphenoid bones and the maxilla and zygoma.

liverfailure,acute.name: liver failure , acute
liverfailure,acute.definition: Acute liver failure is a form of rapid-onset liver failure, also known as fulminant hepatic failure, caused by severe liver injury or massive loss of [MASK]. It is characterized by sudden development of liver dysfunction and jaundice. Acute liver failure may progress to exhibit cerebral dysfunction even hepatic coma depending on the etiology that includes hepatic ischemia, drug toxicity, malignant infiltration, and viral hepatitis such as post-transfusion hepatitis b and hepatitis c.

defensemechanisms.name: defense mechanisms
defensemechanisms.definition: Defense mechanisms is [MASK] process used by an individual or a group of individuals in order to cope with impulses, feelings or ideas which are not acceptable at their conscious level; various types include reaction formation, [MASK] and self reversal.

moleculardockingsimulation.name: molecular docking simulation
moleculardockingsimulation.definition: Molecular docking simulation is a computer simulation technique that is used to model the interaction between two molecules. Typically the docking simulation measures the interactions of a small molecule or ligand with a part of a larger molecule such as a protein.

noblegases.name: noble gases
noblegases.definition: Noble gases is elements that constitute group 18 (formerly the zero group) of the periodic [MASK]. They are gases that generally do not react chemically.

lungdiseases,fungal.name: lung diseases , fungal
lungdiseases,fungal.definition: Fungal lung diseases is pulmonary diseases caused by fungal infections, usually through hematogenous spread.

financing,government.name: financing , government
financing,government.definition: Government financing is federal, state, or local government organized methods of financial assistance.

cellmembrane.name: cell membrane
cellmembrane.definition: Cell membrane is the lipid- and protein-containing, selectively permeable membrane that surrounds the cytoplasm in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

implants,experimental.name: implants , experimental
implants,experimental.definition: Experimental implants is artificial substitutes for [MASK] and materials inserted into organisms during experimental studies.

infectiousdiseasemedicine.name: infectious disease medicine
infectiousdiseasemedicine.definition: Infectious disease medicine is a branch of internal medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases.

entity.name: entity
entity.definition: Entity is an independent thing; that which contains in itself all the conditions essential to individuality; that which forms of itself a complete whole; medically, denoting a separate and distinct disease or condition.

analyticsamplepreparationmethods.name: analytic sample preparation methods
analyticsamplepreparationmethods.definition: Analytic sample preparation methods is use of various chemical separation and extraction methods, such as solid phase extraction; chromatography; and supercritical fluid extraction; to prepare samples for analytical measurement of components.

contraception.name: contraception
contraception.definition: Contraception is prevention of conception by blocking fertility temporarily, or permanently (sterilization, reproductive). Common means of reversible contraception include natural family planning methods; contraceptive agents; or contraceptive devices.

grouppractice.name: group practice
grouppractice.definition: Group practice is any group of three or more full-time physicians organized in a legally recognized entity for the provision of health care services, sharing space, equipment, personnel and records for both patient care and business management, and who have a predetermined arrangement for the distribution of income.

hospitals,grouppractice.name: hospitals , group practice
hospitals,grouppractice.definition: Group practice hospitals is hospitals organized and controlled by a group of physicians who practice together and provide each other with mutual support.

populationsurveillance.name: population surveillance
populationsurveillance.definition: Population surveillance is ongoing scrutiny of a population (general population, study population, target population, etc.), generally using methods distinguished by their practicability, uniformity, and frequently their rapidity, rather than by complete accuracy.

skindiseases,genetic.name: skin diseases , genetic
skindiseases,genetic.definition: Genetic skin diseases is diseases of the skin with a genetic component, usually the result of various inborn errors of metabolism.

oligonucleotidearraysequenceanalysis.name: oligonucleotide array sequence analysis
oligonucleotidearraysequenceanalysis.definition: Oligonucleotide array sequence analysis is hybridization of a nucleic acid sample to a very large [MASK] of [MASK], which have been attached individually in columns and rows to a solid support, to determine a base sequence, or to detect variations in a gene sequence, gene expression, or for gene mapping.

axonaltransport.name: axonal transport
axonaltransport.definition: Axonal transport is the directed transport of organelles and molecules along nerve cell axons. Transport can be anterograde (from the cell body) or retrograde (toward the cell body). (Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 3d ed, pG3)

therapeuticocclusion.name: therapeutic occlusion
therapeuticocclusion.definition: Therapeutic occlusion is methods used to temporarily or permanently block the flow of body fluids through various ducts and tubules throughout the body, including blood vessels and lymphatic vessels such as by therapeutic embolization or [MASK].

registries.name: registries
registries.definition: Registries is the systems and processes involved in the establishment, support, management, and operation of registers, e.g., disease registers.

caspase14.name: caspase 14
caspase14.definition: Caspase 14 is a short pro-domain caspase that is almost exclusively expressed in the epidermis and may play a role in the differentiation of epidermal keratinocytes.

potassiummagnesiumaspartate.name: potassium magnesium aspartate
potassiummagnesiumaspartate.definition: Potassium magnesium aspartate is an intra-extracellular electrolyte exchange agent with a variety of effects.

immunity,humoral.name: immunity , humoral
