immunity,humoral.definition: Humoral immunity is antibody-mediated immune response. Humoral immunity is brought about by antibody formation, resulting from th2 cells activating b-lymphocytes, followed by complement activation.

searchengine.name: search engine
searchengine.definition: Search engine is software used to locate data or information stored in machine-readable form locally or at a distance such as an internet site.

patientacceptanceofhealthcare.name: patient acceptance of health care
patientacceptanceofhealthcare.definition: Patient acceptance of health care is patients' willingness to receive health care.

clopidogrel.name: clopidogrel
clopidogrel.definition: Clopidogrel is a ticlopidine analog and platelet purinergic p2y receptor antagonist that inhibits adenosine diphosphate-mediated [MASK]. It is used to prevent thromboembolism in patients with arterial occlusive diseases; myocardial infarction; stroke; or atrial fibrillation.

cornealopacity.name: corneal opacity
cornealopacity.definition: Corneal opacity is disorder occurring in the central or peripheral area of the cornea. The usual degree of transparency becomes relatively opaque.

mitochondria.name: mitochondria
mitochondria.definition: Mitochondria is semiautonomous, self-reproducing organelles that occur in the cytoplasm of all cells of most, but not all, eukaryotes. Each mitochondrion is surrounded by a double limiting membrane. The inner membrane is highly invaginated, and its projections are called cristae. Mitochondria are the sites of the reactions of oxidative phosphorylation, which result in the formation of atp. They contain distinctive ribosomes, transfer RNAs ([MASK] t rna synthetases; and elongation and termination factors. Mitochondria depend upon genes within the nucleus of the cells in which they reside for many essential messenger RNAs (rna, messenger). Mitochondria are believed to have arisen from [MASK] that established a symbiotic relationship with primitive protoeukaryotes. (King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

herbal.name: herbal
herbal.definition: Herbal is work such as books on herbs or plants usually describing their medicinal value. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

secondmessengersystems.name: second messenger systems
secondmessengersystems.definition: Second messenger systems is systems in which an intracellular signal is generated in response to an intercellular primary messenger such as a hormone or neurotransmitter. They are intermediate signals in cellular processes such as metabolism, secretion, contraction, phototransduction, and cell growth. Examples of second messenger systems are the adenyl cyclase-cyclic amp system, the phosphatidylinositol diphosphate-inositol triphosphate system, and the cyclic gmp system.

aneurysm.name: aneurysm
aneurysm.definition: Aneurysm is pathological outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of any blood vessel (arteries or veins) or the heart ([MASK]). It indicates a thin and weakened area in the wall which may later rupture. Aneurysms are classified by location, etiology, or other characteristics.

yolksac.name: yolk sac
yolksac.definition: Yolk sac is the first of four extra-embryonic membranes to form during embryogenesis. In reptiles and birds, it arises from endoderm and mesoderm to incorporate the [MASK] into the digestive tract for nourishing the embryo. In placental mammals, its nutritional function is vestigial; however, it is the source of intestinal mucosa; blood cells; and germ cells. It is sometimes called the vitelline sac, which should not be confused with the vitelline membrane of the egg.

pancreatitis,alcoholic.name: pancreatitis , alcoholic
pancreatitis,alcoholic.definition: Alcoholic pancreatitis is acute or chronic inflammation of the pancreas due to excessive alcohol drinking. Alcoholic pancreatitis usually presents as an acute episode but it is a chronic progressive disease in alcoholics.

biofilms.name: biofilms
biofilms.definition: Biofilms is encrustations formed from microbes (bacteria, algae, fungi, plankton, or protozoa) embedded in an extracellular polymeric substance matrix that is secreted by the microbes. They occur on body surfaces such as teeth (dental deposits); inanimate objects, and bodies of water. Biofilms are prevented from forming by treating surfaces with dentifrices; disinfectants; anti-infective agents; and anti-fouling agents.

plasmodium.name: plasmodium
plasmodium.definition: Plasmodium is a genus of protozoa that comprise the malaria parasites of mammals. Four species infect humans (although occasional infections with primate malarias may occur). These are plasmodium falciparum; plasmodium malariae; plasmodium ovale, and plasmodium vivax. Species causing infection in vertebrates other than man include: plasmodium berghei; plasmodium chabaudi; p. vinckei, and plasmodium yoelii in rodents; p. brasilianum, plasmodium cynomolgi; and plasmodium knowlesi in monkeys; and plasmodium gallinaceum in [MASK].

sequencedeletion.name: sequence deletion
sequencedeletion.definition: Sequence deletion is deletion of sequences of nucleic acids from the genetic material of an individual.

plantcells.name: plant cells
plantcells.definition: Plant cells is basic functional unit of plants.

pancreatitis.name: pancreatitis
pancreatitis.definition: Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas. Pancreatitis is classified as acute unless there are computed tomographic or endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatographic findings of chronic pancreatitis (International Symposium on Acute Pancreatitis, Atlanta, 1992). The two most common forms of acute pancreatitis are alcoholic pancreatitis and gallstone pancreatitis.

agegroup.name: age group
agegroup.definition: Age group is sersons classified by age from birth (infant, newborn) to octogenarians and older (aged, 80 and over).

deathdomainsuperfamily.name: death domain superfamily
deathdomainsuperfamily.definition: Death domain superfamily is a family of structurally-related protein interaction domains characterized by 6-helical closed bundle fold, with Greek key topology and an internal pseudo two-fold symmetry. Death-like domains occur in many proteins that are essential for apoptosis, including caspase recruitment domain containing proteins and death domain receptors.

hand.name: hand
hand.definition: Hand is the distal part of the [MASK] beyond the wrist in humans and primates, that includes the palm, fingers, and thumb.

drugtherapy,combination.name: drug therapy , combination
drugtherapy,combination.definition: [MASK] therapy is therapy with two or more separate preparations given for a combined effect.

lightning.name: lightning
lightning.definition: Lightning is an abrupt high-current electric discharge that occurs in the atmosphere and that has a path length ranging from hundreds of [MASK] to tens of miles. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

cytogeneticanalysis.name: cytogenetic analysis
cytogeneticanalysis.definition: Cytogenetic analysis is examination of chromosomes to diagnose, classify, screen for, or manage genetic diseases and abnormalities. Following preparation of the sample, karyotyping is performed and/or the specific chromosomes are analyzed.

dentalmarginaladaptation.name: dental marginal adaptation
dentalmarginaladaptation.definition: Dental marginal adaptation is the degree of approximation or fit of filling material or dental prosthetic to the tooth surface. a close marginal adaptation and seal at the interface is important for successful dental restorations.

dentalinstruments.name: dental instruments
dentalinstruments.definition: Dental instruments is hand-held tools or implements especially used by dental professionals for the performance of clinical tasks.

education,dental,graduate.name: education , dental , graduate
education,dental,graduate.definition: Graduate dental education is educational programs for dental graduates entering a specialty. They include formal specialty training as well as academic work in the clinical and basic dental sciences, and may lead to board certification or an advanced dental degree.

seoul.name: seoul
seoul.definition: Seoul is the capital of south korea.

unitedstatesofficeofresearchintegrity.name: united states office of research integrity
unitedstatesofficeofresearchintegrity.definition: United states office of research integrity is an office of the united states public health service organized in June 1992 to promote research integrity and investigate misconduct in research supported by the Public Health Service. It consolidates the Office of Scientific Integrity of the National Institutes of Health and the Office of [MASK] in the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health.

dna,ribosomal.name: dna , ribosomal
dna,ribosomal.definition: Ribosomal dna is dna sequences encoding [MASK] and the segments of dna separating the individual [MASK] genes, referred to as [MASK].

glycogenstoragediseasetypei.name: glycogen storage disease type i
glycogenstoragediseasetypei.definition: Glycogen storage disease type i is an autosomal recessive disease in which gene expression of glucose-6-phosphatase is absent, resulting in hypoglycemia due to lack of glucose production. Accumulation of glycogen in liver and kidney leads to organomegaly, particularly massive hepatomegaly. Increased concentrations of lactic acid and hyperlipidemia appear in the plasma. Clinical gout often appears in early childhood.

mice,inbredcftr.name: mice , inbred cftr
mice,inbredcftr.definition: Inbred cftr mice is a strain of mice widely studied as a model for cystic fibrosis. These mice are generated from embryonic stem cells in which the cftr (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) gene is inactivated by gene targeting. As a result, all mice have one copy of this altered gene in all their tissues. Mice homozygous for the disrupted gene exhibit many features common to young cystic fibrosis patients, including failure to thrive, meconium ileus, and alteration of mucous and serous glands.

hydrogen.name: hydrogen
hydrogen.definition: Hydrogen is the first chemical element in the periodic [MASK] with atomic symbol h, and atomic number 1. Protium (atomic weight 1) is by far the most common hydrogen isotope. Hydrogen also exists as the stable isotope deuterium (atomic weight 2) and the radioactive isotope tritium (atomic weight 3). Hydrogen forms into a diatomic molecule at room temperature and appears as a highly flammable colorless and odorless gas.

systemstheory.name: systems theory
systemstheory.definition: Systems theory is principles, models, and laws that apply to complex interrelationships and interdependencies of sets of linked components which form a functioning whole, a system. Any system may be composed of components which are systems in their own right (sub-systems), such as several organs within an individual organism.

computedtomographyangiography.name: computed tomography angiography
computedtomographyangiography.definition: Computed tomography angiography is a non-invasive method that uses a ct scanner for capturing images of blood vessels and tissues. a contrast material is injected, which helps produce detailed images that aid in diagnosing vascular diseases.

internationalclassificationoffunctioning.name: international classification of functioning , disability and health
internationalclassificationoffunctioning.definition: Disability and [MASK] classification of functioning is the [MASK] Organization's classification categories of health and health-related domains. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (icf) consists of two lists: a list of body functions and structure, and a list of domains of activity and participation. The icf also includes a list of environmental factors.

gingivaldiseases.name: gingival diseases
gingivaldiseases.definition: Gingival diseases is diseases involving the gingiva.

multilevelanalysis.name: multilevel analysis
multilevelanalysis.definition: Multilevel analysis is the statistical manipulation of hierarchically and non-hierarchically nested data. It includes clustered data, such as a sample of subjects within a group of schools. Prevalent in the social, behavioral sciences, and biomedical sciences, both linear and nonlinear regression models are applied.

nursingassessment.name: nursing assessment
nursingassessment.definition: Nursing assessment is evaluation of the nature and extent of nursing problems presented by a patient for the purpose of patient care planning.

internalribosomeentrysites.name: internal ribosome entry sites
internalribosomeentrysites.definition: Internal ribosome entry sites is sequences within messenger rna that enable protein translation initiation independent of 5' capped rna.

limitedenglishproficiency.name: limited english proficiency
limitedenglishproficiency.definition: Limited english proficiency is limited ability to communicate with or understand English.

socialenvironment.name: social environment
socialenvironment.definition: Social environment is the aggregate of social and cultural institutions, forms, patterns, and processes that influence the life of an individual or community.

elbowjoint.name: elbow joint
elbowjoint.definition: Elbow joint is a hinge joint connecting the forearm to the [MASK].

mammals.name: mammals
mammals.definition: Mammals is warm-blooded vertebrate animals belonging to the class Mammalia, including all that possess hair and suckle their young.

transduction,genetic.name: transduction , genetic
transduction,genetic.definition: Genetic transduction is the transfer of [MASK] by phages from an infected bacterium to another bacterium. This also refers to the transfer of genes into eukaryotic cells by viruses. This naturally occurring process is routinely employed as a gene transfer technique.

nestingbehavior.name: nesting behavior
nestingbehavior.definition: Nesting behavior is animal behavior associated with the nest; includes construction, effects of size and material; behavior of the adult during the nesting period and the effect of the nest on the behavior of the young.

spinalcordischemia.name: spinal cord ischemia
spinalcordischemia.definition: Spinal cord ischemia is reduced blood flow to the spinal cord which is supplied by the anterior spinal artery and the paired posterior spinal arteries. This condition may be associated with arteriosclerosis, trauma, emboli, diseases of the aorta, and other disorders. Prolonged ischemia may lead to infarction of spinal cord tissue.

surgicalequipment.name: surgical equipment
surgicalequipment.definition: Surgical equipment is nonexpendable apparatus used during surgical procedures. They are differentiated from surgical instruments, usually hand-held and used in the immediate operative field.

embolism,cholesterol.name: embolism , cholesterol
embolism,cholesterol.definition: Cholesterol embolism is blocking of a blood vessel by CHOLESTEROL-rich atheromatous deposits, generally occurring in the flow from a large artery to small arterial branches. It is also called arterial-arterial embolization or atheroembolism which may be spontaneous or iatrogenic. Patients with spontaneous atheroembolism often have painful, cyanotic digits of acute onset.

immunesystemdiseases.name: immune system diseases
immunesystemdiseases.definition: Immune system diseases is disorders caused by abnormal or absent immunologic mechanisms, whether humoral, cell-mediated, or both.

muscleproteins.name: muscle proteins
muscleproteins.definition: Muscle proteins is the protein constituents of muscle, the major ones being actins and myosins. More than a dozen accessory proteins exist including troponin; tropomyosin; and dystrophin.

ethics.name: ethics
ethics.definition: Ethics is the philosophy or code pertaining to what is ideal in human [MASK] and conduct. Also, the field of study dealing with the principles of morality.

unionlist.name: union list
unionlist.definition: Union list is works consisting of records of the holdings or items owned by two or more libraries.

colorvision.name: color vision
colorvision.definition: [MASK] vision is function of the human eye that is used in bright [MASK] or in daylight (at photopic intensities). Photopic vision is performed by the three types of [MASK] with varied peak absorption wavelengths in the [MASK] spectrum (from violet to red, 400 - 700 nm).

childdaycarecenters.name: child day care centers
childdaycarecenters.definition: Child day care centers is facilities which provide care for pre-school and school-age children.

bibliography,national.name: bibliography , national
bibliography,national.definition: National bibliography is a bibliography which lists all the books and other publications published, or distributed in significant quantity, in a particular country. Sometimes the term is used with respect to the new publications published within a specific period, and sometimes with respect to all those published within a lengthy period of many years. It is also used to indicate a bibliography of publications about a country (whether written by its nationals or not) and those written in the language of the country as well as those published in it. (Harrod's Librarians' Glossary, 7th ed)

pragmaticclinicaltrialsastopic.name: pragmatic clinical trials as topic
pragmaticclinicaltrialsastopic.definition: Pragmatic clinical trials as topic is works about randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

mandibularnerveinjuries.name: mandibular nerve injuries
mandibularnerveinjuries.definition: Mandibular nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the mandibular nerve and its branches. Note that marginal mandibular nerve injury is a type of facial nerve injuries. Injuries to lingual nerve branch of mandibular nerve is lingual nerve injuries.

receptors,estrogen.name: receptors , estrogen
receptors,estrogen.definition: Estrogen receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that bind estrogens and migrate to the nucleus where they regulate dna transcription. Evaluation of the state of estrogen receptors in breast cancer patients has become clinically important.

catalase.name: catalase
catalase.definition: Catalase is an oxidoreductase that catalyzes the conversion of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen. It is present in many animal cells. a deficiency of this enzyme results in acatalasia.

privacy.name: privacy
privacy.definition: Privacy is the state of being free from intrusion or disturbance in one's private life or affairs. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed, 1993)

pulmonaryembolism.name: pulmonary embolism
pulmonaryembolism.definition: Pulmonary embolism is blocking of the [MASK] or one of its branches by an embolus.

hotsprings.name: hot springs
hotsprings.definition: Hot springs is habitat of hot water naturally heated by underlying geologic processes. Surface hot springs have been used for balneology. Underwater hot springs are called hydrothermal vents.

lensplant.name: lens plant
lensplant.definition: Lens plant is a plant genus of the fabaceae family known for the [MASK] used as food.

pressure.name: pressure
pressure.definition: Pressure is a type of stress exerted uniformly in all directions. Its measure is the force exerted per unit area. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

dentalimpressiontechnique.name: dental impression technique
dentalimpressiontechnique.definition: Dental impression technique is procedure of producing an imprint or negative likeness of the teeth and/or edentulous areas. Impressions are made in plastic material which becomes hardened or [MASK] while in contact with the tissue. They are later filled with plaster of Paris or artificial stone to produce a facsimile of the oral structures present. Impressions may be made of a full complement of teeth, of areas where some teeth have been removed, or in a mouth from which all teeth have been extracted. (Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982)

escherichia.name: escherichia
escherichia.definition: Escherichia is a genus of gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria whose organisms occur in the lower part of the intestine of warm-blooded animals. The species are either nonpathogenic or opportunistic pathogens.

europeanunion.name: european union
europeanunion.definition: European union is the collective designation of three organizations with common membership: the European Economic Community (Common Market), the European Coal and Steel Community, and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom). It was known as the European Community until 1994. It is primarily an economic union with the principal objectives of free movement of goods, capital, and labor. Professional services, social, medical and paramedical, are subsumed under labor. The constituent countries are Austria, [MASK], Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, [MASK], Portugal, [MASK], Sweden, and the United Kingdom. (The World Almanac and Book of Facts 1997, p842)

caspase10.name: caspase 10
caspase10.definition: Caspase 10 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a [MASK] in its pro-domain region. Activation of this enzyme can occur via the interaction of its N-terminal [MASK] with death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins. Caspase 10 plays a role in apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases. Several isoforms of this protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its messenger rna.

chlorophyll.name: chlorophyll
chlorophyll.definition: Chlorophyll is porphyrin derivatives containing magnesium that act to convert light energy in photosynthetic organisms.

retinalphotoreceptorcellinnersegment.name: retinal photoreceptor cell inner segment
retinalphotoreceptorcellinnersegment.definition: Retinal photoreceptor cell inner segment is the inner portion of a retinal rod or a [MASK], situated between the photoreceptor connecting cilium and the synapse with the adjacent neurons (retinal bipolar cells; retinal horizontal cells). The inner segment contains the cell body, the nucleus, the mitochondria, and apparatus for protein synthesis.

patientharm.name: patient harm
patientharm.definition: Patient harm is a measure of patient safety considering errors or mistakes which result in harm to the patient. They include errors in the administration of drugs and other medications (medication errors), errors in the performance of procedures or the use of other types of therapy, in the use of equipment, and in the interpretation of laboratory findings and preventable accidents involving patients.

skullbaseneoplasms.name: skull base neoplasms
skullbaseneoplasms.definition: Skull base neoplasms is neoplasms of the base of the skull specifically, differentiated from neoplasms of unspecified sites or bones of the skull (skull neoplasms).

communitymentalhealthservices.name: community mental health services
communitymentalhealthservices.definition: Community mental health services is diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive mental health services provided for individuals in the community.

women,working.name: women , working
women,working.definition: Working women is women who are engaged in gainful activities usually outside the home.

genes,apc.name: genes , apc
genes,apc.definition: Apc genes is tumor suppressor genes located in the 5q21 region on the long [MASK] of human chromosome 5. The mutation of these genes is associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (adenomatous polyposis coli) and gardner syndrome, as well as some sporadic colorectal cancers.

simulationtraining.name: simulation training
simulationtraining.definition: Simulation training is a highly customized interactive medium or program that allows individuals to learn and practice real world activities in an accurate, realistic, safe and secure environment.

genes,transgenic,suicide.name: genes , transgenic , suicide
genes,transgenic,suicide.definition: Suicide transgenic genes is genes that are used transgenically, i.e., via gene transfer techniques to induce cell death.

neutrophilactivation.name: neutrophil activation
neutrophilactivation.definition: Neutrophil activation is the process in which the neutrophil is stimulated by diverse substances, resulting in degranulation and/or generation of reactive oxygen products, and culminating in the destruction of invading pathogens. The stimulatory substances, including opsonized particles, immune complexes, and chemotactic factors, bind to specific cell-surface receptors on the neutrophil.

dentindysplasia.name: dentin dysplasia
dentindysplasia.definition: Dentin dysplasia is an apparently hereditary disorder of dentin formation, marked by a normal appearance of coronal dentin associated with pulpal obliteration, faulty root formation, and a tendency for peripheral lesions without obvious cause. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

forensicdentistry.name: forensic dentistry
forensicdentistry.definition: Forensic dentistry is the application of dental knowledge to questions of law.

collection.name: collection
collection.definition: Collection is items gathered and assembled in some order to facilitate access or use.

absorption,radiation.name: absorption , radiation
absorption,radiation.definition: Radiation absorption is the uptake or transfer of energy from radiation.

pacificstates.name: pacific states
pacificstates.definition: Pacific states is the geographic designation for states bordering on or located in the Pacific Ocean. The states so designated are Alaska, California, [MASK], Oregon, and [MASK]. (u.s. Geologic Survey telephone communication)

osteoporosis.name: osteoporosis
osteoporosis.definition: Osteoporosis is reduction of bone mass without alteration in the composition of bone, leading to fractures. Primary osteoporosis can be of two major types: postmenopausal osteoporosis (osteoporosis, postmenopausal) and age-related or senile osteoporosis.

abortionapplicants.name: abortion applicants
abortionapplicants.definition: Abortion applicants is individuals requesting induced abortions.

nursingstations.name: nursing stations
nursingstations.definition: Nursing stations is an area in a clinic, unit, or ward in a health care facility that serves as the administrative center for nursing care. (from Mosby's Medical Dictionary, 8th ed)

microscopy,scanningprobe.name: microscopy , scanning probe
microscopy,scanningprobe.definition: Scanning probe microscopy is scanning microscopy in which a very sharp probe is employed in close proximity to a surface, exploiting a particular surface-related property. When this property is local topography, the method is [MASK] ([MASK]), and when it is local conductivity, the method is [MASK] ([MASK]).

pelvicinflammatorydisease.name: pelvic inflammatory disease
pelvicinflammatorydisease.definition: Pelvic inflammatory disease is a spectrum of inflammation involving the female upper genital tract and the supporting tissues. It is usually caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix. Infection may be confined to the uterus (endometritis), the fallopian tubes; (salpingitis); the ovaries (oophoritis), the supporting ligaments (parametritis), or may involve several of the above uterine appendages. Such inflammation can lead to functional impairment and infertility.

livercirrhosis,biliary.name: liver cirrhosis , biliary
livercirrhosis,biliary.definition: Biliary liver cirrhosis is fibrosis of the hepatic parenchyma due to obstruction of [MASK] flow (cholestasis) in the intrahepatic or extrahepatic [MASK] ([MASK], intrahepatic; [MASK], extrahepatic). Primary biliary cholangitis involves the destruction of small intra-hepatic [MASK] and decreased [MASK] secretion. Secondary biliary cholangitis is produced by prolonged obstruction of large intrahepatic or extrahepatic [MASK] from a variety of causes.

clonalevolution.name: clonal evolution
clonalevolution.definition: Clonal evolution is the process of accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes over time in individual cells and the effect of the changes on cell proliferation.

armbones.name: arm bones
armbones.definition: [MASK] bones is the bones of the free part of the upper extremity including the humerus; [MASK]; and ulna.

chemicalphenomena.name: chemical phenomena
chemicalphenomena.definition: Chemical phenomena is the composition, structure, conformation, and properties of atoms and molecules, and their reaction and interaction processes.

diseasemodels,animal.name: disease models , animal
diseasemodels,animal.definition: Animal disease models is naturally-occurring or experimentally-induced animal diseases with pathological processes analogous to human diseases.

opticaldevices.name: optical devices
opticaldevices.definition: Optical devices is products or parts of products used to detect, manipulate, or analyze light, such as lenses, refractors, mirrors, filters, prisms, and optical fibers.

healthinformationmanagement.name: health information management
healthinformationmanagement.definition: Health information management is management of the acquisition, organization, retrieval, and dissemination of health information.

polymorphism,genetic.name: polymorphism , genetic
polymorphism,genetic.definition: Genetic polymorphism is the regular and simultaneous occurrence in a single interbreeding population of two or more discontinuous genotypes. The concept includes differences in genotypes ranging in size from a single nucleotide site (polymorphism, single nucleotide) to large nucleotide sequences visible at a chromosomal level.

subcellularfractions.name: subcellular fractions
subcellularfractions.definition: Subcellular fractions is components of a cell produced by various separation techniques which, though they disrupt the delicate anatomy of a cell, preserve the structure and physiology of its functioning constituents for biochemical and ultrastructural analysis. (From Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2d ed, p163)

seasons.name: seasons
seasons.definition: Seasons is divisions of the year according to some regularly recurrent phenomena usually astronomical or climatic. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

5'flankingregion.name: 5 ' flanking region
5'flankingregion.definition: 5' flanking region is the region of DNA which borders the 5' end of a transcription unit and where a variety of regulatory sequences are located.

time.name: time
time.definition: Time is the dimension of the physical universe which, at a given place, orders the sequence of events. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

physicaltherapydepartment,hospital.name: physical therapy department , hospital
physicaltherapydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital physical therapy department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration and provision of diagnostic and medical rehabilitation services to restore or improve the functional capacity of the patient.

adrenalglanddiseases.name: adrenal gland diseases
adrenalglanddiseases.definition: Adrenal gland diseases is pathological processes of the adrenal glands.

pollentube.name: pollen tube
pollentube.definition: Pollen tube is a growth from a pollen grain down into the flower style which allows two sperm to pass, one to the ovum within the ovule, and the other to the central cell of the ovule to produce endosperm of [MASK].

pubmed.name: pubmed
pubmed.definition: Pubmed is a bibliographic [MASK] that includes medline as its primary subset. It is produced by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (ncbi), part of the national library of medicine. PubMed, which is searchable through NLM's Web site, also includes access to additional citations to selected life sciences journals not in medline, and links to other resources such as the full-text of articles at participating publishers' Web sites, NCBI's molecular biology databases, and PubMed Central.

thymusneoplasms.name: thymus neoplasms
thymusneoplasms.definition: Thymus neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the thymus gland.

extracellularspace.name: extracellular space
extracellularspace.definition: Extracellular space is interstitial space between cells, occupied by interstitial fluid as well as amorphous and fibrous substances. For organisms with a cell wall, the extracellular space includes everything outside of the cell membrane including the periplasm and the cell wall.

sweden.name: sweden
sweden.definition: Sweden is country in northern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea, between Finland and Norway. The capital is Stockholm.

chronictraumaticencephalopathy.name: chronic traumatic encephalopathy
chronictraumaticencephalopathy.definition: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is degenerative brain disease linked to repetitive brain trauma. Progressive symptoms may include memory loss; aggression; or depression.

bacterialsecretionsystems.name: bacterial secretion systems
bacterialsecretionsystems.definition: Bacterial secretion systems is in gram negative bacteria, multiprotein complexes that function to translocate pathogen protein effector molecules across the bacterial cell envelope, often directly into the host. These effectors are involved in producing surface structures for adhesion, bacterial motility, manipulation of host functions, modulation of host defense responses, and other functions involved in facilitating survival of the pathogen. Several of the systems have homologous components functioning similarly in gram positive bacteria.

saltgland.name: salt gland
saltgland.definition: [MASK] gland is a compound tubular gland, located around the eyes and nasal passages in marine animals and birds, the physiology of which figures in water-electrolyte balance. The Pekin duck serves as a common research animal in [MASK] gland studies. a rectal gland or rectal [MASK] gland in the dogfish shark is attached at the junction of the intestine and cloaca and aids the kidneys in removing excess [MASK] from the blood. (Storer, Usinger, Stebbins & Nybakken: General Zoology, 6th ed, p658)

docetaxel.name: docetaxel
docetaxel.definition: Docetaxel is a semisynthetic analog of paclitaxel used in the treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast neoplasms and non-small cell lung cancer.

africanhorsesickness.name: african horse sickness
africanhorsesickness.definition: African horse sickness is an insect-borne reovirus infection of horses, mules and donkeys in Africa and the Middle East; characterized by [MASK], cardiac involvement, and edema of the head and [MASK].

resuscitation.name: resuscitation
resuscitation.definition: Resuscitation is the restoration to life or consciousness of one apparently dead. (Dorland, 27th ed)

hospitals,teaching.name: hospitals , teaching
hospitals,teaching.definition: Teaching hospitals is hospitals engaged in educational and research programs, as well as providing medical care to the patients.

dosageforms.name: dosage forms
dosageforms.definition: Dosage forms is completed forms of the pharmaceutical preparation in which prescribed doses of medication are included. They are designed to resist action by gastric fluids, prevent vomiting and nausea, reduce or alleviate the undesirable taste and smells associated with oral administration, achieve a high concentration of drug at target site, or produce a delayed or long-acting drug effect.

psychology,industrial.name: psychology , industrial
psychology,industrial.definition: Industrial psychology is the branch of applied psychology concerned with the application of psychologic principles and methods to industrial problems including selection and training of workers, working conditions, etc.

ambientintelligence.name: ambient intelligence
ambientintelligence.definition: Ambient intelligence is an emerging paradigm in which people are empowered through intelligent (digital) tools embedded in the surrounding environment. These tools proactively support human existence by being sensitive, adaptive, and responsive to the needs, habits, gestures, and emotions of individuals.

governmentprograms.name: government programs
governmentprograms.definition: Government programs is programs and activities sponsored or administered by local, state, or national governments.

timeout,healthcare.name: time out , healthcare
timeout,healthcare.definition: Healthcare time out is a period of time away from normal [MASK] taken to ensure key procedural details have been reviewed for better patient safety and help prevent medical errors.

neoplasms,connectivetissue.name: neoplasms , connective tissue
neoplasms,connectivetissue.definition: Connective tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of connective tissue, including elastic, mucous, reticular, osseous, and cartilaginous tissue. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in connective tissue.

wrist.name: wrist
wrist.definition: Wrist is the region of the upper limb between the metacarpus and the forearm.

moleculartyping.name: molecular typing
moleculartyping.definition: Molecular typing is using molecular biology techniques, such as dna sequence analysis; pulsed-field gel electrophoresis; and dna fingerprinting, to identify, classify, and compare organisms and their subtypes.

sulfuroxides.name: sulfur oxides
sulfuroxides.definition: Sulfur oxides is inorganic oxides of sulfur.

myocytes,smoothmuscle.name: myocytes , smooth muscle
myocytes,smoothmuscle.definition: Smooth muscle myocytes is non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cells found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They are derived from specialized myoblasts (myoblasts, smooth muscle).

diseasenotification.name: disease notification
diseasenotification.definition: Disease notification is notification or reporting by a physician or other health care provider of the occurrence of specified contagious diseases such as tuberculosis and hiv infections to designated public health agencies. The United States system of reporting notifiable diseases evolved from the Quarantine Act of 1878, which authorized the us Public Health Service to collect morbidity data on cholera, smallpox, and yellow fever; each state in the us has its own list of notifiable diseases and depends largely on reporting by the individual health care provider. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

behavioraldisciplinesandactivities.name: behavioral disciplines and activities
behavioraldisciplinesandactivities.definition: Behavioral disciplines and activities is the specialties in psychiatry and psychology, their diagnostic techniques and tests, their therapeutic methods, and psychiatric and psychological services.

bileductdiseases.name: bile duct diseases
bileductdiseases.definition: [MASK] diseases is diseases in any part of the ductal system of the biliary tract from the smallest [MASK] canaliculi to the largest common [MASK].

calciumcompounds.name: calcium compounds
calciumcompounds.definition: Calcium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain calcium as an integral part of the molecule.

behavioralriskfactorsurveillancesystem.name: behavioral risk factor surveillance system
behavioralriskfactorsurveillancesystem.definition: Behavioral risk factor surveillance system is telephone surveys are conducted to monitor [MASK] of the major behavioral risks among adults associated with premature morbidity and mortality. The data collected is in regard to actual behaviors, rather than on attitudes or knowledge. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (cdc) established the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (brfss) in 1984.

carotidarteries.name: carotid arteries
carotidarteries.definition: Carotid arteries is either of the two principal arteries on both sides of the [MASK] that supply blood to the head and [MASK]; each divides into two branches, the internal carotid artery and the external carotid artery.

foodhandling.name: food handling
foodhandling.definition: Food handling is any aspect of the operations in the preparation, processing, transport, storage, packaging, wrapping, exposure for sale, service, or delivery of food.

dnapolymerasei.name: dna polymerase i
dnapolymerasei.definition: Dna polymerase i is a DNA-dependent dna polymerase characterized in prokaryotes and may be present in higher organisms. It has both 3'-5' and 5'-3' exonuclease activity, but cannot use native double-stranded dna as template-primer. It is not inhibited by sulfhydryl reagents and is active in both dna synthesis and repair.

primarycarenursing.name: primary care nursing
primarycarenursing.definition: Primary care nursing is techniques or methods of patient care used by nurses as primary careproviders.

medicationadherence.name: medication adherence
medicationadherence.definition: Medication adherence is voluntary cooperation of the patient in taking drugs or medicine as prescribed. This includes timing, dosage, and frequency.

doubleoutletrightventricle.name: double outlet right ventricle
doubleoutletrightventricle.definition: Double outlet right ventricle is incomplete transposition of the great vessels in which both the aorta and the [MASK] arise from the right ventricle. The only outlet of the left ventricle is a large ventricular septal defect (ventricular septal defects or vsd). The various subtypes are classified by the location of the septal defect, such as subaortic, subpulmonary, or noncommitted.

hospitalbedcapacity,100to299.name: hospital bed capacity , 100 to 299
hospitalbedcapacity,100to299.definition: 100 to 299 hospital bed capacity is hospital bed capacity , 100 to 299

burnunits.name: burn units
burnunits.definition: Burn units is specialized hospital facilities which provide intensive care for burn patients.

nitratereductase.name: nitrate reductase
nitratereductase.definition: Nitrate reductase is an enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of nitrite to nitrate. It is a cytochrome protein that contains iron and molybdenum.

zincoxide.name: zinc oxide
zincoxide.definition: Zinc oxide is a mild astringent and topical protectant with some antiseptic action. It is also used in bandages, pastes, ointments, dental cements, and as a sunblock.

fungi.name: fungi
fungi.definition: Fungi is a kingdom of eukaryotic, heterotrophic organisms that live parasitically as saprobes, including mushrooms; yeasts; smuts, molds, etc. They reproduce either sexually or asexually, and have [MASK] that range from simple to complex. Filamentous fungi, commonly known as molds, refer to those that grow as multicellular colonies.

cellfractionation.name: cell fractionation
cellfractionation.definition: Cell fractionation is techniques to partition various components of the cell into subcellular fractions.

respiratoryprotectivedevices.name: respiratory protective devices
respiratoryprotectivedevices.definition: Respiratory protective devices is respirators to protect individuals from breathing air contaminated with harmful dusts, fogs, fumes, mists, gases, smokes, sprays, or vapors.

lipoproteins.name: lipoproteins
lipoproteins.definition: Lipoproteins is lipid-protein complexes involved in the transportation and metabolism of lipids in the body. They are spherical particles consisting of a hydrophobic core of triglycerides and cholesterol esters surrounded by a layer of hydrophilic free cholesterol; [MASK]; and apolipoproteins. Lipoproteins are classified by their varying buoyant density and sizes.

electrophoresis,polyacrylamidegel.name: electrophoresis , polyacrylamide gel
electrophoresis,polyacrylamidegel.definition: Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which a polyacrylamide gel is used as the diffusion medium.

culturalevolution.name: cultural evolution
culturalevolution.definition: Cultural evolution is the continuous developmental process of a culture from simple to complex forms and from homogeneous to heterogeneous qualities. It is the change of cultures over time. Research in cultural evolution tries to understand the causal relationships that shape and change human culture in both the long and the short term.

comparativestudy.name: comparative study
comparativestudy.definition: Comparative study is comparison of outcomes, results, responses, etc for different techniques, therapeutic approaches or other inputs.

students,nursing.name: students , nursing
students,nursing.definition: Nursing students is individuals enrolled in a school of nursing or a formal educational program leading to a degree in nursing.

decisiontrees.name: decision trees
decisiontrees.definition: Decision trees is a graphic device used in decision analysis, series of decision options are represented as branches (hierarchical).

glasgowcomascale.name: glasgow coma scale
glasgowcomascale.definition: Glasgow coma scale is a scale that assesses the response to stimuli in patients with craniocerebral injuries. The parameters are eye opening, motor response, and verbal response.

popularwork.name: popular work
popularwork.definition: Popular work is work written for non-professional or lay audiences.

pyruvatekinase.name: pyruvate kinase
pyruvatekinase.definition: Pyruvate kinase is aTP:pyruvate 2-O-phosphotransferase. a phosphotransferase that catalyzes reversibly the phosphorylation of pyruvate to phosphoenolpyruvate in the presence of atp. It has four isozymes (l, r, m1, and m2). Deficiency of the enzyme results in hemolytic anemia. ec 2.7.1.40.

methyleneblue.name: methylene blue
methyleneblue.definition: Methylene blue is a compound consisting of dark green crystals or crystalline powder, having a bronze-like luster. Solutions in water or alcohol have a deep blue [MASK]. Methylene blue is used as a bacteriologic stain and as an indicator. It inhibits guanylate cyclase, and has been used to treat cyanide poisoning and to lower levels of methemoglobin.

foodquality.name: food quality
foodquality.definition: Food quality is ratings of the characteristics of food including flavor, appearance, nutritional content, and the amount of microbial and chemical contamination.

anesthesia,rectal.name: anesthesia , rectal
anesthesia,rectal.definition: Rectal anesthesia is procedure involving the instillation of an anesthetic into the rectum.

professionalcorporations.name: professional corporations
professionalcorporations.definition: Professional corporations is legally authorized corporations owned and managed by one or more professionals (medical, dental, legal) in which the income is ascribed primarily to the professional activities of the owners or stockholders.

stromalcells.name: stromal cells
stromalcells.definition: Stromal cells is connective tissue cells of an organ found in the loose connective tissue. These are most often associated with the uterine mucosa and the ovary as well as the hematopoietic system and elsewhere.

orthodonticappliances,functional.name: orthodontic appliances , functional
orthodonticappliances,functional.definition: Functional orthodontic appliances is loose, usually removable intra-oral devices which alter the muscle forces against the teeth and craniofacial skeleton. These are dynamic appliances which depend on altered neuromuscular action to effect bony growth and occlusal development. They are usually used in mixed dentition to treat pediatric malocclusions. (ada, 1992)

glycogensynthase.name: glycogen synthase
glycogensynthase.definition: Glycogen synthase is an enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of D-glucose from UDPglucose into 1,4-alpha-D-glucosyl chains. ec 2.4.1.11.

morphologicalandmicroscopicfindings.name: morphological and microscopic findings
morphologicalandmicroscopicfindings.definition: Morphological and microscopic findings is morphological findings useful in differentiation and classification of results in cytodiagnosis and related techniques.

costcontrol.name: cost control
costcontrol.definition: Cost control is the containment, regulation, or restraint of costs. Costs are said to be contained when the value of resources committed to an activity is not considered excessive. This determination is frequently subjective and dependent upon the specific geographic area of the activity being measured. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

aminoacids,cyclic.name: amino acids , cyclic
aminoacids,cyclic.definition: Cyclic amino acids is a class of amino acids characterized by a closed ring structure.

epithelialcelladhesionmolecule.name: epithelial cell adhesion molecule
epithelialcelladhesionmolecule.definition: Epithelial cell adhesion molecule is a cell adhesion molecule that is expressed on the membranes of nearly all epithelial cells, especially at the junctions between intestinal epithelial cells and intraepithelial lymphocytes. It also is expressed on the surface of adenocarcinoma and epithelial tumor cells.  It may function in the mucosa through homophilic interactions to provide a barrier against infection. It also regulates the proliferation and differentiation of embryonic stem cells.

maternalinheritance.name: maternal inheritance
maternalinheritance.definition: Maternal inheritance is transmission of genetic [MASK], qualities, and traits, solely from maternal extra-nuclear elements such as mitochondrial dna or maternal messenger rna.

proteinc.name: protein c
proteinc.definition: Protein c is a vitamin-K dependent zymogen present in the blood, which, upon activation by thrombin and thrombomodulin exerts anticoagulant properties by inactivating factors Va and VIIIa at the rate-limiting steps of thrombin formation.

substance.name: substance
substance.definition: Substance is the material that makes up an organ or structure.

clinicallaboratoryservices.name: clinical laboratory services
clinicallaboratoryservices.definition: Clinical laboratory services is organized services provided by medical laboratory personnel for the purpose of carrying out clinical laboratory techniques used for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

dna,neoplasm.name: dna , neoplasm
dna,neoplasm.definition: Neoplasm dna is dna present in neoplastic tissue.

geneticbackground.name: genetic background
geneticbackground.definition: Genetic background is the entire genetic composition of a strain or individual that interacts with a gene of interest.

chemicalviewedstructurally.name: chemical viewed structurally
chemicalviewedstructurally.definition: Chemical viewed structurally is chemical viewed structurally

organismattribute.name: organism attribute
organismattribute.definition: Organism attribute is properties or features belonging to living organisms.

genitalneoplasms,male.name: genital neoplasms , male
genitalneoplasms,male.definition: Male genital neoplasms is tumor or cancer of the male genitalia.

nodalsignalingligands.name: nodal signaling ligands
nodalsignalingligands.definition: Nodal signaling ligands is members of the transforming growth factor superfamily that play a role in pattern formation and differentiation during the pregastrulation and gastrulation stages of chordate development. Several nodal signaling ligands are specifically involved in the genesis of left-right asymmetry during development. The protein group is named after a critical region of the vertebrate embryo primitive streak referred to as hensen's node.

syntheticdrugs.name: synthetic drugs
syntheticdrugs.definition: Synthetic drugs is legal or illegal drugs created using synthetic chemistry techniques.

structurecollapse.name: structure collapse
structurecollapse.definition: Structure collapse is failure in built environment with loss of functional integrity.

legislation,nursing.name: legislation , nursing
legislation,nursing.definition: Nursing legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of nursing, proposed for enactment by a legislative body.

epoxycompounds.name: epoxy compounds
epoxycompounds.definition: Epoxy compounds is organic compounds that include a cyclic ether with three ring atoms in their structure. They are commonly used as precursors for polymers such as epoxy resins.

exercisetherapy.name: exercise therapy
exercisetherapy.definition: Exercise therapy is a regimen or plan of physical activities designed and prescribed for specific therapeutic goals. Its purpose is to restore normal musculoskeletal function or to reduce pain caused by diseases or injuries.

healthbehavior.name: health behavior
healthbehavior.definition: Health behavior is combination of health knowledge, attitudes, practice which underlie actions taken by individuals regarding their health.

tooth,artificial.name: tooth , artificial
tooth,artificial.definition: Artificial tooth is a fabricated tooth substituting for a natural tooth in a prosthesis. It is usually made of porcelain or plastic.

activatorappliances.name: activator appliances
activatorappliances.definition: Activator appliances is loose-fitting removable orthodontic appliances which redirect the pressures of the facial and masticatory muscles onto the teeth and their supporting structures to produce improvements in tooth arrangements and occlusal relations.

monitoring,ambulatory.name: monitoring , ambulatory
monitoring,ambulatory.definition: Ambulatory monitoring is the use of electronic equipment to observe or record physiologic processes while the patient undergoes normal daily activities.

selfcare.name: self care
selfcare.definition: Self care is [MASK] for self when ill or positive actions and adopting behaviors to prevent illness.

viralinterference.name: viral interference
viralinterference.definition: Viral interference is a phenomenon in which infection by a first virus results in resistance of cells or tissues to infection by a second, unrelated virus.

elasticity.name: elasticity
elasticity.definition: Elasticity is resistance and recovery from distortion of shape.

pertussisvaccine.name: pertussis vaccine
pertussisvaccine.definition: Pertussis vaccine is a suspension of killed Bordetella pertussis organisms, used for immunization against pertussis (whooping [MASK]). It is generally used in a mixture with diphtheria and tetanus toxoids (dtp). There is an acellular pertussis vaccine prepared from the purified antigenic components of Bordetella pertussis, which causes fewer adverse reactions than whole-cell vaccine and, like the whole-cell vaccine, is generally used in a mixture with diphtheria and tetanus toxoids. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

ireland.name: ireland
ireland.definition: Ireland is a country in western Europe, occupying five-sixths of the island of Ireland in the North Atlantic Ocean, west of Great Britain. The capital is Dublin.

conservationofwaterresources.name: conservation of water resources
conservationofwaterresources.definition: Conservation of water resources is preservation and or management of water resources especially under conditions of scarce supply.

cervicalplexusblock.name: cervical plexus block
cervicalplexusblock.definition: Cervical plexus block is a blocking of [MASK] in the network of nerve fibers innervating the [MASK] and [MASK].

headachedisorders.name: headache disorders
headachedisorders.definition: Headache disorders is various conditions with the symptom of headache. Headache disorders are classified into major groups, such as primary headache disorders (based on characteristics of their headache symptoms) and [MASK] (based on their etiologies). (International Classification of Headache Disorders, 2nd ed. Cephalalgia 2004: suppl 1)

dictionary,classical.name: dictionary , classical
dictionary,classical.definition: Classical dictionary is a reference work containing a list of words related to the Greco-Roman World giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

thymicfactor,circulating.name: thymic factor , circulating
thymicfactor,circulating.definition: Circulating thymic factor is a thymus-dependent nonapeptide found in normal blood. Stimulates the formation of e rosettes and is believed to be involved in T-cell differentiation.

occupationordiscipline.name: occupation or discipline
occupationordiscipline.definition: Occupation or discipline is allied health profession which requires formal training, leading to a recognised professional qualification.

socialcontrolpolicies.name: social control policies
socialcontrolpolicies.definition: Social control policies is decisions for determining and guiding present and future objectives from among alternatives.

anteriorhorncells.name: anterior horn cells
anteriorhorncells.definition: Anterior horn cells is motor neurons in the anterior (ventral) horn of the spinal cord which project to skeletal muscles.

fusionregulatoryprotein1,lightchains.name: fusion regulatory protein 1 , light chains
fusionregulatoryprotein1,lightchains.definition: Light chains fusion regulatory protein 1 is a family of light chains that bind to fusion regulatory protein 1, heavy chain to form a heterodimer. They convey functional specificity to the protein.

fishdiseases.name: fish diseases
fishdiseases.definition: Fish diseases is diseases of freshwater, marine, hatchery or aquarium fish. This term includes diseases of both teleosts (true fish) and elasmobranchs (sharks, rays and skates).

selfefficacy.name: self efficacy
selfefficacy.definition: Self efficacy is cognitive mechanism based on expectations or beliefs about one's ability to perform actions necessary to produce a given effect. It is also a theoretical component of behavior change in various therapeutic treatments. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

dietarysucrose.name: dietary sucrose
dietarysucrose.definition: Dietary sucrose is sucrose present in the diet. It is added to food and drinks as a sweetener.

tertiaryhealthcare.name: tertiary healthcare
tertiaryhealthcare.definition: Tertiary healthcare is care of a highly technical and specialized nature, provided in a medical center, usually one affiliated with a university, for patients with unusually severe, complex, or uncommon health problems.

workofbreathing.name: work of breathing
workofbreathing.definition: Work of breathing is respiratory muscle contraction during [MASK]. The work is accomplished in three phases: lung compliance work, that required to expand the lungs against its elastic forces; tissue resistance work, that required to overcome the [MASK] of the lung and chest wall structures; and airway resistance work, that required to overcome airway resistance during the movement of air into the lungs. Work of breathing does not refer to expiration, which is entirely a passive process caused by elastic recoil of the lung and chest cage. (Guyton, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 8th ed, p406)

qualityimprovement.name: quality improvement
qualityimprovement.definition: Quality improvement is the attainment or process of attaining a new level of performance or quality.

methods.name: methods
methods.definition: Methods is a series of steps taken in order to conduct research.

diagnosticservices.name: diagnostic services
diagnosticservices.definition: Diagnostic services is organized services for the purpose of providing diagnosis to promote and maintain health.

medicineinliterature.name: medicine in literature
medicineinliterature.definition: Medicine in literature is written or other literary works whose subject matter is medical or about the profession of medicine and related areas.

selfadministration.name: self administration
selfadministration.definition: Self administration is administration of a drug or chemical by the individual under the direction of a physician. It includes administration clinically or experimentally, by human or animal.

foreignmedicalgraduates.name: foreign medical graduates
foreignmedicalgraduates.definition: Foreign medical graduates is physicians who hold degrees from medical schools in countries other than the ones in which they practice.

mechanistictargetofrapamycincomplex1.name: mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1
mechanistictargetofrapamycincomplex1.definition: Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 is an evolutionarily conserved multiprotein complex that functions as a cellular energy sensor and regulator of protein synthesis for cell growth and proliferation. It consists of tor serine-threonine kinases; regulatory-associated protein of mtor (raptor); mlst8 protein; and akt1 substrate 1 protein. The activity of the complex is regulated by sirolimus; insulin; growth factors; phosphatidic acids; some amino acids or amino acid derivatives, and oxidative stress.

immunoassay.name: immunoassay
immunoassay.definition: Immunoassay is a technique using antibodies for identifying or quantifying a substance. Usually the substance being studied serves as antigen both in antibody production and in measurement of antibody by the test substance.

lungdiseases,parasitic.name: lung diseases , parasitic
lungdiseases,parasitic.definition: Parasitic lung diseases is infections of the lungs with parasites, most commonly by parasitic worms (helminths).

serumresponsefactor.name: serum response factor
serumresponsefactor.definition: Serum response factor is a mads domain-containing transcription factor that binds to the [MASK] in the promoter-enhancer region of many genes. It is one of the four founder proteins that structurally define the superfamily of mads domain proteins.

multiplemyeloma.name: multiple myeloma
multiplemyeloma.definition: Multiple myeloma is a malignancy of mature plasma cells engaging in monoclonal immunoglobulin production. It is characterized by hyperglobulinemia, excess Bence-Jones proteins (free monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains) in the urine, skeletal destruction, bone pain, and fractures. Other features include anemia; hypercalcemia; and renal insufficiency.

receptors,thyroidhormone.name: receptors , thyroid hormone
receptors,thyroidhormone.definition: Thyroid hormone receptors is specific high affinity binding proteins for thyroid hormones in target cells. They are usually found in the nucleus and regulate dna transcription. These receptors are activated by hormones that leads to transcription, cell differentiation, and growth suppression. Thyroid hormone receptors are encoded by two genes (genes, erba): erbA-alpha and erbA-beta for alpha and beta thyroid hormone receptors, respectively.

heartrate,fetal.name: heart rate , fetal
heartrate,fetal.definition: Fetal heart rate is the heart rate of the fetus. The normal range at term is between 120 and 160 beats per minute.

eyeabnormalities.name: eye abnormalities
eyeabnormalities.definition: Eye abnormalities is congenital absence of or defects in structures of the eye; may also be hereditary.

researchdesign.name: research design
researchdesign.definition: Research design is a plan for collecting and utilizing data so that desired information can be obtained with sufficient precision or so that an hypothesis can be tested properly.

axillaryartery.name: axillary artery
axillaryartery.definition: Axillary artery is the continuation of the subclavian artery; it distributes over the upper limb, axilla, chest and [MASK].

outcomeandprocessassessment,healthcare.name: outcome and process assessment , health care
outcomeandprocessassessment,healthcare.definition: Health care outcome and [MASK] is evaluation procedures that focus on both the outcome or status (outcomes assessment) of the patient at the end of an episode of care - presence of symptoms, level of activity, and mortality; and the [MASK], process) - what is done for the patient diagnostically and therapeutically.

umbilicalcord.name: umbilical cord
umbilicalcord.definition: Umbilical cord is the flexible rope-like structure that connects a developing fetus to the placenta in mammals. The cord contains blood vessels which carry oxygen and nutrients from the mother to the fetus and waste products away from the fetus.

helicobacterpylori.name: helicobacter pylori
helicobacterpylori.definition: Helicobacter pylori is a spiral bacterium active as a human gastric pathogen. It is a gram-negative, urease-positive, curved or slightly spiral organism initially isolated in 1982 from patients with lesions of gastritis or peptic [MASK] in Western Australia. Helicobacter pylori was originally classified in the genus campylobacter, but rna sequencing, cellular fatty acid profiles, growth patterns, and other taxonomic characteristics indicate that the micro-organism should be included in the genus helicobacter. It has been officially transferred to Helicobacter gen. nov. (see Int j Syst Bacteriol 1989 Oct;39(4):297-405).

cadmiumcompounds.name: cadmium compounds
cadmiumcompounds.definition: Cadmium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain cadmium as an integral part of the molecule.

ventriculardysfunction,right.name: ventricular dysfunction , right
ventriculardysfunction,right.definition: Right ventricular dysfunction is a condition in which the right ventricle of the heart was functionally impaired. This condition usually leads to heart failure or myocardial infarction, and other cardiovascular complications. Diagnosis is made by measuring the diminished ejection fraction and a depressed level of motility of the right ventricular wall.

bacterialshedding.name: bacterial shedding
bacterialshedding.definition: Bacterial shedding is the expelling of bacteria from the body. Important routes include the respiratory tract, genital tract, and intestinal tract.

conversiontoopensurgery.name: conversion to open surgery
conversiontoopensurgery.definition: Conversion to open surgery is changing an operative procedure from an endoscopic surgical procedure to an open approach during the intraoperative period.

aviansarcomaviruses.name: avian sarcoma viruses
aviansarcomaviruses.definition: [MASK] viruses is group of alpharetroviruses (alpharetrovirus) producing sarcomata and other tumors in [MASK] and other fowl and also in pigeons, ducks, and rats.

erythrocyteinclusions.name: erythrocyte inclusions
erythrocyteinclusions.definition: Erythrocyte inclusions is pathologic inclusions occurring in erythrocytes.

publishing.name: publishing
publishing.definition: Publishing is "The business or profession of the commercial production and issuance of literature" (Webster's 3d). It includes the publisher, publication processes, editing and editors. Production may be by conventional printing methods or by electronic publishing.

iodinecompounds.name: iodine compounds
iodinecompounds.definition: Iodine compounds is inorganic compounds that contain iodine as an integral part of the molecule.

mentalorbehavioraldysfunction.name: mental or behavioral dysfunction
mentalorbehavioraldysfunction.definition: Mental or behavioral dysfunction is troublesome or disruptive behavioral displays.

backmuscles.name: back muscles
backmuscles.definition: Back muscles is musculature of the back.

contraceptiveagents.name: contraceptive agents
contraceptiveagents.definition: Contraceptive agents is chemical substances that prevent or reduce the probability of conception.

neoplasmsbysite.name: neoplasms by site
neoplasmsbysite.definition: Neoplasms by site is a collective term for precoordinated organ/neoplasm headings locating neoplasms by organ, as brain [MASK] neoplasms; liver neoplasms; etc.

gelatin.name: gelatin
gelatin.definition: Gelatin is a product formed from skin, [MASK] connective tissue, or bone collagen. It is used as a protein food adjuvant, plasma substitute, hemostatic, suspending agent in pharmaceutical preparations, and in the manufacturing of capsules and suppositories.

awareness.name: awareness
awareness.definition: Awareness is the act of "taking account" of an object or state of affairs. It does not imply assessment of, nor attention to the qualities or nature of the object.

anaerobicthreshold.name: anaerobic threshold
anaerobicthreshold.definition: Anaerobic threshold is the oxygen consumption level above which aerobic energy production is supplemented by anaerobic mechanisms during exercise, resulting in a sustained increase in lactate concentration and metabolic acidosis. The anaerobic threshold is affected by factors that modify oxygen delivery to the tissues; it is low in patients with heart disease. Methods of measurement include direct measure of lactate concentration, direct measurement of bicarbonate concentration, and gas exchange measurements.

suspensions.name: suspensions
suspensions.definition: Suspensions is colloids with liquid continuous phase and solid dispersed phase; the term is used loosely also for solid-in-gas (aerosols) and other colloidal systems; water-insoluble drugs may be given as suspensions.

fishproteins.name: fish proteins
fishproteins.definition: Fish proteins is proteins obtained from species of fish (fishes).

binomialdistribution.name: binomial distribution
binomialdistribution.definition: Binomial distribution is the probability distribution associated with two mutually exclusive outcomes; used to model cumulative incidence rates and [MASK] rates. The Bernoulli distribution is a special case of binomial distribution.

iron.name: iron
iron.definition: Iron is a metallic element with atomic symbol Fe, atomic number 26, and atomic weight 55.85. It is an essential constituent of hemoglobins; cytochromes; and iron-binding proteins. It plays a role in cellular redox reactions and in the transport of oxygen.

cytoplasmicstreaming.name: cytoplasmic streaming
cytoplasmicstreaming.definition: Cytoplasmic streaming is the movement of cytoplasm within a cell. It serves as an internal transport system for moving essential substances throughout the cell, and in single-celled organisms, such as the amoeba, it is responsible for the movement (cell movement) of the entire cell.

genes,tumorsuppressor.name: genes , tumor suppressor
genes,tumorsuppressor.definition: Tumor suppressor genes is genes that inhibit expression of the tumorigenic phenotype. They are normally involved in holding cellular growth in check. When tumor suppressor genes are inactivated or lost, a barrier to normal proliferation is removed and unregulated growth is possible.

headachedisorders,primary.name: headache disorders , primary
headachedisorders,primary.definition: Primary headache disorders is conditions in which the primary symptom is headache and the headache cannot be attributed to any known causes.

creatinekinase.name: creatine kinase
creatinekinase.definition: Creatine kinase is a transferase that catalyzes formation of phosphocreatine from atp + creatine. The reaction stores atp energy as phosphocreatine. Three cytoplasmic isoenzymes have been identified in human tissues: the mm type from skeletal muscle, the mb type from myocardial tissue and the bb type from nervous tissue as well as a mitochondrial isoenzyme. Macro-creatine kinase refers to creatine kinase complexed with other serum proteins.

lymphocytecount.name: lymphocyte count
lymphocytecount.definition: Lymphocyte count is the number of lymphocytes per unit volume of blood.

oocytes.name: oocytes
oocytes.definition: Oocytes is female germ cells derived from oogonia and termed oocytes when they enter meiosis. The primary oocytes begin meiosis but are arrested at the diplotene state until ovulation at puberty to give rise to haploid secondary oocytes or ova (ovum).

eggwhite.name: egg white
eggwhite.definition: Egg [MASK] is the [MASK] of an egg, especially a [MASK]'s egg, used in cooking. It contains albumin. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

berlin.name: berlin
berlin.definition: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

permeability.name: permeability
permeability.definition: Permeability is property of membranes and other structures to permit passage of light, heat, gases, liquids, metabolites, and mineral ions.

alaninedehydrogenase.name: alanine dehydrogenase
alaninedehydrogenase.definition: [MASK] dehydrogenase is an NAD-dependent enzyme that catalyzes the reversible deamination of [MASK] to pyruvate and [MASK]. The enzyme is needed for growth when [MASK] is the sole carbon or nitrogen source. It may also play a role in cell wall synthesis because [MASK] is an important constituent of the peptidoglycan layer.

rna,transfer,trp.name: rna , transfer , trp
rna,transfer,trp.definition: Trp transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying tryptophan to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

bodytemperatureregulation.name: body temperature regulation
bodytemperatureregulation.definition: Body temperature regulation is the processes of [MASK] and cooling that an organism uses to control its temperature.

surgicalclearance.name: surgical clearance
surgicalclearance.definition: Surgical clearance is process of evaluating the health of a patient and determining if they are healthy enough for surgery.

nervoussystemdiseases.name: nervous system diseases
nervoussystemdiseases.definition: Nervous system diseases is diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. This includes disorders of the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, peripheral nerves, nerve roots, autonomic nervous system, neuromuscular junction, and muscle.

dialysissolutions.name: dialysis solutions
dialysissolutions.definition: Dialysis solutions is solutions prepared for exchange across a semipermeable membrane of solutes below a molecular size determined by the cutoff threshold of the membrane material.

absorption,physiological.name: absorption , physiological
absorption,physiological.definition: Physiological absorption is uptake of substances by the body, tissues, or cells. The uptake may occur by various forms of biological transport or by simple diffusion.

replicatechniques.name: replica techniques
replicatechniques.definition: Replica techniques is methods of preparing tissue specimens for visualization using an [MASK] microscope, usually a scanning [MASK] microscope. The methods involve the creation of exact copies of the specimens by making a mold or cast (i.e., replica) of the specimen.

allostericregulation.name: allosteric regulation
allostericregulation.definition: Allosteric regulation is the modification of the reactivity of enzymes by the binding of effectors to sites (allosteric sites) on the enzymes other than the substrate binding sites.

vibration.name: vibration
vibration.definition: Vibration is a continuing periodic change in displacement with respect to a fixed reference. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

mooddisorders.name: mood disorders
mooddisorders.definition: Mood disorders is those disorders that have a disturbance in mood as their predominant feature.

substanceabuse,intravenous.name: substance abuse , intravenous
substanceabuse,intravenous.definition: Intravenous substance abuse is abuse, overuse, or misuse of a substance by its injection into a vein.

dielectricspectroscopy.name: dielectric spectroscopy
dielectricspectroscopy.definition: Dielectric spectroscopy is a technique of measuring the dielectric properties of materials, which vary over a range of frequencies depending on the physical properties of the material. The technique involves measuring, over a range of frequencies, electrical impedance and phase shift of an electric field as it passes through the material.

cerebrovasculartrauma.name: cerebrovascular trauma
cerebrovasculartrauma.definition: Cerebrovascular trauma is penetrating and nonpenetrating traumatic injuries to an extracranial or intracranial blood vessel that supplies the brain. This includes the carotid arteries; vertebral arteries; meningeal arteries; cerebral arteries; veins, and venous sinuses.

laboratories.name: laboratories
laboratories.definition: Laboratories is facilities equipped to carry out investigative procedures.

hospitals,federal.name: hospitals , federal
hospitals,federal.definition: Federal hospitals is hospitals controlled by agencies and departments of the u.s. federal government.

triggerfingerdisorder.name: trigger finger disorder
triggerfingerdisorder.definition: Trigger finger disorder is a painful disability in the hand affecting the finger or thumb. It is caused by mechanical impingement of the digital flexor tendons as they pass through a narrowed retinacular pulley at the level of the metacarpal head. Thickening of the sheath and fibrocartilaginous metaplasia can occur, and nodules can form. (From Green's Operative Hand Surgery, 5th ed, p2137-58).

healthplanning.name: health planning
healthplanning.definition: Health planning is planning for needed health and/or welfare services and facilities.

tuberculosis,hepatic.name: tuberculosis , hepatic
tuberculosis,hepatic.definition: Hepatic tuberculosis is infection of the liver with species of mycobacterium, most often [MASK]. It is characterized by localized small tuberculous miliary lesions or tumor-like mass (tuberculoma), and abnormalities in liver function tests.

consensusdevelopmentconferences,nihastop.name: consensus development conferences , nih as topic
consensusdevelopmentconferences,nihastop.definition: Nih as topic [MASK] conferences is articles on conferences sponsored by nih presenting summary statements representing the majority agreement of physicians, scientists, and other professionals convening for the purpose of reaching a [MASK] on a subject of interest. This heading is used for nih [MASK] conferences as a means of scientific communication. In indexing it is viewed as a type of review article and as a tag for any article appearing in any publication of the nih Office of Medical Applications of Research (omar).

polyt.name: poly t
polyt.definition: Poly t is a group of thymine nucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each thymine nucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the deoxyribose moieties.

celldeath.name: cell death
celldeath.definition: Cell death is the termination of the cell's ability to carry out vital functions such as metabolism, growth, reproduction, responsiveness, and adaptability.

ethics,medical.name: ethics , medical
ethics,medical.definition: Medical ethics is the principles of professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the physician, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the physician in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families.

cornealinjuries.name: corneal injuries
cornealinjuries.definition: Corneal injuries is damage or trauma inflicted to the cornea by external means.

mapkinasekinase3.name: map kinase kinase 3
mapkinasekinase3.definition: Map kinase kinase 3 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for a subset of p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases that includes mitogen-activated protein kinase 12; mitogen-activated protein kinase 13; and mitogen-activated protein kinase 14.

italy.name: italy
italy.definition: Italy is a country in southern Europe, a peninsula extending into the central Mediterranean Sea, northeast of Tunisia. The capital is Rome.

internationaleducationalexchange.name: international educational exchange
internationaleducationalexchange.definition: International educational exchange is the exchange of students or professional personnel between countries done under the auspices of an organization for the purpose of further education.

phosphorylation.name: phosphorylation
phosphorylation.definition: Phosphorylation is the introduction of a phosphoryl group into a compound through the formation of an ester bond between the compound and a phosphorus moiety.

salmonellainfections,animal.name: salmonella infections , animal
salmonellainfections,animal.definition: Animal salmonella infections is infections in animals with bacteria of the genus salmonella.

aaadomain.name: aaa domain
aaadomain.definition: Aaa domain is an approximately 250 amino acid domain common to aaa ATPases and aaa Proteins.
