It consists of a highly conserved N-terminal P-Loop ATPase subdomain with an alpha-beta-alpha conformation, and a less-conserved C-terminal subdomain with an all alpha conformation. The N-terminal subdomain includes Walker a and Walker b motifs which function in atp binding and hydrolysis.

geographicinformationsystems.name: geographic information systems
geographicinformationsystems.definition: Geographic information systems is computer systems capable of assembling, storing, manipulating, and displaying geographically referenced information, i.e. data identified according to their locations.

outliers,drg.name: outliers , drg
outliers,drg.definition: Drg outliers is in health care reimbursement, especially in the prospective payment system, those patients who require an unusually long hospital stay or whose stay generates unusually high costs.

patientprotectionandaffordablecareact.name: patient protection and affordable care act
patientprotectionandaffordablecareact.definition: Patient protection and affordable care act is an Act prohibiting a health plan from establishing lifetime limits or annual limits on the dollar value of benefits for any participant or beneficiary after January 1, 2014. It permits a restricted annual limit for plan years beginning prior to January 1, 2014. It provides that a health plan shall not be prevented from placing annual or lifetime per-beneficiary limits on covered benefits. The Act sets up a competitive health insurance market.

nursingassistants.name: nursing assistants
nursingassistants.definition: Nursing assistants is a person who has completed a brief health care training program and who provides support services for RNs and LPNs.

focalinfection.name: focal infection
focalinfection.definition: Focal infection is an infection at a specific location that may spread to another region of the body.

tidalvolume.name: tidal volume
tidalvolume.definition: Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during each normal, quiet respiratory cycle. Common abbreviations are tv or v with subscript t.

hazardouswaste.name: hazardous waste
hazardouswaste.definition: Hazardous waste is waste products which threaten life, health, or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, disposed of, or otherwise managed.

ophthalmicnerve.name: ophthalmic nerve
ophthalmicnerve.definition: Ophthalmic nerve is a sensory branch of the trigeminal (5th cranial) nerve. The ophthalmic nerve carries general afferents from the superficial division of the face including the eyeball, conjunctiva, upper eyelid, upper nose, nasal mucosa, and scalp.

urinarycatheters.name: urinary catheters
urinarycatheters.definition: Urinary catheters is catheters inserted into the [MASK] or kidney for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

interview.name: interview
interview.definition: Interview is work consisting of a conversation with an individual regarding his or her background and other personal and professional details, opinions on specific subjects posed by the interviewer, etc.

linguistics.name: linguistics
linguistics.definition: Linguistics is the science of language, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, and historical linguistics. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

ventricularseptalrupture.name: ventricular septal rupture
ventricularseptalrupture.definition: Ventricular septal rupture is laceration or tearing of the ventricular septum, usually caused by myocardial infarction.

insecthormones.name: insect hormones
insecthormones.definition: Insect hormones is hormones secreted by insects. They influence their growth and development. Also synthetic substances that act like insect hormones.

educationdepartment,hospital.name: education department , hospital
educationdepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital education department is hospital department responsible for administering educational and training activities pertaining to health for patients and staff.

intraoperativeperiod.name: intraoperative period
intraoperativeperiod.definition: Intraoperative period is the period during a surgical operation.

hematopoieticstemcellmobilization.name: hematopoietic stem cell mobilization
hematopoieticstemcellmobilization.definition: Hematopoietic stem cell mobilization is the release of stem cells from the bone marrow into the peripheral blood circulation for the purpose of leukapheresis, prior to stem cell transplantation. Hematopoietic growth factors or chemotherapeutic agents often are used to stimulate the mobilization.

cardiaccarefacilities.name: cardiac care facilities
cardiaccarefacilities.definition: Cardiac care facilities is institutions specializing in the care of patients with heart disorders.

tuberculosis,laryngeal.name: tuberculosis , laryngeal
tuberculosis,laryngeal.definition: Laryngeal tuberculosis is tuberculosis involving the larynx, producing ulceration of the vocal cords and the [MASK].

pediatricnursepractitioners.name: pediatric nurse practitioners
pediatricnursepractitioners.definition: Pediatric nurse practitioners is registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to pediatric patients who are acutely or [MASK].

veins.name: veins
veins.definition: Veins is the vessels carrying blood away from the capillary beds.

ecologicalandenvironmentalphenomena.name: ecological and environmental phenomena
ecologicalandenvironmentalphenomena.definition: Ecological and environmental phenomena is ecological and environmental entities, characteristics, properties, relationships and processes.

clinicalstudiesastopic.name: clinical studies as topic
clinicalstudiesastopic.definition: Clinical studies as topic is works about research studies that evaluate interventions or exposures on biomedical or health-related outcomes.  The two main types of clinical studies are interventional studies (clinical trials) and observational studies.

vitamind.name: vitamin d
vitamind.definition: Vitamin d is a vitamin that includes both cholecalciferols and ergocalciferols, which have the common effect of preventing or curing rickets in animals. It can also be viewed as a hormone since it can be formed in skin by action of ultraviolet rays upon the precursors, 7-dehydrocholesterol and ergosterol, and acts on vitamin d receptors to regulate calcium in opposition to parathyroid hormone.

eligibilitydetermination.name: eligibility determination
eligibilitydetermination.definition: Eligibility determination is criteria to determine eligibility of patients for medical care programs and services.

aminoacidtransportsystems,acidic.name: amino acid transport systems , acidic
aminoacidtransportsystems,acidic.definition: Acidic amino acid transport systems is amino acid transporter systems capable of transporting acidic amino acids (amino acids, acidic).

introducedspecies.name: introduced species
introducedspecies.definition: Introduced species is non-native organisms brought into a region, habitat, or ecosystem by human activity.

dataaccuracy.name: data accuracy
dataaccuracy.definition: Data accuracy is a measure of scientific precision, exactness, or correctness of quantitative or qualitative values, relative to the actual or true measurements.

translations.name: translations
translations.definition: Translations is products resulting from the conversion of one language to another.

nursinghomes.name: nursing homes
nursinghomes.definition: Nursing homes is facilities which provide nursing supervision and limited medical care to persons who do not require hospitalization.

receptors,aminoacid.name: receptors , amino acid
receptors,aminoacid.definition: Amino acid receptors is cell surface proteins that bind amino acids and trigger changes which influence the behavior of cells. [MASK] are the most common receptors for fast excitatory synaptic transmission in the vertebrate central nervous system, and gamma-aminobutyric acid and [MASK] are the most common receptors for fast inhibition.

spintrapping.name: spin trapping
spintrapping.definition: Spin trapping is a technique for detecting short-lived reactive free radicals in biological systems by providing a nitrone or nitrose compound for an addition reaction to occur which produces an [MASK]-detectable aminoxyl radical. In spin trapping, the compound trapping the radical is called the spin trap and the addition product of the radical is identified as the spin adduct. (Free Rad Res Comm 1990;9(3-6):163)

nitratereductase(nad(p)h).name: nitrate reductase ( nad ( p ) h )
nitratereductase(nad(p)h).definition: Nitrate reductase (nad (p) h) is an ENZYME that catalyses the conversion of nitrite to ammonium hydroxide.

vaccines,synthetic.name: vaccines , synthetic
vaccines,synthetic.definition: Synthetic vaccines is small synthetic peptides that mimic surface antigens of pathogens and are immunogenic, or vaccines manufactured with the aid of [MASK] techniques. The latter vaccines may also be whole viruses whose nucleic acids have been modified.

spinalnerves.name: spinal nerves
spinalnerves.definition: Spinal nerves is the 31 paired peripheral nerves formed by the union of the dorsal and ventral spinal roots from each spinal cord segment. The spinal nerve plexuses and the spinal roots are also included.

decisiontheory.name: decision theory
decisiontheory.definition: Decision theory is a theoretical technique utilizing a group of related constructs to describe or prescribe how individuals or groups of people choose a course of action when faced with several alternatives and a variable amount of knowledge about the determinants of the outcomes of those alternatives.

crossreactions.name: cross reactions
crossreactions.definition: Cross reactions is serological reactions in which an antiserum against one antigen reacts with a non-identical but closely related antigen.

supervisedmachinelearning.name: supervised machine learning
supervisedmachinelearning.definition: Supervised machine learning is a machine learning paradigm used to make predictions about future instances based on a given [MASK] of labeled paired input-output training (sample) data.

neoplasticprocesses.name: neoplastic processes
neoplasticprocesses.definition: Neoplastic processes is the pathological mechanisms and forms taken by tissue during degeneration into a neoplasm and its subsequent activity.

drugpackaging.name: drug packaging
drugpackaging.definition: Drug packaging is containers, packaging, and packaging materials for drugs and biological products. These include those in ampule, capsule, tablet, solution or other forms. Packaging includes immediate-containers, secondary-containers, and cartons. In the United States, such packaging is controlled under the Federal [MASK] which also stipulates requirements for tamper-resistance and child-resistance. Similar laws govern use elsewhere. (From Code of Federal Regulations, 21 cfr 1 Section 210, 1993) drug labeling is also available.

marketingofhealthservices.name: marketing of health services
marketingofhealthservices.definition: Marketing of health services is application of marketing principles and techniques to maximize the use of health care resources.

membraneproteins.name: membrane proteins
membraneproteins.definition: Membrane proteins is proteins which are found in membranes including cellular and intracellular membranes. They consist of two types, peripheral and integral proteins. They include most membrane-associated enzymes, antigenic proteins, transport proteins, and drug, hormone, and lectin receptors.

lipids.name: lipids
lipids.definition: Lipids is a generic term for fats and lipoids, the alcohol-ether-soluble constituents of protoplasm, which are insoluble in water. They comprise the fats, fatty oils, essential oils, waxes, [MASK], glycolipids, sulfolipids, aminolipids, chromolipids (lipochromes), and fatty acids. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

endothelialgrowthfactors.name: endothelial growth factors
endothelialgrowthfactors.definition: Endothelial growth factors is these growth factors are soluble mitogens secreted by a variety of organs. The factors are a mixture of two single chain polypeptides which have affinity to heparin. Their molecular weight are organ and species dependent. They have mitogenic and chemotactic effects and can stimulate endothelial cells to grow and synthesize dna. The factors are related to both the basic and acidic fibroblast growth factors but have different amino acid sequences.

collagentypeiii.name: collagen type iii
collagentypeiii.definition: Collagen type iii is a fibrillar collagen consisting of three identical alpha1(III) chains that is widely distributed in many tissues containing collagen type i. It is particularly abundant in blood vessels and may play a role in tissues with elastic characteristics.

intermediatefilamentproteins.name: intermediate filament proteins
intermediatefilamentproteins.definition: [MASK] proteins is filaments 7-11 nm in diameter found in the cytoplasm of all cells. Many specific proteins belong to this group, e.g., desmin, vimentin, prekeratin, decamin, skeletin, neurofilin, [MASK] protein, and glial fibrillary acid protein.

sports.name: sports
sports.definition: Sports is activities or games, usually involving physical effort or skill. Reasons for engagement in sports include pleasure, competition, and/or financial reward.

chromatography,paper.name: chromatography , paper
chromatography,paper.definition: [MASK] chromatography is an analytical technique for resolution of a chemical mixture into its component compounds. Compounds are separated on an adsorbent [MASK] (stationary phase) by their varied degree of solubility/mobility in the eluting solvent (mobile phase).

cornealperforation.name: corneal perforation
cornealperforation.definition: Corneal perforation is a puncture or hole through the corneal stroma resulting from various diseases or trauma.

menstrualcycle.name: menstrual cycle
menstrualcycle.definition: Menstrual cycle is the period from onset of one menstrual bleeding (menstruation) to the next in an ovulating woman or female primate. The menstrual cycle is regulated by endocrine interactions of the hypothalamus; the pituitary gland; the ovaries; and the genital tract. The menstrual cycle is divided by ovulation into two phases. Based on the endocrine status of the ovary, there is a follicular phase and a luteal phase. Based on the response in the endometrium, the menstrual cycle is divided into a proliferative and a secretory phase.

thymocytes.name: thymocytes
thymocytes.definition: Thymocytes is hematopoietic progenitor cells that have migrated to the thymus where they differentiate into t-lymphocytes. Thymocytes are classified into maturational stages based on the expression of cell surface antigens.

glioblastoma.name: glioblastoma
glioblastoma.definition: Glioblastoma is a malignant form of astrocytoma histologically characterized by pleomorphism of cells, nuclear atypia, microhemorrhage, and necrosis. They may arise in any region of the central nervous system, with a predilection for the cerebral hemispheres, basal ganglia, and commissural [MASK] presentation most frequently occurs in the fifth or sixth decade of life with focal neurologic signs or seizures.

cognitivescience.name: cognitive science
cognitivescience.definition: Cognitive science is the study of the precise nature of different mental tasks and the operations of the brain that enable them to be performed, engaging branches of psychology, computer science, philosophy, and linguistics. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

diagnosticusesofchemicals.name: diagnostic uses of chemicals
diagnosticusesofchemicals.definition: Diagnostic uses of chemicals is chemicals administered to patients in order to diagnose or study the pathology of medical conditions, diseases, or syndromes.

gammacameras.name: gamma cameras
gammacameras.definition: Gamma cameras is electronic instruments that produce photographs or cathode-ray tube images of the gamma-ray emissions from organs containing radionuclide tracers.

signalrecognitionparticle.name: signal recognition particle
signalrecognitionparticle.definition: Signal recognition particle is a cytosolic ribonucleoprotein complex that acts to induce elongation arrest of nascent presecretory and membrane proteins until the ribosome becomes associated with the rough endoplasmic reticulum. It consists of a 7s rna and at least six polypeptide subunits (relative molecular masses 9, 14, 19, 54, 68, and 72k).

singapore.name: singapore
singapore.definition: Singapore is country of islands in Southeastern Asia, islands between Malaysia and [MASK]. The capital is Singapore.

insulinaspart.name: insulin aspart
insulinaspart.definition: Insulin aspart is insulin that has been modified to contain an aspartic acid instead of a proline at position 38 of the B-chain.

nuclearfactor45protein.name: nuclear factor 45 protein
nuclearfactor45protein.definition: Nuclear factor 45 protein is a protein subunit that takes part in forming nuclear factor 90 protein complexes.

twinstudy.name: twin study
twinstudy.definition: Twin study is work consisting of reporting using a method of detecting genetic causes in human traits and genetic factors in behavior using sets of twins.

chromatography,agarose.name: chromatography , agarose
chromatography,agarose.definition: Agarose chromatography is a method of gel filtration chromatography using agarose, the non-ionic component of agar, for the separation of compounds with molecular weights up to several million.

silicondioxide.name: silicon dioxide
silicondioxide.definition: Silicon dioxide is transparent, tasteless crystals found in nature as agate, amethyst, chalcedony, cristobalite, flint, sand, quartz, and tridymite. The compound is insoluble in water or acids except hydrofluoric acid.

wholegrains.name: whole grains
wholegrains.definition: Whole grains is edible [MASK] which contain all components of the [MASK] - germ, bran, and endosperm.

nursing.name: nursing
nursing.definition: Nursing is the field of nursing care concerned with the promotion, maintenance, and restoration of health.

liedetection.name: lie detection
liedetection.definition: Lie detection is ascertaining of deception through detection of emotional disturbance as manifested by changes in physiologic processes usually using a polygraph.

lowerurinarytractsymptoms.name: lower urinary tract symptoms
lowerurinarytractsymptoms.definition: Lower urinary tract symptoms is symptoms of disorders of the lower urinary tract including frequency, nocturia; urgency, incomplete voiding, and urinary incontinence. They are often associated with overactive [MASK] incompetence; and interstitial cystitis. Lower urinary tract symptoms in males were traditionally called prostatism.

clinicalnursingresearch.name: clinical nursing research
clinicalnursingresearch.definition: Clinical nursing research is research carried out by nurses in the clinical setting and designed to provide information that will help improve patient care. Other professional staff may also participate in the research.

tandemaffinitypurification.name: tandem affinity purification
tandemaffinitypurification.definition: Tandem affinity purification is a technique used to isolate specific interacting partners of macromolecular complexes that have been assembled with a tagged component (bait) that interacts with other partners in the complex. The interacting bait component is labeled with a dual-affinity tag that allows for capture of the complex by immunoprecipitation, followed by purification of only the partners of the complex interacting with the bait by affinity chromatography.

anastomosis,surgical.name: anastomosis , surgical
anastomosis,surgical.definition: Surgical anastomosis is surgical union or shunt between ducts, tubes or vessels. It may be end-to-end, end-to-side, side-to-end, or side-to-side.

guidelinesastopic.name: guidelines as topic
guidelinesastopic.definition: Guidelines as topic is works about a systematic statement of policy rules or principles. Guidelines may be developed by government agencies at any level, institutions, professional societies, governing boards, or by convening expert panels. For guidelines in the field of health care and clinical medicine, [MASK] is available.

peripheralbloodstemcelltransplantation.name: peripheral blood stem cell transplantation
peripheralbloodstemcelltransplantation.definition: [MASK] transplantation is transplantation of [MASK]. It is a less invasive alternative to direct marrow harvesting of hematopoietic stem cells. Enrichment of stem cells in peripheral blood can be achieved by inducing mobilization of stem cells from the bone marrow.

healtheducation,dental.name: health education , dental
healtheducation,dental.definition: Dental health education is education which increases the awareness and favorably influences the attitudes and knowledge relating to the improvement of dental health on a personal or community basis.

manipulation,orthopedic.name: manipulation , orthopedic
manipulation,orthopedic.definition: Orthopedic manipulation is the planned and carefully managed manual movement of the musculoskeletal system, extremities, and spine to produce increased motion. The term is sometimes used to denote a precise sequence of movements of a joint to determine the presence of disease or to reduce a dislocation. In the case of fractures, orthopedic manipulation can produce better position and alignment of the fracture. (From Blauvelt & Nelson, a Manual of Orthopaedic Terminology, 5th ed, p264)

sinusarrest,cardiac.name: sinus arrest , cardiac
sinusarrest,cardiac.definition: Cardiac sinus arrest is the omission of atrial activation that is caused by transient cessation of impulse generation at the sinoatrial node. It is characterized by a prolonged pause without p wave in an electrocardiogram. Sinus arrest has been associated with sleep apnea (rem sleep-related sinus arrest).

paraffinembedding.name: paraffin embedding
paraffinembedding.definition: [MASK] embedding is the infiltrating of tissue specimens with [MASK], as a supporting substance, to prepare for sectioning with a microtome.

areaundercurve.name: area under curve
areaundercurve.definition: Area under curve is a statistical means of summarizing information from a series of measurements on one individual. It is frequently used in clinical pharmacology where the auc from serum levels can be interpreted as the total uptake of whatever has been administered. As a plot of the concentration of a drug against time, after a single dose of medicine, producing a standard shape curve, it is a means of comparing the bioavailability of the same drug made by different companies. (From Winslade, Dictionary of Clinical Research, 1992)

economicstatus.name: economic status
economicstatus.definition: Economic status is personal or family variables such as household income, assets such as inherited wealth, savings, employment benefits, or ownership of homes or other property.

molecularfunction.name: molecular function
molecularfunction.definition: Molecular function is the biochemical activity of a gene product.

partnershippractice.name: partnership practice
partnershippractice.definition: Partnership practice is a voluntary contract between two or more doctors who may or may not share responsibility for the care of patients, with proportional sharing of profits and losses.

diettherapy.name: diet therapy
diettherapy.definition: Diet therapy is adjusting the quantity and quality of food intake to improve health status of an individual. This term does not include the methods of food intake (nutritional support).

electrontransport.name: electron transport
electrontransport.definition: [MASK] transport is the process by which [MASK] are transported from a reduced substrate to molecular oxygen. (From Bennington, Saunders Dictionary and Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984, p270)

interactivetutorial.name: interactive tutorial
interactivetutorial.definition: Interactive tutorial is video recordings or other files in which the progress of the instruction or content is determined by user response.

gradeapproach.name: grade approach
gradeapproach.definition: Grade approach is a common, sensible, structured  and transparent approach to grading quality (or certainty) of evidence and strength of recommendations developed by the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (short grade) working group.

hazardouswastesites.name: hazardous waste sites
hazardouswastesites.definition: Hazardous waste sites is sites where hazardous substances are deposited. Some have facilities for safely storing, processing, and [MASK] these waste products.

laborstage,third.name: labor stage , third
laborstage,third.definition: Third labor stage is the final period of obstetric labor that is from the expulsion of the fetus to the expulsion of the placenta.

geneticmarkers.name: genetic markers
geneticmarkers.definition: Genetic markers is a phenotypically recognizable genetic trait which can be used to identify a genetic locus, a linkage group, or a recombination event.

drugresistance,multiple,bacterial.name: drug resistance , multiple , bacterial
drugresistance,multiple,bacterial.definition: Bacterial multiple drug resistance is the ability of bacteria to resist or to become tolerant to several structurally and functionally distinct drugs simultaneously. This resistance may be acquired through gene mutation or foreign dna in transmissible plasmids (r factors).

anesthesia,cardiacprocedures.name: anesthesia , cardiac procedures
anesthesia,cardiacprocedures.definition: Cardiac procedures anesthesia is a range of methods used to induce unconsciousness; analgesia; and muscle relaxation during cardiac procedures.

continuouspositiveairwaypressure.name: continuous positive airway pressure
continuouspositiveairwaypressure.definition: Continuous positive airway pressure is a technique of respiratory therapy, in either spontaneously breathing or mechanically ventilated patients, in which airway pressure is maintained above atmospheric pressure throughout the respiratory cycle by pressurization of the ventilatory circuit. (On-Line Medical Dictionary [Internet]. Newcastle upon Tyne(UK): The University Dept. of Medical Oncology: The CancerWEB Project; c1997-2003 [cited 2003 Apr 17]. Available from: http://cancerweb.ncl.ac.uk/omd/)

productpackaging.name: product packaging
productpackaging.definition: Product packaging is form in which product is processed or wrapped and labeled. product labeling is also available.

callcenters.name: call centers
callcenters.definition: Call centers is a facility [MASK] up for the purpose of handling large volumes of telephone calls. Call Centers typically utilize some form of computer automation for receiving, dispatching, screening, logging and forwarding telephone calls.

medicalinformaticscomputing.name: medical informatics computing
medicalinformaticscomputing.definition: Medical informatics computing is precise procedural mathematical and logical operations utilized in the study of medical information pertaining to health care.

embryotransfer.name: embryo transfer
embryotransfer.definition: Embryo transfer is the transfer of mammalian embryos from an in vivo or in vitro environment to a suitable host to improve pregnancy or gestational outcome in human or animal. In human fertility treatment programs, preimplantation embryos ranging from the 4-cell stage to the blastocyst stage are transferred to the uterine cavity between 3-5 days after fertilization in vitro.

sleepstages.name: sleep stages
sleepstages.definition: Sleep stages is periods of sleep manifested by changes in eeg activity and certain behavioral correlates; they formerly included Stage 1: sleep onset, drowsy sleep; Stage 2: light sleep; Stages 3 and 4: delta sleep, light sleep, deep sleep, telencephalic sleep. In 2007, sleep stages were redefined by The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (aasm) as: n1-n2 (sleep onset - light sleep), n3 (slow-wave sleep), and rem sleep.

graftvsleukemiaeffect.name: graft vs leukemia effect
graftvsleukemiaeffect.definition: [MASK] vs leukemia effect is immunological [MASK] of leukemia cells following bone marrow transplantation.

terminologyastopic.name: terminology as topic
terminologyastopic.definition: Terminology as topic is works about the terms, expressions, designations, or symbols used in a particular science, discipline, or specialized subject area.

oralhygieneindex.name: oral hygiene index
oralhygieneindex.definition: Oral hygiene index is a combination of the debris index and the dental calculus index to determine the status of oral hygiene.

ribosomalproteins.name: ribosomal proteins
ribosomalproteins.definition: Ribosomal proteins is proteins found in ribosomes. They are believed to have a catalytic function in reconstituting biologically active ribosomal subunits.

infectioncontrol.name: infection control
infectioncontrol.definition: Infection control is programs of disease surveillance, generally within health care facilities, designed to investigate, prevent, and control the spread of infections and their causative microorganisms.

injectionsitereaction.name: injection site reaction
injectionsitereaction.definition: Injection site reaction is adverse reactions that occur initially at the site of injection or infusion. Milder type is confined to a local allergic flare reaction. a more severe reaction is caused by extravasation of vesicants from the blood vessel at the site of injection and can cause damage to the surrounding tissue. In tumor flare reaction symptoms involve well beyond the injection site such as an increase in the tumor size and tumor markers levels, bone pain, and hypercalcemia.

frenchrevolution.name: french revolution
frenchrevolution.definition: French revolution is [MASK] during which traditional monarchy was ended and modern government functions were instituted.

defensivemedicine.name: defensive medicine
defensivemedicine.definition: Defensive medicine is the alterations of modes of medical practice, induced by the threat of liability, for the principal purposes of forestalling lawsuits by patients as well as providing good legal defense in the event that such lawsuits are instituted.

tissuedonors.name: tissue donors
tissuedonors.definition: Tissue donors is individuals supplying living tissue, organs, cells, blood or blood components for transfer or transplantation to histocompatible recipients.

radiography,thoracic.name: radiography , thoracic
radiography,thoracic.definition: Thoracic radiography is x-ray visualization of the chest and organs of the thoracic cavity. It is not restricted to visualization of the lungs.

viruscultivation.name: virus cultivation
viruscultivation.definition: Virus cultivation is process of growing viruses in live animals, plants, or cultured cells.

adaptiveclinicaltrialsastopic.name: adaptive clinical trials as topic
adaptiveclinicaltrialsastopic.definition: Adaptive clinical trials as topic is works about clinical studies in which a prospectively planned opportunity is included to modify trial designs and hypotheses based on analysis of data from subjects in the study.

lifesupportcare.name: life support care
lifesupportcare.definition: Life support care is care provided patients requiring extraordinary therapeutic measures in order to sustain and prolong life.

population.name: population
population.definition: Population is the total number of individuals inhabiting a particular region or area.

synovialmembrane.name: synovial membrane
synovialmembrane.definition: Synovial membrane is the inner membrane of a joint capsule surrounding a freely movable joint. It is loosely attached to the external fibrous capsule and secretes synovial fluid.

educationalstatus.name: educational status
educationalstatus.definition: Educational status is educational attainment or level of education of an individual.

centralnervoussysteminfections.name: central nervous system infections
centralnervoussysteminfections.definition: Central nervous system infections is pathogenic infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges. dna virus infections; rna virus infections; bacterial infections; mycoplasma infections; spirochaetales infections; fungal infections; protozoan infections; helminthiasis; and prion diseases may involve the central nervous system as a primary or secondary process.

genefrequency.name: gene frequency
genefrequency.definition: Gene frequency is the proportion of one particular in the total of all alleles for one genetic locus in a breeding population.

personnelloyalty.name: personnel loyalty
personnelloyalty.definition: Personnel loyalty is dedication or commitment shown by employees to organizations or institutions where they work.

femoralneuropathy.name: femoral neuropathy
femoralneuropathy.definition: Femoral neuropathy is disease involving the femoral nerve. The femoral nerve may be injured by ischemia (e.g., in association with diabetic neuropathies), nerve compression, trauma, [MASK], and other disease processes. Clinical features include muscle weakness or paralysis of hip flexion and [MASK] extension, atrophy of the quadriceps muscle, reduced or absent patellar reflex, and impaired sensation over the anterior and medial [MASK].

bloodvolume.name: blood volume
bloodvolume.definition: Blood volume is volume of circulating blood. It is the sum of the plasma volume and erythrocyte volume.

molecularstructure.name: molecular structure
molecularstructure.definition: Molecular structure is the location of the atoms, groups or ions relative to one another in a molecule, as well as the number, type and location of covalent bonds.

retinalbipolarcells.name: retinal bipolar cells
retinalbipolarcells.definition: Retinal bipolar cells is interneurons of the vertebrate retina containing two processes. They receive inputs from the retinal photoreceptor cells and send outputs to the [MASK]. The bipolar cells also make lateral connections in the retina with the retinal horizontal cells and with the amacrine cells.

workplace.name: workplace
workplace.definition: Workplace is place or physical location of work or employment.

behaviorobservationtechniques.name: behavior observation techniques
behaviorobservationtechniques.definition: Behavior [MASK] techniques is a wide range of formal and informal techniques used to document behavior.

ganglia,sensory.name: ganglia , sensory
ganglia,sensory.definition: Sensory ganglia is clusters of neurons in the somatic peripheral nervous system which contain the cell bodies of sensory nerve axons. Sensory ganglia may also have intrinsic interneurons and non-neuronal supporting cells.

evolution,planetary.name: evolution , planetary
evolution,planetary.definition: Planetary evolution is creation and development of bodies within solar systems, includes study of early planetary geology.

gabaantagonists.name: gaba antagonists
gabaantagonists.definition: Gaba antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate gaba receptors, thereby blocking the actions of endogenous gamma-aminobutyric acid and gaba receptor agonists.

decisionsupportsystems,management.name: decision support systems , management
decisionsupportsystems,management.definition: Management decision support systems is computer-based systems that enable management to interrogate the computer on an ad hoc basis for various kinds of information in the organization, which predict the effect of potential decisions.

sodiumisotopes.name: sodium isotopes
sodiumisotopes.definition: Sodium isotopes is stable sodium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element sodium, but differ in atomic weight. Na-23 is a stable sodium isotope.

mandibularprosthesis.name: mandibular prosthesis
mandibularprosthesis.definition: Mandibular prosthesis is a prosthetic appliance for the replacement of areas of the mandible missing or defective as a result of deformity, disease, injury, or surgery.

environmentalindicators.name: environmental indicators
environmentalindicators.definition: Environmental indicators is data related to climate change, [MASK], eutrophication, acidification, toxic contamination, urban environmental quality, biodiversity, cultural landscapes, waste, water resources, forest resources, fish resources, and soil degradation including desertification and erosion. (from https://www.oecd.org/env/indicators-modelling-outlooks/37551205.pdfc).

enzymerepression.name: enzyme repression
enzymerepression.definition: Enzyme repression is the interference in synthesis of an enzyme due to the elevated level of an effector substance, usually a metabolite, whose presence would cause depression of the gene responsible for enzyme synthesis.

genes,overlapping.name: genes , overlapping
genes,overlapping.definition: Overlapping genes is genes whose nucleotide sequences overlap to some degree. The overlapped sequences may involve structural or regulatory genes of eukaryotic or prokaryotic cells.

drugcollateralsensitivity.name: drug collateral sensitivity
drugcollateralsensitivity.definition: Drug collateral sensitivity is increase in sensitivity of an organism, disease, or tissue to one drug that develops following the loss of sensitivity (i.e. resistance) to another drug.

statisticsastopic.name: statistics as topic
statisticsastopic.definition: Statistics as topic is works about the science and art of collecting, summarizing, and analyzing data that are subject to random variation.

schools,publichealth.name: schools , public health
schools,publichealth.definition: Public health schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of public health.

cesareansection,repeat.name: cesarean section , repeat
cesareansection,repeat.definition: Repeat cesarean section is extraction of the fetus by abdominal hysterotomy anytime following a previous cesarean.

proteinsdeficiency.name: protein s deficiency
proteinsdeficiency.definition: Protein s deficiency is an autosomal dominant disorder showing decreased levels of plasma protein s antigen or activity, associated with venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. protein s is a vitamin K-dependent plasma protein that inhibits blood clotting by serving as a cofactor for activated protein c (also a vitamin K-dependent protein), and the clinical manifestations of its deficiency are virtually identical to those of protein c deficiency. Treatment with heparin for acute thrombotic processes is usually followed by maintenance administration of coumarin drugs for the prevention of recurrent thrombosis. (From Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p1511; Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 9th ed, p1523)

genes,abl.name: genes , abl
genes,abl.definition: Abl genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (abl) originally isolated from the Abelson murine leukemia virus (Ab-MuLV). The proto-oncogene abl (c-abl) codes for a protein that is a member of the tyrosine kinase family. The human c-abl gene is located at 9q34.1 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 9. It is activated by translocation to bcr on chromosome 22 in chronic myelogenous leukemia.

perfusion.name: perfusion
perfusion.definition: Perfusion is treatment process involving the injection of fluid into an organ or tissue.

vertebrate.name: vertebrate
vertebrate.definition: Vertebrate is animals having a vertebral column, members of the phylum Chordata, subphylum Craniata comprising mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.

neurologicmanifestations.name: neurologic manifestations
neurologicmanifestations.definition: Neurologic manifestations is clinical signs and symptoms caused by nervous system injury or dysfunction.

reproductivebehavior.name: reproductive behavior
reproductivebehavior.definition: Reproductive behavior is human behavior or decision related to reproduction.

signsandsymptoms.name: signs and symptoms
signsandsymptoms.definition: Signs and symptoms is clinical manifestations that can be either objective when observed by a physician, or subjective when perceived by the patient.

nuclearpore.name: nuclear pore
nuclearpore.definition: Nuclear pore is an opening through the nuclear envelope formed by the nuclear pore complex which transports nuclear proteins or rna into or out of the cell nucleus and which, under some conditions, acts as an ion channel.

hypertension,pulmonary.name: hypertension , pulmonary
hypertension,pulmonary.definition: Pulmonary hypertension is increased vascular resistance in the [MASK], usually secondary to heart diseases or lung diseases.

magnesiumhydroxide.name: magnesium hydroxide
magnesiumhydroxide.definition: Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound that occurs in nature as the mineral brucite. It acts as an antacid with cathartic effects.

positivetranscriptionalelongationfactorb.name: positive transcriptional elongation factor b
positivetranscriptionalelongationfactorb.definition: Positive transcriptional elongation factor b is a transcriptional elongation factor complex that is comprised of a heterodimer of cyclin-dependent kinase 9 and one of several cyclins including type t cyclins and cyclin k. It functions by phosphorylating the carboxy-terminal domain of rna polymerase ii.

housing,animal.name: housing , animal
housing,animal.definition: Animal housing is the physical environment in which animals are maintained.

iliacartery.name: iliac artery
iliacartery.definition: Iliac artery is either of two large arteries originating from the abdominal aorta; they supply blood to the pelvis, [MASK] and legs.

hlaantigens.name: hla antigens
hlaantigens.definition: Hla antigens is antigens determined by leukocyte loci found on chromosome 6, the major histocompatibility loci in humans. They are polypeptides or glycoproteins found on most nucleated cells and platelets, determine tissue types for transplantation, and are associated with certain diseases.

airwaymanagement.name: airway management
airwaymanagement.definition: Airway management is evaluation, planning, and use of a range of procedures and airway devices for the maintenance or restoration of a patient's ventilation.

proportionalhazardsmodels.name: proportional hazards models
proportionalhazardsmodels.definition: Proportional hazards models is statistical models used in survival analysis that assert that the effect of the study factors on the hazard rate in the study population is multiplicative and does not change over time.

sulfur.name: sulfur
sulfur.definition: Sulfur is an element that is a member of the chalcogen family. It has an atomic symbol s, atomic number 16, and atomic weight [32.059; 32.076]. It is found in the amino acids [MASK] and methionine.

genetics,medical.name: genetics , medical
genetics,medical.definition: Medical genetics is a subdiscipline of human genetics which entails the reliable prediction of certain human disorders as a function of the lineage and/or genetic makeup of an individual or of any two parents or potential parents.

tumornecrosisfactorligandsuperfamilymemb.name: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13
tumornecrosisfactorligandsuperfamilymemb.definition: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13 is a member of tumor necrosis factor superfamily found on macrophages; [MASK] and t-lymphocytes. It occurs as transmembrane protein that can be cleaved to release a secreted form that specifically binds to transmembrane activator and caml interactor protein; and b cell maturation antigen.

safetymanagement.name: safety management
safetymanagement.definition: Safety management is the development of systems to prevent accidents, injuries, and other adverse occurrences in an institutional setting. The concept includes prevention or reduction of adverse events or incidents involving employees, patients, or facilities. Examples include plans to reduce injuries from falls or plans for fire safety to promote a safe institutional environment.

biologicalphenomena.name: biological phenomena
biologicalphenomena.definition: Biological phenomena is biological processes, properties, and characteristics of the whole organism in human, animal, microorganisms, and plants, and of the biosphere.

substanceabuse,oral.name: substance abuse , oral
substanceabuse,oral.definition: Oral substance abuse is abuse, overuse, or misuse of a substance by ingestion.

restraint,physical.name: restraint , physical
restraint,physical.definition: Physical restraint is use of a device for the purpose of controlling movement of all or part of the body. Splinting and casting are fracture fixation.

celladhesionmolecules.name: cell adhesion molecules
celladhesionmolecules.definition: Cell adhesion molecules is surface ligands, usually glycoproteins, that mediate cell-to-cell adhesion. Their functions include the assembly and interconnection of various vertebrate systems, as well as maintenance of tissue integration, wound healing, morphogenic movements, cellular migrations, and metastasis.

bilepigments.name: bile pigments
bilepigments.definition: [MASK] pigments is linear tetrapyrroles that give a characteristic [MASK] to [MASK] including: bilirubin; biliverdin; and bilicyanin.

antigens,plant.name: antigens , plant
antigens,plant.definition: Plant antigens is substances found in plants that have antigenic activity.

proteinarrayanalysis.name: protein array analysis
proteinarrayanalysis.definition: Protein array analysis is ligand-binding assays that measure protein-protein, protein-small molecule, or protein-nucleic acid interactions using a very large [MASK] of capturing molecules, i.e., those attached separately on a solid support, to measure the presence or interaction of target molecules in the sample.

glutathione.name: glutathione
glutathione.definition: Glutathione is a tripeptide with many roles in cells. It conjugates to drugs to make them more soluble for excretion, is a cofactor for some enzymes, is involved in protein disulfide bond rearrangement and reduces peroxides.

fibroblastgrowthfactor8.name: fibroblast growth factor 8
fibroblastgrowthfactor8.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 8 is a fibroblast growth factor that preferentially activates [MASK]. It was initially identified as an androgen-induced growth factor and plays a role in regulating growth of human breast neoplasms and prostatic neoplasms.

bloodvesselprosthesisimplantation.name: blood vessel prosthesis implantation
bloodvesselprosthesisimplantation.definition: Blood vessel prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of blood vessel prostheses to repair injured or diseased blood vessels.

genes,microbial.name: genes , microbial
genes,microbial.definition: Microbial genes is the functional hereditary units of a microorganism.

solitaryfibroustumor,pleural.name: solitary fibrous tumor , pleural
solitaryfibroustumor,pleural.definition: Pleural solitary fibrous tumor is a rare neoplasm, usually benign, derived from mesenchymal fibroblasts located in the submesothelial lining of the pleura. It spite of its various synonyms, it has no features of mesothelial cells and is not related to malignant mesothelioma or asbestos exposure.

group.name: group
group.definition: Group is a number of atoms forming a recognizable and usually transferable portion of a molecule.

therapeuticindex,drug.name: therapeutic index , drug
therapeuticindex,drug.definition: Drug therapeutic index is the ratio of the dose that produces toxicity to the dose that produces a clinically desired or effective response.

regionalhealthplanning.name: regional health planning
regionalhealthplanning.definition: Regional health planning is planning for health resources at a regional or multi-state level.

bacteria.name: bacteria
bacteria.definition: Bacteria is one of the three domains of life (the others being Eukarya and archaea), also called Eubacteria. They are unicellular prokaryotic microorganisms which generally possess rigid cell walls, multiply by cell division, and exhibit three principal forms: round or coccal, rodlike or bacillary, and spiral or spirochetal. Bacteria can be classified by their response to oxygen: aerobic, anaerobic, or facultatively anaerobic; by the mode by which they obtain their energy: chemotrophy (via chemical reaction) or phototrophy (via light reaction); for chemotrophs by their source of chemical energy: chemolithotrophy (from inorganic compounds) or chemoorganotrophy (from organic compounds); and by their source for carbon; nitrogen; etc.; heterotrophy (from organic sources) or autotrophy (from carbon dioxide). They can also be classified by whether or not they stain (based on the structure of their cell walls) with crystal violet dye: gram-negative or gram-positive.

chromosomesegregation.name: chromosome segregation
chromosomesegregation.definition: Chromosome segregation is the orderly segregation of chromosomes during meiosis or [MASK].

pleuralneoplasms.name: pleural neoplasms
pleuralneoplasms.definition: Pleural neoplasms is neoplasms of the thin serous membrane that envelopes the lungs and lines the thoracic cavity. Pleural neoplasms are exceedingly rare and are usually not diagnosed until they are advanced because in the early stages they produce no symptoms.

constructionindustry.name: construction industry
constructionindustry.definition: Construction industry is the aggregate business enterprise of building.

proteinaggregates.name: protein aggregates
proteinaggregates.definition: Protein aggregates is any mixture of secondary, tertiary, or quaternary protein molecules which appear as clumps in or outside the cell.

vitamine.name: vitamin e
vitamine.definition: Vitamin e is a generic descriptor for all tocopherols and tocotrienols that exhibit alpha-tocopherol activity. By virtue of the phenolic hydrogen on the 2H-1-benzopyran-6-ol nucleus, these compounds exhibit varying degree of antioxidant activity, depending on the site and number of methyl groups and the type of isoprenoids.

galaxies.name: galaxies
galaxies.definition: Galaxies is large aggregates of celestial stars; [MASK]; and gas. (From McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

oncologynursing.name: oncology nursing
oncologynursing.definition: Oncology nursing is a nursing specialty concerned with the care provided to cancer patients. It includes aspects of family functioning through education of both patient and family.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 11
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.definition: Member 11 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette, subfamily b, protein (P-glycoproteins) that functions in the ATP-dependent secretion of [MASK] [MASK] into the [MASK] canaliculi of [MASK]. Mutations in the abcb11 gene are associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis 2 (see cholestasis, intrahepatic).

extremeenvironments.name: extreme environments
extremeenvironments.definition: Extreme environments is an environment which falls outside the range of tolerance for the survival of organisms that are not specifically adapted to survive or thrive in it. Examples of such environments are among the hottest and coldest places on earth.

databasesastopic.name: databases as topic
databasesastopic.definition: Databases as topic is works on organized collections of records, standardized in format and content, that are stored in any of a variety of computer-readable modes.

biomechanicalphenomena.name: biomechanical phenomena
biomechanicalphenomena.definition: Biomechanical phenomena is the properties, processes, and behavior of biological systems under the action of mechanical forces.

augmentedreality.name: augmented reality
augmentedreality.definition: Augmented reality is technology in which images of virtual objects and/or other digital information are superimposed over the real time view of the physical objects providing a composite view with guides for carrying out a task with or on the physical objects.

retinoicacidreceptoralpha.name: retinoic acid receptor alpha
retinoicacidreceptoralpha.definition: Retinoic acid receptor alpha is a nuclear receptor protein which belongs to a family of transcription regulators of ligand-responsive regulatory proteins which include steroid hormone receptors. In addition to a C-terminal ligand-binding domain, these nuclear receptors contain a highly-conserved N-terminal zinc-finger domain that mediates binding ligand-responsive elements.

patientcreditandcollection.name: patient credit and collection
patientcreditandcollection.definition: Patient credit and collection is accounting procedures for determining credit status and methods of obtaining payment.

aminoacid,peptide,orprotein.name: amino acid , peptide , or protein
aminoacid,peptide,orprotein.definition: Or protein peptide amino acid is amino acids and chains of amino acids connected by peptide linkages.

reducedfolatecarrierprotein.name: reduced folate carrier protein
reducedfolatecarrierprotein.definition: Reduced folate carrier protein is a ubiquitously expressed folic acid transporter that functions via an antiporter mechanism which is coupled to the transport of organic phosphates.

contractservices.name: contract services
contractservices.definition: Contract services is outside services provided to an institution under a formal financial agreement.

circulatoryarrest,deephypothermiainduced.name: circulatory arrest , deep hypothermia induced
circulatoryarrest,deephypothermiainduced.definition: Deep hypothermia induced circulatory arrest is a technique to arrest the flow of blood by lowering body temperature to about 20 degrees Centigrade, usually achieved by infusing chilled perfusate. The technique provides a bloodless surgical field for complex surgeries.

knowledgediscovery.name: knowledge discovery
knowledgediscovery.definition: Knowledge discovery is a process that searches for hidden and important connections among information or results.

acutefebrileencephalopathy.name: acute febrile encephalopathy
acutefebrileencephalopathy.definition: Acute febrile encephalopathy is acute onset of fever accompanied by seizures, cerebral inflammation and a change in mental status (e.g., confusion, disorientation, and coma).

toothabnormalities.name: tooth abnormalities
toothabnormalities.definition: Tooth abnormalities is congenital absence of or defects in structures of the teeth.

fecalmicrobiotatransplantation.name: fecal microbiota transplantation
fecalmicrobiotatransplantation.definition: Fecal microbiota transplantation is transfer of gastrointestinal microbiota from one individual to another by infusion of donor feces to the upper or lower gastrointestinal tract of the recipient.

parks,recreational.name: parks , recreational
parks,recreational.definition: Recreational parks is an area of land open to the public for enjoyment.

gastricacid.name: gastric acid
gastricacid.definition: Gastric acid is hydrochloric acid present in gastric juice.

rhoguaninenucleotideexchangefactors.name: rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors
rhoguaninenucleotideexchangefactors.definition: Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors is signaling proteins which function as master molecular switches by activating Rho GTPases through conversion of guanine nucleotides. Rho GTPases in turn control many aspects of cell behavior through the regulation of multiple downstream signal transduction pathways.

institutionalpractice.name: institutional practice
institutionalpractice.definition: Institutional practice is professional practice as an employee or contractee of a health care institution.

physicalendurance.name: physical endurance
physicalendurance.definition: Physical endurance is the time span between the beginning of physical activity by an individual and the termination because of exhaustion.

hepatitis,animal.name: hepatitis , animal
hepatitis,animal.definition: Animal hepatitis is inflammation of the liver in non-human animals.

elementaryparticles.name: elementary particles
elementaryparticles.definition: Elementary particles is individual components of atoms, usually subatomic; subnuclear particles are usually detected only when the atomic nucleus decays and then only transiently, as most of them are unstable, often yielding pure energy without substance, i.e., radiation.

healthcarefinancing.name: healthcare financing
healthcarefinancing.definition: Healthcare financing is methods of generating, allocating, and using financial resources in healthcare systems.

aorta.name: aorta
aorta.definition: Aorta is the main trunk of the systemic arteries.

cardiomyopathy,restrictive.name: cardiomyopathy , restrictive
cardiomyopathy,restrictive.definition: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is a form of cardiac muscle disease in which the ventricular walls are excessively rigid, impeding ventricular filling. It is marked by reduced diastolic volume of either or both ventricles but normal or nearly normal systolic function. It may be idiopathic or associated with other diseases (endomyocardial fibrosis or amyloidosis) causing interstitial fibrosis.

spacesimulation.name: space simulation
spacesimulation.definition: Space simulation is an environment simulating one or more parameters of the space environment, applied in testing space systems or components. Often, a closed chamber is used, capable of approximating the vacuum and normal environments of space. (From nasa Thesaurus, 1988) This also includes simulated extravehicular activity studies in [MASK] or water tanks.

receptors,lh.name: receptors , lh
receptors,lh.definition: Lh receptors is those protein complexes or molecular sites on the surfaces and cytoplasm of gonadal cells that bind luteinizing or chorionic gonadotropic hormones and thereby cause the gonadal cells to synthesize and secrete [MASK] steroids. The hormone-receptor complex is internalized from the plasma membrane and initiates steroid synthesis.

policy.name: policy
policy.definition: Policy is a course or method of action selected to guide and determine present and future decisions.

tyrosine.name: tyrosine
tyrosine.definition: Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid. In animals it is synthesized from phenylalanine. It is also the precursor of epinephrine; thyroid hormones; and melanin.

intellectualproperty.name: intellectual property
intellectualproperty.definition: Intellectual property is property, such as patents, trademarks, and [MASK], that results from creative effort. The Patent and [MASK] Clause (Art. 1, Sec. 8, cl. 8) of the United States Constitution provides for promoting the progress of science and useful arts by securing for limited times to authors and inventors, the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 5th ed, p1014)

pelvis.name: pelvis
pelvis.definition: Pelvis is the space or compartment surrounded by the pelvic girdle (bony pelvis). It is subdivided into the greater pelvis and lesser pelvis. The pelvic girdle is formed by the [MASK] and sacrum.

michigan.name: michigan
michigan.definition: Michigan is state bounded on the north by the Great [MASK], on the east by Canada, on the south by Wisconsin, Indiana, and Ohio, and on the west by [MASK] Michigan and Wisconsin.

manifestanxietyscale.name: manifest anxiety scale
manifestanxietyscale.definition: Manifest anxiety scale is true-false questionnaire made up of items believed to indicate anxiety, in which the subject answers verbally the statement that describes him.

healthcarequality,access,andevaluation.name: health care quality , access , and evaluation
healthcarequality,access,andevaluation.definition: And evaluation access health care quality is the concept concerned with all aspects of the quality, accessibility, and appraisal of health care and health care delivery.

nursingdiagnosis.name: nursing diagnosis
nursingdiagnosis.definition: Nursing diagnosis is conclusions derived from the nursing assessment that establish a health status profile for the patient and from which nursing interventions may be ordered.

embryonicstemcells.name: embryonic stem cells
embryonicstemcells.definition: Embryonic stem cells is cells derived from the blastocyst inner cell mass which forms before implantation in the uterine wall. They retain the ability to divide, proliferate and provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

neutrophilinfiltration.name: neutrophil infiltration
neutrophilinfiltration.definition: Neutrophil infiltration is the diffusion or accumulation of neutrophils in tissues or cells in response to a wide variety of substances released at the sites of inflammatory reactions.

rna,fungal.name: rna , fungal
rna,fungal.definition: Fungal rna is ribonucleic acid in fungi having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

veteransdisabilityclaims.name: veterans disability claims
veteransdisabilityclaims.definition: Veterans disability claims is disorders claimed as a result of military service.

peptidephi.name: peptide phi
peptidephi.definition: Peptide phi is a 27-amino acid peptide with histidine at the N-terminal and isoleucine amide at the C-terminal. The exact amino acid composition of the peptide is species dependent. The peptide is secreted in the intestine, but is found in the nervous system, many organs, and in the majority of peripheral tissues. It has a wide range of biological actions, affecting the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and central nervous systems.

geriatricassessment.name: geriatric assessment
geriatricassessment.definition: Geriatric assessment is evaluation of the level of physical, physiological, or mental functioning in the older population group.

sonication.name: sonication
sonication.definition: Sonication is the application of high intensity ultrasound to liquids.

databases,chemical.name: databases , chemical
databases,chemical.definition: Chemical databases is databases devoted to knowledge about specific chemicals.

maryland.name: maryland
maryland.definition: Maryland is a state bounded on the north by Pennsylvania, on the east by Delaware and the Atlantic Ocean, on the south by Virginia and West Virginia, and on the west by West Virginia.

manufacturingindustry.name: manufacturing industry
manufacturingindustry.definition: Manufacturing industry is an industry which specializes in the fabrication or manufacture of products from raw or intermediate materials.

productlinemanagement.name: product line management
productlinemanagement.definition: Product line management is management control systems for structuring health care delivery strategies around case types, as in DRGs, or specific clinical services.

marriage.name: marriage
marriage.definition: Marriage is the social institution involving legal and/or religious sanction whereby individuals are joined together.

fertilityagents.name: fertility agents
fertilityagents.definition: Fertility agents is drugs used to increase fertility or to treat infertility.

cationicaminoacidtransporter1.name: cationic amino acid transporter 1
cationicaminoacidtransporter1.definition: [MASK] 1 is a high-affinity, low capacity system y+ amino acid transporter found ubiquitously. It has specificity for the transport of [MASK]; lysine; and ornithine. It may also act as an ecotropic leukemia retroviral receptor.

spaceresearch.name: space research
spaceresearch.definition: Space research is studies of interactions between living organisms and characteristics of the extraterrestrial environment. These studies specifically address the structure and function of living organisms in an extraterrestrial environment and interdependent relationships of organisms with each other and/or the extraterrestrial environment while also touching on the origin, evolution and potential for extraterrestrial life. (From www.nasa.gov/audience/foreducators/spacelife/)

receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,typeii.name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type ii
receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,typeii.definition: Type ii tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that is expressed primarily in immune system cells. It has specificity for membrane-bound form of tumor necrosis factors and mediates intracellular-signaling through tnf receptor associated factors.

cardiovascularphysiologicalphenomena.name: cardiovascular physiological phenomena
cardiovascularphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Cardiovascular physiological phenomena is processes and properties of the cardiovascular system as a whole or of any of its parts.

geneorder.name: gene order
geneorder.definition: Gene order is the sequential location of genes on a chromosome.

bindingsites.name: binding sites
bindingsites.definition: Binding sites is the parts of a macromolecule that directly participate in its specific combination with another molecule.

motionperception.name: motion perception
motionperception.definition: Motion perception is the real or apparent movement of objects through the [MASK].

societies,medical.name: societies , medical
societies,medical.definition: Medical societies is societies whose membership is limited to physicians.

noise.name: noise
noise.definition: Noise is any sound which is unwanted or interferes with hearing other sounds.

mammarytumorvirus,mouse.name: mammary tumor virus , mouse
mammarytumorvirus,mouse.definition: Mouse mammary tumor virus is the type species of betaretrovirus commonly latent in mice. It causes mammary adenocarcinoma in a genetically susceptible strain of mice when the appropriate hormonal influences operate.

privatefacilities.name: private facilities
privatefacilities.definition: Private facilities is places designed, built, or installed to provide for a specific, non-medical function or service used by a specific, restricted group of persons.

cardiacconductionsystemdisease.name: cardiac conduction system disease
cardiacconductionsystemdisease.definition: Cardiac conduction system disease is diseases characterized by pathological irregularities in the heart conduction system. They may be associated with other heart diseases and syndromes (e.g., brugada syndrome; neuromuscular disease, heart blocks), isolated or may result from injuries. You can have a conduction disorder without having an arrhythmia, but some arrhythmias arise from conduction disorders. omim: 601144.

southamerica.name: south america
southamerica.definition: South america is the southern continent of the Western Hemisphere, extending southward from the [MASK]-Panama border.

publicserviceannouncement.name: public service announcement
publicserviceannouncement.definition: Public service announcement is work consisting of announcements which promote programs, activities, or services of federal, state, or local governments or those of non-profit organizations and other announcements regarded as serving community interests.

factorviii.name: factor viii
factorviii.definition: Factor viii is factor viii of blood coagulation. Antihemophilic factor that is part of the factor VIII/von Willebrand factor complex. Factor viii is produced in the liver and acts in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. It serves as a cofactor in factor x activation and this action is markedly enhanced by small amounts of thrombin.

physicalphenomena.name: physical phenomena
physicalphenomena.definition: Physical phenomena is the entities of matter and energy, and the processes, principles, properties, and relationships describing their nature and interactions.

randomizedcontrolledtrial.name: randomized controlled trial
randomizedcontrolledtrial.definition: Randomized controlled trial is a work that reports on a clinical trial that involves at least one test treatment and one control treatment, concurrent enrollment and follow-up of the test- and control-treated groups, and in which the treatments to be administered are selected by a random process, such as the use of a random-numbers [MASK].

pregnancytrimester,first.name: pregnancy trimester , first
pregnancytrimester,first.definition: First pregnancy trimester is the beginning third of a human pregnancy, from the first day of the last normal menstrual period (menstruation) through the completion of 14 weeks (98 days) of gestation.

radiotherapy,conformal.name: radiotherapy , conformal
radiotherapy,conformal.definition: Conformal radiotherapy is a therapy using ionizing radiation where there is improved dose homogeneity within the tumor and reduced dosage to uninvolved structures. The precise shaping of dose distribution is achieved via the use of computer-controlled multileaf collimators.

serialextraction.name: serial extraction
serialextraction.definition: Serial extraction is the selective extraction of deciduous teeth during the stage of mixed dentition in accordance with the shedding and eruption of the teeth. It is done over an extended period to allow autonomous [MASK] to relieve crowding of the dental arches during the eruption of the lateral incisors, canines, and premolars, eventually involving the extraction of the first premolar teeth. (Dorland, 28th ed)

fatiguesyndrome,chronic.name: fatigue syndrome , chronic
fatiguesyndrome,chronic.definition: Chronic fatigue syndrome is a syndrome characterized by persistent or recurrent fatigue, diffuse [MASK], sleep disturbances, and subjective cognitive impairment of 6 months duration or longer. Symptoms are not caused by ongoing exertion; are not relieved by rest; and result in a substantial reduction of previous levels of occupational, educational, social, or personal activities. Minor alterations of immune, neuroendocrine, and autonomic function may be associated with this syndrome. There is also considerable overlap between this condition and fibromyalgia. (From Semin Neurol 1998;18(2):237-42; Ann Intern Med 1994 Dec 15;121(12): 953-9)

electricstimulation.name: electric stimulation
electricstimulation.definition: Electric stimulation is use of electric potential or currents to elicit biological responses.

motorneurons.name: motor neurons
motorneurons.definition: Motor neurons is neurons which activate muscle cells.

receptors,transforminggrowthfactorbeta.name: receptors , transforming growth factor beta
receptors,transforminggrowthfactorbeta.definition: Transforming growth factor beta receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind transforming growth factor beta and trigger changes influencing the behavior of cells. Two types of transforming growth factor receptors have been recognized. They differ in affinity for different members of the transforming growth factor beta family and in cellular mechanisms of action.

districtofcolumbia.name: district of columbia
districtofcolumbia.definition: District of columbia is a federal area located between Maryland and Virginia on the Potomac [MASK]; it is coextensive with [MASK], d.c., which is the capital of the United States.

influenzavaccines.name: influenza vaccines
influenzavaccines.definition: Influenza vaccines is vaccines used to prevent infection by viruses in the family orthomyxoviridae. It includes both killed and attenuated vaccines. The composition of the vaccines is changed each year in response to antigenic shifts and changes in [MASK] of influenza virus strains. The flu vaccines may be mono- or multi-valent, which contains one or more influenzavirus a and influenzavirus b strains.

guaninenucleotideexchangefactors.name: guanine nucleotide exchange factors
guaninenucleotideexchangefactors.definition: Guanine nucleotide exchange factors is protein factors that promote the exchange of gtp for gdp bound to gtp-binding proteins.

peptidechainelongation,translational.name: peptide chain elongation , translational
peptidechainelongation,translational.definition: Translational peptide chain elongation is a process of genetic translation, when an amino acid is transferred from its cognate transfer rna to the lengthening chain of peptides.

child.name: child
child.definition: Child is a person 6 to 12 years of age. An individual 2 to 5 years old is child, preschool.

coloradotickfever.name: colorado tick fever
coloradotickfever.definition: Colorado tick fever is a febrile illness characterized by chills, aches, vomiting, leukopenia, and sometimes encephalitis. It is caused by the colorado tick fever virus, a reovirus transmitted by the tick Dermacentor andersoni.

maternalnutritionalphysiologicalphenomen.name: maternal nutritional physiological phenomena
maternalnutritionalphysiologicalphenomen.definition: Maternal nutritional physiological phenomena is nutrition of a mother which affects the health of the fetus and infant as well as herself.

periodontitis.name: periodontitis
periodontitis.definition: Periodontitis is inflammation and loss of connective tissues supporting or surrounding the teeth. This may involve any part of the periodontium. Periodontitis is currently classified by disease progression ([MASK]; aggressive periodontitis) instead of age of onset. (From 1999 International Workshop for a Classification of Periodontal Diseases and Conditions, American Academy of Periodontology)

streptococcus.name: streptococcus
streptococcus.definition: Streptococcus is a genus of gram-positive, coccoid bacteria whose organisms occur in pairs or chains. No endospores are produced. Many species exist as commensals or parasites on man or animals with some being highly pathogenic. a few species are saprophytes and occur in the natural environment.

brain.name: brain
brain.definition: Brain is the part of central nervous system that is contained within the skull (cranium). Arising from the neural tube, the embryonic brain is comprised of three major parts including prosencephalon (the forebrain); mesencephalon (the midbrain); and rhombencephalon (the hindbrain). The developed brain consists of cerebrum; cerebellum; and other structures in the brain stem.

waterpollutants,chemical.name: water pollutants , chemical
waterpollutants,chemical.definition: Chemical water pollutants is chemical compounds which pollute the water of [MASK], [MASK], [MASK], the sea, reservoirs, or other bodies of water.

zincfingers.name: zinc fingers
zincfingers.definition: Zinc fingers is motifs in dna- and RNA-binding proteins whose amino acids are folded into a single structural unit around a zinc atom. In the classic zinc finger, one zinc atom is bound to two cysteines and two histidines. In between the cysteines and histidines are 12 residues which form a dna binding fingertip. By variations in the composition of the sequences in the fingertip and the number and spacing of tandem repeats of the motif, zinc fingers can form a large number of different sequence specific binding sites.

plantpoisoning.name: plant poisoning
plantpoisoning.definition: Plant poisoning is poisoning by the ingestion of plants or its leaves, berries, roots or stalks. The manifestations in both humans and animals vary in severity from mild to life threatening. In animals, especially domestic animals, it is usually the result of ingesting moldy or fermented forage.

articulationdisorders.name: articulation disorders
articulationdisorders.definition: Articulation disorders is disorders of the quality of [MASK] characterized by the substitution, omission, distortion, and addition of phonemes.

urethraldiseases.name: urethral diseases
urethraldiseases.definition: Urethral diseases is pathological processes involving the urethra.

deadboxprotein58.name: dead box protein 58
deadboxprotein58.definition: Dead box protein 58 is a DEAD-box rna helicase that contains an N-terminal death-like domain, aaa+ ATPase domain, and C-terminal rna helicase activity. It functions as an innate immune receptor through its recognition of viral nucleic acids. It also induces the expression of interferon type i and proinflammatory cytokines. Its ligands include: 5'-triphosphorylated single-stranded rna, double-stranded rna (dsRNA), and short dsRNA (less than 1 kb in length).

taqpolymerase.name: taq polymerase
taqpolymerase.definition: Taq polymerase is a heat stable dna-directed dna polymerase from the bacteria Thermus aquaticus. It is widely used for the amplification of genes through the process of polymerase chain reaction. ec 2.7.7.-.

neoplasmproteins.name: neoplasm proteins
neoplasmproteins.definition: Neoplasm proteins is proteins whose abnormal expression (gain or loss) are associated with the development, growth, or progression of neoplasms. Some neoplasm proteins are tumor antigens (antigens, neoplasm), i.e. they induce an immune reaction to their tumor. Many neoplasm proteins have been characterized and are used as tumor markers (biomarkers, tumor) when they are detectable in cells and body fluids as monitors for the presence or growth of tumors. Abnormal expression of oncogene proteins is involved in neoplastic transformation, whereas the loss of expression of tumor suppressor proteins is involved with the loss of growth control and progression of the neoplasm.

lymphoma,follicular.name: lymphoma , follicular
lymphoma,follicular.definition: Follicular lymphoma is malignant lymphoma in which the lymphomatous cells are clustered into identifiable nodules within the [MASK] nodes. The nodules resemble to some extent the germinal center of [MASK] node follicles and most likely represent neoplastic proliferation of [MASK] node-derived follicular center b-lymphocytes.

patientsimulation.name: patient simulation
patientsimulation.definition: Patient simulation is the use of persons coached to feign symptoms or conditions of real diseases in a life-like manner in order to teach or evaluate medical personnel.

sound.name: sound
sound.definition: Sound is a type of non-ionizing radiation in which energy is transmitted through solid, liquid, or gas as compression waves. Sound (acoustic or sonic) radiation with frequencies above the audible range is classified as ultrasonic. Sound radiation below the audible range is classified as infrasonic.

musictherapy.name: music therapy
musictherapy.definition: Music therapy is the use of music as an adjunctive therapy in the treatment of neurological, mental, or behavioral disorders.

hospitalvolunteers.name: hospital volunteers
hospitalvolunteers.definition: Hospital volunteers is individuals who donate their services to the hospital.

plantstructures.name: plant structures
plantstructures.definition: Plant structures is the parts of plants, including [MASK].

visualperception.name: visual perception
visualperception.definition: Visual perception is the selecting and organizing of visual stimuli based on the individual's past experience.

africanamericans.name: african americans
africanamericans.definition: African americans is persons living in the United States having origins in any of the black groups of Africa.

gapjunctions.name: gap junctions
gapjunctions.definition: Gap junctions is connections between cells which allow passage of small molecules and electric current. Gap junctions were first described anatomically as regions of close apposition between cells with a narrow (1-2 nm) gap between cell membranes. The variety in the properties of gap junctions is reflected in the number of connexins, the family of proteins which form the junctions.

sodium.name: sodium
sodium.definition: Sodium is a member of the alkali group of metals. It has the atomic symbol Na, atomic number 11, and atomic weight 23.

diagnosis,dual(psychiatry).name: diagnosis , dual ( psychiatry )
diagnosis,dual(psychiatry).definition: Dual (psychiatry) diagnosis is the co-existence of a substance abuse disorder with a psychiatric disorder.
