The diagnostic principle is based on the fact that it has been found often that chemically dependent patients also have psychiatric problems of various degrees of severity.

proteinaseinhibitoryproteins,secretory.name: proteinase inhibitory proteins , secretory
proteinaseinhibitoryproteins,secretory.definition: Secretory proteinase inhibitory proteins is peptides and proteins found in bodily secretions and body fluids that are protease inhibitors. They play a role in inflammation, tissue repair and innate immunity (immunity, innate) by inhibiting endogenous proteinases such as those produced by leukocytes and exogenous proteases such as those produced by invading microorganisms.

acetone.name: acetone
acetone.definition: Acetone is a colorless liquid used as a solvent and an antiseptic. It is one of the ketone bodies produced during ketoacidosis.

sleepdisorders,circadianrhythm.name: sleep disorders , circadian rhythm
sleepdisorders,circadianrhythm.definition: Circadian rhythm sleep disorders is dyssomnias associated with disruption of the normal 24 hour sleep wake cycle secondary to travel (e.g., jet lag syndrome), shift work, or other causes.

seminalvesiclesecretoryproteins.name: seminal vesicle secretory proteins
seminalvesiclesecretoryproteins.definition: Seminal [MASK] proteins is the secretory proteins of the seminal vesicles are proteins and enzymes that are important in the rapid clotting of the ejaculate. The major clotting protein is seminal vesicle-specific antigen. Many of these seminal vesicle proteins are under androgen regulation, and are substrates for the prostatic enzymes, such as the prostate-specific antigen, a protease and an esterase.

nadhdehydrogenase.name: nadh dehydrogenase
nadhdehydrogenase.definition: Nadh dehydrogenase is a flavoprotein and iron sulfur-containing oxidoreductase that catalyzes the oxidation of nadh to nad. In eukaryotes the enzyme can be found as a component of mitochondrial [MASK] transport complex i. Under experimental conditions the enzyme can use cytochrome c group as the reducing cofactor. The enzyme was formerly listed as ec 1.6.2.1.

vitamina.name: vitamin a
vitamina.definition: Vitamin a is retinol and derivatives of retinol that play an essential role in metabolic functioning of the retina, the growth of and differentiation of epithelial tissue, the growth of bone, reproduction, and the immune response. Dietary vitamin a is derived from a variety of carotenoids found in plants. It is enriched in the liver, [MASK], and the fat component of dairy products.

glycemicindex.name: glycemic index
glycemicindex.definition: Glycemic index is a numerical system of measuring the rate of blood glucose generation from a particular food item as compared to a reference item, such as glucose = 100. Foods with higher glycemic index numbers create greater blood sugar swings.

promoterregions,genetic.name: promoter regions , genetic
promoterregions,genetic.definition: Genetic promoter regions is dna sequences which are recognized (directly or indirectly) and bound by a DNA-dependent rna polymerase during the initiation of transcription. Highly conserved sequences within the promoter include the Pribnow box in bacteria and the tata box in eukaryotes.

therapeuticorpreventiveprocedure.name: therapeutic or preventive procedure
therapeuticorpreventiveprocedure.definition: Therapeutic or preventive procedure is the surgical procedures done to prevent or reduce the risk of developing cancer or other disease conditions in persons who may be predisposed to such conditions.

hepatocytenuclearfactor1.name: hepatocyte nuclear factor 1
hepatocytenuclearfactor1.definition: [MASK] nuclear factor 1 is a transcription factor and homeodomain protein that regulates the expression of a large [MASK] of hepatic proteins including serum albumin; beta-fibrinogen; and alpha 1-antitrypsin. It is composed of hetero- or homo-dimers of [MASK] nuclear factor 1-alpha and [MASK] nuclear factor 1-beta.

sleep,rem.name: sleep , rem
sleep,rem.definition: Rem sleep is a stage of sleep characterized by rapid movements of the eye and low voltage fast pattern eeg. It is usually associated with dreaming.

infant,verylowbirthweight.name: infant , very low birth weight
infant,verylowbirthweight.definition: Very low birth weight infant is an infant whose weight at birth is less than 1500 grams (3.3 lbs), regardless of gestational age.

systematicreviewsastopic.name: systematic reviews as topic
systematicreviewsastopic.definition: Systematic reviews as topic is works about a review of primary literature in health and health policy that attempt to identify, appraise, and synthesize all the empirical evidence that meets specified eligibility criteria to answer a given research question. Its conduct uses explicit methods aimed at minimizing bias in order to produce more reliable findings regarding the effects of interventions for prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation that can be used to inform decision making.

cottonfiber.name: cotton fiber
cottonfiber.definition: Cotton fiber is a textile fiber obtained from the pappus (outside the [MASK]) of cotton plant (gossypium).

collagentypeix.name: collagen type ix
collagentypeix.definition: Collagen type ix is a fibril-associated collagen usually found crosslinked to the surface of collagen type ii fibrils. It is a heterotrimer containing alpha1(IX), alpha2(IX) and alpha3(IX) subunits.

heartconductionsystem.name: heart conduction system
heartconductionsystem.definition: Heart conduction system is an impulse-conducting system composed of modified cardiac muscle, having the power of spontaneous rhythmicity and conduction more highly developed than the rest of the heart.

tastedisorders.name: taste disorders
tastedisorders.definition: Taste disorders is conditions characterized by an alteration in gustatory function or [MASK] disorders are frequently associated with olfaction disorders. Additional potential etiologies include metabolic diseases; drug toxicity; and taste pathway disorders (e.g., taste bud diseases; facial nerve diseases; glossopharyngeal nerve diseases; and brain stem diseases).

lymphaticvesseltumors.name: lymphatic vessel tumors
lymphaticvesseltumors.definition: Lymphatic vessel tumors is neoplasms composed of lymphoid tissue, a lattice work of reticular tissue the interspaces of which contain lymphocytes. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in lymphatic vessels.

sarcoma.name: sarcoma
sarcoma.definition: Sarcoma is a connective tissue neoplasm formed by proliferation of mesodermal cells; it is usually highly malignant.

dnadamage.name: dna damage
dnadamage.definition: Dna damage is injuries to dna that introduce deviations from its normal, intact structure and which may, if left unrepaired, result in a mutation or a block of dna replication. These deviations may be caused by physical or chemical agents and occur by natural or unnatural, introduced circumstances. They include the introduction of illegitimate bases during replication or by deamination or other modification of bases; the loss of a base from the dna backbone leaving an abasic site; single-strand breaks; double strand breaks; and intrastrand (pyrimidine dimers) or interstrand crosslinking. Damage can often be repaired (dna repair). If the damage is extensive, it can induce apoptosis.

hemodialysis,home.name: hemodialysis , home
hemodialysis,home.definition: Home hemodialysis is long-term maintenance hemodialysis in the home.

supportofresearch.name: support of research
supportofresearch.definition: Support of research is organizational source for funding of research activity.

abortion,legal.name: abortion , legal
abortion,legal.definition: Legal abortion is termination of pregnancy under conditions allowed under local laws. (popline Thesaurus, 1991)

forensicmedicine.name: forensic medicine
forensicmedicine.definition: Forensic medicine is the application of medical knowledge to questions of law.

vascularremodeling.name: vascular remodeling
vascularremodeling.definition: Vascular remodeling is the active alterations of vascular wall structures, often leading to elevated vascular resistance. It is associated with aging; atherosclerosis; diabetes mellitus; hypertension; pregnancy; pulmonary hypertension; and stroke, but is also a normal part of embryogenesis.

nervetransfer.name: nerve transfer
nervetransfer.definition: Nerve transfer is surgical reinnervation of a denervated peripheral target using a healthy donor nerve and/or its proximal stump. The direct connection is usually made to a healthy postlesional distal portion of a non-functioning nerve or implanted directly into denervated muscle or insensitive skin. Nerve sprouts will grow from the transferred nerve into the denervated elements and establish contact between them and the neurons that formerly controlled another area.

professionalcompetence.name: professional competence
professionalcompetence.definition: Professional competence is the capability to perform the duties of one's profession generally, or to perform a particular professional task, with skill of an acceptable quality.

classicalswinefever.name: classical swine fever
classicalswinefever.definition: Classical swine fever is an acute, highly contagious disease affecting swine of all ages and caused by the classical swine fever virus. It has a sudden onset with high morbidity and mortality.

hearingloss,functional.name: hearing loss , functional
hearingloss,functional.definition: Functional hearing loss is hearing loss without a physical basis. Often observed in patients with psychological or behavioral disorders.

insurance,nursingservices.name: insurance , nursing services
insurance,nursingservices.definition: Nursing services insurance is insurance providing benefits for the costs of care provided by nurses, especially nurse practitioners and [MASK].

uterinecervicalerosion.name: uterine cervical erosion
uterinecervicalerosion.definition: Uterine cervical erosion is loss or destruction of the epithelial lining of the uterine cervix.

cerebellarcortex.name: cerebellar cortex
cerebellarcortex.definition: Cerebellar cortex is the superficial gray matter of the cerebellum. It consists of two main layers, the stratum moleculare and the stratum granulosum.

protontherapy.name: proton therapy
protontherapy.definition: Proton therapy is the use of an external beam of protons as radiotherapy.

humanexperimentation.name: human experimentation
humanexperimentation.definition: Human experimentation is the use of humans as investigational subjects.

bookselection.name: book selection
bookselection.definition: Book selection is works about lists of books, articles, and other publications.

ontario.name: ontario
ontario.definition: Ontario is a province of Canada lying between the provinces of Manitoba and Quebec. Its capital is Toronto. It takes its name from [MASK] Ontario which is said to represent the Iroquois oniatariio, beautiful [MASK]. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p892 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p391)

genes,bacterial.name: genes , bacterial
genes,bacterial.definition: Bacterial genes is the functional hereditary units of bacteria.

dentistry,operative.name: dentistry , operative
dentistry,operative.definition: Operative dentistry is that phase of clinical dentistry concerned with the restoration of parts of existing teeth that are defective through disease, trauma, or abnormal development, to the state of normal function, health, and esthetics, including preventive, diagnostic, biological, mechanical, and therapeutic techniques, as well as material and instrument science and application. (Jablonski's Dictionary of Dentistry, 2d ed, p237)

virusassembly.name: virus assembly
virusassembly.definition: Virus assembly is the assembly of viral structural proteins and nucleic acid ([MASK] or viral rna) to form a virus particle.

radiationinjuries.name: radiation injuries
radiationinjuries.definition: Radiation injuries is harmful effects of non-experimental exposure to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation in vertebrates.

behavioralmedicine.name: behavioral medicine
behavioralmedicine.definition: Behavioral medicine is the interdisciplinary field concerned with the development and integration of behavioral and biomedical science, knowledge, and techniques relevant to health and illness and the application of this knowledge and these techniques to prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation.

orientation.name: orientation
orientation.definition: Orientation is awareness of oneself in relation to time, place and person.

silentmutation.name: silent mutation
silentmutation.definition: Silent mutation is a change to a dna sequence that doesn't change the amino acid sequence of the protein made.

cholinekinase.name: choline kinase
cholinekinase.definition: Choline kinase is an enzyme that is active in the first step of choline phosphoglyceride (lecithin) biosynthesis by catalyzing the phosphorylation of choline to phosphorylcholine in the presence of atp. Ethanolamine and its methyl and ethyl derivatives can also act as acceptors. ec 2.7.1.32.

vitaminbdeficiency.name: vitamin b deficiency
vitaminbdeficiency.definition: Vitamin b deficiency is a condition due to deficiency in any member of the vitamin b complex. These b vitamins are water-soluble and must be obtained from the diet because they are easily lost in the urine. Unlike the lipid-soluble vitamins, they cannot be stored in the body fat.

radioactivehazardrelease.name: radioactive hazard release
radioactivehazardrelease.definition: Radioactive hazard release is uncontrolled release of radioactive material from its containment. This either threatens to, or does, cause exposure to a radioactive hazard. Such an incident may occur accidentally or deliberately.

proline.name: proline
proline.definition: Proline is a non-essential amino acid that is synthesized from glutamic acid. It is an essential component of collagen and is important for proper functioning of joints and tendons.

drainage,postural.name: drainage , postural
drainage,postural.definition: Postural drainage is a rehabilitation therapy for removal of copious mucus secretion from the lung of patients with diseases such as chronic bronchitis; bronchiectasis; pulmonary abscess; or cystic fibrosis. The patient's head is placed in a downward incline (so the [MASK] is inferior to the affected area) for 15- to 20-minute sessions.

hostvsgraftreaction.name: host vs graft reaction
hostvsgraftreaction.definition: Host vs [MASK] reaction is the immune responses of a host to a [MASK]. a specific response is [MASK] [MASK].

phagetherapy.name: phage therapy
phagetherapy.definition: Phage therapy is therapeutic use of bacteriophages to treat diseases.

precisionmedicine.name: precision medicine
precisionmedicine.definition: Precision medicine is clinical, therapeutic and diagnostic approaches to optimal disease management based on individual variations in a patient's genetic profile.

child,abandoned.name: child , abandoned
child,abandoned.definition: Abandoned child is a child or adolescent who is deserted by parents or parent substitutes without regard for its future care.

metals,alkalineearth.name: metals , alkaline earth
metals,alkalineearth.definition: Alkaline earth metals is metals that constitute the group 2 (formerly group IIa) of the periodic [MASK].

stomachneoplasms.name: stomach neoplasms
stomachneoplasms.definition: Stomach neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the stomach.

milk.name: milk
milk.definition: Milk is the off-[MASK] liquid secreted by the mammary glands of humans and other mammals. It contains proteins, sugar, lipids, vitamins, and minerals.

tomography.name: tomography
tomography.definition: Tomography is imaging methods that result in sharp images of objects located on a chosen plane and blurred images located above or below the plane.

caspase9.name: caspase 9
caspase9.definition: Caspase 9 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a caspase recruitment domain in its pro-domain region. Caspase 9 is activated during cell stress by mitochondria-derived proapoptotic factors and by card signaling adaptor proteins such as apoptotic protease-activating factor 1. It activates apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases.

urinarybladderneoplasms.name: urinary bladder neoplasms
urinarybladderneoplasms.definition: [MASK] neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the [MASK].

laryngealneoplasms.name: laryngeal neoplasms
laryngealneoplasms.definition: Laryngeal neoplasms is cancers or tumors of the larynx or any of its parts: the glottis; epiglottis; laryngeal cartilages; [MASK]; and vocal cords.

celladhesion.name: cell adhesion
celladhesion.definition: Cell adhesion is adherence of cells to surfaces or to other cells.

femoralneckfractures.name: femoral neck fractures
femoralneckfractures.definition: Femoral [MASK] fractures is fractures of the short, constricted portion of the [MASK] bone between the femur head and the trochanters. It excludes intertrochanteric fractures which are hip fractures.

carcinoma,largecell.name: carcinoma , large cell
carcinoma,largecell.definition: Large cell carcinoma is a tumor of undifferentiated (anaplastic) cells of large size. It is usually bronchogenic. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

orfvirus.name: orf virus
orfvirus.definition: Orf virus is the type species of parapoxvirus which causes a skin infection in natural hosts, usually young sheep. Humans may contract local skin lesions by contact. The virus apparently persists in soil.

researchembryocreation.name: research embryo creation
researchembryocreation.definition: Research embryo creation is the creation of embryos specifically for research purposes.

chromosomes,human,pair16.name: chromosomes , human , pair 16
chromosomes,human,pair16.definition: Pair 16 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group e chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

victoria.name: victoria
victoria.definition: Victoria is a state in southeastern Australia, the southernmost state. Its capital is Melbourne. It was discovered in 1770 by Captain Cook and first settled by immigrants from Tasmania. In 1851 it was separated from New South Wales as a separate colony. Self-government was introduced in 1851; it became a state in 1901. It was named for Queen Victoria in 1851. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1295 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, p574)

mice,inbredbalbc.name: mice , inbred balb c
mice,inbredbalbc.definition: Inbred balb c mice is an inbred strain of mouse that is widely used in [MASK] studies and cancer research.

referencebooks,medical.name: reference books , medical
referencebooks,medical.definition: Medical reference books is books in the field of medicine intended primarily for consultation.

leukemia,myeloid.name: leukemia , myeloid
leukemia,myeloid.definition: Myeloid leukemia is form of leukemia characterized by an uncontrolled proliferation of the myeloid lineage and their precursors (myeloid progenitor cells) in the bone marrow and other sites.

radiotherapy.name: radiotherapy
radiotherapy.definition: Radiotherapy is the use of ionizing radiation to treat malignant neoplasms and some benign conditions.

helicobacterinfections.name: helicobacter infections
helicobacterinfections.definition: Helicobacter infections is infections with organisms of the genus helicobacter, particularly, in humans, helicobacter pylori. The clinical manifestations are focused in the stomach, usually the gastric mucosa and antrum, and the upper duodenum. This infection plays a major role in the pathogenesis of type b gastritis and peptic [MASK] disease.

chemistry,clinical.name: chemistry , clinical
chemistry,clinical.definition: Clinical chemistry is the specialty of [MASK] applied to assays of physiologically important substances found in blood, urine, tissues, and other biological fluids for the purpose of aiding the physician in making a diagnosis or following therapy.

peptidetransporter1.name: peptide transporter 1
peptidetransporter1.definition: Peptide transporter 1 is a proton-coupled symporter that transports oligopeptides and dipeptides. It localizes to the brush-border membrane of the intestinal epithelium and plays a critical role in the assimilation of dietary proteins.

photoreceptorcells.name: photoreceptor cells
photoreceptorcells.definition: Photoreceptor cells is specialized cells that detect and transduce light. They are classified into two types based on their light reception structure, the ciliary photoreceptors and the rhabdomeric photoreceptors with microvilli. Ciliary photoreceptor cells use opsins that activate a phosphodiesterase phosphodiesterase cascade. Rhabdomeric photoreceptor cells use opsins that activate a phospholipase c cascade.

hepatitisantigens.name: hepatitis antigens
hepatitisantigens.definition: Hepatitis antigens is antigens from any of the hepatitis viruses including surface, core, and other associated antigens.

dietarysugars.name: dietary sugars
dietarysugars.definition: Dietary sugars is monosaccharides and disaccharides present in food, such as those present in fruits and vegetables and milk products, or those added to food such as dietary sucrose ([MASK] sugar) or high fructose corn syrup.

therapy,softtissue.name: therapy , soft tissue
therapy,softtissue.definition: Soft tissue therapy is the assessment, treatment, and management of soft tissue injury or dysfunction. Therapy is designed to reduce tension and irritation in affected tissues and may include massage; muscle stretching, or direct pressure on muscles, connective tissue, and trigger points.

electromagneticphenomena.name: electromagnetic phenomena
electromagneticphenomena.definition: Electromagnetic phenomena is characteristics of electricity and magnetism such as charged particles and the properties and behavior of charged particles, and other phenomena related to or associated with electromagnetism.

armedconflicts.name: armed conflicts
armedconflicts.definition: Armed [MASK] is any differences arising between two nations or groups and leading to the intervention of armed forces.

kbcells.name: kb cells
kbcells.definition: Kb cells is this line kb is now known to be a subline of the ubiquitous KERATIN-forming tumor cell line HeLa. It was originally thought to be derived from an epidermal carcinoma of the mouth, but was subsequently found, based on isoenzyme analysis, HeLa marker chromosomes, and dna fingerprinting, to have been established via contamination by hela cells. The cells are positive for keratin by immunoperoxidase staining. kb cells have been reported to contain human papillomavirus18 (hpv-18) sequences.

transducers.name: transducers
transducers.definition: Transducers is any device or element which converts an input signal into an output signal of a different form. Examples include the microphone, phonographic pickup, loudspeaker, barometer, photoelectric cell, automobile horn, doorbell, and underwater sound transducer. (McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

dentalanxiety.name: dental anxiety
dentalanxiety.definition: Dental anxiety is abnormal fear or dread of visiting the dentist for preventive care or therapy and unwarranted anxiety over dental procedures.

nursingstaff.name: nursing staff
nursingstaff.definition: Nursing staff is personnel who provide nursing service to patients in an organized facility, institution, or agency.

mouth.name: mouth
mouth.definition: Mouth is the oval-shaped oral cavity located at the apex of the digestive tract and consisting of two parts: the vestibule and the oral cavity proper.

ribosomesubunits.name: ribosome subunits
ribosomesubunits.definition: Ribosome subunits is the two dissimilar sized ribonucleoprotein complexes that comprise a ribosome - the large ribosomal subunit and the small ribosomal subunit. The eukaryotic 80s ribosome is composed of a 60s large subunit and a 40s small subunit. The bacterial 70s ribosome is composed of a 50s large subunit and a 30s small subunit.

endocrinesystemdiseases.name: endocrine system diseases
endocrinesystemdiseases.definition: Endocrine system diseases is pathological processes of the endocrine glands, and diseases resulting from abnormal level of available hormones.

tumorvirusinfections.name: tumor virus infections
tumorvirusinfections.definition: Tumor virus infections is infections produced by oncogenic viruses. The infections caused by dna viruses are less numerous but more diverse than those caused by the rna oncogenic viruses.

neoplasms.name: neoplasms
neoplasms.definition: Neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue. Malignant neoplasms show a greater degree of anaplasia and have the properties of invasion and metastasis, compared to benign neoplasms.

trialoflabor.name: trial of labor
trialoflabor.definition: Trial of labor is allowing a woman to be in labor, obstetric long enough to determine if vaginal birth may be anticipated.

cysteinesynthase.name: cysteine synthase
cysteinesynthase.definition: [MASK] synthase is an enzyme that catalyzes the biosynthesis of [MASK] in microorganisms and plants from O-acetyl-L-serine and [MASK]. This enzyme was formerly listed as ec 4.2.99.8.

formicacidesters.name: formic acid esters
formicacidesters.definition: Formic acid esters is ester derivatives of formic acid with the formula h-coo-r.

heartbypass,right.name: heart bypass , right
heartbypass,right.definition: Right heart bypass is diversion of the flow of blood from the entrance to the right atrium directly to the [MASK], avoiding the right atrium and right ventricle (Dorland, 28th ed). This a permanent procedure often performed to bypass a congenitally deformed right atrium or right ventricle.

artificialgenefusion.name: artificial gene fusion
artificialgenefusion.definition: Artificial gene fusion is the in vitro fusion of genes by [MASK] techniques to analyze protein behavior or gene expression regulation, or to merge protein functions for specific medical or industrial uses.

angiogenesismodulatingagents.name: angiogenesis modulating agents
angiogenesismodulatingagents.definition: Angiogenesis modulating agents is agents that modulate the physiologic angiogenesis process. This is accomplished by endogenous angiogenic proteins and a variety of other chemicals and pharmaceutical agents.

heartrupture.name: heart rupture
heartrupture.definition: Heart rupture is disease-related laceration or tearing of tissues of the heart, including the free-wall myocardium; heart septum; papillary muscles; chordae tendineae; and any of the heart valves. Pathological rupture usually results from myocardial infarction (heart rupture, post-infarction).

atlanticocean.name: atlantic ocean
atlanticocean.definition: Atlantic ocean is body of water separating North and South America from Africa and Europe.

childbehavior.name: child behavior
childbehavior.definition: Child behavior is any observable response or action of a child from 24 months through 12 years of age. For neonates or children younger than 24 months, infant behavior is available.

statedentistry.name: state dentistry
statedentistry.definition: State dentistry is control, direction and financing of the total dental care of the population by a national government.

nationalhealthinsurance,unitedstates.name: national health insurance , united states
nationalhealthinsurance,unitedstates.definition: United states national health insurance is federal system administering national health insurance in the United States.

ribcage.name: rib cage
ribcage.definition: Rib cage is the bony thoracic enclosure consisting of the vertebral column; the ribs; the sternum; and the costal cartilage.

signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculefa.name: signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 1
signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculefa.definition: Signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 1 is a 70-kDa slam family receptor that consists of an extracellular immunoglobulin-like domain and an immunoglobulin c2-[MASK] domain. It is expressed primarily by thymocytes and activated t-lymphocytes, as well as by macrophages and [MASK]. It binds slamf1 receptors on other cells to mediate T-cell maturation and proliferation. It is also a receptor for the measles virus.

hemorrhagicfeverwithrenalsyndrome.name: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome
hemorrhagicfeverwithrenalsyndrome.definition: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome is an acute febrile disease occurring predominately in Asia. It is characterized by fever, prostration, vomiting, hemorrhagic phenonema, shock, and renal failure. It is caused by any one of several closely related species of the genus Hantavirus. The most severe form is caused by hantaan virus whose natural host is the rodent Apodemus agrarius. Milder forms are caused by seoul virus and transmitted by the rodents Rattus rattus and r. norvegicus, and the puumala virus with transmission by Clethrionomys galreolus.

publicreportingofhealthcaredata.name: public reporting of healthcare data
publicreportingofhealthcaredata.definition: Public reporting of healthcare data is required public availability of quality indicators data from health facilities.

esophagealsphincter,lower.name: esophageal sphincter , lower
esophagealsphincter,lower.definition: Lower esophageal sphincter is the physiologic or functional barrier to gastroesophageal reflux at the esophagogastric junction. Sphincteric muscles remain tonically contracted during the resting state and form the high-pressure zone separating the lumen of the esophagus from that of the stomach. (Haubrich et al, Bockus Gastroenterology, 5th ed., pp399, 415)

dnarepairenzymes.name: dna repair enzymes
dnarepairenzymes.definition: Dna repair enzymes is enzymes that are involved in the reconstruction of a continuous two-stranded dna molecule without mismatch from a molecule, which contained damaged regions.

livercirrhosis,experimental.name: liver cirrhosis , experimental
livercirrhosis,experimental.definition: Experimental liver cirrhosis is experimentally induced chronic injuries to the parenchymal cells in the liver to achieve a model for liver cirrhosis.

drugdiscovery.name: drug discovery
drugdiscovery.definition: Drug discovery is the process of finding chemicals for potential therapeutic use.

carbohydratebiochemistry.name: carbohydrate biochemistry
carbohydratebiochemistry.definition: Carbohydrate biochemistry is the study of the structure, biosynthesis, and function of carbohydrates and [MASK].

movementdisorders.name: movement disorders
movementdisorders.definition: Movement disorders is syndromes which feature dyskinesias as a cardinal manifestation of the disease process. Included in this category are degenerative, hereditary, post-infectious, medication-induced, post-inflammatory, and post-traumatic conditions.

trust.name: trust
trust.definition: Trust is confidence in or reliance on a person or thing.

bass.name: bass
bass.definition: Bass is common name for fishes belonging to the order Perciformes and occurring in three different families.

viruslatency.name: virus latency
viruslatency.definition: Virus latency is the ability of a pathogenic virus to lie dormant within a cell (latent infection). In eukaryotes, subsequent activation and viral replication is thought to be caused by extracellular stimulation of cellular transcription factors. Latency in bacteriophage is maintained by the expression of virally encoded repressors.

rapidsequenceinductionandintubation.name: rapid sequence induction and intubation
rapidsequenceinductionandintubation.definition: Rapid sequence induction and [MASK] is a method of maintaining airway patency and administering anesthesia during emergency situations when it cannot be determined if the patient is fasting or not; or in other instances where there is a risk of aspiration. The method includes a series of events that involve the administration of sedatives to induce unconsciousness, followed by neuromuscular block agents to improve the intubating conditions, followed by endotracheal [MASK].

cosmicradiation.name: cosmic radiation
cosmicradiation.definition: Cosmic radiation is high-energy radiation or particles from extraterrestrial space that strike the earth, its atmosphere, or spacecraft and may create secondary radiation as a result of collisions with the atmosphere or spacecraft.

anesthesia,local.name: anesthesia , local
anesthesia,local.definition: Local anesthesia is a blocking of [MASK] to a specific area by an injection of an anesthetic agent.

oralstage.name: oral stage
oralstage.definition: Oral stage is the earliest of the stages of infantile psychosexual development, lasting from birth to 12 months or longer.

leadpoisoning,nervoussystem,childhood.name: lead poisoning , nervous system , childhood
leadpoisoning,nervoussystem,childhood.definition: Childhood nervous system lead poisoning is neurologic disorders occurring in children following lead exposure. The most frequent manifestation of childhood lead toxicity is an encephalopathy associated with chronic ingestion of lead that usually presents between the ages of 1 and 3 years. Clinical manifestations include behavioral changes followed by lethargy; convulsions; hallucinations; delirium; ataxia; and vomiting. Elevated [MASK] (hypertension, intracranial) and cerebral edema may occur. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1210-2)

affect.name: affect
affect.definition: Affect is the feeling-tone accompaniment of an idea or mental representation. It is the most direct psychic derivative of instinct and the psychic representative of the various bodily changes by means of which instincts manifest themselves.

stroke.name: stroke
stroke.definition: Stroke is a group of pathological conditions characterized by sudden, non-convulsive loss of neurological function due to brain ischemia or intracranial hemorrhages. Stroke is classified by the type of tissue necrosis, such as the anatomic location, vasculature involved, etiology, age of the affected individual, and hemorrhagic vs. non-hemorrhagic nature. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp777-810)

bloodflowvelocity.name: blood flow velocity
bloodflowvelocity.definition: Blood flow velocity is a value equal to the total volume flow divided by the cross-sectional area of the vascular bed.

antibodies,viral.name: antibodies , viral
antibodies,viral.definition: Viral antibodies is immunoglobulins produced in response to viral antigens.

escherichiacoliproteins.name: escherichia coli proteins
escherichiacoliproteins.definition: Escherichia coli proteins is proteins obtained from escherichia coli.

foodlabeling.name: food labeling
foodlabeling.definition: Food labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a food or its container or wrapper. The concept includes ingredients, nutritional value, directions, warnings, and other relevant information.

patientcompliance.name: patient compliance
patientcompliance.definition: Patient compliance is voluntary cooperation of the patient in following a prescribed regimen.

cartilage.name: cartilage
cartilage.definition: Cartilage is a non-vascular form of connective tissue composed of chondrocytes embedded in a matrix that includes chondroitin sulfate and various types of fibrillar collagen. There are three major types: hyaline cartilage; fibrocartilage; and elastic cartilage.

fetalproteins.name: fetal proteins
fetalproteins.definition: Fetal proteins is proteins that are preferentially expressed or upregulated during fetal development.

moleculartargetedtherapy.name: molecular targeted therapy
moleculartargetedtherapy.definition: Molecular targeted therapy is treatments with drugs which interact with or block synthesis of specific cellular components characteristic of the individual's disease in order to stop or interrupt the specific biochemical dysfunction involved in progression of the disease.

preventivedentistry.name: preventive dentistry
preventivedentistry.definition: Preventive dentistry is the branch of dentistry concerned with the prevention of disease and the maintenance and promotion of [MASK].

contraceptivedevices,female.name: contraceptive devices , female
contraceptivedevices,female.definition: Female contraceptive devices is contraceptive devices used by females.

tears.name: tears
tears.definition: Tears is the fluid secreted by the lacrimal glands. This fluid moistens the conjunctiva and cornea.

chemotaxis,leukocyte.name: chemotaxis , leukocyte
chemotaxis,leukocyte.definition: Leukocyte chemotaxis is the movement of leukocytes in response to a chemical concentration gradient or to products formed in an immunologic reaction.

clostridium.name: clostridium
clostridium.definition: Clostridium is a genus of motile or nonmotile gram-positive bacteria of the family Clostridiaceae. Many species have been identified with some being pathogenic. They occur in water, soil, and in the intestinal tract of humans and lower animals.

duodenalulcer.name: duodenal ulcer
duodenalulcer.definition: Duodenal [MASK] is a peptic [MASK] located in the duodenum.

immobilization.name: immobilization
immobilization.definition: Immobilization is the restriction of the movement of whole or part of the body by physical means (restraint, physical) or chemically by analgesia, or the use of tranquilizing agents or neuromuscular nondepolarizing agents. It includes experimental protocols used to evaluate the physiologic effects of immobility.

publichealthpractice.name: public health practice
publichealthpractice.definition: Public health practice is the activities and endeavors of the public health services in a community on any level.

pneumonia,viral.name: pneumonia , viral
pneumonia,viral.definition: Viral pneumonia is inflammation of the lung parenchyma that is caused by a viral infection.

salmon.name: salmon
salmon.definition: Salmon is fish of the genera oncorhynchus and Salmo in the family salmonidae. They are anadromous game fish, frequenting the coastal waters of both the North Atlantic and Pacific. They are known for their gameness as a sport fish and for the quality of their flesh as a [MASK] fish. (Webster, 3d ed).

controlledsubstances.name: controlled substances
controlledsubstances.definition: Controlled substances is drugs or chemical agents whose manufacture, possession, or use are regulated by government. This may include narcotics and prescription medications.

receptors,cholinergic.name: receptors , cholinergic
receptors,cholinergic.definition: Cholinergic receptors is cell surface proteins that bind acetylcholine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Cholinergic receptors are divided into two major classes, muscarinic and nicotinic, based originally on their affinity for nicotine and muscarine. Each group is further subdivided based on pharmacology, location, mode of action, and/or molecular biology.

chromosomes,human.name: chromosomes , human
chromosomes,human.definition: Human chromosomes is very long dna molecules and associated proteins, histones, and non-histone chromosomal proteins (chromosomal proteins, non-histone). Normally 46 chromosomes, including two [MASK] chromosomes are found in the nucleus of human cells. They carry the hereditary information of the individual.

medicaloncology.name: medical oncology
medicaloncology.definition: Medical oncology is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of neoplasms.

nursepractitioners.name: nurse practitioners
nursepractitioners.definition: Nurse practitioners is nurses who are specially trained to assume an expanded role in providing medical care under the supervision of a physician.

disabilitystudies.name: disability studies
disabilitystudies.definition: Disability studies is interdisciplinary programs of academic study that de-stigmatize disease, illness, and impairment.

nervoussystemmalformations.name: nervous system malformations
nervoussystemmalformations.definition: Nervous system malformations is structural abnormalities of the central or peripheral nervous system resulting primarily from defects of embryogenesis.

bottlefeeding.name: bottle feeding
bottlefeeding.definition: Bottle feeding is use of nursing bottles for feeding. Applies to humans and animals.

earlyintervention,educational.name: early intervention , educational
earlyintervention,educational.definition: Educational early intervention is procedures and programs that facilitate the development or skill acquisition in infants and young children who have disabilities, who are at risk for developing disabilities, or who are gifted. It includes programs that are designed to prevent handicapping conditions in infants and young children and family-centered programs designed to affect the functioning of infants and children with special needs. (From Journal of Early Intervention, [MASK], 1989, vol. 13, no. 1, p. 3; a Discursive Dictionary of Health Care, prepared for the u.s. House of Representatives Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce, 1976)

heartfailure,diastolic.name: heart failure , diastolic
heartfailure,diastolic.definition: Diastolic heart failure is heart failure caused by abnormal myocardial relaxation during diastole leading to defective cardiac filling.

testiculardiseases.name: testicular diseases
testiculardiseases.definition: Testicular diseases is pathological processes of the testis.

immunity,herd.name: immunity , herd
immunity,herd.definition: Herd immunity is the non-susceptibility to infection of a large group of individuals in a population. a variety of factors can be responsible for herd immunity and this gives rise to the different definitions used in the literature. Most commonly, herd immunity refers to the case when, if most of the population is immune, infection of a single individual will not cause an epidemic. Also, in such immunized populations, susceptible individuals are not likely to become infected. Herd immunity can also refer to the case when unprotected individuals fail to contract a disease because the infecting organism has been banished from the population.

americanpublichealthassociation.name: american public health association
americanpublichealthassociation.definition: American public health association is professional organization concerned with issues affecting personal and environmental health, including federal and state funding for health programs, programs related to chronic and infectious diseases, and professional education in public health.

jawneoplasms.name: jaw neoplasms
jawneoplasms.definition: Jaw neoplasms is cancers or tumors of the maxilla or mandible unspecified. For neoplasms of the maxilla, [MASK] is available and of the mandible, mandibular neoplasms is available.

workcapacityevaluation.name: work capacity evaluation
workcapacityevaluation.definition: Work capacity evaluation is assessment of physiological capacities in relation to job requirements. It is usually done by measuring certain physiological (e.g., circulatory and respiratory) variables during a gradually increasing workload until specific limitations occur with respect to those variables.

complementfactori.name: complement factor i
complementfactori.definition: Complement factor i is a plasma serine proteinase that cleaves the alpha-chains of C3b and C4b in the presence of the cofactors complement factor h and C4-binding protein, respectively. It is a 66-kDa glycoprotein that converts C3b to inactivated C3b (iC3b) followed by the release of two fragments, C3c (150-kDa) and C3dg (41-kDa). It was formerly called kaf, C3bINF, or enzyme 3b inactivator.

intracranialthrombosis.name: intracranial thrombosis
intracranialthrombosis.definition: Intracranial thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in a blood vessel within the skull. Intracranial thrombosis can lead to thrombotic occlusions and brain infarction. The majority of the thrombotic occlusions are associated with atherosclerosis.

genes,lethal.name: genes , lethal
genes,lethal.definition: Lethal genes is genes whose loss of function or gain of function mutation leads to the death of the carrier prior to maturity. They may be essential genes (genes, essential) required for viability, or genes which cause a block of function of an essential gene at a time when the essential gene function is required for viability.

hypothalamus.name: hypothalamus
hypothalamus.definition: Hypothalamus is ventral part of the diencephalon extending from the region of the optic chiasm to the caudal border of the mammillary bodies and forming the inferior and lateral walls of the third ventricle.

plantextracts.name: plant extracts
plantextracts.definition: Plant extracts is concentrated pharmaceutical preparations of plants obtained by removing active constituents with a suitable solvent, which is evaporated away, and adjusting the residue to a prescribed standard.

analcanal.name: anal canal
analcanal.definition: Anal canal is the terminal segment of the large intestine, beginning from the ampulla of the rectum and ending at the anus.

glycineagents.name: glycine agents
glycineagents.definition: Glycine agents is substances used for their pharmacological actions on glycinergic systems. Glycinergic agents include agonists, antagonists, degradation or uptake inhibitors, depleters, precursors, and modulators of receptor function.

compactdisks.name: compact disks
compactdisks.definition: Compact disks is computer disks storing data with a maximum reduction of space and bandwidth. The compact size reduces cost of transmission and storage.

psychology,medical.name: psychology , medical
psychology,medical.definition: Medical psychology is a branch of psychology in which there is collaboration between psychologists and physicians in the management of medical problems. It differs from clinical psychology, which is concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of behavior disorders.

lymphocytes,null.name: lymphocytes , null
lymphocytes,null.definition: Null lymphocytes is a class of lymphocytes characterized by the lack of surface markers specific for either t or b lymphocytes.

breastneoplasms.name: breast neoplasms
breastneoplasms.definition: Breast neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the human breast.

northwestterritories.name: northwest territories
northwestterritories.definition: Northwest territories is a federally administered division of Canada. Its capital is Yellowknife. The former northern and eastern-most parts of the Territory comprise the new territory of Nunavut, effective April 1, 1999.

drinkingwater.name: drinking water
drinkingwater.definition: Drinking water is water that is intended to be ingested.

healthcarecosts.name: health care costs
healthcarecosts.definition: Health care costs is the actual costs of providing services related to the delivery of health care, including the costs of procedures, therapies, and medications. It is differentiated from health expenditures, which refers to the amount of money paid for the services, and from fees, which refers to the amount charged, regardless of cost.

rasproteins.name: ras proteins
rasproteins.definition: Ras proteins is small, monomeric GTP-binding proteins encoded by ras genes (genes, ras). The protooncogene-derived protein, proto-oncogene protein p21(ras), plays a role in normal cellular growth, differentiation and development. The oncogene-derived protein oncogene protein p21(ras) can play a role in aberrant cellular regulation during neoplastic cell transformation (cell transformation, neoplastic). This enzyme was formerly listed as ec 3.6.1.47.

glucosetolerancetest.name: glucose tolerance test
glucosetolerancetest.definition: Glucose tolerance test is a test to determine the ability of an individual to maintain homeostasis of blood glucose. It includes measuring blood glucose levels in a fasting state, and at prescribed intervals before and after oral glucose intake (75 or 100 g) or [MASK] (0.5 g/kg).

immunoglobulina,secretory.name: immunoglobulin a , secretory
immunoglobulina,secretory.definition: Secretory immunoglobulin a is the principle immunoglobulin in exocrine secretions such as milk, respiratory and intestinal mucin, saliva and tears. The complete molecule (around 400 kD) is composed of two four-chain units of immunoglobulin a, one [MASK] and one j chain (immunoglobulin j-chains).

colorvisiondefects.name: color vision defects
colorvisiondefects.definition: [MASK] vision defects is defects of [MASK] vision are mainly hereditary traits but can be secondary to acquired or developmental abnormalities in the [MASK]). Severity of hereditary defects of [MASK] vision depends on the degree of mutation of the rod opsins genes (on x chromosome and chromosome 3) that code the photopigments for red, green and blue.

vitalsigns.name: vital signs
vitalsigns.definition: Vital signs is the signs of life that may be monitored or measured, namely pulse rate, respiratory rate, body temperature, and blood pressure.

neuronaloutgrowth.name: neuronal outgrowth
neuronaloutgrowth.definition: Neuronal outgrowth is formation of neuronal processes (axons; neurites) toward a target cell.

equivalencetrial.name: equivalence trial
equivalencetrial.definition: Equivalence trial is trial that aims to show a new treatment is no better and no worse than the standard treatment.

anemia,neonatal.name: anemia , neonatal
anemia,neonatal.definition: Neonatal anemia is the mildest form of erythroblastosis fetalis in which anemia is the chief manifestation.

parietallobe.name: parietal lobe
parietallobe.definition: Parietal lobe is upper central part of the cerebral hemisphere. It is located posterior to central sulcus, anterior to the occipital lobe, and superior to the temporal lobes.

language.name: language
language.definition: Language is a verbal or nonverbal means of communicating ideas or feelings.

gumarabic.name: gum arabic
gumarabic.definition: Gum arabic is powdered exudate from various Acacia species, especially a. senegal (Leguminosae). It forms mucilage or syrup in water. Gum arabic is used as a suspending agent, excipient, and emulsifier in foods and pharmaceuticals.

ppardelta.name: ppar delta
ppardelta.definition: Ppar delta is a nuclear transcription factor. It is activated by prostacyclin.

gingivalhypertrophy.name: gingival hypertrophy
gingivalhypertrophy.definition: Gingival hypertrophy is abnormal enlargement or overgrowth of the gingivae brought about by enlargement of existing cells.

eggshell.name: egg shell
eggshell.definition: Egg shell is a hard or leathery calciferous exterior covering of an egg.

melanoma.name: melanoma
melanoma.definition: Melanoma is a malignant neoplasm derived from cells that are capable of forming melanin, which may occur in the skin of any part of the body, in the eye, or, rarely, in the mucous membranes of the genitalia, anus, oral cavity, or other sites. It occurs mostly in adults and may originate de novo or from a pigmented nevus or malignant lentigo. Melanomas frequently metastasize widely, and the regional [MASK] nodes, liver, lungs, and brain are likely to be involved. The incidence of malignant skin melanomas is rising rapidly in all parts of the world. (Stedman, 25th ed; from Rook et al., Textbook of [MASK], 4th ed, p2445)

particlesize.name: particle size
particlesize.definition: Particle size is relating to the size of solids.

iron,dietary.name: iron , dietary
iron,dietary.definition: Dietary iron is iron or iron compounds used in foods or as food. Dietary iron is important in oxygen transport and the synthesis of the iron-porphyrin proteins hemoglobin, myoglobin, cytochromes, and [MASK]. Insufficient amounts of dietary iron can lead to iron-deficiency anemia.

peptideelongationfactorg.name: peptide elongation factor g
peptideelongationfactorg.definition: Peptide elongation factor g is peptide Elongation Factor g catalyzes the translocation of peptidyl-tRNA from the a to the p site of bacterial ribosomes by a process linked to hydrolysis of gtp to gdp.

dosagecompensation,genetic.name: dosage compensation , genetic
dosagecompensation,genetic.definition: Genetic dosage compensation is genetic mechanisms that allow genes to be expressed at a similar level irrespective of their gene dosage. This term is usually used in discussing genes that lie on the [MASK] chromosomes. Because the [MASK] chromosomes are only partially homologous, there is a different copy number, i.e., dosage, of these genes in males vs. females. In drosophila, dosage compensation is accomplished by hypertranscription of genes located on the x chromosome. In mammals, dosage compensation of x chromosome genes is accomplished by random [MASK] of one of the two x chromosomes in the female.

verballearning.name: verbal learning
verballearning.definition: Verbal learning is learning to respond verbally to a verbal stimulus cue.

potassiumchannels.name: potassium channels
potassiumchannels.definition: Potassium channels is cell membrane glycoproteins that are selectively permeable to potassium ions. At least eight major groups of k channels exist and they are made up of dozens of different subunits.

angiotensiniitype2receptorblockers.name: angiotensin ii type 2 receptor blockers
angiotensiniitype2receptorblockers.definition: Angiotensin ii type 2 receptor blockers is agents that antagonize the angiotensin ii type 2 receptor.

pressureulcer.name: pressure ulcer
pressureulcer.definition: Pressure [MASK] is an ulceration caused by prolonged pressure on the skin and tissues when one stays in one position for a long period of time, such as lying in bed. The bony areas of the body are the most frequently affected sites which become ischemic (ischemia) under sustained and constant pressure.

sorghum.name: sorghum
sorghum.definition: Sorghum is a plant genus of the family poaceae. The grain is used for food and for [MASK]. This should not be confused with kaffir lime or with kefir milk product.

connectivetissuegrowthfactor.name: connective tissue growth factor
connectivetissuegrowthfactor.definition: Connective tissue growth factor is a ccn protein family member that regulates a variety of extracellular functions including cell adhesion; cell migration; and extracellular matrix synthesis. It is found in hypertrophic chondrocytes where it may play a role in chondrogenesis and endochondral ossification.

genotype.name: genotype
genotype.definition: Genotype is the genetic constitution of the individual, comprising the alleles present at each genetic locus.

leisureactivities.name: leisure activities
leisureactivities.definition: Leisure activities is voluntary use of free time for activities outside the daily routine.

respiratoryaspiration.name: respiratory aspiration
respiratoryaspiration.definition: Respiratory aspiration is [MASK] liquid or solids, such as stomach contents, into the respiratory tract. When this causes severe lung damage, it is called aspiration pneumonia.

surgery,oral.name: surgery , oral
surgery,oral.definition: Oral surgery is a dental specialty concerned with the diagnosis and surgical treatment of disease, injuries, and defects of the human oral and maxillofacial region.

intestinalfistula.name: intestinal fistula
intestinalfistula.definition: Intestinal fistula is an abnormal anatomical passage between the intestine, and another segment of the intestine or other organs. External intestinal fistula is connected to the skin (enterocutaneous fistula). Internal intestinal fistula can be connected to a number of organs, such as stomach (gastrocolic fistula), the biliary tract (cholecystoduodenal fistula), or the [MASK] of the urinary tract (colovesical fistula). Risk factors include inflammatory processes, cancer, radiation treatment, and surgical misadventures (medical errors).

epithelialattachment.name: epithelial attachment
epithelialattachment.definition: Epithelial attachment is a wedge-shaped collar of epithelial cells which form the attachment of the gingiva to the tooth surface at the base of the gingival crevice.

sequenceanalysis,rna.name: sequence analysis , rna
sequenceanalysis,rna.definition: Rna sequence analysis is a multistage process that includes cloning, physical mapping, subcloning, sequencing, and information analysis of an rna sequence.

incidentalfindings.name: incidental findings
incidentalfindings.definition: Incidental findings is unanticipated information discovered in the course of testing or medical care. Used in discussions of information that may have social or psychological consequences, such as when it is learned that a child's biological [MASK] is someone other than the putative [MASK], or that a person tested for one disease or disorder has, or is at risk for, something else.

nitricoxidesynthasetypei.name: nitric oxide synthase type i
nitricoxidesynthasetypei.definition: [MASK] synthase type i is a CALCIUM-dependent, constitutively-expressed form of [MASK] synthase found primarily in nerve tissue.

rootnodules,plant.name: root nodules , plant
rootnodules,plant.definition: Plant root nodules is knobbed structures formed from and attached to plant roots, especially of legumes, which result from symbiotic infection by nitrogen fixing bacteria such as rhizobium or frankia. Root nodules are structures related to mycorrhizae formed by symbiotic associations with fungi.

drugdeliverydevice.name: drug delivery device
drugdeliverydevice.definition: Drug delivery device is engineered technologies for the targeted delivery and/or controlled release of therapeutic agents.

patients.name: patients
patients.definition: Patients is individuals participating in the health care system for the purpose of receiving therapeutic, diagnostic, or preventive procedures.

educationalactivity.name: educational activity
educationalactivity.definition: Educational activity is acquisition of knowledge as a result of instruction in a formal course of study.

managementinformationsystems.name: management information systems
managementinformationsystems.definition: Management information systems is systems designed to provide information primarily concerned with the administrative functions associated with the provision and utilization of services; also includes program planning, etc.

thumb.name: thumb
thumb.definition: Thumb is the first digit on the radial side of the hand which in humans lies opposite the other four.

biomedicalenhancement.name: biomedical enhancement
biomedicalenhancement.definition: Biomedical enhancement is the use of technology-based interventions to improve functional capacities rather than to treat disease.

patientsatisfaction.name: patient satisfaction
patientsatisfaction.definition: Patient [MASK] is the degree to which the individual regards the health care service or product or the manner in which it is delivered by the provider as useful, effective, or beneficial.

hepatitisevirus.name: hepatitis e virus
hepatitisevirus.definition: Hepatitis e virus is a positive-stranded rna virus species in the genus hepevirus, causing enterically-transmitted non-A, non-B hepatitis (hepatitis e).

glycogenstoragedisease.name: glycogen storage disease
glycogenstoragedisease.definition: Glycogen storage disease is a group of inherited metabolic disorders involving the enzymes responsible for the synthesis and degradation of glycogen. In some patients, prominent liver involvement is presented. In others, more generalized storage of glycogen occurs, sometimes with prominent cardiac involvement.

patientcarebundles.name: patient care bundles
patientcarebundles.definition: Patient care bundles is small sets of evidence-based interventions for a defined patient population and care setting.

projectivetechniques.name: projective techniques
projectivetechniques.definition: Projective techniques is techniques to reveal personality attributes by responses to relatively unstructured or ambiguous stimuli.

moraldevelopment.name: moral development
moraldevelopment.definition: Moral development is the process by which individuals internalize standards of right and wrong conduct.

glutamatesynthase(nadh).name: glutamate synthase ( nadh )
glutamatesynthase(nadh).definition: Glutamate synthase (nadh) is A flavoprotein enzyme for [MASK] assimilation in bacteria, microorganisms and plants. It catalyzes the oxidation of 2 molecules of L-glutamate to generate [MASK] and 2-oxoglutarate in the presence of NAD+.

physicalandrehabilitationmedicine.name: physical and rehabilitation medicine
physicalandrehabilitationmedicine.definition: Physical and rehabilitation medicine is a medical specialty concerned with the use of physical agents, mechanical apparatus, and manipulation in rehabilitating physically diseased or injured patients.

somatosensorycortex.name: somatosensory cortex
somatosensorycortex.definition: Somatosensory cortex is area of the parietal lobe concerned with receiving sensations such as movement, pain, pressure, position, temperature, touch, and vibration. It lies posterior to the central sulcus.

perioperativecare.name: perioperative care
perioperativecare.definition: Perioperative care is interventions to provide care prior to, during, and immediately after surgery.

authorship.name: authorship
authorship.definition: Authorship is the profession of writing. Also the identity of the writer as the creator of a literary production.

horses.name: horses
horses.definition: Horses is large, hoofed mammals of the family equidae. Horses are active day and night with most of the day spent seeking and consuming food. Feeding peaks occur in the early morning and late afternoon, and there are several daily periods of rest.

cooperativebehavior.name: cooperative behavior
cooperativebehavior.definition: Cooperative behavior is the interaction of two or more persons or organizations directed toward a common goal which is mutually beneficial. An act or instance of working or acting together for a common purpose or benefit, i.e., joint action. (From Random House Dictionary Unabridged, 2d ed)

adiponectin.name: adiponectin
adiponectin.definition: Adiponectin is a 30-kDa complement C1Q-related protein, the most abundant gene product secreted by fat cells of the [MASK] adipose tissue. Adiponectin modulates several physiological processes, such as metabolism of glucose and fatty acids, and immune responses. Decreased plasma adiponectin levels are associated with insulin resistance; type 2 diabetes mellitus; obesity; and atherosclerosis.

publications.name: publications
publications.definition: Publications is copies of a work or document distributed to the public by sale, rental, lease, or lending. (From ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p181)

antigens,viral.name: antigens , viral
antigens,viral.definition: Viral antigens is substances elaborated by viruses that have antigenic activity.

semiconductors.name: semiconductors
semiconductors.definition: Semiconductors is materials that have a limited and usually variable electrical conductivity. They are particularly useful for the production of solid-state electronic devices.

multipletrauma.name: multiple trauma
multipletrauma.definition: Multiple trauma is multiple physical insults or injuries occurring simultaneously.

broadlyneutralizingantibodies.name: broadly neutralizing antibodies
broadlyneutralizingantibodies.definition: Broadly neutralizing antibodies is neutralizing antibodies that reduce or abolish some biological activity of a soluble antigen or infectious agent (e.g., hiv) by targeting several epitopes.

feeschedules.name: fee schedules
feeschedules.definition: Fee schedules is a listing of established professional service charges, for specified dental and medical procedures.

ventricularfunction.name: ventricular function
ventricularfunction.definition: Ventricular function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the heart ventricles.

logicalobservationidentifiersnamesandcod.name: logical observation identifiers names and codes
logicalobservationidentifiersnamesandcod.definition: Logical [MASK] identifiers names and codes is a vocabulary [MASK] of universal identifiers for laboratory and clinical test results. Its purpose is to facilitate the exchange and pooling of results for clinical care, outcomes management, and research. It is produced by the Regenstrief Institute. (loinc and relma [Internet]. Indianapolis: The Regenstrief Institute; c1995-2001 [cited 2002 Apr 2]. Available from http://www.regenstrief.org/loinc)

coldinjury.name: cold injury
coldinjury.definition: Cold injury is a physical injury caused by exposure of the body to extremely low ambient temperatures that may lead to loss of [MASK], or in extreme cases, death. Examples of cold injury are frostbite and chilblains.

cellnucleusdivision.name: cell nucleus division
cellnucleusdivision.definition: Cell nucleus division is the process by which the cell nucleus is divided.

compliance.name: compliance
compliance.definition: Compliance is distensibility measure of a chamber such as the lungs (lung compliance) or [MASK]. Compliance is expressed as a change in volume per unit change in pressure.

leadpoisoning,nervoussystem.name: lead poisoning , nervous system
leadpoisoning,nervoussystem.definition: Nervous system lead poisoning is injury to the nervous system secondary to exposure to lead compounds. Two distinct clinical patterns occur in children (lead poisoning, nervous system, childhood) and adults (lead poisoning, nervous system, adult). In children, lead poisoning typically produces an encephalopathy. In adults, exposure to toxic levels of lead is associated with a peripheral neuropathy.

lymphnodes.name: lymph nodes
lymphnodes.definition: [MASK] nodes is they are oval or bean shaped bodies (1 - 30 mm in diameter) located along the lymphatic system.

abscess.name: abscess
abscess.definition: Abscess is accumulation of purulent material in tissues, organs, or circumscribed spaces, usually associated with signs of infection.

chromosomes,human,pair21.name: chromosomes , human , pair 21
chromosomes,human,pair21.definition: Pair 21 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group g chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

clinicaltrials,phaseivastopic.name: clinical trials , phase iv as topic
clinicaltrials,phaseivastopic.definition: Phase iv as topic clinical trials is works about planned post-marketing studies of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques that have been approved for general sale. These studies are often conducted to obtain additional data about the safety and efficacy of a product. This concept includes phase iv studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

casereports.name: case reports
casereports.definition: Case reports is clinical presentations that may be followed by evaluative studies that eventually lead to a diagnosis.

multimodalimaging.name: multimodal imaging
multimodalimaging.definition: Multimodal imaging is the use of combination of imaging techniques or platforms (e.g., mri scan and pet scan) encompassing aspects of anatomical, functional, or molecular imaging methods.

identitycrisis.name: identity crisis
identitycrisis.definition: Identity crisis is chaotic concept of self wherein one's role in life appears to be an insoluble dilemma often expressed by isolation, withdrawal, rebellion and extremism.

grouppractice,dental.name: group practice , dental
grouppractice,dental.definition: Dental group practice is any group of three or more full-time dentists, organized in a legally recognized entity for the provision of dental care, sharing space, equipment, personnel and records for both patient care and business management, and who have a predetermined arrangement for the distribution of income.

greenhousegases.name: greenhouse gases
greenhousegases.definition: Greenhouse gases is gaseous elements, chemicals that are in the atmosphere that may contribute to [MASK].

rectum.name: rectum
rectum.definition: Rectum is the distal segment of the large intestine, between the sigmoid colon and the anal canal.

bonescrews.name: bone screws
bonescrews.definition: Bone screws is specialized devices used in orthopedic surgery to repair bone fractures.

mapkinasekinasekinases.name: map kinase kinase kinases
mapkinasekinasekinases.definition: Map kinase kinase kinases is mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinases (MAPKKKs) are serine-threonine protein kinases that initiate protein kinase signaling cascades. They phosphorylate mitogen-activated protein kinase kinases; (MAPKKs) which in turn phosphorylate mitogen-activated protein kinases; (MAPKs).

anteriorchamber.name: anterior chamber
anteriorchamber.definition: Anterior chamber is the space in the eye, filled with aqueous humor, bounded anteriorly by the cornea and a small portion of the sclera and posteriorly by a small portion of the [MASK], the iris, and that part of the crystalline lens which presents through the pupil. (Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed, p109)

probabilitytheory.name: probability theory
probabilitytheory.definition: Probability theory is the branch of mathematics dealing with the purely logical properties of probability. Its theorems underlie most statistical methods. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

bibliographyofmedicine.name: bibliography of medicine
bibliographyofmedicine.definition: Bibliography of medicine is a list of works, documents, and other publications on medical subjects and topics of interest to the field of medicine.

neoplasms,multipleprimary.name: neoplasms , multiple primary
neoplasms,multipleprimary.definition: Multiple primary neoplasms is two or more abnormal growths of tissue occurring simultaneously and presumed to be of separate origin. The neoplasms may be histologically the same or different, and may be found in the same or different sites.

bodysystem.name: body system
bodysystem.definition: Body system is groups of organs and tissues that work together to perform important jobs for the body.

freshwater.name: fresh water
freshwater.definition: Fresh water is water containing no significant amounts of [MASK], such as water from [MASK] and [MASK].

manuallymphaticdrainage.name: manual lymphatic drainage
manuallymphaticdrainage.definition: Manual lymphatic drainage is the application of massage to control edema and improve circulation by manually moving excess [MASK] out of a tissue.

healthworkforce.name: health workforce
healthworkforce.definition: Health workforce is the availability of health personnel. It includes the demand and recruitment of both professional and allied health personnel, their present and future supply and distribution, and their assignment and utilization.

therapeutics.name: therapeutics
therapeutics.definition: Therapeutics is procedures concerned with the remedial treatment or prevention of diseases.

directivecounseling.name: directive counseling
directivecounseling.definition: Directive counseling is counseling during which a professional plays an active role in a client's or patient's decision making by offering advice, guidance, and/or recommendations.

familynursepractitioners.name: family nurse practitioners
familynursepractitioners.definition: Family nurse practitioners is registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to patients of all age levels, and who focus their efforts on the health care needs of the entire family.

neurons,afferent.name: neurons , afferent
neurons,afferent.definition: Afferent neurons is neurons which conduct nerve impulses to the central nervous system.

transfattyacids.name: trans fatty acids
transfattyacids.definition: Trans fatty acids is unsaturated fatty acids that contain at least one double bond in the trans configuration, which results in a greater bond angle than the cis configuration. This results in a more extended fatty acid chain similar to saturated fatty acids, with closer packing and reduced fluidity. hydrogenation of unsaturated fatty acids increases the trans content.

tumornecrosisfactorreceptorsuperfamily,m.name: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 9
tumornecrosisfactorreceptorsuperfamily,m.definition: Member 9 tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily that is specific for 4-1bb ligand. It is found in a variety of immune cell types including activated t-lymphocytes; natural killer cells; and [MASK]. Activation of the receptor on t-lymphocytes plays a role in their expansion, production of cytokines and survival. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

hairpreparations.name: hair preparations
hairpreparations.definition: Hair preparations is hair grooming, cleansing and modifying products meant for topical application to hair, usually human. They include sprays, bleaches, dyes, conditioners, rinses, shampoos, nutrient lotions, etc.

acidsensingionchannelblockers.name: acid sensing ion channel blockers
acidsensingionchannelblockers.definition: Acid sensing ion channel blockers is a subclass of sodium channel blockers that are specific for acid-sensing sodium channels.

receptors,histamine.name: receptors , histamine
receptors,histamine.definition: Histamine receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind histamine and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Histamine receptors are widespread in the central nervous system and in peripheral tissues. Three types have been recognized and designated h1, h2, and h3. They differ in pharmacology, distribution, and mode of action.

ratesettingandreview.name: rate setting and review
ratesettingandreview.definition: Rate setting and review is a method of examining and setting levels of payments.

fibrinfoam.name: fibrin foam
fibrinfoam.definition: Fibrin foam is a dry artificial sterile sponge of fibrin prepared by clotting with thrombin a foam or solution of fibrinogen. It is used in conjunction with thrombin as a hemostatic in surgery at sites where bleeding cannot be controlled by more common methods. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p648)

progressivepatientcare.name: progressive patient care
progressivepatientcare.definition: Progressive patient care is organization of medical and nursing care according to the degree of illness and care requirements in the hospital. The elements are intensive care, intermediate care, self-care, long-term care, and organized home care.

seminalplasmaproteins.name: seminal plasma proteins
seminalplasmaproteins.definition: Seminal plasma proteins is proteins found in semen. Major seminal plasma proteins are secretory proteins from the male [MASK] accessory glands, such as the seminal vesicles and the prostate. They include the seminal vesicle-specific antigen, an ejaculate clotting protein; and the prostate-specific antigen, a protease and an esterase.

dilatation,pathologic.name: dilatation , pathologic
dilatation,pathologic.definition: Pathologic dilatation is the condition of an anatomical structure's being dilated beyond normal dimensions.

respiratorydistresssyndrome,newborn.name: respiratory distress syndrome , newborn
respiratorydistresssyndrome,newborn.definition: Newborn [MASK] is a condition of the newborn marked by dyspnea with cyanosis, heralded by such prodromal signs as dilatation of the alae nasi, expiratory grunt, and retraction of the suprasternal notch or costal margins, mostly frequently occurring in premature infants, children of diabetic mothers, and infants delivered by cesarean section, and sometimes with no apparent predisposing cause.

vaginalbirthaftercesarean.name: vaginal birth after cesarean
vaginalbirthaftercesarean.definition: Vaginal birth after cesarean is delivery of an infant through the vagina in a female who has had a prior cesarean section.

biomedicaltechnology.name: biomedical technology
biomedicaltechnology.definition: Biomedical technology is the application of technology to the solution of medical problems.

familyconflict.name: family conflict
familyconflict.definition: Family [MASK] is struggle or disagreement between parents, parent and child or other members of a family.

filtration.name: filtration
filtration.definition: Filtration is a process of separating particulate matter from a fluid, such as air or a liquid, by passing the fluid carrier through a medium that will not pass the particulates. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

equatorialguinea.name: equatorial guinea
equatorialguinea.definition: Equatorial [MASK] is a republic in central Africa, bordering the Bay of Biafra, cameroon is to the north and gabon to the south. Its capital is Malabo.

multifunctionalenzymes.name: multifunctional enzymes
multifunctionalenzymes.definition: Multifunctional enzymes is molecules that contain multiple [MASK] which are used to catalyze more than one enzymatic reaction. Proteins in this class generally contain multiple [MASK] within a single peptide chain and may also contain more than one enzymatically active subunit. They are distinguished from multienzyme complexes in that their subunits are not found as distinct enzymes.

visceralpain.name: visceral pain
visceralpain.definition: Visceral pain is pain originating from internal organs (viscera) associated with autonomic phenomena (pallor; sweating; nausea; and vomiting). It often becomes a [MASK].

neurologicexamination.name: neurologic examination
neurologicexamination.definition: Neurologic examination is assessment of sensory and motor responses and reflexes that is used to determine impairment of the nervous system.

ventricularseptum.name: ventricular septum
ventricularseptum.definition: Ventricular septum is the muscular structure separating the right and the left lower chambers (heart ventricles) of the heart. The ventricular septum consists of a very small membranous portion just beneath the aortic valve, and a large thick muscular portion consisting of three sections including the inlet septum, the trabecular septum, and the outlet septum.

nursesinstruction.name: nurses instruction
nursesinstruction.definition: Nurses instruction is work consisting of materials developed for a nursing audience.

linearmodels.name: linear models
linearmodels.definition: Linear models is statistical models in which the value of a parameter for a given value of a factor is assumed to be equal to a + bx, where a and b are constants. The models predict a linear regression.

glucosetransportertype5.name: glucose transporter type 5
glucosetransportertype5.definition: Glucose transporter type 5 is a hexose transporter that mediates fructose transport in skeletal muscle and adipocytes and is responsible for luminal uptake of dietary fructose in the small intestine.

ultravioletrays.name: ultraviolet rays
ultravioletrays.definition: Ultraviolet rays is that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum immediately below the visible range and extending into the x-ray frequencies. The longer wavelengths (near-UV or biotic or vital rays) are necessary for the endogenous synthesis of vitamin d and are also called antirachitic rays; the shorter, ionizing wavelengths (far-UV or abiotic or extravital rays) are viricidal, bactericidal, mutagenic, and carcinogenic and are used as disinfectants.

splenicneoplasms.name: splenic neoplasms
splenicneoplasms.definition: Splenic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the spleen.

longevity.name: longevity
longevity.definition: Longevity is the normal length of time of an organism's life.

cellfusion.name: cell fusion
cellfusion.definition: Cell fusion is fusion of somatic cells in vitro or in vivo, which results in somatic cell hybridization.
