publichousing.name: public housing
publichousing.definition: Public housing is housing subsidized by tax funds, usually intended for low income persons or families.

cardiomyopathy,alcoholic.name: cardiomyopathy , alcoholic
cardiomyopathy,alcoholic.definition: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy is disease of cardiac muscle resulting from chronic excessive alcohol consumption. Myocardial damage can be caused by: (1) a toxic effect of alcohol; (2) malnutrition in alcoholics such as thiamine deficiency; or (3) toxic effect of additives in alcoholic beverages such as cobalt. This disease is usually manifested by dyspnea and palpitations with cardiomegaly and congestive heart failure (heart failure).

thyroidhormoneresistancesyndrome.name: thyroid hormone resistance syndrome
thyroidhormoneresistancesyndrome.definition: Thyroid hormone resistance syndrome is an inherited autosomal recessive trait, characterized by peripheral resistance to thyroid hormones and the resulting elevation in serum levels of thyroxine and triiodothyronine. This syndrome is caused by mutations of gene thrb encoding the thyroid hormone receptors beta in target cells. hypothyroidism in these patients is partly overcome by the increased thyroid hormone levels.

gliamaturationfactor.name: glia maturation factor
gliamaturationfactor.definition: Glia maturation factor is a factor identified in the brain that influences the growth and differentiation of neurons and neuroglia. Glia maturation factor beta is the 17-kDa polypeptide product of the gmfb gene and is the principal component of glia maturation factor.

receptors,complement.name: receptors , complement
receptors,complement.definition: Complement receptors is molecules on the surface of some B-lymphocytes and macrophages, that recognize and combine with the C3b, C3d, C1q, and C4b components of complement.

clinicaltrial,phaseiv.name: clinical trial , phase iv
clinicaltrial,phaseiv.definition: Phase iv clinical trial is work that is a report of a planned post-marketing study of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques that have been approved for general sale after clinical trials, phases i, ii, and iii. These studies, conducted in the United States or a foreign country, often garner additional data about the safety and efficacy of a product.

calciumchloride.name: calcium chloride
calciumchloride.definition: Calcium chloride is a [MASK] used to replenish calcium levels, as an acid-producing diuretic, and as an antidote for magnesium poisoning.

paternalage.name: paternal age
paternalage.definition: Paternal age is age of the biological [MASK].

toejoint.name: toe joint
toejoint.definition: Toe joint is the articulation between the head of one phalanx and the base of the one distal to it, in each toe.

ventralstriatum.name: ventral striatum
ventralstriatum.definition: Ventral striatum is a composite structure of the telencephalon that is defined by connectivity. It includes the nucleus accumbens; the islands of calleja; and parts of the caudate nucleus; the putamen; and the substantia innominata.

basementmembrane.name: basement membrane
basementmembrane.definition: Basement membrane is a darkly stained mat-like extracellular matrix (ecm) that separates cell layers, such as epithelium from endothelium or a layer of connective tissue. The ecm layer that supports an overlying epithelium or endothelium is called basal lamina. Basement membrane (bm) can be formed by the fusion of either two adjacent basal laminae or a basal lamina with an adjacent reticular lamina of connective tissue. bm, composed mainly of type iv collagen; glycoprotein laminin; and proteoglycan, provides barriers as well as channels between interacting cell layers.

models,immunological.name: models , immunological
models,immunological.definition: Immunological models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of immune system, processes, or phenomena. They include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electrical equipment.

governmentpublication.name: government publication
governmentpublication.definition: Government publication is work consisting of publications issued by local, regional, or national governments or by their agencies or subdivisions.

massmedia.name: mass media
massmedia.definition: Mass media is instruments or technological means of communication that reach large numbers of people with a common message: press, radio, television, etc.

tobaccousedisorder.name: tobacco use disorder
tobaccousedisorder.definition: Tobacco use disorder is tobacco used to the detriment of a person's health or social functioning. Tobacco dependence is included.

rats,mutantstrains.name: rats , mutant strains
rats,mutantstrains.definition: Mutant strains rats is rats bearing mutant genes which are phenotypically expressed in the animals.

clinicaltrial,phaseii.name: clinical trial , phase ii
clinicaltrial,phaseii.definition: Phase ii clinical trial is work that is a report of a pre-planned, usually controlled, clinical study of the safety and efficacy of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques based on several hundred volunteers, including a limited number of patients, and conducted over a period of about two years in either the United States or a foreign country.

medicalerrors.name: medical errors
medicalerrors.definition: Medical errors is errors or mistakes committed by health professionals which result in harm to the patient. They include errors in diagnosis (diagnostic errors), errors in the administration of drugs and other medications (medication errors), errors in the performance of surgical procedures, in the use of other types of therapy, in the use of equipment, and in the interpretation of laboratory findings. Medical errors are differentiated from malpractice in that the former are regarded as honest mistakes or accidents while the latter is the result of negligence, reprehensible ignorance, or criminal intent.

glutathionereductase.name: glutathione reductase
glutathionereductase.definition: Glutathione reductase is catalyzes the oxidation of glutathione to [MASK] in the presence of nadp+. Deficiency in the enzyme is associated with hemolytic anemia. Formerly listed as ec 1.6.4.2.

latencyperiod,psychological.name: latency period , psychological
latencyperiod,psychological.definition: Psychological latency period is the period from about 5 to 7 years to adolescence when there is an apparent cessation of psychosexual development.

esophagealmucosa.name: esophageal mucosa
esophagealmucosa.definition: Esophageal mucosa is circular innermost layer of the esophagus wall that mediates esophageal peristalsis which pushes ingested food bolus toward the stomach.

graftsurvival.name: graft survival
graftsurvival.definition: [MASK] survival is the survival of a [MASK] in a host, the factors responsible for the survival and the changes occurring within the [MASK] during growth in the host.

pharmacology,clinical.name: pharmacology , clinical
pharmacology,clinical.definition: Clinical pharmacology is the branch of pharmacology that deals directly with the effectiveness and safety of drugs in humans.

communityhealthservices.name: community health services
communityhealthservices.definition: Community health services is diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive health services provided for individuals in the community.

rna,transfer,ile.name: rna , transfer , ile
rna,transfer,ile.definition: Ile transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying isoleucine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

cellmovement.name: cell movement
cellmovement.definition: Cell movement is the movement of cells from one location to another. Distinguish from cytokinesis which is the process of dividing the cytoplasm of a cell.

nasalcavity.name: nasal cavity
nasalcavity.definition: Nasal cavity is the proximal portion of the respiratory passages on either side of the [MASK]. Nasal cavities, extending from the nares to the nasopharynx, are lined with ciliated nasal mucosa.

perinatalmortality.name: perinatal mortality
perinatalmortality.definition: Perinatal mortality is deaths occurring from the 28th week of gestation to the 28th day after birth in a given population.

dentalcare.name: dental care
dentalcare.definition: Dental care is the total of dental diagnostic, preventive, and restorative services provided to meet the needs of a patient (from Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982).

abortion,criminal.name: abortion , criminal
abortion,criminal.definition: Criminal abortion is illegal termination of pregnancy.

controlgroups.name: control groups
controlgroups.definition: Control groups is groups that serve as a standard for comparison in experimental studies. They are similar in relevant characteristics to the experimental group but do not receive the experimental intervention.

intestinalobstruction.name: intestinal obstruction
intestinalobstruction.definition: Intestinal obstruction is any impairment, arrest, or reversal of the normal flow of intestinal contents toward the anal canal.

chromosomalinstability.name: chromosomal instability
chromosomalinstability.definition: Chromosomal instability is an increased tendency to acquire chromosome aberrations when various processes involved in chromosome replication, repair, or segregation are dysfunctional.

roboticsurgicalprocedures.name: robotic surgical procedures
roboticsurgicalprocedures.definition: Robotic surgical procedures is surgical procedures performed remotely using a computer that controls surgical instruments attached to mechanical [MASK] designed to perform the tasks of the surgeon.

cholera.name: cholera
cholera.definition: Cholera is an acute diarrheal [MASK] in India and Southeast Asia whose causative agent is vibrio cholerae. This condition can lead to severe [MASK] in a matter of hours unless quickly treated.

vertebralartery.name: vertebral artery
vertebralartery.definition: Vertebral artery is the first branch of the subclavian artery with distribution to muscles of the [MASK]; vertebrae; spinal cord; cerebellum; and interior of the cerebrum.

immunoglobulinclassswitching.name: immunoglobulin class switching
immunoglobulinclassswitching.definition: Immunoglobulin class switching is gene rearrangement of the B-lymphocyte which results in a substitution in the type of heavy-chain constant region that is expressed. This allows the effector response to change while the antigen binding specificity (variable region) remains the same. The majority of class switching occurs by a dna recombination event but it also can take place at the level of rna processing.

nucleosomeassemblyprotein1.name: nucleosome assembly protein 1
nucleosomeassemblyprotein1.definition: Nucleosome assembly protein 1 is a histone chaperone that facilitates nucleosome assembly by mediating the formation of the histone octamer and its transfer to dna.

medicalrecordssystems,computerized.name: medical records systems , computerized
medicalrecordssystems,computerized.definition: Computerized medical records systems is computer-based systems for input, storage, display, retrieval, and printing of information contained in a patient's medical record.

drugresistance,fungal.name: drug resistance , fungal
drugresistance,fungal.definition: Fungal drug resistance is the ability of fungi to resist or to become tolerant to chemotherapeutic agents, antifungal agents, or antibiotics. This resistance may be acquired through gene mutation.

freezedrying.name: freeze drying
freezedrying.definition: Freeze drying is method of tissue preparation in which the tissue specimen is frozen and then dehydrated at low temperature in a high vacuum. This method is also used for dehydrating pharmaceutical and food products.

paternalexposure.name: paternal exposure
paternalexposure.definition: Paternal exposure is exposure of the male parent, human or animal, to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals that may affect offspring.

peerreview.name: peer review
peerreview.definition: Peer review is an organized procedure carried out by a select committee of professionals in evaluating the performance of other professionals in meeting the standards of their specialty. Review by peers is used by editors in the evaluation of articles and other [MASK] submitted for publication. Peer review is used also in the evaluation of grant applications. It is applied also in evaluating the quality of health care provided to patients.

education,nursing.name: education , nursing
education,nursing.definition: Nursing education is use for general articles concerning nursing education.

complexregionalpainsyndromes.name: complex regional pain syndromes
complexregionalpainsyndromes.definition: Complex regional pain syndromes is conditions characterized by pain involving an extremity or other body region, hyperesthesia, and localized autonomic dysfunction following injury to soft tissue or nerve. The pain is usually associated with erythema; skin temperature changes, abnormal sudomotor activity (i.e., changes in sweating due to altered sympathetic innervation) or edema. The degree of pain and other manifestations is out of proportion to that expected from the inciting event. Two subtypes of this condition have been described: type i; (reflex sympathetic dystrophy) and type ii; (causalgia). (From Pain 1995 Oct;63(1):127-33)

atrophy.name: atrophy
atrophy.definition: Atrophy is decrease in the size of a cell, tissue, organ, or multiple organs, associated with a variety of pathological conditions such as abnormal cellular changes, ischemia, malnutrition, or hormonal changes.

metabolicequivalent.name: metabolic equivalent
metabolicequivalent.definition: Metabolic equivalent is a measurement of oxygen uptake in a sitting, resting person (resting oxygen consumption), varying with age, [MASK], race, and other factors. In normal adult men, one met is approximately 3.5 ml O2/kg/min of body weight. Oxygen uptake during activities or work can be measured in METs which can be use to determine health status and exercise prescription.

comparativeeffectivenessresearch.name: comparative effectiveness research
comparativeeffectivenessresearch.definition: Comparative effectiveness research is conduct and synthesis of systematic research comparing interventions and strategies to prevent, diagnose, treat, and monitor health conditions. The purpose of this research is to inform patients, providers, and decision-makers, responding to their expressed needs, about which interventions are most effective for which patients under specific circumstances. (hhs.gov/recovery/programs/cer/draftdefinition.html accessed 6/12/2009)

gabaagonists.name: gaba agonists
gabaagonists.definition: Gaba agonists is endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate gamma-aminobutyric acid receptors (receptors, gaba).

vision,ocular.name: vision , ocular
vision,ocular.definition: Ocular vision is the process in which light signals are transformed by the photoreceptor cells into electrical signals which can then be transmitted to the brain.

liquidcrystals.name: liquid crystals
liquidcrystals.definition: Liquid crystals is materials in intermediate state between solid and liquid.

sputum.name: sputum
sputum.definition: Sputum is material coughed up from the lungs and expectorated via the mouth. It contains mucus, cellular debris, and microorganisms. It may also contain blood or pus.

nutrients.name: nutrients
nutrients.definition: Nutrients is various components of food that are required for nourishment.

dendriticcellsarcoma,follicular.name: dendritic cell sarcoma , follicular
dendriticcellsarcoma,follicular.definition: Follicular [MASK] sarcoma is sarcoma of follicular [MASK] most often found in the [MASK] nodes. This rare neoplasm occurs predominately in adults.

translocation,genetic.name: translocation , genetic
translocation,genetic.definition: Genetic translocation is a type of chromosome aberration characterized by chromosome breakage and transfer of the broken-off portion to another location, often to a different chromosome.

fractures,cartilage.name: fractures , cartilage
fractures,cartilage.definition: Cartilage fractures is breaks in cartilage.

languagedisorders.name: language disorders
languagedisorders.definition: Language disorders is conditions characterized by deficiencies of comprehension or expression of written and spoken forms of language. These include acquired and developmental disorders.

wetmaculardegeneration.name: wet macular degeneration
wetmaculardegeneration.definition: Wet macular degeneration is a form of retinal degeneration in which abnormal choroidal neovascularization occurs under the retina and macula lutea, causing bleeding and leaking of fluid. This leads to bulging and or lifting of the macula and the distortion or destruction of central vision.

bloodsedimentation.name: blood sedimentation
bloodsedimentation.definition: Blood sedimentation is measurement of rate of settling of erythrocytes in anticoagulated blood.

diagnosticequipment.name: diagnostic equipment
diagnosticequipment.definition: Diagnostic equipment is nonexpendable items used in examination.

survival.name: survival
survival.definition: Survival is continuance of life or existence especially under adverse conditions; includes methods and philosophy of survival.

chemistry.name: chemistry
chemistry.definition: Chemistry is a basic science concerned with the composition, structure, and properties of matter; and the reactions that occur between substances and the associated energy exchange.

fever.name: fever
fever.definition: Fever is an abnormal elevation of body temperature, usually as a result of a pathologic process.

limitofdetection.name: limit of detection
limitofdetection.definition: Limit of detection is concentration or quantity that is derived from the smallest measure that can be detected with reasonable certainty for a given analytical procedure.

braintissuetransplantation.name: brain tissue transplantation
braintissuetransplantation.definition: Brain tissue transplantation is transference of brain tissue, either from a fetus or from a born individual, between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

pituitaryneoplasms.name: pituitary neoplasms
pituitaryneoplasms.definition: Pituitary neoplasms is neoplasms which arise from or metastasize to the pituitary gland. The majority of pituitary neoplasms are adenomas, which are divided into non-secreting and secreting forms. Hormone producing forms are further classified by the type of hormone they secrete. Pituitary adenomas may also be characterized by their staining properties (see adenoma, basophil; adenoma, acidophil; and adenoma, chromophobe). Pituitary tumors may compress adjacent structures, including the hypothalamus, several cranial nerves, and the optic chiasm. Chiasmal compression may result in bitemporal hemianopsia.

arabworld.name: arab world
arabworld.definition: Arab world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across a wide geographical area under the administrative, intellectual, social, and cultural domination of the Arab empire. The Arab world, under the impetus of Islam, by the eighth century a.d., extended from Arabia in the Middle East to all of northern Africa, southern [MASK], Sardinia, and Sicily. Close contact was maintained with Greek and Jewish culture. While the principal service of the Arabs to medicine was the preservation of Greek culture, the Arabs themselves were the originators of algebra, chemistry, geology, and many of the refinements of civilization. (From a. Castiglioni, a [MASK], 2d ed, p260; from f. h. Garrison, An Introduction to the [MASK], 4th ed, p126)

thoracicsurgicalprocedures.name: thoracic surgical procedures
thoracicsurgicalprocedures.definition: Thoracic surgical procedures is surgery performed on the thoracic organs, most commonly the lungs and the heart.

respiratoryrate.name: respiratory rate
respiratoryrate.definition: Respiratory rate is the number of times an organism breathes with the lungs (respiration) per unit time, usually per minute.

enzymes.name: enzymes
enzymes.definition: Enzymes is biological molecules that possess catalytic activity. They may occur naturally or be synthetically created. Enzymes are usually proteins, however catalytic rna and [MASK] molecules have also been identified.

redcross.name: red cross
redcross.definition: Red cross is international collective of humanitarian organizations led by volunteers and guided by its Congressional Charter and the Fundamental Principles of the International Red Cross Movement, to provide relief to victims of disaster and help people prevent, prepare for, and respond to emergencies.

adaptiveimmunity.name: adaptive immunity
adaptiveimmunity.definition: Adaptive immunity is protection from an infectious disease agent that is mediated by b- and t- lymphocytes following exposure to specific antigen, and characterized by immunologic memory. It can result from either previous infection with that agent or vaccination (immunity, active), or transfer of antibody or lymphocytes from an immune donor (immunization, passive).

moleculardiagnostictechniques.name: molecular diagnostic techniques
moleculardiagnostictechniques.definition: Molecular diagnostic techniques is molecular biology techniques used in the diagnosis of disease.

equipmentandsupplies,hospital.name: equipment and supplies , hospital
equipmentandsupplies,hospital.definition: Hospital equipment and supplies is any materials used in providing care specifically in the hospital.

adipocytes,brown.name: adipocytes , brown
adipocytes,brown.definition: Brown adipocytes is fat cells with dark coloration due to the densely packed mitochondria. They contain numerous small [MASK] or vacuoles. Their stored lipids can be converted directly to energy as heat by the mitochondria.

graymatter.name: gray matter
graymatter.definition: Gray matter is region of central nervous system that appears darker in [MASK] than the other type, [MASK] matter. It is composed of neuronal cell bodies; neuropil; glial cells and capillaries but few myelinated nerve fibers.

smokingcessation.name: smoking cessation
smokingcessation.definition: Smoking cessation is discontinuing the habit of smoking.

glycogensynthasekinases.name: glycogen synthase kinases
glycogensynthasekinases.definition: Glycogen synthase kinases is a class of protein-serine-threonine kinases that was originally found as one of the three types of kinases that phosphorylate glycogen synthase. Glycogen synthase kinases along with ca(2+)-calmodulin dependent protein kinases and cyclic amp-dependent protein kinases regulate glycogen synthase activity.

signorsymptom.name: sign or symptom
signorsymptom.definition: Sign or symptom is clinical manifestations that can be either objective when observed by a physician, or subjective when perceived by the patient.

torsion,mechanical.name: torsion , mechanical
torsion,mechanical.definition: Mechanical torsion is a twisting deformation of a solid body about an axis. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

leukocytedisorders.name: leukocyte disorders
leukocytedisorders.definition: Leukocyte disorders is disordered formation of various types of leukocytes or an abnormal accumulation or deficiency of these cells.

receptors,matingfactor.name: receptors , mating factor
receptors,matingfactor.definition: Mating factor receptors is a family of pheromone receptors that were initially discovered in saccharomyces cerevisiae as proteins necessary for fungal conjugation. Each mating factor receptor is expressed in haploid cells of a single mating type.

survivalanalysis.name: survival analysis
survivalanalysis.definition: Survival analysis is a class of statistical procedures for estimating the survival function (function of time, starting with a population 100% well at a given time and providing the percentage of the population still well at later times). The survival analysis is then used for making inferences about the effects of treatments, prognostic factors, exposures, and other covariates on the function.

statehealthplanninganddevelopmentagencie.name: state health planning and development agencies
statehealthplanninganddevelopmentagencie.definition: State health planning and development agencies is agencies established under pl93-641 to coordinate, conduct, and implement state health planning activities. Two primary responsibilities are the preparation of an annual State Health Plan and giving assistance to the Statewide Health Coordinating Council.

heartratedetermination.name: heart rate determination
heartratedetermination.definition: Heart rate determination is methods, techniques, and processes by which heart rate is measured.

qualitativeresearch.name: qualitative research
qualitativeresearch.definition: Qualitative research is any type of research that employs nonnumeric information to explore individual or group characteristics, producing findings not arrived at by statistical procedures or other quantitative means. (Qualitative Inquiry: a Dictionary of Terms Thousand Oaks, ca: Sage Publications, 1997)

radiationequipmentandsupplies.name: radiation equipment and supplies
radiationequipmentandsupplies.definition: Radiation equipment and supplies is instruments and apparatus for radiation applications and their components and associated expendables.

respiratoryphysiologicalphenomena.name: respiratory physiological phenomena
respiratoryphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Respiratory physiological phenomena is physiological processes and properties of the respiratory system as a whole or of any of its parts.

reimbursementmechanisms.name: reimbursement mechanisms
reimbursementmechanisms.definition: Reimbursement mechanisms is processes or methods of reimbursement for services rendered or equipment.

mammography.name: mammography
mammography.definition: Mammography is radiographic examination of the breast.

immersion.name: immersion
immersion.definition: Immersion is the placing of a body or a part thereof into a liquid.

bacterialtransferrinreceptorcomplex.name: bacterial transferrin receptor complex
bacterialtransferrinreceptorcomplex.definition: Bacterial transferrin receptor complex is a complex of proteins that forms a receptor for transferrin in bacteria. Many pathogenic bacteria utilize the transferrin-binding complex to acquire their supply of iron from serum.

placentalfunctiontests.name: placental function tests
placentalfunctiontests.definition: Placental function tests is methods used for the assessment of placental function.

parkinsondisease,secondary.name: parkinson disease , secondary
parkinsondisease,secondary.definition: Secondary parkinson disease is conditions which feature clinical manifestations resembling primary Parkinson disease that are caused by a known or suspected condition. Examples include parkinsonism caused by vascular injury, drugs, trauma, toxin exposure, neoplasms, infections and degenerative or hereditary conditions. Clinical features may include bradykinesia, rigidity, parkinsonian gait, and masked facies. In general, tremor is less prominent in secondary parkinsonism than in the primary form. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1998, Ch38, pp39-42)

iodine.name: iodine
iodine.definition: Iodine is a nonmetallic element of the halogen group that is represented by the atomic symbol i, atomic number 53, and atomic weight of 126.90. It is a nutritionally essential element, especially important in thyroid hormone synthesis. In solution, it has anti-infective properties and is used topically.

gabaergicneurons.name: gabaergic neurons
gabaergicneurons.definition: Gabaergic neurons is neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is gamma-aminobutyric acid.

axons.name: axons
axons.definition: Axons is nerve fibers that are capable of rapidly conducting impulses away from the neuron cell body.

hemoglobinsubunits.name: hemoglobin subunits
hemoglobinsubunits.definition: Hemoglobin subunits is the protein subunits that comprise multimeric hemoglobins.

diet,western.name: diet , western
diet,western.definition: Western diet is a pattern of food consumption adopted mainly by the people of North America and Western Europe. It is mainly characterized by high intake of meat, processed grains, dietary sugars, dairy products, and dietary fats.

insurance,surgical.name: insurance , surgical
insurance,surgical.definition: Surgical insurance is a specific type of health insurance which provides surgeons' fees for specified amounts according to the type of surgery listed in the policy.

cellulose,oxidized.name: cellulose , oxidized
cellulose,oxidized.definition: Oxidized cellulose is a cellulose of varied carboxyl content retaining the fibrous structure. It is commonly used as a local hemostatic and as a matrix for normal blood coagulation.

minorlymphocytestimulatoryantigens.name: minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens
minorlymphocytestimulatoryantigens.definition: Minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens is endogenous superantigens responsible for inducing strong proliferative responses in T-cells in mixed lymphocyte reactions (see lymphocyte culture test, mixed). They are encoded by mouse mammary tumor viruses that have integrated into the germ line as dna proviruses (minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci).

recombinantproteins.name: recombinant proteins
recombinantproteins.definition: Recombinant proteins is proteins prepared by [MASK] technology.

genetics,population.name: genetics , population
genetics,population.definition: Population genetics is the discipline studying genetic composition of populations and effects of factors such as genetic selection, population size, mutation, migration, and [MASK] on the frequencies of various genotypes and phenotypes using a variety of genetic techniques.

facialtransplantation.name: facial transplantation
facialtransplantation.definition: Facial transplantation is the transference between individuals of the entire face or major facial structures. In addition to the skin and cartilaginous tissue (cartilage), it may include muscle and bone as well.

candida.name: candida
candida.definition: Candida is a genus of yeast-like mitosporic Saccharomycetales fungi characterized by producing yeast cells, mycelia, pseudomycelia, and blastophores. It is commonly part of the normal flora of the skin, mouth, intestinal tract, and vagina, but can cause a variety of infections, including candidiasis; onychomycosis; vulvovaginal candidiasis; and candidiasis, oral (thrush).

bloodvessels.name: blood vessels
bloodvessels.definition: Blood vessels is any of the tubular vessels conveying the blood (arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules, and veins).

staffdevelopment.name: staff development
staffdevelopment.definition: Staff development is the process by which the employer promotes staff performance and efficiency consistent with management goals and objectives.

retinalrodphotoreceptorcells.name: retinal rod photoreceptor cells
retinalrodphotoreceptorcells.definition: Retinal rod photoreceptor cells is photosensitive afferent neurons located in the peripheral retina, with their density increases radially away from the fovea centralis. Being much more sensitive to light than the [MASK], the rod cells are responsible for twilight vision (at scotopic intensities) as well as peripheral vision, but provide no [MASK] discrimination.

diabetesmellitus,type1.name: diabetes mellitus , type 1
diabetesmellitus,type1.definition: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is a subtype of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by insulin deficiency. It is manifested by the sudden onset of severe hyperglycemia, rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis, and death unless treated with insulin. The disease may occur at any age, but is most common in childhood or adolescence.

isotopes.name: isotopes
isotopes.definition: Isotopes is atomic species differing in mass number but having the same atomic number. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

agar.name: agar
agar.definition: Agar is a complex sulfated polymer of galactose units, extracted from Gelidium cartilagineum, Gracilaria confervoides, and related red algae. It is used as a gel in the preparation of solid culture media for microorganisms, as a bulk laxative, in making emulsions, and as a supporting medium for immunodiffusion and immunoelectrophoresis.

chromosomeaberrations.name: chromosome aberrations
chromosomeaberrations.definition: Chromosome aberrations is abnormal number or structure of chromosomes. Chromosome aberrations may result in chromosome disorders.

caspase1.name: caspase 1
caspase1.definition: Caspase 1 is a long pro-domain caspase that has specificity for the precursor form of interleukin-1beta. It plays a role in inflammation by catalytically converting the inactive forms of cytokines such as interleukin-1beta to their active, secreted form. Caspase 1 is referred as interleukin-1beta converting enzyme and is frequently abbreviated ice.

cropprotection.name: crop protection
cropprotection.definition: Crop protection is the science and practice of preventing, minimizing, or eliminating damage to agricultural crops by pest organisms, weeds, and disease-causing agents.

standingposition.name: standing position
standingposition.definition: Standing position is human position in which the body is held in an upright orthostatic position and supported only by the [MASK].

organization.name: organization
organization.definition: Organization is groups of people working together in a structured manner to pursue common goals and objectives.

nucleicacidamplificationtechniques.name: nucleic acid amplification techniques
nucleicacidamplificationtechniques.definition: Nucleic acid amplification techniques is laboratory techniques that involve the in-vitro synthesis of many copies of dna or rna from one original template.

thetarhythm.name: theta rhythm
thetarhythm.definition: Theta rhythm is brain waves characterized by a frequency of 4-7 Hz, usually observed in the temporal lobes when the individual is awake, but relaxed and sleepy.

militarypersonnel.name: military personnel
militarypersonnel.definition: Military personnel is persons including soldiers involved with the armed forces.

crowncompounds.name: crown compounds
crowncompounds.definition: Crown compounds is macrocyclic compounds analogous to crown ethers but which lack any oxygen atoms.

syphilis,congenital.name: syphilis , congenital
syphilis,congenital.definition: Congenital syphilis is syphilis acquired in utero and manifested by any of several characteristic tooth (Hutchinson's teeth) or bone malformations and by active mucocutaneous syphilis at birth or shortly thereafter. Ocular and neurologic changes may also occur.

methylation.name: methylation
methylation.definition: Methylation is addition of methyl groups. In histo-chemistry methylation is used to esterify carboxyl groups and remove sulfate groups by treating tissue sections with hot methanol in the presence of hydrochloric acid. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

severityofillnessindex.name: severity of illness index
severityofillnessindex.definition: Severity of illness index is levels within a diagnostic group which are established by various measurement criteria applied to the seriousness of a patient's disorder.

cornea.name: cornea
cornea.definition: Cornea is the transparent anterior portion of the fibrous coat of the eye consisting of five layers: stratified squamous corneal epithelium; bowman membrane; corneal stroma; descemet membrane; and mesenchymal [MASK]. It serves as the first refracting medium of the eye. It is structurally continuous with the sclera, avascular, receiving its nourishment by permeation through spaces between the lamellae, and is innervated by the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve via the ciliary nerves and those of the surrounding conjunctiva which together form plexuses. (Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

diabetescomplications.name: diabetes complications
diabetescomplications.definition: Diabetes complications is conditions or pathological processes associated with the disease of diabetes mellitus. Due to the impaired control of blood glucose level in diabetic patients, pathological processes develop in numerous tissues and organs including the eye, the kidney, the blood vessels, and the nerve tissue.

academicmedicalcenters.name: academic medical centers
academicmedicalcenters.definition: Academic medical centers is medical complexes consisting of medical school, hospitals, clinics, libraries, administrative facilities, etc.

greekworld.name: greek world
greekworld.definition: Greek world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across a wide geographical area under the influence of Greek civilization, culture, and science. The Greek Empire extended from the Greek mainland and the Aegean islands from the 16th century b.c., to the Indus Valley in the 4th century under Alexander the Great, and to southern Italy and Sicily. Greek medicine began with Homeric and Aesculapian medicine and continued unbroken to Hippocrates (480-355 b.c.). The classic period of Greek medicine was 460-136 b.c. and the Graeco-Roman period, 156 b.c.-576 a.d. (From a. Castiglioni, a [MASK], 2d ed; from f. h. Garrison, An Introduction to the [MASK], 4th ed)

spermretrieval.name: sperm retrieval
spermretrieval.definition: Sperm retrieval is procedures to obtain viable sperm from the male reproductive tract, including the testes, the epididymis, or the vas deferens.

bileacidsandsalts.name: bile acids and salts
bileacidsandsalts.definition: [MASK] acids and [MASK] is steroid acids and [MASK]. The primary [MASK] acids are derived from cholesterol in the liver and usually conjugated with glycine or taurine. The secondary [MASK] acids are further modified by bacteria in the intestine. They play an important role in the [MASK] and absorption of fat. They have also been used pharmacologically, especially in the treatment of gallstones.

adenovirusvaccines.name: adenovirus vaccines
adenovirusvaccines.definition: Adenovirus vaccines is vaccines used to prevent infection by any virus from the family adenoviridae.

catalog,union.name: catalog , union
catalog,union.definition: Union catalog is lists of books and other information sources held among a cooperating group of libraries.

incidence.name: incidence
incidence.definition: Incidence is the number of new cases of a given disease during a given period in a specified population. It also is used for the rate at which new events occur in a defined population. It is differentiated from [MASK], which refers to all cases in the population at a given time.

serine.name: serine
serine.definition: Serine is a non-essential amino acid occurring in natural form as the L-isomer. It is synthesized from glycine or threonine. It is involved in the biosynthesis of purines; pyrimidines; and other amino acids.

formsandrecordscontrol.name: forms and records control
formsandrecordscontrol.definition: Forms and records control is a management function in which standards and guidelines are developed for the development, maintenance, and handling of forms and records.

datacollection.name: data collection
datacollection.definition: Data collection is systematic gathering of data for a particular purpose from various sources, including questionnaires, interviews, [MASK], existing records, and electronic devices. The process is usually preliminary to statistical analysis of the data.

dna,complementary.name: dna , complementary
dna,complementary.definition: Complementary dna is single-stranded complementary dna synthesized from an rna template by the action of RNA-dependent dna polymerase. cDNA (i.e., complementary dna, not circular dna, not c-dna) is used in a variety of molecular cloning experiments as well as serving as a specific hybridization probe.

socialcommunicationdisorder.name: social communication disorder
socialcommunicationdisorder.definition: Social communication disorder is persistent difficulties in the social uses of verbal and nonverbal communications. ([MASK])

eyeinjuries,penetrating.name: eye injuries , penetrating
eyeinjuries,penetrating.definition: Penetrating eye injuries is deeply perforating or puncturing type intraocular injuries.

nucleartransfertechniques.name: nuclear transfer techniques
nucleartransfertechniques.definition: Nuclear transfer techniques is methods of implanting a cell nucleus from a donor cell into an enucleated acceptor cell.

adrenalcortexneoplasms.name: adrenal cortex neoplasms
adrenalcortexneoplasms.definition: Adrenal cortex neoplasms is tumors or cancers of the adrenal cortex.

blog.name: blog
blog.definition: Blog is a website that contains conversational personal reflections, comments and sometimes links to other sites; typically run by an individual or small group.

rnaediting.name: rna editing
rnaediting.definition: Rna editing is a process that changes the nucleotide sequence of mRNA from that of the dna template encoding it. Some major classes of rna editing are as follows: 1, the conversion of cytosine to uracil in mRNA; 2, the addition of variable number of guanines at pre-determined sites; and 3, the addition and deletion of uracils, templated by guide-RNAs (rna, guide).

medicaldevice.name: medical device
medicaldevice.definition: Medical device is expendable and nonexpendable equipment, supplies, apparatus, and instruments that are used in diagnostic, surgical, therapeutic, scientific, and experimental procedures.

reproductivetractinfections.name: reproductive tract infections
reproductivetractinfections.definition: Reproductive tract infections is infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

kidneyfunctiontests.name: kidney function tests
kidneyfunctiontests.definition: Kidney function tests is laboratory tests used to evaluate how well the kidneys are working through examination of blood and urine.

instructionalfilmandvideo.name: instructional film and video
instructionalfilmandvideo.definition: Instructional film and video is works consisting of nonfiction films and video designed to teach, instruct, or train. (From Moving Image Materials: Genre Terms, 1988)

dentalsac.name: dental sac
dentalsac.definition: Dental sac is dense fibrous layer formed from mesodermal tissue that surrounds the epithelial enamel organ. The cells eventually migrate to the external surface of the newly formed root dentin and give rise to the cementoblasts that deposit cementum on the developing root, fibroblasts of the developing periodontal ligament, and [MASK] of the developing alveolar bone.

referencebooks.name: reference books
referencebooks.definition: Reference books is books designed by the arrangement and treatment of their subject matter to be consulted for definite terms of information rather than to be read consecutively. Reference books include dictionaries; encyclopedias; atlases; etc. (From the ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983)

freeassociation.name: free association
freeassociation.definition: Free association is spontaneous verbalization of whatever comes to mind.

automation,laboratory.name: automation , laboratory
automation,laboratory.definition: Laboratory automation is controlled operations of analytic or diagnostic processes, or systems by mechanical or electronic devices.

cathepsinz.name: cathepsin z
cathepsinz.definition: Cathepsin z is a ubiquitously-expressed [MASK] peptidase that exhibits carboxypeptidase activity. It is highly expressed in a variety of immune cell types and may play a role in inflammatory processes and immune responses.

encephalitisvirus,murrayvalley.name: encephalitis virus , murray valley
encephalitisvirus,murrayvalley.definition: Murray valley encephalitis virus is a species of flavivirus, one of the Japanese encephalitis virus group (encephalitis viruses, japanese), found in Australia and [MASK]. It causes a fulminating viremia resembling Japanese encephalitis (encephalitis, japanese).

vehicleemissions.name: vehicle emissions
vehicleemissions.definition: Vehicle emissions is gases, fumes, vapors, and odorants escaping from the cylinders of a gasoline or diesel internal-combustion engine. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed & Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

biomarkers.name: biomarkers
biomarkers.definition: Biomarkers is measurable and quantifiable biological parameters (e.g., specific enzyme concentration, specific hormone concentration, specific gene phenotype distribution in a population, presence of biological substances) which serve as indices for health- and physiology-related assessments, such as disease risk, psychiatric disorders, environmental exposure and its effects, disease diagnosis; metabolic processes; substance abuse; pregnancy; cell line development; epidemiologic studies; etc.

societies.name: societies
societies.definition: Societies is organizations composed of members with common interests and whose professions may be similar.

anesthesia,spinal.name: anesthesia , spinal
anesthesia,spinal.definition: Spinal anesthesia is procedure in which an anesthetic is injected directly into the spinal cord.

epithelium,corneal.name: epithelium , corneal
epithelium,corneal.definition: Corneal epithelium is stratified squamous epithelium that covers the outer surface of the cornea. It is smooth and contains many free nerve endings.

feedingandeatingdisordersofchildhood.name: feeding and eating disorders of childhood
feedingandeatingdisordersofchildhood.definition: Feeding and eating disorders of childhood is mental disorders related to feeding and eating usually diagnosed in infancy or early childhood.

reversetranscription.name: reverse transcription
reversetranscription.definition: Reverse transcription is the biosynthesis of dna carried out on a template of rna.

nuclearphysics.name: nuclear physics
nuclearphysics.definition: Nuclear physics is the study of the characteristics, behavior, and internal structures of the atomic nucleus and its interactions with other nuclei. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

carbonfootprint.name: carbon footprint
carbonfootprint.definition: Carbon footprint is a measure of the total greenhouse gas emissions produced by an individual, organization, event, or product. It is measured in units of equivalent kilograms of carbon dioxide generated in a given time frame.

parkinsondisease.name: parkinson disease
parkinsondisease.definition: Parkinson disease is a progressive, degenerative neurologic disease characterized by a tremor that is maximal at rest, retropulsion (i.e. a tendency to fall backwards), rigidity, stooped posture, slowness of voluntary movements, and a masklike facial expression. Pathologic features include loss of melanin containing neurons in the substantia nigra and other pigmented nuclei of the brainstem. lewy bodies are present in the substantia nigra and locus coeruleus but may also be found in a related condition (lewy body disease, diffuse) characterized by dementia in combination with varying degrees of parkinsonism. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1059, pp1067-75)

disastermedicine.name: disaster medicine
disastermedicine.definition: Disaster medicine is branch of medicine involved with management and organization of public health response to disasters and major events including the special health and medical needs of a community in a disaster.

healthpriorities.name: health priorities
healthpriorities.definition: Health priorities is preferentially rated health-related activities or functions to be used in establishing health planning goals. This may refer specifically to pl93-641.

esophagealneoplasms.name: esophageal neoplasms
esophagealneoplasms.definition: Esophageal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the esophagus.

qualitativeconcept.name: qualitative concept
qualitativeconcept.definition: Qualitative concept is works about studies that determine the effectiveness or value of processes, personnel, and equipment, or the material on conducting such studies.

gallbladderneoplasms.name: gallbladder neoplasms
gallbladderneoplasms.definition: Gallbladder neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the gallbladder.

intermediatebackmuscles.name: intermediate back muscles
intermediatebackmuscles.definition: Intermediate back muscles is two muscles, the serratus posterior superior and serratus posterior inferior, located in between the deep and the [MASK] layers. Their function is to control thorax movement.

pharmaceuticalpreparations,dental.name: pharmaceutical preparations , dental
pharmaceuticalpreparations,dental.definition: Dental pharmaceutical preparations is drugs intended for dentistry.

orthodonticspaceclosure.name: orthodontic space closure
orthodonticspaceclosure.definition: Orthodontic space closure is therapeutic closure of spaces caused by the extraction of teeth, the congenital absence of teeth, or the excessive space between teeth.

patientpreference.name: patient preference
patientpreference.definition: Patient preference is individual's expression of desirability or value of one course of action, outcome, or selection in contrast to others.

violence.name: violence
violence.definition: Violence is great force, either physical or emotional, usually exerted in order to damage or otherwise abuse something or someone.

games,recreational.name: games , recreational
games,recreational.definition: Recreational games is activity typically involving several individuals for the purpose of leisure, amusement, entertainment or pleasure.

intestinalneoplasms.name: intestinal neoplasms
intestinalneoplasms.definition: Intestinal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the intestines.

membranes.name: membranes
membranes.definition: Membranes is thin layers of tissue which cover parts of the body, separate adjacent cavities, or connect adjacent structures.

radiography,interventional.name: radiography , interventional
radiography,interventional.definition: Interventional radiography is diagnostic and therapeutic procedures that are invasive or surgical in nature, and require the expertise of a specially trained radiologist. In general, they are more invasive than diagnostic imaging but less invasive than major surgery. They often involve catheterization, fluoroscopy, or computed tomography. Some examples include percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography, percutaneous transthoracic biopsy, balloon angioplasty, and arterial embolization.

laborstage,second.name: labor stage , second
laborstage,second.definition: Second labor stage is the period of obstetric labor that is from the complete dilatation of the cervix uteri to the expulsion of the fetus.

rna.name: rna
rna.definition: Rna is a polynucleotide consisting essentially of chains with a repeating backbone of phosphate and ribose units to which nitrogenous bases are attached. rna is unique among biological macromolecules in that it can encode genetic information, serve as an abundant structural component of cells, and also possesses catalytic activity. (Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

bigdata.name: big data
bigdata.definition: Big data is extremely large amounts of data which require rapid and often complex computational analyses to reveal patterns, trends, and associations, relating to various facets of human and non-human entities.

congenital,hereditary,andneonataldisease.name: congenital , hereditary , and neonatal diseases and abnormalities
congenital,hereditary,andneonataldisease.definition: And neonatal diseases and abnormalities hereditary congenital is diseases existing at birth and often before birth, or that develop during the first month of life (infant, newborn, diseases), regardless of causation. Of these diseases, those characterized by structural deformities are termed congenital abnormalities.

childlabor.name: child labor
childlabor.definition: Child labor is employment of minors in work that deprives children of their childhood, potential, dignity, and is harmful to their physical and mental development. (International Labor Organization, un)

cationicaminoacidtransporter2.name: cationic amino acid transporter 2
cationicaminoacidtransporter2.definition: [MASK] 2 is a high-affinity, low capacity system y+ amino acid transporter with strong similarity to [MASK] 1. The two isoforms of the protein, cat-2a and cat-2b, exist due to alternative mRNA splicing. The transporter has specificity for the transport of [MASK]; lysine; and ornithine.

administration,topical.name: administration , topical
administration,topical.definition: Topical administration is the application of drug preparations to the surfaces of the body, especially the skin (administration, cutaneous) or mucous membranes. This method of treatment is used to avoid systemic side effects when high doses are required at a localized area or as an alternative systemic administration route, to avoid hepatic processing for example.

costofillness.name: cost of illness
costofillness.definition: Cost of illness is the personal cost of disease which may be economic, social, or psychological. The cost of illness may be reflected in absenteeism, productivity, response to treatment, peace of mind, or [MASK]. It differs from health care costs, the societal cost of providing services related to the delivery of health care.

models,economic.name: models , economic
models,economic.definition: Economic models is statistical models of the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, as well as of financial considerations. For the application of statistics to the testing and quantifying of economic theories [MASK] is available.

managedcompetition.name: managed competition
managedcompetition.definition: Managed competition is a strategy for purchasing health care in a manner which will obtain maximum value for the price for the purchasers of the health care and the recipients. The concept was developed primarily by Alain Enthoven of Stanford University and promulgated by the Jackson Hole Group. The strategy depends on sponsors for groups of the population to be insured. The sponsor, in some cases a [MASK], acts as an intermediary between the group and competing provider groups (accountable health plans). The competition is price-based among annual premiums for a defined, standardized benefit package. (From Slee and Slee, Health Care Reform Terms, 1993)

leishmania.name: leishmania
leishmania.definition: Leishmania is a genus of flagellate protozoa comprising several species that are pathogenic for humans. Organisms of this genus have an amastigote and a promastigote stage in their [MASK]. As a result of enzymatic studies this single genus has been divided into two subgenera: Leishmania leishmania and Leishmania viannia. Species within the Leishmania leishmania subgenus include: l. aethiopica, l. arabica, l. donovani, l. enrietti, l. gerbilli, l. hertigi, l. infantum, l. major, l. mexicana, and l. tropica. The following species are those that compose the Leishmania viannia subgenus: l. braziliensis, l. guyanensis, l. lainsoni, l. naiffi, and l. shawi.

antibodyspecificity.name: antibody specificity
antibodyspecificity.definition: Antibody specificity is the property of antibodies which enables them to react with some antigenic determinants and not with others. Specificity is dependent on chemical composition, physical forces, and molecular structure at the binding site.

airbags.name: air bags
airbags.definition: Air bags is automotive safety devices consisting of a bag designed to inflate upon collision and prevent passengers from pitching forward. (American Heritage Dictionary, 1982)

commitmentofmentallyill.name: commitment of mentally ill
commitmentofmentallyill.definition: Commitment of [MASK] is legal process required for the institutionalization of a patient with severe mental problems.

blacksea.name: black sea
blacksea.definition: Black sea is an inland sea between Europe and Asia. It is connected with the Aegean Sea by the Bosporus, the Sea of Marmara, and the Dardanelles.

veterinarymedicine.name: veterinary medicine
veterinarymedicine.definition: Veterinary medicine is the medical science concerned with the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases in animals.

intensivecare,neonatal.name: intensive care , neonatal
intensivecare,neonatal.definition: Neonatal intensive care is continuous care and monitoring of newborn infants with life-threatening conditions, in any setting.

foodsupply.name: food supply
foodsupply.definition: Food supply is the production and movement of food items from point of origin to use or consumption.

cellularreprogramming.name: cellular reprogramming
cellularreprogramming.definition: Cellular reprogramming is a process where fully differentiated or specialized cells revert to pluripotency or a less differentiated cell type.

smadproteins,inhibitory.name: smad proteins , inhibitory
smadproteins,inhibitory.definition: Inhibitory smad proteins is a sub-family of smad proteins that inhibit cell signaling by receptor-regulated smad proteins. They form autoinhibitory [MASK] loops in the tgf-beta signaling pathway and mediate signaling cross-talk with other signaling pathways

facialinjuries.name: facial injuries
facialinjuries.definition: Facial injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the soft tissue or bony portions of the face.

opticneuropathy,ischemic.name: optic neuropathy , ischemic
opticneuropathy,ischemic.definition: Ischemic optic neuropathy is ischemic injury to the optic nerve which usually affects the [MASK] (optic neuropathy, anterior ischemic) and less frequently the retrobulbar portion of the nerve (optic neuropathy, posterior ischemic). The injury results from occlusion of arterial blood supply which may result from temporal arteritis; atherosclerosis; [MASK]; embolism; diabetes mellitus; and other conditions. The disease primarily occurs in the sixth decade or later and presents with the sudden onset of painless and usually severe monocular visual loss. Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy also features [MASK] edema with microhemorrhages. The [MASK] appears normal in posterior ischemic optic neuropathy. (Glaser, Neuro-Ophthalmology, 2nd ed, p135)

dependentpersonalitydisorder.name: dependent personality disorder
dependentpersonalitydisorder.definition: Dependent personality disorder is a personality disorder characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of that leads to submissive and clinging behavior and fears of separation, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. (From [MASK], 1994)

skullfractures.name: skull fractures
skullfractures.definition: Skull fractures is fractures of the skull which may result from penetrating or nonpenetrating head injuries or rarely bone diseases (see also [MASK]). Skull fractures may be classified by location (e.g., skull fracture, basilar), radiographic appearance (e.g., linear), or based upon cranial integrity (e.g., skull fracture, depressed).

enzymemultipliedimmunoassaytechnique.name: enzyme multiplied immunoassay technique
enzymemultipliedimmunoassaytechnique.definition: Enzyme multiplied immunoassay technique is an immunoenzyme test for the presence of drugs and other substances in urine and blood. The test uses enzyme linked antibodies that react only with the particular drug for which the sample is being tested.

malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.name: malformations of cortical development , group iii
malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.definition: Group iii malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after cell migration in neurogenesis. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as polymicrogyria and focal cortical dysplasias.

smearlayer.name: smear layer
smearlayer.definition: Smear layer is adherent debris produced when cutting the enamel or dentin in cavity preparation. It is about 1 micron thick and its composition reflects the underlying dentin, although different quantities and qualities of smear layer can be produced by the various instrumentation techniques. Its function is presumed to be protective, as it lowers [MASK]. However, it masks the underlying dentin and interferes with attempts to bond dental material to the dentin.

basalmetabolism.name: basal metabolism
basalmetabolism.definition: Basal metabolism is metabolism (e.g., heat production) of an organism in an inactive, awake, fasting state. It may be determined directly by means of a calorimeter or indirectly by calculating the end products of oxidation within the organism or from the amount of oxygen utilized.

bloodphysiologicalphenomena.name: blood physiological phenomena
bloodphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Blood physiological phenomena is physiological processes and properties of the blood.

childguidance.name: child guidance
childguidance.definition: Child guidance is the psychiatric, sociological and psychological study and treatment of the developing child with emphasis on preventive or prophylactic measures focused on the familial, educational and socio-environmental milieu of the child.

transforminggrowthfactors.name: transforming growth factors
transforminggrowthfactors.definition: Transforming growth factors is hormonally active polypeptides that can induce the transformed phenotype when added to normal, non-transformed cells. They have been found in culture fluids from retrovirally transformed cells and in tumor-derived cells as well as in non-neoplastic sources. Their transforming activities are due to the simultaneous action of two otherwise unrelated factors, transforming growth factor alpha and transforming growth factor beta.

celldifferentiation.name: cell differentiation
celldifferentiation.definition: Cell differentiation is progressive restriction of the developmental potential and increasing specialization of function that leads to the formation of specialized cells, tissues, and organs.

rfactors.name: r factors
rfactors.definition: R factors is a class of plasmids that transfer antibiotic resistance from one bacterium to another by conjugation.

arrhythmias,cardiac.name: arrhythmias , cardiac
arrhythmias,cardiac.definition: Cardiac arrhythmias is any disturbances of the normal rhythmic beating of the heart or [MASK]. Cardiac arrhythmias can be classified by the abnormalities in heart rate, disorders of electrical impulse generation, or impulse conduction.

blotting,southern.name: blotting , southern
blotting,southern.definition: Southern blotting is a method (first developed by e.m. Southern) for detection of dna that has been electrophoretically separated and immobilized by blotting on nitrocellulose or other type of [MASK] or nylon membrane followed by hybridization with labeled nucleic acid probes.

prostaticdiseases.name: prostatic diseases
prostaticdiseases.definition: Prostatic diseases is pathological processes involving the prostate or its component tissues.

europe,eastern.name: europe , eastern
europe,eastern.definition: Eastern europe is the region of Europe generally from the area of the Baltic Sea to the Ural Mountains of Russia.

socialclass.name: social class
socialclass.definition: Social class is a stratum of people with similar position and prestige; includes social stratification. Social class is measured by criteria such as education, occupation, and income.

hematopoieticsystem.name: hematopoietic system
hematopoieticsystem.definition: Hematopoietic system is the blood-making organs and tissues, principally the bone marrow and [MASK] nodes.

tissuesurvival.name: tissue survival
tissuesurvival.definition: Tissue survival is the span of viability of a tissue or an organ.

conservationofenergyresources.name: conservation of energy resources
conservationofenergyresources.definition: Conservation of energy resources is planned management, use, and preservation of energy resources.

food,geneticallymodified.name: food , genetically modified
food,geneticallymodified.definition: Genetically modified food is food derived from genetically modified organisms (organisms, genetically modified).

organizationalinnovation.name: organizational innovation
organizationalinnovation.definition: Organizational innovation is introduction of changes which are new to the organization and are created by management.

viralvaccines.name: viral vaccines
viralvaccines.definition: Viral vaccines is suspensions of attenuated or killed viruses administered for the prevention or treatment of infectious viral disease.

mapkinasekinase6.name: map kinase kinase 6
mapkinasekinase6.definition: Map kinase kinase 6 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases.

channelislands.name: channel islands
channelislands.definition: Channel islands is a group of four British islands and several islets in the English Channel off the coast of France. They are known to have been occupied prehistorically. They were a part of Normandy in 933 but were united to the British crown at the time of the Norman Conquest in 1066. Guernsey and Jersey originated noted breeds of cattle. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p242)

healthstatus.name: health status
healthstatus.definition: Health status is the level of health of the individual, group, or population as subjectively assessed by the individual or by more objective measures.

regulatoryfactorxtranscriptionfactors.name: regulatory factor x transcription factors
regulatoryfactorxtranscriptionfactors.definition: Regulatory factor x transcription factors is a family of eukaryotic transcription factors that recognize and bind to a highly-conserved cis-regulatory sequence (X-box) within the promoter region of mhc class ii genes. They contain a conserved winged-helix dna binding domain and function as homo or heterodimers.

geneexpressionregulation,plant.name: gene expression regulation , plant
geneexpressionregulation,plant.definition: Plant gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in plants.

neutralred.name: neutral red
neutralred.definition: Neutral red is a vital dye used as an indicator and biological stain. Various adverse effects have been observed in biological systems.

americancancersociety.name: american cancer society
americancancersociety.definition: American cancer society is a voluntary organization concerned with the prevention and treatment of cancer through education and research.

centralnervoussystembacterialinfections.name: central nervous system bacterial infections
centralnervoussystembacterialinfections.definition: Central nervous system bacterial infections is bacterial infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges, including infections involving the perimeningeal spaces.

transcriptioninitiation,genetic.name: transcription initiation , genetic
transcriptioninitiation,genetic.definition: Genetic transcription initiation is the process that starts the transcription of an rna molecule. It includes the assembly of the initiation complex and establishment of the start site.

arthritis,reactive.name: arthritis , reactive
arthritis,reactive.definition: Reactive arthritis is an aseptic, inflammatory arthritis developing secondary to a primary extra-articular infection, most typically of the gastrointestinal tract or urogenital system. The initiating trigger pathogens are usually shigella; salmonella; yersinia; campylobacter; or chlamydia trachomatis. Reactive arthritis is strongly associated with hla-b27 antigen.

peripheralnervoussystemdiseases.name: peripheral nervous system diseases
peripheralnervoussystemdiseases.definition: Peripheral nervous system diseases is diseases of the peripheral nerves external to the brain and spinal cord, which includes diseases of the nerve roots, ganglia, plexi, autonomic nerves, sensory nerves, and motor nerves.

substancep.name: substance p
substancep.definition: Substance p is an eleven-amino acid neurotransmitter that appears in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. It is involved in transmission of pain, causes rapid contractions of the gastrointestinal smooth muscle, and modulates inflammatory and immune responses.

nervoussystem.name: nervous system
nervoussystem.definition: Nervous system is the entire nerve apparatus, composed of a central part, the brain and spinal cord, and a peripheral part, the cranial and spinal nerves, autonomic ganglia, and plexuses. (Stedman, 26th ed)

dentategyrus.name: dentate gyrus
dentategyrus.definition: Dentate gyrus is gray matter situated above the gyrus hippocampi. It is composed of three layers. The molecular layer is continuous with the hippocampus in the hippocampal fissure. The granular layer consists of closely arranged spherical or oval neurons, called granule cells, whose axons pass through the polymorphic layer ending on the dendrites of pyramidal cells in the hippocampus.

hepaticartery.name: hepatic artery
hepaticartery.definition: Hepatic artery is a branch of the celiac artery that distributes to the stomach, pancreas, duodenum, liver, gallbladder, and greater omentum.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilya.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily a
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilya.definition: Subfamily a atp binding cassette transporter is a large, highly conserved, subfamily of atp binding cassette transporters structurally characterized by a membrane-spanning domain composed of six alpha-helices, a large extracellular loop, nucleotide-binding domain, and a conserved cytoplasmic 80 amino acid sequence. In humans, it includes abca1(atp binding cassette transporter 1) through abca10, as well as abca12 and abca13.

electricconductivity.name: electric conductivity
electricconductivity.definition: Electric conductivity is the ability of a substrate to allow the passage of [MASK].

epilepsy,complexpartial.name: epilepsy , complex partial
epilepsy,complexpartial.definition: Complex partial epilepsy is a disorder characterized by recurrent partial seizures marked by impairment of cognition. During the seizure the individual may experience a wide variety of psychic phenomenon including formed hallucinations, illusions, deja vu, intense emotional feelings, confusion, and spatial disorientation. Focal motor activity, sensory alterations and automatism may also occur. Complex partial seizures often originate from foci in one or both temporal lobes. The etiology may be idiopathic (cryptogenic partial complex epilepsy) or occur as a secondary manifestation of a focal cortical lesion (symptomatic partial complex epilepsy). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp317-8)

maternalhealthservices.name: maternal health services
maternalhealthservices.definition: Maternal health services is organized services to provide health care to expectant and nursing mothers.

rna,plant.name: rna , plant
rna,plant.definition: Plant rna is ribonucleic acid in plants having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

drugstorage.name: drug storage
drugstorage.definition: Drug storage is the process of keeping pharmaceutical products in an appropriate location.

graphicnovel.name: graphic novel
graphicnovel.definition: Graphic novel is book-length narratives told using a combination of words and sequential art, often presented in comic book style. from (Fletcher-Spear et al., ala Review, Winter 2005)

nicotine.name: nicotine
nicotine.definition: Nicotine is nicotine is highly toxic alkaloid. It is the prototypical agonist at nicotinic cholinergic receptors where it dramatically stimulates neurons and ultimately blocks synaptic transmission. Nicotine is also important medically because of its presence in tobacco smoke.

animals,exotic.name: animals , exotic
animals,exotic.definition: Exotic animals is animals native to a foreign country or of foreign origin or [MASK], that are not native to the United States.

animals,zoo.name: animals , zoo
animals,zoo.definition: Zoo animals is animal population groups or individual animals that reside in captivity at a zoological park.

diseasereservoirs.name: disease reservoirs
diseasereservoirs.definition: Disease reservoirs is animate or inanimate sources which normally harbor disease-causing organisms and thus serve as potential sources of [MASK]. Reservoirs are distinguished from vectors (disease vectors) and carriers, which are agents of disease transmission rather than continuing sources of potential [MASK]. Humans may serve both as disease reservoirs and carriers.

electrophoresis,celluloseacetate.name: electrophoresis , cellulose acetate
electrophoresis,celluloseacetate.definition: Cellulose acetate electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which cellulose acetate is the diffusion medium.

receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,typei.name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type i
receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,typei.definition: Type i tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that has specificity for tumor necrosis factor alpha and lymphotoxin alpha. It is constitutively expressed in most tissues and is a key mediator of tumor necrosis factor signaling in the vast majority of cells. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm.

fetalviability.name: fetal viability
fetalviability.definition: Fetal viability is the potential of the fetus to survive outside the uterus after birth, natural or induced. Fetal viability depends largely on the fetal organ maturity, and environmental conditions.

employment,supported.name: employment , supported
employment,supported.definition: Supported employment is paid work for mentally or physically disabled persons, taking place in regular or normal work settings. It may be competitive employment (work that pays minimum wage) or employment with subminimal wages in individualized or group placement situations. It is intended for persons with severe disabilities who require a range of support services to maintain employment. Supported employment differs from sheltered workshops in that work in the latter takes place in a controlled working environment. Federal regulations are authorized and administered by the u.s. Department of Education, Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services.

alkaloids.name: alkaloids
alkaloids.definition: Alkaloids is organic nitrogenous bases. Many alkaloids of medical importance occur in the animal and vegetable kingdoms, and some have been synthesized. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

pharmaceuticalresearch.name: pharmaceutical research
pharmaceuticalresearch.definition: Pharmaceutical research is research activity focused on pharmaceutical products and services.

cathepsinb.name: cathepsin b
cathepsinb.definition: Cathepsin b is a lysosomal [MASK] proteinase with a specificity similar to that of papain. The enzyme is present in a variety of tissues and is important in many physiological and pathological processes. In pathology, cathepsin b has been found to be involved in demyelination; emphysema; rheumatoid arthritis, and neoplasm invasiveness.

lossofheterozygosity.name: loss of heterozygosity
lossofheterozygosity.definition: Loss of heterozygosity is the loss of one allele at a specific locus, caused by a deletion mutation; or loss of a chromosome from a chromosome pair, resulting in abnormal hemizygosity. It is detected when heterozygous markers for a locus appear monomorphic because one of the alleles was deleted.

tandemrepeatsequences.name: tandem repeat sequences
tandemrepeatsequences.definition: Tandem repeat sequences is copies of dna sequences which lie adjacent to each other in the same orientation (direct tandem repeats) or in the opposite direction to each other (inverted tandem repeats).

inflation,economic.name: inflation , economic
inflation,economic.definition: Economic inflation is an increase in the volume of money and credit relative to available goods resulting in a substantial and continuing rise in the general price level.

dnaprobes.name: dna probes
dnaprobes.definition: Dna probes is species- or subspecies-specific dna (including complementary dna; conserved genes, whole chromosomes, or whole genomes) used in hybridization studies in order to identify microorganisms, to measure dna-dna homologies, to group subspecies, etc. The dna probe hybridizes with a specific mRNA, if present. Conventional techniques used for testing for the hybridization product include dot blot assays, Southern blot assays, and dna:rna hybrid-specific antibody tests. Conventional labels for the dna probe include the radioisotope labels 32p and 125i and the chemical label biotin. The use of dna probes provides a specific, sensitive, rapid, and inexpensive replacement for cell culture techniques for diagnosing infections.

examinationtables.name: examination tables
examinationtables.definition: Examination [MASK] is a raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during a physical examination.

environmentalpollution.name: environmental pollution
environmentalpollution.definition: Environmental pollution is contamination of the air, bodies of water, or land with substances that are harmful to human health and the environment.

extremeweather.name: extreme weather
extremeweather.definition: Extreme weather is events that have extreme values of important meteorological variables. Extreme is generally defined as either taking maximum values or exceedance above pre-existing high thresholds. Such events are generally rare; for example, extreme [MASK] speeds exceeding the 100-year return value, which have a probability of only 0.01 of occurring in any particular year. (Stephenson, 2008)

colonicneoplasms.name: colonic neoplasms
colonicneoplasms.definition: Colonic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the colon.

sentinellymphnode.name: sentinel lymph node
sentinellymphnode.definition: Sentinel [MASK] node is first [MASK] node to receive drainage from the primary tumor. sentinel [MASK] node biopsy is performed to determine early metastasis status because cancer cells may appear first in the sentinel node.

chromatography,thinlayer.name: chromatography , thin layer
chromatography,thinlayer.definition: Thin layer chromatography is chromatography on thin layers of adsorbents rather than in columns. The adsorbent can be [MASK], [MASK], silicates, charcoals, or cellulose. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

pituitarydiseases.name: pituitary diseases
pituitarydiseases.definition: Pituitary diseases is disorders involving either the adenohypophysis or the [MASK]. These diseases usually manifest as hypersecretion or hyposecretion of pituitary hormones. Neoplastic pituitary masses can also cause compression of the optic chiasm and other adjacent structures.

dnapolymeraseiii.name: dna polymerase iii
dnapolymeraseiii.definition: Dna polymerase iii is a DNA-dependent dna polymerase characterized in e. coli and other lower organisms but may be present in higher organisms.
