Use also for a more complex form of dna polymerase iii designated as dna polymerase iii* or pol iii* which is 15 times more active biologically than dna polymerase i in the synthesis of dna. This polymerase has both 3'-5' and 5'-3' exonuclease activities, is inhibited by sulfhydryl reagents, and has the same template-primer dependence as pol ii.

volunteers.name: volunteers
volunteers.definition: Volunteers is persons who donate their services.

geriatricdentistry.name: geriatric dentistry
geriatricdentistry.definition: Geriatric dentistry is the branch of dentistry concerned with the dental problems of older people.

assistedlivingfacilities.name: assisted living facilities
assistedlivingfacilities.definition: Assisted living facilities is a housing and health care alternative combining independence with personal care. It provides a combination of housing, personalized supportive services and health care designed to meet the needs, both scheduled and unscheduled, of those who need help with activities of daily living. (www.alfa.org)

postpartumperiod.name: postpartum period
postpartumperiod.definition: Postpartum period is in females, the period that is shortly after giving birth (parturition).

molecularbiology.name: molecular biology
molecularbiology.definition: Molecular biology is a discipline concerned with studying biological phenomena in terms of the chemical and physical interactions of molecules.

dualmedicaidmedicareeligibility.name: dual medicaid medicare eligibility
dualmedicaidmedicareeligibility.definition: Dual medicaid medicare eligibility is coordination of coverage eligibility of those individuals who are entitled to medicaid and medicare.

mitochondrialmembranetransportproteins.name: mitochondrial membrane transport proteins
mitochondrialmembranetransportproteins.definition: [MASK] transport proteins is proteins involved in the transport of specific substances across the membranes of the mitochondria.

cellcycleproteins.name: cell cycle proteins
cellcycleproteins.definition: Cell cycle proteins is proteins that control the cell division cycle. This family of proteins includes a wide variety of classes, including cyclin-dependent kinases, mitogen-activated kinases, cyclins, and phosphoprotein phosphatases as well as their putative substrates such as chromatin-associated proteins, cytoskeletal proteins, and transcription factors.

cysteineproteases.name: cysteine proteases
cysteineproteases.definition: [MASK] proteases is a subclass of peptide hydrolases that depend on a [MASK] residue for their activity.

dnaprobes,hla.name: dna probes , hla
dnaprobes,hla.definition: Hla dna probes is dna probes specific for the human leukocyte antigen genes, which represent the major histocompatibility determinants in humans. The four known loci are designated as a, b, c, and d. Specific antigens are identified by a locus notation and number, e.g., hla-a11. The inheritance of certain hla alleles is associated with increased risk for certain diseases (e.g., insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus).

biomarkers,tumor.name: biomarkers , tumor
biomarkers,tumor.definition: Tumor biomarkers is molecular products metabolized and secreted by neoplastic tissue and characterized biochemically in cells or body fluids. They are indicators of tumor stage and grade as well as useful for monitoring responses to treatment and predicting recurrence. Many chemical groups are represented including hormones; antigens; amino and nucleic acids; enzymes; polyamines; and specific cell membrane proteins and lipids.

gammarays.name: gamma rays
gammarays.definition: Gamma rays is penetrating, high-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted from atomic nuclei during nuclear decay. The range of wavelengths of emitted radiation is between 0.1 - 100 pm which overlaps the shorter, more energetic hard x-rays wavelengths. The distinction between gamma rays and X-rays is based on their radiation source.

receptors,adiponectin.name: receptors , adiponectin
receptors,adiponectin.definition: Adiponectin receptors is cell surface receptors for adiponectin, an antidiabetic hormone secreted by adipocytes. Adiponectin receptors are membrane proteins with multiple cytoplasmic and extracellular regions. They are about 43 kDa and encoded by at least two genes with different affinities for globular and full-length adiponectin.

libraryassociations.name: library associations
libraryassociations.definition: Library associations is organizations of persons and institutions associated with a type of library or region.

accessorynervediseases.name: accessory nerve diseases
accessorynervediseases.definition: Accessory nerve diseases is diseases of the eleventh cranial (spinal accessory) nerve. This nerve originates from motor neurons in the lower medulla (accessory portion of nerve) and upper spinal cord (spinal portion of nerve). The two components of the nerve join and exit the skull via the jugular foramen, innervating the sternocleidomastoid and [MASK], which become weak or paralyzed if the nerve is injured. The nerve is commonly involved in motor neuron disease, and may be injured by trauma to the posterior triangle of the [MASK].

radiography,abdominal.name: radiography , abdominal
radiography,abdominal.definition: Abdominal radiography is radiographic visualization of the body between the thorax and the pelvis, i.e., within the peritoneal cavity.

hematopoieticstemcelltransplantation.name: hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
hematopoieticstemcelltransplantation.definition: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is transfer of hematopoietic stem cells from bone marrow or blood between individuals within the same species (transplantation, homologous) or transfer within the same individual (transplantation, autologous). Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation has been used as an alternative to bone marrow transplantation in the treatment of a variety of neoplasms.

smadproteins.name: smad proteins
smadproteins.definition: Smad proteins is a family of proteins that are involved in the translocation of signals from tgf-beta receptors; bone morphogenetic protein receptors; and other surface receptors to the cell nucleus. They were originally identified as a class of proteins that are related to the mothers against decapentaplegic protein, Drosophila and sma proteins from caenorhabditis elegans.

hospitalmortality.name: hospital mortality
hospitalmortality.definition: Hospital mortality is a vital statistic measuring or recording the rate of death from any cause in hospitalized populations.

republicofkorea.name: republic of korea
republicofkorea.definition: Republic of korea is the capital is Seoul. The country, established September 9, 1948, is located on the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. Its northern border is shared with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

contactinhibition.name: contact inhibition
contactinhibition.definition: Contact inhibition is arrest of cell locomotion or cell division when two cells come into contact.

receptors,chimericantigen.name: receptors , chimeric antigen
receptors,chimericantigen.definition: Chimeric antigen receptors is synthetic cellular receptors that reprogram t-lymphocytes to selectively bind antigens.

generegulatorynetworks.name: gene regulatory networks
generegulatorynetworks.definition: Gene regulatory networks is interacting DNA-encoded regulatory subsystems in the genome that coordinate input from activator and repressor transcription factors during development, cell differentiation, or in response to environmental cues. The networks function to ultimately specify expression of particular sets of genes for specific conditions, times, or locations.

environment.name: environment
environment.definition: Environment is the external elements and conditions which surround, influence, and affect the life and development of an organism or population.

cystfluid.name: cyst fluid
cystfluid.definition: Cyst fluid is liquid material found in epithelial-lined closed cavities or sacs.

id.name: id
id.definition: Id is the part of the personality structure which harbors the [MASK] instinctive desires and strivings of the individual.

simplifiedacutephysiologyscore.name: simplified acute physiology score
simplifiedacutephysiologyscore.definition: Simplified acute physiology score is a severity of disease classification system designed to measure the severity of disease for patients aged 15 and over admitted to intensive care units.

sorptiondetoxification.name: sorption detoxification
sorptiondetoxification.definition: Sorption detoxification is elimination of toxic or biologically active substances from body fluids by interaction with a sorbent medium. The types of media include absorbents, adsorbents, ion-exchange materials, and complexing agents. Detoxification can be extracorporeal (hemodialysis, hemofiltration, hemoperfusion, plasmapheresis), or occur inside the body (enterosorption, peritoneal dialysis).

libraries,dental.name: libraries , dental
libraries,dental.definition: Dental libraries is collections of [MASK] relevant to dentistry.

olfactorybulb.name: olfactory bulb
olfactorybulb.definition: Olfactory bulb is ovoid body resting on the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone where the olfactory nerve terminates. The olfactory bulb contains several types of nerve cells including the mitral cells, on whose dendrites the olfactory nerve synapses, forming the olfactory glomeruli. The accessory olfactory bulb, which receives the [MASK] from the vomeronasal organ via the vomeronasal nerve, is also included here.

pyramidalcells.name: pyramidal cells
pyramidalcells.definition: Pyramidal cells is [MASK] neurons in the cerebral cortex and the hippocampus. Pyramidal cells have a pyramid-shaped soma with the apex and an apical dendrite pointed toward the pial surface and other dendrites and an axon emerging from the base. The axons may have local collaterals but also project outside their cortical region.

aging.name: aging
aging.definition: Aging is the gradual irreversible changes in structure and function of an organism that occur as a result of the passage of time.

respiratorytractneoplasms.name: respiratory tract neoplasms
respiratorytractneoplasms.definition: Respiratory tract neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the respiratory system.

receptor,igftype1.name: receptor , igf type 1
receptor,igftype1.definition: Igf type 1 receptor is a protein-tyrosine kinase receptor that is closely related in structure to the insulin receptor. Although commonly referred to as the igf-i receptor, it binds both igf-i and igf-ii with high affinity. It is comprised of a tetramer of two alpha and two beta subunits which are derived from cleavage of a single precursor protein. The beta subunit contains an intrinsic tyrosine kinase domain.

water.name: water
water.definition: Water is a clear, odorless, tasteless liquid that is essential for most animal and plant life and is an excellent solvent for many substances. The chemical formula is hydrogen oxide (h2o). (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

mitosismodulators.name: mitosis modulators
mitosismodulators.definition: [MASK] modulators is agents that affect [MASK] of cells.

austria.name: austria
austria.definition: Austria is a country located in Central Europe, north of Italy and Slovenia. The capital is Vienna.

mosaicviruses.name: mosaic viruses
mosaicviruses.definition: Mosaic viruses is viruses which produce a mottled appearance of the leaves of plants.

gastrichypothermia.name: gastric hypothermia
gastrichypothermia.definition: Gastric hypothermia is a method of lowering core body temperature by filling the stomach with chilled fluids.

nuclearmatrix.name: nuclear matrix
nuclearmatrix.definition: Nuclear matrix is the residual framework structure of the cell nucleus that maintains many of the overall architectural features of the cell nucleus including the nuclear lamina with nuclear pore complex structures, residual cell nucleoli and an extensive fibrogranular structure in the nuclear interior. (Advan. Enzyme Regul. 2002; 42:39-52)

professionaloroccupationalgroup.name: professional or occupational group
professionaloroccupationalgroup.definition: Professional or occupational group is professional or occupational group

immunoglobulindomains.name: immunoglobulin domains
immunoglobulindomains.definition: Immunoglobulin domains is compact globular protein domains of about 80 to 110 amino acids.They are characterized by two antiparallel beta sheets stabilized by hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds between opposing strands. Three major subtypes of Ig domains are recognized: variable (v), intermediate (i), and constant (c1 or c2). Members of the immunoglobulin superfamily include antigen receptors; cytokine receptors; and cell adhesion molecules which possess immunoglobulin domains.

adolescentdevelopment.name: adolescent development
adolescentdevelopment.definition: Adolescent development is the continuous sequential physiological and psychological changes during adolescence, approximately between the age of 13 and 18.

bloodpatch,epidural.name: blood patch , epidural
bloodpatch,epidural.definition: Epidural blood patch is the injection of autologous blood into the [MASK] either as a prophylactic treatment immediately following an epidural puncture or for treatment of headache as a result of an epidural puncture.

physicalfitness.name: physical fitness
physicalfitness.definition: Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities in a highly functional state, often as a result of physical conditioning.

eyeburns.name: eye burns
eyeburns.definition: Eye burns is injury to any part of the eye by extreme heat, chemical agents, or ultraviolet radiation.

meatproteins.name: meat proteins
meatproteins.definition: Meat proteins is dietary proteins from meat.

nursingadministrationresearch.name: nursing administration research
nursingadministrationresearch.definition: Nursing administration research is research concerned with establishing costs of nursing care, examining the relationships between nursing services and quality patient care, and viewing problems of nursing service delivery within the broader context of policy analysis and delivery of health services (from a national study, presented at the 1985 Council on Graduate Education for Administration in Nursing (cgean) meeting).

nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member2.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 4 , group a , member 2
nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member2.definition: Member 2 group a nuclear receptor subfamily 4 is an orphan nuclear receptor that is found at high levels in brain tissue. The protein is believed to play a role in development and maintenance of neurons, particularly [MASK].

veterinarysportsmedicine.name: veterinary sports medicine
veterinarysportsmedicine.definition: Veterinary sports medicine is the field of veterinary medicine concerned with physical fitness of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

earcartilage.name: ear cartilage
earcartilage.definition: Ear cartilage is cartilage of the ear auricle and the [MASK].

genomecomponents.name: genome components
genomecomponents.definition: Genome components is the parts of a genome sequence that are involved with the different functions or properties of genomes as a whole as opposed to those of individual genes.

calciumchannels.name: calcium channels
calciumchannels.definition: Calcium channels is voltage-dependent cell membrane glycoproteins selectively permeable to calcium ions. They are categorized as l-, t-, n-, p-, q-, and R-types based on the activation and inactivation kinetics, ion specificity, and sensitivity to drugs and toxins. The l- and T-types are present throughout the cardiovascular and central nervous systems and the n-, p-, q-, & R-types are located in neuronal tissue.

extracellularpolymericsubstancematrix.name: extracellular polymeric substance matrix
extracellularpolymericsubstancematrix.definition: Extracellular polymeric substance matrix is extracellular matrix formed by secreted polymeric organic compounds by microorganisms. This secreted compound is mostly polysaccharides but may include proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. The matrix facilitates attachment of microbes to form various biofilm communities.

drawing.name: drawing
drawing.definition: Drawing is work consisting of graphic representations of objects or ideas by lines.

carotidartery,internal.name: carotid artery , internal
carotidartery,internal.definition: Internal carotid artery is branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the anterior part of the brain, the eye and its appendages, the forehead and nose.

rupture,spontaneous.name: rupture , spontaneous
rupture,spontaneous.definition: Spontaneous rupture is tear or break of an organ, vessel or other soft part of the body, occurring in the absence of external force.

heavymetalpoisoning.name: heavy metal poisoning
heavymetalpoisoning.definition: Heavy metal poisoning is poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, [MASK], or skin absorption of heavy metals. Acute and chronic exposures can cause anemia; kidney and liver damage; [MASK]; memory loss and behavioral changes; bone deformities in children; and miscarriage or premature labor in pregnant women.

healthservicesneedsanddemand.name: health services needs and demand
healthservicesneedsanddemand.definition: Health services needs and demand is health services required by a population or community as well as the health services that the population or community is able and willing to pay for.

biologicalcontrolagents.name: biological control agents
biologicalcontrolagents.definition: Biological control agents is organisms, biological agents, or biologically-derived agents used strategically for their positive or adverse effect on the physiology and/or reproductive health of other organisms.

drinking.name: drinking
drinking.definition: Drinking is the consumption of liquids.

intraoperativecare.name: intraoperative care
intraoperativecare.definition: Intraoperative care is patient care procedures performed during the operation that are ancillary to the actual surgery. It includes monitoring, fluid therapy, medication, transfusion, anesthesia, radiography, and laboratory tests.

fitnesscenters.name: fitness centers
fitnesscenters.definition: Fitness centers is facilities having programs intended to promote and maintain a state of physical well-being for optimal performance and health.

index.name: index
index.definition: Index is work providing an analytical subject approach to materials in a field of knowledge.

speechproductionmeasurement.name: speech production measurement
speechproductionmeasurement.definition: [MASK] production measurement is measurement of parameters of the [MASK] product such as vocal tone, loudness, pitch, [MASK], articulation, resonance, phonation, phonetic structure and prosody.

maxillarydiseases.name: maxillary diseases
maxillarydiseases.definition: Maxillary diseases is diseases involving the maxilla.

behaviortherapy.name: behavior therapy
behaviortherapy.definition: Behavior therapy is the application of modern theories of learning and conditioning in the treatment of behavior disorders.

personalitydisorders.name: personality disorders
personalitydisorders.definition: Personality disorders is a major deviation from normal patterns of behavior.

appendix.name: appendix
appendix.definition: Appendix is a worm-like blind tube extension from the cecum.

receptor.name: receptor
receptor.definition: Receptor is a molecule inside or on the surface of a cell that binds to a specific substance and causes a specific effect in the cell.

forestry.name: forestry
forestry.definition: Forestry is the science of developing, [MASK] for, or cultivating forests.

gingivalhemorrhage.name: gingival hemorrhage
gingivalhemorrhage.definition: Gingival hemorrhage is the flowing of blood from the marginal gingival area, particularly the sulcus, seen in such conditions as gingivitis, marginal periodontitis, injury, and ascorbic acid deficiency.

renalinsufficiency,chronic.name: renal insufficiency , chronic
renalinsufficiency,chronic.definition: Chronic renal insufficiency is conditions in which the kidneys perform below the normal level for more than three months. Chronic kidney insufficiency is classified by five stages according to the decline in [MASK] and the degree of kidney damage (as measured by the level of proteinuria). The most severe form is the [MASK] ([MASK]). (Kidney [MASK]: Kidney Disease Outcome Quality Initiative, 2002)

ampicillinresistance.name: ampicillin resistance
ampicillinresistance.definition: Ampicillin resistance is nonsusceptibility of a microbe to the action of ampicillin, a penicillin derivative that interferes with cell wall synthesis.

tickparalysis.name: tick paralysis
tickparalysis.definition: Tick paralysis is paralysis caused by a neurotropic toxin secreted by the salivary glands of ticks.

fibrinogen.name: fibrinogen
fibrinogen.definition: Fibrinogen is plasma glycoprotein clotted by thrombin, composed of a dimer of three non-identical pairs of polypeptide chains (alpha, beta, gamma) held together by disulfide bonds. Fibrinogen clotting is a sol-gel change involving complex molecular arrangements: whereas fibrinogen is cleaved by thrombin to form polypeptides a and b, the proteolytic action of other enzymes yields different fibrinogen degradation products.

hospitalrecords.name: hospital records
hospitalrecords.definition: Hospital records is compilations of data on hospital activities and programs; excludes patient medical records.

serotoninreceptoragonists.name: serotonin receptor agonists
serotoninreceptoragonists.definition: Serotonin receptor agonists is endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate serotonin receptors. Many serotonin receptor agonists are used as antidepressants; anxiolytics; and in the treatment of [MASK].

fasligandprotein.name: fas ligand protein
fasligandprotein.definition: Fas ligand protein is a transmembrane protein belonging to the tumor necrosis factor superfamily that was originally discovered on cells of the lymphoid-myeloid lineage, including activated t-lymphocytes and natural killer cells. It plays an important role in immune homeostasis and cell-mediated toxicity by binding to the fas receptor and triggering apoptosis.

influenzabvirus.name: influenza b virus
influenzabvirus.definition: Influenza b virus is species of the genus influenzavirus b that cause human influenza and other diseases primarily in humans. Antigenic variation is less extensive than in type a viruses (influenza a virus) and consequently there is no basis for distinct subtypes or variants. Epidemics are less likely than with influenza a virus and there have been no pandemics. Previously only found in humans, Influenza b virus has been isolated from seals which may constitute the animal reservoir from which humans are exposed.

dentalrestoration,temporary.name: dental restoration , temporary
dentalrestoration,temporary.definition: Temporary dental restoration is a prosthesis or restoration placed for a limited period, from several days to several months, which is designed to seal the tooth and maintain its position until a permanent restoration (dental restoration, permanent) will replace it. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992)

killercells,natural.name: killer cells , natural
killercells,natural.definition: Natural killer cells is bone marrow-derived lymphocytes that possess cytotoxic properties, classically directed against transformed and virus-infected cells. Unlike t cells; and b cells; nk cells are not antigen specific. The cytotoxicity of natural killer cells is determined by the collective signaling of an array of inhibitory and stimulatory cell surface receptors. a subset of t-lymphocytes referred to as natural killer t cells shares some of the properties of this cell type.

cerebellarnuclei.name: cerebellar nuclei
cerebellarnuclei.definition: Cerebellar nuclei is four clusters of neurons located deep within the [MASK] matter of the cerebellum, which are the nucleus dentatus, nucleus emboliformis, nucleus globosus, and nucleus fastigii.

mineralfibers.name: mineral fibers
mineralfibers.definition: Mineral fibers is long, pliable, cohesive natural or manufactured filaments of various lengths. They form the structure of some minerals. The medical significance lies in their potential ability to cause various types of pneumoconiosis (e.g., asbestosis) after occupational or environmental exposure. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed, p708)

vitaminkdeficiency.name: vitamin k deficiency
vitaminkdeficiency.definition: Vitamin k deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin k in the diet, characterized by an increased tendency to hemorrhage (hemorrhagic disorders). Such bleeding episodes may be particularly severe in newborn infants. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1182)

priondiseases.name: prion diseases
priondiseases.definition: Prion diseases is a group of genetic, infectious, or sporadic degenerative human and animal nervous system disorders associated with abnormal prions. These diseases are characterized by conversion of the normal prion protein to an abnormal configuration via a post-translational process. In humans, these conditions generally feature dementia; ataxia; and a [MASK]. Pathologic features include a spongiform encephalopathy without evidence of inflammation. The older literature occasionally refers to these as unconventional slow virus diseases. (From Proc Natl Acad Sci usa 1998 Nov 10;95(23):13363-83)

selfconcept.name: self concept
selfconcept.definition: Self concept is persons' view of themselves.

adultsurvivorsofchildabuse.name: adult survivors of child abuse
adultsurvivorsofchildabuse.definition: Adult survivors of child abuse is persons who were child victims of violence and abuse including physical, sexual, or emotional maltreatment.

incontinencepads.name: incontinence pads
incontinencepads.definition: Incontinence pads is absorbent pads used for urinary incontinence and usually worn as underpants or pants liners by the elderly.

earlygrowthresponseprotein2.name: early growth response protein 2
earlygrowthresponseprotein2.definition: Early growth response protein 2 is an early growth response transcription factor that controls the formation of the myelin sheath around peripheral axons by schwann cells. Mutations in egr2 transcription factor have been associated with hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies such as charcot-marie-tooth disease.

decompression.name: decompression
decompression.definition: Decompression is decompression external to the body, most often the slow lessening of external pressure on the whole body (especially in caisson workers, deep sea divers, and persons who ascend to great heights) to prevent decompression sickness. It includes also sudden accidental decompression, but not surgical (local) decompression or decompression applied through body openings.

nanotubes.name: nanotubes
nanotubes.definition: Nanotubes is nanometer-sized tubes composed of various substances including carbon (carbon nanotubes), boron nitride, or nickel vanadate.

frontalsinus.name: frontal sinus
frontalsinus.definition: Frontal sinus is one of the paired, but seldom symmetrical, air spaces located between the inner and outer compact layers of the [MASK] in the forehead.

nitrogendioxide.name: nitrogen dioxide
nitrogendioxide.definition: Nitrogen dioxide is nitrogen oxide (no2). a highly poisonous gas. Exposure produces inflammation of lungs that may only cause slight pain or pass unnoticed, but resulting edema several days later may cause death. (From Merck, 11th ed) It is a major atmospheric pollutant that is able to absorb uv light that does not reach the earth's surface.

gravity,altered.name: gravity , altered
gravity,altered.definition: Altered gravity is a change in, or manipulation of, gravitational force. This may be a natural or artificial effect.

pituitaryhormones,posterior.name: pituitary hormones , posterior
pituitaryhormones,posterior.definition: Posterior pituitary hormones is hormones released from the [MASK] ([MASK]). They include a number of peptides which are formed in the neurons in the hypothalamus, bound to neurophysins, and stored in the nerve terminals in the posterior pituitary. Upon stimulation, these peptides are released into the hypophysial portal vessel blood.

advancedoxidationproteinproducts.name: advanced oxidation protein products
advancedoxidationproteinproducts.definition: Advanced oxidation protein products is a class of dityrosine-containing protein-derived molecules formed by oxidative stress. Their accumulation in plasma is associated with certain pathological conditions.

controlledclinicaltrialsastopic.name: controlled clinical trials as topic
controlledclinicaltrialsastopic.definition: Controlled clinical trials as topic is works about clinical trials involving one or more test treatments, at least one control treatment, specified outcome measures for evaluating the studied intervention, and a bias-free method for assigning patients to the test treatment. The treatment may be drugs, devices, or procedures studied for diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic effectiveness. Control measures include placebos, active medicines, no-treatment, dosage forms and regimens, historical comparisons, etc. When randomization using mathematical techniques, such as the use of a random numbers [MASK], is employed to assign patients to test or control treatments, the trials are characterized as randomized controlled trials as topic.

diseaseorsyndrome.name: disease or syndrome
diseaseorsyndrome.definition: Disease or syndrome is a definite pathologic process with a characteristic [MASK] of signs and symptoms.

tissuepreservation.name: tissue preservation
tissuepreservation.definition: Tissue preservation is the process by which a tissue or aggregate of cells is kept alive outside of the organism from which it was derived (i.e., kept from decay by means of a chemical agent, cooling, or a fluid substitute that mimics the natural state within the organism).

auditoryfatigue.name: auditory fatigue
auditoryfatigue.definition: Auditory fatigue is loss of sensitivity to sounds as a result of [MASK], manifesting as a temporary shift in auditory threshold. The temporary threshold shift, tts, is expressed in decibels.

inappropriateprescribing.name: inappropriate prescribing
inappropriateprescribing.definition: Inappropriate prescribing is the practice of administering medications in a manner that poses more risk than benefit, particularly where safer alternatives exist.

lactobacillus.name: lactobacillus
lactobacillus.definition: Lactobacillus is a genus of gram-positive, microaerophilic, rod-shaped bacteria occurring widely in nature. Its species are also part of the many normal flora of the mouth, intestinal tract, and vagina of many mammals, including humans. Pathogenicity from this genus is rare.

tissuefixation.name: tissue fixation
tissuefixation.definition: Tissue fixation is the technique of using fixatives in the preparation of cytologic, histologic, or pathologic specimens for the purpose of maintaining the existing form and structure of all the constituent elements.

uterineinertia.name: uterine inertia
uterineinertia.definition: Uterine inertia is failure of the uterus to contract with normal strength, duration, and intervals during childbirth (labor, obstetric). It is also called uterine atony.

medicalrecords.name: medical records
medicalrecords.definition: Medical records is recording of pertinent information concerning patient's illness or illnesses.

ovulationdetection.name: ovulation detection
ovulationdetection.definition: Ovulation detection is method to determine the occurrence of ovulation by direct or indirect means. Indirect methods examine the effects of progesterone on [MASK] ([MASK]), or basal body temperature. Direct ovulation detection, generally used in fertility treatment, involves analyses of circulating hormones in blood and ultrasonography.

vitamindresponseelement.name: vitamin d response element
vitamindresponseelement.definition: Vitamin d response element is a dna sequence that is found in the promoter region of vitamin d regulated genes. Vitamin d receptor (receptor, calcitriol) binds to and regulates the activity of genes containing this element.

epigeneticrepression.name: epigenetic repression
epigeneticrepression.definition: Epigenetic repression is the turning off of genetic transcription in certain regions of chromatin without changes in the dna sequence. Typically epigenetic repression is a way that developmental changes are programmed at the cellular level.

meningitis,bacterial.name: meningitis , bacterial
meningitis,bacterial.definition: Bacterial meningitis is bacterial infections of the leptomeninges and subarachnoid space, frequently involving the cerebral cortex, cranial nerves, cerebral blood vessels, spinal cord, and nerve roots.

animaltestingalternatives.name: animal testing alternatives
animaltestingalternatives.definition: Animal testing alternatives is procedures, such as tissue culture techniques; mathematical models; etc., when used or advocated for use in place of the use of animals in research or diagnostic laboratories.

insuranceclaimreview.name: insurance claim review
insuranceclaimreview.definition: Insurance claim review is review of claims by insurance companies to determine liability and amount of payment for various services. The review may also include determination of eligibility of the claimant or beneficiary or of the provider of the benefit; determination that the benefit is covered or not payable under another policy; or determination that the service was necessary and of reasonable cost and quality.

benzene.name: benzene
benzene.definition: Benzene is toxic, volatile, flammable liquid hydrocarbon byproduct of coal distillation. It is used as an industrial solvent in paints, varnishes, lacquer thinners, gasoline, etc. Benzene causes central nervous system damage acutely and bone marrow damage chronically and is carcinogenic. It was formerly used as parasiticide.

governmentemployees.name: government employees
governmentemployees.definition: Government employees is persons employed by the government.

infusions,spinal.name: infusions , spinal
infusions,spinal.definition: Spinal infusions is the administration of medication by insertion of a tiny needle or catheter into the spinal sac or epidural cavity.

vascularsurgicalprocedures.name: vascular surgical procedures
vascularsurgicalprocedures.definition: Vascular surgical procedures is operative procedures for the treatment of vascular disorders.

chromiumcompounds.name: chromium compounds
chromiumcompounds.definition: Chromium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain chromium as an integral part of the molecule.

viralcoreproteins.name: viral core proteins
viralcoreproteins.definition: Viral core proteins is proteins found mainly in icosahedral dna and rna viruses. They consist of proteins directly associated with the nucleic acid inside the nucleocapsid.

touchperception.name: touch perception
touchperception.definition: Touch perception is the process by which the nature and meaning of tactile stimuli are recognized and interpreted by the brain, such as realizing the characteristics or name of an object being touched.

worldwari.name: world war i
worldwari.definition: World war i is global [MASK] primarily fought on European continent, that occurred between 1914 and 1918.

heart,artificial.name: heart , artificial
heart,artificial.definition: Artificial heart is a pumping mechanism that duplicates the output, rate, and blood pressure of the natural heart. It may replace the function of the entire heart or a portion of it, and may be an intracorporeal, extracorporeal, or paracorporeal heart. (Dorland, 28th ed)

methylcpgbindingdomain.name: methyl cpg binding domain
methylcpgbindingdomain.definition: Methyl cpg binding domain is a protein domain of about 70 amino acids in length that folds into a sandwich structure consisting of a beta sheet, alpha helix, and C-terminal hairpin loop which forms a hydrophobic methylated-DNA binding patch. It binds to methylated cpg islands in eukaryotes and occurs with other dna and chromatin binding domains such as at-hook motifs in eukaryotic dna binding proteins.

antibodies.name: antibodies
antibodies.definition: Antibodies is immunoglobulin molecules having a specific amino acid sequence by virtue of which they interact only with the antigen (or a very similar shape) that induced their synthesis in cells of the lymphoid series (especially plasma cells).

testicularhormones.name: testicular hormones
testicularhormones.definition: Testicular hormones is hormones produced in the testis.

piper.name: piper
piper.definition: Piper is a plant genus of the family piperaceae that includes species used for spicy and stimulating qualities.

neoplasticstemcells.name: neoplastic stem cells
neoplasticstemcells.definition: Neoplastic stem cells is highly proliferative, self-renewing, and colony-forming stem cells which give rise to neoplasms.

mathematics.name: mathematics
mathematics.definition: Mathematics is the deductive study of shape, quantity, and dependence. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

clinicaltrial.name: clinical trial
clinicaltrial.definition: Clinical trial is a work that reports on the results of a clinical study in which participants are assigned to receive one or more interventions so that researchers can evaluate the interventions on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The assignments are determined by the study protocol. Participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions. For clinical trials on  veterinary animals see clinical trial, veterinary. Clinical Trials was used for both humans and non-humans prior to 2019.

minutevirusofmice.name: minute virus of mice
minutevirusofmice.definition: Minute virus of mice is the type species of parvovirus prevalent in mouse colonies and found as a contaminant of many transplanted tumors or leukemias.

respiratorysystemagents.name: respiratory system agents
respiratorysystemagents.definition: Respiratory system agents is drugs used for their effects on the respiratory system.

ammoniumcompounds.name: ammonium compounds
ammoniumcompounds.definition: Ammonium compounds is inorganic compounds that include a positively charged tetrahedral nitrogen (ammonium ion) as part of their structure. This class of compounds includes a broad variety of simple ammonium [MASK] and derivatives.

pleasure.name: pleasure
pleasure.definition: Pleasure is sensation of enjoyment or gratification.

cues.name: cues
cues.definition: Cues is signals for an action; that specific portion of a perceptual field or pattern of stimuli to which a subject has learned to respond.

probabilitylearning.name: probability learning
probabilitylearning.definition: Probability learning is usually refers to the use of mathematical models in the prediction of learning to perform tasks based on the theory of probability applied to responses; it may also refer to the frequency of occurrence of the responses observed in the particular study.

integrationhostfactors.name: integration host factors
integrationhostfactors.definition: Integration host factors is bacterial proteins that are used by bacteriophages to incorporate their dna into the dna of the "host" bacteria. They are DNA-binding proteins that function in genetic recombination as well as in transcriptional and translational regulation.

complementfactorh.name: complement factor h
complementfactorh.definition: Complement factor h is an important soluble regulator of the alternative pathway of complement activation (complement activation pathway, alternative). It is a 139-kDa glycoprotein expressed by the liver and secreted into the blood. It binds to complement c3b and makes iC3b (inactivated complement 3b) susceptible to cleavage by complement factor i. Complement factor h also inhibits the association of C3b with complement factor b to form the C3bB proenzyme, and promotes the dissociation of Bb from the C3bBb complex (complement c3 convertase, alternative pathway).

protons.name: protons
protons.definition: Protons is stable elementary particles having the smallest known positive charge, found in the nuclei of all elements. The proton mass is less than that of a neutron. a proton is the nucleus of the light hydrogen atom, i.e., the hydrogen ion.

remission,spontaneous.name: remission , spontaneous
remission,spontaneous.definition: Spontaneous remission is a spontaneous diminution or abatement of a disease over time, without formal treatment.

respiratorycenter.name: respiratory center
respiratorycenter.definition: Respiratory center is part of the brain located in the medulla oblongata and pons. It receives neural, chemical and hormonal signals, and controls the rate and depth of respiratory movements of the diaphragm and other respiratory muscles.

excitatoryaminoacidagents.name: excitatory amino acid agents
excitatoryaminoacidagents.definition: [MASK] agents is drugs used for their actions on any aspect of [MASK] neurotransmitter systems. Included are drugs that act on [MASK], affect the [MASK] of [MASK] transmitters, or affect the survival of neurons using [MASK].

overall.name: overall
overall.definition: Overall is a single citation covering [MASK] or [MASK] presented at a meeting. The publication type may be used for a single citation with or without the additional indexing or cataloging of individual [MASK]. The individual [MASK], however, are not labeled overall.

neoplasms,basalcell.name: neoplasms , basal cell
neoplasms,basalcell.definition: Basal cell neoplasms is neoplasms composed of cells from the deepest layer of the epidermis. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in the stratum basale.

retinaldegeneration.name: retinal degeneration
retinaldegeneration.definition: Retinal degeneration is a retrogressive pathological change in the retina, focal or generalized, caused by genetic defects, inflammation, trauma, vascular disease, or aging. Degeneration affecting predominantly the macula lutea of the retina is macular degeneration. (Newell, Ophthalmology: Principles and Concepts, 7th ed, p304)

contrastmedia.name: contrast media
contrastmedia.definition: Contrast media is substances used to allow enhanced visualization of tissues.

rna,viral.name: rna , viral
rna,viral.definition: Viral rna is ribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of viruses.

recurrence.name: recurrence
recurrence.definition: Recurrence is the return of a sign, symptom, or disease after a remission.

dnapackaging.name: dna packaging
dnapackaging.definition: Dna packaging is the folding of an organism's dna molecule into a compact, orderly structure that fits within the limited space of a cell or virus particle.

patientnavigation.name: patient navigation
patientnavigation.definition: Patient navigation is the process of helping patients to effectively and efficiently use the health care system when faced with one or more of these challenges: (1) choosing, understanding, and using health coverage or applying for assistance when uninsured; (2) choosing, using, and understanding different types of health providers and services; (3) making treatment decisions; and (4) managing care received by multiple providers.

pregnancy,multiple.name: pregnancy , multiple
pregnancy,multiple.definition: Multiple pregnancy is the condition of carrying two or more fetuses simultaneously.

woundclosuretechniques.name: wound closure techniques
woundclosuretechniques.definition: Wound closure techniques is methods to repair breaks in tissue caused by trauma or to close [MASK].

proteinuria.name: proteinuria
proteinuria.definition: Proteinuria is the presence of proteins in the urine, an indicator of kidney diseases.

preferredproviderorganizations.name: preferred provider organizations
preferredproviderorganizations.definition: Preferred provider organizations is arrangements negotiated between a third-party payer (often a self-insured company or union trust fund) and a group of health-care providers (hospitals and physicians) who furnish services at lower than usual fees, and, in return, receive prompt payment and an expectation of an increased volume of patients.

reliefwork.name: relief work
reliefwork.definition: Relief work is assistance, such as money, food, or shelter, given to the needy, aged, or victims of disaster. It is usually granted on a temporary basis. (From The American Heritage Dictionary, 2d college ed)

microfluidicanalyticaltechniques.name: microfluidic analytical techniques
microfluidicanalyticaltechniques.definition: Microfluidic analytical techniques is methods utilizing the principles of microfluidics for sample handling, reagent mixing, and separation and detection of specific components in fluids.

childnutritiondisorders.name: child nutrition disorders
childnutritiondisorders.definition: Child nutrition disorders is disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, occurring in children ages 2 to 12 years.

olfactorynervediseases.name: olfactory nerve diseases
olfactorynervediseases.definition: Olfactory nerve diseases is diseases of the first cranial (olfactory) nerve, which usually feature anosmia or other alterations in the sense of smell and taste. Anosmia may be associated with neoplasms; central nervous system infections; craniocerebral trauma; inherited conditions; toxins; metabolic diseases; tobacco abuse; and other conditions. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp229-31)

thoracicoutletsyndrome.name: thoracic outlet syndrome
thoracicoutletsyndrome.definition: Thoracic outlet syndrome is a neurovascular syndrome associated with compression of the brachial plexus; subclavian artery; and subclavian vein at the superior thoracic outlet. This may result from a variety of anomalies such as a cervical rib, anomalous fascial bands, and abnormalities of the origin or insertion of the anterior or medial scalene muscles. Clinical features may include pain in the [MASK] and [MASK] region which radiates into the [MASK], paresis or paralysis of brachial plexus innervated muscles, paresthesia, loss of sensation, reduction of arterial pulses in the affected extremity, ischemia, and edema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp214-5).

randomallocation.name: random allocation
randomallocation.definition: Random allocation is a process involving chance used in therapeutic trials or other research endeavor for allocating experimental subjects, human or animal, between treatment and control groups, or among treatment groups. It may also apply to experiments on inanimate objects.

facialrecognition.name: facial recognition
facialrecognition.definition: Facial recognition is ability to identify an individual from their facial features.

malaysia.name: malaysia
malaysia.definition: Malaysia is a parliamentary democracy with a constitutional monarch in southeast Asia, consisting of 11 states (West Malaysia) on the Malay Peninsula and two states (East Malaysia) on the island of borneo. It is also called the Federation of Malaysia. Its capital is Kuala Lumpur. Before 1963 it was the Union of Malaya. It reorganized in 1948 as the Federation of Malaya, becoming independent from British Malaya in 1957 and becoming Malaysia in 1963 as a federation of Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore (which seceded in 1965). The form Malay- probably derives from the Tamil malay, mountain, with reference to its geography. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p715 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p329)

nervenet.name: nerve net
nervenet.definition: Nerve net is a meshlike structure composed of interconnecting nerve cells that are separated at the synaptic junction or joined to one another by cytoplasmic processes. In invertebrates, for example, the nerve net allows nerve impulses to spread over a wide area of the net because synapses can pass information in any direction.

kidneycortexnecrosis.name: kidney cortex necrosis
kidneycortexnecrosis.definition: Kidney cortex necrosis is death of cells in the kidney cortex, a common final result of various renal injuries including hypoxia; ischemia; and drug toxicity.

peritonealfibrosis.name: peritoneal fibrosis
peritonealfibrosis.definition: Peritoneal fibrosis is disorder characterized by a wide range of structural changes in peritoneum, resulting from fibrogenic or inflammatory processes. Peritoneal fibrosis is a common complication in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis and contributes to its gradual decrease in efficiency.

forearm.name: forearm
forearm.definition: Forearm is part of the upper extremity in humans and primates extending from the elbow to the wrist.

cornoil.name: corn oil
cornoil.definition: Corn oil is oil from zea mays or corn plant.

dna,plant.name: dna , plant
dna,plant.definition: Plant dna is deoxyribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of plants.

diagnostictechniques,neurological.name: diagnostic techniques , neurological
diagnostictechniques,neurological.definition: Neurological diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the nervous system, central and peripheral, or demonstration of neurologic function or dysfunction.

cardiology.name: cardiology
cardiology.definition: Cardiology is the study of the heart, its physiology, and its functions.

renalveins.name: renal veins
renalveins.definition: Renal veins is short thick veins which return blood from the kidneys to the vena cava.

taperecording.name: tape recording
taperecording.definition: Tape recording is recording of information on magnetic or punched [MASK] tape.

lymphoma,primaryeffusion.name: lymphoma , primary effusion
lymphoma,primaryeffusion.definition: Primary effusion lymphoma is a rare neoplasm of large B-cells usually presenting as serious effusions without detectable tumor masses. The most common sites of involvement are the pleural, pericardial, and peritoneal cavities. It is associated with human herpesvirus 8, most often occurring in the setting of immunodeficiency.

portalpressure.name: portal pressure
portalpressure.definition: Portal pressure is the venous pressure measured in the portal vein.

cytochromedgroup.name: cytochrome d group
cytochromedgroup.definition: Cytochrome d group is cytochromes ([MASK]-transporting proteins) with a tetrapyrrolic chelate of iron as a prosthetic group in which the degree of conjugation of double bonds is less than in porphyrin. (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992, p539)

cellularstructures.name: cellular structures
cellularstructures.definition: Cellular structures is components of a cell.

headimpulsetest.name: head impulse test
headimpulsetest.definition: Head impulse test is identification of [MASK] during a rapid head [MASK] to assess vestibuloocular reflex.

receptors,fc.name: receptors , fc
receptors,fc.definition: Fc receptors is molecules found on the surface of some, but not all, B-lymphocytes, T-lymphocytes, and macrophages, which recognize and combine with the Fc (crystallizable) portion of immunoglobulin molecules.

life.name: life
life.definition: Life is the state that distinguishes organisms from inorganic matter, manifested by growth, metabolism, reproduction, and adaptation. It includes the course of existence, the sum of experiences, the mode of existing, or the fact of being. Over the centuries inquiries into the nature of life have crossed the boundaries from philosophy to biology, forensic medicine, anthropology, etc., in creative as well as scientific literature. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed; Dr. James h. Cassedy, nlm [MASK] Division)

growthdifferentiationfactor9.name: growth differentiation factor 9
growthdifferentiationfactor9.definition: Growth differentiation factor 9 is a bone morphogenetic protein that plays an essential role in the regulation of ovarian folliculogenesis.

leukemia,lymphoid.name: leukemia , lymphoid
leukemia,lymphoid.definition: Lymphoid leukemia is leukemia associated with hyperplasia of the lymphoid tissues and increased numbers of circulating malignant lymphocytes and lymphoblasts.

myocardialbridging.name: myocardial bridging
myocardialbridging.definition: Myocardial bridging is a malformation that is characterized by a muscle bridge over a segment of the coronary arteries. Systolic contractions of the muscle bridge can lead to narrowing of coronary artery; coronary compression; myocardial ischemia; myocardial infarction; and [MASK].

professionalstaffcommittees.name: professional staff committees
professionalstaffcommittees.definition: Professional staff committees is committees of professional personnel who have responsibility for determining policies, procedures, and controls related to professional matters in health facilities.

inositol.name: inositol
inositol.definition: Inositol is an isomer of glucose that has traditionally been considered to be a b vitamin although it has an uncertain status as a vitamin and a deficiency syndrome has not been identified in man. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p1379) Inositol [MASK] are important in signal transduction.

proteinsortingsignals.name: protein sorting signals
proteinsortingsignals.definition: Protein sorting signals is amino acid sequences found in transported proteins that selectively guide the distribution of the proteins to specific cellular compartments.

personalitytests.name: personality tests
personalitytests.definition: Personality tests is standardized objective tests designed to facilitate the evaluation of personality.

glycine.name: glycine
glycine.definition: Glycine is a non-essential amino acid. It is found primarily in gelatin and silk fibroin and used therapeutically as a nutrient. It is also a fast inhibitory neurotransmitter.

episodeofcare.name: episode of care
episodeofcare.definition: Episode of care is an interval of care by a health care facility or provider for a specific medical problem or condition. It may be continuous or it may consist of a series of intervals marked by one or more brief separations from care, and can also identify the sequence of care (e.g., emergency, inpatient, outpatient), thus serving as one measure of health care provided.

polyu.name: poly u
polyu.definition: Poly u is a group of uridine ribonucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each uridine ribonucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the ribose moieties.

genome,human.name: genome , human
genome,human.definition: Human genome is the complete genetic complement contained in the dna of a [MASK] of chromosomes in a human. The length of the human genome is about 3 billion [MASK].

dentalphysiologicalphenomena.name: dental physiological phenomena
dentalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Dental physiological phenomena is physiological processes and properties of the dentition.

journalimpactfactor.name: journal impact factor
journalimpactfactor.definition: Journal impact factor is a quantitative measure of the frequency on average with which articles in a journal have been cited in a given period of time.

spinalcordregeneration.name: spinal cord regeneration
spinalcordregeneration.definition: Spinal cord regeneration is repair of the damaged neuron function after spinal cord injury or spinal cord diseases.

maxillarysinusneoplasms.name: maxillary sinus neoplasms
maxillarysinusneoplasms.definition: Maxillary sinus neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the maxillary sinus. They represent the majority of paranasal neoplasms.

philadelphiachromosome.name: philadelphia chromosome
philadelphiachromosome.definition: [MASK] chromosome is an aberrant form of human chromosome 22 characterized by translocation of the distal end of chromosome 9 from 9q34, to the long [MASK] of chromosome 22 at 22q11. It is present in the bone marrow cells of 80 to 90 per cent of patients with chronic myelocytic leukemia (leukemia, myelogenous, chronic, bcr-abl positive).

eosinophils.name: eosinophils
eosinophils.definition: Eosinophils is granular leukocytes with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by a slender thread of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and stainable by eosin.

operatingrooms.name: operating rooms
operatingrooms.definition: Operating rooms is facilities equipped for performing surgery.

microvascularangina.name: microvascular angina
microvascularangina.definition: Microvascular angina is angina pectoris or angina-like [MASK] with a normal coronary arteriogram and positive exercise test. The cause of the syndrome is unknown. While its recognition is of clinical importance, its prognosis is excellent. (Braunwald, Heart Disease, 4th ed, p1346; Jablonski Dictionary of Syndromes & Eponymic Diseases, 2d ed). It is different from metabolic syndrome x, a syndrome characterized by insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia, that has increased risk for cardiovascular disease.

consensusdevelopmentconferencesastopic.name: consensus development conferences as topic
consensusdevelopmentconferencesastopic.definition: [MASK] conferences as topic is works that are about the concept of [MASK] conferences, such as their general design or a means of scientific communication.

nursingstaff,hospital.name: nursing staff , hospital
nursingstaff,hospital.definition: Hospital nursing staff is personnel who provide nursing service to patients in a hospital.

posterioreyesegment.name: posterior eye segment
posterioreyesegment.definition: Posterior eye segment is the back two-thirds of the eye that includes the anterior hyaloid membrane and all of the optical structures behind it: the [MASK]; retina; choroid; and optic nerve.

radiotherapydosage.name: radiotherapy dosage
radiotherapydosage.definition: Radiotherapy dosage is the total amount of radiation absorbed by tissues as a result of radiotherapy.

medicalaudit.name: medical audit
medicalaudit.definition: Medical audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel for evaluating quality of medical care.

carcinoma.name: carcinoma
carcinoma.definition: Carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm made up of epithelial cells tending to infiltrate the surrounding tissues and give rise to metastases. It is a histological type of neoplasm and not a synonym for "cancer."

cysticduct.name: cystic duct
cysticduct.definition: Cystic duct is the duct that is connected to the gallbladder and allows the emptying of [MASK] into the common [MASK].

mechanistictargetofrapamycincomplex2.name: mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2
mechanistictargetofrapamycincomplex2.definition: Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 is a multiprotein complex consisting of mTOR kinase; mlst8 protein;  rapamycin-insensitive companion of mTOR protein (rictor protein); and prr5 (proline-rich protein 5). Like mTORC1, it also regulates cell growth and proliferation in response to growth factors but may not be as sensitive to nutrient availability and is insensitive to sirolimus. In contrast to mTORC1, it can regulate the actin cytoskeleton through rho gtpases to promote the formation of stress fibers. The mTORC2 complex also plays a critical role in akt1 protein kinase phosphorylation and activation.

professionalpracticelocation.name: professional practice location
professionalpracticelocation.definition: Professional practice location is geographic area in which a professional person practices; includes primarily physicians and dentists.

placentadiseases.name: placenta diseases
placentadiseases.definition: Placenta diseases is pathological processes or abnormal functions of the placenta.

foodingredients.name: food ingredients
foodingredients.definition: Food ingredients is substances included in prepared foods and beverages.

electrochemicaltechniques.name: electrochemical techniques
electrochemicaltechniques.definition: Electrochemical techniques is the utilization of an electrical current to measure, analyze, or alter chemicals or chemical reactions in solution, cells, or tissues.

fourthventricle.name: fourth ventricle
fourthventricle.definition: Fourth ventricle is an irregularly shaped cavity in the rhombencephalon, located between the medulla oblongata; the pons; and the isthmus in front, and the cerebellum behind. It is continuous with the central canal of the cord below and with the cerebral aqueduct above, and through its lateral and median apertures it communicates with the subarachnoid space.

freezeetching.name: freeze etching
freezeetching.definition: Freeze etching is a replica technique in which cells are frozen to a very low temperature and cracked with a knife blade to expose the interior surfaces of the cells or cell membranes. The cracked cell surfaces are then freeze-dried to expose their constituents. The surfaces are now ready for shadowing to be viewed using an [MASK] microscope. This method differs from freeze-fracturing in that no cryoprotectant is used and, thus, allows for the sublimation of water during the freeze-drying process to etch the surfaces.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 1
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.definition: Member 1 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is a 170-kDa transmembrane glycoprotein from the superfamily of atp-binding cassette transporters. It serves as an ATP-dependent efflux pump for a variety of chemicals, including many antineoplastic agents. Overexpression of this glycoprotein is associated with multidrug resistance (see drug resistance, multiple).

ultrasonography,doppler,duplex.name: ultrasonography , doppler , duplex
ultrasonography,doppler,duplex.definition: Duplex doppler ultrasonography is ultrasonography applying the Doppler effect combined with real-time imaging. The real-time image is created by rapid movement of the ultrasound beam. a powerful advantage of this technique is the ability to estimate the velocity of flow from the Doppler shift frequency.

aldosterone.name: aldosterone
aldosterone.definition: Aldosterone is a hormone secreted by the adrenal cortex that regulates electrolyte and water balance by increasing the renal retention of sodium and the excretion of potassium.

sodiumhydroxide.name: sodium hydroxide
sodiumhydroxide.definition: Sodium hydroxide is a highly caustic substance that is used to neutralize acids and make sodium [MASK]. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

ovulation.name: ovulation
ovulation.definition: Ovulation is the discharge of an ovum from a rupturing follicle in the ovary.

universities.name: universities
universities.definition: Universities is educational institutions providing facilities for teaching and research and authorized to grant academic degrees.

paternalbehavior.name: paternal behavior
paternalbehavior.definition: Paternal behavior is the behavior patterns associated with or characteristic of a [MASK].

reactivenitrogenspecies.name: reactive nitrogen species
reactivenitrogenspecies.definition: Reactive nitrogen species is nitrogenous products of [MASK] synthases, ranging from [MASK] to nitrates. These reactive nitrogen intermediates also include the inorganic peroxynitrous acid and the organic s-nitrosothiols.

formaldehyde.name: formaldehyde
formaldehyde.definition: Formaldehyde is a highly reactive aldehyde gas formed by oxidation or incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons. In solution, it has a wide range of uses: in the manufacture of resins and textiles, as a disinfectant, and as a laboratory fixative or preservative. Formaldehyde solution (formalin) is considered a hazardous compound, and its vapor toxic. (From Reynolds, Martindale The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p717)

sodiumacetate.name: sodium acetate
sodiumacetate.definition: Sodium acetate is the trihydrate sodium [MASK] of acetic acid, which is used as a source of sodium ions in solutions for dialysis and as a systemic and urinary alkalizer, diuretic, and expectorant.

skinaging.name: skin aging
skinaging.definition: Skin aging is the process of aging due to changes in the structure and elasticity of the skin over time. It may be a part of physiological aging or it may be due to the effects of ultraviolet radiation, usually through exposure to sunlight.

harveymurinesarcomavirus.name: harvey murine sarcoma virus
harveymurinesarcomavirus.definition: Harvey murine sarcoma virus is a replication-defective mouse sarcoma virus (sarcoma viruses, murine) first described by j.j. Harvey in 1964.

transplantation,heterologous.name: transplantation , heterologous
transplantation,heterologous.definition: Heterologous transplantation is transplantation between animals of different species.

microscopy,polarization.name: microscopy , polarization
microscopy,polarization.definition: Polarization microscopy is microscopy using polarized light in which phenomena due to the preferential orientation of optical properties with respect to the vibration plane of the polarized light are made visible and correlated parameters are made measurable.

fish.name: fish
fish.definition: Fish is a group of cold-blooded, aquatic vertebrates having gills, fins, a cartilaginous or bony endoskeleton, and elongated bodies covered with scales.

interleukinreceptorcommongammasubunit.name: interleukin receptor common gamma subunit
interleukinreceptorcommongammasubunit.definition: Interleukin receptor common gamma subunit is an interleukin receptor subunit that was originally discovered as a component of the interleukin 2 receptor. It was subsequently found to be a component of several other receptors including the interleukin 4 receptor, the interleukin 7 receptor, the interleukin-9 receptor, the interleukin-15 receptor, and the interleukin-21 receptor. Mutations in the gene for the interleukin receptor common gamma chain have been associated with x-linked combined immunodeficiency diseases.

scopeofpractice.name: scope of practice
scopeofpractice.definition: Scope of practice is the services that licensed professionals are deemed competent to perform, and permitted to undertake in keeping with the terms of their professional license.

laboratorypersonnel.name: laboratory personnel
laboratorypersonnel.definition: Laboratory personnel is professionals, technicians, and assistants staffing laboratories.

complementactivatingenzymes.name: complement activating enzymes
complementactivatingenzymes.definition: Complement activating enzymes is enzymes that activate one or more complement proteins in the complement system leading to the formation of the complement membrane attack complex, an important response in host defense. They are enzymes in the various complement activation pathways.

ultrasonictherapy.name: ultrasonic therapy
ultrasonictherapy.definition: Ultrasonic therapy is the use of focused, high-frequency sound waves to produce local hyperthermia in certain diseased or injured parts of the body or to destroy the diseased tissue.

healthfacilitymoving.name: health facility moving
healthfacilitymoving.definition: Health facility moving is the relocation of health care institutions or units thereof. The concept includes equipment relocation.

internationalsystemofunits.name: international system of units
internationalsystemofunits.definition: International system of units is a system of physical units in which the fundamental quantities are length, time, mass, electric current, temperature, luminous intensity, and amount of substance, and the corresponding units are the meter, second, kilogram, ampere, kelvin, candela, and mole. The system has been given official status and recommended for universal use by the General Conference on Weights and Measures.

receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,member25.name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 25
receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,member25.definition: Member 25 tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype with specificity for tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15. It is found in tissues containing lymphocytes and may play a role in regulating lymphocyte homeostasis and apoptosis. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm.

complementarytherapies.name: complementary therapies
complementarytherapies.definition: Complementary therapies is therapeutic practices which are not currently considered an integral part of conventional allopathic medical practice. They may lack biomedical explanations but as they become better researched some (physical therapy modalities; diet; acupuncture) become widely accepted whereas others (humors, radium therapy) quietly fade away, yet are important historical footnotes. Therapies are termed as Complementary when used in addition to conventional treatments and as Alternative when used instead of conventional treatment.

geneorgenome.name: gene or genome
geneorgenome.definition: Gene or genome is a category of nucleic acid sequences that function as units of heredity and which code for the basic instructions for the development, reproduction, and maintenance of organisms.

peritonealcavity.name: peritoneal cavity
peritonealcavity.definition: Peritoneal cavity is the space enclosed by the peritoneum. It is divided into two portions, the greater sac and the lesser sac or omental bursa, which lies behind the stomach. The two sacs are connected by the foramen of Winslow, or epiploic foramen.

intramuscularabsorption.name: intramuscular absorption
intramuscularabsorption.definition: Intramuscular absorption is uptake of substances via muscle tissue.

metabolism.name: metabolism
metabolism.definition: Metabolism is the chemical reactions in living organisms by which energy is provided for vital processes and activities and new material is assimilated.

donorselection.name: donor selection
donorselection.definition: Donor selection is the procedure established to evaluate the health status and risk factors of the potential donors of biological materials. Donors are selected based on the principles that their health will not be compromised in the process, and the donated materials, such as tissues or organs, are safe for reuse in the recipients.

rnapolymerasei.name: rna polymerase i
rnapolymerasei.definition: Rna polymerase i is a DNA-dependent rna polymerase present in bacterial, plant, and animal cells. The enzyme functions in the nucleolar structure and transcribes dna into rna. It has different requirements for cations and [MASK] than rna polymerase ii and iii and is not inhibited by alpha-amanitin.

germtheoryofdisease.name: germ theory of disease
germtheoryofdisease.definition: Germ theory of disease is the fundamental tenet of modern medicine that certain diseases are caused by microorganisms. It was confirmed by the work of Pasteur, Lister, and Koch.

glycogenstoragediseasetypeiib.name: glycogen storage disease type iib
glycogenstoragediseasetypeiib.definition: Glycogen storage disease type iib is an X-linked dominant multisystem disorder resulting in cardiomyopathy, myopathy and intellectual disability. It is caused by mutation in the gene encoding lysosomal-associated membrane protein 2.

dualspecificityphosphatase6.name: dual specificity phosphatase 6
dualspecificityphosphatase6.definition: Dual specificity phosphatase 6 is a dual specificity phosphatase subtype that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction by inactivating mitogen-activated protein kinases. It has specificity for extracellular signal-regulated map kinases and is primarily localized to the [MASK].

egypt,ancient.name: egypt , ancient
egypt,ancient.definition: Ancient [MASK] is a civilization of ancient Northeastern Africa, concentrated along the lower reaches of the Nile [MASK] in the area of [MASK]. It was active from 3100 b.c. until its conquest by Alexander the Great in 332 b.c.

genomicinstability.name: genomic instability
genomicinstability.definition: Genomic instability is an increased tendency of the genome to acquire mutations when various processes involved in maintaining and replicating the genome are dysfunctional.

musclefibers,skeletal.name: muscle fibers , skeletal
musclefibers,skeletal.definition: Skeletal muscle fibers is large, multinucleate single cells, either cylindrical or prismatic in shape, that form the basic unit of skeletal muscle. They consist of myofibrils enclosed within and attached to the sarcolemma. They are derived from the fusion of skeletal myoblasts (myoblasts, skeletal) into a syncytium, followed by differentiation.

prostate.name: prostate
prostate.definition: Prostate is a gland in males that surrounds the [MASK] of the [MASK] and the urethra. It secretes a substance that liquefies coagulated semen. It is situated in the pelvic cavity behind the lower part of the pubic symphysis, above the deep layer of the triangular ligament, and rests upon the rectum.

chemokines.name: chemokines
chemokines.definition: Chemokines is class of pro-inflammatory cytokines that have the ability to attract and activate leukocytes. They can be divided into at least three structural branches: c; (chemokines, c); [MASK], cc); and cxc; (chemokines, cxc); according to variations in a shared [MASK] motif.

microtubuleproteins.name: microtubule proteins
microtubuleproteins.definition: [MASK] proteins is proteins found in the [MASK].

braindamage,chronic.name: brain damage , chronic
braindamage,chronic.definition: Chronic brain damage is a condition characterized by long-standing brain dysfunction or damage, usually of three months duration or longer. Potential etiologies include brain infarction; certain neurodegenerative disorders; craniocerebral trauma; anoxia, brain; encephalitis; certain neurotoxicity syndromes; metabolic disorders (see brain diseases, metabolic); and other conditions.

mouthneoplasms.name: mouth neoplasms
mouthneoplasms.definition: Mouth neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the mouth.

tetracyclineresistance.name: tetracycline resistance
tetracyclineresistance.definition: Tetracycline resistance is nonsusceptibility of bacteria to the action of tetracycline which inhibits aminoacyl-tRNA binding to the 30s ribosomal subunit during protein synthesis.

transcriptionfactor4.name: transcription factor 4
transcriptionfactor4.definition: Transcription factor 4 is a basic helix-loop-helix [MASK] zipper transcription factor that functions in neuronal cell differentiation. It dimerizes with other bHLH transcription factors and activates transcription through binding to e-box elements containing 5'-acanntgt-3' or 5'-ccanntgg-3' sequences. Mutations in the tcf-4 gene are associated with Pitt-Hopkins Syndrome, a severe developmental disorder.

managementserviceorganizations.name: management service organizations
managementserviceorganizations.definition: Management service organizations is voluntarily-formed groups of healthcare professionals who join for common management services and other benefits such as collective bargaining agreements with reimbursement agents. The physical assets of a practice are controlled by the mso which also provides billing, collections, and similar services. The practitioner retains control of patient records and management of patient care.

plants.name: plants
plants.definition: Plants is multicellular, eukaryotic life forms of kingdom Plantae (sensu lato), comprising the viridiplantae; rhodophyta; and glaucophyta; all of which acquired chloroplasts by direct endosymbiosis of cyanobacteria. They are characterized by a mainly photosynthetic mode of nutrition; essentially unlimited growth at localized regions of cell divisions (meristems); cellulose within cells providing rigidity; the absence of organs of locomotion; absence of nervous and sensory systems; and an alternation of haploid and diploid generations.

naturalresources.name: natural resources
naturalresources.definition: Natural resources is materials or substances such as land, timber, fresh water, fossil fuels, or mineral deposits that occur in a natural state and have economic value or usefulness to humans.

hepatitis,alcoholic.name: hepatitis , alcoholic
hepatitis,alcoholic.definition: Alcoholic hepatitis is inflammation of the liver due to alcohol abuse. It is characterized by necrosis of [MASK], infiltration by neutrophils, and deposit of mallory bodies. Depending on its severity, the inflammatory lesion may be reversible or progress to liver cirrhosis.

peripheralnervoussystemagents.name: peripheral nervous system agents
peripheralnervoussystemagents.definition: Peripheral nervous system agents is drugs that act principally at one or more sites within the peripheral neuroeffector systems, the autonomic system, and motor nerve-skeletal system. (From Smith and Reynard, Textbook of Pharmacology, 1991, p75)

boneresorption.name: bone resorption
boneresorption.definition: Bone resorption is bone loss due to osteoclastic activity.

hispanicamericans.name: hispanic americans
hispanicamericans.definition: Hispanic americans is persons living in the United States of Mexican ([MASK]), Puerto Rican, Cuban, Central or South American, or other Spanish culture or origin. The concept does not include Brazilian Americans or Portuguese Americans.

sharedgovernance,nursing.name: shared governance , nursing
sharedgovernance,nursing.definition: Nursing shared governance is model of nursing practice with shared decision processes designed to integrate core values and beliefs that professional practice embraces, as a means of achieving quality care.

aminoacids,acidic.name: amino acids , acidic
aminoacids,acidic.definition: Acidic amino acids is amino acids with side chains that are negatively charged at physiological pH.

manuscript,medical.name: manuscript , medical
manuscript,medical.definition: Medical manuscript is medical works prepared by hand including handwritten or typescript drafts of pre-publication [MASK] or works not otherwise reproduced in multiple copies.

skinandconnectivetissuediseases.name: skin and connective tissue diseases
skinandconnectivetissuediseases.definition: Skin and connective tissue diseases is a collective term for diseases of the skin and its appendages and of connective tissue.

hairbleachingagents.name: hair bleaching agents
hairbleachingagents.definition: Hair bleaching agents is chemicals that are used to oxidize pigments in hair.

societies,veterinary.name: societies , veterinary
societies,veterinary.definition: Veterinary societies is organizations having institutional membership limited to veterinarians and veterinary institutions.

silvercompounds.name: silver compounds
silvercompounds.definition: Silver compounds is inorganic compounds that contain silver as an integral part of the molecule.

troponint.name: troponin t
troponint.definition: Troponin t is a troponin complex subunit that binds to tropomyosin. There are three troponin t subtypes: troponin t1, t2 and t3. Troponin t2 is cardiac-specific whereas troponin t2 and t3 are skeletal subtypes. Troponin t2 is a biomarker for damaged or injured [MASK] and mutations in troponin t2 gene are associated with [MASK].

geneproducts,rev.name: gene products , rev
