geneproducts,rev.definition: Rev gene products is trans-acting nuclear proteins whose functional expression are required for retroviral replication. Specifically, the rev gene products are required for processing and translation of the gag and env mRNAs, and thus rev regulates the expression of the viral structural proteins. rev can also regulate [MASK]. a cis-acting antirepression sequence (car) in env, also known as the [MASK] (rre), is responsive to the rev gene product. rev is short for regulator of virion.

bias.name: bias
bias.definition: Bias is any deviation of results or inferences from the truth, or processes leading to such deviation. Bias can result from several sources: one-sided or systematic variations in measurement from the true value (systematic error); flaws in study design; deviation of inferences, interpretations, or analyses based on flawed data or data collection; etc. There is no sense of prejudice or subjectivity implied in the assessment of bias under these conditions.

cyclind.name: cyclin d
cyclind.definition: Cyclin d is a cyclin subtype that is specific for cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and cyclin-dependent kinase 6. Unlike most cyclins, cyclin d expression is not cyclical, but rather it is expressed in response to proliferative signals. Cyclin d may therefore play a role in cellular responses to mitogenic signals.

neoplasms,nervetissue.name: neoplasms , nerve tissue
neoplasms,nervetissue.definition: Nerve tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of nerve tissue. This concept does not refer to neoplasms located in the nervous system or its component nerves.

fibrinclotlysistime.name: fibrin clot lysis time
fibrinclotlysistime.definition: Fibrin clot lysis time is a measurement of the time needed for fibrinolysis to occur.

computers,analog.name: computers , analog
computers,analog.definition: Analog computers is computers in which quantities are represented by physical variables; problem parameters are translated into equivalent mechanical or electrical circuits as an analog for the physical phenomenon being investigated. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

ethics,dental.name: ethics , dental
ethics,dental.definition: Dental ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the dentist, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the dentist in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

neurologicalrehabilitation.name: neurological rehabilitation
neurologicalrehabilitation.definition: Neurological rehabilitation is physician-supervised programs designed to rehabilitate people with diseases, trauma, or disorders of the nervous system.

psychologicaldistress.name: psychological distress
psychologicaldistress.definition: Psychological distress is negative emotional state characterized by physical and/or emotional discomfort, pain, or anguish.

animalpopulationgroups.name: animal population groups
animalpopulationgroups.definition: Animal population groups is animals grouped according to ecological, morphological or genetic populations.

rats.name: rats
rats.definition: Rats is the common name for the genus Rattus.

pharmacy.name: pharmacy
pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy is the practice of compounding and dispensing medicinal preparations.

ironmetabolismdisorders.name: iron metabolism disorders
ironmetabolismdisorders.definition: Iron metabolism disorders is disorders in the processing of iron in the body: its absorption, transport, storage, and utilization. (From Mosby's Medical, Nursing, & Allied Health Dictionary, 4th ed)

adenoma,livercell.name: adenoma , liver cell
adenoma,livercell.definition: Liver cell adenoma is a benign epithelial tumor of the liver.

suicide,completed.name: suicide , completed
suicide,completed.definition: Completed suicide is the successful attempt to kill oneself.

geneticcounseling.name: genetic counseling
geneticcounseling.definition: Genetic counseling is an educational process that provides information and advice to individuals or families about a genetic condition that may affect them. The purpose is to help individuals make informed decisions about marriage, reproduction, and other health management issues based on information about the genetic disease, the available [MASK], and management programs. Psychosocial support is usually offered.

mediterraneanregion.name: mediterranean region
mediterraneanregion.definition: Mediterranean region is the Mediterranean Sea, the Mediterranean islands, and the countries bordering on the sea collectively.

socialworkers.name: social workers
socialworkers.definition: Social workers is professionals who work with persons affected by social disadvantages such as poverty; mental and physical illness or disability, and social injustice.  Their focus is on both the individual and his or her environment, including violations of their civil liberties and human rights.

biologicalontologies.name: biological ontologies
biologicalontologies.definition: Biological ontologies is structured vocabularies describing concepts from the fields of biology and relationships between concepts.

cleavagestimulationfactor.name: cleavage stimulation factor
cleavagestimulationfactor.definition: Cleavage stimulation factor is a RNA-binding protein that stimulates the cleavage of the 3' end of mrna near the polyadenylation site. It is a heterotrimer of 55-, 64- and 77-kDa subunits and combines with cleavage stimulation factor to form a stable complex with mRNA that directs the 3' cleavage and polyadenylation reaction.

fluidsandsecretions.name: fluids and secretions
fluidsandsecretions.definition: Fluids and secretions is liquid substances produced by living organisms to fulfill specific functions or excreted as waste.

cycling.name: cyclin g
cycling.definition: Cyclin g is a cyclin subtype that is found associated with cyclin-dependent kinase 5; cyclin g associated kinase, and protein phosphatase 2.

sarcoma,endometrialstromal.name: sarcoma , endometrial stromal
sarcoma,endometrialstromal.definition: Endometrial stromal sarcoma is a highly malignant subset of neoplasms arising from the endometrial stroma. Tumors in this group infiltrate the stroma with a wide range of atypia cells and numerous [MASK]. They are capable of widespread metastases (neoplasm metastasis).

heartvalvediseases.name: heart valve diseases
heartvalvediseases.definition: Heart valve diseases is pathological conditions involving any of the various heart valves and the associated structures (papillary muscles and chordae tendineae).

rna,bacterial.name: rna , bacterial
rna,bacterial.definition: Bacterial rna is ribonucleic acid in bacteria having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

choleravaccines.name: cholera vaccines
choleravaccines.definition: Cholera vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with vibrio cholerae. The original cholera vaccine consisted of killed bacteria, but other kinds of vaccines now exist.

betaparticles.name: beta particles
betaparticles.definition: Beta particles is high energy [MASK] or [MASK] ejected from a disintegrating atomic nucleus.

fusedkidney.name: fused kidney
fusedkidney.definition: Fused kidney is congenital fusion of two kidneys.

immunoglobuling.name: immunoglobulin g
immunoglobuling.definition: Immunoglobulin g is the major immunoglobulin isotype class in normal human serum. There are several isotype subclasses of IgG, for example, IgG1, IgG2A, and IgG2B.

pleuraleffusion.name: pleural effusion
pleuraleffusion.definition: Pleural effusion is presence of fluid in the pleural cavity resulting from excessive transudation or exudation from the pleural surfaces. It is a sign of disease and not a diagnosis in itself.

lasertherapy.name: laser therapy
lasertherapy.definition: Laser therapy is the use of photothermal effects of lasers to coagulate, incise, vaporize, resect, dissect, or resurface tissue.

socialjustice.name: social justice
socialjustice.definition: Social justice is an interactive process whereby members of a community are concerned for the equality and rights of all.

immunoglobulinconstantregions.name: immunoglobulin constant regions
immunoglobulinconstantregions.definition: Immunoglobulin constant regions is the domains of the immunoglobulin molecules that are invariable in their amino acid sequence within any class or subclass of immunoglobulin. They confer biological as well as structural functions to immunoglobulins. One each on both the light chains and the heavy chains comprises the C-terminus half of the immunoglobulin fab fragment and two or three of them make up the rest of the heavy chains (all of the [MASK])

histology,comparative.name: histology , comparative
histology,comparative.definition: Comparative histology is the study of the similarities and differences in the structures of homologous tissues across various species.

respiration.name: respiration
respiration.definition: Respiration is the act of breathing with the lungs, consisting of [MASK], or the taking into the lungs of the ambient air, and of exhalation, or the expelling of the modified air which contains more carbon dioxide than the air taken in (Blakiston's Gould Medical Dictionary, 4th ed.). This does not include tissue respiration (= oxygen consumption) or cell respiration (= cell respiration).

creatine.name: creatine
creatine.definition: Creatine is an amino acid that occurs in vertebrate tissues and in urine. In muscle tissue, creatine generally occurs as phosphocreatine. Creatine is excreted as creatinine in the urine.

worldhealthorganization.name: world health organization
worldhealthorganization.definition: [MASK] organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations designed as a coordinating authority on [MASK] work; its aim is to promote the attainment of the highest possible level of health by all peoples.

bacterialoutermembraneproteins.name: bacterial outer membrane proteins
bacterialoutermembraneproteins.definition: [MASK] proteins is proteins isolated from the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria.

coordinationcomplexes.name: coordination complexes
coordinationcomplexes.definition: Coordination complexes is neutral or negatively charged ligands bonded to metal cations or neutral atoms. The number of ligand atoms to which the metal center is directly bonded is the metal cation's coordination number, and this number is always greater than the regular valence or oxidation number of the metal. a coordination complex can be negative, neutral, or positively charged.

sensationdisorders.name: sensation disorders
sensationdisorders.definition: Sensation disorders is disorders of the special senses (i.e., vision; hearing; taste; and smell) or somatosensory system (i.e., afferent components of the peripheral nervous system).

bodilysecretions.name: bodily secretions
bodilysecretions.definition: Bodily secretions is endogenous substances produced through the activity of intact cells of glands, tissues, or organs.

newengland.name: new england
newengland.definition: New england is the geographic area of New England in general and when the specific state or states are not indicated. States usually included in this region are Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Rhode Island.

receptoraggregation.name: receptor aggregation
receptoraggregation.definition: Receptor aggregation is chemically stimulated aggregation of cell surface receptors, which potentiates the action of the effector cell.

materialsafetydatasheets.name: material safety data sheets
materialsafetydatasheets.definition: Material safety data sheets is information or data used to ensure the safe handling and disposal of substances in the workplace. Such information includes physical properties (i.e. melting, boiling, flashing points), as well as data on toxicity, health effects, reactivity, storage, disposal, [MASK], protective equipment, and spill-handling procedures.

deathcertificates.name: death certificates
deathcertificates.definition: Death certificates is official records of individual deaths including the [MASK] certified by a physician, and any other required identifying information.

enzymeassays.name: enzyme assays
enzymeassays.definition: Enzyme assays is methods used to measure the relative activity of a specific enzyme or its concentration in solution. Typically an enzyme substrate is added to a [MASK] solution containing enzyme and the rate of conversion of substrate to product is measured under controlled conditions. Many classical enzymatic assay methods involve the use of synthetic colorimetric substrates and measuring the reaction rates using a spectrophotometer.

tooth.name: tooth
tooth.definition: Tooth is one of a [MASK] of bone-like structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing.

pharmaceuticalservices,online.name: pharmaceutical services , online
pharmaceuticalservices,online.definition: Online pharmaceutical services is pharmacy services accessed via electronic means.

esophagealcyst.name: esophageal cyst
esophagealcyst.definition: Esophageal cyst is any fluid-filled closed cavity or sac (cysts) that is lined by an epithelium and found in the esophagus region.

scalp.name: scalp
scalp.definition: Scalp is the outer covering of the calvaria. It is composed of several layers: skin; subcutaneous connective tissue; the occipitofrontal muscle which includes the tendinous galea aponeurotica; loose connective tissue; and the pericranium (the periosteum of the skull).

psychotherapy.name: psychotherapy
psychotherapy.definition: Psychotherapy is a generic term for the treatment of mental illness or emotional disturbances primarily by verbal or nonverbal communication.

fatsubstitutes.name: fat substitutes
fatsubstitutes.definition: Fat substitutes is compounds used in food or in food preparation to replace dietary fats. They may be carbohydrate-, protein-, or fat-based. Fat substitutes are usually lower in calories but provide the same texture as fats.

waistcircumference.name: waist circumference
waistcircumference.definition: Waist circumference is the measurement around the body at the level of the abdomen and just above the [MASK]. The measurement is usually taken immediately after exhalation.

glycemicload.name: glycemic load
glycemicload.definition: Glycemic load is a quantitative value of a measured amount of a specific food that is equal to the glycemic index of that food multiplied by the carbohydrate content of that food.

radiologydepartment,hospital.name: radiology department , hospital
radiologydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital radiology department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration and provision of x-ray diagnostic and therapeutic services.

weildisease.name: weil disease
weildisease.definition: Weil disease is a severe form of leptospirosis, usually caused by leptospira interrogans serovar icterohaemorrhagiae and occasionally other serovars. It is transmitted to humans by the rat and is characterized by hemorrhagic and renal symptoms with accompanying jaundice.

hernia,abdominal.name: hernia , abdominal
hernia,abdominal.definition: Abdominal hernia is a protrusion of abdominal structures through the retaining [MASK]. It involves two parts: an opening in the [MASK], and a hernia sac consisting of peritoneum and abdominal contents. Abdominal hernias include groin hernia (hernia, femoral; [MASK]) and ventral hernia.

replicationorigin.name: replication origin
replicationorigin.definition: Replication origin is a unique dna sequence of a replicon at which dna replication is initiated and proceeds bidirectionally or unidirectionally. It contains the sites where the first separation of the complementary strands occurs, a primer rna is synthesized, and the switch from primer rna to dna synthesis takes place. (Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

tuberculosis,cardiovascular.name: tuberculosis , cardiovascular
tuberculosis,cardiovascular.definition: Cardiovascular tuberculosis is pathological conditions of the cardiovascular system caused by infection of [MASK]. Tuberculosis involvement may include the heart; the blood vessels; or the pericardium.

nervegrowthfactor.name: nerve growth factor
nervegrowthfactor.definition: Nerve growth factor is nerve growth factor is the first of a series of neurotrophic factors that were found to influence the growth and differentiation of sympathetic and sensory neurons. It is comprised of alpha, beta, and gamma subunits. The beta subunit is responsible for its growth stimulating activity.

heartvalveprosthesisimplantation.name: heart valve prosthesis implantation
heartvalveprosthesisimplantation.definition: Heart valve prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of synthetic material to repair injured or diseased heart valves.

herpessimplexvirusvaccines.name: herpes simplex virus vaccines
herpessimplexvirusvaccines.definition: Herpes simplex virus vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with viruses from the genus simplexvirus. This includes vaccines for hsv-1 and hsv-2.

abortion,missed.name: abortion , missed
abortion,missed.definition: Missed abortion is the retention in the uterus of a dead fetus two months or more after its death.

histidinekinase.name: histidine kinase
histidinekinase.definition: Histidine kinase is a member of the transferase superfamily of proteins. In the activated state, protein-histidine kinase autophosphorylates at a histidine residue, subsequently transferring high-energy phosphoryl groups to an aspartate residue of the response-regulator domain, which results in a conformational shift in the effector domain. Histidine kinases mediate signal transduction in a wide range of processes involving cellular adaptation to environmental stress.

lipidaccumulationproduct.name: lipid accumulation product
lipidaccumulationproduct.definition: Lipid accumulation product is an index for monitoring the accumulation of lipids based on the waist circumference measurement and the level of triglycerides circulating in the blood.

rna,heterogeneousnuclear.name: rna , heterogeneous nuclear
rna,heterogeneousnuclear.definition: Heterogeneous nuclear rna is nuclear nonribosomal rna larger than about 1000 nucleotides, the mass of which is rapidly synthesized and degraded within the cell nucleus. Some heterogeneous nuclear rna may be a precursor to mRNA. However, the great bulk of total hnRNA hybridizes with nuclear dna rather than with mRNA.

centralnervoussystemvascularmalformation.name: central nervous system vascular malformations
centralnervoussystemvascularmalformation.definition: Central nervous system vascular malformations is congenital, inherited, or acquired abnormalities involving arteries; veins; or venous sinuses in the brain; spinal cord; and meninges.

vocationaleducation.name: vocational education
vocationaleducation.definition: Vocational education is education that prepares the student for a specific trade such as plumbing, masonry, and carpentry.

bloodcomponentremoval.name: blood component removal
bloodcomponentremoval.definition: Blood component removal is any procedure in which blood is withdrawn from a donor, a portion is separated and retained, at the same time the remainder is returned to the donor.

foodcontamination.name: food contamination
foodcontamination.definition: Food contamination is the presence in food of harmful, unpalatable, or otherwise objectionable foreign substances, e.g. chemicals, microorganisms or diluents, before, during, or after processing or storage.

rnaviruses.name: rna viruses
rnaviruses.definition: Rna viruses is viruses whose genetic material is rna.

fungalstructures.name: fungal structures
fungalstructures.definition: Fungal structures is the parts of fungi.

serotoninagents.name: serotonin agents
serotoninagents.definition: Serotonin agents is drugs used for their effects on serotonergic systems. Among these are drugs that affect serotonin receptors, the [MASK] of serotonin, and the survival of serotonergic neurons.

coronarystenosis.name: coronary stenosis
coronarystenosis.definition: Coronary stenosis is narrowing or constriction of a coronary artery.

unitedstatesgovernmentagencies.name: united states government agencies
unitedstatesgovernmentagencies.definition: United states government agencies is agencies of the federal government of the United States.

steam.name: steam
steam.definition: Steam is water in its gaseous state. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

extracellularvesicles.name: extracellular vesicles
extracellularvesicles.definition: Extracellular vesicles is membrane limited structures derived from cell membranes and cytoplasmic material, and released into extracellular space. They circulate through the extracellular fluid and through the peripheral blood in the microvasculature where cells, much larger, cannot, thereby affecting a variety of intercellular communication processes.

reversegenetics.name: reverse genetics
reversegenetics.definition: Reverse genetics is the use of techniques that produce a functional mutation or an effect on gene expression of a specific gene of interest in order to identify the role or activity of the gene product of that gene.

urinarybladderdiseases.name: urinary bladder diseases
urinarybladderdiseases.definition: [MASK] diseases is pathological processes of the [MASK].

carboxylicacids.name: carboxylic acids
carboxylicacids.definition: Carboxylic acids is organic compounds containing the carboxy group (-cooh). This group of compounds includes amino acids and fatty acids. Carboxylic acids can be saturated, unsaturated, or aromatic.

lysosomalstoragediseases,nervoussystem.name: lysosomal storage diseases , nervous system
lysosomalstoragediseases,nervoussystem.definition: Nervous system lysosomal storage diseases is a group of enzymatic disorders affecting the nervous system and to a variable degree the skeletal system, lymphoreticular system, and other organs. The conditions are marked by an abnormal accumulation of catabolic material within lysosomes.

bluecrossblueshieldinsuranceplans.name: blue cross blue shield insurance plans
bluecrossblueshieldinsuranceplans.definition: Blue cross blue shield insurance plans is prepaid health and hospital insurance plan.

genes,plant.name: genes , plant
genes,plant.definition: Plant genes is the functional hereditary units of plants.

romanworld.name: roman world
romanworld.definition: Roman world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across a wide geographical area under the political domination and influence of ancient Rome, bringing to the conquered people the Roman civilization and culture from 753 b.c. to the beginning of the imperial rule under Augustus in 27 b.c. The early city built on seven hills grew to conquer Sicily, Sardinia, Carthage, Gaul, [MASK], Britain, Greece, Asia Minor, etc., and extended ultimately from Mesopotamia to the Atlantic. Roman medicine was almost entirely in Greek hands, but Rome, with its superior water system, remains a model of sanitation and hygiene. (From a. Castiglioni, a [MASK], 2d ed pp196-99; from f. h. Garrison, An Introduction to the [MASK], 4th ed, pp107-120)

drugcosts.name: drug costs
drugcosts.definition: Drug costs is the amount that a health care institution or organization pays for its drugs. It is one component of the final price that is charged to the consumer (fees, pharmaceutical or [MASK]).

bacillus.name: bacillus
bacillus.definition: Bacillus is a genus of bacillaceae that are spore-forming, rod-shaped cells. Most species are saprophytic soil forms with only a few species being pathogenic.

persistentfetalcirculationsyndrome.name: persistent fetal circulation syndrome
persistentfetalcirculationsyndrome.definition: Persistent fetal circulation syndrome is a syndrome of persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn infant (infant, newborn) without demonstrable heart diseases. This neonatal condition can be caused by severe pulmonary vasoconstriction (reactive type), hypertrophy of pulmonary arterial muscle (hypertrophic type), or abnormally developed pulmonary arterioles (hypoplastic type). The newborn patient exhibits cyanosis and acidosis due to the persistence of fetal circulatory pattern of right-to-left shunting of blood through a patent ductus arteriosus (ductus arteriosus, patent) and at times a patent foramen ovale (foramen ovale, patent).

hygienehypothesis.name: hygiene hypothesis
hygienehypothesis.definition: Hygiene hypothesis is the theory that infectious agents, symbiotic microorganisms, and parasites are normal stimulants for the maturation of the immune system toward a balanced immune response. The theory predicts that lack of such stimulation leads to allergies and autoimmune diseases.

adenoma.name: adenoma
adenoma.definition: Adenoma is a benign epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

goatdiseases.name: goat diseases
goatdiseases.definition: Goat diseases is diseases of the domestic or wild goat of the genus Capra.

facialneoplasms.name: facial neoplasms
facialneoplasms.definition: Facial neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the face.

advisorycommittees.name: advisory committees
advisorycommittees.definition: Advisory committees is groups [MASK] up to advise governmental bodies, societies, or other institutions on policy. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

lacticacid.name: lactic acid
lacticacid.definition: Lactic acid is a normal intermediate in the fermentation (oxidation, metabolism) of sugar. The concentrated form is used internally to prevent gastrointestinal fermentation. (From Stedman, 26th ed)

caspase8.name: caspase 8
caspase8.definition: Caspase 8 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a [MASK] in its pro-domain region. Caspase 8 plays a role in apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases. Activation of this enzyme can occur via the interaction of its N-terminal [MASK] with death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins.

spleen.name: spleen
spleen.definition: Spleen is an encapsulated lymphatic organ through which venous blood filters.

nationalhealthprograms.name: national health programs
nationalhealthprograms.definition: National health programs is components of a national health care system which administer specific services, e.g., national health insurance.

hernia,ventral.name: hernia , ventral
hernia,ventral.definition: Ventral hernia is a hernia caused by weakness of the anterior [MASK] due to midline defects, previous incisions, or increased intra-abdominal pressure. Ventral hernias include umbilical hernia, incisional, epigastric, and spigelian hernias.

spinalcanal.name: spinal canal
spinalcanal.definition: Spinal canal is the cavity within the spinal column through which the spinal cord passes.

squamouscellcarcinomaofheadandneck.name: squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck
squamouscellcarcinomaofheadandneck.definition: Squamous cell carcinoma of head and [MASK] is the most common type of head and [MASK] carcinoma that originates from cells on the surface of the nasal cavity; mouth; paranasal sinuses, salivary glands, and larynx. Mutations in tnfrsf10b, pten, and ing1 genes are associated with this cancer.

immunoglobulinfragments.name: immunoglobulin fragments
immunoglobulinfragments.definition: Immunoglobulin fragments is partial immunoglobulin molecules resulting from selective cleavage by proteolytic enzymes or generated through protein engineering techniques.

toothpreparation.name: tooth preparation
toothpreparation.definition: Tooth preparation is procedures carried out with regard to the teeth or tooth structures preparatory to specified dental therapeutic and surgical measures.

littersize.name: litter size
littersize.definition: Litter size is the number of offspring produced at one birth by a viviparous animal.

ethnicviolence.name: ethnic violence
ethnicviolence.definition: Ethnic violence is violence or other hostile behavior arising when an ethnic group either feels itself under threat, or where it seeks to assert its superiority or dominance over other groups.

seedstorageproteins.name: seed storage proteins
seedstorageproteins.definition: [MASK] storage proteins is one or more types of plant [MASK] proteins providing the large amounts of amino acids utilized in germination and seedling growth. As [MASK] are the major food source from agricultural crops, [MASK] storage proteins are a major source of dietary proteins.

poultrydiseases.name: poultry diseases
poultrydiseases.definition: Poultry diseases is diseases of birds which are raised as a source of meat or eggs for human consumption and are usually found in barnyards, hatcheries, etc. The concept is differentiated from bird diseases which is for diseases of birds not considered poultry and usually found in zoos, parks, and the wild.

rna,transfer,asn.name: rna , transfer , asn
rna,transfer,asn.definition: Asn transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying asparagine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

folatereceptor1.name: folate receptor 1
folatereceptor1.definition: Folate receptor 1 is a subtype of GPI-anchored folate receptors that is expressed in tissues of epithelial origin. This protein is also identified as an ovarian-tumor-specific antigen.

reinforcement,verbal.name: reinforcement , verbal
reinforcement,verbal.definition: Verbal reinforcement is use of word stimulus to strengthen a response during learning.

electricstimulationtherapy.name: electric stimulation therapy
electricstimulationtherapy.definition: Electric stimulation therapy is application of electric current in treatment without the generation of perceptible heat. It includes electric stimulation of nerves or muscles, passage of current into the body, or use of interrupted current of low intensity to raise the detection threshold of the skin to pain.

entericnervoussystem.name: enteric nervous system
entericnervoussystem.definition: Enteric nervous system is two ganglionated neural plexuses in the gut wall which form one of the three major divisions of the autonomic nervous system. The enteric nervous system innervates the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas, and the gallbladder. It contains sensory neurons, interneurons, and motor neurons. Thus the circuitry can autonomously sense the tension and the chemical environment in the gut and regulate blood vessel tone, motility, secretions, and fluid transport. The system is itself governed by the central nervous system and receives both parasympathetic and sympathetic innervation. (From Kandel, Schwartz, and Jessel, Principles of Neural Science, 3d ed, p766)

oregon.name: oregon
oregon.definition: Oregon is state bounded on the north by [MASK], on the east by Idaho, on the south by California and Nevada, and on the west by the Pacific Ocean.

nickel.name: nickel
nickel.definition: Nickel is a trace element with the atomic symbol Ni, atomic number 28, and atomic weight 58.69. It is a cofactor of the enzyme urease.

jcvirus.name: jc virus
jcvirus.definition: Jc virus is a species of polyomavirus, originally isolated from the brain of a patient with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. The patient's initials j.c. gave the virus its name. Infection is not accompanied by any apparent illness but serious demyelinating disease can appear later, probably following reactivation of latent virus.

hormonereplacementtherapy.name: hormone replacement therapy
hormonereplacementtherapy.definition: Hormone replacement therapy is therapeutic use of hormones to alleviate the effects of hormone deficiency.

transplantation,homologous.name: transplantation , homologous
transplantation,homologous.definition: Homologous transplantation is transplantation between individuals of the same species. Usually refers to genetically disparate individuals in contradistinction to isogeneic transplantation for genetically identical individuals.

geneexpressionregulation,developmental.name: gene expression regulation , developmental
geneexpressionregulation,developmental.definition: [MASK] expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action during the developmental stages of an organism.

fetalheart.name: fetal heart
fetalheart.definition: Fetal heart is the heart of the fetus of any viviparous animal. It refers to the heart in the postembryonic period and is differentiated from the embryonic heart (HEART/embryology) only on the basis of time.

receptors,ephfamily.name: receptors , eph family
receptors,ephfamily.definition: Eph family receptors is a large family of receptor protein-tyrosine kinases that are structurally-related. The name of this family of proteins derives from original protein Eph (now called the epha1 receptor), which was named after the cell line it was first discovered in: Erythropoietin-Producing human Hepatocellular carcinoma cell line. Members of this family have been implicated in regulation of cell-cell interactions involved in nervous system patterning and development.

stomachrupture.name: stomach rupture
stomachrupture.definition: Stomach rupture is bursting of the stomach.

transfusionmedicine.name: transfusion medicine
transfusionmedicine.definition: Transfusion medicine is the area of hematology that is concerned with the transfusion of blood and blood components, and in prevention and treatment of adverse effects from blood transfusion errors.

eye,artificial.name: eye , artificial
eye,artificial.definition: Artificial eye is a ready-made or custom-made prosthesis of glass or plastic shaped and colored to resemble the anterior portion of a normal eye and used for cosmetic reasons. It is attached to the anterior portion of an orbital implant (orbital implants) which is placed in the socket of an enucleated or eviscerated eye. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

constructionmaterials.name: construction materials
constructionmaterials.definition: Construction materials is supplies used in building.

arthritis,rheumatoid.name: arthritis , rheumatoid
arthritis,rheumatoid.definition: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic systemic disease, primarily of the joints, marked by inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures, widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, and by atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures. Etiology is unknown, but autoimmune mechanisms have been implicated.

solutecarrierfamily22member5.name: solute carrier family 22 member 5
solutecarrierfamily22member5.definition: Solute carrier family 22 member 5 is a high-affinity, ATP-binding, co-transporter for carnitine that is highly expressed in kidney, skeletal muscle, heart, and placental tissues. It transports one sodium ion with one carnitine molecule. It has a lower affinity for other organic cations and transports them independently of sodium. Mutations in the slc22a5 gene are associated with systemic carnitine deficiency.

nitritereductase(nad(p)h).name: nitrite reductase ( nad ( p ) h )
nitritereductase(nad(p)h).definition: Nitrite reductase (nad (p) h) is an enzyme found primarily in bacteria and fungi that catalyzes the oxidation of ammonium hydroxide to nitrite. It is an iron-sulfur heme; flavoprotein containing siroheme and can utilize both NAD and NADP as cofactors.

sagittalabdominaldiameter.name: sagittal abdominal diameter
sagittalabdominaldiameter.definition: Sagittal abdominal diameter is the height of the abdomen as measured in the [MASK].

prenatalinjuries.name: prenatal injuries
prenatalinjuries.definition: Prenatal injuries is damages to the embryo, mammalian or the fetus before birth. Damages can be caused by any factors including biological, chemical, or physical.

extremeheat.name: extreme heat
extremeheat.definition: Extreme heat is high temperature weather exceeding the average and of several weeks duration. Extreme heat is a dangerous situation that can bring on health emergencies in susceptible people.

serumalbumin,human.name: serum albumin , human
serumalbumin,human.definition: Human serum albumin is serum albumin from humans. It is an essential carrier of both endogenous substances, such as fatty acids and bilirubin, and of xenobitoics in the blood.

cholinergicneurons.name: cholinergic neurons
cholinergicneurons.definition: Cholinergic neurons is neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is acetylcholine.

gabauptakeinhibitors.name: gaba uptake inhibitors
gabauptakeinhibitors.definition: Gaba uptake inhibitors is compounds that suppress or block the plasma membrane transport of gamma-aminobutyric acid by gaba plasma membrane transport proteins.

birthrate.name: birth rate
birthrate.definition: Birth rate is the number of births in a given population per year or other unit of time.

lensnucleus,crystalline.name: lens nucleus , crystalline
lensnucleus,crystalline.definition: Crystalline lens nucleus is the core of the crystalline lens, surrounded by the cortex.

emergencymedicalservices.name: emergency medical services
emergencymedicalservices.definition: Emergency medical services is services specifically designed, staffed, and equipped for the emergency care of patients.

cellextracts.name: cell extracts
cellextracts.definition: Cell extracts is preparations of cell constituents or subcellular materials, isolates, or substances.

physicalexamination.name: physical examination
physicalexamination.definition: Physical examination is systematic and thorough inspection of the patient for physical signs of disease or abnormality.

nervedegeneration.name: nerve degeneration
nervedegeneration.definition: Nerve degeneration is loss of functional activity and trophic degeneration of nerve axons and their terminal arborizations following the destruction of their cells of origin or interruption of their continuity with these cells. The pathology is characteristic of neurodegenerative diseases. Often the process of nerve degeneration is studied in research on neuroanatomical localization and correlation of the neurophysiology of neural pathways.

impulsivebehavior.name: impulsive behavior
impulsivebehavior.definition: Impulsive behavior is an act performed without delay, reflection, voluntary direction or obvious control in response to a stimulus.

potentiallyinappropriatemedicationlist.name: potentially inappropriate medication list
potentiallyinappropriatemedicationlist.definition: Potentially inappropriate medication list is a list, criteria, or screening tool designed to improve patient safety by determining an individual's exposure to potentially inappropriate drugs. They are designed to prevent medication errors by inappropriate prescribing. Analysis for a list includes factors such as dose-response relationship, drug; drug-related side effects and adverse reactions; age factors; gender; and existing medical conditions.

genderidentity.name: gender identity
genderidentity.definition: Gender identity is a person's concept of self as being male and masculine or female and feminine, or ambivalent, based in part on physical characteristics, parental responses, and psychological and social pressures. It is the internal experience of gender role.

dnarepair.name: dna repair
dnarepair.definition: Dna repair is the reconstruction of a continuous two-stranded dna molecule without mismatch from a molecule which contained damaged regions. The major repair mechanisms are excision repair, in which defective regions in one strand are excised and resynthesized using the complementary [MASK] information in the intact strand; photoreactivation repair, in which the lethal and mutagenic effects of ultraviolet light are eliminated; and post-replication repair, in which the primary lesions are not repaired, but the gaps in one daughter duplex are filled in by incorporation of portions of the other (undamaged) daughter duplex. Excision repair and post-replication repair are sometimes referred to as "dark repair" because they do not require light.

healthcaredisparities.name: healthcare disparities
healthcaredisparities.definition: Healthcare disparities is differences in access to or availability of medical facilities and services.

walkingspeed.name: walking speed
walkingspeed.definition: Walking speed is the rate at which steps are made while walking.

sensoryaids.name: sensory aids
sensoryaids.definition: Sensory aids is devices that help people with impaired sensory responses.

myelinproteins.name: myelin proteins
myelinproteins.definition: Myelin proteins is mYELIN-specific proteins that play a structural or regulatory role in the genesis and maintenance of the lamellar myelin sheath structure.

spermhead.name: sperm head
spermhead.definition: Sperm head is the anterior portion of the spermatozoon (spermatozoa) that contains mainly the nucleus with highly compact chromatin material.

peru.name: peru
peru.definition: Peru is a country in western South America, bordering the South Pacific Ocean, and located between [MASK] and Ecuador.

cells.name: cells
cells.definition: Cells is the fundamental, structural, and functional units or subunits of living organisms. They are composed of cytoplasm containing various organelles and a cell membrane boundary.

education,professional.name: education , professional
education,professional.definition: Professional education is formal education and training in preparation for the practice of a profession.

cochlearduct.name: cochlear duct
cochlearduct.definition: Cochlear duct is a spiral tube that is firmly suspended in the bony shell-shaped part of the cochlea. This ENDOLYMPH-filled cochlear duct begins at the vestibule and makes 2.5 turns around a core of spongy bone (the modiolus) thus dividing the PERILYMPH-filled spiral canal into two channels, the scala vestibuli and the scala tympani.

ethics,pharmacy.name: ethics , pharmacy
ethics,pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the pharmacist, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the pharmacist in health care and interpersonal relations with patient families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

plantproteins.name: plant proteins
plantproteins.definition: Plant proteins is proteins found in plants (flowers, herbs, shrubs, trees, etc.). The concept does not include proteins found in vegetables for which plant proteins, dietary is available.

urethralneoplasms.name: urethral neoplasms
urethralneoplasms.definition: Urethral neoplasms is cancer or tumors of the urethra. Benign epithelial tumors of the urethra usually consist of squamous and transitional cells. Primary urethral carcinomas are rare and typically of squamous cells. Urethral carcinoma is the only urological malignancy that is more common in females than in males.

dentalhealthsurveys.name: dental health surveys
dentalhealthsurveys.definition: Dental health surveys is a systematic collection of factual data pertaining to dental or [MASK] and disease in a human population within a given geographic area.

anklejoint.name: ankle joint
anklejoint.definition: Ankle joint is the joint that is formed by the inferior articular and malleolar articular surfaces of the tibia; the malleolar articular surface of the fibula; and the medial malleolar, lateral malleolar, and superior surfaces of the talus.

oantigens.name: o antigens
oantigens.definition: O antigens is the lipopolysaccharide-protein somatic antigens, usually from gram-negative bacteria, important in the serological classification of enteric bacilli. The O-specific chains determine the specificity of the o antigens of a given serotype. o antigens are the immunodominant part of the lipopolysaccharide molecule in the intact bacterial cell. (From Singleton & Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

regression,psychology.name: regression , psychology
regression,psychology.definition: Psychology regression is a return to earlier, especially to infantile, patterns of thought or behavior, or stage of functioning, e.g., feelings of helplessness and dependency in a patient with a serious physical illness. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994).

medicalrecordlinkage.name: medical record linkage
medicalrecordlinkage.definition: Medical record linkage is the creation and maintenance of medical and vital records in multiple institutions in a manner that will facilitate the combined use of the records of identified individuals.

giantcelltumors.name: giant cell tumors
giantcelltumors.definition: Giant cell tumors is tumors of bone tissue or synovial or other soft tissue characterized by the presence of giant cells. The most common are [MASK] and giant cell tumor of bone.

materialsscience.name: materials science
materialsscience.definition: Materials science is an interdisciplinary study of the microstructure and composition of various materials such as metals, semiconductors, ceramics, and polymers, in relation to their macromolecular physical and chemical properties. Materials science enables the custom creation of new materials with specific properties and uses.

intensepulsedlighttherapy.name: intense pulsed light therapy
intensepulsedlighttherapy.definition: Intense pulsed light therapy is treatment of the skin with flashlamps of prescribed wavelengths, fluence, and pulse durations which target specific chromophores to induce photothermolysis at specific locations in the skin such as at the hair follicle or spider veins.

orthopedicprocedures.name: orthopedic procedures
orthopedicprocedures.definition: Orthopedic procedures is procedures used to treat and correct deformities, diseases, and injuries to the musculoskeletal system, its articulations, and associated structures.

diarrheaviruses,bovineviral.name: diarrhea viruses , bovine viral
diarrheaviruses,bovineviral.definition: Bovine viral [MASK] viruses is a group of viruses in the genus pestivirus, causing [MASK], fever, oral ulcerations, hemorrhagic syndrome, and various necrotic lesions among cattle and other domestic animals. The two species (genotypes), [MASK] and [MASK] , exhibit antigenic and pathological differences. The historical designation, bvdv, consisted of both (then unrecognized) genotypes.

proteinphosphatase2.name: protein phosphatase 2
proteinphosphatase2.definition: Protein phosphatase 2 is a phosphoprotein phosphatase subtype that is comprised of a [MASK] and two different regulatory subunits. At least two genes encode isoforms of the protein phosphatase [MASK], while several isoforms of regulatory subunits exist due to the presence of multiple genes and the [MASK] of their mRNAs. Protein phosphatase 2 acts on a broad variety of cellular proteins and may play a role as a regulator of intracellular signaling processes.

animalfur.name: animal fur
animalfur.definition: Animal fur is usually densely-packed hairs on the skin of mammals.

human.name: human
human.definition: Human is members of the species Homo sapiens.

technology,dental.name: technology , dental
technology,dental.definition: Dental technology is the field of dentistry involved in procedures for designing and constructing dental appliances. It includes also the application of any technology to the field of dentistry.

bipolarandrelateddisorders.name: bipolar and related disorders
bipolarandrelateddisorders.definition: Bipolar and related disorders is these disorders are related to both schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders and depressive disorder in terms of symptomatology, family history, and genetics. (dsm-5).

genome,chloroplast.name: genome , chloroplast
genome,chloroplast.definition: Chloroplast genome is the genetic complement of chloroplasts as represented in their dna.

animalexperimentation.name: animal experimentation
animalexperimentation.definition: Animal experimentation is the use of animals as investigational subjects.

unilateralbreastneoplasms.name: unilateral breast neoplasms
unilateralbreastneoplasms.definition: Unilateral breast neoplasms is tumors or cancer found specifically in one human breast, but not in both.

aquaculture.name: aquaculture
aquaculture.definition: Aquaculture is cultivation of natural faunal resources of water. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

glomerularfiltrationbarrier.name: glomerular filtration barrier
glomerularfiltrationbarrier.definition: Glomerular filtration barrier is a specialized barrier in the kidney, consisting of the fenestrated capillary endothelium; [MASK]; and glomerular epithelium (podocytes). The barrier prevents the filtration of plasma proteins.

surgicalprocedures,operative.name: surgical procedures , operative
surgicalprocedures,operative.definition: Operative surgical procedures is operations carried out for the correction of deformities and defects, repair of injuries, and diagnosis and cure of certain diseases. (Taber, 18th ed.)

religionandmedicine.name: religion and medicine
religionandmedicine.definition: Religion and medicine is the interrelationship of medicine and religion.

sand.name: sand
sand.definition: Sand is a hard granular material that is a component of soil. It is composed of very small pieces (between 0.06 and 2.0 millimeters in diameter) of disintegrating rock.

casemanagers.name: case managers
casemanagers.definition: Case managers is professionals who are in charge of assessment, planning, facilitation, care coordination, evaluation, and advocacy for options and services to meet a patient’s and family’s comprehensive health needs.

metals,light.name: metals , light
metals,light.definition: Light metals is metals with low specific gravity, typically smaller than 5, characterized by a single valence (1, 2, or 3), a simple spectrum, strong electromotive force (positive), and colorless compounds. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

culturalcompetency.name: cultural competency
culturalcompetency.definition: Cultural competency is cultural and linguistic competence is a [MASK] of congruent behaviors, attitudes, and policies that come together in a system, agency, or among professionals that enables effective work in cross-cultural situations. Competence implies the capacity to function effectively as an individual and an organization within the context of the cultural beliefs, behaviors, and needs presented by consumers and their communities.

clinicaltrialsdatamonitoringcommittees.name: clinical trials data monitoring committees
clinicaltrialsdatamonitoringcommittees.definition: Clinical trials data monitoring committees is committees established to review interim data and efficacy outcomes in clinical trials. The findings of these committees are used in deciding whether a trial should be continued as designed, changed, or terminated. Government regulations regarding federally-funded research involving human subjects (the "Common Rule") require (45 cfr 46.111) that research ethics committees reviewing large-scale clinical trials monitor the data collected using a mechanism such as a data monitoring committee. fda regulations (21 cfr 50.24) require that such committees be established to monitor studies conducted in emergency settings.

electricalequipmentandsupplies.name: electrical equipment and supplies
electricalequipmentandsupplies.definition: Electrical equipment and supplies is apparatus and instruments that generate and operate with electricity, and their electrical components.

livertransplantation.name: liver transplantation
livertransplantation.definition: Liver transplantation is the transference of a part of or an entire liver from one human or animal to another.

heartseptaldefects,ventricular.name: heart septal defects , ventricular
heartseptaldefects,ventricular.definition: Ventricular heart septal defects is developmental abnormalities in any portion of the ventricular septum resulting in abnormal communications between the two lower chambers of the heart. Classification of ventricular septal defects is based on location of the communication, such as perimembranous, inlet, outlet (infundibular), central muscular, marginal muscular, or apical muscular defect.

smartglasses.name: smart glasses
smartglasses.definition: Smart glasses is computerized eyewear with multiple technological applications for advanced computing and interoperability. Smart glasses are optimized to facilitate information and data access, capture, display, transfer, and manipulation.

coronarysinus.name: coronary sinus
coronarysinus.definition: Coronary sinus is a short vein that collects about two thirds of the venous blood from the myocardium and drains into the right atrium. Coronary sinus, normally located between the left atrium and left ventricle on the posterior surface of the heart, can serve as an anatomical reference for cardiac procedures.

immunoglobulinlightchains.name: immunoglobulin light chains
immunoglobulinlightchains.definition: Immunoglobulin light chains is polypeptide chains, consisting of 211 to 217 amino acid residues and having a molecular weight of approximately 22 kDa. There are two major types of light chains, kappa and lambda. Two Ig light chains and two [MASK] ([MASK]) make one immunoglobulin molecule.

familyleave.name: family leave
familyleave.definition: Family leave is the authorized absence from work of a family member to attend the illness or participate in the care of a parent, a sibling, or other family member. For the care of a parent for a child or for pre- or postnatal leave of a parent, parental leave is available.

phospholipasecgamma.name: phospholipase c gamma
phospholipasecgamma.definition: Phospholipase c gamma is a phosphoinositide phospholipase c subtype that is primarily regulated by protein-tyrosine kinases. It is structurally related to phospholipase c delta with the addition of src homology domains and pleckstrin homology domains located between two halves of the [MASK].

kidneycortex.name: kidney cortex
kidneycortex.definition: Kidney cortex is the outer zone of the kidney, beneath the capsule, consisting of kidney glomerulus; kidney tubules, distal; and kidney tubules, proximal.

estrogenreceptormodulators.name: estrogen receptor modulators
estrogenreceptormodulators.definition: Estrogen receptor modulators is substances that possess antiestrogenic actions but can also produce estrogenic effects as well. They act as complete or partial agonist or as antagonist. They can be either steroidal or nonsteroidal in structure.

semantics.name: semantics
semantics.definition: Semantics is the relationships between symbols and their meanings.

journalarticle.name: journal article
journalarticle.definition: Journal article is the predominant publication type for articles and other items indexed for nlm databases.

smokingcessationagents.name: smoking cessation agents
smokingcessationagents.definition: Smoking cessation agents is substances that facilitate the cessation of tobacco smoking.

egffamilyofproteins.name: egf family of proteins
egffamilyofproteins.definition: Egf family of proteins is a family of proteins that are related to epidermal growth factor. They share in common a [MASK] sequence consisting of six spatially conserved [MASK] residues which form three intramolecular bonds. This [MASK] sequence is commonly referred to egf motif and is considered essential for binding of the proteins to erb receptors.

privatepractice.name: private practice
privatepractice.definition: Private practice is practice of a health profession by an individual, offering services on a person-to-person basis, as opposed to group or partnership practice.

bodyregions.name: body regions
bodyregions.definition: Body regions is anatomical areas of the body.

receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,member14.name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 14
receptors,tumornecrosisfactor,member14.definition: Member 14 tumor necrosis factor receptors is a novel member of the tumor-necrosis factor receptor family that can also mediate herpes simplex virus type 1 entry into cells. It has specificity for [MASK] and the homotrimeric form of lymphotoxin-alpha. The receptor is abundantly expressed on t-lymphocytes and may play a role in regulating [MASK]. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

lasers.name: lasers
lasers.definition: Lasers is an optical source that emits [MASK] in a coherent beam. Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation (laser) is brought about using devices that transform light of varying frequencies into a single intense, nearly nondivergent beam of monochromatic radiation. Lasers operate in the infrared, visible, ultraviolet, or X-ray regions of the spectrum.

bonemarrowcells.name: bone marrow cells
bonemarrowcells.definition: Bone marrow cells is cells contained in the bone marrow including fat cells (see adipocytes); stromal cells; megakaryocytes; and the immediate precursors of most blood cells.

chlorideperoxidase.name: chloride peroxidase
chlorideperoxidase.definition: Chloride peroxidase is an enzyme that catalyzes the chlorination of a range of organic molecules, forming stable carbon-chloride bonds. ec 1.11.1.10.

genes,regulator.name: genes , regulator
genes,regulator.definition: Regulator genes is genes which regulate or circumscribe the activity of other genes; specifically, genes which code for proteins or RNAs which have gene expression regulation functions.

dentalcaries.name: dental caries
dentalcaries.definition: Dental caries is localized destruction of the tooth surface initiated by decalcification of the enamel followed by enzymatic lysis of organic structures and leading to cavity formation. If left unchecked, the cavity may penetrate the enamel and dentin and reach the pulp.

cervicalatlas.name: cervical atlas
cervicalatlas.definition: Cervical atlas is the first cervical vertebra.

researchreport.name: research report
researchreport.definition: Research report is detailed account or statement or formal record of data resulting from empirical inquiry.

work.name: work
work.definition: Work is productive or purposeful activities.

centralnervoussystemcysts.name: central nervous system cysts
centralnervoussystemcysts.definition: Central nervous system cysts is congenital or acquired cysts of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges which may remain stable in size or undergo progressive enlargement.

luminescence.name: luminescence
luminescence.definition: Luminescence is emission of light when [MASK] return to the electronic ground state from an excited state and lose the energy as [MASK]. It is sometimes called cool light in contrast to incandescence. luminescent measurements take advantage of this type of light emitted from luminescent agents.

braininjuries,diffuse.name: brain injuries , diffuse
braininjuries,diffuse.definition: Diffuse brain injuries is brain injuries occurring over a wide area instead of specific focal area.

lotqualityassurancesampling.name: lot quality assurance sampling
lotqualityassurancesampling.definition: Lot quality assurance sampling is a sampling methodology using small sample sizes when conducting surveys in small geographical or population-based areas or lots.

mediatorcomplexsubunit1.name: mediator complex subunit 1
mediatorcomplexsubunit1.definition: Mediator complex subunit 1 is a mediator complex subunit that is believed to play a key role in the coactivation of nuclear receptor-activated transcription by the mediator complex. It interacts with a variety of nuclear receptors including retinoic acid receptors; thyroid hormone receptors; vitamin d receptors; peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors; estrogen receptors; and [MASK].

adversechildhoodexperiences.name: adverse childhood experiences
adversechildhoodexperiences.definition: Adverse childhood experiences is deleterious experiences in first 18 years of life.

calciumfluoride.name: calcium fluoride
calciumfluoride.definition: Calcium fluoride is calcium fluoride. Occurring in nature as the mineral fluorite or fluorspar. It is the primary source of fluorine and its compounds. Pure calcium fluoride is used as a catalyst in [MASK] and dehydrogenation and is used to fluoridate drinking water. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

handling,psychological.name: handling , psychological
handling,psychological.definition: Psychological handling is physical manipulation of animals and humans to induce a behavioral or other psychological reaction. In [MASK], the animal is handled to induce a stress situation or to study the effects of "gentling" or "mothering".

growthdifferentiationfactor10.name: growth differentiation factor 10
growthdifferentiationfactor10.definition: Growth differentiation factor 10 is a growth differentiation factor that is closely-related in structure to bone morphogenetic protein 3. Growth differentiation factor 10 is found at high levels in bone, however it plays an additional roles in regulating embryonic development.

women.name: women
women.definition: Women is human females as cultural, psychological, sociological, political, and economic entities.

laboratories,dental.name: laboratories , dental
laboratories,dental.definition: Dental laboratories is facilities for the performance of services related to dental treatment but not done directly in the patient's mouth.

manganesepoisoning.name: manganese poisoning
manganesepoisoning.definition: [MASK] poisoning is [MASK] poisoning is associated with chronic [MASK] of [MASK] particles by individuals who work with [MASK] ore. Clinical features include confusion; hallucinations; and an extrapyramidal syndrome (parkinson disease, secondary) that includes rigidity; dystonia; retropulsion; and tremor. (Adams, Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1213)

aorticdiseases.name: aortic diseases
aorticdiseases.definition: Aortic diseases is pathological processes involving any part of the aorta.

tootherosion.name: tooth erosion
tootherosion.definition: Tooth erosion is progressive loss of the hard substance of a tooth by chemical processes that do not involve bacterial action. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p296)

eye.name: eye
eye.definition: Eye is the organ of sight constituting a pair of globular organs made up of a three-layered roughly spherical structure specialized for receiving and responding to light.

complementfixationtests.name: complement fixation tests
complementfixationtests.definition: Complement fixation tests is serologic tests based on inactivation of complement by the antigen-antibody complex (stage 1). Binding of free complement can be visualized by addition of a second antigen-antibody system such as red cells and appropriate red cell antibody (hemolysin) requiring complement for its completion (stage 2). Failure of the red cells to lyse indicates that a specific antigen-antibody reaction has taken place in stage 1. If red cells lyse, free complement is present indicating no antigen-antibody reaction occurred in stage 1.

attitudetodeath.name: attitude to death
attitudetodeath.definition: Attitude to death is conceptual response of the person to the various aspects of death, which are based on individual psychosocial and cultural experience.

cholesteroloxidase.name: cholesterol oxidase
cholesteroloxidase.definition: Cholesterol oxidase is an enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of cholesterol in the presence of molecular oxygen to 4-cholesten-3-one and hydrogen peroxide. The enzyme is not specific for cholesterol, but will also oxidize other 3-hydroxysteroids. ec 1.1.3.6.

honey.name: honey
honey.definition: Honey is a sweet viscous liquid food, produced in the honey sacs of various bees from nectar collected from flowers. The nectar is ripened into honey by inversion of its sucrose sugar into fructose and glucose. It is somewhat acidic and has mild antiseptic properties, being sometimes used in the treatment of burns and lacerations.

socialcapital.name: social capital
socialcapital.definition: Social capital is the expected benefits derived from the cooperation between individuals and groups.

mapkinasekinasekinase5.name: map kinase kinase kinase 5
mapkinasekinasekinase5.definition: Map kinase kinase kinase 5 is a 150-kDa map kinase kinase kinase that may play a role in the induction of apoptosis. It has specificity for map kinase kinase 3; map kinase kinase 4; and map kinase kinase 6.

eyeinfections,parasitic.name: eye infections , parasitic
eyeinfections,parasitic.definition: Parasitic eye infections is mild to severe infections of the eye and its adjacent structures (adnexa) by adult or larval protozoan or metazoan parasites.

receptors,arylhydrocarbon.name: receptors , aryl hydrocarbon
receptors,arylhydrocarbon.definition: Aryl hydrocarbon receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that bind certain aryl hydrocarbons, translocate to the nucleus, and activate transcription of particular dna segments. ah receptors are identified by their high-affinity binding to several carcinogenic or teratogenic environmental chemicals including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons found in [MASK] smoke and smog, heterocyclic amines found in cooked foods, and halogenated hydrocarbons including dioxins and polychlorinated biphenyls. No endogenous ligand has been identified, but an unknown natural messenger with a role in cell differentiation and development is suspected.

iggdeficiency.name: igg deficiency
iggdeficiency.definition: Igg deficiency is a dysgammaglobulinemia characterized by a deficiency of immunoglobulin g.

lesserpelvis.name: lesser pelvis
lesserpelvis.definition: Lesser pelvis is the part of the pelvis, inferior to the pelvic brim, that comprises both the pelvic cavity and the part of the perineum lying inferior to the [MASK].

nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member3.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 3
nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member3.definition: Member 3 group f nuclear receptor subfamily 1 is an orphan nuclear receptor found in the thymus where it plays a role in regulating the development and maturation of thymocytes. An isoform of this protein, referred to as RORgammaT, is produced by an alternatively transcribed mRNA.

spectrumanalysis,raman.name: spectrum analysis , raman
spectrumanalysis,raman.definition: Raman spectrum analysis is analysis of the intensity of Raman scattering of monochromatic light as a function of frequency of the scattered light.

amyloid.name: amyloid
amyloid.definition: Amyloid is a fibrous protein complex that consists of proteins folded into a specific cross beta-pleated sheet structure. This fibrillar structure has been found as an alternative folding pattern for a variety of functional proteins. Deposits of amyloid in the form of amyloid plaques are associated with a variety of degenerative diseases. The amyloid structure has also been found in a number of functional proteins that are unrelated to disease.

anionexchangeprotein1,erythrocyte.name: anion exchange protein 1 , erythrocyte
anionexchangeprotein1,erythrocyte.definition: Erythrocyte anion exchange protein 1 is a major integral transmembrane protein of the erythrocyte membrane. It is the anion exchanger responsible for electroneutral transporting in chloride ions in exchange of bicarbonate ions allowing co2 uptake and transport from tissues to lungs by the red blood cells. Genetic mutations that result in a loss of the protein function have been associated with type 4 hereditary spherocytosis.

relativebiologicaleffectiveness.name: relative biological effectiveness
relativebiologicaleffectiveness.definition: Relative biological effectiveness is the ratio of radiation dosages required to produce identical change based on a formula comparing other types of radiation with that of gamma or roentgen rays.

chemicalfractionation.name: chemical fractionation
chemicalfractionation.definition: Chemical fractionation is separation of a mixture in successive stages, each stage removing from the mixture some proportion of one of the substances, for example by differential solubility in water-solvent mixtures. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

france.name: france
france.definition: France is a country in western Europe bordered by the Atlantic Ocean, the English Channel, the Mediterranean Sea, and the countries of [MASK], Germany, Italy, [MASK], [MASK], the principalities of Andorra and Monaco, and by the duchy of Luxembourg. Its capital is Paris.

diskdiffusionantimicrobialtests.name: disk diffusion antimicrobial tests
diskdiffusionantimicrobialtests.definition: Disk diffusion antimicrobial tests is a method where a culturing surface inoculated with microbe is exposed to small disks containing known amounts of a chemical agent resulting in a zone of inhibition (usually in millimeters) of growth of the microbe corresponding to the susceptibility of the strain to the agent.

confidenceintervals.name: confidence intervals
confidenceintervals.definition: Confidence intervals is a range of values for a variable of interest, e.g., a rate, constructed so that this range has a specified probability of including the true value of the variable.

facialnucleus.name: facial nucleus
facialnucleus.definition: Facial nucleus is a region in the pontine tegmentum that is the nucleus of the facial nerve.

sugars.name: sugars
sugars.definition: Sugars is short chain carbohydrate molecules that have hydroxyl groups attached to each carbon atom unit with the exception of one carbon that has a doubly-bond aldehyde or ketone oxygen. Cyclical sugar molecules are formed when the aldehyde or ketone groups respectively form a hemiacetal or hemiketal bond with one of the hydroxyl carbons. The three dimensional structure of the sugar molecule occurs in a vast array of biological and synthetic classes of specialized compounds including amino sugars; carbasugars; deoxy sugars; sugar acids; sugar alcohols; and sugar phosphates.

cathepsind.name: cathepsin d
cathepsind.definition: Cathepsin d is an intracellular proteinase found in a variety of tissue. It has specificity similar to but narrower than that of pepsin a. The enzyme is involved in catabolism of cartilage and connective tissue. ec 3.4.23.5. (Formerly ec 3.4.4.23).

goals.name: goals
goals.definition: Goals is the end-result or objective, which may be specified or required in advance.

magneticfieldtherapy.name: magnetic field therapy
magneticfieldtherapy.definition: Magnetic field therapy is the magnetic stimulation of specific target tissues or areas of the body for therapeutic purposes via the application of magnetic fields generated by [MASK] or [MASK].

gaitanalysis.name: gait analysis
gaitanalysis.definition: Gait analysis is determination of the level of functional limitation that may be due to pathology, and evaluating rehabilitative intervention of the way in which the body moves from one point to another. Most often, this is done by walking.

achievement.name: achievement
achievement.definition: Achievement is success in bringing an effort to the desired end; the degree or level of success attained in some specified area (esp. scholastic) or in general.

borderlinepersonalitydisorder.name: borderline personality disorder
borderlinepersonalitydisorder.definition: Borderline personality disorder is a personality disorder marked by a pattern of instability of interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affects, and marked impulsivity beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. ([MASK])

microglia.name: microglia
microglia.definition: Microglia is the third type of glial cell, along with astrocytes and oligodendrocytes (which together form the macroglia). Microglia vary in appearance depending on developmental stage, functional state, and anatomical location; subtype terms include ramified, perivascular, ameboid, resting, and activated. Microglia clearly are capable of [MASK] and play an important role in a wide spectrum of neuropathologies. They have also been suggested to act in several other roles including in secretion (e.g., of cytokines and neural growth factors), in immunological processing (e.g., antigen presentation), and in central nervous system development and remodeling.

hungary.name: hungary
hungary.definition: Hungary is a country in Europe, northwest of Romania, south of Slovakia, and east of Austria. The capital is Budapest.

pathology.name: pathology
pathology.definition: Pathology is a specialty concerned with the nature and cause of disease as expressed by changes in cellular or tissue structure and function caused by the disease process.

alexanderdisease.name: alexander disease
alexanderdisease.definition: Alexander disease is rare leukoencephalopathy with infantile-onset accumulation of Rosenthal fibers in the subpial, periventricular, and subependymal zones of the brain. Rosenthal fibers are glial fibrillary acidic protein aggregates found in astrocytes. Juvenile- and adult-onset types show progressive atrophy of the lower brainstem instead. De novo mutations in the gfap gene are associated with the disease with propensity for [MASK].

civilrights.name: civil rights
civilrights.definition: Civil rights is legal guarantee protecting the individual from attack on personal liberties, right to fair trial, right to vote, and freedom from discrimination on the basis of race, [MASK], religion, [MASK], age, disability, or national origin. (from http://www.usccr.gov/ accessed 1/31/2003)

receptors,lipoprotein.name: receptors , lipoprotein
receptors,lipoprotein.definition: Lipoprotein receptors is cell surface proteins that bind lipoproteins with high affinity. Lipoprotein receptors in the liver and peripheral tissues mediate the regulation of plasma and cellular cholesterol metabolism and concentration. The receptors generally recognize the apolipoproteins of the lipoprotein complex, and binding is often a trigger for endocytosis.

tissuetherapy,historical.name: tissue therapy , historical
tissuetherapy,historical.definition: Historical tissue therapy is historically, tissue transplantation, especially of refrigerated tissue (after Filatov). It was theorized that nonspecific substances, capable of initiating restorative processes, formed in tissues when refrigerated. Cell therapy (after Niehans) refers to implantation of tissue by injection. Originally this involved fresh cells but later frozen or lyophilized cells.

aggression.name: aggression
aggression.definition: Aggression is behavior which may be manifested by destructive and attacking action which is verbal or physical, by covert attitudes of hostility or by obstructionism.

oxygenconsumption.name: oxygen consumption
oxygenconsumption.definition: Oxygen consumption is the rate at which oxygen is used by a tissue; microliters of oxygen stpd used per milligram of tissue per hour; the rate at which oxygen enters the blood from alveolar gas, equal in the steady state to the consumption of oxygen by tissue metabolism throughout the body. (Stedman, 25th ed, p346)

diffuseaxonalinjury.name: diffuse axonal injury
diffuseaxonalinjury.definition: Diffuse axonal injury is a relatively common sequela of blunt head injury, characterized by a global disruption of axons throughout the brain. Associated clinical features may include neurobehavioral manifestations; [MASK]; dementia; and other disorders.

interleukin1receptorantagonistprotein.name: interleukin 1 receptor antagonist protein
interleukin1receptorantagonistprotein.definition: Interleukin 1 receptor antagonist protein is a ligand that binds to but fails to activate the interleukin 1 receptor. It plays an inhibitory role in the regulation of inflammation and fever. Several isoforms of the protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its mRNA.

radiationhybridmapping.name: radiation hybrid mapping
radiationhybridmapping.definition: Radiation hybrid mapping is a method for ordering genetic loci along chromosomes. The method involves fusing irradiated donor cells with host cells from another species. Following cell fusion, fragments of dna from the irradiated cells become integrated into the chromosomes of the host cells. Molecular probing of dna obtained from the fused cells is used to determine if two or more genetic loci are located within the same fragment of donor cell dna.

satellitecells,skeletalmuscle.name: satellite cells , skeletal muscle
satellitecells,skeletalmuscle.definition: Skeletal muscle satellite cells is elongated, spindle-shaped, quiescent myoblasts lying in close contact with adult skeletal muscle. They are thought to play a role in muscle repair and regeneration.

physicalstimulation.name: physical stimulation
physicalstimulation.definition: Physical stimulation is act of eliciting a response from a person or organism through physical contact.

typevsecretionsystems.name: type v secretion systems
typevsecretionsystems.definition: Type v secretion systems is secretion systems of gram-negative bacteria (single membrane proteins or multiprotein complexes) that carry out secretion of proteins from the periplasmic space to the extracellular space via a beta-barrel transmembrane pore. There are several t5ss subtypes: T5aSS monomeric autotransporters, T5bSS two-partner secretions systems (tpss), T5cSS trimeric autotransporters, T5dSS fused two-partner secretion systems, and T5eSS autotransporters with inverted domains.

psoriasis.name: psoriasis
psoriasis.definition: Psoriasis is a common genetically determined, chronic, inflammatory skin disease characterized by rounded erythematous, dry, scaling patches. The lesions have a predilection for nails, scalp, genitalia, extensor surfaces, and the lumbosacral region. Accelerated epidermopoiesis is considered to be the fundamental pathologic feature in psoriasis.

goldcolloid,radioactive.name: gold colloid , radioactive
goldcolloid,radioactive.definition: Radioactive gold colloid is a suspension of radioactive gold particles emitting negative beta particles and gamma irradiation. It was formerly used for liver scans and irradiation treatment of some metastatic malignancies.

dopamineagents.name: dopamine agents
dopamineagents.definition: Dopamine agents is any drugs that are used for their effects on dopamine receptors, on the [MASK] of dopamine, or on the survival of [MASK].

clinicalcompetence.name: clinical competence
clinicalcompetence.definition: Clinical competence is the capability to perform acceptably those duties directly related to patient care.

libraries,nursing.name: libraries , nursing
libraries,nursing.definition: Nursing libraries is collections of [MASK] relevant to nursing.

socialchange.name: social change
socialchange.definition: Social change is a shift, alteration, modification, or evolution of human behavior and culture, which over time, results in measurable consequences on societal values and norms.

nervoussystemneoplasms.name: nervous system neoplasms
nervoussystemneoplasms.definition: Nervous system neoplasms is benign and malignant neoplastic processes arising from or involving components of the central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous systems, cranial nerves, and meninges. Included in this category are primary and metastatic nervous system neoplasms.

medicallaboratoryscience.name: medical laboratory science
medicallaboratoryscience.definition: Medical laboratory science is the specialty related to the performance of techniques in clinical pathology such as those in hematology, microbiology, and other general clinical laboratory applications.

amplifiers,electronic.name: amplifiers , electronic
amplifiers,electronic.definition: Electronic amplifiers is electronic devices that increase the magnitude of a signal's power level or current.
