mediterraneanislands.name: mediterranean islands
mediterraneanislands.definition: Mediterranean islands is islands in the Mediterranean Sea. The chief islands are the [MASK], Corsica, Crete, Cyprus, the Cyclades, Dodecanese and Ionian Islands, Malta, Sardinia and Sicily.

spiralganglion.name: spiral ganglion
spiralganglion.definition: Spiral ganglion is the sensory ganglion of the cochlear nerve. The cells of the spiral ganglion send fibers peripherally to the cochlear hair cells and centrally to the cochlear nuclei of the brain stem.

repetitivesequences,aminoacid.name: repetitive sequences , amino acid
repetitivesequences,aminoacid.definition: Amino acid repetitive sequences is a sequential pattern of amino acids occurring more than once in the same protein sequence. There often is some sequence variation between the repeated segments. Many protein domains are constituted from repeats.

virusinactivation.name: virus inactivation
virusinactivation.definition: Virus inactivation is inactivation of viruses by non-immune related techniques. They include extremes of pH, heat treatment, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation; desiccation; antiseptics; disinfectants; organic solvents, and detergents.

professionalautonomy.name: professional autonomy
professionalautonomy.definition: Professional autonomy is the quality or state of being independent and self-directing, especially in making decisions, enabling professionals to exercise judgment as they see fit during the performance of their jobs.

light.name: light
light.definition: Light is that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum in the visible, ultraviolet, and infrared range.

faithhealing.name: faith healing
faithhealing.definition: Faith healing is the use of faith and spirit to cure disease.

delayeddiagnosis.name: delayed diagnosis
delayeddiagnosis.definition: Delayed diagnosis is non-optimal interval of time between onset of symptoms, identification, and initiation of treatment.

hivreversetranscriptase.name: hiv reverse transcriptase
hivreversetranscriptase.definition: Hiv reverse transcriptase is a reverse transcriptase encoded by the [MASK] of hiv. It is a heterodimer of 66 kDa and 51 kDa subunits that are derived from a common precursor protein. The heterodimer also includes an RNAse h activity (ribonuclease h, human immunodeficiency virus) that plays an essential role the viral replication process.

dentin,secondary.name: dentin , secondary
dentin,secondary.definition: Secondary dentin is dentin formed by normal pulp after completion of root end formation.

toothmobility.name: tooth mobility
toothmobility.definition: Tooth mobility is horizontal and, to a lesser degree, axial movement of a tooth in response to normal forces, as in occlusion. It refers also to the movability of a tooth resulting from loss of all or a portion of its attachment and supportive apparatus, as seen in periodontitis, occlusal trauma, and periodontosis. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p507 & Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p313)

benzylcompounds.name: benzyl compounds
benzylcompounds.definition: Benzyl compounds is benzene derivatives that contain a benzyl group with the general formula Phenyl-CH2-R.

records.name: records
records.definition: Records is works on authentic evidence, of something having legal importance. The concept includes certificates of birth, death, etc., as well as hospital, medical, and other institutional records.

icecream.name: ice cream
icecream.definition: Ice cream is a frozen dairy food made from cream or butterfat, milk, sugar, and flavorings. Frozen custard and French-type ice creams also contain eggs.

medicalhistorytaking.name: medical history taking
medicalhistorytaking.definition: Medical history taking is acquiring information from a patient on past medical conditions and treatments.

gainoffunctionmutation.name: gain of function mutation
gainoffunctionmutation.definition: Gain of function mutation is a mutation that results in an increase in a gene's activity or in acquiring a new molecular function or a new pattern of gene expression.

corticalexcitability.name: cortical excitability
corticalexcitability.definition: Cortical excitability is measurable changes in activities in the cerebral cortex upon a stimulation. a change in cortical excitability as measured by various techniques (e.g., transcranial magnetic stimulation) is associated with brain disorders.

endoplasmicreticulum,rough.name: endoplasmic reticulum , rough
endoplasmicreticulum,rough.definition: Rough endoplasmic reticulum is a type of endoplasmic reticulum (er) where polyribosomes are present on the cytoplasmic surfaces of the er membranes. This form of er is prominent in cells specialized for protein secretion and its principal function is to segregate proteins destined for export or intracellular utilization.

pancreaticjuice.name: pancreatic juice
pancreaticjuice.definition: Pancreatic juice is the fluid containing digestive enzymes secreted by the pancreas in response to food in the duodenum.

genes,mhcclassii.name: genes , mhc class ii
genes,mhcclassii.definition: Mhc class ii genes is genetic loci in the vertebrate major histocompatibility complex that encode polymorphic products which control the immune response to specific antigens. The genes are found in the hla-d region in humans and include h-2m, i-a, and i-e loci in mice.

cellnucleussize.name: cell nucleus size
cellnucleussize.definition: Cell nucleus size is the quantity of volume or surface area of a cell nucleus.

hygiene.name: hygiene
hygiene.definition: Hygiene is the science dealing with the establishment and maintenance of health in the individual and the group. It includes the conditions and practices conducive to health. (Webster, 3d ed)

psychiatry.name: psychiatry
psychiatry.definition: Psychiatry is the medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders.

musclerelaxation.name: muscle relaxation
musclerelaxation.definition: Muscle relaxation is that phase of a muscle twitch during which a muscle returns to a resting position.

aggressiveperiodontitis.name: aggressive periodontitis
aggressiveperiodontitis.definition: Aggressive periodontitis is inflammation and loss of periodontium that is characterized by rapid attachment loss and bone destruction in the presence of little local factors such as dental plaque and dental calculus. This highly destructive form of periodontitis often occurs in young people and was called early-onset periodontitis, but this disease also appears in old people.

angioplasty.name: angioplasty
angioplasty.definition: Angioplasty is reconstruction or repair of a blood vessel, which includes the widening of a pathological narrowing of an artery or vein by the removal of [MASK] material and/or the endothelial lining as well, or by dilatation (balloon angioplasty) to compress an [MASK]. Except for endarterectomy, usually these procedures are performed via catheterization as minimally invasive endovascular procedures.

rnasplicesites.name: rna splice sites
rnasplicesites.definition: Rna splice sites is nucleotide sequences located at the ends of exons and recognized in pre-messenger rna by spliceosomes. They are joined during the rna splicing reaction, forming the junctions between exons.

cardiomyopathy,dilated.name: cardiomyopathy , dilated
cardiomyopathy,dilated.definition: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a form of cardiac muscle disease that is characterized by ventricular dilation, ventricular dysfunction, and heart failure. Risk factors include smoking; alcohol drinking; hypertension; infection; pregnancy; and mutations in the lmna gene encoding lamin type a, a nuclear lamina protein.

crisisintervention.name: crisis intervention
crisisintervention.definition: Crisis intervention is brief therapeutic approach which is ameliorative rather than curative of acute psychiatric emergencies. Used in contexts such as emergency rooms of psychiatric or [MASK], or in the home or place of crisis occurrence, this treatment approach focuses on interpersonal and intrapsychic factors and environmental modification. (apa Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 7th ed)

tobaccosmokepollution.name: tobacco smoke pollution
tobaccosmokepollution.definition: Tobacco smoke pollution is contamination of the air by tobacco smoke.

viralmatrixproteins.name: viral matrix proteins
viralmatrixproteins.definition: Viral matrix proteins is proteins associated with the inner surface of the lipid bilayer of the viral envelope. These proteins have been implicated in control of viral transcription and may possibly serve as the "glue" that binds the nucleocapsid to the appropriate membrane site during viral budding from the host cell.

rats,inbredwf.name: rats , inbred wf
rats,inbredwf.definition: Inbred wf rats is an inbred strain of rat that is used in biomedical research.

electrophoresis,paper.name: electrophoresis , paper
electrophoresis,paper.definition: [MASK] electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which [MASK] is used as the diffusion medium. This technique is confined almost entirely to separations of small molecules such as amino acids, peptides, and nucleotides, and relatively high voltages are nearly always used.

mutantchimericproteins.name: mutant chimeric proteins
mutantchimericproteins.definition: Mutant chimeric proteins is proteins produced from genes that have mutated by the fusing of protein coding regions of more than one gene. Such hybrid proteins are responsible for some instances of antibiotic resistance and defective biological processes such as neoplasms.

sigmoiddiseases.name: sigmoid diseases
sigmoiddiseases.definition: Sigmoid diseases is pathological processes in the sigmoid colon region of the large intestine (intestine, large).

cocaine.name: cocaine
cocaine.definition: Cocaine is an alkaloid ester extracted from the leaves of plants including coca. It is a local anesthetic and vasoconstrictor and is clinically used for that purpose, particularly in the eye, ear, nose, and throat. It also has powerful central nervous system effects similar to the amphetamines and is a drug of abuse. Cocaine, like amphetamines, acts by multiple mechanisms on brain catecholaminergic neurons; the mechanism of its reinforcing effects is thought to involve inhibition of dopamine uptake.

subcutaneousfat,abdominal.name: subcutaneous fat , abdominal
subcutaneousfat,abdominal.definition: Abdominal subcutaneous fat is fatty tissue under the skin in the region of the abdomen.

polyvinylalcohol.name: polyvinyl alcohol
polyvinylalcohol.definition: Polyvinyl alcohol is a polymer prepared from polyvinyl acetates by replacement of the acetate groups with hydroxyl groups. It is used as a pharmaceutic aid and ophthalmic lubricant as well as in the manufacture of surface coatings artificial sponges, cosmetics, and other products.

naturalphenomenonorprocess.name: natural phenomenon or process
naturalphenomenonorprocess.definition: Natural phenomenon or process is natural phenomenon or process

thermodynamics.name: thermodynamics
thermodynamics.definition: Thermodynamics is a rigorously mathematical analysis of energy relationships (heat, work, temperature, and equilibrium). It describes systems whose states are determined by thermal parameters, such as temperature, in addition to mechanical and electromagnetic parameters. (From Hawley's Condensed Chemical Dictionary, 12th ed)

dominance,ocular.name: dominance , ocular
dominance,ocular.definition: Ocular dominance is the functional superiority and preferential use of one eye over the other. The term is usually applied to superiority in sighting (visual perception) or motor task but not difference in visual acuity or dysfunction of one of the eyes. Ocular dominance can be modified by visual input and neurotrophic factors.

proteinstructure,tertiary.name: protein structure , tertiary
proteinstructure,tertiary.definition: Tertiary protein structure is the level of protein structure in which combinations of secondary protein structures (alpha helices; beta sheets; loop regions, and amino acid motifs) pack together to form folded shapes. Disulfide bridges between cysteines in two different parts of the polypeptide chain along with other interactions between the chains play a role in the formation and stabilization of tertiary structure.

soxtranscriptionfactors.name: sox transcription factors
soxtranscriptionfactors.definition: Sox transcription factors is a large family of structurally-related transcription factors that were originally discovered based upon their close sequence homology to an HMG-box domain found in [MASK]-determining region y protein. Many sox transcription factors play important roles in regulating cell differentiation. The numerous members of this family are organized in several subgroups according to structural identities found within the proteins.

prenataleducation.name: prenatal education
prenataleducation.definition: Prenatal education is training for pregnant women and parents-to-be to prepare for childbirth; child care; and parenthood.

pneumonia.name: pneumonia
pneumonia.definition: Pneumonia is infection of the lung often accompanied by inflammation.

enzymeprecursors.name: enzyme precursors
enzymeprecursors.definition: Enzyme precursors is physiologically inactive substances that can be converted to active enzymes.

plantoils.name: plant oils
plantoils.definition: Plant oils is oils derived from plants or plant products.

drugadministrationschedule.name: drug administration schedule
drugadministrationschedule.definition: Drug administration schedule is time schedule for administration of a drug in order to achieve optimum effectiveness and convenience.

dataset.name: dataset
dataset.definition: Dataset is works consisting of organized collections of data, which have been stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

animalcommunication.name: animal communication
animalcommunication.definition: Animal communication is communication between animals involving the giving off by one individual of some chemical or physical signal, that, on being received by another, influences its behavior.

chromosomes,fungal.name: chromosomes , fungal
chromosomes,fungal.definition: Fungal chromosomes is structures within the nucleus of fungal cells consisting of or containing dna, which carry genetic information essential to the cell.

virulencefactors.name: virulence factors
virulencefactors.definition: Virulence factors is those components of an organism that determine its capacity to cause disease but are not required for its viability per se. Two classes have been characterized: toxins, biological and surface adhesion molecules that effect the ability of the microorganism to invade and colonize a host. (From Davis et al., Microbiology, 4th ed. p486)

motorskills.name: motor skills
motorskills.definition: Motor skills is performance of complex motor acts.

ascorbicaciddeficiency.name: ascorbic acid deficiency
ascorbicaciddeficiency.definition: Ascorbic acid deficiency is a condition due to a dietary deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin c), characterized by malaise, lethargy, and weakness. As the disease progresses, joints, muscles, and [MASK] may become the sites of hemorrhage. Ascorbic acid deficiency frequently develops into scurvy in young children fed unsupplemented cow's milk exclusively during their first year. It develops also commonly in chronic alcoholism. (Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1177)

fungalviruses.name: fungal viruses
fungalviruses.definition: Fungal viruses is viruses infecting species of fungi.

foodandbeverages.name: food and beverages
foodandbeverages.definition: Food and beverages is edible or potable substances.

informedconsent.name: informed consent
informedconsent.definition: Informed consent is voluntary authorization, by a patient or research subject, with full comprehension of the risks involved, for diagnostic or investigative procedures, and for medical and surgical treatment.

peptidefragments.name: peptide fragments
peptidefragments.definition: Peptide fragments is partial proteins formed by partial hydrolysis of complete proteins or generated through protein engineering techniques.

geneexpression.name: gene expression
geneexpression.definition: Gene expression is the phenotypic manifestation of a gene or genes by the processes of genetic transcription and genetic translation.

cellwall.name: cell wall
cellwall.definition: Cell wall is the outermost layer of a cell in most plants; bacteria; fungi; and algae. The cell wall is usually a rigid structure that lies external to the cell membrane, and provides a protective barrier against physical or chemical agents.

myeloiddifferentiationfactor88.name: myeloid differentiation factor 88
myeloiddifferentiationfactor88.definition: Myeloid differentiation factor 88 is an intracellular signaling adaptor protein that plays a role in toll-like receptor and interleukin 1 receptors signal transduction. It forms a signaling complex with the activated cell surface receptors and members of the irak kinases.

geneexpressionregulation,leukemic.name: gene expression regulation , leukemic
geneexpressionregulation,leukemic.definition: Leukemic gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in leukemia.

semanticweb.name: semantic web
semanticweb.definition: Semantic web is a framework for development and promotion of common data formats and exchange protocols linked in a way that can be read directly by computers. Semantic Web is a platform for sharing and reusing data across application, enterprise, and community boundaries, by linking concepts rather than just documents.

toothdiseases.name: tooth diseases
toothdiseases.definition: Tooth diseases is diseases involving the teeth.

rnaitherapeutics.name: rnai therapeutics
rnaitherapeutics.definition: Rnai therapeutics is a form of disease treatment which involves the silencing of genes that are associated with a disease by the process of rna interference.

testtakingskills.name: test taking skills
testtakingskills.definition: Test taking skills is skills and strategies, unrelated to the traits a test is intended to measure, that may increase test takers' scores -- may include the effects of coaching or experience in taking tests. (eric Thesaurus)

remissioninduction.name: remission induction
remissioninduction.definition: Remission induction is therapeutic act or process that initiates a response to a complete or partial remission level.

basalgangliahemorrhage.name: basal ganglia hemorrhage
basalgangliahemorrhage.definition: Basal ganglia hemorrhage is bleeding within the subcortical regions of cerebral hemispheres (basal ganglia). It is often associated with hypertension or arteriovenous malformations. Clinical manifestations may include headache; dyskinesias; and hemiparesis.

resuscitationorders.name: resuscitation orders
resuscitationorders.definition: Resuscitation orders is instructions issued by a physician pertaining to the institution, continuation, or withdrawal of life support measures. The concept includes policies, laws, statutes, decisions, guidelines, and discussions that may affect the issuance of such orders.

vestibularnuclei.name: vestibular nuclei
vestibularnuclei.definition: Vestibular nuclei is the four cellular masses in the floor of the fourth ventricle giving rise to a widely dispersed special sensory system. Included is the superior, medial, inferior, and lateral vestibular nucleus. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

abdominalcavity.name: abdominal cavity
abdominalcavity.definition: Abdominal cavity is the region in the abdomen extending from the thoracic diaphragm to the plane of the superior pelvic aperture (pelvic inlet). The abdominal cavity contains the peritoneum and abdominal viscera, as well as the extraperitoneal space which includes the retroperitoneal space.

sleepwakedisorders.name: sleep wake disorders
sleepwakedisorders.definition: Sleep wake disorders is abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the circadian rhythm which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

wastemanagement.name: waste management
wastemanagement.definition: Waste management is disposal, processing, controlling, [MASK], and reusing the solid, liquid, and gaseous wastes of plants, animals, humans, and other organisms. It includes control within a closed ecological system to maintain a habitable environment.

rnapolymeraseiii.name: rna polymerase iii
rnapolymeraseiii.definition: Rna polymerase iii is a DNA-dependent rna polymerase present in bacterial, plant, and animal cells. It functions in the nucleoplasmic structure where it transcribes dna into rna. It has specific requirements for cations and [MASK] and has shown an intermediate sensitivity to alpha-amanitin in comparison to rna polymerase i and ii.

bees.name: bees
bees.definition: Bees is insect members of the superfamily Apoidea, found almost everywhere, particularly on flowers. About 3500 species occur in North America. They differ from most wasps in that their young are fed honey and pollen rather than animal food.

naturalhistory.name: natural history
naturalhistory.definition: Natural history is a former branch of knowledge embracing the study, description, and classification of natural objects (as animals, plants, and minerals) and thus including the modern sciences of zoology, botany, and mineralogy insofar as they existed at that time. In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries it was much used for the generalized pursuit of certain areas of science. (Webster, 3d ed; from Dr. James h. Cassedy, nlm [MASK] Division)

quartz.name: quartz
quartz.definition: Quartz is quartz (SiO2). a glassy or crystalline form of silicon dioxide. Many colored varieties are semiprecious stones. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

stromalinteractionmolecule2.name: stromal interaction molecule 2
stromalinteractionmolecule2.definition: Stromal interaction molecule 2 is a stromal interaction molecule that functions as a highly sensitive calcium sensor in the endoplamsic reticulum and [MASK]. It can regulate calcium release activated calcium channels in response to minor variations in intracellular calcium.

wasteproducts.name: waste products
wasteproducts.definition: Waste products is debris resulting from a process that is of no further use to the system producing it. The concept includes materials discharged from or stored in a system in inert form as a by-product of vital activities. (From Webster's New Collegiate Dictionary, 1981)

pharmacology.name: pharmacology
pharmacology.definition: Pharmacology is the study of the origin, nature, properties, and actions of drugs and their effects on living organisms.

graftvshostreaction.name: graft vs host reaction
graftvshostreaction.definition: [MASK] vs host reaction is an immunological attack mounted by a [MASK] against the host because of tissue incompatibility when immunologically competent cells are transplanted to an immunologically incompetent host; the resulting clinical picture is that of [MASK] vs host disease.

health.name: health
health.definition: Health is the state of the organism when it functions optimally without evidence of disease.

hydrophobicandhydrophilicinteractions.name: hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions
hydrophobicandhydrophilicinteractions.definition: Hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions is the thermodynamic interaction between a substance and water.

typedpersonality.name: type d personality
typedpersonality.definition: Type d personality is behavior pattern characterized by negative emotionality, an inability to express emotions, and [MASK], which has been linked to greater cardiovascular disease and increased mortality. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 217)

naturaldisasters.name: natural disasters
naturaldisasters.definition: Natural disasters is disasters linked to natural hazards including widespread fires, floods, storms, earthquakes and drought.These events may result in significant damage and loss of lives.

contraceptiveprevalencesurveys.name: contraceptive prevalence surveys
contraceptiveprevalencesurveys.definition: Contraceptive [MASK] surveys is collections of data, obtained from voluntary subjects, that measure the usage rate of methods of contraception; contraceptive devices; or contraceptive agents.

artifacts.name: artifacts
artifacts.definition: Artifacts is any visible result of a procedure which is caused by the procedure itself and not by the entity being analyzed. Common examples include histological structures introduced by tissue processing, radiographic images of structures that are not naturally present in living tissue, and products of chemical reactions that occur during analysis.

extracellularfluid.name: extracellular fluid
extracellularfluid.definition: Extracellular fluid is the fluid of the body that is outside of cells. It is the external environment for the cells.

waterpollutants.name: water pollutants
waterpollutants.definition: Water pollutants is substances or organisms which pollute the water or bodies of water. Use for water pollutants in general or those for which there is no specific heading.

acetylcholine.name: acetylcholine
acetylcholine.definition: Acetylcholine is a neurotransmitter found at neuromuscular junctions, autonomic ganglia, parasympathetic effector junctions, a subset of sympathetic effector junctions, and at many sites in the central nervous system.

giantaxonalneuropathy.name: giant axonal neuropathy
giantaxonalneuropathy.definition: Giant axonal neuropathy is rare autosomal recessive disorder of [MASK] proteins. The disease is caused by mutations in the gene that codes gigaxonin protein. The mutations result in disorganization of axonal [MASK] proteins, formation of the characteristic giant axons, and progressive neuropathy. The clinical features of the disease include early-onset progressive peripheral motor and sensory neuropathies often associated with central nervous system involvement (intellectual disability, seizures, dysmetria, and congenital nystagmus).

healthylifestyle.name: healthy lifestyle
healthylifestyle.definition: Healthy lifestyle is a pattern of behavior involving life style choices which ensure optimum health. Examples are eating right; maintaining physical, emotional, and spiritual wellness, and taking preemptive steps against communicable diseases.

rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.name: rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor beta
rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.definition: Rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor beta is a rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that is highly expressed in hematopoietic cells and in lymphocytes. The expression of this subtype is associated with the regulation of cell proliferation; tumorigenesis; and apoptosis.

uterinehemorrhage.name: uterine hemorrhage
uterinehemorrhage.definition: Uterine hemorrhage is bleeding from blood vessels in the uterus, sometimes manifested as vaginal bleeding.

respiratorytherapy.name: respiratory therapy
respiratorytherapy.definition: Respiratory therapy is care of patients with deficiencies and abnormalities associated with the cardiopulmonary system. It includes the therapeutic use of medical gases and their administrative apparatus, environmental control systems, humidification, aerosols, ventilatory support, bronchopulmonary drainage and exercise, respiratory rehabilitation, assistance with cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and maintenance of natural, artificial, and mechanical airways.

skinmanifestations.name: skin manifestations
skinmanifestations.definition: Skin manifestations is dermatologic disorders attendant upon non-dermatologic disease or injury.

typeisecretionsystems.name: type i secretion systems
typeisecretionsystems.definition: Type i secretion systems is gram-negative bacterial secretion systems which translocate effectors in a single step across the inner and outer membranes. The one-step secretion is carried out by a channel that passes from the cytoplasm, through the inner membrane, periplasmic space, and outer membrane, to the extracellular space. The specificity of type i secretions systems are determined by the specificity of the three subcomponents forming the channel - an atp transporter (atp-binding cassette transporters); a [MASK] protein ([MASK] proteins); and an outer membrane protein ([MASK] proteins.)

transplantdonorsite.name: transplant donor site
transplantdonorsite.definition: [MASK] donor site is the body location or part from which tissue is taken for transplantation.

cloudcomputing.name: cloud computing
cloudcomputing.definition: Cloud computing is storing and processing data on multiple servers that can be accessed through the Internet.

pathologicfunction.name: pathologic function
pathologicfunction.definition: Pathologic function is the structural and functional manifestations of a disease.

frozensections.name: frozen sections
frozensections.definition: Frozen sections is thinly cut sections of frozen tissue specimens prepared with a cryostat or freezing microtome.

healthstatusindicators.name: health status indicators
healthstatusindicators.definition: Health status indicators is the measurement of the health status for a given population using a variety of indices, including morbidity, mortality, and available health resources.

carbohydrates.name: carbohydrates
carbohydrates.definition: Carbohydrates is a class of organic compounds composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in a ratio of Cn(H2O)n. The largest class of organic compounds, including [MASK]; glycogen; cellulose; polysaccharides; and simple monosaccharides.

cardiacimagingtechniques.name: cardiac imaging techniques
cardiacimagingtechniques.definition: Cardiac imaging techniques is visualization of the heart structure and cardiac blood flow for diagnostic evaluation or to guide cardiac procedures via techniques including endoscopy (cardiac endoscopy, sometimes refered to as cardioscopy), radionuclide imaging; magnetic resonance imaging; tomography; or ultrasonography.

sugaralcohols.name: sugar alcohols
sugaralcohols.definition: Sugar alcohols is polyhydric alcohols having no more than one hydroxy group attached to each carbon atom. They are formed by the reduction of the carbonyl group of a sugar to a hydroxyl group.(From Dorland, 28th ed)

lipidmetabolismdisorders.name: lipid metabolism disorders
lipidmetabolismdisorders.definition: Lipid metabolism disorders is pathological conditions resulting from abnormal anabolism or catabolism of lipids in the body.

postandcoretechnique.name: post and core technique
postandcoretechnique.definition: Post and core technique is use of a metal casting, usually with a post in the pulp or root canal, designed to support and retain an artificial crown.

wisconsincardsortingtest.name: wisconsin card sorting test
wisconsincardsortingtest.definition: Wisconsin card sorting test is a neuropsychological test designed to assess executive function typically assigned to the frontal lobe (e.g., [MASK] thinking, and [MASK]). The subjects are asked to sort numbered response cards according to different principles and to alter their approach during testing.

spectroscopy,fouriertransforminfrared.name: spectroscopy , fourier transform infrared
spectroscopy,fouriertransforminfrared.definition: [MASK] infrared spectroscopy is a spectroscopic technique in which a range of wavelengths is presented simultaneously with an interferometer and the spectrum is mathematically derived from the pattern thus obtained.

caribbeannetherlands.name: caribbean netherlands
caribbeannetherlands.definition: Caribbean [MASK] is a group Caribbean islands including Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, and Saba.

heavyions.name: heavy ions
heavyions.definition: Heavy ions is positively-charged atomic nuclei that have been stripped of their [MASK]. These particles have one or more units of electric charge and a mass exceeding that of the [MASK] nucleus ([MASK]).

dentistry.name: dentistry
dentistry.definition: Dentistry is the profession concerned with the teeth, oral cavity, and associated structures, and the diagnosis and treatment of their diseases including prevention and the restoration of defective and missing tissue.

oralmanifestations.name: oral manifestations
oralmanifestations.definition: Oral manifestations is disorders of the mouth attendant upon non-oral disease or injury.

medicine.name: medicine
medicine.definition: Medicine is the art and science of studying, performing research on, preventing, diagnosing, and treating disease, as well as the maintenance of health.

mentalprocess.name: mental process
mentalprocess.definition: Mental process is conceptual functions or thinking in all its forms.

histamineantagonists.name: histamine antagonists
histamineantagonists.definition: Histamine antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate histamine receptors, thereby blocking the actions of histamine or [MASK]. Classical antihistaminics block the histamine h1 receptors only.

communicationsmedia.name: communications media
communicationsmedia.definition: Communications media is the means of interchanging or transmitting and receiving information. Historically the media were written: books, journals, newspapers, and other publications; in the modern age the media include, in addition, radio, television, computers, and information networks.

healthypeopleprograms.name: healthy people programs
healthypeopleprograms.definition: Healthy people programs is healthy People Programs are a [MASK] of health objectives to be used by governments, communities, professional organizations, and others to help develop programs to improve health. It builds on initiatives pursued over the past two decades beginning with the 1979 Surgeon General's Report, Healthy People, Healthy People 2000: National Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Objectives, and Healthy People 2010. These established national health objectives and served as the basis for the development of state and community plans. These are administered by the Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (odphp). Similar programs are conducted by other national governments.

intracranialhemorrhage,traumatic.name: intracranial hemorrhage , traumatic
intracranialhemorrhage,traumatic.definition: Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage is bleeding within the skull induced by penetrating and nonpenetrating traumatic injuries, including hemorrhages into the tissues of cerebrum; brain stem; and cerebellum; as well as into the epidural, subdural and subarachnoid spaces of the meninges.

connectivetissuediseases.name: connective tissue diseases
connectivetissuediseases.definition: Connective tissue diseases is a heterogeneous group of disorders, some hereditary, others acquired, characterized by abnormal structure or function of one or more of the elements of connective tissue, i.e., collagen, elastin, or the mucopolysaccharides.

blotting,northern.name: blotting , northern
blotting,northern.definition: Northern blotting is detection of rna that has been electrophoretically separated and immobilized by blotting on nitrocellulose or other type of [MASK] or nylon membrane followed by hybridization with labeled nucleic acid probes.

drugresistance,bacterial.name: drug resistance , bacterial
drugresistance,bacterial.definition: Bacterial drug resistance is the ability of bacteria to resist or to become tolerant to chemotherapeutic agents, antimicrobial agents, or antibiotics. This resistance may be acquired through gene mutation or foreign dna in transmissible plasmids (r factors).

drugmisuse.name: drug misuse
drugmisuse.definition: Drug misuse is use of a drug for a purpose not consistent with legal or medical guidelines.

weightgain.name: weight gain
weightgain.definition: Weight gain is increase in body weight over existing weight.

architecturaldrawing.name: architectural drawing
architecturaldrawing.definition: Architectural drawing is work consisting of drawings of architecture and architectural projects, whether the project was executed or not. (Art & Architecture Thesaurus, 1990, v.2)

geographicarea.name: geographic area
geographicarea.definition: Geographic area is The continents and countries situated on those continents; the United States and each of the constituent states arranged by region; Canada and each of its provinces; Australia and each of its states; the major bodies of water and major islands on both hemispheres; and selected major cities.

smokingpipes.name: smoking pipes
smokingpipes.definition: Smoking pipes is devices used for smoking which convey smoke directly into the mouth.

neoplasms,experimental.name: neoplasms , experimental
neoplasms,experimental.definition: Experimental neoplasms is experimentally induced new abnormal growth of tissues in animals to provide models for studying human neoplasms.

patientmedicationknowledge.name: patient medication knowledge
patientmedicationknowledge.definition: Patient medication knowledge is patient health knowledge related to medications including what is being used and why as well as instructions and precautions.

liver.name: liver
liver.definition: Liver is a large lobed glandular organ in the abdomen of vertebrates that is responsible for detoxification, metabolism, synthesis and storage of various substances.

thyroidcartilage.name: thyroid cartilage
thyroidcartilage.definition: Thyroid cartilage is the largest cartilage of the larynx consisting of two laminae fusing anteriorly at an acute angle in the midline of the [MASK]. The point of fusion forms a subcutaneous [MASK] known as the Adam's apple.

growthdifferentiationfactor15.name: growth differentiation factor 15
growthdifferentiationfactor15.definition: Growth differentiation factor 15 is a growth differentiation factor that is secreted in response to cell stress and in response to macrophage activation. In addition growth differentiation factor 15 demonstrates a diverse array of biological properties including the induction of cartilage formation, the inhibition of hematopoietic progenitor proliferation, and the induction of neuronal migration.

responseelements.name: response elements
responseelements.definition: Response elements is nucleotide sequences, usually upstream, which are recognized by specific regulatory transcription factors, thereby causing gene response to various regulatory agents. These elements may be found in both promoter and enhancer regions.

receptors,vascularendothelialgrowthfacto.name: receptors , vascular endothelial growth factor
receptors,vascularendothelialgrowthfacto.definition: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptors is a family of closely related receptor protein-tyrosine kinases that bind vascular endothelial growth factors. They share a cluster of seven extracellular ig-like domains which are important for ligand binding. They are highly expressed in vascular endothelial cells and are critical for the physiological and pathological growth, development and maintenance of blood and lymphatic vessels.

rheum.name: rheum
rheum.definition: Rheum is a plant genus of the family polygonaceae. Members contain chrysophanic acid, rhein, emodin, and other anthraquinones. The roots were formerly used as purgatives.

plateletactivation.name: platelet activation
plateletactivation.definition: Platelet activation is a series of progressive, overlapping events, triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue. These events include shape change, adhesiveness, aggregation, and release reactions. When carried through to completion, these events lead to the formation of a stable hemostatic plug.

peritonealneoplasms.name: peritoneal neoplasms
peritonealneoplasms.definition: Peritoneal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the peritoneum.

retinalvessels.name: retinal vessels
retinalvessels.definition: Retinal vessels is the blood vessels which supply and drain the retina.

boron.name: boron
boron.definition: Boron is a trace element with the atomic symbol b, atomic number 5, and atomic weight [10.806; 10.821]. Boron-10, an isotope of boron, is used as a neutron absorber in [MASK].

mitralvalvestenosis.name: mitral valve stenosis
mitralvalvestenosis.definition: Mitral valve stenosis is narrowing of the passage through the mitral valve due to fibrosis, and calcinosis in the leaflets and chordal areas. This elevates the left atrial pressure which, in turn, raises pulmonary venous and capillary pressure leading to bouts of dyspnea and tachycardia during physical exertion. rheumatic fever is its primary cause.

aorticaneurysm,abdominal.name: aortic aneurysm , abdominal
aorticaneurysm,abdominal.definition: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is an abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the abdominal aorta which gives rise to the visceral, the parietal, and the terminal (iliac) branches below the aortic hiatus at the diaphragm.

guidelineadherence.name: guideline adherence
guidelineadherence.definition: Guideline adherence is conformity in fulfilling or following official, recognized, or institutional requirements, guidelines, recommendations, protocols, pathways, or other standards.

sagittalsinusthrombosis.name: sagittal sinus thrombosis
sagittalsinusthrombosis.definition: Sagittal sinus thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in the superior sagittal sinus or the inferior sagittal sinus. Sagittal sinus thrombosis can result from infections, hematological disorders, craniocerebral trauma; and neurosurgical procedures. Clinical features are primarily related to the increased [MASK] causing headache; nausea; and vomiting. Severe cases can evolve to seizures or coma.

mining.name: mining
mining.definition: Mining is the process of extracting mineral deposits from the earth.

alienhandsyndrome.name: alien hand syndrome
alienhandsyndrome.definition: Alien hand syndrome is an apraxia characterized by the affected limb having involuntary, autonomous, and purposeful behaviors that are perceived as being controlled by an external force. Often the affected limb interferes with the actions of the normal limb. Symptoms develop from lesions in the corpus callosum or medial frontal cortex, stroke, infarction, and neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., creutzfeldt-jakob syndrome, corticobasal degeneration).

nuclearporecomplexproteins.name: nuclear pore complex proteins
nuclearporecomplexproteins.definition: Nuclear pore complex proteins is proteins that form the structure of the nuclear pore. They are involved in active, facilitated and passive transport of molecules in and out of the cell nucleus.

graftrejection.name: graft rejection
graftrejection.definition: [MASK] [MASK] is an immune response with both cellular and humoral components, directed against an allogeneic [MASK], whose tissue antigens are not compatible with those of the recipient.

childreactivedisorders.name: child reactive disorders
childreactivedisorders.definition: Child reactive disorders is reactions to an event or [MASK] of events which are considered to be of pathological degree, that have not developed into a neurosis, psychosis, or personality disorder with fixed patterns.

collectedwork.name: collected work
collectedwork.definition: Collected work is work consisting of collections of previously published works.

malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.name: malformations of cortical development , group ii
malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.definition: Group ii malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal cell migration in neurogenesis. This group includes cobblestone lissencephaly and periventricular nodular heterotopia.

consensussequence.name: consensus sequence
consensussequence.definition: [MASK] sequence is a theoretical representative nucleotide or amino acid sequence in which each nucleotide or amino acid is the one which occurs most frequently at that site in the different sequences which occur in nature. The phrase also refers to an actual sequence which approximates the theoretical [MASK]. a known conserved sequence [MASK] is represented by a [MASK] sequence. Commonly observed supersecondary protein structures (amino acid motifs) are often formed by conserved sequences.

neoplasms,muscletissue.name: neoplasms , muscle tissue
neoplasms,muscletissue.definition: Muscle tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of muscle tissue: skeletal, cardiac, or smooth. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in muscles.

textmessaging.name: text messaging
textmessaging.definition: Text messaging is communication between cell phone users via the Short Message Service protocol which allows the interchange of short written messages.

asiancontinentalancestrygroup.name: asian continental ancestry group
asiancontinentalancestrygroup.definition: Asian continental ancestry group is individuals whose ancestral origins are in the southeastern and eastern areas of the Asian continent.

escapereaction.name: escape reaction
escapereaction.definition: Escape reaction is innate response elicited by sensory stimuli associated with a threatening situation, or actual confrontation with an enemy.

nuclearlamina.name: nuclear lamina
nuclearlamina.definition: Nuclear lamina is a lattice of fibrils which covers the entire inner surface of the nuclear envelope and interlinks nuclear pores (nuclear pore).

knowledgeofresults,psychological.name: knowledge of results , psychological
knowledgeofresults,psychological.definition: Psychological knowledge of results is a principle that learning is facilitated when the learner receives immediate evaluation of learning performance. The concept also hypothesizes that learning is facilitated when the learner is promptly informed whether a response is correct, and, if incorrect, of the direction of error.

growthdifferentiationfactor5.name: growth differentiation factor 5
growthdifferentiationfactor5.definition: Growth differentiation factor 5 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a role in early chondrogenesis and joint formation.

personnelmanagement.name: personnel management
personnelmanagement.definition: Personnel management is planning, organizing, and administering all activities related to personnel.

homecareservices.name: home care services
homecareservices.definition: Home care services is community health and nursing services providing coordinated multiple services to the patient at the patient's homes. These home-care services are provided by a [MASK], [MASK], hospitals, or organized community groups using professional staff for care delivery. It differs from home nursing which is provided by non-professionals.

livercirrhosis,alcoholic.name: liver cirrhosis , alcoholic
livercirrhosis,alcoholic.definition: Alcoholic liver cirrhosis is fibrosis of the hepatic parenchyma due to chronic excess alcohol drinking.

rna,guide.name: rna , guide
rna,guide.definition: Guide rna is small kinetoplastid mitochondrial rna that plays a major role in rna editing. These molecules form perfect hybrids with edited mRNA sequences and possess nucleotide sequences at their 5'-ends that are complementary to the sequences of the mRNA's immediately downstream of the pre-edited regions.

narrativetherapy.name: narrative therapy
narrativetherapy.definition: Narrative therapy is a form of psychotherapy that centers on the individuals as the experts in their own lives and views problems as separate from people. It is assumed that people have many skills, competencies, beliefs, values, commitments, and abilities that will assist them to reduce the influence of problems in their lives.

bodypart,organ,ororgancomponent.name: body part , organ , or organ component
bodypart,organ,ororgancomponent.definition: Or organ component organ body part is body part , organ , or organ component

prolactin.name: prolactin
prolactin.definition: Prolactin is a lactogenic hormone secreted by the adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). It is a polypeptide of approximately 23 kD. Besides its major action on lactation, in some species prolactin exerts effects on reproduction, maternal behavior, fat metabolism, immunomodulation and osmoregulation. Prolactin receptors are present in the mammary gland, hypothalamus, liver, ovary, testis, and prostate.

cerebralarterialdiseases.name: cerebral arterial diseases
cerebralarterialdiseases.definition: Cerebral arterial diseases is pathological conditions of intracranial arteries supplying the cerebrum. These diseases often are due to abnormalities or pathological processes in the anterior cerebral artery; middle cerebral artery; and posterior cerebral artery.

nematodeinfections.name: nematode infections
nematodeinfections.definition: Nematode infections is infections by nematodes, general or unspecified.

pseudomonasvaccines.name: pseudomonas vaccines
pseudomonasvaccines.definition: Pseudomonas vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat pseudomonas infections.

ringfingerdomains.name: ring finger domains
ringfingerdomains.definition: Ring finger domains is a zinc-binding domain defined by the sequence [MASK]-X2-[MASK]-X(9-39)-[MASK]-X(l-3)-His-X(2-3)-[MASK]-X2-[MASK] -X(4-48)-[MASK]-X2-[MASK], where x is any amino acid. The ring finger motif binds two atoms of zinc, with each zinc atom ligated tetrahedrally by either four cysteines or three cysteines and a histidine. The motif also forms into a unitary structure with a central cross-brace region and is found in many proteins that are involved in protein-protein interactions. The acronym ring stands for Really Interesting New Gene.

ruralpopulation.name: rural population
ruralpopulation.definition: Rural population is the inhabitants of rural areas or of small towns classified as rural.

salivaryelimination.name: salivary elimination
salivaryelimination.definition: Salivary elimination is the discharge of substances from the blood supply via diffusion into the saliva from the [MASK] or from the salivary glands.

intensivecareunits.name: intensive care units
intensivecareunits.definition: Intensive care units is hospital units providing continuous surveillance and care to acutely ill patients.

centrifugation.name: centrifugation
centrifugation.definition: Centrifugation is process of using a rotating machine to generate centrifugal force to separate substances of different densities, remove moisture, or simulate gravitational effects. It employs a large motor-driven apparatus with a long [MASK], at the end of which human and animal subjects, biological specimens, or equipment can be revolved and rotated at various speeds to study gravitational effects. (From Websters, 10th ed; McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

culture.name: culture
culture.definition: Culture is a collective expression for all behavior patterns acquired and socially transmitted through symbols. Culture includes customs, traditions, and language.

wholebloodcoagulationtime.name: whole blood coagulation time
wholebloodcoagulationtime.definition: Whole blood coagulation time is the time required by whole blood to produce a visible clot.

angiogenesisinducingagents.name: angiogenesis inducing agents
angiogenesisinducingagents.definition: Angiogenesis inducing agents is agents that induce or stimulate physiologic angiogenesis or pathologic angiogenesis.

adipocytes.name: adipocytes
adipocytes.definition: Adipocytes is cells in the body that store fats, usually in the form of triglycerides. [MASK] are the predominant type and found mostly in the abdominal cavity and [MASK]. brown adipocytes are thermogenic cells that can be found in newborns of some species and hibernating mammals.

erythrocytes,abnormal.name: erythrocytes , abnormal
erythrocytes,abnormal.definition: Abnormal erythrocytes is oxygen-carrying red blood cells in mammalian blood that are abnormal in structure or function.

consultants.name: consultants
consultants.definition: Consultants is individuals referred to for expert or professional advice or services.

kidneytubules,collecting.name: kidney tubules , collecting
kidneytubules,collecting.definition: Collecting kidney tubules is straight tubes commencing in the radiate part of the kidney cortex where they receive the curved ends of the distal convoluted tubules. In the medulla the collecting tubules of each pyramid converge to join a central tube (duct of Bellini) which opens on the summit of the papilla.

membranecofactorprotein.name: membrane cofactor protein
membranecofactorprotein.definition: Membrane cofactor protein is a ubiquitously expressed complement receptor that binds complement c3b and complement c4b and serves as a co-factor for their inactivation by complement factor i. It also interacts with a wide variety of pathogens and mediates the immune response.

tissueandorganharvesting.name: tissue and organ harvesting
tissueandorganharvesting.definition: Tissue and organ harvesting is the procedure of removing tissues, organs, or specimens from donors for reuse, such as transplantation.

receptors,ldl.name: receptors , ldl
receptors,ldl.definition: Ldl receptors is receptors on the plasma membrane of nonhepatic cells that specifically bind ldl. The receptors are localized in specialized regions called coated pits. Hypercholesteremia is caused by an allelic genetic defect of three types: 1, receptors do not bind to ldl; 2, there is reduced binding of ldl; and 3, there is normal binding but no internalization of ldl. In consequence, entry of cholesterol esters into the cell is impaired and the intracellular [MASK] by cholesterol on 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl CoA reductase is lacking.

transplantationconditioning.name: transplantation conditioning
transplantationconditioning.definition: Transplantation conditioning is preparative treatment of [MASK] recipient with various conditioning regimens including radiation, immune sera, chemotherapy, and/or immunosuppressive agents, prior to transplantation. Transplantation conditioning is very common before bone marrow transplantation.

ventricularpressure.name: ventricular pressure
ventricularpressure.definition: Ventricular pressure is the pressure within a cardiac ventricle. Ventricular pressure waveforms can be measured in the beating heart by catheterization or estimated using imaging techniques (e.g., doppler echocardiography). The information is useful in evaluating the function of the myocardium; cardiac valves; and pericardium, particularly with simultaneous measurement of other (e.g., aortic or atrial) pressures.

thermaldiffusion.name: thermal diffusion
thermaldiffusion.definition: Thermal diffusion is the movement of molecules from one location to another as effected by temperature changes.

qfever.name: q fever
qfever.definition: Q fever is an acute infectious disease caused by coxiella burnetii. It is characterized by a sudden onset of fever; headache; malaise; and weakness. In humans, it is commonly contracted by [MASK] of infected dusts derived from infected domestic animals (animals, domestic).

lateralsinusthrombosis.name: lateral sinus thrombosis
lateralsinusthrombosis.definition: Lateral sinus thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in the lateral sinuses. This condition is often associated with ear infections (otitis media or mastoiditis) without antibiotic treatment. In [MASK], lateral sinus thrombosis can result from craniocerebral trauma; brain neoplasms; neurosurgical procedures; thrombophilia; and other conditions. Clinical features include headache; vertigo; and increased [MASK].

physicaltherapymodalities.name: physical therapy modalities
physicaltherapymodalities.definition: Physical therapy modalities is therapeutic modalities frequently used in physical therapy specialty by physical therapists or physiotherapists to promote, maintain, or restore the physical and physiological well-being of an individual.

leukocytetransfusion.name: leukocyte transfusion
leukocytetransfusion.definition: Leukocyte transfusion is the transfer of leukocytes from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor.

musclefatigue.name: muscle fatigue
musclefatigue.definition: Muscle fatigue is a state arrived at through prolonged and strong contraction of a muscle. Studies in [MASK] during prolonged submaximal exercise have shown that muscle fatigue increases in almost direct proportion to the rate of muscle glycogen depletion. Muscle fatigue in short-term maximal exercise is associated with oxygen lack and an increased level of blood and muscle lactic acid, and an accompanying increase in hydrogen-ion concentration in the exercised muscle.

insulinresistance.name: insulin resistance
insulinresistance.definition: Insulin resistance is diminished effectiveness of insulin in lowering blood sugar levels: requiring the use of 200 units or more of insulin per day to prevent hyperglycemia or ketosis.

afferentpathways.name: afferent pathways
afferentpathways.definition: Afferent pathways is nerve structures through which impulses are conducted from a peripheral part toward a nerve center.

lactoseintolerance.name: lactose intolerance
lactoseintolerance.definition: Lactose intolerance is the condition resulting from the absence or deficiency of lactase in the mucosa cells of the gastrointestinal tract, and the inability to break down lactose in milk for absorption. Bacterial fermentation of the unabsorbed lactose leads to symptoms that range from a mild indigestion (dyspepsia) to severe [MASK]. Lactose intolerance may be an inborn error or acquired.

autopsy.name: autopsy
autopsy.definition: Autopsy is postmortem examination of the body.

studyguide.name: study guide
studyguide.definition: Study guide is tool used to help facilitate learning and comprehension of a topic or to help prepare for an examination.

conversiondisorder.name: conversion disorder
conversiondisorder.definition: Conversion disorder is a disorder whose predominant feature is a loss or alteration in physical functioning that suggests a physical disorder but that is actually a direct expression of a [MASK] or need.

regulationorlaw.name: regulation or law
regulationorlaw.definition: Regulation or law is the science or philosophy of law. Also, the application of the principles of law and justice to health and medicine.

hearingtests.name: hearing tests
hearingtests.definition: Hearing tests is part of an ear examination that measures the ability of sound to reach the brain.

epilepsy,reflex.name: epilepsy , reflex
epilepsy,reflex.definition: Reflex epilepsy is a subtype of epilepsy characterized by seizures that are consistently provoked by a certain specific stimulus. Auditory, visual, and somatosensory stimuli as well as the acts of writing, reading, eating, and decision making are examples of events or activities that may induce seizure activity in affected individuals. (From Neurol Clin 1994 Feb;12(1):57-8)

organtransplantation.name: organ transplantation
organtransplantation.definition: Organ transplantation is transference of an organ between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

bonebanks.name: bone banks
bonebanks.definition: Bone banks is centers for acquiring, characterizing, and storing bones or bone tissue for future use.

dogdiseases.name: dog diseases
dogdiseases.definition: Dog diseases is diseases of the domestic dog (Canis familiaris). This term does not include diseases of wild dogs, wolves; foxes; and other Canidae for which the heading carnivora is used.

freeradicals.name: free radicals
freeradicals.definition: Free radicals is highly reactive molecules with an unsatisfied [MASK] valence pair. Free radicals are produced in both normal and pathological processes. They are proven or suspected agents of tissue damage in a wide variety of circumstances including radiation, damage from environment chemicals, and aging. Natural and pharmacological prevention of free radical damage is being actively investigated.

contactlenses.name: contact lenses
contactlenses.definition: Contact lenses is lenses designed to be worn on the front surface of the eyeball. (umdns, 1999)

vascularendothelialgrowthfactord.name: vascular endothelial growth factor d
vascularendothelialgrowthfactord.definition: Vascular endothelial growth factor d is a vascular endothelial growth factor that specifically binds to vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-3. In addition to being an angiogenic factor it can act on lymphatic vessels to stimulate lymphangiogenesis. It is similar in structure to [MASK] in that they both contain n- and C-terminal extensions that were not found in other vegf family members.

combinedmodalitytherapy.name: combined modality therapy
combinedmodalitytherapy.definition: Combined modality therapy is the treatment of a disease or condition by several different means simultaneously or sequentially. Chemoimmunotherapy, radioimmunotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, cryochemotherapy, and salvage therapy are seen most frequently, but their combinations with each other and surgery are also used.

diseasesusceptibility.name: disease susceptibility
diseasesusceptibility.definition: Disease susceptibility is a constitution or condition of the body which makes the tissues react in special ways to certain extrinsic stimuli and thus tends to make the individual more than usually susceptible to certain diseases.

advancedtraumalifesupportcare.name: advanced trauma life support care
advancedtraumalifesupportcare.definition: Advanced trauma life support care is the initial life support care of the severely injured patient.

socialworkdepartment,hospital.name: social work department , hospital
socialworkdepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital social work department is hospital department responsible for administering and providing social services to patients and their families.

libraryscience.name: library science
libraryscience.definition: Library science is study of the principles and practices of [MASK] and services.

systemsanalysis.name: systems analysis
systemsanalysis.definition: Systems analysis is the analysis of an activity, procedure, method, technique, or business to determine what must be accomplished and how the necessary operations may best be accomplished.

deoxysugars.name: deoxy sugars
deoxysugars.definition: Deoxy sugars is sugars that in which one or more hydroxyl groups of the pyranose or furanose ring is substituted by hydrogen.

hemoglobine.name: hemoglobin e
hemoglobine.definition: Hemoglobin e is an abnormal hemoglobin that results from the substitution of lysine for glutamic acid at position 26 of the beta chain. It is most frequently observed in southeast Asian populations.

macularpigment.name: macular pigment
macularpigment.definition: Macular pigment is a yellow pigment that accumulates in the macula lutea. It is composed of lutein, meso-zeaxanthin, and zeaxanthin.

aorticbodies.name: aortic bodies
aorticbodies.definition: Aortic bodies is small clusters of chemoreceptive and supporting cells located near the arch of the aorta; the [MASK]; and the coronary arteries. The aortic bodies sense ph; carbon dioxide; and oxygen concentrations in the blood and participate in the control of respiration. The aortic bodies should not be confused with the para-aortic bodies in the abdomen (which are sometimes also called aortic bodies).

viralstructuralproteins.name: viral structural proteins
viralstructuralproteins.definition: Viral structural proteins is viral proteins that are components of the mature assembled virus particles. They may include nucleocapsid core proteins (gag proteins), enzymes packaged within the virus particle (pol proteins), and membrane components (env proteins). These do not include the proteins encoded in the viral genome that are produced in infected cells but which are not packaged in the mature virus particle,i.e. the so called non-structural proteins (viral nonstructural proteins).

chemicalanddruginducedliverinjury.name: chemical and drug induced liver injury
chemicalanddruginducedliverinjury.definition: Chemical and drug induced liver injury is a spectrum of clinical liver diseases ranging from mild biochemical abnormalities to acute liver failure, caused by drugs, drug metabolites, herbal and dietary supplements and chemicals from the environment.

respect.name: respect
respect.definition: Respect is a feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities, qualities, or achievements and regard for the feelings, wishes, or rights of others.

chemistry,organic.name: chemistry , organic
chemistry,organic.definition: Organic chemistry is the study of the structure, preparation, properties, and reactions of carbon compounds. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

cerebralhemorrhage,traumatic.name: cerebral hemorrhage , traumatic
cerebralhemorrhage,traumatic.definition: Traumatic cerebral hemorrhage is bleeding into one or both cerebral hemispheres due to trauma. Hemorrhage may involve any part of the cerebral cortex and the basal ganglia. Depending on the severity of bleeding, clinical features may include seizures; aphasia; vision disorders; movement disorders; paralysis; and coma.

unitedstatesenvironmentalprotectionagenc.name: united states environmental protection agency
unitedstatesenvironmentalprotectionagenc.definition: United states environmental protection agency is an agency in the Executive Branch of the Federal Government. It was created as an independent regulatory agency responsible for the implementation of federal laws designed to protect the environment. Its mission is to protect human health and the environment.

infertility,male.name: infertility , male
infertility,male.definition: Male infertility is the inability of the male to effect fertilization of an ovum after a specified period of unprotected intercourse. Male sterility is permanent infertility.

tomography,spiralcomputed.name: tomography , spiral computed
tomography,spiralcomputed.definition: Spiral computed tomography is computed tomography where there is continuous X-ray exposure to the patient while being transported in a spiral or helical pattern through the beam of irradiation. This provides improved three-dimensional contrast and spatial resolution compared to conventional computed tomography, where data is obtained and computed from individual sequential exposures.

aminoacidtransportsysteml.name: amino acid transport system l
aminoacidtransportsysteml.definition: Amino acid transport system l is a sodium-independent neutral amino acid transporter system with specificity for large amino acids. One of the functions of the transporter system is to supply large neutral amino acids to the brain.

reversetranscriptaseinhibitors.name: reverse transcriptase inhibitors
reversetranscriptaseinhibitors.definition: Reverse transcriptase inhibitors is inhibitors of reverse transcriptase (rna-directed dna polymerase), an enzyme that synthesizes dna on an rna template.

screwworminfection.name: screw worm infection
screwworminfection.definition: Screw worm infection is infection with larvae of the blow fly Cochliomyia hominivorax (Callitroga americanum), a common cause of disease in livestock in the southern and southwestern u.s.a.

enzymes,immobilized.name: enzymes , immobilized
enzymes,immobilized.definition: Immobilized enzymes is enzymes which are immobilized on or in a variety of water-soluble or water-insoluble matrices with little or no loss of their catalytic activity. Since they can be reused continuously, immobilized enzymes have found wide application in the industrial, medical and research fields.

lungdiseases.name: lung diseases
lungdiseases.definition: Lung diseases is pathological processes involving any part of the lung.

medicalofficebuildings.name: medical office buildings
medicalofficebuildings.definition: Medical office buildings is office and laboratory facilities constructed for the use of physicians and other health personnel.

spermmotility.name: sperm motility
spermmotility.definition: Sperm motility is movement characteristics of spermatozoa in a fresh specimen. It is measured as the percentage of sperms that are moving, and as the percentage of sperms with productive flagellar motion such as rapid, linear, and forward progression.

insurancecarriers.name: insurance carriers
insurancecarriers.definition: Insurance carriers is organizations which assume the financial responsibility for the risks of policyholders.

cats.name: cats
cats.definition: Cats is the domestic cat, Felis catus, of the carnivore family felidae, comprising over 30 different breeds. The domestic cat is descended primarily from the wild cat of Africa and extreme southwestern Asia. Though probably present in towns in Palestine as long ago as 7000 years, actual domestication occurred in [MASK] about 4000 years ago. (From Walker's Mammals of the World, 6th ed, p801)

argonplasmacoagulation.name: argon plasma coagulation
argonplasmacoagulation.definition: [MASK] plasma coagulation is a method of tissue ablation and bleeding control that uses [MASK] plasma (ionized [MASK] gas) to deliver a current of thermocoagulating energy to the area of tissue to be coagulated.

jobdescription.name: job description
jobdescription.definition: Job description is statement of the position requirements, qualifications for the position, wage range, and any special conditions expected of the employee.

eyemovements.name: eye movements
eyemovements.definition: Eye movements is voluntary or reflex-controlled movements of the eye.

accidents,traffic.name: accidents , traffic
accidents,traffic.definition: Traffic accidents is accidents on streets, roads, and highways involving drivers, passengers, pedestrians, or vehicles. Traffic accidents refer to automobiles (passenger cars, buses, and trucks), bicycling, and motorcycles but not off-road motor vehicles; railroads nor snowmobiles.

erythrocyteindices.name: erythrocyte indices
erythrocyteindices.definition: Erythrocyte indices is erythrocyte size and hemoglobin content or concentration, usually derived from erythrocyte count; blood hemoglobin concentration; and hematocrit. The indices include the mean corpuscular volume (mcv), the mean corpuscular hemoglobin (mch), and the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (mchc).

contrastsensitivity.name: contrast sensitivity
contrastsensitivity.definition: Contrast sensitivity is the ability to detect sharp boundaries (stimuli) and to detect slight changes in luminance at regions without distinct contours. Psychophysical measurements of this visual function are used to evaluate visual acuity and to detect eye disease.

openabdomentechniques.name: open abdomen techniques
openabdomentechniques.definition: Open abdomen techniques is abdominal wound closure techniques in which the opening from a laparoscopic abdominal incision is left open, but covered, to reduce or prevent intra-abdominal hypertension.

allergens.name: allergens
allergens.definition: Allergens is antigen-type substances that produce immediate hypersensitivity (hypersensitivity, immediate).

sulfuracids.name: sulfur acids
sulfuracids.definition: Sulfur acids is inorganic or organic acids that contain sulfur as an integral part of the molecule.

geneflow.name: gene flow
geneflow.definition: Gene flow is the change in gene frequency in a population due to migration of gametes or individuals ([MASK]) across population barriers. In contrast, in [MASK] the cause of gene frequency changes are not a result of population or gamete movement.

clinicalattribute.name: clinical attribute
clinicalattribute.definition: Clinical attribute is clinical characteristics of disease or illness.

chlorinecompounds.name: chlorine compounds
chlorinecompounds.definition: Chlorine compounds is inorganic compounds that contain chlorine as an integral part of the molecule.

animalassistedtherapy.name: animal assisted therapy
animalassistedtherapy.definition: Animal assisted therapy is the use of live animal as a means of therapy

mentalhealthservices.name: mental health services
mentalhealthservices.definition: Mental health services is organized services to provide mental health care.

dermatitis,contact.name: dermatitis , contact
dermatitis,contact.definition: Contact dermatitis is a type of acute or chronic skin reaction in which sensitivity is manifested by reactivity to materials or substances coming in contact with the skin. It may involve allergic or non-allergic mechanisms.

generalpractitioners.name: general practitioners
generalpractitioners.definition: General practitioners is physicians whose practice is not restricted to a specific field of medicine.

cellselfrenewal.name: cell self renewal
cellselfrenewal.definition: Cell self renewal is the ability of certain cell types, such as progenitor cells or tumor cells,  to go through numerous cycles of cell division while still maintaining an undifferentiated or partially differentiated state.

occupationalmedicine.name: occupational medicine
occupationalmedicine.definition: Occupational medicine is medical specialty concerned with the promotion and maintenance of the physical and mental health of employees in occupational settings.

nitricoxidesynthasetypeiii.name: nitric oxide synthase type iii
nitricoxidesynthasetypeiii.definition: [MASK] synthase type iii is a CALCIUM-dependent, constitutively-expressed form of [MASK] synthase found primarily in endothelial cells.

medicineinthearts.name: medicine in the arts
medicineinthearts.definition: Medicine in the arts is depiction of medical issues or themes via the arts including visual, oral, or written forms of expression.

cardiacpacing,artificial.name: cardiac pacing , artificial
cardiacpacing,artificial.definition: Artificial cardiac pacing is regulation of the rate of contraction of the heart muscles by an artificial pacemaker.

polyi.name: poly i
polyi.definition: Poly i is a group of inosine ribonucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each inosine ribonucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the ribose moieties.

governmentagencies.name: government agencies
governmentagencies.definition: Government agencies is administrative units of government responsible for policy making and management of governmental activities.

wristjoint.name: wrist joint
wristjoint.definition: Wrist joint is the joint that is formed by the distal end of the [MASK], the articular disc of the distal radioulnar joint, and the proximal row of carpal bones; (scaphoid bone; lunate bone; triquetral bone).

administration,intravenous.name: administration , intravenous
administration,intravenous.definition: Intravenous administration is delivery of substances through venipuncture into the veins.

tuberculosis,spinal.name: tuberculosis , spinal
tuberculosis,spinal.definition: Spinal tuberculosis is osteitis or caries of the vertebrae, usually occurring as a complication of tuberculosis of the lungs.

sexualbehavior.name: sexual behavior
sexualbehavior.definition: Sexual behavior is sexual activities of humans.

relaxation.name: relaxation
relaxation.definition: Relaxation is activity which reduces the feelings of tension and the effects of stress, physiological.

rna,transfer,tyr.name: rna , transfer , tyr
rna,transfer,tyr.definition: Tyr transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying tyrosine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

streptomycin.name: streptomycin
streptomycin.definition: Streptomycin is an antibiotic produced by the soil actinomycete Streptomyces griseus. It acts by inhibiting the initiation and elongation processes during protein synthesis.

facilitydesignandconstruction.name: facility design and construction
facilitydesignandconstruction.definition: Facility design and construction is architecture, exterior and interior design, and construction of facilities other than hospitals, e.g., dental schools, medical schools, ambulatory care clinics, and specified units of health care facilities. The concept also includes architecture, design, and construction of specialized contained, controlled, or closed research environments including those of space labs and stations.

corrosion.name: corrosion
corrosion.definition: Corrosion is the gradual destruction of a metal or alloy due to oxidation or action of a chemical agent. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

bonemarrowtransplantation.name: bone marrow transplantation
bonemarrowtransplantation.definition: Bone marrow transplantation is the transference of bone marrow from one human or animal to another for a variety of purposes including hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or mesenchymal stem cell transplantation.

rheumatology.name: rheumatology
rheumatology.definition: Rheumatology is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of inflammatory or degenerative processes and metabolic derangement of connective tissue structures which pertain to a variety of musculoskeletal disorders, such as arthritis.

motorneurondisease.name: motor neuron disease
motorneurondisease.definition: Motor neuron disease is diseases characterized by a selective degeneration of the motor neurons of the spinal cord, brainstem, or motor cortex. Clinical subtypes are distinguished by the major site of degeneration. In amyotrophic lateral [MASK] there is involvement of upper, lower, and brainstem motor neurons. In progressive muscular atrophy and related syndromes (see muscular atrophy, spinal) the motor neurons in the spinal cord are primarily affected. With progressive bulbar palsy (bulbar palsy, progressive), the initial degeneration occurs in the brainstem. In primary lateral [MASK], the cortical neurons are affected in isolation. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1089)

unnecessaryprocedures.name: unnecessary procedures
unnecessaryprocedures.definition: Unnecessary procedures is diagnostic, therapeutic, and investigative procedures prescribed and performed by health professionals, the results of which do not justify the benefits or hazards and costs to the patient.

nuclearfamily.name: nuclear family
nuclearfamily.definition: Nuclear family is a family composed of spouses and their children.

choleratoxin.name: cholera toxin
choleratoxin.definition: Cholera toxin is an enterotoxin from vibrio cholerae. It consists of two major protomers, the heavy (h) or a subunit and the b protomer which consists of 5 light (l) or b subunits. The catalytic a subunit is proteolytically cleaved into fragments a1 and a2. The a1 fragment is a mono(adp-ribose) transferase. The b protomer binds cholera toxin to intestinal epithelial cells, and facilitates the uptake of the a1 fragment. The a1 catalyzed transfer of adp-ribose to the alpha subunits of heterotrimeric g proteins activates the production of cyclic amp. Increased levels of cyclic amp are thought to modulate release of fluid and electrolytes from intestinal crypt cells.

poultry.name: poultry
poultry.definition: Poultry is domesticated birds raised for food. It typically includes [MASK]; turkeys, ducks; geese; and others.

heartarrest,induced.name: heart arrest , induced
heartarrest,induced.definition: Induced heart arrest is a procedure to stop the contraction of myocardium during heart surgery. It is usually achieved with the use of chemicals (cardioplegic solutions) or cold temperature (such as chilled perfusate).

yellownailsyndrome.name: yellow nail syndrome
