yellownailsyndrome.definition: Yellow nail syndrome is a rare condition characterized by the presence of yellow nails, lymphedema, and/or pleural effusion with respiratory tract involvement. Abnormal lymphatic network may play a role in its etiology. Occasionally inherited, yellow nail syndrome mostly is sporadic without apparent family history.

models,biological.name: models , biological
models,biological.definition: Biological models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of biological processes or diseases. For disease models in living animals, disease models, animal is available. Biological models include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

anxiety.name: anxiety
anxiety.definition: Anxiety is feelings or emotions of dread, apprehension, and impending disaster but not disabling as with anxiety disorders.

judgment.name: judgment
judgment.definition: Judgment is the process of discovering or asserting an objective or intrinsic relation between two objects or concepts; a faculty or power that enables a person to make judgments; the process of bringing to light and asserting the implicit meaning of a concept; a critical evaluation of a person or situation.

thoracicnerves.name: thoracic nerves
thoracicnerves.definition: Thoracic nerves is the twelve spinal nerves on each side of the thorax. They include eleven intercostal nerves and one subcostal nerve. Both sensory and motor, they supply the muscles and skin of the thoracic and abdominal walls.

aberrantcryptfoci.name: aberrant crypt foci
aberrantcryptfoci.definition: Aberrant crypt foci is clusters of colonic crypts that appear different from the surrounding mucosa when visualized after staining. They are of interest as putative precursors to colorectal adenomas and potential biomarkers for colorectal carcinoma.

databases,pharmaceutical.name: databases , pharmaceutical
databases,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical databases is databases devoted to knowledge about pharmaceutical products.

lenscapsule,crystalline.name: lens capsule , crystalline
lenscapsule,crystalline.definition: Crystalline lens capsule is the thin noncellular outer covering of the crystalline lens composed mainly of collagen type iv and glycosaminoglycans. It is secreted by the embryonic anterior and posterior epithelium. The embryonic posterior epithelium later disappears.

leukocytecount.name: leukocyte count
leukocytecount.definition: Leukocyte count is the number of [MASK] blood cells per unit volume in venous blood. a differential leukocyte count measures the relative numbers of the different types of [MASK] cells.

air.name: air
air.definition: Air is the mixture of gases present in the earth's atmosphere consisting of oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and small amounts of other gases.

verticaldimension.name: vertical dimension
verticaldimension.definition: Vertical dimension is the length of the face determined by the distance of separation of jaws. Occlusal vertical dimension (ovd or vdo) or contact vertical dimension is the lower face height with the teeth in centric occlusion. Rest vertical dimension (vdr) is the lower face height measured from a [MASK] point to a point just below the nose, with the mandible in rest position. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p250)

genetransfertechniques.name: gene transfer techniques
genetransfertechniques.definition: Gene transfer techniques is the introduction of functional (usually cloned) genes into cells. a variety of techniques and naturally occurring processes are used for the gene transfer such as cell hybridization, liposomes or microcell-mediated gene transfer, electroporation, chromosome-mediated gene transfer, transfection, and genetic transduction. Gene transfer may result in genetically transformed cells and individual organisms.

ribosomesubunits,large.name: ribosome subunits , large
ribosomesubunits,large.definition: Large ribosome subunits is the largest ribonucleoprotein component of ribosomes. It contains the domains which catalyze formation of the peptide bond and translocation of the ribosome along the messenger rna during genetic translation.

angiography,digitalsubtraction.name: angiography , digital subtraction
angiography,digitalsubtraction.definition: Digital subtraction angiography is a method of delineating blood vessels by subtracting a tissue background image from an image of tissue plus intravascular contrast material that attenuates the X-ray [MASK]. The background image is determined from a digitized image taken a few moments before injection of the contrast material. The resulting angiogram is a high-contrast image of the vessel. This subtraction technique allows extraction of a high-intensity signal from the superimposed background information. The image is thus the result of the differential absorption of X-rays by different tissues.

nutritionpolicy.name: nutrition policy
nutritionpolicy.definition: Nutrition policy is guidelines and objectives pertaining to food supply and nutrition including recommendations for healthy diet.

humangenetics.name: human genetics
humangenetics.definition: Human genetics is the scientific study of inherited human variation.

sexchromatin.name: sex chromatin
sexchromatin.definition: [MASK] chromatin is in the interphase nucleus, a condensed mass of chromatin representing an inactivated x chromosome. Each x chromosome, in excess of one, forms [MASK] chromatin (Barr body) in the mammalian nucleus. (from King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

hepatitisantibodies.name: hepatitis antibodies
hepatitisantibodies.definition: Hepatitis antibodies is immunoglobulins raised by any form of viral hepatitis; some of these antibodies are used to diagnose the specific kind of hepatitis.

skeleton.name: skeleton
skeleton.definition: Skeleton is the rigid framework of connected bones that gives form to the body, protects and supports its soft organs and tissues, and provides attachments for muscles.

latinamerica.name: latin america
latinamerica.definition: Latin america is the geographic area of Latin America in general and when the specific country or countries are not indicated. It usually includes Central America, South America, [MASK], and the islands of the Caribbean.

motordisorders.name: motor disorders
motordisorders.definition: Motor disorders is motor skills deficits that significantly and persistently interfere with activities of daily living appropriate to chronological age.  (from dsm-5)

liverregeneration.name: liver regeneration
liverregeneration.definition: Liver regeneration is repair or renewal of hepatic tissue.

pathology,clinical.name: pathology , clinical
pathology,clinical.definition: Clinical pathology is a subspecialty of pathology applied to the solution of clinical problems, especially the use of laboratory methods in clinical diagnosis. (Dorland, 28th ed.)

iodideperoxidase.name: iodide peroxidase
iodideperoxidase.definition: Iodide peroxidase is a hemeprotein that catalyzes the oxidation of the iodide radical to iodine with the subsequent iodination of many organic compounds, particularly proteins. ec 1.11.1.8.

electronmicroscopetomography.name: electron microscope tomography
electronmicroscopetomography.definition: [MASK] microscope tomography is a tomographic technique for obtaining 3-dimensional images with transmission [MASK] microscopy.

healthmaintenanceorganizations.name: health maintenance organizations
healthmaintenanceorganizations.definition: Health maintenance organizations is organized systems for providing comprehensive prepaid health care that have five basic attributes: (1) provide care in a defined geographic area; (2) provide or ensure delivery of an agreed-upon [MASK] of basic and supplemental health maintenance and treatment services; (3) provide care to a voluntarily enrolled group of persons; (4) require their enrollees to use the services of designated providers; and (5) receive reimbursement through a predetermined, fixed, periodic prepayment made by the enrollee without regard to the degree of services provided. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

gingivalhyperplasia.name: gingival hyperplasia
gingivalhyperplasia.definition: Gingival hyperplasia is non-inflammatory enlargement of the gingivae produced by factors other than local irritation. It is characteristically due to an increase in the number of cells. (From Jablonski's Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p400)

geneticphenomena.name: genetic phenomena
geneticphenomena.definition: Genetic phenomena is the biological processes, properties, and objects that are involved in maintaining, expressing, and transmitting from one organism to another, genetically encoded traits.

inheritancepatterns.name: inheritance patterns
inheritancepatterns.definition: Inheritance patterns is the different ways genes and their alleles interact during the transmission of genetic traits that effect the outcome of gene expression.

glycogenstoragediseasetypev.name: glycogen storage disease type v
glycogenstoragediseasetypev.definition: Glycogen storage disease type v is glycogenosis due to muscle phosphorylase deficiency. Characterized by painful cramps following sustained exercise.

dictionary,chemical.name: dictionary , chemical
dictionary,chemical.definition: Chemical dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to chemistry-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

carcinoma256,walker.name: carcinoma 256 , walker
carcinoma256,walker.definition: Walker carcinoma 256 is a transplantable carcinoma of the rat that originally appeared spontaneously in the mammary gland of a pregnant albino rat, and which now resembles a carcinoma in young [MASK] and a sarcoma in older [MASK]. (Stedman, 25th ed)

creatinekinase,mmform.name: creatine kinase , mm form
creatinekinase,mmform.definition: Mm form creatine kinase is an isoenzyme of creatine kinase found in the muscle.

oxytocin.name: oxytocin
oxytocin.definition: Oxytocin is a nonapeptide hormone released from the [MASK] ([MASK]). It differs from vasopressin by two amino acids at residues 3 and 8. Oxytocin acts on smooth muscle cells, such as causing [MASK] and milk ejection.

intercellularjunctions.name: intercellular junctions
intercellularjunctions.definition: Intercellular junctions is direct contact of a cell with a neighboring cell. Most such junctions are too small to be resolved by light microscopy, but they can be visualized by conventional or freeze-fracture [MASK] microscopy, both of which show that the interacting cell membrane and often the underlying cytoplasm and the intervening extracellular space are highly specialized in these regions. (From Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2d ed, p792)

mitochondrialdiseases.name: mitochondrial diseases
mitochondrialdiseases.definition: Mitochondrial diseases is diseases caused by abnormal function of the mitochondria. They may be caused by mutations, acquired or inherited, in mitochondrial dna or in nuclear genes that code for mitochondrial components. They may also be the result of acquired mitochondria dysfunction due to adverse effects of drugs, infections, or other environmental causes.

colorperception.name: color perception
colorperception.definition: [MASK] perception is mental processing of chromatic signals ([MASK] vision) from the eye by the visual cortex where they are converted into symbolic representations. [MASK] perception involves numerous neurons, and is influenced not only by the distribution of wavelengths from the viewed object, but also by its background [MASK] and brightness contrast at its boundary.

rna,transfer,glu.name: rna , transfer , glu
rna,transfer,glu.definition: Glu transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying glutamic acid to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

substanceabusetreatmentcenters.name: substance abuse treatment centers
substanceabusetreatmentcenters.definition: Substance abuse treatment centers is health facilities providing therapy and/or rehabilitation for substance-dependent individuals. Methadone distribution centers are included.

magneticfields.name: magnetic fields
magneticfields.definition: Magnetic fields is areas of attractive or repulsive force surrounding [MASK].

psychosocialdeprivation.name: psychosocial deprivation
psychosocialdeprivation.definition: Psychosocial deprivation is the absence of appropriate stimuli in the physical or social environment which are necessary for the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the individual.

endurancetraining.name: endurance training
endurancetraining.definition: Endurance training is exercise programs of relatively long duration and moderate intensity, which enhance maximal oxygen uptake, increasing physical stamina.

animals,newborn.name: animals , newborn
animals,newborn.definition: Newborn animals is refers to animals in the period of time just after birth.

carcinoma,ductal.name: carcinoma , ductal
carcinoma,ductal.definition: Ductal carcinoma is malignant neoplasms involving the ductal systems of any of a number of organs, such as the mammary glands, the pancreas, the prostate, or the lacrimal gland.

massspectrometry.name: mass spectrometry
massspectrometry.definition: Mass spectrometry is an analytical method used in determining the identity of a chemical based on its mass using mass analyzers/mass spectrometers.

intracellularfluid.name: intracellular fluid
intracellularfluid.definition: Intracellular fluid is the fluid inside cells.

occupationalstress.name: occupational stress
occupationalstress.definition: Occupational stress is adverse psychological and behavioral reactions caused by the pressures and demands of employers or clients or other factors, such as the physical environment of the workplace, workplace violence; or workplace bullying.

radiationinjuries,experimental.name: radiation injuries , experimental
radiationinjuries,experimental.definition: Experimental radiation injuries is experimentally produced harmful effects of ionizing or non-ionizing radiation in chordata animals.

cartilagediseases.name: cartilage diseases
cartilagediseases.definition: Cartilage diseases is pathological processes involving the chondral tissue (cartilage).

peakexpiratoryflowrate.name: peak expiratory flow rate
peakexpiratoryflowrate.definition: Peak expiratory flow rate is measurement of the maximum rate of airflow attained during a forced vital capacity determination. Common abbreviations are pefr and pfr.

commoncold.name: common cold
commoncold.definition: Common cold is a catarrhal disorder of the upper respiratory tract, which may be viral or a mixed infection. It generally involves a runny nose, nasal congestion, and sneezing.

antigens,differentiation.name: antigens , differentiation
antigens,differentiation.definition: Differentiation antigens is antigens expressed primarily on the membranes of living cells during sequential stages of maturation and differentiation. As immunologic markers they have high organ and tissue specificity and are useful as probes in studies of normal cell development as well as neoplastic transformation.

pulmonaryfibrosis.name: pulmonary fibrosis
pulmonaryfibrosis.definition: Pulmonary fibrosis is a process in which normal lung tissues are progressively replaced by fibroblasts and collagen causing an irreversible loss of the ability to transfer oxygen into the bloodstream via pulmonary alveoli. Patients show progressive dyspnea finally resulting in death.

ophthalmicsolutions.name: ophthalmic solutions
ophthalmicsolutions.definition: Ophthalmic solutions is sterile solutions that are intended for instillation into the eye. It does not include solutions for cleaning eyeglasses or contact lens solutions.

lipida.name: lipid a
lipida.definition: Lipid a is lipid a is the biologically active component of lipopolysaccharides. It shows strong endotoxic activity and exhibits immunogenic properties.

microscopy,acoustic.name: microscopy , acoustic
microscopy,acoustic.definition: Acoustic microscopy is a scientific tool based on ultrasonography and used not only for the [MASK] of microstructure in metalwork but also in living tissue. In biomedical application, the acoustic propagation speed in normal and abnormal tissues can be quantified to distinguish their tissue elasticity and other properties.

ethylchloride.name: ethyl chloride
ethylchloride.definition: Ethyl chloride is a gas that condenses under slight pressure. Because of its low boiling point ethyl chloride sprayed on skin produces an intense cold by evaporation. Cold blocks [MASK]. Ethyl chloride has been used in surgery but is primarily used to relieve local pain in sports medicine.

mentaldisorders.name: mental disorders
mentaldisorders.definition: Mental disorders is psychiatric illness or diseases manifested by breakdowns in the adaptational process expressed primarily as abnormalities of thought, feeling, and behavior producing either distress or impairment of function.

hemodialysisunits,hospital.name: hemodialysis units , hospital
hemodialysisunits,hospital.definition: Hospital hemodialysis units is hospital units in which care is provided the hemodialysis patient. This includes hemodialysis centers in hospitals.

heartvalveprosthesis.name: heart valve prosthesis
heartvalveprosthesis.definition: Heart valve prosthesis is a device that substitutes for a heart valve. It may be composed of biological material (bioprosthesis) and/or synthetic material.

digestivesystemdiseases.name: digestive system diseases
digestivesystemdiseases.definition: Digestive system diseases is diseases in any part of the gastrointestinal tract or the accessory organs (liver; biliary tract; pancreas).

posteriorhorncells.name: posterior horn cells
posteriorhorncells.definition: Posterior horn cells is neurons in the spinal cord dorsal horn whose cell bodies and processes are confined entirely to the central nervous system. They receive collateral or direct terminations of dorsal root fibers. They send their axons either directly to anterior horn cells or to the [MASK] matter ascending and descending longitudinal fibers.

communication.name: communication
communication.definition: Communication is the exchange or transmission of ideas, attitudes, or beliefs between individuals or groups.

magnesiumdeficiency.name: magnesium deficiency
magnesiumdeficiency.definition: Magnesium deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of magnesium in the diet, characterized by anorexia, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and weakness. Symptoms are paresthesias, muscle cramps, irritability, decreased attention span, and mental confusion, possibly requiring months to appear. Deficiency of body magnesium can exist even when serum values are normal. In addition, magnesium deficiency may be organ-selective, since certain tissues become deficient before others. (Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p1936)

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 3
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.definition: Member 3 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette, subfamily b, protein that functions in the transport of antigens from the cytoplasm to the endoplasmic reticulum for association with histocompatibility antigens class i peptides. It functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b, member 2.

hereditarycomplementdeficiencydiseases.name: hereditary complement deficiency diseases
hereditarycomplementdeficiencydiseases.definition: Hereditary complement deficiency diseases is genetic disorders due to mutations in genes involved in complement system proteins. They are often classified into distinct pathway of complement activation where causative mutations are found (e.g., classical pathway, lectin pathway, alternative pathway, and terminal complement pathway).

ambulatorycarefacilities.name: ambulatory care facilities
ambulatorycarefacilities.definition: Ambulatory care facilities is those facilities which administer health services to individuals who do not require hospitalization or institutionalization.

socialconditions.name: social conditions
socialconditions.definition: Social conditions is the state of society as it exists or in flux. While it usually refers to society as a whole in a specified geographical or political region, it is applicable also to restricted strata of a society.

newyorkcity.name: new york city
newyorkcity.definition: New york city is city located at the mouth of the Hudson [MASK], in New York State.

behaviorcontrol.name: behavior control
behaviorcontrol.definition: Behavior control is manipulation of the behavior of persons or animals by biomedical, physical, psychological, or social means, including for nontherapeutic reasons.

evansblue.name: evans blue
evansblue.definition: Evans blue is an azo dye used in blood volume and cardiac output measurement by the dye dilution method. It is very soluble, strongly bound to plasma albumin, and disappears very slowly.

headache.name: headache
headache.definition: Headache is the symptom of pain in the cranial region. It may be an isolated benign occurrence or manifestation of a wide variety of headache disorders.

programmedinstructionsastopic.name: programmed instructions as topic
programmedinstructionsastopic.definition: Programmed instructions as topic is works about instruction in which learners progress at their own rate using workbooks, textbooks, or electromechanical devices that provide information in discrete steps, test learning at each step, and provide immediate [MASK] about achievement. (eric, Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, 1996).

deer.name: deer
deer.definition: Deer is the family Cervidae of 17 genera and 45 species occurring nearly throughout North America, South America, and Eurasia, on most associated continental islands, and in northern Africa. Wild populations of deer have been established through introduction by people in Cuba, [MASK], Australia, [MASK], and other places where the family does not naturally occur. They are slim, long-legged and best characterized by the presence of antlers. Their habitat is forests, [MASK], brush country, deserts, and arctic tundra. They are usually good swimmers; some migrate seasonally. (Walker's Mammals of the World, 5th ed, p1362)

diet,reducing.name: diet , reducing
diet,reducing.definition: Reducing diet is a diet designed to cause an individual to lose weight.

lengthofstay.name: length of stay
lengthofstay.definition: Length of stay is the period of confinement of a patient to a hospital or other health facility.

receptors,nervegrowthfactor.name: receptors , nerve growth factor
receptors,nervegrowthfactor.definition: Nerve growth factor receptors is cell surface receptors that bind nerve growth factor; (ngf) and a NGF-related family of neurotrophic factors that includes neurotrophins, brain-derived neurotrophic factor and ciliary neurotrophic factor.

metals.name: metals
metals.definition: Metals is electropositive chemical elements characterized by ductility, malleability, luster, and conductance of heat and electricity. They can replace the hydrogen of an acid and form bases with hydroxyl radicals. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

replicationproteina.name: replication protein a
replicationproteina.definition: Replication protein a is a single-stranded DNA-binding protein that is found in eukaryotic cells. It is required for dna replication; dna repair; and genetic recombination.

parathyroiddiseases.name: parathyroid diseases
parathyroiddiseases.definition: Parathyroid diseases is pathological processes of the [MASK]. They usually manifest as hypersecretion or hyposecretion of parathyroid hormone that regulates the balance of calcium; phosphorus; and magnesium in the body.

hierarchy,social.name: hierarchy , social
hierarchy,social.definition: Social hierarchy is social rank-order established by certain behavioral patterns.

managementaudit.name: management audit
managementaudit.definition: Management audit is management review designed to evaluate efficiency and to identify areas in need of management improvement within the institution in order to ensure effectiveness in meeting organizational goals.

aspirin.name: aspirin
aspirin.definition: Aspirin is the prototypical analgesic used in the treatment of mild to moderate pain. It has anti-inflammatory and antipyretic properties and acts as an inhibitor of cyclooxygenase which results in the inhibition of the biosynthesis of prostaglandins. Aspirin also inhibits [MASK] and is used in the prevention of arterial and venous thrombosis. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p5)

ohio.name: ohio
ohio.definition: Ohio is state bounded on the north by Michigan and [MASK] Erie, on the east by Ohio [MASK] and Pennsylvania, on the south by Ohio [MASK], and on the west by Indiana.

latentautoimmunediabetesinadults.name: latent autoimmune diabetes in adults
latentautoimmunediabetesinadults.definition: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults is autoimmune diabetes in adults with slowly progressive pancreatic beta cell failure and the presence of circulating autoantibodies to pancreatic islets cell antigens.

receptors,antigen.name: receptors , antigen
receptors,antigen.definition: Antigen receptors is molecules on the surface of b- and T-lymphocytes that recognize and combine with specific antigens.

embolism,fat.name: embolism , fat
embolism,fat.definition: Fat embolism is blocking of a blood vessel by fat deposits in the circulation. It is often seen after fractures of large bones or after administration of corticosteroids.

membraneglycoproteins.name: membrane glycoproteins
membraneglycoproteins.definition: Membrane glycoproteins is glycoproteins found on the membrane or surface of cells.

endometrialneoplasms.name: endometrial neoplasms
endometrialneoplasms.definition: Endometrial neoplasms is tumors or cancer of endometrium, the mucous lining of the uterus. These neoplasms can be benign or malignant. Their classification and grading are based on the various cell types and the percent of undifferentiated cells.

insurance,hospitalization.name: insurance , hospitalization
insurance,hospitalization.definition: Hospitalization insurance is health insurance providing benefits to cover or partly cover hospital expenses.

rarebooks.name: rare books
rarebooks.definition: Rare books is books that are limited in availability, have early printing dates or special characteristics that increase the value of an individual copy, print run, or edition.

nursespecialists.name: nurse specialists
nursespecialists.definition: Nurse specialists is nursing professionals whose practice is limited to a particular area or discipline of medicine.

factorix.name: factor ix
factorix.definition: Factor ix is storage-stable blood coagulation factor acting in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. Its activated form, IXa, forms a complex with factor viii and calcium on platelet factor 3 to activate factor x to Xa. Deficiency of factor ix results in hemophilia b (Christmas Disease).

therapeuticirrigation.name: therapeutic irrigation
therapeuticirrigation.definition: Therapeutic irrigation is the washing of a body cavity or surface by flowing water or solution for therapy or diagnosis.

backgroundradiation.name: background radiation
backgroundradiation.definition: Background radiation is radiation from sources other than the source of interest. It is due to cosmic rays and natural radioactivity in the environment.

bloodvolumedetermination.name: blood volume determination
bloodvolumedetermination.definition: Blood volume determination is method for determining the circulating blood volume by introducing a known quantity of foreign substance into the blood and determining its concentration some minutes later when thorough mixing has occurred. From these two values the blood volume can be calculated by dividing the quantity of injected material by its concentration in the blood at the time of uniform mixing. Generally expressed as cubic centimeters or liters per kilogram of body weight.

uterinecervicaldysplasia.name: uterine cervical dysplasia
uterinecervicaldysplasia.definition: Uterine cervical dysplasia is abnormal development of immature squamous epithelial cells of the uterine cervix, a term used to describe premalignant cytological changes in the cervical epithelium. These atypical cells do not penetrate the epithelial basement membrane.

qualityassurance,healthcare.name: quality assurance , health care
qualityassurance,healthcare.definition: Health care quality assurance is activities and programs intended to assure or improve the quality of care in either a defined medical setting or a program. The concept includes the assessment or evaluation of the quality of care; identification of problems or shortcomings in the delivery of care; designing activities to overcome these deficiencies; and follow-up monitoring to ensure effectiveness of corrective steps.

heartdiseases.name: heart diseases
heartdiseases.definition: Heart diseases is pathological conditions involving the heart including its structural and functional abnormalities.

receptors,kir.name: receptors , kir
receptors,kir.definition: Kir receptors is a family of receptors found on nk cells that have specificity for a variety of hla antigens. kir receptors contain up to three different extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains referred to as d0, d1, and d2 and play an important role in blocking nk cell activation against cells expressing the appropriate hla antigens thus preventing cell lysis. Although they are often referred to as being inhibitory receptors, a subset of kir receptors may also play an activating role in nk cells.

sheep.name: sheep
sheep.definition: Sheep is any of the ruminant mammals with curved horns in the genus Ovis, family Bovidae. They possess lachrymal grooves and interdigital glands, which are absent in goats.

ecologicalparametermonitoring.name: ecological parameter monitoring
ecologicalparametermonitoring.definition: Ecological parameter monitoring is ongoing collection, analysis, and interpretation of ecological data that is used to assess changes in the components, processes, and overall condition and functioning of an ecosystem.

dentin.name: dentin
dentin.definition: Dentin is the hard portion of the tooth surrounding the pulp, covered by enamel on the crown and cementum on the root, which is harder and denser than bone but softer than enamel, and is thus readily abraded when left unprotected. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992)

nadphdehydrogenase.name: nadph dehydrogenase
nadphdehydrogenase.definition: Nadph dehydrogenase is a flavoprotein that reversibly oxidizes nadph to nadp and a reduced acceptor. ec 1.6.99.1.

capsules.name: capsules
capsules.definition: Capsules is hard or soft soluble containers used for the oral administration of medicine.

ionexchange.name: ion exchange
ionexchange.definition: Ion exchange is reversible chemical reaction between a solid, often one of the ion exchange resins, and a fluid whereby ions may be exchanged from one substance to another. This technique is used in [MASK], in research, and in industry.

addictionmedicine.name: addiction medicine
addictionmedicine.definition: Addiction medicine is a medical specialty focused on the diagnosis and treatment of addictive behavior disorders, including substance-related disorders and impulse control disorders; and the management of co-occurring medical and psychiatric conditions

pyruvatedehydrogenasecomplexdeficiencydi.name: pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency disease
pyruvatedehydrogenasecomplexdeficiencydi.definition: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency disease is an inherited metabolic disorder caused by deficient enzyme activity in the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, resulting in deficiency of acetyl CoA and reduced synthesis of acetylcholine. Two clinical forms are recognized: neonatal and juvenile. The neonatal form is a relatively common cause of [MASK] in the first weeks of life and may also feature an erythematous rash. The juvenile form presents with [MASK], alopecia, intermittent ataxia; seizures; and an erythematous rash. (From j Inherit Metab Dis 1996;19(4):452-62) Autosomal recessive and X-linked forms are caused by mutations in the genes for the three different enzyme components of this multisubunit pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. One of the mutations at Xp22.2-p22.1 in the gene for the e1 alpha component of the complex leads to leigh disease.

electricinjuries.name: electric injuries
electricinjuries.definition: Electric injuries is injuries caused by electric currents. The concept excludes electric burns (burns, electric), but includes accidental electrocution and electric shock.

atrialfunction,right.name: atrial function , right
atrialfunction,right.definition: Right atrial function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the right atrium.

celladhesionmolecules,neuronal.name: cell adhesion molecules , neuronal
celladhesionmolecules,neuronal.definition: Neuronal cell adhesion molecules is surface ligands that mediate cell-to-cell adhesion and function in the assembly and interconnection of the vertebrate nervous system. These molecules promote cell adhesion via a homophilic mechanism. These are not to be confused with neural cell adhesion molecules, now known to be expressed in a variety of tissues and cell types in addition to nervous tissue.

immunoglobulinfabfragments.name: immunoglobulin fab fragments
immunoglobulinfabfragments.definition: Immunoglobulin fab fragments is univalent antigen-binding fragments composed of one entire immunoglobulin light chain and the amino terminal end of one of the [MASK] from the hinge region, linked to each other by disulfide bonds. Fab contains the immunoglobulin variable regions, which are part of the antigen-binding site, and the first immunoglobulin constant regions. This fragment can be obtained by [MASK] of immunoglobulins with the proteolytic enzyme papain.

transportationfacilities.name: transportation facilities
transportationfacilities.definition: Transportation facilities is places such as airports, bus stations, and train stations that are used for managing arriving and departing transport vehicles, and included facilities for handling passengers.

youngadult.name: young adult
youngadult.definition: Young adult is a person between 19 and 24 years of age.

typeiiisecretionsystems.name: type iii secretion systems
typeiiisecretionsystems.definition: Type iii secretion systems is multiprotein transmembrane complexes in gram-negative bacteria involved in either the secretion of effector proteins from the bacterial cytoplasm into host cells, or the secretion and assembly of flagellar components. The major component of the T3SSs is called the injectosome or needle complex.

siliconcompounds.name: silicon compounds
siliconcompounds.definition: Silicon compounds is inorganic compounds that contain silicon as an integral part of the molecule.

vitalstatistics.name: vital statistics
vitalstatistics.definition: Vital statistics is used for general articles concerning statistics of births, deaths, marriages, etc.

musculoskeletaldevelopment.name: musculoskeletal development
musculoskeletaldevelopment.definition: Musculoskeletal development is the morphologic and physiological changes of the muscles, bones (bone and bones), and cartilage of the body, i.e., musculoskeletal system, during the prenatal and postnatal stages of development.

blooddonors.name: blood donors
blooddonors.definition: Blood donors is a person who gives blood for use in transfusion.

follicularcyst.name: follicular cyst
follicularcyst.definition: Follicular cyst is cyst due to the occlusion of the duct of a follicle or small gland.

practicemanagement.name: practice management
practicemanagement.definition: Practice management is business management of medical, dental and veterinary practices that may include capital financing, utilization management, and arrangement of capitation agreements with other parties.

aluminumhydroxide.name: aluminum hydroxide
aluminumhydroxide.definition: Aluminum hydroxide is a compound with many biomedical applications: as a gastric antacid, an antiperspirant, in dentifrices, as an emulsifier, as an adjuvant in bacterins and vaccines, in [MASK], etc.

insurance,health,reimbursement.name: insurance , health , reimbursement
insurance,health,reimbursement.definition: Reimbursement health insurance is payment by a third-party payer in a sum equal to the amount expended by a health care provider or facility for health services rendered to an insured or program beneficiary. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

speech,esophageal.name: speech , esophageal
speech,esophageal.definition: Esophageal [MASK] is a method of [MASK] used after laryngectomy, with sound produced by vibration of the column of air in the esophagus against the contracting cricopharyngeal sphincter. (Dorland, 27th ed)

intention.name: intention
intention.definition: Intention is what a person has in mind to do or bring about.

geneamplification.name: gene amplification
geneamplification.definition: Gene amplification is a selective increase in the number of copies of a gene coding for a specific protein without a proportional increase in other genes. It occurs naturally via the excision of a copy of the repeating sequence from the chromosome and its extrachromosomal replication in a plasmid, or via the production of an rna transcript of the entire repeating sequence of [MASK] followed by the reverse transcription of the molecule to produce an additional copy of the original dna sequence. Laboratory techniques have been introduced for inducing disproportional replication by unequal crossing over, uptake of dna from lysed cells, or generation of extrachromosomal sequences from rolling circle replication.

receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type3.name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 3
receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type3.definition: Type 3 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor that regulates chondrocyte growth and cell differentiation. Mutations in the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 have been associated with achondroplasia; thanatophoric dysplasia and neoplastic cell transformation.

inclusionbodies.name: inclusion bodies
inclusionbodies.definition: Inclusion bodies is a generic term for any circumscribed mass of foreign (e.g., lead or viruses) or metabolically inactive materials (e.g., ceroid or mallory bodies), within the cytoplasm or nucleus of a cell. Inclusion bodies are in cells infected with certain filtrable viruses, observed especially in nerve, epithelial, or endothelial cells. (Stedman, 25th ed)

spatialconcept.name: spatial concept
spatialconcept.definition: Spatial concept is concepts relating to space or a space.

ionchannels.name: ion channels
ionchannels.definition: Ion channels is gated, ion-selective glycoproteins that traverse membranes. The stimulus for ion channel gating can be due to a variety of stimuli such as ligands, a transmembrane potential difference, mechanical deformation or through intracellular signaling peptides and proteins.

neuralnetworks,computer.name: neural networks , computer
neuralnetworks,computer.definition: Computer neural networks is a computer architecture, implementable in either hardware or software, modeled after biological neural networks. Like the biological system in which the processing capability is a result of the interconnection strengths between arrays of nonlinear processing nodes, computerized neural networks, often called perceptrons or multilayer connectionist models, consist of neuron-like units. a homogeneous group of units makes up a layer. These networks are good at pattern recognition. They are adaptive, performing tasks by example, and thus are better for decision-making than are linear learning machines or cluster analysis. They do not require explicit programming.

marginsofexcision.name: margins of excision
marginsofexcision.definition: Margins of excision is the edges of tissue removed in a surgery for assessment of the effectiveness of a surgical procedure in achieving the local control of a neoplasm and the adequacy of tumor removal. When the margin is negative or not involved by tumor (e.g., cancer) it suggests all of the tumor has been removed by the surgery.

giantcells.name: giant cells
giantcells.definition: Giant cells is multinucleated masses produced by the fusion of many cells; often associated with viral infections. In aids, they are induced when the envelope glycoprotein of the hiv virus binds to the cd4 antigen of uninfected neighboring t4 cells. The resulting syncytium leads to cell death and thus may account for the cytopathic effect of the virus.

laboratoryanimalscience.name: laboratory animal science
laboratoryanimalscience.definition: Laboratory animal science is the science and technology dealing with the procurement, breeding, care, health, and selection of animals used in biomedical research and testing.

chromosomes,human,pair5.name: chromosomes , human , pair 5
chromosomes,human,pair5.definition: Pair 5 human chromosomes is one of the two pairs of human chromosomes in the group b class (chromosomes, human, 4-5).

visuallyimpairedpersons.name: visually impaired persons
visuallyimpairedpersons.definition: Visually impaired persons is persons with loss of vision such that there is an impact on activities of daily living.

hearingloss,conductive.name: hearing loss , conductive
hearingloss,conductive.definition: Conductive hearing loss is hearing loss due to interference with the mechanical reception or amplification of sound to the cochlea. The interference is in the outer or [MASK] involving the [MASK]; tympanic membrane; or ear ossicles.

nerveblock.name: nerve block
nerveblock.definition: Nerve block is interruption of [MASK] in peripheral nerves or nerve trunks by the injection of a local anesthetic agent (e.g., lidocaine; phenol; botulinum toxins) to manage or treat pain.

facialnervediseases.name: facial nerve diseases
facialnervediseases.definition: Facial nerve diseases is diseases of the facial nerve or nuclei. Pontine disorders may affect the facial nuclei or nerve fascicle. The nerve may be involved intracranially, along its course through the petrous portion of the [MASK], or along its extracranial course. Clinical manifestations include [MASK] weakness, loss of taste from the anterior tongue, hyperacusis, and decreased lacrimation.

extractionandprocessingindustry.name: extraction and processing industry
extractionandprocessingindustry.definition: Extraction and processing industry is the industry concerned with the removal of raw materials from the Earth's crust and with their conversion into refined products.

toothroot.name: tooth root
toothroot.definition: Tooth root is the part of a tooth from the [MASK] to the apex, embedded in the alveolar process and covered with cementum. a root may be single or divided into several branches, usually identified by their relative position, e.g., lingual root or buccal root. Single-rooted teeth include mandibular first and second premolars and the maxillary second premolar teeth. The maxillary first premolar has two roots in most cases. Maxillary molars have three roots. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p690)

adaptorproteins,vesiculartransport.name: adaptor proteins , vesicular transport
adaptorproteins,vesiculartransport.definition: Vesicular transport adaptor proteins is a class of proteins involved in the transport of molecules via transport vesicles. They perform functions such as binding to the cell membrane, capturing cargo molecules and promoting the assembly of clathrin. The majority of adaptor proteins exist as multi-subunit complexes, however monomeric varieties have also been found.

ghrelin.name: ghrelin
ghrelin.definition: Ghrelin is a 28-amino acid, acylated, orexigenic peptide that is a ligand for growth hormone secretagogue receptors. Ghrelin is widely expressed but primarily in the stomach in the adults. Ghrelin acts centrally to stimulate growth hormone secretion and food intake, and peripherally to regulate energy homeostasis. Its large precursor protein, known as appetite-regulating hormone or motilin-related peptide, contains ghrelin and obestatin.

couptranscriptionfactorii.name: coup transcription factor ii
couptranscriptionfactorii.definition: Coup transcription factor ii is a coup transcription factor that negatively regulates genetic transcription and competes with other hormone receptors for the common response element aggtca. It can also stimulate transcription of genes involved in the metabolism of glucose and cholesterol.

plantviruses.name: plant viruses
plantviruses.definition: Plant viruses is viruses parasitic on plants.

vestibularnucleus,lateral.name: vestibular nucleus , lateral
vestibularnucleus,lateral.definition: Lateral vestibular nucleus is vestibular nucleus lying immediately superior to the inferior vestibular nucleus and composed of large multipolar nerve cells. Its upper end becomes continuous with the superior vestibular nucleus.

adultstemcells.name: adult stem cells
adultstemcells.definition: Adult stem cells is tissue-specific stem cells (also known as Somatic Stem Cells) that appear during fetal development and remain in the body throughout life. The key functions of adult stem cells are to maintain and repair the specific tissues where they reside (e.g. skin or blood).

purchasing,hospital.name: purchasing , hospital
purchasing,hospital.definition: Hospital purchasing is hospital department responsible for the purchasing of supplies and equipment.

suicide.name: suicide
suicide.definition: Suicide is the act of killing oneself.

osteoarthritis,spine.name: osteoarthritis , spine
osteoarthritis,spine.definition: Spine osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease involving the spine. It is characterized by progressive deterioration of the spinal articular cartilage (cartilage, articular), usually with hardening of the subchondral bone and outgrowth of bone spurs (osteophyte).

originoflife.name: origin of life
originoflife.definition: Origin of life is the process by which life began.

rootcaries.name: root caries
rootcaries.definition: Root caries is dental caries involving the tooth root, cementum, or cervical area of the tooth.

potassium.name: potassium
potassium.definition: Potassium is an element in the alkali group of metals with an atomic symbol k, atomic number 19, and atomic weight 39.10. It is the chief cation in the intracellular fluid of muscle and other cells. Potassium ion is a strong electrolyte that plays a significant role in the regulation of fluid volume and maintenance of the water-electrolyte balance.

membranes,artificial.name: membranes , artificial
membranes,artificial.definition: Artificial membranes is artificially produced membranes, such as semipermeable membranes used in artificial kidney dialysis (renal dialysis), monomolecular and bimolecular membranes used as models to simulate biological cell membranes. These membranes are also used in the process of guided tissue regeneration.

cervicalplexus.name: cervical plexus
cervicalplexus.definition: Cervical plexus is a network of nerve fibers originating in the upper four [MASK] segments. The cervical plexus distributes cutaneous nerves to parts of the [MASK], [MASK], and back of the head. It also distributes motor fibers to muscles of the cervical spinal column, infrahyoid muscles, and the diaphragm.

endocrineglandneoplasms.name: endocrine gland neoplasms
endocrineglandneoplasms.definition: Endocrine gland neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the endocrine glands.

hipdysplasia,canine.name: hip dysplasia , canine
hipdysplasia,canine.definition: Canine hip dysplasia is a hereditary disease of the hip joints in dogs. Signs of the disease may be evident any time after 4 weeks of age.

cornealtransplantation.name: corneal transplantation
cornealtransplantation.definition: Corneal transplantation is partial or total replacement of the cornea from one human or animal to another.

matingpreference,animal.name: mating preference , animal
matingpreference,animal.definition: Animal mating preference is the selection or choice of [MASK] in animals. Often this reproductive preference is based on traits in the potential mate, such as coloration, size, or behavioral boldness. If the chosen ones are genetically different from the rejected ones, then natural selection is occurring.

isotopelabeling.name: isotope labeling
isotopelabeling.definition: Isotope labeling is techniques for labeling a substance with a stable or radioactive isotope. It is not used for articles involving labeled substances unless the methods of labeling are substantively discussed. Tracers that may be labeled include chemical substances, cells, or microorganisms.

plants,toxic.name: plants , toxic
plants,toxic.definition: Toxic plants is plants or plant parts which are harmful to man or other animals.

therapeuticindex.name: therapeutic index
therapeuticindex.definition: Therapeutic index is an indicator of the benefits and risks of treatment.

bloodglucose.name: blood glucose
bloodglucose.definition: Blood glucose is glucose in blood.

educationalpersonnel.name: educational personnel
educationalpersonnel.definition: Educational personnel is professionals responsible for teaching in an institution or place of learning such as a school, college, vocational institute, or university.

parenting.name: parenting
parenting.definition: Parenting is performing the role of a parent by care-giving, nurturance, and protection of the child by a natural or substitute parent. The parent supports the child by exercising authority and through consistent, empathic, appropriate behavior in response to the child's needs. parenting differs from child rearing in that in child rearing the emphasis is on the act of training or bringing up the children and the interaction between the parent and child, while parenting emphasizes the responsibility and qualities of exemplary behavior of the parent.

informationscience.name: information science
informationscience.definition: Information science is the field of knowledge, theory, and technology dealing with the collection of facts and figures, and the processes and methods involved in their manipulation, storage, dissemination, publication, and retrieval. It includes the fields of communication; publishing; library science; and informatics.

foodirradiation.name: food irradiation
foodirradiation.definition: Food irradiation is treatment of food with radiation.

coppertransportproteins.name: copper transport proteins
coppertransportproteins.definition: [MASK] transport proteins is membrane proteins that facilitate the transport of [MASK] cations across biological membranes.

selfreport.name: self report
selfreport.definition: Self report is method for obtaining information through verbal responses, written or oral, from subjects.

lodscore.name: lod score
lodscore.definition: Lod score is the total relative probability, expressed on a logarithmic scale, that a linkage relationship exists among selected loci. Lod is an acronym for "logarithmic odds."

mammaryneoplasms,experimental.name: mammary neoplasms , experimental
mammaryneoplasms,experimental.definition: Experimental mammary neoplasms is experimentally induced mammary neoplasms in animals to provide a model for studying human breast neoplasms.

trackandfield.name: track and field
trackandfield.definition: Track and field is sports performed on a track, field, or arena and including [MASK] events and other competitions, such as the pole vault, shot put, etc.

recombination,genetic.name: recombination , genetic
recombination,genetic.definition: Genetic recombination is production of new arrangements of dna by various mechanisms such as assortment and segregation, crossing over; [MASK]; genetic transformation; [MASK]; genetic transduction; or mixed infection of viruses.

multicenterstudy.name: multicenter study
multicenterstudy.definition: Multicenter study is a work that reports on a study executed by several cooperating institutions.

swinediseases.name: swine diseases
swinediseases.definition: Swine diseases is diseases of domestic swine and of the wild boar of the genus Sus.

computationalbiology.name: computational biology
computationalbiology.definition: Computational biology is a field of biology concerned with the development of techniques for the collection and manipulation of biological data, and the use of such data to make biological discoveries or predictions. This field encompasses all computational methods and theories for solving biological problems including manipulation of models and datasets.

iowa.name: iowa
iowa.definition: Iowa is state bounded on the north by [MASK], on the east by Wisconsin and Illinois, on the south by Missouri, and on the west by Nebraska and South Dakota.

skull.name: skull
skull.definition: Skull is the skeleton of the head including the facial bones and the bones enclosing the brain.

pulmonaryventilation.name: pulmonary ventilation
pulmonaryventilation.definition: Pulmonary ventilation is the total volume of gas inspired or expired per unit of time, usually measured in liters per minute.

anatomicalabnormality.name: anatomical abnormality
anatomicalabnormality.definition: Anatomical abnormality is an abnormal structure, or one that is abnormal in size or location.

proteinaggregation,pathological.name: protein aggregation , pathological
proteinaggregation,pathological.definition: Pathological protein aggregation is a biochemical phenomenon in which misfolded proteins aggregate either intra- or extracellularly. Triggered by factors such as mutation; post-translational modifications, and environmental stress, it is generally associated with alzheimer disease; parkinson disease; huntington disease; and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

newmexico.name: new mexico
newmexico.definition: New [MASK] is state bounded on the north by Colorado, on the east by Oklahoma and Texas, on the south by Texas and [MASK], and on the west by Arizona.

risksharing,financial.name: risk sharing , financial
risksharing,financial.definition: Financial risk sharing is any system which allows payors to share some of the financial risk associated with a particular patient population with providers. Providers agree to adhere to fixed fee schedules in exchange for an increase in their payor base and a chance to benefit from cost containment measures. Common risk-sharing methods are prospective payment schedules (prospective payment system), capitation (capitation fees), diagnosis-related fees (diagnosis-related groups), and pre-negotiated fees.

fetalalcoholspectrumdisorders.name: fetal alcohol spectrum disorders
fetalalcoholspectrumdisorders.definition: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders is an umbrella term used to describe a pattern of disabilities and abnormalities that result from fetal exposure to ethanol during pregnancy. It encompasses a phenotypic range that can vary greatly between individuals, but reliably includes one or more of the following: characteristic facial dysmorphism, fetal growth retardation, central nervous system abnormalities, cognitive and/or behavioral dysfunction, birth defects. The level of maternal alcohol consumption does not necessarily correlate directly with disease severity.

rna,transfer.name: rna , transfer
rna,transfer.definition: Transfer rna is the small rna molecules, 73-80 nucleotides long, that function during translation (translation, genetic) to align amino acids at the ribosomes in a sequence determined by the mRNA (rna, messenger). There are about 30 different transfer RNAs. Each recognizes a specific codon [MASK] on the mRNA through its own anticodon and as aminoacyl tRNAs ([MASK]), each carries a specific amino acid to the ribosome to add to the elongating peptide chains.

agedistribution.name: age distribution
agedistribution.definition: Age distribution is the frequency of different ages or age groups in a given population. The distribution may refer to either how many or what proportion of the group. The population is usually patients with a specific disease but the concept is not restricted to humans and is not restricted to medicine.

spaceperception.name: space perception
spaceperception.definition: Space perception is the awareness of the spatial properties of objects; includes physical space.

duplicatepublicationsastopic.name: duplicate publications as topic
duplicatepublicationsastopic.definition: Duplicate publications as topic is work about simultaneous or successive publishing of identical or near- identical material in two or more different sources without acknowledgment. It differs from reprinted publication in that a reprint cites sources. It differs from plagiarism in that [MASK] is the product of the same authorship while plagiarism publishes a work or parts of a work of another as one's own.

ventricularremodeling.name: ventricular remodeling
ventricularremodeling.definition: Ventricular remodeling is the geometric and structural changes that the heart ventricles undergo, usually following myocardial infarction. It comprises expansion of the infarct and dilatation of the healthy ventricle segments. While most prevalent in the left ventricle, it can also occur in the right ventricle.

astrocytes.name: astrocytes
astrocytes.definition: Astrocytes is a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from "star" cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with "end [MASK]" which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and "reactive astrocytes" (along with microglia) respond to injury.

neckmuscles.name: neck muscles
neckmuscles.definition: [MASK] muscles is the [MASK] muscles consist of the platysma, splenius cervicis, sternocleidomastoid(eus), longus colli, the anterior, medius, and posterior scalenes, digastric(us), stylohyoid(eus), mylohyoid(eus), geniohyoid(eus), sternohyoid(eus), omohyoid(eus), sternothyroid(eus), and thyrohyoid(eus).

rna,messenger.name: rna , messenger
rna,messenger.definition: Messenger rna is rna sequences that serve as templates for protein synthesis. Bacterial mRNAs are generally primary transcripts in that they do not require post-transcriptional processing. Eukaryotic mRNA is synthesized in the nucleus and must be exported to the cytoplasm for translation. Most eukaryotic mRNAs have a sequence of polyadenylic acid at the 3' end, referred to as the poly(A) tail. The function of this tail is not known for certain, but it may play a role in the export of mature mRNA from the nucleus as well as in helping stabilize some mRNA molecules by retarding their degradation in the cytoplasm.

legislation,hospital.name: legislation , hospital
legislation,hospital.definition: Hospital legislation is laws and regulations concerning hospitals, which are proposed for enactment or enacted by a legislative body.

opticnerveneoplasms.name: optic nerve neoplasms
opticnerveneoplasms.definition: Optic nerve neoplasms is benign and malignant neoplasms that arise from the optic nerve or its sheath. optic nerve glioma is the most common histologic type. Optic nerve neoplasms tend to cause unilateral visual loss and an afferent pupillary defect and may spread via neural pathways to the brain.

bacterialtypingtechniques.name: bacterial typing techniques
bacterialtypingtechniques.definition: Bacterial typing techniques is procedures for identifying types and strains of bacteria. The most frequently employed typing systems are bacteriophage typing and serotyping as well as bacteriocin typing and biotyping.

bonemarrowneoplasms.name: bone marrow neoplasms
bonemarrowneoplasms.definition: Bone marrow neoplasms is neoplasms located in the bone marrow. They are differentiated from neoplasms composed of bone marrow cells, such as multiple myeloma. Most bone marrow neoplasms are metastatic.

mouthdiseases.name: mouth diseases
mouthdiseases.definition: Mouth diseases is diseases involving the mouth.

cyclicimp.name: cyclic imp
cyclicimp.definition: Cyclic imp is inosine cyclic 3',5'-(hydrogen phosphate). An inosine nucleotide which acts as a mild inhibitor of the hydrolysis of cyclic amp and cyclic gmp and as an inhibitor of cat heart cyclic amp phosphodiesterase.

hospitals,veterans.name: hospitals , veterans
hospitals,veterans.definition: Veterans hospitals is hospitals providing medical care to veterans of wars.

inflammation.name: inflammation
inflammation.definition: Inflammation is a pathological process characterized by injury or destruction of tissues caused by a variety of cytologic and chemical reactions. It is usually manifested by typical signs of pain, heat, redness, swelling, and loss of function.

heartrate.name: heart rate
heartrate.definition: Heart rate is the number of times the heart ventricles contract per unit of time, usually per minute.

publicrelations.name: public relations
publicrelations.definition: Public relations is relations of an individual, association, organization, hospital, or corporation with the publics which it must take into consideration in carrying out its functions. Publics may include consumers, patients, pressure groups, departments, etc.

urinarytract.name: urinary tract
urinarytract.definition: Urinary tract is the duct which coveys urine from the pelvis of the kidney through the ureters, [MASK], and urethra.

creatinekinase,bbform.name: creatine kinase , bb form
creatinekinase,bbform.definition: Bb form creatine kinase is a form of creatine kinase found in the brain.

laboratorycriticalvalues.name: laboratory critical values
laboratorycriticalvalues.definition: Laboratory critical values is test results which deviate substantially from normal ranges of reference values or other qualitative results. They trigger clinical laboratory services to place a special alert to ensure patient safety.

schizophrenia.name: schizophrenia
schizophrenia.definition: Schizophrenia is a severe emotional disorder of psychotic depth characteristically marked by a retreat from reality with delusion formation, hallucinations, emotional disharmony, and regressive behavior.

developmentaldisabilities.name: developmental disabilities
developmentaldisabilities.definition: Developmental disabilities is disorders in which there is a delay in development based on that expected for a given age level or stage of development. These impairments or disabilities originate before age 18, may be expected to continue indefinitely, and constitute a substantial impairment. Biological and nonbiological factors are involved in these disorders. (From American Psychiatric Glossary, 6th ed)

abbreviations.name: abbreviations
abbreviations.definition: Abbreviations is works consisting of lists of shortened forms of written words or phrases used for brevity. Acronyms are included here.

olfactorynerveinjuries.name: olfactory nerve injuries
olfactorynerveinjuries.definition: Olfactory nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the olfactory nerve. It may result in various olfactory dysfunction including a complete loss of smell.

plasmaskinregeneration.name: plasma skin regeneration
plasmaskinregeneration.definition: Plasma skin regeneration is a cosmetic technique that uses plasma gases in therapeutic treatment to help achieve skin rejuvenation or regeneration and delay skin aging.

muscle,skeletal.name: muscle , skeletal
muscle,skeletal.definition: Skeletal muscle is a subtype of striated muscle, attached by tendons to the skeleton. Skeletal muscles are innervated and their movement can be consciously controlled. They are also called voluntary muscles.

heavychaindisease.name: heavy chain disease
heavychaindisease.definition: Heavy chain disease is a disorder of immunoglobulin synthesis in which large quantities of abnormal heavy chains are excreted in the urine. The amino acid sequences of the N-(amino-) terminal regions of these chains are normal, but they have a deletion extending from part of the variable domain through the first domain of the constant region, so that they cannot form cross-links to the light chains. The defect arises through faulty coupling of the variable (v) and constant (c) region genes.

viralenvelopeproteins.name: viral envelope proteins
viralenvelopeproteins.definition: Viral envelope proteins is integral membrane proteins that are incorporated into the viral envelope. They are glycosylated during viral assembly.

fluorescenceresonanceenergytransfer.name: fluorescence resonance energy transfer
fluorescenceresonanceenergytransfer.definition: Fluorescence resonance energy transfer is a type of fluorescence spectroscopy using two fluorescent dyes with overlapping emission and absorption spectra, which is used to indicate proximity of labeled molecules. This technique is useful for studying interactions of molecules and protein folding.

clusteranalysis.name: cluster analysis
clusteranalysis.definition: Cluster analysis is a [MASK] of statistical methods used to group variables or observations into strongly inter-related subgroups. In epidemiology, it may be used to analyze a closely grouped series of events or cases of disease or other health-related phenomenon with well-defined distribution patterns in relation to time or place or both.

aurichelements.name: au rich elements
aurichelements.definition: Au rich elements is rna sequences composed of adenine nucleotides and uracil nucleotides, that are located in the 3'untranslated regions of messenger rna molecules that are rapidly degraded. They are also known as AREs.

gold.name: gold
gold.definition: Gold is a yellow metallic element with the atomic symbol Au, atomic number 79, and atomic weight 197. It is used in jewelry, goldplating of other metals, as currency, and in dental restoration. Many of its clinical applications, such as antirheumatic agents, are in the form of its [MASK].

magic.name: magic
magic.definition: Magic is beliefs and practices concerned with producing desired results through supernatural forces or agents as with the manipulation of fetishes or rituals.

medicalassistance.name: medical assistance
medicalassistance.definition: Medical assistance is financing of medical care provided to public assistance recipients.

respiratorymechanics.name: respiratory mechanics
respiratorymechanics.definition: Respiratory mechanics is the physical or mechanical action of the lungs; diaphragm; ribs; and chest wall during respiration. It includes airflow, lung volume, neural and reflex controls, mechanoreceptors, breathing patterns, etc.

anteriorcerebralartery.name: anterior cerebral artery
anteriorcerebralartery.definition: Anterior cerebral artery is artery formed by the bifurcation of the internal carotid artery (carotid artery, internal). Branches of the anterior cerebral artery supply the caudate nucleus; internal capsule; putamen; septal nuclei; gyrus cinguli; and surfaces of the frontal lobe and parietal lobe.

celltransformation,neoplastic.name: cell transformation , neoplastic
celltransformation,neoplastic.definition: Neoplastic cell transformation is cell changes manifested by escape from control mechanisms, increased growth potential, alterations in the cell surface, karyotypic abnormalities, morphological and biochemical deviations from the norm, and other attributes conferring the ability to invade, metastasize, and kill.

gingivalrecession.name: gingival recession
gingivalrecession.definition: Gingival recession is exposure of the root surface when the edge of the gum (gingiva) moves apically away from the crown of the tooth. This is common with advancing age, vigorous tooth brushing, diseases, or tissue loss of the gingiva, the periodontal ligament and the supporting bone (alveolar process).

genedosage.name: gene dosage
genedosage.definition: Gene dosage is the number of copies of a given gene present in the cell of an organism. An increase in gene dosage (by gene duplication for example) can result in higher levels of gene product formation. gene dosage compensation mechanisms result in [MASK] to the level gene expression when there are changes or differences in gene dosage.

fluidtherapy.name: fluid therapy
fluidtherapy.definition: Fluid therapy is therapy whose basic objective is to restore the volume and composition of the body fluids to normal with respect to water-electrolyte balance. Fluids may be administered intravenously, orally, by intermittent gavage, or by hypodermoclysis.

phospholipasecbeta.name: phospholipase c beta
phospholipasecbeta.definition: Phospholipase c beta is a phosphoinositide phospholipase c subtype that is primarily regulated by its association with heterotrimeric g-proteins. It is structurally related to phospholipase c delta with the addition of C-terminal extension of 400 residues.

nursingservice,hospital.name: nursing service , hospital
nursingservice,hospital.definition: Hospital nursing service is the hospital department which is responsible for the organization and administration of nursing activities.

sensoryarttherapies.name: sensory art therapies
sensoryarttherapies.definition: Sensory art therapies is therapies using arts or directed at the senses.

knowledgebases.name: knowledge bases
knowledgebases.definition: Knowledge bases is collections of facts, assumptions, beliefs, and heuristics that are used in combination with databases to achieve desired results, such as a diagnosis, an interpretation, or a solution to a problem (From McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed).

shoulderpain.name: shoulder pain
shoulderpain.definition: [MASK] pain is unilateral or bilateral pain of the [MASK]. It is often caused by physical activities such as work or sports participation, but may also be pathologic in origin.

clinicalstudy.name: clinical study
clinicalstudy.definition: Clinical study is a work that reports on the results of a research study to evaluate interventions or exposures on biomedical or health-related outcomes.  The two main types of clinical studies are interventional studies (clinical trials) and observational studies. While most clinical studies concern humans, this publication type may be used for clinical veterinary articles meeting the requisites for humans.

jetlagsyndrome.name: jet lag syndrome
jetlagsyndrome.definition: Jet lag syndrome is a chronobiologic disorder resulting from rapid travel across a number of time zones, characterized by insomnia or hypersomnolence, fatigue, behavioral symptoms, headaches, and gastrointestinal disturbances. (From Cooper, Sleep, 1994, pp593-8)

transcriptiontermination,genetic.name: transcription termination , genetic
transcriptiontermination,genetic.definition: Genetic transcription termination is the discontinuation of transcription at the end of a transcription unit, including the recognition of termination sites and release of the newly synthesized rna molecule.

thyroidnodule.name: thyroid nodule
thyroidnodule.definition: Thyroid nodule is a small circumscribed mass in the thyroid gland that can be of neoplastic growth or non-neoplastic abnormality. It lacks a well-defined capsule or glandular architecture. Thyroid nodules are often benign but can be malignant. The growth of nodules can lead to a multinodular goiter (goiter, nodular).

exercisetolerance.name: exercise tolerance
exercisetolerance.definition: Exercise tolerance is the exercise capacity of an individual as measured by endurance (maximal exercise duration and/or maximal attained work load) during an exercise test.

tauproteins.name: tau proteins
tauproteins.definition: Tau proteins is [MASK]-associated proteins that are mainly expressed in neurons. Tau proteins constitute several isoforms and play an important role in the assembly of tubulin monomers into [MASK] and in maintaining the cytoskeleton and axonal transport. Aggregation of specific sets of tau proteins in filamentous inclusions is the common feature of intraneuronal and glial fibrillar lesions (neurofibrillary tangles; neuropil threads) in numerous neurodegenerative disorders (alzheimer disease; tauopathies).

economics,medical.name: economics , medical
economics,medical.definition: Medical economics is economic aspects of the field of medicine, the medical profession, and health care. It includes the economic and financial impact of disease in general on the patient, the physician, society, or government.

protectiveclothing.name: protective clothing
protectiveclothing.definition: Protective clothing is clothing designed to protect the individual against possible exposure to known hazards.

nelsonsyndrome.name: nelson syndrome
nelsonsyndrome.definition: Nelson syndrome is a syndrome characterized by hyperpigmentation, enlarging pituitary mass, visual defects secondary to compression of the optic chiasm, and elevated serum acth. It is caused by the expansion of an underlying acth-secreting pituitary adenoma that grows in the absence of [MASK] inhibition by adrenal corticosteroids, usually after adrenalectomy.

dentalcastingtechnique.name: dental casting technique
dentalcastingtechnique.definition: Dental casting technique is the process of producing a form or impression made of metal or plaster using a mold.

coppertransporter1.name: copper transporter 1
coppertransporter1.definition: [MASK] transporter 1 is a high-affinity, saturable [MASK] transporter of the plasma membrane that functions in the absorption of dietary [MASK].

adiposetissue.name: adipose tissue
adiposetissue.definition: Adipose tissue is specialized connective tissue composed of fat cells (adipocytes). It is the site of stored fats, usually in the form of triglycerides. In mammals, there are two types of adipose tissue, the [MASK] fat and the [MASK]. Their relative distributions vary in different species with most adipose tissue being [MASK].

pneumonia,progressiveinterstitial,ofshee.name: pneumonia , progressive interstitial , of sheep
pneumonia,progressiveinterstitial,ofshee.definition: Of sheep progressive interstitial pneumonia is chronic respiratory disease caused by the visna-maedi virus. It was formerly believed to be identical with jaagsiekte (pulmonary adenomatosis, ovine) but is now recognized as a separate entity.

lupuserythematosus,cutaneous.name: lupus erythematosus , cutaneous
lupuserythematosus,cutaneous.definition: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus is a form of lupus erythematosus in which the skin may be the only organ involved or in which skin involvement precedes the spread into other body systems. It has been classified into three forms - acute (= [MASK] with skin lesions), subacute, and chronic (= lupus erythematosus, discoid).

zebrafish.name: zebrafish
zebrafish.definition: Zebrafish is an exotic species of the family cyprinidae, originally from Asia, that has been introduced in North America. Zebrafish is a model organism for drug assay and cancer research.

tobaccomosaicsatellitevirus.name: tobacco mosaic satellite virus
tobaccomosaicsatellitevirus.definition: Tobacco mosaic satellite virus is a spherical rna satellite virus which requires an obligatory helper tobacco mosaic virus for replication.

observationalstudies,veterinaryastopic.name: observational studies , veterinary as topic
observationalstudies,veterinaryastopic.definition: Veterinary as topic observational studies is works about clinical studies in which animal subjects may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions and where the investigator does not assign subjects  to specific interventions.

poster.name: poster
poster.definition: Poster is work consisting of single or multi-sheet notices made to attract attention to events, activities, causes, goods, or services. They are for posting, usually in a public place and are chiefly pictorial. They are intended to make an immediate impression from a distance. Posters do not include poster presentations at conferences and meetings. (From Thesaurus for Graphic Materials ii: Genre and Physical Characteristic Headings, 1995)

transpositionofgreatvessels.name: transposition of great vessels
transpositionofgreatvessels.definition: Transposition of great vessels is a congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the aorta arises entirely from the right ventricle, and the [MASK] arises from the left ventricle. Consequently, the pulmonary and the systemic circulations are parallel and not sequential, so that the venous return from the peripheral circulation is re-circulated by the right ventricle via aorta to the systemic circulation without being oxygenated in the lungs. This is a potentially lethal form of heart disease in newborns and infants.

retinalnecrosissyndrome,acute.name: retinal necrosis syndrome , acute
retinalnecrosissyndrome,acute.definition: Acute retinal necrosis syndrome is mild to fulminant necrotizing vaso-occlusive retinitis associated with a high incidence of retinal detachment and poor vision outcome.

ethics,professional.name: ethics , professional
ethics,professional.definition: Professional ethics is the principles of proper conduct concerning the rights and duties of the professional, relations with patients or consumers and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the professional and interpersonal relations with patient or consumer families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

dnareplicationtiming.name: dna replication timing
dnareplicationtiming.definition: Dna replication timing is the temporal order in which the dna of the genome is replicated.

ocularhypertension.name: ocular hypertension
ocularhypertension.definition: Ocular hypertension is a condition in which the intraocular pressure is elevated above normal and which may lead to glaucoma.

signaltransduction.name: signal transduction
signaltransduction.definition: Signal transduction is the intracellular transfer of information (biological activation/inhibition) through a signal pathway. In each signal transduction system, an activation/inhibition signal from a biologically active molecule (hormone, neurotransmitter) is mediated via the coupling of a receptor/enzyme to a second messenger system or to an ion channel. Signal transduction plays an important role in activating cellular functions, cell differentiation, and cell proliferation. Examples of signal transduction systems are the gamma-aminobutyric ACID-postsynaptic receptor-calcium ion channel system, the receptor-mediated T-cell activation pathway, and the receptor-mediated activation of phospholipases. Those coupled to membrane depolarization or intracellular release of calcium include the receptor-mediated activation of cytotoxic functions in granulocytes and the synaptic potentiation of protein kinase activation. Some signal transduction pathways may be part of larger signal transduction pathways; for example, protein kinase activation is part of the platelet activation signal pathway.

foodchain.name: food chain
foodchain.definition: Food chain is the sequence of transfers of matter and energy from organism to organism in the form of food. Food chains intertwine locally into a food web because most organisms consume more than one type of animal or plant. plants, which convert [MASK] to food by [MASK], are the primary food source.
