In a predator chain, a plant-eating animal is eaten by a larger animal. In a parasite chain, a smaller organism consumes part of a larger host and may itself be parasitized by smaller organisms. In a saprophytic chain, microorganisms live on dead organic matter.

creativity.name: creativity
creativity.definition: Creativity is the ability to generate new ideas or images.

metals,alkali.name: metals , alkali
metals,alkali.definition: Alkali metals is metals that constitute group 1(formerly group Ia) of the periodic [MASK]. They are the most strongly electropositive of the metals. Note that hydrogen is not considered an alkali metal even though it falls under the group 1 heading in the periodic [MASK].

braindeath.name: brain death
braindeath.definition: Brain death is a state of prolonged irreversible cessation of all brain activity, including lower brain stem function with the complete absence of voluntary movements, responses to stimuli, brain stem reflexes, and spontaneous respirations. Reversible conditions which mimic this clinical state (e.g., sedative overdose, hypothermia, etc.) are excluded prior to making the determination of brain death. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp348-9)

cholinedehydrogenase.name: choline dehydrogenase
cholinedehydrogenase.definition: Choline dehydrogenase is an enzyme bound to the [MASK] that catalyzes the oxidation of choline to betaine.

constriction,pathologic.name: constriction , pathologic
constriction,pathologic.definition: Pathologic constriction is the condition of an anatomical structure's being constricted beyond normal dimensions.

dentalscaling.name: dental scaling
dentalscaling.definition: Dental scaling is removal of dental plaque and dental calculus from the surface of a tooth, from the surface of a tooth apical to the gingival margin accumulated in [MASK], or from the surface coronal to the gingival margin.

atrialfibrillation.name: atrial fibrillation
atrialfibrillation.definition: Atrial fibrillation is abnormal cardiac rhythm that is characterized by rapid, uncoordinated firing of electrical impulses in the upper chambers of the heart (heart atria). In such case, blood cannot be effectively pumped into the lower chambers of the heart (heart ventricles). It is caused by abnormal impulse generation.

chemokines,c.name: chemokines , c
chemokines,c.definition: C chemokines is group of chemokines without adjacent cysteines that are chemoattractants for lymphocytes only.

tetracycline.name: tetracycline
tetracycline.definition: Tetracycline is a naphthacene antibiotic that inhibits [MASK] binding during protein synthesis.

statisticaldistributions.name: statistical distributions
statisticaldistributions.definition: Statistical distributions is the complete summaries of the frequencies of the values or categories of a measurement made on a group of items, a population, or other collection of data. The distribution tells either how many or what proportion of the group was found to have each value (or each range of values) out of all the possible values that the quantitative measure can have.

coatproteincomplexi.name: coat protein complex i
coatproteincomplexi.definition: Coat protein complex i is a protein complex comprised of coatomer protein and adp ribosylation factor 1. It is involved in transport of vesicles between the endoplasmic reticulum and the golgi apparatus.

crimevictims.name: crime victims
crimevictims.definition: Crime victims is individuals subjected to and adversely affected by criminal activity. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

proteasela.name: protease la
proteasela.definition: Protease la is a prokaryotic ATP-dependent protease that plays a role in the degradation of many abnormal proteins. It is a tetramer of 87-kDa subunits, each of which contains a proteolytic site and a ATP-binding site.

diagnostictechniques,digestivesystem.name: diagnostic techniques , digestive system
diagnostictechniques,digestivesystem.definition: Digestive system diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases or dysfunction of the digestive system or its organs or demonstration of their physiological processes.

nurses.name: nurses
nurses.definition: Nurses is professionals qualified by graduation from an accredited school of nursing and by passage of a national licensing examination to practice nursing. They provide services to patients requiring assistance in recovering or maintaining their physical or mental health.

dopamineagonists.name: dopamine agonists
dopamineagonists.definition: Dopamine agonists is drugs that bind to and activate dopamine receptors.

plasmagases.name: plasma gases
plasmagases.definition: Plasma gases is ionized gases, consisting of free [MASK] and ionized atoms or molecules which collectively behave differently than gas, solid, or liquid. Plasma gases are used in biomedical fields in surface modification; biological decontamination; dentistry (e.g., [MASK]); and in other treatments (e.g., [MASK] plasma coagulation).

respiratoryinsufficiency.name: respiratory insufficiency
respiratoryinsufficiency.definition: Respiratory insufficiency is failure to adequately provide oxygen to cells of the body and to remove excess carbon dioxide from them. (Stedman, 25th ed)

ganglia,spinal.name: ganglia , spinal
ganglia,spinal.definition: Spinal ganglia is sensory ganglia located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column. The spinal ganglion cells are pseudounipolar. The single primary branch bifurcates sending a peripheral process to carry sensory information from the periphery and a central branch which relays that information to the spinal cord or brain.

postoperativecomplications.name: postoperative complications
postoperativecomplications.definition: Postoperative complications is pathologic processes that affect patients after a surgical procedure. They may or may not be related to the disease for which the surgery was done, and they may or may not be direct results of the surgery.

atpsynthetasecomplexes.name: atp synthetase complexes
atpsynthetasecomplexes.definition: Atp synthetase complexes is multisubunit enzyme complexes that synthesize adenosine triphosphate from energy sources such as ions traveling through channels.

ice.name: ice
ice.definition: Ice is the solid substance formed by the freezing of water.

rna,transfer,arg.name: rna , transfer , arg
rna,transfer,arg.definition: Arg transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying [MASK] to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

receptor,parathyroidhormone,type1.name: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 1
receptor,parathyroidhormone,type1.definition: Type 1 parathyroid hormone receptor is a parathyroid hormone receptor subtype that recognizes both parathyroid hormone and parathyroid hormone-related protein. It is a G-protein-coupled receptor that is expressed at high levels in bone and in kidney.

cerebellargolgicells.name: cerebellar golgi cells
cerebellargolgicells.definition: Cerebellar golgi cells is inhibitory interneurons embedded in the granular layer of the cerebellar cortex.

delayedrectifierpotassiumchannels.name: delayed rectifier potassium channels
delayedrectifierpotassiumchannels.definition: Delayed rectifier potassium channels is a group of slow opening and closing voltage-gated potassium channels. Because of their delayed activation kinetics they play an important role in controlling action potential duration.

angina,stable.name: angina , stable
angina,stable.definition: Stable angina is persistent and reproducible chest discomfort usually precipitated by a physical exertion that dissipates upon cessation of such an activity. The symptoms are manifestations of myocardial ischemia.

pulmonarysurgicalprocedures.name: pulmonary surgical procedures
pulmonarysurgicalprocedures.definition: Pulmonary surgical procedures is surgery performed on the lung.

databasemanagementsystems.name: database management systems
databasemanagementsystems.definition: [MASK] management systems is software designed to store, manipulate, manage, and control data for specific uses.

disasters.name: disasters
disasters.definition: Disasters is calamities producing great damage, loss of life, and distress. They include results of natural phenomena and man-made phenomena. Normal conditions of existence are disrupted and the level of impact exceeds the capacity of the hazard-affected community.

braininjuries,traumatic.name: brain injuries , traumatic
braininjuries,traumatic.definition: Traumatic brain injuries is a form of acquired brain injury which occurs when a sudden trauma causes damage to the brain.

inhibitorofdifferentiationproteins.name: inhibitor of differentiation proteins
inhibitorofdifferentiationproteins.definition: Inhibitor of differentiation proteins is inhibitor of differentiation proteins are negative regulators of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors. They inhibit cell differentiation and induce cell proliferation by modulating different cell cycle regulators.

isoflurane.name: isoflurane
isoflurane.definition: Isoflurane is a stable, non-explosive [MASK] anesthetic, relatively free from significant side effects.

politics.name: politics
politics.definition: Politics is activities concerned with governmental policies, functions, etc.

mercury.name: mercury
mercury.definition: Mercury is a silver metallic element that exists as a liquid at room temperature. It has the atomic symbol Hg (from hydrargyrum, liquid silver), atomic number 80, and atomic weight 200.59. Mercury is used in many industrial applications and its [MASK] have been employed therapeutically as purgatives, antisyphilitics, disinfectants, and astringents. It can be absorbed through the skin and mucous membranes which leads to mercury poisoning. Because of its toxicity, the clinical use of mercury and mercurials is diminishing.

rnaprobes.name: rna probes
rnaprobes.definition: Rna probes is rna, usually prepared by transcription from cloned dna, which complements a specific mRNA or dna and is generally used for studies of virus genes, distribution of specific rna in tissues and cells, integration of [MASK] into genomes, transcription, etc. Whereas dna probes are preferred for use at a more macroscopic level for detection of the presence of dna/rna from specific species or subspecies, rna probes are preferred for genetic studies. Conventional labels for the rna probe include radioisotope labels 32p and 125i and the chemical label biotin. rna probes may be further divided by category into plus-sense rna probes, minus-sense rna probes, and antisense rna probes.

mandibularfractures.name: mandibular fractures
mandibularfractures.definition: Mandibular fractures is fractures of the lower jaw.

caspaseinhibitors.name: caspase inhibitors
caspaseinhibitors.definition: Caspase inhibitors is endogenous and exogenous compounds and that either inhibit caspases or prevent their activation.

communityparticipation.name: community participation
communityparticipation.definition: Community participation is involvement of members of the community in the affairs of that community.

hospitals.name: hospitals
hospitals.definition: Hospitals is institutions with an organized medical staff which provide medical care to patients.

forensicsciences.name: forensic sciences
forensicsciences.definition: Forensic sciences is disciplines that apply sciences to law. Forensic sciences include a wide range of disciplines, such as forensic toxicology; forensic anthropology; forensic medicine; forensic dentistry; and others.

embolism,air.name: embolism , air
embolism,air.definition: Air embolism is blocking of a blood vessel by air bubbles that enter the circulatory system, usually after trauma; surgical procedures, or changes in atmospheric pressure.

serotonin.name: serotonin
serotonin.definition: Serotonin is a biochemical messenger and regulator, synthesized from the essential amino acid l-tryptophan. In humans it is found primarily in the central nervous system, gastrointestinal tract, and blood platelets. Serotonin mediates several important physiological functions including neurotransmission, gastrointestinal motility, hemostasis, and cardiovascular integrity. Multiple receptor families (receptors, serotonin) explain the broad physiological actions and distribution of this biochemical mediator.

woundsandinjuries.name: wounds and injuries
woundsandinjuries.definition: Wounds and injuries is damage inflicted on the body as the direct or indirect result of an external force, with or without disruption of structural continuity.

handbook.name: handbook
handbook.definition: Handbook is work consisting of concise reference works in which facts and information pertaining to a certain subject or field are arranged for ready reference and consultation rather than for continuous reading and study.

cellbody.name: cell body
cellbody.definition: Cell body is the portion of a cell that contains the nucleus and cytoplasm but not cell surface extensions such as flagella and neurites.

attitude.name: attitude
attitude.definition: Attitude is an enduring, learned predisposition to behave in a consistent way toward a given class of objects, or a persistent mental and/or neural state of readiness to react to a certain class of objects, not as they are but as they are conceived to be.

drivingundertheinfluence.name: driving under the influence
drivingundertheinfluence.definition: Driving under the influence is operating a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or other drugs including those prescribed by physicians.

faculty,nursing.name: faculty , nursing
faculty,nursing.definition: Nursing faculty is the teaching staff and members of the administrative staff having academic rank in a [MASK].

olfactorymarkerprotein.name: olfactory marker protein
olfactorymarkerprotein.definition: Olfactory marker protein is a ubiquitous, cytoplasmic protein found in mature [MASK] of all vertebrates. It is a modulator of the olfactory signal transduction pathway.

inflammatoryboweldiseases.name: inflammatory bowel diseases
inflammatoryboweldiseases.definition: Inflammatory bowel diseases is chronic, non-specific inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. Etiology may be genetic or environmental. This term includes crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.

equipmentfailure.name: equipment failure
equipmentfailure.definition: Equipment failure is failure of equipment to perform to standard. The failure may be due to defects or improper use.

glucosetransportertype1.name: glucose transporter type 1
glucosetransportertype1.definition: Glucose transporter type 1 is a ubiquitously expressed glucose transporter that is important for constitutive, basal glucose transport. It is predominately expressed in endothelial cells and erythrocytes at the blood-brain barrier and is responsible for glucose entry into the brain.

diffusiontensorimaging.name: diffusion tensor imaging
diffusiontensorimaging.definition: Diffusion tensor imaging is the use of diffusion anisotropy data from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging results to construct images based on the direction of the faster diffusing molecules.

administration,cutaneous.name: administration , cutaneous
administration,cutaneous.definition: Cutaneous administration is the application of suitable drug dosage forms to the skin for either local or systemic effects.

humantrafficking.name: human trafficking
humantrafficking.definition: Human trafficking is recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring or receipt of persons, by means of the threat or use of force or other forms of coercion, of abduction, of [MASK], of deception, of the abuse of power or of a position of vulnerability or of the giving or receiving of payments or benefits to achieve the consent of a person having control over another person, for the purpose of exploitation. (un. Protocol to prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons, especially women and children, supplementing the United Nations convention against transnational organized crime. General Assembly resolution 55/25. United Nations General Assembly, 2000)

foreignbodies.name: foreign bodies
foreignbodies.definition: Foreign bodies is inanimate objects that become enclosed in the body.

leukocytes,mononuclear.name: leukocytes , mononuclear
leukocytes,mononuclear.definition: Mononuclear leukocytes is mature lymphocytes and monocytes transported by the blood to the body's extravascular space. They are morphologically distinguishable from mature granulocytic leukocytes by their large, non-lobed nuclei and lack of coarse, heavily stained cytoplasmic granules.

mitochondrialproteins.name: mitochondrial proteins
mitochondrialproteins.definition: Mitochondrial proteins is proteins encoded by the [MASK] or proteins encoded by the nuclear genome that are imported to and resident in the mitochondria.

genepool.name: gene pool
genepool.definition: Gene pool is the total genetic information possessed by the reproductive members of a population of sexually reproducing organisms.

verbalbehavior.name: verbal behavior
verbalbehavior.definition: Verbal behavior is includes both producing and responding to words, either written or spoken.

pneumococcalvaccines.name: pneumococcal vaccines
pneumococcalvaccines.definition: Pneumococcal vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infections with streptococcus pneumoniae.

psychiatryinliterature.name: psychiatry in literature
psychiatryinliterature.definition: Psychiatry in literature is written or other literary works whose subject matter is related to mental disorders or psychiatry from the lay or practitioner perspective.

brachialartery.name: brachial artery
brachialartery.definition: Brachial artery is the continuation of the axillary artery; it branches into the radial and ulnar arteries.

unpublishedwork.name: unpublished work
unpublishedwork.definition: Unpublished work is work that has not been formally published.

embolism.name: embolism
embolism.definition: Embolism is blocking of a blood vessel by an embolus which can be a blood clot or other undissolved material in the blood [MASK].

esters.name: esters
esters.definition: Esters is compounds derived from organic or inorganic acids in which at least one hydroxyl group is replaced by an –O-alkyl or other organic group. They can be represented by the structure formula rcoor’ and are usually formed by the reaction between an acid and an alcohol with elimination of water.

sociology.name: sociology
sociology.definition: Sociology is a social science dealing with group relationships, patterns of collective behavior, and social organization.

rape.name: rape
rape.definition: Rape is sexual intercourse without consent of the victim.

sodiumchloride.name: sodium chloride
sodiumchloride.definition: Sodium chloride is a ubiquitous sodium [MASK] that is commonly used to season food.

germcells,plant.name: germ cells , plant
germcells,plant.definition: Plant germ cells is the reproductive cells of plants.

hospitaldepartments.name: hospital departments
hospitaldepartments.definition: Hospital departments is major administrative divisions of the hospital.

vitaminb6deficiency.name: vitamin b 6 deficiency
vitaminb6deficiency.definition: Vitamin b 6 deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin b 6 in the diet, characterized by dermatitis, glossitis, cheilosis, and stomatitis. Marked deficiency causes irritability, weakness, depression, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy, and seizures. In infants and children typical manifestations are [MASK], anemia, and seizures. Deficiency can be caused by certain medications, such as isoniazid.

alcoholdrinking.name: alcohol drinking
alcoholdrinking.definition: Alcohol drinking is behaviors associated with the ingesting of alcoholic beverages, including social drinking.

temporalarteries.name: temporal arteries
temporalarteries.definition: Temporal arteries is arteries arising from the external carotid or the maxillary artery and distributing to the temporal region.

historicalarticle.name: historical article
historicalarticle.definition: Historical article is an article or portion of an article giving an account of past events or circumstances significant in a field of study, a profession, a discovery, an invention, etc. The concept of history is very wide, ranging from the dawn of time to the present. This publication type is often checked in conjunction with biography.

mesentericveins.name: mesenteric veins
mesentericveins.definition: Mesenteric veins is veins which return blood from the intestines; the inferior mesenteric vein empties into the splenic vein, the superior mesenteric vein joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.

professionalpractice.name: professional practice
professionalpractice.definition: Professional practice is the use of one's knowledge in a particular profession. It includes, in the case of the field of biomedicine, professional activities related to health care and the actual performance of the duties related to the provision of health care.

peripheralnerveinjuries.name: peripheral nerve injuries
peripheralnerveinjuries.definition: Peripheral nerve injuries is injuries to the peripheral nerves.

stomachdiseases.name: stomach diseases
stomachdiseases.definition: Stomach diseases is pathological processes involving the stomach.

birddiseases.name: bird diseases
birddiseases.definition: Bird diseases is diseases of birds not considered poultry, therefore usually found in zoos, parks, and the wild. The concept is differentiated from poultry diseases which is for birds raised as a source of meat or eggs for human consumption, and usually found in barnyards, hatcheries, etc.

cadmiumchloride.name: cadmium chloride
cadmiumchloride.definition: Cadmium chloride is a cadmium halide in the form of colorless crystals, soluble in water, methanol, and ethanol. It is used in photography, in dyeing, and calico printing, and as a solution to precipitate sulfides. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

meningitis.name: meningitis
meningitis.definition: Meningitis is inflammation of the coverings of the brain and/or spinal cord, which consist of the pia mater; arachnoid; and dura mater. Infections (viral, bacterial, and fungal) are the most common causes of this condition, but subarachnoid hemorrhage (hemorrhages, subarachnoid), chemical irritation (chemical meningitis), granulomatous conditions, neoplastic conditions (carcinomatous meningitis), and other inflammatory conditions may produce this syndrome. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1994, Ch24, p6)

receptor,igftype2.name: receptor , igf type 2
receptor,igftype2.definition: Igf type 2 receptor is a receptor that is specific for igf-ii and mannose-6-phosphate. The receptor is a 250-kDa single chain polypeptide which is unrelated in structure to the type 1 igf receptor (receptor, igf type 1) and does not have a tyrosine kinase domain.

sutures.name: sutures
sutures.definition: Sutures is materials used in closing a surgical or traumatic wound. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

wool.name: wool
wool.definition: Wool is the hair of sheep or other animals that is used for weaving or felting.

medicaid.name: medicaid
medicaid.definition: Medicaid is federal program, created by Public Law 89-97, Title xix, a 1965 amendment to the Social Security Act, administered by the states, that provides health care benefits to indigent and medically indigent persons.

orthodonticwires.name: orthodontic wires
orthodonticwires.definition: Orthodontic wires is wires of various dimensions and grades made of stainless steel or precious metal. They are used in orthodontic treatment.

peptideelongationfactor1.name: peptide elongation factor 1
peptideelongationfactor1.definition: Peptide elongation factor 1 is peptide elongation factor 1 is a multisubunit protein that is responsible for the GTP-dependent binding of aminoacyl-tRNAs to eukaryotic ribosomes. The alpha subunit (EF-1alpha) binds aminoacyl-tRNA and transfers it to the ribosome in a process linked to gtp hydrolysis. The beta and delta subunits (EF-1beta, EF-1delta) are involved in exchanging gdp for gtp. The gamma subunit (EF-1gamma) is a structural component.

toothgerm.name: tooth germ
toothgerm.definition: Tooth germ is the collective tissues from which an entire tooth is formed, including the dental sac; enamel organ; and dental papilla. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992)

retinalphotoreceptorcelloutersegment.name: retinal photoreceptor cell outer segment
retinalphotoreceptorcelloutersegment.definition: Retinal photoreceptor cell outer segment is the light sensitive outer portion of a retinal rod or a [MASK]. The outer segment contains a stack of disk membranes laden with photoreceptive [MASK] pigments). The outer segment is connected to the inner segment by a photoreceptor connecting cilium.

medicalorderentrysystems.name: medical order entry systems
medicalorderentrysystems.definition: Medical order entry systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, that enable providers to initiate medical procedures, prescribe medications, etc. These systems support medical decision-making and error-reduction during patient care.

codon,initiator.name: codon , initiator
codon,initiator.definition: Initiator codon is a codon that directs initiation of protein translation (translation, genetic) by stimulating the binding of initiator tRNA (rna, transfer, met). In prokaryotes, the codons aug or gug can act as initiators while in eukaryotes, aug is the only initiator codon.

biophysicalphenomena.name: biophysical phenomena
biophysicalphenomena.definition: Biophysical phenomena is the physical characteristics and processes of biological systems.

myeloidcells.name: myeloid cells
myeloidcells.definition: Myeloid cells is the classes of bone MARROW-derived blood cells in the monocytic series (monocytes and their precursors) and granulocytic series (granulocytes and their precursors).

codesofethics.name: codes of ethics
codesofethics.definition: Codes of ethics is systematic statements of principles or rules of appropriate professional conduct, usually established by professional societies.

sociallearning.name: social learning
sociallearning.definition: Social learning is the concept of new knowledge acquisition through [MASK] and interaction with others.

antigenicmodulation.name: antigenic modulation
antigenicmodulation.definition: Antigenic modulation is loss of detectable antigen from the surface of a cell after incubation with antibodies. This is one method in which some tumors escape detection by the immune system. Antigenic modulation of target antigens also reduces the therapeutic effectiveness of treatment by monoclonal antibodies.

rna,transfer,thr.name: rna , transfer , thr
rna,transfer,thr.definition: Thr transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying threonine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

stressdisorders,traumatic,acute.name: stress disorders , traumatic , acute
stressdisorders,traumatic,acute.definition: Acute traumatic stress disorders is a class of traumatic stress disorders that is characterized by the significant dissociative states seen immediately after overwhelming trauma. By definition it cannot last longer than 1 month, if it persists, a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (stress disorders, post-traumatic) is more appropriate.

aminoacids,peptides,andproteins.name: amino acids , peptides , and proteins
aminoacids,peptides,andproteins.definition: And proteins peptides amino acids is amino acids and chains of amino acids connected by peptide linkages.

moralobligations.name: moral obligations
moralobligations.definition: Moral obligations is duties that are based in ethics, rather than in law.

localgovernment.name: local government
localgovernment.definition: Local government is smallest political subdivisions within a country at which general governmental functions are carried-out.

physics.name: physics
physics.definition: Physics is the study of those aspects of energy and matter in terms of elementary principles and laws. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

icecover.name: ice cover
icecover.definition: Ice cover is a thick mass of ice formed over large regions of land; [MASK]; [MASK]; ponds; or seawater.

inhibition,psychological.name: inhibition , psychological
inhibition,psychological.definition: Psychological inhibition is the interference with or prevention of a behavioral or verbal response even though the stimulus for that response is present; in psychoanalysis the [MASK] restraining of an instinctual process.

spatialbehavior.name: spatial behavior
spatialbehavior.definition: Spatial behavior is reactions of an individual or groups of individuals with relation to the immediate surrounding area including the animate or inanimate objects within that area.

empowerment.name: empowerment
empowerment.definition: Empowerment is process of increasing the capacity of individuals or groups to make choices and to transform those choices into desired actions as deigned by the individuals or groups.

esophagealdiseases.name: esophageal diseases
esophagealdiseases.definition: Esophageal diseases is pathological processes in the esophagus.

architecturalaccessibility.name: architectural accessibility
architecturalaccessibility.definition: Architectural accessibility is designs for approaching areas inside or outside facilities.

classification.name: classification
classification.definition: Classification is the systematic arrangement of entities in any field into categories classes based on common characteristics such as properties, morphology, subject matter, etc.

osmoticpressure.name: osmotic pressure
osmoticpressure.definition: Osmotic pressure is the pressure required to prevent the passage of solvent through a semipermeable membrane that separates a pure solvent from a solution of the solvent and solute or that separates different concentrations of a solution. It is proportional to the osmolality of the solution.

testis.name: testis
testis.definition: Testis is the male gonad containing two functional parts: the seminiferous tubules for the production and transport of male germ cells (spermatogenesis) and the interstitial compartment containing leydig cells that produce androgens.

collagentypeviii.name: collagen type viii
collagentypeviii.definition: Collagen type viii is a non-fibrillar collagen originally found in descemet membrane. It is expressed in endothelial cell layers and in tissues undergoing active remodeling. It is heterotrimer comprised of alpha1(VIII) and alpha2(VIII) chains.

leukemia,plasmacell.name: leukemia , plasma cell
leukemia,plasmacell.definition: Plasma cell leukemia is a rare, aggressive variant of multiple myeloma characterized by the circulation of excessive plasma cells in the peripheral blood. It can be a primary manifestation of multiple myeloma or develop as a terminal complication during the disease.

banking,personal.name: banking , personal
banking,personal.definition: Personal banking is a financial account [MASK] up between a financial institution (such as a commercial bank) and a customer (individual, group, or business), whereby the latter may deposit and withdraw money, and where applicable, be paid interest.

corticalsynchronization.name: cortical synchronization
corticalsynchronization.definition: Cortical synchronization is eeg phase synchronization of the cortical brain region (cerebral cortex).

meaningfuluse.name: meaningful use
meaningfuluse.definition: Meaningful use is using certified electronic health records technology to improve quality, safety, efficiency, and reduce healthcare disparities; engage patients and families in their health care; improve care coordination; improve population and public health; while maintaining privacy and security.

radar.name: radar
radar.definition: Radar is a system using beamed and reflected radio signals to and from an object in such a way that range, bearing, and other characteristics of the object may be determined.

spinaldiseases.name: spinal diseases
spinaldiseases.definition: Spinal diseases is diseases involving the spine.

foodservice,hospital.name: food service , hospital
foodservice,hospital.definition: Hospital food service is hospital department that manages and supervises the dietary program in accordance with the patients' requirements.

salinewaters.name: saline waters
salinewaters.definition: Saline waters is water from natural sources which contain significant concentrations of dissolved [MASK] such as sodium chloride.

hepatitisd.name: hepatitis d
hepatitisd.definition: Hepatitis d is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by [MASK], a defective rna virus that can only infect hepatitis b patients. For its viral coating, [MASK] requires the hepatitis b surface antigens produced by these patients. Hepatitis d can occur either concomitantly with (coinfection) or subsequent to (superinfection) hepatitis b infection. Similar to hepatitis b, it is primarily transmitted by parenteral exposure, such as transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products, but can also be transmitted via sexual or intimate personal contact.

toothmovementtechniques.name: tooth movement techniques
toothmovementtechniques.definition: Tooth movement techniques is orthodontic techniques used to correct the malposition of a tooth or teeth.

myosintypeiv.name: myosin type iv
myosintypeiv.definition: Myosin type iv is a subclass of myosin found in acanthamoeba. It is a non-filamentous myosin containing a single 180-kDa myosin heavy chain.

directedmolecularevolution.name: directed molecular evolution
directedmolecularevolution.definition: Directed molecular evolution is the techniques used to produce molecules exhibiting properties that conform to the demands of the experimenter. These techniques combine methods of generating structural changes with methods of selection. They are also used to examine proposed mechanisms of evolution under in vitro selection conditions.

paclitaxel.name: paclitaxel
paclitaxel.definition: Paclitaxel is a cyclodecane isolated from the bark of the Pacific yew tree, taxus brevifolia. It stabilizes [MASK] in their polymerized form leading to cell death.

gcrichsequence.name: gc rich sequence
gcrichsequence.definition: Gc rich sequence is a nucleic acid sequence that contains an above average number of guanine and cytosine bases.

yellowfevervaccine.name: yellow fever vaccine
yellowfevervaccine.definition: Yellow fever vaccine is vaccine used to prevent yellow fever. It consists of a live attenuated 17d strain of the yellow fever virus.

alveolarboneloss.name: alveolar bone loss
alveolarboneloss.definition: Alveolar bone loss is resorption or wasting of the tooth-supporting bone (alveolar process) in the maxilla or mandible.

fluorescentantibodytechnique,direct.name: fluorescent antibody technique , direct
fluorescentantibodytechnique,direct.definition: Direct fluorescent antibody technique is a form of fluorescent antibody technique utilizing a fluorochrome conjugated to an antibody, which is added directly to a tissue or cell suspension for the detection of a specific antigen. (Bennington, Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

failuretorescue,healthcare.name: failure to rescue , health care
failuretorescue,healthcare.definition: Health care failure to rescue is inability to prevent a clinical deterioration resulting from a complication of an underlying medical condition or a complication of medical care. It implies that common risk factors for such a complication were not recognized in a timely manner or treated appropriately.

couptranscriptionfactors.name: coup transcription factors
couptranscriptionfactors.definition: Coup transcription factors is a sub-family of steroid receptor-related orphan nuclear receptors that have specificity for a variety of dna sequences related to aggtca. coup transcription factors can heterodimerize with a variety of factors including retinoic acid receptors; thyroid hormone receptors; and vitamin d receptors.

antarcticregions.name: antarctic regions
antarcticregions.definition: Antarctic regions is the continent lying around the South Pole and the southern waters of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. It includes the Falkland Islands Dependencies. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p55)

contingentnegativevariation.name: contingent negative variation
contingentnegativevariation.definition: Contingent negative variation is a negative shift of the cortical electrical potentials that increases over time. It is associated with an anticipated response to an expected stimulus and is an electrical event indicative of a state of readiness or expectancy.

hypothermia.name: hypothermia
hypothermia.definition: Hypothermia is lower than normal body temperature, especially in warm-blooded animals.

alkalinephosphatase.name: alkaline phosphatase
alkalinephosphatase.definition: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of an orthophosphoric monoester and water to an alcohol and orthophosphate. ec 3.1.3.1.

plateletfunctiontests.name: platelet function tests
plateletfunctiontests.definition: Platelet function tests is laboratory examination used to monitor and evaluate platelet function in a patient's blood.

liposomes.name: liposomes
liposomes.definition: Liposomes is artificial, single or multilaminar vesicles (made from lecithins or other lipids) that are used for the delivery of a variety of biological molecules or molecular complexes to cells, for example, drug delivery and gene transfer. They are also used to study membranes and membrane proteins.

transportationofpatients.name: transportation of patients
transportationofpatients.definition: Transportation of patients is conveying ill or injured individuals from one place to another.

hepatitisbeantigens.name: hepatitis b e antigens
hepatitisbeantigens.definition: Hepatitis b e antigens is a closely related group of antigens found in the plasma only during the infective phase of hepatitis b or in virulent chronic hepatitis b, probably indicating active virus replication; there are three subtypes which may exist in a complex with immunoglobulins g.

intestinaldiseases,parasitic.name: intestinal diseases , parasitic
intestinaldiseases,parasitic.definition: Parasitic intestinal diseases is infections of the intestines with parasites, commonly involving parasitic worms. Infections with roundworms (nematode infections) and tapeworms (cestode infections) are also known as helminthiasis.

receptors,prolactin.name: receptors , prolactin
receptors,prolactin.definition: Prolactin receptors is labile proteins on or in prolactin-sensitive cells that bind prolactin initiating the cells' physiological response to that hormone. Mammary casein synthesis is one of the responses. The receptors are also found in placenta, liver, testes, kidneys, ovaries, and other organs and bind and respond to certain other hormones and their analogs and antagonists. This receptor is related to the growth hormone receptor.

vascularfistula.name: vascular fistula
vascularfistula.definition: Vascular fistula is an abnormal passage between two or more blood vessels, between arteries; veins; or between an artery and a vein.

rna,nuclear.name: rna , nuclear
rna,nuclear.definition: Nuclear rna is rna molecules found in the nucleus either associated with chromosomes or in the nucleoplasm.

stress,physiological.name: stress , physiological
stress,physiological.definition: Physiological stress is the unfavorable effect of environmental factors (stressors) on the physiological functions of an organism. Prolonged unresolved physiological stress can affect homeostasis of the organism, and may lead to damaging or pathological conditions.

silverproteins.name: silver proteins
silverproteins.definition: Silver proteins is compounds of silver and proteins used as topical anti-infective agents.

wastedisposalfacilities.name: waste disposal facilities
wastedisposalfacilities.definition: Waste disposal facilities is sites that receive and store waste products. Some facilities also sort, process, and recycle specific waste products.

fetalhypoxia.name: fetal hypoxia
fetalhypoxia.definition: Fetal hypoxia is deficient oxygenation of [MASK].

groupattribute.name: group attribute
groupattribute.definition: Group attribute is values that reference groups to which this entry belongs.

ironcompounds.name: iron compounds
ironcompounds.definition: Iron compounds is organic and inorganic compounds that contain iron as an integral part of the molecule.

hepatitisc,chronic.name: hepatitis c , chronic
hepatitisc,chronic.definition: Chronic hepatitis c is inflammation of the liver in humans that is caused by hepatitis c virus lasting six months or more. Chronic hepatitis c can lead to liver cirrhosis.

tamoxifen.name: tamoxifen
tamoxifen.definition: Tamoxifen is one of the [MASK] with tissue-specific activities. Tamoxifen acts as an anti-estrogen (inhibiting agent) in the mammary tissue, but as an estrogen (stimulating agent) in cholesterol metabolism, [MASK], and cell proliferation in the endometrium.

myosintypev.name: myosin type v
myosintypev.definition: Myosin type v is a subclass of myosin involved in organelle transport and membrane targeting. It is abundantly found in nervous tissue and neurosecretory cells. The heavy chains of myosin v contain unusually long [MASK] domains that are believed to aid in translocating molecules over large distances.

drinkingbehavior.name: drinking behavior
drinkingbehavior.definition: Drinking behavior is behaviors associated with the ingesting of water and other liquids; includes rhythmic patterns of drinking (time intervals - onset and duration), frequency and satiety.

glycogen.name: glycogen
glycogen.definition: Glycogen is a substance deposited in bodily tissues as a store of carbohydrates. It is a polysaccharide which forms glucose on hydrolysis.

bloodpressuremonitoring,ambulatory.name: blood pressure monitoring , ambulatory
bloodpressuremonitoring,ambulatory.definition: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring is method in which repeated blood pressure readings are made while the patient undergoes normal daily activities. It allows quantitative analysis of the high blood pressure load over time, can help distinguish between types of hypertension, and can assess the effectiveness of antihypertensive therapy.

endometrialstromaltumors.name: endometrial stromal tumors
endometrialstromaltumors.definition: Endometrial stromal tumors is neoplasms of the endometrial stroma that sometimes involve the myometrium. These tumors contain cells that may closely or remotely resemble the normal stromal cells. Endometrial stromal neoplasms are divided into three categories: (1) benign stromal nodules; (2) low-grade stromal sarcoma, or endolymphatic stromal myosis; and (3) malignant endometrial stromal sarcoma (sarcoma, endometrial stromal).

myeloidprogenitorcells.name: myeloid progenitor cells
myeloidprogenitorcells.definition: Myeloid progenitor cells is stem cells derived from hematopoietic stem cells. Derived from these myeloid progenitor cells are the megakaryocytes; erythroid cells; myeloid cells; and some [MASK].

environmentaleffectofhumans.name: environmental effect of humans
environmentaleffectofhumans.definition: Environmental effect of humans is environmental alterations resulting from human activities.

renewableenergy.name: renewable energy
renewableenergy.definition: Renewable energy is forms of energy that are constantly and rapidly renewed by natural processes such as solar, ocean wave, and [MASK] energy. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

liverdiseases,alcoholic.name: liver diseases , alcoholic
liverdiseases,alcoholic.definition: Alcoholic liver diseases is liver diseases associated with alcoholism. It usually refers to the coexistence of two or more subentities, i.e., [MASK]; alcoholic hepatitis; and alcoholic cirrhosis.

isletamyloidpolypeptide.name: islet amyloid polypeptide
isletamyloidpolypeptide.definition: Islet amyloid polypeptide is a pancreatic beta-cell hormone that is co-secreted with insulin. It displays an anorectic effect on nutrient metabolism by inhibiting gastric acid secretion, gastric emptying and postprandial glucagon secretion. Islet amyloid polypeptide can fold into amyloid fibrils that have been found as a major constituent of pancreatic amyloid deposits.

cellplasticity.name: cell plasticity
cellplasticity.definition: Cell plasticity is the ability of a cell to change its phenotype in response to changes in the environment.

indicatorsandreagents.name: indicators and reagents
indicatorsandreagents.definition: Indicators and reagents is substances used for the detection, identification, analysis, etc. of chemical, biological, or pathologic processes or conditions. Indicators are substances that change in physical appearance, e.g., [MASK], at or approaching the endpoint of a chemical titration, e.g., on the passage between acidity and alkalinity. Reagents are substances used for the detection or determination of another substance by chemical or microscopical means, especially analysis. Types of reagents are precipitants, solvents, oxidizers, reducers, fluxes, and colorimetric reagents. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed, p301, p499)

urinarytractinfections.name: urinary tract infections
urinarytractinfections.definition: Urinary tract infections is inflammatory responses of the epithelium of the urinary tract to microbial invasions. They are often bacterial infections with associated bacteriuria and pyuria.

psychiatricsomatictherapies.name: psychiatric somatic therapies
psychiatricsomatictherapies.definition: Psychiatric somatic therapies is the biologic treatment of mental disorders (e.g., electroconvulsive therapy), in contrast with psychotherapy. (Stone, American Psychiatric Glossary, 1988, p159)

priorauthorization.name: prior authorization
priorauthorization.definition: Prior authorization is a decision by a health insurer or plan that a health care service, treatment plan, prescription drug or [MASK] is medically necessary.

plantproteins,dietary.name: plant proteins , dietary
plantproteins,dietary.definition: Dietary plant proteins is proteins which are present in or isolated from vegetables or vegetable products used as food. The concept is distinguished from plant proteins which refers to non-dietary proteins from plants.

libraries.name: libraries
libraries.definition: Libraries is collections of systematically acquired and organized [MASK], and usually providing assistance to users. (eric Thesaurus, http://www.eric.ed.gov/ accessed 2/1/2008)

arcticregions.name: arctic regions
arcticregions.definition: Arctic regions is the Arctic Ocean and the lands in it and adjacent to it. It includes Point Barrow, Alaska, most of the Franklin District in Canada, two thirds of Greenland, Svalbard, Franz Josef Land, Lapland, Novaya Zemlya, and Northern Siberia. (Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p66)

oldageassistance.name: old age assistance
oldageassistance.definition: Old age assistance is financial assistance for the impoverished elderly through public funding of programs, services, and individual income supplements.

adrenalglands.name: adrenal glands
adrenalglands.definition: Adrenal glands is a pair of glands located at the cranial pole of each of the two kidneys. Each adrenal gland is composed of two distinct endocrine tissues with separate embryonic origins, the adrenal cortex producing steroids and the adrenal medulla producing neurotransmitters.

nervefibers.name: nerve fibers
nervefibers.definition: Nerve fibers is slender processes of neurons, including the axons and their glial envelopes (myelin sheath). Nerve fibers conduct nerve impulses to and from the central nervous system.

referencestandards.name: reference standards
referencestandards.definition: Reference standards is a basis of value established for the measure of quantity, weight, extent or quality, e.g. weight standards, standard solutions, methods, techniques, and procedures used in diagnosis and therapy.

skindiseases,infectious.name: skin diseases , infectious
skindiseases,infectious.definition: Infectious skin diseases is skin diseases caused by bacteria, fungi, parasites, or viruses.

venousinsufficiency.name: venous insufficiency
venousinsufficiency.definition: Venous insufficiency is impaired venous blood flow or venous return (venous stasis), usually caused by inadequate venous valves. Venous insufficiency often occurs in the legs, and is associated with edema and sometimes with venous stasis [MASK] at the ankle.

apoptosisinducingfactor.name: apoptosis inducing factor
apoptosisinducingfactor.definition: Apoptosis inducing factor is a flavoprotein that functions as a powerful antioxidant in the mitochondria and promotes apoptosis when released from the mitochondria. In mammalian cells aif is released in response to pro-apoptotic protein members of the bcl-2 protein family. It translocates to the cell nucleus and binds dna to stimulate CASPASE-independent chromatin condensation.

proteinbinding.name: protein binding
proteinbinding.definition: Protein binding is the process in which substances, either endogenous or exogenous, bind to proteins, peptides, enzymes, protein precursors, or allied compounds. Specific protein-binding measures are often used as assays in diagnostic assessments.

membranepotentials.name: membrane potentials
membranepotentials.definition: Membrane potentials is the voltage differences across a membrane. For cellular membranes they are computed by subtracting the voltage measured outside the membrane from the voltage measured inside the membrane. They result from differences of inside versus outside concentration of potassium, sodium, chloride, and other ions across cells' or organelles membranes. For excitable cells, the resting membrane potentials range between -30 and -100 millivolts. Physical, chemical, or electrical stimuli can make a membrane potential more negative (hyperpolarization), or less negative (depolarization).

familygroup.name: family group
familygroup.definition: Family group is a group of family doctors who work together and in close collaboration with other health and social services professionals.

bonematrix.name: bone matrix
bonematrix.definition: Bone matrix is extracellular substance of bone tissue consisting of collagen fibers, ground substance, and inorganic crystalline minerals and [MASK].

genes,ras.name: genes , ras
genes,ras.definition: Ras genes is family of retrovirus-associated dna sequences (ras) originally isolated from Harvey (H-ras, Ha-ras, rasH) and Kirsten (K-ras, Ki-ras, rasK) murine sarcoma viruses. Ras genes are widely conserved among animal species and sequences corresponding to both H-ras and K-ras genes have been detected in human, avian, murine, and non-vertebrate genomes. The closely related N-ras gene has been detected in human neuroblastoma and sarcoma cell lines. All genes of the family have a similar exon-intron structure and each encodes a p21 protein.

brancheddnasignalamplificationassay.name: branched dna signal amplification assay
brancheddnasignalamplificationassay.definition: Branched dna signal amplification assay is a molecular probe technique that utilizes branched dna (bDNA) as a means to amplify the hybridization signal. One end of the bDNA molecule is designed to bind a specific target, while the other end of the bDNA molecule contains many branches of dna that are designed to bind a probe used for signal detection.

food,formulated.name: food , formulated
food,formulated.definition: Formulated food is food and dietary formulations including elemental (chemically defined formula) diets, synthetic and semisynthetic diets, space diets, weight-reduction formulas, tube-feeding diets, complete liquid diets, and supplemental liquid and solid diets.

gallbladderdiseases.name: gallbladder diseases
gallbladderdiseases.definition: Gallbladder diseases is diseases of the gallbladder. They generally involve the impairment of [MASK] flow, gallstones in the biliary tract, infections, neoplasms, or other diseases.

tissuearrayanalysis.name: tissue array analysis
tissuearrayanalysis.definition: Tissue array analysis is the simultaneous analysis of multiple samples of tissues or cells from biopsy or in vitro culture that have been arranged in an array format on slides or microchips.

eyemanifestations.name: eye manifestations
eyemanifestations.definition: Eye manifestations is ocular disorders attendant upon non-ocular disease or injury.

falsepositivereactions.name: false positive reactions
falsepositivereactions.definition: False positive reactions is positive test results in subjects who do not possess the attribute for which the test is conducted. The labeling of healthy persons as diseased when screening in the detection of disease. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

uterinediseases.name: uterine diseases
uterinediseases.definition: Uterine diseases is pathological processes involving any part of the uterus.

maculardegeneration.name: macular degeneration
maculardegeneration.definition: Macular degeneration is degenerative changes in the retina usually of older adults which results in a loss of vision in the center of the [MASK] (the macula lutea) because of damage to the retina. It occurs in dry and wet forms.

pharmacologicalphenomena.name: pharmacological phenomena
pharmacologicalphenomena.definition: Pharmacological phenomena is interactions that occur between a living organism and chemicals that affect normal or abnormal biochemical function.

cellmigrationassays.name: cell migration assays
cellmigrationassays.definition: Cell migration assays is specific assays that measure the migration of cells. They are commonly used to measure the migration of immune cells in response to stimuli and the inhibition of immune cell migration by immunosuppressive factors.

tuberculosis,cutaneous.name: tuberculosis , cutaneous
tuberculosis,cutaneous.definition: Cutaneous tuberculosis is tuberculosis of the skin. It includes scrofuloderma and tuberculid, but not lupus vulgaris.

clinicalaudit.name: clinical audit
clinicalaudit.definition: Clinical audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel to improve the quality of patient care and outcomes. The clinical audit was formally introduced in 1993 into the United Kingdom's National Health Service.

biomedicalresearch.name: biomedical research
biomedicalresearch.definition: Biomedical research is research that involves the application of the natural sciences, especially biology and physiology, to medicine.

eukaryoticinitiationfactors.name: eukaryotic initiation factors
eukaryoticinitiationfactors.definition: Eukaryotic initiation factors is peptide initiation factors from eukaryotic organisms. Over twelve factors are involved in peptide chain initiation, translational in eukaryotic cells. Many of these factors play a role in controlling the rate of mrna translation.

fatnecrosis.name: fat necrosis
fatnecrosis.definition: Fat necrosis is a condition in which the death of adipose tissue results in neutral fats being split into fatty acids and glycerol.

internet.name: internet
internet.definition: Internet is a loose confederation of computer communication networks around the world. The networks that make up the Internet are connected through several backbone networks. The Internet grew out of the us Government ARPAnet project and was designed to facilitate information exchange.

mediterraneansea.name: mediterranean sea
mediterraneansea.definition: Mediterranean sea is an inland sea enclosed by Europe on the west and north, by Asia on the east, and Africa on the south.

aldehydereductase.name: aldehyde reductase
aldehydereductase.definition: Aldehyde reductase is an enzyme that catalyzes reversibly the oxidation of an aldose to an alditol. It possesses broad specificity for many aldoses. ec 1.1.1.21.

freedom.name: freedom
freedom.definition: Freedom is the rights of individuals to act and make decisions without external constraints.

meanplateletvolume.name: mean platelet volume
meanplateletvolume.definition: Mean platelet volume is a measure of the size of platelets.

postnatalcare.name: postnatal care
postnatalcare.definition: Postnatal care is the care provided to women and their newborns for the first few months following childbirth.

careerchoice.name: career choice
careerchoice.definition: Career choice is selection of a type of occupation or profession.

animaldiseases.name: animal diseases
animaldiseases.definition: Animal diseases is diseases that occur in vertebrate animals.

thymusextracts.name: thymus extracts
thymusextracts.definition: Thymus extracts is extracts of the thymus gland that contain specific factors, peptides, and proteins with specific biological activities.

mapkinasekinasekinase1.name: map kinase kinase kinase 1
mapkinasekinasekinase1.definition: Map kinase kinase kinase 1 is a 195-kDa zinc finger motif-containing map kinase kinase kinase with broad specificity for map kinase kinases. It localizes to the cytoskeleton and can activate a variety of map kinase-dependent pathways.

samplesize.name: sample size
samplesize.definition: Sample size is the number of units (persons, animals, patients, specified circumstances, etc.) in a population to be studied. The sample size should be big enough to have a high likelihood of detecting a true difference between two groups. (From Wassertheil-Smoller, Biostatistics and Epidemiology, 1990, p95)

bodyfluidcompartments.name: body fluid compartments
bodyfluidcompartments.definition: Body fluid compartments is the two types of spaces between which water and other body fluids are distributed: extracellular and intracellular.

templates,genetic.name: templates , genetic
templates,genetic.definition: Genetic templates is macromolecular molds for the synthesis of complementary macromolecules, as in dna replication; genetic transcription of dna to rna, and genetic translation of rna into polypeptides.

childwelfare.name: child welfare
childwelfare.definition: Child welfare is organized efforts by communities or organizations to improve the health and well-being of the child.

mandatoryprograms.name: mandatory programs
mandatoryprograms.definition: Mandatory programs is programs in which participation is required.

fetalweight.name: fetal weight
fetalweight.definition: Fetal weight is the weight of the fetus in utero. It is usually estimated by various formulas based on measurements made during prenatal ultrasonography.

potassium,dietary.name: potassium , dietary
potassium,dietary.definition: Dietary potassium is potassium or potassium compounds used in foods or as foods.

ageofonset.name: age of onset
ageofonset.definition: Age of onset is the age, developmental stage, or period of life at which a disease or the initial symptoms or manifestations of a disease appear in an individual.

breast.name: breast
breast.definition: Breast is in humans, one of the paired regions in the anterior portion of the thorax. The breasts consist of the mammary glands, the skin, the muscles, the adipose tissue, and the connective tissues.

ammoniumhydroxide.name: ammonium hydroxide
ammoniumhydroxide.definition: Ammonium hydroxide is the hydroxy [MASK] of ammonium ion. It is formed when [MASK] reacts with water molecules in solution.

environmentalillness.name: environmental illness
environmentalillness.definition: Environmental illness is a polysymptomatic condition believed by clinical ecologists to result from immune dysregulation induced by common foods, allergens, and chemicals, resulting in various physical and mental disorders. The medical community has remained largely skeptical of the existence of this "disease", given the plethora of symptoms attributed to environmental illness, the lack of reproducible laboratory abnormalities, and the use of unproven therapies to treat the condition. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

factorxainhibitors.name: factor xa inhibitors
factorxainhibitors.definition: Factor xa inhibitors is endogenous factors and drugs that inhibit or block the activity of factor xa.

fluorescentantibodytechnique.name: fluorescent antibody technique
fluorescentantibodytechnique.definition: Fluorescent antibody technique is test for tissue antigen using either a direct method, by conjugation of antibody with fluorescent dye (fluorescent antibody technique, direct) or an indirect method, by formation of antigen-antibody complex which is then labeled with fluorescein-conjugated anti-immunoglobulin antibody (fluorescent antibody technique, indirect). The tissue is then examined by fluorescence microscopy.

growthsubstances.name: growth substances
growthsubstances.definition: Growth substances is signal molecules that are involved in the control of cell growth and differentiation.

braindiseases.name: brain diseases
braindiseases.definition: Brain diseases is pathologic conditions affecting the brain, which is composed of the intracranial components of the central nervous system. This includes (but is not limited to) the cerebral cortex; intracranial [MASK] matter; basal ganglia; thalamus; hypothalamus; brain stem; and cerebellum.

genes,matingtype,fungal.name: genes , mating type , fungal
genes,matingtype,fungal.definition: Fungal mating type genes is fungal genes that mostly encode transcription factors. In some fungi they also encode pheromones and pheromone receptors. The transcription factors control expression of specific proteins that give a cell its mating identity. Opposite mating type identities are required for mating.

mapsastopic.name: maps as topic
mapsastopic.definition: Maps as topic is works about representations, normally to scale and on a flat medium, of a selection of material or [MASK] features on the surface of the earth, the heavens, or celestial bodies.

oralmucosalabsorption.name: oral mucosal absorption
oralmucosalabsorption.definition: Oral mucosal absorption is uptake of substances into the body via the mucosal surfaces (mucous membrane) of the oral cavity.

bacterialload.name: bacterial load
bacterialload.definition: Bacterial load is measurable quantity of bacteria in an object, organism, or organism compartment.

bodyweight.name: body weight
bodyweight.definition: Body weight is the mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

pregnancycomplications,parasitic.name: pregnancy complications , parasitic
pregnancycomplications,parasitic.definition: Parasitic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and parasitic diseases. The parasitic infection may precede or follow fertilization.

caregivers.name: caregivers
caregivers.definition: Caregivers is persons who provide care to those who need supervision or assistance in illness or disability. They may provide the care in the home, in a hospital, or in an institution. Although caregivers include trained medical, nursing, and other health personnel, the concept also refers to parents, spouses, or other family members, friends, members of the clergy, teachers, social workers, fellow patients.

carcinoma,papillary,follicular.name: carcinoma , papillary , follicular
carcinoma,papillary,follicular.definition: Follicular papillary carcinoma is a thyroid neoplasm of mixed papillary and follicular arrangement. Its biological behavior and prognosis is the same as that of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1271)

activetransport,cellnucleus.name: active transport , cell nucleus
activetransport,cellnucleus.definition: Cell nucleus active transport is gated transport mechanisms by which proteins or rna are moved across the nuclear membrane.

ovulationprediction.name: ovulation prediction
ovulationprediction.definition: Ovulation prediction is predicting the time of ovulation can be achieved by measuring the preovulatory elevation of estradiol; luteinizing hormone or other hormones in blood or urine. Accuracy of ovulation prediction depends on the completeness of the hormone profiles, and the ability to determine the preovulatory lh peak.

ischemicpreconditioning,myocardial.name: ischemic preconditioning , myocardial
ischemicpreconditioning,myocardial.definition: Myocardial ischemic preconditioning is exposure of myocardial tissue to brief, repeated periods of vascular occlusion in order to render the myocardium resistant to the deleterious effects of ischemia or reperfusion. The period of pre-exposure and the number of times the tissue is exposed to ischemia and reperfusion vary, the average being 3 to 5 minutes.

genomiclibrary.name: genomic library
genomiclibrary.definition: Genomic library is a form of gene library containing the complete dna sequences present in the genome of a given organism. It contrasts with a cDNA library which contains only sequences utilized in protein coding (lacking introns).

familialmediterraneanfever.name: familial mediterranean fever
familialmediterraneanfever.definition: Familial mediterranean fever is a group of hereditary autoinflammation diseases, characterized by recurrent fever, abdominal pain, headache, rash, pleurisy; and arthritis. orchitis; benign meningitis; and amyloidosis may also occur. Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in marenostrin gene result in autosomal recessive transmission; simple heterozygous, autosomal dominant form of the disease.

complementactivation.name: complement activation
complementactivation.definition: Complement activation is the sequential activation of serum complement proteins to create the complement membrane attack complex. Factors initiating complement activation include antigen-antibody complexes, microbial antigens, or cell surface polysaccharides.

rednucleus.name: red nucleus
rednucleus.definition: Red nucleus is a pinkish-yellow portion of the midbrain situated in the rostral mesencephalic tegmentum. It receives a large [MASK] from the contralateral half of the cerebellum via the superior cerebellar peduncle and a [MASK] from the ipsilateral motor cortex.

psychiatricstatusratingscales.name: psychiatric status rating scales
psychiatricstatusratingscales.definition: Psychiatric status rating scales is standardized procedures utilizing rating scales or interview schedules carried out by health personnel for evaluating the degree of mental illness.

chromatography,gel.name: chromatography , gel
chromatography,gel.definition: Gel chromatography is chromatography on non-ionic gels without regard to the mechanism of solute discrimination.

transcriptionfactor3.name: transcription factor 3
transcriptionfactor3.definition: Transcription factor 3 is a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that plays a role in determining cell fate during embryogenesis. It forms a heterodimer with twist-related protein 1 and achaete-scute gene COMPLEX-related transcription factors.

brainregeneration.name: brain regeneration
brainregeneration.definition: Brain regeneration is endogenous repair and regeneration of the brain.

disorderofsexdevelopment,46,xy.name: disorder of sex development , 46 , xy
disorderofsexdevelopment,46,xy.definition: Xy 46 disorder of [MASK] development is disorder of [MASK] development , 46 , xy

autismspectrumdisorder.name: autism spectrum disorder
autismspectrumdisorder.definition: Autism spectrum disorder is wide continuum of associated cognitive and neurobehavioral disorders, including, but not limited to, three core-defining features: impairments in socialization, impairments in verbal and nonverbal communication, and restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviors. (from [MASK])

coalash.name: coal ash
coalash.definition: Coal ash is residue generated from combustion of coal or petroleum.

collagentypeiv.name: collagen type iv
collagentypeiv.definition: Collagen type iv is a non-fibrillar collagen found in the structure of basement membrane. Collagen type iv molecules assemble to form a sheet-like network which is involved in maintaining the structural integrity of basement membranes. The predominant form of the protein is comprised of two alpha1(IV) subunits and one alpha2(IV) subunit, however, at least six different alpha subunits can be incorporated into the heterotrimer.

breathholding.name: breath holding
breathholding.definition: Breath holding is an involuntary or voluntary pause in breathing, sometimes accompanied by loss of consciousness.

atpbindingcassettetransporter1.name: atp binding cassette transporter 1
atpbindingcassettetransporter1.definition: Atp binding cassette transporter 1 is a superfamily of integral ATP-binding cassette membrane proteins whose expression pattern is consistent with a role in lipid (cholesterol) efflux. It is implicated in tangier disease, characterized by accumulation of cholesteryl ester in various tissues.

testosterone.name: testosterone
testosterone.definition: Testosterone is a potent androgenic steroid and major product secreted by the leydig cells of the testis. Its production is stimulated by luteinizing hormone from the pituitary gland. In turn, testosterone exerts [MASK] control of the pituitary lh and fsh secretion. Depending on the tissues, testosterone can be further converted to dihydrotestosterone or estradiol.

mapkinasekinase1.name: map kinase kinase 1
mapkinasekinase1.definition: Map kinase kinase 1 is an abundant 43-kDa mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase subtype with specificity for mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 and mitogen-activated protein kinase 3.

boneplates.name: bone plates
boneplates.definition: Bone plates is implantable fracture fixation devices attached to bone fragments with screws to bridge the fracture gap and shield the fracture site from stress as bone heals. (umdns, 1999)

hepatitis.name: hepatitis
hepatitis.definition: Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver.

parentalconsent.name: parental consent
parentalconsent.definition: Parental consent is informed consent given by a parent on behalf of a minor or otherwise incompetent child.

doubleeffectprinciple.name: double effect principle
doubleeffectprinciple.definition: Double effect principle is guideline for determining when it is morally permissible to perform an action to pursue a good end with knowledge that the action will also bring about bad results. It generally states that, in cases where a contemplated action has such double effect, the action is permissible only if: it is not wrong in itself; the bad result is not intended; the good result is not a direct causal result of the bad result; and the good result is "proportionate to" the bad result. (from Solomon, "Double Effect," in Becker, The Encyclopedia of Ethics, 1992)

encephalitis,herpessimplex.name: encephalitis , herpes simplex
encephalitis,herpessimplex.definition: Herpes simplex encephalitis is an acute (or rarely chronic) inflammatory process of the brain caused by simplexvirus infections which may be fatal. The majority of infections are caused by human herpesvirus 1 (herpesvirus 1, human) and less often by human herpesvirus 2 (herpesvirus 2, human). Clinical manifestations include fever; headache; seizures; hallucinations; behavioral alterations; aphasia; hemiparesis; and coma. Pathologically, the condition is marked by a hemorrhagic necrosis involving the medial and inferior temporal lobe and orbital regions of the frontal lobe. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp751-4)

hepatitisb.name: hepatitis b
hepatitisb.definition: Hepatitis b is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by a member of the orthohepadnavirus genus, hepatitis b virus. It is primarily transmitted by parenteral exposure, such as transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products, but can also be transmitted via sexual or intimate personal contact.

surgicalfixationdevices.name: surgical fixation devices
surgicalfixationdevices.definition: Surgical fixation devices is devices used to hold tissue structures together for repair, reconstruction or to close wounds. They may consist of adsorbable or non-adsorbable, natural or synthetic materials. They include tissue adhesives, skin tape, sutures, buttons, staples, clips, screws, etc., each designed to conform to various tissue geometries.

heartbypass,left.name: heart bypass , left
heartbypass,left.definition: Left heart bypass is diversion of the flow of blood from the pulmonary veins directly to the aorta, avoiding the left atrium and the left ventricle (Dorland, 27th ed). This is a temporary procedure usually performed to assist other surgical procedures.

myosinlightchains.name: myosin light chains
myosinlightchains.definition: Myosin light chains is the smaller subunits of myosins that bind near the head groups of myosin heavy chains. The myosin light chains have a molecular weight of about 20 KDa and there are usually one essential and one regulatory pair of light chains associated with each heavy chain. Many myosin light chains that bind calcium are considered "calmodulin-like" proteins.

predictivevalueoftests.name: predictive value of tests
predictivevalueoftests.definition: Predictive value of tests is in screening and [MASK], the probability that a person with a positive test is a true positive (i.e., has the disease), is referred to as the predictive value of a positive test; whereas, the predictive value of a negative test is the probability that the person with a negative test does not have the disease. Predictive value is related to the sensitivity and specificity of the test.

genes,duplicate.name: genes , duplicate
genes,duplicate.definition: Duplicate genes is two identical genes showing the same phenotypic action but localized in different regions of a chromosome or on different chromosomes. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

clothing.name: clothing
clothing.definition: Clothing is fabric or other material used to cover the body.

mentalstatusanddementiatests.name: mental status and dementia tests
mentalstatusanddementiatests.definition: Mental status and dementia tests is tests designed to assess various aspects of neurocognitive function or dementia.

troponin.name: troponin
troponin.definition: Troponin is one of the minor protein components of skeletal and cardiac muscles. It functions as the calcium-binding component in a complex with beta-tropomyosin; actin; and myosin and confers calcium sensitivity to the cross-linked actin and myosin filaments. Troponin itself is a complex of three regulatory proteins (troponin c; [MASK]; and troponin t).

polyvinylchloride.name: polyvinyl chloride
polyvinylchloride.definition: Polyvinyl chloride is a polyvinyl resin used extensively in the manufacture of plastics, including medical devices, tubing, and other packaging. It is also used as a rubber substitute.

skullneoplasms.name: skull neoplasms
skullneoplasms.definition: Skull neoplasms is neoplasms of the bony part of the skull.

microwaveimaging.name: microwave imaging
microwaveimaging.definition: Microwave imaging is use of microwaves as a diagnostic tool.

infant,newborn,diseases.name: infant , newborn , diseases
infant,newborn,diseases.definition: Diseases newborn infant is diseases of newborn infants present at birth (congenital) or developing within the first month of birth. It does not include hereditary diseases not manifesting at birth or within the first 30 days of life nor does it include inborn errors of metabolism. Both hereditary diseases and metabolism, inborn errors are available as general concepts.

hepatocytenuclearfactor4.name: hepatocyte nuclear factor 4
hepatocytenuclearfactor4.definition: [MASK] nuclear factor 4 is a subfamily of nuclear receptors that regulate genetic transcription of a diverse group of genes involved in the synthesis of blood coagulation factors; and in glucose; cholesterol; and fatty acids metabolism.

enzyme.name: enzyme
enzyme.definition: Enzyme is biological molecules that possess catalytic activity. They may occur naturally or be synthetically created. Enzymes are usually proteins, however catalytic RNA and [MASK] molecules have also been identified.

clay.name: clay
clay.definition: Clay is a naturally-occurring rock or soil constituent characterized by particles with a diameter of less than 0.005 mm. It is composed primarily of hydrous aluminum silicates, trace amounts of metal oxides, and organic matter.

organiccationtransportproteins.name: organic cation transport proteins
organiccationtransportproteins.definition: Organic cation transport proteins is a family of proteins involved in the transport of organic cations. They play an important role in the elimination of a variety of endogenous substances, xenobiotics, and their metabolites from the body.

societies,hospital.name: societies , hospital
societies,hospital.definition: Hospital societies is societies having institutional membership limited to hospitals and other health care institutions.

environmentalhealth.name: environmental health
environmentalhealth.definition: Environmental health is the science of controlling or modifying those conditions, influences, or forces surrounding man which relate to promoting, establishing, and maintaining health.

briefpsychiatricratingscale.name: brief psychiatric rating scale
briefpsychiatricratingscale.definition: Brief psychiatric rating scale is a scale comprising 18 symptom constructs chosen to represent relatively independent dimensions of manifest psychopathology. The initial intended use was to provide more efficient assessment of treatment response in clinical psychopharmacology research; however, the scale was readily adapted to other uses. (From Hersen, m. and Bellack, a.s., Dictionary of Behavioral Assessment Techniques, p. 87)

georgia.name: georgia
georgia.definition: Georgia is a state located in the southeastern United States, The capital is Atlanta.

dentalprosthesisdesign.name: dental prosthesis design
dentalprosthesisdesign.definition: Dental prosthesis design is the plan and delineation of dental prostheses in general or a specific dental prosthesis. It does not include denture design. The framework usually consists of metal.

apoptosisregulatoryproteins.name: apoptosis regulatory proteins
apoptosisregulatoryproteins.definition: Apoptosis regulatory proteins is a large group of proteins that control apoptosis. This family of proteins includes many oncogene proteins as well as a wide variety of classes of intracellular signaling peptides and proteins such as caspases.

bilereflux.name: bile reflux
bilereflux.definition: [MASK] reflux is retrograde [MASK] flow. Reflux of [MASK] can be from the duodenum to the stomach (duodenogastric reflux); to the esophagus (gastroesophageal reflux); or to the pancreas.

growthcharts.name: growth charts
growthcharts.definition: Growth charts is graphic displays of height and weight showing development over time.

secondarymetabolism.name: secondary metabolism
secondarymetabolism.definition: Secondary metabolism is a physiochemical process which occurs in a wide range of organisms which unlike basal metabolism is not required for or essential to short-term survivability but to long-term general well-being of the organism.

nitrogenfixation.name: nitrogen fixation
