nitrogenfixation.definition: Nitrogen fixation is the process in certain bacteria; fungi; and cyanobacteria converting free atmospheric nitrogen to biologically usable forms of nitrogen, such as [MASK]; nitrates; and amino compounds.

pharmacologicactions.name: pharmacologic actions
pharmacologicactions.definition: Pharmacologic actions is a broad category of chemical actions and uses that result in the prevention, treatment, cure or diagnosis of disease. Included here are drugs and chemicals that act by altering normal body functions, such as the reproductive control agents and anesthetics. Effects of chemicals on the environment are also included.

receptors,glucagon.name: receptors , glucagon
receptors,glucagon.definition: Glucagon receptors is cell surface receptors that bind glucagon with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Activation of glucagon receptors causes a variety of effects; the best understood is the initiation of a complex enzymatic cascade in the liver which ultimately increases the availability of glucose to body organs.

genetics,behavioral.name: genetics , behavioral
genetics,behavioral.definition: Behavioral genetics is the experimental study of the relationship between the genotype of an organism and its behavior. The scope includes the effects of genes on simple sensory processes to complex organization of the nervous system.

solutecarrierfamily12,member2.name: solute carrier family 12 , member 2
solutecarrierfamily12,member2.definition: Member 2 solute carrier family 12 is na-K-Cl transporter ubiquitously expressed. It plays a key role in [MASK] secretion in epithelial cells and cell volume regulation in nonepithelial cells.

students.name: students
students.definition: Students is individuals enrolled in a school or formal educational program.

anatomy,veterinary.name: anatomy , veterinary
anatomy,veterinary.definition: Veterinary anatomy is the study of the anatomical structures of animals.

follicularphase.name: follicular phase
follicularphase.definition: Follicular phase is the period of the menstrual cycle representing follicular growth, increase in ovarian estrogen (estrogens) production, and epithelial proliferation of the endometrium. Follicular phase begins with the onset of menstruation and ends with ovulation.

photoperiod.name: photoperiod
photoperiod.definition: Photoperiod is the time period of daily exposure that an organism receives from daylight or artificial light. It is believed that photoperiodic responses may affect the control of energy balance and thermoregulation.

medicalrecordadministrators.name: medical record administrators
medicalrecordadministrators.definition: Medical record administrators is individuals professionally qualified in the management of patients' records. Duties may include planning, designing, and managing systems for patient administrative and clinical data, as well as patient medical records. The concept includes medical record technicians.

socialnorms.name: social norms
socialnorms.definition: Social norms is customary standards that govern behavior in groups, cultures, or societies. They reflect what a group deems acceptable in a social context in terms of appropriate and inappropriate values, beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.

respiratorytractabsorption.name: respiratory tract absorption
respiratorytractabsorption.definition: Respiratory tract absorption is uptake of substances via the respiratory system.

contraceptionbehavior.name: contraception behavior
contraceptionbehavior.definition: Contraception behavior is behavior patterns of those practicing contraception.

softtissueinjuries.name: soft tissue injuries
softtissueinjuries.definition: Soft tissue injuries is injuries of tissue other than bone. The concept is usually general and does not customarily refer to internal organs or viscera. It is meaningful with reference to regions or organs where soft tissue (muscle, fat, skin) should be differentiated from bones or bone tissue, as "soft tissue injuries of the hand".

closedfracturereduction.name: closed fracture reduction
closedfracturereduction.definition: [MASK] reduction is a procedure in which normal alignment of a fractured bone is restored by orthopedic manipulation without incision.

neonatalscreening.name: neonatal screening
neonatalscreening.definition: Neonatal screening is the identification of selected parameters in newborn infants by various tests, examinations, or other procedures. Screening may be performed by clinical or laboratory measures. a screening test is designed to sort out healthy neonates (infant, newborn) from those not well, but the screening test is not intended as a diagnostic device, rather instead as epidemiologic.

mouthbreathing.name: mouth breathing
mouthbreathing.definition: Mouth breathing is abnormal breathing through the mouth, usually associated with obstructive disorders of the nasal passages.

enzymeinduction.name: enzyme induction
enzymeinduction.definition: Enzyme induction is an increase in the rate of synthesis of an enzyme due to the presence of an inducer which acts to derepress the gene responsible for enzyme synthesis.

capillaryaction.name: capillary action
capillaryaction.definition: Capillary action is a phenomenon in which the surface of a liquid where it contacts a solid is elevated or depressed, because of the relative attraction of the molecules of the liquid for each other and for those of the solid. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

foodservices.name: food services
foodservices.definition: Food services is functions, equipment, and facilities concerned with the preparation and distribution of ready-to-eat food.

animalcarecommittees.name: animal care committees
animalcarecommittees.definition: Animal care committees is institutional committees established to protect the welfare of animals used in research and education. The 1971 nih Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals introduced the policy that institutions using warm-blooded animals in projects supported by nih grants either be accredited by a recognized professional laboratory animal accrediting body or establish its own committee to evaluate animal care; the Public Health Service adopted a policy in 1979 requiring such committees; and the 1985 amendments to the Animal Welfare Act mandate review and approval of federally funded research with animals by a formally designated Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (iacuc).

immunoblotting.name: immunoblotting
immunoblotting.definition: Immunoblotting is immunologic method used for detecting or quantifying immunoreactive substances. The substance is identified by first immobilizing it by blotting onto a membrane and then tagging it with labeled antibodies.

generalization,psychological.name: generalization , psychological
generalization,psychological.definition: Psychological generalization is the phenomenon of an organism's responding to all situations similar to one in which it has been conditioned.

biliarytractdiseases.name: biliary tract diseases
biliarytractdiseases.definition: Biliary tract diseases is diseases in any part of the biliary tract including the [MASK] and the gallbladder.

nadphoxidase1.name: nadph oxidase 1
nadphoxidase1.definition: Nadph oxidase 1 is an nadph oxidase that functions as a voltage-gated proton channel expressed by phagocytes, especially in the colon. It regulates intracellular pH, generates superoxides upon activation by [MASK], and may play a role in innate immunity.

boneregeneration.name: bone regeneration
boneregeneration.definition: Bone regeneration is renewal or repair of lost bone tissue. It excludes bony callus formed after bone fractures but not yet replaced by hard bone.

coatedvesicles.name: coated vesicles
coatedvesicles.definition: Coated vesicles is vesicles formed when cell-membrane coated pits (coated pits, cell-membrane) invaginate and pinch off. The outer surface of these vesicles are covered with a lattice-like network of coat proteins, such as clathrin, coat protein complex proteins, or caveolins.

rna,messenger,stored.name: rna , messenger , stored
rna,messenger,stored.definition: Stored messenger rna is messenger rna that is stored in a masked state for translation at a later time. Distinguish from rna, untranslated which refers to non-messenger rna, i.e. rna that does not code for protein.

dnaviruses.name: dna viruses
dnaviruses.definition: Dna viruses is viruses whose nucleic acid is dna.

smokingreduction.name: smoking reduction
smokingreduction.definition: Smoking reduction is a decrease in the incidence and frequency of smoking. Smoking reduction differs from smoking cessation in that the smoker continues to smoke albeit at a lesser frequency without quitting.

musclestretchingexercises.name: muscle stretching exercises
musclestretchingexercises.definition: Muscle stretching exercises is exercises that stretch the muscle fibers with the aim to increase muscle-tendon flexibility, improve range of motion or musculoskeletal function, and prevent injuries. There are various types of stretching techniques including active, passive (relaxed), static, dynamic (gentle), ballistic (forced), isometric, and others.

weightloss.name: weight loss
weightloss.definition: Weight loss is decrease in existing body weight.

maxillarysinus.name: maxillary sinus
maxillarysinus.definition: Maxillary sinus is the air space located in the body of the maxillary bone near each cheek. Each maxillary sinus communicates with the middle passage (meatus) of the nasal cavity on the same side.

genome,bacterial.name: genome , bacterial
genome,bacterial.definition: Bacterial genome is the genetic complement of a bacteria as represented in its dna.

tissueandorganprocurement.name: tissue and organ procurement
tissueandorganprocurement.definition: Tissue and organ procurement is the administrative procedures involved with acquiring tissues or organs for transplantation through various programs, systems, or organizations. These procedures include obtaining consent from tissue donors and arranging for transportation of donated tissues and organs, after tissue harvesting, to hospitals for processing and transplantation.

molecularsequence.name: molecular sequence
molecularsequence.definition: Molecular sequence is descriptions of specific amino acid, carbohydrate, or nucleotide sequences which have appeared in the published literature and/or are deposited in and maintained by databanks such as GENBANK, European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), National Biomedical Research [MASK] (NBRF), or other sequence repositories.

pharmaceuticalpreparations.name: pharmaceutical preparations
pharmaceuticalpreparations.definition: Pharmaceutical preparations is drugs intended for human or veterinary use, presented in their finished dosage form. Included here are materials used in the preparation and/or formulation of the finished dosage form.

genes,tat.name: genes , tat
genes,tat.definition: Tat genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for the protein responsible for trans-activation of transcription (tat) in human immunodeficiency virus (hiv).

independentmedicalevaluation.name: independent medical evaluation
independentmedicalevaluation.definition: Independent medical evaluation is an assessment of health status requested by third parties (e.g. insurers, adjudicating bodies, law enforcement, attorneys, etc) on a subject’s functional ability. Such information may be used in optimizing treatment or making informed decisions on compensation.

ethicaltheory.name: ethical theory
ethicaltheory.definition: Ethical theory is a philosophically coherent [MASK] of propositions (for example, utilitarianism) which attempts to provide general norms for the guidance and evaluation of moral conduct. (from Beauchamp and Childress, Principles of Biomedical Ethics, 4th ed)

cardiaccomplexes,premature.name: cardiac complexes , premature
cardiaccomplexes,premature.definition: Premature cardiac complexes is a group of cardiac arrhythmias in which the cardiac contractions are not initiated at the sinoatrial node. They include both atrial and ventricular premature beats, and are also known as extra or ectopic heartbeats. Their frequency is increased in heart diseases.

panic.name: panic
panic.definition: Panic is a state of extreme acute, intense anxiety and unreasoning fear accompanied by disorganization of personality function.

professionalsociety.name: professional society
professionalsociety.definition: Professional society is organizations composed of members with common interests and whose professions may be similar.

microbiologicaltechniques.name: microbiological techniques
microbiologicaltechniques.definition: Microbiological techniques is techniques used in microbiology.

diagnosticerrors.name: diagnostic errors
diagnosticerrors.definition: Diagnostic errors is incorrect or incomplete diagnoses following clinical or technical diagnostic procedures.

diffusionofinnovation.name: diffusion of innovation
diffusionofinnovation.definition: Diffusion of innovation is the broad dissemination of new ideas, procedures, techniques, materials, and devices and the degree to which these are accepted and used.

legislationastopic.name: legislation as topic
legislationastopic.definition: Legislation as topic is works about the enactment of laws and ordinances and their regulation by official organs of a nation, state, or other legislative organization. It refers also to health-related laws and regulations in general or for which there is no specific descriptor.

auditorybrainstemimplants.name: auditory brain stem implants
auditorybrainstemimplants.definition: Auditory brain stem implants is multi-channel hearing devices typically used for patients who have tumors on the cochlear nerve and are unable to benefit from [MASK] after tumor surgery that severs the cochlear nerve. The device electrically stimulates the nerves of cochlea nucleus in the brain stem rather than the [MASK] as in [MASK].

hydroxylradical.name: hydroxyl radical
hydroxylradical.definition: Hydroxyl radical is the univalent radical oh. Hydroxyl radical is a potent oxidizing agent.

comorbidity.name: comorbidity
comorbidity.definition: Comorbidity is the presence of co-existing or additional diseases with reference to an initial diagnosis or with reference to the index condition that is the subject of study. Comorbidity may affect the ability of affected individuals to function and also their survival; it may be used as a prognostic indicator for length of hospital stay, cost factors, and outcome or survival.

ecologicalsystems,closed.name: ecological systems , closed
ecologicalsystems,closed.definition: Closed ecological systems is systems that provide for the maintenance of life in an isolated living chamber through reutilization of the material available, in particular, by means of a cycle wherein exhaled carbon dioxide, urine, and other waste matter are converted chemically or by [MASK] into oxygen, water, and food. (nasa Thesaurus, 1988)

cranialnervediseases.name: cranial nerve diseases
cranialnervediseases.definition: Cranial nerve diseases is disorders of one or more of the twelve cranial nerves. With the exception of the optic and olfactory nerves, this includes disorders of the brain stem nuclei from which the cranial nerves originate or terminate.

esophagealfistula.name: esophageal fistula
esophagealfistula.definition: Esophageal fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the esophagus. The most common type is tracheoesophageal fistula between the esophagus and the [MASK].

jointprosthesis.name: joint prosthesis
jointprosthesis.definition: Joint prosthesis is prostheses used to partially or totally replace a human or animal joint. (from umdns, 1999)

peptidebiosynthesis.name: peptide biosynthesis
peptidebiosynthesis.definition: Peptide biosynthesis is the production of peptides or proteins by the constituents of a living organism. The biosynthesis of proteins on ribosomes following an rna template is termed translation (translation, genetic). There are other, non-ribosomal peptide biosynthesis (peptide biosynthesis, nucleic acid-independent) mechanisms carried out by peptide synthases and peptidyltransferases. Further modifications of peptide chains yield functional peptide and protein molecules.

ethics,research.name: ethics , research
ethics,research.definition: Research ethics is the moral obligations governing the conduct of research. Used for discussions of research ethics as a general topic.

intercellularsignalingpeptidesandprotein.name: intercellular signaling peptides and proteins
intercellularsignalingpeptidesandprotein.definition: Intercellular signaling peptides and proteins is regulatory proteins and peptides that are signaling molecules involved in the process of paracrine communication. They are generally considered factors that are expressed by one cell and are responded to by receptors on another nearby cell. They are distinguished from hormones in that their actions are local rather than distal.

organortissuefunction.name: organ or tissue function
organortissuefunction.definition: Organ or tissue function is the function of organs or tissues.

infant,extremelypremature.name: infant , extremely premature
infant,extremelypremature.definition: Extremely premature infant is a human infant born before 28 weeks of gestation.

tachycardia,ectopicatrial.name: tachycardia , ectopic atrial
tachycardia,ectopicatrial.definition: Ectopic atrial tachycardia is abnormally rapid heartbeats originating from one or more automatic foci (nonsinus pacemakers) in the heart atrium but away from the sinoatrial node. Unlike the reentry mechanism, automatic tachycardia speeds up and slows down gradually. The episode is characterized by a heart rate between 135 to less than 200 beats per minute and lasting 30 seconds or longer.

headmovements.name: head movements
headmovements.definition: Head movements is voluntary or involuntary motion of head that may be relative to or independent of body; includes animals and humans.

conductdisorder.name: conduct disorder
conductdisorder.definition: Conduct disorder is a repetitive and persistent pattern of behavior in which the basic rights of others or major age-appropriate societal norms or rules are violated. These behaviors include aggressive conduct that causes or threatens physical harm to other people or animals, nonaggressive conduct that causes property loss or damage, deceitfulness or theft, and serious violations of rules. The onset is before age 18. (From [MASK], 1994)

aminosugars.name: amino sugars
aminosugars.definition: Amino sugars is sugars containing an amino group. [MASK] of other compounds with these amino sugars results in aminoglycosides.

heparin.name: heparin
heparin.definition: Heparin is a highly acidic mucopolysaccharide formed of equal parts of sulfated D-glucosamine and D-glucuronic acid with sulfaminic bridges. The molecular weight ranges from six to twenty thousand. Heparin occurs in and is obtained from liver, lung, [MASK], etc., of vertebrates. Its function is unknown, but it is used to prevent blood clotting in vivo and vitro, in the form of many different [MASK].

arthritis,infectious.name: arthritis , infectious
arthritis,infectious.definition: Infectious arthritis is arthritis caused by bacteria; rickettsia; mycoplasma; viruses; fungi; or parasites.

hospitals,urban.name: hospitals , urban
hospitals,urban.definition: Urban hospitals is hospitals located in metropolitan areas.

thymusplant.name: thymus plant
thymusplant.definition: Thymus plant is a plant genus of the family lamiaceae best known for the thyme spice added to foods.

trypanblue.name: trypan blue
trypanblue.definition: Trypan blue is a diazo-naphthalene sulfonate that is widely used as a stain.

gastricdilatation.name: gastric dilatation
gastricdilatation.definition: Gastric dilatation is abnormal distention of the stomach due to accumulation of gastric contents that may reach 10 to 15 liters. Gastric dilatation may be the result of [MASK]; ileus; gastroparesis; or denervation.

bleedingtime.name: bleeding time
bleedingtime.definition: Bleeding time is duration of blood flow after skin puncture. This test is used as a measure of capillary and platelet function.

hyperglycemia.name: hyperglycemia
hyperglycemia.definition: Hyperglycemia is abnormally high blood glucose level.

hardnesstests.name: hardness tests
hardnesstests.definition: Hardness tests is a test to determine the relative hardness of a metal, mineral, or other material according to one of several scales, such as Brinell, Mohs, Rockwell, Vickers, or Shore. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

education,pharmacy,graduate.name: education , pharmacy , graduate
education,pharmacy,graduate.definition: Graduate pharmacy education is educational programs for pharmacists who have a bachelor's degree or a Doctor of Pharmacy degree entering a specific field of pharmacy. They may lead to an advanced degree.

cyclicampresponseelementmodulator.name: cyclic amp response element modulator
cyclicampresponseelementmodulator.definition: Cyclic amp response element modulator is cyclic amp response element modulator is a basic [MASK] zipper transcription factor that is regulated by cyclic amp. It plays an important role in spermatid development in the mammalian testis.

dynamiclightscattering.name: dynamic light scattering
dynamiclightscattering.definition: Dynamic light scattering is an analytical technique for measuring particle size of molecules that are less than a micron in diameter dispersed or dissolved in a liquid.

physiology.name: physiology
physiology.definition: Physiology is the biological science concerned with the life-supporting properties, functions, and processes of living organisms or their parts.

sexdistribution.name: sex distribution
sexdistribution.definition: [MASK] distribution is the number of males and females in a given population. The distribution may refer to how many men or women or what proportion of either in the group. The population is usually patients with a specific disease but the concept is not restricted to humans and is not restricted to medicine.

sleephygiene.name: sleep hygiene
sleephygiene.definition: Sleep hygiene is habits and practices conducive to getting the right amount and quality of sleep, and include  responding to environmental factors that may influence one's sleep.

milkproteins.name: milk proteins
milkproteins.definition: Milk proteins is the major protein constituents of milk are caseins and whey proteins such as lactalbumin and lactoglobulins. immunoglobulins occur in high concentrations in colostrum and in relatively lower concentrations in milk. (Singleton and Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed, p554)

virtualrealityexposuretherapy.name: virtual reality exposure therapy
virtualrealityexposuretherapy.definition: Virtual reality exposure therapy is treatment technique in a virtual environment which allows the participant to experience a sense of presence in an immersive, computer-generated, three-dimensional, interactive environment that minimizes avoidance behavior and facilitates emotional involvement. (from Curr Psychiatry Rep (2010) 12:298)

cyclinh.name: cyclin h
cyclinh.definition: Cyclin h is a cyclin subtype that is found as a component of a heterotrimeric complex containing cyclin-dependent kinase 7 and CDK-activating kinase assembly factor. The complex plays a role in cellular proliferation by phosphorylating several cyclin dependent kinases at specific regulatory threonine sites.

hairdyes.name: hair dyes
hairdyes.definition: Hair dyes is dyes used as cosmetics to change hair [MASK] either permanently or temporarily.

immunity,innate.name: immunity , innate
immunity,innate.definition: Innate immunity is the capacity of a normal organism to remain unaffected by microorganisms and their toxins. It results from the presence of naturally occurring anti-infective agents, constitutional factors such as body temperature and immediate acting immune cells such as natural killer cells.

indiana.name: indiana
indiana.definition: Indiana is state bounded on the north by [MASK] Michigan and Michigan, on the east by Ohio, on the south by Kentucky, and on the west by Illinois.

nanostructures.name: nanostructures
nanostructures.definition: Nanostructures is materials which have structured components with at least one dimension in the range of 1 to 100 nanometers. These include nanocomposites; nanoparticles; nanotubes; and nanowires.

dnacontamination.name: dna contamination
dnacontamination.definition: Dna contamination is the presence of dna from a source foreign to the sample being analysed.

geneexpressionprofiling.name: gene expression profiling
geneexpressionprofiling.definition: Gene expression profiling is the determination of the pattern of genes expressed at the level of genetic transcription, under specific circumstances or in a specific cell.

hysterectomy.name: hysterectomy
hysterectomy.definition: Hysterectomy is excision of the uterus.

repetitivesequences,nucleicacid.name: repetitive sequences , nucleic acid
repetitivesequences,nucleicacid.definition: Nucleic acid repetitive sequences is sequences of dna or rna that occur in multiple copies. There are several types: interspersed repetitive sequences are copies of transposable elements (dna transposable elements or retroelements) dispersed throughout the genome. terminal repeat sequences flank both ends of another sequence, for example, the long terminal repeats (LTRs) on retroviruses. Variations may be direct repeats, those occurring in the same direction, or inverted repeats, those opposite to each other in direction. tandem repeat sequences are copies which lie adjacent to each other, direct or inverted (inverted repeat sequences).

child,foster.name: child , foster
child,foster.definition: Foster child is individual who is unable to live safely with his or her family, usually due to abuse or neglect in the family home.

braininfarction.name: brain infarction
braininfarction.definition: Brain infarction is tissue necrosis in any area of the brain, including the cerebral hemispheres, the cerebellum, and the brain stem. Brain infarction is the result of a cascade of events initiated by inadequate blood flow through the brain that is followed by hypoxia and hypoglycemia in brain tissue. Damage may be temporary, permanent, selective or pan-necrosis.

lipase.name: lipase
lipase.definition: Lipase is an enzyme of the hydrolase class that catalyzes the reaction of triacylglycerol and water to yield diacylglycerol and a fatty acid anion. It is produced by glands on the tongue and by the pancreas and initiates the [MASK] of dietary fats. (From Dorland, 27th ed) ec 3.1.1.3.

olfactorymucosa.name: olfactory mucosa
olfactorymucosa.definition: Olfactory mucosa is that portion of the nasal mucosa containing the sensory nerve endings for smell, located at the dome of each nasal cavity. The yellow-brownish olfactory epithelium consists of [MASK]; brush cells; stem cells; and the associated olfactory glands.

tissueembedding.name: tissue embedding
tissueembedding.definition: Tissue embedding is the technique of placing cells or tissue in a supporting medium so that thin sections can be cut using a microtome. The medium can be [MASK] wax ([MASK] embedding) or plastics ([MASK]) such as epoxy resins.

encephalitisviruses.name: encephalitis viruses
encephalitisviruses.definition: Encephalitis viruses is a collection of single-stranded rna viruses scattered across the Bunyaviridae, Flaviviridae, and Togaviridae families whose common property is the ability to induce encephalitic conditions in infected hosts.

receptors,cyclicamp.name: receptors , cyclic amp
receptors,cyclicamp.definition: Cyclic amp receptors is cell surface proteins that bind cyclic amp with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. The best characterized cyclic amp receptors are those of the slime mold Dictyostelium discoideum. The transcription regulator cyclic amp receptor protein of prokaryotes is not included nor are the eukaryotic cytoplasmic cyclic amp receptor proteins which are the regulatory subunits of cyclic amp-dependent protein kinases.

endothelialcells.name: endothelial cells
endothelialcells.definition: Endothelial cells is highly specialized epithelial cells that line the heart; blood vessels; and [MASK] vessels, forming the endothelium. They are polygonal in shape and joined together by tight junctions. The tight junctions allow for variable permeability to specific macromolecules that are transported across the endothelial layer.

cellfunction.name: cell function
cellfunction.definition: Cell function is the function of cell.

mammaryglands,human.name: mammary glands , human
mammaryglands,human.definition: Human mammary glands is glandular tissue in the breast of human that is under the influence of hormones such as estrogens; progestins; and prolactin. In women, after parturition, the mammary glands secrete milk ([MASK]) for the nourishment of the young.

sunprotectionfactor.name: sun protection factor
sunprotectionfactor.definition: Sun protection factor is a measure of relative protection provided by sunscreening agents against burns due to ultraviolet (uv) radiation from a light source.

chitin.name: chitin
chitin.definition: Chitin is a linear polysaccharide of beta-1->4 linked units of acetylglucosamine. It is the second most abundant biopolymer on earth, found especially in insects and fungi. When deacetylated it is called chitosan.

receptors,progesterone.name: receptors , progesterone
receptors,progesterone.definition: Progesterone receptors is specific proteins found in or on cells of progesterone target tissues that specifically combine with progesterone. The [MASK] progesterone-receptor complex then associates with the nucleic acids to initiate protein synthesis. There are two kinds of progesterone receptors, a and b. Both are induced by estrogen and have short half-lives.

aorticaneurysm,thoracic.name: aortic aneurysm , thoracic
aorticaneurysm,thoracic.definition: Thoracic aortic aneurysm is an abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the thoracic aorta. This proximal descending portion of aorta gives rise to the visceral and the parietal branches above the aortic hiatus at the diaphragm.

spinalstenosis.name: spinal stenosis
spinalstenosis.definition: Spinal stenosis is narrowing of the spinal canal.

chromosomefragilesites.name: chromosome fragile sites
chromosomefragilesites.definition: Chromosome fragile sites is specific loci that show up during karyotyping as a gap (an uncondensed stretch in closer views) on a chromatid [MASK] after culturing cells under specific conditions. These sites are associated with an increase in chromosome fragility. They are classified as common or rare, and by the specific culture conditions under which they develop. Fragile site loci are named by the letters "fra" followed by a designation for the specific chromosome, and a letter which refers to which fragile site of that chromosome (e.g. fraxa refers to fragile site a on the x chromosome. It is a rare, folic acid-sensitive fragile site associated with fragile x syndrome.)

hydrogenperoxide.name: hydrogen peroxide
hydrogenperoxide.definition: Hydrogen peroxide is a strong oxidizing agent used in aqueous solution as a ripening agent, bleach, and topical anti-infective. It is relatively unstable and solutions deteriorate over time unless stabilized by the addition of acetanilide or similar organic materials.

gabamodulators.name: gaba modulators
gabamodulators.definition: Gaba modulators is substances that do not act as agonists or antagonists but do affect the gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor-ionophore complex. gaba-a receptors (receptors, gaba-a) appear to have at least three allosteric sites at which modulators act: a site at which benzodiazepines act by increasing the opening frequency of gamma-aminobutyric ACID-activated chloride channels; a site at which barbiturates act to prolong the duration of channel opening; and a site at which some steroids may act. general anesthetics probably act at least partly by potentiating GABAergic responses, but they are not included here.

hospitalization.name: hospitalization
hospitalization.definition: Hospitalization is the confinement of a patient in a hospital.

sarcoma,synovial.name: sarcoma , synovial
sarcoma,synovial.definition: Synovial sarcoma is a malignant neoplasm arising from tenosynovial tissue of the joints and in synovial cells of tendons and bursae. The legs are the most common site, but the tumor can occur in the [MASK] and other trunk muscles. There are two recognized types: the monophasic (characterized by sheaths of monotonous spindle cells) and the biphasic (characterized by slit-like spaces or clefts within the tumor, lined by cuboidal or tall columnar epithelial cells). These sarcomas occur most commonly in the second and fourth decades of life. (From Dorland, 27th ed; DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1363)

learninghealthsystem.name: learning health system
learninghealthsystem.definition: Learning health system is a system in which internal data and experience are systematically integrated with external evidence and that knowledge is put into practice. As a result, patients get higher quality, safer, more efficient care, and health care delivery organizations become better places to work. (https://healthit.ahrq.gov/health-care-theme/learning-health-system)

adamproteins.name: adam proteins
adamproteins.definition: Adam proteins is a family of membrane-anchored glycoproteins that contain a disintegrin and metalloprotease domain. They are responsible for the proteolytic cleavage of many transmembrane proteins and the release of their extracellular domain.

gastricballoon.name: gastric balloon
gastricballoon.definition: Gastric balloon is an inflatable device implanted in the stomach as an adjunct to therapy of morbid obesity. Specific types include the silicone Garren-Edwards Gastric Bubble (gegb), approved by the fda in 1985, and the Ballobes Balloon.

models,animal.name: models , animal
models,animal.definition: Animal models is non-human animals, selected because of specific characteristics, for use in experimental research, teaching, or testing.

ambulatorycare.name: ambulatory care
ambulatorycare.definition: Ambulatory care is health care services provided to patients on an ambulatory basis, rather than by admission to a hospital or other health care facility. The services may be a part of a hospital, augmenting its inpatient services, or may be provided at a free-standing facility.

nitratereductase(nadph).name: nitrate reductase ( nadph )
nitratereductase(nadph).definition: Nitrate reductase (nadph) is an enzyme that catalyzes the oxidation of nitrite to nitrate in the presence of NADP+. It is a flavoprotein that contains iron and molybdenum. This enzyme was formerly classified as EC 1.6.6.3 and should not be confused with the enzyme nitrate reductase (NAD(P)H).

lipoproteins,hdl.name: lipoproteins , hdl
lipoproteins,hdl.definition: Hdl lipoproteins is a class of lipoproteins of small size (4-13 nm) and dense (greater than 1.063 g/ml) particles. hdl lipoproteins, synthesized in the liver without a lipid core, accumulate cholesterol esters from peripheral tissues and transport them to the liver for re-utilization or elimination from the body (the reverse cholesterol transport). Their major protein component is apolipoprotein a-i. hdl also shuttle apolipoproteins c and apolipoproteins e to and from triglyceride-rich lipoproteins during their catabolism. hdl plasma level has been inversely correlated with the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

occupationalhealthphysicians.name: occupational health physicians
occupationalhealthphysicians.definition: [MASK] physicians is physicians employed in a company or corporate setting that is generally not in the health care industry.

faculty.name: faculty
faculty.definition: Faculty is teaching and administrative staff having academic rank in a post-secondary educational institution.

vascularmalformations.name: vascular malformations
vascularmalformations.definition: Vascular malformations is a spectrum of congenital, inherited, or acquired abnormalities in blood vessels that can adversely affect the normal blood flow in arteries or veins. Most are congenital defects such as abnormal communications between blood vessels (fistula), shunting of arterial blood directly into veins bypassing the capillaries (arteriovenous malformations), formation of large dilated blood blood-filled vessels (cavernous angioma), and swollen capillaries (capillary telangiectases). In rare cases, vascular malformations can result from trauma or diseases.

employment.name: employment
employment.definition: Employment is the state of being engaged in an activity or service for wages or salary.

metalceramicalloys.name: metal ceramic alloys
metalceramicalloys.definition: Metal ceramic alloys is the fusion of ceramics (porcelain) to an alloy of two or more metals for use in restorative and prosthodontic dentistry. Examples of metal alloys employed include cobalt-chromium, gold-palladium, gold-[MASK]-palladium, and nickel-based alloys.

steambath.name: steam bath
steambath.definition: Steam bath is therapy of sitting in a hot steamy room followed by a cool bath or shower.

signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculefa.name: signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family
signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculefa.definition: Signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family is type-I membrane glycoproteins that are expressed primarily on the surface of cd4 or CD8-positive t-cells; natural killer cells; and some populations of b cells. They are characterized by an N-terminal, extracellular immunoglobulin-like domain and a membrane-proximal immunoglobulin c2-[MASK] domain. slamf receptors typically signal through homophilic interactions and are important for mediating the immune response and immune cell differentiation.

centralizedhospitalservices.name: centralized hospital services
centralizedhospitalservices.definition: Centralized hospital services is the coordination of services in one area of a facility to improve efficiency.

leukemicinfiltration.name: leukemic infiltration
leukemicinfiltration.definition: Leukemic infiltration is a pathologic change in leukemia in which leukemic cells permeate various organs at any stage of the disease. All types of leukemia show various degrees of infiltration, depending upon the type of leukemia. The degree of infiltration may vary from site to site. The liver and spleen are common sites of infiltration, the greatest appearing in myelocytic leukemia, but infiltration is seen also in the granulocytic and lymphocytic types. The kidney is also a common site and of the gastrointestinal system, the stomach and ileum are commonly involved. In lymphocytic leukemia the skin is often infiltrated. The central nervous system too is a common site.

foamcells.name: foam cells
foamcells.definition: Foam cells is lipid-laden macrophages originating from monocytes or from smooth muscle cells.

ammoniumsulfate.name: ammonium sulfate
ammoniumsulfate.definition: Ammonium sulfate is sulfuric acid diammonium [MASK]. It is used in chemical fractionation of proteins.

solubility.name: solubility
solubility.definition: Solubility is the ability of a substance to be dissolved, i.e. to form a solution with another substance. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

factorvdeficiency.name: factor v deficiency
factorvdeficiency.definition: Factor v deficiency is a deficiency of blood coagulation factor v (known as proaccelerin or accelerator globulin or labile factor) leading to a rare hemorrhagic tendency known as Owren's disease or parahemophilia. It varies greatly in severity. Factor v deficiency is an autosomal recessive trait. (Dorland, 27th ed)

ventricularprematurecomplexes.name: ventricular premature complexes
ventricularprematurecomplexes.definition: Ventricular premature complexes is a type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature contractions of the heart ventricles. It is characterized by the premature qrs complex on ecg that is of abnormal shape and great duration (generally >129 msec). It is the most common form of all cardiac arrhythmias. Premature ventricular complexes have no clinical significance except in concurrence with heart diseases.

aminoalcohols.name: amino alcohols
aminoalcohols.definition: Amino alcohols is compounds possessing both a hydroxyl (-oh) and an amino group (-nh2).

ureter.name: ureter
ureter.definition: Ureter is one of a pair of thick-walled tubes that transports urine from the [MASK] to the [MASK].

deviceremoval.name: device removal
deviceremoval.definition: Device removal is removal of an implanted therapeutic or prosthetic device.

cerebrospinalfluid.name: cerebrospinal fluid
cerebrospinalfluid.definition: Cerebrospinal fluid is a watery fluid that is continuously produced in the choroid plexus and circulates around the surface of the brain; spinal cord; and in the cerebral ventricles.

eyeinfections,bacterial.name: eye infections , bacterial
eyeinfections,bacterial.definition: Bacterial eye infections is infections in the inner or external eye caused by microorganisms belonging to several families of bacteria. Some of the more common genera found are Haemophilus, Neisseria, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, and Chlamydia.

vitaminb12deficiency.name: vitamin b 12 deficiency
vitaminb12deficiency.definition: Vitamin b 12 deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin b 12 in the diet, characterized by megaloblastic anemia. Since vitamin b 12 is not present in plants, humans have obtained their supply from animal products, from multivitamin supplements in the form of pills, and as additives to food preparations. a wide variety of neuropsychiatric abnormalities is also seen in vitamin b 12 deficiency and appears to be due to an undefined defect involving myelin synthesis. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p848)

stemcelltransplantation.name: stem cell transplantation
stemcelltransplantation.definition: Stem cell transplantation is the transfer of stem cells from one individual to another within the same species (transplantation, homologous) or between species (xenotransplantation), or transfer within the same individual (transplantation, autologous). The source and location of the stem cells determines their potency or pluripotency to differentiate into various cell types.

asia.name: asia
asia.definition: Asia is the largest of the continents. It was known to the Romans more specifically as what we know today as Asia Minor. The name comes from at least two possible sources: from the Assyrian asu (to rise) or from the Sanskrit usa (dawn), both with reference to its being the land of the rising sun, i.e., eastern as opposed to Europe, to the west. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p82 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p34)

collectedcorrespondence.name: collected correspondence
collectedcorrespondence.definition: Collected correspondence is written communication between persons or between institutions or organizations.

nursingrecords.name: nursing records
nursingrecords.definition: Nursing records is data recorded by nurses concerning the nursing care given to the patient, including judgment of the patient's progress.

africa,southern.name: africa , southern
africa,southern.definition: Southern africa is the geographical area of Africa comprising angola; botswana; lesotho; malawi; mozambique; namibia; south africa; swaziland; zambia; and zimbabwe.

memoryandlearningtests.name: memory and learning tests
memoryandlearningtests.definition: Memory and learning tests is tests designed to evaluate general and specific areas of behaviors and abilities associated with memory and/or learning.

auditoryperception.name: auditory perception
auditoryperception.definition: Auditory perception is the process whereby auditory stimuli are selected, organized, and interpreted by the organism.

analysisofvariance.name: analysis of variance
analysisofvariance.definition: Analysis of variance is a statistical technique that isolates and assesses the contributions of categorical independent variables to variation in the mean of a continuous dependent variable.

tumorburden.name: tumor burden
tumorburden.definition: Tumor burden is the total amount (cell number, weight, size or volume) of tumor cells or tissue in the body.

nasalmucosa.name: nasal mucosa
nasalmucosa.definition: Nasal mucosa is the mucous lining of the nasal cavity, including lining of the nostril (vestibule) and the olfactory mucosa. Nasal mucosa consists of ciliated cells, goblet cells, brush cells, small granule cells, basal cells (stem cells) and glands containing both mucous and serous cells.

penicilling.name: penicillin g
penicilling.definition: Penicillin g is a penicillin derivative commonly used in the form of its sodium or potassium [MASK] in the treatment of a variety of infections. It is effective against most gram-positive bacteria and against gram-negative cocci. It has also been used as an experimental convulsant because of its actions on gamma-aminobutyric acid mediated synaptic transmission.

bacterium.name: bacterium
bacterium.definition: Bacterium is single-celled microorganisms that can exist either as independent (free-living) organisms or as parasites (dependent on another organism for life)

criminalpsychology.name: criminal psychology
criminalpsychology.definition: Criminal psychology is the branch of psychology which investigates the psychology of crime with particular reference to the personality factors of the criminal.

fees,dental.name: fees , dental
fees,dental.definition: Dental fees is amounts charged to the patient as payer for dental services.

administration,rectal.name: administration , rectal
administration,rectal.definition: Rectal administration is the insertion of drugs into the rectum, usually for confused or incompetent patients, like children, infants, and the very old or comatose.

transcriptionfactors.name: transcription factors
transcriptionfactors.definition: Transcription factors is endogenous substances, usually proteins, which are effective in the initiation, stimulation, or termination of the genetic transcription process.

bileductneoplasms.name: bile duct neoplasms
bileductneoplasms.definition: [MASK] neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the [MASK].

plantdiseases.name: plant diseases
plantdiseases.definition: Plant diseases is diseases of plants.

hypertension,portal.name: hypertension , portal
hypertension,portal.definition: Portal hypertension is abnormal increase of resistance to blood flow within the hepatic portal system, frequently seen in liver cirrhosis and conditions with obstruction of the portal vein.

thyroidepithelialcells.name: thyroid epithelial cells
thyroidepithelialcells.definition: Thyroid epithelial cells is epithelial cells of the thyroid gland that produce and secrete thyroxine and triiodothyronine.

speechdisorders.name: speech disorders
speechdisorders.definition: [MASK] disorders is acquired or developmental conditions marked by an impaired ability to comprehend or generate spoken forms of language.

parenteralnutrition,total.name: parenteral nutrition , total
parenteralnutrition,total.definition: Total parenteral nutrition is the delivery of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient whose sole source of nutrients is via solutions administered intravenously, subcutaneously, or by some other non-alimentary route. The basic components of tpn solutions are protein hydrolysates or free amino acid mixtures, monosaccharides, and electrolytes. Components are selected for their ability to reverse catabolism, promote anabolism, and build structural proteins.

actionpotentials.name: action potentials
actionpotentials.definition: Action potentials is abrupt changes in the membrane potential that sweep along the cell membrane of excitable cells in response to excitation stimuli.

lateonsetdisorders.name: late onset disorders
lateonsetdisorders.definition: Late onset disorders is pathological conditions (Disorder, syndrome, or disease) whose signs and symptoms manifest late in the life of an individual.

biomedicalordentalmaterial.name: biomedical or dental material
biomedicalordentalmaterial.definition: Biomedical or dental material is biomedical or dental material

virusreplication.name: virus replication
virusreplication.definition: Virus replication is the process of intracellular viral multiplication, consisting of the synthesis of proteins; nucleic acids; and sometimes lipids, and their assembly into a new infectious particle.

chromatography.name: chromatography
chromatography.definition: Chromatography is techniques used to separate mixtures of substances based on differences in the relative affinities of the substances for mobile and stationary phases. a mobile phase (fluid or gas) passes through a column containing a stationary phase of porous solid or liquid coated on a solid support. Usage is both analytical for small amounts and preparative for bulk amounts.

factorx.name: factor x
factorx.definition: Factor x is storage-stable glycoprotein blood coagulation factor that can be activated to factor Xa by both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways. a deficiency of factor x, sometimes called Stuart-Prower factor deficiency, may lead to a systemic coagulation disorder.

cholesterol.name: cholesterol
cholesterol.definition: Cholesterol is the principal sterol of all higher animals, distributed in body tissues, especially the brain and spinal cord, and in animal fats and oils.

ethicscommittees.name: ethics committees
ethicscommittees.definition: Ethics committees is committees established by professional societies, health facilities, or other institutions to consider decisions that have bioethical implications. The role of these committees may include consultation, education, mediation, and/or review of policies and practices. Committees that consider the ethical dimensions of patient care are ethics committees, clinical; committees established to protect the welfare of research subjects are ethics committees, research.

progesterone.name: progesterone
progesterone.definition: Progesterone is the major progestational steroid that is secreted primarily by the corpus luteum and the placenta. Progesterone acts on the uterus, the mammary glands and the brain. It is required in embryo implantation; [MASK], and the development of mammary tissue for milk production. Progesterone, converted from pregnenolone, also serves as an intermediate in the biosynthesis of gonadal steroid hormones and adrenal corticosteroids.

queensland.name: queensland
queensland.definition: Queensland is a state in northeastern Australia. Its capital is Brisbane. Its coast was first visited by Captain Cook in 1770 and its first settlement (penal) was located on Moreton Bay in 1824. The name Cooksland was first proposed but honor to Queen Victoria prevailed. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p996 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p441)

dentalpulpcalcification.name: dental pulp calcification
dentalpulpcalcification.definition: [MASK] calcification is calcinosis of the [MASK] or root canal.

chitinsynthase.name: chitin synthase
chitinsynthase.definition: Chitin synthase is an enzyme that converts udp glucosamine into chitin and udp. ec 2.4.1.16.

motoractivity.name: motor activity
motoractivity.definition: Motor activity is body movements of a human or an animal as a behavioral phenomenon.

geneediting.name: gene editing
geneediting.definition: Gene editing is genetic engineering or molecular biology techniques that involve dna repair mechanisms for incorporating site-specific modifications into a cell's genome.

respiration,artificial.name: respiration , artificial
respiration,artificial.definition: Artificial respiration is any method of artificial breathing that employs mechanical or non-mechanical means to force the air into and out of the lungs. Artificial respiration or ventilation is used in individuals who have stopped breathing or have respiratory insufficiency to increase their intake of oxygen (o2) and excretion of carbon dioxide (co2).

nurses,neonatal.name: nurses , neonatal
nurses,neonatal.definition: Neonatal nurses is qualified nursing professionals specializing in care of newborn infants.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 2
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.definition: Member 2 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter, sub-family g protein that functions as a high capacity urea exporter, transporter of sterols, and in the absorption and efflux of many drugs. Its efflux activity for antineoplastic agents contributes to drug resistance. It functions as a homodimer and is expressed by cells in a variety of organs, as well as by neoplastic stem cells.

mentalnavigationtests.name: mental navigation tests
mentalnavigationtests.definition: Mental navigation tests is measures of spatial cognition and memory.

prospectivepaymentsystem.name: prospective payment system
prospectivepaymentsystem.definition: Prospective payment system is a system wherein reimbursement rates are [MASK], for a given period of time, prior to the circumstances giving rise to actual reimbursement claims.

infectioushematopoieticnecrosisvirus.name: infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus
infectioushematopoieticnecrosisvirus.definition: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus is the type species of novirhabdovirus, in the family rhabdoviridae. It is a major pathogen of trout and salmon.

musculoskeletalandneuralphysiologicalphe.name: musculoskeletal and neural physiological phenomena
musculoskeletalandneuralphysiologicalphe.definition: Musculoskeletal and neural physiological phenomena is properties, and processes of the musculoskeletal system and the nervous system or their parts.

periodontalprosthesis.name: periodontal prosthesis
periodontalprosthesis.definition: Periodontal prosthesis is any restorative and replacement device that is used as a therapeutic aid in the treatment of periodontal disease. It is an adjunct to other forms of periodontal therapy and does not cure periodontal disease by itself. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 3d ed)

dietrecords.name: diet records
dietrecords.definition: Diet records is records of nutrient intake over a specific period of time, usually kept by the patient.

placentalinsufficiency.name: placental insufficiency
placentalinsufficiency.definition: Placental insufficiency is failure of the placenta to deliver an adequate supply of nutrients and oxygen to the fetus.

limdomainproteins.name: lim domain proteins
limdomainproteins.definition: Lim domain proteins is a large class of structurally-related proteins that contain one or more lim zinc finger domains. Many of the proteins in this class are involved in intracellular signaling processes and mediate their effects via lim domain protein-protein interactions. The name lim is derived from the first three proteins in which the motif was found: lin-11, Isl1 and Mec-3.

cathepsine.name: cathepsin e
cathepsine.definition: Cathepsin e is an aspartic endopeptidase that is similar in structure to cathepsin d. It is found primarily in the cells of the immune system where it may play a role in processing of cell surface antigens.

diseaseresistance.name: disease resistance
diseaseresistance.definition: Disease resistance is the capacity of an organism to defend itself against pathological processes or the agents of those processes. This most often involves innate immunity whereby the organism responds to pathogens in a generic way. The term disease resistance is used most frequently when referring to plants.

cell.name: cell
cell.definition: Cell is the fundamental, structural, and functional units or subunits of living organisms. They are composed of cytoplasm containing various organelles and a cell membrane boundary.

back.name: back
back.definition: Back is the rear surface of an upright primate from the [MASK] to the hip, or the dorsal surface of tetrapods.

trailmakingtest.name: trail making test
trailmakingtest.definition: Trail making test is the subject's ability to connect 25 numbered and lettered circles in sequence in a specific length of time. a score of 12 or below is suggestive of organic brain damage.

hypertrophy,rightventricular.name: hypertrophy , right ventricular
hypertrophy,rightventricular.definition: Right ventricular hypertrophy is enlargement of the right ventricle of the heart. This increase in ventricular mass is often attributed to pulmonary hypertension and is a contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

kidneytubules,distal.name: kidney tubules , distal
kidneytubules,distal.definition: Distal kidney tubules is the portion of renal tubule that begins from the enlarged segment of the ascending limb of the loop of henle. It reenters the kidney cortex and forms the convoluted segments of the distal tubule.

paralysis,obstetric.name: paralysis , obstetric
paralysis,obstetric.definition: Obstetric paralysis is paralysis of an infant resulting from injury received at birth. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

upperextremity.name: upper extremity
upperextremity.definition: Upper extremity is the region of the upper limb in animals, extending from the deltoid region to the hand, and including the [MASK]; axilla; and [MASK].

geneknockdowntechniques.name: gene knockdown techniques
geneknockdowntechniques.definition: Gene knockdown techniques is the artificial induction of gene silencing by the use of rna interference to reduce the expression of a specific gene. It includes the use of double-stranded rna, such as small interfering rna and rna containing hairpin loop sequence, and anti-sense oligonucleotides.

atomicbombsurvivors.name: atomic bomb survivors
atomicbombsurvivors.definition: Atomic bomb survivors is persons who survived exposure to radiation due to atomic bombs.

minorlymphocytestimulatoryloci.name: minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci
minorlymphocytestimulatoryloci.definition: Minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci is genetic loci responsible for the encoding of minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens. There are at least two unlinked loci (in the mouse) and they appear to be separate from the major histocompatibility complex and minor histocompatibility loci. The mouse mammary tumor virus (see mammary tumor virus, mouse) has the ability to integrate into these loci. The antigens induce strong T-cell proliferative responses in mixed lymphocyte reactions.

immunetolerance.name: immune tolerance
immunetolerance.definition: Immune tolerance is the specific failure of a normally responsive individual to make an immune response to a known antigen. It results from previous contact with the antigen by an immunologically immature individual (fetus or neonate) or by an adult exposed to extreme high-dose or low-dose antigen, or by exposure to radiation, antimetabolites, antilymphocytic serum, etc.

gestationalage.name: gestational age
gestationalage.definition: Gestational age is the age of the conceptus, beginning from the time of fertilization. In clinical obstetrics, the gestational age is often estimated as the time from the last day of the last menstruation which is about 2 weeks before ovulation and fertilization.

intraocularpressure.name: intraocular pressure
intraocularpressure.definition: Intraocular pressure is the pressure of the fluids in the eye.

neonatalbrachialplexuspalsy.name: neonatal brachial plexus palsy
neonatalbrachialplexuspalsy.definition: Neonatal brachial plexus palsy is perinatal nerve injury involving the brachial plexus involving a weak or paralyzed upper extremity.

activatingtranscriptionfactor2.name: activating transcription factor 2
activatingtranscriptionfactor2.definition: Activating transcription factor 2 is an activating transcription factor that regulates expression of a variety of genes including c-jun genes; cyclin a; cyclin d1; and [MASK].

chargesyndrome.name: charge syndrome
chargesyndrome.definition: Charge syndrome is rare disease characterized by coloboma; choanal atresia; and abnormal semicircular canals. Mutations in chd7 protein resulting in disturbed neural crest development are associated with charge Syndrome.

mineraloil.name: mineral oil
mineraloil.definition: Mineral oil is a mixture of liquid hydrocarbons obtained from petroleum. It is used as laxative, lubricant, ointment base, and emollient.

cellcount.name: cell count
cellcount.definition: Cell count is the number of cells of a specific kind, usually measured per unit volume or area of sample.

genes,myc.name: genes , myc
genes,myc.definition: Myc genes is family of retrovirus-associated dna sequences (myc) originally isolated from an avian myelocytomatosis virus. The proto-oncogene myc (c-myc) codes for a nuclear protein which is involved in nucleic acid metabolism and in mediating the cellular response to growth factors. Truncation of the first exon, which appears to regulate c-myc expression, is crucial for tumorigenicity. The human c-myc gene is located at 8q24 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 8.

lipoproteins,ldl.name: lipoproteins , ldl
lipoproteins,ldl.definition: Ldl lipoproteins is a class of lipoproteins of small size (18-25 nm) and light (1.019-1.063 g/ml) particles with a core composed mainly of cholesterol esters and smaller amounts of triglycerides. The surface monolayer consists mostly of [MASK], a single copy of apolipoprotein b-100, and free cholesterol molecules. The main ldl function is to transport cholesterol and cholesterol esters to extrahepatic tissues.

brainstemhemorrhage,traumatic.name: brain stem hemorrhage , traumatic
brainstemhemorrhage,traumatic.definition: Traumatic brain stem hemorrhage is bleeding into structures of brain stem, including the midbrain; pons; or medulla oblongata, as the result of craniocerebral trauma. diffuse axonal injury is commonly associated. Clinical manifestations may include ocular motility disorders; ataxia; paralysis; [MASK]; and coma.

fibroblastgrowthfactor7.name: fibroblast growth factor 7
fibroblastgrowthfactor7.definition: Fibroblast growth [MASK] is a fibroblast growth factor that is a specific mitogen for epithelial cells. It binds a complex of heparan sulfate and fibroblast growth factor receptor 2b.

neuroprotectiveagents.name: neuroprotective agents
neuroprotectiveagents.definition: Neuroprotective agents is drugs intended to prevent damage to the brain or spinal cord from ischemia, stroke, convulsions, or trauma. Some must be administered before the event, but others may be effective for some time after. They act by a variety of mechanisms, but often directly or indirectly minimize the damage produced by endogenous [MASK].

embryonicandfetaldevelopment.name: embryonic and fetal development
embryonicandfetaldevelopment.definition: Embryonic and fetal development is morphological and physiological development of embryos or fetuses.

epilepsy,generalized.name: epilepsy , generalized
epilepsy,generalized.definition: Generalized epilepsy is recurrent conditions characterized by epileptic seizures which arise diffusely and simultaneously from both hemispheres of the brain. Classification is generally based upon motor manifestations of the seizure (e.g., convulsive, nonconvulsive, akinetic, atonic, etc.) or etiology (e.g., idiopathic, cryptogenic, and symptomatic). (From Mayo Clin Proc, 1996 Apr;71(4):405-14)

singleperson.name: single person
singleperson.definition: Single person is the unmarried man or woman.

psychology.name: psychology
psychology.definition: Psychology is the science dealing with the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.

atrialpressure.name: atrial pressure
atrialpressure.definition: Atrial pressure is the pressure within the cardiac atrium. It can be measured directly by using a pressure catheter (see heart catheterization). It can be also estimated using various imaging techniques or other pressure readings such as [MASK] (an estimate of left atrial pressure) and [MASK] (an estimate of right atrial pressure).

noise,transportation.name: noise , transportation
noise,transportation.definition: Transportation noise is noise associated with transportation, particularly aircraft and automobiles.

diagnosticprocedure.name: diagnostic procedure
diagnosticprocedure.definition: Diagnostic procedure is methods, procedures, and tests performed to diagnose disease, disordered function, or disability.

equivalencetrialsastopic.name: equivalence trials as topic
equivalencetrialsastopic.definition: Equivalence trials as topic is works about trials that aim to show a new treatment is no better and no worse than the standard treatment.

peptidenucleicacids.name: peptide nucleic acids
peptidenucleicacids.definition: Peptide nucleic acids is dna analogs containing neutral amide backbone linkages composed of aminoethyl glycine units instead of the usual phosphodiester linkage of deoxyribose groups. Peptide nucleic acids have high biological stability and higher affinity for complementary dna or rna sequences than analogous dna oligomers.

personality.name: personality
personality.definition: Personality is behavior-response patterns that characterize the individual.

liquidventilation.name: liquid ventilation
liquidventilation.definition: Liquid ventilation is artificial respiration (respiration, artificial) using an oxygenated fluid.

phytoplankton.name: phytoplankton
phytoplankton.definition: Phytoplankton is free-floating minute organisms that are photosynthetic. The term is non-taxonomic and refers to a lifestyle (energy utilization and motility), rather than a particular type of organism. Most, but not all, are unicellular algae. Important groups include diatoms; dinoflagellates; cyanobacteria; chlorophyta; haptophyta; cryptomonads; and silicoflagellates.

surgery,plastic.name: surgery , plastic
surgery,plastic.definition: Plastic surgery is the branch of surgery concerned with restoration, reconstruction, or improvement of defective, damaged, or missing structures.

colorectalneoplasms.name: colorectal neoplasms
colorectalneoplasms.definition: Colorectal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the colon or the rectum or both. Risk factors for colorectal cancer include chronic ulcerative colitis; familial polyposis coli; exposure to asbestos; and irradiation of the cervix uteri.

speechperception.name: speech perception
speechperception.definition: [MASK] perception is the process whereby an utterance is decoded into a representation in terms of linguistic units (sequences of phonetic segments which combine to form lexical and grammatical morphemes).

traumacenters.name: trauma centers
traumacenters.definition: Trauma centers is specialized hospital facilities which provide diagnostic and therapeutic services for trauma patients.

pregnancyrate.name: pregnancy rate
pregnancyrate.definition: Pregnancy rate is the ratio of the number of conceptions (conception) including live birth; stillbirth; and fetal losses, to the mean number of females of reproductive age in a population during a [MASK] time period.

minimalclinicallyimportantdifference.name: minimal clinically important difference
minimalclinicallyimportantdifference.definition: Minimal clinically important difference is a statistically significant minimum [MASK] of clinical outcomes that demonstrates a clinical benefit of an intervention or treatment.

epidemiologicmethods.name: epidemiologic methods
epidemiologicmethods.definition: Epidemiologic methods is research techniques that focus on study designs and data gathering methods in human and animal populations.

income.name: income
income.definition: Income is revenues or receipts accruing from business enterprise, labor, or invested capital.

thoraciccavity.name: thoracic cavity
thoraciccavity.definition: Thoracic cavity is the region of the thorax that includes the pleural cavity and mediastinum.

healthbenefitplans,employee.name: health benefit plans , employee
healthbenefitplans,employee.definition: [MASK] benefit plans is health insurance plans for employees, and generally including their dependents, usually on a cost-sharing basis with the employer paying a percentage of the premium.

retinalveinocclusion.name: retinal vein occlusion
retinalveinocclusion.definition: Retinal vein occlusion is blockage of the retinal vein. Those at high risk for this condition include patients with hypertension; diabetes mellitus; atherosclerosis; and other cardiovascular diseases.

ubiquitin.name: ubiquitin
ubiquitin.definition: Ubiquitin is a highly conserved 76-amino acid peptide universally found in eukaryotic cells that functions as a marker for intracellular protein transport and degradation. Ubiquitin becomes activated through a series of complicated steps and forms an isopeptide bond to lysine residues of specific proteins within the cell. These "ubiquitinated" proteins can be recognized and degraded by proteosomes or be transported to specific compartments within the cell.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 5
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.definition: Member 5 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g protein that functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g, member 8 in the selective transport of dietary cholesterol and phytosterols into and export out of enterocytes. It also functions in selective sterol excretion by the liver into [MASK].

hereditarysensoryandmotorneuropathy.name: hereditary sensory and motor neuropathy
hereditarysensoryandmotorneuropathy.definition: Hereditary sensory and motor neuropathy is a group of slowly progressive inherited disorders affecting motor and sensory peripheral nerves. Subtypes include HMSNs i-vii. hmsn i and ii both refer to charcot-marie-tooth disease. hmsn iii refers to hypertrophic neuropathy of infancy. hmsn iv refers to refsum disease. hmsn v refers to a condition marked by a hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy associated with spastic paraplegia (see spastic paraplegia, hereditary). hmsn vi refers to hmsn associated with an inherited optic atrophy (optic atrophies, hereditary), and hmsn vii refers to hmsn associated with retinitis pigmentosa. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1343)

translating.name: translating
translating.definition: Translating is conversion from one language to another language.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.definition: Subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is a subfamily of atp binding cassette transporters that function primarily in the transport of lipids and sterols across the cell membrane. They also export urea and various drugs resulting in multidrug resistance. They are smaller than most other atp binding cassette proteins, consisting of six transmembrane alpha helices and a distinct N-terminal cytoplasmic ATP-binding domain, and function as homo- or heterodimers with other abcg transporters.

histology.name: histology
histology.definition: Histology is the study of the structure of various tissues of organisms on a microscopic level.

righttowork.name: right to work
righttowork.definition: Right to work is the right of individuals to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favorable conditions of work and to protection against [MASK].

ovariandiseases.name: ovarian diseases
ovariandiseases.definition: Ovarian diseases is pathological processes of the ovary.

administrativepersonnel.name: administrative personnel
administrativepersonnel.definition: Administrative personnel is individuals responsible for the development of policy and supervision of the execution of plans and functional operations.

government.name: government
government.definition: Government is the complex of political institutions, laws, and customs through which the function of governing is carried out in a specific political unit.

esophagealphmonitoring.name: esophageal ph monitoring
esophagealphmonitoring.definition: Esophageal ph monitoring is analysis of the hydrogen ion concentration in the lumen of the esophagus. It is used to record the pattern, frequency, and duration of gastroesophageal reflux.

femurneck.name: femur neck
femurneck.definition: Femur [MASK] is the constricted portion of the [MASK] bone between the femur head and the trochanters.

sodium,dietary.name: sodium , dietary
sodium,dietary.definition: Dietary sodium is sodium or sodium compounds used in foods or as a food. The most frequently used compounds are sodium chloride or sodium glutamate.

foodsafety.name: food safety
foodsafety.definition: Food safety is activities involved in ensuring the safety of food including avoidance of bacterial and other contamination.

metabolicdiseases.name: metabolic diseases
metabolicdiseases.definition: Metabolic diseases is generic term for diseases caused by an abnormal metabolic process. It can be congenital due to inherited enzyme abnormality (metabolism, inborn errors) or acquired due to disease of an endocrine organ or failure of a metabolically important organ such as the liver. (Stedman, 26th ed)

decompressionsickness.name: decompression sickness
decompressionsickness.definition: Decompression sickness is a condition occurring as a result of exposure to a rapid fall in ambient pressure. Gases, nitrogen in particular, come out of solution and form bubbles in body fluid and blood. These gas bubbles accumulate in joint spaces and the peripheral circulation impairing tissue oxygenation causing disorientation, severe pain, and potentially death.

dentalprosthesis.name: dental prosthesis
dentalprosthesis.definition: Dental prosthesis is an artificial replacement for one or more natural teeth or part of a tooth, or associated structures, ranging from a portion of a tooth to a complete denture. The dental prosthesis is used for cosmetic or functional reasons, or both. dentures and specific types of dentures are also available. (From Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p244 & Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p643)

lynchsyndromeii.name: lynch syndrome ii
lynchsyndromeii.definition: Lynch syndrome ii is hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal neoplasms associated with other malignancies, more commonly of ovarian or uterine origin. When also associated with sebaceous gland neoplasms, it is called muir-torre syndrome.

capsidproteins.name: capsid proteins
capsidproteins.definition: Capsid proteins is proteins that form the capsid of viruses.

libraries,special.name: libraries , special
libraries,special.definition: Special libraries is collections covering specialized subjects, containing materials in a special format, or serving a specialized clientele.

collagentypex.name: collagen type x
collagentypex.definition: Collagen type x is a non-fibrillar collagen found primarily in terminally differentiated hypertrophic chondrocytes. It is a homotrimer of three identical alpha1(X) subunits.

sexdifferentiation.name: sex differentiation
sexdifferentiation.definition: [MASK] differentiation is the process in developing [MASK]- or gender-specific tissue, organ, or function after [MASK] determination processes have [MASK] the [MASK] of the gonads. Major areas of [MASK] differentiation occur in the reproductive tract (genitalia) and the brain.

birthinjuries.name: birth injuries
birthinjuries.definition: Birth injuries is mechanical or anoxic trauma incurred by the infant during labor or delivery.

centrifugation,densitygradient.name: centrifugation , density gradient
centrifugation,densitygradient.definition: Density gradient centrifugation is separation of particles according to density by employing a gradient of varying densities. At equilibrium each particle settles in the gradient at a point equal to its density. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

hepatitisd,chronic.name: hepatitis d , chronic
hepatitisd,chronic.definition: Chronic hepatitis d is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by [MASK] in conjunction with hepatitis b virus and lasting six months or more.

cholesterolesterstoragedisease.name: cholesterol ester storage disease
cholesterolesterstoragedisease.definition: Cholesterol ester storage disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the gene for acid lipase (sterol esterase). It is characterized by the accumulation of neutral lipids, particularly cholesterol esters in leukocytes, fibroblasts, and [MASK].

publichealthdentistry.name: public health dentistry
publichealthdentistry.definition: Public health dentistry is a dental specialty concerned with the prevention of disease and the maintenance of [MASK] through promoting organized dental health programs at a community, state, or federal level.

models,neurological.name: models , neurological
models,neurological.definition: Neurological models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of the neurological system, processes or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

polya.name: poly a
polya.definition: Poly a is a group of adenine ribonucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each adenine ribonucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the ribose moieties.

blastinjuries.name: blast injuries
blastinjuries.definition: Blast injuries is injuries resulting when a person is struck by particles impelled with violent force from an explosion. Blast causes pulmonary concussion and hemorrhage, laceration of other thoracic and abdominal viscera, ruptured ear drums, and minor effects in the central nervous system. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

antigenpresentation.name: antigen presentation
antigenpresentation.definition: Antigen presentation is the process by which antigen is presented to lymphocytes in a form they can recognize. This is performed by antigen presenting cells (APCs). Some antigens require processing before they can be recognized. Antigen processing consists of ingestion and partial [MASK] of the antigen by the apc, followed by presentation of fragments on the cell surface. (From Rosen et al., Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

fibroblastgrowthfactor6.name: fibroblast growth factor 6
fibroblastgrowthfactor6.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 6 is a fibroblast growth factor that was initially identified based on its sequence similarity to fibroblast growth factor 4. It is found in myoblasts and plays an important role in muscle development.

persons.name: persons
persons.definition: Persons is persons as individuals (e.g., abortion applicants) or as members of a group (e.g., hispanic americans). It is not used for members of the various professions (e.g., physicians) or occupations (e.g., librarians) for which occupational groups is available.

multifunctionalnanoparticles.name: multifunctional nanoparticles
multifunctionalnanoparticles.definition: Multifunctional nanoparticles is nanoparticles that are engineered to have two or more physical properties.

mapkinasekinase5.name: map kinase kinase 5
