mapkinasekinase5.definition: Map kinase kinase 5 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for mitogen-activated protein kinase 7.

tail.name: tail
tail.definition: Tail is an extension of the posterior of an animal body beyond the torso.

dentalrecords.name: dental records
dentalrecords.definition: Dental records is data collected during dental examination for the purpose of study, diagnosis, or treatment planning.

receptors,angiotensin.name: receptors , angiotensin
receptors,angiotensin.definition: Angiotensin receptors is cell surface proteins that bind angiotensins and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

neuralplate.name: neural plate
neuralplate.definition: Neural plate is the region in the dorsal ectoderm of a chordate embryo that gives rise to the future central nervous system. Tissue in the neural plate is called the neuroectoderm, often used as a synonym of neural plate.

dnaadducts.name: dna adducts
dnaadducts.definition: Dna adducts is the products of chemical reactions that result in the addition of extraneous chemical groups to dna.

rehabilitationnursing.name: rehabilitation nursing
rehabilitationnursing.definition: Rehabilitation nursing is a nursing specialty involved in the diagnosis and treatment of human responses of individuals and groups to actual or potential health problems with the characteristics of altered functional ability and altered life-style.

plantpreparations.name: plant preparations
plantpreparations.definition: Plant preparations is material prepared from plants.

substancewithdrawalsyndrome.name: substance withdrawal syndrome
substancewithdrawalsyndrome.definition: Substance withdrawal syndrome is physiological and psychological symptoms associated with withdrawal from the use of a drug after prolonged administration or habituation. The concept includes withdrawal from smoking or drinking, as well as withdrawal from an administered drug.

rna,transfer,phe.name: rna , transfer , phe
rna,transfer,phe.definition: Phe transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying phenylalanine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

prosthesiscoloring.name: prosthesis coloring
prosthesiscoloring.definition: Prosthesis coloring is coloring, shading, or tinting of prosthetic components, devices, and materials.

breeding.name: breeding
breeding.definition: Breeding is the production of offspring by selective mating or hybridization, genetic in animals or plants.

carbon.name: carbon
carbon.definition: Carbon is a nonmetallic element with atomic symbol c, atomic number 6, and atomic weight [12.0096; 12.0116]. It may occur as several different allotropes including diamond; charcoal; and [MASK]; and as soot from incompletely burned fuel.

calcium.name: calcium
calcium.definition: Calcium is a basic element found in nearly all tissues. It is a member of the alkaline earth family of metals with the atomic symbol Ca, atomic number 20, and atomic weight 40. Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body and combines with phosphorus to form calcium phosphate in the bones and teeth. It is essential for the normal functioning of nerves and muscles and plays a role in blood coagulation (as factor iv) and in many enzymatic processes.

dentalimplants.name: dental implants
dentalimplants.definition: Dental implants is biocompatible materials placed into (endosseous) or onto (subperiosteal) the jawbone to support a crown, bridge, or artificial tooth, or to stabilize a diseased tooth.

sodiumlactate.name: sodium lactate
sodiumlactate.definition: Sodium lactate is the sodium [MASK] of racemic or inactive lactic acid. It is a hygroscopic agent used intravenously as a systemic and urinary alkalizer.

carotidartery,internal,dissection.name: carotid artery , internal , dissection
carotidartery,internal,dissection.definition: [MASK] internal carotid artery is the splitting of the vessel wall in one or both (left and right) internal carotid arteries (carotid artery, internal). Interstitial hemorrhage into the media of the vessel wall can lead to occlusion of the internal carotid artery and aneurysm formation.

thalamicdiseases.name: thalamic diseases
thalamicdiseases.definition: Thalamic diseases is disorders of the centrally located thalamus, which integrates a wide range of cortical and subcortical information. Manifestations include sensory loss, movement disorders; ataxia, pain syndromes, visual disorders, a variety of neuropsychological conditions, and coma. Relatively common etiologies include cerebrovascular disorders; craniocerebral trauma; brain neoplasms; brain hypoxia; intracranial hemorrhages; and infectious processes.

cyclina.name: cyclin a
cyclina.definition: Cyclin a is a cyclin subtype that has specificity for cdc2 protein kinase and cyclin-dependent kinase 2. It plays a role in progression of the cell cycle through g1/s and g2/m phase transitions.

fluorescentdyes.name: fluorescent dyes
fluorescentdyes.definition: Fluorescent dyes is chemicals that emit light after excitation by light. The wave length of the emitted light is usually longer than that of the incident light. Fluorochromes are substances that cause fluorescence in other substances, i.e., dyes used to mark or label other compounds with fluorescent tags.

arterialpressure.name: arterial pressure
arterialpressure.definition: Arterial pressure is the blood pressure in the arteries. It is commonly measured with a sphygmomanometer on the [MASK] which represents the arterial pressure in the brachial artery.

patientdischarge.name: patient discharge
patientdischarge.definition: Patient discharge is the administrative process of discharging the patient, alive or dead, from hospitals or other health facilities.

leukocytereductionprocedures.name: leukocyte reduction procedures
leukocytereductionprocedures.definition: Leukocyte reduction procedures is the removal of leukocytes from blood to reduce blood transfusion reactions and lower the chance of transmitting viruses. This may be performed by filtration or by cytapheresis.

vitaminedeficiency.name: vitamin e deficiency
vitaminedeficiency.definition: Vitamin e deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin e in the diet, characterized by posterior column and spinocerebellar tract abnormalities, areflexia, ophthalmoplegia, and disturbances of gait, proprioception, and vibration. In premature infants vitamin e deficiency is associated with hemolytic anemia, thrombocytosis, edema, intraventricular hemorrhage, and increasing risk of retrolental fibroplasia and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. An apparent inborn error of vitamin e metabolism, named familial isolated vitamin e deficiency, has recently been identified. (Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1181)

animalwelfare.name: animal welfare
animalwelfare.definition: Animal welfare is the protection of animals in laboratories or other specific environments by promoting their health through better nutrition, housing, and care.

genomicislands.name: genomic islands
genomicislands.definition: Genomic islands is distinct units in some bacterial, bacteriophage or plasmid genomes that are types of mobile genetic elements. Encoded in them are a variety of fitness conferring genes, such as virulence factors (in "pathogenicity islands or islets"), antibiotic resistance genes, or genes required for symbiosis (in "symbiosis islands or islets"). They range in size from 10 - 500 kilobases, and their gc content and [MASK] differ from the rest of the genome. They typically contain an integrase gene, although in some cases this gene has been deleted resulting in "anchored genomic islands".

salivaryproteinsandpeptides.name: salivary proteins and peptides
salivaryproteinsandpeptides.definition: Salivary proteins and peptides is proteins and peptides found in saliva and the salivary glands. Some salivary proteins such as alpha-amylases are enzymes, but their composition varies in different individuals.

geneticcomplementationtest.name: genetic complementation test
geneticcomplementationtest.definition: Genetic complementation test is a test used to determine whether or not complementation (compensation in the form of dominance) will occur in a cell with a given mutant phenotype when another mutant genome, encoding the same mutant phenotype, is introduced into that cell.

maternalserumscreeningtests.name: maternal serum screening tests
maternalserumscreeningtests.definition: Maternal serum screening tests is analysis of the level of specific biomarkers in a pregnant woman's sera to identify those at risk for pregnancy complications or birth defects.

ear.name: ear
ear.definition: Ear is the hearing and equilibrium system of the body. It consists of three parts: the external ear, the [MASK], and the [MASK]. Sound waves are transmitted through this organ where vibration is transduced to nerve signals that pass through the acoustic nerve to the central nervous system. The [MASK] also contains the vestibular organ that maintains equilibrium by transducing signals to the vestibular nerve.

motionpictures.name: motion pictures
motionpictures.definition: Motion pictures is the art, technique, or business of producing motion pictures for entertainment, propaganda, or instruction.

electricpowersupplies.name: electric power supplies
electricpowersupplies.definition: Electric power supplies is devices that control the supply of electric current for [MASK] electrical equipment.

taxequityandfiscalresponsibilityact.name: tax equity and fiscal responsibility act
taxequityandfiscalresponsibilityact.definition: Tax equity and fiscal responsibility act is pl97-248. Title ii of the Act specifies "provisions relating to savings in health and income security programs." This includes changes in payment for services, benefits and premiums of Medicare as well as changes in provisions under Medicaid and other specific programs covered by Social Security. Title ii includes various revenue measures.

radiationexposure.name: radiation exposure
radiationexposure.definition: Radiation exposure is phenomenon in which organisms are subjected to radiation.

pseudomonasinfections.name: pseudomonas infections
pseudomonasinfections.definition: Pseudomonas infections is infections with bacteria of the genus pseudomonas.

islands.name: islands
islands.definition: Islands is tracts of land completely surrounded by water.

acidosis.name: acidosis
acidosis.definition: Acidosis is a pathologic condition of acid accumulation or depletion of base in the body. The two main types are [MASK] and metabolic acidosis, due to metabolic acid build up.

housecalls.name: house calls
housecalls.definition: House calls is visits to the patient's home by professional personnel for the purpose of diagnosis and/or treatment.

problemsolving.name: problem solving
problemsolving.definition: Problem solving is a learning situation involving more than one alternative from which a selection is made in order to attain a specific goal.

stimuliresponsivepolymers.name: stimuli responsive polymers
stimuliresponsivepolymers.definition: Stimuli responsive polymers is polymeric materials designed to change properties in response to a stimulus.

blindloopsyndrome.name: blind loop syndrome
blindloopsyndrome.definition: Blind loop syndrome is a malabsorption syndrome that is associated with a blind loop in the upper small intestine that is characterized by the lack of peristaltic movement, stasis of intestinal contents, and the overgrowth of bacteria. Such bacterial overgrowth interferes with [MASK] [MASK] action, fatty acids processing, microvilli integrity, and the absorption of nutrients such as vitamin b12 and folic acid.

americannurses'association.name: american nurses ' association
americannurses'association.definition: American nurses' association is american nurses ' association

airwayresistance.name: airway resistance
airwayresistance.definition: Airway resistance is physiologically, the opposition to flow of air caused by the forces of friction. As a part of pulmonary function testing, it is the ratio of driving pressure to the rate of air flow.

primatediseases.name: primate diseases
primatediseases.definition: Primate diseases is diseases of animals within the order primates. This term includes diseases of Haplorhini and Strepsirhini.

tonguehabits.name: tongue habits
tonguehabits.definition: Tongue habits is acquired responses regularly manifested by tongue movement or positioning.

regionalbloodflow.name: regional blood flow
regionalbloodflow.definition: Regional blood flow is the flow of blood through or around an organ or region of the body.

phrases.name: phrases
phrases.definition: Phrases is work consisting of common terms, phrases, idioms, and typical conversations, e.g., between health professional and patients. These are often intended for use by non-native speakers of a language.

hematologicagents.name: hematologic agents
hematologicagents.definition: Hematologic agents is drugs that act on blood and blood-forming organs and those that affect the hemostatic system.

psychologicaltrauma.name: psychological trauma
psychologicaltrauma.definition: Psychological trauma is an emotionally painful, shocking, stressful, and sometimes life-threatening experience. It can result from witnessing distressing events such as natural disasters, physical or sexual abuse, and terrorism or other acts of violence. (https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/)

cellhypoxia.name: cell hypoxia
cellhypoxia.definition: Cell hypoxia is a condition of decreased oxygen content at the cellular level.

myosintypeiii.name: myosin type iii
myosintypeiii.definition: Myosin type iii is a subclass of myosins originally found in the photoreceptor of drosophila. The heavy chains can occur as two alternatively spliced isoforms of 132 and 174 KDa. The amino terminal of myosin type iii is highly unusual in that it contains a protein kinase domain which may be an important component of the visual process.

microbiota.name: microbiota
microbiota.definition: Microbiota is the full collection of microbes (bacteria, fungi, virus, etc.) that naturally exist within a particular biological niche such as an organism, soil, a body of water, etc.

autoimmunepancreatitis.name: autoimmune pancreatitis
autoimmunepancreatitis.definition: Autoimmune pancreatitis is chronic pancreatitis associated with autoimmune diseases.

adenocarcinoma.name: adenocarcinoma
adenocarcinoma.definition: Adenocarcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

magnesiumcompounds.name: magnesium compounds
magnesiumcompounds.definition: Magnesium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain magnesium as an integral part of the molecule.

receptors,pancreatichormone.name: receptors , pancreatic hormone
receptors,pancreatichormone.definition: Pancreatic hormone receptors is cell surface proteins that bind pancreatic hormones with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. These include receptors for glucagon (secreted by alpha cells), insulin (secreted by beta cells), somatostatin (secreted by delta cells), and pancreatic peptide (secreted by pp cells). Some of these hormones and receptors also support neurotransmission.

ventilation.name: ventilation
ventilation.definition: Ventilation is supplying a building or house, their rooms and corridors, with fresh air. The controlling of the environment thus may be in public or domestic sites and in medical or non-medical locales. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

thyroidnuclearfactor1.name: thyroid nuclear factor 1
thyroidnuclearfactor1.definition: Thyroid nuclear factor 1 is a homeobox protein and transcription factor that localizes to the cell nucleus where it activates expression of thyroid specific genes such as thyroglobulin and the thyrotropin receptor. It is critical for maintaining thyroid tissue in a differentiated state and also plays a role in lung development. Mutations in the nkx2-1 gene are associated with chorea, benign hereditary.

publichealthsurveillance.name: public health surveillance
publichealthsurveillance.definition: Public health surveillance is the ongoing, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data with the purpose of preventing or controlling disease or injury, or of identifying unusual events of public health importance, followed by the dissemination and use of information for public health action. (From Am j Prev Med 2011;41(6):636)

chromosomeduplication.name: chromosome duplication
chromosomeduplication.definition: Chromosome duplication is an aberration in which an extra chromosome or a chromosomal segment is made.

cerebralveins.name: cerebral veins
cerebralveins.definition: Cerebral veins is veins draining the cerebrum.

bodysurfacearea.name: body surface area
bodysurfacearea.definition: Body surface area is the two dimensional measure of the outer layer of the body.

tissuescaffolds.name: tissue scaffolds
tissuescaffolds.definition: Tissue scaffolds is cell growth support structures composed of biocompatible materials. They are specially designed solid support matrices for cell attachment in tissue engineering and guided tissue regeneration uses.

publichealthnursing.name: public health nursing
publichealthnursing.definition: Public health nursing is a nursing specialty concerned with promoting and protecting the health of populations, using knowledge from nursing, social, and public health sciences to develop local, regional, state, and national health policy and research. It is population-focused and community-oriented, aimed at health promotion and disease prevention through educational, diagnostic, and preventive programs.

caseinkinaseii.name: casein kinase ii
caseinkinaseii.definition: Casein kinase ii is a ubiquitous casein kinase that is comprised of two distinct [MASK] and dimeric regulatory subunit. Casein kinase ii has been shown to phosphorylate a large number of substrates, many of which are proteins involved in the regulation of gene expression.

vitalcapacity.name: vital capacity
vitalcapacity.definition: Vital capacity is the volume of air that is exhaled by a maximal expiration following a maximal inspiration.

personnelturnover.name: personnel turnover
personnelturnover.definition: Personnel turnover is a change or shift in personnel due to reorganization, resignation, or discharge.

placentalextracts.name: placental extracts
placentalextracts.definition: Placental extracts is extracts prepared from placental tissue; they may contain specific but uncharacterized factors or proteins with specific activities.

neuronalplasticity.name: neuronal plasticity
neuronalplasticity.definition: Neuronal plasticity is the capacity of the nervous system to change its reactivity as the result of successive activations.

weaponsofmassdestruction.name: weapons of mass destruction
weaponsofmassdestruction.definition: Weapons of mass destruction is weapons that are capable of a high order of destruction and/or of being used to destroy large numbers of people. It includes nuclear weapons, and biological, chemical, and radiation weapons.

communityhealthworkers.name: community health workers
communityhealthworkers.definition: Community health workers is persons trained to assist professional health personnel in communicating with residents in the community concerning needs and availability of health services.

proteintranslocationsystems.name: protein translocation systems
proteintranslocationsystems.definition: Protein translocation systems is multiprotein complexes that carry out protein transport across cell membranes.

guideline.name: guideline
guideline.definition: Guideline is work consisting of a [MASK] of statements, directions, or principles presenting current or future rules or policy. Guidelines may be developed by government agencies at any level, institutions, organizations such as professional societies or governing boards, or by the convening of expert panels. The text may be cursive or in [MASK] form, but it is generally a comprehensive guide to problems and approaches in any discipline or activity. This concept relates to the general conduct and administration of health care activities rather than to specific decisions for a particular clinical condition. For that aspect, practice guideline is available.

smoking.name: smoking
smoking.definition: Smoking is willful or deliberate act of [MASK] and exhaling smoke from burning substances or agents held by hand.

exploratorybehavior.name: exploratory behavior
exploratorybehavior.definition: Exploratory behavior is the tendency to explore or investigate a novel environment. It is considered a motivation not clearly distinguishable from curiosity.

disastervictims.name: disaster victims
disastervictims.definition: Disaster victims is persons adversely effected by disasters, occurrences that result in property damage, deaths, and/or injuries to a community.

barrettesophagus.name: barrett esophagus
barrettesophagus.definition: Barrett esophagus is a condition with damage to the lining of the lower esophagus resulting from chronic acid reflux (esophagitis, reflux). Through the process of metaplasia, the squamous cells are replaced by a columnar epithelium with cells resembling those of the intestine or the salmon-pink mucosa of the stomach. Barrett's columnar epithelium is a marker for severe reflux and precursor to adenocarcinoma of the esophagus.

vegetables.name: vegetables
vegetables.definition: Vegetables is a food group comprised of edible plants or their parts.

diskslargehomolog4protein.name: disks large homolog 4 protein
diskslargehomolog4protein.definition: Disks large homolog 4 protein is a neuronal protein consisting of three pdz domains, an sh3 domain, and a C-terminal guanylate kinase-like region (see maguk proteins). It localizes to the post-synaptic density and associates with the cytoplasmic tail of nmda receptors and shaker potassium channels, playing a critical role in nmda receptor-mediated synaptic plasticity.

hematopoieticcellgrowthfactors.name: hematopoietic cell growth factors
hematopoieticcellgrowthfactors.definition: Hematopoietic cell growth factors is these growth factors comprise a family of hematopoietic regulators with biological specificities defined by their ability to support proliferation and differentiation of blood cells of different lineages. erythropoietin and the colony-stimulating factors belong to this family. Some of these factors have been studied and used in the treatment of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and bone marrow failure syndromes.

drysocket.name: dry socket
drysocket.definition: Dry socket is a condition sometimes occurring after tooth extraction, particularly after traumatic extraction, resulting in a dry appearance of the exposed bone in the socket, due to disintegration or loss of the blood clot. It is basically a focal osteomyelitis without suppuration and is accompanied by severe pain (alveolalgia) and foul odor. (Dorland, 28th ed)

drugscreeningassays,antitumor.name: drug screening assays , antitumor
drugscreeningassays,antitumor.definition: Antitumor drug screening assays is methods of investigating the effectiveness of anticancer cytotoxic drugs and biologic inhibitors. These include in vitro cell-kill models and cytostatic dye exclusion tests as well as in vivo measurement of tumor growth parameters in laboratory animals.

vasculargrafting.name: vascular grafting
vasculargrafting.definition: Vascular grafting is surgical insertion of blood vessel prostheses, or transplanted blood vessels, or other biological material to repair injured or diseased blood vessels.

seeddispersal.name: seed dispersal
seeddispersal.definition: [MASK] dispersal is the various physical methods which include [MASK], insects, animals, tension, and water, by which a plant scatters its [MASK] away from the parent plant.

chemistry,pharmaceutical.name: chemistry , pharmaceutical
chemistry,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical chemistry is chemistry dealing with the composition and preparation of agents having pharmacologic actions or diagnostic use.

goldcompounds.name: gold compounds
goldcompounds.definition: Gold compounds is inorganic compounds that contain gold as an integral part of the molecule.

methylenechloride.name: methylene chloride
methylenechloride.definition: Methylene chloride is a chlorinated hydrocarbon that has been used as an [MASK] anesthetic and acts as a narcotic in high concentrations. Its primary use is as a solvent in manufacturing and food technology.

parathyroidneoplasms.name: parathyroid neoplasms
parathyroidneoplasms.definition: Parathyroid neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the [MASK].

bodyweightchanges.name: body weight changes
bodyweightchanges.definition: Body weight changes is a clinical manifestation consisting of alterations in an individual's weight from his or her norm.

biopsy,needle.name: biopsy , needle
biopsy,needle.definition: Needle biopsy is removal and examination of tissue obtained through a transdermal needle inserted into the specific region, organ, or tissue being analyzed.

respiratorymuscles.name: respiratory muscles
respiratorymuscles.definition: Respiratory muscles is these include the muscles of the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles.

publicpolicy.name: public policy
publicpolicy.definition: Public policy is a course or method of action selected, usually by a government, from among alternatives to guide and determine present and future decisions.

salivaryglands.name: salivary glands
salivaryglands.definition: Salivary glands is glands that secrete saliva in the mouth. There are three pairs of salivary glands (parotid gland; sublingual gland; submandibular gland).

receptors,transferrin.name: receptors , transferrin
receptors,transferrin.definition: Transferrin receptors is membrane glycoproteins found in high concentrations on iron-utilizing cells. They specifically bind iron-bearing transferrin, are endocytosed with its ligand and then returned to the cell surface where transferrin without its iron is released.

chromosomes,artificial,bacterial.name: chromosomes , artificial , bacterial
chromosomes,artificial,bacterial.definition: Bacterial artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, a replication origin, for successful replication, propagation to and maintenance as an extra chromosome in bacteria. In addition, they can carry large amounts (about 200 kilobases) of other sequence for a variety of bioengineering purposes.

rna,transfer,gly.name: rna , transfer , gly
rna,transfer,gly.definition: Gly transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying glycine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

riskassessment.name: risk assessment
riskassessment.definition: Risk assessment is the qualitative or quantitative estimation of the likelihood of adverse effects that may result from exposure to specified health hazards or from the absence of beneficial influences. (Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 1988)

carotidbodytumor.name: carotid body tumor
carotidbodytumor.definition: Carotid body tumor is benign paraganglioma at the bifurcation of the common carotid arteries. It can encroach on the parapharyngeal space and produce dysphagia, pain, and cranial nerve palsies.

femoralnerve.name: femoral nerve
femoralnerve.definition: Femoral nerve is a nerve originating in the lumbar spinal cord (usually l2 to l4) and traveling through the lumbar plexus to provide motor innervation to extensors of the [MASK] and sensory innervation to parts of the [MASK], lower leg, and [MASK], and to the hip and [MASK].

drugresistance,neoplasm.name: drug resistance , neoplasm
drugresistance,neoplasm.definition: Neoplasm drug resistance is resistance or diminished response of a neoplasm to an antineoplastic agent in humans, animals, or cell or tissue cultures.

circadianrhythm.name: circadian rhythm
circadianrhythm.definition: Circadian rhythm is the regular recurrence, in cycles of about 24 hours, of biological processes or activities, such as sensitivity to drugs or environmental and physiological stimuli.

metals,rareearth.name: metals , rare earth
metals,rareearth.definition: Rare earth metals is a group of elements that include scandium; yttrium; and the lanthanoid series elements. Historically, the rare earth metals got their name from the fact that they were never found in their pure elemental form, but as an oxide. In addition they were very difficult to purify. They are not truly rare and comprise about 25% of the metals in the earth's crust.

dna,mitochondrial.name: dna , mitochondrial
dna,mitochondrial.definition: Mitochondrial dna is double-stranded dna of mitochondria. In eukaryotes, the [MASK] is circular and codes for ribosomal RNAs, transfer RNAs, and about 10 proteins.

eyeforeignbodies.name: eye foreign bodies
eyeforeignbodies.definition: Eye foreign bodies is inanimate objects that become enclosed in the eye.

shoulderjoint.name: shoulder joint
shoulderjoint.definition: [MASK] joint is the articulation between the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula.

endoscopy,digestivesystem.name: endoscopy , digestive system
endoscopy,digestivesystem.definition: Digestive system endoscopy is endoscopic examination, therapy or surgery of the digestive tract.

morphogenesis.name: morphogenesis
morphogenesis.definition: Morphogenesis is the development of anatomical structures to create the form of a single- or multi-cell organism. Morphogenesis provides form changes of a part, parts, or the whole organism.

homeinfusiontherapy.name: home infusion therapy
homeinfusiontherapy.definition: Home infusion therapy is use of any infusion therapy on an ambulatory, outpatient, or other non-institutionalized basis.

occupationalhealthnursing.name: occupational health nursing
occupationalhealthnursing.definition: [MASK] nursing is the practice of nursing in the work environment.

palliativecare.name: palliative care
palliativecare.definition: Palliative care is care alleviating symptoms without curing the underlying disease. (Stedman, 25th ed)

oxygen.name: oxygen
oxygen.definition: Oxygen is an element with atomic symbol o, atomic number 8, and atomic weight [15.99903; 15.99977]. It is the most abundant element on earth and essential for respiration.

salivaryglandneoplasms.name: salivary gland neoplasms
salivaryglandneoplasms.definition: Salivary gland neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the salivary glands.

telomerase.name: telomerase
telomerase.definition: Telomerase is an essential ribonucleoprotein reverse transcriptase that adds telomeric dna to the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes.

laryngealdiseases.name: laryngeal diseases
laryngealdiseases.definition: Laryngeal diseases is pathological processes involving any part of the larynx which coordinates many functions such as voice production, breathing, swallowing, and coughing.

occipitalbone.name: occipital bone
occipitalbone.definition: Occipital bone is part of the back and base of the cranium that encloses the foramen magnum.

estrogenreplacementtherapy.name: estrogen replacement therapy
estrogenreplacementtherapy.definition: Estrogen replacement therapy is the use of hormonal agents with estrogen-like activity in postmenopausal or other estrogen-deficient women to alleviate effects of hormone deficiency, such as vasomotor symptoms, dyspareunia, and progressive development of osteoporosis. This may also include the use of progestational agents in combination therapy.

patientcareteam.name: patient care team
patientcareteam.definition: Patient care team is care of patients by a multidisciplinary team usually organized under the [MASK] of a physician; each member of the team has specific responsibilities and the whole team contributes to the care of the patient.

biologicalfactors.name: biological factors
biologicalfactors.definition: Biological factors is endogenously-synthesized compounds that influence biological processes not otherwise classified under enzymes; hormones or hormone antagonists.

porcinerespiratoryandreproductivesyndrom.name: porcine respiratory and reproductive syndrome virus
porcinerespiratoryandreproductivesyndrom.definition: Porcine respiratory and reproductive syndrome virus is a species of arterivirus causing reproductive and respiratory disease in pigs. The European strain is called Lelystad virus. Airborne transmission is common.

nucleotides.name: nucleotides
nucleotides.definition: Nucleotides is the monomeric units from which dna or rna polymers are constructed. They consist of a purine or pyrimidine base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. (From King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

cardiacoutput,low.name: cardiac output , low
cardiacoutput,low.definition: Low cardiac output is a state of subnormal or depressed cardiac output at rest or during stress. It is a characteristic of cardiovascular diseases, including congenital, valvular, rheumatic, hypertensive, coronary, and cardiomyopathic. The serious form of low cardiac output is characterized by marked reduction in [MASK], and systemic vasoconstriction resulting in cold, pale, and sometimes cyanotic extremities.

insituhybridization.name: in situ hybridization
insituhybridization.definition: In situ hybridization is a technique that localizes specific nucleic acid sequences within intact chromosomes, eukaryotic cells, or bacterial cells through the use of specific nucleic acid-labeled probes.

hypertrophy,leftventricular.name: hypertrophy , left ventricular
hypertrophy,leftventricular.definition: Left ventricular hypertrophy is enlargement of the left ventricle of the heart. This increase in ventricular mass is attributed to sustained abnormal pressure or volume loads and is a contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.

cholinergicfibers.name: cholinergic fibers
cholinergicfibers.definition: Cholinergic fibers is nerve fibers liberating acetylcholine at the synapse after an impulse.

encephalitis,viral.name: encephalitis , viral
encephalitis,viral.definition: Viral encephalitis is inflammation of brain parenchymal tissue as a result of viral infection. Encephalitis may occur as primary or secondary manifestation of togaviridae infections; herpesviridae infections; adenoviridae infections; flaviviridae infections; bunyaviridae infections; picornaviridae infections; paramyxoviridae infections; orthomyxoviridae infections; retroviridae infections; and arenaviridae infections.

fertilityagents,male.name: fertility agents , male
fertilityagents,male.definition: Male fertility agents is compounds which increase the capacity of the male to induce conception.

medicalwriting.name: medical writing
medicalwriting.definition: Medical writing is the practice of writing usually by a skilled or specialized writer focused on the reporting or dissemination of medical information for a target audience.

cellmigrationassays,leukocyte.name: cell migration assays , leukocyte
cellmigrationassays,leukocyte.definition: Leukocyte cell migration assays is assays that measure the rate of migration of leukocytes. They may involve a variety of techniques such as measuring the movement of leukocytes through substrates such as agarose gels or the rate of exit of cells from a glass capillary.

multiplepulmonarynodules.name: multiple pulmonary nodules
multiplepulmonarynodules.definition: Multiple pulmonary nodules is a number of small lung lesions characterized by small round masses of 2- to 3-mm in diameter. They are usually detected by chest ct scans (computed tomography, x-ray). Such nodules can be associated with metastases of malignancies inside or outside the lung, benign granulomas, or other lesions.

historicalgeographiclocations.name: historical geographic locations
historicalgeographiclocations.definition: Historical geographic locations is countries known in remote history (as byzantium) or former names of countries reflecting political changes in the 19th or 20th century (as germany, east).

birthcertificates.name: birth certificates
birthcertificates.definition: Birth certificates is official certifications by a physician recording the individual's birth date, place of birth, parentage and other required identifying data which are filed with the local registrar of vital statistics.

yindeficiency.name: yin deficiency
yindeficiency.definition: Yin deficiency is in the yin-yang system of philosophy and medicine, an insufficiency of body fluid (called yinxu), manifesting often as irritability, thirst, constipation, etc. (The Pinyin Chinese-English Dictionary, 1979).

unitedstatesfederaltradecommission.name: united states federal trade commission
unitedstatesfederaltradecommission.definition: United states federal trade commission is an independent administrative agency concerned with maintaining competitive free enterprise by prohibiting unfair methods of competition and unfair deceptive acts or practices.

lewisacids.name: lewis acids
lewisacids.definition: Lewis acids is any chemical species which accepts an [MASK]-pair from a [MASK] in a chemical bonding reaction.

informationservices.name: information services
informationservices.definition: Information services is organized services to provide information on any questions an individual might have using databases and other sources. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

molerats.name: mole rats
molerats.definition: Mole rats is any of several burrowing rodents of the families muridae and Bathyergidae, found in eastern Europe, Africa, and Asia. They have short limbs, small eyes with permanently closed lids, and no tail. Three genera spalax (Muridae), Heterocephalus (Bathyergidae) and Cryptomys (Bathyergidae) are used frequently as experimental animals in biomedical research. (From Walker's Mammals of the World, 6th ed)

sensitivitytraininggroups.name: sensitivity training groups
sensitivitytraininggroups.definition: Sensitivity training groups is a group of people who meet in an unstructured setting to learn about themselves, interpersonal relationships, and group processes and about larger social systems.

abdominalinjuries.name: abdominal injuries
abdominalinjuries.definition: Abdominal injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving organs in the abdominal cavity.

uganda.name: uganda
uganda.definition: Uganda is a republic in eastern Africa, south of sudan and west of kenya. Its capital is Kampala.

terminalrepeatsequences.name: terminal repeat sequences
terminalrepeatsequences.definition: Terminal repeat sequences is nucleotide sequences repeated on both the 5' and 3' ends of a sequence under consideration. For example, the hallmarks of a transposon are that it is flanked by inverted repeats on each end and the inverted repeats are flanked by direct repeats. The Delta element of Ty retrotransposons and LTRs (long terminal repeats) are examples of this concept.

chemistry,physical.name: chemistry , physical
chemistry,physical.definition: Physical chemistry is the study of chemical phenomena and processes in terms of the underlying physical phenomena and processes.

unitedstatesofficeofeconomicopportunity.name: united states office of economic opportunity
unitedstatesofficeofeconomicopportunity.definition: United states office of economic opportunity is a division of the Executive Branch of the United States government concerned with overall planning, promoting, and administering programs relative to the provision of opportunities for economic advancement.

vascularendothelialgrowthfactors.name: vascular endothelial growth factors
vascularendothelialgrowthfactors.definition: Vascular endothelial growth factors is a family of angiogenic proteins that are closely-related to vascular endothelial growth factor a. They play an important role in the growth and differentiation of vascular as well as lymphatic endothelial cells.

encephalitisvirus,california.name: encephalitis virus , california
encephalitisvirus,california.definition: California encephalitis virus is a species in the orthobunyavirus genus of the family bunyaviridae. Serotypes are found in temperate and arctic regions and each is closely associated with a single species of vector mosquito. The vertebrate hosts are usually small mammals but several serotypes infect humans.

ketamine.name: ketamine
ketamine.definition: Ketamine is a cyclohexanone derivative used for induction of anesthesia. Its mechanism of action is not well understood, but ketamine can block nmda receptors (receptors, n-methyl-d-aspartate) and may interact with sigma receptors.

models,anatomic.name: models , anatomic
models,anatomic.definition: Anatomic models is three-dimensional representation to show anatomic structures. Models may be used in place of intact animals or organisms for teaching, practice, and study.

carotidartery,external.name: carotid artery , external
carotidartery,external.definition: External carotid artery is branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the exterior of the head, the face, and the greater part of the [MASK].

asia,central.name: asia , central
asia,central.definition: Central asia is the geographical area of Asia comprising kazakhstan; kyrgyzstan; tajikistan; turkmenistan; and uzbekistan. The desert region of Kara Kum (Qara Qum) is largely in Turkmenistan and the desert region of Kyzyl Kum (Kizil Kum or Qizil Qum), is in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p233, 590, 636)

caspase6.name: caspase 6
caspase6.definition: Caspase 6 is a short pro-domain caspase that plays an effector role in apoptosis. It is activated by initiator caspases such as caspase 7; caspase 8; and caspase 10. Isoforms of this protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its messenger rna.

clinicallaboratoryinformationsystems.name: clinical laboratory information systems
clinicallaboratoryinformationsystems.definition: Clinical laboratory information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative and clinical activities associated with the provision and utilization of clinical laboratory services.

eyeinfections.name: eye infections
eyeinfections.definition: Eye infections is infection, moderate to severe, caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses, which occurs either on the external surface of the eye or intraocularly with probable inflammation, visual impairment, or blindness.

logic.name: logic
logic.definition: Logic is the science that investigates the principles governing correct or reliable inference and deals with the canons and criteria of validity in thought and demonstration. This system of reasoning is applicable to any branch of knowledge or study. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed & Sippl, Computer Dictionary, 4th ed)

patientcomfort.name: patient comfort
patientcomfort.definition: Patient comfort is patient care intended to prevent or relieve suffering in conditions that ensure optimal quality living.

radiationmonitoring.name: radiation monitoring
radiationmonitoring.definition: Radiation monitoring is the [MASK], either continuously or at intervals, of the levels of radiation in a given area, generally for the purpose of assuring that they have not exceeded prescribed amounts or, in case of radiation already present in the area, assuring that the levels have returned to those meeting acceptable safety standards.

phosphorus.name: phosphorus
phosphorus.definition: Phosphorus is a non-metal element that has the atomic symbol p, atomic number 15, and atomic weight 31. It is an essential element that takes part in a broad variety of biochemical reactions.

dnapolymerasebeta.name: dna polymerase beta
dnapolymerasebeta.definition: Dna polymerase beta is a dna repair enzyme that catalyzes dna synthesis during base excision dna repair.

aorticrupture.name: aortic rupture
aorticrupture.definition: Aortic rupture is the tearing or bursting of the wall along any portion of the aorta, such as thoracic or abdominal. It may result from the rupture of an aneurysm or it may be due to trauma.

middleearventilation.name: middle ear ventilation
middleearventilation.definition: [MASK] ventilation is ventilation of the [MASK] in the treatment of secretory (serous) otitis media, usually by placement of tubes or grommets which pierce the tympanic membrane.

cholesterol,dietary.name: cholesterol , dietary
cholesterol,dietary.definition: Dietary cholesterol is cholesterol present in food, especially in animal products.

ataxia.name: ataxia
ataxia.definition: Ataxia is impairment of the ability to perform smoothly coordinated voluntary movements. This condition may affect the limbs, trunk, eyes, pharynx, larynx, and other structures. Ataxia may result from impaired sensory or motor function. Sensory ataxia may result from posterior column injury or peripheral nerve diseases. Motor ataxia may be associated with cerebellar diseases; cerebral cortex diseases; thalamic diseases; basal ganglia diseases; injury to the red nucleus; and other conditions.

pulmonaryvalvestenosis.name: pulmonary valve stenosis
pulmonaryvalvestenosis.definition: Pulmonary valve stenosis is the pathologic narrowing of the orifice of the pulmonary valve. This lesion restricts blood outflow from the right ventricle to the [MASK]. When the trileaflet valve is fused into an imperforate membrane, the blockage is complete.

efhandmotifs.name: ef hand motifs
efhandmotifs.definition: Ef hand motifs is calcium-binding motifs composed of two helices (e and f) joined by a loop. Calcium is bound by the loop region. These motifs are found in many proteins that are regulated by calcium.

thyroiddiseases.name: thyroid diseases
thyroiddiseases.definition: Thyroid diseases is pathological processes involving the thyroid gland.

endometriosis.name: endometriosis
endometriosis.definition: Endometriosis is a condition in which functional endometrial tissue is present outside the uterus. It is often confined to the pelvis involving the ovary, the ligaments, cul-de-sac, and the uterovesical peritoneum.

airtravel.name: air travel
airtravel.definition: Air travel is travel by means of an airplane, helicopter, or balloon.

cytoskeleton.name: cytoskeleton
cytoskeleton.definition: Cytoskeleton is the network of filaments, tubules, and interconnecting filamentous bridges which give shape, structure, and organization to the cytoplasm.

solitaryfibroustumors.name: solitary fibrous tumors
solitaryfibroustumors.definition: Solitary fibrous tumors is rare neoplasms of mesenchymal origin, usually benign, and most commonly involving the pleura (see solitary fibrous tumor, pleural). They also are found in extrapleural sites.

giantviruses.name: giant viruses
giantviruses.definition: Giant viruses is dna viruses that have genomes up to several megabases in length and infect primarily single-celled eukaryotes.

urinespecimencollection.name: urine specimen collection
urinespecimencollection.definition: Urine specimen collection is methods or procedures used to obtain samples of urine.

individualbehavior.name: individual behavior
individualbehavior.definition: Individual behavior is the response of an individual to its environment.

infantdeath.name: infant death
infantdeath.definition: Infant death is the death of a live-born infant within its first year of life.

transitionalcare.name: transitional care
transitionalcare.definition: Transitional care is health care provided during a transition to a different mode of care (e.g., transition to adult care).

biotechnology.name: biotechnology
biotechnology.definition: Biotechnology is body of knowledge related to the use of organisms, cells or cell-derived constituents for the purpose of developing products which are technically, scientifically and clinically useful. Alteration of biologic function at the molecular level (i.e., genetic engineering) is a central focus; laboratory methods used include transfection and cloning technologies, sequence and structure analysis algorithms, computer databases, and gene and protein structure function analysis and prediction.

music.name: music
music.definition: Music is sound that expresses emotion through rhythm, melody, and harmony.

generalization,stimulus.name: generalization , stimulus
generalization,stimulus.definition: Stimulus generalization is the tendency to react to stimuli that are different from, but somewhat similar to, the stimulus used as a conditioned stimulus.

monitoring,intraoperative.name: monitoring , intraoperative
monitoring,intraoperative.definition: Intraoperative monitoring is the constant checking on the state or condition of a patient during the course of a surgical operation (e.g., checking of vital signs).

intracranialarterialdiseases.name: intracranial arterial diseases
intracranialarterialdiseases.definition: Intracranial arterial diseases is pathological conditions involving arteries in the skull, such as arteries supplying the cerebrum, the cerebellum, the brain stem, and associated structures. They include atherosclerotic, congenital, traumatic, infectious, inflammatory, and other pathological processes.

coronarydisease.name: coronary disease
coronarydisease.definition: Coronary disease is an imbalance between myocardial functional requirements and the capacity of the coronary vessels to supply sufficient blood flow. It is a form of myocardial ischemia (insufficient blood supply to the heart muscle) caused by a decreased capacity of the coronary vessels.

footdiseases.name: foot diseases
footdiseases.definition: [MASK] diseases is anatomical and functional disorders affecting the [MASK].

stress,psychological.name: stress , psychological
stress,psychological.definition: Psychological stress is stress wherein emotional factors predominate.

communitypharmacyservices.name: community pharmacy services
communitypharmacyservices.definition: Community pharmacy services is total pharmaceutical services provided to the public through community pharmacies.

obstetricnursing.name: obstetric nursing
obstetricnursing.definition: Obstetric nursing is a nursing specialty involving nursing care given to the pregnant patient before, after, or during childbirth.

ambulatorysurgicalprocedures.name: ambulatory surgical procedures
ambulatorysurgicalprocedures.definition: Ambulatory surgical procedures is surgery performed on an outpatient basis. It may be hospital-based or performed in an office or surgicenter.

acceptanceandcommitmenttherapy.name: acceptance and commitment therapy
acceptanceandcommitmenttherapy.definition: Acceptance and commitment therapy is contextually focused form of cognitive behavioral psychotherapy that uses mindfulness and behavioral activation to increase patients' psychological flexibility in areas such as ability to engage in values-based, positive behaviors while experiencing difficult thoughts, emotions, or sensations.

toothbleaching.name: tooth bleaching
toothbleaching.definition: Tooth bleaching is the use of a chemical oxidizing agent to whiten teeth. In some procedures the oxidation process is activated by the use of heat or light.

angioplasty,laser.name: angioplasty , laser
angioplasty,laser.definition: Laser angioplasty is a technique utilizing a laser coupled to a catheter which is used in the dilatation of occluded blood vessels. This includes laser thermal angioplasty where the laser energy heats up a metal tip, and direct laser angioplasty where the laser energy directly ablates the occlusion. One form of the latter approach uses an excimer laser which creates microscopically precise cuts without thermal injury. When laser angioplasty is performed in combination with balloon angioplasty it is called laser-assisted balloon angioplasty (angioplasty, balloon, laser-assisted).

depression.name: depression
depression.definition: Depression is depressive states usually of moderate intensity in contrast with major depression present in neurotic and psychotic disorders.

vitamink.name: vitamin k
vitamink.definition: Vitamin k is a lipid cofactor that is required for normal blood clotting. Several forms of vitamin k have been identified: [MASK] ([MASK]) derived from plants, vitamin k 2 (menaquinone) from bacteria, and synthetic naphthoquinone provitamins, [MASK] ([MASK]). [MASK] provitamins, after being alkylated in vivo, exhibit the antifibrinolytic activity of vitamin k. Green leafy vegetables, liver, cheese, butter, and [MASK] are good sources of vitamin k.

chestwalloscillation.name: chest wall oscillation
chestwalloscillation.definition: Chest wall oscillation is a respiratory support system used to remove mucus and clear airway by oscillating pressure on the chest.

receptors,naturalcytotoxicitytriggering.name: receptors , natural cytotoxicity triggering
receptors,naturalcytotoxicitytriggering.definition: Natural cytotoxicity triggering receptors is a subclass of natural killer cell receptors that perform an important role in the recognition of tumor cells by nk cells.

fibrintissueadhesive.name: fibrin tissue adhesive
fibrintissueadhesive.definition: Fibrin tissue adhesive is an autologous or commercial tissue adhesive containing fibrinogen and thrombin. The commercial product is a two component system from human plasma that contains more than fibrinogen and thrombin. The first component contains highly concentrated fibrinogen, factor viii, fibronectin, and traces of other plasma proteins. The second component contains thrombin, calcium chloride, and antifibrinolytic agents such as aprotinin. Mixing of the two components promotes blood clotting and the formation and cross-linking of fibrin. The tissue adhesive is used for tissue sealing, hemostasis, and wound healing.

palliativemedicine.name: palliative medicine
palliativemedicine.definition: Palliative medicine is a branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

3'flankingregion.name: 3 ' flanking region
3'flankingregion.definition: 3' flanking region is The region of DNA which borders the 3' end of a transcription unit and where a variety of regulatory sequences are located.

dentalenamelpermeability.name: dental enamel permeability
dentalenamelpermeability.definition: Dental enamel permeability is the property of dental enamel to permit passage of light, heat, gases, liquids, metabolites, mineral ions and other substances. It does not include the penetration of the dental enamel by microorganisms.

epithelium.name: epithelium
epithelium.definition: Epithelium is the layers of epithelial cells which cover the inner and outer surfaces of the cutaneous, mucus, and serous tissues and glands of the body.

anesthesia,caudal.name: anesthesia , caudal
anesthesia,caudal.definition: Caudal anesthesia is epidural anesthesia administered via the sacral canal.

leukemia.name: leukemia
leukemia.definition: Leukemia is a progressive, malignant disease of the blood-forming organs, characterized by distorted proliferation and development of leukocytes and their precursors in the blood and bone marrow. Leukemias were originally termed acute or chronic based on [MASK] but now are classified according to cellular maturity. Acute leukemias consist of predominately immature cells; chronic leukemias are composed of more mature cells. (From The Merck Manual, 2006)

monkeydiseases.name: monkey diseases
monkeydiseases.definition: Monkey diseases is diseases of Old World and New World monkeys. This term includes diseases of baboons but not of chimpanzees or gorillas (= ape diseases).

molecularmedicine.name: molecular medicine
molecularmedicine.definition: Molecular medicine is the field of medicine concerned with understanding the biochemical basis of health and disease and involved in developing diagnostic and therapeutic methods that utilize molecular biology techniques.

hivantigens.name: hiv antigens
hivantigens.definition: Hiv antigens is antigens associated with specific proteins of the human adult T-cell immunodeficiency virus (hiv); also called HTLV-III-associated and lymphadenopathy-associated virus (lav) antigens.

zincisotopes.name: zinc isotopes
zincisotopes.definition: Zinc isotopes is stable zinc atoms that have the same atomic number as the element zinc, but differ in atomic weight. Zn-66-68, and 70 are stable zinc isotopes.

weightreductionprograms.name: weight reduction programs
weightreductionprograms.definition: Weight reduction programs is services providing counseling and activities that help overweight individuals to attain a more healthy body weight.

electrophoresis.name: electrophoresis
electrophoresis.definition: Electrophoresis is an electrochemical process in which macromolecules or colloidal particles with a net electric charge migrate in a solution under the influence of an electric current.

calciumcarbonate.name: calcium carbonate
calciumcarbonate.definition: Calcium carbonate is carbonic acid calcium [MASK] (CaCO3). An odorless, tasteless powder or crystal that occurs in nature. It is used therapeutically as a phosphate [MASK] in hemodialysis patients and as a calcium supplement.

centralnervoussystemfungalinfections.name: central nervous system fungal infections
centralnervoussystemfungalinfections.definition: Central nervous system fungal infections is mycoses of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges which may result in encephalitis; meningitis, fungal; myelitis; brain abscess; and epidural abscess. Certain types of fungi may produce disease in immunologically normal hosts, while others are classified as opportunistic pathogens, causing illness primarily in immunocompromised individuals (e.g., acquired immunodeficiency syndrome).

humanrights.name: human rights
humanrights.definition: Human rights is the right of the individual to cultural, social, economic, and educational opportunities as provided by society, e.g., right to work, right to education, and right to social security.

languagetherapy.name: language therapy
languagetherapy.definition: Language therapy is rehabilitation of persons with language disorders or training of children with language development disorders.

skindiseases,parasitic.name: skin diseases , parasitic
skindiseases,parasitic.definition: Parasitic skin diseases is skin diseases caused by arthropods; helminths; or other parasites.

centralnervoussystemsensitization.name: central nervous system sensitization
centralnervoussystemsensitization.definition: Central nervous system sensitization is an increased response to stimulation that is mediated by amplification of signaling in the central nervous system (cns).

massachusetts.name: massachusetts
massachusetts.definition: Massachusetts is state bounded on the north by New Hampshire and Vermont, on the east by the Atlantic Ocean, on the south by Connecticut and Rhode Island, and on the west by New York.

fishproteins,dietary.name: fish proteins , dietary
fishproteins,dietary.definition: Dietary fish proteins is dietary protein from fish.

sodiumbicarbonate.name: sodium bicarbonate
sodiumbicarbonate.definition: Sodium bicarbonate is a [MASK], crystalline powder that is commonly used as a pH buffering agent, an electrolyte replenisher, systemic alkalizer and in topical cleansing solutions.

bloodculture.name: blood culture
bloodculture.definition: Blood culture is test to determine the presence of blood infection (e.g. sepsis; bacteremia).

painthreshold.name: pain threshold
painthreshold.definition: Pain threshold is amount of stimulation required before the sensation of pain is experienced.

musculoskeletalsystem.name: musculoskeletal system
musculoskeletalsystem.definition: Musculoskeletal system is the muscles, bones (bone and bones), and cartilage of the body.

nerveregeneration.name: nerve regeneration
nerveregeneration.definition: Nerve regeneration is renewal or physiological repair of damaged nerve tissue.

methylchloride.name: methyl chloride
methylchloride.definition: Methyl chloride is a hydrocarbon used as an industrial solvent. It has been used as an aerosal propellent, as a refrigerant and as a local anesthetic. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 31st ed, p1403)

bloodchemicalanalysis.name: blood chemical analysis
bloodchemicalanalysis.definition: Blood chemical analysis is an examination of chemicals in the blood.

minimallyinvasivesurgicalprocedures.name: minimally invasive surgical procedures
minimallyinvasivesurgicalprocedures.definition: Minimally invasive surgical procedures is procedures that avoid use of open, invasive surgery in favor of closed or local surgery. These generally involve use of laparoscopic devices and remote-controlled manipulation of instruments with indirect [MASK] of the surgical field through an endoscope or similar device.

therapeutictouch.name: therapeutic touch
therapeutictouch.definition: Therapeutic touch is placing of the hands of the healer upon the person to be cured with the intent of spiritual energetic healing.

repressorproteins.name: repressor proteins
repressorproteins.definition: Repressor proteins is proteins which maintain the transcriptional quiescence of specific genes or operons. Classical repressor proteins are DNA-binding proteins that are normally bound to the operator region of an operon, or the enhancer sequences of a gene until a signal occurs that causes their release.

remsleepbehaviordisorder.name: rem sleep behavior disorder
remsleepbehaviordisorder.definition: Rem sleep behavior disorder is a disorder characterized by episodes of vigorous and often violent motor activity during rem sleep (sleep, rem). The affected individual may inflict self injury or harm others, and is difficult to awaken from this condition. Episodes are usually followed by a vivid recollection of a dream that is consistent with the aggressive behavior. This condition primarily affects adult males. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p393)

bodyconstitution.name: body constitution
bodyconstitution.definition: Body constitution is the physical characteristics of the body, including the mode of performance of functions, the activity of metabolic processes, the manner and degree of reactions to stimuli, and power of resistance to the attack of pathogenic organisms.

spatiallearning.name: spatial learning
spatiallearning.definition: Spatial learning is a process through which individuals encode information about their environmental cues to facilitate [MASK].

progesteronereductase.name: progesterone reductase
progesteronereductase.definition: Progesterone reductase is an enzyme that catalyzes the reduction of a 3 beta-hydroxy-delta(5)-steroid to 3-oxo-delta(4)-steroid in the presence of nad. It converts pregnenolone to progesterone and dehydroepiandrosterone to androstenedione. ec 1.1.1.145.

legbones.name: leg bones
legbones.definition: Leg bones is the bones of the free part of the lower extremity in humans and of any of the four extremities in animals. It includes the patella; tibia; and fibula.

humans.name: humans
humans.definition: Humans is members of the species Homo sapiens.

forensictoxicology.name: forensic toxicology
forensictoxicology.definition: Forensic toxicology is the application of toxicology knowledge to questions of law.

tuberculosis,ocular.name: tuberculosis , ocular
tuberculosis,ocular.definition: Ocular tuberculosis is tuberculous infection of the eye, primarily the iris, [MASK], and choroid.

dietarysupplements.name: dietary supplements
dietarysupplements.definition: Dietary supplements is products in capsule, tablet or liquid form that provide dietary ingredients, and that are intended to be taken by mouth to increase the intake of nutrients.  Dietary supplements can include macronutrients, such as proteins, carbohydrates, and fats; and/or micronutrients, such as vitamins; minerals; and phytochemicals.

conservativetreatment.name: conservative treatment
conservativetreatment.definition: Conservative treatment is therapeutic approaches that are limited, gradual, or well-established as opposed to radical methods.

chemicalindustry.name: chemical industry
chemicalindustry.definition: Chemical industry is the aggregate enterprise of manufacturing and technically producing chemicals. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

vestibularnerve.name: vestibular nerve
vestibularnerve.definition: Vestibular nerve is the vestibular part of the 8th cranial nerve (vestibulocochlear nerve). The vestibular nerve fibers arise from neurons of Scarpa's ganglion and project peripherally to [MASK] and centrally to the vestibular nuclei of the brain stem. These fibers mediate the sense of balance and head position.

map.name: map
map.definition: Map is works consisting of representations, normally to scale and on a flat medium, of a selection of material or [MASK] features on the surface of the earth. They may be used also in delineating the heavens and celestial bodies. (From Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules, 2d ed, p619)

reagentstrips.name: reagent strips
reagentstrips.definition: Reagent strips is narrow pieces of material impregnated or covered with a substance used to produce a chemical reaction. The strips are used in detecting, measuring, producing, etc., other substances. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

sequencehomology.name: sequence homology
sequencehomology.definition: Sequence homology is the degree of similarity between sequences. Studies of amino acid sequence homology and [MASK] provide useful information about the genetic relatedness of genes, gene products, and species.

hemorrhagicdisorders.name: hemorrhagic disorders
hemorrhagicdisorders.definition: Hemorrhagic disorders is spontaneous or near spontaneous bleeding caused by a defect in clotting mechanisms (blood coagulation disorders) or another abnormality causing a structural flaw in the blood vessels (hemostatic disorders).

genes,dominant.name: genes , dominant
genes,dominant.definition: Dominant genes is genes that influence the phenotype both in the homozygous and the heterozygous state.

decisionsupporttechniques.name: decision support techniques
decisionsupporttechniques.definition: Decision support techniques is mathematical or statistical procedures used as aids in making a decision. They are frequently used in medical decision-making.

aorticvalve.name: aortic valve
aorticvalve.definition: Aortic valve is the valve between the left ventricle and the ascending aorta which prevents backflow into the left ventricle.

actingout.name: acting out
actingout.definition: Acting out is expressing [MASK] emotional [MASK] or feelings, often of hostility or love, through overt behavior.

organsatrisk.name: organs at risk
organsatrisk.definition: Organs at risk is organs which might be damaged during exposure to a toxin or to some form of therapy. It most frequently refers to healthy organs located in the radiation field during radiation therapy.

collagentypevii.name: collagen type vii
collagentypevii.definition: Collagen type vii is a non-fibrillar collagen involved in anchoring the epidermal basement membrane to underlying tissue. It is a homotrimer comprised of C-terminal and N-terminal globular domains connected by a central triple-helical region.

tightjunctions.name: tight junctions
tightjunctions.definition: Tight junctions is cell-cell junctions that seal adjacent epithelial cells together, preventing the passage of most dissolved molecules from one side of the epithelial sheet to the other. (Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2nd ed, p22)

informatics.name: informatics
informatics.definition: Informatics is the field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of data through the application of computers.

riskfactors.name: risk factors
riskfactors.definition: Risk factors is an aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

medicationerrors.name: medication errors
medicationerrors.definition: Medication errors is errors in prescribing, dispensing, or administering medication with the result that the patient fails to receive the correct drug or the indicated proper drug dosage.

folliclestimulatinghormone.name: follicle stimulating hormone
folliclestimulatinghormone.definition: Follicle stimulating hormone is a major gonadotropin secreted by the adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). Follicle-stimulating hormone stimulates gametogenesis and the supporting cells such as the ovarian granulosa cells, the testicular sertoli cells, and leydig cells. fsh consists of two noncovalently linked subunits, alpha and beta. Within a species, the alpha subunit is common in the three pituitary glycoprotein hormones (tsh, lh, and fsh), but the beta subunit is unique and confers its biological specificity.

toothinjuries.name: tooth injuries
toothinjuries.definition: Tooth injuries is traumatic or other damage to teeth including fractures (tooth fractures) or displacements (tooth luxation).

orbitalimplants.name: orbital implants
orbitalimplants.definition: Orbital implants is rounded objects made of coral, teflon, or alloplastic polymer and covered with sclera, and which are implanted in the [MASK] following enucleation. An artificial eye (eye, artificial) is usually attached to the anterior of the orbital implant for cosmetic purposes.

teachingmaterials.name: teaching materials
teachingmaterials.definition: Teaching materials is instructional materials used in teaching.

hepatitisbsurfaceantigens.name: hepatitis b surface antigens
hepatitisbsurfaceantigens.definition: Hepatitis b surface antigens is those hepatitis b antigens found on the surface of the Dane particle and on the 20 nm spherical and tubular particles. Several subspecificities of the surface antigen are known. These were formerly called the Australia antigen.

skinulcer.name: skin ulcer
skinulcer.definition: Skin [MASK] is an [MASK] of the skin and underlying tissues.

comprehensivehealthcare.name: comprehensive health care
comprehensivehealthcare.definition: Comprehensive health care is providing for the full range of personal health services for diagnosis, treatment, follow-up and rehabilitation of patients.

digestivesystemsurgicalprocedures.name: digestive system surgical procedures
digestivesystemsurgicalprocedures.definition: Digestive system surgical procedures is surgery performed on the digestive system or its parts.

glioma.name: glioma
glioma.definition: Glioma is benign and malignant central nervous system neoplasms derived from glial cells (i.e., astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymocytes). Astrocytes may give rise to astrocytomas (astrocytoma) or glioblastoma multiforme (see glioblastoma). Oligodendrocytes give rise to oligodendrogliomas (oligodendroglioma) and ependymocytes may undergo transformation to become ependymoma; choroid plexus neoplasms; or [MASK] of the third ventricle. (From Escourolle et al., Manual of Basic Neuropathology, 2nd ed, p21)

syndrome.name: syndrome
syndrome.definition: Syndrome is a characteristic symptom complex.

phenol.name: phenol
phenol.definition: Phenol is an antiseptic and disinfectant aromatic alcohol.

famouspersons.name: famous persons
famouspersons.definition: Famous persons is individuals widely known or recognized.

secondarycare.name: secondary care
secondarycare.definition: Secondary care is specialized healthcare delivered as a follow-up or referral from a primary care provider.

tubulin.name: tubulin
tubulin.definition: Tubulin is a [MASK] subunit protein found in large quantities in mammalian brain. It has also been isolated from sperm flagellum; cilia; and other sources. Structurally, the protein is a dimer with a molecular weight of approximately 120,000 and a sedimentation coefficient of 5.8s. It binds to colchicine; vincristine; and vinblastine.

temporalconcept.name: temporal concept
temporalconcept.definition: Temporal concept is concepts relating to time.

paralysis.name: paralysis
paralysis.definition: Paralysis is a general term most often used to describe severe or complete loss of muscle strength due to motor system disease from the level of the cerebral cortex to the muscle fiber. This term may also occasionally refer to a loss of sensory function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p45)

molecularweight.name: molecular weight
molecularweight.definition: Molecular weight is the sum of the weight of all the atoms in a molecule.

decisionsupportsystems,clinical.name: decision support systems , clinical
decisionsupportsystems,clinical.definition: Clinical decision support systems is computer-based information systems used to integrate clinical and patient information and provide support for decision-making in patient care.

emergencymedicine.name: emergency medicine
emergencymedicine.definition: Emergency medicine is the branch of medicine concerned with the evaluation and initial treatment of urgent and emergent medical problems, such as those caused by accidents, trauma, sudden illness, poisoning, or disasters. Emergency medical care can be provided at the hospital or at sites outside the medical facility.

porcineepidemicdiarrheavirus.name: porcine epidemic diarrhea virus
porcineepidemicdiarrheavirus.definition: Porcine epidemic [MASK] virus is a species of coronavirus causing acute enteritis in swine. Infections have been seen mostly in Europe, where it is endemic, and in China.

magneticresonanceimaging,cine.name: magnetic resonance imaging , cine
magneticresonanceimaging,cine.definition: Cine magnetic resonance imaging is a type of imaging technique used primarily in the field of cardiology. By coordinating the fast gradient-echo mri sequence with retrospective ECG-gating, numerous short time frames evenly spaced in the cardiac cycle are produced. These images are laced together in a cinematic display so that wall motion of the ventricles, valve motion, and blood flow patterns in the heart and great vessels can be visualized.

intrinsicallydisorderedproteins.name: intrinsically disordered proteins
intrinsicallydisorderedproteins.definition: Intrinsically disordered proteins is functional proteins that do not have unique, stable, folded, three-dimensional native structures or that possess non-ordered regions under physiological conditions. They are characterized by extraordinary structural flexibility and plasticity, which enable them to adopt different conformations in response to different stimuli or different interactions.

grouphomes.name: group homes
grouphomes.definition: Group homes is housing for groups of patients, children, or others who need or desire emotional or physical support. They are usually established as planned, single housekeeping units in residential dwellings that provide care and supervision for small groups of residents, who, although unrelated, live together as a family.

clinicalchemistrytests.name: clinical chemistry tests
clinicalchemistrytests.definition: Clinical chemistry tests is laboratory tests demonstrating the presence of physiologically significant substances in the blood, urine, tissue, and body fluids with application to the diagnosis or therapy of disease.

solutecarrierfamily12,member4.name: solute carrier family 12 , member 4
solutecarrierfamily12,member4.definition: Member 4 solute carrier family 12 is k-Cl cotransporter ubiquitously expressed with higher expression levels in erythrocytes of anemia, sickle cell. It mediates active potassium and chloride cotransport across the plasma membrane and contributes to cell volume homeostasis

cellengineering.name: cell engineering
cellengineering.definition: Cell engineering is methods and techniques used to modify or select cells and develop conditions for growing cells for biosynthetic production of molecules ([MASK]), for generation of tissue structures and organs in vitro (tissue engineering), or for other bioengineering research objectives.

angiotensinreceptorantagonists.name: angiotensin receptor antagonists
angiotensinreceptorantagonists.definition: Angiotensin receptor antagonists is agents that antagonize angiotensin receptors. Many drugs in this class specifically target the angiotensin type 1 receptor.

education,nursing,graduate.name: education , nursing , graduate
education,nursing,graduate.definition: Graduate nursing education is those educational activities engaged in by holders of a bachelor's degree in nursing, which are primarily designed to prepare them for entrance into a specific field of nursing, and may lead to board certification or a more advanced degree.

psychology,clinical.name: psychology , clinical
psychology,clinical.definition: Clinical psychology is the branch of psychology concerned with psychological methods of recognizing and treating behavior disorders.

collagentypev.name: collagen type v
collagentypev.definition: Collagen type v is a fibrillar collagen found widely distributed as a minor component in tissues that contain collagen type i and collagen type iii. It is a heterotrimeric molecule composed of alpha1(V), alpha2(V) and alpha3(V) subunits. Several forms of collagen type v exist depending upon the composition of the subunits that form the trimer.

placecells.name: place cells
placecells.definition: Place cells is pyramidal neurons in the hippocampus that play a role in cognitive representation of a specific location within a space.

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.definition: Architecture is works on the art and science of designing buildings and structures, design of the total built environment, including town planning, urban design, and landscape architecture.

hypertrophy.name: hypertrophy
hypertrophy.definition: Hypertrophy is general increase in bulk of a part or organ due to cell enlargement and accumulation of fluids and secretions, not due to tumor formation, nor to an increase in the number of cells (hyperplasia).

greenchemistrytechnology.name: green chemistry technology
greenchemistrytechnology.definition: Green chemistry technology is pollution prevention through the design of effective chemical products that have low or no toxicity and use of chemical processes that reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.

psychiatricdepartment,hospital.name: psychiatric department , hospital
psychiatricdepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital psychiatric department is hospital department responsible for the organization and administration of psychiatric services.

cysticfibrosis.name: cystic fibrosis
cysticfibrosis.definition: Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive genetic disease of the exocrine glands. It is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator expressed in several organs including the lung, the pancreas, the biliary system, and the sweat glands. Cystic fibrosis is characterized by epithelial secretory dysfunction associated with ductal obstruction resulting in airway obstruction; chronic respiratory infections; pancreatic insufficiency; maldigestion; [MASK] depletion; and heat prostration.

lenses,intraocular.name: lenses , intraocular
lenses,intraocular.definition: Intraocular lenses is artificial implanted lenses.

gallbladder.name: gallbladder
gallbladder.definition: Gallbladder is a storage reservoir for [MASK] secretion. Gallbladder allows the delivery of [MASK] acids at a high concentration and in a controlled manner, via the cystic duct to the duodenum, for degradation of dietary lipid.

engineering.name: engineering
