engineering.definition: Engineering is the practical application of physical, mechanical, and mathematical principles. (Stedman, 25th ed)

oils.name: oils
oils.definition: Oils is unctuous combustible substances that are liquid or easily liquefiable on warming, and are soluble in ether but insoluble in water. Such substances, depending on their origin, are classified as animal, mineral, or vegetable oils. Depending on their behavior on [MASK], they are volatile or fixed. (Dorland, 28th ed)

ultrasonography.name: ultrasonography
ultrasonography.definition: Ultrasonography is the visualization of deep structures of the body by recording the reflections or echoes of ultrasonic pulses directed into the tissues. Use of ultrasound for imaging or diagnostic purposes employs frequencies ranging from 1.6 to 10 megahertz.

fatbody.name: fat body
fatbody.definition: Fat body is a nutritional reservoir of fatty tissue found mainly in insects and amphibians.

legislation,pharmacy.name: legislation , pharmacy
legislation,pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of pharmacy, proposed for enactment or enacted by a legislative body.

rehabilitation,vocational.name: rehabilitation , vocational
rehabilitation,vocational.definition: Vocational rehabilitation is training of the mentally or physically disabled in work skills so they may be returned to regular employment utilizing these skills.

fatigue.name: fatigue
fatigue.definition: Fatigue is the state of weariness following a period of exertion, mental or physical, characterized by a decreased capacity for work and reduced efficiency to respond to stimuli.

glucoseoxidase.name: glucose oxidase
glucoseoxidase.definition: Glucose oxidase is an enzyme of the oxidoreductase class that catalyzes the conversion of beta-D-glucose and oxygen to D-glucono-1,5-lactone and peroxide. It is a flavoprotein, highly specific for beta-D-glucose. The enzyme is produced by Penicillium notatum and other fungi and has antibacterial activity in the presence of glucose and oxygen. It is used to estimate glucose concentration in blood or urine samples through the formation of colored dyes by the hydrogen peroxide produced in the reaction. (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992) ec 1.1.3.4.

aged.name: aged
aged.definition: Aged is a person 65 through 79 years of age. For a person older than 79 years, aged, 80 and over is available.

models,statistical.name: models , statistical
models,statistical.definition: Statistical models is statistical formulations or analyses which, when applied to data and found to fit the data, are then used to verify the assumptions and parameters used in the analysis. Examples of statistical models are the linear model, binomial model, polynomial model, two-parameter model, etc.

emergencyresponders.name: emergency responders
emergencyresponders.definition: Emergency responders is personnel trained to provide the initial services, care, and support in emergencies or disasters.

arteries.name: arteries
arteries.definition: Arteries is the vessels carrying blood away from the heart.

tastethreshold.name: taste threshold
tastethreshold.definition: Taste threshold is the minimum concentration at which taste sensitivity to a particular substance or food can be perceived.

puberty,delayed.name: puberty , delayed
puberty,delayed.definition: Delayed puberty is the lack of development of sexual maturation in boys and girls at a chronological age that is 2.5 standard deviations above the mean age at onset of puberty in a population. Delayed puberty can be classified by defects in the hypothalamic lhrh pulse generator, the pituitary gland, or the gonads. These patients will undergo spontaneous but delayed puberty whereas patients with sexual infantilism will not.

veterinaryservice,military.name: veterinary service , military
veterinaryservice,military.definition: Military veterinary service is a corps of the armed services concerned with animal medicine, the chief interest of which is the care of government-owned working dogs (as in the military [MASK] units), working horses (as in state funerals), and working military dolphins (as in undersea exploration and other activities). In the United States Army Veterinary Corps animal medicine overlaps and interconnects with biomedical research using laboratory research animals. a related activity is laboratory animal care. The Corps provides limited care for privately owned animals of military personnel through non-appropriated funds. Military service veterinarians in the United States Army must be graduates of accredited veterinary schools and must have a state license. (Telephone communication with Lt. Col. William Inskeep ii, u.s. Army Veterinary Corps, October 4, 1994)

antibodydiversity.name: antibody diversity
antibodydiversity.definition: Antibody diversity is the phenomenon of immense variability characteristic of antibodies. It enables the immune system to react specifically against the essentially unlimited kinds of antigens it encounters. Antibody diversity is accounted for by three main theories: (1) the Germ Line Theory, which holds that each antibody-producing cell has genes coding for all possible antibody specificities, but expresses only the one stimulated by antigen; (2) the Somatic Mutation Theory, which holds that antibody-producing cells contain only a few genes, which produce antibody diversity by mutation; and (3) the Gene Rearrangement Theory, which holds that antibody diversity is generated by the rearrangement of immunoglobulin variable region gene segments during the differentiation of the antibody-producing cells.

anticipation,genetic.name: anticipation , genetic
anticipation,genetic.definition: Genetic anticipation is the apparent tendency of certain diseases to appear at earlier age of onset and with increasing severity in successive generations. (Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

medianneuropathy.name: median neuropathy
medianneuropathy.definition: Median neuropathy is disease involving the median nerve, from its origin at the brachial plexus to its termination in the hand. Clinical features include weakness of wrist and finger flexion, forearm pronation, thenar abduction, and loss of sensation over the lateral palm, first three fingers, and radial half of the ring finger. Common sites of injury include the elbow, where the nerve passes through the two heads of the pronator teres muscle (pronator syndrome) and in the carpal tunnel (carpal tunnel syndrome).

cellculturetechniques.name: cell culture techniques
cellculturetechniques.definition: Cell culture techniques is methods for maintaining or growing cells in vitro.

esophagus.name: esophagus
esophagus.definition: Esophagus is the muscular membranous segment between the pharynx and the stomach in the upper gastrointestinal tract.

antioxidants.name: antioxidants
antioxidants.definition: Antioxidants is naturally occurring or synthetic substances that inhibit or retard oxidation reactions. They counteract the damaging effects of oxidation in animal tissues.

mentalfatigue.name: mental fatigue
mentalfatigue.definition: Mental fatigue is a condition of low alertness or cognitive impairment, usually associated with prolonged mental activities or stress.

heparincofactorii.name: heparin cofactor ii
heparincofactorii.definition: Heparin cofactor ii is a sulfated plasma protein with a mw of approximately 66kDa that resembles antithrombin iii. The protein is an inhibitor of thrombin in plasma and is activated by dermatan sulfate or heparin. It is a member of the serpin superfamily.

handinjuries.name: hand injuries
handinjuries.definition: Hand injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the hand.

diagnostictechniques,endocrine.name: diagnostic techniques , endocrine
diagnostictechniques,endocrine.definition: Endocrine diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases or dysfunction of the endocrine glands or demonstration of their physiological processes.

socialparticipation.name: social participation
socialparticipation.definition: Social participation is involvement in community activities or programs.

socialbehaviordisorders.name: social behavior disorders
socialbehaviordisorders.definition: Social behavior disorders is behaviors which are at variance with the expected social norm and which affect other individuals.

pain,postoperative.name: pain , postoperative
pain,postoperative.definition: Postoperative pain is pain during the period after surgery.

streptococcuspneumoniae.name: streptococcus pneumoniae
streptococcuspneumoniae.definition: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a gram-positive organism found in the upper respiratory tract, inflammatory exudates, and various body fluids of normal and/or diseased humans and, rarely, domestic animals.

pneumococcalinfections.name: pneumococcal infections
pneumococcalinfections.definition: Pneumococcal infections is infections with bacteria of the species streptococcus pneumoniae.

waterpollution,chemical.name: water pollution , chemical
waterpollution,chemical.definition: Chemical water pollution is adverse effect upon bodies of water ([MASK]; [MASK]; seas; groundwater etc.) caused by chemical water pollutants.

librarytechnicalservices.name: library technical services
librarytechnicalservices.definition: Library technical services is acquisition, organization, and preparation of library materials for use, including selection, weeding, cataloging, classification, and preservation.

hepaticveins.name: hepatic veins
hepaticveins.definition: Hepatic veins is veins which drain the liver.

lactation.name: lactation
lactation.definition: Lactation is the processes of milk secretion by the maternal mammary glands after parturition. The proliferation of the mammary glandular tissue, milk synthesis, and milk expulsion or [MASK] down are regulated by the interactions of several hormones including estradiol; progesterone; prolactin; and oxytocin.

ultrasonicsurgicalprocedures.name: ultrasonic surgical procedures
ultrasonicsurgicalprocedures.definition: Ultrasonic surgical procedures is the use of high-energy shock waves, in the frequency range of 20-60 kHz, to cut through or remove tissue. The tissue fragmentation by ultrasonic surgical instruments is caused by mechanical effects not heat as with high-intensity focused ultrasound ablation.

tobaccomosaicvirus.name: tobacco mosaic virus
tobaccomosaicvirus.definition: Tobacco mosaic virus is the type species of tobamovirus which causes mosaic disease of tobacco. Transmission occurs by mechanical inoculation.

plasminogenactivators.name: plasminogen activators
plasminogenactivators.definition: Plasminogen activators is a heterogeneous group of proteolytic enzymes that convert plasminogen to fibrinolysin. They are concentrated in the lysosomes of most cells and in the vascular endothelium, particularly in the vessels of the microcirculation.

musclestrength.name: muscle strength
musclestrength.definition: Muscle strength is the amount of force generated by muscle contraction. Muscle strength can be measured during isometric, isotonic, or isokinetic contraction, either manually or using a device such as a muscle strength dynamometer.

nutritiondisorders.name: nutrition disorders
nutritiondisorders.definition: Nutrition disorders is disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition.

hospitalrapidresponseteam.name: hospital rapid response team
hospitalrapidresponseteam.definition: Hospital rapid response team is multidisciplinary team most frequently consisting of intensive care unit trained personnel who are available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week for evaluation of patients who develop signs or symptoms of severe clinical deterioration.

chromosomewalking.name: chromosome walking
chromosomewalking.definition: Chromosome walking is a technique with which an unknown region of a chromosome can be explored. It is generally used to isolate a locus of interest for which no probe is available but that is known to be linked to a gene which has been identified and cloned. a fragment containing a known gene is selected and used as a probe to identify other overlapping fragments which contain the same gene. The nucleotide sequences of these fragments can then be characterized. This process continues for the length of the chromosome.

carcinoma,squamouscell.name: carcinoma , squamous cell
carcinoma,squamouscell.definition: Squamous cell carcinoma is a carcinoma derived from stratified squamous epithelial cells. It may also occur in sites where glandular or columnar epithelium is normally present. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

uterineartery.name: uterine artery
uterineartery.definition: Uterine artery is a branch arising from the internal iliac artery in females, that supplies blood to the uterus.

sexratio.name: sex ratio
sexratio.definition: [MASK] ratio is the number of males per 100 females.

urology.name: urology
urology.definition: Urology is a surgical specialty concerned with the study, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases of the urinary tract in both sexes, and the genital tract in the male. Common urological problems include urinary obstruction, urinary incontinence, infections, and urogenital neoplasms.

organdysfunctionscores.name: organ dysfunction scores
organdysfunctionscores.definition: Organ dysfunction scores is ratings that express in numerical values the degree of impairment or abnormality in the function of specific organs.

abdominalfat.name: abdominal fat
abdominalfat.definition: Abdominal fat is fatty tissue in the region of the abdomen. It includes the abdominal subcutaneous fat and the intra-abdominal fat.

neuralcrest.name: neural crest
neuralcrest.definition: Neural crest is the two longitudinal ridges along the primitive streak appearing near the end of gastrulation during development of nervous system (neurulation). The ridges are formed by folding of neural plate. Between the ridges is a neural groove which deepens as the fold become elevated. When the folds meet at midline, the groove becomes a closed tube, the neural tube.

diseasetransmission,infectious.name: disease transmission , infectious
diseasetransmission,infectious.definition: Infectious disease transmission is the transmission of infectious disease or pathogens. When transmission is within the same species, the mode can be horizontal or vertical (infectious disease transmission, vertical).

infantnutritiondisorders.name: infant nutrition disorders
infantnutritiondisorders.definition: Infant nutrition disorders is disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, occurring in infants ages 1 month to 24 months.

trees.name: trees
trees.definition: Trees is woody, usually tall, perennial higher plants (Angiosperms, Gymnosperms, and some Pterophyta) having usually a main stem and numerous branches.

microsatelliterepeats.name: microsatellite repeats
microsatelliterepeats.definition: Microsatellite repeats is a variety of simple repeat sequences that are distributed throughout the genome. They are characterized by a short repeat unit of 2-8 basepairs that is repeated up to 100 times. They are also known as short tandem repeats (STRs).

internationalagencies.name: international agencies
internationalagencies.definition: International agencies is international organizations which provide health-related or other cooperative services.

dentalprosthesisretention.name: dental prosthesis retention
dentalprosthesisretention.definition: Dental prosthesis retention is holding a dental prosthesis in place by its design, or by the use of additional devices or adhesives.

calciumsignaling.name: calcium signaling
calciumsignaling.definition: Calcium signaling is signal transduction mechanisms whereby calcium mobilization (from outside the cell or from intracellular storage pools) to the cytoplasm is triggered by external stimuli. Calcium signals are often seen to propagate as waves, oscillations, spikes, sparks, or puffs. The calcium acts as an intracellular messenger by activating calcium-responsive proteins.

diseasesintwins.name: diseases in twins
diseasesintwins.definition: Diseases in twins is disorders affecting twins, one or both, at any age.

geneticengineering.name: genetic engineering
geneticengineering.definition: Genetic engineering is directed modification of the gene complement of a living organism by such techniques as altering the dna, substituting genetic material by means of a virus, transplanting whole nuclei, transplanting cell hybrids, etc.

cattlediseases.name: cattle diseases
cattlediseases.definition: Cattle diseases is diseases of domestic cattle of the genus Bos. It includes diseases of cows, yaks, and zebus.

dataanalysis.name: data analysis
dataanalysis.definition: Data analysis is process of systematically applying statistical and/or logical techniques to describe and illustrate, condense and recap, and evaluate data (https://ori.hhs.gov/education).

influenza,human.name: influenza , human
influenza,human.definition: Human influenza is an acute viral infection in humans involving the respiratory tract. It is marked by inflammation of the nasal mucosa; the pharynx; and conjunctiva, and by headache and severe, often generalized, myalgia.

plantpathology.name: plant pathology
plantpathology.definition: Plant pathology is the study of infectious diseases associated with plants.

bodymassindex.name: body mass index
bodymassindex.definition: Body mass index is an indicator of body density as determined by the relationship of body weight to body height. BMI=weight (kg)/height squared (m2). bmi correlates with body fat (adipose tissue). Their relationship varies with age and gender. For adults, bmi falls into these categories: below 18.5 (underweight); 18.5-24.9 (normal); 25.0-29.9 (overweight); 30.0 and above (obese). (National Center for Health Statistics, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)

micrornas.name: micrornas
micrornas.definition: Micrornas is small double-stranded, non-protein coding RNAs, 21-25 nucleotides in length generated from single-stranded microRNA gene transcripts by the same ribonuclease iii, Dicer, that produces small interfering RNAs (rna, small interfering). They become part of the rna-induced silencing complex and repress the translation (translation, genetic) of target rna by binding to homologous 3'utr region as an imperfect match. The small temporal RNAs (stRNAs), [MASK]-7 and lin-4, from c. elegans, are the first 2 miRNAs discovered, and are from a class of miRNAs involved in developmental timing.

growthdifferentiationfactor3.name: growth differentiation factor 3
growthdifferentiationfactor3.definition: Growth differentiation factor 3 is a growth differentiation factor that may play a role in maintaining the undifferentiated state of pluripotent stem cells by inhibiting the actions of bone morphogenetic proteins. Differentiation factor 3 is also considered a nodal signaling ligand that influences the genesis of left-right asymmetry.

polyps.name: polyps
polyps.definition: Polyps is discrete abnormal tissue masses that protrude into the lumen of the digestive tract or the respiratory tract. Polyps can be spheroidal, hemispheroidal, or irregular mound-shaped structures attached to the mucous membrane of the lumen wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or by a broad base.

bonemarrowfailuredisorders.name: bone marrow failure disorders
bonemarrowfailuredisorders.definition: Bone marrow failure disorders is inherited or acquired diseases characterized by insufficient and/or dysplastic blood cells.

costsharing.name: cost sharing
costsharing.definition: Cost sharing is provisions of an insurance policy that require the insured to pay some portion of covered expenses. Several forms of sharing are in use, e.g., deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. Cost sharing does not refer to or include amounts paid in premiums for the coverage. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

tissuebanks.name: tissue banks
tissuebanks.definition: Tissue banks is centers for acquiring, characterizing, and storing organs or tissue for future use.

fruitproteins.name: fruit proteins
fruitproteins.definition: Fruit proteins is proteins found in fruit.

bedoccupancy.name: bed occupancy
bedoccupancy.definition: Bed occupancy is a measure of inpatient health facility use based upon the average number or proportion of beds occupied for a given period of time.

sweetsyndrome.name: sweet syndrome
sweetsyndrome.definition: Sweet syndrome is condition characterized by large, rapidly extending, erythematous, tender plaques on the upper body usually accompanied by fever and dermal infiltration of neutrophilic leukocytes. It occurs mostly in middle-aged women, is often preceded by an upper respiratory infection, and clinically resembles erythema multiforme. Sweet syndrome is associated with leukemia.

personalnarrativesastopic.name: personal narratives as topic
personalnarrativesastopic.definition: Personal narratives as topic is works about accounts of individual experience in relation to a particular field or of participation in related activities.

endocrineglands.name: endocrine glands
endocrineglands.definition: Endocrine glands is ductless glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood circulation. These hormones influence the metabolism and other functions of cells in the body.

sustainabledevelopment.name: sustainable development
sustainabledevelopment.definition: Sustainable development is a process of change in which the exploitation of resources, the direction of investments, the orientation of technological development; and institutional change are all in harmony and enhance both current and future potential to meet human needs and aspirations. (http://www.un-documents.net/ocf-02.htm#I)

diagnosis.name: diagnosis
diagnosis.definition: Diagnosis is the determination of the nature of a disease or condition, or the distinguishing of one disease or condition from another. Assessment may be made through physical examination, laboratory tests, or the likes. Computerized programs may be used to enhance the decision-making process.

etsmotif.name: ets motif
etsmotif.definition: Ets motif is a helix-turn-helix motif characterized by three alpha-helices and four-stranded beta-sheets arranged in the order alpha1-beta1-beta2-alpha2-alpha3-beta3-beta4. The third alpha-helix contacts the major groove of dna. The ets motif and the flanking amino acid sequences of Ets proteins influence the binding affinity, and the alteration of a single amino acid in the Ets domain can change its dna binding specificity.

americanhospitalassociation.name: american hospital association
americanhospitalassociation.definition: American hospital association is a professional society in the United States whose membership is composed of hospitals.

penicillinresistance.name: penicillin resistance
penicillinresistance.definition: Penicillin resistance is nonsusceptibility of an organism to the action of penicillins.

elements,radioactive.name: elements , radioactive
elements,radioactive.definition: Radioactive elements is unstable elements with atomic numbers greater than 83 that exist in nature solely as radioisotopes.

anions.name: anions
anions.definition: Anions is negatively charged atoms, radicals or groups of atoms which travel to the anode or positive pole during electrolysis.

caribbeanregion.name: caribbean region
caribbeanregion.definition: Caribbean region is the area that lies between continental North and South America and comprises the Caribbean Sea, the West Indies, and the adjacent mainland regions of southern [MASK], Central America, [MASK], and Venezuela.

corebindingfactors.name: core binding factors
corebindingfactors.definition: Core binding factors is heterodimeric transcription factors containing a DNA-binding alpha subunits, (core binding factor alpha subunits), along with a non-DNA-binding beta subunits, core binding factor beta subunit. Core Binding Factor regulates genetic transcription of a variety of genes involved primarily in cell differentiation and cell cycle progression.

superoxidedismutase.name: superoxide dismutase
superoxidedismutase.definition: Superoxide dismutase is an oxidoreductase that catalyzes the reaction between superoxides and hydrogen to yield molecular oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. The enzyme protects the cell against dangerous levels of superoxide.

immunesystem.name: immune system
immunesystem.definition: Immune system is the body's defense mechanism against foreign organisms or substances and deviant native cells. It includes the humoral immune response and the cell-mediated response and consists of a complex of interrelated cellular, molecular, and genetic components.

biomass.name: biomass
biomass.definition: Biomass is total mass of all the organisms of a given type and/or in a given area. (From Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990) It includes the yield of vegetative mass produced from any given crop.

socioeconomicfactors.name: socioeconomic factors
socioeconomicfactors.definition: Socioeconomic factors is social and economic factors that characterize the individual or group within the social structure.

dust.name: dust
dust.definition: Dust is earth or other matter in fine, dry particles. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

bodyfatdistribution.name: body fat distribution
bodyfatdistribution.definition: Body fat distribution is deposits of adipose tissue throughout the body. The pattern of fat deposits in the body regions is an indicator of health status. Excess abdominal fat increases health risks more than excess fat around the hips or [MASK], therefore, waist-hip ratio is often used to determine health risks.

drugevaluation,preclinical.name: drug evaluation , preclinical
drugevaluation,preclinical.definition: Preclinical drug evaluation is preclinical testing of drugs in experimental animals or in vitro for their biological and toxic effects and potential clinical applications.

reinforcement,psychology.name: reinforcement , psychology
reinforcement,psychology.definition: Psychology reinforcement is the strengthening of a conditioned response.

dnadegradation,necrotic.name: dna degradation , necrotic
dnadegradation,necrotic.definition: Necrotic dna degradation is the random catabolism of dna accompanying the irreversible damage to tissue which leads to the pathological death of one or more cells.

clinicaltrialsastopic.name: clinical trials as topic
clinicaltrialsastopic.definition: Clinical trials as topic is works about pre-planned studies of the safety, efficacy, or optimum dosage schedule (if appropriate) of one or more diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques selected according to predetermined criteria of eligibility and observed for predefined evidence of favorable and unfavorable effects. This concept includes clinical trials conducted both in the u.s. and in other countries.

analgesia,epidural.name: analgesia , epidural
analgesia,epidural.definition: Epidural analgesia is the relief of pain without loss of consciousness through the introduction of an analgesic agent into the [MASK] of the vertebral canal. It is differentiated from anesthesia, epidural which refers to the state of insensitivity to sensation.

geneknockouttechniques.name: gene knockout techniques
geneknockouttechniques.definition: Gene knockout techniques is techniques to alter a gene sequence that result in an inactivated gene, or one in which the expression can be inactivated at a chosen time during development to study the loss of function of a gene.

weapons.name: weapons
weapons.definition: Weapons is devices or tools used in combat or fighting in order to kill or incapacitate.

retinaldetachment.name: retinal detachment
retinaldetachment.definition: Retinal detachment is separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium. Retinal detachment occurs more commonly in men than in women, in eyes with degenerative myopia, in aging and in aphakia. It may occur after an uncomplicated [MASK] extraction, but it is seen more often if [MASK] has been lost during surgery. (Dorland, 27th ed; Newell, Ophthalmology: Principles and Concepts, 7th ed, p310-12).

screentime.name: screen time
screentime.definition: Screen time is period of activities done in front of an electronic screen, such as watching tv, working on a computer, or playing [MASK].

computers.name: computers
computers.definition: Computers is programmable electronic devices designed to accept data, perform prescribed mathematical and logical operations at high speed, and display the results of these operations.

oncogenicviruses.name: oncogenic viruses
oncogenicviruses.definition: Oncogenic viruses is viruses that produce tumors.

nursing,team.name: nursing , team
nursing,team.definition: Team nursing is coordination of nursing services by various nursing care personnel under the [MASK] of a professional nurse. The team may consist of a professional nurse, nurses' aides, and the practical nurse.

anteriorwallmyocardialinfarction.name: anterior wall myocardial infarction
anteriorwallmyocardialinfarction.definition: Anterior wall myocardial infarction is myocardial infarction in which the anterior wall of the heart is involved. Anterior wall myocardial infarction is often caused by occlusion of the left anterior descending coronary artery. It can be categorized as anteroseptal or anterolateral wall myocardial infarction.

poultryproteins.name: poultry proteins
poultryproteins.definition: Poultry proteins is dietary proteins from poultry.

anticipation,psychological.name: anticipation , psychological
anticipation,psychological.definition: Psychological anticipation is the ability to foresee what is likely to happen on the basis of past experience. It is largely a frontal lobe function.

dentalclinics.name: dental clinics
dentalclinics.definition: Dental clinics is facilities where dental care is provided to patients.

hormones.name: hormones
hormones.definition: Hormones is chemical substances having a specific regulatory effect on the activity of a certain organ or organs. The term was originally applied to substances secreted by various endocrine glands and transported in the bloodstream to the target organs. It is sometimes extended to include those substances that are not produced by the endocrine glands but that have similar effects.

lowerbodynegativepressure.name: lower body negative pressure
lowerbodynegativepressure.definition: Lower body negative pressure is external decompression applied to the lower body. It is used to study orthostatic intolerance and the effects of gravitation and [MASK], to produce simulated hemorrhage in physiologic research, to assess cardiovascular function, and to reduce abdominal stress during childbirth.

integrativemedicine.name: integrative medicine
integrativemedicine.definition: Integrative medicine is the discipline concerned with using the combination of conventional allopathic medicine and alternative medicine to address the biological, psychological, social, and spiritual aspects of health and illness.

lifesupportsystems.name: life support systems
lifesupportsystems.definition: Life support systems is systems that provide all or most of the items necessary for maintaining life and health. Provisions are made for the supplying of oxygen, food, water, temperature and pressure control, disposition of carbon dioxide and body waste. The milieu may be a spacecraft, a submarine, or the surface of the moon. In medical care, usually under hospital conditions, life support care is available. (From Webster's New Collegiate Dictionary)

hearingdisorders.name: hearing disorders
hearingdisorders.definition: Hearing disorders is conditions that impair the transmission of auditory impulses and information from the level of the ear to the temporal cortices, including the sensorineural pathways.

gait.name: gait
gait.definition: Gait is manner or style of walking.

homologousrecombination.name: homologous recombination
homologousrecombination.definition: Homologous recombination is an exchange of dna between matching or similar sequences.

ankle.name: ankle
ankle.definition: Ankle is the region of the lower limb between the [MASK] and the leg.

serineproteases.name: serine proteases
serineproteases.definition: Serine proteases is peptide hydrolases that contain at the [MASK] a serine residue involved in catalysis.

mice,mutantstrains.name: mice , mutant strains
mice,mutantstrains.definition: Mutant strains mice is mice bearing mutant genes which are phenotypically expressed in the animals.

capillaries.name: capillaries
capillaries.definition: Capillaries is the minute vessels that connect arterioles and venules.

cohortstudies.name: cohort studies
cohortstudies.definition: Cohort studies is studies in which subsets of a defined population are identified. These groups may or may not be exposed to factors hypothesized to influence the probability of the occurrence of a particular disease or other outcome. Cohorts are defined populations which, as a whole, are followed in an attempt to determine distinguishing subgroup characteristics.

receptors,collagen.name: receptors , collagen
receptors,collagen.definition: Collagen receptors is cell surface receptors that modulate signal transduction between cells and the extracellular matrix. They are found in many cell types and are involved in the maintenance and regulation of cell shape and behavior, including platelet activation and aggregation, through many different signaling pathways and differences in their affinities for collagen isoforms. Collagen receptors include discoidin domain receptors; integrins; and gp6, one of the platelet membrane glycoproteins.

organicchemical.name: organic chemical
organicchemical.definition: Organic chemical is a broad class of substances containing carbon and its derivatives. Many of these chemicals will frequently contain hydrogen with or without oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, phosphorus, and other elements. They exist in either carbon chain or carbon ring form.

chromatography,highpressureliquid.name: chromatography , high pressure liquid
chromatography,highpressureliquid.definition: High pressure liquid chromatography is liquid chromatographic techniques which feature high inlet pressures, high sensitivity, and high speed.

knowledge.name: knowledge
knowledge.definition: Knowledge is the body of truths or facts accumulated in the course of time, the cumulated sum of information, its volume and nature, in any civilization, period, or country.

cellline,transformed.name: cell line , transformed
cellline,transformed.definition: Transformed cell line is eukaryotic cell line obtained in a quiescent or stationary phase which undergoes conversion to a state of unregulated growth in culture, resembling an in vitro tumor. It occurs spontaneously or through interaction with viruses, oncogenes, radiation, or drugs/chemicals.

jointcapsule.name: joint capsule
jointcapsule.definition: Joint capsule is the sac enclosing a joint. It is composed of an outer fibrous articular capsule and an inner synovial membrane.

septalnuclei.name: septal nuclei
septalnuclei.definition: Septal nuclei is neural nuclei situated in the septal region. They have afferent and cholinergic efferent connections with a variety of forebrain and brain stem areas including the hippocampal formation, the lateral hypothalamus, the tegmentum, and the amygdala. Included are the dorsal, lateral, medial, and triangular septal nuclei, septofimbrial nucleus, nucleus of diagonal band, nucleus of anterior commissure, and the nucleus of stria terminalis.

abortion,veterinary.name: abortion , veterinary
abortion,veterinary.definition: Veterinary abortion is premature expulsion of the fetus in animals.

musculoskeletalphysiologicalphenomena.name: musculoskeletal physiological phenomena
musculoskeletalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Musculoskeletal physiological phenomena is processes and properties of the musculoskeletal system.

rats,wistar.name: rats , wistar
rats,wistar.definition: Wistar rats is a strain of albino rat developed at the Wistar Institute that has spread widely at other institutions. This has markedly diluted the original strain.

remoteconsultation.name: remote consultation
remoteconsultation.definition: Remote consultation is consultation via remote telecommunications, generally for the purpose of diagnosis or treatment of a patient at a site remote from the patient or primary physician.

sexualhealth.name: sexual health
sexualhealth.definition: Sexual health is a state of physical, emotional, mental and social well-being in relation to sexuality, according to the [MASK] Organization.

fetus.name: fetus
fetus.definition: Fetus is the unborn young of a viviparous mammal, in the postembryonic period, after the major structures have been outlined. In humans, the unborn young from the end of the eighth week after conception until birth, as distinguished from the earlier embryo, mammalian.

intermittentrenalreplacementtherapy.name: intermittent renal replacement therapy
intermittentrenalreplacementtherapy.definition: Intermittent renal replacement therapy is procedures with non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration and/or perfusion) via vascular access by increasing blood flow rate compared to continuous rrt.

medline.name: medline
medline.definition: Medline is the premier bibliographic [MASK] of the national library of medicine. medline® (medlars Online) is the primary subset of pubmed and can be searched on NLM's Web site in PubMed or the nlm Gateway. medline references are indexed with medical subject headings (MeSH).

torsionabnormality.name: torsion abnormality
torsionabnormality.definition: Torsion abnormality is an abnormal twisting or [MASK] of a bodily part or member on its axis.

humandevelopment.name: human development
humandevelopment.definition: Human development is continuous sequential changes which occur in the physiological and psychological functions during the life-time of an individual.

urinarybladderneckobstruction.name: urinary bladder neck obstruction
urinarybladderneckobstruction.definition: [MASK] [MASK] obstruction is blocked urine flow through the [MASK] [MASK], the narrow internal urethral opening at the base of the [MASK]. Narrowing or strictures of the urethra can be congenital or acquired. It is often observed in males with enlarged prostate glands.

liverxreceptors.name: liver x receptors
liverxreceptors.definition: Liver x receptors is nuclear receptors that bind oxysterols and function as heterodimers with retinoid x receptors. They have important functions in regulating cholesterol homeostasis, energy metabolism; inflammation; and the immune response.

emergencynursing.name: emergency nursing
emergencynursing.definition: Emergency nursing is the specialty or practice of nursing in the care of patients admitted to the emergency department.

elements.name: elements
elements.definition: Elements is substances that comprise all matter. Each element is made up of atoms that are identical in number of [MASK] and protons and in nuclear charge, but may differ in mass or number of neutrons.

hyperplasia.name: hyperplasia
hyperplasia.definition: Hyperplasia is an increase in the number of cells in a tissue or organ without tumor formation. It differs from hypertrophy, which is an increase in bulk without an increase in the number of cells.

neoplasm,residual.name: neoplasm , residual
neoplasm,residual.definition: Residual neoplasm is remnant of a tumor or cancer after primary, potentially curative therapy.

deviceapproval.name: device approval
deviceapproval.definition: Device approval is process that is gone through in order for a device to receive approval by a government regulatory agency. This includes any required preclinical or clinical testing, review, submission, and evaluation of the applications and test results, and post-marketing surveillance. It is not restricted to fda.

westernaustralia.name: western australia
westernaustralia.definition: Western australia is a state in western Australia. Its capital is Perth. It was first visited by the Dutch in 1616 but the English took possession in 1791 and permanent colonization began in 1829. It was a penal settlement 1850-1888, became part of the colonial government in 1886, and was granted self government in 1890. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1329)

safety.name: safety
safety.definition: Safety is freedom from exposure to danger and protection from the occurrence or risk of injury or loss. It suggests optimal precautions in the workplace, on the street, in the home, etc., and includes personal safety as well as the safety of property.

secondaryprevention.name: secondary prevention
secondaryprevention.definition: Secondary prevention is the prevention of recurrences or exacerbations of a disease or complications of its therapy.

legislation,medical.name: legislation , medical
legislation,medical.definition: Medical legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of medicine, proposed for enactment or enacted by a legislative body.

welding.name: welding
welding.definition: Welding is joining metal pieces or parts together by melting the adjoining surfaces with heat, using a heat source such as a blowtorch or electric arc. The melted surfaces are then pressed together by hammering.

medicallaboratorypersonnel.name: medical laboratory personnel
medicallaboratorypersonnel.definition: Medical laboratory personnel is health care professionals, technicians, and assistants staffing laboratories in research or health care facilities.

seedbank.name: seed bank
seedbank.definition: [MASK] bank is a repository of [MASK] maintained under optimal conditions that ensure long term storage, intended for use as a source of replenishment of [MASK] stock or plant genetic material.

hematologictests.name: hematologic tests
hematologictests.definition: Hematologic tests is tests used in the analysis of the hemic system.

disease.name: disease
disease.definition: Disease is a definite pathologic process with a characteristic [MASK] of signs and symptoms. It may affect the whole body or any of its parts, and its etiology, pathology, and prognosis may be known or unknown.

plateletfactor3.name: platelet factor 3
plateletfactor3.definition: Platelet factor 3 is a [MASK] from the platelet membrane that contributes to the blood clotting cascade by forming a [MASK]-protein complex (thromboplastin) which serves as a cofactor with factor viia to activate factor x in the extrinsic pathway of blood coagulation.

postmortemchanges.name: postmortem changes
postmortemchanges.definition: Postmortem changes is physiological changes that occur in bodies after death.

leadpoisoning.name: lead poisoning
leadpoisoning.definition: Lead poisoning is poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, [MASK], or skin absorption of lead or lead compounds.

ribosomesubunits,small,eukaryotic.name: ribosome subunits , small , eukaryotic
ribosomesubunits,small,eukaryotic.definition: Eukaryotic small ribosome subunits is the small subunit of the 80s ribosome of eukaryotes. It is composed of the 18s [MASK] and 32 different ribosomal proteins.

endoplasmicreticulum,smooth.name: endoplasmic reticulum , smooth
endoplasmicreticulum,smooth.definition: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is a type of endoplasmic reticulum lacking associated ribosomes on the membrane surface. It exhibits a wide range of specialized metabolic functions including supplying enzymes for steroid synthesis, detoxification, and glycogen breakdown. In muscle cells, smooth endoplasmic reticulum is called sarcoplasmic reticulum.

stressfibers.name: stress fibers
stressfibers.definition: Stress fibers is bundles of actin filaments (actin cytoskeleton) and myosin-II that span across the cell attaching to the cell membrane at focal adhesions and to the network of [MASK] that surrounds the nucleus.

dairyproducts.name: dairy products
dairyproducts.definition: Dairy products is raw and processed or manufactured milk and milk-derived products. These are usually from cows (bovine) but are also from goats, sheep, reindeer, and water buffalo.

meteorologicalconcepts.name: meteorological concepts
meteorologicalconcepts.definition: Meteorological concepts is the atmospheric properties, characteristics and other atmospheric phenomena especially pertaining to weather or climate.

healthcaresector.name: health care sector
healthcaresector.definition: Health care sector is economic sector concerned with the provision, distribution, and consumption of health care services and related products.

costsandcostanalysis.name: costs and cost analysis
costsandcostanalysis.definition: Costs and cost analysis is absolute, comparative, or differential costs pertaining to services, institutions, resources, etc., or the analysis and study of these costs.

receptors,tumornecrosisfactor.name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor
receptors,tumornecrosisfactor.definition: Tumor necrosis factor receptors is cell surface receptors that bind tumor necrosis factors and trigger changes which influence the behavior of cells.

roundligamentofuterus.name: round ligament of uterus
roundligamentofuterus.definition: Round ligament of uterus is a fibromuscular band that attaches to the uterus and then passes along the broad ligament, out through the inguinal ring, and into the labium majus.

nosediseases.name: nose diseases
nosediseases.definition: Nose diseases is disorders of the nose, general or unspecified.

receptor,insulin.name: receptor , insulin
receptor,insulin.definition: Insulin receptor is a cell surface receptor for insulin. It comprises a tetramer of two alpha and two beta subunits which are derived from cleavage of a single precursor protein. The receptor contains an intrinsic tyrosine kinase domain that is located within the beta subunit. Activation of the receptor by insulin results in numerous metabolic changes including increased uptake of glucose into the liver, muscle, and adipose tissue.

bodysize.name: body size
bodysize.definition: Body size is the physical measurements of a body.

pulmonarymedicine.name: pulmonary medicine
pulmonarymedicine.definition: Pulmonary medicine is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the respiratory system. It is especially concerned with diagnosis and treatment of diseases and defects of the lungs and bronchial tree.

unitedstatessubstanceabuseandmentalhealt.name: united states substance abuse and mental health services administration
unitedstatessubstanceabuseandmentalhealt.definition: United states substance abuse and mental health services administration is an agency of the public health service concerned with the overall planning, promoting, and administering of programs pertaining to substance abuse and mental health. It is commonly referred to by the acronym samhsa. On 1 October 1992, the United States Alcohol, Drug Abuse, and Mental Health Administration (adamha) became samhsa.

sportsnutritionalsciences.name: sports nutritional sciences
sportsnutritionalsciences.definition: Sports nutritional sciences is the study of nutrition processes during exercise and athletic performance as well as specific [MASK] of [MASK] and the relationship between [MASK] and nutrition disorders in [MASK].

arthroplasty.name: arthroplasty
arthroplasty.definition: Arthroplasty is surgical reconstruction of a joint to relieve pain or restore motion.

emergencymedicaldispatch.name: emergency medical dispatch
emergencymedicaldispatch.definition: Emergency medical dispatch is the mobilization of emergency care to the locations and people that need them.

respiratorysinusarrhythmia.name: respiratory sinus arrhythmia
respiratorysinusarrhythmia.definition: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is a naturally occurring variation in heart rate that occurs during a breathing cycle, where the time between heartbeats is shortened during inspiration and prolonged during expiration. It is not the same as sinus arrhythmia, the disorder.

facialnerveinjuries.name: facial nerve injuries
facialnerveinjuries.definition: Facial nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the facial nerve. This may result in [MASK], decreased lacrimation and salivation, and loss of taste sensation in the anterior tongue. The nerve may regenerate and reform its original pattern of innervation, or regenerate aberrantly, resulting in inappropriate lacrimation in response to gustatory stimuli (e.g., "crocodile tears") and other syndromes.

aluminum.name: aluminum
aluminum.definition: Aluminum is a metallic element that has the atomic number 13, atomic symbol Al, and atomic weight 26.98.

publicexpenditures.name: public expenditures
publicexpenditures.definition: Public expenditures is expenses of public funds incurred by government bodies:  state, regional and local.

ascorbicacid.name: ascorbic acid
ascorbicacid.definition: Ascorbic acid is a six carbon compound related to glucose. It is found naturally in citrus fruits and many vegetables. Ascorbic acid is an essential nutrient in human diets, and necessary to maintain connective tissue and bone. Its biologically active form, vitamin c, functions as a reducing agent and coenzyme in several metabolic pathways. Vitamin c is considered an antioxidant.

socialtheory.name: social theory
socialtheory.definition: Social theory is frameworks of empirical evidence used to study and interpret social phenomena.

rna,transfer,val.name: rna , transfer , val
rna,transfer,val.definition: Val transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying valine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

metabolicfluxanalysis.name: metabolic flux analysis
metabolicfluxanalysis.definition: Metabolic flux analysis is measurement of cells' substrate utilization and biosynthetic output for modeling of metabolic networks.

neuromuscularjunctiondiseases.name: neuromuscular junction diseases
neuromuscularjunctiondiseases.definition: Neuromuscular junction diseases is conditions characterized by impaired transmission of impulses at the neuromuscular junction. This may result from disorders that affect receptor function, pre- or postsynaptic membrane function, or acetylcholinesterase activity. The majority of diseases in this category are associated with autoimmune, toxic, or inherited conditions.

sleepaids,pharmaceutical.name: sleep aids , pharmaceutical
sleepaids,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical sleep aids is drugs used to induce sleep, prevent sleeplessness, or treat sleep initiation and maintenance disorders.

molecularprobes.name: molecular probes
molecularprobes.definition: Molecular probes is a group of atoms or molecules attached to other molecules or cellular structures and used in studying the properties of these molecules and structures. Radioactive dna or rna sequences are used in molecular genetics to detect the presence of a complementary sequence by nucleic acid hybridization.

ovarianfunctiontests.name: ovarian function tests
ovarianfunctiontests.definition: Ovarian function tests is methods used for assessment of ovarian function.

fluorescencepolarizationimmunoassay.name: fluorescence polarization immunoassay
fluorescencepolarizationimmunoassay.definition: Fluorescence polarization immunoassay is fluoroimmunoassay where detection of the hapten-antibody reaction is based on measurement of the increased polarization of fluorescence-labeled hapten when it is combined with antibody. The assay is very useful for the measurement of small haptenic antigens such as drugs at low concentrations.

adeninenucleotides.name: adenine nucleotides
adeninenucleotides.definition: Adenine nucleotides is a nucleotide wherein the nucleobase is adenine.

multiplesclerosis.name: multiple sclerosis
multiplesclerosis.definition: Multiple [MASK] is an autoimmune disorder mainly affecting young adults and characterized by destruction of myelin in the central nervous system. Pathologic findings include multiple sharply demarcated areas of demyelination throughout the [MASK] matter of the central nervous system. Clinical manifestations include visual loss, extra-ocular movement disorders, paresthesias, loss of sensation, weakness, dysarthria, spasticity, ataxia, and [MASK] dysfunction. The usual pattern is one of recurrent attacks followed by partial recovery (see multiple [MASK], relapsing-remitting), but acute fulminating and chronic progressive forms (see [MASK]) also occur. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p903)

airmovements.name: air movements
airmovements.definition: Air movements is the motion of air currents.

pelvicinfection.name: pelvic infection
pelvicinfection.definition: Pelvic infection is infection involving the tissues or organs in the pelvis.

immunoglobulind.name: immunoglobulin d
immunoglobulind.definition: Immunoglobulin d is an immunoglobulin which accounts for less than 1% of plasma immunoglobulin. It is found on the membrane of many circulating b lymphocytes.

oxides.name: oxides
oxides.definition: Oxides is binary compounds of oxygen containing the anion o(2-). The anion combines with metals to form alkaline oxides and non-metals to form acidic oxides.

injections,epidural.name: injections , epidural
injections,epidural.definition: Epidural injections is the injection of drugs, most often analgesics, into the spinal canal without puncturing the dura mater.

livercirrhosis.name: liver cirrhosis
livercirrhosis.definition: Liver cirrhosis is liver disease in which the normal microcirculation, the gross vascular anatomy, and the hepatic architecture have been variably destroyed and altered with fibrous septa surrounding regenerated or regenerating parenchymal nodules.

diagnosis,oral.name: diagnosis , oral
diagnosis,oral.definition: Oral diagnosis is examination of the mouth and teeth toward the identification and diagnosis of intraoral disease or manifestation of non-oral conditions.

cholesterol,ldl.name: cholesterol , ldl
cholesterol,ldl.definition: Ldl cholesterol is cholesterol which is contained in or bound to low density lipoproteins (ldl), including cholesterol esters and free cholesterol.

biologicalavailability.name: biological availability
biologicalavailability.definition: Biological availability is the extent to which the active ingredient of a drug dosage form becomes available at the site of drug action or in a biological medium believed to reflect accessibility to a site of action.

childprotectiveservices.name: child protective services
childprotectiveservices.definition: Child protective services is local governmental offices which investigate reports of abuse and neglect of children, and act to assure a safe environment for minors.

pyramidaltracts.name: pyramidal tracts
pyramidaltracts.definition: Pyramidal tracts is fibers that arise from cells within the cerebral cortex, pass through the medullary pyramid, and descend in the spinal cord. Many authorities say the pyramidal tracts include both the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts.

hospitals,county.name: hospitals , county
hospitals,county.definition: County hospitals is hospitals controlled by the county government.

program.name: program
program.definition: Program is works consisting of lists of the events, pieces, performers, speakers, etc., of an entertainment, ceremony, or the like. (From: Genre Terms: a Thesaurus for Use in Rare Book and Special Collections Cataloging, 2d ed)

methanol.name: methanol
methanol.definition: Methanol is a colorless, flammable liquid used in the manufacture of formaldehyde and acetic acid, in chemical synthesis, antifreeze, and as a solvent. Ingestion of methanol is toxic and may cause blindness.

intestinalpolyps.name: intestinal polyps
intestinalpolyps.definition: Intestinal polyps is discrete abnormal tissue masses that protrude into the lumen of the intestine. a polyp is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or by a broad base.

serialpassage.name: serial passage
serialpassage.definition: Serial passage is inoculation of a series of animals or in vitro tissue with an infectious bacterium or virus, as in virulence studies and the development of vaccines.

steroidsynthesisinhibitors.name: steroid synthesis inhibitors
steroidsynthesisinhibitors.definition: Steroid synthesis inhibitors is compounds that bind to and inhibit enzymes involved in the synthesis of steroids.

hepatitis,chronic.name: hepatitis , chronic
hepatitis,chronic.definition: Chronic hepatitis is inflammation of the liver with ongoing hepatocellular injury for 6 months or more, characterized by necrosis of [MASK] and inflammatory cell (leukocytes) infiltration. Chronic hepatitis can be caused by viruses, medications, autoimmune diseases, and other unknown factors.

foodmicrobiology.name: food microbiology
foodmicrobiology.definition: Food microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in food and food products. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms: the presence of various non-pathogenic bacteria and fungi in cheeses and wines, for example, is included in this concept.

brainedema.name: brain edema
brainedema.definition: Brain edema is increased intracellular or extracellular fluid in brain tissue. Cytotoxic brain edema (swelling due to increased intracellular fluid) is indicative of a disturbance in cell metabolism, and is commonly associated with hypoxic or ischemic injuries (see hypoxia, brain). An increase in extracellular fluid may be caused by increased brain capillary permeability (vasogenic edema), an osmotic gradient, local blockages in interstitial fluid pathways, or by obstruction of csf flow (e.g., obstructive hydrocephalus). (From Childs Nerv Syst 1992 Sep; 8(6):301-6)

occipitallobe.name: occipital lobe
occipitallobe.definition: Occipital lobe is posterior portion of the cerebral hemispheres responsible for processing visual sensory information. It is located posterior to the parieto-occipital sulcus and extends to the preoccipital notch.

populationdynamics.name: population dynamics
populationdynamics.definition: Population dynamics is the pattern of any process, or the interrelationship of phenomena, which affects growth or change within a population.

amylnitrite.name: amyl nitrite
amylnitrite.definition: Amyl nitrite is a vasodilator that is administered by [MASK]. It is also used recreationally due to its supposed ability to induce euphoria and act as an aphrodisiac.

mesentericvascularocclusion.name: mesenteric vascular occlusion
mesentericvascularocclusion.definition: Mesenteric vascular occlusion is obstruction of the flow in the splanchnic circulation by atherosclerosis; embolism; thrombosis; stenosis; trauma; and compression or intrinsic pressure from adjacent tumors. Rare causes are drugs, intestinal parasites, and vascular immunoinflammatory diseases such as periarteritis nodosa and thromboangiitis obliterans. (From Juergens et al., Peripheral Vascular Diseases, 5th ed, pp295-6)

informationliteracy.name: information literacy
informationliteracy.definition: Information [MASK] is the ability to recognize when information is needed and to locate, evaluate, and use the needed information effectively.

acetatekinase.name: acetate kinase
acetatekinase.definition: Acetate kinase is an enzyme that catalyzes reversibly the phosphorylation of acetate in the presence of a divalent cation and atp with the formation of acetylphosphate and adp. It is important in the glycolysis process. ec 2.7.2.1.

woundhealing.name: wound healing
woundhealing.definition: Wound healing is restoration of integrity to traumatized tissue.

bladeimplantation.name: blade implantation
bladeimplantation.definition: Blade implantation is insertion of an endosseous implant with a narrow wedge-shaped infrastructure extending through the [MASK] into the mouth and bearing openings or vents through which tissue grows to obtain retention.

hematoxylin.name: hematoxylin
hematoxylin.definition: Hematoxylin is a dye obtained from the heartwood of logwood (Haematoxylon campechianum Linn., Leguminosae) used as a stain in microscopy and in the manufacture of ink.

acutelunginjury.name: acute lung injury
acutelunginjury.definition: Acute lung injury is a condition of lung damage that is characterized by bilateral pulmonary infiltrates ([MASK]) rich in neutrophils, and in the absence of clinical heart failure. This can represent a spectrum of pulmonary lesions, endothelial and epithelial, due to numerous factors (physical, chemical, or biological).

travel.name: travel
travel.definition: Travel is movement across different geographic locations.

genesilencing.name: gene silencing
genesilencing.definition: Gene silencing is interruption or suppression of the expression of a gene at transcriptional or translational levels.

metals,heavy.name: metals , heavy
metals,heavy.definition: Heavy metals is metals with high specific gravity, typically larger than 5. They have complex spectra, form colored [MASK] and double [MASK], have a low electrode potential, are mainly amphoteric, yield weak bases and weak acids, and are oxidizing or reducing agents (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

suddeninfantdeath.name: sudden infant death
suddeninfantdeath.definition: Sudden infant death is the abrupt and unexplained death of an apparently healthy infant under one year of age, remaining unexplained after a thorough case investigation, including performance of a complete autopsy, examination of the death scene, and review of the clinical history. (Pediatr Pathol 1991 Sep-Oct;11(5):677-84)

ocularabsorption.name: ocular absorption
ocularabsorption.definition: Ocular absorption is uptake of substances by tissues of the eye.

drosophilaproteins.name: drosophila proteins
drosophilaproteins.definition: Drosophila proteins is proteins that originate from insect species belonging to the genus drosophila. The proteins from the most intensely studied species of Drosophila, drosophila melanogaster, are the subject of much interest in the area of morphogenesis and development.

manuscripts,medicalastopic.name: manuscripts , medical as topic
manuscripts,medicalastopic.definition: Medical as topic manuscripts is works about unpublished medical works.

thinking.name: thinking
thinking.definition: Thinking is mental activity that is not predominantly perceptual by which one apprehends some aspect of an object or situation based on past learning and experience.

stemcells.name: stem cells
stemcells.definition: Stem cells is relatively undifferentiated cells that retain the ability to divide and proliferate throughout postnatal life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

intracellularmembranes.name: intracellular membranes
intracellularmembranes.definition: Intracellular membranes is thin structures that encapsulate subcellular structures or organelles in eukaryotic cells. They include a variety of membranes associated with the cell nucleus; the mitochondria; the golgi apparatus; the endoplasmic reticulum; lysosomes; plastids; and vacuoles.

leukemia,myeloid,acceleratedphase.name: leukemia , myeloid , accelerated phase
leukemia,myeloid,acceleratedphase.definition: Accelerated phase myeloid leukemia is the phase of chronic myeloid leukemia following the chronic phase (leukemia, myeloid, chronic-phase), where there are increased systemic symptoms, worsening cytopenias, and refractory leukocytosis.

pathologicprocesses.name: pathologic processes
pathologicprocesses.definition: Pathologic processes is the abnormal mechanisms and forms involved in the dysfunctions of tissues and organs.

backpain.name: back pain
backpain.definition: Back pain is acute or chronic pain located in the posterior regions of the thorax; lumbosacral region; or the adjacent regions.

healtheducation.name: health education
healtheducation.definition: Health education is education that increases the awareness and favorably influences the attitudes and knowledge relating to the improvement of health on a personal or community basis.

rashomologenrichedinbrainprotein.name: ras homolog enriched in brain protein
rashomologenrichedinbrainprotein.definition: Ras homolog enriched in brain protein is a GTP-binding protein with low intrinsic GTPase activity that activates mtorc1 protein kinase activity.

weaning.name: weaning
weaning.definition: Weaning is permanent deprivation of [MASK] and commencement of nourishment with other food. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

laborstage,first.name: labor stage , first
laborstage,first.definition: First labor stage is period from the onset of true obstetric labor to the complete dilatation of the cervix uteri.

musclecells.name: muscle cells
musclecells.definition: Muscle cells is mature contractile cells, commonly known as myocytes, that form one of three kinds of muscle. The three types of muscle cells are skeletal (muscle fibers, skeletal), [MASK], cardiac), and smooth (myocytes, smooth muscle). They are derived from embryonic (precursor) muscle cells called myoblasts.

bodywater.name: body water
bodywater.definition: Body water is fluids composed mainly of water found within the body.

vaccines,dna.name: vaccines , dna
vaccines,dna.definition: Dna vaccines is [MASK] vectors encoding antigens administered for the prevention or treatment of disease. The host cells take up the dna, express the antigen, and present it to the immune system in a manner similar to that which would occur during natural infection. This induces humoral and cellular immune responses against the encoded antigens. The vector is called naked dna because there is no need for complex formulations or delivery agents; the plasmid is injected in saline or other [MASK].

proteininteractionmaps.name: protein interaction maps
proteininteractionmaps.definition: Protein interaction maps is graphs representing sets of measurable, non-covalent physical contacts with specific proteins in living organisms or in cells.

intellectualproduct.name: intellectual product
intellectualproduct.definition: Intellectual product is property, such as patents, trademarks, and [MASK], that results from creative effort. The Patent and [MASK] Clause (Art. 1, Sec. 8, cl. 8) of the United States Constitution provides for promoting the progress of science and useful arts by securing for limited times to authors and inventors, the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 5th ed, p1014)

anatomicalstructure.name: anatomical structure
anatomicalstructure.definition: Anatomical structure is any biological entity that occupies space and is distinguished from its surroundings.

brainwaves.name: brain waves
brainwaves.definition: Brain waves is wave-like oscillations of electric potential between parts of the brain recorded by eeg.

grayliterature.name: gray literature
grayliterature.definition: Gray literature is works that include publications such as reports, theses, conference [MASK], translations and limited circulation government documents which are not normally available through commercial publication sources. (lcsh)

mapkinasekinase4.name: map kinase kinase 4
mapkinasekinase4.definition: Map kinase kinase 4 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for jnk mitogen-activated protein kinases; p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases and the retinoid x receptors. It takes part in a signal transduction pathway that is activated in response to cellular stress.

periodontaldiseases.name: periodontal diseases
periodontaldiseases.definition: Periodontal diseases is pathological processes involving the periodontium including the gum (gingiva), the alveolar bone (alveolar process), the dental cementum, and the periodontal ligament.

musclecontraction.name: muscle contraction
musclecontraction.definition: Muscle contraction is a process leading to shortening and/or development of tension in muscle tissue. Muscle contraction occurs by a sliding filament mechanism whereby actin filaments slide inward among the myosin filaments.

greece,ancient.name: greece , ancient
greece,ancient.definition: Ancient greece is a civilization extant from about 1200 bc. to the death of Alexander the Great, in 323 b.c. It extended from the Greek city states to North Africa and eastward to the Indus [MASK].

irisplant.name: iris plant
irisplant.definition: Iris plant is a plant genus of the family iridaceae that contains irip, a type-1 ribosome-inactivating protein, and iridals (triterpenes).

cellbiology.name: cell biology
cellbiology.definition: Cell biology is the study of the structure, behavior, growth, reproduction, and pathology of cells; and the function and chemistry of cellular components.

glaucoma.name: glaucoma
glaucoma.definition: Glaucoma is an ocular disease, occurring in many forms, having as its primary characteristics an unstable or a sustained increase in the intraocular pressure which the eye cannot withstand without damage to its structure or impairment of its function. The consequences of the increased pressure may be manifested in a variety of symptoms, depending upon type and severity, such as excavation of the [MASK], hardness of the eyeball, corneal anesthesia, reduced visual acuity, seeing of colored halos around lights, disturbed dark adaptation, [MASK] defects, and headaches. (Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

corticalbone.name: cortical bone
corticalbone.definition: Cortical bone is a type of osseous tissue which makes up the outer layer of bone. It is dense, rigid, strong, and forms concentric lamellar osteons.

molecularmechanismsofpharmacologicalacti.name: molecular mechanisms of pharmacological action
molecularmechanismsofpharmacologicalacti.definition: Molecular mechanisms of pharmacological action is pharmacological activities at the molecular level of drugs and other exogenous compounds that are used to treat diseases and affect normal biochemistry.

drugindustry.name: drug industry
drugindustry.definition: Drug industry is that segment of commercial enterprise devoted to the design, development, and manufacture of chemical products for use in the diagnosis and treatment of disease, disability, or other dysfunction, or to improve function.

antibodies,blocking.name: antibodies , blocking
antibodies,blocking.definition: Blocking antibodies is antibodies that inhibit the reaction between antigen and other antibodies or sensitized t-lymphocytes (e.g., antibodies of the immunoglobulin g class that compete with ige antibodies for antigen, thereby blocking an allergic response). Blocking antibodies that bind tumors and prevent destruction of tumor cells by cytotoxic t-lymphocytes have also been called enhancing antibodies. (Rosen et al., Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

vascularaccessdevices.name: vascular access devices
vascularaccessdevices.definition: Vascular access devices is devices to be inserted into veins or arteries for the purpose of carrying fluids into or from a peripheral or central vascular location. They may include component parts such as catheters, ports, reservoirs, and valves. They may be left in place temporarily for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

animal.name: animal
animal.definition: Animal is unicellular or multicellular, heterotrophic organisms, that have sensation and the power of voluntary movement. Under the older five kingdom paradigm, Animalia was one of the kingdoms. Under the modern three domain model, Animalia represents one of the many groups in the domain eukaryota.

inhibitoryconcentration50.name: inhibitory concentration 50
inhibitoryconcentration50.definition: Inhibitory concentration 50 is the concentration of a compound needed to reduce population growth of organisms, including eukaryotic cells, by 50% in vitro. Though often expressed to denote in vitro antibacterial activity, it is also used as a benchmark for cytotoxicity to eukaryotic cells in culture.

placenta,retained.name: placenta , retained
placenta,retained.definition: Retained placenta is a placenta that fails to be expelled after birth of the fetus. a placenta is retained when the uterus fails to contract after the delivery of its content, or when the placenta is abnormally attached to the myometrium.

mixedtumor,malignant.name: mixed tumor , malignant
mixedtumor,malignant.definition: Malignant mixed tumor is a malignant tumor composed of more than one type of neoplastic tissue. (Dorland, 27th ed)

neoplasmtransplantation.name: neoplasm transplantation
neoplasmtransplantation.definition: Neoplasm transplantation is experimental transplantation of neoplasms in laboratory animals for research purposes.

accounting.name: accounting
accounting.definition: Accounting is system of recording financial transactions.

gilbertdisease.name: gilbert disease
gilbertdisease.definition: Gilbert disease is a benign familial disorder, transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait. It is characterized by low-grade chronic hyperbilirubinemia with considerable daily fluctuations of the bilirubin level.

crossprotection.name: cross protection
crossprotection.definition: Cross protection is protection conferred on a host by inoculation with one strain or component of a microorganism that prevents infection when later challenged with a similar strain. Most commonly the microorganism is a virus.

mobilitylimitation.name: mobility limitation
mobilitylimitation.definition: Mobility limitation is difficulty in walking from place to place.

plateletfactor4.name: platelet factor 4
plateletfactor4.definition: Platelet factor 4 is a cxc chemokine that is found in the alpha granules of platelets. The protein has a molecular size of 7800 kDa and can occur as a monomer, a dimer or a tetramer depending upon its concentration in solution. Platelet factor 4 has a high affinity for heparin and is often found complexed with glycoproteins such as protein c.

child,hospitalized.name: child , hospitalized
child,hospitalized.definition: Hospitalized child is child hospitalized for short term care.

dnaligaseatp.name: dna ligase atp
dnaligaseatp.definition: Dna ligase atp is aTP-dependent cellular enzyme which catalyzes dna replication, repair and recombination through formation of internucleotide ester bonds between phosphate and deoxyribose moieties. Vertebrate cells encode three well-characterized dna ligases, dna ligase i, iii and iv, all of which are related in structure and sequence. dna ligases either require atp or nad. However, archaebacterial, viral, and some eubacterial dna ligases are ATP-dependent.

laboratories,hospital.name: laboratories , hospital
laboratories,hospital.definition: Hospital laboratories is hospital facilities equipped to carry out investigative procedures.

hepatitis,viral,human.name: hepatitis , viral , human
hepatitis,viral,human.definition: Human viral hepatitis is inflammation of the liver in humans due to infection by viruses. There are several significant types of human viral hepatitis with infection caused by enteric-transmission (hepatitis a; hepatitis e) or blood transfusion (hepatitis b; hepatitis c; and hepatitis d).

socialnetworking.name: social networking
socialnetworking.definition: Social networking is individuals connected by family, work or other interests. It also includes connectivity facilitated by computer-based communications.

nitrogenoxides.name: nitrogen oxides
nitrogenoxides.definition: Nitrogen oxides is inorganic oxides that contain nitrogen.

hemoglobina.name: hemoglobin a
hemoglobina.definition: Hemoglobin a is normal adult human hemoglobin. The globin moiety consists of two alpha and two beta chains.

pneumonia,atypicalinterstitial,ofcattle.name: pneumonia , atypical interstitial , of cattle
pneumonia,atypicalinterstitial,ofcattle.definition: Of cattle atypical interstitial pneumonia is a cattle disease of uncertain cause, probably an allergic reaction.

roundwindow,ear.name: round window , ear
roundwindow,ear.definition: Ear round window is fenestra of the cochlea, an opening in the basal wall between the [MASK] and the [MASK], leading to the cochlea. It is closed by a secondary tympanic membrane.

milieutherapy.name: milieu therapy
milieutherapy.definition: Milieu therapy is a treatment program based on manipulation of the patient's environment by the medical staff. The patient does not participate in planning the treatment regimen.

foods,specialized.name: foods , specialized
foods,specialized.definition: Specialized foods is foods and beverages prepared for use to meet specific needs such as infant foods.

rectalfistula.name: rectal fistula
rectalfistula.definition: Rectal fistula is an abnormal anatomical passage connecting the rectum to the outside, with an orifice at the site of drainage.

adaptorproteincomplex4.name: adaptor protein complex 4
adaptorproteincomplex4.definition: Adaptor protein complex 4 is an adaptor protein complex involved in transport of molecules between the trans-golgi network and the endosomal-lysosomal system.

helicobacter.name: helicobacter
helicobacter.definition: Helicobacter is a genus of gram-negative, spiral-shaped bacteria that has been isolated from the intestinal tract of mammals, including humans. It has been associated with peptic [MASK].

researchdevice.name: research device
researchdevice.definition: Research device is device for research.

extremehotweather.name: extreme hot weather
extremehotweather.definition: Extreme hot weather is a period of unusually high temperatures.

accommodation,ocular.name: accommodation , ocular
accommodation,ocular.definition: Ocular accommodation is the dioptric [MASK] of the eye (to attain maximal sharpness of retinal [MASK] for an object of regard) referring to the ability, to the mechanism, or to the process. Ocular accommodation is the effecting of refractive changes by changes in the shape of the crystalline lens. Loosely, it refers to ocular [MASK] for vision, ocular at various distances. (Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

sexualdevelopment.name: sexual development
sexualdevelopment.definition: Sexual development is the processes of anatomical and physiological changes related to sexual or reproductive functions during the life span of a human or an animal, from fertilization to death. These include [MASK] determination processes; [MASK] differentiation; sexual maturation; and changes during aging.

colorado.name: colorado
colorado.definition: Colorado is state bounded on the north by Wyoming and Nebraska, on the east by Kansas and Nebraska, on the south by New [MASK] and Oklahoma, and on the west by Utah.

governingboard.name: governing board
governingboard.definition: Governing board is the group in which legal authority is vested for the control of health-related institutions and organizations.

chromosomes,human,pair10.name: chromosomes , human , pair 10
chromosomes,human,pair10.definition: Pair 10 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

hivantibodies.name: hiv antibodies
hivantibodies.definition: Hiv antibodies is antibodies reactive with hiv antigens.

termbirth.name: term birth
termbirth.definition: Term birth is childbirth at the end of a normal duration of pregnancy, between 37 to 40 weeks of gestation or about 280 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period.

respiratorytransport.name: respiratory transport
respiratorytransport.definition: Respiratory transport is the processes of diffusion across the blood-air barrier, and the chemical reactions coupled with diffusion that effect the rate of pulmonary gas exchange, generally at the alveolar level.

lidocaine.name: lidocaine
