lidocaine.definition: Lidocaine is a local anesthetic and cardiac depressant used as an antiarrhythmia agent. Its actions are more intense and its effects more prolonged than those of procaine but its duration of action is shorter than that of bupivacaine or prilocaine.

kidneydiseases.name: kidney diseases
kidneydiseases.definition: Kidney diseases is pathological processes of the kidney or its component tissues.

manufacturingandindustrialfacilities.name: manufacturing and industrial facilities
manufacturingandindustrialfacilities.definition: Manufacturing and industrial facilities is places provided for the processing, fabrication, assembly, and production of a line of products, services, commodities, or merchandise.

rnatransport.name: rna transport
rnatransport.definition: Rna transport is the process of moving specific rna molecules from one cellular compartment or region to another by various sorting and transport mechanisms.

antigens,neoplasm.name: antigens , neoplasm
antigens,neoplasm.definition: Neoplasm antigens is proteins, glycoprotein, or lipoprotein moieties on surfaces of tumor cells that are usually identified by monoclonal antibodies. Many of these are of either embryonic or viral origin.

syphilis,latent.name: syphilis , latent
syphilis,latent.definition: Latent syphilis is the stage of syphilis that occurs following the primary (chancre) and secondary stages. The patient is asymptomatic at the latent stage but remains seropositive for the spirochete.

antigens,fungal.name: antigens , fungal
antigens,fungal.definition: Fungal antigens is substances of fungal origin that have antigenic activity.

spatialregression.name: spatial regression
spatialregression.definition: Spatial regression is methods used to take into account and incorporate spatial autocorrelation and regional variation into regression analysis models of data that has spatial dependency, and also to provide information on the spatial relationships among the variables.

populationgrowth.name: population growth
populationgrowth.definition: Population growth is increase, over a specific period of time, in the number of individuals living in a country or region.

v(d)jrecombination.name: v ( d ) j recombination
v(d)jrecombination.definition: V (d) j recombination is The process by which the V (variable), D (diversity), and J (joining) segments of immunoglobulin genes or T-cell receptor genes are assembled during the development of lymphoid cells using nonhomologous DNA end-joining.

alveolarprocess.name: alveolar process
alveolarprocess.definition: Alveolar process is the thickest and spongiest part of the maxilla and mandible hollowed out into deep cavities for the teeth.

onlinesystems.name: online systems
onlinesystems.definition: Online systems is computer-based Information systems having real-time remote access to information or processes.

peptides.name: peptides
peptides.definition: Peptides is members of the class of compounds composed of amino acids joined together by peptide bonds between adjacent amino acids into linear, branched or cyclical structures. oligopeptides are composed of approximately 2-12 amino acids. Polypeptides are composed of approximately 13 or more amino acids. proteins are linear polypeptides that are normally synthesized on ribosomes.

arrhythmia,sinus.name: arrhythmia , sinus
arrhythmia,sinus.definition: Sinus arrhythmia is irregular heart rate caused by abnormal function of the sinoatrial node. It is characterized by a greater than 10% change between the maximum and the minimum sinus cycle length or 120 milliseconds.

cranialfossa,middle.name: cranial fossa , middle
cranialfossa,middle.definition: Middle cranial fossa is the compartment containing the anterior extremities and half the inferior surface of the temporal lobes (temporal lobe) of the cerebral hemispheres. Lying posterior and inferior to the anterior cranial fossa (cranial fossa, anterior), it is formed by part of the [MASK] and sphenoid bone. It is separated from the posterior cranial fossa (cranial fossa, posterior) by crests formed by the superior borders of the petrous parts of the [MASK].

healthservicesforpersonswithdisabilities.name: health services for persons with disabilities
healthservicesforpersonswithdisabilities.definition: Health services for persons with disabilities is health services and access for disabled persons. Disabilities include impairments, activity limitations, or participation restrictions, and reflect the interaction between the individual with the disability and personal and environmental factors.

coronaryarterydisease.name: coronary artery disease
coronaryarterydisease.definition: Coronary artery disease is pathological processes of coronary arteries that may derive from a congenital abnormality, atherosclerotic, or non-atherosclerotic cause.

laserscanningcytometry.name: laser scanning cytometry
laserscanningcytometry.definition: Laser scanning cytometry is a scanning microscope-based, cytofluorimetry technique for making fluorescence measurements and topographic analysis on individual cells. Lasers are used to excite fluorochromes in labeled cellular specimens. Fluorescence is detected in multiple discrete wavelengths and the locational data is processed to quantitatively assess apoptosis; ploidies; cell proliferation; gene expression; protein transport; and other cellular processes.

primarycellculture.name: primary cell culture
primarycellculture.definition: Primary cell culture is the initial culturing of cells derived directly from fresh tissues.

homeostasis.name: homeostasis
homeostasis.definition: Homeostasis is the processes whereby the internal environment of an organism tends to remain balanced and stable.

chromosomes,artificial.name: chromosomes , artificial
chromosomes,artificial.definition: Artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, elements such as a replication origin; telomere; and centromere, that are required for successful replication, propagation to and maintenance in progeny cells. In addition, they are constructed to carry other sequences for analysis or gene transfer.

workscheduletolerance.name: work schedule tolerance
workscheduletolerance.definition: Work schedule tolerance is physiological or psychological effects of periods of work which may be fixed or flexible such as flexitime, work shifts, and rotating shifts.

uterineneoplasms.name: uterine neoplasms
uterineneoplasms.definition: Uterine neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the uterus.

rituximab.name: rituximab
rituximab.definition: Rituximab is a murine-derived monoclonal antibody and antineoplastic agent that binds specifically to the cd20 antigen and is used in the treatment of leukemia; lymphoma and rheumatoid arthritis.

technicalreport.name: technical report
technicalreport.definition: Technical report is work consisting of a formal report giving details of the investigation and results of a medical or other scientific problem. When issued by a government agency or comparable official body, its contents may be classified, unclassified, or declassified with regard to security clearance. This publication type may also cover a scientific [MASK] or article that records the current state or current position of scientific research and development. If so labeled by the editor or publisher, this publication type may be properly used for journal articles.

biopsy.name: biopsy
biopsy.definition: Biopsy is removal and pathologic examination of specimens from the living body.

hippocampus.name: hippocampus
hippocampus.definition: Hippocampus is a curved elevation of gray matter extending the entire length of the floor of the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle (see also temporal lobe). The hippocampus proper, subiculum, and dentate gyrus constitute the hippocampal formation. Sometimes authors include the entorhinal cortex in the hippocampal formation.

injections,spinal.name: injections , spinal
injections,spinal.definition: Spinal injections is introduction of therapeutic agents into the spinal region using a needle and syringe.

seoulvirus.name: seoul virus
seoulvirus.definition: Seoul virus is a species of hantavirus causing a less severe form of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Asia (primarily Korea and Japan). It is transmitted by rats, especially Rattus rattus and r. norvegicus.

sequenceanalysis,dna.name: sequence analysis , dna
sequenceanalysis,dna.definition: Dna sequence analysis is a multistage process that includes cloning, physical mapping, subcloning, determination of the dna sequence, and information analysis.

childrearing.name: child rearing
childrearing.definition: Child rearing is the training or bringing-up of children by parents or parent-substitutes. It is used also for child rearing practices in different societies, at different economic levels, in different ethnic groups, etc. It differs from parenting in that in child rearing the emphasis is on the act of training or bringing up the child and the interaction between the parent and child, while parenting emphasizes the responsibility and qualities of exemplary behavior of the parent.

protectivedevices.name: protective devices
protectivedevices.definition: Protective devices is devices designed to provide protection against injury.

wastewater.name: waste water
wastewater.definition: Waste water is contaminated water generated as a waste product of human activity.

thyroidgland.name: thyroid gland
thyroidgland.definition: Thyroid gland is a highly vascularized endocrine gland consisting of two lobes joined by a thin band of tissue with one lobe on each side of the [MASK]. It secretes thyroid hormones from the follicular cells and calcitonin from the parafollicular cells thereby regulating metabolism and calcium level in blood, respectively.

areahealtheducationcenters.name: area health education centers
areahealtheducationcenters.definition: Area health education centers is education centers authorized by the Comprehensive Health Manpower Training Act, 1971, for the training of health personnel in areas where health needs are the greatest. May be used for centers other than those established by the United States act.

physicaltherapyspecialty.name: physical therapy specialty
physicaltherapyspecialty.definition: Physical therapy specialty is the auxiliary health profession by which physical therapists make use of physical therapy modalities to prevent, correct, and alleviate movement dysfunction of anatomic or physiological origin.

antibodies,fungal.name: antibodies , fungal
antibodies,fungal.definition: Fungal antibodies is immunoglobulins produced in a response to fungal antigens.

wings,animal.name: wings , animal
wings,animal.definition: Animal wings is movable feathered or membranous paired appendages by means of which certain animals such as birds, bats, or insects are able to fly.

satellitecommunications.name: satellite communications
satellitecommunications.definition: Satellite communications is communications using an active or passive satellite to extend the range of radio, television, or other electronic transmission by returning signals to earth from an orbiting satellite.

cervicalrib.name: cervical rib
cervicalrib.definition: Cervical rib is a supernumerary rib developing from an abnormal enlargement of the costal element of the c7 vertebra. This anomaly is found in 1-2% of the population and can put pressure on adjacent structures causing cervical rib syndrome; thoracic outlet syndrome; or other conditions.

saccharomycescerevisiae.name: saccharomyces cerevisiae
saccharomycescerevisiae.definition: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a species of the genus saccharomyces, family Saccharomycetaceae, order Saccharomycetales, known as "baker's" or "brewer's" yeast. The dried form is used as a dietary supplement.

geneticpredispositiontodisease.name: genetic predisposition to disease
geneticpredispositiontodisease.definition: Genetic predisposition to disease is a latent susceptibility to disease at the genetic level, which may be activated under certain conditions.

acupuncturetherapy.name: acupuncture therapy
acupuncturetherapy.definition: Acupuncture therapy is treatment of disease by inserting needles along specific pathways or meridians. The placement varies with the disease being treated. It is sometimes used in conjunction with heat, moxibustion, acupressure, or electric stimulation.

ultrasonography,prenatal.name: ultrasonography , prenatal
ultrasonography,prenatal.definition: Prenatal ultrasonography is the visualization of tissues during pregnancy through recording of the echoes of [MASK] directed into the body. The procedure may be applied with reference to the mother or the fetus and with reference to organs or the detection of maternal or fetal disease.

computerterminals.name: computer terminals
computerterminals.definition: Computer terminals is input/output devices designed to receive data in an environment associated with the job to be performed, and capable of transmitting entries to, and obtaining output from, the system of which it is a part. (Computer Dictionary, 4th ed.)

datasystems.name: data systems
datasystems.definition: Data systems is organized collection of symbols and symbol-manipulating processes used to operate on such symbols.

magneticresonanceangiography.name: magnetic resonance angiography
magneticresonanceangiography.definition: Magnetic resonance angiography is non-invasive method of vascular imaging and determination of internal anatomy without injection of contrast media or radiation exposure. The technique is used especially in cerebral angiography as well as for studies of other vascular structures.

dogs.name: dogs
dogs.definition: Dogs is the domestic dog, Canis familiaris, comprising about 400 breeds, of the carnivore family canidae. They are worldwide in distribution and live in association with people. (Walker's Mammals of the World, 5th ed, p1065)

epidermalcells.name: epidermal cells
epidermalcells.definition: Epidermal cells is cells from the outermost, non-vascular layer (epidermis) of the skin.

healthinsuranceexchanges.name: health insurance exchanges
healthinsuranceexchanges.definition: Health insurance exchanges is state-provided health insurance marketplaces established under the patient protection and affordable care act.

cardiacvolume.name: cardiac volume
cardiacvolume.definition: Cardiac volume is the volume of the heart, usually relating to the volume of blood contained within it at various periods of the cardiac cycle. The amount of blood ejected from a ventricle at each beat is [MASK].

avoidancelearning.name: avoidance learning
avoidancelearning.definition: Avoidance learning is a response to a cue that is instrumental in avoiding a noxious experience.

bloodplateletdisorders.name: blood platelet disorders
bloodplateletdisorders.definition: Blood platelet disorders is disorders caused by abnormalities in platelet count or function.

radiologyinformationsystems.name: radiology information systems
radiologyinformationsystems.definition: Radiology information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of radiology services and facilities.

dentinsolubility.name: dentin solubility
dentinsolubility.definition: Dentin solubility is the susceptibility of the dentin to dissolution.

colonicdiseases.name: colonic diseases
colonicdiseases.definition: Colonic diseases is pathological processes in the colon region of the large intestine (intestine, large).

neutropenia.name: neutropenia
neutropenia.definition: Neutropenia is a decrease in the number of neutrophils found in the blood.

tryptophansynthase.name: tryptophan synthase
tryptophansynthase.definition: Tryptophan synthase is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of L-serine and 1-(indol-3-yl)glycerol 3-phosphate to L-tryptophan and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. It is a pyridoxal phosphate protein that also catalyzes the conversion of serine and indole into tryptophan and water and of indoleglycerol phosphate into indole and glyceraldehyde phosphate. (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992) ec 4.2.1.20.

golgimatrixproteins.name: golgi matrix proteins
golgimatrixproteins.definition: Golgi matrix proteins is proteins on the cytoplasmic side of the golgi apparatus cisternae that tether the cisternae to each other or to the transport vesicles of the trans-golgi network to maintain the Golgi structure and function.

skincream.name: skin cream
skincream.definition: Skin cream is a water-soluble medicinal preparation applied to the skin.

communitydentistry.name: community dentistry
communitydentistry.definition: Community dentistry is the practice of dentistry concerned with preventive as well as diagnostic and treatment programs in a circumscribed population.

computersystems.name: computer systems
computersystems.definition: Computer systems is systems composed of a computer or computers, peripheral equipment, such as disks, printers, and terminals, and telecommunications capabilities.

consensusdevelopmentconference.name: consensus development conference
consensusdevelopmentconference.definition: [MASK] conference is official statements of the findings or recommendations expressing the outcome of a meeting convened to evaluate current thought and research on a subject of interest.

colitis,microscopic.name: colitis , microscopic
colitis,microscopic.definition: Microscopic colitis is a condition characterized by chronic watery [MASK] of unknown origin, a normal colonoscopy but abnormal histopathology on biopsy. This syndrome was first described in 1980 by Read and associates. Subtypes include collagenous colitis and lymphocytic colitis. Both have similar clinical symptoms and are distinguishable only by histology.

hospitals,rehabilitation.name: hospitals , rehabilitation
hospitals,rehabilitation.definition: Rehabilitation hospitals is free standing rehabilitation hospitals and rehabilitation units in acute care hospitals.  They provide an intensive inpatient rehabilitation program.

uterinecervicalneoplasms.name: uterine cervical neoplasms
uterinecervicalneoplasms.definition: Uterine cervical neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the uterine cervix.

diabetes,gestational.name: diabetes , gestational
diabetes,gestational.definition: Gestational diabetes is diabetes mellitus induced by pregnancy but resolved at the end of pregnancy. It does not include previously diagnosed diabetics who become pregnant (pregnancy in diabetics). Gestational diabetes usually develops in late pregnancy when insulin antagonistic hormones peaks leading to insulin resistance; glucose intolerance; and hyperglycemia.

medicarepartc.name: medicare part c
medicarepartc.definition: Medicare part c is the Balanced Budget Act (bba) of 1997 establishes a Medicare+Choice program under part c of Title xviii, Section 4001, of the Social Security Act. Under this program, an eligible individual may elect to receive Medicare benefits through enrollment in a Medicare+Choice plan. Beneficiaries may choose to use private pay options, establish [MASK], use managed care plans, or join provider-sponsored plans.

asymptomaticinfections.name: asymptomatic infections
asymptomaticinfections.definition: Asymptomatic infections is infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

perfusionindex.name: perfusion index
perfusionindex.definition: Perfusion index is the ratio of arterial blood flow (pulsatile flow) to venous, capillary, and tissue blood flow  (non-pulsatile blood flow) - as measured regionally or peripherally.

trout.name: trout
trout.definition: Trout is various fish of the family salmonidae, usually smaller than salmon. They are mostly restricted to cool clear freshwater. Some are anadromous. They are highly regarded for their handsome [MASK], rich well-flavored flesh, and gameness as an angling fish. The genera Salvelinus, Salmo, and oncorhynchus have been introduced virtually throughout the world.

folliclestimulatinghormone,human.name: follicle stimulating hormone , human
folliclestimulatinghormone,human.definition: Human follicle stimulating hormone is a major gonadotropin secreted by the human adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). Follicle-stimulating hormone stimulates gametogenesis and the supporting cells such as the ovarian granulosa cells, the testicular sertoli cells, and the leydig cells. fsh consists of two noncovalently linked subunits, alpha and beta. The alpha subunit is common in the three human pituitary glycoprotein hormones (tsh, lh, and fsh), but the beta subunit is unique and confers its biological specificity.

restingphase,cellcycle.name: resting phase , cell cycle
restingphase,cellcycle.definition: Cell cycle resting phase is a quiescent state of cells during g1 phase.

alzheimerdisease.name: alzheimer disease
alzheimerdisease.definition: Alzheimer disease is a degenerative disease of the brain characterized by the insidious onset of dementia. Impairment of memory, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe apraxias and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of senile plaques; neurofibrillary tangles; and neuropil threads. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1049-57)

unitednations.name: united nations
unitednations.definition: United nations is an international organization whose members include most of the sovereign nations of the world with headquarters in New York City. The primary objectives of the organization are to maintain peace and security and to achieve international cooperation in solving international economic, social, cultural, or humanitarian problems.

efficiency,organizational.name: efficiency , organizational
efficiency,organizational.definition: Organizational efficiency is the capacity of an organization, institution, or business to produce desired results with a minimum expenditure of energy, time, money, personnel, material, etc.

fluidshifts.name: fluid shifts
fluidshifts.definition: Fluid shifts is translocation of body fluids from one compartment to another, such as from the vascular to the interstitial compartments. Fluid shifts are associated with profound changes in vascular permeability and water-electrolyte imbalance. The shift can also be from the lower body to the upper body as in conditions of weightlessness.

skindiseases.name: skin diseases
skindiseases.definition: Skin diseases is diseases involving the dermis or epidermis.

glycinedehydrogenase.name: glycine dehydrogenase
glycinedehydrogenase.definition: Glycine dehydrogenase is an oxidoreductase that catalyzes the oxidative deamination of glycine to glyoxylate and [MASK] in the presence of nad. In bacteria lacking transaminating pathways the enzyme can act in the reverse direction to synthesize glycine from glyoxylate and [MASK] and nadh.

hospitalbedcapacity,under100.name: hospital bed capacity , under 100
hospitalbedcapacity,under100.definition: Under 100 hospital bed capacity is the number of beds under 100 which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds [MASK] up and staffed for use.

locuscontrolregion.name: locus control region
locuscontrolregion.definition: Locus control region is a regulatory region first identified in the human beta-globin locus but subsequently found in other loci. The region is believed to regulate genetic transcription by opening and remodeling chromatin structure. It may also have enhancer activity.

neoplasmgrading.name: neoplasm grading
neoplasmgrading.definition: Neoplasm grading is methods which attempt to express in replicable terms the level of cell differentiation in neoplasms as increasing anaplasia correlates with the aggressiveness of the neoplasm.

ralguaninenucleotideexchangefactor.name: ral guanine nucleotide exchange factor
ralguaninenucleotideexchangefactor.definition: Ral guanine nucleotide exchange factor is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor that stimulates the dissociation of gdp from ral gtp-binding proteins. It also has gdp exchange activity towards other monomeric gtp-binding proteins.

intentiontotreatanalysis.name: intention to treat analysis
intentiontotreatanalysis.definition: Intention to treat analysis is strategy for the analysis of randomized controlled trials as topic that compares patients in the groups to which they were originally randomly assigned.

porosity.name: porosity
porosity.definition: Porosity is condition of having pores or open spaces. This often refers to bones, bone implants, or bone cements, but can refer to the porous state of any solid substance.

indicatordilutiontechniques.name: indicator dilution techniques
indicatordilutiontechniques.definition: Indicator dilution techniques is methods for assessing flow through a system by injection of a known quantity of an indicator, such as a dye, radionuclide, or chilled liquid, into the system and monitoring its concentration over time at a specific point in the system. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

medicarepartd.name: medicare part d
medicarepartd.definition: Medicare part d is a stand-alone drug plan offered by insurers and other private companies to beneficiaries that receive their Medicare Part a and/or b benefits through the Original Medicare Plan. It includes Medicare Private Fee-for-Service Plans that do not offer prescription drug coverage and Medicare Cost Plans offering Medicare prescription drug coverage. The plan was enacted as the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003 with coverage beginning January 1, 2006.

worksimplification.name: work simplification
worksimplification.definition: Work simplification is the construction or arrangement of a task so that it may be done with the greatest possible efficiency.

centralnervoussystemparasiticinfections.name: central nervous system parasitic infections
centralnervoussystemparasiticinfections.definition: Central nervous system parasitic infections is infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges caused by parasites.

receptors,steroid.name: receptors , steroid
receptors,steroid.definition: Steroid receptors is proteins found usually in the cytoplasm or nucleus that specifically bind steroid hormones and trigger changes influencing the behavior of cells. The steroid receptor-steroid hormone complex regulates the transcription of specific genes.

sexdeterminationprocesses.name: sex determination processes
sexdeterminationprocesses.definition: [MASK] determination processes is the mechanisms by which the [MASK] of an individual's gonads are fixed.

vision,low.name: vision , low
vision,low.definition: Low vision is vision considered to be inferior to normal vision as represented by accepted standards of acuity, field of vision, or motility. Low vision generally refers to visual disorders that are caused by diseases that cannot be corrected by refraction (e.g., macular degeneration; retinitis pigmentosa; diabetic retinopathy, etc.).

proteindomains.name: protein domains
proteindomains.definition: Protein domains is discrete protein structural units that may fold independently of the rest of the protein and have their own functions.

bloodcellcount.name: blood cell count
bloodcellcount.definition: Blood cell count is the number of leukocytes and erythrocytes per unit volume in a sample of venous blood. a complete blood count (cbc) also includes measurement of the hemoglobin; hematocrit; and erythrocyte indices.

fetalmovement.name: fetal movement
fetalmovement.definition: Fetal movement is physical activity of the fetus in utero. Gross or fine fetal body movement can be monitored by the mother, palpation, or ultrasonography.

fossilfuels.name: fossil fuels
fossilfuels.definition: Fossil fuels is any combustible hydrocarbon deposit formed from the remains of prehistoric organisms. Examples are petroleum, coal, and natural gas.

biologicalpsychiatry.name: biological psychiatry
biologicalpsychiatry.definition: Biological psychiatry is an interdisciplinary science concerned with studies of the biological bases of behavior - biochemical, genetic, physiological, and neurological - and applying these to the understanding and treatment of mental illness.

documentation.name: documentation
documentation.definition: Documentation is systematic organization, storage, retrieval, and dissemination of specialized information, especially of a scientific or technical nature (From ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983). It often involves authenticating or validating information.

srchomologydomains.name: src homology domains
srchomologydomains.definition: Src homology domains is regions of amino acid sequence similarity in the src-family tyrosine kinases that fold into specific functional tertiary structures. The sh1 domain is a [MASK]. sh2 and sh3 domains are protein interaction domains. sh2 usually binds PHOSPHOTYROSINE-containing proteins and sh3 interacts with cytoskeletal proteins.

papillarymuscles.name: papillary muscles
papillarymuscles.definition: Papillary muscles is conical muscular projections from the walls of the cardiac ventricles, attached to the cusps of the atrioventricular valves by the chordae tendineae.

reading.name: reading
reading.definition: Reading is acquiring information from text.

vitaminb12.name: vitamin b 12
vitaminb12.definition: Vitamin b 12 is a cobalt-containing coordination compound produced by intestinal micro-organisms and found also in soil and water. Higher plants do not concentrate vitamin b 12 from the soil and so are a poor source of the substance as compared with animal tissues. intrinsic factor is important for the assimilation of vitamin b 12.

prescriptiondrugmonitoringprograms.name: prescription drug monitoring programs
prescriptiondrugmonitoringprograms.definition: Prescription drug monitoring programs is programs, usually run by [MASK], that require pharmacists to collect and distribute data on the prescription and dispensation of controlled substances. They are intended to prevent the abuse of such substances by the patient, or their transfer to recreational users and drug dealers.

clinicaldeterioration.name: clinical deterioration
clinicaldeterioration.definition: Clinical deterioration is a critical disease progression, often measured by a [MASK] of clinical parameters, which activates hospital rapid response team.

cellsize.name: cell size
cellsize.definition: Cell size is the quantity of volume or surface area of cells.

tea.name: tea
tea.definition: Tea is the infusion of leaves of camellia sinensis (formerly Thea sinensis) as a beverage, the familiar Asian tea, which contains catechin (especially epigallocatechin gallate) and caffeine.

amines.name: amines
amines.definition: Amines is a group of compounds derived from [MASK] by substituting organic radicals for the hydrogens. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

decisionmaking,organizational.name: decision making , organizational
decisionmaking,organizational.definition: Organizational decision making is the process by which decisions are made in an institution or other organization.

presynapticterminals.name: presynaptic terminals
presynapticterminals.definition: Presynaptic terminals is the distal terminations of axons which are specialized for the release of neurotransmitters. Also included are varicosities along the course of axons which have similar specializations and also release transmitters. Presynaptic terminals in both the central and peripheral nervous systems are included.

glaucoma,neovascular.name: glaucoma , neovascular
glaucoma,neovascular.definition: Neovascular glaucoma is a form of secondary glaucoma which develops as a consequence of another ocular disease and is attributed to the forming of new vessels in the angle of the anterior chamber.

radiationleukemiavirus.name: radiation leukemia virus
radiationleukemiavirus.definition: Radiation leukemia virus is a strain of Murine leukemia virus (leukemia virus, murine) isolated from radiation-induced lymphomas in c57bl mice. It is leukemogenic, thymotrophic, can be transmitted vertically, and replicates only in vivo.

virusintegration.name: virus integration
virusintegration.definition: Virus integration is insertion of [MASK] into host-cell dna. This includes integration of phage dna into [MASK]; (lysogeny); to form a prophage or integration of retroviral dna into cellular dna to form a provirus.

genes,synthetic.name: genes , synthetic
genes,synthetic.definition: Synthetic genes is biologically functional sequences of dna chemically synthesized in vitro.

magneticphenomena.name: magnetic phenomena
magneticphenomena.definition: Magnetic phenomena is characteristics, properties, and effects of magnetic substances and magnetic fields.

bodyintegrityidentitydisorder.name: body integrity identity disorder
bodyintegrityidentitydisorder.definition: Body integrity identity disorder is condition in which individuals desire the [MASK] of one or more healthy limbs or who desire a paralysis.

beginningofhumanlife.name: beginning of human life
beginningofhumanlife.definition: Beginning of human life is the point at which religious ensoulment or personhood is considered to begin.

prosthesisretention.name: prosthesis retention
prosthesisretention.definition: Prosthesis retention is holding a prosthesis in place.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyd.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily d
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyd.definition: Subfamily d atp binding cassette transporter is a sub-family of ATP-binding cassette transporters that localize to the membranes of peroxisomes; endoplasmic reticulum; and lysosomes. Members contain a transmembrane domain in their N-terminal half and generally function as homodimers in the transport of lipids; [MASK] acids; and vitamin b12. Mutations in some abcd transporter genes are associated with peroxisomal disorders.

dependency,psychological.name: dependency , psychological
dependency,psychological.definition: Psychological dependency is the tendency of an individual or individuals to rely on others for advice, guidance, or support.

organicagriculture.name: organic agriculture
organicagriculture.definition: Organic agriculture is systems of agriculture which adhere to nationally regulated standards that restrict the use of pesticides, non-organic fertilizers, genetic engineering, growth hormones, irradiation, antibiotics, and non-organic [MASK].

satelliteimagery.name: satellite imagery
satelliteimagery.definition: Satellite [MASK] is composition of images of earth or other planets from data collected during space flight by remote sensing instruments onboard spacecraft. The satellite sensor systems measure and record absorbed, emitted, or reflected energy across the spectra, as well as global position and time.

embolismandthrombosis.name: embolism and thrombosis
embolismandthrombosis.definition: Embolism and thrombosis is a collective term for pathological conditions which are caused by the formation of a blood clot (thrombus) in a blood vessel, or by blocking of a blood vessel with an embolus, undissolved materials in the blood [MASK].

capitalfinancing.name: capital financing
capitalfinancing.definition: Capital financing is institutional funding for facilities and for equipment which becomes a part of the assets of the institution.

respiratorytractinfections.name: respiratory tract infections
respiratorytractinfections.definition: Respiratory tract infections is invasion of the host respiratory system by microorganisms, usually leading to pathological processes or diseases.

failedbacksurgerysyndrome.name: failed back surgery syndrome
failedbacksurgerysyndrome.definition: Failed back surgery syndrome is a condition of persistent pain and discomfort in the back and the leg following lumbar surgery, often seen in patients enrolled in [MASK].

neoplasms,complexandmixed.name: neoplasms , complex and mixed
neoplasms,complexandmixed.definition: Complex and mixed neoplasms is neoplasms composed of more than one type of neoplastic tissue.

patienthealthquestionnaire.name: patient health questionnaire
patienthealthquestionnaire.definition: Patient health questionnaire is a self-administered version of the Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders (prime-md), a diagnostic tool containing modules on multiple mental health disorders including anxiety, alcohol, eating, and somatoform modules. The Patient Health Questionnaire (phq-9) is designed specifically for mood/depression scoring each of the 9 [MASK] criteria based on the mood module from the original prime-md. The Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (gad-7) scores 7 common anxiety symptoms.

organismforms.name: organism forms
organismforms.definition: Organism forms is specific states or [MASK] of organisms. These include post-embryonic stages of insects, symbiotic relationships between organisms, and reproductive elements such as spores.

technology,pharmaceutical.name: technology , pharmaceutical
technology,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical technology is the application of scientific knowledge or technology to pharmacy and the pharmaceutical industry. It includes methods, techniques, and instrumentation in the manufacture, preparation, compounding, dispensing, packaging, and storing of drugs and other preparations used in diagnostic and determinative procedures, and in the treatment of patients.

tryptophan.name: tryptophan
tryptophan.definition: Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that is necessary for normal growth in infants and for nitrogen balance in adults. It is a precursor of indole alkaloids in plants. It is a precursor of serotonin (hence its use as an antidepressant and sleep aid). It can be a precursor to niacin, albeit inefficiently, in mammals.

wales.name: wales
wales.definition: Wales is a region of the United Kingdom, in the southwestern area of Great Britain.

ovarianneoplasms.name: ovarian neoplasms
ovarianneoplasms.definition: Ovarian neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the ovary. These neoplasms can be benign or malignant. They are classified according to the tissue of origin, such as the surface epithelium, the stromal endocrine cells, and the totipotent germ cells.

nervoussystemphysiologicalphenomena.name: nervous system physiological phenomena
nervoussystemphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Nervous system physiological phenomena is characteristic properties and processes of the nervous system as a whole or with reference to the peripheral or the central nervous system.

nurses,international.name: nurses , international
nurses,international.definition: International nurses is nurses who provide nursing care in countries other than the ones in which they received their training.

radioactivity.name: radioactivity
radioactivity.definition: Radioactivity is the spontaneous transformation of a nuclide into one or more different nuclides, accompanied by either the emission of particles from the nucleus, nuclear capture or ejection of orbital [MASK], or fission. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

flameionization.name: flame ionization
flameionization.definition: Flame ionization is pyrolysis of organic compounds at the temperature of a hydrogen-air flame to produce ionic intermediates which can be collected and the resulting ion current measured by gas chromatography.

prosthesisimplantation.name: prosthesis implantation
prosthesisimplantation.definition: Prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of a prosthesis.

fermentation.name: fermentation
fermentation.definition: Fermentation is anaerobic degradation of glucose or other organic nutrients to gain energy in the form of atp. End products vary depending on organisms, substrates, and enzymatic pathways. Common fermentation products include ethanol and lactic acid.

pulmonaryveins.name: pulmonary veins
pulmonaryveins.definition: Pulmonary veins is the veins that return the oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.

bloodtransfusion,autologous.name: blood transfusion , autologous
bloodtransfusion,autologous.definition: Autologous blood transfusion is reinfusion of blood or blood products derived from the patient's own circulation. (Dorland, 27th ed)

antibodies,neoplasm.name: antibodies , neoplasm
antibodies,neoplasm.definition: Neoplasm antibodies is immunoglobulins induced by antigens specific for tumors other than the normally occurring histocompatibility antigens.

cognitiveneuroscience.name: cognitive neuroscience
cognitiveneuroscience.definition: Cognitive neuroscience is field of study concerning mental processes; learning; and the brain regions associated with them.

livebirth.name: live birth
livebirth.definition: Live birth is the event that a fetus is born alive with heartbeats or respiration regardless of gestational age. Such liveborn is called a newborn infant (infant, newborn).

olfactorycortex.name: olfactory cortex
olfactorycortex.definition: Olfactory cortex is [MASK] and medial part of temporal lobe areas that receive synaptic inputs from the olfactory bulb.

research.name: research
research.definition: Research is critical and exhaustive investigation or experimentation, having for its aim the discovery of new facts and their correct interpretation, the revision of accepted conclusions, theories, or laws in the light of newly discovered facts, or the practical application of such new or revised conclusions, theories, or laws. (Webster, 3d ed)

counseling.name: counseling
counseling.definition: Counseling is the giving of advice and assistance to individuals with educational or personal problems.

macrophages,alveolar.name: macrophages , alveolar
macrophages,alveolar.definition: Alveolar macrophages is round, granular, mononuclear phagocytes found in the alveoli of the lungs. They ingest small inhaled particles resulting in degradation and presentation of the antigen to immunocompetent cells.

spinlabels.name: spin labels
spinlabels.definition: Spin labels is molecules which contain an atom or a group of atoms exhibiting an unpaired [MASK] spin that can be detected by [MASK] and can be bonded to another molecule. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Chemical and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

infantnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: infant nutritional physiological phenomena
infantnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Infant nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of children from birth to 2 years of age.

helpingbehavior.name: helping behavior
helpingbehavior.definition: Helping behavior is behaviors associated with the giving of assistance or aid to individuals.

compositelymphoma.name: composite lymphoma
compositelymphoma.definition: Composite lymphoma is two or more distinct types of malignant lymphoid tumors occurring within a single organ or tissue at the same time. It may contain different types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells or both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells.

calciumreleaseactivatedcalciumchannels.name: calcium release activated calcium channels
calciumreleaseactivatedcalciumchannels.definition: Calcium release activated calcium channels is specialized calcium channels that localize to the endoplamsic reticulum and plasma membrane. They contain the pore subunit orai1 protein which is activated by stromal interaction molecules upon intracellular calcium depletion.

proteinmodification,translational.name: protein modification , translational
proteinmodification,translational.definition: Translational protein modification is any of the enzymatically catalyzed modifications of the individual amino acids of proteins, and enzymatic cleavage or crosslinking of peptide chains that occur pre-translationally (on the amino acid component of [MASK]), co-translationally (during the process of genetic translation), or after translation is completed (post-translational protein processing).

residentialfacilities.name: residential facilities
residentialfacilities.definition: Residential facilities is long-term care facilities which provide supervision and assistance in activities of daily living with medical and nursing services when required.

movingandliftingpatients.name: moving and lifting patients
movingandliftingpatients.definition: Moving and lifting patients is moving or repositioning patients within their beds, from bed to bed, bed to chair, or otherwise from one posture or surface to another.

unitedstatesdepartmentofveteransaffairs.name: united states department of veterans affairs
unitedstatesdepartmentofveteransaffairs.definition: United states department of veterans affairs is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government concerned with overall planning, promoting, and administering programs pertaining to veterans. It was established March 15, 1989 as a Cabinet-level position.

mice,transgenic.name: mice , transgenic
mice,transgenic.definition: Transgenic mice is laboratory mice that have been produced from a genetically manipulated egg or embryo, mammalian.

chickenanemiavirus.name: chicken anemia virus
chickenanemiavirus.definition: [MASK] anemia virus is the type species of gyrovirus, a small, non-enveloped dna virus originally isolated from contaminated vaccines in Japan. It causes [MASK] infectious anemia and may possibly play a key role in hemorrhagic anemia syndrome, anemia dermatitis, and blue wing disease.

malaria,cerebral.name: malaria , cerebral
malaria,cerebral.definition: Cerebral malaria is a condition characterized by somnolence or coma in the presence of an acute infection with plasmodium falciparum (and rarely other Plasmodium species). Initial clinical manifestations include headaches; seizures; and alterations of mentation followed by a rapid progression to coma. Pathologic features include cerebral capillaries filled with parasitized erythrocytes and multiple small foci of cortical and subcortical necrosis. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p136)

hormone.name: hormone
hormone.definition: Hormone is chemical substances having a specific regulatory effect on the activity of a certain organ or organs. The term was originally applied to substances secreted by various endocrine glands and transported in the bloodstream to the target organs. It is sometimes extended to include those substances that are not produced by the endocrine glands but that have similar effects.

rna,mitochondrial.name: rna , mitochondrial
rna,mitochondrial.definition: Mitochondrial rna is rna molecules encoded by the [MASK].

phospholipidtransferproteins.name: phospholipid transfer proteins
phospholipidtransferproteins.definition: [MASK] transfer proteins is a ubiquitous family of proteins that transport [MASK] such as phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine between membranes. They play an important role in [MASK] metabolism during vesicular transport and signal transduction.

cellnucleusshape.name: cell nucleus shape
cellnucleusshape.definition: Cell nucleus shape is the quality of surface form or [MASK] of the cell nucleus.

resilience,psychological.name: resilience , psychological
resilience,psychological.definition: Psychological resilience is the human ability to adapt in the face of tragedy, trauma, adversity, hardship, and ongoing significant life stressors.

pain,intractable.name: pain , intractable
pain,intractable.definition: Intractable pain is persistent pain that is refractory to some or all forms of treatment.

disabilityevaluation.name: disability evaluation
disabilityevaluation.definition: Disability evaluation is determination of the degree of a physical, mental, or emotional handicap. The diagnosis is applied to legal qualification for benefits and income under disability insurance and to eligibility for Social Security and workmen's compensation benefits.

anesthesia,intravenous.name: anesthesia , intravenous
anesthesia,intravenous.definition: Intravenous anesthesia is process of administering an anesthetic through injection directly into the bloodstream.

pleuralcavity.name: pleural cavity
pleuralcavity.definition: Pleural cavity is paired but separate cavity within the thoracic cavity. It consists of the space between the parietal and visceral pleura and normally contains a capillary layer of serous fluid that lubricates the pleural surfaces.

wwdomains.name: ww domains
wwdomains.definition: Ww domains is an approximately 40 amino acid protein domain that occurs in a variety of unrelated proteins and may be repeated up to four times in some proteins. It is characterized by two tryptophan residues (ww) about 20 amino acids apart and folds into a stable triple-stranded beta-sheet. It binds proline-rich protein domains and phosphoserine or PHOSPHOTHREONINE-containing protein domains that occur in many signal-transducing and cytoskeletal proteins such as dystrophin.

cellcommunication.name: cell communication
cellcommunication.definition: Cell communication is any of several ways in which living cells of an organism communicate with one another, whether by direct contact between cells or by means of chemical signals carried by neurotransmitter substances, hormones, and cyclic amp.

flowers.name: flowers
flowers.definition: Flowers is the reproductive organs of plants.

corpusstriatum.name: corpus striatum
corpusstriatum.definition: Corpus striatum is striped gray matter and [MASK] matter consisting of the neostriatum and paleostriatum (globus pallidus). It is located in front of and lateral to the thalamus in each cerebral hemisphere. The gray substance is made up of the caudate nucleus and the lentiform nucleus (the latter consisting of the globus pallidus and putamen). The [MASK] matter is the internal capsule.

regressionanalysis.name: regression analysis
regressionanalysis.definition: Regression analysis is procedures for finding the mathematical function which best describes the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables. In linear regression (see linear models) the relationship is constrained to be a straight line and least-squares analysis is used to determine the best fit. In [MASK] (see [MASK]) the dependent variable is qualitative rather than continuously variable and [MASK] are used to find the best relationship. In multiple regression, the dependent variable is considered to depend on more than a single independent variable.

answeringservices.name: answering services
answeringservices.definition: Answering services is communication services provided by a person or a machine to record and relay the message from the caller.

lenscortex,crystalline.name: lens cortex , crystalline
lenscortex,crystalline.definition: Crystalline lens cortex is the portion of the crystalline lens surrounding the nucleus and bound anteriorly by the epithelium and posteriorly by the capsule. It contains lens fibers and amorphous, intercellular substance.

socialplanning.name: social planning
socialplanning.definition: Social planning is a systematic process for evaluating and identifying specific needs in the community and the implementation of practical steps for meeting those needs and improving [MASK].

erythrocytes.name: erythrocytes
erythrocytes.definition: Erythrocytes is red blood cells. Mature erythrocytes are non-nucleated, biconcave disks containing hemoglobin whose function is to transport oxygen.

healthpromotion.name: health promotion
healthpromotion.definition: Health promotion is encouraging consumer behaviors most likely to optimize health potentials (physical and psychosocial) through health information, preventive programs, and access to medical care.

specialtyusesofchemicals.name: specialty uses of chemicals
specialtyusesofchemicals.definition: Specialty uses of chemicals is uses of chemicals in a research, industrial, or household setting. This does not include pharmacologic actions.

gingivalretractiontechniques.name: gingival retraction techniques
gingivalretractiontechniques.definition: Gingival retraction techniques is techniques used to expose dental surface below the gingival margin in order to obtain better dental impression during periodental and peri-implant applications. The retraction of the gingival tissue can be achieved surgically (e.g., laser gingivectomy and rotary curettage) or chemically with a retraction cord.

sexwork.name: sex work
sexwork.definition: [MASK] work is the act or practice of engaging in sexual relations for money or other benefit.

calibration.name: calibration
calibration.definition: Calibration is determination, by measurement or comparison with a standard, of the correct value of each scale reading on a meter or other measuring instrument; or determination of the settings of a control device that correspond to particular values of voltage, current, frequency or other output.

dentalcastinginvestment.name: dental casting investment
dentalcastinginvestment.definition: Dental casting investment is material from which the casting mold is made in the fabrication of gold or cobalt-chromium castings. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p168)

alveolarridgeaugmentation.name: alveolar ridge augmentation
alveolarridgeaugmentation.definition: Alveolar ridge augmentation is preprosthetic surgery involving rib, cartilage, or iliac crest bone [MASK], usually autologous, or synthetic implants for rebuilding the alveolar ridge.

dentalleakage.name: dental leakage
dentalleakage.definition: Dental leakage is the seepage of fluids, debris, and micro-organisms between the walls of a prepared dental cavity and the restoration.

datamining.name: data mining
datamining.definition: Data mining is use of sophisticated analysis tools to sort through, organize, examine, and combine large sets of information.

hearingaids.name: hearing aids
hearingaids.definition: Hearing aids is wearable sound-amplifying devices that are intended to compensate for impaired hearing. These generic devices include air-conduction hearing aids and [MASK] aids. (umdns, 1999)

viralproteins.name: viral proteins
viralproteins.definition: Viral proteins is proteins found in any species of virus.

anklebrachialindex.name: ankle brachial index
anklebrachialindex.definition: Ankle brachial index is comparison of the blood pressure between the brachial artery and the [MASK]. It is a predictor of [MASK].

lymphocytecooperation.name: lymphocyte cooperation
lymphocytecooperation.definition: Lymphocyte cooperation is t-cell enhancement of the B-cell response to thymic-dependent antigens.

glucosetransportertype2.name: glucose transporter type 2
glucosetransportertype2.definition: Glucose transporter type 2 is a glucose transport facilitator that is expressed primarily in pancreatic beta cells; liver; and kidneys. It may function as a glucose sensor to regulate insulin release and glucose homeostasis.

compressedair.name: compressed air
compressedair.definition: Compressed air is air that is reduced in volume by pressure.

corticosterone.name: corticosterone
corticosterone.definition: Corticosterone is an adrenocortical steroid that has modest but significant activities as a mineralocorticoid and a [MASK]. (From Goodman and Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 8th ed, p1437)

acousticimpedancetests.name: acoustic impedance tests
acousticimpedancetests.definition: Acoustic impedance tests is objective tests of [MASK] function based on the difficulty (impedance) or ease (admittance) of sound flow through the [MASK]. These include static impedance and dynamic impedance (i.e., tympanometry and impedance tests in conjunction with intra-aural muscle reflex elicitation). This term is used also for various components of impedance and admittance (e.g., compliance, conductance, reactance, resistance, susceptance).

bibliography,descriptive.name: bibliography , descriptive
bibliography,descriptive.definition: Descriptive bibliography is the area of bibliography which makes known precisely the material conditions of books, i.e., the full name of the author, the exact title of the work, the date and place of publication, the publisher's and printer's names, the format, the pagination, typographical particulars, illustrations, and the price, and for old books, other characteristics such as the kind of [MASK], binding, etc. It is also called analytical bibliography and physical bibliography. (Harrod's Librarians' Glossary, 7th ed)

hypothyroidism.name: hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.definition: Hypothyroidism is a syndrome that results from abnormally low secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland, leading to a decrease in basal metabolic rate. In its most severe form, there is accumulation of mucopolysaccharides in the skin and edema, known as myxedema. It may be primary or secondary due to other pituitary disease, or hypothalamic dysfunction.

clinicaltrials,phaseiiiastopic.name: clinical trials , phase iii as topic
clinicaltrials,phaseiiiastopic.definition: Phase iii as topic clinical trials is works about comparative studies to verify the effectiveness of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques determined in phase ii studies. During these trials, patients are monitored closely by physicians to identify any adverse reactions from long-term use. These studies are performed on groups of patients large enough to identify clinically significant responses and usually last about three years. This concept includes phase iii studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

glycolysis.name: glycolysis
glycolysis.definition: Glycolysis is a metabolic process that converts glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid through a series of enzymatic reactions. Energy generated by this process is conserved in two molecules of atp. Glycolysis is the universal catabolic pathway for glucose, free glucose, or glucose derived from complex carbohydrates, such as glycogen and [MASK].

dentalpulpdiseases.name: dental pulp diseases
dentalpulpdiseases.definition: [MASK] diseases is endodontic diseases of the [MASK] inside the tooth, which is distinguished from periapical diseases of the tissue surrounding the root.

tin.name: tin
tin.definition: Tin is a trace element that is required in bone formation. It has the atomic symbol Sn, atomic number 50, and atomic weight 118.71.

receptors,retinoicacid.name: receptors , retinoic acid
receptors,retinoicacid.definition: Retinoic acid receptors is proteins in the nucleus or cytoplasm that specifically bind retinoic acid or retinol and trigger changes in the behavior of cells. Retinoic acid receptors, like steroid receptors, are ligand-activated transcription regulators. Several types have been recognized.

downsyndrome.name: down syndrome
downsyndrome.definition: Down syndrome is a chromosome disorder associated either with an extra chromosome 21 or an effective trisomy for chromosome 21. Clinical manifestations include hypotonia, short stature, brachycephaly, upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthus, Brushfield spots on the iris, protruding tongue, small ears, short, broad hands, fifth finger clinodactyly, Simian crease, and moderate to severe intellectual disability. Cardiac and gastrointestinal malformations, a marked increase in the incidence of leukemia, and the early onset of alzheimer disease are also associated with this condition. Pathologic features include the development of neurofibrillary tangles in neurons and the deposition of amyloid beta-protein, similar to the pathology of alzheimer disease. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p213)

neoplasmregression,spontaneous.name: neoplasm regression , spontaneous
neoplasmregression,spontaneous.definition: Spontaneous neoplasm regression is disappearance of a neoplasm or neoplastic state without the intervention of therapy.

macrophageactivation.name: macrophage activation
macrophageactivation.definition: Macrophage activation is the process of altering the morphology and functional activity of macrophages so that they become avidly phagocytic. It is initiated by lymphokines, such as the macrophage activation factor (maf) and the macrophage migration-inhibitory factor (mmif), immune complexes, C3b, and various peptides, polysaccharides, and immunologic adjuvants.

leg.name: leg
leg.definition: Leg is the inferior part of the lower extremity between the [MASK] and the ankle.

conditioning,classical.name: conditioning , classical
conditioning,classical.definition: Classical conditioning is learning that takes place when a conditioned stimulus is paired with an unconditioned stimulus.

growthhormone.name: growth hormone
growthhormone.definition: Growth hormone is a polypeptide that is secreted by the adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). Growth hormone, also known as somatotropin, stimulates [MASK], cell differentiation and cell growth. Species-specific growth hormones have been synthesized.

jobapplication.name: job application
jobapplication.definition: Job application is process of applying for employment. It includes written application for employment or personal appearance.

erythrocytemembrane.name: erythrocyte membrane
erythrocytemembrane.definition: Erythrocyte membrane is the semi-permeable outer structure of a red blood cell. It is known as a red cell 'ghost' after hemolysis.

receptors,estradiol.name: receptors , estradiol
receptors,estradiol.definition: Estradiol receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that bind estradiol, migrate to the nucleus, and regulate dna transcription.

foodtechnology.name: food technology
foodtechnology.definition: Food technology is the application of knowledge to the food industry.

nutproteins.name: nut proteins
nutproteins.definition: Nut proteins is proteins from nuts.

childabuse.name: child abuse
childabuse.definition: Child abuse is abuse of children in a family, institutional, or other setting. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

chromosomes,insect.name: chromosomes , insect
chromosomes,insect.definition: Insect chromosomes is structures within the cell nucleus of insect cells containing dna.

receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type1.name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 1
receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type1.definition: Type 1 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor with specificity for fibroblast growth factors; heparan sulfate proteoglycan; and neuronal cell adhesion molecules. Several variants of the receptor exist due to multiple [MASK] of its mRNA. Fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 contains three extracellular immunoglobulin c2-[MASK] domains and is a tyrosine kinase that transmits signals through the [MASK].

neonatalabstinencesyndrome.name: neonatal abstinence syndrome
neonatalabstinencesyndrome.definition: Neonatal abstinence syndrome is fetal and neonatal addiction and withdrawal as a result of the mother's dependence on drugs during pregnancy. Withdrawal or abstinence symptoms develop shortly after birth. Symptoms exhibited are loud, high-pitched crying, sweating, yawning and gastrointestinal disturbances.

epithelialcells.name: epithelial cells
epithelialcells.definition: Epithelial cells is cells that line the inner and outer surfaces of the body by forming cellular layers (epithelium) or masses. Epithelial cells lining the skin; the mouth; the nose; and the anal canal derive from ectoderm; those lining the respiratory system and the digestive system derive from endoderm; others (cardiovascular system and lymphatic system) derive from mesoderm. Epithelial cells can be classified mainly by cell shape and function into squamous, glandular and transitional epithelial cells.

heartinjuries.name: heart injuries
heartinjuries.definition: Heart injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the heart.

asianamericans.name: asian americans
asianamericans.definition: Asian americans is persons living in the United States having origins in any of the original peoples of the Far East, Southeast Asia, or the Indian subcontinent.

healthinformationsystems.name: health information systems
healthinformationsystems.definition: Health information systems is a system for the collection and/or processing of data from various sources, and using the information for policy making and management of health services. It could be [MASK]-based or electronic. (From http://web.worldbank.org/WBSITE/EXTERNAL/TOPICS/EXTHEALTHNUTRITIONANDPOPULATION/EXTHSD/0,,contentMDK:22239824~menuPK:376799~pagePK:148956~piPK:216618~theSitePK:376793,00.html. http://www.who.int/healthinfo/systems/en/)

olfactorypathways.name: olfactory pathways
olfactorypathways.definition: Olfactory pathways is [MASK] of nerve fibers conducting impulses from olfactory receptors to the cerebral cortex. It includes the olfactory nerve; olfactory bulb; olfactory tract; olfactory tubercle; anterior perforated substance; and olfactory cortex.

receptors,pituitaryhormone.name: receptors , pituitary hormone
receptors,pituitaryhormone.definition: Pituitary hormone receptors is cell surface proteins that bind pituitary hormones with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Since many pituitary hormones are also released by neurons as neurotransmitters, these receptors are also found in the nervous system.

highvocalcenter.name: high vocal center
highvocalcenter.definition: High vocal center is nucleus in the neostriatum of bird brains that sends signals for song production and receives auditory input. In some adult songbirds, research has shown that the size of this nucleus changes seasonally and that it exhibits neurogenesis.

sequencehomology,aminoacid.name: sequence homology , amino acid
sequencehomology,aminoacid.definition: Amino acid sequence homology is the degree of similarity between sequences of amino acids. This information is useful for the analyzing genetic relatedness of proteins and species.

autoantibodies.name: autoantibodies
autoantibodies.definition: Autoantibodies is antibodies that react with self-antigens (autoantigens) of the organism that produced them.

muscledevelopment.name: muscle development
muscledevelopment.definition: Muscle development is developmental events leading to the formation of adult muscular system, which includes differentiation of the various types of muscle cell precursors, migration of myoblasts, activation of myogenesis and development of muscle anchorage.

rehabilitationofspeechandlanguagedisorde.name: rehabilitation of speech and language disorders
rehabilitationofspeechandlanguagedisorde.definition: Rehabilitation of [MASK] and language disorders is procedures for assisting a person with a [MASK] or language disorder to communicate with maximum efficiency.

militarynursing.name: military nursing
militarynursing.definition: Military nursing is the practice of nursing in military environments.

needsassessment.name: needs assessment
needsassessment.definition: Needs assessment is systematic identification of a population's needs or the assessment of individuals to determine the proper level of services needed.

librarycollectiondevelopment.name: library collection development
librarycollectiondevelopment.definition: Library collection development is development of a library collection, including the determination and coordination of selection policy, assessment of needs of users and potential users, collection use studies, collection evaluation, identification of collection needs, selection of materials, planning for resource sharing, collection maintenance and weeding, and budgeting.

corrosioncasting.name: corrosion casting
corrosioncasting.definition: Corrosion casting is a tissue preparation technique that involves the injecting of plastic (acrylates) into blood vessels or other hollow viscera and treating the tissue with a caustic substance. This results in a negative copy or a solid replica of the enclosed space of the tissue that is ready for viewing under a scanning [MASK] microscope.

cannula.name: cannula
cannula.definition: Cannula is short, hollow cylinders or tubes for insertion into a canal, vessel, or body cavity.

sarcoma,experimental.name: sarcoma , experimental
sarcoma,experimental.definition: Experimental sarcoma is experimentally induced neoplasms of connective tissue in animals to provide a model for studying human sarcoma.

genes,cdc.name: genes , cdc
genes,cdc.definition: Cdc genes is genes that code for proteins that regulate the cell division cycle. These genes form a regulatory network that culminates in the onset of [MASK] by activating the p34cdc2 protein (protein p34cdc2).

africanhorsesicknessvirus.name: african horse sickness virus
africanhorsesicknessvirus.definition: African horse sickness virus is a species of orbivirus that causes disease in horses, mules, and donkeys. Via its principal vector culicoides, it can also infect dogs, elephants, camels, cattle, sheep, goats, and, in special circumstances, humans.

poisoning.name: poisoning
poisoning.definition: Poisoning is a condition or physical state produced by the ingestion, injection, [MASK] of or exposure to a deleterious agent.

factorxa.name: factor xa
factorxa.definition: Factor xa is activated form of factor x that participates in both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways of blood coagulation. It catalyzes the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin in conjunction with other cofactors.

ischemicpreconditioning.name: ischemic preconditioning
ischemicpreconditioning.definition: Ischemic preconditioning is a technique in which tissue is rendered resistant to the deleterious effects of prolonged ischemia and reperfusion by prior exposure to brief, repeated periods of vascular occlusion. (Am j Physiol 1995 May;268(5 Pt 2):h2063-7, [MASK])

globalburdenofdisease.name: global burden of disease
globalburdenofdisease.definition: Global burden of disease is measure of the burden of disease using the disability-adjusted-life-year (daly). This time-based measure combines years of life lost due to premature mortality and years of life lost due to time lived in states of less than full health. The metric was developed to assess the burden of disease consistently across diseases, risk factors and regions.

cardiacsurgicalprocedures.name: cardiac surgical procedures
cardiacsurgicalprocedures.definition: Cardiac surgical procedures is surgery performed on the heart.

anemia.name: anemia
anemia.definition: Anemia is a reduction in the number of circulating erythrocytes or in the quantity of hemoglobin.

psychologicaltests.name: psychological tests
psychologicaltests.definition: Psychological tests is standardized tests designed to measure abilities, as in intelligence, aptitude, and achievement tests, or to evaluate personality traits.

postoperativecare.name: postoperative care
postoperativecare.definition: Postoperative care is the period of care beginning when the patient is removed from surgery and aimed at meeting the patient's psychological and physical needs directly after surgery. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

behavioralresearch.name: behavioral research
behavioralresearch.definition: Behavioral research is research that involves the application of the behavioral and social sciences to the study of the actions or reactions of persons or animals in response to external or internal stimuli. (from American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed)

cardiaccatheterization.name: cardiac catheterization
cardiaccatheterization.definition: Cardiac catheterization is procedures in which placement of cardiac catheters is performed for therapeutic or diagnostic procedures.

reproductivehistory.name: reproductive history
reproductivehistory.definition: Reproductive history is an important aggregate factor in epidemiological studies of women's health. The concept usually includes the number and timing of pregnancies and their outcomes, the incidence of breast feeding, and may include age of menarche and menopause, regularity of menstruation, fertility, gynecological or obstetric problems, or contraceptive usage.

administration,mucosal.name: administration , mucosal
administration,mucosal.definition: Mucosal administration is delivery of a drug or other substance into the body through the epithelium lining of mucous membrane involved with absorption and secretion.

confidentiality.name: confidentiality
confidentiality.definition: Confidentiality is the privacy of information and its protection against unauthorized disclosure.

haplotypes.name: haplotypes
haplotypes.definition: Haplotypes is the genetic constitution of individuals with respect to one member of a pair of allelic genes, or sets of genes that are closely linked and tend to be inherited together such as those of the major histocompatibility complex.

vaginaldiseases.name: vaginal diseases
vaginaldiseases.definition: Vaginal diseases is pathological processes of the vagina.

arthroplasty,replacement,hip.name: arthroplasty , replacement , hip
arthroplasty,replacement,hip.definition: Hip replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the hip joint.

transcriptionalelongationfactors.name: transcriptional elongation factors
transcriptionalelongationfactors.definition: Transcriptional elongation factors is transcription factors whose primary function is to regulate the rate in which rna is transcribed.

butter.name: butter
butter.definition: Butter is the fatty portion of milk, separated as a soft yellowish solid when milk or cream is churned. It is processed for cooking and [MASK] use. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

hope.name: hope
hope.definition: Hope is belief in a positive outcome.

intestinalabsorption.name: intestinal absorption
intestinalabsorption.definition: Intestinal absorption is uptake of substances through the lining of the intestines.

familyseparation.name: family separation
familyseparation.definition: Family separation is geographic separation of members of a family.

faculty,dental.name: faculty , dental
faculty,dental.definition: Dental faculty is the teaching staff and members of the administrative staff having academic rank in a dental school.

korea.name: korea
korea.definition: Korea is former kingdom, located on Korea Peninsula between Sea of Japan and Yellow Sea on east coast of Asia. In 1948, the kingdom ceased and two independent countries were formed, divided by the 38th parallel.

economics,hospital.name: economics , hospital
economics,hospital.definition: Hospital economics is economic aspects related to the management and operation of a hospital.

externaldebt.name: external debt
externaldebt.definition: External debt is money owed to creditors outside of a country.

calciumcitrate.name: calcium citrate
calciumcitrate.definition: Calcium citrate is a colorless crystalline or [MASK] powdery organic, tricarboxylic acid occurring in plants, especially citrus fruits, and used as a flavoring agent, as an antioxidant in foods, and as a sequestrating agent. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

dentalpulptest.name: dental pulp test
dentalpulptest.definition: [MASK] test is investigations conducted on the physical health of teeth involving use of a tool that transmits hot or cold electric currents on a tooth's surface that can determine problems with that tooth based on reactions to the currents.

healthfacilityclosure.name: health facility closure
healthfacilityclosure.definition: Health facility closure is the closing of any health facility, e.g., health centers, residential facilities, and hospitals.

tensilestrength.name: tensile strength
tensilestrength.definition: Tensile strength is the maximum stress a material subjected to a stretching load can withstand without tearing. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed, p2001)

geneticservices.name: genetic services
geneticservices.definition: Genetic services is organized services to provide diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of genetic disorders.

dnavirusinfections.name: dna virus infections
dnavirusinfections.definition: Dna virus infections is diseases caused by dna viruses.

connectivetissue.name: connective tissue
connectivetissue.definition: Connective tissue is tissue that supports and binds other tissues. It consists of connective tissue cells embedded in a large amount of extracellular matrix.

pancreaticextracts.name: pancreatic extracts
pancreaticextracts.definition: Pancreatic extracts is extracts prepared from pancreatic tissue that may contain the pancreatic enzymes or other specific uncharacterized factors or proteins with specific activities. pancreatin is a specific extract containing digestive enzymes and used to treat pancreatic insufficiency.

books.name: books
books.definition: Books is non-periodical written or printed works consisting of sheets of pages fastened or bound together within covers.

neurology.name: neurology
neurology.definition: Neurology is a medical specialty concerned with the study of the structures, functions, and diseases of the nervous system.

dentalpulpcavity.name: dental pulp cavity
dentalpulpcavity.definition: [MASK] cavity is the space in a tooth bounded by the dentin and containing the [MASK]. The portion of the cavity within the crown of the tooth is the pulp chamber; the portion within the root is the pulp canal or root canal.

thymusgland.name: thymus gland
thymusgland.definition: Thymus gland is a single, unpaired primary lymphoid organ situated in the mediastinum, extending superiorly into the [MASK] to the lower edge of the thyroid gland and inferiorly to the fourth costal cartilage. It is necessary for normal development of immunologic function early in life. By puberty, it begins to involute and much of the tissue is replaced by fat.

antibodies,monoclonal.name: antibodies , monoclonal
antibodies,monoclonal.definition: Monoclonal antibodies is antibodies produced by a single clone of cells.

absorption.name: absorption
absorption.definition: Absorption is the physical or physiological processes by which substances, tissue, cells, etc. take up or take in other substances or energy.

oxidativecoupling.name: oxidative coupling
oxidativecoupling.definition: Oxidative coupling is the reaction of two molecular entities via oxidation usually catalyzed by a transition metal compound and involving dioxygen as the oxidant.

adaptation,ocular.name: adaptation , ocular
adaptation,ocular.definition: Ocular adaptation is the [MASK] of the eye to variations in the intensity of light. Light adaptation is the [MASK] of the eye when the light threshold is increased; dark adaptation when the light is greatly reduced. (From Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

rectaldiseases.name: rectal diseases
rectaldiseases.definition: Rectal diseases is pathological developments in the rectum region of the large intestine (intestine, large).

spaceflight.name: space flight
spaceflight.definition: Space flight is travel beyond the earth's atmosphere.

mentalprocesses.name: mental processes
mentalprocesses.definition: Mental processes is conceptual functions or thinking in all its forms.

silicon.name: silicon
silicon.definition: Silicon is a trace element that constitutes about 27.6% of the earth's crust in the form of silicon dioxide. It does not occur free in nature. Silicon has the atomic symbol Si, atomic number 14, and atomic weight [28.084; 28.086].

principalcomponentanalysis.name: principal component analysis
principalcomponentanalysis.definition: Principal component analysis is mathematical procedure that transforms a number of possibly correlated variables into a smaller number of uncorrelated variables called principal components.

smallfiberneuropathy.name: small fiber neuropathy
