smallfiberneuropathy.definition: Small fiber neuropathy is disorder of the peripheral nerves that primarily impair small nerve fibers. The affected small nerve fibers include myelinated A-delta fibers (see a fibers) and unmyelinated c fibers. Because these small fibers innervate skin and help control autonomic function, their neuropathy presents with neuropathic pain, reduced thermal and pain sensitivity, and autonomic dysfunction (e.g. abnormal sweating or facial flushing). Small fiber neuropathy can be idiopathic or associated with underlying diseases (e.g., amyloidosis; diabetes mellitus; sarcoidosis; or vasculitis).

vertebrates.name: vertebrates
vertebrates.definition: Vertebrates is animals having a vertebral column, members of the phylum Chordata, subphylum Craniata comprising mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.

meat.name: meat
meat.definition: Meat is the edible portions of any animal used for food including domestic mammals (the major ones being cattle, swine, and sheep) along with poultry, fish, shellfish, and game.

rootcanalfillingmaterials.name: root canal filling materials
rootcanalfillingmaterials.definition: Root canal filling materials is materials placed inside a root canal for the purpose of obturating or sealing it. The materials may be gutta-percha, silver cones, paste mixtures, or other substances. (Dorland, 28th ed, p631 & Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p187)

speciesspecificity.name: species specificity
speciesspecificity.definition: Species specificity is the restriction of a characteristic behavior, anatomical structure or physical system, such as immune response; metabolic response, or gene or gene variant to the members of one species. It refers to that property which differentiates one species from another but it is also used for phylogenetic levels higher or lower than the species.

ionmobilityspectrometry.name: ion mobility spectrometry
ionmobilityspectrometry.definition: Ion mobility spectrometry is techniques for separation and identification of ionized molecules based on their drift through a gas phase after being accelerated by an electric field. Their mobilities will be effected by their shape, size, and charge.

foreignprofessionalpersonnel.name: foreign professional personnel
foreignprofessionalpersonnel.definition: Foreign professional personnel is persons who have acquired academic or specialized training in countries other than that in which they are working. The concept excludes physicians for which foreign medical graduates is the likely heading.

watermovements.name: water movements
watermovements.definition: Water movements is the flow of water in enviromental bodies of water such as [MASK], oceans, water supplies, aquariums, etc. It includes currents, tides, and waves.

carcinoma,smallcell.name: carcinoma , small cell
carcinoma,smallcell.definition: Small cell carcinoma is an anaplastic, highly malignant, and usually bronchogenic carcinoma composed of small ovoid cells with scanty neoplasm. It is characterized by a dominant, deeply basophilic nucleus, and absent or indistinct nucleoli. (From Stedman, 25th ed; [MASK] et al., Cancer Medicine, 3d ed, p1286-7)

libraries,hospital.name: libraries , hospital
libraries,hospital.definition: Hospital libraries is information centers primarily serving the needs of [MASK] and sometimes also providing patient education and other services.

nuclearenvelope.name: nuclear envelope
nuclearenvelope.definition: Nuclear envelope is the membrane system of the cell nucleus that surrounds the nucleoplasm. It consists of two concentric membranes separated by the perinuclear space. The structures of the envelope where it opens to the cytoplasm are called the nuclear pores (nuclear pore).

rnasplicing.name: rna splicing
rnasplicing.definition: Rna splicing is the ultimate exclusion of nonsense sequences or intervening sequences (introns) before the final rna transcript is sent to the cytoplasm.

eating.name: eating
eating.definition: Eating is the consumption of edible substances.

sodiumchannelagonists.name: sodium channel agonists
sodiumchannelagonists.definition: Sodium channel agonists is a class of drugs that stimulate sodium influx through cell membrane channels.

bloodsafety.name: blood safety
bloodsafety.definition: Blood safety is the degree to which the blood supply for blood transfusions is free of harmful substances or infectious agents, and properly typed and crossmatched (blood grouping and crossmatching) to insure serological compatibility between blood donors and recipients.

serumsickness.name: serum sickness
serumsickness.definition: Serum sickness is immune complex disease caused by the administration of foreign serum or serum proteins and characterized by fever, lymphadenopathy, arthralgia, and urticaria. When they are complexed to protein carriers, some drugs can also cause serum sickness when they act as haptens inducing antibody responses.

colitis,ischemic.name: colitis , ischemic
colitis,ischemic.definition: Ischemic colitis is inflammation of the colon due to colonic ischemia resulting from alterations in systemic circulation or local vasculature.

cerebralsmallvesseldiseases.name: cerebral small vessel diseases
cerebralsmallvesseldiseases.definition: Cerebral small vessel diseases is pathological processes or diseases where cerebral microvessels show abnormalities. They are often associated with aging, hypertension and risk factors for lacunar infarcts (see lacunar infarction); leukoaraiosis; and cerebral hemorrhage.

infantequipment.name: infant equipment
infantequipment.definition: Infant equipment is equipment and furniture used by infants and babies in the home, car, and play area.

nurses,publichealth.name: nurses , public health
nurses,publichealth.definition: Public health nurses is nurses whose goal is to improve health and [MASK] in a population or community through the prevention and treatment of disease and other physical and mental health conditions, the surveillance of cases and health indicators, and the promotion of healthy behaviors through public education and awareness.

vaccines,inactivated.name: vaccines , inactivated
vaccines,inactivated.definition: Inactivated vaccines is vaccines in which the infectious microbial nucleic acid components have been destroyed by chemical or physical treatment (e.g., formalin, beta-propiolactone, gamma radiation) without affecting the antigenicity or immunogenicity of the viral coat or [MASK] proteins.

smoke.name: smoke
smoke.definition: Smoke is visible gaseous suspension of carbon and other particulate matter emitted from burning substances.

climate.name: climate
climate.definition: Climate is the longterm manifestations of weather. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

names.name: names
names.definition: Names is personal names, given or surname, as [MASK], as ethnological or religious patterns, as indications of the geographic distribution of families and inbreeding, etc. Analysis of isonymy, the quality of having the same or similar names, is useful in the study of population genetics. names is used also for the history of names or name changes of corporate bodies, such as medical societies, universities, hospitals, government agencies, etc.

food,preserved.name: food , preserved
food,preserved.definition: Preserved food is food that has been prepared and stored in a way to prevent spoilage.

chesttubes.name: chest tubes
chesttubes.definition: Chest tubes is plastic tubes used for drainage of air or fluid from the pleural space. Their surgical insertion is called tube thoracostomy.

remotesensingtechnology.name: remote sensing technology
remotesensingtechnology.definition: Remote sensing technology is [MASK] and acquisition of physical data from a distance by viewing and making measurements from a distance or receiving transmitted data from observations made at distant location.

publichealthinformatics.name: public health informatics
publichealthinformatics.definition: Public health informatics is the systematic application of information and computer sciences to public health practice, research, and learning.

peripheralnervoussystem.name: peripheral nervous system
peripheralnervoussystem.definition: Peripheral nervous system is the nervous system outside of the brain and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system has autonomic and somatic divisions. The autonomic nervous system includes the enteric, parasympathetic, and sympathetic subdivisions. The somatic nervous system includes the cranial and spinal nerves and their ganglia and the peripheral sensory receptors.

dentalstaff.name: dental staff
dentalstaff.definition: Dental staff is personnel who provide dental service to patients in an organized facility, institution or agency.

soilpollutants.name: soil pollutants
soilpollutants.definition: Soil pollutants is substances which pollute the soil. Use for soil pollutants in general or for which there is no specific heading.

nucleicacids.name: nucleic acids
nucleicacids.definition: Nucleic acids is high molecular weight polymers containing a mixture of purine and pyrimidine nucleotides chained together by ribose or deoxyribose linkages.

prosthesisfailure.name: prosthesis failure
prosthesisfailure.definition: Prosthesis failure is malfunction of implantation shunts, valves, etc., and prosthesis loosening, migration, and breaking.

respirationdisorders.name: respiration disorders
respirationdisorders.definition: Respiration disorders is diseases of the respiratory system in general or unspecified or for a specific respiratory disease not available.

england.name: england
england.definition: England is a part of Great Britain within the United Kingdom.

pparalpha.name: ppar alpha
pparalpha.definition: Ppar alpha is a nuclear transcription factor. Heterodimerization with retinoid x receptor gamma is important to metabolism of lipids. It is the target of fibrates to control hyperlipidemias.

antisenseelements(genetics).name: antisense elements ( genetics )
antisenseelements(genetics).definition: Antisense elements (genetics) is antisense elements ( genetics )

coronarythrombosis.name: coronary thrombosis
coronarythrombosis.definition: Coronary thrombosis is coagulation of blood in any of the coronary vessels. The presence of a blood clot (thrombus) often leads to myocardial infarction.

skinabnormalities.name: skin abnormalities
skinabnormalities.definition: Skin abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the skin.

peptideinitiationfactors.name: peptide initiation factors
peptideinitiationfactors.definition: Peptide initiation factors is protein factors uniquely required during the initiation phase of protein synthesis in genetic translation.

unitedstatesdepartmentofdefense.name: united states department of defense
unitedstatesdepartmentofdefense.definition: United states department of defense is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government whose mission is to provide the military forces needed to deter warfare and to protect the security of our country.

financialaudit.name: financial audit
financialaudit.definition: Financial audit is an examination, review and verification of all financial accounts.

hospitaladministrators.name: hospital administrators
hospitaladministrators.definition: Hospital administrators is managerial personnel responsible for implementing policy and directing the activities of hospitals.

ego.name: ego
ego.definition: Ego is the conscious portion of the personality structure which serves to mediate between the demands of the primitive instinctual drives, (the id), of internalized parental and social prohibitions or the conscience, (the superego), and of reality.

neurotoxicitysyndromes.name: neurotoxicity syndromes
neurotoxicitysyndromes.definition: Neurotoxicity syndromes is neurologic disorders caused by exposure to toxic substances through ingestion, injection, cutaneous application, or other method. This includes conditions caused by biologic, chemical, and pharmaceutical agents.

fisheries.name: fisheries
fisheries.definition: Fisheries is places for cultivation and harvesting of fish, particularly in sea waters. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

braininjury,chronic.name: brain injury , chronic
braininjury,chronic.definition: Chronic brain injury is conditions characterized by persistent brain damage or dysfunction as sequelae of cranial trauma. This disorder may result from diffuse axonal injury; intracranial hemorrhages; brain edema; and other conditions. Clinical features may include dementia; focal neurologic deficits; [MASK]; akinetic mutism; or coma.

jointcapsulerelease.name: joint capsule release
jointcapsulerelease.definition: Joint capsule release is surgical procedure to relax the joint capsule tissues in a joint that has a reduced range of motion due to contracture or tissue adhesions or joint deformities.

testicularneoplasms.name: testicular neoplasms
testicularneoplasms.definition: Testicular neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the testis. Germ cell tumors (germinoma) of the testis constitute 95% of all testicular neoplasms.

emotions.name: emotions
emotions.definition: Emotions is those affective states which can be experienced and have arousing and motivational properties.

actionspectrum.name: action spectrum
actionspectrum.definition: Action spectrum is a technique used to measure the rate of physiological activity plotted against wavelength of light. An action spectrum depicts the most effective wavelength of light (also known as spectral sensitivity) that is required for each specific process.

peritonealdialysis.name: peritoneal dialysis
peritonealdialysis.definition: Peritoneal dialysis is dialysis fluid being introduced into and removed from the peritoneal cavity as either a continuous or an intermittent procedure.

heatstressdisorders.name: heat stress disorders
heatstressdisorders.definition: Heat stress disorders is a group of conditions that develop due to overexposure or overexertion in excessive environmental heat.

toothwear.name: tooth wear
toothwear.definition: Tooth wear is loss of the tooth substance by chemical or mechanical processes

whitedotsyndromes.name: white dot syndromes
whitedotsyndromes.definition: [MASK] dot syndromes is a group of idiopathic multifocal posterior uveitis syndromes involving the choroid; [MASK] epithelium; and retina. They are characterized by multiple lesions of hypoautofluorescent dots in the fundus oculi and reduced visual acuity. Several entities including birdshot chorioretinopathy are hla-a antigens serotype a29 positive.

whitecoathypertension.name: white coat hypertension
whitecoathypertension.definition: [MASK] coat hypertension is phenomenon where blood pressure readings are elevated only when taken in clinical settings.

materialstesting.name: materials testing
materialstesting.definition: Materials testing is the testing of materials and devices, especially those used for prostheses and implants; sutures; tissue adhesives; etc., for hardness, strength, durability, safety, efficacy, and biocompatibility.

asymptomaticdiseases.name: asymptomatic diseases
asymptomaticdiseases.definition: Asymptomatic diseases is diseases that do not exhibit symptoms.

criticalcare.name: critical care
criticalcare.definition: Critical care is health care provided to a [MASK] patient during a medical emergency or crisis.

infarction.name: infarction
infarction.definition: Infarction is formation of an infarct, which is necrosis in tissue due to local ischemia resulting from obstruction of blood circulation, most commonly by a thrombus or embolus.

adultchildren.name: adult children
adultchildren.definition: Adult children is children who have reached maturity or the legal age of majority.

realitytesting.name: reality testing
realitytesting.definition: Reality testing is the individual's objective evaluation of the external world and the ability to differentiate adequately between it and the internal world; considered to be a primary ego function.

killerfactors,yeast.name: killer factors , yeast
killerfactors,yeast.definition: Yeast killer factors is protein factors released from one species of yeast that are selectively toxic to another species of yeast.

organizationalculture.name: organizational culture
organizationalculture.definition: Organizational culture is beliefs and values shared by all members of the organization. These shared values, which are subject to change, are reflected in the day to day management of the organization.

medialcollateralligament,knee.name: medial collateral ligament , knee
medialcollateralligament,knee.definition: [MASK] medial collateral ligament is the ligament that travels from the medial epicondyle of the femur to the medial margin and medial surface of the tibia. The medial meniscus is attached to its deep surface.

hipdislocation.name: hip dislocation
hipdislocation.definition: Hip dislocation is displacement of the femur bone from its normal position at the hip joint.

malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.name: malformations of cortical development , group i
malformationsofcorticaldevelopment,group.definition: Group i malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial cell proliferation or apoptosis in neurogenesis. This group includes congenital microcephalies; microlissencephalies, megalencephalies, hemimegalencephalies and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.

criminalbehavior.name: criminal behavior
criminalbehavior.definition: Criminal behavior is conduct leading to commission of unlawful acts.

meals.name: meals
meals.definition: Meals is a portion of the food eaten for the day, usually at regular occasions during the day.

eyebanks.name: eye banks
eyebanks.definition: Eye banks is centers for storing various parts of the eye for future use.

patientacuity.name: patient acuity
patientacuity.definition: Patient acuity is an assessment of a patient's illness, its chronicity, severity, and other qualitative aspects.

chromosomes,human,pair17.name: chromosomes , human , pair 17
chromosomes,human,pair17.definition: Pair 17 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group e chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

humangrowthhormone.name: human growth hormone
humangrowthhormone.definition: Human growth hormone is a 191-amino acid polypeptide hormone secreted by the human adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior), also known as gh or somatotropin. Synthetic growth hormone, termed somatropin, has replaced the natural form in therapeutic usage such as treatment of dwarfism in children with growth hormone deficiency.

handjoints.name: hand joints
handjoints.definition: Hand joints is the articulations extending from the wrist distally to the fingers. These include the wrist joint; carpal joints; metacarpophalangeal joint; and finger joint.

humanembryonicstemcells.name: human embryonic stem cells
humanembryonicstemcells.definition: Human embryonic stem cells is a type of pluripotent stem cells derived from early stage human embryos, up to and including the blastocyst stage.

sexuallytransmitteddiseases,viral.name: sexually transmitted diseases , viral
sexuallytransmitteddiseases,viral.definition: Viral sexually transmitted diseases is viral diseases which are transmitted or propagated by sexual conduct.

reactiveinhibition.name: reactive inhibition
reactiveinhibition.definition: Reactive inhibition is tendency toward a lessened strength of response due to practice or activity. It is independent of the effect of reward and is a direct function of time interval since the last response and the number of preceding responses.

stainlesssteel.name: stainless steel
stainlesssteel.definition: Stainless steel is stainless steel. a steel containing Ni, Cr, or both. It does not tarnish on exposure and is used in corrosive environments. (Grant & Hack's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

solaractivity.name: solar activity
solaractivity.definition: Solar activity is any type of variation in the appearance of energy output of the sun. (nasa Thesaurus, 1994)

volatileorganiccompounds.name: volatile organic compounds
volatileorganiccompounds.definition: Volatile organic compounds is organic compounds that have a relatively high [MASK] at room temperature.

coronaryaneurysm.name: coronary aneurysm
coronaryaneurysm.definition: Coronary aneurysm is abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of coronary vessels. Most coronary aneurysms are due to coronary atherosclerosis, and the rest are due to inflammatory diseases, such as kawasaki disease.

hivlongterminalrepeat.name: hiv long terminal repeat
hivlongterminalrepeat.definition: Hiv long terminal repeat is regulatory sequences important for viral replication that are located on each end of the hiv genome. The ltr includes the hiv enhancer, promoter, and other sequences. Specific regions in the ltr include the negative regulatory element (nre), NF-kappa b binding sites , Sp1 binding sites, tata box, and trans-acting responsive element (tar). The binding of both cellular and viral proteins to these regions regulates hiv transcription.

musculardystrophy,animal.name: muscular dystrophy , animal
musculardystrophy,animal.definition: Animal muscular dystrophy is muscular dystrophy that occurs in vertebrate animals.

ocularphysiologicalphenomena.name: ocular physiological phenomena
ocularphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Ocular physiological phenomena is processes and properties of the eye as a whole or of any of its parts.

graftvstumoreffect.name: graft vs tumor effect
graftvstumoreffect.definition: [MASK] vs tumor effect is immunological [MASK] of tumor tissue/cells following bone marrow transplantation.

researchpersonnel.name: research personnel
researchpersonnel.definition: Research personnel is those individuals engaged in research.

cataractextraction.name: cataract extraction
cataractextraction.definition: [MASK] extraction is the removal of a cataractous crystalline lens from the eye.

portalvein.name: portal vein
portalvein.definition: Portal vein is a short thick vein formed by union of the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein.

depressivedisorder,major.name: depressive disorder , major
depressivedisorder,major.definition: Major depressive disorder is disorder in which five (or more) of the following symptoms have been present during the same 2-week period and represent a change from previous functioning; at least one of the symptoms is either (1) depressed mood or (2) loss of interest or pleasure. Symptoms include: depressed mood most of the day, nearly every daily; markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities most of the day, nearly every day; significant weight loss when not dieting or weight gain; Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day; psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day; fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day; feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt; diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness, nearly every day; or  recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation without a specific plan, or a suicide attempt. (dsm-5)

occupationalinjuries.name: occupational injuries
occupationalinjuries.definition: Occupational injuries is injuries sustained from incidents in the course of work-related activities.

earthsciences.name: earth sciences
earthsciences.definition: Earth sciences is fields of science encompassing studies and research from the disciplines of physics; chemistry; biological sciences; and mathematics; that are related to the planet earth. Subfields include atmospheric chemistry; climatology; [MASK]; geography; geology; geophysics; meteorology; oceanography; paleontology; mineralogy; and seismology.

beer.name: beer
beer.definition: Beer is an alcoholic beverage usually made from malted cereal grain (as barley), flavored with hops, and brewed by slow fermentation.

intermittenturethralcatheterization.name: intermittent urethral catheterization
intermittenturethralcatheterization.definition: Intermittent urethral catheterization is insertion of a catheter into the urethra to drain the urine from the [MASK] at intervals as needed.

mandibularinjuries.name: mandibular injuries
mandibularinjuries.definition: Mandibular injuries is injuries to the lower jaw bone.

returntowork.name: return to work
returntowork.definition: Return to work is resumption of normal work routine following a hiatus or period of absence due to injury, disability, or other reasons.

genes,mcc.name: genes , mcc
genes,mcc.definition: Mcc genes is tumor suppressor genes located in the 5q21 region on the long [MASK] of human chromosome 5. The mutation of these genes is associated with the formation of colorectal cancer (mcc stands for mutated in colorectal cancer).

patientpositioning.name: patient positioning
patientpositioning.definition: Patient positioning is moving a patient into a specific position or posture to facilitate examination, surgery, or for therapeutic purposes.

animalscales.name: animal scales
animalscales.definition: Animal scales is tough, horny, brittle, smooth, striated or plate-like extensions of the stratum corneum or outer layer of the skin. It serves as a protective layer in fishes, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

highernervousactivity.name: higher nervous activity
highernervousactivity.definition: Higher nervous activity is a term used in Eastern European research literature on brain and behavior physiology for cortical functions. It refers to the highest level of integrative function of the brain, centered in the cerebral cortex, regulating language, thought, and behavior via sensory, motor, and cognitive processes.

alcoholdehydrogenase.name: alcohol dehydrogenase
alcoholdehydrogenase.definition: Alcohol dehydrogenase is a zinc-containing enzyme which oxidizes primary and secondary alcohols or hemiacetals in the presence of nad. In alcoholic fermentation, it catalyzes the final step of reducing an aldehyde to an alcohol in the presence of nadh and hydrogen.

phospholipased.name: phospholipase d
phospholipased.definition: Phospholipase d is an enzyme found mostly in plant tissue. It hydrolyzes glycerophosphatidates with the formation of a phosphatidic acid and a nitrogenous base such as choline. This enzyme also catalyzes transphosphatidylation reactions. ec 3.1.4.4.

infertility.name: infertility
infertility.definition: Infertility is a reduced or absent capacity to reproduce.

unitedstatespublichealthservice.name: united states public health service
unitedstatespublichealthservice.definition: United states public health service is a constituent organization of the department of health and human services concerned with protecting and improving the health of the nation.

smokingwaterpipes.name: smoking water pipes
smokingwaterpipes.definition: Smoking water pipes is pipes for smoking tobacco, cannabis, and other substances, in which smoke is drawn through water. Do not confuse with smoking pipes.

brainchemistry.name: brain chemistry
brainchemistry.definition: Brain chemistry is changes in the amounts of various chemicals (neurotransmitters, receptors, enzymes, and other metabolites) specific to the area of the central nervous system contained within the head. These are monitored over time, during sensory stimulation, or under different disease states.

mutationaccumulation.name: mutation accumulation
mutationaccumulation.definition: Mutation accumulation is concept which describes the incremental effects of mutation in living organisms.

unsupervisedmachinelearning.name: unsupervised machine learning
unsupervisedmachinelearning.definition: Unsupervised machine learning is a machine learning paradigm used to make predictions about future instances based on a given [MASK] of unlabeled paired input-output training (sample) data.

vaccines,conjugate.name: vaccines , conjugate
vaccines,conjugate.definition: Conjugate vaccines is semisynthetic vaccines consisting of polysaccharide antigens from microorganisms attached to protein carrier molecules. The carrier protein is recognized by macrophages and T-cells thus enhancing immunity. Conjugate vaccines induce antibody formation in people not responsive to polysaccharide alone, induce higher levels of antibody, and show a booster response on repeated injection.

carotidarteryinjuries.name: carotid artery injuries
carotidarteryinjuries.definition: Carotid artery injuries is damages to the carotid arteries caused either by blunt force or penetrating trauma, such as craniocerebral trauma; thoracic injuries; and [MASK] injuries. Damaged carotid arteries can lead to [MASK]; carotid-cavernous sinus fistula; [MASK] formation; and internal carotid artery [MASK]. (From Am j Forensic Med Pathol 1997, 18:251; j Trauma 1994, 37:473)

rnafolding.name: rna folding
rnafolding.definition: Rna folding is the processes of rna tertiary structure formation.

complementmembraneattackcomplex.name: complement membrane attack complex
complementmembraneattackcomplex.definition: Complement membrane attack complex is a product of complement activation cascade, regardless of the pathways, that forms transmembrane channels causing disruption of the target cell membrane and cell lysis. It is formed by the sequential assembly of terminal complement components (complement c5b; complement c6; complement c7; complement c8; and complement c9) into the target membrane. The resultant C5b-8-poly-C9 is the "membrane attack complex" or mac.

femoralfractures.name: femoral fractures
femoralfractures.definition: Femoral fractures is fractures of the femur.

disasterplanning.name: disaster planning
disasterplanning.definition: Disaster planning is procedures outlined for the care of casualties and the maintenance of services in disasters.

polyc.name: poly c
polyc.definition: Poly c is a group of cytosine ribonucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each cytosine ribonucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the ribose moieties.

association.name: association
association.definition: Association is a functional relationship between psychological phenomena of such nature that the presence of one tends to evoke the other; also, the process by which such a relationship is established.

hospitaldistributionsystems.name: hospital distribution systems
hospitaldistributionsystems.definition: Hospital distribution systems is systems for delivering hospital supplies, food, laundry, etc., to patient care areas.

bookclassification.name: book classification
bookclassification.definition: Book classification is a general term covering bibliographical and bibliothecal classifications. It mostly refers to library classification for arrangement of books and documents on the shelves. (Harrod's Librarians' Glossary, 7th ed, p85)

thyroid(usp).name: thyroid ( usp )
thyroid(usp).definition: Thyroid (usp) is a dehydrated extract of thyroid glands from domesticated animals. After the removal of fat and connective tissue, the extract is dried or lyophilized to yield a yellowish to buff-colored amorphous powder containing 0.17-0.23% of iodine.

phenotype.name: phenotype
phenotype.definition: Phenotype is the outward appearance of the individual. It is the product of interactions between genes, and between the genotype and the environment.

autoimmunediseasesofthenervoussystem.name: autoimmune diseases of the nervous system
autoimmunediseasesofthenervoussystem.definition: Autoimmune diseases of the nervous system is disorders caused by cellular or humoral immune responses primarily directed towards nervous system autoantigens. The immune response may be directed towards specific tissue components (e.g., myelin) and may be limited to the central nervous system (e.g., multiple [MASK]) or the peripheral nervous system (e.g., guillain-barre syndrome).

compartmentsyndromes.name: compartment syndromes
compartmentsyndromes.definition: Compartment syndromes is conditions in which increased pressure within a limited space compromises the blood circulation and function of tissue within that space. Some of the causes of increased pressure are trauma, tight dressings, hemorrhage, and exercise. Sequelae include nerve compression (nerve compression syndromes); paralysis; and ischemic contracture. fasciotomy is often used to decompress increased pressure and eliminate pain associated with compartment syndromes.

socialcontrol,informal.name: social control , informal
socialcontrol,informal.definition: Informal social control is those forms of control which are exerted in less concrete and tangible ways, as through folkways, mores, conventions, and public sentiment.

genes,immunoglobulinlightchain.name: genes , immunoglobulin light chain
genes,immunoglobulinlightchain.definition: Immunoglobulin light chain genes is genes and gene segments encoding the immunoglobulin light chains. Gene segments of the light chain genes are designated as v (variable), j (joining), and c (constant).

encephalitis,japanese.name: encephalitis , japanese
encephalitis,japanese.definition: Japanese encephalitis is a mosquito-borne encephalitis caused by the Japanese b encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, japanese) occurring throughout Eastern Asia and Australia. The majority of infections occur in children and are subclinical or have features limited to transient fever and gastrointestinal symptoms. Inflammation of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges may occur and lead to transient or permanent neurologic deficits (including a POLIOMYELITIS-like presentation); seizures; coma; and death. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p751; Lancet 1998 Apr 11;351(9109):1094-7)

severeacuterespiratorysyndrome.name: severe acute respiratory syndrome
severeacuterespiratorysyndrome.definition: Severe acute respiratory syndrome is a viral disorder characterized by high fever, dry [MASK], shortness of breath (dyspnea) or breathing difficulties, and atypical pneumonia. a virus in the genus coronavirus is the suspected agent.

carcinomainsitu.name: carcinoma in situ
carcinomainsitu.definition: Carcinoma in situ is a lesion with cytological characteristics associated with invasive carcinoma but the tumor cells are confined to the epithelium of origin, without invasion of the basement membrane.

dopamineuptakeinhibitors.name: dopamine uptake inhibitors
dopamineuptakeinhibitors.definition: Dopamine uptake inhibitors is drugs that block the transport of dopamine into axon terminals or into storage vesicles within terminals. Most of the adrenergic uptake inhibitors also inhibit dopamine uptake.

reactiontime.name: reaction time
reactiontime.definition: Reaction time is the time from the onset of a stimulus until a response is observed.

serumamyloidaprotein.name: serum amyloid a protein
serumamyloidaprotein.definition: Serum amyloid a protein is an acute phase reaction protein present in low concentrations in normal sera, but found at higher concentrations in sera of older persons and in patients with amyloidosis. It is the circulating precusor of amyloid a protein, which is found deposited in aa type amyloid fibrils.

rna,transfer,ser.name: rna , transfer , ser
rna,transfer,ser.definition: Ser transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying serine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

rehabilitationcenters.name: rehabilitation centers
rehabilitationcenters.definition: Rehabilitation centers is facilities which provide programs for rehabilitating the mentally or physically disabled individuals.

cyclinc.name: cyclin c
cyclinc.definition: Cyclin c is a cyclin subtype that binds to the cyclin-dependent kinase 3 and cyclin-dependent kinase 8. Cyclin c plays a dual role as a transcriptional regulator and a g1 phase cell cycle regulator.

marinebiology.name: marine biology
marinebiology.definition: Marine biology is the study of the origin, structure, development, growth, function, genetics, and reproduction of organisms which inhabit the oceans and seas.

translationalmedicalresearch.name: translational medical research
translationalmedicalresearch.definition: Translational medical research is the application of discoveries generated by laboratory research and preclinical studies to the development of clinical trials and studies in humans. a second area of translational research concerns enhancing the adoption of [MASK].

focaladhesions.name: focal adhesions
focaladhesions.definition: Focal adhesions is an anchoring junction of the cell to a non-cellular substrate. It is composed of a specialized area of the plasma membrane where bundles of the actin cytoskeleton terminate and attach to the transmembrane linkers, integrins, which in turn attach through their extracellular domains to extracellular matrix proteins.

dentalrestorationfailure.name: dental restoration failure
dentalrestorationfailure.definition: Dental restoration failure is inability or inadequacy of a dental restoration or prosthesis to perform as expected.

polyg.name: poly g
polyg.definition: Poly g is a group of guanine ribonucleotides in which the phosphate residues of each guanine ribonucleotide act as bridges in forming diester linkages between the ribose moieties.

nucleotidemapping.name: nucleotide mapping
nucleotidemapping.definition: Nucleotide mapping is two-dimensional separation and analysis of nucleotides.

neuralpathways.name: neural pathways
neuralpathways.definition: Neural pathways is neural tracts connecting one part of the nervous system with another.

ultrasonography,doppler.name: ultrasonography , doppler
ultrasonography,doppler.definition: Doppler ultrasonography is ultrasonography applying the Doppler effect, with frequency-shifted ultrasound reflections produced by moving targets (usually red blood cells) in the bloodstream along the ultrasound axis in direct proportion to the velocity of movement of the targets, to determine both direction and velocity of blood flow. (Stedman, 25th ed)

aorticaneurysm.name: aortic aneurysm
aorticaneurysm.definition: Aortic aneurysm is an abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of aorta.

ventricularoutflowobstruction.name: ventricular outflow obstruction
ventricularoutflowobstruction.definition: Ventricular outflow obstruction is occlusion of the outflow tract in either the left ventricle or the right ventricle of the heart. This may result from congenital heart defects, predisposing heart diseases, complications of surgery, or [MASK].

adenovirusinfections,human.name: adenovirus infections , human
adenovirusinfections,human.definition: Human adenovirus infections is respiratory and conjunctival infections caused by 33 identified serotypes of human adenoviruses.

yellowfevervirus.name: yellow fever virus
yellowfevervirus.definition: Yellow fever virus is the type species of the flavivirus genus. Principal vector transmission to humans is by aedes spp. mosquitoes.

ethiopia.name: ethiopia
ethiopia.definition: Ethiopia is an independent state in eastern Africa. Ethiopia is located in the Horn of Africa and is bordered on the north and northeast by Eritrea, on the east by Djibouti and Somalia, on the south by Kenya, and on the west and southwest by Sudan. Its capital is Addis Ababa.

organicaniontransporters.name: organic anion transporters
organicaniontransporters.definition: Organic anion transporters is proteins involved in the transport of organic anions. They play an important role in the elimination of a variety of endogenous substances, xenobiotics and their metabolites from the body.

placeboeffect.name: placebo effect
placeboeffect.definition: Placebo effect is an effect usually, but not necessarily, beneficial that is attributable to an expectation that the regimen will have an effect, i.e., the effect is due to the power of suggestion.

dictionary,medical.name: dictionary , medical
dictionary,medical.definition: Medical dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to medicine-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

postoperativeperiod.name: postoperative period
postoperativeperiod.definition: Postoperative period is the period following a surgical operation.

thoracicsurgery.name: thoracic surgery
thoracicsurgery.definition: Thoracic surgery is a surgical specialty concerned with diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the heart, lungs, and esophagus. Two major types of thoracic surgery are classified as pulmonary and cardiovascular.

rnapolymeraseii.name: rna polymerase ii
rnapolymeraseii.definition: Rna polymerase ii is a DNA-dependent rna polymerase present in bacterial, plant, and animal cells. It functions in the nucleoplasmic structure and transcribes dna into rna. It has different requirements for cations and [MASK] than rna polymerase i and is strongly inhibited by alpha-amanitin. ec 2.7.7.6.

esophagealsquamouscellcarcinoma.name: esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
esophagealsquamouscellcarcinoma.definition: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a carcinoma that originates usually from cells on the surface of the middle and lower third of the esophagus. Tumor cells exhibit typical squamous morphology and form large polypoid lesions. Mutations in rnf6, lzts1, tgfbr2, dec1, and wwox1 genes are associated with this cancer.

cytoplasmicstructures.name: cytoplasmic structures
cytoplasmicstructures.definition: Cytoplasmic structures is components of the cytoplasm excluding the [MASK].

waterwells.name: water wells
waterwells.definition: Water wells is constructions built to access underground water.

lactationdisorders.name: lactation disorders
lactationdisorders.definition: Lactation disorders is disturbances of milk secretion in either [MASK], not necessarily related to pregnancy.

neuroblastoma.name: neuroblastoma
neuroblastoma.definition: Neuroblastoma is a common neoplasm of early childhood arising from neural crest cells in the sympathetic nervous system, and characterized by diverse clinical behavior, ranging from spontaneous remission to rapid metastatic progression and death. This tumor is the most common intraabdominal malignancy of childhood, but it may also arise from thorax, [MASK], or rarely occur in the central nervous system. Histologic features include uniform round cells with hyperchromatic nuclei arranged in nests and separated by fibrovascular septa. Neuroblastomas may be associated with the opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome. (From DeVita et al., Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology, 5th ed, pp2099-2101; Curr Opin Oncol 1998 Jan;10(1):43-51)

poissondistribution.name: poisson distribution
poissondistribution.definition: Poisson distribution is a distribution function used to describe the occurrence of rare events or to describe the sampling distribution of isolated counts in a continuum of time or space.

angioplasty,balloon.name: angioplasty , balloon
angioplasty,balloon.definition: Balloon angioplasty is use of a balloon catheter for dilation of an occluded artery. It is used in treatment of arterial occlusive diseases, including [MASK] stenosis and arterial occlusions in the leg. For the specific technique of balloon dilation in coronary arteries, [MASK] is available.

asia,western.name: asia , western
asia,western.definition: Western asia is the geographical designation for the countries of the middle east and the countries bangladesh; bhutan; india; nepal; pakistan; and sri lanka. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed, 1993 & Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988)

behaviorandbehaviormechanisms.name: behavior and behavior mechanisms
behaviorandbehaviormechanisms.definition: Behavior and behavior mechanisms is the observable response made to a situation and the [MASK] processes underlying it.

homesfortheaged.name: homes for the aged
homesfortheaged.definition: Homes for the aged is geriatric long-term care facilities which provide supervision and assistance in activities of daily living with medical and nursing services when required.

vitamin.name: vitamin
vitamin.definition: Vitamin is organic substances that are required in small amounts for maintenance and growth, but which cannot be manufactured by the [MASK].

medicine,africantraditional.name: medicine , african traditional
medicine,africantraditional.definition: African traditional medicine is a system of traditional medicine which is based on the beliefs and practices of the African peoples. It includes treatment by [MASK] and other materia medica as well as by the ministrations of diviners, medicine men, witch doctors, and sorcerers.

methionine.name: methionine
methionine.definition: Methionine is a sulfur-containing essential L-amino acid that is important in many body functions.

mammaryglands,animal.name: mammary glands , animal
mammaryglands,animal.definition: Animal mammary glands is mammary glands in the non-human mammals.

genetictherapy.name: genetic therapy
genetictherapy.definition: Genetic therapy is techniques and strategies which include the use of coding sequences and other conventional or radical means to transform or modify cells for the purpose of treating or reversing disease conditions.

coldclimate.name: cold climate
coldclimate.definition: Cold climate is a climate characterized by cold temperature for a majority of the time during the year.

birds.name: birds
birds.definition: Birds is warm-blooded vertebrates possessing feathers and belonging to the class Aves.

biomedicaloccupationordiscipline.name: biomedical occupation or discipline
biomedicaloccupationordiscipline.definition: Biomedical occupation or discipline is all of the divisions of the natural sciences dealing with the various aspects of the phenomena of life and vital processes.

lymphocytetransfusion.name: lymphocyte transfusion
lymphocytetransfusion.definition: Lymphocyte transfusion is the transfer of lymphocytes from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor.

magnesiumchloride.name: magnesium chloride
magnesiumchloride.definition: Magnesium chloride is magnesium chloride. An inorganic compound consisting of one magnesium and two chloride ions. The compound is used in medicine as a source of magnesium ions, which are essential for many cellular activities. It has also been used as a cathartic and in alloys.

copyingprocesses.name: copying processes
copyingprocesses.definition: Copying processes is reproduction of data in a new location or other destination, leaving the source data unchanged, although the physical form of the result may differ from that of the source.

tuberculosis.name: tuberculosis
tuberculosis.definition: Tuberculosis is any of the infectious diseases of man and other animals caused by species of [MASK].

dendriticspines.name: dendritic spines
dendriticspines.definition: Dendritic spines is spiny processes on dendrites, each of which receives excitatory input from one nerve ending (nerve endings). They are commonly found on purkinje cells and pyramidal cells.

bodysubstance.name: body substance
bodysubstance.definition: Body substance is the substance of the body.

nursingresearch.name: nursing research
nursingresearch.definition: Nursing research is research carried out by nurses, generally in clinical settings, in the areas of clinical practice, evaluation, nursing education, nursing administration, and methodology.

childguidanceclinics.name: child guidance clinics
childguidanceclinics.definition: Child guidance clinics is facilities which administer the delivery of mental health counseling services to children.

cornealedema.name: corneal edema
cornealedema.definition: Corneal edema is an excessive amount of fluid in the cornea due to damage of the epithelium or endothelium causing decreased visual acuity.

congenitalabnormality.name: congenital abnormality
congenitalabnormality.definition: Congenital abnormality is malformations of organs or [MASK] during development in utero.

mentalcompetency.name: mental competency
mentalcompetency.definition: Mental competency is the ability to understand the nature and effect of the act in which the individual is engaged. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 6th ed).

cerebrospinalfluidproteins.name: cerebrospinal fluid proteins
cerebrospinalfluidproteins.definition: Cerebrospinal fluid proteins is proteins in the cerebrospinal fluid, normally albumin and globulin present in the ratio of 8 to 1. Increases in protein levels are of diagnostic value in neurological diseases. (Brain and Bannister's Clinical Neurology, 7th ed, p221)

informationstorageandretrieval.name: information storage and retrieval
informationstorageandretrieval.definition: Information storage and retrieval is organized activities related to the storage, location, search, and retrieval of information.

nitricoxidedonors.name: nitric oxide donors
nitricoxidedonors.definition: [MASK] donors is a diverse group of agents, with unique chemical structures and biochemical requirements, which generate [MASK]. These compounds have been used in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases and the management of acute myocardial infarction, acute and chronic congestive heart failure, and surgical control of blood pressure. (Adv Pharmacol 1995;34:361-81)

opioidpeptides.name: opioid peptides
opioidpeptides.definition: Opioid peptides is the endogenous peptides with opiate-like activity. The three major classes currently recognized are the enkephalins, the dynorphins, and the endorphins. Each of these families derives from different precursors, proenkephalin, prodynorphin, and pro-opiomelanocortin, respectively. There are also at least three classes of opioid receptors, but the peptide families do not map to the receptors in a simple way.

rnacaps.name: rna caps
rnacaps.definition: Rna caps is nucleic acid structures found on the 5' end of eukaryotic cellular and viral messenger rna and some heterogeneous nuclear RNAs. These structures, which are positively charged, protect the above specified RNAs at their termini against attack by phosphatases and other nucleases and promote mRNA function at the level of initiation of translation. Analogs of the rna caps (rna cap analogs), which lack the positive charge, inhibit the initiation of protein synthesis.

dentdisease.name: dent disease
dentdisease.definition: Dent disease is x-linked recessive nephrolithiasis characterized by hypercalciuria; hypophosphatemia; nephrocalcinosis; and proteinuria. It is associated with mutations in the voltage-gated chloride channel, clc-5 (Dent Disease i). Another group of mutations associated with this disease is in phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate-5-phosphatase gene.

nebraska.name: nebraska
nebraska.definition: Nebraska is state bounded on the north by South Dakota, on the east by Iowa and Missouri, on the south by Kansas and Colorado, and on the west by Colorado and Wyoming.

radiationprotection.name: radiation protection
radiationprotection.definition: Radiation protection is methods and practices adopted to protect against radiation.

ribosomesubunits,small,bacterial.name: ribosome subunits , small , bacterial
ribosomesubunits,small,bacterial.definition: Bacterial small ribosome subunits is the small subunit of eubacterial ribosomes. It is composed of the 16s [MASK] and about 23 different ribosomal proteins.

enzymeinhibitors.name: enzyme inhibitors
enzymeinhibitors.definition: Enzyme inhibitors is compounds or agents that combine with an enzyme in such a manner as to prevent the normal substrate-enzyme combination and the catalytic reaction.

urbanrenewal.name: urban renewal
urbanrenewal.definition: Urban renewal is the planned upgrading of a deteriorating urban area, involving rebuilding, renovation, or restoration. It frequently refers to programs of major demolition and rebuilding of blighted areas.

receptors,interleukin.name: receptors , interleukin
receptors,interleukin.definition: Interleukin receptors is cell surface proteins that bind interleukins and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

dentalocclusion.name: dental occlusion
dentalocclusion.definition: Dental occlusion is the relationship of all the components of the masticatory system in normal function. It has special reference to the position and contact of the maxillary and mandibular teeth for the highest efficiency during the excursive movements of the jaw that are essential for mastication. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p556, p472)

interpersonalrelations.name: interpersonal relations
interpersonalrelations.definition: Interpersonal relations is the reciprocal interaction of two or more persons.

legalepidemiology.name: legal epidemiology
legalepidemiology.definition: Legal epidemiology is scientific study of law as a factor in the cause, distribution, and prevention of disease and injury.  (From https://read.dukeupress.edu/jhppl/article/41/6/1151/40084/Policy-Surveillance-A-Vital-Public-Health-Practice).

twisttranscriptionfactors.name: twist transcription factors
twisttranscriptionfactors.definition: Twist transcription factors is a  highly-conserved family of basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors.  They function as dimers with other bHLH proteins and bind e-box elements to control gene expression during embryogenesis and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

polymerasechainreaction.name: polymerase chain reaction
polymerasechainreaction.definition: Polymerase chain reaction is in vitro method for producing large amounts of specific dna or rna fragments of defined length and sequence from small amounts of short oligonucleotide flanking sequences (primers). The essential steps include thermal denaturation of the double-stranded target molecules, annealing of the primers to their complementary sequences, and extension of the annealed primers by enzymatic synthesis with dna polymerase. The reaction is efficient, specific, and extremely sensitive. Uses for the reaction include disease diagnosis, detection of difficult-to-isolate pathogens, mutation analysis, genetic testing, dna sequencing, and analyzing evolutionary relationships.

fluorescence.name: fluorescence
fluorescence.definition: Fluorescence is the property of emitting radiation while being irradiated. The radiation emitted is usually of longer wavelength than that incident or absorbed, e.g., a substance can be irradiated with invisible radiation and emit visible light. X-ray fluorescence is used in diagnosis.

contraceptivedevices.name: contraceptive devices
contraceptivedevices.definition: Contraceptive devices is devices that diminish the likelihood of or prevent conception. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

financialsupport.name: financial support
financialsupport.definition: Financial support is the provision of monetary resources including money or capital and credit; obtaining or furnishing money or capital for a purchase or enterprise and the funds so obtained. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed.)

naturalsciencedisciplines.name: natural science disciplines
naturalsciencedisciplines.definition: Natural science disciplines is the sciences dealing with processes observable in nature.

embryonicstructure.name: embryonic structure
embryonicstructure.definition: Embryonic structure is the anatomical parts that make up an organism in the early stages of development.

shock,surgical.name: shock , surgical
shock,surgical.definition: Surgical shock is a type of shock that occurs as a result of a surgical procedure.

nursingtheory.name: nursing theory
nursingtheory.definition: Nursing theory is concepts, definitions, and propositions applied to the study of various phenomena which pertain to nursing and nursing research.

exchangetransfusion,wholeblood.name: exchange transfusion , whole blood
exchangetransfusion,wholeblood.definition: Whole blood exchange transfusion is repetitive withdrawal of small amounts of blood and replacement with donor blood until a large proportion of the blood volume has been exchanged. Used in treatment of fetal erythroblastosis, hepatic coma, sickle cell anemia, disseminated intravascular coagulation, septicemia, burns, thrombotic thrombopenic purpura, and fulminant malaria.

waterpipesmoking.name: water pipe smoking
waterpipesmoking.definition: Water pipe smoking is a process by which smoke produced from burning substance is mixed with flavor-altering substances and drawn through water or other liquid into the mouth.

tumornecrosisfactorinhibitors.name: tumor necrosis factor inhibitors
tumornecrosisfactorinhibitors.definition: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors is compounds or agents that bind to and inhibit the synthesis or activity of tumor necrosis FACTOR-alpha. Such agents are used to treat inflammatory bowel diseases and other inflammatory diseases.

exosomes.name: exosomes
exosomes.definition: Exosomes is a type of extracellular vesicle, containing rna and proteins, that is secreted into the extracellular space by exocytosis when multivesicular bodies fuse with the plasma membrane.

cytochromebgroup.name: cytochrome b group
cytochromebgroup.definition: Cytochrome b group is cytochromes ([MASK]-transporting proteins) with protoheme (heme b) as the prosthetic group.

behavior.name: behavior
behavior.definition: Behavior is the observable response of a man or animal to a situation.

chart.name: chart
chart.definition: Chart is work consisting of information presented in graphic form, for example, graphs or diagrams.

genome,plant.name: genome , plant
genome,plant.definition: Plant genome is the genetic complement of a plant (plants) as represented in its dna.

intracranialhypotension.name: intracranial hypotension
intracranialhypotension.definition: Intracranial hypotension is reduction of cerebrospinal fluid pressure characterized clinically by orthostatic headache and occasionally by an abducens nerve palsy; hearing loss; nausea; [MASK] stiffness, and other symptoms. This condition may be spontaneous or secondary to cerebrospinal fluid leak; [MASK]; neurosurgical procedures; [MASK]; uremia; trauma (see also craniocerebral trauma); and other processes. Chronic hypotension may be associated with subdural hematomas (see hematoma, subdural) or hygromas. (From Semin Neurol 1996 Mar;16(1):5-10; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp637-8)

vomiting.name: vomiting
vomiting.definition: Vomiting is the forcible expulsion of the contents of the stomach through the mouth.

middleeast.name: middle east
middleeast.definition: Middle east is the region of southwest Asia and northeastern Africa usually considered as extending from Libya on the west to Afghanistan on the east. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988)

hypoxia.name: hypoxia
hypoxia.definition: Hypoxia is sub-optimal oxygen levels in the ambient air of living organisms.

adolescentmedicine.name: adolescent medicine
adolescentmedicine.definition: Adolescent medicine is a branch of medicine pertaining to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases occurring during the period of adolescence.

basesequence.name: base sequence
basesequence.definition: Base sequence is the sequence of purines and pyrimidines in nucleic acids and polynucleotides. It is also called nucleotide sequence.

cranialfossa,anterior.name: cranial fossa , anterior
cranialfossa,anterior.definition: Anterior cranial fossa is the compartment containing the inferior part and anterior extremities of the frontal lobes (frontal lobe) of the cerebral hemispheres. It is formed mainly by orbital parts of the [MASK] and the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone.

genome,fungal.name: genome , fungal
genome,fungal.definition: Fungal genome is the complete gene complement contained in a [MASK] of chromosomes in a fungus.

thymushormones.name: thymus hormones
thymushormones.definition: Thymus hormones is humoral factors secreted by the thymus gland. They participate in the development of the lymphoid system and the maturation of the cellular immune response.

bloodcomponenttransfusion.name: blood component transfusion
bloodcomponenttransfusion.definition: Blood component transfusion is the transfer of blood components such as erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets, and plasma from a donor to a recipient or back to the donor. This process differs from the procedures undertaken in plasmapheresis and types of cytapheresis; (plateletpheresis and leukapheresis) where, following the removal of plasma or the specific cell components, the remainder is transfused back to the donor.

hipprosthesis.name: hip prosthesis
hipprosthesis.definition: Hip prosthesis is replacement for a hip joint.

bodyheight.name: body height
bodyheight.definition: Body height is the distance from the sole to the crown of the head with body standing on a flat surface and fully extended.

chemicalsafety.name: chemical safety
chemicalsafety.definition: Chemical safety is risk or hazard associated with the handling and use of chemicals.

jointinstability.name: joint instability
jointinstability.definition: Joint instability is lack of stability of a joint or joint prosthesis.

emergencytreatment.name: emergency treatment
emergencytreatment.definition: Emergency treatment is [MASK] or other immediate intervention for accidents or medical conditions requiring immediate care and treatment before definitive medical and surgical management can be procured.

solarsystem.name: solar system
solarsystem.definition: Solar system is the group of celestial bodies, including the earth, orbiting around and gravitationally bound by the sun. It includes eight planets, one minor planet, and 34 natural satellites, more than 1,000 observed comets, and thousands of lesser bodies known as minor planets (asteroids) and meteoroids. (From Academic American Encyclopedia, 1983)

chromatography,liquid.name: chromatography , liquid
chromatography,liquid.definition: Liquid chromatography is chromatographic techniques in which the mobile phase is a liquid.

industrialmicrobiology.name: industrial microbiology
industrialmicrobiology.definition: Industrial microbiology is the study, utilization, and manipulation of those microorganisms capable of economically producing desirable substances or changes in substances, and the control of undesirable microorganisms.

chromosomemapping.name: chromosome mapping
chromosomemapping.definition: Chromosome mapping is any method used for determining the location of and relative distances between genes on a chromosome.

salmonellavaccines.name: salmonella vaccines
salmonellavaccines.definition: Salmonella vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with salmonella. This includes vaccines used to prevent typhoid fever or paratyphoid fever; (typhoid-paratyphoid vaccines), and vaccines used to prevent nontyphoid salmonellosis.

animalshells.name: animal shells
animalshells.definition: Animal shells is the hard rigid covering of animals including molluscs; turtles; insects; and crustaceans.

jobsatisfaction.name: job satisfaction
jobsatisfaction.definition: Job [MASK] is [MASK] relative to the work situation.

nurses,pediatric.name: nurses , pediatric
nurses,pediatric.definition: Pediatric nurses is qualified nursing professionals specializing in the care of children from birth to adolescence.

residentialtreatment.name: residential treatment
residentialtreatment.definition: Residential treatment is a specialized residential treatment program for behavior disorders including substance abuse. It may include therapeutically planned group living and learning situations including teaching of adaptive skills to help patient functioning in the community. (From Kahn, a. p. and Fawcett, j. Encyclopedia of Mental Health, 1993, p320.)

coronaryvessels.name: coronary vessels
coronaryvessels.definition: Coronary vessels is the veins and arteries of the heart.

arthritis,experimental.name: arthritis , experimental
arthritis,experimental.definition: Experimental arthritis is arthritis that is induced in experimental animals. Immunological methods and infectious agents can be used to develop experimental arthritis models. These methods include injections of stimulators of the immune response, such as an adjuvant (adjuvants, immunologic) or collagen.

cleftlip.name: cleft lip
cleftlip.definition: Cleft [MASK] is congenital defect in the upper [MASK] where the maxillary prominence fails to merge with the merged medial nasal prominences. It is thought to be caused by faulty migration of the mesoderm in the head region.

shock.name: shock
shock.definition: Shock is a pathological condition manifested by failure to perfuse or oxygenate vital organs.

cochlearimplantation.name: cochlear implantation
cochlearimplantation.definition: Cochlear implantation is surgical insertion of an electronic hearing device ([MASK]) with electrodes to the cochlear nerve in the [MASK] to create sound sensation in patients with residual nerve fibers.

subcutaneousabsorption.name: subcutaneous absorption
subcutaneousabsorption.definition: Subcutaneous absorption is the uptake of substances via the [MASK].

focaladhesionkinase1.name: focal adhesion kinase 1
focaladhesionkinase1.definition: Focal adhesion kinase 1 is a non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase with protein phosphatase 1 regulatory activity that is localized to focal adhesions and is a central component of integrin-mediated signal transduction pathways. Focal adhesion kinase 1 interacts with paxillin and undergoes phosphorylation in response to adhesion of cell surface integrins to the extracellular matrix. Phosphorylated p125FAK protein binds to a variety of sh2 domain and sh3 domain containing proteins and helps regulate cell adhesion and cell migration.

emotionalregulation.name: emotional regulation
emotionalregulation.definition: Emotional regulation is the manifestation of an emotional response by which individuals influence the intensity, duration, valence, or manifestation of their response. Emotion regulation either precedes (avoidance, interpretation) or follows an emotion (suppression, reappraisal). Emotion regulation is distinct from coping (focuses primarily on decreasing a negative emotional experience), and can include increasing or decreasing both positive and negative emotions consciously or unconsciously.

transformation,genetic.name: transformation , genetic
transformation,genetic.definition: Genetic transformation is change brought about to an organisms genetic composition by unidirectional transfer (transfection; transduction, [MASK], genetic, etc.) and incorporation of foreign dna into prokaryotic or eukaryotic cells by recombination of part or all of that dna into the cell's genome.

cropproduction.name: crop production
cropproduction.definition: Crop production is the science and practice of cultivating plants that have economic value to man. It includes [MASK], [MASK] production, weeding, use of fertilizers, harvesting, storage, transportation, and marketing.

parasiticdiseases.name: parasitic diseases
parasiticdiseases.definition: Parasitic diseases is infections or infestations with parasites. They are often contracted through contact with an intermediate vector, but may occur as the result of direct exposure.

samplingstudies.name: sampling studies
samplingstudies.definition: Sampling studies is studies in which a number of subjects are selected from all subjects in a defined population. Conclusions based on sample results may be attributed only to the population sampled.

feverofunknownorigin.name: fever of unknown origin
feverofunknownorigin.definition: Fever of unknown origin is fever in which the etiology cannot be ascertained.

angiogenicproteins.name: angiogenic proteins
angiogenicproteins.definition: Angiogenic proteins is intercellular signaling peptides and proteins that regulate the proliferation of new blood vessels under normal physiological conditions (angiogenesis, physiological). Aberrant expression of angiogenic proteins during disease states such as tumorigenesis can also result in pathological angiogenesis.

periodicity.name: periodicity
periodicity.definition: Periodicity is the tendency of a phenomenon to recur at regular intervals; in biological systems, the recurrence of certain activities (including hormonal, cellular, neural) may be annual, seasonal, monthly, daily, or more frequently (ultradian).

neuromuscularmanifestations.name: neuromuscular manifestations
neuromuscularmanifestations.definition: Neuromuscular manifestations is signs and symptoms associated with diseases of the muscle, neuromuscular junction, or peripheral nerves.

cysticfibrosistransmembraneconductancere.name: cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator
cysticfibrosistransmembraneconductancere.definition: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator is a chloride channel that regulates secretion in many exocrine tissues. Abnormalities in the cftr gene have been shown to cause cystic fibrosis. (Hum Genet 1994;93(4):364-8)

intestine,small.name: intestine , small
intestine,small.definition: Small intestine is the portion of the gastrointestinal tract between the pylorus of the stomach and the ileocecal valve of the large intestine. It is divisible into three portions: the duodenum, the jejunum, and the ileum.

urinaryretention.name: urinary retention
urinaryretention.definition: Urinary retention is inability to empty the [MASK] with voiding (urination).

caspase12.name: caspase 12
caspase12.definition: Caspase 12 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a caspase recruitment domain in its pro-domain region. Caspase 12 is activated by pro-apoptotic factors that are released during cell stress and by card signaling adaptor proteins. It activates apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases.

carcinoma,medullary.name: carcinoma , medullary
carcinoma,medullary.definition: Medullary carcinoma is a carcinoma composed mainly of epithelial elements with little or no stroma. Medullary carcinomas of the breast constitute 5%-7% of all mammary carcinomas; medullary carcinomas of the thyroid comprise 3%-10% of all thyroid malignancies. (From Dorland, 27th ed; DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1141; Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

dualspecificityphosphatase3.name: dual specificity phosphatase 3
dualspecificityphosphatase3.definition: Dual specificity phosphatase 3 is a dual specificity phosphatase subtype that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction by inactivating mitogen-activated protein kinases. It has specificity for extracellular signal-regulated map kinases.

clockproteins.name: clock proteins
clockproteins.definition: Clock proteins is basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) domain-containing proteins that contain intrinsic histone acetyltransferase activity and play important roles in circadian rhythm regulation. Clock proteins combine with Arntl proteins to form heterodimeric transcription factors that are specific for e-box elements and stimulate the transcription of several E-box genes that are involved in cyclical regulation. This [MASK] also sets into motion a time-dependent [MASK] loop which in turn down-regulates the expression of clock proteins.

eldernutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: elder nutritional physiological phenomena
eldernutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Elder nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of adults aged 65 years of age and older.

genome,insect.name: genome , insect
genome,insect.definition: Insect genome is the genetic complement of an insect (insects) as represented in its dna.

infantbehavior.name: infant behavior
infantbehavior.definition: Infant behavior is any observable response or action of a neonate or infant up through the age of 23 months.

sportsmedicine.name: sports medicine
sportsmedicine.definition: Sports medicine is the field of medicine concerned with physical fitness and the diagnosis and treatment of injuries sustained in exercise and sports activities.

superiorcervicalganglion.name: superior cervical ganglion
superiorcervicalganglion.definition: Superior cervical ganglion is the largest and uppermost of the paravertebral sympathetic ganglia.

denmark.name: denmark
denmark.definition: Denmark is a country in northern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea and the [MASK]. The capital is Copenhagen.

receptors,sigma.name: receptors , sigma
receptors,sigma.definition: Sigma receptors is a class of cell surface receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Sigma receptors were originally considered to be opioid receptors because they bind certain synthetic opioids. However they also interact with a variety of other psychoactive drugs, and their endogenous ligand is not known (although they can react to certain endogenous steroids). Sigma receptors are found in the immune, endocrine, and nervous systems, and in some peripheral tissues.

pharmaceuticalservices.name: pharmaceutical services
pharmaceuticalservices.definition: Pharmaceutical services is total pharmaceutical services provided by qualified pharmacists. In addition to the preparation and distribution of medical products, they may include consultative services provided to agencies and institutions which do not have a qualified pharmacist.

drugresistance,viral.name: drug resistance , viral
drugresistance,viral.definition: Viral drug resistance is the ability of viruses to resist or to become tolerant to chemotherapeutic agents or antiviral agents. This resistance is acquired through gene mutation.

seawater.name: seawater
seawater.definition: Seawater is the salinated water of oceans and seas that provides habitat for [MASK].

liverneoplasms.name: liver neoplasms
liverneoplasms.definition: Liver neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the liver.

patientisolation.name: patient isolation
patientisolation.definition: Patient isolation is the segregation of patients with communicable or other diseases for a specified time. Isolation may be strict, in which movement and social contacts are limited; modified, where an effort to control specified aspects of care is made in order to prevent cross infection; or reverse, where the patient is secluded in a controlled or germ-free environment in order to protect him or her from cross infection.

encephalitis,california.name: encephalitis , california
encephalitis,california.definition: California encephalitis is a viral infection of the brain caused by serotypes of California encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, california) transmitted to humans by the mosquito aedes triseriatus. The majority of cases are caused by the la crosse virus. This condition is endemic to the midwestern United States and primarily affects children between 5-10 years of age. Clinical manifestations include fever; vomiting; headache; and abdominal pain followed by seizures, altered mentation, and focal neurologic deficits. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1996, Ch26, p13)

hardness.name: hardness
hardness.definition: Hardness is the mechanical property of material that determines its resistance to force. hardness tests measure this property.

geriatricpsychiatry.name: geriatric psychiatry
geriatricpsychiatry.definition: Geriatric psychiatry is a subspecialty of psychiatry concerned with the mental health of the aged.

wearableelectronicdevices.name: wearable electronic devices
wearableelectronicdevices.definition: Wearable electronic devices is electronic implements worn on  the body as an implant or as an accessory. Examples include wearable diagnostic devices, wearable activity trackers, wearable infusion pumps, wearable computing devices, sensory aids, and electronic pest repellents.

roccurve.name: roc curve
roccurve.definition: Roc curve is a graphic means for assessing the ability of a screening test to discriminate between healthy and diseased persons; may also be used in other studies, e.g., distinguishing stimuli responses as to a faint stimuli or nonstimuli.

occlusionbodymatrixproteins.name: occlusion body matrix proteins
occlusionbodymatrixproteins.definition: Occlusion body matrix proteins is proteins that assemble into a crystalline polyhedral or ovicylindrical shape around [MASK], including baculoviridae and cypovirus.

indianocean.name: indian ocean
indianocean.definition: Indian ocean is a body of water covering approximately one-fifth of the total ocean area of the earth, extending amidst Africa in the west, Australia in the east, Asia in the north, and Antarctica in the south. Including the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf, it constitutes the third largest ocean after the atlantic ocean and the pacific ocean. (New Encyclopaedia Britannica Micropaedia, 15th ed, 1990, p289)

dentalocclusion,traumatic.name: dental occlusion , traumatic
dentalocclusion,traumatic.definition: Traumatic dental occlusion is an occlusion resulting in overstrain and injury to teeth, periodontal tissue, or other oral structures.

pharmacyadministration.name: pharmacy administration
pharmacyadministration.definition: Pharmacy administration is the business and managerial aspects of pharmacy in its broadest sense.

anesthesia.name: anesthesia
anesthesia.definition: Anesthesia is a state characterized by loss of feeling or sensation. This depression of nerve function is usually the result of pharmacologic action and is induced to allow performance of surgery or other painful procedures.

horseradishperoxidase.name: horseradish peroxidase
horseradishperoxidase.definition: Horseradish peroxidase is an enzyme isolated from horseradish which is able to act as an antigen. It is frequently used as a histochemical tracer for light and [MASK] microscopy. Its antigenicity has permitted its use as a combined antigen and marker in experimental [MASK].

genes,src.name: genes , src
genes,src.definition: Src genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (src) originally isolated from the [MASK] virus (rsv). The proto-oncogene src (c-src) codes for a protein that is a member of the tyrosine kinase family and was the first proto-oncogene identified in the human genome. The human c-src gene is located at 20q12-13 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 20.

anatomy.name: anatomy
anatomy.definition: Anatomy is a branch of biology dealing with the structure of organisms.

differentialthreshold.name: differential threshold
differentialthreshold.definition: Differential threshold is the smallest difference which can be discriminated between two stimuli or one which is barely above the threshold.

publicassistance.name: public assistance
publicassistance.definition: Public assistance is financial assistance to impoverished persons for the essentials of living through federal, state or local government programs.

socialidentification.name: social identification
socialidentification.definition: Social identification is the process by which an aspect of self image is developed based on in-group preference or ethnocentrism and a perception of belonging to a social or cultural group. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

nitricacid.name: nitric acid
nitricacid.definition: Nitric acid is nitric acid (hno3). a colorless liquid that is used in the manufacture of inorganic and organic nitrates and nitro compounds for fertilizers, dye intermediates, explosives, and many different organic chemicals. Continued exposure to vapor may cause chronic bronchitis; chemical pneumonitis may occur. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

infarction,posteriorcerebralartery.name: infarction , posterior cerebral artery
infarction,posteriorcerebralartery.definition: Posterior cerebral artery infarction is necrosis induced by ischemia in the posterior cerebral artery distribution system which supplies portions of the brain stem; the thalamus; temporal lobe, and occipital lobe.
