Depending on the size and location of infarction, clinical features include olfaction disorders and visual problems (agnosia; alexia; hemianopsia).

adenocarcinoma,papillary.name: adenocarcinoma , papillary
adenocarcinoma,papillary.definition: Papillary adenocarcinoma is an adenocarcinoma containing finger-like processes of vascular connective tissue covered by neoplastic epithelium, projecting into cysts or the cavity of glands or follicles. It occurs most frequently in the ovary and thyroid gland. (Stedman, 25th ed)

dnapolymerasegamma.name: dna polymerase gamma
dnapolymerasegamma.definition: Dna polymerase gamma is a DNA-directed dna polymerase that functions in the replication of mitochondrial dna. Mutations in the gene that encodes this enzyme (polg) are associated with some forms of ophthalmoplegia, chronic external progressive.

executivefunction.name: executive function
executivefunction.definition: Executive function is a [MASK] of cognitive functions that controls complex, goal-directed thought and behavior. Executive function involves multiple domains, such as concept formation, goal management, cognitive flexibility, inhibition control, and working memory. Impaired executive function is seen in a range of disorders, e.g., schizophrenia; and adhd.

glucosetransportertype4.name: glucose transporter type 4
glucosetransportertype4.definition: Glucose transporter type 4 is a glucose transport protein found in mature muscle cells and adipocytes. It promotes transport of glucose from the blood into target tissues. The inactive form of the protein is localized in cytoplasmic vesicles. In response to insulin, it is translocated to the plasma membrane where it facilitates glucose uptake.

esophagealsphincter,upper.name: esophageal sphincter , upper
esophagealsphincter,upper.definition: Upper esophageal sphincter is the structure at the pharyngoesophageal junction consisting chiefly of the cricopharyngeus muscle. It normally occludes the lumen of the esophagus, except during swallowing.

dnacopynumbervariations.name: dna copy number variations
dnacopynumbervariations.definition: Dna copy number variations is stretches of genomic dna that exist in different multiples between individuals. Many copy number variations have been associated with susceptibility or resistance to disease.

radiationdosage.name: radiation dosage
radiationdosage.definition: Radiation dosage is the amount of radiation energy that is deposited in a unit mass of material, such as tissues of plants or animal. In radiotherapy, radiation dosage is expressed in gray units (Gy). In radiologic health, the dosage is expressed by the product of absorbed dose (Gy) and quality factor (a function of [MASK]), and is called radiation dose equivalent in sievert units (Sv).

pituitaryhormones.name: pituitary hormones
pituitaryhormones.definition: Pituitary hormones is hormones secreted by the pituitary gland including those from the anterior lobe (adenohypophysis), the posterior lobe ([MASK]), and the ill-defined intermediate lobe. Structurally, they include small peptides, proteins, and glycoproteins. They are under the regulation of neural signals (neurotransmitters) or neuroendocrine signals (hypothalamic hormones) from the hypothalamus as well as [MASK] from their targets such as adrenal cortex hormones; androgens; estrogens.

mechanicalphenomena.name: mechanical phenomena
mechanicalphenomena.definition: Mechanical phenomena is the properties and processes of materials that affect their behavior under force.

ischemia.name: ischemia
ischemia.definition: Ischemia is a hypoperfusion of the blood through an organ or tissue caused by a pathologic constriction or obstruction of its blood vessels, or an absence of blood circulation.

suppression,genetic.name: suppression , genetic
suppression,genetic.definition: Genetic suppression is mutation process that restores the wild-type phenotype in an organism possessing a mutationally altered genotype. The second "suppressor" mutation may be on a different gene, on the same gene but located at a distance from the site of the primary mutation, or in extrachromosomal genes (extrachromosomal inheritance).

antiviralagents.name: antiviral agents
antiviralagents.definition: Antiviral agents is agents used in the prophylaxis or therapy of virus diseases. Some of the ways they may act include preventing viral replication by inhibiting [MASK] polymerase; binding to specific cell-surface receptors and inhibiting viral penetration or uncoating; inhibiting viral protein synthesis; or blocking late stages of virus assembly.

neckinjuries.name: neck injuries
neckinjuries.definition: [MASK] injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the [MASK]. It includes injuries to the skin, muscles, and other soft tissues of the [MASK].

nationalprogramofcancerregistries.name: national program of cancer registries
nationalprogramofcancerregistries.definition: National program of cancer registries is a unit of the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that supports the collection of high-quality data on cancer occurrence (including the type, extent, and location of the cancer), the type of initial treatment, and outcomes.

cellline,tumor.name: cell line , tumor
cellline,tumor.definition: Tumor cell line is a cell line derived from cultured tumor cells.

criticalcarenursing.name: critical care nursing
criticalcarenursing.definition: Critical care nursing is a nursing specialty that deals specifically with the care of patients who are [MASK].

wounds,penetrating.name: wounds , penetrating
wounds,penetrating.definition: Penetrating wounds is wounds caused by objects penetrating the skin.

activatedproteincresistance.name: activated protein c resistance
activatedproteincresistance.definition: Activated protein c resistance is a hemostatic disorder characterized by a poor anticoagulant response to activated protein c (apc). The activated form of Factor v ([MASK]) is more slowly degraded by activated protein c. Factor v Leiden mutation (r506q) is the most common cause of apc resistance.

commissiononprofessionalandhospitalactiv.name: commission on professional and hospital activities
commissiononprofessionalandhospitalactiv.definition: Commission on professional and hospital activities is the non-profit, non-governmental organization which collects, processes, and distributes data on hospital use. Two programs of the Commission are the Professional Activity Study and the Medical Audit Program.

africancontinentalancestrygroup.name: african continental ancestry group
africancontinentalancestrygroup.definition: African continental ancestry group is individuals whose ancestral origins are in the continent of Africa.

tandemmassspectrometry.name: tandem mass spectrometry
tandemmassspectrometry.definition: Tandem mass spectrometry is a mass spectrometry technique using two (ms/ms) or more mass analyzers. With two in tandem, the precursor ions are mass-selected by a first mass analyzer, and focused into a collision region where they are then fragmented into product ions which are then characterized by a second mass analyzer. a variety of techniques are used to separate the compounds, ionize them, and introduce them to the first mass analyzer. For example, for in gc-ms/ms, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry is involved in separating relatively small compounds by gas chromatography prior to injecting them into an ionization chamber for the mass selection.

paris.name: paris
paris.definition: Paris is the capital city of France.

adrenalinsufficiency.name: adrenal insufficiency
adrenalinsufficiency.definition: Adrenal insufficiency is conditions in which the production of adrenal corticosteroids falls below the requirement of the body. Adrenal insufficiency can be caused by defects in the adrenal glands, the pituitary gland, or the hypothalamus.

dietarycarbohydrates.name: dietary carbohydrates
dietarycarbohydrates.definition: Dietary carbohydrates is carbohydrates present in food comprising digestible sugars and starches and indigestible cellulose and other dietary fibers. The former are the major source of energy. The sugars are in beet and cane sugar, fruits, honey, sweet corn, corn syrup, milk and milk products, etc.; the starches are in cereal grains, legumes (fabaceae), tubers, etc. (From Claudio & Lagua, Nutrition and Diet Therapy Dictionary, 3d ed, p32, p277)

maximumallowableconcentration.name: maximum allowable concentration
maximumallowableconcentration.definition: Maximum allowable concentration is the maximum exposure to a biologically active physical or chemical agent that is allowed during an 8-hour period (a workday) in a population of workers, or during a 24-hour period in the general population, which does not appear to cause appreciable harm, whether immediate or delayed for any period, in the target population. (From Lewis Dictionary of Toxicology, 1st ed)

transplantrecipients.name: transplant recipients
transplantrecipients.definition: [MASK] recipients is individuals receiving tissues or organs transferred from another individual of the same or different species, or from within the same individual.

slitlamp.name: slit lamp
slitlamp.definition: Slit lamp is a microscope with a light source that can be projected into a linear beam. It allows cross-sectional viewing of the aqueous humor; conjuncteiva; cornea; eyelids; iris; and lens (see lens, eye) of the eye.

governmentregulation.name: government regulation
governmentregulation.definition: Government regulation is exercise of governmental authority to control conduct.

biotin.name: biotin
biotin.definition: Biotin is a water-soluble, enzyme co-factor present in minute amounts in every living cell. It occurs mainly bound to proteins or polypeptides and is abundant in liver, kidney, pancreas, yeast, and milk.

educationalmeasurement.name: educational measurement
educationalmeasurement.definition: Educational measurement is the assessing of academic or educational achievement. It includes all aspects of testing and test construction.

slitventriclesyndrome.name: slit ventricle syndrome
slitventriclesyndrome.definition: Slit ventricle syndrome is an intermittent and self-limiting headache disorder in individuals with cerebrospinal fluid shunts emplaced for the treatment of hydrocephalus. The symptoms of headache, vomiting, and cranial neuropathies are associated with intermittent obstruction of the shunt.

endothelium.name: endothelium
endothelium.definition: Endothelium is a layer of epithelium that lines the heart, blood vessels (endothelium, vascular), [MASK] vessels ([MASK]), and the serous cavities of the body.

occupationaltherapists.name: occupational therapists
occupationaltherapists.definition: Occupational therapists is professionals trained to help individuals develop or regain skills needed to achieve independence in their lives.

associationlearning.name: association learning
associationlearning.definition: Association learning is the principle that items experienced together enter into a connection, so that one tends to reinstate the other.

bonemarrow.name: bone marrow
bonemarrow.definition: Bone marrow is the soft tissue filling the cavities of bones. Bone marrow exists in two types, yellow and red. Yellow marrow is found in the large cavities of large bones and consists mostly of fat cells and a few primitive blood cells. Red marrow is a hematopoietic tissue and is the site of production of erythrocytes and granular leukocytes. Bone marrow is made up of a framework of connective tissue containing branching fibers with the frame being filled with marrow cells.

bacterialtoxins.name: bacterial toxins
bacterialtoxins.definition: Bacterial toxins is toxic substances formed in or elaborated by bacteria; they are usually proteins with high molecular weight and antigenicity; some are used as antibiotics and some to skin test for the presence of or susceptibility to certain diseases.

consensusdevelopmentconference,nih.name: consensus development conference , nih
consensusdevelopmentconference,nih.definition: Nih [MASK] conference is official statements of the finding or recommendations expressing the outcome from a conference sponsored by nih.

hybridcells.name: hybrid cells
hybridcells.definition: Hybrid cells is any cell, other than a zygote, that contains elements (such as nuclei and cytoplasm) from two or more different cells, usually produced by artificial cell fusion.

interneurons.name: interneurons
interneurons.definition: Interneurons is most generally any neurons which are not motor or sensory. Interneurons may also refer to neurons whose axons remain within a particular brain region in contrast to [MASK] neurons, which have axons projecting to other brain regions.

epilepsy,benignneonatal.name: epilepsy , benign neonatal
epilepsy,benignneonatal.definition: Benign neonatal epilepsy is a condition marked by recurrent seizures that occur during the first 4-6 weeks of life despite an otherwise benign neonatal course. Autosomal dominant familial and sporadic forms have been identified. Seizures generally consist of brief episodes of tonic posturing and other movements, apnea, eye deviations, and blood pressure fluctuations. These tend to remit after the 6th week of life. The risk of developing epilepsy at an older age is moderately increased in the familial form of this disorder. (Neurologia 1996 Feb;11(2):51-5)

catchmentarea,health.name: catchment area , health
catchmentarea,health.definition: Health catchment area is a geographic area defined and served by a health program or institution.

crime.name: crime
crime.definition: Crime is a violation of the criminal law, i.e., a breach of the conduct code specifically sanctioned by the state, which through its administrative agencies prosecutes offenders and imposes and administers punishments. The concept includes unacceptable actions whether prosecuted or going unpunished.

mesenchymalstemcelltransplantation.name: mesenchymal stem cell transplantation
mesenchymalstemcelltransplantation.definition: Mesenchymal stem cell transplantation is transfer of mesenchymal stem cells between individuals within the same species (transplantation, homologous) or transfer within the same individual (transplantation, autologous).

eyehemorrhage.name: eye hemorrhage
eyehemorrhage.definition: Eye hemorrhage is intraocular hemorrhage from the vessels of various tissues of the eye.

complementsystemproteins.name: complement system proteins
complementsystemproteins.definition: Complement system proteins is serum glycoproteins participating in the host defense mechanism of complement activation that creates the complement membrane attack complex. Included are glycoproteins in the various pathways of complement activation ([MASK]; alternative complement pathway; and lectin complement pathway).

fetalorganmaturity.name: fetal organ maturity
fetalorganmaturity.definition: Fetal organ maturity is functional competence of specific organs or body systems of the fetus in utero.

hospitals,rural.name: hospitals , rural
hospitals,rural.definition: Rural hospitals is hospitals located in a rural area.

pharmacologicsubstance.name: pharmacologic substance
pharmacologicsubstance.definition: Pharmacologic substance is the main ingredient in a medicine that causes the desired effect of the medicine.

troponinc.name: troponin c
troponinc.definition: Troponin c is a troponin complex subunit that binds calcium and help regulate calcium-dependent muscle contraction. There are two troponin c subtypes: troponin c1 and c2. Troponin c1 is skeletal and cardiac type whereas troponin c2 is skeletal type. Troponin c1 is a biomarker for damaged or injured [MASK] and mutations in troponin c1 gene are associated with [MASK].

ventriculardysfunction.name: ventricular dysfunction
ventriculardysfunction.definition: Ventricular dysfunction is a condition in which heart ventricles exhibit impaired function.

coronaryocclusion.name: coronary occlusion
coronaryocclusion.definition: Coronary occlusion is complete blockage of blood flow through one of the coronary arteries, usually from coronary atherosclerosis.

programminglanguages.name: programming languages
programminglanguages.definition: Programming languages is specific languages used to prepare computer programs.

maternalexposure.name: maternal exposure
maternalexposure.definition: Maternal exposure is exposure of the female parent, human or animal, to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals that may affect offspring. It includes pre-conception maternal exposure.

physicaltherapistassistants.name: physical therapist assistants
physicaltherapistassistants.definition: Physical therapist assistants is persons who, under the supervision of licensed physical therapists, provide patient treatment using various physical therapy techniques.

colortherapy.name: color therapy
colortherapy.definition: [MASK] therapy is a form of phototherapy using [MASK] to influence health and to treat various physical or mental disorders. The [MASK] rays may be in the visible or invisible spectrum and can be administered through colored lights or applied mentally through suggestion.

splenicartery.name: splenic artery
splenicartery.definition: Splenic artery is the largest branch of the celiac trunk with distribution to the spleen, pancreas, stomach and greater omentum.

ants.name: ants
ants.definition: Ants is insects of the family Formicidae, very common and widespread, probably the most successful of all the insect groups. All ants are social insects, and most colonies contain three castes, queens, males, and workers. Their habits are often very elaborate and a great many studies have been made of ant behavior. Ants produce a number of secretions that function in offense, defense, and communication. (From Borror, et al., An Introduction to the Study of Insects, 4th ed, p676)

cholinergicagonists.name: cholinergic agonists
cholinergicagonists.definition: Cholinergic agonists is drugs that bind to and activate cholinergic receptors.

technology,industry,andagriculture.name: technology , industry , and agriculture
technology,industry,andagriculture.definition: And agriculture industry technology is the science and application of techniques for the extraction of raw materials, provision of services, manufacture of goods, cultivation of crops, and raising of livestock.

imagecytometry.name: image cytometry
imagecytometry.definition: Image cytometry is a technique encompassing morphometry, densitometry, neural networks, and [MASK] that has numerous clinical and research applications and is particularly useful in anatomic pathology for the study of malignant lesions. The most common current application of image cytometry is for dna analysis, followed by quantitation of immunohistochemical staining.

altitudesickness.name: altitude sickness
altitudesickness.definition: Altitude sickness is multiple symptoms associated with reduced oxygen at high altitude.

professionalrevieworganizations.name: professional review organizations
professionalrevieworganizations.definition: Professional review organizations is organizations representing designated geographic areas which have contracts under the pro program to review the medical necessity, appropriateness, quality, and cost-effectiveness of care received by Medicare beneficiaries. Peer Review Improvement Act, pl 97-248, 1982.

friction.name: friction
friction.definition: Friction is surface resistance to the relative motion of one body against the rubbing, sliding, rolling, or flowing of another with which it is in contact.

essay.name: essay
essay.definition: Essay is short literary prose composition, usually dealing with a single theme.

photograph.name: photograph
photograph.definition: Photograph is still image produced from radiation-sensitive materials (sensitive to light, [MASK] beams, or nuclear radiation), generally by means of the chemical action of light on a sensitive film, [MASK], glass, or metal. Photographs may be positive or negative, opaque or transparent.

fluorescentantibodytechnique,indirect.name: fluorescent antibody technique , indirect
fluorescentantibodytechnique,indirect.definition: Indirect fluorescent antibody technique is a form of fluorescent antibody technique commonly used to detect serum antibodies and immune complexes in tissues and microorganisms in specimens from patients with infectious diseases. The technique involves formation of an antigen-antibody complex which is labeled with fluorescein-conjugated anti-immunoglobulin antibody. (From Bennington, Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

receptors,ghrelin.name: receptors , ghrelin
receptors,ghrelin.definition: Ghrelin receptors is transmembrane proteins that recognize and bind ghrelin, a potent stimulator of growth hormone secretion and food intake in mammals. Ghrelin receptors are found in the pituitary and hypothalamus. They belong to the family of g-protein-coupled receptors.

maternaldeprivation.name: maternal deprivation
maternaldeprivation.definition: Maternal deprivation is prolonged separation of the offspring from the mother.

viralfusionproteininhibitors.name: viral fusion protein inhibitors
viralfusionproteininhibitors.definition: Viral fusion protein inhibitors is drugs that are designed to block the action of [MASK] and prevent viruses from entering the cell.

immunoglobulinlightchains,surrogate.name: immunoglobulin light chains , surrogate
immunoglobulinlightchains,surrogate.definition: Surrogate immunoglobulin light chains is an immunolglobulin light chain-like protein composed of an immunoglobulin variable REGION-like peptide (such as light chain like lambda5 peptide) and an immunoglobulin constant REGION-like peptide (such as Vpreb1 peptide). Surrogate light chains associate with mu [MASK] in place of a conventional immunoglobulin light chains to form pre-B cell receptors.

middlelobesyndrome.name: middle lobe syndrome
middlelobesyndrome.definition: Middle lobe syndrome is atelectasis of the right middle pulmonary lobe, with chronic pneumonitis. (Dorland, 27th ed)

englishabstract.name: english abstract
englishabstract.definition: English [MASK] is identifier for English language [MASK] provided with non-English language works.

gastricbypass.name: gastric bypass
gastricbypass.definition: Gastric bypass is surgical procedure in which the stomach is transected high on the body. The resulting small proximal gastric pouch is joined to any parts of the small intestine by an end-to-side surgical anastomosis, depending on the amounts of intestinal surface being bypasses. This procedure is used frequently in the treatment of morbid obesity by limiting the size of functional stomach, food intake, and food absorption.

physicalappearance,body.name: physical appearance , body
physicalappearance,body.definition: Body physical appearance is the superficial physical looks, characteristics or qualities of an individual as distinguished from the underlying unseen nature or attributes.

nanotubes,carbon.name: nanotubes , carbon
nanotubes,carbon.definition: Carbon nanotubes is nanometer-sized tubes composed mainly of carbon. Such nanotubes are used as probes for high-resolution structural and chemical imaging of biomolecules with [MASK].

polyethylene.name: polyethylene
polyethylene.definition: Polyethylene is a vinyl polymer made from ethylene. It can be branched or linear. Branched or low-density polyethylene is tough and pliable but not to the same degree as linear polyethylene. Linear or high-density polyethylene has a greater hardness and tensile strength. Polyethylene is used in a variety of products, including implants and prostheses.

meningitis,fungal.name: meningitis , fungal
meningitis,fungal.definition: Fungal meningitis is meningitis caused by fungal agents which may occur as [MASK] or arise in immunocompetent hosts.

anxiety,separation.name: anxiety , separation
anxiety,separation.definition: Separation anxiety is anxiety experienced by an individual upon separation from a person or object of particular significance to the individual.

donorconception.name: donor conception
donorconception.definition: Donor conception is assisted reproductive techniques where eggs, sperm, both eggs and sperm (double donation), or embryos from donors are used.

politicalsystems.name: political systems
politicalsystems.definition: Political systems is the units based on political theory and chosen by countries under which their governmental power is organized and administered to their citizens.

sanfrancisco.name: san francisco
sanfrancisco.definition: San francisco is a city in northern California.

personalitydevelopment.name: personality development
personalitydevelopment.definition: Personality development is growth of habitual patterns of behavior in childhood and adolescence.

veterans.name: veterans
veterans.definition: Veterans is former members of the armed services.

quercetin.name: quercetin
quercetin.definition: Quercetin is a flavonol widely distributed in plants. It is an antioxidant, like many other phenolic heterocyclic compounds. Glycosylated forms include rutin and quercetrin.

atherosclerosis.name: atherosclerosis
atherosclerosis.definition: Atherosclerosis is a thickening and loss of elasticity of the walls of arteries that occurs with formation of [MASK] within the arterial intima.

celllineauthentication.name: cell line authentication
celllineauthentication.definition: Cell line authentication is techniques used to characterize and confirm the identity of a cell line. Characterization involves authentication to verify that it matches the original description of the cells and ensures that they are not cross-contaminated with another cell line. This is done to avoid attributing data incorrectly to the wrong cell line.

teaching.name: teaching
teaching.definition: Teaching is a formal and organized process of transmitting knowledge to a person or group.

transferagreement.name: transfer agreement
transferagreement.definition: Transfer agreement is a written agreement for the transfer of patients and their medical records from [MASK] care institution to another.

autonomicagents.name: autonomic agents
autonomicagents.definition: Autonomic agents is agents affecting the function of, or mimicking the actions of, the autonomic nervous system and thereby having an effect on such processes as respiration, circulation, [MASK], body temperature regulation, certain endocrine gland secretions, etc.

fibroblasts.name: fibroblasts
fibroblasts.definition: Fibroblasts is connective tissue cells which secrete an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

pleuraldiseases.name: pleural diseases
pleuraldiseases.definition: Pleural diseases is diseases involving the pleura.

drugsubstitution.name: drug substitution
drugsubstitution.definition: Drug substitution is the practice of replacing one prescribed drug with another that is expected to have the same clinical or psychological effect.

synapticvesicles.name: synaptic vesicles
synapticvesicles.definition: Synaptic vesicles is membrane-bound compartments which contain transmitter molecules. Synaptic vesicles are concentrated at presynaptic terminals. They actively sequester transmitter molecules from the cytoplasm. In at least some synapses, transmitter release occurs by fusion of these vesicles with the presynaptic membrane, followed by exocytosis of their contents.

enzymeactivation.name: enzyme activation
enzymeactivation.definition: Enzyme activation is conversion of an inactive form of an enzyme to one possessing metabolic activity. It includes 1, activation by ions (activators); 2, activation by cofactors (coenzymes); and 3, conversion of an enzyme precursor (proenzyme or zymogen) to an active enzyme.

india.name: india
india.definition: India is a country in southern Asia, bordering the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and Pakistan. The capitol is New Delhi.

dyspnea.name: dyspnea
dyspnea.definition: Dyspnea is difficult or labored breathing.

allelicimbalance.name: allelic imbalance
allelicimbalance.definition: Allelic imbalance is a situation where one member (allele) of a gene pair is lost (loss of heterozygosity) or amplified.

stomach.name: stomach
stomach.definition: Stomach is an organ of [MASK] situated in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen between the termination of the esophagus and the beginning of the duodenum.

grossdomesticproduct.name: gross domestic product
grossdomesticproduct.definition: Gross domestic product is value of all final goods and services produced in a country in one year.

militaryfacilities.name: military facilities
militaryfacilities.definition: Military facilities is areas designated for use by the armed forces personnel.

hearttransplantation.name: heart transplantation
hearttransplantation.definition: Heart transplantation is the transference of a heart from one human or animal to another.

correctionofhearingimpairment.name: correction of hearing impairment
correctionofhearingimpairment.definition: Correction of hearing impairment is procedures for correcting hearing disorders.

factorviideficiency.name: factor vii deficiency
factorviideficiency.definition: [MASK] deficiency is an autosomal recessive characteristic or a coagulation disorder acquired in association with vitamin k deficiency. [MASK] is a Vitamin k dependent glycoprotein essential to the extrinsic pathway of coagulation.

manuscript.name: manuscript
manuscript.definition: Manuscript is work written by hand, as one written before the invention or adoption of printing.

pickdiseaseofthebrain.name: pick disease of the brain
pickdiseaseofthebrain.definition: Pick disease of the brain is a rare form of dementia that is sometimes familial. Clinical features include aphasia; apraxia; confusion; anomia; memory loss; and personality deterioration. This pattern is consistent with the pathologic findings of circumscribed atrophy of the poles of the frontal lobe and temporal lobe. Neuronal loss is maximal in the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, and amygdala. Some ballooned cortical neurons contain argentophylic (Pick) bodies. (From Brain Pathol 1998 Apr;8(2):339-54; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1057-9)

legalservices.name: legal services
legalservices.definition: Legal services is services provided by attorneys and paralegal staff.

intracranialembolismandthrombosis.name: intracranial embolism and thrombosis
intracranialembolismandthrombosis.definition: [MASK] and thrombosis is embolism or thrombosis involving blood vessels which supply intracranial structures. Emboli may originate from extracranial or intracranial sources. Thrombosis may occur in arterial or venous structures.

evolution,chemical.name: evolution , chemical
evolution,chemical.definition: Chemical evolution is chemical and physical transformation of the biogenic elements from their nucleosynthesis in stars to their incorporation and subsequent modification in planetary bodies and terrestrial biochemistry. It includes the mechanism of incorporation of biogenic elements into complex molecules and molecular systems, leading up to the origin of life.

morphinedependence.name: morphine dependence
morphinedependence.definition: [MASK] dependence is strong dependence, both physiological and emotional, upon [MASK].

anesthesiaandanalgesia.name: anesthesia and analgesia
anesthesiaandanalgesia.definition: Anesthesia and analgesia is medical methods of either relieving pain caused by a particular condition or removing the sensation of pain during a surgery or other medical procedure.

myosintypeii.name: myosin type ii
myosintypeii.definition: Myosin type ii is the subfamily of myosin proteins that are commonly found in muscle fibers. Myosin ii is also involved a diverse array of cellular functions including cell division, transport within the golgi apparatus, and maintaining microvilli structure.

diseaseeradication.name: disease eradication
diseaseeradication.definition: Disease eradication is termination of all transmission of infection by global extermination of the infectious agent through surveillance and containment (From Porta, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 5th ed).

microbiologicalphenomena.name: microbiological phenomena
microbiologicalphenomena.definition: Microbiological phenomena is physiological processes and properties of microorganisms, such as archaea; bacteria; rickettsia; viruses; and fungi.

lymphoma.name: lymphoma
lymphoma.definition: Lymphoma is a general term for various neoplastic diseases of the lymphoid tissue.

neoplasms,vasculartissue.name: neoplasms , vascular tissue
neoplasms,vasculartissue.definition: Vascular tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of vascular tissue. This concept does not refer to neoplasms located in blood vessels.

ticdisorders.name: tic disorders
ticdisorders.definition: Tic disorders is disorders characterized by recurrent tics that may interfere with [MASK] and other activities. Tics are sudden, rapid, nonrhythmic, stereotyped motor movements or vocalizations which may be exacerbated by stress and are generally attenuated during absorbing activities. Tic disorders are distinguished from conditions which feature other types of abnormal movements that may accompany another another condition. (From [MASK], 1994)

memory.name: memory
memory.definition: Memory is complex mental function having four distinct phases: (1) memorizing or learning, (2) retention, (3) recall, and (4) recognition. Clinically, it is usually subdivided into immediate, recent, and remote memory.

biometricidentification.name: biometric identification
biometricidentification.definition: Biometric identification is a method of differentiating individuals based on the analysis of qualitative or quantitative biological traits or patterns. Biometric identification, which has applications in forensics and identity theft prevention, includes dna profiles or dna fingerprints; fingerprints; automated facial recognition; iris scan; retina scan; hand geometry; vascular patterns; automated voice pattern recognition; ultrasound of fingers; and x-rays.

aggressivedriving.name: aggressive driving
aggressivedriving.definition: Aggressive driving is combination of moving traffic offenses so as to endanger other persons or property. (https://nhtsa.gov/Driving-Safety/Aggressive-Driving)

sarcoma37.name: sarcoma 37
sarcoma37.definition: Sarcoma 37 is an experimental sarcoma of mice.

academicdissertation.name: academic dissertation
academicdissertation.definition: Academic dissertation is work consisting of formal presentations made usually to fulfill requirements for an academic degree.

archives.name: archives
archives.definition: Archives is a collection of historical documents or records providing information about places, institutions, or groups of people; also the place where such records are kept.

hotmeltextrusiontechnology.name: hot melt extrusion technology
hotmeltextrusiontechnology.definition: Hot melt extrusion technology is solvent-free method for preparing numerous types of drug delivery systems and dosage forms for active pharmaceutical ingredients that have solubility issues. It involves pumping polymeric materials at temperatures above their glass transition temperature to mix in active pharmaceutical ingredients with or without binders thus forming an amorphous product with an  increase in the dissolution profile for the active pharmaceutical ingredients.

robotics.name: robotics
robotics.definition: Robotics is the application of electronic, computerized control systems to mechanical devices designed to perform human functions. Formerly restricted to industry, but nowadays applied to artificial organs controlled by bionic (bioelectronic) devices, like automated insulin pumps and other prostheses.

socialwelfare.name: social welfare
socialwelfare.definition: Social welfare is organized institutions which provide services to ameliorate conditions of need or social pathology in the community.

geneproducts,tax.name: gene products , tax
geneproducts,tax.definition: Tax gene products is transcriptional trans-acting proteins of the promoter elements found in the long terminal repeats (ltr) of human t-lymphotropic virus 1 and human t-lymphotropic virus 2. The tax (trans-activator x; x is undefined) proteins act by binding to enhancer elements in the ltr.

pituitarygland.name: pituitary gland
pituitarygland.definition: Pituitary gland is a small, unpaired gland situated in the sella turcica. It is connected to the hypothalamus by a short stalk which is called the infundibulum.

calciumsulfate.name: calcium sulfate
calciumsulfate.definition: Calcium sulfate is a calcium [MASK] that is used for a variety of purposes including: building materials, as a desiccant, in dentistry as an impression material, cast, or die, and in medicine for immobilizing casts and as a tablet excipient. It exists in various forms and states of hydration. Plaster of Paris is a mixture of powdered and heat-treated gypsum.

somatosensorydisorders.name: somatosensory disorders
somatosensorydisorders.definition: Somatosensory disorders is disorders of sensory information received from superficial and deep regions of the body. The somatosensory system conveys neural impulses which pertain to proprioception, tactile sensation, thermal sensation, pressure sensation, and pain. peripheral nervous system diseases; spinal cord diseases; and brain diseases may be associated with impaired or abnormal somatic sensation.

generalsurgery.name: general surgery
generalsurgery.definition: General surgery is a specialty in which manual or operative procedures are used in the treatment of disease, injuries, or deformities.

mechanics.name: mechanics
mechanics.definition: Mechanics is the branch of physics which deals with the motions of material bodies, including kinematics, dynamics, and statics. When the laws of mechanics are applied to living structures, as to the locomotor system, it is referred to as biomechanical phenomena. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

congenitalabnormalities.name: congenital abnormalities
congenitalabnormalities.definition: Congenital abnormalities is malformations of organs or [MASK] during development in utero.

chlorophyllbindingproteins.name: chlorophyll binding proteins
chlorophyllbindingproteins.definition: Chlorophyll binding proteins is a large family of proteins that have been traditionally classified as the light-harvesting proteins of the photosynthetic reaction complex. Chlorophyll binding proteins are also found in non-photosynthetic settings where they may play a photoprotective role in response to light stress.

woundinfection.name: wound infection
woundinfection.definition: Wound infection is invasion of a wound by pathogenic microorganisms.

antigenicvariation.name: antigenic variation
antigenicvariation.definition: Antigenic variation is change in the surface antigen of a microorganism. There are two different types. One is a phenomenon, especially associated with influenza viruses, where they undergo spontaneous variation both as slow antigenic drift and sudden emergence of new strains (antigenic shift). The second type is when certain parasites, especially trypanosomes, plasmodium, and borrelia, survive the immune response of the host by changing the surface coat (antigen switching). (From Herbert et al., The Dictionary of [MASK], 4th ed)

ribosomesubunits,small.name: ribosome subunits , small
ribosomesubunits,small.definition: Small ribosome subunits is the small ribonucleoprotein component of ribosomes. It contains the messenger rna binding site and two transfer rna binding sites - one for the incoming [MASK] (a site) and the other (p site) for the peptidyl tRNA carrying the elongating peptide chain.

ruralhealth.name: rural health
ruralhealth.definition: Rural health is the status of health in rural populations.

clinicaltrial,veterinary.name: clinical trial , veterinary
clinicaltrial,veterinary.definition: Veterinary clinical trial is a work that is a veterinary clinical study in which animal participants are assigned to receive one or more interventions so that researchers can evaluate the interventions on biomedical or health-related outcomes. The assignments are determined by the study protocol. Animal participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions.

oxygenradicalabsorbancecapacity.name: oxygen radical absorbance capacity
oxygenradicalabsorbancecapacity.definition: Oxygen radical absorbance capacity is a measure of the ability of a substance, such as a food, to quench oxygen free radicals in vitro.

dengue.name: dengue
dengue.definition: Dengue is an acute febrile disease transmitted by the bite of aedes mosquitoes infected with dengue virus. It is self-limiting and characterized by fever, myalgia, headache, and rash. severe dengue is a more virulent form of dengue.

psychologicaltechniques.name: psychological techniques
psychologicaltechniques.definition: Psychological techniques is methods used in the diagnosis and treatment of behavioral, personality, and mental disorders.

adjustmentdisorders.name: adjustment disorders
adjustmentdisorders.definition: [MASK] disorders is maladaptive reactions to identifiable psychosocial stressors occurring within a short time after onset of the stressor. They are manifested by either impairment in social or occupational functioning or by symptoms (depression, anxiety, etc.) that are in excess of a normal and expected reaction to the stressor.

languagedevelopmentdisorders.name: language development disorders
languagedevelopmentdisorders.definition: Language development disorders is conditions characterized by language abilities (comprehension and expression of [MASK] and writing) that are below the expected level for a given age, generally in the absence of an intellectual impairment. These conditions may be associated with deafness; brain diseases; mental disorders; or environmental factors.

excitatoryaminoacidagonists.name: excitatory amino acid agonists
excitatoryaminoacidagonists.definition: [MASK] agonists is drugs that bind to and activate [MASK].

prognosis.name: prognosis
prognosis.definition: Prognosis is a prediction of the probable outcome of a disease based on a individual's condition and the usual course of the disease as seen in similar situations.

vestibulardiseases.name: vestibular diseases
vestibulardiseases.definition: Vestibular diseases is pathological processes of the vestibular [MASK] which contains part of the balancing apparatus. Patients with vestibular diseases show instability and are at risk of frequent falls.

physicaleducationandtraining.name: physical education and training
physicaleducationandtraining.definition: Physical education and training is instructional programs in the care and development of the body, often in schools. The concept does not include prescribed exercises, which is exercise therapy.

foodcontamination,radioactive.name: food contamination , radioactive
foodcontamination,radioactive.definition: Radioactive food contamination is exposure of food to radioactive substances, distinguishable from food irradiation, a food preservation technique.

rotavirusinfections.name: rotavirus infections
rotavirusinfections.definition: Rotavirus infections is infection with any of the rotaviruses. Specific infections include human infantile [MASK], neonatal calf [MASK], and epidemic [MASK] of infant mice.

nursingaudit.name: nursing audit
nursingaudit.definition: Nursing audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel for evaluating quality of nursing care.

occupationaltherapydepartment,hospital.name: occupational therapy department , hospital
occupationaltherapydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital [MASK] department is hospital department responsible for the administration and provision of any occupational or work activity for remedial purposes.

activationanalysis.name: activation analysis
activationanalysis.definition: Activation analysis is a method of chemical analysis based on the detection of characteristic radionuclides following a nuclear bombardment. It is also known as radioactivity analysis. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

transplantation,autologous.name: transplantation , autologous
transplantation,autologous.definition: Autologous transplantation is transplantation of an individual's own tissue from one site to another site.

unfoldedproteinresponse.name: unfolded protein response
unfoldedproteinresponse.definition: Unfolded protein response is a cellular response to environmental insults that cause disruptions in protein folding and/or accumulation of defectively folded protein in the endoplasmic reticulum. It consists of a group of regulatory cascades that are triggered as a response to altered levels of calcium and/or the redox state of the endoplasmic reticulum. Persistent activation of the unfolded protein response leads to the induction of apoptosis.

fetaldiseases.name: fetal diseases
fetaldiseases.definition: Fetal diseases is pathophysiological conditions of the fetus in the uterus. Some fetal diseases may be treated with fetal therapies.

workers'compensation.name: workers ' compensation
workers'compensation.definition: Workers' compensation is insurance coverage providing compensation and medical benefits to individuals because of work-connected injuries or disease.

plasminogen.name: plasminogen
plasminogen.definition: Plasminogen is precursor of plasmin (fibrinolysin). It is a single-chain beta-globulin of molecular weight 80-90,000 found mostly in association with fibrinogen in plasma; plasminogen activators change it to fibrinolysin. It is used in wound debriding and has been investigated as a thrombolytic agent.

deltarhythm.name: delta rhythm
deltarhythm.definition: Delta rhythm is brain waves seen on eeg characterized by a high amplitude and a frequency of 4 Hz and below. They are considered the "deep sleep waves" observed during sleep in dreamless states, infancy, and in some brain disorders.

role.name: role
role.definition: Role is the expected and characteristic pattern of behavior exhibited by an individual as a member of a particular social group.

helacells.name: hela cells
helacells.definition: Hela cells is the first continuously cultured human malignant cell line, derived from the cervical carcinoma of Henrietta Lacks. These cells are used for, among other things, virus cultivation and preclinical drug evaluation assays.

mice,129strain.name: mice , 129 strain
mice,129strain.definition: 129 strain mice is strains of mice arising from a parental inbred stock that was subsequently used to produce substrains of knockout and other mutant mice with targeted mutations.

plasmavolume.name: plasma volume
plasmavolume.definition: Plasma volume is volume of plasma in the circulation. It is usually measured by indicator dilution techniques.

chromosomes,human,pair19.name: chromosomes , human , pair 19
chromosomes,human,pair19.definition: Pair 19 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group f chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

receptors,leptin.name: receptors , leptin
receptors,leptin.definition: Leptin receptors is cell surface receptors for obesity factor (leptin), a hormone secreted by the [MASK]. Upon leptin-receptor interaction, the signal is mediated through the jak2/stat3 pathway to regulate food intake, energy balance and fat storage.

pancreastransplantation.name: pancreas transplantation
pancreastransplantation.definition: Pancreas transplantation is the transference of a pancreas from one human or animal to another.

glutathioneperoxidase.name: glutathione peroxidase
glutathioneperoxidase.definition: Glutathione peroxidase is an enzyme catalyzing the oxidation of 2 moles of glutathione in the presence of hydrogen peroxide to yield [MASK] and water.

autoimmunediseases.name: autoimmune diseases
autoimmunediseases.definition: Autoimmune diseases is disorders that are characterized by the production of antibodies that react with host tissues or immune effector cells that are autoreactive to endogenous peptides.

affinitylabels.name: affinity labels
affinitylabels.definition: Affinity labels is analogs of those substrates or compounds which bind naturally at the [MASK] of proteins, enzymes, antibodies, steroids, or physiological receptors. These analogs form a stable covalent bond at the binding site, thereby acting as inhibitors of the proteins or steroids.

drugresistance,microbial.name: drug resistance , microbial
drugresistance,microbial.definition: Microbial drug resistance is the ability of microorganisms, especially bacteria, to resist or to become tolerant to chemotherapeutic agents, antimicrobial agents, or antibiotics. This resistance may be acquired through gene mutation or foreign dna in transmissible plasmids (r factors).

discriminationlearning.name: discrimination learning
discriminationlearning.definition: Discrimination learning is learning that is manifested in the ability to respond differentially to various stimuli.

maternalmortality.name: maternal mortality
maternalmortality.definition: Maternal mortality is maternal deaths resulting from complications of pregnancy and childbirth in a given population.

pregnancytrimester,second.name: pregnancy trimester , second
pregnancytrimester,second.definition: Second pregnancy trimester is the middle third of a human pregnancy, from the beginning of the 15th through the 28th completed week (99 to 196 days) of gestation.

nuclearenergy.name: nuclear energy
nuclearenergy.definition: Nuclear energy is energy released by [MASK] or nuclear fusion.

ethidium.name: ethidium
ethidium.definition: Ethidium is a trypanocidal agent and possible antiviral agent that is widely used in experimental cell biology and biochemistry. Ethidium has several experimentally useful properties including binding to nucleic acids, noncompetitive inhibition of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, and fluorescence among others. It is most commonly used as the bromide.

venousthrombosis.name: venous thrombosis
venousthrombosis.definition: Venous thrombosis is the formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) within a vein.

neurons.name: neurons
neurons.definition: Neurons is the basic cellular units of nervous tissue. Each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. Their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.

mycobacterium.name: mycobacterium
mycobacterium.definition: Mycobacterium is a genus of gram-positive, [MASK]. Most species are free-living in soil and water, but the major habitat for some is the diseased tissue of warm-blooded hosts.

forensicpathology.name: forensic pathology
forensicpathology.definition: Forensic pathology is the application of pathology to questions of law.

brainischemia.name: brain ischemia
brainischemia.definition: Brain ischemia is localized reduction of blood flow to brain tissue due to arterial obstruction or systemic hypoperfusion. This frequently occurs in conjunction with brain hypoxia (hypoxia, brain). Prolonged ischemia is associated with brain infarction.

cellmembranepermeability.name: cell membrane permeability
cellmembranepermeability.definition: Cell membrane permeability is a quality of cell membranes which permits the passage of solvents and solutes into and out of cells.

roleplaying.name: role playing
roleplaying.definition: Role playing is the adopting or performing the role of another significant individual in order to gain insight into the behavior of that person.

datavisualization.name: data visualization
datavisualization.definition: Data visualization is facilitating understanding of the significance of data by placing it in a visual context. Patterns, trends and correlations that might go undetected in text-based data may be exposed and recognized easier.

eggproteins.name: egg proteins
eggproteins.definition: Egg proteins is proteins which are found in eggs (ova) from any species.

cesareansection.name: cesarean section
cesareansection.definition: Cesarean section is extraction of the fetus by means of abdominal hysterotomy.

saccharomyces.name: saccharomyces
saccharomyces.definition: Saccharomyces is a genus of ascomycetous fungi of the family Saccharomycetaceae, order saccharomycetales.

retinaldehydrogenase.name: retinal dehydrogenase
retinaldehydrogenase.definition: Retinal dehydrogenase is a metalloflavoprotein enzyme involved the metabolism of vitamin a, this enzyme catalyzes the oxidation of retinal to retinoic acid, using both nad+ and fad coenzymes. It also acts on both the 11-trans- and 13-cis-forms of retinal.

laborunions.name: labor unions
laborunions.definition: Labor unions is organizations comprising wage and salary workers in health-related fields for the purpose of improving their status and conditions. The concept includes labor union activities toward providing health services to members.

starchsynthase.name: starch synthase
starchsynthase.definition: [MASK] synthase is an enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of glucose from ADPglucose to glucose-containing polysaccharides in 1,4-alpha-linkages. ec 2.4.1.21.

genes,px.name: genes , px
genes,px.definition: Px genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for at least three proteins which regulate the expression of human t-lymphotropic virus 1 and human t-lymphotropic virus 2. The proteins are p21(x), p27(rex), and p40(tax). The tax (trans-activator x) and rex (regulator x) genes are part of pX but are in overlapping reading frames. x was the original designation for the sequences or region (at that time of unknown function) in the long open reading frame (lor) which is now called pX.

fibrinfibrinogendegradationproducts.name: fibrin fibrinogen degradation products
fibrinfibrinogendegradationproducts.definition: Fibrin fibrinogen degradation products is soluble protein fragments formed by the proteolytic action of plasmin on fibrin or fibrinogen. fdp and their complexes profoundly impair the hemostatic process and are a major cause of hemorrhage in intravascular coagulation and fibrinolysis.

unitedstatesvirginislands.name: united states virgin islands
unitedstatesvirginislands.definition: United states virgin islands is a group of islands in the Lesser Antilles in the West Indies, the three main islands being St. Croix, St. Thomas, and St. John. The capital is Charlotte Amalie. Before 1917 the u.s. Virgin Islands were held by the Danish and called the Danish West Indies but the name was changed when the United States acquired them by purchase.

nearmiss,healthcare.name: near miss , healthcare
nearmiss,healthcare.definition: Healthcare near miss is event that presented a risk but did not result in a patient harm.

earprotectivedevices.name: ear protective devices
earprotectivedevices.definition: Ear protective devices is personal devices for protection of the ears from loud or high intensity noise, water, or cold. These include earmuffs and earplugs.

unitedstatesdepartmentofagriculture.name: united states department of agriculture
unitedstatesdepartmentofagriculture.definition: United states department of agriculture is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government concerned with improving and maintaining farm income and developing and expanding markets for agricultural products. Through inspection and grading services it safeguards and insures standards of quality in food supply and production.

diseasemanagement.name: disease management
diseasemanagement.definition: Disease management is a broad approach to appropriate coordination of the entire disease treatment process that often involves shifting away from more expensive inpatient and acute care to areas such as preventive medicine, patient counseling and education, and outpatient care. This concept includes implications of appropriate versus inappropriate therapy on the overall cost and clinical outcome of a particular disease. (From Hosp Pharm 1995 Jul;30(7):596)

fetaldistress.name: fetal distress
fetaldistress.definition: Fetal distress is a nonreassuring fetal status (nrfs) indicating that the fetus is compromised (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists 1988). It can be identified by sub-optimal values in fetal heart rate; oxygenation of [MASK]; and other parameters.

geographiclocations.name: geographic locations
geographiclocations.definition: Geographic locations is the continents and countries situated on those continents; the united states and each of the constituent states arranged by region; canada and each of its provinces; australia and each of its states; the major bodies of water and major islands on both hemispheres; and selected major cities.

rupture.name: rupture
rupture.definition: Rupture is forcible or traumatic tear or break of an organ or other soft part of the body.

zinctransporter8.name: zinc transporter 8
zinctransporter8.definition: Zinc transporter 8 is a zinc efflux transporter highly expressed by islet cells of the pancreas. It functions in the accumulation of zinc in intracellular vesicles and may be involved in insulin maturation and storage processes. Variations in the slc30a8 gene are associated with susceptibility to diabetes mellitus, type 2.

noise,occupational.name: noise , occupational
noise,occupational.definition: Occupational noise is noise present in occupational, industrial, and factory situations.

pacificocean.name: pacific ocean
pacificocean.definition: Pacific ocean is body of water between Asia and South America, extending from the Arctic circle to the Equator and from the Equator to the Antarctic.

organizationandadministration.name: organization and administration
organizationandadministration.definition: Organization and administration is the planning and managing of programs, services, and resources.

physicalfunctionalperformance.name: physical functional performance
physicalfunctionalperformance.definition: Physical functional performance is the level of functional limitation that may be due to pathology, and evaluating rehabilitative intervention of the way in which the body moves from one point to another.

highpressureneurologicalsyndrome.name: high pressure neurological syndrome
highpressureneurologicalsyndrome.definition: High pressure neurological syndrome is a syndrome related to increased atmospheric pressure and characterized by tremors, nausea, dizziness, decreased motor and mental performance, and seizures. This condition may occur in those who dive deeply (c. 1000 ft) usually while breathing a mixture of oxygen and [MASK]. The condition is associated with a neuroexcitatory effect of [MASK].

ciprofloxacin.name: ciprofloxacin
ciprofloxacin.definition: Ciprofloxacin is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial carboxyfluoroquinoline.

healthcarefailuremodeandeffectanalysis.name: healthcare failure mode and effect analysis
healthcarefailuremodeandeffectanalysis.definition: Healthcare failure mode and effect analysis is prospective risk assessment tool aimed at identifying potential risks and their impact in healthcare settings.

neoplasms,secondprimary.name: neoplasms , second primary
neoplasms,secondprimary.definition: Second primary neoplasms is abnormal growths of tissue that follow a previous neoplasm but are not metastases of the latter. The second neoplasm may have the same or different histological type and can occur in the same or different organs as the previous neoplasm but in all cases arises from an independent oncogenic event. The development of the second neoplasm may or may not be related to the treatment for the previous neoplasm since genetic risk or predisposing factors may actually be the cause.

alleles.name: alleles
alleles.definition: Alleles is variant forms of the same gene, occupying the same locus on homologous chromosomes, and governing the variants in production of the same gene product.

nutritionalsupport.name: nutritional support
nutritionalsupport.definition: Nutritional support is the administration of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient by means other than normal eating. It does not include fluid therapy which normalizes body fluids to restore water-electrolyte balance.

commonbileduct.name: common bile duct
commonbileduct.definition: Common [MASK] is the largest [MASK]. It is formed by the junction of the cystic duct and the common hepatic duct.

datacompression.name: data compression
datacompression.definition: Data compression is information application based on a variety of coding methods to minimize the amount of data to be stored, retrieved, or transmitted. Data compression can be applied to various forms of data, such as images and signals. It is used to reduce costs and increase efficiency in the maintenance of large volumes of data.

objectattachment.name: object attachment
objectattachment.definition: Object attachment is emotional attachment to someone or something in the environment.

insurance.name: insurance
insurance.definition: Insurance is coverage by contract whereby one part indemnifies or guarantees another against loss by a specified contingency.

immuneadherencereaction.name: immune adherence reaction
immuneadherencereaction.definition: Immune adherence reaction is a method for the detection of very small quantities of antibody in which the antigen-antibody-complement complex adheres to indicator cells, usually primate erythrocytes or nonprimate blood platelets. The reaction is dependent on the number of bound c3 molecules on the C3b receptor sites of the indicator cell.

proteinstability.name: protein stability
proteinstability.definition: Protein stability is the ability of a protein to retain its structural conformation or its activity when subjected to physical or chemical manipulations.

dentalprophylaxis.name: dental prophylaxis
dentalprophylaxis.definition: Dental prophylaxis is treatment for the prevention of periodontal diseases or other dental diseases by the cleaning of the teeth in the [MASK] using the procedures of dental scaling and dental polishing. The treatment may include plaque detection, removal of supra- and subgingival plaque and calculus, application of caries-preventing agents, checking of restorations and prostheses and correcting overhanging margins and proximal contours of restorations, and checking for signs of food impaction.

neoplasticcells,circulating.name: neoplastic cells , circulating
neoplasticcells,circulating.definition: Circulating neoplastic cells is exfoliate neoplastic cells circulating in the blood and associated with metastasizing tumors.

urine.name: urine
urine.definition: Urine is liquid by-product of excretion produced in the kidneys, temporarily stored in the [MASK] until discharge through the urethra.

artificialorgans.name: artificial organs
artificialorgans.definition: Artificial organs is devices intended to replace non-functioning organs. They may be temporary or permanent. Since they are intended always to function as the natural organs they are replacing, they should be differentiated from prostheses and implants and specific types of prostheses which, though also replacements for [MASK], are frequently cosmetic (eye, artificial) as well as functional ([MASK]).

epilepsy.name: epilepsy
epilepsy.definition: Epilepsy is a disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of paroxysmal brain dysfunction due to a sudden, disorderly, and excessive neuronal discharge. Epilepsy classification systems are generally based upon: (1) clinical features of the seizure episodes (e.g., motor seizure), (2) etiology (e.g., post-traumatic), (3) anatomic site of seizure origin (e.g., frontal lobe seizure), (4) tendency to spread to other structures in the brain, and (5) temporal patterns (e.g., nocturnal epilepsy). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p313)

focaladhesionkinase2.name: focal adhesion kinase 2
focaladhesionkinase2.definition: Focal adhesion kinase 2 is a non-receptor protein-tyrosine kinase that is expressed primarily in the brain; [MASK]; and lymphoid cells. In the central nervous system focal adhesion kinase 2 modulates ion channel function and mitogen-activated protein kinases activity.

salmonellatyphimurium.name: salmonella typhimurium
salmonellatyphimurium.definition: Salmonella typhimurium is a serotype of Salmonella enterica that is a frequent agent of Salmonella gastroenteritis in humans. It also causes paratyphoid fever.

bedrest.name: bed rest
bedrest.definition: Bed rest is confinement of an individual to bed for therapeutic or experimental reasons.

haircells,auditory.name: hair cells , auditory
haircells,auditory.definition: Auditory hair cells is sensory cells in the organ of Corti, characterized by their apical stereocilia (hair-like projections). The inner and outer hair cells, as defined by their proximity to the core of spongy bone (the modiolus), change morphologically along the cochlea. Towards the cochlear apex, the length of hair cell bodies and their apical stereocilia increase, allowing differential responses to various frequencies of sound.

bleachingagents.name: bleaching agents
bleachingagents.definition: Bleaching agents is chemicals that are used to oxidize pigments and thus effect whitening.

genes.name: genes
genes.definition: Genes is a category of nucleic acid sequences that function as units of heredity and which code for the basic instructions for the development, reproduction, and maintenance of organisms.

cartilage,articular.name: cartilage , articular
cartilage,articular.definition: Articular cartilage is a protective layer of firm, flexible cartilage over the articulating ends of bones. It provides a smooth surface for joint movement, protecting the ends of long bones from wear at points of contact.

ether.name: ether
ether.definition: Ether is a mobile, very volatile, highly flammable liquid used as an [MASK] anesthetic and as a solvent for waxes, fats, oils, perfumes, alkaloids, and gums. It is mildly irritating to skin and mucous membranes.

actincytoskeleton.name: actin cytoskeleton
actincytoskeleton.definition: Actin cytoskeleton is fibers composed of microfilament proteins, which are predominately actin. They are the smallest of the cytoskeletal filaments.

appliedbehavioranalysis.name: applied behavior analysis
appliedbehavioranalysis.definition: Applied behavior analysis is behavioral science applied with the aim of improving socially important issues such as behavior problems and learning. For individuals diagnosed with intellectual and developmental disabilities including autism, techniques can be categorized as comprehensive or focused.

biomedicalanddentalmaterials.name: biomedical and dental materials
biomedicalanddentalmaterials.definition: Biomedical and dental materials is substances used in biomedicine or dentistry predominantly for their physical, as opposed to chemical, properties.

substratecycling.name: substrate cycling
substratecycling.definition: Substrate cycling is a [MASK] of opposing, nonequilibrium reactions catalyzed by different enzymes which act simultaneously, with at least one of the reactions driven by atp hydrolysis. The results of the cycle are that atp energy is depleted, heat is produced and no net substrate-to-product conversion is achieved. Examples of substrate cycling are cycling of gluconeogenesis and glycolysis pathways and cycling of the triglycerides and fatty acid pathways. Rates of substrate cycling may be increased many-fold in association with hypermetabolic states resulting from severe burns, cold exposure, hyperthyroidism, or acute exercise.

nursingservices.name: nursing services
nursingservices.definition: Nursing services is a general concept referring to the organization and administration of nursing activities.

aorticarchsyndromes.name: aortic arch syndromes
aorticarchsyndromes.definition: Aortic arch syndromes is conditions resulting from abnormalities in the arteries branching from the ascending aorta, the curved portion of the aorta. These syndromes are results of occlusion or abnormal blood flow to the head-[MASK] or [MASK] region leading to neurological defects and weakness in an [MASK]. These syndromes are associated with vascular malformations; atherosclerosis; trauma; and blood clots.

proteindegradationendproducts.name: protein degradation end products
proteindegradationendproducts.definition: Protein degradation end products is degraded protein components that are found within tissues, bodily fluids, and cells under certain pathological conditions. They are largely formed through chemical reactions which occur during non-physiological conditions such as ischemia; hyperglycemia; and physiological stress.

livingdonors.name: living donors
livingdonors.definition: Living donors is non-cadaveric providers of organs for [MASK] to related or non-related recipients.

militarymedicine.name: military medicine
militarymedicine.definition: Military medicine is the practice of medicine as applied to special circumstances associated with military operations.

sodiumnitrite.name: sodium nitrite
sodiumnitrite.definition: Sodium nitrite is nitrous acid sodium [MASK]. Used in many industrial processes, in meat curing, coloring, and preserving, and as a reagent in analytical chemistry techniques. It is used therapeutically as an antidote in cyanide poisoning. The compound is toxic and mutagenic and will react in vivo with secondary or tertiary amines thereby producing highly carcinogenic nitrosamines.

rarediseases.name: rare diseases
rarediseases.definition: Rare diseases is a large group of diseases which are characterized by a low [MASK] in the population. They frequently are associated with problems in diagnosis and treatment.

risk.name: risk
risk.definition: Risk is the probability that an event will occur. It encompasses a variety of measures of the probability of a generally unfavorable outcome.

brainabscess.name: brain abscess
brainabscess.definition: Brain abscess is a circumscribed collection of purulent exudate in the brain, due to bacterial and other infections. The majority are caused by spread of infected material from a focus of suppuration elsewhere in the body, notably the paranasal sinuses, [MASK] (see [MASK]); heart (see also endocarditis, bacterial), and lung. Penetrating craniocerebral trauma and neurosurgical procedures may also be associated with this condition. Clinical manifestations include headache; seizures; focal neurologic deficits; and alterations of consciousness. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp712-6)

energymetabolism.name: energy metabolism
energymetabolism.definition: Energy metabolism is the chemical reactions involved in the production and utilization of various forms of energy in cells.

misseddiagnosis.name: missed diagnosis
misseddiagnosis.definition: Missed diagnosis is failure to identify or diagnose a medical condition at the time a health professional is acquainted with the symptoms.

reproductivetechniques.name: reproductive techniques
reproductivetechniques.definition: Reproductive techniques is methods pertaining to the generation of new individuals, including techniques used in [MASK], cloning (cloning, organism), and assisted reproduction (reproductive techniques, assisted).

bilirubin.name: bilirubin
bilirubin.definition: Bilirubin is a [MASK] pigment that is a degradation product of heme.

hongkong.name: hong kong
hongkong.definition: Hong kong is the former British crown colony located off the southeast coast of China, comprised of Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peninsula, and New Territories. The three sites were ceded to the British by the Chinese respectively in 1841, 1860, and 1898. Hong Kong reverted to China in July 1997. The name represents the Cantonese pronunciation of the Chinese xianggang, fragrant port, from xiang, perfume and gang, port or harbor, with reference to its currents sweetened by fresh water from a [MASK] west of it.

immunoglobulinvariableregion.name: immunoglobulin variable region
immunoglobulinvariableregion.definition: Immunoglobulin variable region is that region of the immunoglobulin molecule that varies in its amino acid sequence and composition, and comprises the binding site for a specific antigen. It is located at the N-terminus of the Fab fragment of the immunoglobulin. It includes hypervariable [MASK] regions) and framework regions.

receptors,isletamyloidpolypeptide.name: receptors , islet amyloid polypeptide
receptors,isletamyloidpolypeptide.definition: Islet amyloid polypeptide receptors is g-protein coupled receptors that are formed through the [MASK] of the calcitonin receptor with a receptor activity-modifying protein. Their affinity for islet amyloid polypeptide is dependent upon which of several receptor activity-modifying protein subtypes they are bound to.

intracranialhypertension.name: intracranial hypertension
intracranialhypertension.definition: Intracranial hypertension is increased pressure within the cranial vault. This may result from several conditions, including hydrocephalus; brain edema; intracranial masses; severe systemic hypertension; pseudotumor cerebri; and other disorders.

organpreservation.name: organ preservation
organpreservation.definition: Organ preservation is the process by which organs are kept viable outside of the organism from which they were removed (i.e., kept from decay by means of a chemical agent, cooling, or a fluid substitute that mimics the natural state within the organism).

ventricularfibrillation.name: ventricular fibrillation
ventricularfibrillation.definition: Ventricular fibrillation is a potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia that is characterized by uncoordinated extremely rapid firing of electrical impulses (400-600/min) in heart ventricles. Such asynchronous ventricular quivering or fibrillation prevents any effective cardiac output and results in unconsciousness (syncope). It is one of the major electrocardiographic patterns seen with cardiac arrest.

toothcervix.name: tooth cervix
toothcervix.definition: Tooth cervix is the constricted part of the tooth at the junction of the crown and root or roots. It is often referred to as the cementoenamel junction (cej), the line at which the cementum covering the root of a tooth and the enamel of the tooth meet. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p530, p433)

biologicalspecimenbanks.name: biological specimen banks
biologicalspecimenbanks.definition: Biological specimen banks is facilities that collect, store, and distribute tissues, e.g., cell lines, microorganisms, blood, sperm, [MASK] tissue, for use by others. Other uses may include transplantation and comparison of diseased tissues in the identification of cancer.

genes,gag.name: genes , gag
genes,gag.definition: Gag genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for proteins associated with the viral core in retroviruses. gag is short for group-specific antigen.

advancedpracticenursing.name: advanced practice nursing
advancedpracticenursing.definition: Advanced practice nursing is evidence-based nursing, midwifery and healthcare grounded in research and scholarship. Practitioners include nurse practitioners, [MASK], nurse anesthetists, and nurse midwives.

locomotion.name: locomotion
locomotion.definition: Locomotion is movement or the ability to move from one place or another. It can refer to humans, vertebrate or invertebrate animals, and microorganisms.

socialbehavior.name: social behavior
socialbehavior.definition: Social behavior is any behavior caused by or affecting another individual or group usually of the same species.

plantepidermis.name: plant epidermis
plantepidermis.definition: Plant epidermis is a thin layer of cells forming the outer integument of [MASK] plants and ferns. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

unitedstatesofficeoftechnologyassessment.name: united states office of technology assessment
unitedstatesofficeoftechnologyassessment.definition: United states office of technology assessment is an office established to help Congress participate and plan for the consequences of uses of technology. It provided information on both the beneficial and adverse effects of technological applications. The Office of Technology Assessment closed on September 29, 1995.

vascularsysteminjuries.name: vascular system injuries
vascularsysteminjuries.definition: Vascular system injuries is injuries to blood vessels caused by laceration, contusion, puncture, or crush and other types of injuries. Symptoms vary by site and mode of injuries and may include bleeding, bruising, swelling, pain, and numbness. It does not include injuries secondary to pathologic function or diseases such as atherosclerosis.

immunization.name: immunization
immunization.definition: Immunization is deliberate stimulation of the host's immune response. active immunization involves administration of antigens or immunologic adjuvants. passive immunization involves administration of immune sera or lymphocytes or their extracts (e.g., transfer factor, immune rna) or transplantation of immunocompetent cell producing tissue (thymus or bone marrow).

lateralthalamicnuclei.name: lateral thalamic nuclei
lateralthalamicnuclei.definition: Lateral thalamic nuclei is a narrow strip of cell groups on the dorsomedial surface of the thalamus. It includes the lateral dorsal nucleus, lateral posterior nucleus, and the pulvinar.

proteininteractionmapping.name: protein interaction mapping
proteininteractionmapping.definition: Protein interaction mapping is methods for determining interaction between proteins.

healthpolicy.name: health policy
healthpolicy.definition: Health policy is decisions, usually developed by government policymakers, for determining present and future objectives pertaining to the health care system.

kenya.name: kenya
kenya.definition: Kenya is a republic in eastern Africa, south of ethiopia, west of somalia with [MASK] to its south, and coastline on the Indian Ocean. Its capital is Nairobi.

mercurycompounds.name: mercury compounds
mercurycompounds.definition: Mercury compounds is inorganic compounds that contain mercury as an integral part of the molecule.

hypoglycemia.name: hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia.definition: Hypoglycemia is a syndrome of abnormally low blood glucose level. Clinical hypoglycemia has diverse etiologies. Severe hypoglycemia eventually lead to glucose deprivation of the central nervous system resulting in hunger; sweating; paresthesia; impaired mental function; seizures; coma; and even death.

utilizationreview.name: utilization review
utilizationreview.definition: Utilization review is an organized procedure carried out through committees to review admissions, duration of stay, professional services furnished, and to evaluate the medical necessity of those services and promote their most efficient use.

abortion,septic.name: abortion , septic
abortion,septic.definition: Septic abortion is any type of abortion, induced or spontaneous, that is associated with infection of the uterus and its appendages. It is characterized by fever, uterine tenderness, and foul discharge.

antibioticprophylaxis.name: antibiotic prophylaxis
antibioticprophylaxis.definition: Antibiotic prophylaxis is use of antibiotics before, during, or after a diagnostic, therapeutic, or surgical procedure to prevent infectious complications.

bonecysts.name: bone cysts
