bonecysts.definition: Bone cysts is benign unilocular lytic areas in the proximal end of a long bone with well defined and narrow endosteal margins. The cysts contain fluid and the cyst walls may contain some giant cells. Bone cysts usually occur in males between the ages 3-15 years.

singleparent.name: single parent
singleparent.definition: Single parent is a natural, adoptive, or substitute parent of a dependent child, who lives with only one parent. The single parent may live with or visit the child. The concept includes the never-married, as well as the divorced and widowed.

workplaceviolence.name: workplace violence
workplaceviolence.definition: Workplace violence is threatened or actual attempt to harm others at place of employment.

semen.name: semen
semen.definition: Semen is the thick, yellowish-[MASK], viscid fluid secretion of male reproductive organs discharged upon ejaculation. In addition to reproductive organ secretions, it contains spermatozoa and their nutrient plasma.

cocainesmoking.name: cocaine smoking
cocainesmoking.definition: Cocaine smoking is smoking of cocaine.

retina.name: retina
retina.definition: Retina is the ten-layered nervous tissue membrane of the eye. It is continuous with the optic nerve and receives images of external objects and transmits visual impulses to the brain. Its outer surface is in contact with the choroid and the inner surface with the [MASK]. The outer-most layer is pigmented, whereas the inner nine layers are transparent.

occupationalhealthservices.name: occupational health services
occupationalhealthservices.definition: [MASK] services is health services for employees, usually provided by the employer at the place of work.

managedcareprograms.name: managed care programs
managedcareprograms.definition: Managed care programs is health insurance plans intended to reduce unnecessary health care costs through a variety of mechanisms, including: economic incentives for physicians and patients to select less costly forms of care; programs for reviewing the medical necessity of specific services; increased beneficiary cost sharing; controls on inpatient admissions and lengths of stay; the establishment of cost-sharing incentives for outpatient surgery; selective contracting with health care providers; and the intensive management of high-cost health care cases. The programs may be provided in a variety of settings, such as health maintenance organizations and preferred provider organizations.

publicationformats.name: publication formats
publicationformats.definition: Publication formats is specific genre of publication.

observationalstudy.name: observational study
observationalstudy.definition: Observational study is a work that reports on the results of a clinical study in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

westvirginia.name: west virginia
westvirginia.definition: West virginia is state bounded on the north by Ohio, Maryland, and Pennsylvania, bounded on the west by Ohio and Kentucky, on the east and south by Virginia.

mandibulardiseases.name: mandibular diseases
mandibulardiseases.definition: Mandibular diseases is diseases involving the mandible.

playtherapy.name: play therapy
playtherapy.definition: Play therapy is a treatment technique utilizing play as a medium for expression and communication between patient and therapist.

education,continuing.name: education , continuing
education,continuing.definition: Continuing education is educational programs designed to inform individuals of recent advances in their particular field of interest. They do not lead to any formal advanced standing.

dentalarch.name: dental arch
dentalarch.definition: Dental arch is the curve formed by the row of teeth in their normal position in the jaw. The inferior dental arch is formed by the mandibular teeth, and the superior dental arch by the maxillary teeth.

dentalcareforchronicallyill.name: dental care for chronically ill
dentalcareforchronicallyill.definition: Dental care for chronically ill is dental care for patients with chronic diseases. These diseases include chronic cardiovascular, endocrinologic, hematologic, immunologic, neoplastic, and renal diseases. The concept does not include dental care for the mentally or physically disabled which is dental care for disabled.

mentallydisabledpersons.name: mentally disabled persons
mentallydisabledpersons.definition: Mentally disabled persons is mentally disabled persons

celltransformation,viral.name: cell transformation , viral
celltransformation,viral.definition: Viral cell transformation is an inheritable change in cells manifested by changes in cell division and growth and alterations in cell surface properties. It is induced by infection with a transforming virus.

abdominalpain.name: abdominal pain
abdominalpain.definition: Abdominal pain is sensation of discomfort, distress, or agony in the abdominal region.

adolescenthealthservices.name: adolescent health services
adolescenthealthservices.definition: [MASK] services is organized services to provide health care to adolescents, ages ranging from 13 through 18 years.

hepatitisavirus.name: hepatitis a virus
hepatitisavirus.definition: Hepatitis a virus is a species in the genus hepatovirus containing one serotype and two strains: human hepatitis a virus and Simian hepatitis a virus causing hepatitis in humans (hepatitis a) and primates, respectively.

head.name: head
head.definition: Head is the upper part of the [MASK], or the front or upper part of the body of an animal, typically separated from the rest of the body by a [MASK], and containing the brain, mouth, and sense organs.

china.name: china
china.definition: China is a country spanning from central Asia to the Pacific Ocean.

proteinstructure,quaternary.name: protein structure , quaternary
proteinstructure,quaternary.definition: Quaternary protein structure is the characteristic 3-dimensional shape and arrangement of multimeric proteins (aggregates of more than one polypeptide chain).

genomicstructuralvariation.name: genomic structural variation
genomicstructuralvariation.definition: Genomic structural variation is contiguous large-scale (1000-400,000 basepairs) differences in the genomic dna between individuals, due to sequence deletion; sequence insertion; or sequence inversion.

militaryfamily.name: military family
militaryfamily.definition: Military family is men and women serving on active duty in the military, or in a reserve military force, and their immediate family including spouses, children, and parents.

couptranscriptionfactori.name: coup transcription factor i
couptranscriptionfactori.definition: Coup transcription factor i is a coup transcription factor that was originally identified as a homodimer that binds to a direct repeat regulatory element in the [MASK] albumin promoter. It is a transcription factor that plays an important role in embryonic development of the central nervous system.

globalwarming.name: global warming
globalwarming.definition: Global warming is increase in the temperature of the atmosphere near the Earth's surface and in the troposphere, which can contribute to changes in global climate patterns.

hydrogenbonding.name: hydrogen bonding
hydrogenbonding.definition: Hydrogen bonding is a low-energy attractive force between hydrogen and another element. It plays a major role in determining the properties of water, proteins, and other compounds.

philosophy.name: philosophy
philosophy.definition: Philosophy is a love or pursuit of wisdom. a search for the underlying causes and principles of reality. (Webster, 3d ed)

probability.name: probability
probability.definition: Probability is the study of chance processes or the relative frequency characterizing a chance process.

multimedia.name: multimedia
multimedia.definition: Multimedia is materials, frequently computer applications, that combine some or all of text, sound, graphics, animation, and video into integrated packages. (Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, 1994)

methylgreen.name: methyl green
methylgreen.definition: Methyl green is a tri-benzene-ammonium usually compounded with zinc chloride. It is used as a biological stain and for the dyeing and printing of textiles.

parkingfacilities.name: parking facilities
parkingfacilities.definition: Parking facilities is indoor or outdoor areas designated for the parking of vehicles.

footbones.name: foot bones
footbones.definition: [MASK] bones is the tarsal bones; metatarsal bones; and phalanges of toes. The tarsal bones consists of seven bones: calcaneus; talus; cuboid; navicular; internal; middle; and external cuneiform bones. The five metatarsal bones are numbered one through five, [MASK] medial to lateral. There are 14 phalanges in each [MASK], the great toe has two while the other toes have three each.

injections,subcutaneous.name: injections , subcutaneous
injections,subcutaneous.definition: Subcutaneous injections is forceful administration under the skin of liquid medication, nutrient, or other fluid through a hollow needle piercing the skin.

genecomponents.name: gene components
genecomponents.definition: Gene components is the parts of the gene sequence that carry out the different functions of the genes.

maritalstatus.name: marital status
maritalstatus.definition: Marital status is a demographic parameter indicating a person's status with respect to marriage, divorce, widowhood, singleness, etc.

pregnancyproteins.name: pregnancy proteins
pregnancyproteins.definition: Pregnancy proteins is proteins produced by organs of the mother or the placenta during pregnancy. These proteins may be pregnancy-specific (present only during pregnancy) or pregnancy-associated (present during pregnancy or under other conditions such as hormone therapy or certain malignancies.)

healthsmartcards.name: health smart cards
healthsmartcards.definition: Health smart cards is hand-sized cards with built-in computer chips used for accessing, storing, and protecting patients' medical information.

obesity.name: obesity
obesity.definition: Obesity is a status with body weight that is grossly above the acceptable or desirable weight, usually due to accumulation of excess fats in the body. The standards may vary with age, [MASK], genetic or cultural background. In the body mass index, a bmi greater than 30.0 kg/m2 is considered obese, and a bmi greater than 40.0 kg/m2 is considered morbidly obese (morbid obesity).

obstetrics.name: obstetrics
obstetrics.definition: Obstetrics is a medical-surgical specialty concerned with management and care of women during pregnancy, parturition, and the puerperium.

thrombin.name: thrombin
thrombin.definition: Thrombin is an enzyme formed from prothrombin that converts fibrinogen to fibrin.

dopamine.name: dopamine
dopamine.definition: Dopamine is one of the catecholamine neurotransmitters in the brain. It is derived from tyrosine and is the precursor to norepinephrine and epinephrine. Dopamine is a major transmitter in the extrapyramidal system of the brain, and important in regulating movement. a family of receptors (receptors, dopamine) mediate its action.

discrimination,psychological.name: discrimination , psychological
discrimination,psychological.definition: Psychological discrimination is differential response to different stimuli.

laryngealnerves.name: laryngeal nerves
laryngealnerves.definition: Laryngeal nerves is branches of the vagus nerve. The superior laryngeal nerves originate near the nodose ganglion and separate into external branches, which supply motor fibers to the [MASK], and internal branches, which carry sensory fibers. The recurrent laryngeal nerve originates more caudally and carries efferents to all muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid. The laryngeal nerves and their various branches also carry sensory and autonomic fibers to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, tracheal, and cardiac regions.

narrowbandimaging.name: narrow band imaging
narrowbandimaging.definition: Narrow band imaging is imaging techniques that use [MASK] created with several optical interference filters by which the frequency ranges are spectrally narrowed and light scatter is greatly reduced. Thus the reflected [MASK] reconstituting the images are from distinct depths (the surface and deeper layers) of the object being imaged.

rodentdiseases.name: rodent diseases
rodentdiseases.definition: Rodent diseases is diseases of rodents of the order rodentia. This term includes diseases of Sciuridae (squirrels), Geomyidae (gophers), Heteromyidae (pouched mice), Castoridae (beavers), Cricetidae (rats and mice), Muridae (Old World rats and mice), Erethizontidae (porcupines), and Caviidae ([MASK] pigs).

dentalplaque.name: dental plaque
dentalplaque.definition: Dental plaque is a film that attaches to teeth, often causing dental caries and gingivitis. It is composed of mucins, secreted from salivary glands, and microorganisms.

mitochondria,muscle.name: mitochondria , muscle
mitochondria,muscle.definition: Muscle mitochondria is mitochondria of skeletal and smooth muscle. It does not include myocardial mitochondria for which mitochondria, heart is available.

dementia.name: dementia
dementia.definition: Dementia is an acquired organic mental disorder with loss of intellectual abilities of sufficient severity to interfere with social or occupational functioning. The dysfunction is multifaceted and involves memory, behavior, personality, judgment, attention, spatial relations, language, [MASK] thought, and other executive functions. The intellectual decline is usually progressive, and initially spares the level of consciousness.

teargases.name: tear gases
teargases.definition: Tear gases is gases that irritate the eyes, throat, or skin. Severe lacrimation develops upon irritation of the eyes.

congenitaldisordersofglycosylation.name: congenital disorders of glycosylation
congenitaldisordersofglycosylation.definition: Congenital disorders of [MASK] is a genetically heterogeneous group of heritable disorders resulting from defects in protein N-[MASK].

historicallycontrolledstudy.name: historically controlled study
historicallycontrolledstudy.definition: Historically controlled study is a study that compares a group of participants receiving an intervention with a similar group from the past who did not.

directservicecosts.name: direct service costs
directservicecosts.definition: Direct service costs is costs which are directly identifiable with a particular service.

tumorsuppressorproteins.name: tumor suppressor proteins
tumorsuppressorproteins.definition: Tumor suppressor proteins is proteins that are normally involved in holding cellular growth in check. Deficiencies or abnormalities in these proteins may lead to unregulated cell growth and tumor development.

speecharticulationtests.name: speech articulation tests
speecharticulationtests.definition: [MASK] articulation tests is tests of accuracy in pronouncing [MASK] sounds, e.g., Iowa Pressure Articulation Test, Deep Test of Articulation, Templin-Darley Tests of Articulation, Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Screening [MASK] Articulation Test, Arizona Articulation Proficiency Scale.

sulfurcompounds.name: sulfur compounds
sulfurcompounds.definition: Sulfur compounds is inorganic or organic compounds that contain sulfur as an integral part of the molecule.

bacterialadhesion.name: bacterial adhesion
bacterialadhesion.definition: Bacterial adhesion is physicochemical property of fimbriated (fimbriae, bacterial) and non-fimbriated bacteria of attaching to cells, tissue, and nonbiological surfaces. It is a factor in bacterial colonization and pathogenicity.

morningsickness.name: morning sickness
morningsickness.definition: Morning sickness is symptoms of nausea and vomiting in pregnant women that usually occur in the morning during the first 2 to 3 months of pregnancy. Severe persistent vomiting during pregnancy is called hyperemesis gravidarum.

radiography,dental,digital.name: radiography , dental , digital
radiography,dental,digital.definition: Digital dental radiography is a rapid, low-dose, digital imaging system using a small intraoral sensor instead of radiographic film, an intensifying screen, and a charge-coupled device. It presents the possibility of reduced patient exposure and minimal distortion, although resolution and latitude are inferior to standard dental radiography. a receiver is placed in the mouth, routing signals to a computer which images the signals on a screen or in print. It includes digitizing from x-ray film or any other detector. (From medline [MASK]; personal communication from Dr. Charles Berthold, nidr)

physicalobject.name: physical object
physicalobject.definition: Physical object is something that has a fixed shape or form that you can touch or see.

agentorange.name: agent orange
agentorange.definition: Agent orange is a herbicide that contains equal parts of 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-d) and 2,4,5-trichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4,5-t), as well as traces of the contaminant 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin.

smartmaterials.name: smart materials
smartmaterials.definition: Smart materials is materials designed to change properties in response to changes in their environment adopting various predetermined shapes and/or functionalities.

surgicalmesh.name: surgical mesh
surgicalmesh.definition: Surgical mesh is any woven or knit material of open texture used in surgery for the repair, reconstruction, or substitution of tissue. The mesh is usually a synthetic fabric made of various polymers. It is occasionally made of metal.

letter.name: letter
letter.definition: Letter is work consisting of written or printed communication between individuals or between persons and representatives of corporate bodies. The correspondence may be personal or professional. In medical and other scientific publications the letter is usually from one or more authors to the editor of the journal or book publishing the item being commented upon or discussed. letter is often accompanied by comment.

technology.name: technology
technology.definition: Technology is the application of scientific knowledge to practical purposes in any field. It includes methods, techniques, and instrumentation.

africanswinefever.name: african swine fever
africanswinefever.definition: African swine fever is a sometimes fatal asfivirus infection of pigs, characterized by fever, [MASK], [MASK], hemorrhagic [MASK] nodes, and edema of the gallbladder. It is transmitted between domestic swine by direct contact, ingestion of infected meat, or fomites, or mechanically by biting flies or soft ticks (genus Ornithodoros).

diffusion.name: diffusion
diffusion.definition: Diffusion is the tendency of a gas or solute to pass from a point of higher pressure or concentration to a point of lower pressure or concentration and to distribute itself throughout the available space. Diffusion, especially facilitated diffusion, is a major mechanism of biological transport.

sexuallytransmitteddiseases,bacterial.name: sexually transmitted diseases , bacterial
sexuallytransmitteddiseases,bacterial.definition: Bacterial sexually transmitted diseases is bacterial diseases transmitted or propagated by sexual conduct.

powders.name: powders
powders.definition: Powders is substances made up of an aggregation of small particles, as that obtained by grinding or trituration of a solid drug. In pharmacy it is a form in which substances are administered. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

resonancefrequencyanalysis.name: resonance frequency analysis
resonancefrequencyanalysis.definition: Resonance frequency analysis is a non-invasive assessment of the stability of tissue-embedded prosthetic devices such as dental implants.

bkvirus.name: bk virus
bkvirus.definition: Bk virus is a species of polyomavirus apparently infecting over 90% of children but not clearly associated with any clinical illness in childhood. The virus remains latent in the body throughout life and can be reactivated under certain circumstances.

vocationalguidance.name: vocational guidance
vocationalguidance.definition: Vocational guidance is systematic efforts to assist individuals in selecting an occupation or suitable employment on the basis of aptitude, education, etc.

utah.name: utah
utah.definition: Utah is state bounded on the north by Idaho and Wyoming, on the east by Wyoming and Colorado, on the south by Arizona, and on the west by Nevada.

typeapersonality.name: type a personality
typeapersonality.definition: Type a personality is established behavior pattern characterized by excessive drive and ambition, impatience, competitiveness, sense of time urgency, and poorly contained aggression.

contraceptiveagents,female.name: contraceptive agents , female
contraceptiveagents,female.definition: Female contraceptive agents is chemical substances or agents with contraceptive activity in females. Use for female contraceptive agents in general or for which there is no specific heading.

substanceabusedetection.name: substance abuse detection
substanceabusedetection.definition: Substance abuse detection is detection of drugs that have been abused, overused, or misused, including legal and illegal drugs. Urine screening is the usual method of detection.

headkidney.name: head kidney
headkidney.definition: Head kidney is a primitive form of vertebrate kidney that is found in adults of some primitive fishes and in the embryos of more advanced fishes. In some species of fishes it contains phagocytic cells and is also a major site of hematopoiesis, analogous to the mammalian bone marrow.

ethics,business.name: ethics , business
ethics,business.definition: Business ethics is the moral obligations governing the conduct of commercial or industrial enterprises.

retinalneoplasms.name: retinal neoplasms
retinalneoplasms.definition: Retinal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the retina.

heavymetalpoisoning,nervoussystem.name: heavy metal poisoning , nervous system
heavymetalpoisoning,nervoussystem.definition: Nervous system heavy metal poisoning is conditions associated with damage or dysfunction of the nervous system caused by exposure to heavy metals, which may cause a variety of central, peripheral, or autonomic nervous system injuries.

seminalvesicles.name: seminal vesicles
seminalvesicles.definition: Seminal vesicles is a saclike, glandular diverticulum on each ductus deferens in male vertebrates. It is united with the excretory duct and serves for temporary storage of semen. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

slitlampmicroscopy.name: slit lamp microscopy
slitlampmicroscopy.definition: Slit lamp microscopy is a procedure that uses a slit lamp to examine structures in the front of the eye, such as the conjunctiva; cornea; iris; and aqueous humor.

joints.name: joints
joints.definition: Joints is also known as articulations, these are points of connection between the ends of certain separate bones, or where the borders of other bones are juxtaposed.

accessorynerve.name: accessory nerve
accessorynerve.definition: Accessory nerve is the 11th cranial nerve which originates from neurons in the medulla and in the [MASK]. It has a cranial root, which joins the vagus nerve (10th cranial) and sends motor fibers to the muscles of the larynx, and a spinal root, which sends motor fibers to the [MASK] and the sternocleidomastoid muscles.

rootcanaltherapy.name: root canal therapy
rootcanaltherapy.definition: Root canal therapy is a treatment modality in endodontics concerned with the therapy of diseases of the [MASK]. For preparatory procedures, root canal preparation is available.

rossrivervirus.name: ross river virus
rossrivervirus.definition: Ross [MASK] virus is a species of alphavirus associated with epidemic exanthema and polyarthritis in Australia.

transplantationimmunology.name: transplantation immunology
transplantationimmunology.definition: Transplantation [MASK] is a general term for the complex phenomena involved in allo- and xenograft [MASK] by a host and [MASK] vs host reaction. Although the reactions involved in transplantation [MASK] are primarily thymus-dependent phenomena of cellular immunity, humoral factors also play a part in late [MASK].

pseudomonas.name: pseudomonas
pseudomonas.definition: Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria widely distributed in nature. Some species are pathogenic for humans, animals, and plants.

tissueadhesions.name: tissue adhesions
tissueadhesions.definition: Tissue adhesions is pathological processes consisting of the union of the opposing surfaces of a wound.

liverfunctiontests.name: liver function tests
liverfunctiontests.definition: Liver function tests is blood tests that are used to evaluate how well a patient's liver is working and also to help diagnose liver conditions.

researchsubjects.name: research subjects
researchsubjects.definition: Research subjects is persons who are enrolled in research studies or who are otherwise the subjects of research.

pairbond.name: pair bond
pairbond.definition: Pair bond is in animals, the social relationship established between a male and female for reproduction. It may include raising of young.

macrophageactivationsyndrome.name: macrophage activation syndrome
macrophageactivationsyndrome.definition: Macrophage activation syndrome is a serious complication of childhood systemic inflammatory disorders that is thought to be caused by excessive activation and proliferation of t-lymphocytes and macrophages. It is seen predominantly in children with systemic onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

commonbileductdiseases.name: common bile duct diseases
commonbileductdiseases.definition: Common [MASK] diseases is diseases of the common [MASK] including the ampulla of vater and the sphincter of oddi.

xenopusproteins.name: xenopus proteins
xenopusproteins.definition: Xenopus proteins is proteins obtained from various species of Xenopus. Included here are proteins from the African clawed frog (xenopus laevis). Many of these proteins have been the subject of scientific investigations in the area of morphogenesis and development.

bloodviscosity.name: blood viscosity
bloodviscosity.definition: Blood [MASK] is the internal resistance of the blood to shear forces. The in vitro measure of whole blood [MASK] is of limited clinical utility because it bears little relationship to the actual [MASK] within the circulation, but an increase in the [MASK] of circulating blood can contribute to morbidity in patients suffering from disorders such as sickle cell anemia and polycythemia.

tomography,optical.name: tomography , optical
tomography,optical.definition: Optical tomography is [MASK] of near-IR light (infrared rays), in the 700-1000 nm region, across an object in parallel beams to an array of sensitive photodetectors. This is repeated at various angles and a mathematical reconstruction provides three dimensional medical imaging of tissues. Based on the relative transparency of tissues to this spectra, it has been used to monitor local oxygenation, brain and joints.

idealbodyweight.name: ideal body weight
idealbodyweight.definition: Ideal body weight is expected weight of a healthy normal individual based on age, [MASK], and height. Thus, a malnourished person would weigh less than their ideal body weight.

plantgrowthregulators.name: plant growth regulators
plantgrowthregulators.definition: Plant growth regulators is any of the hormones produced naturally in plants and active in controlling growth and other functions. There are three primary classes: auxins, cytokinins, and gibberellins.

vaccinepotency.name: vaccine potency
vaccinepotency.definition: Vaccine potency is the relationship between an elicited adaptive immune response and the dose of the vaccine administered.

proteinengineering.name: protein engineering
proteinengineering.definition: Protein engineering is procedures by which protein structure and function are changed or created in vitro by altering existing or synthesizing new structural genes that direct the synthesis of proteins with sought-after properties. Such procedures may include the design of molecular models of proteins using [MASK] or other molecular modeling techniques; site-specific mutagenesis (mutagenesis, site-specific) of existing genes; and directed molecular evolution techniques to create new genes.

growth.name: growth
growth.definition: Growth is gradual increase in the number, the size, and the complexity of cells of an individual. Growth generally results in increase in organ weight; body weight; and body height.

insulin,regular,human.name: insulin , regular , human
insulin,regular,human.definition: Human regular insulin is regular insulin preparations that contain the human insulin peptide sequence.

catheterablation.name: catheter ablation
catheterablation.definition: Catheter ablation is removal of tissue with electrical current delivered via electrodes positioned at the distal end of a catheter. Energy sources are commonly direct current (DC-shock) or alternating current at radiofrequencies (usually 750 kHz). The technique is used most often to ablate the av junction and/or accessory pathways in order to interrupt av conduction and produce av block in the treatment of various tachyarrhythmias.

personalnarrative.name: personal narrative
personalnarrative.definition: Personal narrative is work consisting of accounts of individual experience in relation to a particular field or of participation in related activities.

hormoneantagonists.name: hormone antagonists
hormoneantagonists.definition: Hormone antagonists is chemical substances which inhibit the function of the endocrine glands, the biosynthesis of their secreted hormones, or the action of hormones upon their specific sites.

tobaccosmoking.name: tobacco smoking
tobaccosmoking.definition: Tobacco smoking is the process of smoking specific to tobacco.

dentalmaterials.name: dental materials
dentalmaterials.definition: Dental materials is materials used in the production of dental bases, restorations, impressions, prostheses, etc.

septumofbrain.name: septum of brain
septumofbrain.definition: Septum of brain is gray matter structures of the telencephalon and limbic system in the brain, but containing widely varying definitions among authors. Included here is the cortical septal area, subcortical septal nuclei, and the septum pellucidum.

spores,bacterial.name: spores , bacterial
spores,bacterial.definition: Bacterial spores is heat and stain resistant, metabolically inactive bodies formed within the vegetative cells of bacteria of the genera Bacillus and Clostridium.

endothelialproteincreceptor.name: endothelial protein c receptor
endothelialproteincreceptor.definition: Endothelial protein c receptor is a glycosylated transmembrane receptor for protein c that is highly expressed by endothelial cells on the surface of large blood vessels in the heart and lungs.  It facilitates protein c activation by the thrombin and thrombomodulin complex in blood coagulation.

adaptorproteincomplexmusubunits.name: adaptor protein complex mu subunits
adaptorproteincomplexmusubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex mu subunits is a family of medium adaptin protein subunits of approximately 45 KDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of adaptor protein complex 3 and adaptor protein complex 4.

heartseptaldefects.name: heart septal defects
heartseptaldefects.definition: Heart septal defects is abnormalities in any part of the heart septum resulting in abnormal communication between the left and the right chambers of the heart. The abnormal blood flow inside the heart may be caused by defects in the atrial septum, the ventricular septum, or both.

saltstress.name: salt stress
saltstress.definition: [MASK] stress is the condition that results from ion toxicity due to ion imbalances (e.g., excessive Na+ and deficiency in Mg++).

reproductivemedicine.name: reproductive medicine
reproductivemedicine.definition: Reproductive medicine is a medical-surgical specialty concerned with the morphology, physiology, biochemistry, and pathology of reproduction in man and other animals, and on the biological, medical, and veterinary problems of fertility and lactation. It includes ovulation induction, diagnosis of infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss, and assisted reproductive technologies such as embryo transfer, in vitro fertilization, and intrafallopian transfer of zygotes. (From Infertility and Reproductive Medicine Clinics of North America, Foreword 1990; Journal of Reproduction and Fertility, Notice to Contributors, Jan 1979)

studentrunclinic.name: student run clinic
studentrunclinic.definition: Student run clinic is healthcare setting managed by medical personnel in training.

epidemiology.name: epidemiology
epidemiology.definition: Epidemiology is field concerned with the determination of causes, incidence, and characteristic behavior of [MASK] affecting human populations. It includes the interrelationships of host, agent, and environment as related to the distribution and control of disease.

sleepapneasyndromes.name: sleep apnea syndromes
sleepapneasyndromes.definition: Sleep apnea syndromes is disorders characterized by multiple cessations of respirations during sleep that induce partial arousals and interfere with the maintenance of sleep. Sleep apnea syndromes are divided into central (see [MASK]), obstructive (see [MASK]), and mixed central-obstructive types.

synapses.name: synapses
synapses.definition: Synapses is specialized junctions at which a neuron communicates with a target cell. At classical synapses, a neuron's presynaptic terminal releases a chemical transmitter stored in synaptic vesicles which diffuses across a narrow synaptic cleft and activates receptors on the postsynaptic membrane of the target cell. The target may be a dendrite, cell body, or axon of another neuron, or a specialized region of a muscle or secretory cell. Neurons may also communicate via direct electrical coupling with electrical synapses. Several other non-synaptic chemical or electric signal transmitting processes occur via extracellular mediated interactions.

toothmigration.name: tooth migration
toothmigration.definition: Tooth migration is the movement of teeth into altered positions in relationship to the basal bone of the alveolar process and to adjoining and opposing teeth as a result of loss of approximating or opposing teeth, occlusal interferences, habits, inflammatory and dystrophic disease of the attaching and supporting structures of the teeth. (From Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed)

placenta.name: placenta
placenta.definition: Placenta is a highly vascularized mammalian fetal-maternal organ and major site of transport of oxygen, nutrients, and fetal waste products. It includes a fetal portion (chorionic villi) derived from trophoblasts and a maternal portion (decidua) derived from the uterine endometrium. The placenta produces an array of steroid, protein and peptide [MASK] hormones).

nerveagents.name: nerve agents
nerveagents.definition: Nerve agents is a class of compounds that adversely affect the transmission of impulses through the nervous system.

tumornecrosisfactors.name: tumor necrosis factors
tumornecrosisfactors.definition: Tumor necrosis factors is a family of proteins that were originally identified by their ability to cause necrosis of neoplasms. Their necrotic effect on cells is mediated through tumor necrosis factor receptors which induce apoptosis.

cranialnerves.name: cranial nerves
cranialnerves.definition: Cranial nerves is twelve pairs of nerves that carry general afferent, visceral afferent, special afferent, somatic efferent, and autonomic efferent fibers.

softwaredesign.name: software design
softwaredesign.definition: Software design is specifications and instructions applied to the software.

expiratoryreservevolume.name: expiratory reserve volume
expiratoryreservevolume.definition: Expiratory reserve volume is the extra volume of air that can be expired with maximum effort beyond the level reached at the end of a normal, quiet expiration. Common abbreviation is erv.

sentinelsurveillance.name: sentinel surveillance
sentinelsurveillance.definition: Sentinel surveillance is monitoring of rate of occurrence of specific conditions to assess the stability or change in health levels of a population. It is also the study of disease rates in a specific cohort such as in a geographic area or population subgroup to estimate trends in a larger population. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

tissueexpansion.name: tissue expansion
tissueexpansion.definition: Tissue expansion is a procedure whereby the body is stimulated to generate extra soft tissue by the application of stretching forces that stimulate new growth of tissue which, over a period of time, results in a 2-dimensional expansion of the tissue. The procedure is used in reconstructive surgery for injuries caused by trauma, burns, or ablative surgery. Various types of tissue expansion devices have been developed that exert stretching forces.

coalindustry.name: coal industry
coalindustry.definition: Coal industry is enterprise associated with the mining, processing, marketing and distribution of coal.

familyplanningpolicy.name: family planning policy
familyplanningpolicy.definition: Family planning policy is a course or method of action selected, usually by a government, to guide and determine present and future decisions on population control by limiting the number of children or controlling fertility, notably through family planning and contraception within the nuclear family.

olfactorynerve.name: olfactory nerve
olfactorynerve.definition: Olfactory nerve is the 1st cranial nerve. The olfactory nerve conveys the sense of smell. It is formed by the axons of [MASK] which project from the olfactory epithelium (in the nasal epithelium) to the olfactory bulb.

immunotherapy,active.name: immunotherapy , active
immunotherapy,active.definition: Active immunotherapy is active immunization where vaccine is administered for therapeutic or preventive purposes. This can include administration of immunopotentiating agents such as [MASK] and Corynebacterium parvum as well as biological response modifiers such as interferons, interleukins, and colony-stimulating factors in order to directly stimulate the immune system.

infraredrays.name: infrared rays
infraredrays.definition: Infrared rays is that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum usually sensed as heat. Infrared wavelengths are longer than those of visible light, extending into the microwave frequencies. They are used therapeutically as heat, and also to warm food in restaurants.

cellulose.name: cellulose
cellulose.definition: Cellulose is a polysaccharide with glucose units linked as in cellobiose. It is the chief constituent of plant fibers, cotton being the purest natural form of the substance. As a raw material, it forms the basis for many derivatives used in [MASK] materials, explosives manufacturing, and pharmaceutical preparations.

hip.name: hip
hip.definition: Hip is the projecting part on each side of the body, formed by the side of the pelvis and the top portion of the femur.

goats.name: goats
goats.definition: Goats is any of numerous agile, hollow-horned ruminants of the genus Capra, in the family Bovidae, closely related to the sheep.

crop,avian.name: crop , avian
crop,avian.definition: Avian crop is a thin-walled distention of the alimentary tract protruding just outside the body cavity in the distal end of the [MASK] (esophagus), used for the temporary storage of food and water.

empiricalresearch.name: empirical research
empiricalresearch.definition: Empirical research is the study, based on direct [MASK], use of statistical records, interviews, or experimental methods, of actual practices or the actual impact of practices or policies.

laminin.name: laminin
laminin.definition: Laminin is large, noncollagenous glycoprotein with antigenic properties. It is localized in the basement membrane lamina lucida and functions to bind epithelial cells to the basement membrane. Evidence suggests that the protein plays a role in tumor invasion.

rna,transfer,lys.name: rna , transfer , lys
rna,transfer,lys.definition: Lys transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying lysine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

fertility.name: fertility
fertility.definition: Fertility is the capacity to conceive or to induce conception. It may refer to either the male or female.

radiographicimageenhancement.name: radiographic image enhancement
radiographicimageenhancement.definition: Radiographic image enhancement is improvement in the quality of an x-ray image by use of an intensifying screen, tube, or filter and by optimum exposure techniques. Digital processing methods are often employed.

scintillationcounting.name: scintillation counting
scintillationcounting.definition: Scintillation counting is detection and counting of scintillations produced in a fluorescent material by ionizing radiation.

epidemiologicmeasurements.name: epidemiologic measurements
epidemiologicmeasurements.definition: Epidemiologic measurements is statistical calculations on the occurrence of disease or other health-related conditions in defined populations.

renalcirculation.name: renal circulation
renalcirculation.definition: Renal circulation is the circulation of the blood through the vessels of the kidney.

drugresistance,multiple.name: drug resistance , multiple
drugresistance,multiple.definition: Multiple drug resistance is simultaneous resistance to several structurally and functionally distinct drugs.

metabolicnetworksandpathways.name: metabolic networks and pathways
metabolicnetworksandpathways.definition: Metabolic networks and pathways is complex sets of enzymatic reactions connected to each other via their product and substrate metabolites.

medicationsystems.name: medication systems
medicationsystems.definition: Medication systems is overall systems, traditional or automated, to provide medication to patients.

mandibularprosthesisimplantation.name: mandibular prosthesis implantation
mandibularprosthesisimplantation.definition: Mandibular prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of an appliance for the replacement of areas of the mandible.

legislation.name: legislation
legislation.definition: Legislation is works consisting of the text of proposed or enacted legislation that may be in the form of bills, laws, statutes, ordinances, or government regulations.

culturetechniques.name: culture techniques
culturetechniques.definition: Culture techniques is methods of maintaining or growing biological materials in controlled laboratory conditions. These include the cultures of cells; tissues; organs; or embryo in vitro. Both animal and plant tissues may be cultured by a variety of methods. Cultures may derive from normal or abnormal tissues, and consist of a single cell type or mixed cell types.

photoreceptorcells,vertebrate.name: photoreceptor cells , vertebrate
photoreceptorcells,vertebrate.definition: Vertebrate photoreceptor cells is specialized phototransduction neurons in the vertebrates, such as the retinal rod cells and the [MASK]. Non-visual photoreceptor neurons have been reported in the deep brain, the pineal gland and organs of the circadian system.

germany,west.name: germany , west
germany,west.definition: West germany is the former Federal Republic of Germany which was reunified with the former German Democratic Republic in 1990.

activatingtranscriptionfactor6.name: activating transcription factor 6
activatingtranscriptionfactor6.definition: Activating transcription factor 6 is one of the basic-[MASK] zipper transcription factors that is synthesized as a membrane-bound protein in the endoplasmic reticulum. In response to endoplasmic reticulum stress it translocates to the golgi apparatus. It is activated by proteases and then moves to the cell nucleus to regulate genetic transcription of genes involved in the unfolded protein response.

cellnucleusstructures.name: cell nucleus structures
cellnucleusstructures.definition: Cell nucleus structures is structures that are part of or contained in the cell nucleus.

circadianrhythmsignalingpeptidesandprote.name: circadian rhythm signaling peptides and proteins
circadianrhythmsignalingpeptidesandprote.definition: Circadian rhythm signaling peptides and proteins is a broad category of proteins that regulate the circadian rhythm of an organism. Included here are proteins that transmit intracellular and intercellular signals in a chronological manner along with proteins that sense light and time-dependent changes in the environment such as the photoperiod.

observervariation.name: observer variation
observervariation.definition: Observer variation is the failure by the observer to measure or identify a phenomenon accurately, which results in an error. Sources for this may be due to the observer's missing an abnormality, or to faulty technique resulting in incorrect test measurement, or to misinterpretation of the data. Two varieties are inter-observer variation (the amount observers vary from one another when reporting on the same material) and intra-observer variation (the amount one observer varies between observations when reporting more than once on the same material).

epilepticsyndromes.name: epileptic syndromes
epilepticsyndromes.definition: Epileptic syndromes is epileptic seizures that are of similar type and age of onset and have other similar features (e.g., clinical course, eeg findings, genetic association and neuropathology).

receptors,gaba.name: receptors , gaba
receptors,gaba.definition: Gaba receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind gamma-aminobutyric acid with high affinity and trigger changes that influence the behavior of cells. gaba-a receptors control chloride channels formed by the receptor complex itself. They are blocked by bicuculline and usually have modulatory sites sensitive to benzodiazepines and barbiturates. gaba-b receptors act through G-proteins on several effector systems, are insensitive to bicuculline, and have a high affinity for L-baclofen.

validationstudy.name: validation study
validationstudy.definition: Validation study is works consisting of research using processes by which the reliability and relevance of a procedure for a specific purpose are established.

connectivetissuecells.name: connective tissue cells
connectivetissuecells.definition: Connective tissue cells is a group of cells that includes fibroblasts, cartilage cells, adipocytes, smooth muscle cells, and bone cells.

upstreamstimulatoryfactors.name: upstream stimulatory factors
upstreamstimulatoryfactors.definition: Upstream stimulatory factors is ubiquitously expressed basic helix-loop-helix motif transcription factors. They bind canntg sequences in the promoters of a variety of genes involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.

rnapolymerasesigma54.name: rna polymerase sigma 54
rnapolymerasesigma54.definition: Rna polymerase sigma 54 is a DNA-directed rna polymerase found in bacteria. It is a holoenzyme that consists of multiple subunits including [MASK] 54.

biologicallyactivesubstance.name: biologically active substance
biologicallyactivesubstance.definition: Biologically active substance is biologically active substance

nucleotides,cyclic.name: nucleotides , cyclic
nucleotides,cyclic.definition: Cyclic nucleotides is a single-phosphate nucleotide with a cyclic bond arrangement between the sugar and phosphate groups.

drugdevelopment.name: drug development
drugdevelopment.definition: Drug development is the entire process of bringing a new drug to the market. It includes both preclinical and clinical testing, and regulatory approval.

healthknowledge,attitudes,practice.name: health knowledge , attitudes , practice
healthknowledge,attitudes,practice.definition: Practice attitudes health knowledge is knowledge, attitudes, and associated behaviors which pertain to health-related topics such as pathologic processes or diseases, their prevention, and treatment. This term refers to non-health workers and health workers (health personnel).

officemanagement.name: office management
officemanagement.definition: Office management is planning, organizing, and administering activities in an office.

dictionary.name: dictionary
dictionary.definition: Dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words - usually in alphabetical order - giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning. a foreign-language dictionary is an alphabetical list of words of one language with their meaning and equivalents in another language.

cooking.name: cooking
cooking.definition: Cooking is the art or practice of preparing food. It includes the preparation of special foods for diets in various diseases.

child,exceptional.name: child , exceptional
child,exceptional.definition: Exceptional child is a child whose needs, abilities, or other characteristics vary so much from the average in mental, physical, or social areas that a greater than usual level of services is needed to facilitate the child's maximum potential development.

infusionpumps.name: infusion pumps
infusionpumps.definition: Infusion pumps is fluid propulsion systems driven mechanically, electrically, or osmotically that are used to inject (or infuse) over time agents into a patient or experimental animal; used routinely in hospitals to maintain a patent intravenous line, to administer antineoplastic agents and other drugs in thromboembolism, heart disease, diabetes mellitus ([MASK] is also available), and other disorders.

ink.name: ink
ink.definition: Ink is pigmented or colored fluid used for writing, staining, painting, drawing, printing, or copying images.

ectopicgeneexpression.name: ectopic gene expression
ectopicgeneexpression.definition: Ectopic gene expression is the expression of a gene in an abnormal place,  or at an abnormal  time in an organism. Ectopic Gene  Expression is often induced artificially by genetic techniques.

apache.name: apache
apache.definition: Apache is an acronym for Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation, a scoring system using routinely collected data and providing an accurate, objective description for a broad range of intensive care unit admissions, measuring severity of illness in [MASK] patients.

parenteralnutrition.name: parenteral nutrition
parenteralnutrition.definition: Parenteral nutrition is the administering of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient who cannot maintain adequate nutrition by enteral feeding alone. Nutrients are administered by a route other than the alimentary canal (e.g., intravenously, subcutaneously).

tissueengineering.name: tissue engineering
tissueengineering.definition: Tissue engineering is generating tissue in vitro for clinical applications, such as replacing wounded tissues or impaired organs. The use of tissue scaffolding enables the generation of complex multi-layered tissues and tissue structures.

hernia,umbilical.name: hernia , umbilical
hernia,umbilical.definition: Umbilical hernia is a hernia due to an imperfect closure or weakness of the umbilical ring. It appears as a skin-covered protrusion at the umbilicus during crying, coughing, or straining. The hernia generally consists of omentum or small intestine. The vast majority of umbilical hernias are congenital but can be acquired due to severe abdominal distention.

intuition.name: intuition
intuition.definition: Intuition is knowing or understanding without conscious use of reasoning. (Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, 1994)

dilatation.name: dilatation
dilatation.definition: Dilatation is the act of dilating.

dialysis.name: dialysis
dialysis.definition: Dialysis is a process of selective diffusion through a membrane. It is usually used to separate low-molecular-weight solutes which diffuse through the membrane from the colloidal and high-molecular-weight solutes which do not. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

acupuncture.name: acupuncture
acupuncture.definition: Acupuncture is the occupational discipline of the traditional Chinese methods of acupuncture therapy for treating disease by inserting needles along specific pathways or meridians.

cerebralbloodvolume.name: cerebral blood volume
cerebralbloodvolume.definition: Cerebral blood volume is volume of circulating blood in a region of the brain. It is a functional measure of the brain perfusion status which relates changes in this to changes in cerebrovasular circulation that are often seen in brain diseases.

cellsurfacedisplaytechniques.name: cell surface display techniques
cellsurfacedisplaytechniques.definition: Cell surface display techniques is techniques utilizing cells that express recombinant fusion proteins engineered to translocate through the cell membrane and remain attached to the outside of the cell.

defectiveviruses.name: defective viruses
defectiveviruses.definition: Defective viruses is viruses which lack a complete genome so that they cannot completely replicate or cannot form a protein coat. Some are host-dependent defectives, meaning they can replicate only in cell systems which provide the particular genetic function which they lack. Others, called satellite viruses, are able to replicate only when their genetic defect is complemented by a helper virus.

retinalneurons.name: retinal neurons
retinalneurons.definition: Retinal neurons is nerve cells of the retina in the pathway of transmitting light signals to the central nervous system. They include the outer layer of photoreceptor cells, the intermediate layer of retinal bipolar cells and amacrine cells, and the internal layer of [MASK].

estrogenantagonists.name: estrogen antagonists
estrogenantagonists.definition: Estrogen antagonists is compounds which inhibit or antagonize the action or biosynthesis of estrogenic compounds.

patentsastopic.name: patents as topic
patentsastopic.definition: Patents as topic is works about exclusive legal rights or privileges applied to inventions, plants, etc.

finiteelementanalysis.name: finite element analysis
finiteelementanalysis.definition: Finite element analysis is a computer based method of simulating or analyzing the behavior of structures or components.

renalarteryobstruction.name: renal artery obstruction
renalarteryobstruction.definition: [MASK] obstruction is narrowing or occlusion of the [MASK] or arteries. It is due usually to atherosclerosis; fibromuscular dysplasia; thrombosis; embolism, or external pressure. The reduced renal perfusion can lead to renovascular hypertension (hypertension, renovascular).

vascularcalcification.name: vascular calcification
vascularcalcification.definition: Vascular calcification is deposition of calcium into the blood vessel structures. Excessive calcification of the vessels are associated with [MASK] formation particularly after myocardial infarction (see monckeberg medial calcific [MASK]) and chronic kidney diseases which in turn increase vascular stiffness.

mammaryanaloguesecretorycarcinoma.name: mammary analogue secretory carcinoma
mammaryanaloguesecretorycarcinoma.definition: Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm of epithelial cells of the salivary glands, with microcystic architecture, low-grade nuclei, and granular vacuolated cytoplasm.

cells,cultured.name: cells , cultured
cells,cultured.definition: Cultured cells is cells propagated in vitro in special media conducive to their growth. Cultured cells are used to study developmental, morphologic, metabolic, physiologic, and genetic processes, among others.

gastricinhibitorypolypeptide.name: gastric inhibitory polypeptide
gastricinhibitorypolypeptide.definition: Gastric inhibitory polypeptide is a gastrointestinal peptide hormone of about 43-amino acids. It is found to be a potent stimulator of insulin secretion and a relatively poor inhibitor of gastric acid secretion.

sterilealphamotif.name: sterile alpha motif
sterilealphamotif.definition: Sterile alpha motif is a putative protein interaction module, approximately 70 amino acids long, that forms a small five-helix bundle with two large interfaces which may homo- and hetero-oligomerize, or bind non-sterile-alpha motif targets. The sterile alpha motif is present in a wide variety of eukaryotic proteins that function in diverse biological processes.

news.name: news
news.definition: News is works consisting of an announcement or statement of recent or current events of new data and matters of interest in the field of medicine or science. In some publications, such as "Nature" or "Science," the news reports are substantively written and herald medical and scientific data of vital or controversial importance.

venousvalves.name: venous valves
venousvalves.definition: Venous valves is flaps within the veins that allow the blood to flow only in one direction. They are usually in the medium size veins that carry blood to the heart against gravity.

serotoninuptakeinhibitors.name: serotonin uptake inhibitors
serotoninuptakeinhibitors.definition: Serotonin uptake inhibitors is compounds that specifically inhibit the reuptake of serotonin in the brain.

meningitis,pneumococcal.name: meningitis , pneumococcal
meningitis,pneumococcal.definition: Pneumococcal meningitis is an acute purulent infection of the meninges and subarachnoid space caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, most prevalent in children and adults over the age of 60. This illness may be associated with otitis media; mastoiditis; sinusitis; respiratory tract infections; sickle cell disease (anemia, sickle cell); skull fractures; and other disorders. Clinical manifestations include fever; headache; [MASK] stiffness; and somnolence followed by seizures; focal neurologic deficits (notably deafness); and coma. (From Miller et al., Merritt's Textbook of Neurology, 9th ed, p111)

clusterheadache.name: cluster headache
clusterheadache.definition: Cluster headache is a primary headache disorder that is characterized by severe, strictly unilateral pain which is orbital, supraorbital, temporal or in any combination of these sites, lasting 15-180 min. occurring 1 to 8 times a day. The attacks are associated with one or more of the following, all of which are ipsilateral: conjunctival injection, lacrimation, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, facial sweating, eyelid edema, and miosis. (International Classification of Headache Disorders, 2nd ed. Cephalalgia 2004: suppl 1)

introns.name: introns
introns.definition: Introns is sequences of dna in the genes that are located between the exons. They are transcribed along with the exons but are removed from the primary gene transcript by rna splicing to leave mature rna. Some introns code for separate genes.

headinjuries,closed.name: head injuries , closed
headinjuries,closed.definition: Closed head injuries is traumatic injuries to the cranium where the integrity of the skull is not compromised and no bone fragments or other objects penetrate the skull and dura mater. This frequently results in mechanical injury being transmitted to intracranial structures which may produce traumatic brain injuries, hemorrhage, or cranial nerve injuries. (From Rowland, Merritt's Textbook of Neurology, 9th ed, p417)

conditioning,psychological.name: conditioning , psychological
conditioning,psychological.definition: Psychological conditioning is simple form of learning involving the formation, strengthening, or weakening of an association between a stimulus and a response.

wholegenomesequencing.name: whole genome sequencing
wholegenomesequencing.definition: Whole genome sequencing is techniques to determine the entire sequence of the genome of an organism or individual.

freshwaterbiology.name: freshwater biology
freshwaterbiology.definition: Freshwater biology is the study of life and ecologic systems in bodies of freshwater.

immunecomplexdiseases.name: immune complex diseases
immunecomplexdiseases.definition: Immune complex diseases is group of diseases mediated by the deposition of large soluble complexes of antigen and antibody with resultant damage to tissue. Besides serum sickness and the arthus reaction, evidence supports a pathogenic role for immune complexes in many other immune system diseases including glomerulonephritis, [MASK] ([MASK]) and polyarteritis nodosa.

virusphysiologicalphenomena.name: virus physiological phenomena
virusphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Virus physiological phenomena is biological properties, processes, and activities of viruses, including the interactions with the cells they infect.

radiography,dental.name: radiography , dental
radiography,dental.definition: Dental radiography is radiographic techniques used in dentistry.

television.name: television
television.definition: Television is the transmission and reproduction of transient images of fixed or moving objects. An electronic system of transmitting such images together with sound over a wire or through space by apparatus that converts light and sound into electrical waves and reconverts them into visible light rays and audible sound. (From Webster, 3rd ed)

immediatedentalimplantloading.name: immediate dental implant loading
immediatedentalimplantloading.definition: Immediate dental implant loading is endosseous dental implantation where implants are fitted with an abutment or where an implant with a transmucosal coronal portion is used immediately (within 1 week) after the initial extraction. Conventionally, the implantation is performed in two stages with more than two months in between the stages.

tissues.name: tissues
tissues.definition: Tissues is collections of differentiated cells, such as epithelium; connective tissue; muscles; and nerve tissue. Tissues are cooperatively arranged to form organs with specialized functions such as respiration; [MASK]; reproduction; movement; and others.

closingvolume.name: closing volume
closingvolume.definition: Closing volume is the lung volume at which the dependent lung zones cease to ventilate presumably as a result of airway closure.

competitivebidding.name: competitive bidding
competitivebidding.definition: Competitive bidding is pricing statements presented by more than one party for the purpose of securing a contract.

lymphocytedepletion.name: lymphocyte depletion
lymphocytedepletion.definition: Lymphocyte depletion is immunosuppression by reduction of circulating lymphocytes or by T-cell depletion of bone marrow. The former may be accomplished in vivo by thoracic duct drainage or administration of antilymphocyte serum. The latter is performed ex vivo on bone marrow before its transplantation.

rna,complementary.name: rna , complementary
rna,complementary.definition: Complementary rna is synthetic transcripts of a specific dna molecule or fragment, made by an in vitro transcription system. This cRNA can be labeled with radioactive uracil and then used as a probe. (King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

nutritiontherapy.name: nutrition therapy
nutritiontherapy.definition: Nutrition therapy is improving health status of an individual by adjusting the quantities, qualities, and methods of nutrient intake.

skindiseases,metabolic.name: skin diseases , metabolic
skindiseases,metabolic.definition: Metabolic skin diseases is diseases of the skin associated with underlying metabolic disorders.

brainstemneoplasms.name: brain stem neoplasms
brainstemneoplasms.definition: Brain stem neoplasms is benign and malignant intra-axial tumors of the mesencephalon; pons; or medulla oblongata of the brain stem. Primary and metastatic neoplasms may occur in this location. Clinical features include ataxia, cranial neuropathies (see cranial nerve diseases), nausea, hemiparesis (see hemiplegia), and quadriparesis. Primary brain stem neoplasms are more frequent in children. Histologic subtypes include glioma; hemangioblastoma; ganglioglioma; and ependymoma.

insectvectors.name: insect vectors
insectvectors.definition: Insect vectors is insects that transmit infective organisms from one host to another or from an inanimate reservoir to an animate host.

splenicvein.name: splenic vein
splenicvein.definition: Splenic vein is vein formed by the union (at the hilus of the spleen) of several small veins from the stomach, pancreas, spleen and mesentery.

popularculture.name: popular culture
popularculture.definition: Popular culture is choices and ways of doing things that predominate or are fashionable among ordinary people in a society during a point in time.

embryoresearch.name: embryo research
embryoresearch.definition: Embryo research is experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus during the prenatal stage of development that is characterized by rapid morphological changes and the differentiation of basic structures. In humans, this includes the period from the time of fertilization to the end of the eighth week after fertilization.

patientgeneratedhealthdata.name: patient generated health data
patientgeneratedhealthdata.definition: Patient generated health data is health-related data created, recorded, or gathered by patients, family members, or caregivers, to help address a health concern. Distinct from data generated in clinical settings and through encounters with providers.

couplestherapy.name: couples therapy
couplestherapy.definition: Couples therapy is psychotherapy used for either unmarried couples or married couples, of mixed or same [MASK].

postoperativehemorrhage.name: postoperative hemorrhage
postoperativehemorrhage.definition: Postoperative hemorrhage is hemorrhage following any surgical procedure. It may be immediate or delayed and is not restricted to the [MASK].

cognitiondisorders.name: cognition disorders
cognitiondisorders.definition: Cognition disorders is disorders characterized by disturbances in mental processes related to learning, thinking, reasoning, and judgment.

tumorlysissyndrome.name: tumor lysis syndrome
tumorlysissyndrome.definition: Tumor lysis syndrome is a syndrome resulting from cytotoxic therapy, occurring generally in aggressive, rapidly proliferating lymphoproliferative disorders. It is characterized by combinations of hyperuricemia, [MASK], hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia and hypocalcemia.

depressivedisorder.name: depressive disorder
depressivedisorder.definition: Depressive disorder is an affective disorder manifested by either a dysphoric mood or loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities. The mood disturbance is prominent and relatively persistent.

lungcompliance.name: lung compliance
lungcompliance.definition: Lung compliance is the capability of the lungs to distend under pressure as measured by pulmonary volume change per unit pressure change. While not a complete description of the pressure-volume properties of the lung, it is nevertheless useful in practice as a measure of the comparative stiffness of the lung. (From Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p562)

behavior,animal.name: behavior , animal
behavior,animal.definition: Animal behavior is the observable response an animal makes to any situation.

bloodalcoholcontent.name: blood alcohol content
bloodalcoholcontent.definition: Blood alcohol content is mass of alcohol per unit of blood volume.

tibialneuropathy.name: tibial neuropathy
tibialneuropathy.definition: Tibial neuropathy is disease of the tibial nerve (also referred to as the posterior tibial nerve). The most commonly associated condition is the tarsal tunnel syndrome. However, leg injuries; ischemia; and inflammatory conditions (e.g., [MASK]) may also affect the nerve. Clinical features include paralysis of plantar flexion, ankle inversion and toe flexion as well as loss of sensation over the sole of the [MASK]. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1995, Ch51, p32)

rrnaoperon.name: rrna operon
rrnaoperon.definition: Rrna operon is genetic loci which direct transcription of [MASK] in bacterial operons. They are designated rrnB, rrnC, rrnD, etc. according to the structural position of the transcription unit in the dna sequence.

infectiouspancreaticnecrosisvirus.name: infectious pancreatic necrosis virus
infectiouspancreaticnecrosisvirus.definition: Infectious pancreatic necrosis virus is the type species of aquabirnavirus, causing infectious pancreatic necrosis in salmonid fish and other freshwater and marine animals including mollusks.

microscopy,electron.name: microscopy , electron
microscopy,electron.definition: [MASK] microscopy is microscopy using an [MASK] beam, instead of light, to visualize the sample, thereby allowing much greater magnification. The interactions of [MASK] with specimens are used to provide information about the fine structure of that specimen. In transmission [MASK] microscopy the reactions of the [MASK] that are transmitted through the specimen are imaged. In scanning [MASK] microscopy an [MASK] beam falls at a non-normal angle on the specimen and the image is derived from the reactions occurring above the plane of the specimen.

nitrogenisotopes.name: nitrogen isotopes
nitrogenisotopes.definition: Nitrogen isotopes is stable nitrogen atoms that have the same atomic number as the element nitrogen, but differ in atomic weight. n-15 is a stable nitrogen isotope.

medicalwaste.name: medical waste
medicalwaste.definition: Medical waste is blood, mucus, tissue removed at surgery or autopsy, soiled surgical dressings, and other materials requiring special disposal procedures.

taxes.name: taxes
taxes.definition: Taxes is governmental levies on property, inheritance, [MASK], etc.

myeloidcellleukemiasequence1protein.name: myeloid cell leukemia sequence 1 protein
myeloidcellleukemiasequence1protein.definition: Myeloid cell leukemia sequence 1 protein is a member of the myeloid leukemia factor (mlf) protein family with multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants encoding different protein isoforms. In hematopoietic cells, it is located mainly in the nucleus, and in non-hematopoietic cells, primarily in the cytoplasm with a punctate nuclear localization. mlf1 plays a role in cell cycle differentiation.

aircraft.name: aircraft
aircraft.definition: Aircraft is a weight-carrying structure for navigation of the air that is supported either by its own buoyancy or by the dynamic action of the air against its surfaces. (Webster, 1973)

splenicrupture.name: splenic rupture
splenicrupture.definition: Splenic rupture is rupture of the spleen due to trauma or disease.

youthsports.name: youth sports
youthsports.definition: Youth sports is sports activities designed and/or organized for children or youth.

vimentin.name: vimentin
vimentin.definition: Vimentin is an [MASK] protein found in most differentiating cells, in cells grown in tissue culture, and in certain fully differentiated cells. Its insolubility suggests that it serves a structural function in the cytoplasm. mw 52,000.

neutrophils.name: neutrophils
neutrophils.definition: Neutrophils is granular leukocytes having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.

dangerousbehavior.name: dangerous behavior
dangerousbehavior.definition: Dangerous behavior is actions which have a high risk of being harmful or injurious to oneself or others.

chloroplastproteins.name: chloroplast proteins
chloroplastproteins.definition: Chloroplast proteins is proteins encoded by the chloroplast genome or proteins encoded by the nuclear genome that are imported to and resident in the choroplasts.

reproductivecontrolagents.name: reproductive control agents
reproductivecontrolagents.definition: Reproductive control agents is substances used either in the prevention or facilitation of pregnancy.

melatonin.name: melatonin
melatonin.definition: Melatonin is a biogenic amine that is found in animals and plants. In mammals, melatonin is produced by the pineal gland. Its secretion increases in darkness and decreases during exposure to light. Melatonin is implicated in the regulation of sleep, mood, and reproduction. Melatonin is also an effective antioxidant.

diet.name: diet
diet.definition: Diet is regular course of eating and drinking adopted by a person or animal.

minorityhealth.name: minority health
minorityhealth.definition: Minority health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of members of minority groups.

fibroblastgrowthfactor3.name: fibroblast growth factor 3
fibroblastgrowthfactor3.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 3 is a fibroblast growth factor that is expressed primarily during development.

immobilizedproteins.name: immobilized proteins
immobilizedproteins.definition: Immobilized proteins is proteins that are chemically bound to a substrate material which renders their location fixed. The immobilization of proteins allows their use in chemical reactions without being diluted by solvent.

bundleofhis.name: bundle of his
bundleofhis.definition: Bundle of his is small band of specialized cardiac muscle fibers that originates in the atrioventricular node and extends into the membranous part of the interventricular septum. The bundle of His, consisting of the left and the right bundle branches, conducts the electrical impulses to the heart ventricles in generation of [MASK].

transcriptionfactorchop.name: transcription factor chop
transcriptionfactorchop.definition: Transcription factor chop is a CCAAT-enhancer binding protein that is induced by dna damage and growth arrest. It serves as a dominant negative inhibitor of other CCAAT-enhancer binding proteins.

algorithms.name: algorithms
algorithms.definition: Algorithms is a procedure consisting of a sequence of algebraic formulas and/or logical steps to calculate or determine a given task.

maternalbehavior.name: maternal behavior
maternalbehavior.definition: Maternal behavior is the behavior patterns associated with or characteristic of a mother.

annualreport.name: annual report
annualreport.definition: Annual report is annual statements concerning the administrative and operational functions of an institution or organization.

healthstatusdisparities.name: health status disparities
healthstatusdisparities.definition: Health status disparities is variation in rates of disease occurrence and disabilities between population groups defined by socioeconomic characteristics such as age, ethnicity, economic resources, or gender and populations identified geographically or similar measures.

lactatedehydrogenase5.name: lactate dehydrogenase 5
lactatedehydrogenase5.definition: Lactate dehydrogenase 5 is a member of the lactate dehydrogenases isozyme family, Lactate Dehydrogenase 5 is localized to liver and skeletal muscle cells where its expression increases in liver disease and striated muscle trauma respectively.

eyeproteins.name: eye proteins
eyeproteins.definition: Eye proteins is proteins derived from tissues of the eye.

vitaminbcomplex.name: vitamin b complex
vitaminbcomplex.definition: Vitamin b complex is a group of water-soluble vitamins, some of which are coenzymes.

hingeexons.name: hinge exons
hingeexons.definition: Hinge exons is [MASK] gene exons coding for the hinge region of the heavy chains between the first constant region (on the fab fragments) and the second constant region (on the [MASK]).

propofolinfusionsyndrome.name: propofol infusion syndrome
propofolinfusionsyndrome.definition: Propofol infusion syndrome is rare and often fatal drug complication which affects patients undergoing long-term treatment with high doses of propofol. It is characterized by metabolic acidosis; hyperlipidemia; rhabdomyolysis; cardiovascular circulatory collapse; cardiac failure; and kidney failure.

phenomenonorprocess.name: phenomenon or process
phenomenonorprocess.definition: Phenomenon or process is a symptom; an occurrence of any sort, whether ordinary or extraordinary, in relation to a disease.

airpollutants.name: air pollutants
airpollutants.definition: Air pollutants is any substance in the air which could, if present in high enough concentration, harm humans, animals, vegetation or materials. Substances include gases; particulate matter; and volatile organic chemicals.

nanoparticles.name: nanoparticles
nanoparticles.definition: Nanoparticles is nanometer-sized particles that are nanoscale in three dimensions. They include nanocrystaline materials; nanocapsules; [MASK]; dendrimers, and quantum dots. The uses of nanoparticles include drug delivery systems and cancer targeting and imaging.

viralstructures.name: viral structures
viralstructures.definition: Viral structures is the structural parts of the virion.

haircolor.name: hair color
haircolor.definition: Hair [MASK] is [MASK] of hair or fur.

repression,psychology.name: repression , psychology
repression,psychology.definition: Psychology repression is the active mental process of keeping out and ejecting, banishing from consciousness, ideas or impulses that are unacceptable to it.

infanthealth.name: infant health
infanthealth.definition: Infant health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of infants.

intracellularspace.name: intracellular space
intracellularspace.definition: Intracellular space is the area within cells.

virusinternalization.name: virus internalization
virusinternalization.definition: Virus internalization is the entering of cells by viruses following virus attachment. This is achieved by endocytosis, by translocation of the whole virus across the cell membrane, by direct [MASK] of the viral membrane with the cell membrane, or by fusion of the membrane of infected cells with the membrane of non-infected cells causing syncytia to be formed.

nuclearpowerplants.name: nuclear power plants
nuclearpowerplants.definition: Nuclear power plants is facilities that convert nuclear energy into electrical energy.

reproductiverights.name: reproductive rights
reproductiverights.definition: Reproductive rights is reproductive rights rest on the recognition of the basic right of all couples and individuals to decide freely and responsibly the number, spacing and timing of their children and to have the information and means to do so, and the right to attain the highest standard of sexual and reproductive health. They also include the right of all to make decisions concerning reproduction free of discrimination, coercion and violence.

bird.name: bird
bird.definition: Bird is warm-blooded vertebrates possessing feathres and belonging to the class Aves.

flight,animal.name: flight , animal
flight,animal.definition: Animal flight is the use of wings or wing-like appendages to remain aloft and move through the air.

occupationaldiseases.name: occupational diseases
occupationaldiseases.definition: Occupational diseases is diseases caused by factors involved in one's employment.

nuclearreactors.name: nuclear reactors
nuclearreactors.definition: Nuclear reactors is devices containing fissionable material in sufficient quantity and so arranged as to be capable of maintaining a controlled, self-sustaining [MASK] chain reaction. They are also known as atomic piles, atomic reactors, fission reactors, and nuclear piles, although such names are deprecated. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

spindleapparatus.name: spindle apparatus
