spindleapparatus.definition: Spindle apparatus is a [MASK] structure that forms during cell division. It consists of two spindle poles, and sets of [MASK] that may include the astral [MASK], the polar [MASK], and the kinetochore [MASK].

unitedstatesdept.ofhealthandhumanservice.name: united states dept . of health and human services
unitedstatesdept.ofhealthandhumanservice.definition: United states dept . of health and human services is united states dept . of health and human services

highmobilitygroupproteins.name: high mobility group proteins
highmobilitygroupproteins.definition: High mobility group proteins is a family of low-molecular weight, non-histone proteins found in chromatin.

abdominalabscess.name: abdominal abscess
abdominalabscess.definition: Abdominal abscess is an abscess located in the abdominal cavity, i.e., the cavity between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

waterpollution.name: water pollution
waterpollution.definition: Water pollution is contamination of bodies of water (such as [MASK]; [MASK]; seas; and groundwater.)

duodenalobstruction.name: duodenal obstruction
duodenalobstruction.definition: Duodenal obstruction is hindrance of the passage of luminal contents in the duodenum. Duodenal obstruction can be partial or complete, and caused by intrinsic or extrinsic factors. Simple obstruction is associated with diminished or stopped flow of luminal contents. Strangulating obstruction is associated with impaired blood flow to the duodenum in addition to obstructed flow of luminal contents.

sleepparalysis.name: sleep paralysis
sleepparalysis.definition: Sleep paralysis is a common condition characterized by transient partial or total paralysis of skeletal muscles and areflexia that occurs upon awakening from sleep or less often while falling asleep. Stimuli such as touch or sound may terminate the episode, which usually has a duration of seconds to minutes. This condition may occur in normal subjects or be associated with narcolepsy; cataplexy; and hypnagogic hallucinations. The pathophysiology of this condition is closely related to the normal hypotonia that occur during rem sleep. (From Adv Neurol 1995;67:245-271)

kidneys,artificial.name: kidneys , artificial
kidneys,artificial.definition: Artificial kidneys is devices which can substitute for normally functioning kidneys in removing components from the blood by dialysis that are normally eliminated in the urine.

cellormoleculardysfunction.name: cell or molecular dysfunction
cellormoleculardysfunction.definition: Cell or molecular dysfunction is cell or molecular dysfunction

infant,premature.name: infant , premature
infant,premature.definition: Premature infant is a human infant born before 37 weeks of gestation.

childbehaviordisorders.name: child behavior disorders
childbehaviordisorders.definition: Child behavior disorders is disturbances considered to be pathological based on age and stage appropriateness, e.g., conduct disturbances and anaclitic depression. This concept does not include psychoneuroses, psychoses, or personality disorders with fixed patterns.

sensoryreceptorcells.name: sensory receptor cells
sensoryreceptorcells.definition: Sensory receptor cells is specialized afferent neurons capable of transducing sensory stimuli into nerve impulses to be transmitted to the central nervous system. Sometimes sensory receptors for external stimuli are called exteroceptors; for internal stimuli are called interoceptors and proprioceptors.

sodiumiodide.name: sodium iodide
sodiumiodide.definition: Sodium iodide is a compound forming [MASK], odorless deliquescent crystals and used as iodine supplement, expectorant or in its radioactive (i-131) form as an diagnostic aid, particularly for thyroid function tests.

rna,transfer,his.name: rna , transfer , his
rna,transfer,his.definition: His transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying histidine to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

environmentalmonitoring.name: environmental monitoring
environmentalmonitoring.definition: Environmental monitoring is the monitoring of the level of toxins, chemical pollutants, microbial contaminants, or other harmful substances in the environment (soil, air, and water), workplace, or in the bodies of people and animals present in that environment.

hemoglobinscdisease.name: hemoglobin sc disease
hemoglobinscdisease.definition: Hemoglobin sc disease is one of the sickle cell disorders characterized by the presence of both hemoglobin s and hemoglobin c. It is similar to, but less severe than sickle cell anemia.

drugutilizationreview.name: drug utilization review
drugutilizationreview.definition: Drug utilization review is formal programs for assessing drug prescription against some standard. Drug utilization review may consider clinical appropriateness, cost effectiveness, and, in some cases, outcomes. Review is usually retrospective, but some analysis may be done before drugs are dispensed (as in computer systems which advise physicians when prescriptions are entered). Drug utilization review is mandated for Medicaid programs beginning in 1993.

heartblock.name: heart block
heartblock.definition: Heart block is impaired conduction of cardiac impulse that can occur anywhere along the conduction pathway, such as between the sinoatrial node and the right atrium (sa block) or between atria and ventricles (av block). Heart blocks can be classified by the duration, frequency, or completeness of conduction block. Reversibility depends on the degree of structural or functional defects.

totallungcapacity.name: total lung capacity
totallungcapacity.definition: Total lung capacity is the volume of air contained in the lungs at the end of a maximal inspiration. It is the equivalent to each of the following sums: vital capacity plus residual volume; inspiratory capacity plus functional residual capacity; tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume plus functional residual capacity; or tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume plus expiratory reserve volume plus residual volume.

sleepdisorders,intrinsic.name: sleep disorders , intrinsic
sleepdisorders,intrinsic.definition: Intrinsic sleep disorders is dyssomnias (i.e., insomnias or hypersomnias) associated with dysfunction of internal sleep mechanisms or secondary to a sleep-related medical disorder (e.g., sleep apnea, post-traumatic sleep disorders, etc.). (From Thorpy, Sleep Disorders Medicine, 1994, p187)

geographicatrophy.name: geographic atrophy
geographicatrophy.definition: Geographic atrophy is a form of macular degeneration also known as dry macular degeneration marked by occurrence of a well-defined progressive lesion or atrophy in the central part of the retina called the macula lutea. It is distinguishable from wet macular degeneration in that the latter involves neovascular exudates.

transplantationtolerance.name: transplantation tolerance
transplantationtolerance.definition: Transplantation tolerance is an induced state of non-reactivity to grafted tissue from a donor organism that would ordinarily trigger a cell-mediated or humoral immune response.

multiplebirthoffspring.name: multiple birth offspring
multiplebirthoffspring.definition: Multiple birth offspring is the offspring in multiple pregnancies (pregnancy, multiple): twins; triplets; quadruplets; quintuplets; etc.

silvernitrate.name: silver nitrate
silvernitrate.definition: Silver nitrate is a silver [MASK] with powerful germicidal activity. It has been used topically to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum.

men.name: men
men.definition: Men is human males as cultural, psychological, sociological, political, and economic entities.

behavioralsymptoms.name: behavioral symptoms
behavioralsymptoms.definition: Behavioral symptoms is observable manifestations of impaired psychological functioning.

xenopus.name: xenopus
xenopus.definition: Xenopus is an aquatic genus of the family, Pipidae, occurring in Africa and distinguished by having black horny claws on three inner hind toes.

thrombosis.name: thrombosis
thrombosis.definition: Thrombosis is formation and development of a thrombus or blood clot in the blood vessel.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 2
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.definition: Member 2 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is an ATP-binding cassette, sub-family b protein (atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b) that functions in the transport of antigens from the cytoplasm to the endoplasmic reticulum for association with histocompatibility antigens class i peptides. It also acts as a molecular scaffold for the final stage of mhc class i protein folding.

socialsegregation.name: social segregation
socialsegregation.definition: Social segregation is barriers based on group membership.

ironoverload.name: iron overload
ironoverload.definition: Iron overload is an excessive accumulation of iron in the body due to a greater than normal absorption of iron from the gastrointestinal tract or from parenteral injection. This may arise from idiopathic hemochromatosis, excessive iron intake, chronic alcoholism, certain types of refractory anemia, or transfusional hemosiderosis. (From Churchill's Illustrated Medical Dictionary, 1989)

northcarolina.name: north carolina
northcarolina.definition: North carolina is state bounded on the north by Virginia, on the east and Southeast by the Atlantic Ocean, on the south by Georgia and South Carolina, and on the west by Tennessee.

suppressorofcytokinesignaling1protein.name: suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 protein
suppressorofcytokinesignaling1protein.definition: Suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 protein is a suppressor of cytokine signaling protein that consists of an N-terminal kinase-inhibitory region, a central sh2 domain, a characteristic C-terminal socs box (a 40-amino acid motif, which functions to recruit e3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes). socs1 functions as a negative regulator of cytokines that signal through the janus kinases-stat 3 transcription factor (jak/stat3) pathway by inhibiting the activity of janus kinases.

factoranalysis,statistical.name: factor analysis , statistical
factoranalysis,statistical.definition: Statistical factor analysis is a [MASK] of statistical methods for analyzing the correlations among several variables in order to estimate the number of fundamental dimensions that underlie the observed data and to describe and measure those dimensions. It is used frequently in the development of scoring systems for rating scales and questionnaires.

sleepmedicinespecialty.name: sleep medicine specialty
sleepmedicinespecialty.definition: Sleep medicine specialty is a medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of sleep wake disorders and their causes.

retention,psychology.name: retention , psychology
retention,psychology.definition: Psychology retention is the persistence to perform a learned behavior (facts or experiences) after an interval has elapsed in which there has been no performance or practice of the behavior.

prostaticneoplasms.name: prostatic neoplasms
prostaticneoplasms.definition: Prostatic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the prostate.

hepatocytenuclearfactors.name: hepatocyte nuclear factors
hepatocytenuclearfactors.definition: [MASK] nuclear factors is [MASK] nuclear factors are a family of evolutionarily conserved transcription factors that are preferentially expressed in [MASK]. They play important roles in liver-specific transcription and are critical for cell differentiation and metabolism.

workforce.name: workforce
workforce.definition: Workforce is the number of people working or available for work or service.

rnavirusinfections.name: rna virus infections
rnavirusinfections.definition: Rna virus infections is diseases caused by rna viruses.

infarction,middlecerebralartery.name: infarction , middle cerebral artery
infarction,middlecerebralartery.definition: Middle cerebral artery infarction is necrosis occurring in the middle cerebral artery distribution system which brings blood to the entire lateral aspects of each cerebral hemisphere. Clinical signs include impaired cognition; aphasia; agraphia; weak and numbness in the face and [MASK], contralaterally or bilaterally depending on the infarction.

pupil.name: pupil
pupil.definition: Pupil is the aperture in the iris through which light passes.

timemanagement.name: time management
timemanagement.definition: Time management is planning and control of time to improve efficiency and effectiveness.

bonediseases,infectious.name: bone diseases , infectious
bonediseases,infectious.definition: Infectious bone diseases is bone diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms.

plantroots.name: plant roots
plantroots.definition: Plant roots is the usually underground portions of a plant that serve as support, store food, and through which water and mineral nutrients enter the plant. (From American Heritage Dictionary, 1982; Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)

tobaccousecessation.name: tobacco use cessation
tobaccousecessation.definition: Tobacco use cessation is ending the tobacco habits of smoking, chewing, or snuff use.

smartphone.name: smartphone
smartphone.definition: Smartphone is a cell phone with advanced computing and connectivity capability built on an operating system.

immunoglobulinm.name: immunoglobulin m
immunoglobulinm.definition: Immunoglobulin m is a class of immunoglobulin bearing mu chains (immunoglobulin mu-chains). IgM can fix complement. The name comes from its high molecular weight and originally being called a macroglobulin.

accidents.name: accidents
accidents.definition: Accidents is unexpected and unintentional events, typically resulting in accidental injuries.

coronaryvesselanomalies.name: coronary vessel anomalies
coronaryvesselanomalies.definition: Coronary vessel anomalies is malformations of coronary vessels, either arteries or veins. Included are anomalous origins of coronary arteries; arteriovenous fistula; coronary aneurysm; myocardial bridging; and others.

riskadjustment.name: risk adjustment
riskadjustment.definition: Risk [MASK] is the use of severity-of-illness measures, such as age, to estimate the risk (measurable or predictable chance of loss, injury or death) to which a patient is subject before receiving some health care intervention. This [MASK] allows comparison of performance and quality across organizations, practitioners, and communities. (from jcaho, Lexikon, 1994)

receptors,cytoplasmicandnuclear.name: receptors , cytoplasmic and nuclear
receptors,cytoplasmicandnuclear.definition: Cytoplasmic and nuclear receptors is intracellular receptors that can be found in the cytoplasm or in the nucleus. They bind to extracellular signaling molecules that migrate through or are transported across the cell membrane. Many members of this class of receptors occur in the cytoplasm and are transported to the cell nucleus upon ligand-binding where they signal via DNA-binding and transcription regulation. Also included in this category are receptors found on intracellular membranes that act via mechanisms similar to cell surface receptors.

naturalfamilyplanningmethods.name: natural family planning methods
naturalfamilyplanningmethods.definition: Natural family planning methods is a class of natural contraceptive methods in which [MASK] is practiced a few days before and after the estimated day of ovulation, during the fertile phase. Methods for determining the [MASK] or ovulation detection are based on various physiological indicators, such as circulating hormones, changes in [MASK] ([MASK]), and the basal body temperature.

populationforecast.name: population forecast
populationforecast.definition: Population forecast is estimates of projected population.

fusedteeth.name: fused teeth
fusedteeth.definition: Fused teeth is two teeth united during development by the union of their tooth germs; the teeth may be joined by the enamel of their crowns, by their root dentin, or by both.

northamerica.name: north america
northamerica.definition: North america is the northern continent of the Western Hemisphere, extending northward from the [MASK]-Panama border and including central america, [MASK], Caribbean area, the united states, canada and greenland. The term often refers more narrowly to [MASK], continental united states, and canada.

cathepsing.name: cathepsin g
cathepsing.definition: Cathepsin g is a serine protease found in the azurophil granules of neutrophils. It has an enzyme specificity similar to that of chymotrypsin c.

palate,soft.name: palate , soft
palate,soft.definition: Soft palate is a movable fold suspended from the posterior border of the [MASK]. The uvula hangs from the middle of the lower border.

cisplatin.name: cisplatin
cisplatin.definition: Cisplatin is an inorganic and water-soluble [MASK] complex. After undergoing hydrolysis, it reacts with dna to produce both intra and interstrand crosslinks. These crosslinks appear to impair replication and transcription of dna. The cytotoxicity of cisplatin correlates with cellular arrest in the g2 phase of the cell cycle.

pharmacists.name: pharmacists
pharmacists.definition: Pharmacists is those persons legally qualified by education and training to engage in the practice of pharmacy.

deepsedation.name: deep sedation
deepsedation.definition: Deep sedation is drug-induced depression of consciousness during which patients cannot be easily aroused but respond purposely following repeated painful stimulation. The ability to independently maintain ventilatory function may be impaired. (From: American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines)

genome,viral.name: genome , viral
genome,viral.definition: Viral genome is the complete genetic complement contained in a dna or rna molecule in a virus.

complementpathway,alternative.name: complement pathway , alternative
complementpathway,alternative.definition: Alternative complement pathway is complement activation initiated by the interaction of microbial antigens with complement c3b. When complement factor b binds to the membrane-bound C3b, complement factor d cleaves it to form alternative c3 convertase (c3bbb) which, stabilized by complement factor p, is able to cleave multiple complement c3 to form alternative c5 convertase (c3bbb3b) leading to cleavage of complement c5 and the assembly of complement membrane attack complex.

targetedgenerepair.name: targeted gene repair
targetedgenerepair.definition: Targeted gene repair is a technique which uses synthetic oligonucleotides to direct the cell's inherent dna repair system to correct a mutation at a specific site in an episome or chromosome.

receptors,interferon.name: receptors , interferon
receptors,interferon.definition: Interferon receptors is specific molecular sites or structures on or in cells with which interferons react or to which they bind in order to modify the function of the cells. Interferons exert their pleiotropic effects through two different receptors. alpha- and beta-interferon crossreact with common receptors, while gamma-interferon initiates its biological effects through its own specific receptor system.

terminology.name: terminology
terminology.definition: Terminology is work consisting of lists of the technical terms or expressions used in a specific field. These lists may or may not be formally adopted or sanctioned by usage.

geneticfunction.name: genetic function
geneticfunction.definition: Genetic function is function of genes.

esophagealstenosis.name: esophageal stenosis
esophagealstenosis.definition: Esophageal stenosis is a stricture of the esophagus. Most are acquired but can be congenital.

severeacutemalnutrition.name: severe acute malnutrition
severeacutemalnutrition.definition: Severe acute malnutrition is acute form of malnutrition which usually affects children, characterized by a very low weight for height (below -3z scores of the median [MASK] Organization standards), visible severe wasting, or occurrence of nutritional edema.  It can be a direct or indirect cause of fatality in children suffering from [MASK] and pneumonia. Do not confuse with [MASK], a condition in which the body is not getting enough food, usually for extended periods of time.

reproducibilityofresults.name: reproducibility of results
reproducibilityofresults.definition: Reproducibility of results is the statistical reproducibility of measurements (often in a clinical context), including the testing of instrumentation or techniques to obtain reproducible results. The concept includes reproducibility of physiological measurements, which may be used to develop rules to assess probability or prognosis, or response to a stimulus; reproducibility of occurrence of a condition; and reproducibility of experimental results.

lung.name: lung
lung.definition: Lung is either of the pair of organs occupying the cavity of the thorax that effect the aeration of the blood.

myelinbasicprotein.name: myelin basic protein
myelinbasicprotein.definition: Myelin basic protein is an abundant cytosolic protein that plays a critical role in the structure of multilamellar myelin. Myelin basic protein binds to the cytosolic sides of myelin cell membranes and causes a tight adhesion between opposing cell membranes.

elbow.name: elbow
elbow.definition: Elbow is region of the body immediately surrounding and including the elbow joint.

confinedspaces.name: confined spaces
confinedspaces.definition: Confined spaces is a space which has limited openings for entry and exit combined with unfavorable natural ventilation such as caves, refrigerators, deep tunnels, pipelines, sewers, silos, tanks, vats, mines, deep trenches or pits, vaults, manholes, chimneys, etc.

parasiticsensitivitytests.name: parasitic sensitivity tests
parasiticsensitivitytests.definition: Parasitic sensitivity tests is tests that demonstrate the relative effectiveness of chemotherapeutic agents against specific parasites.

microscopy,electron,transmission.name: microscopy , electron , transmission
microscopy,electron,transmission.definition: Transmission [MASK] microscopy is [MASK] microscopy in which the [MASK] or their reaction products that pass down through the specimen are imaged below the plane of the specimen.

celllineage.name: cell lineage
celllineage.definition: Cell lineage is the developmental history of specific differentiated cell types as traced back to the original stem cells in the embryo.

dnarestrictionenzymes.name: dna restriction enzymes
dnarestrictionenzymes.definition: Dna restriction enzymes is enzymes that are part of the restriction-modification systems. They catalyze the endonucleolytic cleavage of dna sequences which lack the species-specific methylation pattern in the host cell's dna. Cleavage yields random or specific double-stranded fragments with terminal 5'-phosphates. The function of restriction enzymes is to destroy any foreign dna that invades the host cell. Most have been studied in bacterial systems, but a few have been found in eukaryotic organisms. They are also used as tools for the systematic [MASK] and mapping of chromosomes, in the determination of base sequences of DNAs, and have made it possible to splice and recombine genes from one organism into the genome of another. ec 3.21.1.

fetalhemoglobin.name: fetal hemoglobin
fetalhemoglobin.definition: Fetal hemoglobin is the major component of hemoglobin in the fetus. This hemoglobin has two alpha and two gamma polypeptide subunits in comparison to normal adult hemoglobin, which has two alpha and two beta polypeptide subunits. Fetal hemoglobin concentrations can be elevated (usually above 0.5%) in children and adults affected by leukemia and several types of anemia.

pregnancycomplications,cardiovascular.name: pregnancy complications , cardiovascular
pregnancycomplications,cardiovascular.definition: Cardiovascular pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and a cardiovascular disease. The disease may precede or follow fertilization and it may or may not have a deleterious effect on the pregnant woman or fetus.

rna,transfer,met.name: rna , transfer , met
rna,transfer,met.definition: Met transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying methionine to sites on the ribosomes. During initiation of protein synthesis, tRNA(f)Met in prokaryotic cells and tRNA(i)Met in eukaryotic cells binds to the start codon (codon, initiator).

hospitalunits.name: hospital units
hospitalunits.definition: Hospital units is those areas of the hospital organization not considered departments which provide specialized patient care. They include various hospital special care wards.

friends.name: friends
friends.definition: Friends is persons whom one knows, likes, and trusts.

southafrica.name: south africa
southafrica.definition: South africa is a republic in southern Africa, the southernmost part of Africa. It has three capitals: Pretoria (administrative), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial). Officially the Republic of South Africa since 1960, it was called the Union of South Africa 1910-1960.

cellmembranestructures.name: cell membrane structures
cellmembranestructures.definition: Cell membrane structures is structures which are part of the cell membrane or have cell membrane as a major part of their structure.

auditorydiseases,central.name: auditory diseases , central
auditorydiseases,central.definition: Central auditory diseases is disorders of hearing or auditory perception due to pathological processes of the [MASK] in the central nervous system. These include [MASK] and auditory perceptual disorders.

brachialplexusblock.name: brachial plexus block
brachialplexusblock.definition: Brachial plexus block is a blocking of [MASK] in the network of nerve fibers innervating the upper extremity.

microscopy,electron,scanningtransmission.name: microscopy , electron , scanning transmission
microscopy,electron,scanningtransmission.definition: Scanning transmission [MASK] microscopy is a type of transmission [MASK] microscopy in which the object is examined directly by an extremely narrow [MASK] beam scanning the specimen point-by-point and using the reactions of the [MASK] that are transmitted through the specimen to create the image. It should not be confused with scanning [MASK] microscopy.

panicdisorder.name: panic disorder
panicdisorder.definition: Panic disorder is a type of anxiety disorder characterized by unexpected panic attacks that last minutes or, rarely, hours. Panic attacks begin with intense apprehension, fear or terror and, often, a feeling of impending doom. Symptoms experienced during a panic attack include dyspnea or sensations of being smothered; dizziness, loss of balance or faintness; choking sensations; palpitations or accelerated heart rate; shakiness; sweating; nausea or other form of abdominal distress; depersonalization or derealization; paresthesias; hot flashes or chills; chest discomfort or pain; fear of dying and fear of not being in control of oneself or going crazy. Agoraphobia may also develop. Similar to other anxiety disorders, it may be inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.

bacterialcapsules.name: bacterial capsules
bacterialcapsules.definition: Bacterial capsules is an envelope of loose gel surrounding a bacterial cell which is associated with the virulence of pathogenic bacteria. Some capsules have a well-defined border, whereas others form a slime layer that trails off into the medium. Most capsules consist of relatively simple polysaccharides but there are some bacteria whose capsules are made of polypeptides.

bonewires.name: bone wires
bonewires.definition: Bone wires is steel wires, often threaded through the skin, soft tissues, and bone, used to fix broken bones. Kirschner wires or apparatus also includes the application of traction to the healing bones through the wires.

methane.name: methane
methane.definition: Methane is the simplest saturated hydrocarbon. It is a colorless, flammable gas, slightly soluble in water. It is one of the chief constituents of natural gas and is formed in the decomposition of organic matter. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

subcutaneousfat.name: subcutaneous fat
subcutaneousfat.definition: Subcutaneous fat is fatty tissue under the skin through out the body.

vaccines,subunit.name: vaccines , subunit
vaccines,subunit.definition: Subunit vaccines is vaccines consisting of one or more antigens that stimulate a strong immune response. They are purified from microorganisms or produced by [MASK] techniques, or they can be chemically synthesized peptides.

interferontypei.name: interferon type i
interferontypei.definition: Interferon type i is interferon secreted by leukocytes, fibroblasts, or lymphoblasts in response to viruses or interferon inducers other than mitogens, antigens, or allo-antigens. They include alpha- and beta-interferons (interferon-alpha and interferon-beta).

weightperception.name: weight perception
weightperception.definition: Weight perception is recognition and discrimination of the heaviness of a lifted object.

gametheory.name: game theory
gametheory.definition: Game theory is theoretical construct used in applied mathematics to analyze certain situations in which there is an interplay between parties that may have similar, opposed, or mixed interests. In a typical game, decision-making "players," who each have their own goals, try to gain advantage over the other parties by anticipating each other's decisions; the game is finally resolved as a consequence of the players' decisions.

traumaseverityindices.name: trauma severity indices
traumaseverityindices.definition: Trauma severity indices is systems for assessing, classifying, and coding injuries. These systems are used in medical records, surveillance systems, and state and national registries to aid in the collection and reporting of trauma.

tubulinmodulators.name: tubulin modulators
tubulinmodulators.definition: Tubulin modulators is agents that interact with tubulin to inhibit or promote [MASK] of [MASK].

foodanalysis.name: food analysis
foodanalysis.definition: Food analysis is measurement and evaluation of the components of substances to be taken as food.

directedtissuedonation.name: directed tissue donation
directedtissuedonation.definition: Directed tissue donation is tissue, organ, or gamete donation intended for a designated recipient.

glass.name: glass
glass.definition: Glass is hard, amorphous, brittle, inorganic, usually transparent, polymerous silicate of basic oxides, usually potassium or sodium. It is used in the form of hard sheets, vessels, tubing, fibers, ceramics, beads, etc.

molecularconformation.name: molecular conformation
molecularconformation.definition: Molecular conformation is the characteristic three-dimensional shape of a molecule.

employeeincentiveplans.name: employee incentive plans
employeeincentiveplans.definition: Employee incentive plans is programs designed by management to motivate employees to work more efficiently with increased productivity, and greater employee [MASK].

socialwork.name: social work
socialwork.definition: Social work is the use of community resources, individual case work, or group work to promote the adaptive capacities of individuals in relation to their social and economic environments. It includes social service agencies.

molecularbiologyresearchtechnique.name: molecular biology research technique
molecularbiologyresearchtechnique.definition: Molecular biology research technique is molecular biology research technique

doxorubicin.name: doxorubicin
doxorubicin.definition: Doxorubicin is antineoplastic antibiotic obtained from Streptomyces peucetius. It is a hydroxy derivative of daunorubicin.

toxicology.name: toxicology
toxicology.definition: Toxicology is the science concerned with the detection, chemical composition, and biological action of toxic substances or poisons and the treatment and prevention of toxic manifestations.

embryoloss.name: embryo loss
embryoloss.definition: Embryo loss is early pregnancy loss during the embryo, mammalian stage of development. In the human, this period comprises the second through eighth week after fertilization.

cellphoneuse.name: cell phone use
cellphoneuse.definition: Cell phone use is utilization of wireless phones for communication.

fibrinmodulatingagents.name: fibrin modulating agents
fibrinmodulatingagents.definition: Fibrin modulating agents is agents that affect the function of fibrin in blood coagulation. They used as coagulants for hemorrhage or anticoagulants for thrombosis.

glycogenstoragediseasetypevi.name: glycogen storage disease type vi
glycogenstoragediseasetypevi.definition: Glycogen storage disease type vi is a hepatic glycogen storage disease in which there is an apparent deficiency of hepatic phosphorylase (glycogen phosphorylase, liver form) activity.

japan.name: japan
japan.definition: Japan is a country in eastern Asia, island chain between the North Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Japan, east of the Korean Peninsula. The capital is Tokyo.

aminoacidtransportsystems,neutral.name: amino acid transport systems , neutral
aminoacidtransportsystems,neutral.definition: Neutral amino acid transport systems is amino acid transporter systems capable of transporting neutral amino acids (amino acids, neutral).

giantcelltumorofbone.name: giant cell tumor of bone
giantcelltumorofbone.definition: Giant cell tumor of bone is a bone tumor composed of cellular spindle-cell stroma containing scattered multinucleated giant cells resembling osteoclasts. The tumors range from benign to frankly malignant lesions. The tumor occurs most frequently in an end of a long tubular bone in young adults. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

femur.name: femur
femur.definition: Femur is the longest and largest bone of the skeleton, it is situated between the hip and the [MASK].

aorta,thoracic.name: aorta , thoracic
aorta,thoracic.definition: Thoracic aorta is the portion of the descending aorta proceeding from the arch of the aorta and extending to the diaphragm, eventually connecting to the abdominal aorta.

lead.name: lead
lead.definition: Lead is a soft, grayish metal with poisonous [MASK]; atomic number 82, atomic weight 207.2, symbol Pb.

multiplexpolymerasechainreaction.name: multiplex polymerase chain reaction
multiplexpolymerasechainreaction.definition: Multiplex polymerase chain reaction is methods for using more than one primer [MASK] in a polymerase chain reaction to amplify more than one segment of the target dna sequence in a single reaction.

visitorstopatients.name: visitors to patients
visitorstopatients.definition: Visitors to patients is patients' guests and rules for visiting.

adolescentnutritionalphysiologicalphenom.name: adolescent nutritional physiological phenomena
adolescentnutritionalphysiologicalphenom.definition: Adolescent nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of children aged 13-18 years.

nucleicacidprecursors.name: nucleic acid precursors
nucleicacidprecursors.definition: Nucleic acid precursors is use for nucleic acid precursors in general or for which there is no specific heading.

inhibitorofapoptosisproteins.name: inhibitor of apoptosis proteins
inhibitorofapoptosisproteins.definition: Inhibitor of apoptosis proteins is a conserved class of proteins that control apoptosis in both vertebrates and invertebrates. iap proteins interact with and inhibit caspases, and they function as anti-apoptotic proteins. The protein class is defined by an approximately 80-amino acid motif called the baculoviral inhibitor of apoptosis repeat; some members have ubiquitin-protein ligase activity.

biologicalassay.name: biological assay
biologicalassay.definition: Biological assay is a method of measuring the effects of a biologically active substance using an intermediate in vivo or in vitro tissue or cell model under controlled conditions. It includes virulence studies in animal fetuses in utero, mouse convulsion bioassay of insulin, quantitation of tumor-initiator systems in mouse skin, calculation of potentiating effects of a hormonal factor in an isolated strip of contracting stomach muscle, etc.

tastebuds.name: taste buds
tastebuds.definition: Taste buds is small sensory organs which contain gustatory receptor cells, basal cells, and supporting cells. Taste buds in humans are found in the epithelia of the tongue, palate, and pharynx. They are innervated by the chorda tympani nerve (a branch of the facial nerve) and the glossopharyngeal nerve.

vesicularglutamatetransportproteins.name: vesicular glutamate transport proteins
vesicularglutamatetransportproteins.definition: Vesicular glutamate transport proteins is a family of vesicular neurotransmitter transporter proteins that were originally characterized as sodium dependent inorganic phosphate cotransporters. Vesicular glutamate transport proteins sequester the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate from the cytoplasm into [MASK] in exchange for lumenal protons.

perceptualdisorders.name: perceptual disorders
perceptualdisorders.definition: Perceptual disorders is cognitive disorders characterized by an impaired ability to perceive the nature of objects or concepts through use of the sense organs. These include spatial neglect syndromes, where an individual does not attend to visual, auditory, or sensory stimuli presented from one side of the body.

surgery,veterinary.name: surgery , veterinary
surgery,veterinary.definition: Veterinary surgery is a board-certified specialty of veterinary medicine, requiring at least four years of special education, training, and practice of veterinary surgery after graduation from veterinary school. In the written, oral, and practical examinations candidates may choose either large or small animal surgery. (From avma Directory, 43d ed, p278)

animalidentificationsystems.name: animal identification systems
animalidentificationsystems.definition: Animal identification systems is procedures for recognizing individual animals and certain identifiable characteristics pertaining to them; includes computerized methods, ear tags, etc.

orthopedicfixationdevices.name: orthopedic fixation devices
orthopedicfixationdevices.definition: Orthopedic fixation devices is devices which are used in the treatment of orthopedic injuries and diseases.

proteinsplicing.name: protein splicing
proteinsplicing.definition: Protein splicing is the excision of in-frame internal protein sequences (inteins) of a precursor protein, coupled with [MASK] of the flanking sequences (exteins). Protein splicing is an autocatalytic reaction and results in the production of two proteins from a single primary translation product: the intein and the mature protein.

immunoglobulinsubunits.name: immunoglobulin subunits
immunoglobulinsubunits.definition: Immunoglobulin subunits is the protein subunits of the multimeric immunoglobulin proteins, such as iga; igd; ige; igg; and igm. Included are the heavy and light chains which contain the specific antigen binding domains, as well as the accessory proteins that are part of the the secreted forms of igm and iga; (secretory iga).

crops,agricultural.name: crops , agricultural
crops,agricultural.definition: Agricultural crops is cultivated plants or agricultural produce such as grain, vegetables, or fruit. (From American Heritage Dictionary, 1982)

stainingandlabeling.name: staining and labeling
stainingandlabeling.definition: Staining and labeling is the marking of biological material with a dye or other reagent for the purpose of identifying and quantitating components of tissues, cells or their extracts.

physicalconditioning,human.name: physical conditioning , human
physicalconditioning,human.definition: Human physical conditioning is diet modification and physical exercise to improve the ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities.

arthroplasty,replacement,elbow.name: arthroplasty , replacement , elbow
arthroplasty,replacement,elbow.definition: Elbow replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the elbow joint.

cloning,organism.name: cloning , organism
cloning,organism.definition: Organism cloning is the formation of one or more genetically identical organisms derived by vegetative reproduction from a single cell. The source nuclear material can be embryo-derived, fetus-derived, or taken from an adult somatic cell.

axiallength,eye.name: axial length , eye
axiallength,eye.definition: Eye axial length is the distance between the anterior and posterior poles of the eye, measured either by ultrasonography or by partial coherence interferometry.

nanowires.name: nanowires
nanowires.definition: Nanowires is nanometer-scale wires made of materials that conduct electricity. They can be coated with molecules such as antibodies that will bind to proteins and other substances.

plateletcount.name: platelet count
plateletcount.definition: Platelet count is the number of platelets per unit volume in a sample of venous blood.

dentalrestorationwear.name: dental restoration wear
dentalrestorationwear.definition: Dental restoration wear is occlusal wear of the surfaces of restorations and surface wear of dentures.

sphase.name: s phase
sphase.definition: S phase is phase of the cell cycle following g1 and preceding g2 when the entire dna content of the nucleus is replicated. It is achieved by bidirectional replication at multiple sites along each chromosome.

publicopinion.name: public opinion
publicopinion.definition: Public opinion is the attitude of a significant portion of a population toward any given proposition, based upon a measurable amount of factual evidence, and involving some degree of reflection, analysis, and reasoning.

rna,transfer,cys.name: rna , transfer , cys
rna,transfer,cys.definition: Cys transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying [MASK] to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

militarydentistry.name: military dentistry
militarydentistry.definition: Military dentistry is the practice of dentistry as applied to special circumstances associated with military operations.

edemadiseaseofswine.name: edema disease of swine
edemadiseaseofswine.definition: Edema disease of swine is an [MASK] of young pigs that is usually associated with weaning. It is characterized clinically by paresis and subcutaneous edema.

contactlenssolutions.name: contact lens solutions
contactlenssolutions.definition: Contact lens solutions is sterile solutions used to clean and disinfect contact lenses.

curcumin.name: curcumin
curcumin.definition: Curcumin is a yellow-orange dye obtained from tumeric, the powdered root of curcuma longa. It is used in the preparation of curcuma [MASK] and the detection of boron. Curcumin appears to possess a spectrum of pharmacological properties, due primarily to its inhibitory effects on metabolic enzymes.

mobilehealthunits.name: mobile health units
mobilehealthunits.definition: Mobile health units is movable or portable facilities in which diagnostic and therapeutic services are provided to the community.

obstetriclaborcomplications.name: obstetric labor complications
obstetriclaborcomplications.definition: Obstetric labor complications is medical problems associated with obstetric labor, such as breech presentation; premature obstetric labor; hemorrhage; or others. These complications can affect the well-being of the mother, the fetus, or both.

motorcortex.name: motor cortex
motorcortex.definition: Motor cortex is area of the frontal lobe concerned with primary motor control located in the dorsal precentral gyrus immediately anterior to the central sulcus. It is comprised of three areas: the primary motor cortex located on the anterior paracentral lobule on the medial surface of the brain; the premotor cortex located anterior to the primary motor cortex; and the supplementary motor area located on the midline surface of the hemisphere anterior to the primary motor cortex.

hybridization,genetic.name: hybridization , genetic
hybridization,genetic.definition: Genetic hybridization is the genetic process of crossbreeding between genetically dissimilar parents to produce a hybrid.

visualfieldtests.name: visual field tests
visualfieldtests.definition: [MASK] tests is method of measuring and mapping the scope of vision, from central to peripheral of each eye.

coldischemia.name: cold ischemia
coldischemia.definition: Cold ischemia is the chilling of a tissue or organ during decreased blood perfusion or in the absence of blood supply. Cold ischemia time during organ transplantation begins when the organ is cooled with a cold perfusion solution after organ procurement surgery, and ends after the tissue reaches physiological temperature during implantation procedures.

terminalcare.name: terminal care
terminalcare.definition: Terminal care is medical and nursing care of patients in the terminal stage of an illness.

dailyorrecreationalactivity.name: daily or recreational activity
dailyorrecreationalactivity.definition: Daily or recreational activity is daily or recreational activity

umbilicalarteries.name: umbilical arteries
umbilicalarteries.definition: Umbilical arteries is specialized arterial vessels in the umbilical cord. They carry waste and deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the mother via the placenta. In humans, there are usually two umbilical arteries but sometimes one.

glutamatesynthase.name: glutamate synthase
glutamatesynthase.definition: Glutamate synthase is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of 2 molecules of glutamate from [MASK] plus alpha-ketoglutarate in the presence of nadph. ec 1.4.1.13.

foodpreservation.name: food preservation
foodpreservation.definition: Food preservation is procedures or techniques used to keep food from spoiling.

geneontology.name: gene ontology
geneontology.definition: Gene ontology is sets of structured vocabularies used for describing and categorizing genes, and gene products by their molecular function, involvement in biological processes, and cellular location. These vocabularies and their associations to genes and gene products (Gene Ontology annotations) are generated and curated by the Gene Ontology Consortium.

transferrin.name: transferrin
transferrin.definition: Transferrin is an iron-binding beta1-globulin that is synthesized in the liver and secreted into the blood. It plays a central role in the transport of iron throughout the circulation. a variety of transferrin isoforms exist in humans, including some that are considered markers for specific disease states.

productlabeling.name: product labeling
productlabeling.definition: Product labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a product or its container or wrapper. It includes purpose, effect, description, directions, hazards, warnings, and other relevant information.

healthfacilityadministration.name: health facility administration
healthfacilityadministration.definition: Health facility administration is management of the organization of health facilities.

neoplasms,connectiveandsofttissue.name: neoplasms , connective and soft tissue
neoplasms,connectiveandsofttissue.definition: Connective and soft tissue neoplasms is neoplasms developing from some structure of the connective and [MASK]. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in connective or soft tissue.

juvenileliterature.name: juvenile literature
juvenileliterature.definition: Juvenile literature is works produced for children through age 15 or through the ninth grade.

bacterialinfections.name: bacterial infections
bacterialinfections.definition: Bacterial infections is infections by bacteria, general or unspecified.

cellnucleus.name: cell nucleus
cellnucleus.definition: Cell nucleus is within a eukaryotic cell, a membrane-limited body which contains chromosomes and one or more nucleoli (cell nucleolus). The nuclear membrane consists of a double unit-type membrane which is perforated by a number of pores; the outermost membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum. a cell may contain more than one nucleus. (From Singleton & Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

stemcellfactor.name: stem cell factor
stemcellfactor.definition: Stem cell factor is a hematopoietic growth factor and the ligand of the cell surface c-kit protein (proto-oncogene proteins c-kit). It is expressed during embryogenesis and is a growth factor for a number of cell types including the [MASK] and the melanocytes in addition to the hematopoietic stem cells.

veterinarydrugs.name: veterinary drugs
veterinarydrugs.definition: Veterinary drugs is drugs used by veterinarians in the treatment of animal diseases. The veterinarian's pharmacological armamentarium is the counterpart of drugs treating human diseases, with dosage and administration adjusted to the size, weight, disease, and idiosyncrasies of the species. In the United States most drugs are subject to federal regulations with special reference to the safety of drugs and residues in edible animal products.

genes,rev.name: genes , rev
genes,rev.definition: Rev genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for a protein that regulates the expression of the viral structural and regulatory proteins in human immunodeficiency virus (hiv). rev is short for regulator of virion.

medicareparta.name: medicare part a
medicareparta.definition: Medicare part a is the compulsory portion of Medicare that is known as the Hospital Insurance Program. All persons 65 years and older who are entitled to benefits under the Old Age, Survivors, Disability and Health Insurance Program or railroad [MASK], persons under the age of 65 who have been eligible for disability for more than two years, and insured workers (and their dependents) requiring renal dialysis or kidney transplantation are automatically enrolled in Medicare Part a.

fibroblastgrowthfactor1.name: fibroblast growth factor 1
fibroblastgrowthfactor1.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 1 is a 17-kDa single-chain polypeptide growth factor that plays a significant role in the process of wound healing and is a potent inducer of physiologic angiogenesis. It binds to heparin, which potentiates its biological activity and protects it from proteolysis. The growth factor is an extremely potent inducer of dna synthesis in a variety of cell types from mesoderm and neuroectoderm lineages, and also has chemotactic and mitogenic activities. It was originally named acidic fibroblast growth factor based upon its chemical properties and to distinguish it from basic fibroblast growth factor (fibroblast growth factor 2).

tuberculosissocieties.name: tuberculosis societies
tuberculosissocieties.definition: Tuberculosis societies is voluntary agencies concerned with prevention and treatment of tuberculosis.

transitionelements.name: transition elements
transitionelements.definition: Transition elements is elements with partially filled d orbitals. They constitute groups 3-12 of the periodic [MASK] of elements.

capsid.name: capsid
capsid.definition: Capsid is the outer protein protective shell of a virus, which protects the viral nucleic acid. Capsids are composed of repeating units (capsomers or capsomeres) of capsid proteins which when assembled together form either an icosahedral or helical shape.

seizures.name: seizures
seizures.definition: Seizures is clinical or subclinical disturbances of cortical function due to a sudden, abnormal, excessive, and disorganized discharge of brain cells. Clinical manifestations include abnormal motor, sensory and psychic phenomena. Recurrent seizures are usually referred to as epilepsy or "seizure disorder."

organsize.name: organ size
organsize.definition: Organ size is the measurement of an organ in volume, mass, or heaviness.

cathepsinl.name: cathepsin l
cathepsinl.definition: Cathepsin l is a ubiquitously-expressed [MASK] protease that plays an enzymatic role in post-translational protein processing of proteins within [MASK].

hair.name: hair
hair.definition: Hair is a filament-like structure consisting of a shaft which projects to the surface of the skin from a root which is softer than the shaft and lodges in the cavity of a hair follicle. It is found on most surfaces of the body.

satelliteviruses.name: satellite viruses
satelliteviruses.definition: Satellite viruses is defective viruses which can multiply only by association with a helper virus which complements the defective gene. Satellite viruses may be associated with certain plant viruses, animal viruses, or bacteriophages. They differ from satellite rna; (rna, satellite) in that satellite viruses encode their own coat protein.

tooth,impacted.name: tooth , impacted
tooth,impacted.definition: Impacted tooth is a tooth that is prevented from erupting by a physical barrier, usually other teeth. Impaction may also result from orientation of the tooth in an other than vertical position in the periodontal structures.

seedlings.name: seedlings
seedlings.definition: Seedlings is young plants produced at the completion of germination of [MASK].

alveolarbonegrafting.name: alveolar bone grafting
alveolarbonegrafting.definition: Alveolar bone grafting is surgical procedure to add bone to the alveolar ridge in children born with a cleft [MASK] and a cleft palate.

fungus.name: fungus
fungus.definition: Fungus is a kingdom of eukaryotic, heterotrophic organisms that live parasitically as saprobes, including mushrooms; yeasts; smuts, molds, etc.

oxygenisotopes.name: oxygen isotopes
oxygenisotopes.definition: Oxygen isotopes is stable oxygen atoms that have the same atomic number as the element oxygen, but differ in atomic weight. o-17 and 18 are stable oxygen isotopes.

salinity.name: salinity
salinity.definition: Salinity is degree of saltiness, which is largely the osmolar concentration of sodium chloride plus any other [MASK] present. It is an ecological factor of considerable importance, influencing the types of organisms that live in an environment.

deficiencydiseases.name: deficiency diseases
deficiencydiseases.definition: Deficiency diseases is a condition produced by dietary or metabolic deficiency. The term includes all diseases caused by an insufficient supply of essential nutrients, i.e., protein (or amino acids), vitamins, and minerals. It also includes an inadequacy of calories. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

hernia,femoral.name: hernia , femoral
hernia,femoral.definition: Femoral hernia is a groin hernia occurring inferior to the inguinal ligament and medial to the femoral vein and [MASK]. The femoral hernia sac has a small [MASK] but may enlarge considerably when it enters the [MASK] of the [MASK]. It is caused by defects in the [MASK].

socialwork,psychiatric.name: social work , psychiatric
socialwork,psychiatric.definition: Psychiatric social work is use of all social work processes in the treatment of patients in a psychiatric or mental health setting.

ocularhypotension.name: ocular hypotension
ocularhypotension.definition: Ocular hypotension is abnormally low intraocular pressure often related to chronic inflammation (uveitis).

spermtail.name: sperm tail
spermtail.definition: Sperm tail is the posterior filiform portion of the spermatozoon (spermatozoa) that provides sperm motility.

acupuncture,ear.name: acupuncture , ear
acupuncture,ear.definition: Ear acupuncture is acupuncture therapy by inserting needles in the ear. It is used to control pain and for treating various ailments.

medicine,chinesetraditional.name: medicine , chinese traditional
medicine,chinesetraditional.definition: Chinese traditional medicine is a system of traditional medicine which is based on the beliefs and practices of the Chinese culture.

genedeletion.name: gene deletion
genedeletion.definition: Gene deletion is a genetic rearrangement through loss of segments of dna or rna, bringing sequences which are normally separated into close proximity. This deletion may be detected using cytogenetic techniques and can also be inferred from the phenotype, indicating a deletion at one specific locus.

obesitymanagement.name: obesity management
obesitymanagement.definition: Obesity management is an integrated professional approach to screening, evaluation, control, and reduction of abnormal weight gain.

healthfacilities.name: health facilities
healthfacilities.definition: Health facilities is institutions which provide medical or health-related services.

transcriptionalregulatorerg.name: transcriptional regulator erg
transcriptionalregulatorerg.definition: Transcriptional regulator erg is a trans-activator and member of the erythroblast transformation-specific family of transcriptions factors that contain a characteristic ets motif. It is required for platelet cell adhesion to the subendothelium and associates with [MASK] in prostate cancer; ewing's sarcoma; and [MASK].

fluorescein.name: fluorescein
fluorescein.definition: Fluorescein is a phthalic indicator dye that appears yellow-green in normal tear film and bright green in a more alkaline medium such as the aqueous humor.

humanumbilicalveinendothelialcells.name: human umbilical vein endothelial cells
humanumbilicalveinendothelialcells.definition: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells is endothelial cells that line venous vessels of the umbilical cord.

retinalpigmentepithelium.name: retinal pigment epithelium
retinalpigmentepithelium.definition: [MASK] epithelium is the single layer of pigment-containing epithelial cells in the retina, situated closely to the tips (outer segments) of the retinal photoreceptor cells. These epithelial cells are macroglia that perform essential functions for the photoreceptor cells, such as in nutrient transport, [MASK] of the shed photoreceptor membranes, and ensuring retinal attachment.

allostericsite.name: allosteric site
allostericsite.definition: Allosteric site is a site on an enzyme which upon binding of a modulator, causes the enzyme to undergo a conformational change that may alter its catalytic or binding properties.

guineapigs.name: guinea pigs
guineapigs.definition: [MASK] pigs is a common name used for the genus Cavia. The most common species is Cavia porcellus which is the domesticated [MASK] pig used for pets and biomedical research.

whitematter.name: white matter
whitematter.definition: [MASK] matter is the region of central nervous system that appears lighter in [MASK] than the other type, gray matter. It mainly consists of myelinated nerve fibers and contains few neuronal cell bodies or dendrites.

peptidet.name: peptide t
peptidet.definition: Peptide t is n-(N-(N(2)-(N-(N-(N-(N-D-Alanyl L-seryl)-L-threonyl)-L-threonyl) L-threonyl)-L-asparaginyl)-L-tyrosyl) L-threonine. Octapeptide sharing sequence homology with hiv envelope protein gp120. It is potentially useful as antiviral agent in aids therapy. The core pentapeptide sequence, ttnyt, consisting of amino acids 4-8 in peptide t, is the hiv envelope sequence required for attachment to the cd4 receptor.

epilepsy,partial,motor.name: epilepsy , partial , motor
epilepsy,partial,motor.definition: Motor partial epilepsy is a disorder characterized by recurrent localized paroxysmal discharges of cerebral neurons that give rise to seizures that have motor manifestations. The majority of partial motor seizures originate in the frontal lobe (see also epilepsy, frontal lobe). Motor seizures may manifest as tonic or clonic movements involving the face, one limb or one side of the body. a variety of more complex patterns of movement, including abnormal posturing of extremities, may also occur.

chromosomestructures.name: chromosome structures
chromosomestructures.definition: Chromosome structures is structures which are contained in or part of chromosomes.

braindiseases,metabolic.name: brain diseases , metabolic
braindiseases,metabolic.definition: Metabolic brain diseases is acquired or inborn metabolic diseases that produce brain dysfunction or damage. These include primary (i.e., disorders intrinsic to the brain) and secondary (i.e., extracranial) metabolic conditions that adversely affect cerebral function.

nervetissueproteins.name: nerve tissue proteins
nervetissueproteins.definition: Nerve tissue proteins is biological molecule related to the function and maintenance of normal nervous tissue.

marketing.name: marketing
marketing.definition: Marketing is activity involved in transfer of goods from producer to consumer or in the exchange of services.

factorxia.name: factor xia
factorxia.definition: Factor xia is activated form of factor xi. In the intrinsic pathway, Factor xi is activated to XIa by factor XIIa in the presence of cofactor hmwk; (high molecular weight kininogen). Factor XIa then activates factor ix to factor IXa in the presence of calcium.

punishment.name: punishment
punishment.definition: Punishment is the application of an unpleasant stimulus or penalty for the purpose of eliminating or correcting undesirable behavior.

esophagealmotilitydisorders.name: esophageal motility disorders
esophagealmotilitydisorders.definition: Esophageal motility disorders is disorders affecting the motor function of the upper esophageal sphincter; lower esophageal sphincter; the esophagus body, or a combination of these parts. The failure of the sphincters to maintain a tonic pressure may result in gastric reflux of food and acid into the esophagus (gastroesophageal reflux). Other disorders include hypermotility (spastic disorders) and markedly increased amplitude in contraction (nutcracker esophagus).

inactivation,metabolic.name: inactivation , metabolic
inactivation,metabolic.definition: Metabolic inactivation is reduction of pharmacologic activity or toxicity of a drug or other foreign substance by a living system, usually by enzymatic action. It includes those metabolic transformations that make the substance more soluble for faster renal excretion.

geneticfitness.name: genetic fitness
geneticfitness.definition: Genetic fitness is the capability of an organism to survive and reproduce. The phenotypic expression of the genotype in a particular environment determines how genetically fit an organism will be.

nature.name: nature
nature.definition: Nature is the system of all phenomena in space and time; the totality of physical reality. It is both a scientific and philosophic concept appearing in all historic eras. (Webster 2d; Dr. James h. Cassedy, nlm [MASK] Division)

contraceptiveeffectiveness.name: contraceptive effectiveness
contraceptiveeffectiveness.definition: Contraceptive effectiveness is the rate of success or failure of a method of contraception; contraceptive agents; or contraceptive devices.

growthdifferentiationfactor2.name: growth differentiation factor 2
growthdifferentiationfactor2.definition: Growth differentiation factor 2 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a regulatory role as a paracrine factor for a diverse array of cell types during embryonic development and in the adult tissues. Growth differentiation factor 2 is also a potent regulator of chondrogenesis and was previously referred to as bone morphogenetic protein 9.

myosintypei.name: myosin type i
myosintypei.definition: Myosin type i is a subclass of myosins found generally associated with actin-rich membrane structures such as filopodia. Members of the myosin type i family are ubiquitously expressed in eukaryotes. The heavy chains of myosin type i lack coiled-coil forming sequences in their tails and therefore do not dimerize.

humangenomeproject.name: human genome project
humangenomeproject.definition: Human genome project is a coordinated effort of researchers to map (chromosome mapping) and sequence (sequence analysis, dna) the human genome.

hepaticduct,common.name: hepatic duct , common
hepaticduct,common.definition: Common hepatic duct is predominantly extrahepatic [MASK] which is formed by the junction of the right and left hepatic ducts, which are predominantly intrahepatic, and, in turn, joins the cystic duct to form the common [MASK].

mandibularreconstruction.name: mandibular reconstruction
mandibularreconstruction.definition: Mandibular reconstruction is the physical restoration of oromandibular defects.

face.name: face
face.definition: Face is the anterior portion of the head that includes the skin, muscles, and structures of the forehead, eyes, nose, mouth, cheeks, and jaw.

uterus.name: uterus
uterus.definition: Uterus is the hollow thick-walled muscular organ in the female pelvis. It consists of the fundus which is the site of embryo implantation and fetal development. Beyond the isthmus at the perineal end of fundus, is cervix uteri (the [MASK]) opening into vagina. Beyond the isthmi at the upper abdominal end of fundus, are the fallopian tubes.

rna,chloroplast.name: rna , chloroplast
rna,chloroplast.definition: Chloroplast rna is ribonucleic acid in chloroplasts having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

hipjoint.name: hip joint
hipjoint.definition: Hip joint is the joint that is formed by the articulation of the head of femur and the acetabulum of the pelvis.

skintemperature.name: skin temperature
skintemperature.definition: Skin temperature is the temperature at the outer surface of the body.

socialdominance.name: social dominance
socialdominance.definition: Social dominance is social structure of a group as it relates to the relative social rank of dominance status of its members. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

neuromuscularmonitoring.name: neuromuscular monitoring
neuromuscularmonitoring.definition: Neuromuscular monitoring is the use of peripheral nerve stimulation to assess transmission at the neuromuscular junction, especially in the response to anesthetics, such as the intensity of neuromuscular blockade by [MASK].

chromosomepainting.name: chromosome painting
chromosomepainting.definition: Chromosome painting is a technique for visualizing chromosome aberrations using fluorescently labeled dna probes which are hybridized to chromosomal dna. Multiple fluorochromes may be attached to the probes. Upon hybridization, this produces a multicolored, or painted, effect with a unique [MASK] at each site of hybridization. This technique may also be used to identify cross-species homology by labeling probes from one species for hybridization with chromosomes from another species.

attentiondeficitdisorderwithhyperactivit.name: attention deficit disorder with hyperactivity
attentiondeficitdisorderwithhyperactivit.definition: Attention deficit disorder with hyperactivity is a behavior disorder originating in childhood in which the essential features are signs of developmentally inappropriate inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity. Although most individuals have symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity, one or the other pattern may be predominant. The disorder is more frequent in males than females. Onset is in childhood. Symptoms often attenuate during late   adolescence although a minority experience the full complement of symptoms into mid-adulthood. (From [MASK])

druglabeling.name: drug labeling
druglabeling.definition: Drug labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a drug container or wrapper. It includes contents, indications, effects, dosages, routes, methods, frequency and duration of administration, warnings, hazards, contraindications, side effects, precautions, and other relevant information.

reflex,abnormal.name: reflex , abnormal
reflex,abnormal.definition: Abnormal reflex is an abnormal response to a stimulus applied to the sensory components of the nervous system. This may take the form of increased, decreased, or absent reflexes.

cytochromecgroup.name: cytochrome c group
cytochromecgroup.definition: Cytochrome c group is a group of cytochromes with covalent thioether linkages between either or both of the vinyl side chains of protoheme and the protein. (Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992, p539)

dendriticcells,follicular.name: dendritic cells , follicular
dendriticcells,follicular.definition: Follicular [MASK] is non-hematopoietic cells, with extensive dendritic processes, found in the primary and secondary follicles of lymphoid tissue (the b cell zones). They are different from conventional [MASK] associated with t-cells. They are derived from mesenchymal stem cells and are negative for class ii mhc antigen and do not process or present antigen like the conventional [MASK] do. Instead, follicular [MASK] have fc receptors and c3b receptors that hold antigen in the form of antigen-antibody complexes on their surfaces for long periods for recognition by b-cells.

prolineoxidase.name: proline oxidase
prolineoxidase.definition: Proline oxidase is the first enzyme of the proline degradative pathway. It catalyzes the oxidation of proline to pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid in the presence of oxygen and water. The action is not reversible. The specific activity of proline oxidase increases with age. ec 1.5.3.-.

erythrocyteaggregation.name: erythrocyte aggregation
erythrocyteaggregation.definition: Erythrocyte aggregation is the formation of clumps of red blood cells under low or non-flow conditions, resulting from the attraction forces between the red blood cells. The cells adhere to each other in rouleaux aggregates. Slight mechanical force, such as occurs in the circulation, is enough to disperse these aggregates. Stronger or weaker than normal aggregation may result from a variety of effects in the erythrocyte membrane or in blood plasma. The degree of aggregation is affected by erythrocyte deformability, erythrocyte membrane sialylation, masking of negative surface charge by plasma proteins, etc. blood [MASK] and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate are affected by the amount of erythrocyte aggregation and are parameters used to measure the aggregation.

membranelipids.name: membrane lipids
membranelipids.definition: Membrane lipids is lipids, predominantly [MASK], cholesterol and small amounts of glycolipids found in membranes including cellular and intracellular membranes. These lipids may be arranged in bilayers in the membranes with integral proteins between the layers and peripheral proteins attached to the outside. Membrane lipids are required for active transport, several enzymatic activities and membrane formation.

arminjuries.name: arm injuries
arminjuries.definition: [MASK] injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the [MASK] and the forearm.

catheterization,centralvenous.name: catheterization , central venous
catheterization,centralvenous.definition: Central venous catheterization is placement of an intravenous catheter in the subclavian, jugular, or other central vein.

causality.name: causality
causality.definition: Causality is the relating of causes to the effects they produce. Causes are termed necessary when they must always precede an effect and sufficient when they initiate or produce an effect. Any of several factors may be associated with the potential disease causation or outcome, including predisposing factors, enabling factors, precipitating factors, reinforcing factors, and risk factors.

cadmium.name: cadmium
cadmium.definition: Cadmium is an element with atomic symbol Cd, atomic number 48, and atomic weight 112.41. It is a metal and ingestion will lead to [MASK].

viralhepatitisvaccines.name: viral hepatitis vaccines
viralhepatitisvaccines.definition: Viral hepatitis vaccines is any vaccine raised against any virus or viral derivative that causes hepatitis.

neoplasmseeding.name: neoplasm seeding
neoplasmseeding.definition: Neoplasm seeding is the local implantation of tumor cells by contamination of instruments and surgical equipment during and after surgical resection, resulting in local growth of the cells and tumor formation.

hypertensiveencephalopathy.name: hypertensive encephalopathy
hypertensiveencephalopathy.definition: Hypertensive encephalopathy is brain dysfunction or damage resulting from sustained [MASK]. When blood pressure exceeds the limits of cerebral autoregulation, [MASK] is impaired (brain ischemia). Clinical manifestations include headache; nausea; vomiting; seizures; altered mental status (in some cases progressing to coma); papilledema; and retinal hemorrhage.

fungalvaccines.name: fungal vaccines
fungalvaccines.definition: Fungal vaccines is suspensions of attenuated or killed fungi administered for the prevention or treatment of infectious fungal disease.

receptors,virus.name: receptors , virus
receptors,virus.definition: Virus receptors is specific molecular components of the cell capable of recognizing and interacting with a virus, and which, after binding it, are capable of generating some signal that initiates the chain of events leading to the biological response.

virusattachment.name: virus attachment
virusattachment.definition: Virus attachment is the binding of virus particles to virus receptors on the host cell surface, facilitating virus entry into the cell.

intellectualdisability.name: intellectual disability
intellectualdisability.definition: Intellectual disability is subnormal intellectual functioning which originates during the developmental period. This has multiple potential etiologies, including genetic defects and perinatal insults. Intelligence quotient (iq) scores are commonly used to determine whether an individual has an intellectual disability. iq scores between 70 and 79 are in the borderline range. Scores below 67 are in the disabled range. (from Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1992, Ch55, p28)

ovarianfollicle.name: ovarian follicle
ovarianfollicle.definition: Ovarian follicle is an OOCYTE-containing structure in the cortex of the ovary. The oocyte is enclosed by a layer of granulosa cells providing a nourishing microenvironment (follicular fluid). The number and size of follicles vary depending on the age and reproductive state of the female. The growing follicles are divided into five stages: primary, secondary, tertiary, Graafian, and atretic. Follicular growth and steroidogenesis depend on the presence of gonadotropins.

pregnantwomen.name: pregnant women
pregnantwomen.definition: Pregnant women is human females who are pregnant, as cultural, psychological, or sociological entities.

nationalpractitionerdatabank.name: national practitioner data bank
nationalpractitionerdatabank.definition: National practitioner data bank is a databank established by the Health Care Quality Improvement Act of 1986 authorizing the Department of Health and Human Services to collect and release information on the professional competence and conduct of physicians, dentists, nurses, and other health care practitioners. The data include adverse actions on physicians' malpractice, licensure, hospital privileges, concealing of pertinent information, and the like.

earth,planet.name: earth , planet
earth,planet.definition: Planet earth is planet that is the third in order from the sun. It is one of the four inner or terrestrial planets of the solar system.

pregnancycomplications,hematologic.name: pregnancy complications , hematologic
pregnancycomplications,hematologic.definition: Hematologic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and a blood disease (hematologic diseases) which involves blood cells or coagulation factors. The hematologic disease may precede or follow fertilization and it may or may not have a deleterious effect on the pregnant woman or fetus.

durationoftherapy.name: duration of therapy
durationoftherapy.definition: Duration of therapy is planned or actual duration of various treatments or preventive measures.

evokedpotentials,motor.name: evoked potentials , motor
evokedpotentials,motor.definition: Motor evoked potentials is the electrical response evoked in a muscle or motor nerve by electrical or magnetic stimulation. Common methods of stimulation are by transcranial electrical and transcranial magnetic stimulation. It is often used for monitoring during neurosurgery.

hypothalamichormones.name: hypothalamic hormones
hypothalamichormones.definition: Hypothalamic hormones is peptide hormones produced by neurons of various regions in the hypothalamus. They are released into the pituitary portal circulation to stimulate or inhibit pituitary gland functions. vasopressin and oxytocin, though produced in the hypothalamus, are not included here for they are transported down the axons to the [MASK] before being released into the portal circulation.

histamineagents.name: histamine agents
histamineagents.definition: Histamine agents is drugs used for their actions on histaminergic systems. Included are drugs that act at histamine receptors, affect the [MASK] of histamine, or affect the state of histaminergic cells.

lymphocytes.name: lymphocytes
lymphocytes.definition: Lymphocytes is [MASK] blood cells formed in the body's lymphoid tissue. The nucleus is round or ovoid with coarse, irregularly clumped chromatin while the cytoplasm is typically pale blue with azurophilic (if any) granules. Most lymphocytes can be classified as either t or b (with subpopulations of each), or natural killer cells.

cells,immobilized.name: cells , immobilized
cells,immobilized.definition: Immobilized cells is microbial, plant, or animal cells which are immobilized by attachment to solid structures, usually a column matrix. a common use of immobilized cells is in biotechnology for the bioconversion of a substrate to a particular product. (From Singleton & Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

jointdiseases.name: joint diseases
jointdiseases.definition: Joint diseases is diseases involving the joints.

budgets.name: budgets
budgets.definition: Budgets is detailed financial plans for carrying out specific activities for a certain period of time. They include proposed income and expenditures.

orthodonticfriction.name: orthodontic friction
orthodonticfriction.definition: Orthodontic friction is physical resistance to motion between dental surfaces.

originrecognitioncomplex.name: origin recognition complex
originrecognitioncomplex.definition: Origin recognition complex is the origin recognition complex is a multi-subunit DNA-binding protein that initiates dna replication in eukaryotes.

dnamismatchrepair.name: dna mismatch repair
dnamismatchrepair.definition: Dna mismatch repair is a dna repair pathway involved in correction of errors introduced during dna replication when an incorrect base, which cannot form hydrogen bonds with the corresponding base in the parent strand, is incorporated into the daughter strand. Excinucleases recognize the [MASK] and cause a segment of polynucleotide chain to be excised from the daughter strand, thereby removing the mismatched base. (from Oxford Dictionary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 2001)

prenataldiagnosis.name: prenatal diagnosis
prenataldiagnosis.definition: Prenatal diagnosis is determination of the nature of a pathological condition or disease in the postimplantation embryo; fetus; or pregnant female before birth.

electromagneticradiation.name: electromagnetic radiation
electromagneticradiation.definition: Electromagnetic radiation is waves of oscillating electric and magnetic fields which move at right angles to each other and outward from the source.

biologicalmonitoring.name: biological monitoring
biologicalmonitoring.definition: Biological monitoring is monitoring of the level of toxins, chemical pollutants, microbial contaminants, or other harmful substances in the bodies of living organisms, by diagnostic imaging or by analyzing blood; urine; [MASK]; saliva, etc.

memorydisorders.name: memory disorders
