memorydisorders.definition: Memory disorders is disturbances in registering an impression, in the retention of an acquired impression, or in the recall of an impression. Memory impairments are associated with dementia; craniocerebral trauma; encephalitis; alcoholism (see also alcohol amnestic disorder); schizophrenia; and other conditions.

musculoskeletaldiseases.name: musculoskeletal diseases
musculoskeletaldiseases.definition: Musculoskeletal diseases is diseases of the muscles and their associated ligaments and other connective tissue and of the bones and cartilage viewed collectively.

idiopathicpulmonaryfibrosis.name: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
idiopathicpulmonaryfibrosis.definition: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is a common interstitial lung disease of unknown etiology, usually occurring between 50-70 years of age. Clinically, it is characterized by an insidious onset of breathlessness with exertion and a nonproductive [MASK], leading to progressive dyspnea. Pathological features show scant interstitial inflammation, patchy collagen fibrosis, prominent fibroblast proliferation foci, and microscopic honeycomb change.

schools,dental.name: schools , dental
schools,dental.definition: Dental schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of dentistry.

ovarianreserve.name: ovarian reserve
ovarianreserve.definition: Ovarian reserve is capacity of the ovary to provide viable eggs.

polymers.name: polymers
polymers.definition: Polymers is compounds formed by the joining of smaller, usually repeating, units linked by covalent bonds. These compounds often form large macromolecules (e.g., biopolymers; plastics).

bloodureanitrogen.name: blood urea nitrogen
bloodureanitrogen.definition: Blood urea nitrogen is the urea concentration of the blood stated in terms of nitrogen content. Serum (plasma) urea nitrogen is approximately 12% higher than blood urea nitrogen concentration because of the greater protein content of red blood cells. Increases in blood or serum urea nitrogen are referred to as azotemia and may have prerenal, renal, or postrenal causes. (From Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

asterplant.name: aster plant
asterplant.definition: Aster plant is a plant genus of the family asteraceae. This plant should not be confused with [MASK] asters ([MASK]) nor with aster yellows phytoplasma (mycoplasma-like organisms).

workload.name: workload
workload.definition: Workload is the total amount of work to be performed by an individual, a department, or other group of workers in a period of time.

thoracicarteries.name: thoracic arteries
thoracicarteries.definition: Thoracic arteries is arteries originating from the subclavian or axillary arteries and distributing to the anterior thoracic wall, mediastinal structures, diaphragm, pectoral muscles, mammary gland and the axillary aspect of the chest wall.

myocardialreperfusioninjury.name: myocardial reperfusion injury
myocardialreperfusioninjury.definition: Myocardial reperfusion injury is damage to the myocardium resulting from myocardial reperfusion (restoration of blood flow to ischemic areas of the heart.) Reperfusion takes place when there is spontaneous thrombolysis, thrombolytic therapy, collateral flow from other coronary vascular beds, or reversal of vasospasm.

osteoporosis,postmenopausal.name: osteoporosis , postmenopausal
osteoporosis,postmenopausal.definition: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is metabolic disorder associated with fractures of the femoral [MASK], vertebrae, and distal forearm. It occurs commonly in women within 15-20 years after menopause, and is caused by factors associated with menopause including estrogen deficiency.

latenttuberculosis.name: latent tuberculosis
latenttuberculosis.definition: Latent tuberculosis is the dormant form of tuberculosis where the person shows no obvious symptoms and no sign of the causative agent ([MASK]) in the sputum despite being positive for tuberculosis infection skin test.

drugresistantepilepsy.name: drug resistant epilepsy
drugresistantepilepsy.definition: Drug resistant epilepsy is epileptic condition in which adequate trials of two tolerated and appropriately chosen and used antiepileptic drugs schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom failed.

confusion.name: confusion
confusion.definition: Confusion is a mental state characterized by bewilderment, emotional disturbance, lack of clear thinking, and perceptual disorientation.

cytoskeletalproteins.name: cytoskeletal proteins
cytoskeletalproteins.definition: Cytoskeletal proteins is major constituent of the cytoskeleton found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. They form a flexible framework for the cell, provide attachment points for organelles and formed bodies, and make communication between parts of the cell possible.

portugal.name: portugal
portugal.definition: Portugal is a country in southwestern Europe, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, west of [MASK]. The capital is Lisbon.

habits.name: habits
habits.definition: Habits is acquired or learned responses which are regularly manifested.

drugapproval.name: drug approval
drugapproval.definition: Drug approval is process that is gone through in order for a drug to receive approval by a government regulatory agency. This includes any required pre-clinical or clinical testing, review, submission, and evaluation of the applications and test results, and post-marketing surveillance of the drug.

powerplants.name: power plants
powerplants.definition: Power plants is units that convert some other form of energy into electrical energy.

anklefractures.name: ankle fractures
anklefractures.definition: Ankle fractures is fractures of any of the bones of the ankle.

musculoskeletalabnormalities.name: musculoskeletal abnormalities
musculoskeletalabnormalities.definition: Musculoskeletal abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities and deformities of the musculoskeletal system.

cytokinereleasesyndrome.name: cytokine release syndrome
cytokinereleasesyndrome.definition: Cytokine release syndrome is a severe immune reaction characterized by excessive release of cytokines. Symptoms include dyspnea; fever; headache; hypotension; nausea; rash; tachycardia; hypoxia; hyperferritinemia, and [MASK]. It is associated with viral infections, sepsis, autoimmune diseases and a variety of factors used in immunotherapy.

caspase2.name: caspase 2
caspase2.definition: Caspase 2 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a caspase recruitment domain in its pro-domain region. Activation of this enzyme can occur via the interaction of its caspase recruitment domain with card signaling adaptor proteins. Caspase 2 plays a role in apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector pro-caspases. Several isoforms of this protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its messenger rna.

refractoryperiod,psychological.name: refractory period , psychological
refractoryperiod,psychological.definition: Psychological refractory period is a delayed response interval occurring when two stimuli are presented in close succession.

socialmedia.name: social media
socialmedia.definition: Social media is platforms that provide the ability and tools to create and publish information accessed via the internet. Generally these platforms have three characteristics with content user generated, high degree of interaction between creator and viewer, and easily integrated with other sites.

extracellularmatrixproteins.name: extracellular matrix proteins
extracellularmatrixproteins.definition: Extracellular matrix proteins is macromolecular organic compounds that contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and usually, sulfur. These macromolecules (proteins) form an intricate meshwork in which cells are embedded to construct tissues. Variations in the relative types of macromolecules and their organization determine the type of extracellular matrix, each adapted to the functional requirements of the tissue. The two main classes of macromolecules that form the extracellular matrix are: glycosaminoglycans, usually linked to proteins (proteoglycans), and fibrous proteins (e.g., collagen; elastin; fibronectins; and laminin).

education,nursing,associate.name: education , nursing , associate
education,nursing,associate.definition: Associate nursing education is a two-year program in nursing education in a community or junior college leading to an a.d. (Associate Degree). Graduates of this program are eligible for state examination for licensure as rn (Registered Nurse).

heartseptaldefects,atrial.name: heart septal defects , atrial
heartseptaldefects,atrial.definition: Atrial heart septal defects is developmental abnormalities in any portion of the atrial septum resulting in abnormal communications between the two upper chambers of the heart. Classification of atrial septal defects is based on location of the communication and types of incomplete fusion of atrial septa with the endocardial cushions in the fetal heart. They include ostium primum, ostium secundum, sinus venosus, and coronary sinus defects.

vectorbornediseases.name: vector borne diseases
vectorbornediseases.definition: Vector borne diseases is infectious diseases transmitted by disease vectors.

electromagneticfields.name: electromagnetic fields
electromagneticfields.definition: Electromagnetic fields is fields representing the joint interplay of electric and magnetic forces.

dnaprimers.name: dna primers
dnaprimers.definition: Dna primers is short sequences (generally about 10 [MASK]) of dna that are complementary to sequences of messenger rna and allow reverse transcriptases to start copying the adjacent sequences of mRNA. Primers are used extensively in genetic and molecular biology techniques.

woolfiber.name: wool fiber
woolfiber.definition: Wool fiber is filament, thread, or yarn produced from wool.

healthservices.name: health services
healthservices.definition: Health services is services for the diagnosis and treatment of disease and the maintenance of health.

feces.name: feces
feces.definition: Feces is excrement from the intestines, containing unabsorbed solids, waste products, secretions, and bacteria of the digestive system.

flour.name: flour
flour.definition: Flour is ground up [MASK] of wheat.

missouri.name: missouri
missouri.definition: Missouri is state bounded on the east by Illinois and Kentucky, on the south by Arkansas, on the west by Kansas, and on the north by Iowa.

southaustralia.name: south australia
southaustralia.definition: South australia is a state in south central Australia. Its capital is Adelaide. It was probably first visited by f. Thyssen in 1627. Later discoveries in 1802 and 1830 opened up the southern part. It became a British province in 1836 with this self-descriptive name and became a state in 1901. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1135)

electronichealthrecords.name: electronic health records
electronichealthrecords.definition: Electronic health records is media that facilitate transportability of pertinent information concerning patient's illness across varied providers and geographic locations. Some versions include direct linkages to online consumer health information that is relevant to the health conditions and treatments related to a specific patient.

sleeparousaldisorders.name: sleep arousal disorders
sleeparousaldisorders.definition: Sleep arousal disorders is sleep disorders characterized by impaired arousal from the deeper stages of sleep (generally stage iii or iv sleep).

steroids.name: steroids
steroids.definition: Steroids is a group of polycyclic compounds closely related biochemically to terpenes. They include cholesterol, numerous hormones, precursors of certain vitamins, [MASK] acids, alcohols (sterols), and certain natural drugs and poisons. Steroids have a common nucleus, a fused, reduced 17-carbon atom ring system, cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene. Most steroids also have two methyl groups and an aliphatic side-chain attached to the nucleus. (From Hawley's Condensed Chemical Dictionary, 11th ed)

reviewliteratureastopic.name: review literature as topic
reviewliteratureastopic.definition: Review literature as topic is works about published materials which provide an examination of recent or current literature. These articles can cover a wide range of subject matter at various levels of completeness and comprehensiveness based on analyses of literature that may include research findings. The review may reflect the state of the art and may also include reviews as a literary form.

transferfactor.name: transfer factor
transferfactor.definition: Transfer factor is factor derived from leukocyte lysates of immune donors which can transfer both local and systemic cellular immunity to nonimmune recipients.

nucleicacidsynthesisinhibitors.name: nucleic acid synthesis inhibitors
nucleicacidsynthesisinhibitors.definition: Nucleic acid synthesis inhibitors is compounds that inhibit cell production of dna or rna.

plantcomponents,aerial.name: plant components , aerial
plantcomponents,aerial.definition: Aerial plant components is the above-ground plant without the roots.

caseinkinases.name: casein kinases
caseinkinases.definition: Casein kinases is a group of protein-serine-threonine kinases that was originally identified as being responsible for the phosphorylation of caseins. They are ubiquitous enzymes that have a preference for acidic proteins. Casein kinases play a role in signal transduction by phosphorylating a variety of regulatory cytoplasmic and regulatory nuclear proteins.

snowsports.name: snow sports
snowsports.definition: [MASK] sports is sports activities in the [MASK].

asymmetriccelldivision.name: asymmetric cell division
asymmetriccelldivision.definition: Asymmetric cell division is unequal cell division that results in daughter cells of different sizes.

darkadaptation.name: dark adaptation
darkadaptation.definition: Dark adaptation is [MASK] of the eyes under conditions of low light. The sensitivity of the eye to light is increased during dark adaptation.

epinephrine.name: epinephrine
epinephrine.definition: Epinephrine is the active sympathomimetic hormone from the adrenal medulla. It stimulates both the alpha- and beta- adrenergic systems, causes systemic vasoconstriction and gastrointestinal relaxation, stimulates the heart, and dilates bronchi and cerebral vessels. It is used in asthma and cardiac failure and to delay absorption of local anesthetics.

centralnervoussystemviraldiseases.name: central nervous system viral diseases
centralnervoussystemviraldiseases.definition: Central nervous system viral diseases is viral infections of the brain, spinal cord, meninges, or perimeningeal spaces.

femurheadnecrosis.name: femur head necrosis
femurheadnecrosis.definition: Femur head necrosis is aseptic or avascular necrosis of the femoral head. The major types are idiopathic (primary), as a complication of fractures or dislocations, and legg-calve-perthes disease.

safesex.name: safe sex
safesex.definition: Safe [MASK] is sexual behavior that prevents or reduces the spread of sexually transmitted diseases or pregnancy.

cellenlargement.name: cell enlargement
cellenlargement.definition: Cell enlargement is growth processes that result in an increase in cell size.

sportsequipment.name: sports equipment
sportsequipment.definition: Sports equipment is equipment required for engaging in a sport (such as balls, bats, rackets, skis, skates, ropes, weights) and devices for the protection of [MASK] during their performance (such as masks, gloves, mouth pieces).

consumerhealthinformation.name: consumer health information
consumerhealthinformation.definition: Consumer health information is information intended for potential users of medical and healthcare services. There is an emphasis on self-care and preventive approaches as well as information for community-wide dissemination and use.

auditoryperceptualdisorders.name: auditory perceptual disorders
auditoryperceptualdisorders.definition: Auditory perceptual disorders is acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of auditory perception characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact [MASK]. Affected individuals have difficulty with [MASK] perception, [MASK], and comprehending the meaning of inflections of [MASK].

nigeria.name: nigeria
nigeria.definition: Nigeria is a republic in western Africa, south of [MASK] between benin and cameroon. Its capital is Abuja.

dentalassistants.name: dental assistants
dentalassistants.definition: Dental assistants is individuals who assist the dentist or the dental hygienist.

murinehepatitisvirus.name: murine hepatitis virus
murinehepatitisvirus.definition: Murine hepatitis virus is a species of the coronavirus genus causing hepatitis in mice. Four strains have been identified as mhv 1, mhv 2, mhv 3, and mhv 4 (also known as mhv-jhm, which is neurotropic and causes disseminated encephalomyelitis with demyelination as well as focal liver necrosis).

clostridiuminfections.name: clostridium infections
clostridiuminfections.definition: Clostridium infections is infections with bacteria of the genus clostridium and closely related clostridioides species.

occupationalactivity.name: occupational activity
occupationalactivity.definition: Occupational activity is skilled treatment that helps individuals achieve independence in all facets of their lives. It assists in the development of skills needed for [MASK].

spinalneoplasms.name: spinal neoplasms
spinalneoplasms.definition: Spinal neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the spine.

eggs.name: eggs
eggs.definition: Eggs is animal reproductive bodies, or the contents thereof, used as food. The concept is differentiated from ovum, the anatomic or physiologic entity.

complementfactord.name: complement factor d
complementfactord.definition: Complement factor d is a serum protein which is important in the alternative complement activation pathway. This enzyme cleaves the complement C3B-bound complement factor b to form C3bBb which is alternative pathway c3 convertase.

denguevirus.name: dengue virus
denguevirus.definition: Dengue virus is a species of the genus flavivirus which causes an acute febrile and sometimes hemorrhagic disease in man. Dengue is mosquito-borne and four serotypes are known.

traceelements.name: trace elements
traceelements.definition: Trace elements is a group of chemical elements that are needed in minute quantities for the proper growth, development, and physiology of an organism. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

bonemarrowdiseases.name: bone marrow diseases
bonemarrowdiseases.definition: Bone marrow diseases is diseases involving the bone marrow.

drugimplants.name: drug implants
drugimplants.definition: Drug implants is small containers or pellets of a solid drug implanted in the body to achieve sustained release of the drug.

focusgroups.name: focus groups
focusgroups.definition: Focus groups is a method of data collection and a qualitative research tool in which a small group of individuals are brought together and allowed to interact in a discussion of their opinions about topics, issues, or questions.

skin,artificial.name: skin , artificial
skin,artificial.definition: Artificial skin is synthetic material used for the treatment of burns and other conditions involving large-scale loss of skin. It often consists of an outer (epidermal) layer of silicone and an inner (dermal) layer of collagen and chondroitin 6-sulfate. The dermal layer elicits new growth and vascular invasion and the outer layer is later removed and replaced by a [MASK].

laboratoryinfection.name: laboratory infection
laboratoryinfection.definition: Laboratory infection is accidentally acquired infection in laboratory workers.

hepatitisa.name: hepatitis a
hepatitisa.definition: Hepatitis a is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by a member of the hepatovirus genus, human hepatitis a virus. It can be transmitted through fecal contamination of food or water.

reinforcement,social.name: reinforcement , social
reinforcement,social.definition: Social reinforcement is the strengthening of a response with a social reward such as a nod of approval, a parent's love or attention.

healthcareeconomicsandorganizations.name: health care economics and organizations
healthcareeconomicsandorganizations.definition: Health care economics and organizations is the economic aspects of health care, its planning, and delivery. It includes government agencies and organizations in the private sector.

endoscopicmucosalresection.name: endoscopic mucosal resection
endoscopicmucosalresection.definition: Endoscopic mucosal resection is a method for removing lesions from gastrointestinal mucous membranes. The mucosal  tissue with the lesion is elevated by injecting a solution into the submucosal layer underneath it. The elevated tissue with the lesion is then cut out.

fracturefixation.name: fracture fixation
fracturefixation.definition: Fracture fixation is the use of metallic devices inserted into or through bone to hold a fracture in a [MASK] position and alignment while it heals.

facialnerve.name: facial nerve
facialnerve.definition: Facial nerve is the 7th cranial nerve. The facial nerve has two parts, the larger motor root which may be called the facial nerve proper, and the smaller intermediate or sensory root. Together they provide efferent innervation to the muscles of facial expression and to the lacrimal and salivary glands, and convey afferent information for taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and for touch from the external ear.

bloodtransfusion,intrauterine.name: blood transfusion , intrauterine
bloodtransfusion,intrauterine.definition: Intrauterine blood transfusion is in utero transfusion of blood into the fetus for the treatment of fetal diseases, such as fetal erythroblastosis (erythroblastosis, fetal).

carcinoma,neuroendocrine.name: carcinoma , neuroendocrine
carcinoma,neuroendocrine.definition: Neuroendocrine carcinoma is a group of carcinomas which share a characteristic morphology, often being composed of clusters and trabecular sheets of round "blue cells", granular chromatin, and an attenuated rim of poorly demarcated cytoplasm. Neuroendocrine tumors include carcinoids, small ("oat") cell carcinomas, medullary carcinoma of the thyroid, Merkel cell tumor, cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma, [MASK], and pheochromocytoma. Neurosecretory granules are found within the tumor cells. (Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

tonguediseases.name: tongue diseases
tonguediseases.definition: Tongue diseases is diseases involving the tongue.

epitopes.name: epitopes
epitopes.definition: Epitopes is sites on an antigen that interact with specific antibodies.

greatlakesregion.name: great lakes region
greatlakesregion.definition: Great [MASK] region is the geographic area of the Great [MASK] in general and when the specific state or states are not indicated. It usually includes Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, [MASK], New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin.

islam.name: islam
islam.definition: Islam is a monotheistic religion promulgated by the Prophet Mohammed with Allah as the deity.

virginia.name: virginia
virginia.definition: Virginia is state bounded on the north by Maryland and West Virginia, on the east by the Atlantic Ocean, the Chesapeake Bay and Maryland, and on the south by North Carolina and Tennessee, and on the west by Kentucky and West Virginia.

cannabis.name: cannabis
cannabis.definition: Cannabis is the plant genus in the Cannabaceae plant family, Urticales order, Hamamelidae subclass. The flowering tops are called many slang terms including pot, marijuana, hashish, bhang, and ganja. The stem is an important source of hemp fiber.

ventriculardysfunction,left.name: ventricular dysfunction , left
ventriculardysfunction,left.definition: Left ventricular dysfunction is a condition in which the left ventricle of the heart was functionally impaired. This condition usually leads to heart failure; myocardial infarction; and other cardiovascular complications. Diagnosis is made by measuring the diminished ejection fraction and a depressed level of motility of the left ventricular wall.

lensimplantation,intraocular.name: lens implantation , intraocular
lensimplantation,intraocular.definition: Intraocular lens implantation is insertion of an artificial lens to replace the natural crystalline lens after [MASK] extraction or to supplement the natural lens which is left in place.

integrativeoncology.name: integrative oncology
integrativeoncology.definition: Integrative oncology is these evidence-based therapies to reduce symptoms associated with treatment of cancer.

spectrumanalysis.name: spectrum analysis
spectrumanalysis.definition: Spectrum analysis is the measurement of the amplitude of the components of a complex waveform throughout the frequency range of the waveform. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

history.name: history
history.definition: History is record and study of past events.

laterallinesystem.name: lateral line system
laterallinesystem.definition: Lateral line system is aquatic vertebrate sensory system in fish and amphibians. It is composed of sense organs (canal organs and pit organs) containing neuromasts (mechanoreceptors) that detect water displacement caused by moving objects.

finland.name: finland
finland.definition: Finland is a country in northern Europe, bordering the Baltic Sea, Gulf of Bothnia, and Gulf of Finland, between Sweden and Russia. The capital is Helsinki.

sodiumcitrate.name: sodium citrate
sodiumcitrate.definition: Sodium citrate is sodium [MASK] of citric acid that are used as [MASK] and food preservatives. They are used medically as anticoagulants in stored blood, and for urine alkalization in the prevention of kidney stones.

tablets.name: tablets
tablets.definition: Tablets is solid dosage forms, of varying weight, size, and shape, which may be molded or compressed, and which contain a medicinal substance in pure or diluted form. (Dorland, 28th ed)

hemorrhage.name: hemorrhage
hemorrhage.definition: Hemorrhage is bleeding or escape of blood from a vessel.

betarhythm.name: beta rhythm
betarhythm.definition: Beta rhythm is brain waves with frequency between 15-30 Hz seen on eeg during wakefulness and mental activity.

coal.name: coal
coal.definition: Coal is a natural fuel formed by partial decomposition of vegetable matter under certain environmental conditions.

insectproteins.name: insect proteins
insectproteins.definition: Insect proteins is proteins found in any species of insect.

drugevaluation.name: drug evaluation
drugevaluation.definition: Drug evaluation is any process by which toxicity, metabolism, absorption, elimination, preferred route of administration, safe dosage range, etc., for a drug or group of drugs is determined through clinical assessment in humans or veterinary animals.

randomamplifiedpolymorphicdnatechnique.name: random amplified polymorphic dna technique
randomamplifiedpolymorphicdnatechnique.definition: Random amplified polymorphic dna technique is technique that utilizes low-stringency polymerase chain reaction (pcr) amplification with single primers of arbitrary sequence to generate strain-specific arrays of anonymous dna fragments. rapd technique may be used to determine taxonomic identity, assess kinship relationships, analyze mixed genome samples, and create specific probes.

ganglia.name: ganglia
ganglia.definition: Ganglia is clusters of multipolar neurons surrounded by a capsule of loosely organized connective tissue located outside the central nervous system.

pathology,molecular.name: pathology , molecular
pathology,molecular.definition: Molecular pathology is a subspecialty of pathology concerned with the molecular basis (e.g., mutations) of various diseases.

xchromosome.name: x chromosome
xchromosome.definition: X chromosome is the female [MASK] chromosome, being the differential [MASK] chromosome carried by half the male gametes and all female gametes in human and other male-heterogametic species.

abdominalneoplasms.name: abdominal neoplasms
abdominalneoplasms.definition: Abdominal neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the abdomen.

catheterobstruction.name: catheter obstruction
catheterobstruction.definition: Catheter obstruction is a hindrance to the passage of fluids through a catheter.

sexcounseling.name: sex counseling
sexcounseling.definition: [MASK] counseling is advice and support given to individuals to help them understand and resolve their sexual [MASK] problems. It excludes treatment for psychosexual disorders or psychosexual dysfunction.

vascularstiffness.name: vascular stiffness
vascularstiffness.definition: Vascular stiffness is loss of vascular elasticity due to factors such as aging; and arteriosclerosis. Increased arterial stiffness is one of the risk factors for many cardiovascular diseases.

kidneytubules,proximal.name: kidney tubules , proximal
kidneytubules,proximal.definition: Proximal kidney tubules is the renal tubule portion that extends from the bowman capsule in the kidney cortex into the [MASK]. The proximal tubule consists of a convoluted proximal segment in the cortex, and a distal straight segment descending into the medulla where it forms the U-shaped loop of henle.

nonlinearopticalmicroscopy.name: nonlinear optical microscopy
nonlinearopticalmicroscopy.definition: Nonlinear optical microscopy is microscopic imaging techniques that utilize nonlinear responses of light-matter interactions which occur with high-intensity [MASK], such as from lasers, and specialized light signal detection instrumentation to produce images without the need for dyes or fluorescent labels.

smokeinhalationinjury.name: smoke inhalation injury
smokeinhalationinjury.definition: Smoke [MASK] injury is pulmonary injury following the breathing in of toxic smoke from burning materials such as plastics, synthetics, building materials, etc. This injury is the most frequent [MASK] in burn patients.

culturedmilkproducts.name: cultured milk products
culturedmilkproducts.definition: Cultured milk products is derivatives of milk that are produced by controlled fermentation.

opioidepidemic.name: opioid epidemic
opioidepidemic.definition: Opioid epidemic is widespread use of opioids by disproportionately large numbers of individuals within a population, community, or region occurring within a relatively narrow window of time.

ethicalreview.name: ethical review
ethicalreview.definition: Ethical review is a formal process of examination of patient care or research proposals for conformity with ethical standards. The review is usually conducted by an organized clinical or research ethics committee (clinical ethics committees or research ethics committees), sometimes by a subset of such a committee, an ad hoc group, or an individual ethicist (ethicists).

spermcount.name: sperm count
spermcount.definition: Sperm count is a count of sperm in the ejaculum, expressed as number per milliliter.

hypothalamus,anterior.name: hypothalamus , anterior
hypothalamus,anterior.definition: Anterior hypothalamus is the front portion of the hypothalamus separated into the preoptic region and the supraoptic region. The preoptic region is made up of the periventricular gray matter of the rostral portion of the third ventricle and contains the preoptic ventricular nucleus and the medial preoptic nucleus. The supraoptic region contains the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus, the supraoptic nucleus, the anterior hypothalamic nucleus, and the suprachiasmatic nucleus.

rootcanalpreparation.name: root canal preparation
rootcanalpreparation.definition: Root canal preparation is preparatory activities in root canal therapy by partial or complete extirpation of diseased pulp, cleaning and sterilization of the empty canal, enlarging and shaping the canal to receive the sealing material. The cavity may be prepared by mechanical, sonic, chemical, or other means. (From Dorland, 28th ed, p1700)

collagentypevi.name: collagen type vi
collagentypevi.definition: Collagen type vi is a non-fibrillar collagen that forms a network of microfibrils within the extracellular matrix of connective tissue. The alpha subunits of collagen type vi assemble into antiparallel, overlapping dimers which then align to form tetramers.

shawpotassiumchannels.name: shaw potassium channels
shawpotassiumchannels.definition: Shaw potassium channels is a shaker subfamily that is prominently expressed in neurons and are necessary for high-frequency, repetitive firing of action potentials.

nadphoxidase5.name: nadph oxidase 5
nadphoxidase5.definition: Nadph oxidase 5 is an nadph oxidase that contains four ef hands and is expressed primarily by spermatocytes and lymphocytes, as well as by endothelial cells. It functions as a calcium-dependent proton channel to generate superoxides that regulate cell growth, apoptosis; and physiologic angiogenesis.

dentalimplantation.name: dental implantation
dentalimplantation.definition: Dental implantation is the grafting or inserting of a prosthetic device of alloplastic material into the oral tissue beneath the mucosal or periosteal layer or within the bone. Its purpose is to provide support and retention to a partial or complete denture.

petroleum.name: petroleum
petroleum.definition: Petroleum is naturally occurring complex liquid hydrocarbons which, after distillation, yield combustible fuels, petrochemicals, and lubricants.

creatinekinase,mbform.name: creatine kinase , mb form
creatinekinase,mbform.definition: Mb form creatine kinase is an isoenzyme of creatine kinase found in the cardiac muscle.

perioperativeperiod.name: perioperative period
perioperativeperiod.definition: Perioperative period is the time periods immediately before, during and following a surgical operation.

deeplearning.name: deep learning
deeplearning.definition: Deep learning is supervised or unsupervised machine learning methods that use multiple layers of data representations generated by nonlinear transformations, instead of individual task-specific algorithms, to build and train neural network models.

cornellmedicalindex.name: cornell medical index
cornellmedicalindex.definition: Cornell medical index is self-administered health questionnaire developed to obtain details of the medical history as an adjunct to the medical interview. It consists of 195 questions divided into eighteen sections; the first twelve deal with somatic complaints and the last six with mood and feeling patterns. The Index is used also as a personality inventory or in epidemiologic studies.

brainneoplasms.name: brain neoplasms
brainneoplasms.definition: Brain neoplasms is neoplasms of the intracranial components of the central nervous system, including the cerebral hemispheres, basal ganglia, hypothalamus, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum. Brain neoplasms are subdivided into primary (originating from brain tissue) and secondary (i.e., metastatic) forms. Primary neoplasms are subdivided into benign and malignant forms. In general, brain tumors may also be classified by age of onset, histologic type, or presenting location in the brain.

neoplasms,bonetissue.name: neoplasms , bone tissue
neoplasms,bonetissue.definition: Bone tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of bony tissue, whether normal or of a soft tissue which has become ossified. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in bones.

cardiovascularsystem.name: cardiovascular system
cardiovascularsystem.definition: Cardiovascular system is the heart and the blood vessels by which blood is pumped and circulated through the body.

growthplate.name: growth plate
growthplate.definition: Growth plate is the area between the epiphysis and the diaphysis within which bone growth occurs.

autoimmunity.name: autoimmunity
autoimmunity.definition: Autoimmunity is process whereby the immune system reacts against the body's own tissues. Autoimmunity may produce or be caused by autoimmune diseases.

religiousmissions.name: religious missions
religiousmissions.definition: Religious missions is programs or projects established by religious groups or institution to support and provide missionary activities, including sharing faith or providing educational, medical, or other assistance.

ovalwindow,ear.name: oval window , ear
ovalwindow,ear.definition: Ear oval window is fenestra or oval opening on the lateral wall of the vestibular [MASK] adjacent to the [MASK]. It is located above the cochlear round window and normally covered by the base of the stapes.

neuromuscularjunction.name: neuromuscular junction
neuromuscularjunction.definition: Neuromuscular junction is the synapse between a neuron and a muscle.

myocardialischemia.name: myocardial ischemia
myocardialischemia.definition: Myocardial ischemia is a disorder of cardiac function caused by insufficient blood flow to the muscle tissue of the heart. The decreased blood flow may be due to narrowing of the coronary arteries (coronary artery disease), to obstruction by a thrombus (coronary thrombosis), or less commonly, to diffuse narrowing of arterioles and other small vessels within the heart. Severe interruption of the blood supply to the myocardial tissue may result in necrosis of cardiac muscle (myocardial infarction).

academicperformance.name: academic performance
academicperformance.definition: Academic performance is a quantitative or qualitative measure of intellectual, scholarly, or scholastic accomplishment.

aldehydeoxidase.name: aldehyde oxidase
aldehydeoxidase.definition: Aldehyde oxidase is an aldehyde oxidoreductase expressed predominantly in the liver; lungs; and kidney. It catalyzes the oxidation of a variety of organic aldehydes and N-heterocyclic compounds to carboxylic acids, and also oxidizes quinoline and pyridine derivatives. The enzyme utilizes molybdenum cofactor and fad as cofactors.

radiationgenetics.name: radiation genetics
radiationgenetics.definition: Radiation genetics is a subdiscipline of genetics that studies radiation effects on the components and processes of biological inheritance.

culturaldiversity.name: cultural diversity
culturaldiversity.definition: Cultural diversity is coexistence of numerous distinct ethnic, racial, religious, or cultural groups within one social unit, organization, or population. (From American Heritage Dictionary, 2d college ed., 1982, p955)

attitudetohealth.name: attitude to health
attitudetohealth.definition: Attitude to health is public attitudes toward health, disease, and the medical care system.

staphylococcusaureus.name: staphylococcus aureus
staphylococcusaureus.definition: Staphylococcus aureus is potentially pathogenic bacteria found in nasal membranes, skin, hair follicles, and perineum of warm-blooded animals. They may cause a wide range of infections and intoxications.

deliveryofhealthcare.name: delivery of health care
deliveryofhealthcare.definition: Delivery of health care is the concept concerned with all aspects of providing and distributing health services to a patient population.

movement.name: movement
movement.definition: Movement is the act, process, or result of passing from one place or position to another. It differs from locomotion in that locomotion is restricted to the passing of the whole body from one place to another, while movement encompasses both locomotion but also a change of the position of the whole body or any of its parts. Movement may be used with reference to humans, vertebrate and invertebrate animals, and microorganisms. Differentiate also from motor activity, movement associated with behavior.

personalhealthservices.name: personal health services
personalhealthservices.definition: Personal health services is health care provided to individuals.

conservedsequence.name: conserved sequence
conservedsequence.definition: Conserved sequence is a sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide or of nucleotides in dna or rna that is similar across multiple species. a known [MASK] of conserved sequences is represented by a [MASK] sequence. amino acid motifs are often composed of conserved sequences.

lungneoplasms.name: lung neoplasms
lungneoplasms.definition: Lung neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the lung.

heavyionradiotherapy.name: heavy ion radiotherapy
heavyionradiotherapy.definition: Heavy ion radiotherapy is the use of a heavy ion particle beam for radiotherapy, such as the heavy ions of carbon.

multipleendocrineneoplasia.name: multiple endocrine neoplasia
multipleendocrineneoplasia.definition: Multiple endocrine neoplasia is a group of autosomal dominant diseases characterized by the combined occurrence of tumors involving two or more endocrine glands that secrete peptide hormones or amines. These neoplasias are often benign but can be malignant. They are classified by the endocrine glands involved and the degree of aggressiveness. The two major forms are [MASK] and men2 with gene mutations on chromosome 11 and chromosome 10, respectively.

periodical.name: periodical
periodical.definition: Periodical is publication intended to be issued on an ongoing basis, generally more frequently than annually, containing separate articles, stories, or writings.

schizophrenia,childhood.name: schizophrenia , childhood
schizophrenia,childhood.definition: Childhood schizophrenia is an obsolete concept, historically used for childhood mental disorders thought to be a form of schizophrenia. It was in earlier versions of dsm but is now included within the broad concept of pervasive development disorders.

culturallycompetentcare.name: culturally competent care
culturallycompetentcare.definition: Culturally competent care is health care services that are respectful of and responsive to the health beliefs, practices and cultural and linguistic needs of diverse patients. The provider and the patient each bring their individual learned patterns of language and culture to the health care experience which must be transcended to achieve equal access and quality health care.

childhealthservices.name: child health services
childhealthservices.definition: Child health services is organized services to provide health care for children.

randomizedcontrolledtrial,veterinary.name: randomized controlled trial , veterinary
randomizedcontrolledtrial,veterinary.definition: Veterinary randomized controlled trial is a work that reports on a clinical trial with animal subjects that involves at least one test treatment and one control treatment, concurrent enrollment and follow-up of the test- and control-treated groups, and in which the treatments to be administered are selected by a random process, such as the use of a random-numbers [MASK].

eyediseases.name: eye diseases
eyediseases.definition: Eye diseases is diseases affecting the eye.

planets.name: planets
planets.definition: Planets is celestial bodies orbiting around the sun or other stars.

medicalrecordsdepartment,hospital.name: medical records department , hospital
medicalrecordsdepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital medical records department is hospital department responsible for the creating, care, storage and retrieval of medical records. It also provides statistical information for the medical and administrative staff.

carotidstenosis.name: carotid stenosis
carotidstenosis.definition: Carotid stenosis is narrowing or stricture of any part of the carotid arteries, most often due to [MASK] formation. Ulcerations may form in [MASK] and induce thrombus formation. Platelet or cholesterol emboli may arise from stenotic carotid lesions and induce a transient ischemic attack; cerebrovascular accident; or temporary blindness (amaurosis fugax). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp 822-3)

skeletalmuscleventricle.name: skeletal muscle ventricle
skeletalmuscleventricle.definition: Skeletal muscle ventricle is autologous skeletal muscle that is wrapped around the heart and electrically stimulated in order to provide mechanical heart assistance. The [MASK] muscle is commonly used to form this ventricle that functions to independently augment cardiac performance by pumping in series with the heart.

personalautonomy.name: personal autonomy
personalautonomy.definition: Personal autonomy is self-directing freedom and especially moral independence. An ethical principle holds that the autonomy of persons ought to be respected. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

proteinunfolding.name: protein unfolding
proteinunfolding.definition: Protein unfolding is conformational transitions of the shape of a protein to various unfolded states.

signlanguage.name: sign language
signlanguage.definition: Sign language is a system of hand gestures used for communication by the deaf or by people speaking different languages.

religiouspersonnel.name: religious personnel
religiouspersonnel.definition: Religious personnel is persons that live and work according to a religious vocation, or calling, to a consecrated or ordained life.

insurance,liability.name: insurance , liability
insurance,liability.definition: Liability insurance is insurance against loss resulting from liability for injury or damage to the persons or property of others.

interruptedtimeseriesanalysis.name: interrupted time series analysis
interruptedtimeseriesanalysis.definition: Interrupted time series analysis is a study that uses observations at multiple time points before and after an intervention (the "interruption"), in an attempt to detect whether the intervention has had an effect significantly greater than any underlying trend over time.

fractures,bone.name: fractures , bone
fractures,bone.definition: Bone fractures is breaks in bones.

hepaticencephalopathy.name: hepatic encephalopathy
hepaticencephalopathy.definition: Hepatic encephalopathy is a syndrome characterized by central nervous system dysfunction in association with liver failure, including portal-systemic shunts. Clinical features include lethargy and confusion (frequently progressing to coma); asterixis; nystagmus, pathologic; brisk oculovestibular reflexes; decorticate and decerebrate posturing; muscle spasticity; and bilateral extensor plantar reflexes (see reflex, babinski). electroencephalography may demonstrate triphasic waves. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1117-20; Plum & Posner, Diagnosis of Stupor and Coma, 3rd ed, p222-5)

plantbark.name: plant bark
plantbark.definition: Plant bark is the outer layer of the woody parts of plants.

hydrolysis.name: hydrolysis
hydrolysis.definition: Hydrolysis is the process of cleaving a chemical compound by the addition of a molecule of water.

russia.name: russia
russia.definition: Russia is a country located in north Asia bordering the Arctic Ocean, extending from Europe (the portion west of the Urals) to the North Pacific Ocean. The capital is [MASK].

cathoderaytube.name: cathode ray tube
cathoderaytube.definition: Cathode ray tube is a vacuum tube equipped with an [MASK] emitting cathode and a fluorescent screen which emits visible light when excited by the cathode ray. Cathode ray tubes are used as imaging devises for televisions; computer terminals; text telecommunication devices; oscilloscopes; and other data display devices.

grapeseedextract.name: grape seed extract
grapeseedextract.definition: Grape [MASK] extract is exudate from [MASK] of the grape plant Vitis vinifera, composed of oils and secondary plant metabolites (bioflavonoids and polyphenols) credited with important medicinal properties.

fattyacids.name: fatty acids
fattyacids.definition: Fatty acids is organic, monobasic acids derived from hydrocarbons by the equivalent of oxidation of a methyl group to an alcohol, aldehyde, and then acid. Fatty acids are saturated and unsaturated (fatty acids, unsaturated). (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

coronarycirculation.name: coronary circulation
coronarycirculation.definition: Coronary circulation is the circulation of blood through the coronary vessels of the heart.

bloodspecimencollection.name: blood specimen collection
bloodspecimencollection.definition: Blood specimen collection is the taking of a blood sample to determine its [MASK] as a whole, to identify levels of its component cells, chemicals, gases, or other constituents, to perform pathological examination, etc.

plaque,amyloid.name: plaque , amyloid
plaque,amyloid.definition: Amyloid plaque is accumulations of extracellularly deposited amyloid fibrils within tissues.

molar.name: molar
molar.definition: Molar is the most posterior teeth on either side of the jaw, totaling eight in the deciduous dentition (2 on each side, upper and lower), and usually 12 in the permanent dentition (three on each side, upper and lower). They are grinding teeth, having large crowns and broad chewing surfaces. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p821)

radiologists.name: radiologists
radiologists.definition: Radiologists is physicians specializing in the use of x-ray and other forms of radiant energy to diagnose and treat disease.

informalsector.name: informal sector
informalsector.definition: Informal sector is a component of the private sector characterized by ease of entry; reliance on indigenous resources; family ownership; small scale operations;  skills acquired outside of the formal sector; and unregulated markets.

opticatrophy.name: optic atrophy
opticatrophy.definition: Optic atrophy is atrophy of the [MASK] which may be congenital or acquired. This condition indicates a deficiency in the number of nerve fibers which arise in the retina and converge to form the [MASK]; optic nerve; optic chiasm; and optic tracts. glaucoma; ischemia; inflammation, a chronic elevation of [MASK], toxins, optic nerve compression, and inherited conditions (see optic atrophies, hereditary) are relatively common causes of this condition.

arabidopsis.name: arabidopsis
arabidopsis.definition: Arabidopsis is a plant genus of the family brassicaceae that contains arabidopsis proteins and mads domain proteins. The species a. thaliana is used for experiments in classical plant genetics as well as molecular genetic studies in plant physiology, biochemistry, and development.

occupationalexposure.name: occupational exposure
occupationalexposure.definition: Occupational exposure is the exposure to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents that occurs as a result of one's occupation.

slowvirusdiseases.name: slow virus diseases
slowvirusdiseases.definition: Slow virus diseases is diseases of viral origin, characterized by incubation periods of months to years, insidious onset of clinical manifestations, and protracted clinical course. Though the disease process is protracted, viral multiplication may not be unusually slow. Conventional viruses produce slow virus diseases such as subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (leukoencephalopathy, progressive multifocal), and aids. Diseases produced by unconventional agents were originally considered part of this group. They are now called prion diseases.

death,sudden.name: death , sudden
death,sudden.definition: Sudden death is the abrupt cessation of all vital bodily functions, manifested by the permanent loss of total cerebral, respiratory, and cardiovascular functions.

massscreening.name: mass screening
massscreening.definition: Mass screening is organized periodic procedures performed on large groups of people for the purpose of detecting disease.

hemodynamicmonitoring.name: hemodynamic monitoring
hemodynamicmonitoring.definition: Hemodynamic monitoring is continuous measurement of the movement and forces of blood in the cardiovascular system.

beverages.name: beverages
beverages.definition: Beverages is liquids that are suitable for drinking. (From Merriam Webster Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

reagentkits,diagnostic.name: reagent kits , diagnostic
reagentkits,diagnostic.definition: Diagnostic reagent kits is commercially prepared reagent sets, with accessory devices, containing all of the major components and literature necessary to perform one or more designated [MASK] or procedures. They may be for laboratory or personal use.

cognitivereserve.name: cognitive reserve
cognitivereserve.definition: Cognitive reserve is capacity that enables an individual to cope with and/or recover from the impact of a neural injury or a psychotic episode.

reproductiveisolation.name: reproductive isolation
reproductiveisolation.definition: Reproductive isolation is mechanisms that prevent different populations from exchanging genes (gene flow), resulting in or maintaining [MASK]. It can either prevent mating to take place or ensure that any offspring produced is either inviable or sterile, thereby preventing further reproduction.

learningcurve.name: learning curve
learningcurve.definition: Learning curve is the course of learning of an individual or a group. It is a measure of performance plotted over time.

infusions,parenteral.name: infusions , parenteral
infusions,parenteral.definition: Parenteral infusions is the administration of liquid medication, nutrient, or other fluid through some other route than the alimentary canal, usually over minutes or hours, either by gravity flow or often by infusion pumping.

groupprocesses.name: group processes
groupprocesses.definition: Group processes is the procedures through which a group approaches, attacks, and solves a common problem.

fibroblastgrowthfactor9.name: fibroblast growth factor 9
fibroblastgrowthfactor9.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 9 is a fibroblast growth factor that was originally identified as a mitogen for glial cells. It is expressed primarily in neurons.

cations.name: cations
cations.definition: Cations is positively charged atoms, radicals or groups of atoms which travel to the cathode or negative pole during electrolysis.

receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type5.name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 5
receptor,fibroblastgrowthfactor,type5.definition: Type 5 fibroblast growth factor receptor is the most divergent of the known fibroblast growth factor receptors. It does not contain an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain and has been shown to interact with fibroblast growth factor 2. Fibroblast growth factor receptor 5 is found primarily in skeletal tissue.

basalganglia.name: basal ganglia
basalganglia.definition: Basal ganglia is large subcortical nuclear masses derived from the telencephalon and located in the basal regions of the cerebral hemispheres.

calcification,physiologic.name: calcification , physiologic
calcification,physiologic.definition: Physiologic calcification is process by which organic tissue becomes hardened by the physiologic deposit of calcium [MASK].

climatechange.name: climate change
climatechange.definition: Climate change is any significant change in measures of climate (such as temperature, precipitation, or [MASK]) lasting for an extended period (decades or longer). It may result from natural factors such as changes in the sun's intensity, natural processes within the climate system such as changes in ocean circulation, or human activities.

essentialtremor.name: essential tremor
essentialtremor.definition: Essential tremor is a relatively common disorder characterized by a fairly specific pattern of tremors which are most prominent in the upper extremities and [MASK], inducing titubations of the head. The tremor is usually mild, but when severe may be disabling. An autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance may occur in some families (i.e., familial tremor). (Mov Disord 1988;13(1):5-10)

galactose.name: galactose
galactose.definition: Galactose is an aldohexose that occurs naturally in the D-form in lactose, cerebrosides, gangliosides, and mucoproteins. Deficiency of galactosyl-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (galactose-1-phosphate uridyl-transferase deficiency disease) causes an error in galactose metabolism called galactosemia, resulting in elevations of galactose in the blood.

shoulderprosthesis.name: shoulder prosthesis
shoulderprosthesis.definition: [MASK] prosthesis is replacement for a [MASK] joint.

oxidativephosphorylation.name: oxidative phosphorylation
oxidativephosphorylation.definition: Oxidative phosphorylation is [MASK] transfer through the cytochrome system liberating free energy which is transformed into high-energy phosphate bonds.

mortality.name: mortality
mortality.definition: Mortality is all deaths reported in a given population.

gastricjuice.name: gastric juice
gastricjuice.definition: Gastric juice is the liquid secretion of the stomach mucosa consisting of hydrochloric acid (gastric acid); pepsinogens; intrinsic factor; gastrin; mucus; and the bicarbonate ion (bicarbonates). (From Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p651)

microsomes.name: microsomes
microsomes.definition: Microsomes is artifactual vesicles formed from the endoplasmic reticulum when cells are disrupted. They are isolated by differential centrifugation and are composed of three structural features: rough vesicles, smooth vesicles, and ribosomes. Numerous enzyme activities are associated with the microsomal fraction. (Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990; from Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

exposuretoviolence.name: exposure to violence
exposuretoviolence.definition: Exposure to violence is experience of and exposure to violence.

intestinalsecretions.name: intestinal secretions
intestinalsecretions.definition: Intestinal secretions is fluids originating from the epithelial lining of the intestines, adjoining exocrine glands and from organs such as the liver, which empty into the cavity of the intestines.

geneexpressionregulation.name: gene expression regulation
geneexpressionregulation.definition: Gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control (induction or repression) of gene action at the level of transcription or translation.

biochemicalphenomena.name: biochemical phenomena
biochemicalphenomena.definition: Biochemical phenomena is the chemical processes, enzymatic activities, and pathways of living things and related temporal, dimensional, qualitative, and quantitative concepts.

comment.name: comment
comment.definition: Comment is work consisting of a critical or explanatory note written to discuss, support, or dispute an article or other presentation previously published. It may take the form of an article, letter, [MASK], etc. It appears in publications under a variety of names: comment, commentary, [MASK] comment, viewpoint, etc.

dryeyesyndromes.name: dry eye syndromes
dryeyesyndromes.definition: Dry eye syndromes is corneal and conjunctival dryness due to deficient tear production, predominantly in menopausal and post-menopausal women. Filamentary keratitis or erosion of the conjunctival and corneal epithelium may be caused by these disorders. Sensation of the presence of a foreign body in the eye and burning of the eyes may occur.

healthsystemsagencies.name: health systems agencies
healthsystemsagencies.definition: Health systems agencies is health planning and resources development agencies which function in each health service area of the United States (pl 93-641).

cranialfossa,posterior.name: cranial fossa , posterior
cranialfossa,posterior.definition: Posterior cranial fossa is the infratentorial compartment that contains the cerebellum and brain stem. It is formed by the posterior third of the superior surface of the body of the sphenoid (sphenoid bone), by the occipital, the petrous, and mastoid portions of the [MASK], and the posterior inferior angle of the [MASK].

reflex,acoustic.name: reflex , acoustic
reflex,acoustic.definition: Acoustic reflex is intra-aural contraction of tensor tympani and stapedius in response to sound.

menopause,premature.name: menopause , premature
menopause,premature.definition: Premature menopause is the premature cessation of menses (menstruation) when the last menstrual period occurs in a woman under the age of 40. It is due to the depletion of ovarian follicles. Premature menopause can be caused by diseases; ovariectomy; radiation; chemicals; and chromosomal abnormalities.

druginteractions.name: drug interactions
druginteractions.definition: Drug interactions is the action of a drug that may affect the activity, metabolism, or toxicity of another drug.

cerebrovasculardisorders.name: cerebrovascular disorders
cerebrovasculardisorders.definition: Cerebrovascular disorders is a spectrum of pathological conditions of impaired blood flow in the brain. They can involve vessels (arteries or veins) in the cerebrum, the cerebellum, and the brain stem. Major categories include intracranial arteriovenous malformations; brain ischemia; cerebral hemorrhage; and others.

treatmentadherenceandcompliance.name: treatment adherence and compliance
treatmentadherenceandcompliance.definition: Treatment adherence and compliance is extent to which the patient follows prescribed treatment such as keeping appointments and schedules and medication adherence for desired therapeutic outcome. It implies active responsibility shared by patient and health care providers.

nationallongitudinalstudyofadolescenthea.name: national longitudinal study of adolescent health
nationallongitudinalstudyofadolescenthea.definition: National longitudinal study of [MASK] is longitudinal study of a nationally representative sample of adolescents in grades 7-12 in the United States during the 1994-95 school year. The Add Health cohort has been followed into young adulthood. (from http://www.cpc.unc.edu/projects/addhealth accessed 08/2012)

visualprosthesis.name: visual prosthesis
visualprosthesis.definition: Visual prosthesis is artificial device such as an externally-worn camera attached to a stimulator on the retina, optic nerve, or visual cortex, intended to restore or amplify vision.

sexfactors.name: sex factors
sexfactors.definition: [MASK] factors is maleness or femaleness as a constituent element or influence contributing to the production of a result. It may be applicable to the cause or effect of a circumstance. It is used with human or animal concepts but should be differentiated from [MASK] characteristics, anatomical or physiological manifestations of [MASK], and from [MASK] distribution, the number of males and females in given circumstances.

integrinalphachains.name: integrin alpha chains
integrinalphachains.definition: Integrin alpha chains is the alpha subunits of integrin heterodimers (integrins), which mediate ligand specificity. There are approximately 18 different alpha chains, exhibiting great sequence diversity; several chains are also spliced into alternative isoforms. They possess a long extracellular portion (1200 amino acids) containing a midas (metal ion-dependent adhesion site) motif, and seven 60-amino acid tandem repeats, the last 4 of which form ef hand motifs. The intracellular portion is short with the exception of integrin alpha4.

umbilicalveins.name: umbilical veins
umbilicalveins.definition: Umbilical veins is venous vessels in the umbilical cord. They carry oxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from the mother to the fetus via the placenta. In humans, there is normally one umbilical vein.

spinalcord.name: spinal cord
spinalcord.definition: Spinal cord is a cylindrical column of tissue that lies within the vertebral canal. It is composed of [MASK] matter and gray matter.

genes,suppressor.name: genes , suppressor
genes,suppressor.definition: Suppressor genes is genes that have a suppressor allele or suppressor mutation (suppression, genetic) which cancels the effect of a previous mutation, enabling the wild-type phenotype to be maintained or partially restored. For example, amber suppressors cancel the effect of an amber nonsense mutation.

chromosomes,human,pair20.name: chromosomes , human , pair 20
chromosomes,human,pair20.definition: Pair 20 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group f chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

antipsychoticagents.name: antipsychotic agents
antipsychoticagents.definition: Antipsychotic agents is agents that control agitated psychotic behavior, alleviate acute psychotic states, reduce psychotic symptoms, and exert a quieting effect. They are used in schizophrenia; senile dementia; transient psychosis following surgery; or myocardial infarction; etc. These drugs are often referred to as neuroleptics alluding to the tendency to produce neurological side effects, but not all antipsychotics are likely to produce such effects. Many of these drugs may also be effective against nausea, emesis, and pruritus.

moon.name: moon
moon.definition: Moon is the natural satellite of the planet Earth. It includes the lunar cycles or phases, the lunar month, lunar landscapes, geography, and soil.

computers,hybrid.name: computers , hybrid
computers,hybrid.definition: Hybrid computers is computers that combine the functions of analog and digital computers. (Sippl, Computer Dictionary, 4th ed)

pregnancy.name: pregnancy
pregnancy.definition: Pregnancy is the status during which female mammals carry their developing young (embryos or fetuses) in utero before birth, beginning from fertilization to birth.

cellcomponent.name: cell component
cellcomponent.definition: Cell component is components of a cell.

catecholoxidase.name: catechol oxidase
catecholoxidase.definition: Catechol oxidase is an enzyme of the oxidoreductase class that catalyzes the reaction between catechol and oxygen to yield benzoquinone and water. It is a complex of [MASK]-containing proteins that acts also on a variety of substituted catechols. ec 1.10.3.1.

radiotherapy,adjuvant.name: radiotherapy , adjuvant
radiotherapy,adjuvant.definition: Adjuvant radiotherapy is radiotherapy given to augment some other form of treatment such as surgery or chemotherapy. Adjuvant radiotherapy is commonly used in the therapy of cancer and can be administered before or after the primary treatment.

indicator,reagent,ordiagnosticaid.name: indicator , reagent , or diagnostic aid
indicator,reagent,ordiagnosticaid.definition: Or diagnostic aid reagent indicator is indicator , reagent , or diagnostic aid

environmentaldna.name: environmental dna
environmentaldna.definition: Environmental dna is dna found in the environment that is from the residual biological materials of the organisms in the environment.

ethicsconsultation.name: ethics consultation
ethicsconsultation.definition: Ethics consultation is services provided by an individual ethicist (ethicists) or an ethics team or committee (ethics committees, clinical) to address the ethical issues involved in a specific clinical case. The central purpose is to improve the process and outcomes of patients' care by helping to identify, analyze, and resolve ethical problems.

chromosomes,human,pair12.name: chromosomes , human , pair 12
chromosomes,human,pair12.definition: Pair 12 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

excitatoryaminoacidtransporter4.name: excitatory amino acid transporter 4
excitatoryaminoacidtransporter4.definition: [MASK] transporter 4 is a glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein that is primarily expressed in cerebellar purkinje cells on postsynaptic dendritic spines.

cytokines.name: cytokines
cytokines.definition: Cytokines is non-antibody proteins secreted by inflammatory leukocytes and some non-leukocytic cells, that act as intercellular mediators. They differ from classical hormones in that they are produced by a number of tissue or cell types rather than by specialized glands. They generally act locally in a paracrine or autocrine rather than endocrine manner.

inflammationmediators.name: inflammation mediators
inflammationmediators.definition: Inflammation mediators is the endogenous compounds that mediate inflammation (autacoids) and related exogenous compounds including the synthetic prostaglandins (prostaglandins, synthetic).

roundligamentofliver.name: round ligament of liver
roundligamentofliver.definition: Round ligament of liver is a cord-like remnant structure formed from the closed left fetal umbilical vein. It is located along the lower edge of the falciform ligament.

attention.name: attention
attention.definition: Attention is focusing on certain aspects of current experience to the exclusion of others. It is the act of heeding or taking notice or concentrating.

lymphoidtissue.name: lymphoid tissue
lymphoidtissue.definition: Lymphoid tissue is specialized tissues that are components of the lymphatic system. They provide fixed locations within the body where a variety of lymphocytes can form, mature and multiply. The lymphoid tissues are connected by a network of lymphatic vessels.

breastimplants.name: breast implants
breastimplants.definition: Breast implants is implants used to reconstruct and/or cosmetically enhance the female breast. They have an outer shell or envelope of silicone elastomer and are filled with either saline or silicone gel. The outer shell may be either smooth or textured.

leukemia,largegranularlymphocytic.name: leukemia , large granular lymphocytic
leukemia,largegranularlymphocytic.definition: Large granular lymphocytic leukemia is a spectrum of disorders characterized by clonal expansions of the peripheral blood lymphocyte populations known as large granular lymphocytes which contain abundant cytoplasm and azurophilic granules. Subtypes develop from either CD3-negative natural killer cells or CD3-positive t-cells. The clinical course of both subtypes can vary from spontaneous regression to progressive, malignant disease.

officeautomation.name: office automation
officeautomation.definition: Office automation is use of computers or computer systems for doing routine clerical work, e.g., billing, records pertaining to the administration of the office, etc.

freezing.name: freezing
freezing.definition: Freezing is liquids transforming into solids by the removal of heat.

homenursing.name: home nursing
homenursing.definition: Home nursing is nursing care given to an individual in the home. The care may be provided by a family member or a friend. Home nursing as care by a non-professional is differentiated from home care services provided by professionals: [MASK], [MASK], hospital, or other organized community group.

secretoryrate.name: secretory rate
secretoryrate.definition: Secretory rate is the amount of a substance secreted by cells or by a specific organ or organism over a given period of time; usually applies to those substances which are formed by glandular tissues and are released by them into biological fluids, e.g., secretory rate of corticosteroids by the adrenal cortex, secretory rate of gastric acid by the gastric mucosa.

opticalphenomena.name: optical phenomena
opticalphenomena.definition: Optical phenomena is light, its processes and properties, and the characteristics of materials interacting with it.

anisotropy.name: anisotropy
anisotropy.definition: Anisotropy is a physical property showing different values in relation to the direction in or along which the measurement is made. The physical property may be with regard to thermal or electric conductivity or light refraction. In crystallography, it describes crystals whose index of refraction varies with the direction of the incident light. It is also called acolotropy and colotropy. The opposite of anisotropy is isotropy wherein the same values characterize the object when measured along axes in all directions.

supremecourtdecisions.name: supreme court decisions
supremecourtdecisions.definition: Supreme court decisions is decisions made by the United States Supreme Court.

tissueplasminogenactivator.name: tissue plasminogen activator
tissueplasminogenactivator.definition: Tissue plasminogen activator is a proteolytic enzyme in the serine protease family found in many tissues which converts plasminogen to fibrinolysin. It has fibrin-binding activity and is immunologically different from urokinase-type plasminogen activator. The primary sequence, composed of 527 amino acids, is identical in both the naturally occurring and synthetic proteases.

carcinoma,krebs2.name: carcinoma , krebs 2
carcinoma,krebs2.definition: Krebs 2 carcinoma is a transplantable neoplasm of mice.

lipoprotein(a).name: lipoprotein ( a )
lipoprotein(a).definition: Lipoprotein (a) is a lipoprotein that resembles the low-density lipoproteins but with an extra protein moiety, aporoteinN (A) also known as apolipoprotein (A), linked to apolipoprotein B-100 on the LDL by one or two disulfide bonds. High plasma level of lipoprotein (a) is associated with increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

specificgravity.name: specific gravity
specificgravity.definition: Specific gravity is the ratio of the density of a material to the density of some standard material, such as water or air, at a specified temperature.

synapticmembranes.name: synaptic membranes
synapticmembranes.definition: Synaptic membranes is cell membranes associated with synapses. Both presynaptic and postsynaptic membranes are included along with their integral or tightly associated specializations for the release or reception of transmitters.

communityhealthnursing.name: community health nursing
communityhealthnursing.definition: Community health nursing is general and comprehensive nursing practice directed to individuals, families, or groups as it relates to and contributes to the health of a population or community. This is not an official program of a Public Health Department.

neutroncapturetherapy.name: neutron capture therapy
neutroncapturetherapy.definition: Neutron capture therapy is a technique for the treatment of neoplasms in which an isotope is introduced into target cells followed by irradiation with thermal neutrons.

videorecording.name: video recording
videorecording.definition: Video recording is the storing or preserving of video signals to be played back later via a transmitter or receiver.

weightsandmeasures.name: weights and measures
weightsandmeasures.definition: Weights and measures is measuring and weighing systems and processes.

glucoseintolerance.name: glucose intolerance
glucoseintolerance.definition: Glucose intolerance is a pathological state in which blood glucose level is less than approximately 140 mg/100 ml of plasma at fasting, and above approximately 200 mg/100 ml plasma at 30-, 60-, or 90-minute during a glucose tolerance test. This condition is seen frequently in diabetes mellitus, but also occurs with other diseases and malnutrition.

cathepsinf.name: cathepsin f
cathepsinf.definition: Cathepsin f is a lysosomal papain-related [MASK] proteinase that is expressed in a broad variety of cell types.

transcriptome.name: transcriptome
transcriptome.definition: Transcriptome is the pattern of gene expression at the level of genetic transcription in a specific organism or under specific circumstances in specific cells.

functionalresidualcapacity.name: functional residual capacity
functionalresidualcapacity.definition: Functional residual capacity is the volume of air remaining in the lungs at the end of a normal, quiet expiration. It is the sum of the residual volume and the expiratory reserve volume. Common abbreviation is frc.

decisionmaking.name: decision making
decisionmaking.definition: Decision making is the process of making a selective intellectual judgment when presented with several complex alternatives consisting of several variables, and usually defining a course of action or an idea.

centralcordsyndrome.name: central cord syndrome
centralcordsyndrome.definition: Central cord syndrome is a syndrome associated with traumatic injury to the cervical or upper thoracic regions of the spinal cord characterized by weakness in the [MASK] with relative sparing of the legs and variable sensory loss. This condition is associated with ischemia, hemorrhage, or necrosis involving the central portions of the spinal cord. Corticospinal fibers destined for the legs are spared due to their more external location in the spinal cord. This clinical pattern may emerge during recovery from spinal shock. Deficits may be transient or permanent.

heart.name: heart
heart.definition: Heart is the hollow, muscular organ that maintains the circulation of the blood.

animals.name: animals
animals.definition: Animals is unicellular or multicellular, heterotrophic organisms, that have sensation and the power of voluntary movement. Under the older five kingdom paradigm, Animalia was one of the kingdoms. Under the modern three domain model, Animalia represents one of the many groups in the domain eukaryota.

environmentalbiomarkers.name: environmental biomarkers
environmentalbiomarkers.definition: Environmental biomarkers is a factor associated with the well-being of living organisms that is used as a measure of environmental change and or influence. For example, aldehyde dehydrogenase expression in earthworm tissue is used as an indication of heavy metal pollution in soils. Distinguish from biomarkers.

hivinfections.name: hiv infections
hivinfections.definition: Hiv infections is includes the spectrum of human immunodeficiency virus infections that range from asymptomatic seropositivity, thru AIDS-related complex (arc), to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (aids).

bodyburden.name: body burden
bodyburden.definition: Body burden is the total amount of a chemical, metal or radioactive substance present at any time after absorption in the body of man or animal.

penicillinv.name: penicillin v
penicillinv.definition: Penicillin v is a broad-spectrum penicillin antibiotic used orally in the treatment of mild to moderate infections by susceptible gram-positive organisms.

cytoplasmicgranules.name: cytoplasmic granules
cytoplasmicgranules.definition: Cytoplasmic granules is condensed areas of cellular material that may be bounded by a membrane.

electrodes.name: electrodes
electrodes.definition: Electrodes is electric conductors through which electric currents enter or leave a medium, whether it be an electrolytic solution, solid, molten mass, gas, or vacuum.

ovary.name: ovary
ovary.definition: Ovary is the reproductive organ (gonads) in female animals. In vertebrates, the ovary contains two functional parts: the ovarian follicle for the production of female germ cells (oogenesis); and the endocrine cells (granulosa cells; theca cells; and luteal cells) for the production of estrogens and progesterone.

radiationeffects.name: radiation effects
radiationeffects.definition: Radiation effects is the effects of ionizing and nonionizing radiation upon living organisms, organs and tissues, and their constituents, and upon physiologic processes. It includes the effect of irradiation on food, drugs, and chemicals.

cordfactors.name: cord factors
cordfactors.definition: Cord factors is toxic glycolipids composed of trehalose dimycolate derivatives. They are produced by [MASK] and other species of mycobacterium. They induce cellular dysfunction in animals.

reproduction.name: reproduction
reproduction.definition: Reproduction is the total process by which organisms produce offspring. (Stedman, 25th ed)

cardiopulmonarybypass.name: cardiopulmonary bypass
cardiopulmonarybypass.definition: Cardiopulmonary bypass is diversion of the flow of blood from the entrance of the right atrium directly to the aorta (or [MASK]) via an oxygenator thus bypassing both the heart and lungs.

systemsbiology.name: systems biology
