systemsbiology.definition: Systems biology is comprehensive, methodical analysis of complex biological systems by monitoring responses to perturbations of biological processes. Large scale, computerized collection and analysis of the data are used to develop and test models of biological systems.

peptideelongationfactortu.name: peptide elongation factor tu
peptideelongationfactortu.definition: Peptide elongation factor tu is a protein found in bacteria and eukaryotic mitochondria which delivers aminoacyl-tRNA's to the a site of the ribosome. The aminoacyl-tRNA is first bound to a complex of elongation factor Tu containing a molecule of bound gtp. The resulting complex is then bound to the 70s initiation complex. Simultaneously the gtp is hydrolyzed and a Tu-GDP complex is released from the 70s ribosome. The Tu-GTP complex is regenerated from the Tu-GDP complex by the Ts elongation factor and gtp.

pacificislands.name: pacific islands
pacificislands.definition: Pacific islands is the islands of the Pacific Ocean divided into micronesia; melanesia; and polynesia (including [MASK]). The collective name Oceania includes the aforenamed islands, adding australia; [MASK]; and the [MASK] ([MASK]). (Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p910, 880)

cpgislands.name: cpg islands
cpgislands.definition: Cpg islands is areas of increased density of the dinucleotide sequence cytosine--phosphate diester--guanine. They form stretches of dna several hundred to several thousand [MASK] long. In humans there are about 45,000 CpG islands, mostly found at the 5' ends of genes. They are unmethylated except for those on the inactive x chromosome and some associated with imprinted genes.

spinalinjuries.name: spinal injuries
spinalinjuries.definition: Spinal injuries is injuries involving the vertebral column.

limkinases.name: lim kinases
limkinases.definition: Lim kinases is serine protein kinases involved in the regulation of actin [MASK] and [MASK] disassembly. Their activity is regulated by phosphorylation of a threonine residue within the activation loop by intracellular signaling kinases such as p21-activated kinases and by rho kinase.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.definition: Maintenance is the upkeep of property or equipment.

bodylocationorregion.name: body location or region
bodylocationorregion.definition: Body location or region is anatomical areas of the body.

senseofcoherence.name: sense of coherence
senseofcoherence.definition: Sense of coherence is a view of the world and the individual's environment as comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful, claiming that the way people view their life has a positive influence on their health.

complexmixtures.name: complex mixtures
complexmixtures.definition: Complex mixtures is mixtures of many components in inexact proportions, usually natural, such as plant extracts; venoms; and [MASK]. These are distinguished from [MASK] which have only a few components in definite proportions.

lupuscoagulationinhibitor.name: lupus coagulation inhibitor
lupuscoagulationinhibitor.definition: Lupus coagulation inhibitor is an antiphospholipid antibody found in association with [MASK] ([MASK];), antiphospholipid syndrome; and in a variety of other diseases as well as in healthy individuals. In vitro, the antibody interferes with the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and prolongs the partial thromboplastin time. In vivo, it exerts a procoagulant effect resulting in thrombosis mainly in the larger veins and arteries. It further causes obstetrical complications, including fetal death and spontaneous abortion, as well as a variety of hematologic and neurologic complications.

posture.name: posture
posture.definition: Posture is the position or physical attitude of the body.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyb.definition: Subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is a subfamily of transmembrane proteins from the superfamily of atp-binding cassette transporters that are closely related in sequence to atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b, member 1. When overexpressed, they function as ATP-dependent efflux pumps able to extrude lipophilic drugs (especially antineoplastic agents) from cells, causing multidrug resistance (drug resistance, multiple). Although atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b share functional similarities to multidrug resistance-associated proteins they are two distinct subclasses of atp-binding cassette transporters, and have little sequence homology.

sequencealignment.name: sequence alignment
sequencealignment.definition: Sequence alignment is the arrangement of two or more amino acid or base sequences from an organism or organisms in such a way as to align areas of the sequences sharing common properties. The degree of relatedness or homology between the sequences is predicted computationally or statistically based on weights assigned to the elements aligned between the sequences. This in turn can serve as a potential indicator of the genetic relatedness between the organisms.

rawfoods.name: raw foods
rawfoods.definition: Raw foods is food prepared for consumption without exposure to heat.

cognitivedysfunction.name: cognitive dysfunction
cognitivedysfunction.definition: Cognitive dysfunction is diminished or impaired mental and/or intellectual function.

dietaryapproachestostophypertension.name: dietary approaches to stop hypertension
dietaryapproachestostophypertension.definition: Dietary approaches to stop hypertension is dietary recommendations that promote reduction in or prevention of high blood pressure. Recommendations include increasing intake of fruits and vegetables, and high-fiber, low-fat foods and reducing the intake of dietary sodium and high fat foods.

calciumisotopes.name: calcium isotopes
calciumisotopes.definition: Calcium isotopes is stable calcium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element calcium, but differ in atomic weight. Ca-42-44, 46, and 48 are stable calcium isotopes.

lactose.name: lactose
lactose.definition: Lactose is a disaccharide of glucose and galactose in human and cow milk. It is used in pharmacy for tablets, in medicine as a nutrient, and in industry.

chemicalanddruginducedliverinjury,chroni.name: chemical and drug induced liver injury , chronic
chemicalanddruginducedliverinjury,chroni.definition: Chronic chemical and drug induced liver injury is liver disease lasting six months or more, caused by an adverse effect of a drug or chemical. The adverse effect may be caused by drugs, drug metabolites, chemicals from the environment, or an idiosyncratic response.

geneticvariation.name: genetic variation
geneticvariation.definition: Genetic variation is genotypic differences observed among individuals in a population.

foodintolerance.name: food intolerance
foodintolerance.definition: Food intolerance is digestive system disorder where a particular food irritates the digestive tract or cannot be properly digested (i.e., due to a lack of a digestive enzyme). It differs from food hypersensitivity which is an immune system disorder, usually due to specific proteins in food.  http://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/problem-foods-is-it-an-allergy-or-intolerance.

seasonalaffectivedisorder.name: seasonal affective disorder
seasonalaffectivedisorder.definition: Seasonal affective disorder is a syndrome characterized by depressions that recur annually at the same time each year, usually during the winter months. Other symptoms include anxiety, irritability, decreased energy, increased appetite (carbohydrate cravings), increased duration of sleep, and weight gain. sad (seasonal affective disorder) can be treated by daily exposure to bright artificial lights (phototherapy), during the season of recurrence.

stelevationmyocardialinfarction.name: st elevation myocardial infarction
stelevationmyocardialinfarction.definition: St elevation myocardial infarction is a clinical syndrome defined by myocardial ischemia symptoms; persistent elevation in the st segments of the electrocardiogram; and release of biomarkers of myocardial necrosis (e.g., elevated troponin levels). st segment elevation in the ecg is often used in determining the treatment protocol (see also non-st elevation myocardial infarction).

thoracicwall.name: thoracic wall
thoracicwall.definition: Thoracic wall is the outer margins of the thorax containing skin, deep fascia; thoracic vertebrae; ribs; sternum; and muscles.

uterinearteryembolization.name: uterine artery embolization
uterinearteryembolization.definition: Uterine artery embolization is the use of embolizing agents to block the arterial blood supply to parts or all of the uterus. The procedures are done to control bleeding or to cause destruction of uterine tissues.

arthroplasty,replacement,knee.name: arthroplasty , replacement , knee
arthroplasty,replacement,knee.definition: [MASK] replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the [MASK].

hemorrhagicfever,american.name: hemorrhagic fever , american
hemorrhagicfever,american.definition: American hemorrhagic fever is diseases caused by American hemorrhagic fever viruses (arenaviruses, new world).

hospitals,state.name: hospitals , state
hospitals,state.definition: State hospitals is hospitals controlled by agencies and departments of the [MASK].

diffusionchambers,culture.name: diffusion chambers , culture
diffusionchambers,culture.definition: Culture diffusion chambers is devices used in a technique by which cells or tissues are grown in vitro or, by implantation, in vivo within chambers permeable to diffusion of solutes across the chamber walls. The chambers are used for studies of drug effects, osmotic responses, cytogenic and immunologic phenomena, metabolism, etc., and include tissue cages.

colitis,ulcerative.name: colitis , ulcerative
colitis,ulcerative.definition: Ulcerative colitis is inflammation of the colon that is predominantly confined to the mucosa. Its major symptoms include [MASK], rectal bleeding, the passage of mucus, and abdominal pain.

models,genetic.name: models , genetic
models,genetic.definition: Genetic models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of genetic processes or phenomena. They include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

lactosesynthase.name: lactose synthase
lactosesynthase.definition: Lactose synthase is an enzyme complex that catalyzes the transfer of galactose from udp galactose to glucose, forming lactose. The enzyme complex is composed of a b subunit, alpha-lactalbumin, which changes the substrate specificity of the a subunit, n-acetyllactosamine synthase, from n-acetylglucosamine to glucose making lactose synthesis the preferred reaction.

graftvshostdisease.name: graft vs host disease
graftvshostdisease.definition: [MASK] vs host disease is the clinical entity characterized by anorexia, [MASK], loss of hair, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, growth retardation, and eventual death brought about by the [MASK] vs host reaction.

laboratoryproficiencytesting.name: laboratory proficiency testing
laboratoryproficiencytesting.definition: Laboratory proficiency testing is assessments aimed at determining agreement in [MASK] results among laboratories. Identical survey samples are distributed to participating laboratories, with results stratified according to testing methodologies.

milkejection.name: milk ejection
milkejection.definition: Milk ejection is expulsion of milk from the mammary alveolar lumen, which is surrounded by a layer of milk-secreting epithelial cells and a network of myoepithelial cells. Contraction of the myoepithelial cells is regulated by neuroendocrine signals.

thyroidcancer,papillary.name: thyroid cancer , papillary
thyroidcancer,papillary.definition: Papillary thyroid cancer is an adenocarcinoma that originates from follicular cells of the thyroid gland and accounts for the majority of thyroid cancer cases. Cells exhibit enlarged, oval, or elongated morphologies with clear, round, nuclei. Fusions of ret, ntrk1, tpm3, and pcm1 genes are associated with this cancer.

hazardoussubstances.name: hazardous substances
hazardoussubstances.definition: Hazardous substances is elements, compounds, mixtures, or solutions that are considered severely harmful to human health and the environment. They include substances that are toxic, corrosive, flammable, or explosive.

microscopy,electrochemical,scanning.name: microscopy , electrochemical , scanning
microscopy,electrochemical,scanning.definition: Scanning electrochemical microscopy is a scanning probe microscopy technique that uses an ultramicroelectrode as the scanning probe that simultaneously records changes in electrochemical potential as it scans thereby creating topographical images with localized electrochemical information.

speechrecognitionsoftware.name: speech recognition software
speechrecognitionsoftware.definition: [MASK] recognition software is software capable of recognizing dictation and transcribing the spoken words into written text.

aminoacidmotifs.name: amino acid motifs
aminoacidmotifs.definition: Amino acid motifs is three-dimensional protein structural elements that are composed of a combination of secondary structures. They include helix-loop-helix motifs and zinc fingers. Motifs are typically the most conserved regions of protein domains and are critical for domain function. However, the same motif may occur in proteins or enzymes with different functions.

britishvirginislands.name: british virgin islands
britishvirginislands.definition: British virgin islands is a British overseas territory, part of the British West Indies, lying about 60 miles east of Puerto Rico. Tortola is the main island, other islands include Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and Anegada.

osteoarthritis.name: osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.definition: Osteoarthritis is a progressive, degenerative joint disease, the most common form of arthritis, especially in older persons. The disease is thought to result not from the aging process but from biochemical changes and biomechanical stresses affecting articular cartilage. In the foreign literature it is often called osteoarthrosis deformans.

guidedtissueregeneration.name: guided tissue regeneration
guidedtissueregeneration.definition: Guided tissue regeneration is procedures for enhancing and directing tissue repair and renewal processes, such as bone regeneration; nerve regeneration; etc. They involve surgically implanting growth conducive tracks or conduits (tissue scaffolding) at the damaged site to stimulate and control the location of cell repopulation. The tracks or conduits are made from synthetic and/or natural materials and may include support cells and induction factors for cell growth processes; or cell migration.

drainage.name: drainage
drainage.definition: Drainage is the removal of fluids or discharges from the body, such as from a wound, sore, or cavity.

measlesvirus.name: measles virus
measlesvirus.definition: Measles virus is the type species of morbillivirus and the cause of the highly infectious human disease measles, which affects mostly children.

nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member1.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 4 , group a , member 1
nuclearreceptorsubfamily4,groupa,member1.definition: Member 1 group a nuclear receptor subfamily 4 is an orphan nuclear receptor that is closely related to members of the thyroid-steroid receptor gene family. It was originally identified in nerve cells and may play a role in mediation of nerve growth FACTOR-induced cell differentiation. However, several other functions have been attributed to this protein including the positive and negative regulation of apoptosis.

skinneoplasms.name: skin neoplasms
skinneoplasms.definition: Skin neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the skin.

constipation.name: constipation
constipation.definition: Constipation is infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces. These symptoms are associated with a variety of causes, including low dietary fiber intake, emotional or nervous disturbances, systemic and structural disorders, drug-induced aggravation, and infections.

japaneseencephalitisvaccines.name: japanese encephalitis vaccines
japaneseencephalitisvaccines.definition: Japanese encephalitis vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with Japanese b encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, japanese).

dnareplication.name: dna replication
dnareplication.definition: Dna replication is the process by which a dna molecule is duplicated.

steel.name: steel
steel.definition: Steel is a tough, malleable, iron-based alloy containing up to, but no more than, two percent carbon and often other metals. It is used in medicine and dentistry in implants and instrumentation.

daycare,medical.name: day care , medical
daycare,medical.definition: Medical day care is institutional health care of patients during the day. The patients return home at night.

codliveroil.name: cod liver oil
codliveroil.definition: Cod liver oil is oil obtained from fresh livers of the cod family, Gadidae. It is a source of vitamin a and vitamin d.

leucinedehydrogenase.name: leucine dehydrogenase
leucinedehydrogenase.definition: [MASK] dehydrogenase is an octameric enzyme belonging to the superfamily of amino acid dehydrogenases. [MASK] dehydrogenase catalyzes the reversible oxidative deamination of [MASK], to 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate (2-ketoisocaproate) and [MASK], with the corresponding reduction of the cofactor nad+.

freezesubstitution.name: freeze substitution
freezesubstitution.definition: Freeze substitution is a modification of the freeze-drying method in which the ice within the frozen tissue is replaced by alcohol or other solvent at a very low temperature.

catheterization.name: catheterization
catheterization.definition: Catheterization is use or insertion of a tubular device into a duct, blood vessel, hollow organ, or body cavity for injecting or withdrawing fluids for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. It differs from [MASK] in that the tube here is used to restore or maintain patency in obstructions.

carotidsinus.name: carotid sinus
carotidsinus.definition: Carotid sinus is the dilated portion of the common carotid artery at its bifurcation into external and internal carotids. It contains baroreceptors which, when stimulated, cause slowing of the heart, vasodilatation, and a fall in blood pressure.

cloning,molecular.name: cloning , molecular
cloning,molecular.definition: Molecular cloning is the insertion of [MASK] molecules from prokaryotic and/or eukaryotic sources into a replicating vehicle, such as a plasmid or virus vector, and the introduction of the resultant hybrid molecules into recipient cells without altering the viability of those cells.

atmosphericpressure.name: atmospheric pressure
atmosphericpressure.definition: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure at any point in an atmosphere due solely to the weight of the atmospheric gases above the point concerned.

walktest.name: walk test
walktest.definition: Walk test is a measure of endurance tests that show how far and fast an individual can walk without stopping within a certain period of time.

dietaryservices.name: dietary services
dietaryservices.definition: Dietary services is services provided by dietitians or nutritionists to meet the nutritional needs of individuals, including consultation with other professional personnel.

lawenforcement.name: law enforcement
lawenforcement.definition: Law enforcement is organized efforts to insure obedience to the laws of a community.

wordprocessing.name: word processing
wordprocessing.definition: Word processing is text editing and storage functions using computer software.

economics,pharmaceutical.name: economics , pharmaceutical
economics,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical economics is economic aspects of the fields of pharmacy and pharmacology as they apply to the development and study of medical economics in rational drug therapy and the impact of pharmaceuticals on the cost of medical care. Pharmaceutical economics also includes the economic considerations of the pharmaceutical care delivery system and in drug prescribing, particularly of cost-benefit values. (From j Res Pharm Econ 1989;1(1); PharmacoEcon 1992;1(1))

transfection.name: transfection
transfection.definition: Transfection is the uptake of naked or purified dna by cells, usually meaning the process as it occurs in eukaryotic cells. It is analogous to bacterial transformation (transformation, bacterial) and both are routinely employed in gene transfer techniques.

programmedinstruction.name: programmed instruction
programmedinstruction.definition: Programmed instruction is works consisting of sequenced self-correction texts.

affectivesymptoms.name: affective symptoms
affectivesymptoms.definition: Affective symptoms is mood or emotional responses dissonant with or inappropriate to the behavior and/or stimulus.

radiology.name: radiology
radiology.definition: Radiology is a specialty concerned with the use of x-ray and other forms of radiant energy in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

muscularatrophy,spinal.name: muscular atrophy , spinal
muscularatrophy,spinal.definition: Spinal muscular atrophy is a group of disorders marked by progressive degeneration of motor neurons in the spinal cord resulting in weakness and muscular atrophy, usually without evidence of injury to the corticospinal tracts. Diseases in this category include Werdnig-Hoffmann disease and later onset spinal muscular atrophies of childhood, most of which are hereditary. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1089)

ghana.name: ghana
ghana.definition: Ghana is a republic in western Africa, south of burkina faso and west of togo. Its capital is Accra.

burns,inhalation.name: burns , inhalation
burns,inhalation.definition: [MASK] burns is burns of the respiratory tract caused by heat or inhaled chemicals.

legulcer.name: leg ulcer
legulcer.definition: Leg [MASK] is ulceration of the skin and underlying structures of the lower extremity. About 90% of the cases are due to venous insufficiency (varicose [MASK]), 5% to arterial disease, and the remaining 5% to other causes.

preventivemedicine.name: preventive medicine
preventivemedicine.definition: Preventive medicine is a medical specialty primarily concerned with prevention of disease (primary prevention) and the promotion and preservation of health in the individual.

lenses.name: lenses
lenses.definition: Lenses is pieces of glass or other transparent materials used for magnification or increased visual acuity.

cardiomyopathy,hypertrophic.name: cardiomyopathy , hypertrophic
cardiomyopathy,hypertrophic.definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a form of cardiac muscle disease, characterized by left and/or right ventricular hypertrophy (hypertrophy, left ventricular; hypertrophy, right ventricular), frequent asymmetrical involvement of the heart septum, and normal or reduced left ventricular volume. Risk factors include hypertension; [MASK]; and gene mutation; ([MASK]).

mapkinasekinasekinase2.name: map kinase kinase kinase 2
mapkinasekinasekinase2.definition: Map kinase kinase kinase 2 is a 70-kDa map kinase kinase kinase with specificity for map kinase kinase 5. It is activated during the cellular response to growth factors, oxidative stress, and hyperosmotic conditions.

plasmacells.name: plasma cells
plasmacells.definition: Plasma cells is specialized forms of antibody-producing b-lymphocytes. They synthesize and secrete immunoglobulin. They are found only in lymphoid organs and at sites of immune responses and normally do not circulate in the blood or [MASK]. (Rosen et al., Dictionary of [MASK], 1989, p169 & Abbas et al., Cellular and Molecular [MASK], 2d ed, p20)

refraction,ocular.name: refraction , ocular
refraction,ocular.definition: Ocular refraction is refraction of light effected by the media of the eye.

adaptorproteincomplex3.name: adaptor protein complex 3
adaptorproteincomplex3.definition: Adaptor protein complex 3 is an adaptor protein complex found primarily on perinuclear compartments.

dermatitis.name: dermatitis
dermatitis.definition: Dermatitis is any inflammation of the skin.

fibroblastgrowthfactor2.name: fibroblast growth factor 2
fibroblastgrowthfactor2.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 2 is a single-chain polypeptide growth factor that plays a significant role in the process of wound healing and is a potent inducer of physiologic angiogenesis. Several different forms of the human protein exist ranging from 18-24 kDa in size due to the use of alternative start sites within the fgf-2 gene. It has a 55 percent amino acid residue identity to fibroblast growth factor 1 and has potent heparin-binding activity. The growth factor is an extremely potent inducer of dna synthesis in a variety of cell types from mesoderm and neuroectoderm lineages. It was originally named basic fibroblast growth factor based upon its chemical properties and to distinguish it from acidic fibroblast growth factor (fibroblast growth factor 1).

mouthfloor.name: mouth floor
mouthfloor.definition: Mouth floor is the area of the mouth beneath the tongue.

populationcontrol.name: population control
populationcontrol.definition: Population control is includes mechanisms or programs which control the numbers of individuals in a population of humans or animals.

cellgrowthprocesses.name: cell growth processes
cellgrowthprocesses.definition: Cell growth processes is processes required for cell enlargement and cell proliferation.

trpvcationchannels.name: trpv cation channels
trpvcationchannels.definition: Trpv cation channels is a subgroup of trp cation channels named after the vanilloid receptor. They are very sensitive to temperature; hot spicy food, and capsaicin. They contain a trp domain (a five-turn amphipathic helix with an invariant tryptophan) and ankyrin repeats. Selectivity for calcium over sodium ranges from 3 to 100 fold.

spinalcordneoplasms.name: spinal cord neoplasms
spinalcordneoplasms.definition: Spinal cord neoplasms is benign and malignant neoplasms which occur within the substance of the spinal cord (intramedullary neoplasms) or in the space between the dura and spinal cord (intradural extramedullary neoplasms). The majority of intramedullary spinal tumors are primary cns neoplasms including astrocytoma; ependymoma; and lipoma. Intramedullary neoplasms are often associated with syringomyelia. The most frequent histologic types of intradural-extramedullary tumors are meningioma and neurofibroma.

hepatitisbantigens.name: hepatitis b antigens
hepatitisbantigens.definition: Hepatitis b antigens is antigens of the virion of the hepatitis b virus or the Dane particle, its surface (hepatitis b surface antigens), core ([MASK]), and other associated antigens, including the hepatitis b e antigens.

regulatedcelldeath.name: regulated cell death
regulatedcelldeath.definition: Regulated cell death is genetically encoded mechanisms in multicellular and unicellular eukaryotes that function to eliminate cells that are superfluous either during development, or to maintain tissue and organism homeostasis; and cells that are irreversibly damaged, abnormal, and/or potentially harmful.

technologytransfer.name: technology transfer
technologytransfer.definition: Technology transfer is spread and adoption of inventions and techniques from one geographic area to another, from one discipline to another, or from one sector of the economy to another. For example, improvements in medical equipment may be transferred from industrial countries to developing countries, advances arising from aerospace engineering may be applied to equipment for persons with disabilities, and innovations in science arising from government research are made available to private enterprise.

mandibularnerve.name: mandibular nerve
mandibularnerve.definition: Mandibular nerve is a branch of the trigeminal (5th cranial) nerve. The mandibular nerve carries motor fibers to the muscles of mastication and sensory fibers to the teeth and gingivae, the face in the region of the mandible, and parts of the dura.

perinatalcare.name: perinatal care
perinatalcare.definition: Perinatal care is the care of women and a fetus or newborn given before, during, and after delivery from the 28th week of gestation through the 7th day after delivery.

communitymedicine.name: community medicine
communitymedicine.definition: Community medicine is a branch of medicine concerned with the total health of the individual within the home environment and in the community, and with the application of comprehensive care to the prevention and treatment of illness in the entire community.

dnatransformationcompetence.name: dna transformation competence
dnatransformationcompetence.definition: Dna transformation competence is the ability of bacterial cells to take up exogenous dna and be genetically transformed by it.

medicare.name: medicare
medicare.definition: Medicare is federal program, created by Public Law 89-97, Title XVIII-Health Insurance for the Aged, a 1965 amendment to the Social Security Act, that provides health [MASK] to persons over the age of 65 and others eligible for Social Security benefits. It consists of two separate but coordinated programs: hospital insurance (medicare part a) and supplementary medical insurance ([MASK]). (Hospital Administration Terminology, aha, 2d ed and a Discursive Dictionary of Health Care, us House of Representatives, 1976)

therapeuticcommunity.name: therapeutic community
therapeuticcommunity.definition: Therapeutic community is psychotherapeutic technique which emphasizes socioenvironmental and interpersonal influences in the resocialization and rehabilitation of the patient. The setting is usually a hospital unit or ward in which professional and nonprofessional staff interact with the patients.

datadisplay.name: data display
datadisplay.definition: Data display is the visual representation of data via a manufactured system.

languagetests.name: language tests
languagetests.definition: Language tests is tests designed to assess language behavior and abilities. They include tests of vocabulary, comprehension, grammar and functional use of language, e.g., Development Sentence Scoring, Receptive-Expressive Emergent Language Scale, Parsons Language Sample, Utah Test of Language Development, Michigan Language Inventory and Verbal Language Development Scale, Illinois Test of Psycholinguistic Abilities, Northwestern Syntax Screening Test, Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test, Ammons Full-Range Picture Vocabulary Test, and Assessment of Children's Language Comprehension.

collagentypexi.name: collagen type xi
collagentypexi.definition: Collagen type xi is a fibrillar collagen found primarily in interstitial cartilage. Collagen type xi is heterotrimer containing alpha1(XI), alpha2(XI) and alpha3(XI) subunits.

familynursing.name: family nursing
familynursing.definition: Family nursing is the provision of care involving the nursing process, to families and family members in health and illness situations. From Lippincott Manual of Nursing Practice. 6th ed.

nodsignalingadaptorproteins.name: nod signaling adaptor proteins
nodsignalingadaptorproteins.definition: Nod signaling adaptor proteins is cytosolic signaling adaptor proteins that were initially discovered by their role in the innate immunity (immunity, innate) response of organisms that lack an adaptive immune system. This class of proteins contains three domains, a C-terminal ligand recognition domain, an N-terminal effector-binding domain, and a centrally located nuclear-binding oligomerization domain. Many members of this class contain a C-terminal [MASK] rich domain which binds to peptidoglycan on the surface of bacteria and plays a role in pathogen resistance.

sequenceanalysis,protein.name: sequence analysis , protein
sequenceanalysis,protein.definition: Protein sequence analysis is a process that includes the determination of amino acid sequence of a protein (or peptide, oligopeptide or peptide fragment) and the information analysis of the sequence.

insurance,health.name: insurance , health
insurance,health.definition: Health insurance is insurance providing coverage of medical, surgical, or hospital care in general or for which there is no specific heading.

evokedpotentials,auditory,brainstem.name: evoked potentials , auditory , brain stem
evokedpotentials,auditory,brainstem.definition: Brain stem auditory evoked potentials is electrical waves in the cerebral cortex generated by brain stem structures in response to auditory click stimuli. These are found to be abnormal in many patients with cerebellopontine angle lesions, multiple [MASK], or other demyelinating diseases.

glycoproteins.name: glycoproteins
glycoproteins.definition: Glycoproteins is conjugated protein-carbohydrate compounds including mucins, mucoid, and amyloid glycoproteins.

intestinalmucosa.name: intestinal mucosa
intestinalmucosa.definition: Intestinal mucosa is lining of the intestines, consisting of an inner epithelium, a middle lamina propria, and an outer muscularis mucosae. In the small intestine, the mucosa is characterized by a series of folds and abundance of absorptive cells (enterocytes) with microvilli.

fertilizationinvitro.name: fertilization in vitro
fertilizationinvitro.definition: Fertilization in vitro is an assisted reproductive technique that includes the direct handling and manipulation of oocytes and sperm to achieve fertilization in vitro.

alumcompounds.name: alum compounds
alumcompounds.definition: Alum compounds is aluminum metal sulfate compounds used medically as astringents and for many industrial purposes. They are used in veterinary medicine for the treatment of ulcerative stomatitis, leukorrhea, conjunctivitis, pharyngitis, metritis, and minor wounds.

hydroxyacids.name: hydroxy acids
hydroxyacids.definition: Hydroxy acids is organic compounds containing both the hydroxyl and carboxyl radicals.

airwayobstruction.name: airway obstruction
airwayobstruction.definition: Airway obstruction is any hindrance to the passage of air into and out of the lungs.

rheumatoidfactor.name: rheumatoid factor
rheumatoidfactor.definition: Rheumatoid factor is antibodies found in adult rheumatoid arthritis patients that are directed against gamma-chain immunoglobulins.

petroleumpollution.name: petroleum pollution
petroleumpollution.definition: Petroleum pollution is release of oil into the environment usually due to human activity.

gastricartery.name: gastric artery
gastricartery.definition: Gastric artery is any of several branches of the splenic artery distributed to the greater curvature of the stomach.

colorectalsurgery.name: colorectal surgery
colorectalsurgery.definition: Colorectal surgery is a surgical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of disorders and abnormalities of the colon; rectum; and anal canal.

immunity,cellular.name: immunity , cellular
immunity,cellular.definition: Cellular immunity is manifestations of the immune response which are mediated by antigen-sensitized T-lymphocytes via lymphokines or direct cytotoxicity. This takes place in the absence of circulating antibody or where antibody plays a subordinate role.

generalpractice.name: general practice
generalpractice.definition: General practice is patient-based medical care provided across age and gender or specialty boundaries.

history,ancient.name: history , ancient
history,ancient.definition: Ancient history is the period of history before 500 of the common era.

purplemembrane.name: purple membrane
purplemembrane.definition: Purple membrane is functionally and structurally differentiated, purple-pigmented regions of the cytoplasmic membrane of some strains of Halobacterium halobium. The membrane develops under anaerobic conditions and is made almost entirely of the purple pigment bacteriorhodopsins. (From Singleton & Sainsbury Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

retinaldiseases.name: retinal diseases
retinaldiseases.definition: Retinal diseases is diseases involving the retina.

hostspecificity.name: host specificity
hostspecificity.definition: Host specificity is the properties of a pathogen that makes it capable of infecting one or more specific hosts. The pathogen can include parasites as well as viruses; bacteria; fungi; or plants.

populationgroup.name: population group
populationgroup.definition: Population group is individuals classified according to their [MASK], racial origin, religion, common place of living, financial or [MASK], or some other cultural or behavioral attribute.

dryice.name: dry ice
dryice.definition: Dry ice is a solid form of carbon dioxide used as a refrigerant.

ammoniumchloride.name: ammonium chloride
ammoniumchloride.definition: Ammonium chloride is an acidifying agent that has expectorant and diuretic effects. Also used in etching and batteries and as a flux in electroplating.

returntosport.name: return to sport
returntosport.definition: Return to sport is resumption of sporting activity following a hiatus or period of absence due to injury or other reasons.

therapeuticalliance.name: therapeutic alliance
therapeuticalliance.definition: Therapeutic alliance is a relational factor in counseling that includes three dimensions: goal [MASK] between counselor and client, collaboration on counseling-related tasks, and emotional bonding.  It is referred to as the working alliance between a therapist and a client in psychotherapy and closely correlated with positive client outcomes.

canada.name: canada
canada.definition: Canada is the largest country in North America, comprising 10 provinces and three territories. Its capital is Ottawa.

animalnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: animal nutritional physiological phenomena
animalnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Animal nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of animals.

rats,inbredbn.name: rats , inbred bn
rats,inbredbn.definition: Inbred bn rats is an inbred strain of rat that is widely used in a variety of research areas such as the study of asthma; carcinogenesis; aging; and leukemia.

cohorteffect.name: cohort effect
cohorteffect.definition: Cohort effect is variation in health status arising from different causal factors to which each birth cohort in a population is exposed as environment and society change.

tendoninjuries.name: tendon injuries
tendoninjuries.definition: Tendon injuries is injuries to the fibrous cords of connective tissue which attach muscles to bones or other structures.

visualcortex.name: visual cortex
visualcortex.definition: Visual cortex is area of the occipital lobe concerned with the processing of visual information relayed via visual pathways.

animalstructures.name: animal structures
animalstructures.definition: Animal structures is organs and other anatomical structures of non-human vertebrate and invertebrate animals.

healthservicesfortheaged.name: health services for the aged
healthservicesfortheaged.definition: Health services for the aged is services for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the aged and the maintenance of health in the elderly.

chromosomes,human,pair4.name: chromosomes , human , pair 4
chromosomes,human,pair4.definition: Pair 4 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group b chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

lunginjury.name: lung injury
lunginjury.definition: Lung injury is damage to any compartment of the lung caused by physical, chemical, or biological agents which characteristically elicit inflammatory reaction. These inflammatory reactions can either be acute and dominated by neutrophils, or chronic and dominated by lymphocytes and macrophages.

staphylococcus.name: staphylococcus
staphylococcus.definition: Staphylococcus is a genus of gram-positive, facultatively anaerobic, coccoid bacteria. Its organisms occur singly, in pairs, and in tetrads and characteristically divide in more than one plane to form irregular clusters. Natural populations of Staphylococcus are found on the skin and mucous membranes of warm-blooded animals. Some species are opportunistic pathogens of humans and animals.

chromatin.name: chromatin
chromatin.definition: Chromatin is the material of chromosomes. It is a complex of dna; histones; and nonhistone proteins (chromosomal proteins, non-histone) found within the nucleus of a cell.

colon,sigmoid.name: colon , sigmoid
colon,sigmoid.definition: Sigmoid colon is a segment of the colon between the rectum and the [MASK].

solutions.name: solutions
solutions.definition: Solutions is the homogeneous mixtures formed by the mixing of a solid, liquid, or gaseous substance (solute) with a liquid (the solvent), from which the dissolved substances can be recovered by physical processes. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

silverstaining.name: silver staining
silverstaining.definition: Silver staining is the use of silver, usually silver nitrate, as a reagent for producing contrast or coloration in tissue specimens.

hemoglobinm.name: hemoglobin m
hemoglobinm.definition: Hemoglobin m is a group of abnormal hemoglobins in which [MASK] take place in either the alpha or beta chains but near the heme iron. This results in facilitated oxidation of the hemoglobin to yield excess methemoglobin which leads to cyanosis.

abdominalobliquemuscles.name: abdominal oblique muscles
abdominalobliquemuscles.definition: Abdominal oblique muscles is muscles of the anterolateral [MASK] consisting of the external oblique and the internal oblique muscles. The external abdominal oblique muscle fibers extend from lower thoracic ribs to the linea alba and the iliac crest. The internal abdominal oblique extend superomedially beneath the external oblique muscles.

chromosomeinversion.name: chromosome inversion
chromosomeinversion.definition: Chromosome inversion is an aberration in which a chromosomal segment is deleted and reinserted in the same place but turned 180 degrees from its original orientation, so that the gene sequence for the segment is reversed with respect to that of the rest of the chromosome.

longitudinalstudies.name: longitudinal studies
longitudinalstudies.definition: Longitudinal studies is studies in which variables relating to an individual or group of individuals are assessed over a period of time.

spacemaintenance,orthodontic.name: space maintenance , orthodontic
spacemaintenance,orthodontic.definition: Orthodontic space maintenance is common treatment method used in pediatric dentistry that involves the use of fixed or removable space maintainers in order to keep the space left by a baby tooth safe in the event it is lost early. Space maintainers also help permanent teeth to grow safely.

bloodproteins.name: blood proteins
bloodproteins.definition: Blood proteins is proteins that are present in blood serum, including serum albumin; blood coagulation factors; and many other types of proteins.

rafkinases.name: raf kinases
rafkinases.definition: Raf kinases is a family of closely-related serine-threonine kinases that were originally identified as the cellular homologs of the retrovirus-derived v-raf kinases. They are map kinase kinase kinases that play important roles in signal transduction.

genes,immunoglobulinheavychain.name: genes , immunoglobulin heavy chain
genes,immunoglobulinheavychain.definition: [MASK] genes is genes and gene segments encoding the [MASK]. Gene segments of the heavy chain genes are symbolized v (variable), d (diversity), j (joining), and c (constant).

aldehydedehydrogenase1.name: aldehyde dehydrogenase 1
aldehydedehydrogenase1.definition: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 is a subfamily of the aldehyde dehydrogenase family of enzymes involved in the synthesis of acetate from ethanol.

epiduralneoplasms.name: epidural neoplasms
epiduralneoplasms.definition: Epidural neoplasms is neoplasms located in the space between the vertebral periosteum and dura mater surrounding the spinal cord. Tumors in this location are most often metastatic in origin and may cause neurologic deficits by mass effect on the spinal cord or nerve roots or by interfering with blood supply to the spinal cord.

nervegrowthfactors.name: nerve growth factors
nervegrowthfactors.definition: Nerve growth factors is factors which enhance the growth potentialities of sensory and sympathetic nerve cells.

aidsvaccines.name: aids vaccines
aidsvaccines.definition: Aids vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines containing inactivated hiv or some of its component antigens and designed to prevent or treat aids. Some vaccines containing antigens are recombinantly produced.

mercurypoisoning.name: mercury poisoning
mercurypoisoning.definition: Mercury poisoning is poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, [MASK], or skin absorption of mercury or mercury compounds.

lipoproteinlipaseactivators.name: lipoprotein lipase activators
lipoproteinlipaseactivators.definition: Lipoprotein lipase activators is compounds that increase the enzymatic activity of lipoprotein lipase. Lipoprotein lipase activators have a potential role in the treatment of obesity by increasing lipid metabolism. Note that substances that increase the synthesis of lipoprotein lipase are not included here.

pureautonomicfailure.name: pure autonomic failure
pureautonomicfailure.definition: Pure autonomic failure is a degenerative disease of the autonomic nervous system that is characterized by idiopathic orthostatic hypotension and a greatly reduced level of catecholamines. No other neurological deficits are present.

hematologicneoplasms.name: hematologic neoplasms
hematologicneoplasms.definition: Hematologic neoplasms is neoplasms located in the blood and blood-forming tissue (the bone marrow and lymphatic tissue). The commonest forms are the various types of leukemia, of lymphoma, and of the progressive, life-threatening forms of the myelodysplastic syndromes.

bronchialfistula.name: bronchial fistula
bronchialfistula.definition: Bronchial fistula is an abnormal passage or communication between a bronchus and another part of the body.

electrontransportchaincomplexproteins.name: electron transport chain complex proteins
electrontransportchaincomplexproteins.definition: [MASK] transport chain complex proteins is a complex of enzymes and proton pumps located on the inner membrane of the mitochondria and in bacterial membranes. The protein complex provides energy in the form of an electrochemical gradient, which may be used by either mitochondrial proton-translocating atpases or bacterial proton-translocating atpases.

stattranscriptionfactors.name: stat transcription factors
stattranscriptionfactors.definition: Stat transcription factors is a family of transcription factors containing sh2 domains that are involved in CYTOKINE-mediated signal transduction. stat transcription factors are recruited to the cytoplasmic region of cell surface receptors and are activated via phosphorylation. Once activated they dimerize and translocate into the cell nucleus where they influence gene expression. They play a role in regulating cell growth processes and cell differentiation. stat transcription factors are inhibited by suppressor of cytokine signaling proteins and protein inhibitors of activated stat.

prospectivepaymentassessmentcommission.name: prospective payment assessment commission
prospectivepaymentassessmentcommission.definition: Prospective payment assessment commission is the commission charged with evaluating issues and factors which affect the implementation of the prospective payment system.

livercirculation.name: liver circulation
livercirculation.definition: Liver circulation is the circulation of blood through the liver.

pesticides.name: pesticides
pesticides.definition: Pesticides is chemicals used to destroy pests of any sort. The concept includes fungicides (fungicides, industrial); insecticides; rodenticides; etc.

fracturefixation,internal.name: fracture fixation , internal
fracturefixation,internal.definition: Internal fracture fixation is the use of internal devices (metal plates, nails, rods, etc.) to hold the position of a fracture in proper alignment.

learningdisabilities.name: learning disabilities
learningdisabilities.definition: Learning disabilities is conditions characterized by a significant discrepancy between an individual's perceived level of intellect and their ability to acquire new language and other cognitive skills. These may result from organic or psychological conditions. Relatively common subtypes include dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dysgraphia.

fishoils.name: fish oils
fishoils.definition: Fish oils is oils high in unsaturated fats extracted from the bodies of fish or fish parts, especially the liver. Those from the liver are usually high in vitamin a. The oils are used as dietary supplements. They are also used in soaps and detergents and as protective coatings.

neuralcelladhesionmolecules.name: neural cell adhesion molecules
neuralcelladhesionmolecules.definition: Neural cell adhesion molecules is cell adhesion molecule involved in a diverse range of contact-mediated interactions among neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and myotubes. It is widely but transiently expressed in many tissues early in embryogenesis. Four main isoforms exist, including cd56; (cd56 antigen); but there are many other variants resulting from [MASK] and post-translational modifications. (From Pigott & Power, The Adhesion Molecule FactsBook, 1993, pp115-119)

librarymaterials.name: library materials
librarymaterials.definition: Library materials is print and non-print materials collected, processed, and stored by libraries. They comprise books, periodicals, pamphlets, reports, microforms, maps, manuscripts, motion pictures, and all other forms of audiovisual records. (Harrod, The Librarians' Glossary, 4th ed, p497)

nervesheathneoplasms.name: nerve sheath neoplasms
nervesheathneoplasms.definition: Nerve sheath neoplasms is neoplasms which arise from nerve sheaths formed by schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system or by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors, neurofibroma, and neurilemmoma are relatively common tumors in this category.

needles.name: needles
needles.definition: Needles is sharp instruments used for puncturing or suturing.

randomizedcontrolledtrialsastopic.name: randomized controlled trials as topic
randomizedcontrolledtrialsastopic.definition: Randomized controlled trials as topic is works about clinical trials that involve at least one test treatment and one control treatment, concurrent enrollment and follow-up of the test- and control-treated groups, and in which the treatments to be administered are selected by a random process, such as the use of a random-numbers [MASK].

equipmentdesign.name: equipment design
equipmentdesign.definition: Equipment design is methods and patterns of fabricating machines and related hardware.

sensorythresholds.name: sensory thresholds
sensorythresholds.definition: Sensory thresholds is the minimum amount of stimulus energy necessary to elicit a sensory response.

operativetime.name: operative time
operativetime.definition: Operative time is the duration of a surgical procedure in hours and minutes.

chronicpain.name: chronic pain
chronicpain.definition: Chronic pain is aching sensation that persists for more than a few months. It may or may not be associated with trauma or disease, and may persist after the initial injury has healed. Its localization, [MASK], and timing are more vague than with acute pain.

bronchialneoplasms.name: bronchial neoplasms
bronchialneoplasms.definition: Bronchial neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the bronchi.

librarysurveys.name: library surveys
librarysurveys.definition: Library surveys is collection and analysis of data pertaining to operations of a particular library, library system, or group of independent libraries, with recommendations for improvement and/or ordered plans for further development.

games,experimental.name: games , experimental
games,experimental.definition: Experimental games is games designed to provide information on hypotheses, policies, procedures, or strategies.

corebindingfactoralpha1subunit.name: core binding factor alpha 1 subunit
corebindingfactoralpha1subunit.definition: Core binding factor alpha 1 subunit is a transcription factor that dimerizes with core binding factor beta subunit to form core binding factor. It contains a highly conserved DNA-binding domain known as the runt domain and is involved in genetic regulation of skeletal development and cell differentiation.

antibodyformation.name: antibody formation
antibodyformation.definition: Antibody formation is the production of antibodies by proliferating and differentiated b-lymphocytes under stimulation by antigens.

apnea.name: apnea
apnea.definition: Apnea is a transient absence of spontaneous respiration.

totalqualitymanagement.name: total quality management
totalqualitymanagement.definition: Total quality management is the application of industrial management practice to systematically maintain and improve organization-wide performance. Effectiveness and success are determined and assessed by quantitative quality measures.

poreformingcytotoxicproteins.name: pore forming cytotoxic proteins
poreformingcytotoxicproteins.definition: Pore forming cytotoxic proteins is proteins secreted from an organism which form membrane-spanning pores in target cells to destroy them. This is in contrast to porins and membrane transport proteins that function within the synthesizing organism and complement immune proteins. These pore forming cytotoxic proteins are a form of primitive cellular defense which are also found in human lymphocytes.

cardiovasculardiseases.name: cardiovascular diseases
cardiovasculardiseases.definition: Cardiovascular diseases is pathological conditions involving the cardiovascular system including the heart; the blood vessels; or the pericardium.

molecularimaging.name: molecular imaging
molecularimaging.definition: Molecular imaging is the use of molecularly targeted imaging probes to localize and/or monitor biochemical and cellular processes via various imaging modalities that include radionuclide imaging; ultrasonography; magnetic resonance imaging; fluorescence imaging; and microscopy.

ischemicattack,transient.name: ischemic attack , transient
ischemicattack,transient.definition: Transient ischemic attack is brief reversible episodes of focal, nonconvulsive ischemic dysfunction of the brain having a duration of less than 24 hours, and usually less than one hour, caused by transient thrombotic or embolic blood vessel occlusion or stenosis. Events may be classified by arterial distribution, temporal pattern, or etiology (e.g., embolic vs. thrombotic). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp814-6)

formsastopic.name: forms as topic
formsastopic.definition: Forms as topic is works about documents used for acquiring particular information or for presenting particular information in a prescribed sequence and format, often with blank spaces or lines or other methods to prompt for insertion of the requested information.

activatingtranscriptionfactor4.name: activating transcription factor 4
activatingtranscriptionfactor4.definition: Activating transcription factor 4 is an activating transcription factor that regulates the expression of a variety of genes involved in amino acid metabolism and transport. It also interacts with htlv-i transactivator protein.

displacement,psychological.name: displacement , psychological
displacement,psychological.definition: Psychological displacement is the process by which an emotional or behavioral response that is appropriate for one situation appears in another situation for which it is inappropriate.

continentalpopulationgroups.name: continental population groups
continentalpopulationgroups.definition: Continental population groups is groups of individuals whose putative ancestry is from native continental populations based on similarities in physical appearance.

adenocarcinomaoflung.name: adenocarcinoma of lung
adenocarcinomaoflung.definition: Adenocarcinoma of lung is a carcinoma originating in the lung and the most common lung cancer type in never-smokers. Malignant cells exhibit distinct features such as glandular epithelial, or tubular morphology. Mutations in kras, egfr, braf, and erbb2 genes are associated with this cancer.

hospitals,psychiatric.name: hospitals , psychiatric
hospitals,psychiatric.definition: Psychiatric hospitals is special hospitals which provide care to the [MASK] patient.

primedinsitulabeling.name: primed in situ labeling
primedinsitulabeling.definition: Primed in situ labeling is a technique that labels specific sequences in whole chromosomes by in situ dna chain elongation or pcr (polymerase chain reaction).

bloodcirculation.name: blood circulation
bloodcirculation.definition: Blood circulation is the movement of the blood as it is pumped through the cardiovascular system.

fistula.name: fistula
fistula.definition: Fistula is abnormal communication most commonly seen between two internal organs, or between an internal organ and the surface of the body.

irisdiseases.name: iris diseases
irisdiseases.definition: Iris diseases is diseases, dysfunctions, or disorders of or located in the iris.

reproductivephysiologicalphenomena.name: reproductive physiological phenomena
reproductivephysiologicalphenomena.definition: Reproductive physiological phenomena is physiological processes, factors, properties and characteristics pertaining to reproduction.

coalmining.name: coal mining
coalmining.definition: Coal mining is the practice of extracting coal from the earth.

address.name: address
address.definition: Address is work consisting of speeches, orations, or written statements, usually formal, directed to a particular group of persons. These are different from a [MASK] that is usually delivered to classes for instructional purposes.

transcriptioninitiationsite.name: transcription initiation site
transcriptioninitiationsite.definition: Transcription initiation site is the first nucleotide of a transcribed dna sequence where rna polymerase (dna-directed rna polymerase) begins synthesizing the rna transcript.

accidentprevention.name: accident prevention
accidentprevention.definition: Accident prevention is efforts and designs to reduce the incidence of unexpected undesirable events in various environments and situations.

immunity,mucosal.name: immunity , mucosal
immunity,mucosal.definition: Mucosal immunity is nonsusceptibility to the pathogenic effects of foreign microorganisms or antigenic substances as a result of antibody secretions of the mucous membranes. Mucosal epithelia in the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and reproductive tracts produce a form of IgA (immunoglobulin a, secretory) that serves to protect these ports of entry into the body.

receptors,opioid,mu.name: receptors , opioid , mu
receptors,opioid,mu.definition: Mu opioid receptors is a class of opioid receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Mu opioid receptors bind, in decreasing order of affinity, endorphins, dynorphins, met-enkephalin, and leu-enkephalin. They have also been shown to be molecular receptors for [MASK].

relativevaluescales.name: relative value scales
relativevaluescales.definition: Relative value scales is coded listings of physician or other professional services using units that indicate the relative value of the various services they perform. They take into account time, skill, and overhead cost required for each service, but generally do not consider the relative cost-effectiveness. Appropriate conversion factors can be used to translate the [MASK] units of the relative value scales into dollar fees for each service based on work expended, practice costs, and training costs.

isolatedheartpreparation.name: isolated heart preparation
isolatedheartpreparation.definition: Isolated heart preparation is method of isolation and maintenance of a working heart for various cardiac measurements. The model allows for the separation of cardiac and systemic variables in the denervated heart.

conceptformation.name: concept formation
conceptformation.definition: Concept formation is a cognitive process involving the formation of ideas generalized from the knowledge of qualities, aspects, and relations of objects.

emergencymedicalservicecommunicationsyst.name: emergency medical service communication systems
emergencymedicalservicecommunicationsyst.definition: Emergency medical service communication systems is the use of communication systems, such as telecommunication, to transmit emergency information to appropriate providers of health services.

bevacizumab.name: bevacizumab
bevacizumab.definition: Bevacizumab is an anti-VEGF humanized murine monoclonal antibody. It inhibits vegf receptors and helps to prevent pathologic angiogenesis.

spermatozoa.name: spermatozoa
spermatozoa.definition: Spermatozoa is mature male germ cells derived from spermatids. As spermatids move toward the lumen of the seminiferous tubules, they undergo extensive structural changes including the loss of cytoplasm, condensation of chromatin into the sperm head, formation of the acrosome cap, the sperm midpiece and the sperm tail that provides motility.

congenitalhypothyroidism.name: congenital hypothyroidism
congenitalhypothyroidism.definition: Congenital hypothyroidism is a condition in infancy or early childhood due to an in-utero deficiency of thyroid hormones that can be caused by genetic or environmental factors, such as thyroid dysgenesis or hypothyroidism in infants of mothers treated with thiouracil during pregnancy. Endemic cretinism is the result of iodine deficiency. Clinical symptoms include severe mental retardation, impaired skeletal development, short stature, and myxedema.

committeemembership.name: committee membership
committeemembership.definition: Committee membership is the composition of a committee; the state or status of being a member of a committee.

expressedemotion.name: expressed emotion
expressedemotion.definition: Expressed emotion is a measurement of collective behavior and attitudes that exist towards a specific person—a measurement of the social environment or social relationships of an individual.

neoplasms,plasmacell.name: neoplasms , plasma cell
neoplasms,plasmacell.definition: Plasma cell neoplasms is neoplasms associated with a proliferation of a single clone of plasma cells and characterized by the secretion of paraproteins.

shortbowelsyndrome.name: short bowel syndrome
shortbowelsyndrome.definition: Short bowel syndrome is a malabsorption syndrome resulting from extensive operative resection of the small intestine, the absorptive region of the gastrointestinal tract.

sectranslocationchannels.name: sec translocation channels
sectranslocationchannels.definition: Sec translocation channels is universally conserved multiprotein complexes that form the protein transport channel of the general secretory (sec) pathway. The sec translocase is present in all bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes. It is in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane of eukaryotic cells, in the thylakoid membrane in chloroplasts and in some protozoa in the [MASK].

preservation,biological.name: preservation , biological
preservation,biological.definition: Biological preservation is the process of protecting various samples of biological material.

glucose.name: glucose
glucose.definition: Glucose is a primary source of energy for living organisms. It is naturally occurring and is found in fruits and other parts of plants in its free state. It is used therapeutically in fluid and nutrient replacement.

proteinsynthesisinhibitors.name: protein synthesis inhibitors
proteinsynthesisinhibitors.definition: Protein synthesis inhibitors is compounds which inhibit the synthesis of proteins. They are usually anti-bacterial agents or toxins. Mechanism of the action of inhibition includes the interruption of peptide-chain elongation, the blocking the a site of ribosomes, the misreading of the genetic code or the prevention of the attachment of oligosaccharide side chains to glycoproteins.

intensivecareunits,neonatal.name: intensive care units , neonatal
intensivecareunits,neonatal.definition: Neonatal intensive care units is hospital units providing continuing surveillance and care to acutely ill newborn infants.

autonomicnerveblock.name: autonomic nerve block
autonomicnerveblock.definition: Autonomic nerve block is interruption of sympathetic pathways, by local injection of an anesthetic agent, at any of four levels: peripheral nerve block, sympathetic ganglion block, extradural block, and subarachnoid block.

kneeinjuries.name: knee injuries
kneeinjuries.definition: [MASK] injuries is injuries to the [MASK] or the [MASK].

neoplasticsyndromes,hereditary.name: neoplastic syndromes , hereditary
neoplasticsyndromes,hereditary.definition: Hereditary neoplastic syndromes is the condition of a pattern of malignancies within a family, but not every individual's necessarily having the same neoplasm. Characteristically the tumor tends to occur at an earlier than average age, individuals may have more than one primary tumor, the tumors may be multicentric, usually more than 25 percent of the individuals in direct lineal descent from the proband are affected, and the cancer predisposition in these families behaves as an autosomal dominant trait with about 60 percent penetrance.

serineproteinaseinhibitors.name: serine proteinase inhibitors
serineproteinaseinhibitors.definition: Serine proteinase inhibitors is exogenous or endogenous compounds which inhibit serine endopeptidases.

benzylalcohols.name: benzyl alcohols
benzylalcohols.definition: Benzyl alcohols is alcohols derived from the aryl radical (c6h5ch2-) and defined by c6h5choh. The concept includes derivatives with any substituents on the benzene ring.

serotoninantagonists.name: serotonin antagonists
serotoninantagonists.definition: Serotonin antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate serotonin receptors, thereby blocking the actions of serotonin or serotonin receptor agonists.

vitaminddeficiency.name: vitamin d deficiency
vitaminddeficiency.definition: Vitamin d deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin d in the diet, insufficient production of vitamin d in the skin, inadequate absorption of vitamin d from the diet, or abnormal conversion of vitamin d to its bioactive metabolites. It is manifested clinically as rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1406)

nursingfacultypractice.name: nursing faculty practice
nursingfacultypractice.definition: Nursing faculty practice is clinical practice by members of the nursing faculty in order to maintain a balance in their nursing activities--clinical, education, and research.

tissueextracts.name: tissue extracts
tissueextracts.definition: Tissue extracts is preparations made from animal tissues or organs (animal structures). They usually contain many components, any one of which may be pharmacologically or physiologically active. Tissue extracts may contain specific, but uncharacterized factors or proteins with specific actions.

insulincoma.name: insulin coma
insulincoma.definition: Insulin coma is severe hypoglycemia induced by a large dose of exogenous insulin resulting in a coma or profound state of unconsciousness from which the individual cannot be aroused.

farms.name: farms
farms.definition: Farms is areas of land [MASK] aside to grow crops or raise livestock.

drugcontamination.name: drug contamination
drugcontamination.definition: Drug contamination is the presence of organisms, or any foreign material that makes a drug preparation impure.

caspaseactivationandrecruitmentdomain.name: caspase activation and recruitment domain
caspaseactivationandrecruitmentdomain.definition: Caspase activation and recruitment domain is a homotypic protein interaction module of the death domain superfamily. It is composed of a bundle of six alpha-helices that is related in sequence and structure to the death domain and [MASK]. The Caspase Activation and Recruitment Domain (card domain) typically associates with other CARD-containing proteins, forming either dimers or trimers. card domains may occur in isolation, or in combination with other domains in card signaling adaptor proteins and initiator caspases that function in apoptosis.

lightsignaltransduction.name: light signal transduction
lightsignaltransduction.definition: Light signal transduction is the conversion of absorbed light energy into molecular signals.

mentalrecall.name: mental recall
mentalrecall.definition: Mental recall is the process whereby a representation of past experience is elicited.

galactoseoxidase.name: galactose oxidase
galactoseoxidase.definition: Galactose oxidase is an enzyme that oxidizes galactose in the presence of molecular oxygen to D-galacto-hexodialdose. It is a [MASK] protein. ec 1.1.3.9.

watermicrobiology.name: water microbiology
watermicrobiology.definition: Water microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in water. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms.

epithelialsodiumchannelblockers.name: epithelial sodium channel blockers
epithelialsodiumchannelblockers.definition: [MASK] blockers is a subclass of sodium channel blockers that are specific for [MASK].

receptors,pheromone.name: receptors , pheromone
receptors,pheromone.definition: Pheromone receptors is cell surface receptors that respond to pheromones.

nurses,male.name: nurses , male
nurses,male.definition: Male nurses is nurses of the male [MASK].

carotidbody.name: carotid body
carotidbody.definition: Carotid body is a small cluster of chemoreceptive and supporting cells located near the bifurcation of the internal carotid artery. The carotid body, which is richly supplied with fenestrated capillaries, senses the pH, carbon dioxide, and oxygen concentrations in the blood and plays a crucial role in their homeostatic control.

healthfacilitysize.name: health facility size
healthfacilitysize.definition: Health facility size is the physical space or dimensions of a facility. Size may be indicated by bed capacity.

receptors,naturalkillercell.name: receptors , natural killer cell
receptors,naturalkillercell.definition: Natural killer cell receptors is receptors that are specifically found on the surface of natural killer cells. They play an important role in regulating the cellular component of innate immunity.

leginjuries.name: leg injuries
leginjuries.definition: Leg injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the leg.

panamericanhealthorganization.name: pan american health organization
panamericanhealthorganization.definition: Pan american health organization is who regional office for the Americas acting as a coordinating agency for the improvement of health conditions in the hemisphere. The four main functions are: control or eradication of communicable diseases, strengthening of national and local health services, education and training, and research.

insulatorelements.name: insulator elements
insulatorelements.definition: Insulator elements is nucleic acid regulatory sequences that limit or oppose the action of enhancer elements and define the boundary between differentially regulated gene loci.

creatinekinase,mitochondrialform.name: creatine kinase , mitochondrial form
creatinekinase,mitochondrialform.definition: Mitochondrial form creatine kinase is a form of creatine kinase found in the mitochondria.

earlygrowthresponsetranscriptionfactors.name: early growth response transcription factors
earlygrowthresponsetranscriptionfactors.definition: Early growth response transcription factors is a family of transcription factors that are induced by growth factors and contain a highly conserved DNA-binding domain composed of three zinc finger motifs.

planningtechniques.name: planning techniques
planningtechniques.definition: Planning techniques is procedures, strategies, and theories of planning.

reflex,abdominal.name: reflex , abdominal
reflex,abdominal.definition: Abdominal reflex is contractions of the abdominal muscles upon stimulation of the skin (superficial abdominal reflex) or tapping neighboring bony structures (deep abdominal reflex). The superficial reflex may be weak or absent, for example, after a stroke, a sign of upper (suprasegmental) motor neuron lesions. (Stedman, 25th ed & Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p1073)

diseasevectors.name: disease vectors
diseasevectors.definition: Disease vectors is invertebrates or non-human vertebrates which transmit infective organisms from one host to another.

granularcelltumor.name: granular cell tumor
granularcelltumor.definition: Granular cell tumor is unusual tumor affecting any site of the body, but most often encountered in the head and [MASK]. Considerable debate has surrounded the histogenesis of this neoplasm; however, it is considered to be a myoblastoma of, usually, a benign nature. It affects women more often than men. When it develops beneath the epidermis or mucous membrane, it can lead to proliferation of the squamous cells and mimic squamous cell carcinoma.

fibrin.name: fibrin
fibrin.definition: Fibrin is a protein derived from fibrinogen in the presence of thrombin, which forms part of the blood clot.

antigens,cd.name: antigens , cd
antigens,cd.definition: Cd antigens is differentiation antigens residing on mammalian leukocytes. cd stands for cluster of differentiation, which refers to groups of monoclonal antibodies that show similar reactivity with certain subpopulations of antigens of a particular lineage or differentiation stage. The subpopulations of antigens are also known by the same cd designation.

oilandgasfields.name: oil and gas fields
oilandgasfields.definition: Oil and gas fields is areas of the earth where hydrocarbon deposits of petroleum and/or natural gas are located.

chromosomes,human,pair11.name: chromosomes , human , pair 11
chromosomes,human,pair11.definition: Pair 11 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

adrenalhyperplasia,congenital.name: adrenal hyperplasia , congenital
adrenalhyperplasia,congenital.definition: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is a group of inherited disorders of the adrenal glands, caused by enzyme defects in the synthesis of cortisol (hydrocortisone) and/or aldosterone leading to accumulation of precursors for androgens. Depending on the hormone imbalance, congenital adrenal hyperplasia can be classified as [MASK]-wasting, hypertensive, virilizing, or feminizing. Defects in steroid 21-hydroxylase; steroid 11-beta-hydroxylase; steroid 17-alpha-hydroxylase; 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (3-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases); testosterone 5-alpha-reductase; or steroidogenic acute regulatory protein; among others, underlie these disorders.

yellowfever.name: yellow fever
yellowfever.definition: Yellow fever is an acute infectious disease primarily of the tropics, caused by a virus and transmitted to man by mosquitoes of the genera Aedes and Haemagogus. The severe form is characterized by fever, hemolytic jaundice, and renal damage.

sosresponse,genetics.name: sos response , genetics
sosresponse,genetics.definition: Genetics sos response is an error-prone mechanism or [MASK] of functions for repairing damaged microbial dna. sos functions (a concept reputedly derived from the sos of the international distress signal) are involved in dna repair and mutagenesis, in cell division inhibition, in recovery of normal physiological conditions after dna repair, and possibly in cell death when dna damage is extensive.

severedengue.name: severe dengue
severedengue.definition: Severe dengue is a virulent form of dengue characterized by thrombocytopenia and an increase in vascular permeability (grades i and ii) and distinguished by a positive pain test (e.g., [MASK]). When accompanied by shock (grades iii and iv), it is called dengue shock syndrome.

tokyo.name: tokyo
tokyo.definition: Tokyo is capital of the country of japan.

carrierproteins.name: carrier proteins
carrierproteins.definition: Carrier proteins is proteins that bind or transport specific substances in the blood, within the cell, or across cell membranes.

genitaldiseases,male.name: genital diseases , male
genitaldiseases,male.definition: Male genital diseases is pathological processes involving the male reproductive tract (genitalia, male).

spouseabuse.name: spouse abuse
spouseabuse.definition: Spouse abuse is deliberate severe and repeated injury to one domestic partner by the other.

taskperformanceandanalysis.name: task performance and analysis
taskperformanceandanalysis.definition: Task performance and analysis is the detailed examination of observable activity or behavior associated with the execution or completion of a required function or unit of work.

fattyliver.name: fatty liver
fattyliver.definition: Fatty liver is lipid infiltration of the hepatic parenchymal cells resulting in a yellow-colored liver. The abnormal lipid accumulation is usually in the form of triglycerides, either as a single large droplet or multiple small droplets. Fatty liver is caused by an imbalance in the metabolism of fatty acids.

costsavings.name: cost savings
costsavings.definition: Cost savings is reductions in all or any portion of the costs of providing goods or services. Savings may be incurred by the provider or the consumer.

biliarytract.name: biliary tract
biliarytract.definition: Biliary tract is the [MASK] and the gallbladder.

insurance,accident.name: insurance , accident
insurance,accident.definition: Accident insurance is insurance providing coverage for physical injury suffered as a result of unavoidable circumstances.

organisms,geneticallymodified.name: organisms , genetically modified
organisms,geneticallymodified.definition: Genetically modified organisms is organisms whose genome has been changed by a genetic engineering technique.

fishproducts.name: fish products
fishproducts.definition: Fish products is food products manufactured from fish (e.g., fish flour, fish meal).

muscleneoplasms.name: muscle neoplasms
muscleneoplasms.definition: Muscle neoplasms is tumors or cancer located in muscle tissue or specific muscles. They are differentiated from neoplasms, muscle tissue which are neoplasms composed of skeletal, cardiac, or smooth muscle tissue, such as myosarcoma or leiomyoma.

toothattrition.name: tooth attrition
toothattrition.definition: Tooth attrition is the wearing away of a tooth as a result of tooth-to-tooth contact, as in mastication, occurring only on the occlusal, incisal, and proximal surfaces. It is chiefly associated with aging. It is differentiated from tooth abrasion (the pathologic wearing away of the tooth substance by friction, as brushing, bruxism, clenching, and other mechanical causes) and from tooth erosion (the loss of substance caused by chemical action without bacterial action). (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p86)

healthservicesaccessibility.name: health services accessibility
healthservicesaccessibility.definition: Health services accessibility is the degree to which individuals are inhibited or facilitated in their ability to gain entry to and to receive care and services from the health care system. Factors influencing this ability include geographic, architectural, transportational, and financial considerations, among others.
