hospitals,private.name: hospitals , private
hospitals,private.definition: Private hospitals is a class of hospitals that includes profit or not-for-profit hospitals that are controlled by a legal entity other than a government agency. (Hospital Administration Terminology, aha, 2d ed)

healthyaging.name: healthy aging
healthyaging.definition: Healthy aging is the development and maintenance of optimal physical, mental, spiritual, and social well-being and function with advancing age.

ophthalmology.name: ophthalmology
ophthalmology.definition: Ophthalmology is a surgical specialty concerned with the structure and function of the eye and the medical and surgical treatment of its defects and diseases.

erythrocyteaging.name: erythrocyte aging
erythrocyteaging.definition: Erythrocyte aging is the senescence of red blood cells. Lacking the organelles that make protein synthesis possible, the mature erythrocyte is incapable of self-repair, reproduction, and carrying out certain functions performed by other cells. This limits the average life span of an erythrocyte to 120 days.

sulfatetransporters.name: sulfate transporters
sulfatetransporters.definition: Sulfate transporters is highly conserved families of transmembrane anion transporters that occur in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. In humans, they are expressed by epithelial cells in a variety of tissues and participate in diverse physiologic functions such as cell motility and regulating the composition and acidity of body fluids. Some Slc13 family proteins function as sodium ion-coupled co-transporters of sulfate and other anions.

cyclicamp.name: cyclic amp
cyclicamp.definition: Cyclic amp is an adenine nucleotide containing one phosphate group which is esterified to both the 3'- and 5'-positions of the sugar moiety. It is a second messenger and a key intracellular regulator, functioning as a mediator of activity for a number of hormones, including epinephrine, glucagon, and acth.

ganglia,sympathetic.name: ganglia , sympathetic
ganglia,sympathetic.definition: Sympathetic ganglia is ganglia of the sympathetic nervous system including the paravertebral and the prevertebral ganglia. Among these are the sympathetic chain ganglia, the superior, middle, and inferior cervical ganglia, and the aorticorenal, celiac, and stellate ganglia.

parasiticdiseases,animal.name: parasitic diseases , animal
parasiticdiseases,animal.definition: Animal parasitic diseases is animal diseases caused by parasites.

orthopedicequipment.name: orthopedic equipment
orthopedicequipment.definition: Orthopedic equipment is nonexpendable items used in the performance of orthopedic surgery and related therapy. They are differentiated from orthotic devices, apparatus used to prevent or correct deformities in patients.

epidermalgrowthfactor.name: epidermal growth factor
epidermalgrowthfactor.definition: Epidermal growth factor is a 6-kDa polypeptide growth factor initially discovered in mouse submaxillary glands. Human epidermal growth factor was originally isolated from urine based on its ability to inhibit gastric secretion and called urogastrone. Epidermal growth factor exerts a wide variety of biological effects including the promotion of proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal and epithelial cells. It is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which can be cleaved to release a soluble active form.

nuclearfusion.name: nuclear fusion
nuclearfusion.definition: Nuclear fusion is thermonuclear reaction in which the nuclei of an element of low atomic weight unite under extremely high temperature and pressure to form a nucleus of a heavier atom.

ganglia,autonomic.name: ganglia , autonomic
ganglia,autonomic.definition: Autonomic ganglia is clusters of neurons and their processes in the autonomic nervous system. In the autonomic ganglia, the preganglionic fibers from the central nervous system synapse onto the neurons whose axons are the postganglionic fibers innervating target organs. The ganglia also contain intrinsic neurons and supporting cells and preganglionic fibers passing through to other ganglia.

corebindingfactoralphasubunits.name: core binding factor alpha subunits
corebindingfactoralphasubunits.definition: Core binding factor alpha subunits is a family of transcription factors that bind to the cofactor core binding factor beta subunit to form core binding factor. Family members contain a highly conserved DNA-binding domain known as the runt domain. They can act as both activators and repressors of expression of genes involved in cell differentiation and cell cycle progression.

fertilization.name: fertilization
fertilization.definition: Fertilization is the fusion of a spermatozoon (spermatozoa) with an ovum thus resulting in the formation of a zygote.

skullfracture,depressed.name: skull fracture , depressed
skullfracture,depressed.definition: Depressed skull fracture is a skull fracture characterized by inward depression of a fragment or section of cranial bone, often compressing the underlying dura mater and brain. Depressed cranial fractures which feature open skin wounds that communicate with skull fragments are referred to as compound depressed skull fractures.

oils,volatile.name: oils , volatile
oils,volatile.definition: Volatile oils is oils which evaporate readily. The volatile oils occur in aromatic plants, to which they give odor and other characteristics. Most volatile oils consist of a mixture of two or more terpenes or of a mixture of an eleoptene (the more volatile constituent of a volatile oil) with a stearopten (the more solid constituent). The synonym essential oils refers to the essence of a plant, as its perfume or scent, and not to its indispensability.

evokedpotentials,somatosensory.name: evoked potentials , somatosensory
evokedpotentials,somatosensory.definition: Somatosensory evoked potentials is the electric response evoked in the cerebral cortex by stimulation along afferent pathways from peripheral nerves to cerebrum.

perioperativenursing.name: perioperative nursing
perioperativenursing.definition: Perioperative nursing is nursing care of the surgical patient before, during, and after surgery.

puberty.name: puberty
puberty.definition: Puberty is a period in the human life in which the development of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal system takes place and reaches full maturity. The onset of synchronized endocrine events in puberty lead to the capacity for reproduction (fertility), development of secondary [MASK] characteristics, and other changes seen in adolescent development.

chemicalhazardrelease.name: chemical hazard release
chemicalhazardrelease.definition: Chemical hazard release is uncontrolled release of a chemical from its containment that either threatens to or causes exposure to a chemical hazard. Such an incident may occur accidentally or deliberately.

proteolysis.name: proteolysis
proteolysis.definition: Proteolysis is cleavage of proteins into smaller peptides or amino acids either by proteases or non-enzymatically (e.g., Hydrolysis). It does not include Protein Processing, Post-Translational.

chromosomes,human,1-3.name: chromosomes , human , 1-3
chromosomes,human,1-3.definition: 1-3 human chromosomes is the large, metacentric human chromosomes, called group a in the human chromosome classification. This group consists of chromosome pairs 1, 2, and 3.

dentalimpressionmaterials.name: dental impression materials
dentalimpressionmaterials.definition: Dental impression materials is substances used to create an impression, or negative reproduction, of the teeth and dental arches. These materials include dental plasters and cements, metallic oxide pastes, silicone base materials, or elastomeric materials.

electronicnose.name: electronic nose
electronicnose.definition: Electronic nose is a device used to detect airborne odors, gases, flavors, volatile substances or vapors.

nuclearrespiratoryfactors.name: nuclear respiratory factors
nuclearrespiratoryfactors.definition: Nuclear respiratory factors is a family of transcription factors that control expression of a variety of nuclear genes encoding proteins that function in the respiratory chain of the mitochondria.

vaccines.name: vaccines
vaccines.definition: Vaccines is suspensions of killed or attenuated microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa), antigenic proteins,  synthetic constructs, or other bio-molecular derivatives, administered for the prevention, amelioration, or treatment of infectious and other diseases.

transforminggrowthfactoralpha.name: transforming growth factor alpha
transforminggrowthfactoralpha.definition: Transforming growth factor alpha is an epidermal growth factor related protein that is found in a variety of tissues including epithelium, and maternal decidua. It is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which can be cleaved to release a soluble active form which binds to the [MASK].

animals,domestic.name: animals , domestic
animals,domestic.definition: Domestic animals is animals which have become adapted through breeding in captivity to a life intimately associated with humans. They include animals domesticated by humans to live and breed in a tame condition on farms or ranches for economic reasons, including livestock (specifically cattle; sheep; horses; etc.), poultry; and those raised or kept for pleasure and companionship, e.g., pets; or specifically dogs; cats; etc.

refractivesurgicalprocedures.name: refractive surgical procedures
refractivesurgicalprocedures.definition: Refractive surgical procedures is surgical procedures employed to correct [MASK] such as myopia; hyperopia; or astigmatism. These may involve altering the curvature of the cornea; removal or replacement of the crystalline lens; or modification of the sclera to change the axial length of the eye.

patientadmission.name: patient admission
patientadmission.definition: Patient admission is the process of accepting patients. The concept includes patients accepted for medical and nursing care in a hospital or other health care institution.

geneexpressionregulation,viral.name: gene expression regulation , viral
geneexpressionregulation,viral.definition: Viral gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which cytoplasmic factors influence the differential control of gene action in viruses.

receptors,growthfactor.name: receptors , growth factor
receptors,growthfactor.definition: Growth factor receptors is cell surface receptors that bind growth or trophic factors with high affinity, triggering intracellular responses which influence the growth, differentiation, or survival of cells.

psychology,applied.name: psychology , applied
psychology,applied.definition: Applied psychology is the science which utilizes psychologic principles to derive more effective means in dealing with practical problems.

burnout,psychological.name: burnout , psychological
burnout,psychological.definition: Psychological burnout is an excessive reaction to stress caused by one's environment that may be characterized by feelings of emotional and physical exhaustion, coupled with a sense of frustration and failure.

publicfacilities.name: public facilities
publicfacilities.definition: Public facilities is any facility  owned, leased, or otherwise operated, or funded by a governmental body or public entity.

carboncycle.name: carbon cycle
carboncycle.definition: Carbon cycle is the cycle by which the element carbon is exchanged between organic matter and the earth's physical environment.

cationtransportproteins.name: cation transport proteins
cationtransportproteins.definition: Cation transport proteins is membrane proteins whose primary function is to facilitate the transport of positively charged molecules (cations) across a biological membrane.

ironregulatoryprotein1.name: iron regulatory protein 1
ironregulatoryprotein1.definition: Iron regulatory protein 1 is a multifunctional iron-sulfur protein that is both an iron regulatory protein and cytoplasmic form of aconitate hydratase. It binds to iron regulatory elements found on mRNAs involved in iron metabolism and regulates their translation. Its rna binding ability and its aconitate hydrolase activity are dependent upon availability of iron.

creatinine.name: creatinine
creatinine.definition: Creatinine is a byproduct of a chemical compound called creatine, which helps muscles get the energy that they need.

mandibularneoplasms.name: mandibular neoplasms
mandibularneoplasms.definition: Mandibular neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the mandible.

chitosan.name: chitosan
chitosan.definition: Chitosan is deacetylated chitin, a linear polysaccharide of deacetylated beta-1,4-D-glucosamine. It is used in [MASK] and to treat wounds.

autonomicnervoussystem.name: autonomic nervous system
autonomicnervoussystem.definition: Autonomic nervous system is the enteric nervous system; parasympathetic nervous system; and sympathetic nervous system taken together. Generally speaking, the autonomic nervous system regulates the internal environment during both peaceful activity and physical or emotional stress. Autonomic activity is controlled and integrated by the central nervous system, especially the hypothalamus and the solitary nucleus, which receive information relayed from visceral afferents.

populationgroups.name: population groups
populationgroups.definition: Population groups is individuals classified according to their [MASK], racial origin, religion, common place of living, financial or [MASK], or some other cultural or behavioral attribute. ([MASK], 2003)

thalamicnuclei.name: thalamic nuclei
thalamicnuclei.definition: Thalamic nuclei is several groups of nuclei in the thalamus that serve as the major relay centers for sensory impulses in the brain.

economicdevelopment.name: economic development
economicdevelopment.definition: Economic development is mobilization of human, financial, capital, physical and or natural resources to generate goods and services.

intracranialhemorrhage,hypertensive.name: intracranial hemorrhage , hypertensive
intracranialhemorrhage,hypertensive.definition: Hypertensive intracranial hemorrhage is bleeding within the skull that is caused by systemic hypertension, usually in association with intracranial arteriosclerosis. Hypertensive hemorrhages are most frequent in the basal ganglia; cerebellum; pons; and thalamus; but may also involve the cerebral cortex, subcortical [MASK] matter, and other brain structures.

nervecompressionsyndromes.name: nerve compression syndromes
nervecompressionsyndromes.definition: Nerve compression syndromes is mechanical compression of nerves or nerve roots from internal or external causes. These may result in a conduction block to nerve impulses (due to myelin sheath dysfunction) or axonal loss. The nerve and nerve sheath injuries may be caused by ischemia; inflammation; or a direct mechanical effect.

happiness.name: happiness
happiness.definition: Happiness is highly pleasant emotion characterized by outward manifestations of gratification.

hottemperature.name: hot temperature
hottemperature.definition: Hot temperature is presence of warmth or heat or a temperature notably higher than an accustomed norm.

maxillaryartery.name: maxillary artery
maxillaryartery.definition: Maxillary artery is a branch of the external carotid artery which distributes to the deep structures of the face (internal maxillary) and to the side of the face and nose (external maxillary).

iris.name: iris
iris.definition: Iris is the most anterior portion of the uveal layer, separating the anterior chamber from the posterior. It consists of two layers - the stroma and the pigmented epithelium. [MASK] of the iris depends on the amount of melanin in the stroma on reflection from the pigmented epithelium.

collectivebargaining.name: collective bargaining
collectivebargaining.definition: Collective bargaining is the process of negotiation between representatives of an employee organization, association or union, and representatives of the employer.

transitiontemperature.name: transition temperature
transitiontemperature.definition: Transition temperature is the temperature at which a substance changes from one state or conformation of matter to another.

seniorcenters.name: senior centers
seniorcenters.definition: Senior centers is community centers for older adults and providers of resources for the community. In addition to providing services and activities for older adults that reflect the community's diversity, they link participants with resources offered by other agencies.

fluoresceinangiography.name: fluorescein angiography
fluoresceinangiography.definition: Fluorescein angiography is visualization of a vascular system after intravenous injection of a fluorescein solution. The images may be photographed or televised. It is used especially in studying the retinal and uveal vasculature.

pleuraleffusion,malignant.name: pleural effusion , malignant
pleuraleffusion,malignant.definition: Malignant pleural effusion is presence of fluid in the pleural cavity as a complication of malignant disease. Malignant pleural effusions often contain actual malignant cells.

flowinjectionanalysis.name: flow injection analysis
flowinjectionanalysis.definition: Flow injection analysis is the analysis of a chemical substance by inserting a sample into a carrier [MASK] of reagent using a sample injection valve that propels the sample downstream where mixing occurs in a coiled tube, then passes into a flow-through detector and a recorder or other data handling device.

professionalimpairment.name: professional impairment
professionalimpairment.definition: Professional impairment is the inability of a health professional to provide proper professional care of patients due to his or her physical and/or mental disability.

vascularring.name: vascular ring
vascularring.definition: Vascular ring is congenital vascular malformation in which the aorta arch and its branches encircle the [MASK] and esophagus. Signs and symptoms include dyspnea; respiratory sounds, especially with eating, dysphagia, persistent [MASK], and gastroesophageal reflux or may be asymptomatic. Two most common types are double aortic arch and right aortic arch. It may be associated with other anomalies (e.g., digeorge syndrome).

intraoperativecomplications.name: intraoperative complications
intraoperativecomplications.definition: Intraoperative complications is complications that affect patients during surgery. They may or may not be associated with the disease for which the surgery is done, or within the same surgical procedure.

adaptorproteincomplexsigmasubunits.name: adaptor protein complex sigma subunits
adaptorproteincomplexsigmasubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex sigma subunits is a family of small adaptin protein complex subunits of approximately 19 KDa in size.

spinalcorddiseases.name: spinal cord diseases
spinalcorddiseases.definition: Spinal cord diseases is pathologic conditions which feature spinal cord damage or dysfunction, including disorders involving the meninges and perimeningeal spaces surrounding the spinal cord. Traumatic injuries, vascular diseases, infections, and inflammatory/autoimmune processes may affect the spinal cord.

smallbusiness.name: small business
smallbusiness.definition: Small business is for-profit enterprise with relatively few to moderate number of employees and low to moderate volume of sales.

radioactivepollutants.name: radioactive pollutants
radioactivepollutants.definition: Radioactive pollutants is radioactive substances which act as pollutants. They include chemicals whose radiation is released via [MASK], nuclear accidents, fallout from nuclear explosions, and the like.

irisneoplasms.name: iris neoplasms
irisneoplasms.definition: Iris neoplasms is tumors of the iris characterized by increased pigmentation of melanocytes. Iris nevi are composed of proliferated melanocytes and are associated with neurofibromatosis and malignant melanoma of the choroid and [MASK]. Malignant melanoma of the iris often originates from preexisting nevi.

cochleardiseases.name: cochlear diseases
cochleardiseases.definition: Cochlear diseases is pathological processes of the snail-like structure (cochlea) of the [MASK] ([MASK]) which can involve its nervous tissue, blood vessels, or fluid (endolymph).

hiv.name: hiv
hiv.definition: Hiv is human immunodeficiency virus. a non-taxonomic and historical term referring to any of two species, specifically hiv-1 and/or hiv-2. Prior to 1986, this was called human T-lymphotropic virus type III/lymphadenopathy-associated virus (htlv-iii/lav). From 1986-1990, it was an official species called hiv. Since 1991, hiv was no longer considered an official species name; the two species were designated hiv-1 and hiv-2.

embryoculturetechniques.name: embryo culture techniques
embryoculturetechniques.definition: Embryo culture techniques is the technique of maintaining or growing mammalian embryos in vitro. This method offers an opportunity to observe embryonic development; metabolism; and susceptibility to teratogens.

hand,footandmouthdisease.name: hand , foot and mouth disease
hand,footandmouthdisease.definition: [MASK] and mouth disease hand is a mild, highly infectious viral disease of children, characterized by vesicular lesions in the mouth and on the hands and [MASK]. It is caused by coxsackieviruses a.

postoperativecognitivecomplications.name: postoperative cognitive complications
postoperativecognitivecomplications.definition: Postoperative cognitive complications is cognitive impairment or functional decline after a surgical procedure.

vitamink2.name: vitamin k 2
vitamink2.definition: Vitamin k 2 is a group of substances similar to [MASK] which contains a ring of 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinione and an isoprenoid side chain of varying number of isoprene units. In vitamin k 2, each isoprene unit contains a double bond. They are produced by bacteria including the normal intestinal flora.

medicalstaff.name: medical staff
medicalstaff.definition: Medical staff is professional medical personnel who provide care to patients in an organized facility, institution or agency.

vietnam.name: vietnam
vietnam.definition: Vietnam is a country in southeastern Asia, bordering the Gulf of Thailand, Gulf of Tonkin, and South China Sea, as well as China, Laos, and Cambodia. The capital is Hanoi.

writing.name: writing
writing.definition: Writing is the act or practice of literary composition, the occupation of writer, or producing or engaging in literary work as a profession.

vaginalneoplasms.name: vaginal neoplasms
vaginalneoplasms.definition: Vaginal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the vagina.

neoplasms,unknownprimary.name: neoplasms , unknown primary
neoplasms,unknownprimary.definition: Unknown primary neoplasms is metastases in which the tissue of origin is unknown.

exercisetest.name: exercise test
exercisetest.definition: Exercise test is controlled physical activity which is performed in order to allow assessment of physiological functions, particularly cardiovascular and pulmonary, but also aerobic capacity. Maximal (most intense) exercise is usually required but submaximal exercise is also used.

occupations.name: occupations
occupations.definition: Occupations is crafts, trades, professions, or other means of earning a living.

cardiacrehabilitation.name: cardiac rehabilitation
cardiacrehabilitation.definition: Cardiac rehabilitation is restoration of functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from a cardiovascular disease. It also includes cardiac conditioning and secondary prevention in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk profile.

myocardium.name: myocardium
myocardium.definition: Myocardium is the muscle tissue of the heart. It is composed of striated, involuntary muscle cells ([MASK]) connected to form the contractile pump to generate blood flow.

fueloils.name: fuel oils
fueloils.definition: Fuel oils is complex petroleum hydrocarbons consisting mainly of residues from crude oil distillation. These liquid products include [MASK] oils, stove oils, and furnace oils and are burned to generate energy.

adaptation,biological.name: adaptation , biological
adaptation,biological.definition: Biological adaptation is changes in biological features that help an organism cope with its environment. These changes include physiological (adaptation, physiological), phenotypic and genetic changes.

stress,mechanical.name: stress , mechanical
stress,mechanical.definition: Mechanical stress is a purely physical condition which exists within any material because of strain or deformation by external forces or by non-uniform thermal expansion; expressed quantitatively in units of force per unit area.

rna,circular.name: rna , circular
rna,circular.definition: Circular rna is rna molecules in which the 3' and 5' ends are covalently joined to form a closed continuous loop. They are resistant to [MASK] by exoribonucleases.

surgerydepartment,hospital.name: surgery department , hospital
surgerydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital surgery department is hospital department which administers all departmental functions and the provision of surgical diagnostic and therapeutic services.

diamond.name: diamond
diamond.definition: Diamond is diamond. a crystalline form of carbon that occurs as hard, colorless or tinted isomeric crystals. It is used as a precious stone, for cutting glass, and as bearings for delicate mechanisms. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

perception.name: perception
perception.definition: Perception is the process by which the nature and meaning of sensory stimuli are recognized and interpreted.

feedback,physiological.name: feedback , physiological
feedback,physiological.definition: Physiological [MASK] is a mechanism of communication with a physiological system for homeostasis, adaptation, etc. Physiological [MASK] is mediated through extensive [MASK] mechanisms that use physiological cues as [MASK] loop signals to control other systems.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 8
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyg.definition: Member 8 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter, sub-family g protein that functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g, member 5 in the selective transport of dietary cholesterol and phytosterols into and export out of enterocytes. It also functions in selective sterol excretion by the liver into [MASK].

systemicinflammatoryresponsesyndrome.name: systemic inflammatory response syndrome
systemicinflammatoryresponsesyndrome.definition: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome is a systemic inflammatory response to a variety of clinical insults, characterized by two or more of the following conditions: (1) fever >38 degrees c or hypothermia <36 degrees c; (2) tachycardia >90 beat/minute; (3) tachypnea >24 breaths/minute; (4) leukocytosis >12,000 cells/cubic mm or 10% immature forms. While usually related to infection, sirs can also be associated with noninfectious insults such as trauma; burns; or pancreatitis. If infection is involved, a patient with sirs is said to have sepsis.

programming,linear.name: programming , linear
programming,linear.definition: Linear programming is a technique of operations research for solving certain kinds of problems involving many variables where a best value or [MASK] of best values is to be found. It is most likely to be feasible when the quantity to be optimized, sometimes called the objective function, can be stated as a mathematical expression in terms of the various activities within the system, and when this expression is simply proportional to the measure of the activities, i.e., is linear, and when all the restrictions are also linear. It is different from computer programming, although problems using linear programming techniques may be programmed on a computer.

pregnancy,ovarian.name: pregnancy , ovarian
pregnancy,ovarian.definition: Ovarian pregnancy is a type of pregnancy in which embryo implantation occurs in an ovary instead of in the uterine cavity.

heme.name: heme
heme.definition: Heme is the [MASK]-furnishing portion of hemoglobin. It is found free in tissues and as the prosthetic group in many hemeproteins.

backinjuries.name: back injuries
backinjuries.definition: Back injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the posterior part of the trunk. It includes injuries to the muscles of the back.

communityhealthcenters.name: community health centers
communityhealthcenters.definition: Community health centers is facilities which administer the delivery of health care services to people living in a community or neighborhood.

standardofcare.name: standard of care
standardofcare.definition: Standard of care is the minimum acceptable patient care, based on statutes, court decisions, policies, or professional guidelines.

maternaldeath.name: maternal death
maternaldeath.definition: Maternal death is the death of the female parent.

guaninenucleotidedissociationinhibitors.name: guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitors
guaninenucleotidedissociationinhibitors.definition: Guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitors is protein factors that inhibit the dissociation of gdp from gtp-binding proteins.

opticalfibers.name: optical fibers
opticalfibers.definition: Optical fibers is thin strands of transparent material, usually glass, that are used for transmitting light waves over long distances.

personalityinventory.name: personality inventory
personalityinventory.definition: Personality inventory is check list, usually to be filled out by a person about himself, consisting of many statements about personal characteristics which the subject checks.

glutamatedehydrogenase.name: glutamate dehydrogenase
glutamatedehydrogenase.definition: Glutamate dehydrogenase is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of L-glutamate and water to 2-oxoglutarate and nh3 in the presence of nad+. (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992) ec 1.4.1.2.

thoracicduct.name: thoracic duct
thoracicduct.definition: Thoracic duct is the largest lymphatic vessel that passes through the chest and drains into the subclavian vein.

controlledclinicaltrial.name: controlled clinical trial
controlledclinicaltrial.definition: Controlled clinical trial is a work that reports on a clinical trial involving one or more test treatments, at least one control treatment, specified outcome measures for evaluating the studied intervention, and a bias-free method for assigning patients to the test treatment. The treatment may be drugs, devices, or procedures studied for diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic effectiveness. Control measures include placebos, active medicine, no-treatment, dosage forms and regimens, historical comparisons, etc. When randomization using mathematical techniques, such as the use of a random numbers [MASK], is employed to assign patients to test or control treatments, the trial is characterized as a randomized controlled trial.

indexoforthodontictreatmentneed.name: index of orthodontic treatment need
indexoforthodontictreatmentneed.definition: Index of orthodontic treatment need is a dental health survey developed to evaluate a patient's orthodontic treatment need and priority for orthodontic care. The index is based on an assessment of degree of malocclusion and the potential aesthetic and dental [MASK] of the treatment under consideration.

education,dental,continuing.name: education , dental , continuing
education,dental,continuing.definition: Continuing dental education is educational programs designed to inform dentists of recent advances in their fields.

bonemarrowstromalantigen2.name: bone marrow stromal antigen 2
bonemarrowstromalantigen2.definition: Bone marrow stromal antigen 2 is a GPI-linked membrane glycoprotein and antiviral factor that functions as a homodimer. It is induced by interferon-gamma and blocks the release of enveloped mammalian viruses by directly tethering nascent viral particles to the membranes of infected cells.

extracellulartraps.name: extracellular traps
extracellulartraps.definition: Extracellular traps is extracellular structure primarily composed of chromatin and associated proteases.

americanheartassociation.name: american heart association
americanheartassociation.definition: American heart association is a voluntary organization concerned with the prevention and treatment of heart and vascular diseases.

sodiumcompounds.name: sodium compounds
sodiumcompounds.definition: Sodium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain sodium as an integral part of the molecule.

receptors,serotonin.name: receptors , serotonin
receptors,serotonin.definition: Serotonin receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind serotonin and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Several types of serotonin receptors have been recognized which differ in their pharmacology, molecular biology, and mode of action.

democracy.name: democracy
democracy.definition: Democracy is a system of government in which there is free and equal participation by the people in the political decision-making process.

adrenalcortex.name: adrenal cortex
adrenalcortex.definition: Adrenal cortex is the outer layer of the adrenal gland. It is derived from mesoderm and comprised of three zones (outer zona glomerulosa, middle zona fasciculata, and inner zona reticularis) with each producing various steroids preferentially, such as aldosterone; hydrocortisone; dehydroepiandrosterone; and androstenedione. Adrenal cortex function is regulated by pituitary adrenocorticotropin.

digestivesystemfistula.name: digestive system fistula
digestivesystemfistula.definition: Digestive system fistula is an abnormal passage communicating between any components of the digestive system, or between any part of the digestive system and surrounding organ(s).

endovascularprocedures.name: endovascular procedures
endovascularprocedures.definition: Endovascular procedures is minimally invasive procedures, diagnostic or therapeutic, performed within the blood vessels. They may be perfomed via angioscopy; [MASK]; interventional radiography; or [MASK].

microscopy,confocal.name: microscopy , confocal
microscopy,confocal.definition: Confocal microscopy is a light microscopic technique in which only a small spot is illuminated and observed at a time. An image is constructed through point-by-point scanning of the field in this manner. Light sources may be conventional or laser, and fluorescence or transmitted observations are possible.

pregnancyoutcome.name: pregnancy outcome
pregnancyoutcome.definition: Pregnancy outcome is results of conception and ensuing pregnancy, including live birth; stillbirth; or spontaneous abortion. The outcome may follow natural or artificial insemination or any of the various assisted reproductive techniques, such as embryo transfer or fertilization in vitro.

musclerigidity.name: muscle rigidity
musclerigidity.definition: Muscle rigidity is continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction which is often a manifestation of basal ganglia diseases. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p73)

mouseembryonicstemcells.name: mouse embryonic stem cells
mouseembryonicstemcells.definition: Mouse embryonic stem cells is pluripotent stem cells derived from the blastocyst inner cell mass of day 3.5 mouse embryos.

israel.name: israel
israel.definition: Israel is a country in the Middle East, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between [MASK] and Lebanon. The capital is Jerusalem.

commondataelements.name: common data elements
commondataelements.definition: Common data elements is data elements that are common to multiple data sets across different studies.

cellpolarity.name: cell polarity
cellpolarity.definition: Cell polarity is orientation of intracellular structures especially with respect to the apical and basolateral domains of the plasma membrane. Polarized cells must direct proteins from the Golgi apparatus to the appropriate domain since tight junctions prevent proteins from diffusing between the two domains.

palate.name: palate
palate.definition: Palate is the structure that forms the roof of the mouth. It consists of the anterior [MASK] ([MASK]) and the posterior soft palate (palate, soft).

sexuallytransmitteddiseases.name: sexually transmitted diseases
sexuallytransmitteddiseases.definition: Sexually transmitted diseases is diseases due to or propagated by sexual contact.

infant,premature,diseases.name: infant , premature , diseases
infant,premature,diseases.definition: Diseases premature infant is diseases that occur in premature infants.

cornealstroma.name: corneal stroma
cornealstroma.definition: Corneal stroma is the lamellated connective tissue constituting the thickest layer of the cornea between the Bowman and Descemet membranes.

basolateralnuclearcomplex.name: basolateral nuclear complex
basolateralnuclearcomplex.definition: Basolateral nuclear complex is a [MASK] of amygdalar nuclei bordered laterally by the external capsule and medially by the central amygdaloid nucleus.

householdproducts.name: household products
householdproducts.definition: Household products is substances or materials used in the course of housekeeping or personal routine.

ganglioncysts.name: ganglion cysts
ganglioncysts.definition: Ganglion cysts is nodular tumor-like lesions or mucoid flesh, arising from tendon sheaths, ligaments, or joint capsule, especially of the hands, wrists, or [MASK]. They are not true cysts as they lack epithelial wall. They are distinguished from synovial cysts by the lack of communication with a joint cavity or the synovial membrane.

financing,personal.name: financing , personal
financing,personal.definition: Personal financing is payment by individuals or their family for health care services which are not covered by a third-party payer, either insurance or medical assistance.

lymphnodeexcision.name: lymph node excision
lymphnodeexcision.definition: [MASK] node excision is surgical excision of one or more [MASK] nodes. Its most common use is in cancer surgery. (From Dorland, 28th ed, p966)

psychology,sports.name: psychology , sports
psychology,sports.definition: Sports psychology is field of research that studies mental factors influencing the attainment of athletic skills and athletic performance.

rnasplicingfactors.name: rna splicing factors
rnasplicingfactors.definition: Rna splicing factors is rNA-binding proteins that facilitate or inhibit rna splicing.

spinalcordstimulation.name: spinal cord stimulation
spinalcordstimulation.definition: Spinal cord stimulation is application of electric current to the spine for treatment of a variety of conditions involving innervation from the spinal cord.

atrichsequence.name: at rich sequence
atrichsequence.definition: At rich sequence is a nucleic acid sequence that contains an above average number of adenine and thymine bases.

geneticlinkage.name: genetic linkage
geneticlinkage.definition: Genetic linkage is the co-inheritance of two or more non-allelic genes due to their being located more or less closely on the same chromosome.

skin.name: skin
skin.definition: Skin is the outer covering of the body that protects it from the environment. It is composed of the dermis and the epidermis.

hospitals,proprietary.name: hospitals , proprietary
hospitals,proprietary.definition: Proprietary hospitals is hospitals owned and operated by a corporation or an individual that operate on a for-profit basis, also referred to as investor-owned hospitals.

thyroidhormonereceptorsbeta.name: thyroid hormone receptors beta
thyroidhormonereceptorsbeta.definition: Thyroid hormone receptors beta is high affinity receptors for thyroid hormones, especially triiodothyronine. These receptors are usually found in the nucleus where they regulate dna transcription. They are encoded by the thrb gene (also known as nr1a2, thrb1, or erba2 gene) as several isoforms produced by [MASK]. Mutations in the thrb gene cause thyroid hormone resistance syndrome.

receptors,hiv.name: receptors , hiv
receptors,hiv.definition: Hiv receptors is cellular receptors that bind the human immunodeficiency virus that causes aids. Included are cd4 antigens, found on t4 lymphocytes, and monocytes/macrophages, which bind to the hiv envelope protein gp120.

pregnancy,ectopic.name: pregnancy , ectopic
pregnancy,ectopic.definition: Ectopic pregnancy is a potentially life-threatening condition in which embryo implantation occurs outside the cavity of the uterus. Most ectopic pregnancies (>96%) occur in the fallopian tubes, known as tubal pregnancy. They can be in other locations, such as uterine cervix; ovary; and abdominal cavity ([MASK]).

sheepdiseases.name: sheep diseases
sheepdiseases.definition: Sheep diseases is diseases of domestic and mountain sheep of the genus Ovis.

databases,genetic.name: databases , genetic
databases,genetic.definition: Genetic databases is databases devoted to knowledge about specific genes and gene products.

immunesystemphenomena.name: immune system phenomena
immunesystemphenomena.definition: Immune system phenomena is the characteristic properties and processes involved in immunity and an organism's immune response.

proteinkinasec.name: protein kinase c
proteinkinasec.definition: Protein kinase c is an serine-threonine protein kinase that requires the presence of physiological concentrations of calcium and membrane [MASK]. The additional presence of diacylglycerols markedly increases its sensitivity to both calcium and [MASK]. The sensitivity of the enzyme can also be increased by phorbol esters and it is believed that protein kinase c is the receptor protein of tumor-promoting phorbol esters.

internalcapsule.name: internal capsule
internalcapsule.definition: Internal capsule is [MASK] matter pathway, flanked by nuclear masses, consisting of both afferent and efferent fibers projecting between the [MASK] matter and the brainstem. It consists of three distinct parts: an anterior limb, posterior limb, and genu.

ancientlands.name: ancient lands
ancientlands.definition: Ancient lands is geographical sites known to be extant in a remote period in the history of civilization, familiar as the names of ancient countries and empires.

industry.name: industry
industry.definition: Industry is any enterprise centered on the processing, assembly, production, or marketing of a line of products, services, commodities, or merchandise, in a particular field often named after its principal product. Examples include the automobile, fishing, music, publishing, insurance, and [MASK].

selectionbias.name: selection bias
selectionbias.definition: Selection bias is the introduction of error due to systematic differences in the characteristics between those selected and those not selected for a given study. In sampling bias, error is the result of failure to ensure that all members of the reference population have a known chance of selection in the sample.

plantrootcap.name: plant root cap
plantrootcap.definition: Plant root cap is a cone-shaped structure in plants made up of a mass of meristematic cells that covers and protects the tip of a growing root. It is the putative site of [MASK] in plant roots.

auditorythreshold.name: auditory threshold
auditorythreshold.definition: Auditory threshold is the audibility limit of discriminating sound intensity and pitch.

coma.name: coma
coma.definition: Coma is a profound state of unconsciousness associated with depressed cerebral activity from which the individual cannot be aroused. Coma generally occurs when there is dysfunction or injury involving both cerebral hemispheres or the brain stem reticular formation.

diffusionmagneticresonanceimaging.name: diffusion magnetic resonance imaging
diffusionmagneticresonanceimaging.definition: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging is a diagnostic technique that incorporates the measurement of molecular diffusion (such as water or metabolites) for tissue assessment by mri. The degree of molecular movement can be measured by changes of apparent diffusion coefficient (adc) with time, as reflected by tissue microstructure. Diffusion mri has been used to study brain ischemia and tumor response to treatment.

radiofrequencyidentificationdevice.name: radio frequency identification device
radiofrequencyidentificationdevice.definition: Radio frequency identification device is machine readable patient or equipment identification device using radio frequency from 125 kHz to 5.8 Ghz.

toxicopticneuropathy.name: toxic optic neuropathy
toxicopticneuropathy.definition: Toxic optic neuropathy is damage to the eye or its function (e.g., visual impairment) due to optic nerve damage secondary to toxic substances such as drugs used in chemotherapy; immunotherapy; or radiation.

microbiology.name: microbiology
microbiology.definition: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms such as fungi, bacteria, algae, archaea, and viruses.

holisticnursing.name: holistic nursing
holisticnursing.definition: Holistic nursing is a philosophy of nursing practice that takes into account total patient care, considering the physical, emotional, social, economic, and spiritual needs of patients, their response to their illnesses, and the effect of illness on patients' abilities to meet self-care needs. (From Mosby's Medical, Nursing, & Allied Health Dictionary, 4th ed, p745)

mice.name: mice
mice.definition: Mice is the common name for the genus Mus.

dnabreaks.name: dna breaks
dnabreaks.definition: Dna breaks is interruptions in the sugar-phosphate backbone of dna.

cognition.name: cognition
cognition.definition: Cognition is intellectual or mental process whereby an organism obtains knowledge.

clinicaltrials,phaseiiastopic.name: clinical trials , phase ii as topic
clinicaltrials,phaseiiastopic.definition: Phase ii as topic clinical trials is works about studies that are usually controlled to assess the effectiveness and dosage (if appropriate) of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques. These studies are performed on several hundred volunteers, including a limited number of patients with the target disease or disorder, and last about two years. This concept includes phase ii studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

languagedevelopment.name: language development
languagedevelopment.definition: Language development is the gradual expansion in complexity and meaning of symbols and sounds as perceived and interpreted by the individual through a maturational and learning process. Stages in development include babbling, cooing, word imitation with cognition, and use of short sentences.

temporallobe.name: temporal lobe
temporallobe.definition: Temporal lobe is lower lateral part of the cerebral hemisphere responsible for auditory, olfactory, and semantic processing. It is located inferior to the lateral fissure and anterior to the occipital lobe.

phasetransition.name: phase transition
phasetransition.definition: Phase transition is a change of a substance from one form or state to another.

plateletmembraneglycoproteins.name: platelet membrane glycoproteins
plateletmembraneglycoproteins.definition: Platelet membrane glycoproteins is surface glycoproteins on platelets which have a key role in hemostasis and thrombosis such as platelet adhesion and aggregation. Many of these are receptors.

dentaletching.name: dental etching
dentaletching.definition: Dental etching is preparation of tooth surfaces, and of materials bonded to teeth or dental implants, with agents and methods which roughen the surface to facilitate adhesion. Agents include phosphoric or other acids ([MASK]) and methods include lasers.

adverseoutcomepathways.name: adverse outcome pathways
adverseoutcomepathways.definition: Adverse outcome pathways is models connecting initiating events at the cellular and molecular level to population-wide impacts. Computational models may be at levels relating toxicology to adverse effects.

celldivision.name: cell division
celldivision.definition: Cell division is the fission of a cell. It includes cytokinesis, when the cytoplasm of a cell is divided, and cell nucleus division.

basalgangliacerebrovasculardisease.name: basal ganglia cerebrovascular disease
basalgangliacerebrovasculardisease.definition: Basal ganglia cerebrovascular disease is a pathological condition caused by impaired blood flow in the basal regions of cerebral hemispheres (basal ganglia), such as infarction; hemorrhage; or ischemia in vessels of this brain region including the lateral lenticulostriate arteries. Primary clinical manifestations include involuntary movements (dyskinesias) and muscle weakness (hemiparesis).

rnacleavage.name: rna cleavage
rnacleavage.definition: Rna cleavage is a reaction that severs one of the sugar-phosphate linkages of the phosphodiester backbone of rna. It is catalyzed enzymatically, chemically, or by radiation. Cleavage may be exonucleolytic, or endonucleolytic.

singlemoleculeimaging.name: single molecule imaging
singlemoleculeimaging.definition: Single molecule imaging is high resolution imaging techniques that allow visualization of individual molecules of proteins, lipids, or nucleic acids within cells or tissues.

morphinederivatives.name: morphine derivatives
morphinederivatives.definition: [MASK] derivatives is analogs or derivatives of [MASK].

endpointdetermination.name: endpoint determination
endpointdetermination.definition: Endpoint determination is establishment of the level of a quantifiable effect indicative of a biologic process. The evaluation is frequently to detect the degree of toxic or therapeutic effect.

povertyareas.name: poverty areas
povertyareas.definition: Poverty areas is city, urban, rural, or suburban areas which are characterized by severe economic deprivation and by accompanying physical and social decay.

factorxi.name: factor xi
factorxi.definition: Factor xi is stable blood coagulation factor involved in the intrinsic pathway. The activated form XIa activates factor ix to IXa. Deficiency of factor xi is often called [MASK].

intrauterinedevices,copper.name: intrauterine devices , copper
intrauterinedevices,copper.definition: [MASK] [MASK] is [MASK] that depend on the release of metallic [MASK].

cancercarefacilities.name: cancer care facilities
cancercarefacilities.definition: Cancer care facilities is institutions specializing in the care of cancer patients.

cardiopulmonaryresuscitation.name: cardiopulmonary resuscitation
cardiopulmonaryresuscitation.definition: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is the artificial substitution of heart and lung action as indicated for heart arrest resulting from electric shock, drowning, respiratory arrest, or other causes. The two major components of cardiopulmonary resuscitation are artificial ventilation (respiration, artificial) and closed-chest cardiac massage.

bonesofupperextremity.name: bones of upper extremity
bonesofupperextremity.definition: Bones of upper extremity is the bones of the upper and lower [MASK]. They include the clavicle and scapula.

sittingposition.name: sitting position
sittingposition.definition: Sitting position is a standard patient position in which the patient is seated in a semi-sitting position (45-60 degrees) and may have [MASK] either bent or straight.

patientoutcomeassessment.name: patient outcome assessment
patientoutcomeassessment.definition: Patient outcome assessment is patient-generated evaluation data of treatment outcome or interaction in healthcare environment.

chromiumisotopes.name: chromium isotopes
chromiumisotopes.definition: Chromium isotopes is stable chromium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element chromium, but differ in atomic weight. Cr-50, 53, and 54 are stable chromium isotopes.

renalinsufficiency.name: renal insufficiency
renalinsufficiency.definition: Renal insufficiency is conditions in which the kidneys perform below the normal level in the ability to remove wastes, concentrate urine, and maintain electrolyte balance; blood pressure; and calcium metabolism. Renal insufficiency can be classified by the degree of kidney damage (as measured by the level of proteinuria) and reduction in [MASK].

rna,catalytic.name: rna , catalytic
rna,catalytic.definition: Catalytic rna is rna that has catalytic activity. The catalytic rna sequence folds to form a complex surface that can function as an enzyme in reactions with itself and other molecules. It may function even in the absence of protein. There are numerous examples of rna species that are acted upon by catalytic rna, however the scope of this enzyme class is not limited to a particular type of substrate.

cerebellardiseases.name: cerebellar diseases
cerebellardiseases.definition: Cerebellar diseases is diseases that affect the structure or function of the cerebellum. Cardinal manifestations of cerebellar dysfunction include dysmetria, [MASK], and muscle hypotonia.

medicine,arabic.name: medicine , arabic
medicine,arabic.definition: Arabic medicine is traditional concepts of medicine and associated methods reflected in medicine in the arab world.

databases,nucleicacid.name: databases , nucleic acid
databases,nucleicacid.definition: Nucleic acid databases is databases containing information about nucleic acids such as base sequence; snps; nucleic acid conformation; and other properties. Information about the dna fragments kept in a gene library or genomic library is often maintained in dna databases.

socialsciences.name: social sciences
socialsciences.definition: Social sciences is disciplines concerned with the interrelationships of individuals in a social environment including social organizations and institutions. Includes Sociology and Anthropology.

interviewsastopic.name: interviews as topic
interviewsastopic.definition: Interviews as topic is works about conversations with an individual or individuals held in order to obtain information about their background and other personal biographical data, their attitudes and opinions, etc. It includes works about school admission or job interviews.

radiation,ionizing.name: radiation , ionizing
radiation,ionizing.definition: Ionizing radiation is electromagnetic radiation or particle radiation (high energy elementary particles) capable of directly or indirectly producing ions in its passage through matter. The wavelengths of ionizing electromagnetic radiation are equal to or smaller than those of short (far) ultraviolet radiation and include gamma and X-rays.

metformin.name: metformin
metformin.definition: Metformin is a biguanide hypoglycemic agent used in the treatment of non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus not responding to dietary modification. Metformin improves glycemic control by improving insulin sensitivity and decreasing intestinal absorption of glucose. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p289)

boneandbones.name: bone and bones
boneandbones.definition: Bone and bones is a specialized connective tissue that is the main constituent of the skeleton. The principal cellular component of bone is comprised of [MASK]; osteocytes; and osteoclasts, while fibrillar collagens and hydroxyapatite crystals form the bone matrix.

stomachulcer.name: stomach ulcer
stomachulcer.definition: Stomach [MASK] is ulceration of the gastric mucosa due to contact with gastric juice. It is often associated with helicobacter pylori infection or consumption of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (nsaids).

thyroidfunctiontests.name: thyroid function tests
thyroidfunctiontests.definition: Thyroid function tests is blood tests used to evaluate the functioning of the thyroid gland.

sexchromosomedisorders.name: sex chromosome disorders
sexchromosomedisorders.definition: [MASK] chromosome disorders is clinical conditions caused by an abnormal [MASK] chromosome constitution ([MASK]), in which there is extra or missing [MASK] chromosome material (either a whole chromosome or a chromosome segment).

education.name: education
education.definition: Education is acquisition of knowledge as a result of instruction in a formal course of study.

rats,inbredstrains.name: rats , inbred strains
rats,inbredstrains.definition: Inbred strains rats is genetically identical individuals developed from brother and sister matings which have been carried out for twenty or more generations or by parent x offspring matings carried out with certain restrictions. This also includes animals with a long history of closed colony breeding.

fasreceptor.name: fas receptor
fasreceptor.definition: Fas receptor is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype found in a variety of tissues and on activated lymphocytes. It has specificity for fas ligand and plays a role in regulation of peripheral immune responses and apoptosis. Multiple isoforms of the protein exist due to multiple [MASK]. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm. Mutations in the cd95 gene are associated with cases of autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome.

adenocarcinoma,follicular.name: adenocarcinoma , follicular
adenocarcinoma,follicular.definition: Follicular adenocarcinoma is an adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland, in which the cells are arranged in the form of follicles. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

computersimulation.name: computer simulation
computersimulation.definition: Computer simulation is computer-based representation of physical systems and phenomena such as chemical processes.

radialneuropathy.name: radial neuropathy
radialneuropathy.definition: Radial neuropathy is disease involving the radial nerve. Clinical features include weakness of elbow extension, elbow flexion, supination of the forearm, wrist and finger extension, and thumb abduction. Sensation may be impaired over regions of the dorsal forearm. Common sites of compression or traumatic injury include the axilla and radial groove of the humerus.

fetaltherapies.name: fetal therapies
fetaltherapies.definition: Fetal therapies is prenatal interventions to correct fetal anomalies or treat fetal diseases in utero. Fetal therapies include several major areas, such as open surgery; fetoscopy; pharmacological therapy; intrauterine transfusion; stem cell transplantation; and genetic therapy.

spectrometry,fluorescence.name: spectrometry , fluorescence
spectrometry,fluorescence.definition: Fluorescence spectrometry is measurement of the intensity and quality of fluorescence.

sensation.name: sensation
sensation.definition: Sensation is the process in which specialized sensory receptor cells transduce peripheral stimuli (physical or chemical) into nerve impulses which are then transmitted to the various sensory centers in the central nervous system.

cholesterolesters.name: cholesterol esters
cholesterolesters.definition: Cholesterol esters is fatty acid esters of cholesterol which constitute about two-thirds of the cholesterol in the plasma. The accumulation of cholesterol esters in the arterial intima is a characteristic feature of atherosclerosis.

genitalneoplasms,female.name: genital neoplasms , female
genitalneoplasms,female.definition: Female genital neoplasms is tumor or cancer of the female reproductive tract (genitalia, female).

openreadingframes.name: open reading frames
openreadingframes.definition: Open reading frames is a sequence of successive nucleotide triplets that are read as codons specifying amino acids and begin with an initiator codon and end with a stop codon (codon, terminator).

colitis,lymphocytic.name: colitis , lymphocytic
colitis,lymphocytic.definition: Lymphocytic colitis is a subtype of microscopic colitis, characterized by chronic watery [MASK] of unknown origin, a normal colonoscopy but abnormal histopathology on biopsy. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the colon show infiltration of lymphocytes in the superficial epithelium and the underlying connective tissue (lamina propria).

cysteineproteinaseinhibitors.name: cysteine proteinase inhibitors
cysteineproteinaseinhibitors.definition: [MASK] proteinase inhibitors is exogenous and endogenous compounds which inhibit [MASK] endopeptidases.

timefactors.name: time factors
timefactors.definition: Time factors is elements of limited time intervals, contributing to particular results or situations.

facilitateddiffusion.name: facilitated diffusion
facilitateddiffusion.definition: Facilitated diffusion is the passive movement of molecules exceeding the rate expected by simple diffusion. No energy is expended in the process. It is achieved by the introduction of passively diffusing molecules to an enviroment or path that is more favorable to the movement of those molecules. Examples of facilitated diffusion are passive transport of hydrophilic substances across a lipid membrane through hydrophilic pores that traverse the membrane, and the sliding of a dna binding protein along a strand of dna.

housingfortheelderly.name: housing for the elderly
housingfortheelderly.definition: Housing for the elderly is housing arrangements for the elderly or aged, intended to foster [MASK]. The housing may take the form of group homes or small apartments. It is available to the economically self-supporting but the concept includes housing for the elderly with some physical limitations. The concept should be differentiated from homes for the aged which is restricted to long-term geriatric facilities providing supervised medical and nursing services.

shiftworkschedule.name: shift work schedule
shiftworkschedule.definition: Shift work schedule is job schedule in which working hours deviate from the standard hours (e.g., evening shift, night shift or rotating shift).

sexualbehavior,animal.name: sexual behavior , animal
sexualbehavior,animal.definition: Animal sexual behavior is sexual activities of animals.

hepatitisavaccines.name: hepatitis a vaccines
hepatitisavaccines.definition: Hepatitis a vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with hepatitis a virus (hepatovirus).

lifting.name: lifting
lifting.definition: Lifting is moving or bringing something from a lower level to a higher one. The concept encompasses biomechanic stresses resulting from work done in transferring objects from one plane to another as well as the effects of varying techniques of patient handling and transfer.

rna,antisense.name: rna , antisense
rna,antisense.definition: Antisense rna is rna molecules which hybridize to complementary sequences in either rna or dna altering the function of the latter. Endogenous antisense RNAs function as regulators of gene expression by a variety of mechanisms. Synthetic antisense RNAs are used to effect the functioning of specific genes for investigative or therapeutic purposes.

annualreportsastopic.name: annual reports as topic
annualreportsastopic.definition: Annual reports as topic is works on annual statements reviewing the status of the administrative and operational functions and accomplishments of an institution or organization.

antifungalagents.name: antifungal agents
antifungalagents.definition: Antifungal agents is substances that destroy fungi by suppressing their ability to grow or reproduce. They differ from fungicides, industrial because they defend against fungi present in human or animal tissues.

hypotension.name: hypotension
hypotension.definition: Hypotension is abnormally low blood pressure that can result in inadequate blood flow to the brain and other vital organs. Common symptom is dizziness but greater negative impacts on the body occur when there is prolonged depravation of oxygen and nutrients.

aneurysm,infected.name: aneurysm , infected
aneurysm,infected.definition: Infected aneurysm is aneurysm due to growth of microorganisms in the arterial wall, or infection arising within preexisting arteriosclerotic aneurysms.

nuclearweapons.name: nuclear weapons
nuclearweapons.definition: Nuclear weapons is a weapon that derives its destructive force from [MASK] and/or fusion.

schools,healthoccupations.name: schools , health occupations
schools,healthoccupations.definition: Health occupations schools is schools which offer training in the area of health.

learning.name: learning
learning.definition: Learning is relatively permanent change in behavior that is the result of past experience or practice. The concept includes the acquisition of knowledge.

filteringsurgery.name: filtering surgery
filteringsurgery.definition: Filtering surgery is a surgical procedure used in treatment of glaucoma in which an opening is created through which aqueous fluid may pass from the anterior chamber into a sac created beneath the conjunctiva, thus lowering the pressure within the eye. (Hoffman, Pocket Glossary of Ophthalmologic Terminology, 1989)

enzymeactivators.name: enzyme activators
enzymeactivators.definition: Enzyme activators is compounds or factors that act on a specific enzyme to increase its activity.

columbiaskvirus.name: columbia sk virus
columbiaskvirus.definition: Columbia sk virus is a strain of encephalomyocarditis virus, a species of cardiovirus, that infects rodents.

regulatorysequences,nucleicacid.name: regulatory sequences , nucleic acid
regulatorysequences,nucleicacid.definition: Nucleic acid regulatory sequences is nucleic acid sequences involved in regulating the expression of genes.

conceptualentity.name: conceptual entity
conceptualentity.definition: Conceptual entity is something that has a conceptual reality.

practicevaluationandpurchase.name: practice valuation and purchase
practicevaluationandpurchase.definition: Practice valuation and purchase is determination of economic value of an established health care provider practice including value of patient lists, equipment, and other assets, and process of buying or selling rights to said practice.

atypicalsquamouscellsofthecervix.name: atypical squamous cells of the cervix
atypicalsquamouscellsofthecervix.definition: Atypical squamous cells of the cervix is morphological abnormalities of the cervical epithelium, usually revealed in pap smear, which do not meet the criteria for squamous cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or squamous cell carcinomas of the cervix . It may be a sign of infection with certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).or sign of a benign (not cancer) growth, such as a cyst or polyp or, in menopausal women, of low hormone levels. More testing, such as hpv test, may be needed.

nuclearfactor90proteins.name: nuclear factor 90 proteins
nuclearfactor90proteins.definition: Nuclear factor 90 proteins is a family of double-stranded RNA-binding proteins that are related to nfatc transcription factors. In addition to binding to rna, nuclear factor 90 proteins form heterodimeric complexes that regulate genetic transcription and may play a role in t-cell activation.

governmentalorregulatoryactivity.name: governmental or regulatory activity
governmentalorregulatoryactivity.definition: Governmental or regulatory activity is governmental or regulatory activity

roundligamentoffemur.name: round ligament of femur
roundligamentoffemur.definition: Round ligament of femur is ligament that connects the fovea of the femur head and the acetabulum notch in the hip joint.

erythrocytecount.name: erythrocyte count
erythrocytecount.definition: Erythrocyte count is the number of red blood cells per unit volume in a sample of venous blood.

weedcontrol.name: weed control
weedcontrol.definition: Weed control is the prevention of growth and or spread of unwanted plants.

folliclestimulatinghormone,betasubunit.name: follicle stimulating hormone , beta subunit
folliclestimulatinghormone,betasubunit.definition: Beta subunit follicle stimulating hormone is the beta subunit of follicle stimulating hormone. It is a 15-kDa glycopolypeptide. Full biological activity of fsh requires the non-covalently bound heterodimers of an alpha and a beta subunit. Mutation of the fshb gene causes delayed puberty, or infertility.

oncogeneproteins,viral.name: oncogene proteins , viral
oncogeneproteins,viral.definition: Viral oncogene proteins is products of viral oncogenes, most commonly retroviral oncogenes. They usually have transforming and often protein kinase activities.

cattle.name: cattle
cattle.definition: Cattle is domesticated bovine animals of the genus Bos, usually kept on a farm or ranch and used for the production of meat or dairy products or for heavy labor.

bloodcoagulationfactorinhibitors.name: blood coagulation factor inhibitors
bloodcoagulationfactorinhibitors.definition: Blood coagulation factor inhibitors is substances, usually endogenous, that act as inhibitors of blood coagulation. They may affect one or multiple enzymes throughout the process. As a group, they also inhibit enzymes involved in processes other than blood coagulation, such as those from the complement system, fibrinolytic enzyme system, blood cells, and bacteria.

cochlearnerve.name: cochlear nerve
cochlearnerve.definition: Cochlear nerve is the cochlear part of the 8th cranial nerve (vestibulocochlear nerve). The cochlear nerve fibers originate from neurons of the spiral ganglion and project peripherally to cochlear hair cells and centrally to the cochlear nuclei (cochlear nucleus) of the brain stem. They mediate the sense of hearing.

excitatoryaminoacidtransporter1.name: excitatory amino acid transporter 1
excitatoryaminoacidtransporter1.definition: [MASK] transporter 1 is a glial type glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein found predominately in astrocytes. It is also expressed in heart and skeletal muscle and in the placenta.

builtenvironment.name: built environment
builtenvironment.definition: Built environment is the man-made physical elements of the environment (e.g., homes, buildings, streets, open spaces, and infrastructure). The built environment influences a person's level of physical activity and may have other impacts on health in a community.

peerinfluence.name: peer influence
peerinfluence.definition: Peer influence is the effect or sway that a peer group exerts on the beliefs, value systems and behavior of each member of a group. The social expectations for individuals to conform to peer group influence is known as peer pressure.

fractures,multiple.name: fractures , multiple
fractures,multiple.definition: Multiple fractures is injuries involving the breaking of either several bones or one bone in two or more places.

death.name: death
death.definition: Death is irreversible cessation of all bodily functions, manifested by absence of spontaneous breathing and total loss of cardiovascular and cerebral functions.

statistics.name: statistics
statistics.definition: Statistics is works consisting of presentations of numerical data on particular subjects.

heartfunctiontests.name: heart function tests
heartfunctiontests.definition: Heart function tests is examinations used to diagnose and treat heart conditions.

primarygraftdysfunction.name: primary graft dysfunction
primarygraftdysfunction.definition: Primary [MASK] dysfunction is a form of ischemia-reperfusion injury occurring in the early period following transplantation. Significant pathophysiological changes in mitochondria are the main cause of the dysfunction. It is most often seen in the transplanted lung, liver, or kidney and can lead to [MASK] [MASK].

multiplechronicconditions.name: multiple chronic conditions
multiplechronicconditions.definition: Multiple chronic conditions is two or more concurrent chronic physical, mental, or behavioral health problems in an individual.

cellmigrationinhibition.name: cell migration inhibition
cellmigrationinhibition.definition: Cell migration inhibition is phenomenon of cell-mediated immunity measured by in vitro inhibition of the migration or [MASK] of antigen-stimulated leukocytes or macrophages. Specific cell migration assays have been developed to estimate levels of migration inhibitory factors, immune reactivity against tumor-associated antigens, and immunosuppressive effects of infectious microorganisms.

betavulgaris.name: beta vulgaris
betavulgaris.definition: Beta vulgaris is a species of the Beta genus. Cultivars are used as a source of beets (root) or chard (leaves).

chromosomalpositioneffects.name: chromosomal position effects
chromosomalpositioneffects.definition: Chromosomal position effects is the effects on gene expression that depend on the location of a gene with respect to its neighboring genes and region of chromosome. Stable position effects are sequence dependent. Variegated position effects depend on whether the gene is located in or adjacent to heterochromatin or euchromatin.

hemorrhagicsyndrome,bovine.name: hemorrhagic syndrome , bovine
hemorrhagicsyndrome,bovine.definition: Bovine hemorrhagic syndrome is clinically severe [MASK] of cattle caused by noncytopathic forms of [MASK] ([MASK]). [MASK] are characterized by high morbidity and high mortality.

opticnerveinjuries.name: optic nerve injuries
opticnerveinjuries.definition: Optic nerve injuries is injuries to the optic nerve induced by a trauma to the face or head. These may occur with closed or penetrating injuries. Relatively minor compression of the superior aspect of [MASK] may also result in trauma to the optic nerve. Clinical manifestations may include visual loss, papilledema, and an afferent pupillary defect.

pregnancytrimester,third.name: pregnancy trimester , third
pregnancytrimester,third.definition: Third pregnancy trimester is the last third of a human pregnancy, from the beginning of the 29th through the 42nd completed week (197 to 294 days) of gestation.

lungdiseases,interstitial.name: lung diseases , interstitial
lungdiseases,interstitial.definition: Interstitial lung diseases is a diverse group of lung diseases that affect the lung parenchyma. They are characterized by an initial inflammation of pulmonary alveoli that extends to the interstitium and beyond leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis. Interstitial lung diseases are classified by their etiology (known or unknown causes), and radiological-pathological features.

forests.name: forests
forests.definition: Forests is an ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation.

labor,obstetric.name: labor , obstetric
labor,obstetric.definition: Obstetric labor is the repetitive [MASK] during childbirth which is associated with the progressive dilation of the uterine cervix (cervix uteri). Successful labor results in the expulsion of the fetus and placenta. Obstetric labor can be spontaneous or induced (labor, induced).

ethyleneglycol.name: ethylene glycol
ethyleneglycol.definition: Ethylene glycol is a colorless, odorless, viscous dihydroxy alcohol. It has a sweet taste, but is poisonous if ingested. Ethylene glycol is the most important glycol commercially available and is manufactured on a large scale in the United States. It is used as an antifreeze and coolant, in hydraulic fluids, and in the manufacture of low-freezing dynamites and resins.

cornealulcer.name: corneal ulcer
cornealulcer.definition: Corneal [MASK] is loss of epithelial tissue from the surface of the cornea due to progressive erosion and necrosis of the tissue; usually caused by bacterial, fungal, or viral infection.

extremities.name: extremities
extremities.definition: Extremities is the farthest or outermost projections of the body, such as the hand and [MASK].

phdzincfingers.name: phd zinc fingers
phdzincfingers.definition: Phd zinc fingers is zinc finger domains of approximately 50 to 80 amino acids in length that are characterized by a conserved [MASK](3)-Histidine-[MASK](4) amino acid motif which coordinates binding of two zinc ions. They are similar structurally to ring finger domains, with a globular fold topology of two beta-sheets and an alpha-helix. phd fingers occur in many proteins that function in chromatin-mediated gene expression and epigenetics such as polycomb-group proteins.

influenzaavirus.name: influenza a virus
influenzaavirus.definition: Influenza a virus is the type species of the genus influenzavirus a that causes influenza and other diseases in humans and animals. Antigenic variation occurs frequently between strains, allowing classification into subtypes and variants. Transmission is usually by aerosol (human and most non-aquatic hosts) or waterborne (ducks). Infected birds shed the virus in their saliva, nasal secretions, and feces.

hipfractures.name: hip fractures
hipfractures.definition: Hip fractures is fractures of the femur head; the femur [MASK]; (femoral [MASK] fractures); the trochanters; or the inter- or subtrochanteric region. Excludes fractures of the acetabulum and fractures of the femoral shaft below the subtrochanteric region (femoral fractures).

exercise.name: exercise
exercise.definition: Exercise is physical activity which is usually regular and done with the intention of improving or maintaining physical fitness or health. Contrast with physical exertion which is concerned largely with the physiologic and metabolic response to energy expenditure.

silentinformationregulatorproteins,sacch.name: silent information regulator proteins , saccharomyces cerevisiae
silentinformationregulatorproteins,sacch.definition: Saccharomyces cerevisiae silent information regulator proteins is a [MASK] of nuclear proteins in saccharomyces cerevisiae that are required for the transcriptional repression of the silent mating type loci. They mediate the formation of silenced chromatin and repress both transcription and recombination at other loci as well. They are comprised of 4 non-homologous, interacting proteins, Sir1p, Sir2p, Sir3p, and Sir4p. Sir2p, an NAD-dependent histone deacetylase, is the founding member of the family of sirtuins.

drugdeliverysystems.name: drug delivery systems
drugdeliverysystems.definition: Drug delivery systems is systems for the delivery of drugs to target sites of pharmacological actions. Technologies employed include those concerning drug preparation, route of administration, site targeting, metabolism, and toxicity.

africa.name: africa
africa.definition: Africa is the continent south of europe, east of the atlantic ocean and west of the indian ocean.

pancreatitis,chronic.name: pancreatitis , chronic
pancreatitis,chronic.definition: Chronic pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas that is characterized by recurring or persistent abdominal pain with or without steatorrhea or diabetes mellitus. It is characterized by the irregular destruction of the pancreatic parenchyma which may be focal, segmental, or diffuse.

frontallobe.name: frontal lobe
frontallobe.definition: Frontal lobe is the part of the cerebral hemisphere anterior to the central sulcus, and anterior and superior to the lateral sulcus.

intensivecareunits,pediatric.name: intensive care units , pediatric
intensivecareunits,pediatric.definition: Pediatric intensive care units is hospital units providing continuous surveillance and care to acutely ill infants and children. Neonates are excluded since intensive care units, neonatal is available.

epilepsy,partial,sensory.name: epilepsy , partial , sensory
epilepsy,partial,sensory.definition: Sensory partial epilepsy is a disorder characterized by recurrent focal onset seizures which have sensory (i.e., olfactory, visual, tactile, gustatory, or auditory) manifestations. Partial seizures that feature alterations of consciousness are referred to as complex partial seizures (epilepsy, complex partial).

heartfailure.name: heart failure
