heartfailure.definition: Heart failure is a heterogeneous condition in which the heart is unable to pump out sufficient blood to meet the metabolic need of the body. Heart failure can be caused by structural defects, functional abnormalities (ventricular dysfunction), or a sudden overload beyond its capacity. Chronic heart failure is more common than acute heart failure which results from sudden insult to cardiac function, such as myocardial infarction.

mars.name: mars
mars.definition: Mars is the fourth planet in order from the sun. Its two natural satellites are Deimos and Phobos. It is one of the four inner or terrestrial planets of the solar system.

spirocompounds.name: spiro compounds
spirocompounds.definition: Spiro compounds is cyclic compounds that include two rings which share a single atom (usually a carbon). The simplest example of this type of compound is Spiro[2.2]pentane, which looks like a bow tie.

clinicaltrial,phasei.name: clinical trial , phase i
clinicaltrial,phasei.definition: [MASK] is work that is the report of a pre-planned, usually controlled, clinical study of the safety and efficacy of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques based on a small number of healthy persons and conducted over the period of about a year in either the United States or a foreign country.

infantformula.name: infant formula
infantformula.definition: Infant formula is formulations for the nutrition of infants that are substituted for [MASK].

parenchymaltissue.name: parenchymal tissue
parenchymaltissue.definition: Parenchymal tissue is the tissue that constitutes the essential or functional part of an organ (e.g., parenchyma of lung, parenchyma of liver, or parenchyma of kidney).

calcium,dietary.name: calcium , dietary
calcium,dietary.definition: Dietary calcium is calcium compounds used as food supplements or in food to supply the body with calcium. Dietary calcium is needed during growth for bone development and for maintenance of skeletal integrity later in life to prevent osteoporosis.

aorta,abdominal.name: aorta , abdominal
aorta,abdominal.definition: Abdominal aorta is the aorta from the diaphragm to the bifurcation into the right and left common iliac arteries.

alcoholabstinence.name: alcohol abstinence
alcoholabstinence.definition: Alcohol abstinence is non-consumption of alcoholic beverages.

clinicalmedicine.name: clinical medicine
clinicalmedicine.definition: Clinical medicine is the study and practice of medicine by direct examination of the patient.

cornealdiseases.name: corneal diseases
cornealdiseases.definition: Corneal diseases is diseases of the cornea.

centraltolerance.name: central tolerance
centraltolerance.definition: Central tolerance is the mechanism, in central lymphoid organs (thymus; bone marrow), that prevents immature lymphocytes from reacting to self-antigens. This is accomplished by clonal anergy and clonal deletion.

poland.name: poland
poland.definition: Poland is a country in central Europe, east of Germany. The capital is Warsaw.

patent.name: patent
patent.definition: Patent is work consisting of documents granted by a government giving exclusive rights to an inventor or assignee to manufacture, use, or sell an invention for a certain number of years.

trauma,nervoussystem.name: trauma , nervous system
trauma,nervoussystem.definition: Nervous system trauma is traumatic injuries to the brain, cranial nerves, spinal cord, autonomic nervous system, or neuromuscular system, including iatrogenic injuries induced by surgical procedures.

advancedcardiaclifesupport.name: advanced cardiac life support
advancedcardiaclifesupport.definition: Advanced cardiac life support is the use of sophisticated methods and equipment to treat cardiopulmonary arrest. Advanced Cardiac Life Support (acls) includes the use of specialized equipment to maintain the airway, early defibrillation and pharmacological therapy.

receptors,fibroblastgrowthfactor.name: receptors , fibroblast growth factor
receptors,fibroblastgrowthfactor.definition: Fibroblast growth factor receptors is specific molecular sites or structures on cell membranes that react with fibroblast growth factors (both the basic and acidic forms), their analogs, or their antagonists to elicit or to inhibit the specific response of the cell to these factors. These receptors frequently possess tyrosine kinase activity.

atypicalbacterialforms.name: atypical bacterial forms
atypicalbacterialforms.definition: Atypical bacterial forms is microorganisms that have undergone greater changes than normal in morphology, physiology, or [MASK].

leukemiavirus,bovine.name: leukemia virus , bovine
leukemiavirus,bovine.definition: Bovine leukemia virus is the type species of deltaretrovirus that causes a form of bovine lymphosarcoma (enzootic bovine leukosis) or persistent lymphocytosis.

chemotherapy,cancer,regionalperfusion.name: chemotherapy , cancer , regional perfusion
chemotherapy,cancer,regionalperfusion.definition: Regional perfusion cancer chemotherapy is neoplasm drug therapy involving an extracorporeal circuit with temporary exclusion of the tumor-bearing area from the general circulation during which high concentrations of the drug are perfused to the isolated part.

bloomsyndrome.name: bloom syndrome
bloomsyndrome.definition: Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by telangiectatic erythema of the face, photosensitivity, dwarfism and other abnormalities, and a predisposition toward developing cancer. The Bloom syndrome gene (blm) encodes a RecQ-like dna helicase.

hepatitise.name: hepatitis e
hepatitise.definition: Hepatitis e is acute inflammation of the liver in humans; caused by hepatitis e virus, a non-enveloped single-stranded rna virus. Similar to hepatitis a, its incubation period is 15-60 days and is enterically transmitted, usually by fecal-oral transmission.

tuberculosis,endocrine.name: tuberculosis , endocrine
tuberculosis,endocrine.definition: Endocrine tuberculosis is infection of the endocrine glands with species of mycobacterium, most often [MASK].

orthodonticextrusion.name: orthodontic extrusion
orthodonticextrusion.definition: Orthodontic extrusion is orthodontic movement in the coronal direction achieved by outward tension on the periodontal ligament. It does not include the operative procedure that crown lengthening involves.

insurance,pharmaceuticalservices.name: insurance , pharmaceutical services
insurance,pharmaceuticalservices.definition: Pharmaceutical services insurance is insurance providing for payment of services rendered by the pharmacist. Services include the preparation and distribution of medical products.

scholarlycommunication.name: scholarly communication
scholarlycommunication.definition: Scholarly communication is system through which research and other scholarly writings are created, evaluated for quality, disseminated to the scholarly community, and preserved for future use. It includes both formal means of communication, such as publication in peer-reviewed journals, and informal channels, such as electronic listservs. (from Association of College & Research Libraries, “Principles and Strategies for the Reform of Scholarly Communication 1,” 2003)

costallocation.name: cost allocation
costallocation.definition: Cost allocation is the assignment, to each of several particular cost-centers, of an equitable proportion of the costs of activities that serve all of them. Cost-center usually refers to institutional departments or services.

environmentandpublichealth.name: environment and public health
environmentandpublichealth.definition: Environment and public health is natural and man-made environments and their impact on public health.

skinphysiologicalphenomena.name: skin physiological phenomena
skinphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Skin physiological phenomena is the functions of the skin in the human and animal body. It includes the pigmentation of the skin.

chromosomes,human,pair7.name: chromosomes , human , pair 7
chromosomes,human,pair7.definition: Pair 7 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

facialexpression.name: facial expression
facialexpression.definition: Facial expression is observable changes of expression in the face in response to emotional stimuli.

unitedstatesindianhealthservice.name: united states indian health service
unitedstatesindianhealthservice.definition: United states indian health service is a division of the united states public health service that is responsible for the public health and the provision of medical services to native americans in the United States, primarily those residing on reservation lands.

sportsnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: sports nutritional physiological phenomena
sportsnutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Sports nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology related to exercise or athletic performance.

embryonicgermcells.name: embryonic germ cells
embryonicgermcells.definition: Embryonic germ cells is pluripotent stem cells that are derived from early germ cells.

glucosetransportertype3.name: glucose transporter type 3
glucosetransportertype3.definition: Glucose transporter type 3 is a major glucose transporter found in neurons.

healthfacilityadministrators.name: health facility administrators
healthfacilityadministrators.definition: Health facility administrators is managerial personnel responsible for implementing policy and directing the activities of health care facilities such as nursing homes.

glycogenstoragediseasetypeiii.name: glycogen storage disease type iii
glycogenstoragediseasetypeiii.definition: Glycogen storage disease type iii is an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder due to deficient expression of amylo-1,6-glucosidase (one part of the glycogen debranching enzyme system). The clinical course of the disease is similar to that of glycogen storage disease type i, but milder. Massive hepatomegaly, which is present in young children, diminishes and occasionally disappears with age. Levels of glycogen with short outer branches are elevated in muscle, liver, and erythrocytes. Six subgroups have been identified, with subgroups Type IIIa and Type IIIb being the most prevalent.

travelmedicine.name: travel medicine
travelmedicine.definition: Travel medicine is multidisciplinary field focusing on prevention of infectious diseases and patient safety during international travel. Key element of patient's pre-travel visit to the physician is a health risk assessment.

pregnancy,angular.name: pregnancy , angular
pregnancy,angular.definition: Angular pregnancy is a rare type of abnormal pregnancy in which embryo implantation occurs at a lateral angle of the uterus, medial to the uterotubal junction and the round ligament of uterus.

splenicinfarction.name: splenic infarction
splenicinfarction.definition: Splenic infarction is insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply to the spleen due to emboli, thrombi, vascular torsion, or pressure that produces a macroscopic area of necrosis. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

drugtherapy.name: drug therapy
drugtherapy.definition: Drug therapy is the use of drugs to treat a disease or its symptoms. One example is the use of antineoplastic agents to treat cancer.

physicians.name: physicians
physicians.definition: Physicians is individuals licensed to practice medicine.

invitrotechniques.name: in vitro techniques
invitrotechniques.definition: In vitro techniques is methods to study reactions or processes taking place in an artificial environment outside the living organism.

tachycardia,ventricular.name: tachycardia , ventricular
tachycardia,ventricular.definition: Ventricular tachycardia is an abnormally rapid ventricular rhythm usually in excess of 150 beats per minute. It is generated within the ventricle below the bundle of his, either as autonomic impulse formation or reentrant impulse conduction. Depending on the etiology, onset of ventricular tachycardia can be paroxysmal (sudden) or nonparoxysmal, its wide qrs complexes can be uniform or polymorphic, and the ventricular beating may be independent of the atrial beating (av dissociation).

adrenalcortexdiseases.name: adrenal cortex diseases
adrenalcortexdiseases.definition: Adrenal cortex diseases is pathological processes of the adrenal cortex.

medialforebrainbundle.name: medial forebrain bundle
medialforebrainbundle.definition: Medial forebrain bundle is a complex group of fibers arising from the basal olfactory regions, the periamygdaloid region, and the septal nuclei, and passing to the lateral hypothalamus. Some fibers continue into the tegmentum.

chromosomes,human,pair22.name: chromosomes , human , pair 22
chromosomes,human,pair22.definition: Pair 22 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group g chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

carcinoma,isletcell.name: carcinoma , islet cell
carcinoma,isletcell.definition: Islet cell carcinoma is a primary malignant neoplasm of the pancreatic islet cells. Usually it involves the non-INSULIN-producing cell types, the pancreatic alpha cells and the pancreatic delta cells (somatostatin-secreting cells) in glucagonoma and somatostatinoma, respectively.

blood.name: blood
blood.definition: Blood is the body fluid that circulates in the vascular system (blood vessels). Whole blood includes plasma and blood cells.

vulnerablepopulations.name: vulnerable populations
vulnerablepopulations.definition: Vulnerable populations is groups of persons whose range of options is severely limited, who are frequently subjected to coercion in their decision making, or who may be compromised in their ability to give informed consent.

tachycardia,sinus.name: tachycardia , sinus
tachycardia,sinus.definition: Sinus tachycardia is simple rapid heartbeats caused by rapid discharge of impulses from the sinoatrial node, usually between 100 and 180 beats/min in adults. It is characterized by a gradual onset and termination. Sinus tachycardia is common in infants, young children, and adults during strenuous physical activities.

biologicalproducts.name: biological products
biologicalproducts.definition: Biological products is complex pharmaceutical substances, preparations, or matter derived from organisms usually obtained by biological methods or assay.

neuroimaging.name: neuroimaging
neuroimaging.definition: Neuroimaging is non-invasive methods of visualizing the central nervous system, especially the brain, by various imaging modalities.

sensorimotorcortex.name: sensorimotor cortex
sensorimotorcortex.definition: Sensorimotor cortex is a composite area of the cerebral cortex concerned with motor control and sensory perception comprising the motor cortex areas, the somatosensory areas, the gustatory cortex, the olfactory areas, the auditory cortex, and the visual cortex.

bronchialdiseases.name: bronchial diseases
bronchialdiseases.definition: Bronchial diseases is diseases involving the bronchi.

liverfailure.name: liver failure
liverfailure.definition: Liver failure is severe inability of the liver to perform its normal metabolic functions, as evidenced by severe jaundice and abnormal serum levels of [MASK]; bilirubin; alkaline phosphatase; aspartate aminotransferase; lactate dehydrogenases; and albumin/globulin ratio. (Blakiston's Gould Medical Dictionary, 4th ed)

pigmentepitheliumofeye.name: pigment epithelium of eye
pigmentepitheliumofeye.definition: Pigment epithelium of eye is the layer of pigment-containing epithelial cells in the retina; the [MASK]; and the iris in the eye.

fetalmortality.name: fetal mortality
fetalmortality.definition: Fetal mortality is number of fetal deaths with stated or presumed gestation of 20 weeks or more in a given population. Late fetal mortality is death after of 28 weeks or more.

pituitaryfunctiontests.name: pituitary function tests
pituitaryfunctiontests.definition: Pituitary function tests is examinations that evaluate functions of the pituitary gland.

zinc.name: zinc
zinc.definition: Zinc is a metallic element of atomic number 30 and atomic weight 65.38. It is a necessary trace element in the diet, forming an essential part of many enzymes, and playing an important role in protein synthesis and in cell division. Zinc deficiency is associated with anemia, short stature, hypogonadism, impaired wound healing, and geophagia. It is known by the symbol Zn.

bloodcoagulationdisorders,inherited.name: blood coagulation disorders , inherited
bloodcoagulationdisorders,inherited.definition: Inherited blood coagulation disorders is hemorrhagic and thrombotic disorders that occur as a consequence of inherited abnormalities in blood coagulation.

adenovirusearlyproteins.name: adenovirus early proteins
adenovirusearlyproteins.definition: Adenovirus early proteins is proteins encoded by adenoviruses that are synthesized prior to, and in the absence of, [MASK] replication. The proteins are involved in both positive and negative regulation of expression in viral and cellular genes, and also affect the stability of viral mRNA. Some are also involved in oncogenic transformation.

multiplechemicalsensitivity.name: multiple chemical sensitivity
multiplechemicalsensitivity.definition: Multiple chemical sensitivity is an acquired disorder characterized by recurrent symptoms, referable to multiple organ systems, occurring in response to demonstrable exposure to many chemically unrelated compounds at doses below those established in the general population to cause harmful effects. (Cullen mr. The worker with multiple chemical sensitivities: an overview. Occup Med 1987;2(4):655-61)

guaninenucleotides.name: guanine nucleotides
guaninenucleotides.definition: Guanine nucleotides is family of signal-transducing molecules coupling the seven-transmembrane-helix family of cell membrane receptors (including the TSH receptor) to activating cellular effector systems such as adenyl cyclase.

crossinfection.name: cross infection
crossinfection.definition: Cross infection is any infection which a patient contracts in a health-care institution.

lungvolumemeasurements.name: lung volume measurements
lungvolumemeasurements.definition: Lung volume measurements is measurement of the amount of air that the lungs may contain at various points in the respiratory cycle.

nasalsurgicalprocedures.name: nasal surgical procedures
nasalsurgicalprocedures.definition: Nasal surgical procedures is surgical operations on the nose and nasal cavity.

checkpointkinase1.name: checkpoint kinase 1
checkpointkinase1.definition: Checkpoint kinase 1 is a serine/threonine-specific protein kinase which is encoded by the chek1 gene in humans. Checkpoint kinase 1 (also known as Chk1) coordinates dna damage response and cell cycle checkpoint response. Under these conditions, activation of Chk1 results in the initiation of cell cycle checkpoints, cell cycle arrest, dna repair and cell death, to prevent damaged cells from progressing through the cell cycle.

escherichiacoliinfections.name: escherichia coli infections
escherichiacoliinfections.definition: Escherichia coli infections is infections with bacteria of the species escherichia coli.

tuberculosis,oral.name: tuberculosis , oral
tuberculosis,oral.definition: Oral tuberculosis is tuberculosis of the mouth, tongue, and salivary glands.

fertilitypreservation.name: fertility preservation
fertilitypreservation.definition: Fertility preservation is a method of providing future reproductive opportunities before a medical treatment with known risk of loss of fertility. Typically reproductive organs or tissues (e.g., sperm, egg, embryos and ovarian or testicular tissues) are cryopreserved for future use before the medical treatment (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation) begins.

prescriptiondrugs.name: prescription drugs
prescriptiondrugs.definition: Prescription drugs is drugs that cannot be sold legally without a prescription.

competitivemedicalplans.name: competitive medical plans
competitivemedicalplans.definition: Competitive medical plans is alternative health care delivery mechanisms, such as preferred provider organizations or other health insurance services or prepaid plans (other than health maintenance organizations), that meet Medicare qualifications for a risk-sharing contract. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

foodadditives.name: food additives
foodadditives.definition: Food additives is substances used in the processing or storage of foods or [MASK] including antioxidants; food preservatives; food coloring agents; flavoring agents; anti-infective agents; excipients and other similarly used substances. Many of the same substances are used as pharmaceutic aids.

fusionregulatoryprotein1,heavychain.name: fusion regulatory protein 1 , heavy chain
fusionregulatoryprotein1,heavychain.definition: Heavy chain fusion regulatory protein 1 is a transmembrane glycoprotein subunit that can dimerize with a variety of light chain subunits such as slc7a5; slc7a6, and 4f2 light chains. This protein subunit serves a diverse array of functions including amino acid transport and cell fusion. Its function is altered depending which of the light chain subunits it interacts with.

ethicscommittees,research.name: ethics committees , research
ethicscommittees,research.definition: Research ethics committees is hospital or other institutional committees established to protect the welfare of research subjects. Federal regulations (the "Common Rule" (45 cfr 46)) mandate the use of these committees to monitor federally-funded biomedical and behavioral research involving human subjects.

aminoacidtransportsystemasc.name: amino acid transport system asc
aminoacidtransportsystemasc.definition: Amino acid transport system asc is a ubiquitous sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter. The preferred substrates for this transporter system include [MASK]; serine; and [MASK].

adaptorproteincomplexgammasubunits.name: adaptor protein complex gamma subunits
adaptorproteincomplexgammasubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex gamma subunits is a family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 90 KDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of adaptor protein complex 1.

epidemiologicresearchdesign.name: epidemiologic research design
epidemiologicresearchdesign.definition: Epidemiologic research design is the form and structure of analytic studies in epidemiologic research.

parity.name: parity
parity.definition: Parity is the number of offspring a female has borne. It is contrasted with gravidity, which refers to the number of pregnancies, regardless of outcome.

anemia,refractory.name: anemia , refractory
anemia,refractory.definition: Refractory anemia is a severe sometimes chronic anemia, usually macrocytic in type, that does not respond to ordinary antianemic therapy.

certification.name: certification
certification.definition: Certification is compliance with a [MASK] of standards defined by non-governmental organizations. Certification is applied for by individuals on a voluntary basis and represents a professional status when achieved, e.g., certification for a medical specialty.

rain.name: rain
rain.definition: Rain is water particles that fall from the atmosphere.

abdominalwoundclosuretechniques.name: abdominal wound closure techniques
abdominalwoundclosuretechniques.definition: Abdominal wound closure techniques is methods to repair breaks in abdominal tissues caused by trauma or to close [MASK] during abdominal surgery.

spatialanalysis.name: spatial analysis
spatialanalysis.definition: Spatial analysis is investigative techniques which measure the topological, geometric, and or geographic properties of the entities studied.

infantcare.name: infant care
infantcare.definition: Infant care is care of infants in the home or institution.

education,medical,graduate.name: education , medical , graduate
education,medical,graduate.definition: Graduate medical education is educational programs for medical graduates entering a specialty. They include formal specialty training as well as academic work in the clinical and basic medical sciences, and may lead to board certification or an advanced medical degree.

serotoninsyndrome.name: serotonin syndrome
serotoninsyndrome.definition: Serotonin syndrome is an adverse drug interaction characterized by altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and neuromuscular abnormalities. It is most frequently caused by use of both serotonin reuptake inhibitors and monoamine oxidase inhibitors, leading to excess serotonin availability in the cns at the serotonin 1a receptor.

rna,satellite.name: rna , satellite
rna,satellite.definition: Satellite rna is small, linear single-stranded rna molecules functionally acting as molecular parasites of certain rna plant viruses. Satellite RNAs exhibit four characteristic traits: (1) they require helper viruses to replicate; (2) they are unnecessary for the replication of helper viruses; (3) they are encapsidated in the coat protein of the helper virus; (4) they have no extensive sequence homology to the helper virus. Thus they differ from satellite viruses which encode their own coat protein, and from the genomic rna; (=rna, viral); of satellite viruses. (From Maramorosch, Viroids and Satellites, 1991, p143)

dermatitis,atopic.name: dermatitis , atopic
dermatitis,atopic.definition: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory genetically determined disease of the skin marked by increased ability to form reagin (IgE), with increased susceptibility to allergic rhinitis and asthma, and hereditary disposition to a lowered threshold for pruritus. It is manifested by lichenification, excoriation, and crusting, mainly on the flexural surfaces of the elbow and [MASK]. In infants it is known as infantile eczema.

respiratorytractdiseases.name: respiratory tract diseases
respiratorytractdiseases.definition: Respiratory tract diseases is diseases involving the respiratory system.

dextransulfate.name: dextran sulfate
dextransulfate.definition: Dextran sulfate is long-chain polymer of glucose containing 17-20% sulfur. It has been used as an anticoagulant and also has been shown to inhibit the binding of hiv-1 to cd4-positive t-lymphocytes. It is commonly used as both an experimental and clinical laboratory reagent and has been investigated for use as an antiviral agent, in the treatment of hypolipidemia, and for the prevention of free radical damage, among other applications.

pathologicalconditions,anatomical.name: pathological conditions , anatomical
pathologicalconditions,anatomical.definition: Anatomical pathological conditions is an abnormal structural condition of the [MASK], usually macroscopic, that is common to a variety of different diseases.

opticnerve.name: optic nerve
opticnerve.definition: Optic nerve is the 2nd cranial nerve which conveys visual information from the retina to the brain. The nerve carries the axons of the [MASK] which sort at the optic chiasm and continue via the optic tracts to the brain. The largest [MASK] is to the lateral geniculate nuclei; other targets include the superior colliculi and the suprachiasmatic nuclei. Though known as the second cranial nerve, it is considered part of the central nervous system.

carcinoma,papillary.name: carcinoma , papillary
carcinoma,papillary.definition: Papillary carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm characterized by the formation of numerous, irregular, finger-like projections of fibrous stroma that is covered with a surface layer of neoplastic epithelial cells. (Stedman, 25th ed)

grouppurchasing.name: group purchasing
grouppurchasing.definition: Group purchasing is a shared service which combines the purchasing power of individual organizations or facilities in order to obtain lower prices for equipment and supplies. (From Health Care Terms, 2nd ed)

evokedpotentials,auditory.name: evoked potentials , auditory
evokedpotentials,auditory.definition: Auditory evoked potentials is the electric response evoked in the cerebral cortex by [MASK] or stimulation of the [MASK].

akinaseanchorproteins.name: a kinase anchor proteins
akinaseanchorproteins.definition: A kinase anchor proteins is a structurally-diverse family of intracellular-signaling adaptor proteins that selectively tether specific protein kinase a subtypes to distinct subcellular sites. They play a role in focusing the protein kinase a activity toward relevant substrates. Over fifty members of this family exist, most of which bind specifically to regulatory subunits of cyclic amp-dependent protein kinase type ii such as camp protein kinase riialpha or camp protein kinase riibeta.

autonomicnervoussystemdiseases.name: autonomic nervous system diseases
autonomicnervoussystemdiseases.definition: Autonomic nervous system diseases is diseases of the parasympathetic or sympathetic divisions of the autonomic nervous system; which has components located in the central nervous system and peripheral nervous system. Autonomic dysfunction may be associated with hypothalamic diseases; brain stem disorders; spinal cord diseases; and peripheral nervous system diseases. Manifestations include impairments of vegetative functions including the maintenance of blood pressure; heart rate; pupil function; sweating; reproductive and urinary physiology; and [MASK].

proteinkinaseinhibitors.name: protein kinase inhibitors
proteinkinaseinhibitors.definition: Protein kinase inhibitors is agents that inhibit protein kinases.

programmedcelldeath1receptor.name: programmed cell death 1 receptor
programmedcelldeath1receptor.definition: Programmed cell death 1 receptor is an inhibitory T-lymphocyte receptor that has specificity for cd274 antigen and programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 protein. Signaling by the receptor limits t cell proliferation and interferon gamma synthesis. The receptor also may play an essential role in the regulatory pathway that induces [MASK].

urinaryfistula.name: urinary fistula
urinaryfistula.definition: Urinary fistula is an abnormal passage in any part of the urinary tract between itself or with other organs.

insomnia,fatalfamilial.name: insomnia , fatal familial
insomnia,fatalfamilial.definition: Fatal familial insomnia is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by degeneration of the thalamus and progressive insomnia. It is caused by a mutation in the prion protein (prions).

geneexpressionregulation,bacterial.name: gene expression regulation , bacterial
geneexpressionregulation,bacterial.definition: Bacterial gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which cytoplasmic or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in bacteria.

beds.name: beds
beds.definition: Beds is equipment on which one may lie and sleep, especially as used to care for the hospital patient.

fishes.name: fishes
fishes.definition: Fishes is a group of cold-blooded, aquatic vertebrates having gills, fins, a cartilaginous or bony endoskeleton, and elongated bodies covered with scales.

poisoncontrolcenters.name: poison control centers
poisoncontrolcenters.definition: Poison control centers is facilities which provide information concerning poisons and treatment of poisoning in emergencies.

nutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.name: nutritional physiological phenomena
nutritionalphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Nutritional physiological phenomena is the processes and properties of living organisms by which they take in and balance the use of nutritive materials for energy, heat production, or building material for the growth, maintenance, or repair of tissues and the nutritive properties of food.

oxygencompounds.name: oxygen compounds
oxygencompounds.definition: Oxygen compounds is inorganic compounds that contain oxygen as an integral part of the molecule.

neglecteddiseases.name: neglected diseases
neglecteddiseases.definition: Neglected diseases is diseases that are underfunded and have low name recognition but are major burdens in less [MASK]. The [MASK] Organization has designated six tropical infectious diseases as being neglected in [MASK] that are endemic in many developing countries (helminthiasis; leprosy; lymphatic filariasis; onchocerciasis; schistosomiasis; and trachoma).

cerebrospinalfluidleak.name: cerebrospinal fluid leak
cerebrospinalfluidleak.definition: Cerebrospinal fluid leak is discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea) or the ear (cerebrospinal fluid otorrhea).

fishflour.name: fish flour
fishflour.definition: Fish flour is a flour made of pulverized, dried fish or fish parts.

geneticcarrierscreening.name: genetic carrier screening
geneticcarrierscreening.definition: Genetic carrier screening is identification of individuals who are heterozygous at a genetic locus for a recessive phenotype.

bloodsubstitutes.name: blood substitutes
bloodsubstitutes.definition: Blood substitutes is substances that are used in place of blood, for example, as an alternative to blood transfusions after blood loss to restore blood volume and oxygen-carrying capacity to the blood circulation, or to perfuse isolated organs.

chemical.name: chemical
chemical.definition: Chemical is a substance obtained by a chemical process or producing a chemical effect.

solidwaste.name: solid waste
solidwaste.definition: Solid waste is garbage, refuse, or [MASK], or other discarded materials from a [MASK] plant, water supply treatment plant, and air pollution [MASK] that include solid, semi-solid, or contained material. It does not include materials dissolved in domestic [MASK], irrigation return flows, or industrial discharges.

traction.name: traction
traction.definition: Traction is the pull on a limb or a part thereof. Skin traction (indirect traction) is applied by using a bandage to pull on the skin and fascia where light traction is required. Skeletal traction (direct traction), however, uses pins or wires inserted through bone and is attached to weights, pulleys, and ropes. (From Blauvelt & Nelson, a Manual of Orthopaedic Terminology, 5th ed)

toolusebehavior.name: tool use behavior
toolusebehavior.definition: Tool use behavior is modifying, carrying, or manipulating an item external to itself by an animal, before using it to effect a change on the environment or itself (from Beck, Animal Tool Behavior, 1980).

attitudetocomputers.name: attitude to computers
attitudetocomputers.definition: Attitude to computers is the attitude and behavior associated with an individual using the computer.

geographicmapping.name: geographic mapping
geographicmapping.definition: Geographic mapping is creating a representation of areas of the earth or other celestial bodies, for the purpose of visualizing spatial distributions of various information.

cardiovascularsurgicalprocedures.name: cardiovascular surgical procedures
cardiovascularsurgicalprocedures.definition: Cardiovascular surgical procedures is surgery performed on the heart or blood vessels.

nausea.name: nausea
nausea.definition: Nausea is an unpleasant sensation in the stomach usually accompanied by the urge to vomit. Common causes are early pregnancy, sea and motion sickness, emotional stress, intense pain, food poisoning, and various enteroviruses.

capillaryleaksyndrome.name: capillary leak syndrome
capillaryleaksyndrome.definition: Capillary leak syndrome is a condition characterized by recurring episodes of fluid leaking from capillaries into extra-vascular compartments causing hematocrit to rise precipitously. If not treated, generalized vascular leak can lead to generalized edema; shock; cardiovascular collapse; and [MASK].

lithiumcarbonate.name: lithium carbonate
lithiumcarbonate.definition: [MASK] carbonate is a [MASK] [MASK], classified as a mood-stabilizing agent. [MASK] ion alters the metabolism of biogenic monoamines in the central nervous system, and affects multiple neurotransmission systems.

mesoderm.name: mesoderm
mesoderm.definition: Mesoderm is the middle germ layer of an embryo derived from three paired mesenchymal aggregates along the neural tube.

faculty,pharmacy.name: faculty , pharmacy
faculty,pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy faculty is teaching and administrative staff having academic rank in a [MASK] or department.

spacemotionsickness.name: space motion sickness
spacemotionsickness.definition: Space motion sickness is disorder characterized by nausea, vomiting, and dizziness, possibly in response to vestibular disorientation or fluid shifts associated with space flight. (From Webster's New World Dictionary)

genes,recessive.name: genes , recessive
genes,recessive.definition: Recessive genes is genes that influence the phenotype only in the homozygous state.

hospitalplanning.name: hospital planning
hospitalplanning.definition: Hospital planning is areawide planning for hospitals or planning of a particular hospital unit on the basis of projected consumer need. This does not include [MASK] or architectural plans.

alcohols.name: alcohols
alcohols.definition: Alcohols is alkyl compounds containing a hydroxyl group. They are classified according to relation of the carbon atom: primary alcohols, r-ch2oh; secondary alcohols, r2-choh; tertiary alcohols, r3-coh. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

insulinantagonists.name: insulin antagonists
insulinantagonists.definition: Insulin antagonists is compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or action of insulin.

trainingsupport.name: training support
trainingsupport.definition: Training support is financial support for training including both student stipends and loans and training grants to institutions.

epidemiologicstudycharacteristics.name: epidemiologic study characteristics
epidemiologicstudycharacteristics.definition: Epidemiologic study characteristics is works about types and formulations of studies used in epidemiological research.

adaptorproteincomplexalphasubunits.name: adaptor protein complex alpha subunits
adaptorproteincomplexalphasubunits.definition: Adaptor protein complex alpha subunits is a family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 100 kDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of [MASK].

photosyntheticreactioncentercomplexprote.name: photosynthetic reaction center complex proteins
photosyntheticreactioncentercomplexprote.definition: Photosynthetic reaction center complex proteins is protein complexes that take part in the process of [MASK]. They are located within the thylakoid membranes of plant chloroplasts and a variety of structures in more primitive organisms. There are two major complexes involved in the photosynthetic process called photosystem i and photosystem ii.

proteinkinases.name: protein kinases
proteinkinases.definition: Protein kinases is a family of enzymes that catalyze the conversion of atp and a protein to adp and a phosphoprotein.

immersionfoot.name: immersion foot
immersionfoot.definition: Immersion [MASK] is a condition of the [MASK] produced by prolonged exposure of the [MASK] to water. Exposure for 48 hours or more to warm water causes tropical immersion [MASK] or warm-water immersion [MASK] common in Vietnam where troops were exposed to prolonged or repeated wading in paddy fields or [MASK]. Trench [MASK] results from prolonged exposure to cold, without actual freezing. It was common in trench warfare during World War i, when soldiers stood, sometimes for hours, in trenches with a few inches of cold water in them. (Andrews' Diseases of the Skin, 8th ed, p27)

iran.name: iran
iran.definition: Iran is a country bordering the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and the Caspian Sea, between Iraq and Pakistan. The capital is Tehran.

pregnancy,twin.name: pregnancy , twin
pregnancy,twin.definition: Twin pregnancy is the condition of carrying twins simultaneously.

pupildisorders.name: pupil disorders
pupildisorders.definition: Pupil disorders is conditions which affect the structure or function of the pupil of the eye, including disorders of innervation to the pupillary constrictor or dilator muscles, and disorders of pupillary reflexes.

receptors,cellsurface.name: receptors , cell surface
receptors,cellsurface.definition: Cell surface receptors is cell surface proteins that bind signalling molecules external to the cell with high affinity and convert this extracellular event into one or more intracellular signals that alter the behavior of the target cell (From Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2nd ed, pp693-5). Cell surface receptors, unlike enzymes, do not chemically alter their ligands.

respiratorytractfistula.name: respiratory tract fistula
respiratorytractfistula.definition: Respiratory tract fistula is an abnormal passage communicating between any component of the respiratory tract or between any part of the respiratory system and surrounding organs.

vascularcapacitance.name: vascular capacitance
vascularcapacitance.definition: Vascular capacitance is the measure of a blood VESSEL's ability to increase the volume of blood it holds without a large increase in blood pressure. The vascular capacitance is equal to the change in volume divided by the change in pressure.

soil.name: soil
soil.definition: Soil is the unconsolidated mineral or organic matter on the surface of the earth that serves as a natural medium for the growth of land plants.

officevisits.name: office visits
officevisits.definition: Office visits is visits made by patients to health service providers' offices for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.

chromosomes,human,pair13.name: chromosomes , human , pair 13
chromosomes,human,pair13.definition: Pair 13 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group d chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

lacoperon.name: lac operon
lacoperon.definition: Lac operon is the genetic unit consisting of three structural genes, an operator and a regulatory gene. The regulatory gene controls the synthesis of the three structural genes: beta-galactosidase and beta-galactoside permease (involved with the metabolism of lactose), and beta-thiogalactoside acetyltransferase.

birthintervals.name: birth intervals
birthintervals.definition: Birth intervals is the lengths of intervals between births to women in the population.

bedconversion.name: bed conversion
bedconversion.definition: Bed conversion is the reallocation of beds from one type of care service to another, as in converting acute care beds to long term care beds.

mazeprocedure.name: maze procedure
mazeprocedure.definition: Maze procedure is a surgical treatment in which heart tissue is scarred (cut-and-sew method), excised or otherwise destroyed in an open chest approach to direct electrical signals through a more controlled path via the atrioventricular node. It is often used to restore normal rhythms in atrial fibrillation.

mouthrehabilitation.name: mouth rehabilitation
mouthrehabilitation.definition: Mouth rehabilitation is process of restoring damaged or decayed teeth using various restorative and non-cosmetic materials so that [MASK] is improved.

carcinoma,basalcell.name: carcinoma , basal cell
carcinoma,basalcell.definition: Basal cell carcinoma is a malignant skin neoplasm that seldom metastasizes but has potentialities for local invasion and destruction. Clinically it is divided into types: nodular, cicatricial, morphaic, and erythematoid (pagetoid). They develop on hair-bearing skin, most commonly on sun-exposed areas. Approximately 85% are found on the head and [MASK] area and the remaining 15% on the trunk and limbs. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1471)

communitymentalhealthcenters.name: community mental health centers
communitymentalhealthcenters.definition: Community mental health centers is facilities which administer the delivery of psychologic and psychiatric services to people living in a neighborhood or community.

centralpatterngenerators.name: central pattern generators
centralpatterngenerators.definition: Central pattern generators is networks of nerve cells that control the firing patterns of motor neurons to produce rhythmic movements such as mastication; walking; [MASK]; respiration; and peristalsis.

alcoholdrinkingincollege.name: alcohol drinking in college
alcoholdrinkingincollege.definition: Alcohol drinking in college is alcohol consumption among college students.

wisconsin.name: wisconsin
wisconsin.definition: Wisconsin is state bounded on the north by [MASK] Superior and Michigan, on the east by [MASK] Michigan, on the south by Illinois and Iowa, and on the west by [MASK] and Iowa.

socialdeterminantsofhealth.name: social determinants of health
socialdeterminantsofhealth.definition: Social determinants of health is the circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider [MASK] of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (http://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/).

cleftpalate.name: cleft palate
cleftpalate.definition: Cleft palate is congenital fissure of the soft and/or [MASK], due to faulty fusion.

vitreousdetachment.name: vitreous detachment
vitreousdetachment.definition: Vitreous detachment is detachment of the corpus vitreum ([MASK]) from its normal attachments, especially the retina, due to shrinkage from degenerative or inflammatory conditions, trauma, myopia, or senility.

serum.name: serum
serum.definition: Serum is the clear portion of blood that is left after blood coagulation to remove blood cells and clotting proteins.

familyrelations.name: family relations
familyrelations.definition: Family relations is behavioral, psychological, and social relations among various members of the nuclear family and the extended family.

diary.name: diary
diary.definition: Diary is work consisting of records, usually private, of writers' experiences, observations, feelings, attitudes, etc. They may also be works marked in [MASK] order in which to note appointments and the like. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

diagnostictechniques,respiratorysystem.name: diagnostic techniques , respiratory system
diagnostictechniques,respiratorysystem.definition: Respiratory system diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the respiratory tract or its organs. It includes respiratory function tests.

alcoholicbeverages.name: alcoholic beverages
alcoholicbeverages.definition: Alcoholic beverages is drinkable liquids containing ethanol.

infarction,anteriorcerebralartery.name: infarction , anterior cerebral artery
infarction,anteriorcerebralartery.definition: Anterior cerebral artery infarction is necrosis occurring in the anterior cerebral artery system, including branches such as Heubner's artery. These arteries supply blood to the medial and superior parts of the cerebral hemisphere, Infarction in the anterior cerebral artery usually results in sensory and motor impairment in the lower body.

siliconeoils.name: silicone oils
siliconeoils.definition: Silicone oils is organic siloxanes which are polymerized to the oily stage. The oils have low [MASK] and density less than 1. They are used in industrial applications and in the treatment of retinal detachment, complicated by proliferative vitreoretinopathy.

orthodonticappliances.name: orthodontic appliances
orthodonticappliances.definition: Orthodontic appliances is devices used for influencing tooth position. Orthodontic appliances may be classified as fixed or removable, active or retaining, and intraoral or extraoral. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p19)

drugmonitoring.name: drug monitoring
drugmonitoring.definition: Drug monitoring is the process of observing, recording, or detecting the effects of a chemical substance administered to an individual therapeutically or diagnostically.

spores,fungal.name: spores , fungal
spores,fungal.definition: Fungal spores is reproductive bodies produced by fungi.

hormones,ectopic.name: hormones , ectopic
hormones,ectopic.definition: Ectopic hormones is hormones released from neoplasms or from other cells that are not the usual sources of hormones.

forearminjuries.name: forearm injuries
forearminjuries.definition: Forearm injuries is injuries to the part of the upper limb of the body between the wrist and elbow.

depression,postpartum.name: depression , postpartum
depression,postpartum.definition: Postpartum depression is depression in postpartum women, usually within four weeks after giving birth (parturition). The degree of depression ranges from mild transient depression to neurotic or psychotic depressive disorders. (From [MASK], p386)

receptor,ciliaryneurotrophicfactor.name: receptor , ciliary neurotrophic factor
receptor,ciliaryneurotrophicfactor.definition: Ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor is cell surface receptors for ciliary neurotrophic factor. They are heterotrimeric proteins formed by the association of the ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit with the [MASK] and the cytokine receptor gp130. Although the receptor regulates neuronal development, it is structurally similar to the cytokine receptor for interleukin-6; (receptors, interleukin-6).

students,publichealth.name: students , public health
students,publichealth.definition: Public health students is individuals enrolled in a school of public health or a formal educational program in public health.

swine.name: swine
swine.definition: Swine is any of various animals that constitute the family Suidae and comprise stout-bodied, short-legged omnivorous mammals with thick skin, usually covered with coarse bristles, a rather long mobile snout, and small tail. Included are the genera Babyrousa, Phacochoerus (wart hogs), and Sus, the latter containing the domestic pig (see sus scrofa).

tuberculosis,pulmonary.name: tuberculosis , pulmonary
tuberculosis,pulmonary.definition: Pulmonary tuberculosis is mycobacterium infections of the lung.

vocabulary.name: vocabulary
vocabulary.definition: Vocabulary is the sum or the stock of words used by a language, a group, or an individual. (From Webster, 3d ed)

commerce.name: commerce
commerce.definition: Commerce is the interchange of goods or commodities, especially on a large scale, between different countries or between populations within the same country. It includes trade (the buying, selling, or exchanging of commodities, whether wholesale or retail) and business (the purchase and sale of goods to make a profit). (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed, p411, p2005 & p283)

benchmarking.name: benchmarking
benchmarking.definition: Benchmarking is method of measuring performance against established standards of [MASK].

pipesmoking.name: pipe smoking
pipesmoking.definition: Pipe smoking is smoking by use of a narrow conveying tube which feeds from an open cavity where smoked product is loaded and burned.

jointloosebodies.name: joint loose bodies
jointloosebodies.definition: Joint loose bodies is fibrous, bony, cartilaginous and osteocartilaginous fragments in a synovial joint. Major causes are osteochondritis dissecans, synovial chondromatosis, osteophytes, fractured articular surfaces and damaged menisci.

caspase7.name: caspase 7
caspase7.definition: Caspase 7 is a short pro-domain caspase that plays an effector role in apoptosis. It is activated by initiator caspases such as caspase 3 and caspase 10. Several isoforms of this protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its messenger rna.

lasers,semiconductor.name: lasers , semiconductor
lasers,semiconductor.definition: Semiconductor lasers is lasers with a semiconductor diode as the active medium. Diode lasers transform electric energy to light using the same principle as a light-emitting diode (led), but with internal reflection capability, thus forming a resonator where a stimulated light can reflect back and forth, allowing only a certain wavelength to be emitted. The emission of a given device is determined by the active compound used (e.g., gallium arsenide crystals doped with aluminum or indium). Typical wavelengths are 810, 1,060 and 1,300 nm. (From umdns, 2005)

environmentalpolicy.name: environmental policy
environmentalpolicy.definition: Environmental policy is a course of action or principle adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual that concerns human interactions with nature and natural resources.

airpollution.name: air pollution
airpollution.definition: Air pollution is the presence of contaminants or pollutant substances in the air (air pollutants) that interfere with human health or welfare, or produce other harmful environmental effects. The substances may include gases; particulate matter; or volatile organic chemicals.

vesicularglutamatetransportprotein2.name: vesicular glutamate transport protein 2
vesicularglutamatetransportprotein2.definition: Vesicular glutamate transport protein 2 is a vesicular glutamate transporter protein that is predominately expressed in the diencephalon and lower brainstem regions of the central nervous system.

americanrevolution.name: american revolution
americanrevolution.definition: American revolution is armed [MASK] that resulted in separation of American colonies from Britain and established the United States of America.

bodypatterning.name: body patterning
bodypatterning.definition: Body patterning is the processes occurring in early development that direct morphogenesis. They specify the body plan ensuring that cells will proceed to differentiate, grow, and diversify in size and shape at the correct relative positions. Included are axial patterning, segmentation, compartment specification, limb position, organ boundary patterning, blood vessel patterning, etc.

cycline.name: cyclin e
cycline.definition: Cyclin e is a 50-kDa protein that complexes with cyclin-dependent kinase 2 in the late g1 phase of the cell cycle.

digestivesystemphysiologicalphenomena.name: digestive system physiological phenomena
digestivesystemphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Digestive system physiological phenomena is properties and processes of the digestive system as a whole or of any of its parts.

nursingprocess.name: nursing process
nursingprocess.definition: Nursing process is the sum total of nursing activities which includes assessment (identifying needs), intervention (ministering to needs), and evaluation (validating the effectiveness of the help given).

anatomicvariation.name: anatomic variation
anatomicvariation.definition: Anatomic variation is peculiarities associated with the internal structure, form, topology, or architecture of organisms that distinguishes them from others of the same species or group.

rnainterference.name: rna interference
rnainterference.definition: Rna interference is a gene silencing phenomenon whereby specific dsRNAs (rna, double-stranded) trigger the degradation of homologous mRNA (rna, messenger). The specific dsRNAs are processed into small interfering rna (siRNA) which serves as a guide for cleavage of the homologous mRNA in the rna-induced silencing complex. [MASK] may also be triggered during this process.

nursingcare.name: nursing care
nursingcare.definition: Nursing care is care given to patients by nursing service personnel.

nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member1.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 1
nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member1.definition: Member 1 group f nuclear receptor subfamily 1 is a DNA-binding orphan nuclear receptor that positively regulates expression of arntl transcription factors and is a regulatory component of the circadian clock system. The protein also has a role in neuron cell survival and differentiation in that loss of function mutations of its gene result in the mouse phenotype referred to as the staggerer mouse.

hnprotein.name: hn protein
hnprotein.definition: Hn protein is glycoprotein from Sendai, para-influenza, Newcastle Disease, and other viruses that participates in binding the virus to cell-surface receptors. The hn protein possesses both hemagglutinin and neuraminidase activity.

criticalperiod,psychological.name: critical period , psychological
criticalperiod,psychological.definition: Psychological critical period is a specific stage in animal and human development during which certain types of behavior normally are shaped and molded for life.

altitude.name: altitude
altitude.definition: Altitude is a vertical distance measured from a known level on the surface of a planet or other celestial body.

geneticvectors.name: genetic vectors
geneticvectors.definition: Genetic vectors is dna molecules capable of autonomous replication within a host cell and into which other dna sequences can be inserted and thus amplified. Many are derived from plasmids; bacteriophages; or viruses. They are used for transporting foreign genes into recipient cells. Genetic vectors possess a functional replicator site and contain genetic markers to facilitate their selective recognition.

leptin.name: leptin
leptin.definition: Leptin is a 16-kDa peptide hormone secreted from [MASK]. Leptin serves as a [MASK] signal from fat cells to the central nervous system in regulation of food intake, energy balance, and fat storage.

proxy.name: proxy
proxy.definition: Proxy is a person authorized to decide or act for another person, for example, a person having durable power of attorney.

growthinhibitors.name: growth inhibitors
growthinhibitors.definition: Growth inhibitors is endogenous or exogenous substances which inhibit the normal growth of human and animal cells or micro-organisms, as distinguished from those affecting plant growth (= plant growth regulators).

inguinalcanal.name: inguinal canal
inguinalcanal.definition: Inguinal canal is the tunnel in the lower anterior [MASK] through which the spermatic cord, in the male; round ligament, in the female; nerves; and vessels pass. Its internal end is at the deep inguinal ring and its external end is at the superficial inguinal ring.

coronarycareunits.name: coronary care units
coronarycareunits.definition: Coronary care units is the hospital unit in which patients with acute cardiac disorders receive intensive care.

breastcyst.name: breast cyst
breastcyst.definition: Breast cyst is a fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an epithelium and found in the breast. It may appear as a single large cyst in one breast, multifocal, or bilateral in fibrocystic breast disease.

birthsetting.name: birth setting
birthsetting.definition: Birth setting is physical setting or location of birth.

insurancecoverage.name: insurance coverage
insurancecoverage.definition: Insurance coverage is generally refers to the amount of protection available and the kind of loss which would be paid for under an insurance contract with an insurer. (Slee & Slee, Health Care Terms, 2d ed)

patientaccesstorecords.name: patient access to records
patientaccesstorecords.definition: Patient access to records is the freedom of patients to review their own medical, genetic, or other health-related records.

lupusvulgaris.name: lupus vulgaris
lupusvulgaris.definition: Lupus vulgaris is a form of cutaneous tuberculosis. It is seen predominantly in women and typically involves the nasal mucosa; [MASK]; and conjunctival mucosa.

chromosomes,human,pair3.name: chromosomes , human , pair 3
chromosomes,human,pair3.definition: Pair 3 human chromosomes is a specific pair of human chromosomes in group a (chromosomes, human, 1-3) of the human chromosome classification.

dentalhealthservices.name: dental health services
dentalhealthservices.definition: Dental health services is services designed to promote, maintain, or restore dental health.

immunizationprograms.name: immunization programs
immunizationprograms.definition: Immunization programs is organized services to administer immunization procedures in the prevention of various diseases. The programs are made available over a wide range of sites: schools, hospitals, public health agencies, voluntary health agencies, etc. They are administered to an equally wide range of population groups or on various administrative levels: community, municipal, state, national, international.

microscopy,electron,scanning.name: microscopy , electron , scanning
microscopy,electron,scanning.definition: Scanning [MASK] microscopy is microscopy in which the object is examined directly by an [MASK] beam scanning the specimen point-by-point. The image is constructed by detecting the products of specimen interactions that are projected above the plane of the sample, such as backscattered [MASK]. Although scanning transmission [MASK] microscopy also scans the specimen point by point with the [MASK] beam, the image is constructed by detecting the [MASK], or their interaction products that are transmitted through the sample plane, so that is a form of transmission [MASK] microscopy.

sodiumglutamate.name: sodium glutamate
sodiumglutamate.definition: Sodium glutamate is one of the flavoring agents used to impart a meat-like flavor.

peptidehormones.name: peptide hormones
peptidehormones.definition: Peptide hormones is hormones synthesized from amino acids. They are distinguished from intercellular signaling peptides and proteins in that their actions are systemic.

minorplanets.name: minor planets
minorplanets.definition: Minor planets is small solar system planetary bodies including asteroids. Most asteroids are found within the gap lying between the [MASK] of Mars and Jupiter.

oralulcer.name: oral ulcer
oralulcer.definition: Oral [MASK] is a loss of mucous substance of the mouth showing local excavation of the surface, resulting from the sloughing of inflammatory necrotic tissue. It is the result of a variety of causes, e.g., denture irritation, aphthous stomatitis (stomatitis, aphthous); noma; necrotizing gingivitis (gingivitis, necrotizing ulcerative); toothbrushing; and various irritants. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p842)

colonycount,microbial.name: colony count , microbial
colonycount,microbial.definition: Microbial colony count is enumeration by direct count of viable, isolated bacterial, archaeal, or fungal cells or spores capable of growth on solid culture media. The method is used routinely by environmental microbiologists for quantifying organisms in air; food; and water; by clinicians for measuring patients' microbial load; and in antimicrobial drug testing.

druginformationservices.name: drug information services
druginformationservices.definition: Drug information services is services providing pharmaceutic and therapeutic drug information and consultation.

rnastability.name: rna stability
rnastability.definition: Rna stability is the extent to which an rna molecule retains its structural integrity and resists degradation by rnase, and base-catalyzed hydrolysis, under changing in vivo or in vitro conditions.

spontaneouscombustion.name: spontaneous combustion
spontaneouscombustion.definition: Spontaneous combustion is a circumstance where a substance or organism takes fire and burns without an exogenous source. Spontaneous human combustion differs from preternatural human combustibility in that in the latter, some spark or trivial flame sets the fire and the body tissues, which have a greatly enhanced inflammability, continue to undergo incineration without any external heat source or combustible materials. (Bergman na. Spontaneous human combustion: its role in literature and science. Pharos 1988;Fall;51(4):18-21)

gaitdisorders,neurologic.name: gait disorders , neurologic
gaitdisorders,neurologic.definition: Neurologic gait disorders is gait abnormalities that are a manifestation of nervous system dysfunction. These conditions may be caused by a wide variety of disorders which affect motor control, sensory [MASK], and muscle strength including: central nervous system diseases; peripheral nervous system diseases; neuromuscular diseases; or muscular diseases.

bloodcoagulationtests.name: blood coagulation tests
bloodcoagulationtests.definition: Blood coagulation tests is laboratory tests for evaluating the individual's clotting mechanism.

heartdefects,congenital.name: heart defects , congenital
heartdefects,congenital.definition: Congenital heart defects is developmental abnormalities involving structures of the heart. These defects are present at birth but may be discovered later in life.

reperfusioninjury.name: reperfusion injury
reperfusioninjury.definition: Reperfusion injury is adverse functional, metabolic, or structural changes in ischemic tissues resulting from the restoration of blood flow to the tissue (reperfusion), including swelling; hemorrhage; necrosis; and damage from free radicals. The most common instance is myocardial reperfusion injury.

fareast.name: far east
fareast.definition: Far east is a geographic area of east and southeast Asia encompassing china; hong kong; japan; korea; macao; mongolia; and [MASK].

infantwelfare.name: infant welfare
infantwelfare.definition: Infant welfare is organized efforts by communities or organizations to improve the health and well-being of infants.

computerusertraining.name: computer user training
computerusertraining.definition: Computer user training is process of teaching a person to interact and communicate with a computer.

watercycle.name: water cycle
watercycle.definition: Water cycle is circulation of water among various ecological systems, in various states, on, above, and below the surface of the earth.

internationallaw.name: international law
internationallaw.definition: International law is the body of law that governs the legal relations between or among sovereign states or nations.

syntheticbiology.name: synthetic biology
syntheticbiology.definition: Synthetic biology is a field of biological research combining engineering in the formulation, design, and building (synthesis) of novel biological structures, functions, and systems.

lymphaticvessels.name: lymphatic vessels
lymphaticvessels.definition: Lymphatic vessels is tubular vessels that are involved in the transport of [MASK] and lymphocytes.

conedystrophy.name: cone dystrophy
conedystrophy.definition: Cone dystrophy is a general term which describes a group of rare eye disorders that affect the cone cells of the retina. Cone dystrophy can cause a variety of symptoms including decreased visual clarity or acuity when looking straight ahead (central vision), a reduced ability to see [MASK], and an increased sensitivity to light (photophobia).

ocularmotilitydisorders.name: ocular motility disorders
ocularmotilitydisorders.definition: Ocular motility disorders is disorders that feature impairment of eye movements as a primary manifestation of disease. These conditions may be divided into infranuclear, nuclear, and supranuclear disorders. Diseases of the eye muscles or oculomotor cranial nerves (iii, iv, and vi) are considered infranuclear. Nuclear disorders are caused by disease of the oculomotor, trochlear, or abducens nuclei in the brain stem. Supranuclear disorders are produced by dysfunction of higher order sensory and motor systems that control eye movements, including neural networks in the cerebral cortex; basal ganglia; cerebellum; and brain stem. Ocular torticollis refers to a head tilt that is caused by an ocular misalignment. Opsoclonus refers to rapid, conjugate oscillations of the eyes in multiple directions, which may occur as a parainfectious or paraneoplastic condition (e.g., opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome). (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p240)

spacecraft.name: spacecraft
spacecraft.definition: Spacecraft is devices, manned and unmanned, which are designed to be placed into an [MASK] about the Earth or into a trajectory to another celestial body. (nasa Thesaurus, 1988)

poverty.name: poverty
poverty.definition: Poverty is a situation in which the level of living of an individual, family, or group is below the standard of the community. It is often related to a specific income level.

healthlevelseven.name: health level seven
healthlevelseven.definition: Health level seven is an American National Standards Institute-accredited organization working on specifications to support development and advancement of clinical and administrative standards for healthcare.

anteriorcompartmentsyndrome.name: anterior compartment syndrome
anteriorcompartmentsyndrome.definition: Anterior compartment syndrome is rapid swelling, increased tension, pain, and ischemic necrosis of the muscles of the anterior tibial compartment of the leg, often following excessive physical exertion.

mitralvalve.name: mitral valve
mitralvalve.definition: Mitral valve is the valve between the left atrium and left ventricle of the heart.

contraceptiveagents,hormonal.name: contraceptive agents , hormonal
contraceptiveagents,hormonal.definition: Hormonal contraceptive agents is contraceptive agents that act on the endocrine system.

socialvalues.name: social values
socialvalues.definition: Social values is [MASK] standards or empirical variables in social life which are believed to be important and/or desirable.

aminoacids,sulfur.name: amino acids , sulfur
aminoacids,sulfur.definition: Sulfur amino acids is methionine and [MASK].

medialtibialstresssyndrome.name: medial tibial stress syndrome
medialtibialstresssyndrome.definition: Medial tibial stress syndrome is skeletal muscle pain and tenderness along the posteromedial tibia resulting from exercise such as [MASK] and other physical activity.

educationofvisuallydisabled.name: education of visually disabled
educationofvisuallydisabled.definition: Education of visually disabled is the teaching or training of those individuals with visual disability.

educationaltechnology.name: educational technology
educationaltechnology.definition: Educational technology is systematic identification, development, organization, or utilization of educational resources and the management of these processes. It is occasionally used also in a more limited sense to describe the use of equipment-oriented techniques or audiovisual aids in educational settings. (Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, December 1993, p132)

olfactoryperception.name: olfactory perception
olfactoryperception.definition: Olfactory perception is the process by which the nature and meaning of olfactory stimuli, such as odors, are recognized and interpreted by the brain.

pilotprojects.name: pilot projects
pilotprojects.definition: Pilot projects is small-scale tests of methods and procedures to be used on a larger scale if the pilot study demonstrates that these methods and procedures can work.

inducedpluripotentstemcells.name: induced pluripotent stem cells
inducedpluripotentstemcells.definition: Induced pluripotent stem cells is cells from adult organisms that have been reprogrammed into a pluripotential state similar to that of embryonic stem cells.

signsandsymptoms,digestive.name: signs and symptoms , digestive
signsandsymptoms,digestive.definition: Digestive signs and symptoms is digestive system manifestations of diseases of the gastrointestinal system or of other organs.

jobsyndrome.name: job syndrome
jobsyndrome.definition: Job syndrome is primary immunodeficiency syndrome characterized by recurrent infections and hyperimmunoglobulinemia e. Most cases are sporadic. Of the rare familial forms, the dominantly inherited subtype has additional connective tissue, dental and skeletal involvement that the recessive type does not share.

vesicularglutamatetransportprotein1.name: vesicular glutamate transport protein 1
vesicularglutamatetransportprotein1.definition: Vesicular glutamate transport protein 1 is a vesicular glutamate transporter protein that is predominately expressed in telencephalon of the brain.

ablationtechniques.name: ablation techniques
ablationtechniques.definition: Ablation techniques is removal of tissue by vaporization, abrasion, or destruction. Methods used include [MASK] tissue by hot liquids or microwave thermal [MASK], freezing (cryoablation), chemical ablation, and photoablation with lasers.

receptors,thrombin.name: receptors , thrombin
receptors,thrombin.definition: Thrombin receptors is a family of proteinase-activated receptors that are specific for thrombin. They are found primarily on platelets and on endothelial cells. Activation of thrombin receptors occurs through the proteolytic action of thrombin, which cleaves the N-terminal peptide from the receptor to reveal a new N-terminal peptide that is a cryptic ligand for the receptor. The receptors signal through heterotrimeric gtp-binding proteins. Small synthetic peptides that contain the unmasked N-terminal peptide sequence can also activate the receptor in the absence of proteolytic activity.

bodyweightsandmeasures.name: body weights and measures
bodyweightsandmeasures.definition: Body weights and measures is measurements of the height, weight, length, area, etc., of the human and animal body or its parts.

longtermadverseeffects.name: long term adverse effects
longtermadverseeffects.definition: Long term adverse effects is persistent detrimental effects from treatment for a condition. Included are effects from surgery such as postoperative complications, and from drug therapy, such as chemically induced disorders, or other therapeutics. Failure to attain a desired outcome from treatment for the condition is not considered an adverse effect.

arttherapy.name: art therapy
arttherapy.definition: Art therapy is the use of art as an adjunctive therapy in the treatment of neurological, mental, or behavioral disorders.

sensorysystemagents.name: sensory system agents
sensorysystemagents.definition: Sensory system agents is drugs that act on neuronal sensory receptors resulting in an increase, decrease, or modification of afferent nerve activity. (From Smith and Reynard, Textbook of Pharmacology, 1991, p367)

sarcomaviruses,murine.name: sarcoma viruses , murine
sarcomaviruses,murine.definition: Murine sarcoma viruses is a group of replication-defective viruses, in the genus gammaretrovirus, which are capable of transforming cells, but which replicate and produce tumors only in the presence of Murine leukemia viruses (leukemia virus, murine).

metaphor.name: metaphor
metaphor.definition: Metaphor is the application of a concept to that which it is not literally the same but which suggests a resemblance and comparison. Medical metaphors were widespread in ancient literature; the description of a sick body was often used by ancient writers to define a critical condition of the State, in which one corrupt part can ruin the entire system. (From Med Secoli Arte Sci, 1990;2(3):[MASK] 331)

childnutritionsciences.name: child nutrition sciences
childnutritionsciences.definition: Child nutrition sciences is the study of nutrition processes as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease of children, infants or adolescents.

rotavirus.name: rotavirus
rotavirus.definition: Rotavirus is a genus of reoviridae, causing acute gastroenteritis in birds and mammals, including humans. Transmission is horizontal and by environmental contamination. Seven species (Rotaviruses a thru g) are recognized.

physiologicfunction.name: physiologic function
physiologicfunction.definition: Physiologic function is the physiologic property of an organ or other part of the body.

feesandcharges.name: fees and charges
feesandcharges.definition: Fees and charges is amounts charged to the patient as payer for health care services.

wine.name: wine
wine.definition: Wine is fermented juice of fresh grapes or of other fruit or plant products used as a beverage.

fibrousdysplasiaofbone.name: fibrous dysplasia of bone
fibrousdysplasiaofbone.definition: Fibrous dysplasia of bone is a disease of bone marked by thinning of the cortex by fibrous tissue containing bony spicules, producing pain, disability, and gradually increasing deformity. Only one bone may be involved (fibrous dysplasia, monostotic) or several (fibrous dysplasia, polyostotic).

tumorstemcellassay.name: tumor stem cell assay
tumorstemcellassay.definition: Tumor stem cell assay is a cytologic technique for measuring the functional capacity of tumor stem cells by assaying their activity. It is used primarily for the in vitro testing of antineoplastic agents.

colon.name: colon
colon.definition: Colon is the segment of large intestine between the cecum and the rectum. It includes the ascending colon; the transverse colon; the [MASK]; and the sigmoid colon.

automation.name: automation
automation.definition: Automation is controlled operation of an apparatus, process, or system by mechanical or electronic devices that take the place of human organs of [MASK], effort, and decision. (From Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 1993)

libraries,medical.name: libraries , medical
libraries,medical.definition: Medical libraries is collection of [MASK] relevant to medicine.

waterresources.name: water resources
waterresources.definition: Water resources is environmental reservoirs of water related to natural water cycle by which water is obtained for various purposes. This includes but is not limited to watersheds, aquifers and springs.

mercuryisotopes.name: mercury isotopes
mercuryisotopes.definition: Mercury isotopes is stable mercury atoms that have the same atomic number as the element mercury, but differ in atomic weight. Hg-196, 198-201, and 204 are stable mercury isotopes.

sptranscriptionfactors.name: sp transcription factors
sptranscriptionfactors.definition: Sp transcription factors is a family of DNA-binding proteins that contain three zinc fingers at their carboxy termini. They are transcription factors that have specificity for gc boxes.

braininjuries.name: brain injuries
braininjuries.definition: Brain injuries is acute and chronic (see also brain injuries, chronic) injuries to the brain, including the cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, and brain stem. Clinical manifestations depend on the nature of injury. Diffuse trauma to the brain is frequently associated with diffuse axonal injury or coma, post-traumatic. Localized injuries may be associated with neurobehavioral manifestations; hemiparesis, or other focal neurologic deficits.

laboratorychemicals.name: laboratory chemicals
laboratorychemicals.definition: Laboratory chemicals is chemicals necessary to perform experimental and/or investigative procedures and for the preparation of drugs and other chemicals.

cerebralarteries.name: cerebral arteries
cerebralarteries.definition: Cerebral arteries is the arterial blood vessels supplying the cerebrum.

education,nursing,continuing.name: education , nursing , continuing
education,nursing,continuing.definition: Continuing nursing education is educational programs designed to inform nurses of recent advances in their fields.

membranetransportproteins.name: membrane transport proteins
membranetransportproteins.definition: Membrane transport proteins is membrane proteins whose primary function is to facilitate the transport of molecules across a biological membrane. Included in this broad category are proteins involved in active transport (biological transport, active), facilitated transport and ion channels.

chromosomedisorders.name: chromosome disorders
chromosomedisorders.definition: Chromosome disorders is clinical conditions caused by an abnormal chromosome constitution in which there is extra or missing chromosome material (either a whole chromosome or a chromosome segment). (from Thompson et al., Genetics in Medicine, 5th ed, p429)

growthcones.name: growth cones
