growthcones.definition: Growth cones is bulbous enlargement of the growing tip of nerve axons and dendrites. They are crucial to neuronal development because of their pathfinding ability and their role in synaptogenesis.

angiotensinii.name: angiotensin ii
angiotensinii.definition: Angiotensin ii is an octapeptide that is a potent but labile vasoconstrictor. It is produced from angiotensin i after the removal of two amino acids at the C-terminal by angiotensin converting enzyme. The amino acid in position 5 varies in different species. To block vasoconstriction and hypertension effect of angiotensin ii, patients are often treated with ace inhibitors or with [MASK].

burns,chemical.name: burns , chemical
burns,chemical.definition: Chemical burns is burns caused by contact with or exposure to caustics or strong acids.

amputation,traumatic.name: amputation , traumatic
amputation,traumatic.definition: Traumatic [MASK] is loss of a limb or other bodily appendage by accidental injury.

receptors,parathyroidhormone.name: receptors , parathyroid hormone
receptors,parathyroidhormone.definition: Parathyroid hormone receptors is cell surface proteins that bind parathyroid hormone with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Parathyroid hormone receptors on bone; kidney; and gastrointestinal cells mediate the hormone's role in calcium and phosphate homeostasis.

dietaryfiber.name: dietary fiber
dietaryfiber.definition: Dietary fiber is the remnants of plant cell walls that are resistant to [MASK] by the alimentary enzymes of man. It comprises various polysaccharides and lignins.

encephalitisvirus,japanese.name: encephalitis virus , japanese
encephalitisvirus,japanese.definition: Japanese encephalitis virus is a species of flavivirus, one of the Japanese encephalitis virus group (encephalitis viruses, japanese), which is the etiological agent of Japanese encephalitis found in Asia, southeast Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

deathdomain.name: death domain
deathdomain.definition: Death domain is a conserved protein interaction domain of the death domain superfamily that is structurally similar to the [MASK] and caspase recruitment domain. Death domains bind each other to form oligomers and occur on death domain receptors, where they are required for apoptosis signaling and non-apoptotic functions.

dentalequipment.name: dental equipment
dentalequipment.definition: Dental equipment is the nonexpendable items used by the dentist or dental staff in the performance of professional duties. (From Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p106)

pesticideresidues.name: pesticide residues
pesticideresidues.definition: Pesticide residues is pesticides or their breakdown products remaining in the environment following their normal use or accidental contamination.

gestures.name: gestures
gestures.definition: Gestures is movement of a part of the body for the purpose of communication.

solutecarrierproteins.name: solute carrier proteins
solutecarrierproteins.definition: Solute carrier proteins is a large diverse group of membrane transport proteins whose families are generally classified according to function. Most SLCs localize to the cell membrane; however, some families such as slc25, localize to [MASK] or other organelles.

plantarplate.name: plantar plate
plantarplate.definition: Plantar plate is fibrocartilaginous ligament at the metatarsophalangeal and the interphalangeal joint of the toe.

aidsdementiacomplex.name: aids dementia complex
aidsdementiacomplex.definition: Aids dementia complex is a neurologic condition associated with the acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and characterized by impaired concentration and memory, slowness of hand movements, ataxia, incontinence, apathy, and gait difficulties associated with hiv-1 viral infection of the central nervous system. Pathologic examination of the brain reveals [MASK] matter rarefaction, perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes, foamy macrophages, and multinucleated giant cells. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp760-1; n Engl j Med, 1995 Apr 6;332(14):934-40)

biologicaltransport,active.name: biological transport , active
biologicaltransport,active.definition: Active biological transport is the movement of materials across cell membranes and epithelial layers against an electrochemical gradient, requiring the expenditure of metabolic energy.

indianoceanislands.name: indian ocean islands
indianoceanislands.definition: Indian ocean islands is numerous islands in the Indian Ocean situated east of Madagascar, north to the Arabian Sea and east to Sri Lanka. Included are comoros (republic), madagascar (republic), Maldives (republic), mauritius (parliamentary democracy), Pemba (administered by [MASK]), reunion (a department of France), and seychelles (republic).

eyemovementmeasurements.name: eye movement measurements
eyemovementmeasurements.definition: Eye movement measurements is methods and procedures for recording eye movements.

healthcareevaluationmechanisms.name: health care evaluation mechanisms
healthcareevaluationmechanisms.definition: Health care evaluation mechanisms is methods and techniques used in evaluating the quality of health care, its planning, and delivery.

mutagenesis.name: mutagenesis
mutagenesis.definition: Mutagenesis is process of generating a genetic mutation. It may occur spontaneously or be induced by mutagens.

urbanpopulation.name: urban population
urbanpopulation.definition: Urban population is the inhabitants of a city or town, including metropolitan areas and suburban areas.

polarbodies.name: polar bodies
polarbodies.definition: Polar bodies is minute cells produced during development of an oocyte as it undergoes meiosis. a polar body contains one of the nuclei derived from the first or second meiotic cell division. Polar bodies have practically no cytoplasm. They are eventually discarded by the oocyte. (from King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

healthcommunication.name: health communication
healthcommunication.definition: Health communication is the transfer of information from experts in the medical and public health fields to patients and the public. The study and use of communication strategies to inform and influence individual and community decisions that enhance health.

rats,inbredshr.name: rats , inbred shr
rats,inbredshr.definition: Inbred shr rats is a strain of Rattus norvegicus with elevated blood pressure used as a model for studying hypertension and stroke.

naturalgas.name: natural gas
naturalgas.definition: Natural gas is a combustible, gaseous mixture of low-molecular weight [MASK] hydrocarbons, generated below the surface of the earth. It contains mostly methane and ethane with small amounts of propane; butanes; and higher hydrocarbons, and sometimes nitrogen; carbon dioxide; [MASK]; and [MASK]. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

lymphaticdiseases.name: lymphatic diseases
lymphaticdiseases.definition: Lymphatic diseases is diseases of [MASK]; [MASK] nodes; or lymphatic vessels.

spermmaturation.name: sperm maturation
spermmaturation.definition: Sperm maturation is the maturing process of spermatozoa after leaving the testicular seminiferous tubules. Maturation in sperm motility and fertility takes place in the epididymis as the sperm migrate from caput epididymis to cauda epididymis.

amplifiedfragmentlengthpolymorphismanaly.name: amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis
amplifiedfragmentlengthpolymorphismanaly.definition: Amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis is the detection of restriction fragment length polymorphisms by selective pcr amplification of restriction fragments derived from genomic dna followed by electrophoretic analysis of the amplified restriction fragments.

experimentalmodelofdisease.name: experimental model of disease
experimentalmodelofdisease.definition: Experimental model of disease is experimental model of disease

chromosomes,artificial,mammalian.name: chromosomes , artificial , mammalian
chromosomes,artificial,mammalian.definition: Mammalian artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, all elements, such as a replication origin; telomere; and centromere, that are required for successful replication, propagation to and maintainance in progeny mammalian cells. In addition, they are constructed to carry other sequences for analysis or gene transfer.

periodontalligament.name: periodontal ligament
periodontalligament.definition: Periodontal ligament is the fibrous connective tissue surrounding the tooth root, separating it from and attaching it to the alveolar bone (alveolar process).

societies,nursing.name: societies , nursing
societies,nursing.definition: Nursing societies is societies whose membership is limited to nurses.

surgicalinstruments.name: surgical instruments
surgicalinstruments.definition: Surgical instruments is hand-held tools or implements used by health professionals for the performance of surgical tasks.

diet,healthy.name: diet , healthy
diet,healthy.definition: Healthy diet is dietary patterns which have been found to be important in reducing disease risk.

pancreaticfistula.name: pancreatic fistula
pancreaticfistula.definition: Pancreatic fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the pancreas.

measles.name: measles
measles.definition: Measles is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by morbillivirus, common among children but also seen in the nonimmune of any age, in which the virus enters the respiratory tract via droplet nuclei and multiplies in the epithelial cells, spreading throughout the mononuclear phagocyte system.

drugutilization.name: drug utilization
drugutilization.definition: Drug utilization is the utilization of drugs as reported in individual hospital studies, fda studies, marketing, or consumption, etc. This includes drug stockpiling, and patient drug profiles.

virusdiseases.name: virus diseases
virusdiseases.definition: Virus diseases is a general term for diseases caused by viruses.

pituitarygland,anterior.name: pituitary gland , anterior
pituitarygland,anterior.definition: Anterior pituitary gland is the anterior glandular lobe of the pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis. It secretes the adenohypophyseal hormones that regulate vital functions such as growth; metabolism; and reproduction.

renalelimination.name: renal elimination
renalelimination.definition: Renal elimination is the discharge of substances from the blood supply via the urinary tract.

cerebralangiography.name: cerebral angiography
cerebralangiography.definition: Cerebral angiography is radiography of the vascular system of the brain after injection of a contrast medium.

immunotherapy.name: immunotherapy
immunotherapy.definition: Immunotherapy is manipulation of the host's immune system in treatment of disease. It includes both active and passive immunization as well as immunosuppressive therapy to prevent [MASK] [MASK].

carotidartery,common.name: carotid artery , common
carotidartery,common.definition: Common carotid artery is the two principal arteries supplying the structures of the head and [MASK]. They ascend in the [MASK], one on each side, and at the level of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, each divides into two branches, the external (carotid artery, external) and internal (carotid artery, internal) carotid arteries.

histidine.name: histidine
histidine.definition: Histidine is an essential amino acid that is required for the production of histamine.

activation,metabolic.name: activation , metabolic
activation,metabolic.definition: Metabolic activation is the conversion of an exogenous substance by a biological system resulting in the production on an active metabolite.

plasma.name: plasma
plasma.definition: Plasma is the residual portion of blood that is left after removal of blood cells by centrifugation without prior blood coagulation.

salmonellainfections.name: salmonella infections
salmonellainfections.definition: Salmonella infections is infections with bacteria of the genus salmonella.

lungdiseases,obstructive.name: lung diseases , obstructive
lungdiseases,obstructive.definition: Obstructive lung diseases is any disorder marked by obstruction of conducting airways of the lung. airway obstruction may be acute, chronic, intermittent, or persistent.

adultgermlinestemcells.name: adult germline stem cells
adultgermlinestemcells.definition: Adult germline stem cells is progenitor stem cells found in the testicles.

vancomycin.name: vancomycin
vancomycin.definition: Vancomycin is antibacterial obtained from Streptomyces orientalis. It is a glycopeptide related to ristocetin that inhibits bacterial cell wall assembly and is toxic to kidneys and the [MASK].

greenfluorescentproteins.name: green fluorescent proteins
greenfluorescentproteins.definition: Green fluorescent proteins is protein analogs and derivatives of the Aequorea victoria green fluorescent protein that emit light (fluorescence) when excited with ultraviolet rays. They are used in [MASK] in doing genetic techniques. Numerous mutants have been made to emit other [MASK] or be sensitive to pH.

fibrosis.name: fibrosis
fibrosis.definition: Fibrosis is any pathological condition where fibrous connective tissue invades any organ, usually as a consequence of inflammation or other injury.

drugantagonism.name: drug antagonism
drugantagonism.definition: Drug antagonism is phenomena and pharmaceutics of compounds that inhibit the function of agonists (drug agonism) and inverse agonists (drug inverse agonism) for a specific receptor. On their own, antagonists produce no effect by themselves to a receptor, and are said to have neither intrinsic activity nor efficacy.

statehealthplans.name: state health plans
statehealthplans.definition: State health plans is state plans prepared by the State Health Planning and Development Agencies which are made up from plans submitted by the Health Systems Agencies and subject to review and revision by the Statewide Health Coordinating Council.

portalsystem.name: portal system
portalsystem.definition: Portal system is a system of vessels in which blood, after passing through one capillary bed, is conveyed through a second [MASK] of capillaries before it returns to the systemic circulation. It pertains especially to the hepatic portal system.

dnarepeatexpansion.name: dna repeat expansion
dnarepeatexpansion.definition: Dna repeat expansion is an increase number of repeats of a genomic, tandemly repeated dna sequence from one generation to the next.

methotrexate.name: methotrexate
methotrexate.definition: Methotrexate is an antineoplastic antimetabolite with immunosuppressant properties. It is an inhibitor of tetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase and prevents the formation of tetrahydrofolate, necessary for synthesis of thymidylate, an essential component of dna.

anesthesia,epidural.name: anesthesia , epidural
anesthesia,epidural.definition: Epidural anesthesia is procedure in which an anesthetic is injected into the [MASK].

genes,mdr.name: genes , mdr
genes,mdr.definition: Mdr genes is genes for membrane transport proteins that confer resistance to toxic compounds. Several superfamilies of these multidrug export proteins are known and found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

genetargeting.name: gene targeting
genetargeting.definition: Gene targeting is the integration of exogenous dna into the genome of an organism at sites where its expression can be suitably controlled. This integration occurs as a result of homologous recombination.

acupuncturepoints.name: acupuncture points
acupuncturepoints.definition: Acupuncture points is designated locations along nerves or organ meridians for inserting acupuncture needles.

lymphaticabnormalities.name: lymphatic abnormalities
lymphaticabnormalities.definition: Lymphatic abnormalities is congenital or acquired structural abnormalities of the lymphatic system (lymphoid tissue) including the [MASK] vessels.

hematologicdiseases.name: hematologic diseases
hematologicdiseases.definition: Hematologic diseases is disorders of the blood and blood forming tissues.

tremor.name: tremor
tremor.definition: Tremor is cyclical movement of a body part that can represent either a physiologic process or a manifestation of disease. Intention or action tremor, a common manifestation of cerebellar diseases, is aggravated by movement. In contrast, resting tremor is maximal when there is no attempt at voluntary movement, and occurs as a relatively frequent manifestation of parkinson disease.

christianscience.name: christian science
christianscience.definition: Christian science is a religion founded by Mary Baker Eddy in 1866 that was organized under the official name of the Church of Christ, Scientist. It includes the practice of spiritual healing.

rna,transfer,pro.name: rna , transfer , pro
rna,transfer,pro.definition: Pro transfer rna is a transfer rna which is specific for carrying proline to sites on the ribosomes in preparation for protein synthesis.

externalcapsule.name: external capsule
externalcapsule.definition: External capsule is thin layer of [MASK] matter mostly of gabaergic neurons located between the putamen and the claustrum.

insectcontrol.name: insect control
insectcontrol.definition: Insect control is the reduction or regulation of the population of noxious, destructive, or dangerous insects through chemical, biological, or other means.

patientordisabledgroup.name: patient or disabled group
patientordisabledgroup.definition: Patient or disabled group is patient or disabled group

propofol.name: propofol
propofol.definition: Propofol is an intravenous anesthetic agent which has the advantage of a very rapid onset after infusion or bolus injection plus a very short recovery period of a couple of minutes. (From Smith and Reynard, Textbook of Pharmacology, 1992, 1st ed, p206). Propofol has been used as anticonvulsants and antiemetics.

electronics.name: electronics
electronics.definition: Electronics is the study, control, and application of the conduction of electricity through gases or vacuum, or through semiconducting or conducting materials. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

surfaceproperties.name: surface properties
surfaceproperties.definition: Surface properties is characteristics or attributes of the outer boundaries of objects, including molecules.

clinicalconference.name: clinical conference
clinicalconference.definition: Clinical conference is work that consists of a conference of physicians on their observations of a patient at the bedside, regarding the physical state, laboratory and other diagnostic findings, clinical manifestations, results of current therapy, etc. a clinical conference usually ends with a confirmation or correction of clinical findings by a pathological diagnosis performed by a pathologist. "Clinical conference" is often referred to as a "clinico-pathological conference."

psychoticdisorders.name: psychotic disorders
psychoticdisorders.definition: Psychotic disorders is disorders in which there is a loss of ego boundaries or a gross impairment in reality testing with delusions or prominent hallucinations. (From [MASK], 1994)

factorxdeficiency.name: factor x deficiency
factorxdeficiency.definition: Factor x deficiency is blood coagulation disorder usually inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, though it can be acquired. It is characterized by defective activity in both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways, impaired thromboplastin time, and impaired prothrombin consumption.

formperception.name: form perception
formperception.definition: Form perception is the sensory discrimination of a pattern shape or [MASK].

agefactors.name: age factors
agefactors.definition: Age factors is age as a constituent element or influence contributing to the production of a result. It may be applicable to the cause or the effect of a circumstance. It is used with human or animal concepts but should be differentiated from aging, a physiological process, and time factors which refers only to the passage of time.

orthopedicsurgeons.name: orthopedic surgeons
orthopedicsurgeons.definition: Orthopedic surgeons is physicians specializing in medical, surgical, and physical methods used to treat and correct deformities, diseases, and injuries to the skeletal system, its articulations, and associated structures.

nucleotidetransportproteins.name: nucleotide transport proteins
nucleotidetransportproteins.definition: Nucleotide transport proteins is proteins involved in the transport of nucleotides across cellular membranes.

cyclini.name: cyclin i
cyclini.definition: Cyclin i is a cyclin subtype that is found abundantly in post-mitotic tissues. In contrast to the classical cyclins, its level does not fluctuate during the cell cycle.

dendrites.name: dendrites
dendrites.definition: Dendrites is extensions of the nerve cell body. They are short and branched and receive stimuli from other neurons.

cardsignalingadaptorproteins.name: card signaling adaptor proteins
cardsignalingadaptorproteins.definition: Card signaling adaptor proteins is a family of intracellular signaling adaptor proteins that contain caspase activation and recruitment domains (card). They play a role in APOPTOSIS-related signal transduction by associating with other card domain-containing members and activating initiator caspases that contain card domains within their N-terminal pro-domain region.

transfer,psychology.name: transfer , psychology
transfer,psychology.definition: Psychology transfer is change in learning in one situation due to prior learning in another situation. The transfer can be positive (with second learning improved by first) or negative (where the reverse holds).

potassiumacetate.name: potassium acetate
potassiumacetate.definition: Potassium acetate is a potassium [MASK] used to replenish electrolytes, for restoration of water-electrolyte balance, as well as a urinary and systemic alkalizer, which can be administered orally or by [MASK]. Formerly, it was used in diuretics and expectorants.

coffee.name: coffee
coffee.definition: Coffee is a beverage made from ground coffea beans ([MASK]) infused in hot water. It generally contains caffeine and theophylline unless it is decaffeinated.

recurrentlaryngealnerve.name: recurrent laryngeal nerve
recurrentlaryngealnerve.definition: Recurrent laryngeal nerve is branches of the vagus (tenth cranial) nerve. The recurrent laryngeal nerves originate more caudally than the superior laryngeal nerves and follow different paths on the right and left sides. They carry efferents to all muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and carry sensory and autonomic fibers to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, tracheal, and cardiac regions.

nutritionalandmetabolicdiseases.name: nutritional and metabolic diseases
nutritionalandmetabolicdiseases.definition: Nutritional and metabolic diseases is a collective term for nutritional disorders resulting from poor absorption or nutritional imbalance, and metabolic disorders resulting from defects in biosynthesis (anabolism) or breakdown (catabolism) of endogenous substances.

trypsin.name: trypsin
trypsin.definition: Trypsin is a serine endopeptidase that is formed from trypsinogen in the pancreas. It is converted into its active form by enteropeptidase in the small intestine. It catalyzes hydrolysis of the carboxyl group of either [MASK] or lysine. ec 3.4.21.4.

residualvolume.name: residual volume
residualvolume.definition: Residual volume is the volume of air remaining in the lungs at the end of a maximal expiration. Common abbreviation is rv.

specimenhandling.name: specimen handling
specimenhandling.definition: Specimen handling is procedures for collecting, preserving, and transporting of specimens sufficiently stable to provide accurate and precise results suitable for clinical interpretation.

overweight.name: overweight
overweight.definition: Overweight is a status with body weight that is above certain standard of acceptable or desirable weight. In the scale of body mass index, overweight is defined as having a bmi of 25.0-29.9 kg/m2. Overweight may or may not be due to increases in body fat (adipose tissue), hence overweight does not equal "over fat".

neurosciencenursing.name: neuroscience nursing
neurosciencenursing.definition: Neuroscience nursing is the nursing specialty focusing on the needs of patients with dysfunction of the nervous system.

basalbodies.name: basal bodies
basalbodies.definition: Basal bodies is structures which form the base of flagella and cilia. They contain nine triplets of [MASK] that are arranged around the periphery and that serve as the nucleation center for axoneme assembly.

westernworld.name: western world
westernworld.definition: Western world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across the wide geographical area of Europe, as opposed to the East, Asia, and Africa. The term was used by scholars through the late medieval period. Thereafter, with the impact of colonialism and the transmission of cultures, Western World was sometimes expanded to include the Americas. (Dr. James h. Cassedy, nlm [MASK] Division)

redmeat.name: red meat
redmeat.definition: Red meat is meat such as beef, goat, pork, or lamb which contains more myoglobin than poultry or seafood.

receptor,angiotensin,type1.name: receptor , angiotensin , type 1
receptor,angiotensin,type1.definition: Type 1 angiotensin receptor is an angiotensin receptor subtype that is expressed at high levels in a variety of adult tissues including the cardiovascular system, the kidney, the endocrine system and the nervous system. Activation of the type 1 angiotensin receptor causes vasoconstriction and sodium retention.

oceanicancestrygroup.name: oceanic ancestry group
oceanicancestrygroup.definition: Oceanic ancestry group is individuals whose ancestral origins are in the islands of the central and South Pacific, including Micronesia, Melanesia, Polynesia, traditionally Australasia including [MASK]..

acuteradiationsyndrome.name: acute radiation syndrome
acuteradiationsyndrome.definition: Acute radiation syndrome is a condition caused by a brief whole body exposure to more than one sievert dose equivalent of radiation. Acute radiation syndrome is initially characterized by anorexia; nausea; vomiting; but can progress to hematological, gastrointestinal, neurological, pulmonary, and other major organ dysfunction.

chemotherapy,adjuvant.name: chemotherapy , adjuvant
chemotherapy,adjuvant.definition: Adjuvant chemotherapy is drug therapy given to augment or stimulate some other form of treatment such as surgery or radiation therapy. Adjuvant chemotherapy is commonly used in the therapy of cancer and can be administered before or after the primary treatment.

foodpackaging.name: food packaging
foodpackaging.definition: Food packaging is containers, packaging, and packaging materials for processed and raw foods and beverages. It includes packaging intended to be used for storage and also used for preparation of foods such as microwave food containers versus cooking and eating utensils. Packaging materials may be intended for food contact or designated non-contact, for example, shipping containers. food labeling is also available.

chickembryo.name: chick embryo
chickembryo.definition: Chick embryo is the developmental entity of a fertilized [MASK] egg (zygote). The developmental process begins about 24 h before the egg is laid at the blastodisc, a small whitish spot on the surface of the [MASK]. After 21 days of incubation, the embryo is fully developed before hatching.

respiratorymucosa.name: respiratory mucosa
respiratorymucosa.definition: Respiratory mucosa is the mucous membrane lining the respiratory tract, including the nasal cavity; the larynx; the [MASK]; and the bronchi tree. The respiratory mucosa consists of various types of epithelial cells ranging from ciliated columnar to simple squamous, mucous goblet cells, and glands containing both mucous and serous cells.

rodcelloutersegment.name: rod cell outer segment
rodcelloutersegment.definition: Rod cell outer segment is the portion of a retinal rod cell situated between the rod inner segment and the [MASK] epithelium. It contains a stack of photosensitive disk membranes laden with rhodopsin.

adenine.name: adenine
adenine.definition: Adenine is a purine base and a fundamental unit of adenine nucleotides.

receptors,artificial.name: receptors , artificial
receptors,artificial.definition: Artificial receptors is receptors that are created by synthetic chemistry techniques. They are usually designed to mimic endogenous cell surface receptors.

malariavaccines.name: malaria vaccines
malariavaccines.definition: Malaria vaccines is vaccines made from antigens arising from any of the four strains of Plasmodium which cause malaria in humans, or from p. berghei which causes malaria in rodents.

sarcoma,alveolarsoftpart.name: sarcoma , alveolar soft part
sarcoma,alveolarsoftpart.definition: Alveolar soft part sarcoma is a variety of rare sarcoma having a reticulated fibrous stroma enclosing groups of sarcoma cells, which resemble epithelial cells and are enclosed in alveoli walled with connective tissue. It is a rare tumor, usually occurring between 15 and 35 years of age. It appears in the muscles of the extremities in adults and most commonly in the head and [MASK] regions of children. Though slow-growing, it commonly metastasizes to the lungs, brain, bones, and [MASK] nodes. (DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1365)

physicianassistants.name: physician assistants
physicianassistants.definition: Physician assistants is health professionals who practice medicine as members of a team with their supervising physicians. They deliver a broad range of medical and surgical services to diverse populations in rural and urban settings. Duties may include physical exams, diagnosis and treatment of disease, interpretation of tests, assist in surgery, and prescribe medications. (from http://www.aapa.orglabout-pas accessed 2114/2011)

proteincinhibitor.name: protein c inhibitor
proteincinhibitor.definition: Protein c inhibitor is a member of the serpin family of proteins that is found in plasma and urine. It is dependent on heparin and is able to inhibit activated protein c; thrombin; kallikrein; and other serine endopeptidases.

sedentarybehavior.name: sedentary behavior
sedentarybehavior.definition: Sedentary behavior is behaviors during waking hours that have low energy expenditure and are often performed in a sitting or reclining posture.

fungalproteins.name: fungal proteins
fungalproteins.definition: Fungal proteins is proteins found in any species of fungus.

microbialinteractions.name: microbial interactions
microbialinteractions.definition: Microbial interactions is the inter- and intra-relationships between various microorganisms. This can include both positive (like symbiosis) and negative (like antibiosis) interactions. Examples include virus - bacteria and bacteria - bacteria.

protectiveagents.name: protective agents
protectiveagents.definition: Protective agents is synthetic or natural substances which are given to prevent a disease or disorder or are used in the process of treating a disease or injury due to a poisonous agent.

consumerbehavior.name: consumer behavior
consumerbehavior.definition: Consumer behavior is behavior associated with the procurement of goods, services, or experiences.

drugcarriers.name: drug carriers
drugcarriers.definition: Drug carriers is forms to which substances are incorporated to improve the delivery and the effectiveness of drugs. Drug carriers are used in drug-delivery systems such as the controlled-release technology to prolong in vivo drug actions, decrease drug metabolism, and reduce drug toxicity. Carriers are also used in designs to increase the effectiveness of drug delivery to the target sites of pharmacological actions. Liposomes, albumin microspheres, soluble synthetic polymers, dna complexes, protein-drug conjugates, and carrier erythrocytes among others have been employed as biodegradable drug carriers.

stromalinteractionmolecules.name: stromal interaction molecules
stromalinteractionmolecules.definition: Stromal interaction molecules is membrane-associated calcium-binding proteins that are characterized by N-terminal ef hand motifs and a sterile alpha motif. They function as sensors of endoplasmic reticulum calcium levels and translocate from the er to the plasma membrane to activate calcium channels in response to intracellular calcium depletion.

neuroendocrinetumors.name: neuroendocrine tumors
neuroendocrinetumors.definition: Neuroendocrine tumors is tumors whose cells possess [MASK] and originate from the neuroectoderm, i.e., the cells of the ectoblast or epiblast that program the neuroendocrine system. Common properties across most neuroendocrine tumors include ectopic hormone production (often via apud cells), the presence of tumor-associated antigens, and isozyme composition.

excitationcontractioncoupling.name: excitation contraction coupling
excitationcontractioncoupling.definition: Excitation contraction coupling is a process fundamental to muscle physiology whereby an electrical stimulus or action potential triggers a myocyte to depolarize and contract. This mechanical muscle contraction response is regulated by entry of calcium ions into the cell.

geneticenhancement.name: genetic enhancement
geneticenhancement.definition: Genetic enhancement is the use of genetic methodologies to improve functional capacities of an organism rather than to treat disease.

arabia.name: arabia
arabia.definition: Arabia is the great peninsula of southwest Asia comprising most of the present countries of the Middle East. It has been known since the first millennium b.c. In early times it was divided into Arabia Petraea, the northwest part, the only part ever conquered, becoming a Roman province; Arabia Deserta, the northern part between Syria and Mesopotamia; and Arabia Felix, the main part of the peninsula but by some geographers restricted to modern Yemen. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p63)

analgesia.name: analgesia
analgesia.definition: Analgesia is methods of pain relief that may be used with or in place of analgesics.

reward.name: reward
reward.definition: Reward is an object or a situation that can serve to reinforce a response, to satisfy a motive, or to afford pleasure.

energydrinks.name: energy drinks
energydrinks.definition: Energy drinks is beverages that contain stimulants such as a combination of caffeine with other substances such as vitamins; amino acids; and sugar or sugar derivatives.

ribfractures.name: rib fractures
ribfractures.definition: Rib fractures is fractures of any of the ribs.

virusshedding.name: virus shedding
virusshedding.definition: Virus shedding is the expelling of virus particles from the body. Important routes include the respiratory tract, genital tract (important in infectious disease transmission, vertical), and intestinal tract.

reproductivehealth.name: reproductive health
reproductivehealth.definition: Reproductive health is the state of the reproductive system when functioning optimally without evidence of disease, disorders, or deficiencies.

chloroform.name: chloroform
chloroform.definition: Chloroform is a commonly used laboratory solvent. It was previously used as an anesthetic, but was banned from use in the u.s. due to its suspected carcinogenicity.

rescuework.name: rescue work
rescuework.definition: Rescue work is activities devoted to freeing persons or animals from danger to life or well-being in accidents, fires, bombings, floods, earthquakes, other disasters and life-threatening conditions. While usually performed by team efforts, rescue work is not restricted to organized services.

infant,newborn.name: infant , newborn
infant,newborn.definition: Newborn infant is an infant during the first 28 days after birth.

intestinalelimination.name: intestinal elimination
intestinalelimination.definition: Intestinal elimination is the discharge of substances from the blood supply into the intestinal lumen for excretion by defecation.

limbsalvage.name: limb salvage
limbsalvage.definition: Limb salvage is an alternative to [MASK] in patients with neoplasms, ischemia, fractures, and other limb-threatening conditions. Generally, sophisticated surgical procedures such as vascular surgery and reconstruction are used to salvage diseased limbs.

hematology.name: hematology
hematology.definition: Hematology is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with morphology, physiology, and pathology of the blood and blood-forming tissues.

multicenterstudiesastopic.name: multicenter studies as topic
multicenterstudiesastopic.definition: Multicenter studies as topic is works about controlled studies which are planned and carried out by several cooperating institutions to assess certain variables and outcomes in specific patient populations, for example, a multicenter study of congenital anomalies in children.

chromosomes,human,pair8.name: chromosomes , human , pair 8
chromosomes,human,pair8.definition: Pair 8 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

schoolteachers.name: school teachers
schoolteachers.definition: School teachers is members of staff responsible for teaching students in a school from pre-kindergarten through twelfth grade.

proneposition.name: prone position
proneposition.definition: Prone position is the posture of an individual lying face down.

sexualmaturation.name: sexual maturation
sexualmaturation.definition: Sexual maturation is achievement of full sexual capacity in animals and in humans.

toothpermeability.name: tooth permeability
toothpermeability.definition: Tooth permeability is the property of teeth to permit passage of light, heat, gases, liquids, metabolites, mineral ions and other substances. It does not include the penetration of the teeth by microorganisms.

potassiumchannelblockers.name: potassium channel blockers
potassiumchannelblockers.definition: Potassium channel blockers is a class of drugs that act by inhibition of potassium efflux through cell membranes. Blockade of potassium channels prolongs the duration of action potentials. They are used as anti-arrhythmia agents and vasodilator agents.

genetictechniques.name: genetic techniques
genetictechniques.definition: Genetic techniques is chromosomal, biochemical, intracellular, and other methods used in the study of genetics.

bonediseases,metabolic.name: bone diseases , metabolic
bonediseases,metabolic.definition: Metabolic bone diseases is diseases that affect the metabolic processes of bone tissue.

peritonealdiseases.name: peritoneal diseases
peritonealdiseases.definition: Peritoneal diseases is pathological processes involving the peritoneum.

hepatitisb,chronic.name: hepatitis b , chronic
hepatitisb,chronic.definition: Chronic hepatitis b is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by hepatitis b virus lasting six months or more. It is primarily transmitted by parenteral exposure, such as transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products, but can also be transmitted via sexual or intimate personal contact.

chemistrytechniques,synthetic.name: chemistry techniques , synthetic
chemistrytechniques,synthetic.definition: Synthetic chemistry techniques is methods used for the chemical synthesis of compounds. Included under this heading are laboratory methods used to synthesize a variety of chemicals and drugs.

nitrogencycle.name: nitrogen cycle
nitrogencycle.definition: Nitrogen cycle is the circulation of nitrogen in nature, consisting of a cycle of biochemical reactions in which atmospheric nitrogen is compounded, dissolved in rain, and deposited in the soil, where it is assimilated and metabolized by animals, plants, bacteria, and fungi, eventually returning to the atmosphere by bacterial decomposition of organic matter.

healthfacilitymerger.name: health facility merger
healthfacilitymerger.definition: Health facility merger is the combining of administrative and organizational resources of two or more health care facilities.

longqtsyndrome.name: long qt syndrome
longqtsyndrome.definition: Long qt syndrome is a condition that is characterized by episodes of fainting (syncope) and varying degree of ventricular arrhythmia as indicated by the prolonged qt interval. The inherited forms are caused by mutation of genes encoding cardiac ion channel proteins. The two major forms are romano-ward syndrome and jervell-lange nielsen syndrome.

geneproducts,tat.name: gene products , tat
geneproducts,tat.definition: Tat gene products is trans-acting transcription factors produced by retroviruses such as hiv. They are nuclear proteins whose expression is required for viral replication. The tat protein stimulates long terminal REPEAT-driven rna synthesis for both viral regulatory and viral structural proteins. tat stands for trans-activation of transcription.

kidney.name: kidney
kidney.definition: Kidney is body organ that filters blood for the secretion of urine and that regulates ion concentrations.

anesthesiadepartment,hospital.name: anesthesia department , hospital
anesthesiadepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital anesthesia department is hospital department responsible for the administration of functions and activities pertaining to the delivery of anesthetics.

thoracicneoplasms.name: thoracic neoplasms
thoracicneoplasms.definition: Thoracic neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the thorax.

sexchromosomes.name: sex chromosomes
sexchromosomes.definition: [MASK] chromosomes is the homologous chromosomes that are dissimilar in the heterogametic [MASK]. There are the x chromosome, the y chromosome, and the w, z chromosomes (in animals in which the female is the heterogametic [MASK] (the silkworm moth Bombyx mori, for example)). In such cases the w chromosome is the female-determining and the male is zz. (From King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

populationhealth.name: population health
populationhealth.definition: Population health is the health outcomes of a group of individuals, including the distribution of such outcomes within the group. These populations are often geographic regions, such as nations or communities, but they can also be other groups. (From Am j Public Health. 2003 March; 93(3): 380–383)

cytochromeagroup.name: cytochrome a group
cytochromeagroup.definition: Cytochrome a group is cytochromes ([MASK]-transporting proteins) in which the heme prosthetic group is heme a, i.e., the iron chelate of cytoporphyrin ix. (From Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992, p539)

managementqualitycircles.name: management quality circles
managementqualitycircles.definition: Management quality circles is participation of employees with management as a labor-management team, in decisions pertaining to the operational activities of the organization or industry.

dentalocclusion,balanced.name: dental occlusion , balanced
dentalocclusion,balanced.definition: Balanced dental occlusion is dental occlusion in which the occlusal contact of the teeth on the working side of the jaw is accompanied by the harmonious contact of the teeth on the opposite (balancing) side. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p556)

bloodpressure.name: blood pressure
bloodpressure.definition: Blood pressure is pressure of the blood on the arteries and other blood vessels.

horsediseases.name: horse diseases
horsediseases.definition: Horse diseases is diseases of domestic and wild horses of the species Equus caballus.

intelligencetests.name: intelligence tests
intelligencetests.definition: Intelligence tests is standardized tests that measure the present general ability or aptitude for intellectual performance.

reflex.name: reflex
reflex.definition: Reflex is an involuntary movement or exercise of function in a part, excited in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery and transmitted to the brain or spinal cord.

cyanobacteria.name: cyanobacteria
cyanobacteria.definition: Cyanobacteria is a phylum of oxygenic photosynthetic bacteria comprised of unicellular to multicellular bacteria possessing [MASK] and carrying out oxygenic [MASK]. Cyanobacteria are the only known organisms capable of fixing both carbon dioxide (in the presence of light) and nitrogen. Cell morphology can include nitrogen-fixing heterocysts and/or resting cells called akinetes. Formerly called blue-green algae, cyanobacteria were traditionally treated as algae.

childdevelopmentdisorders,pervasive.name: child development disorders , pervasive
childdevelopmentdisorders,pervasive.definition: Pervasive child development disorders is severe distortions in the development of many basic psychological functions that are not normal for any stage in development. These distortions are manifested in sustained social impairment, [MASK] abnormalities, and peculiar motor movements.

religion.name: religion
religion.definition: Religion is a [MASK] of beliefs concerning the nature, cause, and purpose of the universe, especially when considered as the creation of a superhuman agency. It usually involves devotional and ritual observances and often a moral code for the conduct of human affairs. (Random House Collegiate Dictionary, rev. ed.)

peripheralnerves.name: peripheral nerves
peripheralnerves.definition: Peripheral nerves is the nerves outside of the brain and spinal cord, including the autonomic, cranial, and spinal nerves. Peripheral nerves contain non-neuronal cells and connective tissue as well as axons. The connective tissue layers include, from the outside to the inside, the epineurium, the perineurium, and the endoneurium.

medicine,traditional.name: medicine , traditional
medicine,traditional.definition: Traditional medicine is systems of medicine based on cultural beliefs and practices handed down from generation to generation. The concept includes mystical and magical rituals (spiritual therapies); phytotherapy; and other treatments which may not be explained by modern medicine.

escherichiacoli.name: escherichia coli
escherichiacoli.definition: Escherichia coli is a species of gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria (gram-negative facultatively anaerobic rods) commonly found in the lower part of the intestine of warm-blooded animals. It is usually nonpathogenic, but some strains are known to produce [MASK] and pyogenic infections. Pathogenic strains (virotypes) are classified by their specific pathogenic mechanisms such as toxins (enterotoxigenic escherichia coli), etc.

education,special.name: education , special
education,special.definition: Special education is education of the individual who markedly deviates intellectually, physically, socially, or emotionally from those considered to be normal, thus requiring special instruction.

pregnancycomplications,neoplastic.name: pregnancy complications , neoplastic
pregnancycomplications,neoplastic.definition: Neoplastic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and neoplasms. The neoplastic disease may precede or follow fertilization.

healthyworkereffect.name: healthy worker effect
healthyworkereffect.definition: Healthy worker effect is phenomenon of workers' usually exhibiting overall death rates lower than those of the general population due to the fact that the severely ill and disabled are ordinarily excluded from employment.

literature.name: literature
literature.definition: Literature is writings having excellence of form or expression and expressing ideas of permanent or universal interest. The body of written works produced in a particular language, country, or age. (Webster, 3d ed)

appetiteregulation.name: appetite regulation
appetiteregulation.definition: Appetite regulation is physiologic mechanisms which regulate or control the appetite and food intake.

cerebrospinalfluidpressure.name: cerebrospinal fluid pressure
cerebrospinalfluidpressure.definition: Cerebrospinal fluid pressure is manometric pressure of the cerebrospinal fluid as measured by lumbar, cerebroventricular, or cisternal puncture. Within the cranial cavity it is called [MASK].

operatingtables.name: operating tables
operatingtables.definition: Operating [MASK] is a raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during surgical procedures.

education,graduate.name: education , graduate
education,graduate.definition: Graduate education is studies beyond the bachelor's degree at an institution having graduate programs for the purpose of preparing for entrance into a specific field, and obtaining a higher degree.

aspergillus.name: aspergillus
aspergillus.definition: Aspergillus is a genus of mitosporic fungi containing about 100 species and eleven different teleomorphs in the family Trichocomaceae.

parathyroidhormone.name: parathyroid hormone
parathyroidhormone.definition: Parathyroid hormone is a polypeptide hormone (84 amino acid residues) secreted by the [MASK] which performs the essential role of maintaining intracellular calcium levels in the body. Parathyroid hormone increases intracellular calcium by promoting the release of calcium from bone, increases the intestinal absorption of calcium, increases the renal tubular reabsorption of calcium, and increases the renal excretion of phosphates.

evaluationstudiesastopic.name: evaluation studies as topic
evaluationstudiesastopic.definition: Evaluation studies as topic is works about studies that determine the effectiveness or value of processes, personnel, and equipment, or the material on conducting such studies.

adult.name: adult
adult.definition: Adult is a person having attained full growth or maturity. Adults are of 19 through 44 years of age. For a person between 19 and 24 years of age, young adult is available.

operon.name: operon
operon.definition: Operon is in bacteria, a group of metabolically related genes, with a common promoter, whose transcription into a single polycistronic messenger rna is under the control of an operator region.

adolescentbehavior.name: adolescent behavior
adolescentbehavior.definition: Adolescent behavior is any observable response or action of an adolescent.

diagnostictechniquesandprocedures.name: diagnostic techniques and procedures
diagnostictechniquesandprocedures.definition: Diagnostic techniques and procedures is methods, procedures, and tests performed to diagnose disease, disordered function, or disability.

tobacco.name: tobacco
tobacco.definition: Tobacco is a plant genus of the family solanaceae. Members contain nicotine and other biologically active chemicals; its dried leaves are used for smoking.

respiratoryfunctiontests.name: respiratory function tests
respiratoryfunctiontests.definition: Respiratory function tests is measurement of the various processes involved in the act of respiration: inspiration, expiration, oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange, lung volume and compliance, etc.

sucrose.name: sucrose
sucrose.definition: Sucrose is a nonreducing disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose linked via their anomeric carbons. It is obtained commercially from sugarcane, sugar beet (beta vulgaris), and other plants and used extensively as a food and a sweetener.

bonedevelopment.name: bone development
bonedevelopment.definition: Bone development is the growth and development of bones from fetus to adult. It includes two principal mechanisms of bone growth: growth in length of long bones at the epiphyseal cartilages and growth in thickness by depositing new bone (osteogenesis) with the actions of [MASK] and osteoclasts.

emotionaladjustment.name: emotional adjustment
emotionaladjustment.definition: Emotional [MASK] is psychological process that occurs when an individual adapts to a significant emotional event or stimulus.

murinepneumoniavirus.name: murine pneumonia virus
murinepneumoniavirus.definition: Murine pneumonia virus is a species of the genus pneumovirus causing pneumonia in mice.

minerals.name: minerals
minerals.definition: Minerals is native, inorganic or fossilized organic substances having a definite chemical composition and formed by inorganic reactions. They may occur as individual crystals or may be disseminated in some other mineral or rock. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed; McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

physiologicaleffectsofdrugs.name: physiological effects of drugs
physiologicaleffectsofdrugs.definition: Physiological effects of drugs is activities which affect organs and systemic functions without regard to a particular disease.

curriculum.name: curriculum
curriculum.definition: Curriculum is a course of study offered by an educational institution.

lymphaticirradiation.name: lymphatic irradiation
lymphaticirradiation.definition: Lymphatic irradiation is external or interstitial irradiation to treat lymphomas (e.g., Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphomas) and [MASK] and also some autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis.

embryonicinduction.name: embryonic induction
embryonicinduction.definition: Embryonic induction is the complex processes of initiating cell differentiation in the embryo. The precise regulation by cell interactions leads to diversity of cell types and specific pattern of organization (embryogenesis).

generalization,response.name: generalization , response
generalization,response.definition: Response generalization is the principle that after an organism learns to respond in a particular manner to a stimulus, that stimulus is effective in eliciting similar responses.

heartarrest.name: heart arrest
heartarrest.definition: Heart arrest is cessation of heart beat or [MASK]. If it is treated within a few minutes, heart arrest can be reversed in most cases to normal cardiac rhythm and effective circulation.

decompression,surgical.name: decompression , surgical
decompression,surgical.definition: Surgical decompression is a surgical operation for the relief of pressure in a body compartment or on a body part. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

healthfacilityplanning.name: health facility planning
healthfacilityplanning.definition: Health facility planning is areawide planning for health care institutions on the basis of projected consumer need.

nuclearreceptorsubfamily2,groupc,member2.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 2 , group c , member 2
nuclearreceptorsubfamily2,groupc,member2.definition: Member 2 group c nuclear receptor subfamily 2 is an orphan nuclear receptor that has specificity for hormone response elements found in the promoters of target genes. It binds dna either as a homodimer or as heterodimer with the closely-related orphan nuclear receptor nuclear receptor subfamily 2, group c, member 1. The protein was originally identified as a TESTES-specific protein and is involved in the regulation of variety of cellular processes, including cell differentiation; cell proliferation; and apoptosis.

respiratorysounds.name: respiratory sounds
respiratorysounds.definition: Respiratory sounds is noises, normal and abnormal, heard on auscultation over any part of the respiratory tract.

proteininteractiondomainsandmotifs.name: protein interaction domains and motifs
proteininteractiondomainsandmotifs.definition: Protein interaction domains and motifs is protein modules with conserved ligand-binding surfaces which mediate specific interaction functions in signal transduction pathways and the specific binding sites of their cognate protein ligands.

bacterialphysiologicalphenomena.name: bacterial physiological phenomena
bacterialphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Bacterial physiological phenomena is physiological processes and properties of bacteria.

hepatitiscantigens.name: hepatitis c antigens
hepatitiscantigens.definition: Hepatitis c antigens is antigens of the virions of hepacivirus, their surface, core, or other associated antigens.

mice,inbreda.name: mice , inbred a
mice,inbreda.definition: Inbred a mice is an inbred strain of mouse that is widely used in [MASK] studies and cancer research.

mitochondrialturnover.name: mitochondrial turnover
mitochondrialturnover.definition: Mitochondrial turnover is the cellular processes involved in [MASK] to the mitochondrial volume, content, and activity, that depend on the energy demands of the cell.

taste.name: taste
taste.definition: Taste is the ability to detect chemicals through gustatory receptors in the mouth, including those on the tongue; the palate; the pharynx; and the epiglottis.

wirelesstechnology.name: wireless technology
wirelesstechnology.definition: Wireless technology is techniques using energy such as radio frequency, infrared light, laser light, visible light, or acoustic energy to transfer information without the use of wires, over both short and long distances.

insurance,majormedical.name: insurance , major medical
insurance,majormedical.definition: Major medical insurance is insurance providing a broad range of medical services and supplies, when prescribed by a physician, whether or not the patient is hospitalized. It frequently is an extension of a basic policy and benefits will not begin until the basic policy is exhausted.

phosphoruscompounds.name: phosphorus compounds
phosphoruscompounds.definition: Phosphorus compounds is inorganic compounds that contain phosphorus as an integral part of the molecule.

mudtherapy.name: mud therapy
mudtherapy.definition: Mud therapy is the therapeutic use of mud in packs or baths taking advantage of the absorptive qualities of the mud. It has been used for rheumatism and skin problems.

iodineisotopes.name: iodine isotopes
iodineisotopes.definition: Iodine isotopes is stable iodine atoms that have the same atomic number as the element iodine, but differ in atomic weight. i-127 is the only naturally occurring stable iodine isotope.

invitrooocytematurationtechniques.name: in vitro oocyte maturation techniques
invitrooocytematurationtechniques.definition: In vitro oocyte maturation techniques is methods used to induce premature oocytes, that are maintained in tissue culture, to progress through developmental stages including to a stage that is competent to undergo fertilization.

cardiovascularinfections.name: cardiovascular infections
cardiovascularinfections.definition: Cardiovascular infections is pathological conditions of the cardiovascular system caused by infections.

metadata.name: metadata
metadata.definition: Metadata is structured data elements used to describe other data.

investments.name: investments
investments.definition: Investments is use for articles on the investing of funds for income or profit.

muscularatrophy.name: muscular atrophy
muscularatrophy.definition: Muscular atrophy is derangement in size and number of muscle fibers occurring with aging, reduction in blood supply, or following immobilization, prolonged weightlessness, malnutrition, and particularly in denervation.

oocyteretrieval.name: oocyte retrieval
oocyteretrieval.definition: Oocyte retrieval is procedures to obtain viable oocytes from the host. Oocytes most often are collected by needle aspiration from ovarian follicles before ovulation.

bonesoflowerextremity.name: bones of lower extremity
bonesoflowerextremity.definition: Bones of lower extremity is the bones of the upper and lower leg. They include the [MASK].

lipidmetabolism.name: lipid metabolism
lipidmetabolism.definition: Lipid metabolism is physiological processes in biosynthesis (anabolism) and degradation (catabolism) of lipids.

swimmingpools.name: swimming pools
swimmingpools.definition: [MASK] pools is excavations or containment structures filled with water and used for [MASK].

heartvalves.name: heart valves
heartvalves.definition: Heart valves is flaps of tissue that prevent regurgitation of blood from the heart ventricles to the heart atria or from the [MASK] or aorta to the ventricles.

cornealtopography.name: corneal topography
cornealtopography.definition: Corneal topography is the measurement of curvature and shape of the anterior surface of the cornea using techniques such as keratometry, keratoscopy, photokeratoscopy, profile photography, computer-assisted image processing and videokeratography. This measurement is often applied in the fitting of contact lenses and in diagnosing corneal diseases or corneal changes including keratoconus, which occur after keratotomy and keratoplasty.

cumulativetraumadisorders.name: cumulative trauma disorders
cumulativetraumadisorders.definition: Cumulative trauma disorders is harmful and painful condition caused by overuse or overexertion of some part of the musculoskeletal system, often resulting from work-related physical activities. It is characterized by inflammation, pain, or dysfunction of the involved joints, bones, ligaments, and nerves.

ironregulatoryprotein2.name: iron regulatory protein 2
ironregulatoryprotein2.definition: Iron regulatory protein 2 is a multifunctional iron-sulfur protein that is both an iron regulatory protein and cytoplasmic form of aconitate hydratase. It binds to iron regulatory elements found on mRNAs involved in iron metabolism and regulates their translation. Its rate of degradation is increased in the presence of iron.

genes,jun.name: genes , jun
genes,jun.definition: Jun genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (jun) originally isolated from the [MASK] virus 17 (asv 17). The proto-oncogene jun (c-jun) codes for a nuclear protein which is involved in growth-related transcriptional control. Insertion of c-jun into asv-17 or the constitutive expression of the c-jun protein produces tumorgenicity. The human c-jun gene is located at 1p31-32 on the short [MASK] of [MASK].

plasmodiumfalciparum.name: plasmodium falciparum
plasmodiumfalciparum.definition: Plasmodium falciparum is a species of protozoa that is the causal agent of falciparum malaria (malaria, falciparum). It is most prevalent in the tropics and subtropics.

diagnosticscreeningprograms.name: diagnostic screening programs
diagnosticscreeningprograms.definition: Diagnostic screening programs is services for the presumptive identification of unrecognized disease in an apparently healthy, asymptomatic population by means of tests, examinations or other procedures that can be applied rapidly and easily to the target population. (from [MASK] Organization http://www.who.int/cancer/prevention/diagnosis-screening/screening/en/ Oct. 24,2017)

proteincdeficiency.name: protein c deficiency
proteincdeficiency.definition: Protein c deficiency is an absence or deficiency in protein c which leads to impaired regulation of blood coagulation. It is associated with an increased risk of severe or premature thrombosis. (Stedman's Med. Dict., 26th ed.)

losangeles.name: los angeles
losangeles.definition: Los angeles is city in California.

proteinsubunits.name: protein subunits
proteinsubunits.definition: Protein subunits is single chains of amino acids that are the units of multimeric proteins. Multimeric proteins can be composed of identical or non-identical subunits. One or more monomeric subunits may compose a protomer which itself is a subunit structure of a larger assembly.

breastdiseases.name: breast diseases
breastdiseases.definition: Breast diseases is pathological processes of the breast.

biologicalevolution.name: biological evolution
biologicalevolution.definition: Biological evolution is the process of cumulative change over successive generations through which organisms acquire their distinguishing morphological and physiological characteristics.

gases.name: gases
gases.definition: Gases is the vapor state of matter; nonelastic fluids in which the molecules are in free movement and their mean positions far apart. Gases tend to expand indefinitely, to diffuse and mix readily with other gases, to have definite relations of volume, temperature, and pressure, and to condense or liquefy at low temperatures or under sufficient pressure. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

spine.name: spine
spine.definition: Spine is the spinal or vertebral column.

tickcontrol.name: tick control
tickcontrol.definition: Tick control is chemical, biological, or medical measures designed to prevent the spread of ticks or the concomitant infestations which result in tick-borne diseases. It includes the veterinary as well as the public health aspects of tick and mite control.

ubiquitination.name: ubiquitination
ubiquitination.definition: Ubiquitination is the act of ligating ubiquitins to proteins to form ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes to label proteins for transport to the proteasome endopeptidase complex where proteolysis occurs.

sexworkers.name: sex workers
sexworkers.definition: [MASK] workers is people who engage in occupational sexual behavior in exchange for economic rewards or other extrinsic considerations.

growthdifferentiationfactors.name: growth differentiation factors
growthdifferentiationfactors.definition: Growth differentiation factors is a family of bone morphogenetic PROTEIN-related proteins that are primarily involved in regulation of cell differentiation.

atmosphere.name: atmosphere
atmosphere.definition: Atmosphere is the gaseous envelope surrounding a planet or similar body. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

bloodvesselprosthesis.name: blood vessel prosthesis
bloodvesselprosthesis.definition: Blood vessel prosthesis is device constructed of either synthetic or biological material that is used for the repair of injured or diseased blood vessels.

foodaddiction.name: food addiction
foodaddiction.definition: Food addiction is a cluster of chemical dependencies to specific foods or food in general in which there develops a physical craving for these foods.

lewisbloodgroupantigens.name: lewis blood group antigens
lewisbloodgroupantigens.definition: Lewis blood group antigens is carbohydrate antigens structurally related to the abh blood-group system. They may occur as a modification of saccharide chains on glycolipids or glycoproteins on cell surfaces or in plasma, or as free oligosaccharides in secretions. Lewis  antigens are not synthesized in blood cells. Instead Lewis glycolipids present in plasma are absorbed onto the surface of erythrocytes; lymphocytes; and platelets. The phenotypes Le(a) and Le(b) are the result of the actions of two genes the Le gene (fucosyltransferase fut3) and the Se gene (fucosyltransferase fut2) on the precursor carbohydrate, glycolipid or glycoprotein. Other fucosyltransferases can also synthesize the Lewis antigens.

transcription,genetic.name: transcription , genetic
transcription,genetic.definition: Genetic transcription is the biosynthesis of rna carried out on a template of dna. The biosynthesis of dna from an rna template is called reverse transcription.

virtualreality.name: virtual reality
virtualreality.definition: Virtual reality is using computer technology to create and maintain an environment and project a user's physical presence in that environment allowing the user to interact with it.

philosophy,dental.name: philosophy , dental
philosophy,dental.definition: Dental philosophy is the underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of dentistry.

antibodies,catalytic.name: antibodies , catalytic
antibodies,catalytic.definition: Catalytic antibodies is antibodies that can catalyze a wide variety of chemical reactions. They are characterized by high substrate specificity and share many mechanistic features with enzymes.

genes,sis.name: genes , sis
genes,sis.definition: Sis genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (v-sis) originally isolated from the simian sarcoma virus (ssv). The proto-oncogene c-sis codes for a growth factor which is the b chain of platelet-derived growth factor. v-sis or overexpression of c-sis causes tumorigenesis. The human sis gene is located at 22q12.3-13.1 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 22.

geneticstructures.name: genetic structures
geneticstructures.definition: Genetic structures is the biological objects that contain genetic information and that are involved in transmitting genetically encoded traits from one organism to another.

insurance,physicianservices.name: insurance , physician services
insurance,physicianservices.definition: Physician services insurance is insurance providing benefits for the costs of care by a physician which can be comprehensive or limited to surgical expenses or for care provided only in the hospital. It is frequently called "regular medical expense" or "surgical expense".

libraries,digital.name: libraries , digital
libraries,digital.definition: Digital libraries is libraries in which a major proportion of the resources are available in machine-readable format, rather than on [MASK] or microform.

dnaprobes,hpv.name: dna probes , hpv
dnaprobes,hpv.definition: Hpv dna probes is dna probes specific for the identification of human papilloma virus.

healthcarerelatedorganization.name: health care related organization
healthcarerelatedorganization.definition: Health care related organization is health care related organization

hemoglobincdisease.name: hemoglobin c disease
hemoglobincdisease.definition: Hemoglobin c disease is a disease characterized by compensated hemolysis with a normal hemoglobin level or a mild to moderate anemia. There may be intermittent abdominal discomfort, splenomegaly, and slight jaundice.

angiography.name: angiography
angiography.definition: Angiography is radiography of blood vessels after injection of a contrast medium.

education,dental.name: education , dental
education,dental.definition: Dental education is use for articles concerning dental education in general.

contracts.name: contracts
contracts.definition: Contracts is agreements between two or more parties, especially those that are written and enforceable by law (American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed). It is sometimes used to characterize the nature of the professional-patient relationship.

hivfusioninhibitors.name: hiv fusion inhibitors
hivfusioninhibitors.definition: Hiv fusion inhibitors is inhibitors of the fusion of hiv to host cells, preventing viral entry. This includes compounds that block attachment of hiv envelope protein gp120 to cd4 receptors.

vitaminadeficiency.name: vitamin a deficiency
vitaminadeficiency.definition: Vitamin a deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin a in the diet, characterized by [MASK] and other ocular manifestations such as dryness of the conjunctiva and later of the cornea (xerophthalmia). Vitamin a deficiency is a very common problem worldwide, particularly in developing countries as a consequence of [MASK] or shortages of vitamin A-rich foods. In the United States it is found among the urban poor, the elderly, alcoholics, and patients with malabsorption. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1179)

codon.name: codon
codon.definition: Codon is a [MASK] of three nucleotides in a protein coding sequence that specifies individual amino acids or a termination signal (codon, terminator). Most codons are universal, but some organisms do not produce the transfer RNAs (rna, transfer) complementary to all codons. These codons are referred to as unassigned codons (codons, nonsense).

gabaagents.name: gaba agents
gabaagents.definition: Gaba agents is substances used for their pharmacological actions on GABAergic systems. GABAergic agents include agonists, antagonists, degradation or uptake inhibitors, depleters, precursors, and modulators of receptor function.

suddenunexpecteddeathinepilepsy.name: sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
suddenunexpecteddeathinepilepsy.definition: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy is sudden death in a patient with epilepsy associated with seizures and seizure-related symptoms (e.g., apnea; hypoxemia) without other identifiable accidental causes (e.g., drowning; wounds and injuries).

vaccines,contraceptive.name: vaccines , contraceptive
vaccines,contraceptive.definition: Contraceptive vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent conception.

endoplasmicreticulumstress.name: endoplasmic reticulum stress
endoplasmicreticulumstress.definition: Endoplasmic reticulum stress is various physiological or molecular disturbances that impair endoplasmic reticulum function. It triggers many responses, including unfolded protein response, which may lead to apoptosis; and [MASK].

mediannerve.name: median nerve
mediannerve.definition: Median nerve is a major nerve of the upper extremity. In humans, the fibers of the median nerve originate in the lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal cord (usually c6 to t1), travel via the brachial plexus, and supply sensory and motor innervation to parts of the forearm and hand.

fibroblastgrowthfactors.name: fibroblast growth factors
fibroblastgrowthfactors.definition: Fibroblast growth factors is a family of small polypeptide growth factors that share several common features including a strong affinity for heparin, and a central barrel-shaped core region of 140 amino acids that is highly homologous between family members. Although originally studied as proteins that stimulate the growth of fibroblasts this distinction is no longer a requirement for membership in the fibroblast growth factor family.

privatesector.name: private sector
privatesector.definition: Private sector is that distinct portion of the institutional, industrial, or economic structure of a country that is controlled or owned by non-governmental, private interests.

hospitals,university.name: hospitals , university
hospitals,university.definition: University hospitals is hospitals maintained by a university for the teaching of medical students, postgraduate training programs, and clinical research.

students,pharmacy.name: students , pharmacy
students,pharmacy.definition: Pharmacy students is individuals enrolled in a school of pharmacy or a formal educational program leading to a degree in pharmacy.

manufacturedmaterials.name: manufactured materials
manufacturedmaterials.definition: Manufactured materials is substances and materials manufactured for use in various technologies and industries and for domestic use.

cellproliferation.name: cell proliferation
cellproliferation.definition: Cell proliferation is all of the processes involved in increasing cell number including cell division.

insuranceclaimreporting.name: insurance claim reporting
insuranceclaimreporting.definition: Insurance claim reporting is the design, completion, and filing of forms with the insurer.

parasites.name: parasites
parasites.definition: Parasites is invertebrate organisms that live on or in another organism (the host), and benefit at the expense of the other. Traditionally excluded from definition of parasites are pathogenic bacteria; fungi; viruses; and plants; though they may live parasitically.

socialresponsibility.name: social responsibility
socialresponsibility.definition: Social responsibility is the obligations and accountability assumed in carrying out actions or ideas on behalf of others.

diaphragm.name: diaphragm
diaphragm.definition: Diaphragm is the musculofibrous partition that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. Contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic cavity aiding [MASK].

psychology,social.name: psychology , social
psychology,social.definition: Social psychology is the branch of psychology concerned with the effects of group membership upon the behavior, attitudes, and beliefs of an individual.

orbitaldiseases.name: orbital diseases
orbitaldiseases.definition: Orbital diseases is diseases of the bony [MASK] and contents except the eyeball.

genetictesting.name: genetic testing
genetictesting.definition: Genetic testing is detection of a mutation; genotype; karyotype; or specific alleles associated with genetic traits, heritable diseases, or predisposition to a disease, or that may lead to the disease in descendants. It includes prenatal genetic testing.

constriction.name: constriction
constriction.definition: Constriction is the act of constricting.

magnesiumoxide.name: magnesium oxide
magnesiumoxide.definition: Magnesium oxide is magnesium oxide (MgO). An inorganic compound that occurs in nature as the mineral periclase. In aqueous media combines quickly with water to form magnesium hydroxide. It is used as an antacid and mild laxative and has many nonmedicinal uses.

historyofdentistry.name: history of dentistry
historyofdentistry.definition: History of dentistry is study of past events and development in the field of dentistry.

schwanncells.name: schwann cells
schwanncells.definition: Schwann cells is neuroglial cells of the peripheral nervous system which form the insulating myelin sheaths of peripheral axons.

developmentalbiology.name: developmental biology
developmentalbiology.definition: Developmental biology is the field of biology which deals with the process of the growth and differentiation of an organism.

motivation.name: motivation
motivation.definition: Motivation is those factors which cause an organism to behave or act in either a goal-seeking or satisfying manner. They may be influenced by physiological drives or by external stimuli.

sodiumchloride,dietary.name: sodium chloride , dietary
sodiumchloride,dietary.definition: Dietary sodium chloride is sodium chloride used in foods.

bodytemperature.name: body temperature
bodytemperature.definition: Body temperature is the measure of the level of heat of a human or animal.

nutritionsurveys.name: nutrition surveys
nutritionsurveys.definition: Nutrition surveys is a systematic collection of factual data pertaining to the [MASK] of a human population within a given geographic area. Data from these surveys are used in preparing nutrition assessments.

watersports.name: water sports
watersports.definition: Water sports is activities or games performed in a body of water.

electronicwaste.name: electronic waste
electronicwaste.definition: Electronic waste is discarded electronic devices containing valuable and sometimes hazardous materials such as lead, nickel, cadmium, and mercury. (from http://www.epa.gov/osw/conserve/materials/ecycling/faq.htm#impact accessed 4/25/2010)

colorperceptiontests.name: color perception tests
colorperceptiontests.definition: [MASK] perception tests is type of vision test used to determine [MASK] vision defects.

phosphorusisotopes.name: phosphorus isotopes
phosphorusisotopes.definition: Phosphorus isotopes is stable phosphorus atoms that have the same atomic number as the element phosphorus, but differ in atomic weight. p-31 is a stable phosphorus isotope.

posteriorthalamicnuclei.name: posterior thalamic nuclei
posteriorthalamicnuclei.definition: Posterior thalamic nuclei is a transitional diencephalic zone of the thalamus consisting of complex and varied cells lying caudal to the [MASK], medial to the rostral part of the pulvinar, and dorsal to the medial geniculate body. It contains the limitans, posterior, suprageniculate, and submedial nuclei.

respiratoryaspirationofgastriccontents.name: respiratory aspiration of gastric contents
respiratoryaspirationofgastriccontents.definition: Respiratory aspiration of gastric contents is [MASK] refluxed gastric or duodenal contents.

multivariateanalysis.name: multivariate analysis
multivariateanalysis.definition: Multivariate analysis is a [MASK] of techniques used when variation in several variables has to be studied simultaneously. In statistics, multivariate analysis is interpreted as any analytic method that allows simultaneous study of two or more dependent variables.

carbonylreductase(nadph).name: carbonyl reductase ( nadph )
