carbonylreductase(nadph).definition: Carbonyl reductase (nadph) is carbonyl reductase ( nadph )

pulmonaryheartdisease.name: pulmonary heart disease
pulmonaryheartdisease.definition: Pulmonary heart disease is hypertrophy and dilation of the right ventricle of the heart that is caused by pulmonary hypertension. This condition is often associated with pulmonary parenchymal or vascular diseases, such as [MASK] and pulmonary embolism.

receptors,chemokine.name: receptors , chemokine
receptors,chemokine.definition: Chemokine receptors is cell surface glycoproteins that bind to chemokines and thus mediate the migration of pro-inflammatory molecules. The receptors are members of the seven-transmembrane g protein-coupled receptor family. Like the chemokines themselves, the receptors can be divided into at least three structural branches: cr, ccr, and cxcr, according to variations in a shared [MASK] motif.

cholinergicantagonists.name: cholinergic antagonists
cholinergicantagonists.definition: Cholinergic antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate cholinergic receptors, thereby blocking the actions of acetylcholine or cholinergic agonists.

prefrontalcortex.name: prefrontal cortex
prefrontalcortex.definition: Prefrontal cortex is the rostral part of the frontal lobe, bounded by the inferior precentral fissure in humans, which receives [MASK] fibers from the mediodorsal nucleus of the thalamus. The prefrontal cortex receives afferent fibers from numerous structures of the diencephalon; mesencephalon; and limbic system as well as cortical afferents of visual, auditory, and somatic origin.

currentproceduralterminology.name: current procedural terminology
currentproceduralterminology.definition: Current procedural terminology is descriptive terms and identifying codes for reporting medical services and procedures performed by physicians. It is produced by the [MASK] and used in insurance claim reporting for medicare; medicaid; and private health insurance programs (From cpt 2002).

angiotensini.name: angiotensin i
angiotensini.definition: Angiotensin i is a decapeptide that is cleaved from precursor angiotensinogen by renin. Angiotensin i has limited biological activity. It is converted to angiotensin ii, a potent vasoconstrictor, after the removal of two amino acids at the C-terminal by angiotensin converting enzyme.

reproductiveandurinaryphysiologicalpheno.name: reproductive and urinary physiological phenomena
reproductiveandurinaryphysiologicalpheno.definition: Reproductive and urinary physiological phenomena is physiology of the human and animal body, male or female, in the processes and characteristics of reproduction and the urinary tract.

genes,immunoglobulin.name: genes , immunoglobulin
genes,immunoglobulin.definition: Immunoglobulin genes is genes encoding the different subunits of the immunoglobulins, for example the immunoglobulin light chain genes and the [MASK] genes. The heavy and light immunoglobulin genes are present as gene segments in the germline cells. The completed genes are created when the segments are shuffled and assembled (b-lymphocyte gene rearrangement) during b-lymphocyte maturation. The gene segments of the human light and heavy chain germline genes are symbolized v (variable), j (joining) and c (constant). The heavy chain germline genes have an additional segment d (diversity).

diagnostictestapproval.name: diagnostic test approval
diagnostictestapproval.definition: [MASK] approval is the process of gaining approval by a government regulatory agency for diagnostic reagents and test kits. This includes any required preclinical or clinical testing, review, submission, and evaluation of the applications and test results, and post-marketing surveillance.

cathepsinw.name: cathepsin w
cathepsinw.definition: Cathepsin w is a [MASK] endopeptidase found in natural killer cells and cytotoxic t-lymphocytes. It may have a specific function in the mechanism or regulation of cytolytic activity of immune cells.

adenosine.name: adenosine
adenosine.definition: Adenosine is a nucleoside that is composed of adenine and d-ribose. Adenosine or adenosine derivatives play many important biological roles in addition to being components of dna and rna. Adenosine itself is a neurotransmitter.

skullbase.name: skull base
skullbase.definition: Skull base is the inferior region of the skull consisting of an internal (cerebral), and an external (basilar) surface.

heparinantagonists.name: heparin antagonists
heparinantagonists.definition: Heparin antagonists is coagulant substances inhibiting the anticoagulant action of heparin.

genes,fos.name: genes , fos
genes,fos.definition: Fos genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (fos) originally isolated from the Finkel-Biskis-Jinkins (fbj-msv) and Finkel-Biskis-Reilly (fbr-msv) murine sarcoma viruses. The proto-oncogene protein c-fos codes for a nuclear protein which is involved in growth-related transcriptional control. The insertion of c-fos into fbj-msv or fbr-msv induces [MASK] in mice. The human c-fos gene is located at 14q21-31 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 14.

naturalcytotoxicitytriggeringreceptor3.name: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 3
naturalcytotoxicitytriggeringreceptor3.definition: Natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 3 is a 30 kDa stimulatory receptor found on resting and activated natural killer cells.

ironcarbonylcompounds.name: iron carbonyl compounds
ironcarbonylcompounds.definition: Iron carbonyl compounds is complexes of iron atoms chelated with carbonyl ions.

infections.name: infections
infections.definition: Infections is invasion of the host organism by microorganisms or their toxins or by parasites that can cause pathological conditions or diseases.

pregnancycomplications.name: pregnancy complications
pregnancycomplications.definition: Pregnancy complications is conditions or pathological processes associated with pregnancy. They can occur during or after pregnancy, and range from minor discomforts to serious diseases that require medical interventions. They include diseases in pregnant females, and pregnancies in females with diseases.

toxicactions.name: toxic actions
toxicactions.definition: Toxic actions is a broad category of chemical actions with harmful or deadly effect on living organisms.

growthanddevelopment.name: growth and development
growthanddevelopment.definition: Growth and development is the series of changes to the shape, size, components, and functions of an individual organism that occur over time as the organism progresses from its initial form to full size and maturity.

mixedconnectivetissuedisease.name: mixed connective tissue disease
mixedconnectivetissuedisease.definition: Mixed connective tissue disease is a syndrome with overlapping clinical features of [MASK], scleroderma, polymyositis, and Raynaud's phenomenon. The disease is differentially characterized by high serum titers of antibodies to ribonuclease-sensitive extractable (saline soluble) nuclear antigen and a "speckled" epidermal nuclear staining pattern on direct immunofluorescence.

linkagedisequilibrium.name: linkage disequilibrium
linkagedisequilibrium.definition: Linkage disequilibrium is nonrandom association of linked genes. This is the tendency of the alleles of two separate but already linked loci to be found together more frequently than would be expected by chance alone.

insurance,disability.name: insurance , disability
insurance,disability.definition: Disability insurance is insurance designed to compensate persons who lose wages because of illness or injury; insurance providing periodic payments that partially replace lost wages, salary, or other income when the insured is unable to work because of illness, injury, or disease. Individual and group disability insurance are two types of such coverage. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988, p207)

cellcycle.name: cell cycle
cellcycle.definition: Cell cycle is the complex series of phenomena, occurring between the end of one cell division and the end of the next, by which cellular material is duplicated and then divided between two daughter cells. The cell cycle includes interphase, which includes g0 phase; g1 phase; s phase; and g2 phase, and cell division phase.

posteriorcervicalsympatheticsyndrome.name: posterior cervical sympathetic syndrome
posteriorcervicalsympatheticsyndrome.definition: Posterior cervical sympathetic syndrome is a pathological condition that is characterized by a host of cranial symptoms, such as headaches, abnormal functions of the eyes and the ears, and psychological and mental disorders. This syndrome usually appears after [MASK] injuries, inflammation, or neoplasm.

lateralligament,ankle.name: lateral ligament , ankle
lateralligament,ankle.definition: Ankle lateral ligament is lateral ligaments of the ankle joint. It includes inferior tibiofibular ligaments.

parenteralnutrition,home.name: parenteral nutrition , home
parenteralnutrition,home.definition: Home parenteral nutrition is the at-home administering of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient who cannot maintain adequate nutrition by enteral feeding alone. Nutrients are administered via a route other than the alimentary canal (e.g., intravenously, subcutaneously).

arthroplasty,replacement.name: arthroplasty , replacement
arthroplasty,replacement.definition: Replacement arthroplasty is partial or total replacement of a skeletal joint.

chromiumalloys.name: chromium alloys
chromiumalloys.definition: Chromium alloys is specific alloys not less than 85% chromium and nickel or cobalt, with traces of either nickel or cobalt, molybdenum, and other substances. They are used in partial dentures, orthopedic implants, etc.

metabolicsyndrome.name: metabolic syndrome
metabolicsyndrome.definition: Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of symptoms that are risk factors for cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The major components of metabolic syndrome include [MASK]; atherogenic dyslipidemia; hypertension; hyperglycemia; insulin resistance; a proinflammatory state; and a prothrombotic (thrombosis) state.

neutralizationtests.name: neutralization tests
neutralizationtests.definition: Neutralization tests is the measurement of infection-blocking titer of antisera by testing a series of dilutions for a given virus-antiserum interaction end-point, which is generally the dilution at which tissue cultures inoculated with the serum-virus mixtures demonstrate cytopathology (cpe) or the dilution at which 50% of test animals injected with serum-virus mixtures show infectivity (id50) or die ([MASK]).

markovchains.name: markov chains
markovchains.definition: Markov chains is a stochastic process such that the conditional probability distribution for a state at any future instant, given the present state, is unaffected by any additional knowledge of the past history of the system.

drugresistance.name: drug resistance
drugresistance.definition: Drug resistance is diminished or failed response of an organism, disease or tissue to the intended effectiveness of a chemical or drug. It should be differentiated from [MASK] which is the progressive diminution of the susceptibility of a human or animal to the effects of a drug, as a result of continued administration.

ricebranoil.name: rice bran oil
ricebranoil.definition: Rice bran oil is oil extracted from the hard outer brown layer of rice bran after the husk has been removed.

gambling.name: gambling
gambling.definition: Gambling is an activity distinguished primarily by an element of risk in trying to obtain a desired goal, e.g., playing a game of chance for money.

genes,rrna.name: genes , rrna
genes,rrna.definition: Rrna genes is genes, found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes, which are transcribed to produce the rna which is incorporated into ribosomes. Prokaryotic rRNA genes are usually found in operons dispersed throughout the genome, whereas eukaryotic rRNA genes are clustered, multicistronic transcriptional units.

turkey.name: turkey
turkey.definition: Turkey is country in Southeastern Europe and Southwestern Asia bordering the Black Sea, between Bulgaria and Georgia, and bordering the Aegean Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, between Greece and Syria. The capital is Ankara.

viruses.name: viruses
viruses.definition: Viruses is minute infectious agents whose genomes are composed of dna or rna, but not both. They are characterized by a lack of independent metabolism and the inability to replicate outside living host cells.

organspecificity.name: organ specificity
organspecificity.definition: Organ specificity is characteristic restricted to a particular organ of the body, such as a cell type, metabolic response or expression of a particular protein or antigen.

ions.name: ions
ions.definition: Ions is an atom or group of atoms that have a positive or negative electric charge due to a gain (negative charge) or loss (positive charge) of one or more [MASK]. Atoms with a positive charge are known as cations; those with a negative charge are anions.

toothcomponents.name: tooth components
toothcomponents.definition: Tooth components is the anatomical components of a tooth, its tissues, and correlated parts.

acetylation.name: acetylation
acetylation.definition: Acetylation is formation of an acetyl derivative. (Stedman, 25th ed)

wholebodyimaging.name: whole body imaging
wholebodyimaging.definition: Whole body imaging is the creation of a visual display of the inside of the entire body of a human or animal for the purposes of diagnostic evaluation. This is most commonly achieved by using magnetic resonance imaging; or [MASK] emission tomography.

greece.name: greece
greece.definition: Greece is a country in southern Europe, bordering the Aegean Sea, Ionian Sea, and the Mediterranean Sea, between Albania and Turkey. The capital is Athens.

diagnostictechniques,cardiovascular.name: diagnostic techniques , cardiovascular
diagnostictechniques,cardiovascular.definition: Cardiovascular diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases or dysfunction of the cardiovascular system or its organs or demonstration of their physiological processes.

vestibularfunctiontests.name: vestibular function tests
vestibularfunctiontests.definition: Vestibular function tests is a number of tests used to determine if the brain or balance portion of the [MASK] are causing dizziness.

chronicdisease.name: chronic disease
chronicdisease.definition: Chronic disease is diseases which have one or more of the following characteristics: they are permanent, leave residual disability, are caused by nonreversible pathological alteration, require special training of the patient for rehabilitation, or may be expected to require a long period of supervision, [MASK], or care. (Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

activatingtranscriptionfactors.name: activating transcription factors
activatingtranscriptionfactors.definition: Activating transcription factors is activating transcription factors were originally identified as dna-binding proteins that interact with early promoters from adenoviruses. They are a family of basic [MASK] zipper transcription factors that bind to the [MASK] site tgacgtca of the cyclic amp response element, and are closely related to cyclic amp-responsive dna-binding protein.

aspartatekinase.name: aspartate kinase
aspartatekinase.definition: Aspartate kinase is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of beta-aspartyl phosphate from aspartic acid and atp. Threonine serves as an allosteric regulator of this enzyme to control the biosynthetic pathway from aspartic acid to threonine. ec 2.7.2.4.

radialnerve.name: radial nerve
radialnerve.definition: Radial nerve is a major nerve of the upper extremity. In humans the fibers of the radial nerve originate in the lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal cord (usually c5 to t1), travel via the posterior cord of the brachial plexus, and supply motor innervation to extensor muscles of the [MASK] and cutaneous sensory fibers to extensor regions of the [MASK] and hand.

neuraltube.name: neural tube
neuraltube.definition: Neural tube is a tube of ectodermal tissue in an embryo that will give rise to the central nervous system, including the spinal cord and the brain. Lumen within the neural tube is called neural canal which gives rise to the central canal of the spinal cord and the ventricles of the brain. For malformation of the neural tube, see [MASK].

intelligence.name: intelligence
intelligence.definition: Intelligence is the ability to learn and to deal with new situations and to deal effectively with tasks involving abstractions.

communicationdisorders.name: communication disorders
communicationdisorders.definition: Communication disorders is disorders of verbal and nonverbal communication caused by receptive or expressive language disorders, cognitive dysfunction (e.g., mental retardation), psychiatric conditions, and hearing disorders.

suicide,assisted.name: suicide , assisted
suicide,assisted.definition: Assisted suicide is provision (by a physician or other health professional, or by a family member or friend) of support and/or means that gives a patient the power to terminate his or her own life. (from apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed).

fullyformedanatomicalstructure.name: fully formed anatomical structure
fullyformedanatomicalstructure.definition: Fully formed anatomical structure is fully formed anatomical structure

embryonicdevelopment.name: embryonic development
embryonicdevelopment.definition: Embryonic development is morphological and physiological development of embryos.

bloodplatelets.name: blood platelets
bloodplatelets.definition: Blood platelets is non-nucleated disk-shaped cells formed in the megakaryocyte and found in the blood of all mammals. They are mainly involved in blood coagulation.

pitchperception.name: pitch perception
pitchperception.definition: Pitch perception is a dimension of auditory sensation varying with cycles per second of the sound stimulus.

phosphorus,dietary.name: phosphorus , dietary
phosphorus,dietary.definition: Dietary phosphorus is phosphorus used in foods or obtained from food. This element is a major intracellular component which plays an important role in many biochemical pathways relating to normal physiological functions. High concentrations of dietary phosphorus can cause nephrocalcinosis which is associated with impaired kidney function. Low concentrations of dietary phosphorus cause an increase in calcitriol in the blood and osteoporosis.

geologicalphenomena.name: geological phenomena
geologicalphenomena.definition: Geological phenomena is structures, properties, and processes involving the inanimate matter of Earth.

socialvalidity,research.name: social validity , research
socialvalidity,research.definition: Research social validity is evaluation of the degree of acceptance for the immediate variables associated with a procedure or program designed to change behavior. This includes the social significance of the goals of treatment, the social appropriateness of the treatment procedures, and the social importance of the effects of treatments.

capsuleendoscopy.name: capsule endoscopy
capsuleendoscopy.definition: Capsule endoscopy is non-invasive, endoscopic imaging by use of video capsule endoscopes to perform examination of the gastrointestinal tract, especially the small bowel.

ultrasonography,doppler,color.name: ultrasonography , doppler , color
ultrasonography,doppler,color.definition: [MASK] doppler ultrasonography is ultrasonography applying the Doppler effect, with the superposition of flow information as [MASK] on a gray scale in a real-time image. This type of ultrasonography is well-suited to identifying the location of high-velocity flow (such as in a stenosis) or of mapping the extent of flow in a certain region.

mapkinasekinase7.name: map kinase kinase 7
mapkinasekinase7.definition: Map kinase kinase 7 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase with specificity for jnk mitogen-activated protein kinases. It takes part in a signal transduction pathway that is activated in response to cytokines.

pulmonarystretchreceptors.name: pulmonary stretch receptors
pulmonarystretchreceptors.definition: Pulmonary stretch receptors is stretch receptors found in the bronchi and bronchioles. Pulmonary stretch receptors are sensors for a reflex which stops inspiration. In humans, the reflex is protective and is probably not activated during normal respiration.

datamanagement.name: data management
datamanagement.definition: Data management is processes that include acquiring, validating, storing, protecting, and processing data to ensure accessibility, reliability, and timeliness for users.

surgicaloncology.name: surgical oncology
surgicaloncology.definition: Surgical oncology is a surgical specialty concerned with management of cancer.

chromatography,affinity.name: chromatography , affinity
chromatography,affinity.definition: Affinity chromatography is a chromatographic technique that utilizes the ability of biological molecules, often antibodies, to bind to certain ligands specifically and reversibly. It is used in protein biochemistry. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

respiratorytherapydepartment,hospital.name: respiratory therapy department , hospital
respiratorytherapydepartment,hospital.definition: Hospital respiratory therapy department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration of diagnostic pulmonary function tests and of procedures to restore optimum pulmonary ventilation.

ovulationinduction.name: ovulation induction
ovulationinduction.definition: Ovulation induction is techniques for the artifical induction of ovulation, the rupture of the follicle and release of the ovum.

healthsurveys.name: health surveys
healthsurveys.definition: Health surveys is a systematic collection of factual data pertaining to health and disease in a human population within a given geographic area.

abortion,therapeutic.name: abortion , therapeutic
abortion,therapeutic.definition: Therapeutic abortion is abortion induced to save the life or health of a pregnant woman. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

sodiumchannelblockers.name: sodium channel blockers
sodiumchannelblockers.definition: Sodium channel blockers is a class of drugs that act by inhibition of sodium influx through cell membranes. Blockade of sodium channels slows the rate and amplitude of initial rapid depolarization, reduces cell excitability, and reduces conduction velocity.

atrialseptum.name: atrial septum
atrialseptum.definition: Atrial septum is the thin membrane-like muscular structure separating the right and the left upper chambers (heart atria) of a heart.

sexdeterminationanalysis.name: sex determination analysis
sexdeterminationanalysis.definition: [MASK] determination analysis is validation of the [MASK] of an individual by inspection of the gonads and/or by genetic tests.

peptideterminationfactors.name: peptide termination factors
peptideterminationfactors.definition: Peptide termination factors is proteins that are involved in the peptide chain termination reaction (peptide chain termination, translational) on ribosomes. They include codon-specific class-I release factors, which recognize stop signals (terminator codon) in the messenger rna; and codon-nonspecific class-II release factors.

polandsyndrome.name: poland syndrome
polandsyndrome.definition: Poland syndrome is a syndrome which is characterized by symbrachydactyly and aplasia of the sternal head of pectoralis major.

datasetsastopic.name: datasets as topic
datasetsastopic.definition: Datasets as topic is subject matter related to the curation of data from research projects, stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

cosmetictechniques.name: cosmetic techniques
cosmetictechniques.definition: Cosmetic techniques is procedures for the improvement or enhancement of the appearance of the visible parts of the body.

czechrepublic.name: czech republic
czechrepublic.definition: Czech republic is created 1 January 1993 as a result of the division of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

love.name: love
love.definition: Love is affection; in psychiatry commonly refers to pleasure, particularly as it applies to gratifying experiences between individuals.

vietnamconflict.name: vietnam conflict
vietnamconflict.definition: Vietnam [MASK] is a [MASK] occurring from 1954 through 1975 within the Republic of Vietnam. It involved neighboring nations and the United States and other members of the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization.

primaryhealthcare.name: primary health care
primaryhealthcare.definition: Primary health care is care which provides integrated, accessible health care services by clinicians who are accountable for addressing a large majority of personal health care needs, developing a sustained partnership with patients, and practicing in the context of family and community. (jama 1995;273(3):192)

tissueculturetechniques.name: tissue culture techniques
tissueculturetechniques.definition: Tissue culture techniques is a technique for maintaining or growing tissue in vitro, usually by diffusion, perifusion, or perfusion. The tissue is cultured directly after removal from the host without being dispersed for cell culture.

handtransplantation.name: hand transplantation
handtransplantation.definition: Hand transplantation is the transference of a complete hand, as a composite of many tissue types, from one individual to another.

distancecounseling.name: distance counseling
distancecounseling.definition: Distance counseling is counseling conducted via electronic or other non-face-to-face interactions.

ethicalanalysis.name: ethical analysis
ethicalanalysis.definition: Ethical analysis is the use of systematic methods of ethical examination, such as casuistry or ethical theory, in reasoning about moral problems.

uterinecervicaldiseases.name: uterine cervical diseases
uterinecervicaldiseases.definition: Uterine cervical diseases is pathological processes of the uterine cervix.

antigens,ly.name: antigens , ly
antigens,ly.definition: Ly antigens is a group of lymphocyte surface antigens located on mouse lymphocytes. Specific Ly antigens are useful markers for distinguishing subpopulations of lymphocytes.

environment,controlled.name: environment , controlled
environment,controlled.definition: Controlled environment is a state in which the environs of hospitals, laboratories, domestic and animal housing, work places, spacecraft, and other surroundings are under technological control with regard to air conditioning, [MASK], [MASK], humidity, ventilation, and other ambient features. The concept includes control of atmospheric composition. (From Jane's Aerospace Dictionary, 3d ed)

hepatitis,infectiouscanine.name: hepatitis , infectious canine
hepatitis,infectiouscanine.definition: Infectious canine hepatitis is a contagious disease caused by canine adenovirus (adenoviruses, canine) infecting the liver, the eye, the kidney, and other organs in dogs, other canids, and bears. Symptoms include fever; edema; vomiting; and [MASK].

organizations.name: organizations
organizations.definition: Organizations is groups of people working together in a structured manner to pursue common goals and objectives.

familyplanningservices.name: family planning services
familyplanningservices.definition: Family planning services is health care programs or services designed to assist individuals in the planning of family size. Various methods of contraception can be used to control the number and timing of childbirths.

weightlifting.name: weight lifting
weightlifting.definition: Weight lifting is a sport in which weights are lifted competitively or as an exercise.

brachialplexus.name: brachial plexus
brachialplexus.definition: Brachial plexus is the large network of nerve fibers which distributes the innervation of the upper extremity. The brachial plexus extends from the [MASK] into the axilla. In humans, the nerves of the plexus usually originate from the lower cervical and the first thoracic spinal cord segments (c5-c8 and t1), but variations are not uncommon.

breathingexercises.name: breathing exercises
breathingexercises.definition: Breathing exercises is therapeutic exercises aimed to deepen inspiration or expiration or even to alter the rate and rhythm of respiration.

peptideelongationfactors.name: peptide elongation factors
peptideelongationfactors.definition: Peptide elongation factors is protein factors uniquely required during the elongation phase of protein synthesis.

london.name: london
london.definition: London is the capital of the United Kingdom. It is located in England.

generearrangement.name: gene rearrangement
generearrangement.definition: Gene rearrangement is the ordered rearrangement of gene regions by dna recombination such as that which occurs normally during development.

chromosomes,human,pair9.name: chromosomes , human , pair 9
chromosomes,human,pair9.definition: Pair 9 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group c chromsomes of the human chromosome classification.

oralsurgicalprocedures.name: oral surgical procedures
oralsurgicalprocedures.definition: Oral surgical procedures is surgical procedures used to treat disease, injuries, and defects of the oral and maxillofacial region.

comprehension.name: comprehension
comprehension.definition: Comprehension is the act or fact of grasping the meaning, nature, or importance of; understanding. (American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed) Includes understanding by a patient or research subject of information disclosed orally or in writing.

muscle,smooth,vascular.name: muscle , smooth , vascular
muscle,smooth,vascular.definition: Vascular smooth muscle is the nonstriated involuntary muscle tissue of blood vessels.

leukocytes.name: leukocytes
leukocytes.definition: Leukocytes is [MASK] blood cells. These include granular leukocytes (basophils; eosinophils; and neutrophils) as well as non-granular leukocytes (lymphocytes and monocytes).

cheese.name: cheese
cheese.definition: Cheese is a nutritious food consisting primarily of the curd or the semisolid substance formed when milk coagulates.

studycharacteristics.name: study characteristics
studycharacteristics.definition: Study characteristics is type of empirical method used.

pyruvateoxidase.name: pyruvate oxidase
pyruvateoxidase.definition: Pyruvate oxidase is an important enzyme in bacterial metabolism for increasing ATP production and providing a fitness advantage via hydrogen peroxide production.

diabeticretinopathy.name: diabetic retinopathy
diabeticretinopathy.definition: Diabetic retinopathy is disease of the retina as a complication of diabetes mellitus. It is characterized by the progressive microvascular complications, such as aneurysm, interretinal edema, and intraocular pathologic neovascularization.

psychotherapy,group.name: psychotherapy , group
psychotherapy,group.definition: Group psychotherapy is a form of therapy in which two or more patients participate under the guidance of one or more psychotherapists for the purpose of treating emotional disturbances, social maladjustments, and psychotic states.

internalmedicine.name: internal medicine
internalmedicine.definition: Internal medicine is a medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the internal organ systems of adults.

internetaccess.name: internet access
internetaccess.definition: Internet access is ability to connect to access services available on the Internet.

aluminumcompounds.name: aluminum compounds
aluminumcompounds.definition: Aluminum compounds is inorganic compounds that contain aluminum as an integral part of the molecule.

electricalsynapses.name: electrical synapses
electricalsynapses.definition: Electrical synapses is specialized junctions between neurons which connect the cytoplasm of one neuron to another allowing direct passage of an ion current.

feedback,sensory.name: feedback , sensory
feedback,sensory.definition: Sensory [MASK] is a mechanism of communicating one's own sensory system information about a task, movement or skill.

behavioralsciences.name: behavioral sciences
behavioralsciences.definition: Behavioral sciences is disciplines concerned with the study of human and animal behavior.

reversetranscriptasepolymerasechainreact.name: reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction
reversetranscriptasepolymerasechainreact.definition: Reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction is a variation of the pcr technique in which cDNA is made from rna via reverse transcription. The resultant cDNA is then amplified using standard pcr protocols.

programmedcelldeath1ligand2protein.name: programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 protein
programmedcelldeath1ligand2protein.definition: Programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 protein is a costimulatory b7 antigen that has specificity for the t-cell receptor programmed cell death 1 receptor. It is closely-related to cd274 antigen; however, its expression is restricted to [MASK] and activated macrophages.

bookprices.name: book prices
bookprices.definition: Book prices is amount paid to purchase individual volumes or [MASK] from a bookseller.

thyroidcrisis.name: thyroid crisis
thyroidcrisis.definition: Thyroid crisis is a dangerous life-threatening hypermetabolic condition characterized by high fever and dysfunction of the cardiovascular, the nervous, and the gastrointestinal systems.

receptor,angiotensin,type2.name: receptor , angiotensin , type 2
receptor,angiotensin,type2.definition: Type 2 angiotensin receptor is an angiotensin receptor subtype that is expressed at high levels in fetal tissues. Many effects of the angiotensin type 2 receptor such as vasodilation and sodium loss are the opposite of that of the angiotensin type 1 receptor.

drugprescriptions.name: drug prescriptions
drugprescriptions.definition: Drug prescriptions is directions written for the obtaining and use of drugs.

vaccination.name: vaccination
vaccination.definition: Vaccination is administration of vaccines to stimulate the host's immune response. This includes any preparation intended for active immunological prophylaxis.

pituitaryhormones,anterior.name: pituitary hormones , anterior
pituitaryhormones,anterior.definition: Anterior pituitary hormones is hormones secreted by the adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). Structurally, they include polypeptide, protein, and glycoprotein molecules.

aminoacids,neutral.name: amino acids , neutral
aminoacids,neutral.definition: Neutral amino acids is amino acids with uncharged r groups or side chains.

bread.name: bread
bread.definition: Bread is baked food product made of flour or meal that is moistened, kneaded, and sometimes fermented. a major food since prehistoric times, it has been made in various forms using a variety of ingredients and methods.

doublebindinteraction.name: double bind interaction
doublebindinteraction.definition: Double bind interaction is simultaneous communication of conflicting messages in which the response to either message evokes [MASK] or disapproval. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

biologicalsciencedisciplines.name: biological science disciplines
biologicalsciencedisciplines.definition: Biological science disciplines is all of the divisions of the natural sciences dealing with the various aspects of the phenomena of life and vital processes. The concept includes anatomy and physiology, biochemistry and biophysics, and the biology of animals, plants, and microorganisms. It should be differentiated from biology, one of its subdivisions, concerned specifically with the origin and life processes of living organisms.

teachingrounds.name: teaching rounds
teachingrounds.definition: Teaching rounds is systematic discussions and teaching conducted in hospitals and healthcare facilities related to patient care.

printing.name: printing
printing.definition: Printing is process of reproducing words or images on a physical media.

dualspecificityphosphatase2.name: dual specificity phosphatase 2
dualspecificityphosphatase2.definition: Dual specificity phosphatase 2 is a dual specificity phosphatase subtype that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction by inactivating mitogen-activated protein kinases. It has specificity for extracellular signal-regulated map kinases and is primarily localized to the cell nucleus.

muscles.name: muscles
muscles.definition: Muscles is contractile tissue that produces movement in animals.

cochlearnucleus.name: cochlear nucleus
cochlearnucleus.definition: Cochlear nucleus is the brain stem nucleus that receives the central input from the cochlear nerve. The cochlear nucleus is located lateral and dorsolateral to the inferior cerebellar peduncles and is functionally divided into dorsal and ventral parts. It is tonotopically organized, performs the first stage of central auditory processing, and projects (directly or indirectly) to higher auditory areas including the superior olivary nuclei, the medial geniculi, the inferior colliculi, and the auditory cortex.

cityplanning.name: city planning
cityplanning.definition: City planning is comprehensive planning for the physical development of the city.

nitratereductase(nadh).name: nitrate reductase ( nadh )
nitratereductase(nadh).definition: Nitrate reductase (nadh) is nitrate reductase ( nadh )

enamelorgan.name: enamel organ
enamelorgan.definition: Enamel organ is epithelial cells surrounding the dental papilla and differentiated into three layers: the inner enamel epithelium, consisting of ameloblasts which eventually form the enamel, and the enamel pulp and external enamel epithelium, both of which atrophy and disappear before and upon eruption of the tooth, respectively.

prescriptiondrugmisuse.name: prescription drug misuse
prescriptiondrugmisuse.definition: Prescription drug misuse is improper use of prescription drugs or medications outside the intended purpose, scope, or guidelines for use.

mice,knockout,apoe.name: mice , knockout , apoe
mice,knockout,apoe.definition: Apoe knockout mice is strains of mice that contain genetic disruptions (knockout) of apolipoproteins e genes. They are used as models for atherosclerosis research.

disordersofenvironmentalorigin.name: disorders of environmental origin
disordersofenvironmentalorigin.definition: Disorders of environmental origin is disorders caused by external forces rather than by physiologic dysfunction or by pathogens.

models,cardiovascular.name: models , cardiovascular
models,cardiovascular.definition: Cardiovascular models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of the cardiovascular system, processes, or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers and other electronic equipment.

physiology,comparative.name: physiology , comparative
physiology,comparative.definition: Comparative physiology is the biological science concerned with similarities or differences in the life-supporting functions and processes of different species.

endometrialablationtechniques.name: endometrial ablation techniques
endometrialablationtechniques.definition: Endometrial ablation techniques is procedures used for the targeted destruction of the mucous membrane lining of the uterine cavity.

urinaryincontinence,stress.name: urinary incontinence , stress
urinaryincontinence,stress.definition: Stress urinary incontinence is involuntary discharge of urine as a result of physical activities that increase abdominal pressure on the [MASK] without detrusor contraction or overdistended [MASK]. The subtypes are classified by the degree of leakage, descent and opening of the [MASK] [MASK] and urethra without [MASK] contraction, and sphincter deficiency.

diseaseattributes.name: disease attributes
diseaseattributes.definition: Disease attributes is clinical characteristics of disease or illness.

administration,oral.name: administration , oral
administration,oral.definition: Oral administration is the giving of drugs, chemicals, or other substances by mouth.

outpatientclinics,hospital.name: outpatient clinics , hospital
outpatientclinics,hospital.definition: Hospital outpatient clinics is organized services in a hospital which provide medical care on an outpatient basis.

respiratorysystemabnormalities.name: respiratory system abnormalities
respiratorysystemabnormalities.definition: Respiratory system abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the respiratory system.

facialpain.name: facial pain
facialpain.definition: Facial pain is pain in the facial region including orofacial pain and craniofacial pain. Associated conditions include local inflammatory and neoplastic disorders and neuralgic syndromes involving the trigeminal, facial, and glossopharyngeal nerves. Conditions which feature recurrent or persistent facial pain as the primary manifestation of disease are referred to as facial pain syndromes.

intrinsicfactor.name: intrinsic factor
intrinsicfactor.definition: Intrinsic factor is a glycoprotein secreted by the cells of the gastric glands that is required for the absorption of vitamin b 12 (cyanocobalamin). Deficiency of intrinsic factor leads to vitamin b 12 deficiency and anemia, pernicious.

plasmids.name: plasmids
plasmids.definition: Plasmids is extrachromosomal, usually circular dna molecules that are self-replicating and transferable from one organism to another. They are found in a variety of bacterial, archaeal, fungal, algal, and plant species. They are used in genetic engineering as cloning vectors.

hospitals,district.name: hospitals , district
hospitals,district.definition: District hospitals is government-controlled hospitals which represent the major health facility for a designated geographic area.

dentalservice,hospital.name: dental service , hospital
dentalservice,hospital.definition: Hospital dental service is hospital department providing dental care.

boneneoplasms.name: bone neoplasms
boneneoplasms.definition: Bone neoplasms is tumors or cancer located in bone tissue or specific bones.

embryonicstructures.name: embryonic structures
embryonicstructures.definition: Embryonic structures is the anatomical parts that make up an organism in the early stages of development.

rats,nude.name: rats , nude
rats,nude.definition: Nude rats is a mutant strain of Rattus norvegicus without a thymus and with depressed or absent T-cell function. This strain of rats may have a small amount of hair at times, but then lose it.

preventivehealthservices.name: preventive health services
preventivehealthservices.definition: Preventive health services is services designed for health promotion.

economics,dental.name: economics , dental
economics,dental.definition: Dental economics is economic aspects of the dental profession and dental care.

physiologicalphenomena.name: physiological phenomena
physiologicalphenomena.definition: Physiological phenomena is the functions and properties of living organisms, including both the physical and chemical factors and processes, supporting life in single- or multi-cell organisms from their origin through the progression of life.

geneticresearch.name: genetic research
geneticresearch.definition: Genetic research is research into the cause, transmission, amelioration, elimination, or enhancement of inherited disorders and traits.

embryoimplantation.name: embryo implantation
embryoimplantation.definition: Embryo implantation is endometrial implantation of embryo, mammalian at the blastocyst stage.

rnarecognitionmotifproteins.name: rna recognition motif proteins
rnarecognitionmotifproteins.definition: Rna recognition motif proteins is a family of rna-binding proteins that contain an rna recognition motif and two ribonucleoprotein (rnp) domains which bind rna, in addition to other domains that allow for high affinity binding, sequence specificity, and protein interactions. Examples of rna recognition motif proteins include heterogeneous nuclear ribonuclearproteins (hnRNP) and embryonic lethal abnormal-vision (elav) proteins.

embolization,therapeutic.name: embolization , therapeutic
embolization,therapeutic.definition: Therapeutic embolization is a method of hemostasis utilizing various agents such as Gelfoam, silastic, metal, glass, or plastic pellets, autologous clot, fat, and muscle as emboli. It has been used in the treatment of spinal cord and intracranial arteriovenous malformations, renal arteriovenous fistulas, gastrointestinal bleeding, epistaxis, hypersplenism, certain highly vascular tumors, traumatic rupture of blood vessels, and control of operative hemorrhage.

helperviruses.name: helper viruses
helperviruses.definition: Helper viruses is viruses which enable defective viruses to replicate or to form a protein coat by complementing the missing gene function of the defective (satellite) virus. Helper and satellite may be of the same or different genus.

sequenceinversion.name: sequence inversion
sequenceinversion.definition: Sequence inversion is the deletion and reinsertion of a segment of a nucleic acid sequence in the same place, but flipped in an opposite orientation.

receptors,melatonin.name: receptors , melatonin
receptors,melatonin.definition: Melatonin receptors is a family of G-protein-coupled receptors that are specific for and mediate the effects of melatonin. Activation of melatonin receptors has been associated with decreased intracellular cyclic amp and increased hydrolysis of phosphoinositides.

myelinsheath.name: myelin sheath
myelinsheath.definition: Myelin sheath is the lipid-rich sheath surrounding axons in both the central nervous systems and peripheral nervous system. The myelin sheath is an electrical insulator and allows faster and more energetically efficient conduction of impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of glial cells (schwann cells in the peripheral and oligodendroglia in the central nervous system). Deterioration of the sheath in demyelinating diseases is a serious clinical problem.

preoperativecare.name: preoperative care
preoperativecare.definition: Preoperative care is care given during the period prior to undergoing surgery when psychological and physical preparations are made according to the special needs of the individual patient. This period spans the time between admission to the hospital to the time the surgery begins. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

aminoacidsequence.name: amino acid sequence
aminoacidsequence.definition: Amino acid sequence is the order of amino acids as they occur in a polypeptide chain. This is referred to as the primary structure of proteins. It is of fundamental importance in determining protein conformation.

colitis.name: colitis
colitis.definition: Colitis is inflammation of the colon section of the large intestine (intestine, large), usually with symptoms such as [MASK] (often with blood and mucus), abdominal pain, and fever.

alpharhythm.name: alpha rhythm
alpharhythm.definition: Alpha rhythm is brain waves characterized by a relatively high voltage or amplitude and a frequency of 8-13 Hz. They constitute the majority of waves recorded by eeg registering the activity of the parietal and occipital lobes when the individual is awake, but relaxed with the eyes closed.

footulcer.name: foot ulcer
footulcer.definition: [MASK] [MASK] is lesion on the surface of the skin of the [MASK], usually accompanied by inflammation. The lesion may become infected or necrotic and is frequently associated with diabetes or leprosy.

forensicpsychiatry.name: forensic psychiatry
forensicpsychiatry.definition: Forensic psychiatry is psychiatry in its legal aspects. This includes criminology, penology, commitment of [MASK], the psychiatrist's role in compensation cases, the problems of releasing information to the court, and of expert testimony.

mutationrate.name: mutation rate
mutationrate.definition: Mutation rate is the number of mutations that occur in a specific sequence, gene, or genome over a specified period of time such as years, cell divisions, or generations.

arsenic.name: arsenic
arsenic.definition: Arsenic is a shiny gray element with atomic symbol As, atomic number 33, and atomic weight 75. It occurs throughout the universe, mostly in the form of metallic arsenides. Most forms are toxic. According to the Fourth Annual Report on Carcinogens (ntp 85-002, 1985), arsenic and certain arsenic compounds have been listed as known carcinogens. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

ampicillin.name: ampicillin
ampicillin.definition: Ampicillin is semi-synthetic derivative of penicillin that functions as an orally active broad-spectrum antibiotic.

nucleotidesequence.name: nucleotide sequence
nucleotidesequence.definition: Nucleotide sequence is a succession of bases signified by a series of a [MASK] of five different letters that indicate the order of nucleotides forming alleles within a DNA (using GACT) or RNA (GACU) molecule.

antigens,nuclear.name: antigens , nuclear
antigens,nuclear.definition: Nuclear antigens is immunologically detectable substances found in the cell nucleus.

soymilk.name: soy milk
soymilk.definition: Soy milk is a beverage prepared from soybeans.

conflictofinterest.name: conflict of interest
conflictofinterest.definition: [MASK] of interest is a situation in which an individual might benefit personally from official or professional actions. It includes a [MASK] between a person's private interests and official responsibilities in a position of trust. The term is not restricted to government officials. The concept refers both to actual [MASK] of interest and the appearance or perception of [MASK].

pestcontrol.name: pest control
pestcontrol.definition: Pest control is the reduction or regulation of the population of noxious, destructive, or dangerous plants, insects, or other animals.  This includes control of plants that serve as habitats or food sources for animal pests.

crossingover,genetic.name: crossing over , genetic
crossingover,genetic.definition: Genetic crossing over is the reciprocal exchange of segments at corresponding positions along pairs of homologous chromosomes by symmetrical breakage and crosswise rejoining forming cross-over sites (holliday junctions) that are resolved during chromosome segregation. Crossing-over typically occurs during meiosis but it may also occur in the absence of meiosis, for example, with bacterial chromosomes, organelle chromosomes, or somatic cell nuclear chromosomes.

enzymetherapy.name: enzyme therapy
enzymetherapy.definition: Enzyme therapy is the use of enzymes to correct metabolic and physiological processes.

survivors.name: survivors
survivors.definition: Survivors is persons who have experienced a prolonged survival after serious disease or who continue to live with a usually life-threatening condition as well as family members, significant others, or individuals surviving traumatic life events.

lymphaticsystem.name: lymphatic system
lymphaticsystem.definition: Lymphatic system is a system of organs and tissues that process and transport immune cells and [MASK].

consciousnessdisorders.name: consciousness disorders
consciousnessdisorders.definition: Consciousness disorders is organic mental disorders in which there is impairment of the ability to maintain awareness of self and environment and to respond to environmental stimuli. Dysfunction of the cerebral hemispheres or brain stem reticular formation may result in this condition.

norepinephrineplasmamembranetransportpro.name: norepinephrine plasma membrane transport proteins
norepinephrineplasmamembranetransportpro.definition: Norepinephrine plasma membrane transport proteins is sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters located primarily on the plasma membrane of noradrenergic neurons. They remove norepinephrine from the extracellular space by high affinity reuptake into presynaptic terminals. The norepinephrine transporter regulates signal amplitude and duration at noradrenergic synapses and is the target of adrenergic uptake inhibitors.

lungabscess.name: lung abscess
lungabscess.definition: Lung abscess is solitary or multiple collections of pus within the lung parenchyma as a result of infection by bacteria, protozoa, or other agents.

cholinergicagents.name: cholinergic agents
cholinergicagents.definition: Cholinergic agents is any drug used for its actions on cholinergic systems. Included here are agonists and antagonists, drugs that affect the [MASK] of acetylcholine, and drugs that affect the survival of cholinergic neurons. The term cholinergic agents is sometimes still used in the narrower sense of muscarinic agonists, although most modern texts discourage that usage.

hospitalbedcapacity,500andover.name: hospital bed capacity , 500 and over
hospitalbedcapacity,500andover.definition: 500 and over hospital bed capacity is the number of beds 500 or more which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds [MASK] up and staffed for use.

integrinbetachains.name: integrin beta chains
integrinbetachains.definition: Integrin beta chains is integrin beta chains combine with integrin alpha chains to form heterodimeric cell surface receptors. Integrins have traditionally been classified into functional groups based on the identity of one of three beta chains present in the heterodimer. The beta chain is necessary and sufficient for integrin-dependent signaling. Its short cytoplasmic tail contains sequences critical for inside-out signaling.

aged,80andover.name: aged , 80 and over
aged,80andover.definition: 80 and over aged is a person 80 years of age and older.

arthritis,juvenile.name: arthritis , juvenile
arthritis,juvenile.definition: Juvenile arthritis is arthritis in children, with onset before 16 years of age. The terms juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (jra) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (jia) refer to classification systems for chronic arthritis in children. Only one subtype of juvenile arthritis (polyarticular-onset, rheumatoid factor-positive) clinically resembles adult rheumatoid arthritis and is considered its childhood equivalent.

illinois.name: illinois
illinois.definition: Illinois is state bounded on the north by Wisconsin, on the east by [MASK] Michigan, Indiana, and Kentucky, on the west by Missouri and Iowa, and on the south by Kentucky.

peripheralvasculardiseases.name: peripheral vascular diseases
peripheralvasculardiseases.definition: Peripheral vascular diseases is pathological processes involving any one of the blood vessels in the vasculature outside the heart.

aminoacids,basic.name: amino acids , basic
aminoacids,basic.definition: Basic amino acids is amino acids with side chains that are positively charged at physiological pH.

dentalresearch.name: dental research
dentalresearch.definition: Dental research is the study of laws, theories, and hypotheses through a systematic examination of pertinent facts and their interpretation in the field of dentistry. (From Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982, p674)

financing,organized.name: financing , organized
financing,organized.definition: Organized financing is all organized methods of funding.

middlecerebralartery.name: middle cerebral artery
middlecerebralartery.definition: Middle cerebral artery is the largest of the cerebral arteries. It trifurcates into temporal, frontal, and parietal branches supplying blood to most of the parenchyma of these lobes in the cerebral cortex. These are the areas involved in motor, sensory, and [MASK] activities.

internationalnormalizedratio.name: international normalized ratio
internationalnormalizedratio.definition: International normalized ratio is system established by the [MASK] Organization and the International Committee on Thrombosis and Hemostasis for monitoring and reporting blood coagulation tests. Under this system, results are standardized using the International Sensitivity Index for the particular test reagent/instrument combination used.

organizationalaffiliation.name: organizational affiliation
organizationalaffiliation.definition: Organizational affiliation is formal relationships established between otherwise independent organizations. These include affiliation agreements, interlocking boards, common controls, hospital medical school affiliations, etc.

replicationproteinc.name: replication protein c
replicationproteinc.definition: Replication protein c is a DNA-binding protein and aaa ATPase that consists of 5 polypeptides and plays an essential role in dna replication in eukaryotes. It binds dna PRIMER-template junctions and recruits proliferating cell nuclear antigen and dna polymerases to the site of dna synthesis.

rehabilitationresearch.name: rehabilitation research
rehabilitationresearch.definition: Rehabilitation research is studies and research concerning the psychological, educational, social, vocational, industrial, and economic aspects of rehabilitation.

energytransfer.name: energy transfer
energytransfer.definition: Energy transfer is the transfer of energy of a given form among different scales of motion. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed). It includes the transfer of kinetic energy and the transfer of chemical energy. The transfer of chemical energy from one molecule to another depends on proximity of molecules so it is often used as in techniques to measure distance such as the use of forster resonance energy transfer.

minoritygroups.name: minority groups
minoritygroups.definition: Minority groups is a subgroup having special characteristics within a larger group, often bound together by special ties which distinguish it from the larger group.

harmreduction.name: harm reduction
harmreduction.definition: Harm reduction is the application of methods designed to reduce the risk of harm associated with certain behaviors without reduction in frequency of those behaviors. The risk-associated behaviors include ongoing and active addictive behaviors.

biologicalvariation,population.name: biological variation , population
biologicalvariation,population.definition: Population biological variation is differences in measurable biological values, characteristics, or traits, among individuals of a population or between population groups.

socialmobility.name: social mobility
socialmobility.definition: Social mobility is the movement or shifting of membership between or within social classes by individuals or by groups.

microbialviability.name: microbial viability
microbialviability.definition: Microbial viability is ability of a microbe to survive under given conditions. This can also be related to a colony's ability to replicate.

administration,inhalation.name: administration , inhalation
administration,inhalation.definition: [MASK] administration is the administration of drugs by the respiratory route. It includes insufflation into the respiratory tract.

pregnancy,animal.name: pregnancy , animal
pregnancy,animal.definition: Animal pregnancy is the process of bearing developing young (embryos or fetuses) in utero in non-human mammals, beginning from fertilization to birth.

heuristics.name: heuristics
heuristics.definition: Heuristics is experience-based techniques for problem-solving, learning, and discovery that find a solution which is not guaranteed to be optimal, but sufficient for a given [MASK] of goals.

infant.name: infant
infant.definition: Infant is a child between 1 and 23 months of age.

cerebralcortex.name: cerebral cortex
cerebralcortex.definition: Cerebral cortex is the thin layer of gray matter on the surface of the cerebral hemispheres that develops from the telencephalon and folds into gyri and sulchi. It reaches its highest development in humans and is responsible for intellectual faculties and higher mental functions.

virulence.name: virulence
virulence.definition: Virulence is the degree of pathogenicity within a group or species of microorganisms or viruses as indicated by case fatality rates and/or the ability of the organism to invade the tissues of the host. The pathogenic capacity of an organism is determined by its virulence factors.

mesentericarteries.name: mesenteric arteries
mesentericarteries.definition: Mesenteric arteries is arteries which arise from the abdominal aorta and distribute to most of the intestines.

fluorescencepolarization.name: fluorescence polarization
fluorescencepolarization.definition: Fluorescence polarization is measurement of the polarization of fluorescent light from solutions or microscopic specimens. It is used to provide information concerning molecular size, shape, and conformation, molecular anisotropy, electronic energy transfer, molecular interaction, including dye and coenzyme binding, and the antigen-antibody reaction.

eyepain.name: eye pain
eyepain.definition: Eye pain is a dull or sharp painful sensation associated with the outer or inner structures of the eyeball, having different causes.

hydrocarbons,aromatic.name: hydrocarbons , aromatic
hydrocarbons,aromatic.definition: Aromatic hydrocarbons is organic compounds containing carbon and hydrogen in the form of an unsaturated, usually hexagonal ring structure. The compounds can be single ring, or double, triple, or multiple fused rings.

periodontalcyst.name: periodontal cyst
periodontalcyst.definition: Periodontal cyst is an epithelium-lined sac containing fluid; usually found at the apex of a pulp-involved tooth. The lateral type occurs less frequently along the side of the root.

fattyacidbindingprotein3.name: fatty acid binding protein 3
fattyacidbindingprotein3.definition: Fatty acid binding protein 3 is a small cytosolic fatty-acid binding protein that forms a lipid-binding beta-barrel structure and is expressed by [MASK] and at lower levels in brain tissue. It is released into plasma immediately following cardiac injury and may therefore serve as a useful biomarker for the early detection of myocardial infarction.

elongationfactor2kinase.name: elongation factor 2 kinase
elongationfactor2kinase.definition: Elongation factor 2 kinase is a monomeric calcium-calmodulin-dependent protein kinase subtype that specifically phosphorylates peptide elongation factor 2. The enzyme lacks a phosphorylatable activation domain that can respond to calcium-calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase, however it is regulated by phosphorylation by protein kinase a and through intramolecular autophosphorylation.

pathologicalconditions,signsandsymptoms.name: pathological conditions , signs and symptoms
pathologicalconditions,signsandsymptoms.definition: Signs and symptoms pathological conditions is abnormal anatomical or physiological conditions and objective or subjective manifestations of disease, not classified as disease or syndrome.

insituhybridization,fluorescence.name: in situ hybridization , fluorescence
insituhybridization,fluorescence.definition: Fluorescence in situ hybridization is a type of in situ hybridization in which target sequences are stained with fluorescent dye so their location and size can be determined using fluorescence microscopy. This staining is sufficiently distinct that the hybridization signal can be seen both in metaphase spreads and in interphase nuclei.

whitespotsyndromevirus1.name: white spot syndrome virus 1
whitespotsyndromevirus1.definition: [MASK] spot syndrome virus 1 is a species of dna virus, in the genus whispovirus, infecting penaeid shrimp.

surgeons.name: surgeons
surgeons.definition: Surgeons is medical practitioners qualified to practice surgery.

magneticresonanceimaging.name: magnetic resonance imaging
magneticresonanceimaging.definition: Magnetic resonance imaging is non-invasive method of demonstrating internal anatomy based on the principle that atomic nuclei in a strong magnetic field absorb pulses of radiofrequency energy and emit them as radiowaves which can be reconstructed into computerized images. The concept includes proton spin tomographic techniques.

epilepsy,absence.name: epilepsy , absence
epilepsy,absence.definition: Absence epilepsy is a seizure disorder usually occurring in childhood characterized by rhythmic electrical brain discharges of generalized onset. Clinical features include a sudden cessation of ongoing activity usually without loss of postural tone. Rhythmic blinking of the eyelids or [MASK] smacking frequently accompanies the seizures. The usual duration is 5-10 seconds, and multiple episodes may occur daily. Juvenile absence epilepsy is characterized by the juvenile onset of absence seizures and an increased incidence of myoclonus and tonic-clonic seizures. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p736)

dentalcariessusceptibility.name: dental caries susceptibility
dentalcariessusceptibility.definition: Dental caries susceptibility is the predisposition to tooth decay (dental caries).

dentalrestoration,permanent.name: dental restoration , permanent
dentalrestoration,permanent.definition: Permanent dental restoration is a restoration designed to remain in service for not less than 20 to 30 years, usually made of gold casting, cohesive gold, or amalgam. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992)

herpessimplex.name: herpes simplex
herpessimplex.definition: Herpes simplex is a group of acute infections caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 or type 2 that is characterized by the development of one or more small fluid-filled vesicles with a raised erythematous base on the skin or mucous membrane. It occurs as a primary infection or recurs due to a reactivation of a latent infection. (Dorland, 27th ed.)

spinalfusion.name: spinal fusion
spinalfusion.definition: Spinal fusion is operative immobilization or ankylosis of two or more vertebrae by fusion of the vertebral bodies with a short bone [MASK] or often with diskectomy or laminectomy. (From Blauvelt & Nelson, a Manual of Orthopaedic Terminology, 5th ed, p236; Dorland, 28th ed)

convection.name: convection
convection.definition: Convection is transmission of energy or mass by a medium involving movement of the medium itself. The circulatory movement that occurs in a fluid at a nonuniform temperature owing to the variation of its density and the action of gravity. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed; Webster, 10th ed)

foodassistance.name: food assistance
foodassistance.definition: Food assistance is food or financial assistance for food given to those in need.

electrophoresis,capillary.name: electrophoresis , capillary
electrophoresis,capillary.definition: Capillary electrophoresis is a highly-sensitive (in the picomolar range, which is 10,000-fold more sensitive than conventional electrophoresis) and efficient technique that allows separation of proteins; nucleic acids; and carbohydrates. (Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

liverdiseases.name: liver diseases
liverdiseases.definition: Liver diseases is pathological processes of the liver.

norepinephrine.name: norepinephrine
norepinephrine.definition: Norepinephrine is precursor of epinephrine that is secreted by the adrenal medulla and is a widespread central and autonomic neurotransmitter. Norepinephrine is the principal transmitter of most postganglionic sympathetic fibers, and of the diffuse [MASK] system in the brain that arises from the locus ceruleus. It is also found in plants and is used pharmacologically as a sympathomimetic.

peptides,cyclic.name: peptides , cyclic
peptides,cyclic.definition: Cyclic peptides is peptides whose amino acid residues are linked together forming a circular chain. Some of them are anti-infective agents; some are biosynthesized non-ribosomally (peptide biosynthesis, non-ribosomal).

chromosomes,human,pair6.name: chromosomes , human , pair 6
chromosomes,human,pair6.definition: Pair 6 human chromosomes is a specific pair group c chromsomes of the human chromosome classification.

coldtemperature.name: cold temperature
coldtemperature.definition: Cold temperature is an absence of warmth or heat or a temperature notably below an accustomed norm.

thirdventricle.name: third ventricle
thirdventricle.definition: Third ventricle is a narrow cleft inferior to the corpus callosum, within the diencephalon, between the paired thalami. Its floor is formed by the hypothalamus, its anterior wall by the lamina terminalis, and its roof by ependyma. It communicates with the fourth ventricle by the cerebral aqueduct, and with the lateral ventricles by the interventricular foramina.

cerebralinfarction.name: cerebral infarction
cerebralinfarction.definition: Cerebral infarction is the formation of an area of necrosis in the cerebrum caused by an insufficiency of arterial or venous blood flow. Infarcts of the cerebrum are generally classified by hemisphere (i.e., left vs. right), lobe (e.g., frontal lobe infarction), arterial distribution (e.g., infarction, anterior cerebral artery), and etiology (e.g., embolic infarction).

familypractice.name: family practice
familypractice.definition: Family practice is a medical specialty concerned with the provision of continuing, comprehensive primary health care for the entire family.

neoplasticprocess.name: neoplastic process
neoplasticprocess.definition: Neoplastic process is the accumulation of somatic mutations in certain genes that thus give rise to tumor cells.

guidedtissueregeneration,periodontal.name: guided tissue regeneration , periodontal
guidedtissueregeneration,periodontal.definition: Periodontal guided tissue regeneration is techniques for enhancing and directing cell growth to repopulate specific parts of the periodontium that have been damaged by periodontal diseases; tooth diseases; or trauma, or to correct tooth abnormalities. Repopulation and repair is achieved by guiding the progenitor cells to reproduce in the desired location by blocking contact with surrounding tissue by use of membranes composed of synthetic or natural material that may include growth inducing factors as well.

collagen.name: collagen
collagen.definition: Collagen is a polypeptide substance comprising about one third of the total protein in mammalian organisms. It is the main constituent of skin; connective tissue; and the organic substance of bones (bone and bones) and teeth (tooth).

monitoring,physiologic.name: monitoring , physiologic
monitoring,physiologic.definition: Physiologic monitoring is the continuous measurement of physiological processes, blood pressure, heart rate, renal output, reflexes, respiration, etc., in a patient or experimental animal; includes pharmacologic monitoring, the measurement of administered drugs or their metabolites in the blood, tissues, or urine.

goldalloys.name: gold alloys
goldalloys.definition: Gold alloys is alloys that contain a high percentage of gold. They are used in restorative or prosthetic dentistry.

skintests.name: skin tests
skintests.definition: Skin tests is epicutaneous or intradermal application of a sensitizer for demonstration of either delayed or immediate hypersensitivity. Used in diagnosis of hypersensitivity or as a test for cellular immunity.

fingerjoint.name: finger joint
fingerjoint.definition: Finger joint is the articulation between the head of one phalanx and the base of the one distal to it, in each finger.

mortality,premature.name: mortality , premature
mortality,premature.definition: Premature mortality is deaths that occur before [MASK] is reached within a given population.

genes,essential.name: genes , essential
genes,essential.definition: Essential genes is those genes found in an organism which are necessary for its viability and normal function.

attitudeofhealthpersonnel.name: attitude of health personnel
attitudeofhealthpersonnel.definition: Attitude of health personnel is attitudes of personnel toward their patients, other professionals, toward the medical care system, etc.

femoralvein.name: femoral vein
femoralvein.definition: Femoral vein is the vein accompanying the [MASK] in the same sheath; it is a continuation of the popliteal vein and becomes the external [MASK].

genes,rel.name: genes , rel
genes,rel.definition: Rel genes is family of retrovirus-associated dna sequences (v-rel) originally isolated from an avian reticuloendotheliosis virus strain. The proto-oncogene rel (c-rel) codes for a subcellular (nuclear and cytoplasmic) transcription factor that has a role in lymphocyte differentiation. Translocation or overexpression of c-rel or competition from v-rel causes oncogenesis. The human rel gene is located at 2p12-13 on the short [MASK] of [MASK].

ownership.name: ownership
ownership.definition: Ownership is the legal relation between an entity (individual, group, corporation, or-profit, secular, government) and an object. The object may be corporeal, such as equipment, or completely a creature of law, such as a patent; it may be movable, such as an animal, or immovable, such as a building.

mitochondrialsize.name: mitochondrial size
mitochondrialsize.definition: Mitochondrial size is the quantity of volume or surface area of mitochondria.

synaptictransmission.name: synaptic transmission
synaptictransmission.definition: Synaptic transmission is the communication from a neuron to a target (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) across a synapse. In chemical synaptic transmission, the presynaptic neuron releases a neurotransmitter that diffuses across the synaptic cleft and binds to specific synaptic receptors, activating them. The activated receptors modulate specific ion channels and/or second-messenger systems in the postsynaptic cell. In electrical synaptic transmission, electrical signals are communicated as an ionic current flow across electrical synapses.

biologicaloxygendemandanalysis.name: biological oxygen demand analysis
biologicaloxygendemandanalysis.definition: Biological oxygen demand analysis is testing for the amount of biodegradable organic material in a water sample by measuring the quantity of oxygen consumed by biodegradation of those materials over a specific time period.

qualityofhealthcare.name: quality of health care
qualityofhealthcare.definition: Quality of health care is the levels of excellence which characterize the health service or health care provided based on accepted standards of quality.

injuryorpoisoning.name: injury or poisoning
injuryorpoisoning.definition: Injury or poisoning is injury or poisoning

zinccompounds.name: zinc compounds
zinccompounds.definition: Zinc compounds is inorganic compounds that contain zinc as an integral part of the molecule.

healthfacilityenvironment.name: health facility environment
healthfacilityenvironment.definition: Health facility environment is physical surroundings or conditions of a hospital or other health facility and influence of these factors on patients and staff.

pennsylvania.name: pennsylvania
pennsylvania.definition: Pennsylvania is state bounded on the north by New York and [MASK] Erie, on the east by Delaware and New Jersey, on the south by Delaware and Maryland, and on the west by Ohio and West Virginia.

golgiapparatus.name: golgi apparatus
golgiapparatus.definition: Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened vesicles that functions in posttranslational processing and sorting of proteins, receiving them from the rough endoplasmic reticulum and directing them to [MASK], lysosomes, or the cell membrane. The movement of proteins takes place by transfer vesicles that bud off from the rough endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus and fuse with the Golgi, lysosomes or cell membrane. (From Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990)

anterioreyesegment.name: anterior eye segment
anterioreyesegment.definition: Anterior eye segment is the front third of the eyeball that includes the structures between the front surface of the cornea and the front of the [MASK].

consciousness.name: consciousness
consciousness.definition: Consciousness is sense of awareness of self and of the environment.

neoplasmrecurrence,local.name: neoplasm recurrence , local
neoplasmrecurrence,local.definition: Local neoplasm recurrence is the local recurrence of a neoplasm following treatment. It arises from microscopic cells of the original neoplasm that have escaped therapeutic intervention and later become clinically visible at the original site.

memory,episodic.name: memory , episodic
memory,episodic.definition: Episodic memory is type of declarative memory, consisting of personal memory in contrast to general knowledge.

criminallaw.name: criminal law
criminallaw.definition: Criminal law is a branch of law that defines criminal offenses, regulates the apprehension, charging and trial of suspected persons, and fixes the penalties and modes of treatment applicable to convicted offenders.

healthoccupations.name: health occupations
healthoccupations.definition: Health occupations is professions or other business activities directed to the cure and prevention of disease. For occupations of medical personnel who are not physicians but who are working in the fields of medical technology, physical therapy, etc., allied health occupations is available.

mirrorneurons.name: mirror neurons
mirrorneurons.definition: Mirror neurons is neurons that fire when an animal acts or observes the same action of another thus coding the motor response. They were originally discovered in the premotor and parietal cortex of the monkey and studies have shown that neurons that have a similar mechanism are present in humans. Mirror neurons are theorized to be related to social cognition.

peptidechaintermination,translational.name: peptide chain termination , translational
peptidechaintermination,translational.definition: Translational peptide chain termination is a process of genetic translation whereby the terminal amino acid is added to a lengthening polypeptide. This termination process is signaled from the messenger rna, by one of three termination codons (codon, terminator) that immediately follows the last amino acid-specifying codon.

genitaldiseases,female.name: genital diseases , female
genitaldiseases,female.definition: Female genital diseases is pathological processes involving the female reproductive tract (genitalia, female).

breakthroughpain.name: breakthrough pain
breakthroughpain.definition: Breakthrough pain is acute pain that comes on rapidly despite the use of pain medication.

oralhemorrhage.name: oral hemorrhage
oralhemorrhage.definition: Oral hemorrhage is bleeding from the blood vessels of the mouth, which may occur as a result of injuries to the mouth, accidents in oral surgery, or diseases of the gums.

painperception.name: pain perception
painperception.definition: Pain perception is the process by which pain is recognized and interpreted by the brain.

genetics.name: genetics
genetics.definition: Genetics is the branch of science concerned with the means and consequences of transmission and generation of the components of biological inheritance. (Stedman, 26th ed)

childhealth.name: child health
childhealth.definition: Child health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of children.

laborpain.name: labor pain
laborpain.definition: Labor pain is pain associated with obstetric labor in childbirth. It is caused primarily by [MASK] as well as pressure on the cervix; [MASK]; and the gastrointestinal tract. Labor pain mostly occurs in the abdomen; the groin; and the back.

stochasticprocesses.name: stochastic processes
stochasticprocesses.definition: Stochastic processes is processes that incorporate some element of randomness, used particularly to refer to a time series of random variables.

adaptiveclinicaltrial.name: adaptive clinical trial
