adaptiveclinicaltrial.definition: Adaptive clinical trial is clinical study in which a prospectively planned opportunity is included to modify trial designs and hypotheses based on analysis of data from subjects in the study.

insulinsecretion.name: insulin secretion
insulinsecretion.definition: Insulin secretion is production and release of insulin from pancreatic beta cells that primarily occurs in response to elevated blood glucose levels.

plantstems.name: plant stems
plantstems.definition: Plant stems is parts of plants that usually grow vertically upwards towards the light and support the leaves, buds, and reproductive structures. (From Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)

46,xxdisordersofsexdevelopment.name: 46 , xx disorders of sex development
46,xxdisordersofsexdevelopment.definition: Xx disorders of [MASK] development 46 is congenital conditions in individuals with a female karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical [MASK] is atypical.

ffactor.name: f factor
ffactor.definition: F factor is a plasmid whose presence in the cell, either extrachromosomal or integrated into the bacterial chromosome, determines the "[MASK]" of the bacterium, host chromosome mobilization, transfer via conjugation ([MASK]) of genetic material, and the formation of [MASK] pili.

proteasomeinhibitors.name: proteasome inhibitors
proteasomeinhibitors.definition: Proteasome inhibitors is compounds that inhibit the function or proteolytic action of the proteasome.

heatexhaustion.name: heat exhaustion
heatexhaustion.definition: Heat exhaustion is a clinical syndrome caused by heat stress, such as over-exertion in a hot environment or excessive exposure to sun. It is characterized by sweating, water (volume) depletion, [MASK] depletion, cool clammy skin, nausea, and headache.

education,pharmacy,continuing.name: education , pharmacy , continuing
education,pharmacy,continuing.definition: Continuing pharmacy education is educational programs designed to inform graduate pharmacists of recent advances in their particular field.

sleepinitiationandmaintenancedisorders.name: sleep initiation and maintenance disorders
sleepinitiationandmaintenancedisorders.definition: Sleep initiation and maintenance disorders is disorders characterized by impairment of the ability to initiate or maintain sleep. This may occur as a primary disorder or in association with another medical or psychiatric condition.

nanotubes,peptide.name: nanotubes , peptide
nanotubes,peptide.definition: Peptide nanotubes is nanotubes formed from cyclic peptides (peptides, cyclic). Alternating d and l linkages create planar rings that self assemble by stacking into nanotubes. They can form pores through cell membrane causing damage to cells.

wntsignalingpathway.name: wnt signaling pathway
wntsignalingpathway.definition: Wnt signaling pathway is a complex signaling pathway whose name is derived from the drosophila Wg gene, and the vertebrate int gene. The signaling pathway is initiated by the binding of [MASK] to cell surface wnt receptors which interact with the axin signaling complex and an array of second messengers that influence the actions of beta catenin.

cardiovascularnursing.name: cardiovascular nursing
cardiovascularnursing.definition: Cardiovascular nursing is a specialty concerned with the nursing care of patients suffering from disorders of the cardiovascular system as well as those identified as at risk for adverse cardiac or vascular events.

antiretroviraltherapy,highlyactive.name: antiretroviral therapy , highly active
antiretroviraltherapy,highlyactive.definition: Highly active antiretroviral therapy is drug regimens, for patients with hiv infections, that aggressively suppress hiv replication. The regimens usually involve administration of three or more different drugs including a protease inhibitor.

nuclearproteins.name: nuclear proteins
nuclearproteins.definition: Nuclear proteins is proteins found in the nucleus of a cell. Do not confuse with nucleoproteins which are proteins conjugated with nucleic acids, that are not necessarily present in the nucleus.

interpersonalpsychotherapy.name: interpersonal psychotherapy
interpersonalpsychotherapy.definition: Interpersonal psychotherapy is interpersonal modification of psychodynamic psychotherapy. Therapy is present-focused and seeks to resolve problems in interpersonal relations. Aspects of attachment theory are used to analyze how past relationships affect current relationships.

insurance,life.name: insurance , life
insurance,life.definition: Life insurance is insurance providing for payment of a stipulated sum to a designated beneficiary upon death of the insured.

vitreoushemorrhage.name: vitreous hemorrhage
vitreoushemorrhage.definition: Vitreous hemorrhage is hemorrhage into the [MASK].

pragmaticclinicaltrial.name: pragmatic clinical trial
pragmaticclinicaltrial.definition: Pragmatic clinical trial is randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

ciliaryneurotrophicfactor.name: ciliary neurotrophic factor
ciliaryneurotrophicfactor.definition: Ciliary neurotrophic factor is a neurotrophic factor that promotes the survival of various neuronal cell types and may play an important role in the injury response in the nervous system.

pierrerobinsyndrome.name: pierre robin syndrome
pierrerobinsyndrome.definition: Pierre robin syndrome is congenital malformation characterized by micrognathia or retrognathia; glossoptosis and cleft palate. The mandibular abnormalities often result in difficulties in sucking and swallowing. The syndrome may be isolated or associated with other syndromes (e.g., andersen syndrome; campomelic dysplasia). Developmental mis-expression of sox9 transcription factor gene on chromosome 17q and its surrounding region is associated with the syndrome.

trachealdiseases.name: tracheal diseases
trachealdiseases.definition: Tracheal diseases is diseases involving the [MASK].

chromosomepositioning.name: chromosome positioning
chromosomepositioning.definition: Chromosome positioning is the mechanisms of eukaryotic cells that place or keep the chromosomes in a particular subnuclear space.

informationseekingbehavior.name: information seeking behavior
informationseekingbehavior.definition: Information seeking behavior is how information is gathered in personal, academic or work environments and the resources used.

therapeuticuses.name: therapeutic uses
therapeuticuses.definition: Therapeutic uses is uses of chemicals which affect the course of conditions, diseases, syndromes or pathology to benefit the health of an individual.

jawfractures.name: jaw fractures
jawfractures.definition: Jaw fractures is fractures of the upper or lower jaw.

pancreaticpolypeptide.name: pancreatic polypeptide
pancreaticpolypeptide.definition: Pancreatic polypeptide is a 36-amino acid pancreatic hormone that is secreted mainly by endocrine cells found at the periphery of the islets of langerhans and adjacent to cells containing somatostatin and glucagon. Pancreatic polypeptide (pp), when administered peripherally, can suppress gastric secretion, gastric emptying, pancreatic enzyme secretion, and appetite. a lack of pancreatic polypeptide (pp) has been associated with obesity in rats and mice.

silver.name: silver
silver.definition: Silver is an element with the atomic symbol Ag, atomic number 47, and atomic weight 107.87. It is a soft metal that is used medically in surgical instruments, dental prostheses, and alloys. Long-continued use of silver [MASK] can lead to a form of poisoning known as argyria.

fees,pharmaceutical.name: fees , pharmaceutical
fees,pharmaceutical.definition: Pharmaceutical fees is amounts charged to the patient or third-party payer for medication. It includes the pharmacist's professional fee and cost of ingredients, containers, etc.

problemsandexercises.name: problems and exercises
problemsandexercises.definition: Problems and exercises is works consisting of collections of practice questions and drills, generally for instructional or review use.

colon,transverse.name: colon , transverse
colon,transverse.definition: Transverse colon is the segment of large intestine between ascending colon and [MASK]. It passes from the right colic flexure across the abdomen, then turns sharply at the left colonic flexure into the [MASK].

cytokinereceptorcommonbetasubunit.name: cytokine receptor common beta subunit
cytokinereceptorcommonbetasubunit.definition: Cytokine receptor common beta subunit is a receptor subunit that is a shared component of the interleukin-3 receptor; the interleukin-5 receptor; and the gm-csf receptor. High affinity receptor complexes are formed with each of these receptors when their respective alpha subunits are combined with this shared beta subunit.

survivalofmotorneuron1protein.name: survival of motor neuron 1 protein
survivalofmotorneuron1protein.definition: Survival of motor neuron 1 protein is an smn complex protein that contains a tudor domain and is essential for the function of the smn protein complex. In humans, the protein is encoded by a single gene found near the inversion telomere of a large inverted region of chromosome 5. Mutations in the gene coding for survival of motor neuron 1 protein may result in spinal muscular atrophies of childhood.

astronomy.name: astronomy
astronomy.definition: Astronomy is the science concerned with celestial bodies and the [MASK] and interpretation of the radiation received in the vicinity of the earth from the component parts of the universe (McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

syntheticlethalmutations.name: synthetic lethal mutations
syntheticlethalmutations.definition: Synthetic lethal mutations is mutations in genes which lead to cell or organism death when occurring in combination with mutations in one or more other genes.

vascularendothelialgrowthfactora.name: vascular endothelial growth factor a
vascularendothelialgrowthfactora.definition: Vascular endothelial growth factor a is the original member of the family of endothelial cell growth factors referred to as vascular endothelial growth factors. Vascular endothelial growth factor-A was originally isolated from tumor cells and referred to as "tumor angiogenesis factor" and "vascular permeability factor". Although expressed at high levels in certain tumor-derived cells it is produced by a wide variety of cell types. In addition to stimulating vascular growth and vascular permeability it may play a role in stimulating vasodilation via [MASK]-dependent pathways. [MASK] of the mRNA for vascular endothelial growth factor a results in several isoforms of the protein being produced.

scienceinliterature.name: science in literature
scienceinliterature.definition: Science in literature is literary works whose subject matter is science or about the profession of science and related areas.

meiosis.name: meiosis
meiosis.definition: Meiosis is a type of cell nucleus division, occurring during maturation of the germ cells. Two successive cell nucleus divisions following a single chromosome duplication (s phase) result in daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cells.

livestock.name: livestock
livestock.definition: Livestock is domesticated farm animals raised for home use or profit but excluding poultry. Typically livestock includes cattle; sheep; horses; swine; goats; and others.

kidneydiseases,cystic.name: kidney diseases , cystic
kidneydiseases,cystic.definition: Cystic kidney diseases is a heterogeneous group of hereditary and acquired disorders in which the kidney contains one or more cysts unilaterally or bilaterally (kidney, cystic).

salvagetherapy.name: salvage therapy
salvagetherapy.definition: Salvage therapy is a therapeutic approach, involving chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery, after initial regimens have failed to lead to improvement in a patient's condition. Salvage therapy is most often used for neoplastic diseases.

lipoproteinlipase.name: lipoprotein lipase
lipoproteinlipase.definition: Lipoprotein lipase is an enzyme of the hydrolase class that catalyzes the reaction of triacylglycerol and water to yield diacylglycerol and a fatty acid anion. The enzyme hydrolyzes triacylglycerols in chylomicrons, very-low-density lipoproteins, low-density lipoproteins, and diacylglycerols. It occurs on capillary endothelial surfaces, especially in mammary, muscle, and adipose tissue. Genetic deficiency of the enzyme causes familial hyperlipoproteinemia Type i. (Dorland, 27th ed) ec 3.1.1.34.

pulsewaveanalysis.name: pulse wave analysis
pulsewaveanalysis.definition: Pulse wave analysis is evaluation of the contour of the pulse waves which vary in different parts of the circulation and depend on physiological as well as pathophysiological conditions of the individual.

retinalhorizontalcells.name: retinal horizontal cells
retinalhorizontalcells.definition: Retinal horizontal cells is neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina that synapse with both the retinal photoreceptor cells and the retinal bipolar cells, as well as other horizontal cells. The horizontal cells modulate the sensory signal.

matrixattachmentregionbindingproteins.name: matrix attachment region binding proteins
matrixattachmentregionbindingproteins.definition: [MASK] binding proteins is proteins that bind to the [MASK] of dna.

developingcountries.name: developing countries
developingcountries.definition: Developing countries is countries in the process of change with economic growth, that is, an increase in production, per capita consumption, and income. The process of economic growth involves better utilization of natural and human resources, which results in a change in the social, political, and economic structures.

accidentalinjuries.name: accidental injuries
accidentalinjuries.definition: Accidental injuries is injuries resulting from events or circumstances that are unforeseen, unplanned, unanticipated, and without premeditation.

cerebralpalsy.name: cerebral palsy
cerebralpalsy.definition: Cerebral palsy is a heterogeneous group of nonprogressive motor disorders caused by chronic brain injuries that originate in the prenatal period, perinatal period, or first few years of life. The four major subtypes are spastic, athetoid, ataxic, and mixed cerebral palsy, with spastic forms being the most common. The motor disorder may range from difficulties with fine motor control to severe spasticity (see muscle spasticity) in all limbs. Spastic diplegia (Little disease) is the most common subtype, and is characterized by spasticity that is more prominent in the legs than in the [MASK]. Pathologically, this condition may be associated with leukomalacia, periventricular. (From Dev Med Child Neurol 1998 Aug;40(8):520-7)

socialdiscrimination.name: social discrimination
socialdiscrimination.definition: Social discrimination is group behavior toward others by virtue of their group membership.

operationsresearch.name: operations research
operationsresearch.definition: Operations research is a group of techniques developed to apply scientific methods and tools to solve the problems of decision making in complex organizations and systems. Operations research searches for optimal solutions in situations of conflicting goals and makes use of mathematical models from which solutions for actual problems may be derived. (From Psychiatric Dictionary, 6th ed)

solutecarrierfamily12,member3.name: solute carrier family 12 , member 3
solutecarrierfamily12,member3.definition: Member 3 solute carrier family 12 is na-Cl cotransporter in the convoluted segments of the distal kidney tubule. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium and chloride and is inhibited by thiazide diuretics.

malformationsofcorticaldevelopment.name: malformations of cortical development
malformationsofcorticaldevelopment.definition: Malformations of cortical development is abnormalities in the development of the cerebral cortex. These include malformations arising from abnormal neuronal and glial cell proliferation or apoptosis (Group i); abnormal neuronal migration (Group ii); and abnormal establishment of cortical organization (Group iii). Many inborn metabolic brain disorders affecting cns formation are often associated with cortical malformations. They are common causes of epilepsy and developmental delay.

transistors,electronic.name: transistors , electronic
transistors,electronic.definition: Electronic transistors is electrical devices that are composed of semiconductor material, with at least three connections to an external electronic circuit. They are used to amplify electrical signals, detect signals, or as switches.

macrophageinflammatoryproteins.name: macrophage inflammatory proteins
macrophageinflammatoryproteins.definition: Macrophage inflammatory proteins is heparin-binding proteins that exhibit a number of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. Originally identified as secretory products of macrophages, these chemokines are produced by a variety of cell types including neutrophils; fibroblasts; and epithelial cells. They likely play a significant role in respiratory tract defenses.

physicaltherapists.name: physical therapists
physicaltherapists.definition: Physical therapists is persons trained in physical therapy specialty to make use of physical therapy modalities to prevent, correct, and alleviate movement dysfunction.

optictract.name: optic tract
optictract.definition: Optic tract is nerve fiber originating from the optic chiasm that connects predominantly to the lateral geniculate bodies. It is the continuation of the visual pathway that conveys the visual information originally from the retina to the optic chiasm via the optic nerves.

spinalcordvasculardiseases.name: spinal cord vascular diseases
spinalcordvasculardiseases.definition: Spinal cord vascular diseases is pathological processes involving any of the blood vessels feeding the spinal cord, such as the anterior and paired posterior spinal arteries or their many branches. Disease processes may include atherosclerosis; embolism; and arteriovenous malformations leading to ischemia or hemorrhage into the spinal cord (hematomyelia).

unitedstatessocialsecurityadministration.name: united states social security administration
unitedstatessocialsecurityadministration.definition: United states social security administration is an independent agency within the Executive Branch of the United States Government. It administers a national social insurance program whereby employees, employers, and the self-employed pay contributions into pooled trust funds. Part of the contributions go into a separate hospital insurance trust fund for workers at age 65 to provide help with medical expenses. Other programs include the supplemental social security income program for the aged, blind, and disabled and the Old Age Survivors and Disability Insurance Program. It became an independent agency March 31, 1995. It had previously been part of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, later the Department of Health and Human Services. (From United States Government Manual, 1994-95)

choline.name: choline
choline.definition: Choline is a basic constituent of lecithin that is found in many plants and animal organs. It is important as a precursor of acetylcholine, as a methyl donor in various metabolic processes, and in lipid metabolism.

organismhydrationstatus.name: organism hydration status
organismhydrationstatus.definition: Organism hydration status is quantitative measure of water or fluids contained in the body of a living organism.

collapsetherapy.name: collapse therapy
collapsetherapy.definition: Collapse therapy is surgical treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis whereby the lung is totally or partially, temporarily or permanently, immobilized. The procedure was based on the popular concept that collapsing the affected portion of a tuberculous lung allowed the infected area to rest and thereby recover. At the beginning of the 20th century artificially induced pneumothorax (pneumothorax, artificial) was popular. Later a variety of other techniques was used to encourage collapse of the infected portion of the lung: unilateral phrenic nerve division, pneumonolysis, pneumoperitoneum (pneumoperitoneum, artificial), and thoracoplasty. Collapse therapy has declined since the advent of antitubercular chemotherapy. (Stedman, 25th ed; from Sabiston Jr, Textbook of Surgery, 14th ed, p1733-4)

extinction,psychological.name: extinction , psychological
extinction,psychological.definition: Psychological extinction is the procedure of presenting the conditioned stimulus without reinforcement to an organism previously conditioned. It refers also to the diminution of a conditioned response resulting from this procedure.

conscioussedation.name: conscious sedation
conscioussedation.definition: Conscious sedation is a drug-induced depression of consciousness during which patients respond purposefully to verbal commands, either alone or accompanied by light tactile stimulation. No interventions are required to maintain a patent airway. (From: American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines)

householdarticles.name: household articles
householdarticles.definition: Household articles is various material objects and items in the home. It includes temporary or permanent machinery and appliances. It does not include furniture or interior furnishings (furniture see interior design and furnishings; interior furnishings see interior design and furnishings).

shock,traumatic.name: shock , traumatic
shock,traumatic.definition: Traumatic shock is shock produced as a result of trauma.

hospitalrestructuring.name: hospital restructuring
hospitalrestructuring.definition: Hospital restructuring is reorganization of the hospital corporate structure.

consumerproductsafety.name: consumer product safety
consumerproductsafety.definition: Consumer product safety is the sum total of measures taken and regulatory policies enacted to ensure the safe use of consumer products.

genome.name: genome
genome.definition: Genome is the genetic complement of an organism, including all of its genes, as represented in its dna, or in some cases, its rna.

healthresources.name: health resources
healthresources.definition: Health resources is available manpower, facilities, revenue, equipment, and supplies to produce requisite health care and services.

cardiovascularabnormalities.name: cardiovascular abnormalities
cardiovascularabnormalities.definition: Cardiovascular abnormalities is congenital, inherited, or acquired anomalies of the cardiovascular system, including the heart and blood vessels.

adaptation,psychological.name: adaptation , psychological
adaptation,psychological.definition: Psychological adaptation is a state of harmony between internal needs and external demands and the processes used in achieving this condition. (From apa Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed)

artificialintelligence.name: artificial intelligence
artificialintelligence.definition: Artificial intelligence is theory and development of computer systems which perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. Such tasks may include [MASK] recognition, learning; visual perception; [MASK]; reasoning, problem solving, decision-making, and translation of language.

electrontransportcomplexii.name: electron transport complex ii
electrontransportcomplexii.definition: [MASK] transport complex ii is a flavoprotein oxidase complex that contains iron-sulfur centers. It catalyzes the oxidation of succinate to fumarate and couples the reaction to the reduction of ubiquinone to ubiquinol.

geography,medical.name: geography , medical
geography,medical.definition: Medical geography is the area of medicine concerned with the effects on health and disease due to geographic factors such as climate, environmental conditions, and geographic location.

tcelltranscriptionfactor1.name: t cell transcription factor 1
tcelltranscriptionfactor1.definition: T cell transcription factor 1 is a tcf transcription factor that was originally identified as a DNA-binding protein that interacts with the enhancers of t-cell receptor alpha genes. It plays a role in t-lymphocyte development.

openbite.name: open bite
openbite.definition: Open bite is a condition in which certain opposing teeth fail to establish occlusal contact when the jaws are closed.

glycerolkinase.name: glycerol kinase
glycerolkinase.definition: Glycerol kinase is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of glycerol 3-phosphate from atp and glycerol. Dihydroxyacetone and L-glyceraldehyde can also act as acceptors; utp and, in the case of the yeast enzyme, itp and gtp can act as donors. It provides a way for glycerol derived from fats or glycerides to enter the glycolytic pathway. ec 2.7.1.30.

evokedpotentials.name: evoked potentials
evokedpotentials.definition: Evoked potentials is electrical responses recorded from nerve, muscle, sensory receptor, or area of the central nervous system following stimulation. They range from less than a microvolt to several microvolts. The evoked potential can be auditory (evoked potentials, auditory), somatosensory (evoked potentials, somatosensory), [MASK], visual), or motor (evoked potentials, motor), or other modalities that have been reported.

thorax.name: thorax
thorax.definition: Thorax is the upper part of the trunk between the [MASK] and the abdomen. It contains the chief organs of the circulatory and respiratory systems. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

digitalrectalexamination.name: digital rectal examination
digitalrectalexamination.definition: Digital rectal examination is a physical examination in which the qualified health care worker inserts a lubricated, gloved finger of one hand into the rectum and may use the other hand to press on the lower abdomen or pelvic area to palpate for abnormalities in the lower rectum, and nearby organs or tissues. The method is commonly used to check the lower rectum, the prostate gland in men, and the uterus and ovaries in women.

manipulation,spinal.name: manipulation , spinal
manipulation,spinal.definition: Spinal manipulation is [MASK] and manipulation of the vertebral column.

bangladesh.name: bangladesh
bangladesh.definition: Bangladesh is a country in Southern Asia, bordering the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and India. The capital is Dhaka.

extracellularmatrix.name: extracellular matrix
extracellularmatrix.definition: Extracellular matrix is a meshwork-like substance found within the extracellular space and in association with the basement membrane of the cell surface. It promotes cellular proliferation and provides a supporting structure to which cells or cell lysates in culture dishes adhere.

cerebralventricleneoplasms.name: cerebral ventricle neoplasms
cerebralventricleneoplasms.definition: Cerebral ventricle neoplasms is neoplasms located in the brain ventricles, including the two lateral, the third, and the fourth ventricle. Ventricular tumors may be primary (e.g., choroid plexus neoplasms and glioma, subependymal), metastasize from distant organs, or occur as extensions of locally invasive tumors from adjacent brain structures.

equipmentandsupplies.name: equipment and supplies
equipmentandsupplies.definition: Equipment and supplies is expendable and nonexpendable equipment, supplies, apparatus, and instruments that are used in diagnostic, surgical, therapeutic, scientific, and experimental procedures.

fattyacidsynthase,typeii.name: fatty acid synthase , type ii
fattyacidsynthase,typeii.definition: Type ii fatty acid synthase is the form of fatty acid synthase complex found in bacteria; fungi; and plants. Catalytic steps are like the animal form but the protein structure is different with dissociated enzymes encoded by separate genes. It is a target of some anti-infective agents which result in disruption of the cell membrane and cell wall.

patientcaremanagement.name: patient care management
patientcaremanagement.definition: Patient care management is generating, planning, organizing, and administering medical and nursing care and services for patients.

syphilis,cardiovascular.name: syphilis , cardiovascular
syphilis,cardiovascular.definition: Cardiovascular syphilis is cardiovascular manifestations of syphilis, an infection of treponema pallidum. In the late stage of syphilis, sometimes 20-30 years after the initial infection, damages are often seen in the blood vessels including the aorta and the aortic valve. Clinical signs include syphilitic aortitis, aortic insufficiency, or aortic aneurysm.

sarcoma,smallcell.name: sarcoma , small cell
sarcoma,smallcell.definition: Small cell sarcoma is a sarcoma characterized by the presence of small cells, cells measuring 9-14 micrometers with a faint or indistinct rim of cytoplasm and an oval-to-elongated nucleus with relatively dense chromatin. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

fetalgrowthretardation.name: fetal growth retardation
fetalgrowthretardation.definition: Fetal growth retardation is failure of a fetus to attain expected growth.

administrativeclaims,healthcare.name: administrative claims , healthcare
administrativeclaims,healthcare.definition: Healthcare administrative claims is information relating to itemized coding of procedures and costs associated with healthcare delivery, used as a means for tracking healthcare utilization, patterns of care, and treatment outcomes.

communicationaidsfordisabled.name: communication aids for disabled
communicationaidsfordisabled.definition: Communication aids for disabled is equipment that provides mentally or physically disabled persons with a means of communication. The aids include display boards, typewriters, cathode ray tubes, computers, and [MASK] synthesizers. The output of such aids includes written words, artificial [MASK], language signs, Morse code, and pictures.

metabolicclearancerate.name: metabolic clearance rate
metabolicclearancerate.definition: Metabolic clearance rate is volume of biological fluid completely cleared of drug metabolites as measured in unit time. Elimination occurs as a result of metabolic processes in the kidney, liver, saliva, sweat, intestine, heart, brain, or other site.

southcarolina.name: south carolina
southcarolina.definition: South carolina is state bounded on the north by North Carolina, on the east and south by the Atlantic Ocean, and on the west by Georgia.

chemicalviewedfunctionally.name: chemical viewed functionally
chemicalviewedfunctionally.definition: Chemical viewed functionally is chemical viewed functionally

lensdiseases.name: lens diseases
lensdiseases.definition: Lens diseases is diseases involving the crystalline lens.

advertisement.name: advertisement
advertisement.definition: Advertisement is work consisting of publicly distributed notices, usually as paid announcements in mass media such as newspapers, magazines, or on billboards. They include those in motion picture, television [MASK], radio, or electronic media.

reproductivehealthservices.name: reproductive health services
reproductivehealthservices.definition: Reproductive health services is health care services related to human reproduction and diseases of the reproductive system. Services are provided to both sexes and usually by physicians in the medical or the surgical specialties such as reproductive medicine; andrology; [MASK]; obstetrics; and perinatology.

vesicularacetylcholinetransportproteins.name: vesicular acetylcholine transport proteins
vesicularacetylcholinetransportproteins.definition: Vesicular acetylcholine transport proteins is vesicular amine transporter proteins that transport the neurotransmitter acetylcholine into small [MASK]. Proteins of this family contain 12 transmembrane domains and exchange vesicular protons for cytoplasmic acetylcholine.

treatmentfailure.name: treatment failure
treatmentfailure.definition: Treatment failure is a measure of the quality of health care by assessment of unsuccessful results of management and procedures used in combating disease, in individual cases or series.

lateralmedullarysyndrome.name: lateral medullary syndrome
lateralmedullarysyndrome.definition: Lateral medullary syndrome is infarction of the dorsolateral aspect of medulla oblongata in the brain stem. It is caused by occlusion of the vertebral artery and/or the posterior inferior cerebellar artery. Clinical manifestations vary with the size of infarction, but may include loss of pain and temperature sensation in the ipsilateral face and contralateral body below the [MASK]; ipsilateral horner syndrome; ipsilateral ataxia; dysarthria; vertigo; nausea, hiccup; dysphagia; and vocal cord paralysis. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p801)

siblingrelations.name: sibling relations
siblingrelations.definition: Sibling relations is interactions and relationships between sisters and/or brothers. The concept also applies to animal studies.

epilepsy,frontallobe.name: epilepsy , frontal lobe
epilepsy,frontallobe.definition: Frontal lobe epilepsy is a localization-related (focal) form of epilepsy characterized by seizures which arise in the frontal lobe.

emotionalintelligence.name: emotional intelligence
emotionalintelligence.definition: Emotional intelligence is the ability to understand and manage emotions and to use emotional knowledge to enhance thought and deal effectively with tasks. Components of emotional intelligence include [MASK], self-motivation, self-awareness, self-regulation, and social skill. Emotional intelligence is a measurement of one's ability to socialize or relate to others.

antigens.name: antigens
antigens.definition: Antigens is substances that are recognized by the immune system and induce an immune reaction.

civildefense.name: civil defense
civildefense.definition: Civil defense is preventive emergency measures and programs designed to protect the individual or community in times of hostile attack.

animation.name: animation
animation.definition: Animation is a film or video wholly or partially created by photographing drawings, sculptures, or other inanimate things in sequence to create the illusion of motion. Animations are also generated by computers. (From Moving Image Materials: Genre Terms, 1988)

cerebellarataxia.name: cerebellar ataxia
cerebellarataxia.definition: Cerebellar ataxia is incoordination of voluntary movements that occur as a manifestation of cerebellar diseases. Characteristic features include a tendency for limb movements to overshoot or undershoot a target (dysmetria), a tremor that occurs during attempted movements (intention tremor), impaired force and rhythm of diadochokinesis (rapidly alternating movements), and [MASK]. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p90)

bonediseases,endocrine.name: bone diseases , endocrine
bonediseases,endocrine.definition: Endocrine bone diseases is diseases of the bones related to hyperfunction or hypofunction of the endocrine glands.

fattyacids,unsaturated.name: fatty acids , unsaturated
fattyacids,unsaturated.definition: Unsaturated fatty acids is fatty acids in which the carbon chain contains one or more double or triple carbon-carbon bonds.

electrontransportcomplexi.name: electron transport complex i
electrontransportcomplexi.definition: [MASK] transport complex i is a flavoprotein and iron sulfur-containing oxidoreductase complex that catalyzes the conversion of ubiquinone to ubiquinol. In mitochondria the complex also couples its reaction to the transport of protons across the internal [MASK]. The nadh dehydrogenase component of the complex can be isolated and is listed as ec 1.6.99.3.

mammaryarteries.name: mammary arteries
mammaryarteries.definition: Mammary arteries is arteries originating from the subclavian or axillary arteries and distributing to the anterior thoracic wall, mediastinal structures, diaphragm, pectoral muscles and mammary gland.

membranetransportmodulators.name: membrane transport modulators
membranetransportmodulators.definition: Membrane transport modulators is agents that affect ion pumps; ion channels; abc transporters; and other membrane transport proteins.

adolescent.name: adolescent
adolescent.definition: Adolescent is a person 13 to 18 years of age.

philosophy,medical.name: philosophy , medical
philosophy,medical.definition: Medical philosophy is the underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of medicine.

urinarytractphysiologicalphenomena.name: urinary tract physiological phenomena
urinarytractphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Urinary tract physiological phenomena is properties, functions, and processes of the urinary tract as a whole or of any of its parts.

mathematicalconcepts.name: mathematical concepts
mathematicalconcepts.definition: Mathematical concepts is numeric or quantitative entities, descriptions, properties, relationships, operations, and events.

statemedicine.name: state medicine
statemedicine.definition: State medicine is a system of medical care regulated, controlled and financed by the government, in which the government assumes responsibility for the health needs of the population.

carboncompounds,inorganic.name: carbon compounds , inorganic
carboncompounds,inorganic.definition: Inorganic carbon compounds is inorganic compounds that contain carbon as an integral part of the molecule but are not derived from hydrocarbons.

ethics,clinical.name: ethics , clinical
ethics,clinical.definition: Clinical ethics is the identification, analysis, and resolution of moral problems that arise in the care of patients. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

preliminarydata.name: preliminary data
preliminarydata.definition: Preliminary data is first-released version of study results in a series of data collection efforts used for the purpose of generating further interest in and or funding of a research study.

silk.name: silk
silk.definition: Silk is a continuous protein fiber consisting primarily of fibroins. It is synthesized by a variety of insects and arachnids.

follicularfluid.name: follicular fluid
follicularfluid.definition: Follicular fluid is the fluid surrounding the ovum and granulosa cells in the Graafian follicle (ovarian follicle). The follicular fluid contains [MASK] steroids, glycoprotein hormones, plasma proteins, mucopolysaccharides, and enzymes.

nursing,privateduty.name: nursing , private duty
nursing,privateduty.definition: Private duty nursing is the practice of nursing by a registered or licensed nurse to care for a specific patient in a health facility or in the home.

renalplasmaflow,effective.name: renal plasma flow , effective
renalplasmaflow,effective.definition: Effective renal plasma flow is the amount of plasma flowing to the parts of the kidney that function in the production of urine. It is the amount of plasma perfusing the kidney tubules per unit time, generally measured by p-aminohippurate clearance. It should be differentiated from renal plasma flow which is approximately 10% greater than the effective renal plasma flow.

bibliography.name: bibliography
bibliography.definition: Bibliography is a work consisting of a list of books, articles, documents, publications, and other items, usually on a single subject or related subjects.

electrophoresis,disc.name: electrophoresis , disc
electrophoresis,disc.definition: Disc electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which discontinuities in both the voltage and pH gradients are introduced by using [MASK] of different composition and pH in the different parts of the gel column. The term 'disc' was originally used as an abbreviation for 'discontinuous' referring to the [MASK] employed, and does not have anything to do with the shape of the separated zones.

expressionofconcern.name: expression of concern
expressionofconcern.definition: Expression of concern is a notification about the integrity of a published article that is typically written by an editor and should be labelled prominently in the item title. It is the responsibility of the editor to initiate appropriate investigative procedures, discover the outcome of the investigation, and notify readers of that outcome in a subsequent published item. The outcome may require the publication of a retraction notice.

dnapolymeraseii.name: dna polymerase ii
dnapolymeraseii.definition: Dna polymerase ii is a DNA-dependent dna polymerase characterized in e. coli and other lower organisms. It may be present in higher organisms and has an intrinsic molecular activity only 5% of that of dna Polymerase i. This polymerase has 3'-5' exonuclease activity, is effective only on duplex dna with gaps or single-strand ends of less than 100 nucleotides as template, and is inhibited by sulfhydryl reagents.

aldehydedehydrogenase.name: aldehyde dehydrogenase
aldehydedehydrogenase.definition: Aldehyde dehydrogenase is an enzyme that oxidizes an aldehyde in the presence of nad+ and water to an acid and nadh. This enzyme was formerly classified as ec 1.1.1.70.

biology.name: biology
biology.definition: Biology is one of the biological science disciplines concerned with the origin, structure, development, growth, function, genetics, and reproduction of animals, plants, and microorganisms.

parenteralnutrition,hometotal.name: parenteral nutrition , home total
parenteralnutrition,hometotal.definition: Home total parenteral nutrition is the at-home administering of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient whose sole source of nutrients is via solutions administered intravenously, subcutaneously or by some other non-alimentary route.

mediatorcomplex.name: mediator complex
mediatorcomplex.definition: Mediator complex is a large protein complex which acts as a signaling adaptor protein that allows communication between the various regulatory and functional components of genetic transcription including dna polymerase ii; general transcription factors; and transcription factors that are bound to upstream enhancer elements. The mediator complex was originally studied in yeast where at least 21 subunits were identified. Many of the yeast subunits are homologs to proteins in higher organisms that are found associated with specific nuclear receptors such as thyroid hormone receptors and vitamin d receptors.

sensitivityandspecificity.name: sensitivity and specificity
sensitivityandspecificity.definition: Sensitivity and specificity is binary classification measures to assess test results. Sensitivity or recall rate is the proportion of true positives. Specificity is the probability of correctly determining the absence of a condition. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

malnutrition.name: malnutrition
malnutrition.definition: Malnutrition is an imbalanced [MASK] resulting from insufficient intake of nutrients to meet normal physiological requirement.

bacterialproteins.name: bacterial proteins
bacterialproteins.definition: Bacterial proteins is proteins found in any species of bacterium.

education,medical.name: education , medical
education,medical.definition: Medical education is use for general articles concerning medical education.

reticulum.name: reticulum
reticulum.definition: Reticulum is the second stomach of ruminants. It lies almost in the midline in the front of the abdomen, in contact with the liver and diaphragm and communicates freely with the rumen via the ruminoreticular orifice. The lining of the reticulum is raised into folds forming a honeycomb pattern over the surface. (From Concise Veterinary Dictionary, 1988)

lactosefactors.name: lactose factors
lactosefactors.definition: Lactose factors is plasmids which determine the ability of a bacterium to ferment lactose.

naturalsprings.name: natural springs
naturalsprings.definition: Natural springs is water that emerges to the surface of the earth from underground.

visiondisorders.name: vision disorders
visiondisorders.definition: Vision disorders is visual impairments limiting one or more of the basic functions of the eye: visual acuity, dark adaptation, [MASK] vision, or peripheral vision. These may result from eye diseases; optic nerve diseases; visual pathway diseases; occipital lobe diseases; ocular motility disorders; and other conditions (From Newell, Ophthalmology: Principles and Concepts, 7th ed, p132).

coloradotickfevervirus.name: colorado tick fever virus
coloradotickfevervirus.definition: Colorado tick fever virus is a species of coltivirus transmitted by the tick dermacentor andersonii and causing fever, chills, aching head and limbs, and often vomiting. It occurs in the northwestern United States, except the Pacific Coast.

regenerativemedicine.name: regenerative medicine
regenerativemedicine.definition: Regenerative medicine is a field of medicine concerned with developing and using strategies aimed at repair or replacement of damaged, diseased, or metabolically deficient organs, tissues, and cells via tissue engineering; cell transplantation; and artificial organs and bioartificial organs and tissues.

dentaldevices,homecare.name: dental devices , home care
dentaldevices,homecare.definition: Home care dental devices is devices used in the home by persons to maintain dental and periodontal health. The devices include toothbrushes, dental flosses, water irrigators, gingival stimulators, etc.

enhancedrecoveryaftersurgery.name: enhanced recovery after surgery
enhancedrecoveryaftersurgery.definition: Enhanced recovery after surgery is a protocol of components related to preadmission, preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative care. The protocol is implemented with the goal of improving patient recovery, facilitating earlier discharge from the hospital, and potentially reducing health care costs without increasing complications or hospital readmissions. The protocol components may contribute to minimizing, and/or improving the response to, physiological stress associated with surgery.

secondharmonicgenerationmicroscopy.name: second harmonic generation microscopy
secondharmonicgenerationmicroscopy.definition: Second harmonic generation microscopy is a microscopic imaging technique that takes advantage of the process of harmonic generation that occurs when [MASK] interact to generate new [MASK] of a different wavelength. In second harmonic generation, two [MASK] of the same wavelength and frequency, such as from a laser, interact inside a medium and are converted to a photon of twice the frequency and half of the wavelength of the two incident [MASK]. The light signals captured are used to produce images that are dependent on the unique optical properties of the material.

healthcarereform.name: health care reform
healthcarereform.definition: Health care reform is innovation and improvement of the health care system by reappraisal, amendment of services, and removal of faults and abuses in providing and distributing health services to patients. It includes a re-alignment of health services and health insurance to maximum demographic elements (the unemployed, indigent, uninsured, elderly, inner cities, rural areas) with reference to coverage, hospitalization, pricing and cost containment, insurers' and employers' costs, pre-existing medical conditions, prescribed drugs, equipment, and services.

eardiseases.name: ear diseases
eardiseases.definition: Ear diseases is pathological processes of the ear, the hearing, and the equilibrium system of the body.

reactiveattachmentdisorder.name: reactive attachment disorder
reactiveattachmentdisorder.definition: Reactive attachment disorder is markedly disturbed and developmentally inappropriate social relatedness that begins before age 5 and is associated with grossly pathological child care. The child may persistently fail to initiate and respond to social interactions in a developmentally appropriate way (inhibited type) or there may be a pattern of diffuse attachments with nondiscriminate sociability (disinhibited type). (From [MASK])

proactiveinhibition.name: proactive inhibition
proactiveinhibition.definition: Proactive inhibition is the state or process hypothesized to account for poorer learning rate for elements later in a series as compared to the learning rate for elements coming earlier in a series.

folatereceptor2.name: folate receptor 2
folatereceptor2.definition: Folate receptor 2 is a subtype of GPI-anchored folate receptors that is expressed in placenta and hematopoietic cells.

hivprotease.name: hiv protease
hivprotease.definition: Hiv protease is enzyme of the human immunodeficiency virus that is required for post-translational cleavage of gag and gag-pol precursor polyproteins into functional products needed for viral assembly. hiv protease is an aspartic protease encoded by the amino terminus of the [MASK].

nadphoxidase2.name: nadph oxidase 2
nadphoxidase2.definition: Nadph oxidase 2 is an nadph oxidase that is expressed by phagocytes where it transfers [MASK] across the plasma membrane from cytosolic nadph to molecular oxygen on the exterior. It regulates proton (h+) flux into resting phagocytes to control intracellular pH. Mutations in the cybb gene are associated with x-linked chronic granulomatous disease.

scattering,radiation.name: scattering , radiation
scattering,radiation.definition: Radiation scattering is the diversion of radiation (thermal, electromagnetic, or nuclear) from its original path as a result of interactions or collisions with atoms, molecules, or larger particles in the atmosphere or other media. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

plasmaexchange.name: plasma exchange
plasmaexchange.definition: Plasma exchange is removal of plasma and replacement with various fluids, e.g., fresh frozen plasma, plasma protein fractions (ppf), albumin preparations, dextran solutions, saline. Used in treatment of autoimmune diseases, immune complex diseases, diseases of excess plasma factors, and other conditions.

schizophreniaspectrumandotherpsychoticdi.name: schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders
schizophreniaspectrumandotherpsychoticdi.definition: Schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders is marked disorders of thought (delusions, hallucinations, or other thought disorder accompanied by disordered affect or behavior), and deterioration from a previous level of functioning. Individuals have one o more of the following symptoms: delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized [MASK]. (from dsm-5)

circulatingtumordna.name: circulating tumor dna
circulatingtumordna.definition: Circulating tumor dna is dna released from tumor cells that is found circulating in plasma; serum; or other body fluids.

diseaseprogression.name: disease progression
diseaseprogression.definition: Disease progression is the worsening of a disease over time. This concept is most often used for chronic and incurable diseases where the stage of the disease is an important determinant of therapy and prognosis.

populationdensity.name: population density
populationdensity.definition: Population density is number of individuals in a population relative to space.

fibroblastgrowthfactor4.name: fibroblast growth factor 4
fibroblastgrowthfactor4.definition: Fibroblast growth factor 4 is a heparin binding fibroblast growth factor that may play a role in limb buds development.

signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculeas.name: signaling lymphocytic activation molecule associated protein
signalinglymphocyticactivationmoleculeas.definition: Signaling lymphocytic activation molecule associated protein is a signal transducing adaptor protein that contains a single sh2 domain and is essential for the regulation of slam family receptors in the immune response. Mutations in the SLAM-associated protein gene have been identified in cases of x-linked lymphoproliferative disease.

ciliaryarteries.name: ciliary arteries
ciliaryarteries.definition: Ciliary arteries is three groups of arteries found in the eye which supply the iris, pupil, sclera, conjunctiva, and the muscles of the iris.

retentionincare.name: retention in care
retentionincare.definition: Retention in care is patient's regular engagement with medical care after initial entry into the system.

hospitals,religious.name: hospitals , religious
hospitals,religious.definition: Religious hospitals is private hospitals that are owned or sponsored by religious organizations.

diagnostictechniques,surgical.name: diagnostic techniques , surgical
diagnostictechniques,surgical.definition: Surgical diagnostic techniques is methods and procedures for the diagnosis of disease or dysfunction by examination of the pathological site or operative field during surgical intervention.

cardiaccatheters.name: cardiac catheters
cardiaccatheters.definition: Cardiac catheters is catheters inserted into various locations within the heart for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes.

tongue.name: tongue
tongue.definition: Tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth that is covered with pink tissue called mucosa, tiny bumps called papillae, and thousands of taste buds. The tongue is anchored to the mouth and is vital for chewing, swallowing, and for [MASK].

maternalwelfare.name: maternal welfare
maternalwelfare.definition: Maternal welfare is organized efforts by communities or organizations to improve the health and well-being of the mother.

students,healthoccupations.name: students , health occupations
students,healthoccupations.definition: Health occupations students is individuals enrolled in a school or formal educational program in the health occupations.

serumalbumin,bovine.name: serum albumin , bovine
serumalbumin,bovine.definition: Bovine serum albumin is serum albumin from cows, commonly used in in vitro biological studies. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

acidsensingionchannels.name: acid sensing ion channels
acidsensingionchannels.definition: Acid sensing ion channels is a family of proton-gated sodium channels that are primarily expressed in neuronal tissue. They are AMILORIDE-sensitive and are involved in the signaling of a variety of neurological stimuli, most notably that of pain in response to acidic conditions.

centralnervoussystemneoplasms.name: central nervous system neoplasms
centralnervoussystemneoplasms.definition: Central nervous system neoplasms is benign and malignant neoplastic processes that arise from or secondarily involve the brain, spinal cord, or meninges.

obstetriclabor,premature.name: obstetric labor , premature
obstetriclabor,premature.definition: Premature obstetric labor is onset of obstetric labor before term (term birth) but usually after the fetus has become viable. In humans, it occurs sometime during the 29th through 38th week of pregnancy. tocolysis inhibits premature labor and can prevent the birth of premature infants (infant, premature).

bacterialstructures.name: bacterial structures
bacterialstructures.definition: Bacterial structures is the parts of bacteria.

motorskillsdisorders.name: motor skills disorders
motorskillsdisorders.definition: Motor skills disorders is marked impairments in the development of motor coordination such that the impairment interferes with activities of daily living. (From [MASK])

pain.name: pain
pain.definition: Pain is an unpleasant sensation induced by noxious stimuli which are detected by nerve endings of nociceptive neurons.

adenosinekinase.name: adenosine kinase
adenosinekinase.definition: Adenosine kinase is an enzyme that catalyzes the formation of adp plus amp from adenosine plus atp. It can serve as a salvage mechanism for returning adenosine to nucleic acids. ec 2.7.1.20.

uterinemonitoring.name: uterine monitoring
uterinemonitoring.definition: Uterine monitoring is measurement or recording of contraction activity of the uterine muscle. It is used to determine progress of labor, obstetric and assess status of pregnancy. It is also used in conjunction with [MASK] to determine fetal response to stress of maternal [MASK].

dualspecificityphosphatase1.name: dual specificity phosphatase 1
dualspecificityphosphatase1.definition: Dual specificity phosphatase 1 is a dual specificity phosphatase subtype that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction by inactivating mitogen-activated protein kinases. It has specificity for p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases and jnk mitogen-activated protein kinases.

parkinsondiseaseassociatedproteins.name: parkinson disease associated proteins
parkinsondiseaseassociatedproteins.definition: Parkinson disease associated proteins is proteins associated with sporadic or familial cases of parkinson disease.

adversedrugreactionreportingsystems.name: adverse drug reaction reporting systems
adversedrugreactionreportingsystems.definition: Adverse drug reaction reporting systems is systems developed for collecting reports from government agencies, manufacturers, hospitals, physicians, and other sources on adverse drug reactions.

axonguidance.name: axon guidance
axonguidance.definition: Axon guidance is the mechanism by which a neuronal process outgrows toward a target led by the growth cone. Local guidance cues are provided by cell surface proteins that act on the growing axon.

medicationtherapymanagement.name: medication therapy management
medicationtherapymanagement.definition: Medication therapy management is assistance in managing and monitoring drug therapy for patients receiving treatment for cancer or chronic conditions such as asthma and diabetes, consulting with patients and their families on the proper use of medication; conducting wellness and disease prevention programs to improve public health; overseeing medication use in a variety of settings.

opticatrophy,hereditary,leber.name: optic atrophy , hereditary , leber
opticatrophy,hereditary,leber.definition: Leber hereditary optic atrophy is a maternally linked genetic disorder that presents in mid-life as acute or subacute central vision loss leading to central scotoma and blindness. The disease has been associated with missense mutations in the mtDNA, in genes for Complex i, iii, and iv polypeptides, that can act autonomously or in association with each other to cause the disease. (from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Omim/, mim#535000 (April 17, 2001))

delivery,obstetric.name: delivery , obstetric
delivery,obstetric.definition: Obstetric delivery is delivery of the fetus and placenta under the care of an obstetrician or a health worker. Obstetric deliveries may involve physical, psychological, medical, or surgical interventions.

aminoacidtransportsystems.name: amino acid transport systems
aminoacidtransportsystems.definition: Amino acid transport systems is cellular proteins and protein complexes that transport amino acids across biological membranes.

adiposetissue,white.name: adipose tissue , white
adiposetissue,white.definition: [MASK] adipose tissue is fatty tissue composed of [MASK] and generally found directly under the skin (subcutaneous fat) and around the internal organs (abdominal fat). It has less vascularization and less coloration than the [MASK]. [MASK] fat provides heat insulation, mechanical cushion, and source of energy.

peptidechaininitiation,translational.name: peptide chain initiation , translational
peptidechaininitiation,translational.definition: Translational peptide chain initiation is a process of genetic translation whereby the formation of a peptide chain is started. It includes assembly of the ribosome components, the messenger rna coding for the polypeptide to be made, initiator trna, and peptide initiation factors; and placement of the first amino acid in the peptide chain. The details and components of this process are unique for prokaryotic protein biosynthesis and eukaryotic protein biosynthesis.

immunity.name: immunity
immunity.definition: Immunity is nonsusceptibility to the invasive or pathogenic effects of foreign microorganisms or to the toxic effect of antigenic substances.

rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.name: rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor alpha
rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.definition: Rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor alpha is an abundantly-expressed rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that regulates a broad variety of rho gtpases.

leglengthinequality.name: leg length inequality
leglengthinequality.definition: Leg length inequality is a condition in which one of a pair of legs fails to grow as long as the other, which could result from injury or surgery.

tumornecrosisfactorligandsuperfamilymemb.name: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15
tumornecrosisfactorligandsuperfamilymemb.definition: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15 is a member of tumor necrosis factor superfamily found on endothelial cells that plays a role in the inhibition of endothelial cell growth and physiologic angiogenesis.

radiowaves.name: radio waves
radiowaves.definition: Radio waves is electromagnetic waves with frequencies between about 3 kilohertz (very low frequency - vlf) and 300,000 megahertz (extremely high frequency - ehf). They are used in television and radio broadcasting, land and satellite communications systems, radionavigation, radiolocation, and diathermy. The highest frequency radio waves are microwaves.

militaryhygiene.name: military hygiene
militaryhygiene.definition: Military hygiene is science dealing with the maintenance of health in servicemen.

gastricmucosa.name: gastric mucosa
gastricmucosa.definition: Gastric mucosa is lining of the stomach, consisting of an inner epithelium, a middle lamina propria, and an outer muscularis mucosae. The surface cells produce mucus that protects the stomach from attack by digestive acid and enzymes. When the epithelium invaginates into the lamina propria at various region of the stomach (cardia; gastric fundus; and pylorus), different tubular gastric glands are formed. These glands consist of cells that secrete mucus, enzymes, hydrochloric acid, or hormones.

laryngealedema.name: laryngeal edema
laryngealedema.definition: Laryngeal edema is abnormal accumulation of fluid in tissues of any part of the larynx, commonly associated with laryngeal injuries and allergic reactions.

ascites.name: ascites
ascites.definition: Ascites is accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity.

quantumdots.name: quantum dots
quantumdots.definition: Quantum dots is nanometer sized fragments of semiconductor crystalline material which emit [MASK]. The wavelength is based on the quantum confinement size of the dot. They can be embedded in microbeads for high throughput analytical chemistry techniques.

guanine.name: guanine
guanine.definition: Guanine is one of four chemical bases in DNA.

aminoacids,essential.name: amino acids , essential
aminoacids,essential.definition: Essential amino acids is amino acids that are not synthesized by the [MASK] in amounts sufficient to carry out physiological functions. They are obtained from dietary foodstuffs.

fragilexsyndrome.name: fragile x syndrome
fragilexsyndrome.definition: Fragile x syndrome is a condition characterized genotypically by mutation of the distal end of the long [MASK] of the x chromosome (at gene loci fraxa or fraxe) and phenotypically by cognitive impairment, hyperactivity, seizures, language delay, and enlargement of the ears, head, and testes. intellectual disability occurs in nearly all males and roughly 50% of females with the full mutation of fraxa. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p226)

presumedconsent.name: presumed consent
presumedconsent.definition: Presumed consent is an [MASK] of granting authority to health personnel to perform procedures on patients or to remove organs from cadavers for transplantation unless an objection is registered by family members or by the patient prior to death. This also includes emergency care of minors without prior parental consent.

africa,central.name: africa , central
africa,central.definition: Central africa is the geographical area of Africa comprising cameroon; [MASK]; chad; congo; equatorial [MASK]; gabon; and democratic republic of the congo.

borderdiseasevirus.name: border disease virus
borderdiseasevirus.definition: [MASK] virus is a species of pestivirus causing a congenital sheep disease characterized by an abnormally hairy birth-coat, tremors, and poor growth.

eyediseases,hereditary.name: eye diseases , hereditary
eyediseases,hereditary.definition: Hereditary eye diseases is transmission of gene defects or chromosomal aberrations/abnormalities which are expressed in extreme variation in the structure or function of the eye. These may be evident at birth, but may be manifested later with progression of the disorder.

proteinkinasecbeta.name: protein kinase c beta
proteinkinasecbeta.definition: Protein kinase c beta is pkc beta encodes two proteins (pkcb1 and pkcbii) generated by [MASK] of C-terminal exons. It is widely distributed with wide-ranging roles in processes such as B-cell receptor regulation, oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, androgen receptor-dependent transcriptional regulation, insulin signaling, and endothelial cell proliferation.

mouthabnormalities.name: mouth abnormalities
mouthabnormalities.definition: Mouth abnormalities is congenital absence of or defects in structures of the mouth.

immunoglobulinjoiningregion.name: immunoglobulin joining region
immunoglobulinjoiningregion.definition: Immunoglobulin joining region is a segment of the [MASK], encoded by the [MASK] genes in the j segment where, during the maturation of b-lymphocytes; the gene segment for the variable region upstream is joined to a constant region gene segment downstream. The exact position of joining of the two gene segments is variable and contributes to antibody diversity. It is distinguished from the immunoglobulin j chains; a separate polypeptide that serves as a linkage piece in polymeric iga or igm.

adrenalmedulla.name: adrenal medulla
adrenalmedulla.definition: Adrenal medulla is the inner portion of the adrenal gland. Derived from ectoderm, adrenal medulla consists mainly of chromaffin cells that produces and stores a number of neurotransmitters, mainly adrenaline (epinephrine) and norepinephrine. The activity of the adrenal medulla is regulated by the sympathetic nervous system.

pancreatichormones.name: pancreatic hormones
pancreatichormones.definition: Pancreatic hormones is peptide hormones secreted into the blood by cells in the islets of langerhans of the pancreas. The alpha cells secrete glucagon; the beta cells secrete insulin; the delta cells secrete somatostatin; and the pp cells secrete pancreatic polypeptide.

qualityindicators,healthcare.name: quality indicators , health care
qualityindicators,healthcare.definition: Health care quality indicators is norms, criteria, standards, and other direct qualitative and quantitative measures used in determining the quality of health care.

parents.name: parents
parents.definition: Parents is persons functioning as natural, adoptive, or substitute parents. The heading includes the concept of parenthood as well as preparation for becoming a parent.

dentalcalculus.name: dental calculus
dentalcalculus.definition: Dental calculus is abnormal concretion or calcified deposit that forms around the teeth or dental prostheses.

jawrelationrecord.name: jaw relation record
jawrelationrecord.definition: Jaw relation record is a registration of any positional relationship of the mandible in reference to the maxillae. These records may be any of the many vertical, horizontal, or orientation relations. (Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry)

inductionchemotherapy.name: induction chemotherapy
inductionchemotherapy.definition: Induction chemotherapy is initial drug treatment designed to bring about remission induction. It is typically a short-term and high-dose drug treatment that is followed by [MASK] and then [MASK].

nuclearexportsignals.name: nuclear export signals
nuclearexportsignals.definition: Nuclear export signals is specific amino acid sequences present in the primary amino acid sequence of proteins which mediate their export from the cell nucleus. They are rich in hydrophobic residues, such as [MASK] and isoleucine.

receptors,prostaglandin.name: receptors , prostaglandin
receptors,prostaglandin.definition: Prostaglandin receptors is cell surface receptors that bind prostaglandins with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Prostaglandin receptor subtypes have been tentatively named according to their relative affinities for the endogenous prostaglandins. They include those which prefer prostaglandin d2 (dp receptors), prostaglandin e2 (ep1, ep2, and ep3 receptors), prostaglandin F2-alpha (fp receptors), and prostacyclin (ip receptors).

poultryproducts.name: poultry products
poultryproducts.definition: Poultry products is food products manufactured from poultry.

tissueexpansiondevices.name: tissue expansion devices
tissueexpansiondevices.definition: Tissue expansion devices is devices used to generate extra soft tissue in vivo to be used in surgical reconstructions. They exert stretching forces on the tissue and thus stimulate new growth and result in tissue expansion. They are commonly inflatable reservoirs, usually made of silicone, which are implanted under the tissue and gradually inflated. Other tissue expanders exert stretching forces by attaching to outside of the body, for example, vacuum tissue expanders. Once the tissue has grown, the expander is removed and the expanded tissue is used to cover the area being reconstructed.

motorvehicles.name: motor vehicles
motorvehicles.definition: Motor vehicles is automobiles, trucks, buses, or similar engine-driven conveyances. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

lifestyle.name: life style
lifestyle.definition: Life style is typical way of life or manner of living characteristic of an individual or group. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed)

drugs,generic.name: drugs , generic
drugs,generic.definition: Generic drugs is drugs whose drug name is not protected by a trademark. They may be manufactured by several companies.

economics.name: economics
economics.definition: Economics is the science of utilization, distribution, and consumption of services and materials.

genefusion.name: gene fusion
genefusion.definition: Gene fusion is the genetic recombination of the parts of two or more genes resulting in a gene with different or additional regulatory regions, or a new chimeric gene product. oncogene fusion includes an oncogene as at least one of the fusion partners and such gene fusions are often detected in neoplastic cells and are transcribed into [MASK]. artificial gene fusion is carried out in vitro by [MASK] technology.

mandatorytesting.name: mandatory testing
mandatorytesting.definition: Mandatory testing is testing or screening required by federal, state, or local law or other agencies for the diagnosis of specified conditions. It is usually limited to specific populations such as categories of health care providers, members of the military, and prisoners or to specific situations such as premarital examinations or donor screening.

opticalimaging.name: optical imaging
opticalimaging.definition: Optical imaging is the use of light interaction (scattering, absorption, and fluorescence) with biological tissue to obtain morphologically based information. It includes measuring inherent tissue optical properties such as scattering, absorption, and autofluorescence; or optical properties of exogenous targeted fluorescent molecular probes such as those used in optical molecular imaging, or nontargeted optical contrast agents.

selftolerance.name: self tolerance
selftolerance.definition: Self tolerance is the normal lack of the ability to produce an immunological response to autologous (self) antigens. a breakdown of self tolerance leads to autoimmune diseases. The ability to recognize the difference between self and non-self is the prime function of the immune system.

shock,septic.name: shock , septic
shock,septic.definition: Septic shock is sepsis associated with hypotension or hypoperfusion despite adequate fluid resuscitation. Perfusion abnormalities may include, but are not limited to [MASK]; oliguria; or acute alteration in mental status.

treatmentoutcome.name: treatment outcome
treatmentoutcome.definition: Treatment outcome is evaluation undertaken to assess the results or consequences of management and procedures used in combating disease in order to determine the efficacy, effectiveness, safety, and practicability of these interventions in individual cases or series.

professionalrole.name: professional role
professionalrole.definition: Professional role is the expected function of a member of a particular profession.

resveratrol.name: resveratrol
resveratrol.definition: Resveratrol is a stilbene and non-flavonoid polyphenol produced by various plants including grapes and blueberries. It has anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective, anti-mutagenic, and anti-carcinogenic properties. It also inhibits [MASK] and the activity of several dna helicases in vitro.

invertebrates.name: invertebrates
invertebrates.definition: Invertebrates is animals that have no spinal column.

glucosemetabolismdisorders.name: glucose metabolism disorders
glucosemetabolismdisorders.definition: Glucose metabolism disorders is pathological conditions in which the blood glucose cannot be maintained within the normal range, such as in hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia. Etiology of these disorders varies. Plasma glucose concentration is critical to survival for it is the predominant fuel for the central nervous system.

databases,protein.name: databases , protein
databases,protein.definition: Protein databases is databases containing information about proteins such as amino acid sequence; protein conformation; and other properties.

organmotion.name: organ motion
organmotion.definition: Organ motion is movement of internal organs due to physiological processes.

sleepdeprivation.name: sleep deprivation
sleepdeprivation.definition: Sleep deprivation is the state of being deprived of sleep under experimental conditions, due to life events, or from a wide variety of pathophysiologic causes such as medication effect, chronic illness, psychiatric illness, or sleep disorder.

celltransplantation.name: cell transplantation
celltransplantation.definition: Cell transplantation is transference of cells within an individual, between individuals of the same species, or between individuals of different species.

morbidity.name: morbidity
morbidity.definition: Morbidity is the proportion of patients with a particular disease during a given year per given unit of population.

molecularepidemiology.name: molecular epidemiology
molecularepidemiology.definition: Molecular epidemiology is the application of molecular biology to the answering of epidemiological questions. The examination of patterns of changes in dna to implicate particular carcinogens and the use of molecular markers to predict which individuals are at highest risk for a disease are common examples.

populationcharacteristics.name: population characteristics
populationcharacteristics.definition: Population characteristics is qualities and characterization of various types of populations within a social or geographic group, with emphasis on demography, health status, and socioeconomic factors.

wastedisposal,fluid.name: waste disposal , fluid
wastedisposal,fluid.definition: Fluid waste disposal is the discarding or destroying of liquid waste products or their transformation into something useful or innocuous.

tuberculosis,avian.name: tuberculosis , avian
tuberculosis,avian.definition: Avian tuberculosis is a variety of tuberculosis affecting various birds, including [MASK] and ducks. It is caused by mycobacterium avium and characterized by tubercles consisting principally of epithelioid cells.

chemicalprecipitation.name: chemical precipitation
chemicalprecipitation.definition: Chemical precipitation is the formation of a solid in a solution as a result of a chemical reaction or the aggregation of soluble substances into complexes large enough to fall out of solution.

pluripotentstemcells.name: pluripotent stem cells
pluripotentstemcells.definition: Pluripotent stem cells is cells that can give rise to cells of the three different germ layers.

argentina.name: argentina
argentina.definition: Argentina is country located in southern South America, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between [MASK] and Uruguay.

pediatrics.name: pediatrics
pediatrics.definition: Pediatrics is a medical specialty concerned with maintaining health and providing medical care to children from birth to adolescence.

vocalcordparalysis.name: vocal cord paralysis
vocalcordparalysis.definition: Vocal cord paralysis is congenital or acquired paralysis of one or both vocal cords. This condition is caused by defects in the central nervous system, the vagus nerve and branches of laryngeal nerves. Common symptoms are [MASK] including hoarseness or aphonia.

cranialnerveinjuries.name: cranial nerve injuries
cranialnerveinjuries.definition: Cranial nerve injuries is dysfunction of one or more cranial nerves causally related to a traumatic injury. Penetrating and nonpenetrating craniocerebral trauma; [MASK] injuries; and trauma to the facial region are conditions associated with cranial nerve injuries.

fires.name: fires
fires.definition: Fires is combustion or burning in which substances combine chemically with oxygen typically giving out bright light, heat, and smoke.

retrogradedegeneration.name: retrograde degeneration
retrogradedegeneration.definition: Retrograde degeneration is pathologic changes that occur in the axon and cell body of a neuron proximal to an axonal lesion. The process is characterized by central chromatolysis which features flattening and displacement of the nucleus, loss of Nissl bodies, and cellular edema. Central chromatolysis primarily occurs in lower motor neurons.

computercommunicationnetworks.name: computer communication networks
computercommunicationnetworks.definition: Computer communication networks is a system containing any combination of computers, computer terminals, printers, audio or visual display devices, or telephones interconnected by telecommunications equipment or cables: used to transmit or receive information. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

urinarycatheterization.name: urinary catheterization
urinarycatheterization.definition: Urinary catheterization is passage of a catheter into the [MASK] or kidney.

diet,carbohydrateloading.name: diet , carbohydrate loading
diet,carbohydrateloading.definition: Carbohydrate loading diet is a diet rich in dietary carbohydrates.

hospitalinformationsystems.name: hospital information systems
hospitalinformationsystems.definition: Hospital information systems is integrated, computer-assisted systems designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information concerned with the administrative and clinical aspects of providing medical services within the hospital.

chloridechannels.name: chloride channels
chloridechannels.definition: Chloride channels is cell membrane glycoproteins that form channels to selectively pass chloride ions. Nonselective blockers include fenamates; ethacrynic acid; and tamoxifen.

bloodcells.name: blood cells
bloodcells.definition: Blood cells is the cells found in the body fluid circulating throughout the cardiovascular system.

pertussistoxin.name: pertussis toxin
