pertussistoxin.definition: Pertussis toxin is one of the virulence factors produced by bordetella pertussis. It is a multimeric protein composed of five subunits s1 - s5. s1 contains mono ADPribose transferase activity.

chlorine.name: chlorine
chlorine.definition: Chlorine is an element with atomic symbol Cl, atomic number 17, and atomic weight 35, and member of the halogen family.

mammaryneoplasms,animal.name: mammary neoplasms , animal
mammaryneoplasms,animal.definition: Animal mammary neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the mammary gland in animals (mammary glands, animal).

postprandialperiod.name: postprandial period
postprandialperiod.definition: Postprandial period is the time frame after a meal or food intake.

caspase3.name: caspase 3
caspase3.definition: Caspase 3 is a short pro-domain caspase that plays an effector role in apoptosis. It is activated by initiator caspases such as caspase 9. Isoforms of this protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its messenger rna.

toothextraction.name: tooth extraction
toothextraction.definition: Tooth extraction is the surgical removal of a tooth. (Dorland, 28th ed)

semenanalysis.name: semen analysis
semenanalysis.definition: Semen analysis is the quality of semen, an indicator of male fertility, can be determined by semen volume, pH, sperm concentration (sperm count), total sperm number, sperm viability, sperm vigor (sperm motility), normal sperm morphology, acrosome integrity, and the concentration of [MASK] blood cells.

breastfeeding.name: breast feeding
breastfeeding.definition: Breast feeding is the nursing of an infant at the breast.

nucleicacidconformation.name: nucleic acid conformation
nucleicacidconformation.definition: Nucleic acid conformation is the spatial arrangement of the atoms of a nucleic acid or polynucleotide that results in its characteristic 3-dimensional shape.

medicarepaymentadvisorycommission.name: medicare payment advisory commission
medicarepaymentadvisorycommission.definition: Medicare payment advisory commission is the Commission was created by the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 under Title xviii. It is specifically charged to review the effect of Medicare+Choice under Medicare Part c and to review payment policies under Parts a and b. It is also generally charged to evaluate the effect of prospective payment policies and their impact on health care delivery in the us. The former Prospective Payment Assessment Commission (ProPAC) and the [MASK] (pprc) were merged to form medpac.

fingerinjuries.name: finger injuries
fingerinjuries.definition: Finger injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the fingers.

immunereconstitutioninflammatorysyndrome.name: immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
immunereconstitutioninflammatorysyndrome.definition: [MASK] inflammatory syndrome is exuberant inflammatory response towards a previously acquired or undiagnosed [MASK]. It is frequently seen in aids patients following antiretroviral treatment.

vegetableproducts.name: vegetable products
vegetableproducts.definition: Vegetable products is food that is manufactured from various parts of vegetables.

chronicdiseaseindicators.name: chronic disease indicators
chronicdiseaseindicators.definition: Chronic disease indicators is a [MASK] of surveillance indicators of disease developed by [MASK] among the cdc, the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists, and the National Association of Chronic Disease Directors. It enables public health professionals and policymakers to retrieve uniformly defined state and selected metropolitan-level data for chronic diseases and risk factors that impact public health.(https://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/data/index.htm)

chromosomes,plant.name: chromosomes , plant
chromosomes,plant.definition: Plant chromosomes is complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic dna and are part of the cell nucleus of plants.

cellmigrationassays,macrophage.name: cell migration assays , macrophage
cellmigrationassays,macrophage.definition: Macrophage cell migration assays is assays that measure the rate of migration of macrophages. They may involve the use hollow plastic chamber, sealed at one end with a porous membrane and suspended over a larger well which may contain chemotactic factors. The migration of cell through the pores to the other side of the membrane is measured.

nose.name: nose
nose.definition: Nose is a part of the upper respiratory tract. It contains the organ of smell. The term includes the external nose, the nasal cavity, and the paranasal sinuses.

nucleotidemotifs.name: nucleotide motifs
nucleotidemotifs.definition: Nucleotide motifs is commonly observed base sequence or nucleotide structural components which can be represented by a [MASK] sequence or a sequence logo.

activitiesofdailyliving.name: activities of daily living
activitiesofdailyliving.definition: Activities of daily living is the performance of the basic activities of self care, such as dressing, ambulation, or eating.

fractionalflowreserve,myocardial.name: fractional flow reserve , myocardial
fractionalflowreserve,myocardial.definition: Myocardial fractional flow reserve is the ratio of maximum blood flow to the myocardium with coronary stenosis present, to the maximum equivalent blood flow without stenosis. The measurement is commonly used to verify borderline stenosis of coronary arteries.

pulmonaryinfarction.name: pulmonary infarction
pulmonaryinfarction.definition: Pulmonary infarction is necrosis of lung tissue that is cause by the lack of oxygen or blood supply. The most common cause of pulmonary infarction is a blood clot in the lung.

genes,mhcclassi.name: genes , mhc class i
genes,mhcclassi.definition: Mhc class i genes is genetic loci in the vertebrate major histocompatibility complex which encode polymorphic characteristics not related to immune responsiveness or complement activity, e.g., b loci ([MASK]), dla (dog), gpla ([MASK] pig), h-2 (mouse), rt-1 (rat), hla-a, -b, and -c class i genes of man.

histamine.name: histamine
histamine.definition: Histamine is an amine derived by enzymatic decarboxylation of histidine. It is a powerful stimulant of gastric secretion, a constrictor of bronchial smooth muscle, a vasodilator, and also a centrally acting neurotransmitter.

bloodproteindisorders.name: blood protein disorders
bloodproteindisorders.definition: Blood protein disorders is hematologic diseases caused by structural or functional defects of blood proteins.

societies,dental.name: societies , dental
societies,dental.definition: Dental societies is societies whose membership is limited to dentists.

collagentypei.name: collagen type i
collagentypei.definition: Collagen type i is the most common form of fibrillar collagen. It is a major constituent of bone (bone and bones) and skin and consists of a heterotrimer of two alpha1(I) and one alpha2(I) chains.

practicemanagement,dental.name: practice management , dental
practicemanagement,dental.definition: Dental practice management is the organization and operation of the business aspects of a dental practice.

centralnervoussystem.name: central nervous system
centralnervoussystem.definition: Central nervous system is the main information-processing organs of the nervous system, consisting of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges.

chromosomes,human,pair15.name: chromosomes , human , pair 15
chromosomes,human,pair15.definition: Pair 15 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group d chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

clinicalcoding.name: clinical coding
clinicalcoding.definition: Clinical coding is process of substituting a symbol or code for a term such as a diagnosis or procedure. (from Slee's Health Care Terms, 3d ed.)

oralfistula.name: oral fistula
oralfistula.definition: Oral fistula is an abnormal passage within the mouth communicating between two or more anatomical structures.

dna,ancient.name: dna , ancient
dna,ancient.definition: Ancient dna is dna isolated from fossils or other ancient specimens.

molecularmotorproteins.name: molecular motor proteins
molecularmotorproteins.definition: Molecular motor proteins is proteins that are involved in or cause cell movement such as the rotary structures (flagellar motor) or the structures whose movement is directed along cytoskeletal filaments (myosin; kinesin; and dynein motor families).

regeneration.name: regeneration
regeneration.definition: Regeneration is the physiological renewal, repair, or replacement of tissue.

rubberdams.name: rubber dams
rubberdams.definition: Rubber dams is sheets of latex rubber punched and placed over the teeth during dental procedures to isolate the field of operation from the rest of the oral cavity (Jablonski; Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982). Rubber dams are useful in preventing the swallowing of instruments or restorations during dental work.

acthsyndrome,ectopic.name: acth syndrome , ectopic
acthsyndrome,ectopic.definition: Ectopic acth syndrome is symptom complex due to acth production by non-pituitary neoplasms.

rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.name: rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor gamma
rhoguaninenucleotidedissociationinhibito.definition: Rho guanine nucleotide dissociation inhibitor gamma is a rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor subtype that has a unique C-terminal alpha helical membrane-binding domain. It is found bound to cytoplasmic vesicles such as those associated with the golgi apparatus.

nerveexpansion.name: nerve expansion
nerveexpansion.definition: Nerve expansion is procedures that stimulate nerve elongation over a period of time. They are used in repairing nerve tissue.

editorialpolicies.name: editorial policies
editorialpolicies.definition: [MASK] policies is the guidelines and policy statements [MASK] forth by the editor(s) or [MASK] board of a publication.

cerebellarneoplasms.name: cerebellar neoplasms
cerebellarneoplasms.definition: Cerebellar neoplasms is primary or metastatic neoplasms of the cerebellum. Tumors in this location frequently present with ataxia or signs of intracranial hypertension due to obstruction of the fourth ventricle. Common primary cerebellar tumors include fibrillary astrocytoma and cerebellar hemangioblastoma. The cerebellum is a relatively common site for tumor metastases from the lung, breast, and other distant organs. (From Okazaki & Scheithauer, Atlas of Neuropathology, 1988, p86 and p141)

transfusionreaction.name: transfusion reaction
transfusionreaction.definition: Transfusion reaction is complications of blood transfusion. Included adverse reactions are common allergic and febrile reactions; hemolytic (delayed and acute) reactions; and other non-hemolytic adverse reactions such as infections and adverse immune reactions related to immunocompatibility.

carbondisulfide.name: carbon disulfide
carbondisulfide.definition: Carbon disulfide is a colorless, flammable, poisonous liquid, cs2. It is used as a solvent, and is a counterirritant and has local anesthetic properties but is not used as such. It is highly toxic with pronounced cns, hematologic, and dermatologic effects.

patienteducationastopic.name: patient education as topic
patienteducationastopic.definition: Patient education as topic is the teaching or training of patients concerning their own health needs.

pulmonarysurfactants.name: pulmonary surfactants
pulmonarysurfactants.definition: Pulmonary surfactants is substances and drugs that lower the [MASK] of the mucoid layer lining the pulmonary alveoli.

ideaorconcept.name: idea or concept
ideaorconcept.definition: Idea or concept is the mental representational images of some object.

agriculture.name: agriculture
agriculture.definition: Agriculture is the science, art or practice of cultivating soil, producing crops, and raising livestock.

lysine.name: lysine
lysine.definition: Lysine is an essential amino acid. It is often added to [MASK].

neuralinhibition.name: neural inhibition
neuralinhibition.definition: Neural inhibition is the function of opposing or restraining the excitation of neurons or their target excitable cells.

plantphysiologicalphenomena.name: plant physiological phenomena
plantphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Plant physiological phenomena is the physiological processes, properties, and states characteristic of plants.

machinelearning.name: machine learning
machinelearning.definition: Machine learning is a type of artificial intelligence that enable computers to independently initiate and execute learning when exposed to new data.

genes,mos.name: genes , mos
genes,mos.definition: Mos genes is retrovirus-associated dna sequences (mos) originally isolated from the Moloney murine sarcoma virus (Mo-MSV). The proto-oncogene mos (c-mos) codes for a protein which is a member of the serine kinase family. There is no evidence as yet that human c-mos can become transformed or has a role in human cancer. However, in mice, activation can occur when the retrovirus-like intracisternal A-particle inserts itself near the c-mos sequence. The human c-mos gene is located at 8q22 on the long [MASK] of chromosome 8.

anesthesia,inhalation.name: anesthesia , inhalation
anesthesia,inhalation.definition: [MASK] anesthesia is anesthesia caused by the breathing of anesthetic gases or vapors or by insufflating anesthetic gases or vapors into the respiratory tract.

drosophilamelanogaster.name: drosophila melanogaster
drosophilamelanogaster.definition: Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fruit fly frequently used in genetics because of the large size of its chromosomes.

dna,chloroplast.name: dna , chloroplast
dna,chloroplast.definition: Chloroplast dna is deoxyribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of chloroplasts.

industrialwaste.name: industrial waste
industrialwaste.definition: Industrial waste is worthless, damaged, defective, superfluous or effluent material from industrial operations.

reperfusion.name: reperfusion
reperfusion.definition: Reperfusion is restoration of blood supply to tissue which is ischemic due to decrease in normal blood supply. The decrease may result from any source including atherosclerotic obstruction, narrowing of the artery, or surgical clamping. It is primarily a procedure for treating infarction or other ischemia, by enabling viable ischemic tissue to recover, thus limiting further necrosis. However, it is thought that reperfusion can itself further damage the ischemic tissue, causing reperfusion injury.

jaw.name: jaw
jaw.definition: Jaw is bony structure of the mouth that holds the teeth. It consists of the mandible and the maxilla.

mycobacteriuminfections.name: mycobacterium infections
mycobacteriuminfections.definition: Mycobacterium infections is infections with bacteria of the genus mycobacterium.

rna,smallcytoplasmic.name: rna , small cytoplasmic
rna,smallcytoplasmic.definition: Small cytoplasmic rna is small RNAs found in the cytoplasm usually complexed with proteins in scRNPs (ribonucleoproteins, small cytoplasmic).

boneremodeling.name: bone remodeling
boneremodeling.definition: Bone remodeling is the continuous turnover of bone matrix and mineral that involves first an increase in bone resorption (osteoclastic activity) and later, reactive bone formation (osteoblastic activity). The process of bone remodeling takes place in the adult skeleton at discrete foci. The process ensures the mechanical integrity of the skeleton throughout life and plays an important role in calcium homeostasis. An imbalance in the regulation of bone remodeling's two contrasting events, bone resorption and bone formation, results in many of the metabolic bone diseases, such as osteoporosis.

influenzainbirds.name: influenza in birds
influenzainbirds.definition: Influenza in birds is infection of domestic and wild fowl and other birds with influenza a virus. Avian influenza usually does not sicken birds, but can be highly pathogenic and fatal in domestic poultry.

evolution,molecular.name: evolution , molecular
evolution,molecular.definition: Molecular evolution is the process of cumulative change at the level of dna; rna; and proteins, over successive generations.

diabeticcoma.name: diabetic coma
diabeticcoma.definition: Diabetic coma is a state of unconsciousness as a complication of diabetes mellitus. It occurs in cases of extreme hyperglycemia or extreme hypoglycemia as a complication of insulin therapy.

antigens,surface.name: antigens , surface
antigens,surface.definition: Surface antigens is antigens on surfaces of cells, including infectious or foreign cells or viruses. They are usually protein-containing groups on cell membranes or walls and may be isolated.

ventricularfunction,left.name: ventricular function , left
ventricularfunction,left.definition: Left ventricular function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left heart ventricle. Its measurement is an important aspect of the clinical evaluation of patients with heart disease to determine the effects of the disease on cardiac performance.

tonicpupil.name: tonic pupil
tonicpupil.definition: Tonic pupil is a pupillary abnormality characterized by a poor pupillary light reaction, reduced accommodation, iris sector palsies, an enhanced pupillary response to near effort that results in a prolonged, "tonic" constriction, and slow pupillary redilation. This condition is associated with injury to the postganglionic parasympathetic innervation to the pupil. (From Miller et al., Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology, 4th ed, pp492-500)

fundraising.name: fund raising
fundraising.definition: Fund raising is usually organized community efforts to raise money to promote financial programs of institutions. The funds may include individual [MASK].

nucleicacidhybridization.name: nucleic acid hybridization
nucleicacidhybridization.definition: Nucleic acid hybridization is widely used technique which exploits the ability of complementary sequences in single-stranded DNAs or RNAs to pair with each other to form a double helix. Hybridization can take place between two complimentary dna sequences, between a single-stranded dna and a complementary rna, or between two rna sequences. The technique is used to detect and isolate specific sequences, measure homology, or define other characteristics of one or both strands. (Kendrew, Encyclopedia of Molecular Biology, 1994, p503)

tissuedistribution.name: tissue distribution
tissuedistribution.definition: Tissue distribution is accumulation of a drug or chemical substance in various organs (including those not relevant to its pharmacologic or therapeutic action). This distribution depends on the blood flow or perfusion rate of the organ, the ability of the drug to penetrate organ membranes, tissue specificity, protein binding. The distribution is usually expressed as tissue to plasma ratios.

nucleicacidprobes.name: nucleic acid probes
nucleicacidprobes.definition: Nucleic acid probes is nucleic acid which complements a specific mRNA or dna molecule, or fragment thereof; used for hybridization studies in order to identify microorganisms and for genetic studies.

hairanalysis.name: hair analysis
hairanalysis.definition: Hair analysis is examination of hair by chemical, physical, or microscopic means.

resistancetraining.name: resistance training
resistancetraining.definition: Resistance training is a type of strength-building exercise program that requires the body muscle to exert a force against some form of resistance, such as weight, stretch bands, water, or immovable objects. Resistance exercise is a combination of static and dynamic contractions involving shortening and lengthening of skeletal muscles.

adrenalcortexfunctiontests.name: adrenal cortex function tests
adrenalcortexfunctiontests.definition: Adrenal cortex function tests is examinations that evaluate and monitor hormone production in the adrenal cortex.

activity.name: activity
activity.definition: Activity is an event that an agent performs for a purpose, that is guided by the person's intention.

proteinisoforms.name: protein isoforms
proteinisoforms.definition: Protein isoforms is different forms of a protein that may be produced from different genes, or from the same gene by [MASK].

exercisemovementtechniques.name: exercise movement techniques
exercisemovementtechniques.definition: Exercise movement techniques is methods or programs of physical activities which can be used to promote, maintain, or restore the physical and physiological well-being of an individual.

environmentdesign.name: environment design
environmentdesign.definition: Environment design is the structuring of the environment to permit or promote specific patterns of behavior.

chromosomes,human,pair18.name: chromosomes , human , pair 18
chromosomes,human,pair18.definition: Pair 18 human chromosomes is a specific pair of group e chromosomes of the human chromosome classification.

version,fetal.name: version , fetal
version,fetal.definition: Fetal version is the artificial alteration of the fetal position to facilitate birth.

hearingloss.name: hearing loss
hearingloss.definition: Hearing loss is a general term for the complete or partial loss of the ability to hear from one or both ears.

prosthesisdesign.name: prosthesis design
prosthesisdesign.definition: Prosthesis design is the plan and delineation of prostheses in general or a specific prosthesis.

adaptorproteincomplex1.name: adaptor protein complex 1
adaptorproteincomplex1.definition: Adaptor protein complex 1 is a clathrin adaptor protein complex primarily involved in clathrin-related transport at the trans-golgi network.

assistedcirculation.name: assisted circulation
assistedcirculation.definition: Assisted circulation is pumping that aids the natural activity of the heart. (Dorland, 27th ed)

structuralhomology,protein.name: structural homology , protein
structuralhomology,protein.definition: Protein structural homology is the degree of 3-dimensional shape similarity between proteins. It can be an indication of distant amino acid sequence homology and used for rational [MASK].

shoulderfractures.name: shoulder fractures
shoulderfractures.definition: [MASK] fractures is fractures of the proximal humerus, including the head, anatomic and surgical [MASK], and tuberosities.

neoplasms,adiposetissue.name: neoplasms , adipose tissue
neoplasms,adiposetissue.definition: Adipose tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of fatty tissue or connective tissue made up of fat cells in a meshwork of areolar tissue. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in adipose tissue.

digestivesystemandoralphysiologicalpheno.name: digestive system and oral physiological phenomena
digestivesystemandoralphysiologicalpheno.definition: Digestive system and oral physiological phenomena is properties and processes of the digestive system and dentition as a whole or of any of its parts.

hospitals,military.name: hospitals , military
hospitals,military.definition: Military hospitals is hospitals which provide care for the military personnel and usually for their dependents.

benzenederivatives.name: benzene derivatives
benzenederivatives.definition: Benzene derivatives is organic compounds derived from benzene.

acids,acyclic.name: acids , acyclic
acids,acyclic.definition: Acyclic acids is carboxylic acids that have open-chain molecular structures as opposed to ring-shaped structures.

earlywarningscore.name: early warning score
earlywarningscore.definition: Early warning score is tool for bedside evaluation based on five physiological parameters: systolic pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, body temperature and avpu (alert, voice, pain, unresponsive) score.

renaldialysis.name: renal dialysis
renaldialysis.definition: Renal dialysis is therapy for the insufficient cleansing of the blood by the kidneys based on dialysis and including hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and hemodiafiltration.

painmanagement.name: pain management
painmanagement.definition: Pain management is a form of therapy that employs a coordinated and interdisciplinary approach for easing the suffering and improving the [MASK] of those experiencing pain.

medicalwastedisposal.name: medical waste disposal
medicalwastedisposal.definition: Medical waste disposal is management, removal, and elimination of biologic, infectious, pathologic, and [MASK]. The concept includes blood, mucus, tissue removed at surgery or autopsy, soiled surgical dressings, and other materials requiring special control and handling. Disposal may take place where the waste is generated or elsewhere.

limbbuds.name: limb buds
limbbuds.definition: Limb buds is distinct regions of mesenchymal outgrowth at both flanks of an embryo during the somite period. Limb buds, covered by ectoderm, give rise to forelimb, hindlimb, and eventual functional limb structures. Limb bud cultures are used to study cell differentiation; organogenesis; and morphogenesis.

libraryschools.name: library schools
libraryschools.definition: Library schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of library science or information.

norway.name: norway
norway.definition: Norway is a country located in northern Europe, bordering the [MASK] and the Atlantic Ocean, west of Sweden. The capital is Oslo.

salivaryglanddiseases.name: salivary gland diseases
salivaryglanddiseases.definition: Salivary gland diseases is diseases involving the salivary glands.

arthritis.name: arthritis
arthritis.definition: Arthritis is acute or chronic inflammation of joints.

lasercoagulation.name: laser coagulation
lasercoagulation.definition: Laser coagulation is the use of green light-producing lasers to stop bleeding. The green light is selectively absorbed by hemoglobin, thus triggering blood coagulation.

sinusflooraugmentation.name: sinus floor augmentation
sinusflooraugmentation.definition: Sinus floor augmentation is guided bone transplantation of the maxillary sinus surface with a bone substitute grafting. It increases the bone volume at the site of the dental implant and helps stabilize it.

superiorsagittalsinus.name: superior sagittal sinus
superiorsagittalsinus.definition: Superior sagittal sinus is the long large endothelium-lined venous channel on the top outer surface of the brain. It receives blood from a vein in the nasal cavity, runs backwards, and gradually increases in size as blood drains from veins of the brain and the dura mater. Near the lower back of the cranium, the superior sagittal sinus deviates to one side (usually the right) and continues on as one of the transverse sinuses.

facilitiesandservicesutilization.name: facilities and services utilization
facilitiesandservicesutilization.definition: Facilities and services utilization is extent of use of facilities or services. It includes overuse and underuse.

immobilizednucleicacids.name: immobilized nucleic acids
immobilizednucleicacids.definition: Immobilized nucleic acids is dna or rna bound to a substrate thereby having fixed positions.

publichealth.name: public health
publichealth.definition: Public health is branch of medicine concerned with the prevention and control of disease and disability, and the promotion of physical and mental health of the population on the international, national, state, or municipal level.

glycerol.name: glycerol
glycerol.definition: Glycerol is a trihydroxy sugar alcohol that is an intermediate in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism. It is used as a solvent, emollient, pharmaceutical agent, or sweetening agent.

humancharacteristics.name: human characteristics
humancharacteristics.definition: Human characteristics is the fundamental dispositions and traits of humans. (Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

psychiatricrehabilitation.name: psychiatric rehabilitation
psychiatricrehabilitation.definition: Psychiatric rehabilitation is specialty field that promotes recovery, community functioning, and increased well-being of individuals diagnosed with mental disorders that impair their ability to live meaningful lives.

proceduresandtechniquesutilization.name: procedures and techniques utilization
proceduresandtechniquesutilization.definition: Procedures and techniques utilization is extent of use of procedures or techniques. It includes overuse and underuse.

opticalrestrictionmapping.name: optical restriction mapping
opticalrestrictionmapping.definition: Optical restriction mapping is a technique to generate restriction maps from single large dna molecules by spreading the dna onto a glass surface, digesting with dna restriction enzymes, staining with fluorescent dyes, and visualizing the dna cleavage sites by fluorescence microscopy.

latexfixationtests.name: latex fixation tests
latexfixationtests.definition: Latex fixation tests is passive agglutination tests in which antigen is adsorbed onto latex particles which then clump in the presence of antibody specific for the adsorbed antigen. (From Stedman, 26th ed)

ionicliquids.name: ionic liquids
ionicliquids.definition: Ionic liquids is [MASK] that melt below 100 c. Their low volatilization can be an advantage over volatile organic solvents.

africa,eastern.name: africa , eastern
africa,eastern.definition: Eastern africa is the geographical area of Africa comprising burundi, djibouti, eritrea, ethiopia, kenya, rwanda, somalia, south sudan, sudan, [MASK], and uganda.

aminoacids.name: amino acids
aminoacids.definition: Amino acids is organic compounds that generally contain an amino (-nh2) and a carboxyl (-cooh) group. Twenty alpha-amino acids are the subunits which are polymerized to form proteins.

receptors,presynaptic.name: receptors , presynaptic
receptors,presynaptic.definition: Presynaptic receptors is neurotransmitter receptors located on or near presynaptic terminals or varicosities. Presynaptic receptors which bind transmitter molecules released by the terminal itself are termed autoreceptors.

subtractiontechnique.name: subtraction technique
subtractiontechnique.definition: Subtraction technique is combination or superimposition of two images for demonstrating differences between them (e.g., radiograph with contrast vs. one without, radionuclide images using different radionuclides, radiograph vs. radionuclide image) and in the preparation of audiovisual materials (e.g., offsetting identical images, coloring of vessels in angiograms).

intestinalperforation.name: intestinal perforation
intestinalperforation.definition: Intestinal perforation is opening or penetration through the wall of the intestines.

motion.name: motion
motion.definition: Motion is physical motion, i.e., a change in position of a body or subject as a result of an external force. It is distinguished from movement, a process resulting from biological activity.

receptors,opioid.name: receptors , opioid
receptors,opioid.definition: Opioid receptors is cell membrane proteins that bind opioids and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. The endogenous ligands for opioid receptors in mammals include three families of peptides, the enkephalins, endorphins, and dynorphins. The receptor classes include mu, delta, and kappa receptors. Sigma receptors bind several psychoactive substances, including certain opioids, but their endogenous ligands are not known.

sensorydeprivation.name: sensory deprivation
sensorydeprivation.definition: Sensory deprivation is the absence or restriction of the usual external sensory stimuli to which the individual responds.

dentalfacilities.name: dental facilities
dentalfacilities.definition: Dental facilities is use for material on dental facilities in general or for which there is no specific heading.

clinicaldrug.name: clinical drug
clinicaldrug.definition: Clinical drug is a field of medicine that deals primarily with the practice and study of medicine based on the direct examination of the patient.

lifechangeevents.name: life change events
lifechangeevents.definition: Life change events is those occurrences, including social, psychological, and environmental, which require an [MASK] or effect a change in an individual's pattern of living.

pancreas,artificial.name: pancreas , artificial
pancreas,artificial.definition: Artificial pancreas is devices for simulating the activity of the pancreas. They can be either electromechanical, consisting of a glucose sensor, computer, and insulin pump or bioartificial, consisting of isolated islets of Langerhans in an artificial membrane.

hepatitisc.name: hepatitis c
hepatitisc.definition: Hepatitis c is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by hepatitis c virus, a single-stranded rna virus. Its incubation period is 30-90 days. Hepatitis c is transmitted primarily by contaminated blood parenterally, and is often associated with transfusion and intravenous drug abuse. However, in a significant number of cases, the source of hepatitis c infection is unknown.

fetaldevelopment.name: fetal development
fetaldevelopment.definition: Fetal development is morphological and physiological development of fetuses.

rubber.name: rubber
rubber.definition: Rubber is a high-molecular-weight polymeric elastomer derived from the milk juice (latex) of hevea brasiliensis and other trees and plants. It is a substance that can be stretched at room temperature to at least twice its original length and after releasing the stress, retract rapidly, and recover its original dimensions fully.

injections.name: injections
injections.definition: Injections is introduction of substances into the body using a needle and syringe.

cellphysiologicalphenomena.name: cell physiological phenomena
cellphysiologicalphenomena.definition: Cell physiological phenomena is cellular processes, properties, and characteristics.

proteininhibitorsofactivatedstat.name: protein inhibitors of activated stat
proteininhibitorsofactivatedstat.definition: Protein inhibitors of activated stat is a family of structurally related proteins that are constitutively expressed and that negatively regulate cytokine-mediated signal transduction pathways. pias proteins inhibit the activity of signal transducers and activators of transcription.

residencecharacteristics.name: residence characteristics
residencecharacteristics.definition: Residence characteristics is elements of residence that characterize a population. They are applicable in determining need for and utilization of health services.

fattyacidsynthase,typei.name: fatty acid synthase , type i
fattyacidsynthase,typei.definition: Type i fatty acid synthase is animal form of fatty acid synthase which is encoded by a single gene and consists of seven [MASK] and is functional as a homodimer. It is overexpressed in some neoplasms and is a target in humans of some antineoplastic agents and some anti-obesity agents.

typevisecretionsystems.name: type vi secretion systems
typevisecretionsystems.definition: Type vi secretion systems is multiprotein complexes in gram negative bacteria that deliver effector proteins into eukaryotic or prokaryotic cells by a mechanism similar to the contractile tail of bacteriophages. They are composed of a cell envelope-spanning tube which is surrounded by a contractile sheath and tipped by a cell puncturing complex; a base plate structure that anchors the assembly to the cell envelope; and an ATPase involved in the sheath contraction and disassembly of the complex.

unitedstatesfoodanddrugadministration.name: united states food and drug administration
unitedstatesfoodanddrugadministration.definition: United states food and drug administration is an agency of the public health service concerned with the overall planning, promoting, and administering of programs pertaining to maintaining standards of quality of foods, drugs, therapeutic devices, etc.

abdomen.name: abdomen
abdomen.definition: Abdomen is that portion of the body that lies between the thorax and the pelvis.

hepaticinsufficiency.name: hepatic insufficiency
hepaticinsufficiency.definition: Hepatic insufficiency is conditions in which the liver functions fall below the normal ranges. Severe hepatic insufficiency may cause liver failure or death. Treatment may include liver transplantation.

calciummetabolismdisorders.name: calcium metabolism disorders
calciummetabolismdisorders.definition: Calcium metabolism disorders is disorders in the processing of calcium in the body: its absorption, transport, storage, and utilization.

nad.name: nad
nad.definition: Nad is a coenzyme composed of ribosylnicotinamide 5'-diphosphate coupled to adenosine 5'-phosphate by pyrophosphate linkage. It is found widely in nature and is involved in numerous enzymatic reactions in which it serves as an [MASK] carrier by being alternately oxidized (nad+) and reduced (nadh). (Dorland, 27th ed)

fracturehealing.name: fracture healing
fracturehealing.definition: Fracture healing is the physiological restoration of bone tissue and function after a fracture. It includes bony callus formation and normal replacement of bone tissue.

energyintake.name: energy intake
energyintake.definition: Energy intake is total number of calories taken in daily whether ingested or by parenteral routes.

jawdiseases.name: jaw diseases
jawdiseases.definition: Jaw diseases is diseases involving the jaw.

openaccesspublishing.name: open access publishing
openaccesspublishing.definition: Open access publishing is agreement in which author(s) and [MASK] holder(s) grant(s) to all users a free, irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual right of access to, and a license to copy, use, distribute, transmit and display the work publicly and to make and distribute derivative works, in any digital medium for any responsible purpose, subject to proper attribution of authorship, as well as the right to make small numbers of printed copies for their personal use. a complete version of the work and all supplemental materials, including a copy of the permission as stated above, in a suitable standard electronic format is deposited immediately upon initial publication in at least one online repository that is supported by an academic institution, scholarly society, government agency, or other well-established organization that seeks to enable open access, unrestricted distribution, interoperability, and long-term archiving. (from Bethesda Statement on Open Access Publishing)

informationsystems.name: information systems
informationsystems.definition: Information systems is integrated [MASK] of files, procedures, and equipment for the storage, manipulation, and retrieval of information.

immunosorbenttechniques.name: immunosorbent techniques
immunosorbenttechniques.definition: Immunosorbent techniques is techniques for removal by [MASK] and subsequent elution of a specific antibody or antigen using an immunosorbent containing the homologous antigen or antibody.

stromalinteractionmolecule1.name: stromal interaction molecule 1
stromalinteractionmolecule1.definition: Stromal interaction molecule 1 is a stromal interaction molecule that functions in the regulation of calcium influx following depletion of intracellular calcium in the endoplasmic reticulum. It translocates to the plasma membrane upon calcium depletion where it activates the calcium release activated calcium channel orai1.

femurhead.name: femur head
femurhead.definition: Femur head is the hemispheric articular surface at the upper extremity of the [MASK] bone. (Stedman, 26th ed)

technologyassessment,biomedical.name: technology assessment , biomedical
technologyassessment,biomedical.definition: Biomedical technology assessment is evaluation of biomedical technology in relation to cost, efficacy, utilization, etc., and its future impact on social, ethical, and legal systems.

electrontransportcomplexiii.name: electron transport complex iii
electrontransportcomplexiii.definition: [MASK] transport complex iii is a multisubunit enzyme complex that contains cytochrome b group; cytochrome c1; and iron-sulfur centers. It catalyzes the oxidation of ubiquinol to ubiquinone, and transfers the [MASK] to cytochrome c. In mitochondria the redox reaction is coupled to the transport of protons across the [MASK].

waterpollution,radioactive.name: water pollution , radioactive
waterpollution,radioactive.definition: Radioactive water pollution is contamination of water with radioactive materials and/or substances.

haircells,auditory,outer.name: hair cells , auditory , outer
haircells,auditory,outer.definition: Outer auditory hair cells is sensory cells of organ of Corti. In mammals, they are usually arranged in three or four rows, and away from the core of spongy bone (the modiolus), lateral to the [MASK] and other supporting structures. Their cell bodies and stereocilia increase in length from the cochlear base toward the apex and laterally across the rows, allowing differential responses to various frequencies of sound.

clinicallaboratorytechniques.name: clinical laboratory techniques
clinicallaboratorytechniques.definition: Clinical laboratory techniques is techniques used to carry out clinical investigative procedures in the diagnosis and therapy of disease.

correlationofdata.name: correlation of data
correlationofdata.definition: Correlation of data is determination of whether or not two variables are correlated. This means to study whether an increase or decrease in one variable corresponds to an increase or decrease in the other variable.

diabetesmellitus.name: diabetes mellitus
diabetesmellitus.definition: Diabetes mellitus is a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

toothsocket.name: tooth socket
toothsocket.definition: Tooth socket is a hollow part of the alveolar process of the maxilla or mandible where each tooth fits and is attached via the periodontal ligament.

solutecarrierfamily12,member1.name: solute carrier family 12 , member 1
solutecarrierfamily12,member1.definition: Member 1 solute carrier family 12 is na-K-Cl transporter in the ascending limb of loop of henle. It mediates active reabsorption of sodium chloride and is inhibited by loop diuretics such as furosemide; and bumetanide. Mutations in the gene encoding slc12a1 are associated with a bartter syndrome.

hematopoieticstemcells.name: hematopoietic stem cells
hematopoieticstemcells.definition: Hematopoietic stem cells is progenitor cells from which all blood cells derived. They are found primarily in the bone marrow and also in small numbers in the peripheral blood.

dietaryproteins.name: dietary proteins
dietaryproteins.definition: Dietary proteins is proteins obtained from foods. They are the main source of the essential amino acids.

geneduplication.name: gene duplication
geneduplication.definition: Gene duplication is processes occurring in various organisms by which new genes are copied. Gene duplication may result in a multigene family; supergenes or pseudogenes.

transformation,bacterial.name: transformation , bacterial
transformation,bacterial.definition: Bacterial transformation is the heritable modification of the properties of a competent bacterium by naked dna from another source. The uptake of naked dna is a naturally occuring phenomenon in some bacteria. It is often used as a gene transfer technique.

science.name: science
science.definition: Science is the study of natural phenomena by [MASK], measurement, and experimentation.

family.name: family
family.definition: Family is a social group consisting of parents or parent substitutes and children.

kidneypapillarynecrosis.name: kidney papillary necrosis
kidneypapillarynecrosis.definition: Kidney papillary necrosis is a complication of kidney diseases characterized by cell death involving [MASK] in the [MASK]. Damages to this area may hinder the kidney to concentrate urine resulting in polyuria. Sloughed off necrotic tissue may block [MASK] or ureter. Necrosis of multiple renal papillae can lead to kidney failure.

menopause.name: menopause
menopause.definition: Menopause is the last menstrual period. Permanent cessation of menses (menstruation) is usually defined after 6 to 12 months of amenorrhea in a woman over 45 years of age. In the United States, menopause generally occurs in women between 48 and 55 years of age.

equipmentsafety.name: equipment safety
equipmentsafety.definition: Equipment safety is freedom of equipment from actual or potential hazards.

cellsurfaceextensions.name: cell surface extensions
cellsurfaceextensions.definition: Cell surface extensions is specialized structures of the cell that extend the cell membrane and project out from the cell surface.

healthplanningorganizations.name: health planning organizations
healthplanningorganizations.definition: Health planning organizations is organizations involved in all aspects of health planning activities.

solvents.name: solvents
solvents.definition: Solvents is liquids that dissolve other substances (solutes), generally solids, without any change in chemical composition, as, water containing sugar. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

tinnitus.name: tinnitus
tinnitus.definition: Tinnitus is a nonspecific symptom of hearing disorder characterized by the sensation of buzzing, ringing, clicking, pulsations, and other noises in the ear. Objective tinnitus refers to noises generated from within the ear or adjacent structures that can be heard by other individuals. The term subjective tinnitus is used when the sound is audible only to the affected individual. Tinnitus may occur as a manifestation of cochlear diseases; vestibulocochlear nerve diseases; intracranial hypertension; craniocerebral trauma; and other conditions.

sizeperception.name: size perception
sizeperception.definition: Size perception is the sensory interpretation of the dimensions of objects.

primarynursing.name: primary nursing
primarynursing.definition: Primary nursing is the primary responsibility of one nurse for the planning, evaluation, and care of a patient throughout the course of illness, convalescence, and recovery.

massdrugadministration.name: mass drug administration
massdrugadministration.definition: Mass drug administration is administration of a medication to at-risk individuals in a population without individual diagnosis. It is often used in order to treat, control, and/or prevent spread of often [MASK] [MASK] such as neglected diseases in high disease burden areas.

operatingroomnursing.name: operating room nursing
operatingroomnursing.definition: Operating room nursing is the functions of the professional nurse in the operating room.

estradiol.name: estradiol
estradiol.definition: Estradiol is the 17-beta-isomer of estradiol, an aromatized c18 steroid with hydroxyl group at 3-beta- and 17-beta-position. Estradiol-17-beta is the most potent form of mammalian estrogenic steroids.

alzheimervaccines.name: alzheimer vaccines
alzheimervaccines.definition: Alzheimer vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat alzheimer disease.

healthservicesadministration.name: health services administration
healthservicesadministration.definition: Health services administration is the organization and administration of health services dedicated to the delivery of health care.

thyroidhormones.name: thyroid hormones
thyroidhormones.definition: Thyroid hormones is natural hormones secreted by the thyroid gland, such as thyroxine, and their synthetic analogs.

lithiumcompounds.name: lithium compounds
lithiumcompounds.definition: [MASK] compounds is inorganic compounds that contain [MASK] as an integral part of the molecule.

geography.name: geography
geography.definition: Geography is the science dealing with the earth and its life, especially the description of land, sea, and air and the distribution of plant and animal life, including humanity and human industries with reference to the mutual relations of these elements. (From Webster, 3d ed)

thalamus.name: thalamus
thalamus.definition: Thalamus is paired bodies containing mostly gray matter and forming part of the lateral wall of the third ventricle of the brain.

biodiversity.name: biodiversity
biodiversity.definition: Biodiversity is the variety of all native living organisms and their various forms and interrelationships.

abortion,spontaneous.name: abortion , spontaneous
abortion,spontaneous.definition: Spontaneous abortion is expulsion of the product of fertilization before completing the term of gestation and without deliberate interference.

hepatitis,autoimmune.name: hepatitis , autoimmune
hepatitis,autoimmune.definition: Autoimmune hepatitis is a chronic self-perpetuating hepatocellular inflammation of unknown cause, usually with hypergammaglobulinemia and serum autoantibodies.

florida.name: florida
florida.definition: Florida is state bounded on east by the Atlantic Ocean, on the south by the [MASK], on the west by Alabama and on the north by Alabama and Georgia.

waitinglists.name: waiting lists
waitinglists.definition: Waiting lists is prospective patient listings for appointments or treatments.

nucleicaciddenaturation.name: nucleic acid denaturation
nucleicaciddenaturation.definition: Nucleic acid denaturation is disruption of the secondary structure of nucleic acids by heat, extreme pH or chemical treatment. Double strand dna is "melted" by dissociation of the non-covalent hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Denatured dna appears to be a single-stranded flexible structure. The effects of denaturation on rna are similar though less pronounced and largely reversible.

biosyntheticpathways.name: biosynthetic pathways
biosyntheticpathways.definition: Biosynthetic pathways is sets of enzymatic reactions occurring in organisms and that form biochemicals by making new covalent bonds.

plants,geneticallymodified.name: plants , genetically modified
plants,geneticallymodified.definition: Genetically modified plants is plants, or their progeny, whose genome has been altered by genetic engineering.

forecasting.name: forecasting
forecasting.definition: Forecasting is the prediction or [MASK] of the nature of future problems or existing conditions based upon the extrapolation or interpretation of existing scientific data or by the application of scientific methodology.

rna,smallnuclear.name: rna , small nuclear
rna,smallnuclear.definition: Small nuclear rna is short chains of rna (100-300 nucleotides long) that are abundant in the nucleus and usually complexed with proteins in snRNPs (ribonucleoproteins, small nuclear). Many function in the processing of messenger rna precursors. Others, the snoRNAs (rna, small nucleolar), are involved with the processing of [MASK] precursors.

plantimmunity.name: plant immunity
plantimmunity.definition: Plant immunity is the inherent or induced capacity of plants to withstand or ward off biological attack by pathogens.

specialization.name: specialization
specialization.definition: Specialization is an occupation limited in scope to a subsection of a broader field.

abortion,induced.name: abortion , induced
abortion,induced.definition: Induced abortion is intentional removal of a fetus from the uterus by any of a number of techniques. (popline, 1978)

crosses,genetic.name: crosses , genetic
crosses,genetic.definition: Genetic crosses is deliberate breeding of two different individuals that results in offspring that carry part of the genetic material of each parent. The parent organisms must be genetically compatible and may be from different varieties or closely related species.

matrixbands.name: matrix bands
matrixbands.definition: Matrix bands is devices which provide an artificial temporary wall, or matrix, used in filling a prepared cavity.

preoperativeperiod.name: preoperative period
preoperativeperiod.definition: Preoperative period is the period before a surgical operation.

quaternaryprevention.name: quaternary prevention
quaternaryprevention.definition: Quaternary prevention is actions taken to protect individuals (i.e. persons/patients) from unnecessary medical interventions that are likely to cause more harm than good.

hairfollicle.name: hair follicle
hairfollicle.definition: Hair follicle is a tube-like invagination of the epidermis from which the hair shaft develops and into which sebaceous glands open. The hair follicle is lined by a cellular inner and outer root sheath of epidermal origin and is invested with a fibrous sheath derived from the dermis. (Stedman, 26th ed) Follicles of very long hairs extend into the subcutaneous layer of tissue under the skin.

watersupply.name: water supply
watersupply.definition: Water supply is means or process of supplying water (as for a community) usually including reservoirs, tunnels, and pipelines and often the watershed from which the water is ultimately drawn. (Webster, 3d ed)

healthfacilities,proprietary.name: health facilities , proprietary
healthfacilities,proprietary.definition: Proprietary health facilities is health care institutions operated by private groups or corporations for a profit.

growthdisorders.name: growth disorders
growthdisorders.definition: Growth disorders is deviations from the average values for a specific age and [MASK] in any or all of the following: height, weight, skeletal proportions, osseous development, or maturation of features. Included here are both [MASK] and retardation of growth.

saliva.name: saliva
saliva.definition: Saliva is the clear, viscous fluid secreted by the salivary glands and mucous glands of the mouth. It contains mucins, water, organic [MASK], and ptylin.

cellularreprogrammingtechniques.name: cellular reprogramming techniques
cellularreprogrammingtechniques.definition: Cellular reprogramming techniques is procedures used for the induction of cellular reprogramming to change the terminal phenotype of a cell, such as the generation of induced pluripotent stem cells from differentiated adult cells by the forced expression of specific genes.

ticks.name: ticks
ticks.definition: Ticks is blood-sucking acarid parasites of the order Ixodida comprising two families: the softbacked ticks (argasidae) and hardbacked ticks (ixodidae). Ticks are larger than their relatives, the mites. They penetrate the skin of their host by means of highly specialized, hooked mouth parts and feed on its blood. Ticks attack all groups of terrestrial vertebrates. In humans they are responsible for many tick-borne diseases, including the transmission of rocky mountain spotted fever; tularemia; babesiosis; african swine fever; and relapsing fever. (From Barnes, Invertebrate Zoology, 5th ed, pp543-44)

bodyfluids.name: body fluids
bodyfluids.definition: Body fluids is liquid components of living organisms.

restrictionmapping.name: restriction mapping
restrictionmapping.definition: Restriction mapping is use of restriction endonucleases to analyze and generate a physical map of genomes, genes, or other segments of dna.

decisionmaking,shared.name: decision making , shared
decisionmaking,shared.definition: Shared decision making is collaborative process of reaching a decision.

software.name: software
software.definition: Software is sequential operating programs and data which instruct the functioning of a digital computer.

smokers.name: smokers
smokers.definition: Smokers is persons with a history or habit of smoking.

antigens,humanplatelet.name: antigens , human platelet
antigens,humanplatelet.definition: Human platelet antigens is human alloantigens expressed only on platelets, specifically on platelet membrane glycoproteins. These platelet-specific antigens are immunogenic and can result in pathological reactions to transfusion therapy.

invertedrepeatsequences.name: inverted repeat sequences
invertedrepeatsequences.definition: Inverted repeat sequences is copies of nucleic acid sequence that are arranged in opposing orientation. They may lie adjacent to each other (tandem) or be separated by some sequence that is not part of the repeat (hyphenated). They may be true palindromic repeats, i.e. read the same backwards as forward, or complementary which reads as the base complement in the opposite orientation. Complementary inverted repeats have the potential to form hairpin loop or stem-loop structures which results in cruciform structures (such as cruciform dna) when the complementary inverted repeats occur in double stranded regions.

books,illustrated.name: books , illustrated
books,illustrated.definition: Illustrated books is books containing photographs, prints, drawings, portraits, plates, diagrams, facsimiles, maps, [MASK], or other representations or systematic arrangement of data designed to elucidate or decorate its contents. (From The ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p114)

oncogenefusion.name: oncogene fusion
oncogenefusion.definition: Oncogene fusion is the genetic recombination of the parts of two or more genes, including an oncogene as at least one of the fusion partners. Such gene fusions are often detected in neoplastic cells and are transcribed into [MASK].

glucoseclamptechnique.name: glucose clamp technique
glucoseclamptechnique.definition: Glucose clamp technique is maintenance of a constant blood glucose level by perfusion or infusion with glucose or insulin. It is used for the study of metabolic rates (e.g., in glucose, lipid, amino acid metabolism) at constant glucose concentration.

computingmethodologies.name: computing methodologies
computingmethodologies.definition: Computing methodologies is computer-assisted analysis and processing of problems in a particular area.

catalysis.name: catalysis
catalysis.definition: Catalysis is the facilitation of a chemical reaction by material (catalyst) that is not consumed by the reaction.

proteindisulfidereductase(glutathione).name: protein disulfide reductase ( glutathione )
proteindisulfidereductase(glutathione).definition: Protein disulfide reductase (glutathione) is protein disulfide reductase ( glutathione )

neuromuscularblockade.name: neuromuscular blockade
neuromuscularblockade.definition: Neuromuscular blockade is the intentional interruption of transmission at the neuromuscular junction by external agents, usually [MASK]. It is distinguished from nerve block in which [MASK] ([MASK]) is interrupted rather than neuromuscular transmission. Neuromuscular blockade is commonly used to produce muscle relaxation as an adjunct to anesthesia during surgery and other medical procedures. It is also often used as an experimental manipulation in basic research. It is not strictly speaking anesthesia but is grouped here with anesthetic techniques. The failure of neuromuscular transmission as a result of pathological processes is not included here.

receptors,ampa.name: receptors , ampa
receptors,ampa.definition: Ampa receptors is a class of ionotropic [MASK] characterized by their affinity for the agonist ampa (alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid).

psychology,child.name: psychology , child
psychology,child.definition: Child psychology is branch of psychology involving the study of normal and abnormal behavior of children.

bonedensityconservationagents.name: bone density conservation agents
bonedensityconservationagents.definition: [MASK] conservation agents is agents that inhibit bone resorption and/or favor bone mineralization and bone regeneration. They are used to heal bone fractures and to treat metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis.

capillarypermeability.name: capillary permeability
capillarypermeability.definition: Capillary permeability is the property of blood capillary endothelium that allows for the selective exchange of substances between the blood and surrounding tissues and through membranous barriers such as the blood-air barrier; blood-aqueous barrier; blood-brain barrier; blood-nerve barrier; blood-retinal barrier; and blood-testis barrier. Small lipid-soluble molecules such as carbon dioxide and oxygen move freely by diffusion. Water and water-soluble molecules cannot pass through the endothelial walls and are dependent on microscopic pores. These pores show narrow areas (tight junctions) which may limit large molecule movement.

tuberculosis,malegenital.name: tuberculosis , male genital
tuberculosis,malegenital.definition: Male genital tuberculosis is mycobacterium infections of the male reproductive tract (genitalia, male).

uterinerupture.name: uterine rupture
uterinerupture.definition: Uterine rupture is a complete separation or tear in the wall of the uterus with or without expulsion of the fetus. It may be due to injuries, multiple pregnancies, large fetus, previous scarring, or obstruction.

salinesolution.name: saline solution
salinesolution.definition: Saline solution is a crystalloid solution that contains 9.0g of sodium chloride per liter of water. It has a variety of uses, including: as a contact lens solution, in ophthalmic solutions and nasal lavage, in wound irrigation, and for fluid therapy.

opticnerveglioma.name: optic nerve glioma
opticnerveglioma.definition: Optic nerve glioma is glial cell derived tumors arising from the optic nerve, usually presenting in childhood.

afferentloopsyndrome.name: afferent loop syndrome
afferentloopsyndrome.definition: Afferent loop syndrome is a complication of gastrojejunostomy (billroth ii procedure), a reconstructive gastroenterostomy. It is caused by acute (complete) or chronic (intermittent) obstruction of the afferent jejunal loop due to hernia, intussusception, kinking, volvulus, etc. It is characterized by pain and vomiting of [MASK]-stained fluid.

chromosomes,bacterial.name: chromosomes , bacterial
chromosomes,bacterial.definition: Bacterial chromosomes is structures within the nucleus of bacterial cells consisting of or containing dna, which carry genetic information essential to the cell.

transitiontoadultcare.name: transition to adult care
transitiontoadultcare.definition: Transition to adult care is transfer from pediatric to adult care.

signsandsymptoms,respiratory.name: signs and symptoms , respiratory
signsandsymptoms,respiratory.definition: Respiratory signs and symptoms is respiratory system manifestations of diseases of the respiratory tract or of other organs.

microbialsensitivitytests.name: microbial sensitivity tests
microbialsensitivitytests.definition: Microbial sensitivity tests is any tests that demonstrate the relative efficacy of different chemotherapeutic agents against specific microorganisms (i.e., bacteria, fungi, viruses).

animalproteins,dietary.name: animal proteins , dietary
animalproteins,dietary.definition: Dietary animal proteins is dietary proteins derived from animals.

cranialnerveneoplasms.name: cranial nerve neoplasms
cranialnerveneoplasms.definition: Cranial nerve neoplasms is benign and malignant neoplasms that arise from one or more of the twelve cranial nerves.

molecularsequencedata.name: molecular sequence data
molecularsequencedata.definition: Molecular sequence data is descriptions of specific amino acid, carbohydrate, or nucleotide sequences which have appeared in the published literature and/or are deposited in and maintained by databanks such as genbank, European Molecular Biology Laboratory (embl), National Biomedical Research [MASK] (nbrf), or other sequence repositories.

facialbones.name: facial bones
facialbones.definition: Facial bones is the facial skeleton, consisting of bones situated between the cranial base and the mandibular region. While some consider the facial bones to comprise the hyoid (hyoid [MASK] ([MASK]), and zygomatic (zygoma) bones, mandible, and maxilla, others include also the lacrimal and [MASK], inferior nasal concha, and vomer but exclude the hyoid bone. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p113)

hernia.name: hernia
hernia.definition: Hernia is protrusion of tissue, structure, or part of an organ through the bone, muscular tissue, or the membrane by which it is normally contained. Hernia may involve tissues such as the [MASK] or the respiratory diaphragm. Hernias may be internal, external, congenital, or acquired.

saccharomycescerevisiaeproteins.name: saccharomyces cerevisiae proteins
saccharomycescerevisiaeproteins.definition: Saccharomyces cerevisiae proteins is proteins obtained from the species saccharomyces cerevisiae. The function of specific proteins from this organism are the subject of intense scientific interest and have been used to derive basic understanding of the functioning similar proteins in higher eukaryotes.

heartsounds.name: heart sounds
heartsounds.definition: Heart sounds is the sounds heard over the cardiac region produced by the functioning of the heart. There are four distinct sounds: the first occurs at the beginning of systole and is heard as a "lubb" sound; the second is produced by the closing of the aortic valve and pulmonary valve and is heard as a "dupp" sound; the third is produced by vibrations of the ventricular walls when suddenly distended by the rush of blood from the heart atria; and the fourth is produced by atrial contraction and ventricular filling.

eyeprotectivedevices.name: eye protective devices
eyeprotectivedevices.definition: Eye protective devices is personal devices for protection of the eyes from impact, flying objects, glare, liquids, or injurious radiation.

atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyd.name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily d , member 1
atpbindingcassettetransporter,subfamilyd.definition: Member 1 subfamily d atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter that functions in the import of long chain (13-21 carbons) and very long chain fatty acids (> 22 carbons), or their acyl-CoA-derivatives, into peroxisomes. Mutations in the abcd1 gene are associated with the X-linked form of adrenoleukodystrophy.

gbvirusb.name: gb virus b
gbvirusb.definition: Gb virus b is a species of virus (tentatively placed in the genus hepacivirus) in the family flaviviridae, that was recovered from a tamarin monkey, but may have been of human origin. It causes hepatitis in several species of New World monkeys.

organculturetechniques.name: organ culture techniques
organculturetechniques.definition: Organ culture techniques is a technique for maintenance or growth of animal organs in vitro. It refers to three-dimensional cultures of undisaggregated tissue retaining some or all of the histological features of the tissue in vivo. (Freshney, Culture of Animal Cells, 3d ed, p1)

riskevaluationandmitigation.name: risk evaluation and mitigation
riskevaluationandmitigation.definition: Risk evaluation and mitigation is strategies required by the us Food and Drug Administration (fda) Amendments Act of 2007 when a question exists as to whether the benefits of a drug outweigh its risks. These constitute a safety plan with several potential components, including a medication guide, a communication plan, elements to ensure safe use and an implementation system to help guide the prescribers, pharmacists and patients.

inorganicchemical.name: inorganic chemical
inorganicchemical.definition: Inorganic chemical is compounds that do not contain both carbon and hydrogen.

keratinocytes.name: keratinocytes
keratinocytes.definition: Keratinocytes is epidermal cells which synthesize keratin and undergo characteristic changes as they move upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin. Successive stages of differentiation of the keratinocytes forming the epidermal layers are basal cell, spinous or prickle cell, and the granular cell.

dentalcareforchildren.name: dental care for children
dentalcareforchildren.definition: Dental care for children is the giving of attention to the special dental needs of children, including the prevention of tooth diseases and instruction in dental hygiene and dental health. The dental care may include the services provided by dental specialists.

vocabulary,controlled.name: vocabulary , controlled
vocabulary,controlled.definition: Controlled vocabulary is a specified list of terms with a fixed and unalterable meaning, and from which a selection is made when cataloging; abstracting and indexing; or searching books; journals as topic; and other documents. The control is intended to avoid the scattering of related subjects under different headings (subject headings). The list may be altered or extended only by the publisher or issuing agency. (From Harrod's Librarians' Glossary, 7th ed, p163)

potassiumcitrate.name: potassium citrate
potassiumcitrate.definition: Potassium citrate is a powder that dissolves in water, which is administered orally, and is used as a diuretic, expectorant, systemic alkalizer, and electrolyte replenisher.

form.name: form
form.definition: Form is document used for acquiring particular information or for presenting particular information in a prescribed sequence and format, often with blank spaces or lines or other methods to prompt for insertion of the requested information.

hypertension.name: hypertension
hypertension.definition: Hypertension is persistently high systemic arterial blood pressure. Based on multiple readings (blood pressure determination), hypertension is currently defined as when systolic pressure is consistently greater than 140 mm Hg or when diastolic pressure is consistently 90 mm Hg or more.

laboratoryortestresult.name: laboratory or test result
laboratoryortestresult.definition: Laboratory or test result is the result that health care provider takes a sample of your blood, urine, other bodily fluid, or body tissue to get information about your health.

pneumonia,bacterial.name: pneumonia , bacterial
pneumonia,bacterial.definition: Bacterial pneumonia is inflammation of the lung parenchyma that is caused by bacterial infections.

catastrophicillness.name: catastrophic illness
catastrophicillness.definition: Catastrophic illness is an acute or prolonged illness usually considered to be life-threatening or with the threat of serious residual disability. Treatment may be radical and is frequently costly.

ychromosome.name: y chromosome
ychromosome.definition: Y chromosome is the male [MASK] chromosome, being the differential [MASK] chromosome carried by half the male gametes and none of the female gametes in humans and in some other male-heterogametic species in which the homologue of the x chromosome has been retained.

regionalmedicalprograms.name: regional medical programs
regionalmedicalprograms.definition: Regional medical programs is coordination of activities and programs among health care institutions within defined geographic areas for the purpose of improving delivery and quality of medical care to the patients. These programs are mandated under u.s. Public Law 89-239.

neckdissection.name: neck dissection
neckdissection.definition: [MASK] [MASK] is [MASK] in the [MASK] to remove all disease tissues including cervical [MASK] nodes and to leave an adequate margin of normal tissue. This type of surgery is usually used in tumors or cervical metastases in the head and [MASK]. The prototype of [MASK] [MASK] is the radical [MASK] [MASK] described by Crile in 1906.

prescriptions.name: prescriptions
prescriptions.definition: Prescriptions is directions written for the obtaining and use of pharmaceutical preparations; medical devices; corrective lenses; and a variety of other medical remedies.

ligands.name: ligands
ligands.definition: Ligands is a molecule that binds to another molecule, used especially to refer to a small molecule that binds specifically to a larger molecule, e.g., an antigen binding to an antibody, a hormone or neurotransmitter binding to a receptor, or a substrate or allosteric effector binding to an enzyme. Ligands are also molecules that donate or accept a pair of [MASK] to form a coordinate covalent bond with the central metal atom of a coordination complex. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

education,distance.name: education , distance
education,distance.definition: Distance education is education via communication media (correspondence, radio, television, computer networks) with little or no in-person face-to-face contact between students and teachers. (eric Thesaurus, 1997)

bloodpressuredetermination.name: blood pressure determination
bloodpressuredetermination.definition: Blood pressure determination is techniques used for measuring blood pressure.

glutathionetransferase.name: glutathione transferase
glutathionetransferase.definition: Glutathione transferase is a transferase that catalyzes the addition of aliphatic, aromatic, or heterocyclic free radicals as well as epoxides and arene oxides to glutathione. Addition takes place at the sulfur. It also catalyzes the reduction of polyol nitrate by glutathione to polyol and nitrite.

mosquitovectors.name: mosquito vectors
mosquitovectors.definition: Mosquito vectors is mosquitoes (members of the family culicidae) that transmit pathogens or their intermediate forms from one host to another.

recoveryoffunction.name: recovery of function
recoveryoffunction.definition: Recovery of function is a partial or complete return to the normal or proper physiologic activity of an organ or part following disease or trauma.

walking.name: walking
walking.definition: Walking is an activity in which the body advances at a slow to moderate pace by moving the [MASK] in a coordinated fashion. This includes recreational walking, walking for fitness, and competitive race-walking.

proliferatingcellnuclearantigen.name: proliferating cell nuclear antigen
proliferatingcellnuclearantigen.definition: Proliferating cell nuclear antigen is nuclear antigen with a role in dna synthesis, dna repair, and cell cycle progression. pcna is required for the coordinated synthesis of both leading and lagging strands at the replication fork during dna replication. pcna expression correlates with the proliferation activity of several malignant and non-malignant cell types.

biologicalvariation,individual.name: biological variation , individual
biologicalvariation,individual.definition: Individual biological variation is differences in measurable biological values, characteristics, or traits, within one individual under different conditions for the individual such as fasting, season of the year, age, or state of wellness.

newyork.name: new york
newyork.definition: New york is state bounded on the north by [MASK] Ontario and Canada, on the east by Vermont, Massachusetts, and Connecticut, on the south by the Atlantic Ocean, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania, and on the west by Pennsylvania, [MASK] Erie, and Canada.

anesthesia,conduction.name: anesthesia , conduction
anesthesia,conduction.definition: Conduction anesthesia is injection of an anesthetic to inhibit nerve transmission in a specific part of the body.

digitaldivide.name: digital divide
digitaldivide.definition: Digital divide is gap between individuals, households, businesses and geographic areas at different socioeconomic levels with regard to both their opportunities to access electronic  information and communication technologies (ICTs). Their use of the Internet for a wide variety of activities, reflects various differences among and within countries.

potassiumcompounds.name: potassium compounds
potassiumcompounds.definition: Potassium compounds is inorganic compounds that contain potassium as an integral part of the molecule.

particulatematter.name: particulate matter
particulatematter.definition: Particulate matter is particles of any solid substance, generally under 30 microns in size, often noted as pm30. There is special concern with pm1 which can get down to pulmonary alveoli and induce macrophage activation and [MASK] leading to foreign body reaction and lung diseases.

art.name: art
art.definition: Art is processes and results of aesthetic expression.

endometrialhyperplasia.name: endometrial hyperplasia
endometrialhyperplasia.definition: Endometrial hyperplasia is benign proliferation of the endometrium in the uterus. Endometrial hyperplasia is classified by its cytology and glandular tissue. There are simple, complex (adenomatous without atypia), and atypical hyperplasia representing also the ascending risk of becoming malignant.

latex.name: latex
latex.definition: Latex is a milky, product excreted from the latex canals of a variety of plant species that contain cauotchouc. Latex is composed of 25-35% caoutchouc, 60-75% water, 2% protein, 2% resin, 1.5% sugar & 1% ash. rubber is made by the removal of water from latex.(From Concise Encyclopedia Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 3rd ed). Hevein proteins are responsible for latex hypersensitivity. Latexes are used as inert vehicles to carry antibodies or antigens in latex fixation tests.

cornealendothelialcellloss.name: corneal endothelial cell loss
cornealendothelialcellloss.definition: Corneal endothelial cell loss is loss of [MASK] usually following intraocular surgery (e.g., [MASK] surgery) or due to fuchs' endothelial dystrophy; angle-closure glaucoma; iritis; or aging.

leukemiavirus,murine.name: leukemia virus , murine
leukemiavirus,murine.definition: Murine leukemia virus is species of gammaretrovirus, containing many well-defined strains, producing leukemia in mice. Disease is commonly induced by injecting filtrates of propagable tumors into newborn mice.

cytoplasm.name: cytoplasm
cytoplasm.definition: Cytoplasm is the part of a cell that contains the [MASK] and small structures excluding the cell nucleus; mitochondria; and large vacuoles. (Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990)

rangeofmotion,articular.name: range of motion , articular
rangeofmotion,articular.definition: Articular range of motion is the distance and direction to which a bone joint can be extended. Range of motion is a function of the condition of the joints, muscles, and connective tissues involved. Joint flexibility can be improved through appropriate muscle stretching exercises.

indolealkaloids.name: indole alkaloids
indolealkaloids.definition: Indole alkaloids is group of alkaloids containing a benzylpyrrole group (derived from tryptophan).

temperature.name: temperature
temperature.definition: Temperature is the property of objects that determines the direction of heat flow when they are placed in direct thermal contact. The temperature is the energy of microscopic motions (vibrational and translational) of the particles of atoms.

celltracking.name: cell tracking
celltracking.definition: Cell tracking is non-invasive imaging of cells that have been labeled non-destructively, such as with nanoemulsions or [MASK] that can be detected by molecular imaging, to monitor their location, viability, cell lineage expansion, response to drugs, movement, or other behaviors in vivo.

immunoglobuline.name: immunoglobulin e
immunoglobuline.definition: Immunoglobulin e is an immunoglobulin associated with [MASK]. Overexpression has been associated with allergic hypersensitivity (hypersensitivity, immediate).

communitypsychiatry.name: community psychiatry
communitypsychiatry.definition: Community psychiatry is branch of psychiatry concerned with the provision and delivery of a coordinated program of mental health care to a specified population. The foci included in this concept are: all social, psychological and physical factors related to etiology, prevention, and maintaining positive mental health in the community.

menstrualhygieneproducts.name: menstrual hygiene products
menstrualhygieneproducts.definition: Menstrual hygiene products is personal care items used during menstruation.

schools,medical.name: schools , medical
schools,medical.definition: Medical schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of medicine.

glaucomadrainageimplants.name: glaucoma drainage implants
glaucomadrainageimplants.definition: Glaucoma drainage implants is devices, usually incorporating unidirectional valves, which are surgically inserted in the sclera to maintain normal intraocular pressure.
