psychologicaltheory.name: psychological theory
psychologicaltheory.definition: Psychological theory is principles applied to the analysis and explanation of psychological or behavioral phenomena.

salivaryducts.name: salivary ducts
salivaryducts.definition: Salivary ducts is any of the ducts which transport saliva. Salivary ducts include the parotid duct, the major and minor sublingual ducts, and the submandibular duct.

tumornecrosisfactorreceptorsuperfamily,m.name: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 7
tumornecrosisfactorreceptorsuperfamily,m.definition: Member 7 tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily found on most t-lymphocytes. Activation of the receptor by cd70 antigen results in the increased proliferation of cd4-positive t-lymphocytes and cd8-positive t-lymphocytes. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

adoption.name: adoption
adoption.definition: Adoption is voluntary acceptance of a child of other parents to be as one's own child, usually with legal confirmation.

nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member2.name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 2
nuclearreceptorsubfamily1,groupf,member2.definition: Member 2 group f nuclear receptor subfamily 1 is an orphan nuclear receptor that is expressed at high levels in neuronal tissues, the retina; epididymis; and vas deferens. The receptor is believed to play a role in regulating a variety of functions including the processing of sensory information, the differentiation of photoreceptor cells and the circadian rhythm.

webbrowser.name: web browser
webbrowser.definition: Web browser is software application for retrieving, presenting and traversing [MASK] on the World Wide Web.

chromosomedeletion.name: chromosome deletion
chromosomedeletion.definition: Chromosome deletion is actual loss of portion of a chromosome.

vesicularinhibitoryaminoacidtransportpro.name: vesicular inhibitory amino acid transport proteins
vesicularinhibitoryaminoacidtransportpro.definition: Vesicular inhibitory amino acid transport proteins is a family of vesicular neurotransmitter transporter proteins that sequester the inhibitory neurotransmitters glycine; gamma-aminobutyric acid; and possibly gamma-hydroxybutyrate into [MASK].

antibodies,neutralizing.name: antibodies , neutralizing
antibodies,neutralizing.definition: Neutralizing antibodies is antibodies that reduce or abolish some biological activity of a soluble antigen or infectious agent, usually a virus.

venouspressure.name: venous pressure
venouspressure.definition: Venous pressure is the blood pressure in the veins. It is usually measured to assess the filling pressure to the heart ventricle.

anteriorspinalarterysyndrome.name: anterior spinal artery syndrome
anteriorspinalarterysyndrome.definition: Anterior spinal artery syndrome is ischemia or infarction of the spinal cord in the distribution of the anterior spinal artery, which supplies the ventral two-thirds of the spinal cord. This condition is usually associated with atherosclerosis of the aorta and may result from [MASK] of an aortic aneurysm or rarely [MASK] of the anterior spinal artery. Clinical features include weakness and loss of pain and temperature sensation below the level of injury, with relative sparing of position and vibratory sensation. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1249-50)

angina,unstable.name: angina , unstable
angina,unstable.definition: Unstable angina is precordial pain at rest, which may precede a myocardial infarction.

animals,geneticallymodified.name: animals , genetically modified
animals,geneticallymodified.definition: Genetically modified animals is animals whose genome has been altered by genetic engineering, or their offspring.

chemotaxis.name: chemotaxis
chemotaxis.definition: Chemotaxis is the movement of cells or organisms toward or away from a substance in response to its concentration gradient.

genomics.name: genomics
genomics.definition: Genomics is the systematic study of the complete dna sequences (genome) of organisms.

cysts.name: cysts
cysts.definition: Cysts is any fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an epithelium. Cysts can be of normal, abnormal, non-neoplastic, or neoplastic tissues.

plantdispersal.name: plant dispersal
plantdispersal.definition: Plant dispersal is the physical distribution of plants in various forms and stages of development through time and space.

mitochondrialswelling.name: mitochondrial swelling
mitochondrialswelling.definition: Mitochondrial swelling is an increase in mitochondrial volume due to an influx of fluid; it occurs in hypotonic solutions due to osmotic pressure and in isotonic solutions as a result of altered permeability of the membranes of respiring mitochondria.

conservationofnaturalresources.name: conservation of natural resources
conservationofnaturalresources.definition: Conservation of natural resources is the protection, preservation, restoration, and rational use of all resources in the total environment.

genes,fungal.name: genes , fungal
genes,fungal.definition: Fungal genes is the functional hereditary units of fungi.

iontransport.name: ion transport
iontransport.definition: Ion transport is the movement of ions across energy-transducing cell membranes. Transport can be active, passive or facilitated. Ions may travel by themselves (uniport), or as a group of two or more ions in the same (symport) or opposite (antiport) directions.

bloodcoagulationfactors.name: blood coagulation factors
bloodcoagulationfactors.definition: Blood coagulation factors is endogenous substances, usually proteins, that are involved in the blood coagulation process.

colon,ascending.name: colon , ascending
colon,ascending.definition: Ascending colon is the segment of large intestine between the cecum and the transverse colon. It passes cephalad from the cecum to the caudal surface of the right lobe of the liver where it bends sharply to the left, forming the right colic flexure.

rectalabsorption.name: rectal absorption
rectalabsorption.definition: Rectal absorption is uptake of substances from the rectum.

models,theoretical.name: models , theoretical
models,theoretical.definition: Theoretical models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of systems, processes, or phenomena. They include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

alertfatigue,healthpersonnel.name: alert fatigue , health personnel
alertfatigue,healthpersonnel.definition: Health personnel alert fatigue is mental fatigue experienced by health care providers who encounter numerous alerts and reminders from the use of clinical decision support systems. As the numbers of alerts and reminders designed to provide meaningful assistance to the patient care process increases, many health personnel may ignore them.

burns,electric.name: burns , electric
burns,electric.definition: Electric burns is burns produced by contact with electric current or from a sudden discharge of electricity.

hemoglobinj.name: hemoglobin j
hemoglobinj.definition: Hemoglobin j is a group of abnormal hemoglobins with similar electrophoretic characteristics. They have faster electrophoretic mobility and different [MASK] in either the alpha or beta chains than normal adult hemoglobin. Some of the variants produce hematologic abnormalities, others result in no clinical disorders.

civildisorders.name: civil disorders
civildisorders.definition: Civil disorders is deliberate and planned acts of unlawful behavior engaged in by aggrieved segments of the population in seeking social change.

lymphocyteculturetest,mixed.name: lymphocyte culture test , mixed
lymphocyteculturetest,mixed.definition: Mixed lymphocyte culture test is measure of histocompatibility at the hl-a locus. Peripheral blood lymphocytes from two individuals are mixed together in tissue culture for several days. Lymphocytes from incompatible individuals will stimulate each other to proliferate significantly (measured by tritiated thymidine uptake) whereas those from compatible individuals will not. In the one-way mlc test, the lymphocytes from one of the individuals are inactivated (usually by treatment with mitomycin or radiation) thereby allowing only the untreated remaining population of cells to proliferate in response to foreign histocompatibility antigens.

mutation.name: mutation
mutation.definition: Mutation is any detectable and heritable change in the genetic material that causes a change in the genotype and which is transmitted to daughter cells and to succeeding generations.

hepatitis,viral,animal.name: hepatitis , viral , animal
hepatitis,viral,animal.definition: Animal viral hepatitis is inflammation of the liver in animals due to viral infection.

fattyacidsynthesisinhibitors.name: fatty acid synthesis inhibitors
fattyacidsynthesisinhibitors.definition: Fatty acid synthesis inhibitors is compounds that interfere with fatty acid synthase resulting in a reduction of fatty acids. This is a target mechanism in humans of some antineoplastic agents and anti-obesity agents and of some anti-infective agents which interfere with cell wall and cell membrane formation.

kansas.name: kansas
kansas.definition: Kansas is state bounded on the north by Nebraska on the east by Missouri, on the south by Oklahoma, and on the west by Colorado.

pancreas.name: pancreas
pancreas.definition: Pancreas is a nodular organ in the abdomen that contains a mixture of endocrine glands and exocrine glands. The small endocrine portion consists of the islets of langerhans secreting a number of hormones into the blood [MASK]. The large exocrine portion (exocrine pancreas) is a compound acinar gland that secretes several digestive enzymes into the pancreatic ductal system that empties into the duodenum.

sugaracids.name: sugar acids
sugaracids.definition: Sugar acids is monosaccharides and other sugars that contain one or more carboxylic acid moieties.

escherichiacolivaccines.name: escherichia coli vaccines
escherichiacolivaccines.definition: Escherichia coli vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat both enterotoxigenic and enteropathogenic Escherichia coli infections.

molecularprobetechniques.name: molecular probe techniques
molecularprobetechniques.definition: Molecular probe techniques is the use of devices which use detector molecules to detect, investigate, or analyze other molecules, macromolecules, molecular aggregates, or organisms.

peripheralnervoussystemneoplasms.name: peripheral nervous system neoplasms
peripheralnervoussystemneoplasms.definition: Peripheral nervous system neoplasms is neoplasms which arise from peripheral nerve tissue. This includes neurofibromas; schwannomas; granular cell tumors; and malignant peripheral nerve sheath neoplasms. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology, 5th ed, pp1750-1)

rabbits.name: rabbits
rabbits.definition: Rabbits is a burrowing plant-eating mammal with hind limbs that are longer than its fore limbs. It belongs to the family Leporidae of the order Lagomorpha, and in contrast to hares, possesses 22 instead of 24 pairs of chromosomes.

receptors,ige.name: receptors , ige
receptors,ige.definition: Ige receptors is specific molecular sites on the surface of b- and T-lymphocytes which combine with IgEs. Two subclasses exist: low affinity receptors (Fc epsilon rii) and high affinity receptors (Fc epsilon ri).

proteomics.name: proteomics
proteomics.definition: Proteomics is the systematic study of the complete complement of proteins (proteome) of organisms.

atlas.name: atlas
atlas.definition: Atlas is work consisting of collections of illustrative plates, charts, etc., usually with explanatory captions.

medicine,eastasiantraditional.name: medicine , east asian traditional
medicine,eastasiantraditional.definition: East asian traditional medicine is medical practice or discipline that is based on the knowledge, cultures, and beliefs of the people in east asia.

twinstudiesastopic.name: twin studies as topic
twinstudiesastopic.definition: Twin studies as topic is works about methods of detecting genetic etiology in human traits. The basic premise of twin studies is that monozygotic twins carry identical genes, while zygotic twins are genetically no more similar than two siblings born after separate pregnancies. (Last, j.m., a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

infectioncontrolpractitioners.name: infection control practitioners
infectioncontrolpractitioners.definition: Infection control practitioners is physicians or other qualified individuals responsible for implementing and overseeing the policies and procedures followed by a health care facility to reduce the risk of infection to patients and staff.

transcriptionelongation,genetic.name: transcription elongation , genetic
transcriptionelongation,genetic.definition: Genetic transcription elongation is the lengthening of a nascent rna molecule by rna polymerase during transcription.

emergencyservices,psychiatric.name: emergency services , psychiatric
emergencyservices,psychiatric.definition: Psychiatric emergency services is organized services to provide immediate psychiatric care to patients with acute psychological disturbances.

aniontransportproteins.name: anion transport proteins
aniontransportproteins.definition: Anion transport proteins is membrane proteins whose primary function is to facilitate the transport of negatively charged molecules (anions) across a biological membrane.

rnacapanalogs.name: rna cap analogs
rnacapanalogs.definition: Rna cap analogs is analogs of rna cap compounds which do not have a positive charge. These compounds inhibit the initiation of translation of both capped and uncapped messenger rna.

pregnancy,prolonged.name: pregnancy , prolonged
pregnancy,prolonged.definition: Prolonged pregnancy is a term used to describe pregnancies that exceed the upper limit of a normal gestational period. In humans, a prolonged pregnancy is defined as one that extends beyond 42 weeks (294 days) after the first day of the last menstrual period (menstruation), or birth with gestational age of 41 weeks or more.

worldwarii.name: world war ii
worldwarii.definition: World war ii is global [MASK] involving countries of Europe, Africa, Asia, and North America that occurred between 1939 and 1945.

hammertoesyndrome.name: hammer toe syndrome
hammertoesyndrome.definition: Hammer toe syndrome is a condition characterized by a series of interrelated digital symptoms and joint changes of the lesser digits and metatarsophalangeal joints of the [MASK]. The syndrome can include some or all of the following conditions: hammer toe, claw toe, mallet toe, overlapping fifth toe, curly toe, exostosis; hyperostosis; interdigital heloma, or contracted toe.

receptors,mitogen.name: receptors , mitogen
receptors,mitogen.definition: Mitogen receptors is glycoprotein molecules on the surface of b- and T-lymphocytes, that react with molecules of antilymphocyte sera, lectins, and other agents which induce [MASK] of lymphocytes.

protonpumps.name: proton pumps
protonpumps.definition: Proton pumps is integral membrane proteins that transport protons across a membrane. This transport can be linked to the hydrolysis of adenosine triphosphate. What is referred to as [MASK] frequently is about potassium hydrogen atpase.

blindness.name: blindness
blindness.definition: Blindness is the inability to see or the loss or absence of perception of visual stimuli. This condition may be the result of eye diseases; optic nerve diseases; optic chiasm diseases; or brain diseases affecting the visual pathways or occipital lobe.

immunity,active.name: immunity , active
immunity,active.definition: Active immunity is resistance to a disease agent resulting from the production of specific antibodies by the host, either after exposure to the disease or after vaccination.
